name: Romancelvania
detailed_description: Play as a lovelorn, brooding Drac who, after a century of moping around post-heartbreak, is thrown into a monster reality-dating show, hosted by the Grim Reaper! Explore Transylvania’s perilous countryside as you slay absurd baddies on your hunt for the most eligible monsters. Will Drac find “Love at first Bite”, or will he discover “Love Sucks”?” Discover the 'human' inside each monster as you romance, befriend or eliminate a cast of 12 fully-voiced supernatural contestants! Taking your relationships to the next level progresses your own strength, abilities, and more. It's not a reality show until there's some drama! Make-up or break-up - we don't judge! With a weaving story full of dialogue and narrative options, as well as the ability to choose your body type and voice, become the ultimate decision-maker in YOUR story. From the voluptuous Smashmounds, to the back alleys of Booty Bay, and everything in between, discover an unpredictable, interconnected world filled with monsters to recruit, hidden date spots, and outlandish baddies and boss encounters. As the former glorious Drac, stripped of their old powers, it’s up to you to become your best bloodthirsty self. Vanquish goons with iconic weapons, elementals, bats, and even Medusa’s 'headouken!' on the road to your victorious rampage in this side-scrolling platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: TLDR so far: Play on keyboard and don't expect the best of either world (smut or Metroidvania). Expect a lot of silly and cheesy humor along with puns, which I'm all down for. There are some glitches that get annoying.Okay I'm going to give this a thumbs up AND HOPE THE DEVS READ THIS.This game has a lot of potential, but it is not ready.  Edit: There is a growing issue of my character just getting stuck and NOT moving. Verified integrity and hoping that fixes it. This was not an issue prior but it has caused major loss of progress and even happened in a big boss fight where I just couldn't move and died. Had to Alt f4I agree with everyone else. It needs a map. I play more romance games than metroidvania games (though I have done both) and realize how detrimental now it is that you need a map. There's too much back tracking, too many things triggered even though it's not CLEAR that we've triggered something (like doors that unlocked, awards we can now have) to not have a map. You get the double jump too late in the game to NOT have a map. The controls are painful.  EDIT: I stopped using the joystick and started using D-pad (again I don't play MV's often) and this was also when my character started getting stuck in place. But even with D-pad, The headukin and the tornado blood heal triggers randomly. It's far too sensitive and those take way too long to recharge for it to be messing up the way it does. Controller support for something like this HAS to be spot on.  The character list still seems a little one sided. Again I understand why, as Drac wasn't intentionally going to have a female option, but if you are going to ADD something like that, you need to commit. I can hear male grunts and groans while attacking.  I noticed some complaints on the pixel VS smooth animation and how bad/tacky it is. I have to say 1) that is NOT how this game is. 2) The back drops are GORGEOUS. My favorite so far is the pumpkin patch back drop, but no, the pixelated back drop isn't a theme throughout and it's actually REALLY nice sets and back drops. Another great thing is the voice acting and writing. This game has no business delivering such strong voices to these characters lol Bravo to both aspects. (Mind you, if this kinda cheese isn't your style, you won't like the writing, but the characters are really well thought out and the writing is genuinely good). The music is also a 10/10!I mentioned random flashing but it has not happened since.The models can look down right hilariously goofy, but not in a charming way, just in a graphic design error kinda way. But it fits the vibes, not really a complaint of mine, just an observation.They also made it a point to say they didn't want this game raunchy, but have sexual elements, some cursing, but keep it kinda sfw. I admire that approach, but the problem is, when you don't go all in on an idea, everything seems half baked. The combat isn't a *successful* metroidvania, and the dating sim side is only a tease, so I can see it as turning some people off (not pun intended). I personally do not mind this. I think this is perfectly fine for me, but I wish SOMETHING they went for would be given more. This review will change as I play it, but I REALLY want this to succeed. I want people to see that we want games like this, and even if this didn't hit the mark, maybe someone else can do it or they can buff things up.  I am having a blast, I swear, but this is for people who want an objective thought. Some reviews are just saying it's not working or this game isn't done, and maybe they could have taken a bit more time and care into fixing these. I think the price could be lowered or the game be patched really soon or I fear the negative reviews will tank it. I think it's worth it if you are willing to play around the problems, which are all very small, but CAN add up the frustration over time.Edit: If I had finished a quest I was on at the time of writing this I would have met another male, so that's good. I have discovered more choices, playing heavily on the drama of reality dating tv, which I also greatly enjoy. My headukin is still poppin off but it's too late to move to keyboard for me lol I also think the grunts and groans of attacking and being attacked as female drac still has the male grunts in it? I can't tell 100%, but found it half amusing, half annoying lol If you hold down the button one millisecond too long it skips dialogue, which I often forget, so I do skip some talking or pop ups to tell me what I just got

_childDocuments_.review: For context: I kickstarted this project and purchased the game separately. I played through the first act, meeting all 3 initial contestants, completing the bar scene and going on a date. I played through some conversations multiple times. I don't currently recommend the game. I'm leaving review meant as constructive criticism. There's a term called "Bethesda's Bug," a play on Schroedinger's cat, that a certain YouTube games critic game up with. It describes how difficult it is to judge Bethesda games at launch due to how buggy they usually are - is a given issue an actual bug, a design flaw, or something that just didn't get finished in time? Since you can never know without developer insight, how do you fairly critique the game? Now, add to that a layer of comedy, and it gets even harder - if you're playing a game designed as a parody and you come across something that feels broken, is it actually a flaw, or just part of the joke you didn't get? It's hard to judge Romancelvania because pretty much every aspect of the game - UI, menus, attacks, animations, enemies, voices, audio - feels broken, unpolished, or incomplete. But, how much of that is intentional? How much of that is "the joke?" Whether or not you enjoy this game is going to depend on your take on that question, and whether or not you think that joke is funny. Here are some examples of what I mean. When you press a button to attack, the enemy takes damage immediately, and THEN your character (Drac) unsheathes their weapon and performs an attack animation. The damage happens BEFORE Drac moves. Is that the joke? Is it critiquing older games with janky attacks, or is it just implemented incorrectly? How about, when you use your spear attack, sometimes your camera stays in place and your character shoots forward, other times the camera snaps disorientingly to Drac's destination. Sometimes when you let go of the jump button while Drac is gaining height, he stops rising IMMEDIATELY as if hitting a brick wall, sometimes (seemingly past a certain height threshold) he gradually loses momentum then falls. Is that a parody of how in old Castlevania games, jumping was janky? Or just a bug? How about the enemies... there's a dog that seems to be playing a looping running animation and is just rotated 180 degrees when it turns at the end of a platform. A miniboss that literally, no joke has only one move and a ton of health, and the move causes your camera to shake uncontrollably. The first boss which has three moves, one of which spawns an enemy, another of which... spawns an enemy. Is that a parody of bad boss design? Let's say you're in a room with 3 enemies and 3 breakable objects. With a single spear dash you could destroy everything in the room, after which text for XP, Gold, and Damage appears over everything. Only, some of it stays in place, some of it floats around, some of it fades away to gray, some of it overlays on top of Drac's head (the $ amount) and layers over itself so you can't read it. A parody of games like Borderlands that have dmg and xp text flying everywhere or just a mess?Let's talk about the dating sim / visual novel stuff. You know how in most VNs, since there aren’t many cinematics or animations, they make sure to give every character a collection of illustrated portraits with different expressions, and swap them out to match the emotion of the dialogue they're saying? There's a scene early on where you're chatting up romantic prospects at a bar. Each character, including Drac, only gets one portrait, with one expression, that then gets resized/scaled and placed in seemingly random places on the screen. Is that a lampoon of VNs, or did they only get to draw one portrait and not know where to position it?More on the dating sim aspect - when I talked to one of the first three romanceable characters, I was only given positive dialogue options, and my "relationship meter" went up a full progress bar from saying two things to them. Later when trying to be not interested in other characters, my only dialogue choices were sometimes forced to "Flirty," "Sexy" or "Friendly." Or you would get asked to do a quest, and could only say "yes" or "yes and I'll do a side quest too." When you get to your first real date, conversation options are removed entirely and you simply watch a 3D cutscene of the characters talking (amusingly, Drac stares at something off-camera the whole time, not your date partner). So, is the limited choice and autonomy in the VN side of the game a parody of other VNs - or just not very fleshed out? Let's talk about audio for a minute. So the airhorn sound that plays when you press OK is obviously a joke - but what about the cheesy wolf howl when you dash? The fart reverb sound when you double jump? The voices that are so quiet that you can barely hear them sometimes? The horrible pitched-down grunting sounds all the enemies make? The uncomfortable high pitch sound it makes when you hit a marble enemy? Are these parodies of other games's audio? And weirdly there seems to be a problem with the game's echo effect? Like in many areas it sounds like characters are talking in a big cathedral even if they're in a small room, and that echo makes it hard to hear the next thing they say. Not sure about that one.Here’s the thing - the game does actually, genuinely make me laugh at times. The first boss has an introduction during which he only communicates with you passive-aggressively via bureaucratic memos and forms. The skeletons with pool noodle weapons got a laugh, as did the Down-N-Out burger sign. The music and atmosphere in the gallery was genuinely creepy, the marble skin being stripped from the marble men to reveal flesh underneath was so good! I liked the Spitter enemy visual design, very cool. The tongue was random but an interesting idea for an enemy. And I admit, it got old eventually, but the airhorn got more than one laugh. So with all that being said, do I recommend this game... sadly no. I do think the devs have a unique sense of humor and creative spark, and when it works, it's genuinely funny and sometimes endearing. I think it's most funny though, when it's developing its own sense of humor rather than just referencing things. Like, ♥♥♥♥'s interactions via printed out forms was hilarious. The half-dozen on-the-nose Ghostbusters references were not. In my opinion, if you're going to parody something most effectively, you kind of have to understand what makes it work to break it down and joke about it. I didn't really get the sense that the devs were fully parodying or providing any specific commentary either on VNs or Metroidvanias, more just throwing a bunch of references and gameplay bits together to see what sticks. And the more I played the more I felt that the janky mechanics were just that, janky, not part of the joke. Your mileage may vary but it didn't work for me. My advice to the devs is maybe consider labelling this an early access title. Double down on your own unique sense of humor, less on the references. Make sure that the "core" each of your main gameplay parts, the dating and the Metroidvania, is at least solid and somewhat polished and consistent with some depth - then from that baseline, strike out and parody away. Fix the bugs and expand on your strong suits and re-release as a full title in a little while. Then I think this could really be a hit. Until then I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!  Very unique and full of laughs.  The characters were more 3 dimensional than you would expect and the story was mostly good too.I do want to warn anyone who struggles with suicidal ideation though that there is an unavoidable part of the game that forces you to "sacrifice yourself."  I struggle with these thoughts almost daily and use video games as an escape mechanism, so it messed me up to suddenly come across that in such a seemingly light-hearted and fun game, and maybe I'm not far enough removed, but I don't feel like it really added anything to the story either.  I wish there'd been an alternate choice or that part could've been left out.  At the very least maybe a warning could be added.

_childDocuments_.review: When this game works, it is a lot of fun. It is genuinely hilarious, at times, heart-warming, and extremely clever. I love these characters so dearly and the world building is great. I am at the last chapter of the game and I cannot stress how good the writing is on just about every level. The level design and the places this story were surprisingly well done for the horny vampire game. That doesn't mean the game is flawless and it shows a pretty extreme level of disrespect for the player's time with egregious fetch quests that will see you transporting across the map just to turn around and do it three more times with little in the way of actual gameplay in-between. But the biggest strike against this game is the technical state. For one thing, I've had a straight up hardlock in the beginning of the game because of sequencing that could reasonably happen fairly often and various softlocks. I've also had quests display incorrect descriptions, dialogue simply not play, and more.The controls are also incredibly frustrating and the charge timers for flares are baffling. Wolf run specifically makes no sense. You can wolf run infinitely (unless you hit an obstacle or take damage) and no matter how long you used the skill, whether it's a minute or half a second, your CD is the exact same, making backtracking (a core part of this genre) more tedious than it ever needed to be.Beyond that the controls don't feel that good and some inputs you'd expect to work, don't. For example if you crouch and use a weapon attack, you'll stand and use the attack, but when you stop attacking you don't return to a crouch even when you're holding the button. You have to stop attacking then click crouch. This game is fairly easy on normal mode and I haven't died on trash mobs yet but I think most players will take a lot of unexpected damage over things not working the way you'd expect it to.The game needs a patch or a few.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually can't recommend this game enough and I will be nominating it for most innovative gameplay. I was expecting a few laughs from this game for sure but what I didn't expect was to actually only maybe have 3 small problems with it. Romancelvania is essentially a mixture of the show "The Bachelor" (dating sim) and a metroidvania. You have a cast of monsters (who are player sexual might I add) who are all trying to win your heart in a competition for your love. Let me go ahead and just hop into the pros and cons. As always, Pros first. Pros: - The Game is Player Sexuality and Gender friendly. They let the player pick they're gender in a way that I think leaves it up for interpretation on how they came to their gender identification. Which I think is refreshing. Also, as previously stated, the monsters are player sexual. I think aside from Asexual (which, even that I'm pretty sure some monsters imply that sex isn't important, the feelings are what matters so even Asexual people can have a romantic relationship. However, it does imply that Drac messes around with some contestants soooo. Iffy on that), you can confidently play this with any sexuality in mind and be totally fine. (Some monsters specifically state that they're down for open/poly/etc relationships!)- The Story is really fleshed out. Each character does seem to have their own story, insecurities, flaws, things they're good at, etc. Drac (the player) has a background, but not a lot of specific details. I think that's so players can insert their own story as well. Even the "villain" who tries to apologize for their actions doesn't get forgiven instantly. It's a great story for the funny lil dating sim that it is. - The characters follow tropes, but not always in the way you expect which is refreshing. All dating sims have "tropes" for the potential love interests and this game is no different, but I feel like this game adds little twists to the tropes that make them different and new to the players.  - The gameplay, controls, the overall feel for the way this game plays is smooth. It's definitely better on controller, but even on keyboard I found it relatively easy to play. It all flows really well which can be a toss up for metroidvanias/platformers sometimes in my opinion. - The music, THE MUSIC! *Chef's kiss* I love it. The songs will be added to playlists for me to have on in the background while I'm doing work. Only bangin soundtracks (Hades, Hotline Miami, Etc) earn that honor for me.- The game is HYSTERICAL. I was only expecting a few laughs but this game had my laughing out loud on numerous occasions.  Admittedly, though,  I do have a couple of small things I would change. The Cons: - I really feel like the game doesn't properly give you time to get to know all the characters. For example, rather than give you all the love interests at once, they start you with 3 and then before you can go get more added to the cast, you already have to vote one off. Like I feel like it should be more like The Bachelor and just give us all the contestants at once and let me meet all of them before I go voting people off. It just feels like you more have time to get to know 2 of the first 3 WAY more than the others. Later characters get almost no time on screen whereas the first 3 have all the time with you. Unless you look up where all you can take certain dates and specifically plan things out to make sure you spend, roughly, the same amount of time to get to know them all, you miss out on some characters. Which, I know it inspires multiple playthroughs that way, but I think most people would've played multiple times anyway just to get to interact with other love interests in a more focused fashion. So I wish they would've just given us all the characters from the start. - Backer Recognition rooms: This is admittedly a small and petty complaint, but I hate when developers put in backer rewards into the game itself. In this game there are multiple rooms in the mansion where its just dedicated to the backers of the game on kickstarter which I feel is super immersion breaking. I'm not saying that the devs shouldn't recognize their backers, I just think after/during the credits with minigames/cutscenes are a better use for that so it's not just awkwardly out of place in the middle of my game. - Boring Final Boss: This game has one of my least favorite things about final bosses. Its a "hard" boss, but they've only made them hard by giving them a super large health pool. Which makes the fight drawn out, repetitive, boring, and honestly, anti-climatic. - No big warning for a particular scene that could be triggering to those with mental health issues or who know people with them. SPOILER/TRIGGER WARNING: As someone who personally struggles with this, it was very.. sudden and uncomfortable compared to the rest of the game. I wish there had been an option to skip this scene with the warning of what occurs. Other than those things though I do actually really like this game. Just for those of us out there fighting a war with our own brains, please keep that trigger in mind. I really recommend this game, faults and all. I would give it a 9/10. If you feel the need to wait for the sale, do so, but it's worth the full price too!

_childDocuments_.review: In all my time of reviewing games on Steam, there are not of a lot of instances where I get legitimately angry at a game. Sure, I have moments of frustration and disappointment, but game development is not an easy task, and so many things can go wrong in a very small period of time. There are games that are much worse then Romancelvania, but in most cases, you can see it right away. And there are games with a lot worse potential then Romancelvania. But the combination of the interesting concept with a technical execution that at one point made me physically ill, along with some of the most baffling decisions on a gameplay perspective that I have ever seen: makes it so that I have not only to indicate to not buy this game: but question how things went so wrong on the development side.Let me try to start with the positive. The concept of playing as Dracula looking for love again has potential, and you can see it in here and times. Some of the few characters I came across have some depth to them, and does make me want to see what the game's story had for them. The humor, while overall missing for me, did have moments that got a legit chuckle out of me, and the character designs do have some interesting elements and thought put into them. Now that I got that out of the way, I have to question to the developers why the actual Metroidvania element of this game wasn't scrapped, because my god it doesn't work. First of all: of all the things that I don't expect to be a problem in a metroidvania/platforming type game:  the camera. The camera is way too fast in most instances, causing a swing that makes it hard to follow even the simplest of movements. It really emphasizes some of the most baffling animations and attacks that look like it's skipping frames at several points. The fact that the ability to “peek” when looking down happens so quickly when playing with a analog stick controller caused screen shake that physically made me ill at times with the violent nature of it. A simple eye test would have said “wait, something's wrong here”, and I'm not exactly sure how it was allowed to release in this state.Then let's move to the exploration and the combat. The weird mixture of 2D and 3D elements feel like two completely different teams were working on the game, and combine poorly in what isn't exactly a looker of a game to begin with. There are times where I felt like the cohesion of the environments and enemies made absolutely no sense: sure, skeletons in the castlevania theme make sense, but the walking tongue that feels completely seperate art wise from them just leads to confusion and wondering if the game picked up assets and didn't modify them for the game's overall theming. It doesn't help that menu navigation feels clunky on looking at even simple information in the menu (hint, it shouldn't be a problem to exit the menu from different sub screens), and the lack of a map is a baffling design decision especially when you consider the game's namesake. There's no real in environment tools in most cases to figure out what you have seen before. And while the idea of a bat holding a spotlight on you is a cool idea in theory: in practice leads to moments where I'm making leaps of faith because I literally can't see where I'm going. Then, we move to the combat, which has no impact whatsoever and feels like an early game developer project that is more of a prototype more then anything else. Look, I don't want to be mean despite my frustration here: I get it, this may have not been the forte of the developer. I want them to grow. But when animations and hits feel like I'm hitting air: that I'm not getting the feedback that I need to know if things are going right, and the combat feeling so lifeless and stiff that I wonder if I need to pull a Pinocchio to get some fun out of it: something went terribly wrong. I hate how even killing a simple series of enemies felt like a chore. The one boss I came across felt like it was slapped together with little rhyme and reason, and once again I have to question to the developers: it's clear this is on another distant level compared to the story: and I get that you had the game kickstarted so you had obligations to fill. But at some point, you had to realize how clunky and bad the game felt, and needed to make a decision to save the core concept of your game. It's not like the story and presentation would have been a world beater eater. There are decisions that really make me question the sanity off the developer: the horns on certain confirmation elements that digs into my skull like the Cereberal Bore makes me wonder if the game was trying to present itself as an ironic joke, but it's more then that. The writing still can be very groan worthy and makes me ask a lot more questions then I get answers at times, and not giving more back story about Drac and his lost love makes me question how truly heart broken he is when he literally in the next moment is trying to smooth talk his way through things without a care in the world. The game needed a lot more build up of his character and his struggles to really connect with him: for us to care about him, before anything along the lines of dating came up. I do question if one of the early choices in the game were designed to literally make us hate him, but I may be bias in the dude-bro attitude presented there. Look, I stream and play a lot of indie games. I have rules about what I cover and what I look for in that coverage. One of those rules is that no matter what I cover, I do not refund the game. I made content, I paid for the game, but it would be against my code to then turn around and refund it. This game literally made me test that my will on that point. I felt so disappointed, so misled in terms of the game's concept and execution that I literally had to stop my stream, go and get a chocolate shake to deal with the disappointment and anger I felt.I'm sorry, there's a game that can be salvaged under the surface in the Visual Novel type dating element here: but what's presented is one of the most frustrating and soul crushing experiences that I've had on Steam in a long while.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, this game tries to do too many things at once. Billed as a cross between a dating-sim and a Castlevania spoof, it really does neither of those mechanics well. The Romance sim is a cheesy corn ball send off of eroge style dating games, but doesn't give you any of the meat that would normally warrant, and the castlevania mechanics are really sloppy. Hit boxes are all over the place, moves occur totally unintended, the lighting in the game tries for a gimmicky bat with a spotlight thing but then hides enemies in near total dark platforms that you can't see. Literally my second boss fight, there were so many things happening and so many different mechanics going on at once that I gave up. If I hadn't put more than 2 hours into it, I'd be asking for a refund. Cannot recommend without a lot being done to the action side of the game to make much less sloppy.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mix of a Metroidvania && a dating sim.  That is a cool idea, but this execution is less than ideal.They produced a:B- Dating simC+ Metroidvania gameThe Pros:- Fun Voice acting.- Good characters- Decent Story- OK platformingCons:- Extremely Easy Combat- Lack in variety in enemies. - Weird 3D modeling & 2D combinations- Dating sim has poor mechanics. - - Gift giving is extremely basic.- - Unlike normal dating sims there is no location/day cycle.- - There doesn't appear to be a way to loose favor with your dates.- - They do a "Rose Ceremony" to eliminate people you can date before you even meet all of your options.Over all this game is worth playing if you have spare time and you get it for less than $10 (2023 dollars).But it isn't worth playing more than once, and definitely don't bother trying to get the achievements.  You play it once for the story and then shelve it.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a good game in here, but it needs a decent amount of love for me to recommend it, especially at its current price. Between bugs galore (seriously, save fairly often, I ran into multiple soft locks and hard crashed at least twice), lack of deep commit to the metroidvania movement and combat fundamentals (back dash/dodge is crazy inconsistent, attack animations+movement+recoil are meh, etc), and other random jank (the map is...well, better than not having one, I guess), its just not there. But, it is one or two real solid updates focusing on polish and core features from being something I can recommend. Hoping the DLC will address these issues and add more fun. There really is something good here, it just hasn't been fully articulated yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this so much. I love the silly premise. I love vampires. I love metroidvanias. This had a recipe for success.It doesn't come across in the trailers but the controls are unresponsive, laggy, and buggy almost to the point of making the game unplayable. Sometimes attacks simply don't work for no discernible reason. The down-to-forward special move triggers whenever it's on cooldown no matter what I do. My character won't turn and attack fast enough to react to anything.Combine that with a camera that's too close to see immediate threats, atrocious lighting making enemies practically invisible in some spots, enemies that will smack you immediately after a screen transition, and many more annoyances that should have been caught in testing, and the metroidvania portion is rendered unenjoyable on any level.The writing and voice acting are the standouts. While there are a handful of missteps, most of it is entertaining and corny in exactly the right way. I pushed through more of the horrible gameplay than I would have otherwise but in the end I simply couldn't do it.Maybe if it was $10 I could recommend it with the above caveats, but a game with controls this broken absolutely does not warrant a $25 pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent concept ruined by lack of support from the devs. The core premise and overall design of the game could have lead to something truly amazing, but instead the devs hit 1.0 and basically called it quits. I genuinely think if the devs had committed to a few months of patches, it'd be a much better experience.Besides just the game itself, I backed this as a project on Kickstarter and never received any of the physical rewards. _childDocuments_.review: This game's a little rough. I can see what they were going for, and the background art is pretty great, but this feels more like a demo than a finished game. * Enemies often can't be seen in the dark. You get a bat companion who can feed you power ups, and it's also a source of light which I suspect might've been a bandaid for the lighting issue.* Attack controls are floaty and occasionally completely unresponsive.* Entrances into new zones need to be made more obvious.* UI is sometimes VERY hard to see. Nearly impossible to tell which color you're selecting for text.* UI is also not very informative. When am I due for a Rating Up, which I'm assuming is like a level up? What is the element of a crystal when viewed in the quick switch menu? How long can I stay in Wolf or Mist form?* I've never been glad to have a double jump ability taken away before. The camera movement is very jarring, and I got pretty motion sick. Maybe lock camera movement to the character instead of having it jump so far above Drac.* YMMV here, but the writing is... not great. I eventually turned the voices completely off so I wouldn't have to hear some of those lines read out loud.* Even if you turn voices off, sometimes you still get voiced lines?* Some of the SFX could stand to be switched up. You can only hear an airhorn so many times before it stops being amusing, if it was ever amusing at all.* Control while talking to another character switches randomly between keyboard and controller.* Please, for the love of god, we need a map we can open at any time, not just for fast travel.* A female Drac was one of the stretch goals, which didn't actually get met but I appreciated the developers unlocking it for us anyway. That being said, why can you only start as male Drac? I didn't hate what I played, but I certainly didn't love it either, and I can't in good conscience recommend the game to anyone else until Romancelvania's spent a little more time cooking. I'm not sure I want to pick it back up, especially if I'm going to be getting that nauseating double jump back in the future. I appreciate that the developers worked very hard and I'm glad the game is out, but it isn't yet an enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I've actually 100% the game and got all achievements. The normal blind playthrough is about 12 hours if you are wondering. It is a very fun experience: the voice acting, dialogue, soundtrack, areas - all great, BUT... this game needs a LOT of polish and improvement to be considered a great game and not just fun experience. I agree with a lot of reviews here - the game underdelivers on both Platformer and Dating Sim aspects. Here are the some glaring problems in my opinion:  - the weakest part of the game, oh where to start...- You just get overpowered way too fast and that removes any challenge or care regarding (janky) combat and platforming. Two spells (called flairs in game) are broken and functionally make you invincible. Once you get them fully upgraded (which is super cheap) - you can forget about avoiding enemy attacks and stage hazards at all, even on the hardest mode. Imagine if the throne fountain followed you in DOTA 2? That's one of the spells - exactly as broken as it sounds. To make you even more OP you can buy immunities (again - super cheap) BEFORE you even beat the stages where these immunities are applicable. One of the joys of platformers is beating all hazards with your own finger acrobatics and it's just gone too fast in this game - which makes an already boring combat even more boring. IMHO immunities should be removed altogether for Hard Mode or the cost for them increased significantly.- It is very hard to see the enemies sometimes. Early on there is an area with a lot of flashing lights in the background that obscures some small enemy bats. It's so annoying and it happens in other areas as well where some ghosts or whatnot get mashed together with grey background etc.- Exploration is rewarded, but some "out of the way" areas that you can find LOOK as if they are supposed to have some reward, but just don't - they are completely empty. There is even a whole new "screen" with new background in one area that is only accessible later on when you backtrack to it and there is just nothing there - empty space.- As many have mentioned - there is no map. I don't think its such a big deal but on my first playthrough it did annoy me.- Not sure about this one but some upgrades just straight up don't work? There is an upgrade that supposedly heals you when you attack enemies. In all three of my playthroughs I did not see this working once or maybe did not pay attention. In any case I think something like this should be made noticeable.- You keep getting upgrades that increase your attack but the increase is usually like: from 31 damage per strike to 32 - which is hilarious I will admit, but does not make me feel rewarded at all, lol.- There is 0 smut. Or maybe even -1 smut. Let me explain: sometimes you get conversation with a cast member that goes something like: "Hell yeah, let's do this on kitchen table, hot stuff!" and Drac answers: "Yeah, let's get it ON, baby".... and nothing happens. You just exit the dialogue and continue on. You don't even get the courtesy of a "fade to black" with some sweet talk afterwards. Literally nothing happens. This is one of the most awkward and jarring things I've ever seen in a game. Why have a conversation like this if there is going to be no payoff at all? I do not expect a full on porn (nor do I need it in a game) but give me at least SOMETHING to feel rewarded for romancing these characters!- Your choices don't matter at all. You can literally call one cast member "dirty dog" when you first meet them and they will act like nothing happened 5 seconds later, fully ready to be your eternal love. You also don't get a choice to truly become an enemy to anybody (which is alluded to several times in the game), most of the choice selections are Friendly, Flirty or Sexy, with only a few instances of Antagonistic or Annoyed - and they have 0 impact besides not granting you some relationship points. It would be cool if the cast members really did come to hate you and maybe even attack you depending on your choices.- Cast feels unbalanced: there is 7 female choices and only 4 males. There is technically one more genderless character who you can make male or female, which means you can potentially have 4 males and 8 females - the double amount... I mean, obviously this is not a negative for everyone, but I think it's better to have a balanced cast in a game like this.- Lots and lots of small errors where cast members keep talking about other cast members as if they are still in the "game" despite you eliminating them. Also, one character is not available for a Golden Hour bar date for no reason at all.I understand the game is still going to be developed further and I hope the devs will fix some of the issues above. It is really a fun game with a lot of potential, but you must be willing to forgive a LOT of shortcomings to truly enjoy it. I say give this game a shot if you are more interested in a "romance" and "story" part of the game - it is done quite well and clearly with lots of love, as amazing voice acting, script and soundtrack will attest.However if you are looking for a good platformer - I seriously cannot recommend this. Wait for sale or future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 y'll are haters towards Brocifer get real and vote for him #voteforbrociferOn a serious note, I want to leave this review out here to hopefully give a realistic take on what you will get from Romancelvania after binging the entire game last night since these reviews are mixed.Is it a perfect game - NO. Is it a good entertaining game - YES. Based on what I knew about the game, it met my expectations and sometimes exceeded them with the clever voice performances, cheeky writing, amazing OST, and quirky visuals. There are definitely things I can see that can be improved like visual polish or gameplay bugs, but the package is there.I'll give it a 7.5/10 overall to be fair to some of the reviewers - come for the funny pumpkin boobz and stay for Drac's sweet sweet emotional journey.This is definitely a game for the romance lovers out there. Dating sims, visual novels, with platforming action to mix things up. If you want hardcore gameplay, this probably won't fulfill your expectations but you can still have fun - just go in casually and maybe play with a friend. The elimination section is fun to stream too but make sure to save a lot (VN fans know the drill) if you want to see multiple routes.The visuals in this game - you can absolutely tell are creative and are made by the love of the developers. The 3D/2D fusion can sometimes be a hit or miss, but to be honest, most of the time, it's hardly noticeable since you're playing from a wide camera with your character taking up a small amount of space. The pop culture sprinkled in is kind of cheeky but not in a way that's super distracting. There is a lot of variety in character and environment design that personally picks at my artistic brain on second look - which made the exploration part a lot more enjoyable as you often have to return to spots for quests, dates, etc. I'm a huge sucker too for Drac's design which definitely makes me biased lol8/10Writing is definitely the game's strongest point (which if you're reading this after watching the trailer - you probably already could guess). For those who may feel under-represented, there is a variety of choices that you can make that not only determines your final soulmate but also define how you (as Drac) sees yourself. Honestly, like most visual novels, I tend to play my character as straight as possible to myself since I find it sort of (weirdly?) enriching. I ended up going towards Brocifer because I'm a sucker for Jersey boys but to be honest, I found myself really connecting with a lot of characters by midgame. It'd be nice to see some of them sooner like Fenton, but I'm not mad - it's likely just a pacing issue.9.5/10 because I can't give perfect scores.I don't need a writeup. This is a solid 10/10 and I take back all previous statements about how I score.As someone who generally enjoys dating sims and visual novels + the occasional TLC binge with friends, this game has all the right ingredients to make an enjoyable (and spicy) dish. I'm not a huge fan of platform games but found the controls easy to use with some occasional experimenting to get the "feeling" right. I played with a controller too on a semi robust PC if that offers any clarity. Gameplay felt overall solid but I did occasionally have the camera move strangely when I jump extremely high and or run really fast. Some of the commands that I gained were a bit difficult to pull off but I'm also garbage at Guilty Gear, which probably invalidates my point. I see many point out a lack of map but to be honest, I prefer without one because I'm a sucker for exploration and maps sometimes pigeon-hole me too much into one direction.7/10 with just some minor tweakings needed to address smoothness of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s worth noting that this isn’t the type of game I typically play, so I wasn’t entirely sure what to expect, however, I did receive a free game key courtesy of Reset Nation.I played about 8 hours of this game, on stream. What I did play, I enjoyed overall, but I did find core parts of it frustrating. Visually, the game is very dark. I can see what they were going for, with the bat and the spotlight following you around, I can appreciate the idea behind it. The more that I played, the more frustrated I was with how dark the game is. There were times when I could not even see my character, let alone the enemies around me. Occasionally, especially when picking up the awards, the character looked pretty goofy. Speaking of Drac, I found it a bit weird that you start as male Drac, but are able to change your gender after the prologue. Why not just let you choose your gender before you start the prologue? I also found that doing a jump attack would cause my female Drac to let out some very male-Drac-sounding grunts.I enjoyed the character designs. P.S. Elle is top-tier character design and no other character can change my mind. I’m absolutely, shamelessly smitten. But, there were times I wished I could have gotten to know some of the characters better. After meeting the first three, I felt like I immediately had to vote one off (sorry not sorry, Brocifer, you made the choice easy for me). After that though, the pacing seemed weird. The game seemed to push you to meet the next few contestants but didn’t give you a ton of time to really get to know them before making you kick some more contestants off. It felt like you had a ton of time while you were collecting the next contestants, but as soon as you had them, it was immediately voting time.Something I wasn’t aware of, was that voting a character off will lock certain upgrades, making them impossible to get later. As some of the upgrades are tied to weapons and immunities, I was a bit disappointed, especially with how quickly the game seems to want you to vote contestants off, but I can see how that would contribute to the game’s replayability. I also found it a bit difficult to find some of the characters after I had recruited them. A map would have been nice. I often found myself getting lost and frustrated that I couldn’t find certain characters or where to go. Some of the “levels” also seemed a bit confusing to navigate, and a lot of places in the game were limited until I was able to unlock the double jumping in Chapter 3. I also found it a bit weird, that you couldn’t look down below you if you crouched. A lot of the time I felt like I needed to navigate down in the level, but had no idea what was below me and I was jumping off of platforms and hoping for the best. It may be worth mentioning that I played with an Xbox controller, but I did not find the combat enjoyable. It was very buggy, sometimes hitting the attack button wouldn’t do anything, and there was no way to block or dodge incoming attacks. You do have a mist ability that turns you into mist, but it does have a cooldown and can’t be used constantly. Depending on what weapon you’re using, if your attack is slower then the enemies can just keep attacking you while you’re winding up or in your attack animation. It felt like the enemies could just brute-force you. I’ve also had enemies stuck inside of walls and bridges able to hit me, while I couldn’t hit them back or lure them out. Your abilities could fire off at any time, even when you weren’t inputting the commands, especially the blood tornado or the Headdoken, which was sometimes very inconvenient given the cooldown. The weapon/item wheel was not great to use or navigate.Overall, I feel like I did enjoy the game. I enjoyed the banter between the characters and a lot of the punny humor, but if I had not received a free key for it, it’s not something I would have picked up. The characters are carrying the game, and it seems pretty buggy. At one point I was stuck “falling” in one section of a level and thought I’d have to completely restart the game. All in all, if it’s a game that interests you, or you’re thinking of picking the game up, I’d say go for it, but it’s probably best to wait for the devs to iron out some of the kinks, and/or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game?The first thing to realize is that it's a hybrid game. If you like fully fleshed out dating sim *or* a fully fleshed out metroidvania you won't find it here. You're not supposed to. Like most of the best hybrid games, each aspect is made a little simpler, a little more accessible than in a dedicated title. After all, it's audience includes fans of each.However, if you like the Persona games, where your relationship links are a means to advancing your dungeon crawling prowess, and your dungeon crawling itself is constrained by the progression of the main plot, I think you'll find a lot to love here (beyond just the 12 potential romantic interests).The settings are gorgeous, the dialog clever, and the characters each have a unique narrative voice which still fits into the overall charming, raunchy, and punderful setting. And if one of the characters is too much for you, vote them off. After all, the main conceit is that this is a reality TV show. Yes, this may have some impact on which abilities you can advance or learn, but there are several ways to get through the game, and no matter who you cut from the cast, you can still finish the main narrative.Side stories... well that is a slightly different matter. But what would be the point of choices if they didn't have some consequences?

_childDocuments_.review: Romancelvania brings a blend of various genres into this awesome fun style igavania. Venture throughout Dracula’s castle and it’s backyard and enjoy the beautifully crafted visuals. Find yourself laughing at the witty humor of the characters in the game and even fall in love with many of them. This is a side scrolling, dating sim and Metroidvania all in one which makes this a very unique take on a blended genre of a game. If you’re a fan of a dating sim but never played a platformer or vise versa, this introduces beginner players to a whole different experience. Some thing I hope to see implemented in the future is map integration, it would be nice to remember where certain things are in the game but otherwise, if you want to focus more on the dating portion choose the easiest gameplay and if you want to focus on the platformer portion with a challenge choose the more difficult level- you’ll feel the challenge. I urge everyone to try this game- it is definitely the most fun I’ve had, and my entire discord looks forward to Friday nights for us to continue on the story. It has brought us a lot of laughter so far.

_childDocuments_.review: (Quick edit because of something another review reminded me of. The Jump height and seemingly failing to be able to get up to platforms, I found turning down setting fixed this...makes zero sense, but this game runs so bad on on Ultra that even the player character seems to feel the effects, whas weirder though is I saw little difference between epic and ultra its not like game is full of high fidelity assest, though nothing seemed to fix not being able to exit the pause menu at times, thats just the sluggish unrefined controls probably)Literally before the ending I would have recommended this game on the advise of not getting the DLC (the sound track is not that good or worth the high price, there's flawless tracks out there for a couple of pounds, also pricey considering several musicians are literally just listed as thanks not credited artists)There's much humour to this game and you should have a laugh, some genuinely likable characters often for surprising reasons, but the game as a whole is unpolished, feeling rushed at points and unfinished or unrefined might be fairer. Overall trying so hard to so many things it fails to have its own personality. And some of the references are not done in a good way, the "big evil group pulling the strings" being rammed down my throat as the DLC over and over again not only seemed like a lame reference to cuphead, a game whose polish and personality is without issue, but also a slap in the face considering you literally just started the game, I had to check for a moment that EA did not publish this. But its not just shameless and heavy handed....theres an area you pass in the game that says you can't enter yet...it's not a case of beat the game and go back, no, its locked out, it is implied it is in fact TBA DLC.I could go on pointing out this inconsistent art style (often seeming like they've left in placeholders), the features that don't seem fleshed out or with much point, the padded item list without actual flavour, or the tempermental controls for such a limited moveset, Setting off combos when it feels like. And that goes hand in hand with messy boss fights unlike it's name sake boss fights that when done well are like a stylish dance. And even a praised point I think lacks, "everyone will do anyone" isn't the diversity people think it is, It was a lame cop out from 20 years ago and having it stagnant as the same thing is not progress.  but thats a dissertation for another day.But I'll leave it at considering the incredible lengthy list of backers this game had, this niche game got, which seems such a privilege, I think they deserved a better product than what was called version 1.0 of this game.It it goes on sale for less than £15 bucks pick it up, have a laugh, but like PS elle it's something for a good time, not a long time (I have zero interest in going for a round 2, a NG+ might have helped that but even then I doubt it)

_childDocuments_.review: Put yourself into the shoes of Drac, one of, if not the most famous vampire to ever exist, who had conquered, slain and enjoyed a life of luxury for eons now. However, this has been a lonesome road, with flings inbetween, some of them ending in tragedy, while your one true love is not here anymore to provide comfort. Drac, understandably, spends their time sulking, brooding, not wanting to get involved with the affairs of the world around. This is, however, a fate that one of their oldest fr-...aquaintances can not bare to watch for any longer: Grim. Ever inspired by a sense of creativity and showmanship, the good ol' reaper wants to help Drac back on their feet, while turning it into a reality show, with a twist: To help them find their  true love from a pool of contestants, eliminating them one by one, till only one may remain."Romancelvania" really is an oddity in the gaming landscape. Had you told me, that there exists a game that blends "The Bachelor" and Metroidvania-gameplay into one package, I would have laughed you off the stage, yet here we are. It is readily apparent, that there was a lot of love being poured into this title, with decent voice acting, splendid humor at times and serviceable gameplay, however, me choosing this last aspect deliberately, should get you to raise an eyebrow. I wanted to, I really really wanted to love this game, but I can't. Its gameplay-loop is not terrible by any stretch of the imagination, mind, in fact, I found it highly entertaining on multiple occasion, but it feels half-baked, released too early, until all the bugs and most importantly, the overly janky gameplay would have been fixed. You will have a decent enough time in "Romancelvania", I just wish the title would have been as bombastic and enjoyable, as Grim likes for his show to be.As it stands, I can only partly recommend this game. For a bit of casual, metroidvania-fun, this is certainly enough, but those hoping for a well written story (and dialogues) attached to this still somewhat steep pricetag, might feel somewhat disappointed. Still, hopes are high that future patches remedy this.

_childDocuments_.review: First game I've fully completed in a long time, and an absolute gem despite my first impressions. I was on the fence about this but the premise of a monster dating sim that was more that your standard visual novel was something I couldn't help but give a try, and I was far from disappointed. Romancelvania was above my expectations and I had a blast.---Summary---Story & Setting: 7/10Characters & Dialogue: 9/10Combat & Levels: 5/10Graphics & Visuals: 5/10Audio & Music: 7/10Unique Aspects & Fun Factor: 10/10---Detailed---Pros:The characters and dialogue are the highlight of this game. I was cracking up with laughter over and over because of the cast, a few members in particular. Mostly from what they said, to some of the quirky things about how a scene was set up (one date with a certain sideways character model comes to mind here.) The writers were cleaver with the tropes by leaning into them, while also bringing something new or inverting it. The jokes, references and other easter eggs are great for setting the tone of the game from early on and maintain all the way through in a way that kept me on my toes into the late stages with some of the "minigames" they toss at you. They make no sense, but at the same time absolutely do, due to the wacky nature of a reality-tv-monster-dating sim. I honestly found it really hard to chose at the end because there were so many great options of personalities, backstories and of course, the continued romance with Drac from all the dates and conversations. There were a few that I wasn't to jazzed about from first meeting, but got quickly invested after a proper conversation to get to know them that they over-seeded my initial picks. Though I felt some of the 'men' options were a bit lacking compared to the women especially with the uneven split but I think that comes down more to personal taste as I know many friends who'd go wild over the few 3 I wasn't too crazy about.Cons:3D character models and some continuity errors.Unlike most of the reviews, I wasn't as bothered by the combat, or even the (rare) glitch. I wish a little bit more love had been put into the 3D models. Some of them look well enough, others get a bit to close to the uncanny area when the face animations run, especially when the dialogue and mouths are'nt fully synced. It's far from the best, but I was able to ignore it and get past it, thanks to the good writing. (Which is saying something, as I work in the art department of the games industry and my standards are usually quite high and hard to dismiss.) The 2D character art was much-much better, but I could still nit-pick.For continuity, there were a few times I completed a character mission which progressed their story, only for some of the dates to have conversations that seemed to go backwards in the relationship. I think the developers assumed you'd do some of the main story check points before side quests in a certain order which let something to be desired in the romance mechanic.  Unfortunately, some of this extended to a date location locked by progression with a stage 1 character, who I didn't progress with, yet other cast members would mention said character on occasion despite not being around. It wasn't enough to ruin the experience and a minor complaint in the end, as nothing completely blocked current characters and story, but I felt it would have been nicer to get alternative dialogue instead. However for budget reasons being a kickstarter game, I understand why it didn't work out that way. These are the only strong reasons why story and characters don't quite make it to 10/10 for me.Middle Ground:The levels and set were well done and had a good amount of variety. I enjoyed exploring the different zones and it kept things fresh, but there were a few extra places that could have had used fast travel checkpoints. The enemies were great with their gimmicks and worked well into the humor of the game. (The underwater boss was awesome, lol!) I wasn't anticipating any groundbreaking combat based on the reviews so I went in with low expectations there. Although I still ended up putting my settings to easy after the first boss just to avoid petty frustrations with the occasional clunkly-ness and improve my overall enjoyment and get to the story faster. If I wanted tougher or more intricate combat, I'd have played something else. That said, I can see what it has to offer if you prefer to dive more into that, but it serves better as an engagement element while you explore the world in making the experience more interactive than clicking buttons to say "go here" and "I do this". Those things being why I was initially interested in Romancelvania more than other monster VN games that may be out there. Though, it did drag out a bit in act 3, the pace picked up again for 4 & 5.---Final Thoughts---Aside from the theme of monsters and vampires (which was the main grab for me), Romancelvania is far from anything of my usual type of game as I've never played or been into the idea of dating sims, nor have I played castlevanina(specifically) and most of all... I don't like reality TV! Yet against all that, the trailer got my attention and there was charm right from the get go that I played it for a week straight until I got to the end. I had so much fun I came to leave a review right away! I've only completed a handful of games from start to finish in my life, but this 20hr(ish) game play was perfect for someone with a busy life and 9-5 schedule looking for something casual, yet engaging enough to keep me coming back to it every night. I'm already considering doing a second play through (and not just for the steam achievements)! All in all, great game and already have a few friends in mind I know who will love it more than myself.p.s Lulu I love you!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic concept questionable execution but I will say the more I play this game the more it grows on me.I had no clue Romancelvania existed before this week but when I saw a trailer with a Busty Pumpkin witch and the promise of reality show drama meets Metroidvania I WAS IN !  I'm playing on the Steam Deck so I'll leave my Steamdeck specific comments at the bottom and dive more into the game itself at the top.  Also bear in mind I LOVE JANKY GAMES so if you're looking for something polished come back in a few months but  if you can find a good time in between the  jank I'd say the game is worth a play right now.Overview:Romancelvania is an unfortunate case of an excellent concept well executed in some areas but bogged down in others  . It has a ton of great ideas but lots of clumsy execution that's harder to forgive at the start but the mechanics and my appreciation for the gameplay has grown as Drac has leveled up and I gradually unlock more of their skills. Narrative: First and Foremost do I think this game delivers on the concept of a trashy reality TV - themed Castelvania... to that I would say Yes the colorful cast of characters with a large variety of personalities, the interesting conversations you can have with each of them, seeing wh the castmates interact with each other all of that satisfies my inner basic  reality TV lover.  The writing itself has made me laugh a few times . It's unfortunate I feel like it's a bit of a slowburn because Vess is closed off , Brocifer is just a frat boy and really the only kind of interesting opening character of the 3 was Medusa. However to the games credit I will say the more I talk to the various characters and get to see the variety of their different personalities the more I am enjoying the narrative elements of this title.  One of the more interesting conversations happens between Pumpkin Witch P.S. Elle and the Genie Vess  where they have a strong disagreement between their varying views of  submission and consent. It's brief but surprisingly nuanced in touching upon the way consent and personal power can color an interaction . Not every conversation is that deep but I found that to be surprisingly interesting. With that level of thoughtfulness comes plenty of more basic and humor-focused bickering too . I love the cast so far and I think the once the gameplay improves the characters and writing will get more of the attention it deserves.The voice acting is great and while Van Helsing voice choice is questionable it made more sense when I learned that they were angelic humans and not just mortals like you and I .Gameplay: At this point in time I would say the narrative carries the gameplay in Romancelvania which is unfortunate because it's not that the gameplay is wrong it just feels very clunky.  Lots of reviews mention there's not much feedback when enemies are hit or you are hit, there is no real way to interrupt attacks  so certain enemies like the skeletons with the revolving scythes can easily trap and put you into a  damage loop situation early on. I gave up on the Impaler lance almost immediately, it thrusts Drac forward and basically tosses you into a situation to get damaged so i just stuck with the sword .Earl on dying is easy , there isn't a lot of feedback or a go-to defensive maneuver until AFTER you defeat the first boss ( The mist slows time and allows you to briefly be invulnerable) . There's lots of small items used to help you in combat but I usually end up stockpiling the items for the bosses  where I often will burn through my whole supply in order. Also the lighting does leave a lot to be desired and only makes the gameplay frustrations more frustrating as you get cheap shotted by an enemy who blended in with the background.It's not that the gameplay of Romancelvania is irredeemable, it's that it feels like in Romancelvania enemies are just setup to be obstacles to your progress and not puzzles you solve throughout your exploration and because of that it makes all of the enemy encounters feel a little cumbersome .  In most Metroidvanias I feel like enemies are designed to teach you mastery of a skill but I very rarely know the best way to tackle an enemy in this game and boss fights are the worst culprits in that they start off kind of fair but usually devolve into a mess of you avoiding the BIG BAD GUY while they infinitely spawn waves of less enemies to get in the way and I have decided to just stop  killing the lesser enemies and just dodge them because  they are just respawned IMMEDIATELY when you clear them . It's deflating and it makes it feel like the crazy cluttered  combat experience was the goal and  that is so confusing from a gameplay perspective.What I will say I am enjoying is seeing how the relationship building narratively roles back into your perk and upgrades systems, as you build certain relationships specific weapons are upgraded, skills become available, you gain specific invulnerabilities . I think that works awesome with the theme. The unfortunate thing is once you vote characters off the show you can no longer develop those relationships and so those perks will no longer be available but  I also think it's a good incentive to be strategic about which characters you like the most and which ones are the most useful being a part of your decision equation .Art: I think the 2D character portraits are the majority of the best artwork in this game and I think conveyed characters much better than their 3D models did but with that said not all of the 3D models are bad their quality is just far less consistent than the 2D portrait quality is.Music: I feel like the music fluctuates between awesome and forgettable . Certain themes like Brocifer , Sol's house, and  Dracs general castle theme are great ear candy but other times the music is just background noise. Not dissapointing but also not something I can write about extensively eitherSteamdeck :I'm playing this game on my Steamdeck which only just recently was patched to run it so there have been some issues playing it but for the most part playing on Steamdeck has been very smooth .. There were weird moments where the game chugs ( anytime the Headoken particles are on screen ) and over a 4 hour playtime the game  has done this weird thing where my controls stop working right after a cinematic or interstitial moment. The first one was during the intro sequence after getting the impaler and being asked how you want to disband some unruly servants, the second time was after me seeing Sol and Van Helsing getting into a petty Squabble. It's an unfortunate issue which forces a complete restart and is  as bad as the timing of its appearance, 2 minutes into the intro wasn't so bad, right after I grinded for some coins and jsut after I saved the game ? I would have been quite annoyed to have my coin grinding time wasted. Otherwise it's for the most part playable on the Steamdeck  and after 4 hours I'd say if you're on the fence and on the Steamdeck and ok with the possibility of running into a game breaking issue I'd go for it.Final Thoughts :So when it's all said and done I think this is a fun indie game project do I wish it was more polished ? Definitely, but I also think this is a novel blend of theme and genres  that should be celebrated for how well it brings two very different types of media together ( Reality shows and Metroidvanias) .  After you build Drac up the gameplay feels better, you better understand how to develop strategies to handle the enemies and the cast is the star of the show that keeps me playing even when i do find the gameplay less enjoyable. If you like the idea of participating in a monster dating show as the backdrop to monster hunting then  I think Romancelvania is worth your time and will scratch that itch ! It's a little rough around the edges but I think worth the time if you don't mind experiencing some jank whileenjoying osmething kind of novel!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a bit buggy in terms of both gameplay and achievements, and the ending is a bit of a letdown, but for the most part, this is a fun homage/parody of both Castlevania and dating sims. It's a neat blend of the two - the likes of which I haven't seen since Thousand Arms, but that was a turn based RPG, and this is an action platformer. Although I'm a straight male, I appreciate that you can have Drac's gender be either male or female and you can mate with any of the potential partners, be they male, female or Pumpkins. There are also multiple difficulty levels, meaning you can play this for a challenge or just the story. On the easiest setting you still have to jump, dodge and hit things, but it is super easy. _childDocuments_.review: When I first saw Romancelvania, I knew immediately that it was a game for me. I'm a long-time player of Metroidvanias, all the way back to the first Metroid, and in recent years, I've really enjoyed Visual novel dating sims. Hatoful Boyfriend is one of my favourite games to date. I love media that has a silly-seeming premise that end ups surprising you with the level of thoughtfulness and depth put into the concept, and Romancelvania is just that. I came to see the weird and wacky concept, and stayed to see how Drac and the cast develop as characters. That's my favourite aspect of the game. The Metroidvania part of the game isn't the smoothest I've ever played, and there's a lot of great ideas here but it feels like there are just some dots missing to make it go from okay to GREAT.  As it is, it can be at moments frustrating but is overall a fun play. I am playing on bite difficulty but I totally exploited the invincibility and damage treats at times to make it through boss battles. My least favourite part so far has been voting off cast members. I'm the kind of gamer who 10 stars every dating option in every game-- everyone in my Stardew and Rune Factory playthroughs gets a bouquet before I decide who I want to go with. I just feel like even characters that come off as really cliche have a lot of depth to them as you talk to them more, and I'm missing out on that without a lot of gameplay repeats.However, the writing is just the kind of zany and punny humour I really enjoy in dating sims-- reminds me a lot of Dream Daddy but with monsters. I enjoyed this aspect so much I sometimes felt I was rushing myself to get through the gameplay, and had to remind myself to chill out and slow down so I'd stop getting smacked down by the platforming.I'm not finished with the game yet, so I'll update if anything is vastly different in the last chapters.

Whether I was exploring the halls of the haunted castle or battling fearsome monsters, every moment felt like a nostalgic trip down memory lane.But what truly sets Romancelvania apart is its clever gameplay and engaging mechanics. As players guide the lovable protagonist on their quest to rescue their beloved from the clutches of Dracula, they'll encounter a variety of challenges and obstacles that require quick reflexes and sharp thinking to overcome. From platforming segments to challenging boss battles, the game offers plenty of variety and excitement to keep players entertained from start to finish.In addition to its addictive gameplay, Romancelvania also delivers a hilarious and charming story that had me laughing out loud throughout my entire playthrough. The game's witty dialogue and clever writing are a joy to behold, and the quirky characters and humorous situations only add to the overall charm of the experience.Overall, Romancelvania is a delightful romp that's sure to put a smile on your face. With its charming visuals, engaging gameplay, and witty humor, it's a must-play for anyone looking for a fun and lighthearted gaming experience. So grab your whip, sharpen your fangs, and get ready to embark on an unforgettable adventure through the whimsical world of Romancelvania!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall score 8/10.Graphics: 6.5/10.Gameplay: 8/10.Music: 8/10.UI/UX: 9/10.This game was a good bit of fun and sit through, for the most part, I really enjoyed the experience. This had a very good side-scroller Castlevania or Metroidvania type of game, despite the 3D elements, and a lack of 'zones' like you'd see in rogue legacy or a lot of those older games. It also had somewhat of a confusing/slow start and I'd wished you had been able to pick a female or male character at the very start of the game. [it doesn't take too long to get the choice though.] It had a lot of well-crafted areas, the feel and vibe was very castle-vania-like. Cool spooky mansions, cool spooky locations, lots of funny or silly enemies and the 'tropes' of the various romanceable characters were absolutely hilarious. The music always felt accurate to the areas and scenes at hand, and I didn't feel like the background sounds were too out of place. I did need to turn the voices down just a touch, as well as the music, but overall everything was balanced, and felt very much on theme for what the game is. If you like old retro-arcade style Metroidvania-esque platformers, and want some kooky silly laughs about a monster reality T.V dating show... Give this game a shot. I'd definitely recommend it despite the few bugs and dislikes I had, personally. All of which I'll list below.Disliked: 1.  One character's romance progression quest, it felt out of place with the rest of the game.2. One of drac's later unlock abilities  was pretty much unnecessary in my opinion and could have been removed. I didn't make use of it once as I'd found other ways to get around using it prior to unlocking the ability itself. You can absolutely bypass it at least twice, through clever use of  double jumping, and having some familiarity with general platformers and how to cheese them a little bit. 3. Story progression could use a marker or trail for specific character acquisition. It didn't occur to me that in booty bay I could  get another means into a place there, so I spent several hours re-checking booty bay, the swamp area and the lightning plains, thinking I'd missed an important quest and was 'stuck' for several hours, confused. This could have been avoided with another little quest saying "find a way into X." It would have saved me several hours of confusion. I also feel like there could have been a few general pointers on where to go next.4. The supporter areas. Not only are several backers listed for way too long during the credits there are actually -two- areas with several screens that Drac can Interact with and a note to read. If you're going to add those areas in, it should contain all of the names, and thus condense the credits. Make the room larger, or make use of the currently empty space below that room/add a sub-floor and just cram a giant wall-scroll with names in there that you interact with to read. Then you save 5 minutes (at least, seriously way too long) of credits time. Or give us a fast-scroll credit button.5. The ending felt rushed, and I wish they'd have some sort of end cut-scene with the character Drac picked as "love at first bite." Credits are very very slow as already mentioned, and Drac sees a few interactions between a few different characters. It was distracting from the slow credits. What would have been better IMO, would be to just have the credits go through (preferably with a fast-skip button for faster strolling) then have one final big "end party" with an end message from Drac and their picked partner.The bugs: 1. If playing female Drac, you meet Vess, Brocifer, then Medusa. If you don't go down and left instead of toward the right, after talking to them in the gold room, Grim's message doesn't show up, which causes a big "fatal error" crash/hard crash. I repeated the starting mission 3 times because of this exact crash, going three different directions first and then reported this bug via email. The creator of the game was polite about it, but it really should get patched out, as it almost made me quit playing in case I'd needed to refund from the game not being playable. [It was fine though. Just go down/left post gold-room interactions with those three at the beginning.]2. During a character's progression quest aka  if you die a bunch, or perhaps just in regular game-play... After you complete the quest, the game will remain zoomed out and like Drac is still traveling  in a wrong way. If you save after completion, and reload the save, it fixes itself... But this still took away from the overall experience. This should get looked at and patched out.3. During the very final end boss fight if you use several unholy hand grenades, or rats or bats, it will absolutely crash the game. Luckily I'd saved right before entering that boss fight. It was also more annoying than difficult. All of that bosses' moves are predictable, and the spawns just get in the way. I actually found getting a certain tentacled romance partner much more interesting than that final fight, as at least they required me to use certain abilities to get past it.Despite all that I'd still give this game a shot if you liked Castlevania or you like Metroidvania ability based "unlock to progress" types of games. I'd probably recommend you wait until it's on sale though, as I spent only 14 hours on a single playthrough. (3 of those hours was me just aimlessly confused when I needed to find the last 3 characters and got stuck.) Fun, but not a ton of replay-ability. as Story is linear and characters aren't that diverse to where I feel I'm missing out, not reloading or replaying.
