_childDocuments_.review: This is such a great game. One of my favorites now, after 100% the achievements. Can't wait for the new content in the future!! The characters are well built with deep story lines that are easy to get involved in, and the dialogue is so funny. A great game and not as slutty as you may think when looking at the store page pictures. The game gets deep and heartfelt and is goofy when needed. A perfectly balanced story. The fighting game play is fun enough too and breaks through the story as it should. A good purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay itself is that of a fairly standard metroidvania, but the plot and sense of style makes the game so much fun. It is not a property that takes itself seriously. I hugely enjoyed learning more about the characters and experiencing every plot twist as they came.  The ending especially was really excellent. Overall, I loved the game and am looking forward to a second playthrough sometime soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and unique game with some interesting characters and great writing.  I enjoyed the humor and the silliness of the whole affair, but also appreciated that the characters were deeper than they initially appear.  The game is kinda rough around the edges and the Castlevania-style gameplay isnt winning any awards, but the fun characters and unique stories make for an enjoyable romantic adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: Romancelvania marries traditional side-scrolling adventure (like Simon's Quest on the NES--sometimes with the same 8-bit graphics) with the contrived melodrama required of reality television. The voice acting was excellent, the humor was genuinely funny, and the level design and gameplay was very well done. Simply a joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hilarious game that takes a while to get use to, but once you do this is one heck of an experience.  Romancelvania playfully riffs on some of the best games of the past, with a modern day twist. It's challenging, entertaining and entirely unique.  If you’re willing to overlook the gameplay issues, and love fun and sleazy gameplay, this one is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for Metroidvanias. I grow tired of the same old gothic tromp through uninteresting areas. This game takes the tired formula and puts a fun spin on it!I've seen some a lot of reviews complaining about weird things that aren't really a problem, or maybe the game just isn't for them. The game feels like a fun PS1 game I missed out on (the vibe, not the graphics or the gameplay). Of course it seems inspired by Symphony of the Night, but if you were forced to go through silly antics to redeem yourself.The game is filled with colorful characters that all have unique traits. It's great that it let's you make a lot of choices--some big and some small. There's a decent amount of choices like gender and dating preference and how you want to flirt or not flirt, and you even get to send contestants home just like in a dating show!The gameplay is reminiscent of SotN, and it has a lot of homages to other games. Drac does a similar pose to Link when he receives an item or an upgrade, and you even get a hadoken move that literally uses the input from Street Fighter, so it adds different versatility to the combat!Honestly this is truly a good time for this game to release, as people are growing more obsessed with watching reality TV shows lately on sexy islands with a bunch of beautiful people. This has that but in a metroidvania.Another thing I want to point out is--when I play this genre, I love for the areas and settings to stand out and feel unique. I didn't feel that recently when I played Metroid Dread. A lot of the areas felt and looked the same and I would grow bored or  get lost. This game has a lot of fun and unique areas that stand out!If you enjoy a fun time and don't take things too seriously and have a sense of humor, and if you love dumb romance reality shows and Metroidvanias or even side scrollers--this game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: At 4.4 hours of game time, I can say this - I'm thoroughly enjoying this game.I have not experienced any bugs YET (PC/Keyboard/Medium Settings). However I will update as I play!I will say it could use some more polishing on the quest lines.I've yet to find one of the first characters items and its thrown me already onto 5 others people.I wish the Van Helsing's had voices. It seems odd they are just harp sounds.Also at times, female Dracs face looks like a 'sim' character creation. Especially the trophy pose face.Not sure if there will be more male characters along the way, but it would be nice to see more!So far out of 7 potential dates, you have 4 girls, either a male/female choice with the VanHelsings, and then 2 males ; one guy whose just a chad and the other a more silent chad?The game is silly and the dating game show aspect is fun, however I hope to see it cleaned up![TL;DR: If you like cheeky cheese ball romance goofyness go for it! If you are looking for fight mechanics - don't. If you're looking for in depth character backgrounds - dont. It's a very simple 'cut to the chase' and goofy game that I look forward to seeing worked on :) My chat on stream enjoyed watching it with me.]

_childDocuments_.review: I completed my first playthrough on console and decided to move on to Steam as well. Every aspect of the game - from the platforming, the romance, the graphics, the combat and metroidvania aspects - is underwhelming at best, and outright awful at worst. _childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: It's true that this game has clunky platforming and combat mechanics. Yes, some of the 3D models are quite terrible (more in line with the PS2/PS3 than current gen) and, yes, the level designs can be a bit tedious. It has tonal issues, wanting to be a castlevania title while also wanting to make low-brow jokes mixed with genuine romance. Some of the sound effects are random and annoying, like the fog horn sound effect or Drac shouting 'yee-haw!' The monster designs are random and silly, totally breaking immersion in some sections. On first play, you feel rushed into completing the main questline, when I learned on a second playthrough that I can take my time and find/talk to some of the characters in different parts of the castle. This is never explained or hinted at. It could use a better dating tutorial system. However, where this game shines is in the characters, the writing and the voice acting. Even the shallowest characters (at first glance), have a surprising amount of depth to them and the player is rewarded for going out of their way to talk to them. It's a fun premise that's so close to being a really good game. It just needs a few little tweaking here and there. Even with all it's problems, it's one of the most unique and fun metroidvania titles I've ever played. The end date payoffs are lovely too. Again, great writing...when the game allows for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: As a dating game: Highly recommend.As a metroidvania game: Wait for a sale.Let me start by saying if you're looking for a straight up metroidvania game, you may wish to either look elsewhere or wait until a sale. This is a product of a kickstarter campaign so the game isn't polished as others out there. The controls are a bit janky so I would recommend you look at the game as a casual platformer with an emphasis on character interaction. What Romancelvania may lack in combat it makes up for in heart. You can tell that the team involved really loved this game and put a lot of passion into it. The VA's and artists are where the game truly shines in my opinion. The cast really did a great job with their roles and I loved getting to see the different sides of characters as time went on. The VA for Brocifer really knocked it out of the park and elevated a joke character into someone who actually made it to the final date because of how well their actor voiced them. Passion projects like this are fun to play because you can feel the love the team had for their game. It may not always be love at first bite but if you give it a chance; much like my beloved Brocifer you may find there's more to it than what you first see and there's plenty to love.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: The game has its shortcomings (the combat, mostly, and the lack of map), but they're not dire enough for me to not absolutely LOVE this game. One can hope the devs will listen to the feedback they've received so far, but even if the handful of minor complaints aren't addressed, I would still urge people to give this one a try. It's devilishly witty and surprisingly wholesome; the cast is full of characters with depth and personality you don't often see in romance games.

_childDocuments_.review: A little rough outside the gate, but it's a really fun take on a dating sim! The music, artwork and voice acting are really good for an indie game! The characters are really unique and interesting though. I'm excited to see where the game will go!

_childDocuments_.review: I avoided playing Romancelvania when it first came out because a) I had backed the PS4 version on Kickstarter which has yet to be released so got the PC version instead which is not my preferred format for action game and b) heard it was in pretty rough shape on first release. It has gotten several updates so I decided to bite the bullet and see how it turned out. Romancelvania bills itself as a hybrid dating sim/metriodvania, but I would say it is primarily a humor game. You take on the role of Drac, a depressed and lovelorn vampire, who gets roped into a reality dating show hosted by the the Grim Reaper. Drac must travel the world, recruiting a bevy of monsters to romance by finding gifts and romantic dating spots in each local. As a metroidvania, it is pretty underbaked. Drac's castle, the main hub, is more secret-laden and interconnected than the larger world which consists of many smaller levels that split off from the main road. You can tell the developers ran out of resources making this because the the opening areas feel better designed than the final ones. But that's okay, because the absurd humor in the dating sim part is where the game shines (Flying Spaghetti Monster boss battle anyone?) The colorful cast of monsters ranges offers a bevy of personalities and some of the challenges Drac has to go to to complete the quest lines will give you a good chuckle which makes up for the some of the less than polished gameplay in my book. At certain points, you will have to eliminate contestants from the competition and these can be agonizing since you have to weigh how much you like the characters and against the power-ups you gain from deepening your relationship with them. Culling them can cut off some weapon and skill upgrades permanently. I followed my heart as it was ultimately Fenton, the sophisticated wolf-man, who won me over. It did not matter much to my playthrough to not be able to upgrade certain weapons, but it might on the higher difficulty levels. I can confirm that as of June 2023, the game does have controller support.
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: Romancelvania-SteamTake Bloodstained/Castlevania’s 2.5D combat and aesthetics mixed with Hades style quest lines add an emphasis on dating/bromances and you have Romancelvania. I was pretty leery about this game at first as I was concerned with how it was going to all come together. Plus 2.5D seems to really be hit or miss generally speaking. Luckily the 2.5D just pops and I think they pulled it off!The parody elements are blended together in a humorous way, but if you can’t get over the premise and cheesiness of it all, you probably won’t enjoy this game. If you don’t mind games they don’t take themselves seriously, then you may enjoy it like I do.This game seems very polished to me. I am playing on a modern W11 laptop, and a 8bitdo controller and I haven’t had any of the issues some down-voters are commenting on so ymmv. You can tell that a lot of time and money has gone into its presentation and game play.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly impressed by the designs, The first scene of Drac's old castle seem familiar,The persona of casts were impressive. Vess was casual just like my friends enjoying their holidays, Brocifer talks frankly and salty as well as cute in a special way, Initially, I approached the game as a casual dating cast RPG with a combat system, so I focused on the dating scenes. Fortunately, I didn't forget to upgrade my gear and learn new tricks with gadgets, which made later combat much more enjoyable.As the plot progressed, and I became more invested in the dating aspect, I realized that my choice of character wouldn't significantly impact the main storyline. The game cleverly tells its story, complemented by beautiful soundtracks. Perhaps I should consider purchasing the soundtrack during notable upgrades.Although I had a great time playing the game and was moved by the experience, I don't plan on replaying it in the near future. The story has concluded, and it's time for me to move on, as the game reminded me. :)Additionally, the game's engine crashed multiple times, and the usual restarting method didn't solve the issue. If any developers come across this comment, I suggest contacting your engineers to address this problem.

_childDocuments_.review: Think dating sim and metroidvania and you have this game. Too bad the character models are not to my taste (epecially MC). It's weird because in the videos I assumed I'd like the style, but in action it doesn't look that good or play super gratifyingly. Pacing seems off and I can't tell if I'd want more interactions between characters or just adventuring around. The first two characters I met didn't intrigue me really. I wish there was real character customization because there was just choosing gender. I wish it was more sexy and perverted or something because it was too clean for a raunchy setup like this. I'm not sure what the end goal would really be, pick the character I like the most for the MC to marry? What if I don't care about the MC or the cast, like I wish I could've customized the cast even.The combat doesn't feel as rewarding as other metroidvanias, the running is very slow and the beginning is very slow for a metroidvania. The lighting is not good and everything just looks dark and gloomy. Sad because it's full of saturation but blackens the eff out of it all because of the lighting gimicks. Refund requested.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial thoughts:I had a pretty good time with the early parts of the game. I enjoyed the throwback vibe to trashy VH1 reality TV. I wanted a little bit more depth to the combat, but I started to feel a sense of combat options as I unlocked more abilities. I'm a little frustrated with the cooldown mechanic, since it feels more restrictive than forcing me to make interesting choices, but I hope that as I get more tools to use, I'll spend less time waiting on cooldowns.As someone who doesn't really play dating sim games (although Mass Effect 2 probably counts when I think about it), I'm not really the best person to judge how it compares to other games; however I did like the interactions I had with the cast so far, even if they seem to stick to their archetypes (at the beginning at least).The game is visually a little dark for my taste, but there seems to be a feature (gag?) after the intro that makes it a little easier to see.Recommendation:I think Romancelvania is worth trying if you're looking for an indie game that reminds you of late-2000's dating shows with chuckle-worthy humor. I don't know how much play time is in the game, but since it seems I've only scratched the surface there should be plenty of gameplay as long as you explore the map and finish the side quests. It seems like there might be some replay value since you can change your relationship choices, but I've yet to see how much the content changes with your choices.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into Romancelvania only knowing that it was a Visual Novel-meets-Metroidvania game and nothing about the kickstarter.  Additionally, I'm a person who never really played metroidvanias as I enjoy going forward in the plot rather than doubling back.When I started the game and messed with the settings, I was a bit concerned as it felt like the 'brightness' setting wasn't working at all.  I had to lower the game settings to stream and it made the game rather difficult to see at points with only changing all the settings together making any visual difference.  At a few points during my game I did have to tweak the graphic settings to be able to make out the environments better.After that though, I thoroughly have been enjoying the game.  Eliminating people only reinforced to myself that I'll have to go back and play the game again.  I've enjoyed the dark humor and highly respect the 'Naughty, but not Dirty' philosophy of the game's writing.  Coming from the Monster Prom series, I felt right at home.  The game does have some bugs to iron out, but I definitely find the game has great potential.  I can easily see more content in the future whether it be DLC areas and characters or hopefully a sequel in some manner.The only pacing issues I've had are the out of nowhere Dessert Desert stage that I don't know how to return to as well as inviting the Nefret to the show.  It felt odd that the Dessert Desert stage was out of left field and didn't appear to add to the story beyond 'candy unicorn'.  I honestly thought we were going to get a centaur or anthro horsewoman as an option, but then I was returned to the main map.  As for Nefret, due to a lack of a map function, I've noticed in the steam forums that people aren't aware of the second exit from the crystal caverns that lead to getting the lightning ability.  That and there was a small area in the lightning caves where I thought I had to run and double jump up, but could not; I didn't realize until after twenty minutes of jumping that I was going the wrong way.  A simple Super Metroid-like map would be GREATLY appreciate and a reasonable request.Beyond those two elements than can be ironed out, I need to reiterate: I'm having fun.  I know I will be replaying the game to properly max out all character's stories and help them grow as people.  The references ranging from the Gold Room from The Shining to the accountant being a Ghostbusters reference had me laughing.  I won't spoil the 'Dying for Love' boss but I had to pause the game due to me laughing so hard at each stage of the boss fight.  I am getting my money's worth in spades with this game.  Unique concepts for the ROs are great (a drunk new yorker being 'the beast' inside the werewolf, an undead Jamaican pirate as our Frankenstein stand-in and the ability to pick your Van Helsing of choice).

_childDocuments_.review: Romancelvania is an ambitious, yet stumbling mess that spreads itself thin across two genres that hypothetically should blend well enough but in practice not only fail to intermingle whatsoever, but get in one another's way in development time and resources as both sides come out undercooked.Before I tear into this game I'd like to say that I don't despise it. In fact, I respect it to a degree. It's a great concept I've personally never seen attempted before, merging two genres I've a great deal of experience in and capped off with an ensemble of characters  that I am immediately drawn to. Purely on paper, this works incredibly well. A metroidvania borrowing much of its setting from the latter half of the namesake wherein you play as the legendary Dracula himself, an experience you'd be hard pressed to find elsewhere. Layered atop this is the underlying goal to marry off our protagonist through a dating sim intertwining a broad cast of characters from a horny pumpkin, a horny medusa, a horny devil, a horny succubus, and a slightly broader spectrum of characters that aren't as horny.Unfortunately, this is all the game really seems to get right; what it says on paper. In practice ,the game balances two entirely different game genres on a tightrope it can't even stand on. Beginning with the gameplay, it's frankly unbelievable that this ever got through testing, assuming it ever underwent any. Glitches so innumerable they became unquestionably commonplace by the third act, level design that felt closer to a Mario Maker level than a platformer with any amount of budget put behind it, balancing that inflates your health to overcompensate for the thousands of weapon power up collectibles you'll run into that change nothing, competing with the dozens of enemies whose unacceptable placement, physics, and attacks will drain Drac's health faster than any boss, mini-boss, or obstacle ever even came close to, the core design of the game is beyond saving. It makes me wonder if they'd ever considered scrapping the project altogether, only to decide they're in too deep to stop now. The core movement is sluggish and cumbersome, not in a powerful nor intentional feeling akin to that of older Castlevania titles' strict, slow movement, but akin to opening Unreal Engine 4's automatic movement system kits and never tweaking or refining them past a couple sliders. Weapons are nearly useless past the sword, as it's quick enough to dispel most foes at short range (especially with a couple of power ups), and *so* quick, in fact, that it will deal more DPS to anything in your path than the seemingly useless hammer could ever even conceive of. Combat is not all that makes up a metroidvania, however, as the genre is arguably entirely defined by the exploration and discovery provided by locked doors and the keys you'll find to them later. Romancelvania's idea of this concept, done well by hundreds of games over the course of the last thirty odd years is to make it as well known as absolutely possible that you cannot pass into an area early until the game wants you to. I'd argue that a metroidvania does not necessarily *need* its progression to be non-linear, only that it be done via backtracking and abilities. Romancelvania does none of this. It's linear, it's done by neither backtracking nor abilities, you will explore new areas when Grim wants you to and only when Grim wants you to. Rather than locking off areas (save for a scarce few) behind abilities gained through further exploration, compounding the gameplay into a feedback loop, it instead locks much of it behind doors and rooms you'll be either kicked out of nor flat out barred entry from with a message from Grim telling you to "come back later". From a narrative standpoint this only just barely makes sense. A brand new castle was erected overnight, but a scarce few rooms take apparent eons to fully furnish. Oftentimes this is done to more of a detriment to progression than the developers likely even knew of, as the inherent draw to returning to old locations born of a player's curiosity and intuitive knowledge of how the genre works in relation to skills and abilities is instead replaced by text boxes and dialogue telling you exactly where to go and why, if at all. Many times, whether it be due to forgetting or missing dialogue or said dialogue just being absent, the path forward was a mystery as it was placed behind a door silently unlocked that I'd already been told was locked. On the note of abilities, very few are actually used for progression. Your double jump, bat jump, and mist are all I can recall that actually help access new areas, with the rest largely being used for combat and barely any actually finding much use in my own gameplay. Mist was great for combat, as it not only makes you invincible, but slows down the enemies for added DPS, blood tornado essentially means you'll scarce ever be at risk of death from more than laziness or its cooldown, and wolf dash makes traversing the castle occasionally bearable. Beyond that, nothing else ever got used for any reason other than out of pity for my underutilized skillset. Headouken in particular is too cumbersome to ever find any use. All of this culminates in Dracula feeling less of an all-powerful demon of the night, responsible for wreaking havoc among civilizations and slaughtering men in the thousands, and more like Adam Sandler's Dracula with a couple nifty party tricks. Blood tornado is a band-aid on the enemy's tendency to drain your health rapidly due to a complete lack of invincibility frames or knockback on hit, wolf dash was done first by Symphony of the Night, and better, the backdash is pitiful, and the double jump is one of, if not the absolute worst feeling jumps I've had the displeasure of interacting with. How Dracula ever survived without the dozen odd volunteers giving him their lives for an added health pool is so far beyond me it's genuinely a knock against the story in my book.On the note of the story, there is scarce any to speak of. Whoever Dracula's wife or adversary we hear of at the beginning of the game, we never see or hear more about. I for sure didn't in my run, and with the abysmal game design and unlikable cast, I doubt most other players did much better to find a true ending wherein Belmont and Draculady make an appearance. The most we know of Dracula is largely found in dialogue with our ex, Medua, and fellow vampire Sol. Coincidentally, these are the only two characters I felt a strong connection to, likely because they are the only ones whom our character has even a modicum of chemistry with. Our paper thin plot revolves around Grim setting up our protagonist on a series of dates for the sake of a game show, and evolves to include him finding his own suitors and bringing them to the castle to be promptly ignored forever. The idea is simple, but doesn't need to be much more than that. Its sole duty is to act as a narrative device to set Dracula into action, and to string together the many suitors. Unfortunately this is also all we get. The dates we do get are sparse, the dialogue is minimal, we barely get to know our suitors beyond a few questlines they can give us and date spots set around the game's locations. Getting to know your date in a dating sim is the lifeblood of the game, and this one couldn't have fallen flatter if it was an Olympic competitor in faceplants. Many of our potential spouses are one-note, as is likely necessary of a game spreading itself so thin betwixt a wider cast and an entirely separate game genre. This would be acceptable, if that note was intriguing or even likable, but between PSL's incessant sexual harassment of Drac, Brocifer's insufferable partysona, and the vast majority of our remaining cast providing absolutely no personality whatsoever, I would prefer to step out into the sunlight and meet our fate to see if the afterlife provides any suitors that can muster a conversation that

There needs to be a lot more polish at that price point. Bad writing, bad crossover genres, etc. aside, the game should function a lot better. I'm likely past the point to refund the game, but I certainly would if I could.I could go on about the camera, broken hitboxes, other poor design choices, and death warps soft locking you (where I called it quits), but you get it. Unfortunately a game like this likely won't improve much. The premise appears to be a joke, and as such the goal post can be moved for any argument you make against it. _childDocuments_.review: A cute and quirky love letter to metroidvanias and dating sims. Despite it being janky in pretty much every area, it's still enjoyable to play with some genuinely nice and funny moments at times. Not to mention its premise being entirely comedic itself, with Dracula thrust into a reality TV dating show by his friend, the Grim Reaper.Where this game suffers is in the animations and, most jarringly, in the dialogue. Characters will often refer to characters that no longer exist after you've voted them out. Animations often look stiff and off for most characters and enemies. But it's obviously a labor of love by a small team that love both the genres they're mashing together, so it becomes easy to overlook the small flaws and enjoy it for what it is.Two protips you need to keep in mind:1) P.S Elle is best girl (But I still picked Lulu because I'm a freak)2) Voting Brocifer off first is a noob trap
_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: A game that does a great job using what mechanics we loved from Castlevania and Metroid, while adding in elements that wouldn't seem to work but do for the sake of storytelling. _childDocuments_.review: This game has an immense amount of charm and fun in it! It's a really fun metroidvania both mechanically and exploratively. The 3D character models and animations for the main cast are a bit janky but the largest selling point is the writing. It swaps between genuine dialogue about relationships, emotional baggage, personal growth, boundaries and some of the wackiest groan-inducing wordplay that the human brain can muster. It made every dialogue with the cast an absolute delight and with the pick-a-side moments really gave it that trashy daytime reality TV feel in the best way. I've played through it twice both as masc and femme Drac and while I prefer masc Drac both are great in their own ways. All of the characters are interesting and choosing  is not easy, ever. Characters that seem like they're just caricatures and jokes to wordplay off their premise had so much to offer in realizing that these personas can be masking real fears and insecurities. I did experience a couple bugs when trying to talk to primarily P.S. Elle later on and trying to enter Brocifer's room but a quick exit and reload seems to have resolved it. The game is not perfect but it has an amazing charm and wonderful experience you're not going to find anywhere else. I'd give it an 8/10 with some points knocked for some bugs and some of the character model jank that presents itself intermittently. It's an incredible game well worth your time AND multiple playthroughs! It took me about 12-13 hours per run so it's not a very long experience and it gets shorter as you replay.

_childDocuments_.name: Romancelvania

_childDocuments_.review: While Romancelvania has a few good characters and a surprising number of heartwarming moments, as well as some fun and funny ideas, ultimately it tries to do too much. In trying to be both a metroidvania and a dating simulator, it fails to flesh out either very well - the metroidvania elements feel sluggish and many of the unlocks are uninspired at best (for example, a number of places are simply closed off by the show's host saying "come back later"), and the dating elements don't offer enough interaction with most of the characters, who have few available interactions. Introducing romanceable characters over time throughout the game also feels like a strange choice, as you have barely any time to get to know most of them before you have to vote them out and it leaves the player biased towards the older characters (who are both more likely to have higher relationship levels and have more opportunities to be taken on dates and otherwise get interactions). I finished the game in 8 hours, and while that time could be extended with replays to focus on other romances, neither gameplay nor dating simulator is compelling enough to make it worth replaying given the length - if it was shorter, a replay could be worth doing, while the length wouldn't be an issue if the gameplay was less of a slog.Ultimately, I can't recommend the game - at least not at its $25 price point. If it goes on sale for $15 or less, give it a short - otherwise, not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty nice dating sim with tacked on combat. Story is pretty simple - Dracula is absent from top of the massacre charts for 100 years after losing love of his life, so he was forced to participate in the show to find him new partner by Death. So you go around different location, discovering participants and regaining your powers to access new areas and secrets and even more participants. On your way, you collect various stuff that helps in combat and to woo your chosen ones. There are also sometimes moments when you see a pair of candidates arguing with each other, so taking side gives you some brownie points and dating spots. Game is also divided into chapters and after first three you'd have to choose 1-2-3 person who is eliminated from participation. So in the end you could get to finishing line with exactly half of total cast. There are only two major issues encountered during my playthroughs. Combat - it's simple, easy and boring, not many weapons\powers, not many types of enemies or bosses, very floaty fights with questionable hitboxes and stuff. And second issue is character design - particularly jarring gap between 2d art and 3d models, almost all 3d models especially their faces look like cheap parodies of 2d counterparts and honestly making you feel like not dating any of them. So better try to do your best to only look at 2d representations every time you have to interact.

_childDocuments_.review: So as a sucker for dating sims, this is a unique and charming addition to my roster. A dating sim is always better with gameplay rather than just a VN; be it this insane metroidvania mash up, or simply adding stats. Any addition can take a great story and make it into a game. Similar to the likes of Boyfriend Dungeon, this addition of combat amplifies the story to a replayable fun fest. I had a lot of fun. The stories are charming, the dates are all very unique. Each character feels really fleshed out and leaves a last impression. The ones near the end, leave you wanting to do a reply to get those extra dates.With the "get it all" mindset, you'll lock yourself out of a few possibilities, leading to a need for a reply to experience them. As someone who wants to see all interactions, I recommend having a few saves, at least before voting off the contestants. On top of saving your dates until near the end, so you don't miss the route you wanna take cause you used up a location's date options. All in all, I really loved this game. I would recommend it. Instead of having their dialogue, their voices are filled in with an annoying little harp sound effect that gets tiresome really quickly. The Dating Sim aspect is weak at best. A lot of the conversation and dialogue feels meaningful, but a lot of options feel like you're not being given much in the way of actual choice. Just the illusion of it. Despite the marketing toting being able to be friends with or romance the NPCs, there doesn't really feel like an actual division there. Just whatever head canon you give it. In addition, while I understand the elimination thing is meant to be like The Bachelor, it's really frustrating that you're walled off on getting to know characters because you have to eliminate so many of them from a small pool as you go, and the number you have to eliminate grows larger every time. Some abilities disappear or are unable to be unlocked if you vote someone off, so be extra careful who you choose. Also, the date scenes are super flat, and you have a limited number of them per location, and if you don't do it in the right order, you may not be able to fully complete all of the dates for the one character you want to take on every possible date they have. There's no reason to limit the number of dates you can go on per location, save (and my guess) that you don't notice the repeated conversation beats between characters. Also, the gifts. There is no tutorial about where to go to give your presents to people. (If you're curious, next to the Gallery there's a Christmas Themed room where you give the gifts. Why Christmas themed when the game doesn't seem to take place during Christmas? I've no earthly idea.) The JUMPING! My God, before you get the double jump it is an absolute nightmare to get anywhere. In the first episode there's a jump in the gallery that I swear is nearly frame and pixel perfect or you just can't get up there. The final boss fight (No spoilers). There's a bit of dialogue that kind of points towards the correct course of action being "Doing nothing". That is not the correct course of action. Otherwise, you have to start the fight over again, and it felt much harder the second time around. The ending (No spoilers). It felt really anti-climactic. Even after the final scene, I'd have liked an epilogue tailored to who I chose for my final date. While it's a sweet sentiment that let's Drac get his ending, I'd like more detail so (as mentioned in my frustration regarding the Sim Dating aspect), I feel like my choice of partner actually has an impact on the end of the game other than just a cookie cutter end scene. The credits. Look, I'm all for giving credit where it's due. And I understand the importance of thanking your Kickstarter backers, too. But 10 minutes?! 10 minutes of unskippable credits, a majority of which is Kickstarter Backers, many of which have the same name "Yes"? Now for what I really enjoyed about the game. It was very reminiscent of old school Metroidvanias. I enjoyed the slightly old fashioned textures and backgrounds, and some of the weapons were great call backs to Castlevania. A map would have been appreciated outside of me guessing based on what I saw on the Fast Travel select screen, but I could make do. The combat isn't anything especially fancy or unique, but seeing as it's made to resemble the old fashioned side scrollers of yesteryear, that's basically it. Trust me when I say the whip is the best weapon in the game. I got the deluxe edition so I had the reaper too, which was a great secondary, but the whip will get you through a majority of the fights without issue. The voice acting (excluding Van Helsing) was fantastic. Some of the text doesn't always sync up exactly with what they say, but considering that the game is very much a small team passion project, they did an amazing job. The dialogue felt well written (mostly), and the character stories were engaging enough that I was interested to learn more about them. I found myself agonizing over the eliminations because a lot of the characters were ones that I really didn't want to block off for me if I could have had more opportunity to socialize with them. It never felt like an easy choice, even when I had to eliminate one from the starting three. Even though she didn't end up being my final choice, I really enjoyed P.S. Elle's conversations. Even as lewd and forward as she was, it was also really nice to find that she's incredibly supportive of the rest of the cast, which is what kept her in as long as she did. The humor and absurdity is great and entertaining. The boss fights varied from creative to repetitive, but they were never so bad that I felt like I couldn't play the game again to go through them if I wanted to. I played on normal mode, so i can't speak to the challenge seekers out there, but for a normal difficulty, I felt it was well balanced, even though some of the rough edges did cause frustration (looking at you Spitters). All in all, 7/10. May replay in the future with different choices/eliminations, but seeing as it didn't feel like the end would change based on who I chose, I'm not seeing a major reason to rush back again after I beat it. The Deluxe edition didn't feel worth the extra ten dollars, and I'm still trying to figure out what the area that the DLC (a frustratingly confusing acronym that's used repeatedly) has deemed me as being "Not ready for" is. Even at the end of the game I was "Not ready", so I question as to how I'm supposed to ever be ready for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Romancelvania is a 3D platforming game with a dating sim twist that I honestly enjoyed more than I expected to. Especially the camera—it's really difficult—I keep getting stuck on tricky positions where I can’t see what I’m trying to hit. The devs have been really responsive and are pushing updates out swiftly, which I appreciate.  I really enjoy the story and the characters, though—so many of them are a blast. _childDocuments_.review: Romancelvania is a love letter to the action platformers we all grew up with, combined with a saucy take on the dating sim narrative. It's not adult or hentai though—it's something you shouldn’t be afraid to play online on Steam. Romancelvania isn't a game that tells you more than a minimum of where to go, or what to do. You have the levels to explore, which are filled with collectables.  But you need to be in the right mindset or you might bounce from the game. Romancelvania has very little tracking or progression—there's some minimum stuff in the menu, but there’s no map, no waypoints. It’s old school and it might be somewhat hard to understand where you need to go. I remember playing Super Metroid and just having to bump around until I had the right upgrades. You gotta do that kind of stuff. The game is very much about the journey more than the destination. Even if the destination is some hot monster’s bed. If you KNOW that’s what to expect, then I think you can enjoy the game better than if you’re just like trying to dive through the levels to unlock the next character. But if you find yourself questioning ‘where the heck is that thing?’ or ‘what am I doing here?’ the best advice I can give you is just put that question in the back of your head, and explore. That’s what the game expects of you.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Haven't completed the game yet. About 3/4 through atm. Feel though that I have played enough to write a decent review.First of all, huge props to this development team for such a unique and ambitious idea! Castlevania is part of my lifeblood, having been a fan of the Belmont clan since I was 9 years old in 1986. I also spent a few years working on Post-Punk versions of all of the CV soundtracks, so you could say I'm a bit of a vania fan. Taking such an audacious (yet genius) idea of mashing up a Metroidvania platformer, with a comical dating-sim. The Deep End Games have a lot to live up to here. And do they pull it off? Did they stick the landing? Hmmmmm... yeaaaahhhh almost. Almost. Now the things that are holding me back from giving this game a hearty "must-play recommendation" are almost entirely because of jankiness and bugs. Things which can be patched out over time. Even the following design choices could easily be resolved through patching.Such as not providing the user any sort of navigational aid. No castle map (there's a map of the outskirts around the castle). These games really need to have that classic pause menu/map option, It's a standard design trope in almost every Metroidvania. Either that or some sort of objective tracker to point the user towards the next goal. I put up with this frustrating navigation system, because I really love everything else about this game, but I can easily see a more casual fan giving up quickly and going for that refund. Also the game could really use an auto-save feature. I had two different instances, where I got caught in geometry and had to quit without saving and I lost over an hour of progress each timeWith those small issues out of the way, what is here is definitely worth it if your even a casual fan of retro gaming. There's lots of cute lil' inside jokes for gamers of a certain age. The overall vibe captures a ton of classic horror settings and even some surprise locales I won't spoil. The platforming, combat and exploration, are all perfectly adequate. I really am not that invested in the platforming, what really shines here though is the dating-sim/reality show part of the game. The writing feels very natural and hilarious. I also really appreciate the modern and more progressive aspects to the writing and letting the player choose their Dracs gender/voice is a thoughtful choice that more game designers could learn from. Most of the supporting cast is fleshed out really well through multiple dates and conversations. I'm not really a fan of VizNovels or dating-sim games usually. But surprisingly, it's really addicting in this game. Also, given the nature of the dating aspect, the replay value of Romancelvania is pretty high. It would be pretty sweet to be able to do a NG+ without all of the platforming and questing. And just get into the dating part to see how different choices play out.Overall, yeah this game is fun and worth your time, if you like good writing, charming characters, and enjoy more mature humor and content, definitely worth your $25-------------------------~ I am a former Quality Assurance Lead Tester, with over 20 years in the industry and nearly 40 years of PC and Console gaming experience. ~ Video Games are my lifeblood and I hope my reviews provide potential buyers with ample information to help them make a decision regarding their purchases.

_childDocuments_.review:
Romancelvania is a both a loving parody of Metroidvanias and fresh take on dating in games. It's an RPG that features in-depth weapon and magic based combat, exploration based platforming, and a cast of gorgeous monsters that you won't be able to resist.

You play as the legendary playboy vampire himself, Drac, as he battles and romances his way across Transylvania. After being reluctantly recruited by the Grim Reaper to star in a "reality dating show," he's on a mission to find the world's most eligible monsters, get them to move into his party mansion, and restore his former glory by killing everything in his path along the way.

name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope
detailed_description: Experience the upgraded version of Little Hope, available now. New to this upgrade: difficulty settings & QTE warnings, improved UI & interactions, updated bearing’s art & event triggers, increased walk speeds and wider accessibility options including subtitle sizing. *Free upgrade for owners of Little Hope on PC. The Dark Pictures Anthology is a series of intense, standalone, branching cinematic horror games featuring single and multiplayer modes. 4 college students and their professor become stranded in the abandoned town of Little Hope. Trapped by an impenetrable fog they try desperately to escape whilst witnessing terrifying visions from the past. They must figure out the motivation of these apparitions before the evil forces at work drags each of their souls to hell. Witness terrifying visions of the past, haunted by the events of the XVIIth century Andover Witch Trials Escape the hideous apparitions that relentlessly pursue them through the fog! Play online with a friend or up to 5 friends offline. Abandon Hope...all who enter here! The Curator's Cut The Curator's cut features new scenes playable from the other characters' perspective with brand new choices and decisions to make. The Curator's cut is only available once you have completed the main story.

This is especially great when the game randomly decides to change your mouse sensitivity to -9000 or constantly hides your mouse pointer so you have to find it first. _childDocuments_.review: Little Hope is a compelling story with incredible build up and atmosphere. It occasionally suffers from some generic horror traits, and has some vague plot points that are sometimes used to push the story forward. The towns layout and design has been thoroughly researched which leads to a world where its details and collectables feel believably interwoven with the story beats. The game has some incredible set pieces and awesome cinematic moments that are definitely worth enjoying. Admittedly the quick time events found in some of the more dramatic areas of the game do halt some of the fun and the game can often times rely too much on them, but there are settings to disable the timeouts and alternating button presses which make those sections less of a problem so that you can focus more on the visuals and the story unfolding. The great visual comparisons and motifs found throughout Little Hope between three distinct time periods definitely presents a game worth experiencing.

Its interesting to see how the character relationships drastically differ depending on the different choices that my friends have made while playing.  All in all, I've enjoyed it.

The twist at the end sort of makes a lot of the game feel pointless, and would have better suited a movie than a game where you interacted with/ controlled all the characters. _childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: By far the worst entry in a series that usually ranges from great to decent games. I played Little Hope cooperatively online with a friend, and the game generously provided us with natural breaks everytime it crashed, froze, or got stuck when loading scenes. It's a good thing that the game can be played cooperatively because half of the time it was only one of us who were able to interact with, or inspect, things in the environment. Other than all the technical bugs, the characters and dialogue felt awkward and forced.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: I was ready to give this one a decent review, the plot up until the end was pretty good, I liked the flashbacks and how they were tying in with the present world. I enjoyed that these select characters all had similar fates throughout the different eras, but in the game you had a choice to break that destiny, I also liked the aspect of mystery in trying to find out who was the villain during the trials and the decisions you had to make...and then they decided they wanted to put an idiotic, and completely unnecessary "plot twist" in the end for no reason at all, it did nothing for the game, your choices you made, the characters you started warming up to and how invested you got in the trials was undone. SPOILERS: Everything was fake, it was all in the bus drivers head, he was just delusional and walking around alone. You should have left it with the students getting out. I once again would not recommend this one or Man of Medan, I'll have to wait and see if I play the others. I just am not a fan of pointless "plot twists" and stale, cheap endings. I am huge into narrative games but these just aren't it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: The second game in the acclaimed series will give you little hope of ever playing another Dark Pictures game again. I was so excited after playing the first game that I jumped straight into this one and salivated like a haunted baby. Cumbersome. Tiresome. Flawed. I don't know why the second instalment went down the drain faster than a lost coin touched by a ghost, but the game stutters, figuratively, and seems to never hold purchase with the rest of the series. I don't want to spoil the game, but certain events happen even if different choices are made. Keeping up with the ever-changing, ambiguous narrative made this game hellish to play. I despised it.

_childDocuments_.review: Little hope is a alright game overall but with few issues here and thereStory - 6/10 - reason for this is after you get to the end there's a little twist in which kinda makes the game unplayable again but the story itself is worth playing onceaudio - 8/10 - great audio overall and but sometimes it gets overly loud which make sense for the horror however it really is too much. at least for megame play - 4/10 a lot of the time you succeeded the QTEs but still lose lose the overall matter, some cases the character dies even if you tried your best to save them. also one of the players has way more actions than the other, my friend had to deal with all the major Action events while i was there either walking in the world at times or having random dialect with the charactersi will only list these as the rest is either average or just "works just fine" type of feel, let's go over bugs real quick as this game was very buggy at times but mainly in Co-op experience.bugs/issues - a lot of the bugs comes from this game trying to keep you and your friend on the same patch but did it horribly as the pacing of the game at times does not match between you and your friend, so in a lot of situations you will end up waiting for your friend to finish their cutscene or their part of the story, best example would be you waiting in an area not able to do anything for minutes on end. a lot of cutscene are buggy and you phase through the world and laggy scenes where some of the world is not there and stuttering sorry for making this little long
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: "We each have our own demons. They are ours and ours alone, and they are often born out of regret."The second entry into the Dark Pictures Anthology focuses on 4 college students and their teacher who become trapped and isolated in the abandoned town of Little Hope and they must attempt to escape the nightmarish, deviant ghouls that mercilessly stalk them through a seemingly endless fog.The second entry into the series, this game was disappointing and treads downhill from its predecessor.  It follows in the same footsteps by delivering an interactive movie with a supernatural narrative, gripping jumpscares, and thrilling quick-time events.  In terms of graphics, the game looks great;  The developers are clearly skilled at providing an incredibly cinematic gaming experience, and at times you forget that it's a video game and not a film.  However, its weaknesses lie within the story and the characters in the sense that there’s really not much there.  I did enjoy the kind of seamless connection between the two time periods of the story but it’s really not enough.  The characters are very hollow and you really don’t care about any of them so you are not very motivated to save them all and make it to the ending where everyone lives.  Also, the ending that I got and the rest of the story are so disconnected to the point where it just doesn’t make sense and it is just weak storytelling.  The second one is definitely the weakest one in the series and I hope the following games only get better;  I still have really high hopes for the series.  Unless you want to replay the game multiple times to experience the multiple endings, the game really only has around 8-10 hours of playtime so definitely wait for a sale if you’re interested in buying.  Little Hope is a somewhat steep decline in the storytelling and world-building that the first game set up and it was pretty underwhelming and disappointing; It still gives the player a decent horror experience with a lot of jumpscares but there’s not much else there.  5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, although with a HUGE BUT. Hear me out.It's better made than the first one, the acting and animations are really good (except for the character of John - his facial expressions look like contortions a lot of the time, but that's motion capture's fault, I guess). The abysmal controls are mostly gone, we're now given the option to point and click (on PC).The story is good, almost Silent Hill-like. The only thing that bummed me out were the "scaredy ghost" time transitions. It should've happened with a bit more...variety. Through objects, maybe?Here comes the huge but: This game is anxiety-inducing as hell. The controls on PC are still lacking, so you simply cannot make all the QTE work. AND you have to save your characters over and over again. BUT if you screw up once - they're done with. If you play co-op, either you or your buddy could accidentally do in any of the characters. By the end of the game I was having a full-on panic-attack - nausea, increased heartbeat and all.Sooo... not a very pleasant experience for me. It didn't scare me as much as stress me out - I felt like a doctor who's failing again and again. Seems... a bit like hell, doesn't it?Still, I do recommend this one for its story and how beautiful it is visually.P.S. PREMONITIONS ARE WORTHLESS

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope is the first game I've played from 'The Dark Pictures Anthology'. Until now I've only played through it once but I might give it another go in the future. Basically playing Little Hope is just like watching a decent horror movie, except that your choices may alter the outcome and who get's to live or die. Graphically the game looks so stunning you almost can't see the difference between this and a movie. Especially since the developer hired some decent actors like Will Poulter (The Maze Runner) and completing the game takes about the same time. The gameplay is quite minimal; you will be walking around a lot and interact with (optional) books, photos and other items. In danger/combat you simply have to press the right buttons (quicktime events), pressing the wrong button could mean a character dies and you can't just load and try again. The most important aspect of a game like this has got to be the story/writing which I personally liked a lot. Anyone who loves horror/mystery movies will probably like this one.

CONS:• The co-op system of the game didn't work and ended up paying for another license• Used the same formula as Man Of Medan and was too easy to predict certain outcomes.• The controls are awful and the camera angles made it hard to see throughout the game.Overall another mediocre "horror" game. _childDocuments_.review: I received this product on sale for $10 off and I still would not recommend it, this review is based off of the strong precedent Dark Anthologies: Man of Medan set. I will mention some elements from this game that some may be considered minor spoilers, nothing directly related to the story. Even now with the update to allow one friend a free play-through of the game I would not recommend this unless you intend to be a completionist for the Dark Anthologies series. But trust me when I say one play-through will be sufficient.The positives: - this game looks incredible, the voice acting is well done and the characters feel alive. The "prelude" type beginning is a welcome set up. The negatives: - The story constantly puts you and your Co-Op partner in the same scenes meaning you see the same thing, making repeated play-throughs to see other stories unlikely. In Man of Medan you would often be separated from your Co-Op partner, this added tension and raised the curiosity of how their choices would impact your story. This feature in Man of Medan made us excited to play through again as different characters and experience the other side of the story.- The developers removed and changed features from Man of Medan that worked very well, namely the WASD movement was removed for point-and-click locked movement that feels janky and limiting, along with this quick-time events now are isolated to the mouse making some easy and some very unforgiving as the mouse may be lost on the screen (no cursor) and you have to shake it to find it in time to click the correct quick-time marker. This being said the quick-time events are much easier and there is less than in Man of Medan making each failed on matter much more.- The characters are very unlikable and less charming than in Man of Medan. - The jump scares are incredibly predictable and over-used, along with this they are often cut short due to the direction the developers took with the story (trying to avoid spoilers).- There seems to be less things to look at and interact with compared to Man of Medan, and even when you do find something your partner is right beside you ready to look at it also because the game refuses to separate you.-MINOR SPOILER:- If your looking for a good walk-down a road simulator you have found a beautiful looking one, the branching paths of Man of Medan are gone in this game, and while there are some interesting locations when you are not on a road, too much of the game uses a long road as a way to break up scenes.

_childDocuments_.review: For 50 AUD, I can in no way recommend this game. It is a 4 hour walking simulator with a VERY cheap jump scare every 10 - 15 mins that might get you the first time, but as it becomes a plot device for the time jumping back to the 17th century story line, it becomes pretty obnoxious after a while.The entire story is cheapened by the ending which makes every choices you made pretty much pointless. Man of Medan was at least sort of entertaining with different endings (even if it was poor in comparison to Until Dawn). This somehow is even worse than Man of Medan. The script is bad, the story is bad, and holding forward and just moving through the game was tedious at best. Co-op was kind of a laugh but for 50 bucks it is in no way worth it. These games should be released at 10-15 each then charged s a full priced game for all four. Not 200.00 for four 4 hour games.... You've been warned!

_childDocuments_.review: The second entry into Supermassive Game’s Dark Pictures Anthology follows a group of four hapless college students and their professor after they are involved in a road accident which leaves them stranded on the outskirts of the town Little Hope, a rundown ghost town covered in a dense fog that prevents anyone from leaving.The story jumps between modern times and the past as Little Hope was once the site of witch trials and the ghosts of the past are still active in haunting it today.Each of the five playable characters experience their own flashback to the time of the witch trials where they see the version of themselves from that time be tried and executed on suspicion of witchcraft. Back in the present day they are each pursued by a demon representing the execution from the past. It’s all very confusing and doesn’t make a lot of sense and the story or characters aren’t strong enough to warrant much care.The gameplay of Little Hope consists of walking, talking, and quicktime events, bog standard for the genre. Occasionally you’ll come across something your character can slowly interact with in an effort to extend playtime and bore you with uninteresting background information or a cheap jumpscare. Little Hope follows a formula of: Slowly walk through a linear section, sit through some cringe worthy dialogue, fire off a cheap jumpscare, cue the unneeded quick-time events, rinse and repeat, and while this is fine for the genre so long as the story, characters, and pacing make up for it, it’s not the case here as too much time is given to pointless exploration and uneventful filler scenes.Little Hope lacks any of the intrigue or tension of the previous entry in the series as the presentation here feels very rushed. Action scenes feel stilted and sloppy, often throwing way too many camera cuts and slow-motion shifts in character perspective in your face at once. Combine this with a generic, uninteresting cast and writing that is saturated with a disconnect from what’s happening on screen and any sense of immersion the story could’ve had is ruined.The monster design was easily the best aspect of the game. Each of the demons have their own style, incorporating their method of execution into the aesthetic and way they attack the player. However, again the presentation ruins the atmosphere as the animations and cinematography in most scenes involving the demons is incredibly jarring and often ends up teleporting the slow-moving demons in an artificial attempt to make scenes more intense.Overall I didn’t find Little Hope to be all that interesting and definitely not worth the 6ish hours to complete. If you have a friend to play it with I could see some merit in playing the co-op story for a laugh, but if you’re looking for a serious horror tale with actual scares pass this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally I loved this game. I really felt like this was a step in the right direction compared to Man of Medan. I enjoyed the camera angles, the dialogue, the action sequences and the characters in general more than I did in the first game of the Anthology. _childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise it is a massive improvement over Man of Medan (which I also found fun). The story is engaging and the characters are surprisingly well written so far. I didn't like them at first, but that is precisely why they make for such strong characters. There is always some form of tension brewing in the narrative, often due to these character's differing opinions and attitudes. I simply had to leave this review when I saw so many negative ones here. I haven't finished the story but the graphics and sounds are great, and the scares are much more abundant on this Dark Picture game compared to their last. The prologue alone sucked me in, and I can't tell you how exciting it was to experience the fog first hand in this game when I finally had control over my character. Definitely a creative "visual novel/walking simulator"     I would recommend this game to any fans of horror movies or any fans of Telltale games. After having completed my 1st playthrough I was left with many questions. I have seen countless horror films and I honestly did not see the twist coming even though there were definitely a few warning signs to give it away. Because of this, I'm currently focusing my entire 2nd playthrough around uncovering the truth behind the truth and will update this review for a 2nd time once I have finished with that.      I also wanted to mention that the overall structure of the setting & the storyline itself is handled more interestingly than Man of Medan. One is able to explore a bit more freely and walk at a more reasonable pacing which all helps to lend to the atmosphere set up by the plot. The game is fairly short, but keep in mind that these games are essentially short stories and they're supposed to be able to be played and completed alongside friends on couch-play, so it would have to be decently short. At the end of the day, I'm excited to see what else The Dark Pictures anthology has in store for us in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope is the new entry of the Dark Pictures Anthology, set in the mysterious town of Little Hope. After a bus accident a group of college students and a professor are stuck in Little Hope and are trying to find help and their way home.  Story 7.5 of 10You are starting off after a bus accident has the team (college students and a professor) stuck in the outskirts of Little Hope, an eerie little town surrounded by a mysterious fog with a dark history. As you are trying to find a way out you will encounter dangerous creatures and will have at times a quick glimpse of the dark and gory past of Little Hope.Graphics 8.5 of 10The character faces are hands town the best of all games I ever played, maybe aside from Call of Duty Modern Warfare. It just so seamlessly feels like you are playing a movie that it is breathtaking at times. They make subtle moves and gestures and all this comes together and makes the team feel very realistic. On the downside I have to say that I experienced some annoying glitches (voice and character being out of sync during cut scenes, being stuck at an invisible wall, no sound) and I have to take this into account and have to subtract one point from my scoreGameplay 7.5 of 10I was kind of disappointed from this game as I played both Until Dawn and Man of Medan and liked the exploring and the fact that it did feel like a lot more open world. Little Hope will not let you go on explore the neighborhood to the extent that the others did and there is also the mysterious fog that keeps you on track (Silent Hill anyone?). Aside from this for my first play through I played the “shared story mode” with a friend and we had a so much fun on Halloween and this mode alone is worth the 7.5 rating. Even though it was very short… we like played 5 hours and used some time to adjust our settings and had a bug so we restarted. As this is a Supermassive game I will definitely play it again to see if there are different outcomes and because we sadly did not manage to keep everyone alive. There are some quick time events which can be challenging, even though to me it feels like you have slightly more time to react as in Man of Medan. One more point I absolutely did not like was the fact that everyone moves very slow (if I had to compare it to another game I would compare it to Red Dead Redemption campground speed). At some point in the game I had a feeling that the game was rushed and a part was cut due to the deadline approaching. Also I somehow could not feel as invested in the team as I did in Man of Medan or Until Dawn. The chemistry somehow did not click with me and did not feel as natural as the previous games. Little Hope is Music 9 of 10 While there is no real music, there is a lot of nature and creepy sounds, creaking doors and stuff. The voice acting is top notch, never feels campy and aside from the glitches I experienced, all is good.Final Verdict:Would I recommend it? Yes, for the shared gameplay alone it is worth it, even though the price tag of 29 USD for a 5-hour game may be a little steep. But hey it’s been a rough year, let’s treat ourselves. Follow Cat Curations  on Steam

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a FMV experience with an enjoyable horror story, be sure to check this game out.  I completed 1 solo playthrough and had a good time. If you enjoy FMV type games you're sure to enjoy this as it plays like a solid FMV with choices made along the way affecting future outcomes.  Then this has a slight amount of adventure gaming with hunting around for additional story details and clues, nothing too devious though.  Lastly it has quick time events to save your ass from the nasties out there.  Going with the default settings I found the QTE to be much easier this game than past ones and I appreciated that as it's a pain to make many good decisions to die to mucking up too many QTE. Give it a try, I look forward to the next installment.

_childDocuments_.review: If Man of Medan was extreme babysitting, this one is an extreme guilt trip.An entertaining game with a couple of negative points:- The "Stay Calm" quick time events are never fun;- A couple of seemingly inconspicuous choices prevented me from attaining the best ending. This is a common problem with this type of games, since what you may think is a good choice, may not be so for the writer(s) of the story. And there is no way for you to know what is the best path other than just by pure luck and, perhaps, a bit of common sense.On the positive side, you can now select a scene (chapter) as you complete each one while playing the game. You couldn't do this in the previous game (Man of Medan), as you had to finish it in order for all the chapters to be available. And even then, you had to create a new Story (save file) so to not lose access to that facility; otherwise you would have to finish the game again for the chapters to be unlocked...again. Always create a new save file should you wish to play a previous chapter. You can thank me later.I would recommend this game for those who like horror stories and psychological thrillers.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon replaying Little Hope, I don't hate it. It does what the devs intended well enough. However, that value isn't truly seen until you replay the game. Knowing how it ends frames the things characters say and the events that happen in a different light which is interesting. For that first playthrough though, I found myself confused and disappointed, turning to YouTube for answers and closure after the ending. For this reason, I have kept my rating of the game set to negative. To be clear - it is not a bad game, many love it. I consider myself a fan of Supermassive's work. But, my disappointment with what could have been still persists.For 95% of Little Hope, I liked it more than I liked Man of Medan, the series' first entry.  I connected with the characters more, I liked the setting more, and I thought it was an exciting adventure.  I was eager to find out how it ended.  The ending, though... it felt really out of nowhere, and didn't provide me with the emotional closure I wanted.Looking back on some aspects of the story like , I can see what they were going for.  That is clever, I'll admit.  The ending ties into that theme nicely.  But, I wish that ending had been built up more appropriately.  Instead, the game leads you into thinking you're getting a very different kind of story, which I was very invested in because , then pulls the rug out from you.  This left me feeling grossly unsatisfied with many questions that didn't matter anymore due to the nature of the ending.  That felt cheap.  Man of Medan does a similar thing, but at least that game's story does a better job of making you question it.  In Little Hope, it seems pretty straight forward until the very ending.  The problem here isn't with the content of the ending itself, it's how they went about building up to and presenting it.  Poor execution.This is one of the few games I've played where the ending really ruined the whole thing for me.  Why did we spend all that time doing what we did and building character relationships if the story was just going to end like that?  It feels like I wasted my time.  There is a right way to do what this game's story failed to accomplish.  We needed more hints, buildup, and closure for that kind of story to work.  The ending especially needed to be longer and explain more.Also, the ending my friend and I got had a character die from a choice we had made way earlier in the game.  We saved everyone else, but now we essentially have to replay half the game to have that one character survive which sucks.  The way they died was really flat out stupid too, it didn't make sense.  It would've been nice if the finale gave us one final chance to correct our mistake considering we saved everyone else.  But, it just takes away your control and makes you watch them die.  Lame.  For those who have beaten the game, I'm talking about I'm disappointed that this series is shaping up to be a collection of stories which   I would've been fine with that for just Man of Medan, I liked it for that game's ending.  But, not Little Hope.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be my last Dark Pictures game. The game claims to be about choice but most of your choices don't really matter at all, the game just railroads you into whatever it thinks you should be doing. In my case, it railroaded me into a completely nonsensical ending even though, by the game's own rules, I did everything right (or tried to—on several occasions, it flat out wouldn't let me make that choice and forced me to do something else).If you want to write a game with a linear story, knock yourself out. In fact, I prefer linear stories most of the time. But don't write a story where my choices don't matter and then tell me that they do.

Really spot on and plays super smooth with amazing optimisation.Audio: Again, spot on sound quality from the voice acting to the atmosphere sounds or just the simple walking up the street and noises behind, the jump scare sounds are loud but designed to be loud to make you jump I believe.Controls: My issue here is that it would not allow me to change the keys, so it has forced me to use my controller instead, which is fine but still.. _childDocuments_.review: A very intriguing story, with gorgeous visual and music. Played through once solo with a PS4 controller. I loved the witch trials premise, and it's obvious that the devs put in a lot of effort into researching for accuracy of the time periods represented, which really helped to create an immersive experience. Voice acting was also phenomenal, which you can learn a bit more about in the documentaries that you can unlock after playing the game. Some story beats reminded me a lot of The Crucible by Arthur Miller, and the fog definitely gave off Silent Hill vibes. Gameplay was much like the studio's other titles, so if you enjoyed them then this game won't disappoint.One gripe that I have is that the most of the deaths felt mostly beyond my ability to choose, and one was entirely not my fault because the game froze during an intense QTE section. But despite this I still enjoyed the ending I got. Definitely anticipating the next game in the anthology, especially after the trailer at the end of the game.
