_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Man of Medan then you'll likely enjoy Little Hope even more. There are various quality of life improvements across the board, the gameplay is more refined. The setting is interesting too, since it's far more horror-oriented this time around. Action scenes in particular have new tricks and end up being dramatic and enjoyable. The duration of a first complete exploration play through would be around 6 hours, and if you don't like to smell the roses then a skip most of the interaction points approach would net you around 4 hours. It's more or less the same in terms of the duration as Man of Medan and it is expected, that the players are to replay the game multiple times to see different results.This review is WIP, so pardon my typos. Since I've managed to clear the game just once so far and I will update this review with more info and corrections as I play it.There are now QTE warnings, so the players are aware when the prompts are going to appear and at which screen location. On top of that, it displays what kind of action is being performed, so the player can guess which QTE type it is and what would be the outcome of it. This actually makes some decisions easier.In Man of Medan there was no efficient way of replaying chapters without overwriting your save, which would lock you out of chapter select. In Little Hope there's actually an option to save in a new slot, which is a major quality of life improvement which addresses my biggest gripe with Man of Medan.The visuals look eye pleasing and the game runs well. It's the same quality of assets as on Man of Medan all across the board. Good lighting, good use of post-processing, the model and texture quality is smooth, there's not much to complain about. There were some occasional physics glitches in the previous game, but during my initial play through here I didn't see anything that would be as jarring. This leads me to believe that this game received more polish in general.Another complaint of mine was that it's difficult to pick characters for your first play through if you're trying to split them between friends. And this was addressed too, as there's now an option to auto-assign characters. I'm honestly surprised that both of my complaints ended up being addressed in the sequel, so I'm running out of things to complain about.The flow of the game is just right, it doesn't get stale or boring after a while, it keeps the suspense up and players themselves can spice things up if they wish to. You can finish the game in one sitting if you dedicate around 5 hours of your free time to it. Upon reaching the ending you'll likely want to experiment and see other outcomes, not to mention that there's Curator's Cut, which will spice things up even more.The setting of the game might remind you of Silent Hill, as it happens to use very familiar horror elements: a small abandoned town, covered in fog, survivors with flashlights trying to understand what's going on while facing supernatural demonic beings. Of course, it's nothing like Silent Hill gameplay-wise, but the general mood reminded me of it in a good way.Character dialogue picks sometimes aren't too clear and you might end up picking something you didn't intend to pick. This stems from too brief descriptions and could possibly be patched if necessary.One thing that wasn't added (at least from my brief testing) is that you still can't skip to relevant dialogue, so there's no way for a quick play through. You have to sit through every scene over and over, to the point where you'll start memorizing quotes, something which happened to me with Man of Medan. I suppose it's this way so you can have full context of ongoing conversation, but still, it could have been implemented for those that wanted to get 100% completion quickly.A complaint that is specific to Movie Night, the local co-op mode is that there's still no automatic gamepad recognition. If one player is on Xbox gamepad and the other one is on DualShock 4, then they'll end up needing to switch button layouts in the game's menu every single time the game switches players. Of course, you can just play with one layout if you want to, but that's not exactly optimal or a good idea.The playable characters aren't as distinct as they were in Man of Medan. It could be that my dialogue picks caused that, since I didn't explore other routes yet. Man of Medan cast had far stronger baseline characteristics which ended up being more memorable, especially when you see them going out of their way in redemption scenes.In the previous game there were occasional frame dips, stutters. They weren't happening often, but some of them happened during active QTE sequences, which made things unfair. Little Hope runs much better in that regard and while I did notice visual and audio stutters here and there, in general it's more stable and smooth.Little Hope still runs on Unreal Engine 4, it has the same graphics and a pretty basic graphics options menu. If you ran the previous game well then you'll be running this one same way, which is a good thing.The game still runs letterboxed and there's no way to disable it within the game's options, same as in Man of Medan. All other options are more or less the same, including gamepad button prompt layout switch between Xbox and PlayStation.I was looking forward to playing Little Hope ever since it was teased and I had a good time in Movie Night. It's a nice way of spending your evening with friends and this game builds upon the success of Man of Medan and makes the experience even more fun. I had hopes for it and it delivered, so for those that liked the previous game this one should be a treat.Review copy provided by BANDAI NAMCO Entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright, more like a neutral rating. Worse than Man of Medan imho, but not the cluster♥♥♥♥ some people make it out to be.But compared to MoM the story is less spine-chilling and the characters are A LOT more irritating, as well as inconsistent. Some of the choices had me scratching my head, like "why would I ever say that in this situation?" kind of deal... I was seriously tempted to just let EVERY character die asap ... but I think that is almost harder than having them survive.Animations are a bit weird though. They are massively uncanny, ranging from good to mediocre, and some of the reactions just feel disjointed.There also seems to be a lot less action and possibilities for characters to meet a gruesome and premature end, but this might just be me remembering MoM differently. It's been 2 years after all.The story is ... well, I think it's a lot better after I've finished the game. But I can see why people think it's silly or just plodding along.Controls and everything else is pretty much like in the previous game. You walk, you make choices, you (hopefully or not) complete QTEs, and you look for clues and secrets. I've found most on my first playthrough and was also able to save all characters pretty easily. If you pay a bit of attention you can figure out what to do even if you don't get the whole picture, woe is me ... Should have paid closer attention, since the signs are all there, but then the game tries to obfuscate and mislead. And it succeeded, so, kudos.As with the previous game there are multiplayer modes (only local I think) and a Curator's Cut that lets you play out scenes you didn't get to in the solo mode (if you so desire... maybe I'll do that in a few years if I ever want to play through those games again).All in all you get at least about 5 hours out of it, unless you completely rush through or fail at everything. Twice that amount if you want to see the Curator's version or play through it again with friends (not sure what the deal with the complaints about the multiplayer is, since I did not play that).And now, please excuse me, I will watch all the gory death scenes now!

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't feeling too confident about this game, especially after my experience with the Man of Medan, and how that was such a let down from their previous game, Until Dawn. It had such mixed reviews, and the fact that I had gotten partially spoiled about the ending (which didn't really end up being a big deal in the end), I didn't think I was going to enjoy it and didn't plan on taking it seriously. Then the game pulled me right in from the very start.I'll start with the positive side first. The prologue was really fun and startling. So much went down at once and you feel like you have little control, and without warning it throws you into present day. Then you're left wondering, what does this all have to do with what just happened? The game doesn't waste time setting up the scares and introducing the supernatural, unlike Man of Medan. I was immersed every second of the game, and I scare easily, so between the atmosphere and the jumpscares, it really got to me. The QTEs were fun and certain aspects made combat fun while freaking out at the same time, not as annoying as Man of Medan. Also, the soundtrack is amazing!! The music is so intense and hair-raising, and the opening rendition of O' Death... Flashbacks to Until Dawn came rushing back. Plus the small stuff like accessibility options, dyslexic and or color coded font, ability to disable QTE timers or button mashing. Makes conversation less stressful and also lets you do a casual playthrough if needed.Ok, here's where I'll start with the negatives about the game. The biggest thing first is the amount of replayability. With all the routes, the previous two games they've done had a lot of value in replayability. I don't quite feel the same with this game. I felt no drive to start over and try to get everyone to survive, even though a few characters died in my run. I played the other games multiple times in my first session to either get the prime ending, or just to see what happened. Here I  I'll probably play once more just to see things from the other characters POV that I missed out on.Another big thing is that the characters also make very little smalltalk. Most of the time walking around investigating, there's no casual comments about anything and you can't even talk to the others. I want to be able to talk to everyone between events, get to know how they feel and build relationships with them, even learn a bit more of their history together. I played it with a friend so we could at least talk to each other, but for those who play single player, I think it would make for a silent and unlively game.Then there are smaller things like, sometimes I didn't quite catch when I swapped from one character to the other because it happened mid conversation. I didn't respond as I thought that character would, because I still thought I was the person I started out as. This game is unplayable when using keyboard & mouse, and I still had a bit of trouble using a controller. It was hard to aim during QTE events because you either moved way too far or too slow and you wouldn't make it to the target on time. It was a bit of a nightmare to control the flashlight, as it always moved too much despite the gentlest nudges and I couldn't properly use it to examine the area. The camera angles made it hard to walk, as they really focused on making the camera angles look like you were being watched or priming you for a jumpscare. Sure it works out for the most part, but sometimes there's awkward scene changes that end up with me getting turned around. I never experienced any lag or frame drops running the game on ultra, but there was this visual glitch with lighting and backgrounds not loading in that happened a couple times.All in all, it's a 4/5. I liked it loads more than Man of Medan. The story was way more interesting, the characters more likeable, and dialogue actually felt like it was something a real person would say (most of the time). I recommend that you catch it during a sale, then play it using the online coop with a friend. It makes it so much more enjoyable in my experience. I'm writing this directly after playing the game so I hope I didn't ramble too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Played "House of ashes" and loved it. I was quite reticent to try the other titles as there are some more modern, amazing QTE games out there (Detroit: becoming human pretty much setting the standard)."Little Hope" is VERY different from "House of Ashes" Sure - if you played ANY games in the quadrilogy, you'll recognize the mechanics. THANKFULLY - even without a 'proper' save system, its' trivial to restart from the scene beginning, and correct the shot, so to speak. In HoA, not doing so was not the end of the world. Death was part of the deal. It usually is in these games - bad decisions lead to bad outcomes. Here, however,  'save scumming' - correcting errors made with good intents - is very much needed. The game has extremely specific mechanics which aren't explained clearly:1. You must ALWAYS wait for 'specific encounters' and ALWAYS make the 'hero choice'. Always. Anything else leads to death. Anything else, even correct actions. 2. Text is meaningless. Here's an example: a monster appears, but it's unclear. You played that game before, so you select "Wait until you get a clear shot", right? WRONG, It's boom headshot and dead friend to boot.3. And, here's the  an underlying mechanic that underpins the entire game (in fact, it's the key to winning this game with 100% achievements). But the worst of all issues, is that traits define 'saving rolls'. Forget to unlock these, and you lose ALL saving rolls Lose all saving rolls and you die. EVEN IF you finish the game 100% perfect QTEs, you still will lose characters because you didn't 'unlock' negative traits like 'deceptive'. Traits change constantly, and you have to constantly check them to keep up and keep them memorized.Sadly, a) it's not exactly made clear to you and b) it's game breaking, at least immersion breaking.On the tech side, they got a lot of things right.  There is a way to move the camera independent of movement, it's just 'unclear'. The game runs at 75 fps steady smooth on a 2080/i9900k. It looks good, but not as good as "HoA" .  One the 'wrong side' of things, there's no DLSS for those that want RT and don't have a modern rig, and some textures are bizarelly compressed. In addition, it's really easy to miss some hidden secrets because you clicked a button that moves the story forward and had no way of knowing how or why.All of this should hurt the reviews - and it has. In all honestly, I only finished this because I love the brand, but I admit -I'm grateful they changed these mechanics in the next titles. Despite an overall 'decent' narrative and decent (but not great) characters, I give this 1/5 and a thumb down, only buy if on discount AND PLEASE LEARN THE MECHANICS.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do. Immediately after playing Man of Medan, I binge-played this one in a single session. I loved every minute... right until the ending. The premise hooked me instantly, the story is rife with mystery I was eager to solve before the big reveal, the Silent Hill-esque ambiance is delightfully eerie, and the character dynamics kept me invested throughout. Then the ending abruptly slapped me across the face and said "lol jk, it's not that deep." For a moment, I was sure it had to be a joke, a fake-out, a bad ending through poor choices on my part... something, anything other than what it really is: a cheap cop-out ending that invalidates the entire journey and makes you ask yourself if you just wasted 4-5 hours of your life. It's an ending that undermines the entire experience because the more you examine it in retrospect, the less the story makes sense. It sets high stakes and promises a clever twist it never makes good on. As a writer and avid fan of the Choices Matter game genre, I can't forgive such a lazy, cliche ending to a narrative with so much potential. This could have been a phenomenal game, but instead it damns itself to being the most frustratingly skippable entry of the entire anthology. Like a chocolate-covered brussels sprout, Little Hope creates expectations and offers only the most shocking disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the Dark Pictures Anthology series. Having played all three in the series I think they all have their strengths and weaknesses but are generally of the same (high) level of quality. Little Hope was definitely the creepiest and most unnerving of all three games, and it had by far the most jump-scares (some might say too many-- they work on me so the game was a suitably stressful experience). It's a horror game and it is scary. I was also a fan of the the setting (an abandoned town). They had a lot of classic horror themes to work with and they used them well. My major criticism is that, overall, the story didn't deliver quite as well as the other games. It was scary, and the game keeps a mystery regarding the witch-trials and the secret of the town and the subsequent need to escape in front of you, but it feels a little disjointed. There is a mystery but it isn't really something that is treated as a mystery because key parts are revealed at what feels like "check points." The characters aren't bad by any stretch but they feel a little inconsistent as they develop during the narrative. There really isn't a lot of well written tension between the characters but the writing sometimes tries to act like there is. As a consequence, some dialogue choices (the story choices are solid) feel a little unrealistic. It still works fairly well but of all three games I'd say some conversational choices are very obvious and more frequently so than in other games.The ending will be divisive. I see a lot of reasons for saying that it was actually a clever and strong ending, and I can see reasons for saying that it was the least interesting way to resolve the events of the game. I liked it. Overall, I really enjoyed Little Hope. If you are interested in an interactive horror experience (not quite a game really) then Little Hope will be worth your time. If you are interested in the Dark Pictures Anthology and wondering if you should try another title in the series, Little Hope will be worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: While the story Is not new or earthshattering, the presentation, acting and narration are so well presented! It is beautifully done.The game lulls you onto "movie mode" and I was unprepared to react quick enough when I needed to more than a few times so don’t get too comfortable.The opening and ending "Oh Death" song, made popular by bluegrass legend Ralph Stanley was certainly appropriate for my characters!You always know what your objective is; you always know beforehand if there is a menace nearby.The game autosaves at checkpoints. The checkpoints are generous occurring after a major event or decision has been made.You can play WASD, Point and Click, or with a controller, you can play solo or with a partner.I suffered no crashes or screen tearing. I had a very slight lag just a couple of timesI finished the game in solo mode in about 6.5 hours. I missed half the achievements in this play through using WASD controls. There are 50 secrets you can reveal that connect this group, I only found 30 on this playthrough.When I started a new game, I see my old “secrets” are still there, so you can continue to build on what you have already discovered.Slight annoyances:The controls were unwieldy at times. You have to get your mouse to a target area and click in a circle or press the “A” or “S” key within a certain amount of time. It was slow enough that I would not call it a timed event, but I was unable to get zeroed in where I needed to be several times.Extra clicking…if I click and pick something up why do I need to do anything else to examine it?After completion I wanted to try a different outcome. There is no chapter select. I will have to replay the game to see the other outcomes. Is the story arc so far-reaching that it justifies not having a chapter select? I don't know yet, but I'm interested enough to play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Supermassive Games have really outdone themselves with their latest spooky joint. The game takes place in the small town of the title - Little Hope. After a bus crash, a group of college students and their professor are stranded among the trees, fog, and darkness with only their camera phone flashlights to guide them. But as you can imagine, something about this quaint factory town isn't quite right...In classic Supermassive fashion, you will have to make decisions and defeat QTEs (Quick Time Events) in order to progress the story. But not all well intentioned decisions are good, nor are all logical ones. The game places a heavy emphasis on the war between the heart and the head. Do you take the rational route? Or do you go with your gut? There is no "right" way to play.The story is fantastic this time around. If you were disappointed with Man of Medan like I was, chances are you will enjoy this go around much, MUCH better. And I dare say it surpasses Until Dawn. Not as scary, but just as tense. The "visions" that are present in past games are here, and the amount of love and care put into the notes and books littered around the town shined through. I was sad I didn't find all of them in my first playthrough considering how interesting and well written they were! The characters were natural and well acted. There were some hiccups and jarring transitions in a few scenes, but I think those are hard to remedy in a game with so many different and branching story beats. Overall, very impressed with the story and characters.Graphically, it looks just as good as previous games. Maybe even slightly better. It was hard to notice if they were, but Supermassive has the graphics down and the game looks beautiful despite the brooding and dark aesthetic. My biggest gripe was the syncing of audio with characters speaking. They didn't match up amazingly, but not bad enough to look cheap, and not often enough to be jarring and annoying. This game is very much a "AA" game, and it shows, but I think it punches above its weight in places too. Very happy with the game graphically.Sound was passable. In a game like this, you *really* want to be using headphones, and I didn't encounter any sound issues with the game. It also wasn't all that remarkable. Decent sound is better than bad (or no!) sound!Overall, this is probably the second best entry in the Supermassive catalog of this style of game, and arguably better than Until Dawn. With the hole left in the hobby by Telltale, I think that Supermassive is filling the niche spectacularly, and doing a hell of a job with the medium. I congratulate the entire studio on a job well done with Little Hope, and am looking forward to the next entry in the Dark Pictures Anthology next year!

_childDocuments_.review: I recently completed Man of Medan with a friend and essentially bought Little Hope on the strength of my experience.It's hard to properly describe the game without either giving too much away or not doing it justice. If you enjoy games with a strong, movie-like narrative and those in which your choices can affect the story, you really should like Little Hope. If you have a good friend to play the game co-op with, even better. Being able to play a game similar to Heavy Rain or Detroit with a friend, and have you both working together in a way that almost feels seamless is a big deal, IMHO. My suggestion is to fire up the game with a friend when you have several hours to spare and try to complete it in one sitting. Don't use voice chat to talk to one another, just play it how you feel is right and enjoy the experience.Normally I wouldn't even pay the sale price of ~£17 for a game I knew would essentially be completed within 4-5 hours, but the Dark Pictures games offer a really unique experience which I think is well worth the money (long story short - if you're a cheapass like me don't be put off that the game is short!) I really enjoyed the story of this one and appreciated that it was more story-focused than Man of Medan.Can confidently recommend this game, not that the opinion of some internet random should matter to you ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't like the writing in this game. It feels inhuman, and just like not much care was paid to making the writing good or the characters likable. I found only one or two of the characters kind of likable, with some verging on having unbearable personalities. I wish I had killed one of the characters because my god was Taylor unbearable the ENTIRE game. (The choices you make with her dialog also do not mean ♥♥♥♥ in the beginning. I made her say of yeah lets leave the bus in go into town and the next words out of her mouth are whining because she wants to stay at the bus. Why would you give me the dialog option to leave if the character is not going to leave no matter what?) Unfortunately my friend was controlling her most of the time.It was about halfway through the game that I was just frustrated nonstop with how annoying the writing for the characters was, as opposed to every now and then. Taylor was always frustrating though.The two player version set up is not great. There were whole parts of the story that I didn't get, and the things I saw my friend didn't get. This may have been by design, but it lead to both of us having very different opinions and conclusions on characters and plot. It also lead to periods where my friend was exploring a building while I was sitting in an area with nothing to do for a while, wandering into the fog just to get moved back to the area. Which was very frustrating since I thought I was doing something wrong. And it was also very boring.The continuity and transitions between dialog and scenes is not very good when some of your characters are dead. The point of this game is that your choices matter, but it really felt like only a handful mattered, and you'd think that a game where making choices is the whole point of it would have different and good transition writing, that would make the story transitions smooth based on your choices. Nope. There were a lot of weird cut offs and jump cuts, and dialog that just didn't make a lot of sense, or things that were only addressed once or not at all. When a character dies, the other characters don't seem to care much, which makes them feel even less human.There were many, many times when me and my friend would chose to have the character say nothing, because both options were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible. All of the characters are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. And the dialog options were just two different flavors of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Choices you make are sometimes punished by the game, despite you having no information to inform your decision which really got me. I think that's just part of the game design throughout the whole game series though. And when a character dies after you succeeded a bunch of QTE's but failed one despite mashing the button as fast as I could, the mood kind of gets ruined.I didn't find the game compelling, which is really sad because I do think the game could have been very fun with better writing. The story itself is interesting, its just the WRITING. The writing is so aggravating the whole time! It feels like a ♥♥♥♥ ton of people were involved in writing the game, so all passion was lost in the process.TLDR: the writing is bad [terrible] and I hate all the characters, which ruined the whole gaming experience. The writing of the characters really did make the whole game frustrating to me, I think I would have had a great time if they just felt human and didn't all have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dialog options all of the time. Frankly, I don't understand how people like the writing in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope is a captivating addition to "The Dark Pictures Anthology" by Supermassive Games, delivering a chilling and atmospheric experience that horror fans will appreciate. Set in the eerie, abandoned town of Little Hope, the game offers a compelling narrative filled with suspense, mystery, and plenty of heart-pounding moments. While the story is engaging, offering multiple branching paths, the game suffers from a frustrating flaw that may leave some players disappointed.The narrative of Little Hope is its strongest aspect, drawing players into a twisted tale that seamlessly weaves together elements of horror, folklore, and psychological drama. As players navigate the abandoned town and its surroundings, they are constantly on edge, unsure of what horrors await them next. The game's characters are well-written and expertly portrayed, adding depth to the overall experience.However, despite the game's many strengths, it is not without its flaws. The most notable issue is the reliance on quick-time events (QTEs) to progress through certain segments of the game. While QTEs can add tension and excitement, they can also be unforgiving. Failing a single QTE can result in the permanent loss of a character, which can be incredibly frustrating and may lead to a sense of unfairness. I found myself disappointed by this aspect, as it felt like an artificial way to inject difficulty into the game and penalized players for minor mistakes.Overall, despite this flaw, Little Hope is a decent horror game that offers an engaging story and plenty of thrills. Fans of the genre will find much to enjoy here, from its chilling atmosphere to its well-crafted narrative. Just be prepared for some frustrating moments due to the unforgiving nature of the QTEs. If you can look past this flaw, Little Hope is definitely worth experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying these a lot and don't mind getting a new one each year, they arn't perfect or for everyone but they are at least a unique experience in horror gaming. I think this might be the strongest narrative so far in the anthology and some solid if not heavy handed use of metaphor. Characters are a step up from Man of Medan for me personally I liked them all for different reasons, the performances are good but some inconsistencies for sure. I enjoy the little mini documentaries they put in these games as incentives helps put how much work that goes into these into perspective. Ran into some FPS issues again seems to be an issue early on with these games but Man of Medan ended up improved in that regard over time, had 1 hard crash as well as janky scene changes and awkward mocap I feel there is room for some polish here. Even tho I like these sort of games they still leave so much to be desired in terms of gameplay they are very poor in that aspect they leave so much on the table, disappointing. Again with the excessive use of cheap jump scares? Jumpers do have there place in Horror and if done well they are actually very scary(The Conjuring) but the devs just don't use them right now 3 games in a row still doing this wrong, it's annoying. Visually it's a stunning game especially the lighting, some real eye candy best looking graveyard haha. The creature design is also extremely impressive and a real highlight, disturbing stuff. I recommend playing both the Original path through the game along with the Curator's Cut, it adds some nice details and alternate dialogue, Overall it's another entertaining entry to an enjoyable series I just hope they arn't getting complacent. Recommend to anyone looking for a narrative driven interactable horror experience. 8.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad. Entertaining, but I didn't particularly like the twist ending. It kind of ruins the replay value. The Quarry was better, but in general the biggest problem with these Supermassive Games is that they don't lean into the strengths of it's storytelling full-on. It should play out every possible scenario to the end, including false endings and entirely different solutions like a David Cage game. If the game only has one ending you feel like nothing matters that you do as long as you survive to the end. You don't necessarily want to feel like your success in a QTE means you can't get the best ending, but just that your choices matter, to a ridiculous extent. I know it's not just as easy as more dialogue, but the mocap data is less data that video, so if you're selling this for 60, you better lean into why this form of storytelling is better than a movie. You don't have to give me a hollywood blockbuster, but you can give me the best horror game experience I can imagine because the game reacts and has an answer for anything I can think of in the give predicament.Love these games though, just wish they gave me more a reason to replay them like Life is Strange.

_childDocuments_.review: Like in most Dark Pictures Anthology games the only reason your characters will die in Little Hope is because you failed one Quick Time Event (QTE) out of a rapid chain of about 20 of them.Seemingly intelligent choices will never pay off, which also means that making really stupid choices will not matter either. An example from a different game from this publisher: You have a premonition about a character dying in a fire. So naturally, when it comes to picking up a lighter in the game, you decide not to pick it up. However, your NPC partner will instead pick it up for you. What was the point? There is none.It might be unreasonable to expect a developer to make every choice matter in such a game, but I always believed that it was the choices in those games that got people/characters killed, but after playing through this game twice and watching multiple videos about it on youtube, I have concluded that in every single one of these games, your choices do not matter at all. It doesn't matter which dialogue option you pick of if you choose door A or door B or what have you, in the end of the day the game will progress the same way about 95% of the time. And the only way to screw up and get a character killed is by failing a QTE.I just wanted to clarify this for everyone who is looking to buy this game and is thinking that by playing "smart" you can keep your characters alive. This is not true. You keep your characters alive by pressing the right buttons when they appear on screen. Trying to get immersed in the story and predict what is going to happen / what makes sense does not reward you with a more interesting ending or unique events/dialogue scenes in the game.However, I did enjoy the very last cinematic as that was something I did not expect to happen. PS: Filling your game to the brim with jumpscares does not make it "Psychologial Horror" or "Horror" in general. It just makes it annoying. My verdict: Buy it on sale, it is not worth 20€, especially since it will crash occasionally and the multiplayer is still full of issues as well, mainly connectivity issues and desync. And that after 2 years still, and their newest game has the same issues. Lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start off with some positives:I actually appreciate the idea of keeping characters alive by making them act more empathetic towards each other. That also makes sense in terms of story if you look at it from a condemning vs forgiving or self healing vs self destructive angle. That was new & fresh to me. Even though having them start off "bad" in order to make them better of course comes with the inherent problem that it's hard to care for them right away. At first I was like "Wth is everyone so antagonistical? What a bunch of a-holes! I don't wanna spend time with these people." But I came to enjoy the mechanics of "bearings" & "traits".I also like the variations in character designs. Having a middle aged woman for example, and that no one is traditionally pretty or beautiful. They look like normal people.The intro scenario reminded me of a Final Destination film, and had me giggling with glee. That was fun!The enemy designs are what I liked the most. Johns personal demon for example is amazing, and interestingly enough it is supposedly the only completely hand animated one, due to the complexity of its jerky movements and broken limbs bending in the wrong directions. Also liked the idea of everyone having their own assigned demon that focuses solely on them, and how the presence of them lingers everywhere, sort of relentlessly, unavoidable, just a matter of time. When you catch glimpses of them in the background, almost out of focus, that's when the game occasionally shines.Overall the game looks fantastic.Now onto the negatives:The acting and voice acting, apart from the Curator, isn't very good. I never once believed any of the characters sincerity, it all came across pretty flat & uneven. Combine this with the exaggerated motion capture acting, and it becomes even worse, with wildly flailing arms and what not. People don't move like that, we don't flap our arms like we're a bird taking flight when we're angry (apart from toddlers perhaps). And the eyes often don't seem to be looking in the right direction. And you occasionally have the usual weird grins on peoples faces, that could be either a smile, or a pain grimache, or the worlds biggest smelliest fart taking place. You can't make it out. Daniel in particular looks really goofy all the time.There are too many jump scares that aren't in any way earned. If you build up to them correctly and you earn them, then they work (look at James Wans horror films for good examples), but almost none of them work here. Maybe one or possibly two. But the fact is, it would be a better horror game without them. It's just not very scary.Premonitions were of no help whatsoever in my opinion. They are simply collectibles without use masquerading as something more.And here I'm going to make a massive dump. It overstays its welcome by hours. The story and script is weak, locations are boring, dialouge consists mainly of "Wth was that?" & "We gotta move on." And exploring doesn't feel natural since you'll accidentally walk into triggers that won't allow you to finish exploring areas, so to explore properly you have to know all triggers beforehand which sort of defeats the purpose of exploring to a degree.Some have complained that the QTEs are far too generous and that saving everyone is too easy. I did my best first run and still lost one to a QTE and another one I believe for not facing their demon on their own, something I didn't realise was a thing until I read up on it after the fact. A nice detail is that, apparently, the worse your character is the faster the QTEs and "Stay Calm!" segments get. And so maybe that's why most players got slower/more time for those sections of the game?I also seem to be in the minority in this, but I didn't really mind the ending that much, it's fine to me.There are some different modes and collectibles to find, I haven't tried the true co op, I only did the pass-the-controller-around for some pickups and the achievement associated with it. I do admit I like the idea of playing something like this with a beer-infused gang on a sofa, that's about how seriously you can take it. It's dumb fun, but unfortunately a far bit onto the boring end of the playable movie spectrum.All in all I can't recommend it. There are much better examples of these types of games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying I love this installment of the anthology. Between the witch trials, doppelganger demons and an ominous secluded ghost-town shrouded in fog, the aesthetics of this game hit the right spot. The characters in this installment can easily brush some as irritating, but if you play your cards right they can all have redemption arcs, be it major or minor changes of caricature, and I've come to love or appreciate them all - or they can remain unbearable if you so wish, but that's just as these games should allow you to do. The biggest talking point is the ending. The plot twist certainly would leave any average player more than disgruntled. It makes you feel like all your choices and efforts were pointless and you shouldn't have even bothered getting attached to these characters you tried your damnedest to save; which is the last take-away a game built around choice making should leave you feeling.My personal take on it is that the ending isn't by any means bad, just one that wasn't fitting for a video game setting.  However, as previously stated, for a game centered around choices, it shatters any interest in the story for many players. So, good plot used in the wrong setting; but a good plot nonetheless. . Another issue is that the game doesn't explain the ending all too well. .Lastly, some of the routes that lead to character deaths are extremely harsh and even unfair on the player. The arbitrary high-stakes choices and QTE related deaths are fine, but there are instances in which your character is on death's doorstep, and naturally you're panicking in an attempt to save them, and the dialogue you choose on a whim in which you beg for help from another character seals your fate to die almost 5 chapters later. I get what they were going for with the locked traits thing, and it is a very unique idea that fits the story perfectly, but its execution was particularly poor in Daniel and especially Taylor's cases.Even with all that said, if you look past these debatable flaws this game is a lovable and enjoyable experience for you to bunker down with on a dim night if prepared for some stressful decision making, reflex testing and lots scares - and believe me there's an absurd amount of jump-scares.. like seriously too many.

_childDocuments_.review: A good gaming experience, ruined by poor writing when it really mattered. That's how I'd sum up 'The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope'.Pros:- Looks amazing, the game gets given the AAA polish and looks great even on average graphics cards. Especially the motion capture and facial animation.- Plenty of decision making! Really felt like a step up compared to 'Until Dawn' (I haven't played Man of Medan) in terms of controlling the story in the moment.- Very atmospheric. Like I said previously, the game looks great and throughout, delivers an unsettling environment that at times can be really creepy.- Co-op! The multiplayer is surprisingly good! Albeit a little glitchy at times. Both players feel like they drive the story as a unit (at least most of the time) and when the group split up and you're simultaneously put in different areas of the map, really helps to drive the horror aspects of the game.Cons:-Short. 5.1 hours. That's how long it took me and a friend to finish the game looking out for collectibles as we went. We'd heard it was short going in so we spaced it out over the week but if I hadn't of known that I would have felt a little cheated. I will say though that it's an exciting 5.1 hours, especially when the game starts to pickup halfway through and starts snowballing.-Riddled with Jump scares. There are times when the game does a good job at creeping you out, building atmosphere etc. Unfortunately its over shadowed by endless jump scares. There are times when it feels like the writers had never heard of the phrase "everything in moderation".-Glitchy at times. I'll let them off a little because the game has just come out, but there were times when we were stuck in endless loading screens that required full game restarts to fix. We also had issues where one of us would bug out during a cutscene, unable to see what the other person was experiencing, although this didn't happen very often.- 'LOST' TV show tier ending. I won't spoil the ending obviously, but sufficed to say, it was incredibly disappointing. Which is a massive shame because throughout, me and my friend were honestly enjoying the themes and mystery that surrounded the story. The story up until the end is honestly, a joy to play and it's a real bummer because the game could have ended in so many other, more interesting ways that it had already laid the groundwork for.Overall the game is a fun Single Player/Co-op horror experience! Me and my friend had a great time playing this game. Unfortunately the ending really lets it down and leaves a bad taste in your mouth, so much so that I had to come and give it a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is spectacular, but I'll get to that later on in this review.First off, I have not had a horror game with such an evocative set of characters before. You will find that in this game, no character is written poorly, they are all five unique personalities thrown into a set of circumstances that they do not, and can not, understand. Without spoiling anything, you are four college students and a professor on their way to a field trip related to your field in Creative Writing. Your bus crashes and from then on you are plagued with the need to locate your bus-driver, while also being stranded, given the totaled bus.The game has almost everything, monster-design, good voice-acting, amazing looks and beautiful animation, triumphant showdowns, intuitive and impressive writing, as well as an extremely-talented cast of voice actors, for the most part. (Some lines are hit or miss, but the lines that are meant to hit home, do exactly that.)Let's get to some categories, Story, Characters, Scare-Factor, Design, and Ending, to be exact.Story (6/10): This game doesn't do the most original things as far as story-telling is concerned, sure, it pulls from a lot of other media and historical events to make it's point, but I never felt bored, or like anything they did was cliche or particularly unforgivable. I found myself leaning in when characters spoke and listened to what they had to say, which is a rarity for adventure games in the modern era. I would make decisions that benefited the story, and what would keep everyone alive, and as someone who enjoys feeling tricked by a narrative, personally, having 3 people die on my first playthrough near the end of the game was a real slap to the face. I tend to enjoy that in choice-based games, being able to brainstorm critically on what I could've done differently to save those characters. I consider it an above-average story.Characters: Let's get onto the characters. Each character starts with a trait that could be considered their good trait, and bad traits. Your job, if you choose to hunt for achievements, is to raise these traits to the max with your choices, which isn't the hardest thing to do. Read your choices, use common sense, and pick the one that goes most hand-in-hand with the certain outcomes you want.There are five playable characters in Little Hope, and each one you may max out either their positive, or negative traits, they are as follows, (at least as far as achievements are concerned.) Along with a short, spoiler-free synopsis of their character.Andrew - The Unifier (6/10)Positive: CompassionateNegative: DetachedAndrew's a self-insert, for lack of a better term. He's definitely the blankest slate that you have to work with out of the entire cast, this is achieved from a writing point of view by making him an amnesiac from the bus-crash, given his obvious head wound post-accident. Regardless, he still manages to become his own character from the choices you make, there are still personality traits, or pieces of them that you may begin to put together like a puzzle, and that is my best way to describe Andrew, as a puzzle that you get to put together yourself. One of the better self-insert characters I've seen in a video game, at least in recent memory.John - The Professor (8/10)Positive: RationalNegative: OverbearingJohn is a man trying to do everything right in his position. You can relate to his desperation to be a decent leader and to look after his own. He isn't very agreeable in the beginning of the game, having quite a bit of a "My way or the highway" attitude after the bus-crash. If you are capable of putting yourself in his shoes, it makes it very easy to relate to the "I'm doing the best I can, given the circumstances."-attitude, but as with any character in the game, your job is to make them more likable by the end, and John is not hard to make likable, given your last few scenes outside with him. No spoilers, but he gets much better, as do all of the characters that you play as, moving on!Angela - The Mature Student (9/10)Positive: UnderstandingNegative: AbrasiveNow, if you're like me, and you saw the promotional material, you confused Angela for John's wife as well. They are not married. Angela is merely a 48-year-old woman going back to college after not being there for quite some time, enrolling in John's creative-writing class. It slipped my mind completely that old people can go to college, too. Regardless, Angela wound up being my favorite character, and you learn just about everything you need to know from her first line in the game, which I won't spoil. Nevertheless, Angela can grow from a bitter old shrew into an understanding woman who knows the most about her environment and learns to cool her attitude a bit. Her story is... understandable, ironically. You learn to commiserate with her plight, and can understand why she was written the way she was when you listen to her speak. All in all, a very well-written character. Not to mention, Ellen David's performance as Angela was very impressive. The voice matches the character perfectly, in my eyes. I definitely felt the worst watching Angela die in my second playthrough. She was the only one to survive my first go-around.Taylor- The Hothead (6/10)Positive: HeadstrongNegative: SensitiveTaylor reads to me as a confident, proud person, but deep down hides a lot of insecurities. You can definitely draw comparisons to her and Jessica from "Until Dawn", another Supermassive title, where proud bravado secretly yields itself to troubled insecurities. Taylor isn't hard to like, either, though she can seem loud and obnoxious at times, you commiserate with her plight to understand that which is happening around and to our main 5, and getting frustrated with herself when she simply cannot figure it out, as the world around you can defy rational logic. Taylor is stubborn, and to pop her achievement of "Headstrong Heroine", which is maxing out her Headstrong trait, you may have to make her appear more-so, but I never felt negatively toward her as a character.Daniel - The Backbone (4/10)Positive Trait: AmiableNegative Trait: SensitiveThere isn't a lot to say about Daniel when it comes to character, so I'll keep this brief. There isn't the most here, but he is kind, and a little goofy. A character that remains lighthearted through most of the game, if you can keep him that way. It's very hard to say a lot of good things about a character whose biggest characteristic is that they're Amiable. Kindness isn't much for a primary personality-trait, though he hammers his redeeming traits home quite well.Scare-Factor (5/10) - It is right down the middle for me on this. There is some atmospheric horror, and some beautiful cinematography to this game. Tight corridors and fixed camera-angles give you a sense of claustrophobia when playing, though most of the actual payoff in scares are jumpscare-related, if you're squeamish, some of the monsters are terrifying. And yes, I did say "monsters". Play the game to see what I mean. I do not feel negatively about the scares in this game, as some of them actually got me, though it pains me to admit.Design (10/10) - The best thing this game has going for it are it's looks. It's absolutely gorgeous with it's rendering of characters, shadows, light, and special care to realistic motion-capture. Though this isn't anything new for Supermassive, it will still always be a mainstay to a good Supermassive game, to be able to catch every gross twitching facial muscle on a human being's expression. Incredible!Ending (6/10) - The ending leaves some to be desired, as the game breaks the Cardinal Rule of what makes a good horror game. Your choices have impact, whether you know it or not. I would think about any ending you get from an abstract point of view. You might like it more.Overall Score: (8/10) Good game! For only $30, it's well-worth it if you've got it lying around!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope offers an intriguing horror experience that combines a gripping storyline with supernatural elements. The game immerses you in a fog-covered town haunted by eerie visions from the 17th-century witch trials, creating a chilling atmosphere filled with suspense. While the story is compelling, especially for fans of the Dark Pictures Anthology, it can feel repetitive, with a predictable cycle of jump scares and exploration.The choices you make in the game impact the fate of the characters, but some players found the consequences of those choices inconsistent or underwhelming. The game’s visuals and ambiance are impressive, particularly when played on a high-quality screen and with a good sound system. However, issues like bugs, awkward character writing, and some control frustrations can detract from the experience. The acting and dialogue choices for some characters, such as Taylor, were mentioned as weak points, with several players feeling disconnected from the characters due to poor writing.Despite its flaws, Little Hope shines in its atmosphere and mystery. If you’re into choose-your-own-adventure games with a horror twist, you’ll likely enjoy it, though you might be left wanting more in terms of depth and smoother execution.

_childDocuments_.review: A few positives: the voice acting is great, the atmosphere is pretty good and there aren't too many cheap jump scares. The graphics also look great.However, the bad:  The QTE's f*cking suck.  They're a combination of LMB/RMB and a heartbeat sensor.  There's an aim mechanic that is so bad.  You need to be aiming at the 'right' spot in order to land a hit.  So, even if the head is closer than the body, if you don't click the right part, you fail the QTE.  The aim is also atrocious.  Some instances you can't even drag your cross hair in time no matter how fast you drag the mouse.  The story is all over the place and the ending is literally .  The clues you pickup are mostly useless lore.  The whole witch trial horror and the doppelgangers are explained in the ending and it is so underwhelming.  The dialogue is mostly 'huh? what's going on?' what's happening?' and the character relationship meters do absolutely nothing for the narrative. By the end, the whole game just feels like a giant nothing burger.  I just don't think good graphics and voice acting are enough to make a game worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: If you go in with the right expectations, Little Hope and its kin (games like Man of Medan, and Until Dawn on PS4) offer up very enjoyable and quite thrilling experiences that warrant more than one playthrough each. This particular go around I played the game solo, but having experienced Man of Medan in multiplayer mode, I can't wait to do the same for this one, as it transforms the experience substantially.With games like this where the story essentially  the gameplay, it is impossible to discuss it in any detail without heading into spoilery territory. With that in mind I'll stick to the general characteristics. The atmosphere of Little Hope is sufficiently tense and spooky, and never once while playing did I feel at ease or comfortable. Jumpscares abound, of course, but they never feel cheap. The story presents questions and discussions of innocence, guilt and forgiveness, and the struggle against personal demons is an ever present motif throughout.If you enjoy modern horror, and the style of gameplay that can only be described as the Telltale formula (albeit with more impactful choices) then Little Hope, as well as Supermassive's other games warrant a purchase and a playthrough. Little Hope, like Man of Medan before it, leaves me excited for the next entry in the anthology.

_childDocuments_.review: After a great "Until Dawn" and a disastrous "Man of Medan", I thought to give Supermassive another chance...and I didn't regret it! "Little Hope" is way better than the first installment of the Anthology-Series. The characters aren't as plain and way more likable than the previous set. The atmosphere is a mix between Silent Hill, traditional American ghost town and a good old witchcraft plot. Even though some aspects are really predictable, the final twist at the end of the story managed to blow me away. It was unexpected, emotional and melancholic in some way. So, all in all, after hating the Medan-stuff with its many stupid, often unlogical mistakes and flat chars, I definitely recommend "Little Hope" and hope the best for "House of Ashes"!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like scary games that focus on story rather than kill-all-the-monsters gameplay I bet you would enjoy Little Hope. I loved it, and if this type of game appeals to you I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.I was a bit disappointed by Man of Medan, the previous game in the Dark Pictures series. If you are in the same boat (ha!) I would say not to worry; I liked Little Hope as much as or better than I liked Until Dawn.If you don't like these kinds of games at all (story-focused, with light gameplay and contextual quick time events), however, then I doubt you would like Little Hope. Although executed very well it doesn't change the core game mechanics of the previous games at all. I don't think I personally wouldn't classify it as a "walking simulator", but you will spend your time walking, looking for clues, choosing dialog options, watching cutscenes, and doing quick time events during said cutscenes. If what I just described sounds kind of boring to you but the subject matter is appealing then there's still a chance that you might like Little Hope; even if you might complain that it's too much like an interactive movie it's still a pretty interesting movie and there's enough to do that it might keep your interest. If, on the other hand, you  that you never like games like I described then you should probably give this one a pass.[Update after reading some other reviews]: I played with an Xbox controller and by myself. I can imagine that it might be more frustrating with a keyboard/mouse, and I can't speak for how the multiplayer works. For what it's worth I didn't encounter any bugs in my playthrough. [/end]I don't want to spoil the story at all (my opinion is that it's best to go in completely blind), but I can at least give some tonal comparisons to help you decide. It felt a little bit like the VVitch movie (which didn't surprise me), and also quite a bit like Silent Hill 2 (which I hadn't expected, but was a welcome surprise). If either of those appeal to you I would recommend Little Hope even more.I was really interested in the story the whole way through and wanted to figure out what was going on. I also liked all the characters (except one ;), even though they all had flaws. I also found the game more scary and tense than I had expected; your reaction may vary depending on what you find scary and I would never describe this as the scariest game I had ever played, but it definitely got  heart beating fast in places. Finally, I thought that the pacing of how the story unfolded might be the best I've ever experienced in a branching "choices matter" storyline (where the combinatorial possibilities can sometimes make stories feel disjointed and patched together); there were a lot of things the story set up that had satisfying payoffs through all of the twists and turns, and there was a gradual crescendo of tension right up until the end.I'm resisting my natural tendency to give more analysis so that I don't risk accidentally spoiling anything, but not only have I found myself still thinking about the game's story and themes after the ending but I even immediately started a new game the day after finishing just to see things again with new understanding.If any of this sounds like something you would enjoy then I would highly recommend playing Little Hope!

_childDocuments_.review: While I thought the way the game did a fairly good job at creating an eerie setting and the story line had some interesting stuff going on when it linked itself to the past, overall it wasn't great. A lot of the time when I see people criticise the dark pictures anthology they immediately get responses saying 'well you can't expect it to be as good as Until Dawn. the whole point is that they're lower budget games', but a game being lower budget isn't an excuse for it being bad. Plenty of low budget games are good because they are still well executed.It doesn't excuse the poor choice system where decisions that have no real meaning behind them in the moment lead to a character death, or the crappy (in my opinion, ik some people like it) ending, or the weird writing of the characters dynamics with each other where they seem to stir conflict for no reason even if you pick friendly dialogue. One thing I will give it is that while I find the ending to be cliche and to detract from the main struggle of the story in keeping everyone alive, the story does actually consistently support the build to the twist, so the thought into the writing there was good. But damn I hate the ending. Just wasn't it imo. However, the characters feel pretty one-dimensional, although the voice acting is done well. I also enjoyed the curator as a narrator. Parts of the story seemed to get interesting and pulled me in, just for it to lull again. Also, why does a 5-6 hour game take up 42GB of space? RE2R takes up a little over half of that and is a bigger game and about twice as long.A lot of people like this game, and I see why they do, especially if you're a fan of the ending. However I just found the game to be a bit lackluster, especially when there's so many solidly good horror games out there that are worth playing instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Little Hope is the second game in the Anthology. Just like Man Of Medan, it is a story-driven horror game, where you decide how it ends. After a car accident, four students and their professor end up in a town named Little Hope. That's enough to know since more than that would contain spoilers. You can play alone, with a friend online (both have to own the game), or with up to five friends in couch-coop. Playing alone lets you play all five characters in different scenes. Playing online gives you the possibility to play a few scenes you don't experience when playing alone, but you also miss a few you would've experienced otherwise.All five characters build up a relationship with one another. Characters you don't control act based on their relationship to the character you control. Relationships will also give or take options in conversations or actions. You can change relationships through your actions, as well as the story changes based on that. Gameplay-wise it's no different from Man Of Medan. You walk around, do quick-time events, and that one little mini-game where you control your heartbeat.Again, you can find a lot of letters and pictures to gain background information about the world. Most of the time, they are interesting and add a lot of value to the game. Improvements: - walking still feels like driving a truck, but it's a bit less clunky than before- you still get stuck in small areas sometimes and the camera still changes when going into a room, which changes the directions of the left stick but it's a lot less annoying now- graphic, especially light effects are way better- teeth look more natural- facial expressions Negative:- turning directions with your character is very sluggish- akward seconds when your friend chooses what to say, as well as when the game calculates what the other characters say sometimes- character's actions still are illogical sometimesAs everyone who loves these games knows, the most important part is the story and Little Hope can shine here. It has it's longueurs after the first high but after some time one intense scene followers the other. All in all, it's less predictable and has way fewer logic errors than MoM's. What makes the story really good, is everything surrounding and supporting it. The characters again are stereotypes, but not in a bad way this time, and the (voice) acting is good. The sound effects and music are very atmospheric. Some scenes live off that.Little Hope strictly follows the same structure Man Of Medan did but does everything better. Many negative aspects of the previous game got improved which is huge for an AA game. It's around five hours long with different endings and creates the perfect B-Movie experience you would want for Halloween!

_childDocuments_.review: While I did enjoy my first run of the game, I cannot personally recommend that a person buy it if the biggest draw for you is to replay it. The replay-ability and seeing things from different points of view were a huge draw to the first game in this series and it was a fun ride. Unfortunately, the ending for this game did not make me feel as though it mattered whether I replayed it or not. I did enjoy the story elements, and did feel for the characters, but the end of the game made it difficult for me to care about replaying because I had already achieved one of the good ends and the finality of it all was so concrete. I felt as though there was nothing really left to learn about the characters or the setting. That said, if that is not the kind of thing that would bother you, then feel free to check it out. Especially when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game i tried from the anthology and it definetly left me with Little Hope for the other games in the seriesI expected at least a fun schlocky horror experience, but, honestly i should have just watched any 80's slasher or splatter film, because frankly, i would get more enjoyment out of 90 - 120 minute movie than sitting through this 4.5 hour bore. Story revolves around students on a bus trip crashing and ending up in town shrouded in fog called Little Hope. The main character is being played by Will Poulter and he, along with the rest of the cast, does decent job, which is one of few positives. However the characters they portray are unfortunately kind of annoying. Aside the Rod Sterling - esque presenter, everyone was either bland or unlikeable.Another flaw is that, despite the game being short, it still feels weirdly padded. You could cut it down to a 2 hour horror movie/game and not miss a thing. It's very repetetive. It's almost always scooby doo routine (i.e. running from undead ghouls) followed up by short exploration section, where the goal is to find something that triggers a flashback, which shows Town's witch hunting past. That actually made me stay till the end, because it was interesting enough to keep me playing and i wanted to see what the game will do with it. So what i got for being patient? Middle finger to the face with the ending that gives Mass Effect 3 ending run for it's money. It makes the most interesting part of the game pointless. They did foreshadow it, but it still feels like they had 2 writers in studio, the first wanting cursed town witch hunting extravaganza and the other psychological horror about processing grief and couldn't decide, so they just mashed it into one.I didn't talk about the gameplay, because there is not much to talk about. It's an interactive movie with QTE's and shoehorned in exploration sequences so it could be barely called an adventure game. And that would be fine, but these games should compensate the lack of gameplay by focusing on story, which has a few bright spots, but it's not enough to save it from being dull, uninteresting and having an ending that erases anything good that plot had to offer. To sumarize, it would be cheaper and better to just buy a horror movie to watch on a friday night.

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed and highly recommend Man of Medan, This game seemed to fall short in comparison. Gameplay :The repetitive but predictable jump scares and slightly confusing emotion system detracted a bit in my opinion, and the way the game dealt with your choices led too many situations to be predictable. Also picking one character in 2 player then the other person getting control of that character seems counterproductive. Story : I don't hold any particular affinity to the subject matter in the town of little hope but I enjoyed the story and the eventual result. Technical : Big issues here, the game had several game breaking issues: crashes, disconnects from coop. inability to load a save file forced us to restart the game TWICE then make sure we managed to complete it in one sitting. The last straw was the default controls changed from mouse and keyboard to point and click... not sure why they did this because there's multiple environments where point and click is really hard to maneuver with some of the camera angles and several times I missed out on exploring rooms due to time constraints after getting stuck walking back and forth trying to enter specific rooms. Why not just change it you ask? You CAN'T. Changing the control scheme breaks the game. You can't select options and quick time events break. Also you can't change back and when you quit to fix the issue and live with the bad controls... the game refuses to load with an infinite load screen and you have to start the entire game again. Due to the above technical issues I cannot recommend this game at all especially if you want to play multiplayer or the control system sounds annoying to you. If these issues get patched out I would change my review to recommend, however I still think I'd suggest you play Man of Medan over this one if you have to choose.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, the game is broken.  When I read reviews of people saying they couldn't proceed, well, that seemed to be a glitch only affecting certain people under certain circumstances.   But, man, my friend and I had the glitch several times tonight.  We replayed earlier points and made different choices.  One time it glitched earlier than it did in our initial play though.The glitch expresses itself with a "Connection Issues" (it may have been "Problems") over and over where you can do nothing until a "Connection Lost with Host Player."  The host player (my friend in this case) gets a load screen that is happens until the "connection" is lost.  The game ends at that point and you have to re-invite your friend.  And it happens at the exact same point every time until you try a previous save.Looking up the issue, it happens to different players at different points in the game.  So there's no clear path to getting past the bug.  We made different choices and made it further, and then it happened again.  I didn't look up what percentage it was.   We were near enough to the endgame to say, well, at this point let's watch a game play video to see how this ends.   (And how differently it could end.)Which I haven't done yet.  I'm frustrated enough in this night of game play with my co-op friend to write a negative review.  Maybe this is why they delayed co-op oi The Quarry.  To get it right?  The next game (House of Ashes) played flawlessly for us, as did Man of Medan.  We're fans.  So this sucked for fans of the series.  I won't buy the 4th one unless it gets glitch-free reviews.  Ugh.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like what these developers have done with Until Dawn, and to a lesser extent Man of Medan, but this is easily their worst offering I’ve played. I didn’t hate playing it, but ultimately I’d probably give it 6/10 (for reference I’d give Until Dawn 9-10/10). It’s definitely not a bad game, and I enjoyed playing it, but I don’t think it reaches the level of recommending others to play it unless there’s a good deal or you’re desperate to play something like this.Pros:- Spooky atmosphere- Good acting- AAA production quality and graphics - I personally really like this style of game that’s more choice focused than action focused, but that might be a con to someCons:- Unsatisfying story (can’t say more without spoiling it, but I would be very surprised if that wasn’t the consensus with this one)- Boring characters that I didn’t care to keep alive- Immersion-breaking stuff like the narrator guy and the premonitions that constantly remind you you’re playing a video game. Maybe for some this is a pro though.- Some choices lead to your characters making dumb decisions that you wouldn’t expect based on your choice- In my playthrough at least one character died for what I would consider no reason. Apparently there are some stats that go up or down with certain choices and this particular character didn’t have the winning combination because I wasn’t nice enough or something. I’m fine with my choices affecting that if there’s a strong or obvious connection, but in this case the connection was very loose and based on unrelated stuff.- Some of the dialogue is kinda cliché. Not a dealbreaker for me, but there were maybe 30 of these pointless stupid lines.If none of the cons listed are dealbreakers for you, you’ll probably like the game enough. Just know what you’re getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly a thumbs down even on a sale.  No spoilers.Firstly having to use a number of work around's just to get the thing working leaves a very bad taste in the mouth.  That aside this is a big step down from the previous title anyway.Technically it's marginally better than Medan and runs smoothly maxed out but this is due to using the Silent Hill trick of covering everything in thick fog reducing the resources needed.Unfortunately this reeks of being rushed through and could have done with being delayed for at least another Six Months and has all the feeling of an outsourced project.  The acting is very poor compared to Medan and comes across as people just reading lines with no investment in them.  There is no connection with any of the characters and the interpersonal relationships are distinctly synthetic as opposed to the stellar performances in Medan.  Even the legendary Pip Torrens is curiously bland and unconvincing in this like he's just doing it for a paycheck.A handful of the monster cut-scenes are well done and nicely creepy but that's about it.  The sound is inconsistent and will often have you reaching for the volume control.What kills it though (as is often spoken about so it's not a spoiler) is that nothing you do makes any differences no matter what choice is made either in conversation or action.   Failing a QTE can result in a character being bumped off but even so there is still only One ending.  I'm on my Third run through and making different choices with the same outcomes so it's pointless.The final nail in the coffin regarding value for money is that there isn't a Curator's Cut either so when you're done then you're done.I would only recommend this on a very deep sale for a One and Done experience unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first series of the game, and this game was just a complete disappointment. Not only do the controls suck (You can only use the point and click method, if you try switching it to keyboard and mouse your mouse will be stuck in the corner whenever you have to make any decisions. The first game allowed keyboard + mouse no issue so I don't really understand why they decided to switch to the point and click method only.)Not only that but the game really isn't all that scary. They reuse the same jump scare over and over and over again, to the point where you know it's just leading you into a flashback. Honestly compared to the jump scares from the first game....this seems very sloppy. Not to mention the many plot holes in the story and how characters still die despite passing every single timed check that they have you do.Also there's a glitch (one among many in the game) where if you're in the middle of reading something and a cut scene comes on (whether due to the game itself or the person you're playing with progressing faster than you) what you were reading previously will be stuck on half of your screen until you either come across something else to read or restart the game completely. The game seemed like it was rushed and wasn't thought out nearly as well as the first game. And seeing how these are also the creators of Until Dawn, it's a double letdown as I enjoyed both of those games and was expecting a lot more.The only thing about it that I did like was the surprise ending and who they chose as the narrator (who's in the first game too so not really a big plus.) Otherwise I would not recommend the game. I do not plan on playing the game over to change results as I have in their other games because it's honestly not worth my time. If they would add a variety of jump scares and fix the controls to where I can use my keyboard and mouse, as well as even make the game longer (it took less than 4hrs for my boyfriend and I to complete the game) then maybe I'd be happier with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Hope is an excellent experience, one that has clearly learned a lot of lessons from Man of Medan. Don't get me wrong, I love Man of Medan-- but when I recommend that game to friends it's with a caveat: play it in co-op. The unique and engaging co-op experience carries Man of Medan through a lot of things I wouldn't necessarily put up with in a single player game. That unique and engaging experience is still present (and highly recommended) in Little Hope, but this game doesn't need that crutch to stand on its own. It's a wonderfully written and well-executed horror game start to finish. The performance and graphics are much improved from its predecessor. The sound design in particular is en pointe and really adds to some of the death sequences. All in all, I fully recommend this game.
