_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've seen tackle this genre. The base building and raiding is a rewarding experience that I have enjoyed so far but this game does have some problems as it stands.- Raiding is fun but once you understand each trap and the majority of ways they can be combined or placed, it becomes a challenge of patience more than skill.- There seems to be a strong bias towards normal and dangerous player bases. My brutal base gets maybe 2 plays each time I activate it while my normal/dangerous base gets over 20 each time (champion outpost). This same champ outpost only got 2 plays over 12 hours when I upgraded it to brutal. This essentially makes it pointless to ever make a base at the highest difficulty.- The decorations and block types that you can place allow for nice customization but it never really looks anything more than a bunch of blocks.- Progression exists but feels rather shallow and pointless. You level up your chimera and administrators but it never gives you anything other than more resources to spend. I have never seen the admins get new things to sell and I have never gotten anything from leveling the chimera. You are just grinding to unlock what exists at the start and then you are done.- The replay system is really cool as it lets you watch other players raid your bases. It's a bit buggy and sometimes lags causing the players to jump around but overall works well. As you become more confident in your bases layout this system becomes less interesting as watching players do the same thing over and over gets pointless.- The world and lore are interesting but are not a major part of the game. For some reason all of the interesting lore stuff is hidden in the settings menu of all places.Overall I think the game needs a good amount of work to create more value in terms of progression and base creation. I still enjoy it and would recommend this to anyone who enjoys creating and raiding player made bases.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: The definition of a neutral review. As it stands I don't think it's super worth it, but assuming the game doesn't die within a year, content additions will likely make it substantially better.While most negatove reviews complain about "impossible" levels, I've yet to run into one. The worst I've seen was one where essentially all traps were in the first 2 rooms, with primarily flamethrowers and eye sentinels. There's not enough ammo to tale out the sentinels, and not enough rool to maneuver to pick your bolts up again, but it only took me a few tries to realize you can just take out 2 key targets and just, grapple to the exit as fast as possible. A lot of harder levels are like that, and with some upgrades you get more offensive and defensive options for raiding, so it becomes even easier.I'm sure people have found ways to make actually impossible levels; it's inevitable, really. But I haven't seen one, it'll likely get patched quickly, and there's no penalty for quitting a map.The actual problems the game has is a lack of content and an agonizing grind. 2 suits, 2 crossbows with one being flesh only so it doesn't break traps or armor which makes it useless, and 2 melees, which aren't particularly different enough imo. As for bases; 4 enemy types and like 8-9 traps. There just isn't much to work with since there's nothing that can be used to create emergent gameplay in the way mario maker does with things like shells hitting on off blocks or anit-jump mechanisms etc. Even worse is that you likely wont want to make a base till you unlock way more stuff, but the grind is kind of atrocious. Badically everything gives you parts and synthite. 2-3 tombs per map, enemies and traps drop it, it's the reward for completing a level, etc. etc. Cells though, you ONLY get from a select few things, but EVERY SINGLE PURCHASE needs them. Unlock a trap, guard, weapon, suit, or utility item? Cells. Upgrade said items? Sells. Thd only thing that doesn't cost cells are utility refills, buying a new map, and boosts, which are frankly useless for quite a long time because by default they only last 9 minutes, with maybe 2 minutes added on per level. 20 minutes for at best a 30% increase in resources (which most of them only affect things that give synthite/parts) for a ton of resources is laughable. You can maybe do 2 missions in that time. Thing is, if the grind wasn't that arduous, you'd be done in no time, and legitimately good, fun levels are rare. Most levels just suck, even if they aren't raider pov rimworld killboxes or recreations of the worst boomer shooter arenas ever conceived. I've enjoyed some but it's maybe ~30% because there just isn't enough to work with yet.I'll keep playing for now, but this is a game that could be forgotten about within 3 months, or one that grows just enough to get the updates it needs like Dead by Daylight did. Guess we'll see.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Before the review, let's start off with this: -There is NO SUCH THING as impossible levels. You guys need experiment with your loadouts! Most levels you can literally just run past with grapple/shield spamming. ESPECIALLY DEATHBOXES. Also don't forget grenades.-Death boxes can be a little bit tedious, but certainly not an issue. As previously stated, every single level is possible with the right planning and equipment. Sure, more imaginative levels are highlights, but you also have to remember that these are random people making the levels.-Biggest and definitely the worst issue is, most people are always looking for the next unlock and skin.. And sad to say, it took me about 10-12 hours of grappling through brutal levels to unlock everything. And i mean EVERYTHING.With that said: The game is great fun! The level creation tools are great and feel intuitive. You can express yourself relatively well, from an artistic perspective, with decals etc. I've seen and made actually themed levels. One of my favorites was a giant mansion with radiation decals around it. Upon exploring deeper, you discover a room with machinery decals with blood all over them, signifying an important change. After said room, you'll notice the mansion has turned "upside down",  with all the following buildings being flipped. Levels like this stand out to me, because of how they've managed to use the limited resources to tell a story. Kind of like NPU with Master Lego builders. (Nice Piece Use)Coolest part is that this level was clearly designed first and foremost as an art piece, but it still had a kill rate of 15. No killboxes btw.Traps are great and have great combination potential. Enemy path making is one of my favorite features. Though the enemies definitely need a buff on their AI. Also pro tip for builders: DO NOT USE LAVA BLOCKS AS WALLS. THEY CAN BE USED AS BACKDOORS! You can pass through TWO lava blocks without dying with the grapple. Not to even mention how many you can go through with Arc Barrier. (Unless you make them solid, but resources are limited. Use walls behind the lava blocks instead.)Last note on building: I personally wouldn't mind having every single level's resources increased by 50%, though this would obviously promote even more killboxes which people whine about. So, actually clearing other people's levels then? FANTASTIC. Absolutely fantastic. You have options for many playstyles, which can always be changed through your loadout at the start of the level. (My personal favorite combo being the Volt Lancer & Arc barrier. I love blasting through deathboxes without shooting ONCE.) Shoutouts to Falconic Plasmabow for being a great offense tool in enemy heavy levels! The melee weapons i never found too useful though, but that's just my playstyle.Movement feels great, though grapple spam can be pretty tough for controller players. Which, sad to say, is absolutely essential! Most of the movement you make should be done by grappling and double jumping mid-air. The drop-off and projectile speed of the weapons feels perfectly balanced, not giving you too much range in larger open areas. In a nutshell: The level building is great. Definitely sucks you in when you get an inspiration for a theme. No need for level clearing before posting because literally all levels can be beaten, if you are TRULY familiar with the levels and tools you are given. Still, the issue of a lack of progression remains. Kids these days want their battlepasses and skins.. Sad but very profitable.Absolutely fantastic game. Give it a shot. At the price and memory cost, it's a STEAL.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start out by saying I feel like I got my money worth out of this game but I only reluctantly recommend it. I started at release and it was a buggy mess that crashed constantly. I love this genre so I stuck with it and the experience has been mixed. BHVR have since issued patches to fix the stability issues and the 10-15 minute crashes have been greatly reduced, but right before my review I had a hard crash that rebooted my PC so there's still a lot of work to be done. The game is in mostly working condition though but it's still one of the most unstable games I have played in years.The controls are smooth, the atmosphere is great, the concept is fun.Raiding is hit and miss. It can feel like a chore because there isn't a requirement for Maker's to clear their own base before activating it (a feature the community and reviewers have passionately asked for) leading to an out-pour of tedious bases that are easy to make and only 'technically' beatable. Raiding can also feel adrenaline pumping and exciting! It all depends on the base you are raiding. Base building feels smooth and easily accessible. Having a replay feature to watch raider attempts is incredibly satisfying. Bases do expire though, and become socially accessible after 10 ranks so don't get attached to your creations.All the upgrades are lackluster, giving you a .1 reduction to reload speed or .1 reduction to swing speed and they take a lot of grinding to get. The traps are basic but they get the job done. Everything feel very generic and nothing feel rewarding to unlock or activate.Overall, the game feels unpolished but the core game play is fun. If BHVR manages to utilize all the feedback they have been getting there is a lot of potential for MYM.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: The Game has fun and flexible core game mechanics and a give you good back and forth between Raiding an Outpost and Building you own one, if you like both!In the beginning the gameplay loop is exciting and interesting but after 100h in, I see that there are some grinds that need to balanced. Also, the game has definitely some problems with nearly unbeatable levels and player who trying to abuse the game mechanics to the extreme (like exploiting trap to kill harvester).Imho I can’t see that you can play as Builder only in the end game, even with cheesy outpost or KillBoxes which I don’t like so I don’t build such kind of Maps i can't see it.The Ranking System is a little bit clunky and only a real ranking system if you reach the Mastered Rank. Before that it is only getting point when your successful raid an outpost or loosing point when you get to much deaths or leaving a frustrating Map.I got enough Playtime for the money I paid (35€) and it was fun, but I think the content is only good for around 80-100 hours.At the moment I can’t recommend the game and I think the following things need to be changed before I will come back:-	The earning of Synthetic needs to be increased for Builder so that you also can as Builder Only. At the moment you Raid more then you Build your own Outposts.  -	QoL Feature that you can collect resources and see the remaining time of an Outpost without entering an Outpost over and over again.-	The Ranking System need to be clear for everybody-	Quicker Response to Exploits -	Filter for the Size of a Map-	Skip a base

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game but know what you're getting into. Regarding the developer content itself, it looks good and the traps and their properties feel balanced. A little too balanced (will get into what I mean by that further on). It's grindy but at the same time it's enjoyable watching the replays of people dying to your favorite traps and learning new trap combos and building techniques so for me the grind isn't an issue, there's a lot to enjoy other than progression. It could use optimization regarding the sudden pop of resources when you hit a cache (always get a lag spike with the sudden instancing of the resources). This also happens with bomb ejections from the trap and even at times with the cannonbacks. It runs well enough but not spectacular on Nvidia 1060 on low. This probably isn't even an issue on higher end cards(?) Now onto the real issues.As I said with being "too balanced", it's hard to make clever levels that are fun for the raider while getting a K/D ratio above 2 or 3. It's really either make fun levels or kill boxes which many in this game find to be cancer. It's balanced enough where anyone with enough hours playing a fun level can get through it with 0 to 2 kills if they check all their corners and know the dirty little tricks for hiding and using traps. As you can read in the guides though, the people who want high K/D find no other choice but to make "kill boxes" (levels where their is one central room jam packed with traps instead of spreading them out). If you're running this on a console or a higher end PC that mine, kill boxes can be the ultimate reflex challenge. If you're running lower end, not-so-much. I used to be in the camp of kill boxes being cancer but now, no, I see why. Most traps are too slow and easily avoidable. Never thought I'd criticize a game for being too balanced.But on that note, I have 180+ hours in at the time of this review, Master rank and I am recently seeing a lot less kill boxes. Either I think that the sweatier players left the game or raiders got sick of the kill boxes so they abort and abandon (I've done this from time to time) so people stop making them. Or maybe it's just my matchmaking(?) There's no penalty to abandon other than elo/LD (I think) but if you don't care about that, it's no big deal. I just play to have fun and enjoy the replays.It's gratifying watching people either nod yes (look up/down a bunch) when looking at your level or dying to your favorite traps (especially when they shake their head in frustration) during the replays so this game offers something you don't see in other games (closest I can think of is Mario Maker). It's fun to build, fun to see other people's levels, fun to raid and performs decent for the most part. That's why I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought and played this game long after it was considered "dead" and must say that I had (and still have) a lot of fun with it. You're getting inspired by outposts you encounter to improve your own, buy new upgrades & traps and then watch other players walk right into your carefully engineered traps. Granted, you will probably not be playing this game for thousands of hours, but I invested 80+ h by now and will certainly add some to them. So I recommend you buy this game when it's cheap and try it.Some pros:- no game is the same bc bases are unique- great variety of traps, guards and upgrades- If you've never watched somebody dying to your traps, you haven't fully lived.- nice optics and atmosphere- rewarding loop of looting & buildingSome cons:- some bases are just dumb 'oops all plasma sentinel' rooms (thankfully you can skip outposts)- the late game offers too few challenges- weird prices for ingame purchases (most stuff costs 100 cells, some things randomly cost 1500)

_childDocuments_.review: Was really excited to try this game. It has an excellent idea to go off of. What couldn't be loved more than a super-mario maker style game, but in 3D, with various game progression mechanics to boot.Unfortunately, the execution of the game feels, lackluster, if not straight up terrible. And I'll explain why.- You don't have to beat your levels in order to put them out there. This, coupled with the reward mechanic for if your level kills someone, encourages players to create levels that are cheesy kill rooms, often feeling unfair and infuriating. Given that this is the PRIMARY reason to play this game, it feels unplayable in it's current state.- More often then not, you are forced to run through a long level, only to be met by a death room rife with traps that can hit you at literally every angle, accompanied by enemies. You can't even slowly clear these rooms, because they are often activated entirely at once, while you are standing in the middle of it, from grabbing the GenMat. Again, the people who build these levels, never have to beat the level, no, they don't even need to attempt to beat it if they do not want to, so they can sadistically place you in a situation like this, without ever experiencing it themselves.- Perhaps in a vacuum with some friends, where you build levels and see if you/your friends can beat each other's maps, you could have a lot of fun in this game, but unfortunately it is widely a troll map creator, and I can't recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Combine MGSV multiplayer with DOOM gameplay and a Tarkov-esque progression system and mash it all together into a writing cube of steel-ridden flesh and you have Meet Your Maker. Raid bases for resources to upgrade your gear while building your own bases that will passively earn you income as people get murdered inside of them. There are some issues with people making borderline unwinnable mazes, but patches will inevitably iron things out and there are plenty of enjoyable ones to tackle outside of that.Highly recommended, and made even better by being an asynchronous PvP experience where concurrent player numbers are less of an issue. There will always be thousands of mazes to raid and I'm very much looking forward to future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Too many levels are not fun.  There is no way to find the kinds of maps you personally enjoy.  There is no way to give feedback to builders in the form of criticism.  They can see that you abandoned the raid presumably due to frustration at least.  Maps end up being functionally removed from the pool which considering I have multiple times been randomly given the same maps (that I already didn't like) is silly.They really should develop an ELO system for levels.  Good levels get bumped up the algorithm and more players get to experience them.  Levels with a lot of abandons or rated poorly get moved down the algorithm and less players have to suffer.  The game does not encourage builders to make the best, most fun levels.  It encourages builders to put as little time as possible in a level for as many kills (fun or not) they can get.  I have no issue dying.  I have an issue with tedious deaths.Fixes:Don't give players the option of which outposts to raid.  15 outposts to choose from where you get no real information about them is pointless and means 14/15 outposts won't be raided as players just pick the first one that is automatically selected.  Instead just give players an outpost to raid which they can skip if it's bad.That or have a filter system to only play maps that fit your criteria.  I still think players shouldn't get to pick which outposts to raid as most are just going to raid whatever is the first one selected by the game.Creating an ELO system for outposts would then filter out the crap.

_childDocuments_.review: I am split between recommending this and not. I decided on a 'yes' but in reality I have stopped playing, The reason is that it is a fun game and at the start I saw myself playing it for a long time, however I soon had to close it and I never went back to it for one specific reason: Loading times. This game is very similar to the concept of Mario maker, in which you build a level and people try to complete it on the best time possible. The idea is that you will have to play and replay the level many times to get the hang of it. The more complex a level is, the higher number of attempts it will require before you finish it. This means that you could be playing-dying-retrying hundreds of times to beat a level. I was excited to do so on my first try, but what was my surprise when after dying the first time a loading screen came up and stayed for minutes. It seems ok to wait a few minutes for the level to load, but if you try 10 times it might be half an hour, if you try 100 times 2 minutes becomes over 2 hours of waiting, even one minute adds up. The developers need to optimize this as much as possible so that the retries are practically seamless, and then this game will live up to its full potential. Otherwise im out.

_childDocuments_.review: Making trap dungeons or adventuring trap dungeons.  Take your pick.  I like building the dungeons.  It gives me techno Minecraft vibs. _childDocuments_.review: Closed and open beta participant here, just getting back into the game for this free weekend (June 27th - July 3rd), and beyond disappointed to find my  suggestion to make this game  more enjoyable has been ignored after all this time. At present, many of you may find that some traps are overpowered, but this is not quite so--the true problem with this game is that  on what can be published aside from the basic rule that the harvester must have an unobstructed route to and from the objective within an outpost. What this means is that you can make wall-to-wall, floor-to-ceiling repeating ranged traps without any consequence (in fact, players are strictly rewarded for this)! The  change this game needs to immediately fix this issue of players constructing levels strictly designed to be impossible to survive is to force playtesting to be a requirement to publish, as I stated during the beta testing exit surveys. If you cannot extract from your own outpost successfully, you should be made to work on that outpost until you can. It is extremely disheartening to see this game's potential to be really fun utterly squandered by a severe lack of foresight on the part of the developers, as someone who has been excited for this game from the onset, and I hope to see that corrected in the near future. Should that happen, I'll update this review, but until then I can't recommend the game in good faith.

You can build bases or raid - both seem like a viable way to level up. _childDocuments_.review: It's fun yes, raiding is fun, building is good, but can be better. Killboxes are an issue and the fact that you don't have to confirm your levels. Easily solvable and for whoever thinks that hidden paths will be a problem, just add some way to eventually see the creators path or somehow hint it in the level. Easy fix. But the main issue is how they scaled down your credits accumulation since the beta. I now have too much blue and red resources and no credits. You barely get any from raiding, getting kills on your maps barely gets you some scraps. I have one finished base with almost 1k kills and no credits to show that. I have 3 maps waiting to prestiege but I have no points.BUT the biggest issue is when you spend your hard earned credits on a level, spend a lot of time carefully planning it and making it look good, but then you get one raider who dies 7 times, making you 5 points behind from prestieging the map, and it expires, making your 800 credits wasted. You wasted your time in every possible way and got nothing out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, at first i was like the other reviewers - thinking that creators should have to beat their levels like in super mario maker. After realising instead I just have to not be ♥♥♥♥, 99.9% of the brutal difficulty dungeons are done in under 5 mins. Run Shield + Sword, get the movespeed boost equipment, and just run through every base, deflect every arrow with your sword, and its easy. Use your shield to jump through the lava. The more scared you play the more you will lose. Run grenades as secondary equipment as the biggest enemy is the random pistons and flamethrowers running the range buff.This game really is for speedrunners AND for creative build designers. You can play it as a slow and cautious player, but you will be advancing a lot slower. This game is basically mighty quest for epic loot(which shut down like a decade ago), but instead is a FPS quake like speedrunning game. Very addictive speedrunning through peoples boring killboxes.

_childDocuments_.review: All written by :BubbaLovesYa-TTVHe's is what this game needs.TL;DR: This game has under 100 people playing it most of the time currently, let this game die and be a monument to BHVRs failures.As someone who was extremely hyped since this game was announced, it's with a heavy heart that I need to review this game negatively.There's so many artificial/poorly thought out limitations to this game. It's unbelievable how it could be blundered so badly. It's clear BHVR doesn't realize what makes a game like this good.They added ranks like this is some sort of competitive game (Silver/gold/platinum/etc) and limited lots of aspects to try to make it fit into their competitive mindset and it severely hurts the game and is really non-sensical. You can't create a balanced competitive experience out of player-generated content, you just cannot.There's just so many basic things that other maker-type games have that they tried to reinvent in this game that's akin to trying to reinvent the wheel for no reason.Most maker-type games make you verify your level by completing it. Here, you have to have a valid path for your HRV which is basically a slow-crawling supposedly helpful but basically an obstacle of a character that can push you around and block your path. The problem with this, aside for him being able to screw you when it comes to him pushing you into traps the fact you need a valid path for him is extremely limiting due to him having pretty much no movement capabilities aside for crawling over even surfaces, he can't jump up, he can't even drop down to a triangle slope from an adjacent flat block. He's so limiting in what you can do as a builder.As a raider you're given the ability to do all sorts of stuff, you have a grappling hook, you have invincibility frames, you have super-speed but builders are ultimately restricted to making hallways with rooms attached. No parkour, no outside courses, nothing. After a while every level feels the same and there's little expression for artistic freedom in this maker game.You're also limited to "buying" plots of land to make your fortress. These plots of land are randomly generated and have unmovable blocks and unmovable objectives. Again, taking agency and artistic ability away from the player. They won't even allow you to name your map. If Mario Maker, the most family-friendly maker game out there allows you to name your level, I don't know why this game about a mutant wasteland with extreme gore would feel the need to restrict you in naming your stuff, as if a report button for potentially offensive names couldn't solve the whole issue.But worst of all, and what I think restricts creativity the most is the fact that your bases have timers. They can only be active for a certain period of time. I believe it's 10 days, before they're "depleted" and are just deleted forever. I'm not joking. Not only that, but you need to grind resources as a raider to keep paying a fee to keep your base up every 24 hours.You can't search for bases you want to raid, that's not an option.There's a way in which your friend has to set it to a "social" raid base which rewards them nothing as far as kills go, and awards the raiders nothing as well. But again, you need to know your friends name because you can't name your levels and the names are all auto-generated. You can't search cool terms that you might think are fun like "parkour". No, you gotta know someone's name then go play the level "New Seattle".Outside of the building elements being limited, there's just so many pointless upgrades. Almost none of the gear upgrades are worth anything, and your starter gear is better than a lot of the gear you can buy. Levelling up your advisors let's you get a couple minutes more for a minor boost to resource collecting, or even boring stuff like giving you a vague idea of how many traps are in a base before you raid it. Mind you, even after unlocking the upgrades you still need to "Rent" the boost by paying resources to...get slightly more resources for an hour.There's some loose lore where people mention stuff but there's no story at all. Nothing ever happens no matter how many times you level up "fetus-mommy" Chimera, who literally just looks like an overgrown abomination in a jar. She never changes forms, no dialogue is ever unlocked, you get *nothing* as a reward essentially.The game is also just barebones. 3 months before release there was a beta, and people liked it but thought it must be an early beta test because there just wasn't many traps, guards or mods...everyone of course huffed copium saying they were going to add a bunch before release....no, they added nothing before release and have only added one mod for one trap since then.There's just also no way to provide player feedback to a base builder as ar aider. In Mario Maker you can make comments in the world that other people can see, heck, you can even draw pictures. In this you can reward a base builder with 2 of 4 vague accolades such as "Brutal" or "Ingenious" but nothing beyond that. There's also no "downvote" button if someone made a trolly base full of monsters in a giant box and nothing else.I could go on and on but I've already written so much. Just don't buy it. The playercount is below 100 people most of the time. Let this game be shutdown as a monument to BHVRs failures and a lesson to any other ego-maniac game directors.There's just...so many mind-numbingly bad decisions that I genuinely can't believe got past any sort of meeting discussing the game. I have no clue what's going on at BHVR behind closed doors but it clearly isn't good. It feels like the game was designed with a director who had an ego and felt the need to try to reinvent the wheel and bloat the game with a lot of unneeded or poorly thought out crap.I could go on and on but I've already written so much. Just don't buy it. The playercount is below 100 people most of the time. Let this game be shutdown as a monument to BHVRs failures and a lesson to any other ego-maniac game directors.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a well made asymmetric FPS and base builder that can dance the line between tense dungeon crawling and frantic movement shooter chaos. The game is split between building your own outposts and raiding outposts made by others. Both are appealing for different reasons and can be rewarding but it is not mandatory to do both if you find yourself gravitating towards one over the other.Raiding sees you entering another player's outpost and trying to steal a key resource (referred to in-game as GenMat) while avoiding all of the traps and guards the opposing player has set up to kill you. Everything in this game operates on a one-hit-kill basis so raiding is based predominantly on quick reactions and carefully taking stock of your surroundings. Something that should be said is that while I quite enjoy the raiding, Meet Your Maker is  the game for you if you get easily frustrated when having to repeat a challenging level over and over. Many of the outposts available to raid are brutally difficult and you will be reminded constantly that the builder's goal is the kill you as many times as possible. If you find that kind of challenge rewarding, you'll have a very satisfying experience with this game. There's an undeniable joy to finally finishing a difficult outpost that's had you tensely moving around every corner desperately on edge because you've made it further than you ever had before and don't want to lose your progress.The gameplay options available to you as a raider are simple yet efficient. You can only carry two weapons and a couple special items. These can range from guns to swords to grenades to shields. This is in addition to passive buffs you can apply to your character via either your suit abilities or single use enhancements. The game's received a few updates by this point and the options for equipment loadout now offer a decent variety of playstyles. The systems aren't overly complicated but that's because most outposts are designed to be completed in only a few minutes (provided that you don't die. In practice some of the harder outposts can taken considerably longer to finish as you go through multiple attempts)Something that is remarkably strong is the movement system for the raider. You can use a grappling hook (seemingly a necessity in all sci-fi FPS games now) and can move around an environment very fast, zipping around enemies and traps dodging dozens of projectiles as you try to clear a room. My one major criticism of the raiding experience is that while this type of movement is , it is only viable in specific circumstances. In most outposts, it's much more reliable to take it slow and only put yourself in least amount of danger at a time, which feels like a waste of the movement mechanics. Rushing in, especially when you don't know the trap layout will certainly get you killed. The other half of the game is building outposts for other players to raid. While the raiding can be equal parts tense and chaotic, the building is obviously much more relaxed and almost meditative. The layout of each outpost is based on a 3D grid of blocks, looking very much like a high-res version of minecraft but also including 45 degree slopes. You can place blocks or create entire walls/floors at a time. Traps and guards can also be easily dotted around your environment. Everything has to be placed manually though. There is no way to copy entire sections and paste them or rotate them elsewhere. This can make certain features like repeated decorations or trap layouts a bit tedious, but the tradeoff is that that building system is very . There's a very low learning curve to the technical side of building, although the more creative side both in terms of visuals as well as good trap placement and level design will take quite a bit of practice to become really proficient with.There are several limitations to the building system. The main one is that there needs to be a clear path from the entrance of the level to the GenMat for the raider to collect. This path needs to be navigable by the Harvester Unit (HRV) which cannot jump or climb walls. This means that the path must be continuous. This can feel a bit limiting, but it's vital for ensuring that the raider has some idea of where to go. If you could put the entrance to the GenMat down a hole or tucked away in a wall somewhere, the raiding experience would be defined more by boredom from trying to find out where he/she is supposed to go rather than by the challenge of contending with your traps. Another limitation is that the plot of land you can build on is auto-populated by immovable bedrock which shows up in random patterns for every outpost you create. Once the bedrock is generated it is impossible to remove it and you must build around it. I understand that this was done to force builders to use different layouts for each outpost they make, but sometimes the amount of bedrock generated can get frankly obnoxious.Something else I want to highlight though is the possibility for artistic expression. Having to build exclusively with cubes and 45 degree slopes may sound limiting, but Meet Your Maker provides a lot of cosmetic options for customizing your outpost. These are all entirely optional, but there's a lot of flexibility for some visually impressive maps as demonstrated by the community. Not every outpost you run into will have that kind of love put into it, but some of the ones that do really shine.Up until very recently, this was something the game really struggled with. It's improved significantly with recent updates, but it's still in my opinion the game's weakest part. This mostly stems from how there isn't much to spend the different types of currency on. You'll find that unless you are building and activating/reactivating outposts a , you'll quickly find yourself with a buildup of currency. Something you can spend the money on are boosts that result in you getting slightly more money for a short duration (only an hour or so depending on your level) which seems baffling and like the kind of thing that would be done in a free-2-play game... except Meet Your Maker isn't free-2-playRecently though, there's been a collection of cosmetics you can unlock by raiding a lot. These help provide some more incentive to raid more outposts (which in turn gives the builders more rewards, as they earn progress for kills and accolades given to their outposts) but it doesn't solve the aforementioned currency issue. The cosmetics themselves are pretty good. Given the game's very serious tone they can't go into wild territory for suit/weapon skins like a more cartoony game could, but it's still a welcome addition.Meet Your Maker is a game that tries and  succeeds at balancing both fast paced and tense first person combat with more relaxing and user friendly base building. The raiding can lend to frustration sometimes and the building takes a while to develop as a skill, but both offer a satisfying gameplay loop, even if the meta-game progression still needs to be ironed out a bit as the development progresses.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could only tell you only one thing about this game, I'd warn you: You'll probably enjoy this game the most if you really want to do both - build AND raid. You'll need knowledge from both to improve in both aspects.I really enjoy this game. I did play the Open Beta a bit during NextFest, and I got right back in after it released.The controls are good, the graphics are pretty good, it runs well even on my slightly aged machine, loading times aren't too bad. It can be a bit grindy, but in general, you play some, you get some stuff. The time to raid a base is usually pretty short... depending on size and how methodical or daring you are, between 30 seconds and 20 minutes. The balance between raider equipment and traps feels pretty good, the selection of both is limited, but they're recognizable and have enough differences to matter - mods offer some nice additional variety and make a ton of sense. Being able to destroy traps is great. Oh, and I love the Second Wave mod and that your default traps start with the mod unlocked.Weaknesses are mostly limited building block selections (only 2-3 per style category) and the fact that Forsaken Tombs aren't properly tutorialised. Also, while it fits the underlying story and theme, the visuals are a bit niche.The game can be played in 2-player-coop, but playing solo almost has an abstract cooperative quality to it: As a builder, you want to build a base you'd enjoy (and feel challenged while) playing. As a raider, you want to really test the defenses and explore the base built for you... and if you did enjoy a good challenge as a raider, give it an accolade or two!The fact that you don't lose anything when a raid is successful (and dying also doesn't cost you anything as a raider, unless you used consumables) plays nicely into this notion. (And I know some people view this differently, but I am very happy with this game having this perspective on it.)I am NOT an elite player. I can not claim that I have never seen a base I couldn't beat, but from what I've seen from raids on my bases, I do believe those who say they haven't. Most bases I've raided were somewhere along the lines of serviceable to good, some standard fare, some tricky ones, some easy, some challenging... but there have been more utterly brilliant, great bases than annoying / frustrating ones that felt unbeatable to me, or at least not worth the effort.I had THREE of the latter, among ALL bases I raided, and I did quit two of them.Most of the best bases I raided, that I enjoyed the most, did kill me at least once.I have built three bases myself, two small, one medium. One rated normal, two dangerous.All of them have been beaten by players with 0 deaths, both in a speedy fashion and while thoroughly destroying most or all traps for the loot.All of them had at least one instance with one player attempting it dying 4 or more times. Only one player has ever quit a raid on one of my bases (after one death, 1:08 minutes in, dying to the second trap they encountered, before even getting to the fully trapped areas).One of my bases killed a raider 5 times over, and they still made it through, taking 15 minutes to do so, but awarding the base two accolades, so they seemingly enjoyed the experience. (I get it, though: My favorite raid thus far was very similar - 3 deaths, 11 minutes, but two accolades well earned. I tip my hat to the builder.)Some people claim that the game only rewards kills (and this is why everyone builds death traps and kill boxes), but accolades count more than kills for prestige purposes (and that's  important for the longevity of a base). I'm also against the requirement to validate a base. This mechanic has proven pretty insufficient in comparable games, and I think the mechanisms in place in this game might be more useful long-term. That said, if I had to, I could validate my bases, pretty easily. I could probably make them a fair bit more deadly and still validate them without too much of a hassle. But the mechanisms currently in place (limited runtime for bases and accolades > kills for prestige points) really make me want to create bases that, yes, genuinely try to kill you, but also kinda want to be a thrilling experience for you that you will be able to beat in the end....just the kind of bases I'd like to play myself.See you in the wasteland, Custodian.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game, I've already recommended it to a few friends. It's fun solo, and it's an absolute delight in co-op.Will you like Meet your Maker? That depends on what you're looking for.This is not a good skinner box, numbers go up, kind of game. If you're looking for limitless unlocks to spend your in-game currencies on you won't find them here. There is a small set of unlocks and they all contribute to gameplay directly. If you're looking for a gameplay loop where you run through levels quickly to grind XP you will be disappointed. Grinding will get you nowhere, each level is only worth the fun you had playing through it.This game's main strength is the player generated content. You just don't run out of content and you never stop being surprised. There are absolutely memes that you see frequently, trap A always followed by trap B in a certain configuration, but frankly I really like that. I've been playing since the beta and it's been really enjoyable to see what ideas phase in and out. You'll also see the same archetypes fairly often, but again I really like that. After a little while you can look at a level and tell how you're expected to engage with it. Is this level a maze? Is it an outdoor fight? Is it a kill box? etc.That said, you will certainly come across levels you don't enjoy. Sometimes these levels are so hard they aren't fun, other times they're so easy they aren't fun. Sometimes they're just entirely uninteresting, or exhausting to play. Fortunately there is NO PENALTY for leaving a level you aren't enjoying. If you aren't having fun just bounce.That's a recurring theme too, the game never punishes you for playing it, not playing it, playing it poorly, w/e. If you don't like building you don't have to do it. If you don't like raiding you don't have to do that either. If you like raiding but you find it too hard you can choose to play easy levels exclusively. If you run into levels that just swarm you with bad guys, etc. you can bring defensive gear and just run passed the hard parts. It's really up to you how much you want to engage with the game.Frankly I'm impressed overall with the design decisions the developers made. There were a lot of things that struck me as odd at first, but the more I played the more I realized that they made the right call. For example, this game doesn't do the traditional "the builder must complete the level to prove its possible" thing. Instead there's an NPC (Harvey) that has to be able to path through the level. At first I was like "boo, I don't like that, it limits the things I can build." And it does, but as a result you can always find your way to the goal by asking "what could Harvey do?" This is streets ahead of having a time limit and praying that you can find the path the builder memorized to complete the level in time.There's also a mechanic in the game called "forsaken tombs." These provide a tiny bonus if you find them, but there is no requirement that Harvey has to be able to reach them. This allows builders to put in additional, unconstrained challenges that you are under no obligation to complete.If you decide to give this game a try and find you aren't having fun stop and ask yourself "What's the fun way to approach this?" If you can't come up with an answer leave the level and pick another one, or take a break to build something instead. Throwing yourself into a level you aren't enjoying again and again is an easy way to burn yourself out.Oh, one other thing. If you build and publish levels you can access a replay console that will show you people's runs through your levels in first person. Honestly, watching these replays is some of the most fun you can have in this game. The moment where someone clears the difficult part of your level just to get sniped by something you forgot you left in? The moment when someone runs through your level EXACTLY the way you wanted them to? The moment when someone does something really cool that you didn't expect? It's just the best.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great! The reviews claiming to be getting "7 unraidable bases in a row" or similar need to get good, don't let them discourage you. In 11 straight hours of raiding on the hardest difficulty, I had 1 single base that I couldn't get through and eventually just decided to give in and try a new raid. If something feels "unraidable", try a new approach. Try speed-grappling to a safe spot. Change up your loadout. Don't forget to use your equipment outside of the basic gun + sword.There are definitely difficult bases, but the claims of getting an "unraidable" base every-other raid are grossly exaggerated.The raiding is great, when a raid ends you can be in a new one in under 30 seconds, the base building is something you could get lost in for hours, and the little dopamine hits from seeing your base start to rake in the kills feels incredible.Mario Maker FPS has been done properly!
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, but I recommend against it. Here's why.This is super mario maker meets quake. And its actually a really, really good idea. The problem is that it has harmstrung level designers.Every level will boil down to a straight line to the finish. This is because the way the game ensures you don't make unbeatable levels is to make a requirement that the Harvester, a lil dude that walks in and out of your base, can reach the objective and get back out. He can't jump, he can only walk on flat surfaces and slopes.You can't build a maze, because people will just follow the Harvester.You can't build platforming challenges, because the Harvester will not be able to reach the goal if you do.So the only thing you can do is try to blindside people, overwhelm them with enemy spam, or make the most frustrating killbox designs.Even the options they give you for trickery, like the Holocube which are fake walls/floors are way too obvious. Especially since the Holocube will mostly be used as a fake wall/ceiling because it can never be in the harvester's path if its just a corridor.The game needs more content, or to loosen up on a builder's ability to make more interesting level designs.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: I am impressed with the game!Before I bought it I had some concern about the issues people mentioned. However, I decided to give it a try and the game turned out to be better than I could expect. I usually cannot play the same game over and over again many hours and days in a row, but this one is an exception.The implementation is great. The game loop is fantastic. But let me cover some negatives opinion I saw on youtube and some of the comments here.1) Your base is rarely visited by other raiders.Totally not true. My base has been published 2 days ago and it already has 33 raid attempts! Another one - 11 in less than one day.I assume that some players focus only on brutal bases and maybe raiders prefer dangerous, but also a lot of them are completely new and stick to normal. Try other difficulties, adjust your setup accordingly.2) There's no review system in the game.Wrong. After each play you can praise the outpost. I believe that it affects how often your base is being proposed to other raiders. Because after I received my first likes I got a lot of raiders coming after.3) You don't have to pass your own outpost before publishing it.That is true. I also saw it as a disadvantage a little bit. However, the game mechanics do not allow you to build an impossible setup because the harvester needs to have a clear path and you can follow it. Also the tools that your character has allow to neglect pretty much every trap.The problem might be with stupid killboxes setup, but I haven't encountered one I couldn't beat yet. And even if there're exploits existing in the game, you can always block that player profile and their bases will not show up anymore... ever... In fact it's a significant punishment and I believe the community tends to come up with something interesting and entertaining. As I said before, I beat them all, even the ones I assumed too difficult at first (one took me 30+ attempts though, but it was incredibly fun).If you reading this go and buy this game. It's awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: The core game loop of: Raid bases, get resources, get inspiration.Build outpostraid more, watch replays of attempts on your outpost, get inspired moremodify outpost, watch more and more people die in your outpost.Its just REALLY fun. I really enjoy the core raiding gameplay, and its even more fun in co-op. And I'm equally having a great time just watching replays from other raiders on my outposts.There is definitely a lack of content right now, in that the game could use more trap types, enemies and weapons/upgrades for when you go on raids. But there's still lots of room for creativity and ingenuity in the outpost design and trap placement to both keep raiding fresh and give you plenty of inspiration. I'm looking forward to future updates to change up the gameplay, but still logging in every chance I get to check on my replays and sneak in a cheeky raid.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm changing my review, again, and for once to positive...I had 2 major gripes, 1, there were zero restrictions on traps, and 2, there were so little restrictions on building, you could create mazes rather than labyrinths.There are now restrictions on having 80 trillion of a trap, AND they fixed the exploit where your guide would die, leaving you lost in any mazes. (Since this is not a maze game, it's a boobie trap survival simulator, indiana jones style.)I wish that meant I had ZERO complaints, but unfortunately despite the inability to make "mazes", players can still make "time wasters". Maps that are not hard, are not complicated, but are instead marathons that take 10-20 minutes to walk through. Aside from that, the game is fine, and works as intended.

_childDocuments_.review: I really recommend this game but be warned it's a niche genre and some people might buy it thinking it's a fast paced survival/builder fps and be disappointed, it might seem like that at first glance but it's not.  This game is a building-and-raiding game at its core, similar to the cancelled "The Mighty Quest for Epic Loot", "Mario Maker" or "Clash of Clans" but with a Doom twist. You build Outposts full of traps and guards while you can also raid other players’ creations, going in guns blazing will most likely get you killed since everything can one shot you but keep in mind that you can also one shot traps and enemies that are unarmored(except for head shots) and you have to take it slowly and watch your step at every corner because you'll die, a lot, before getting out with the "loot" but the good part is that you can respawn indefinitely with no repercussion. As for the base building, it's really simple and intuitive and it's addicting to fine-tune your outpost after watching replays of raids where you noticed the flaws.The game is not without its cons tho, you'll find generic kill boxes that aren't fun to raid, made by players with no incentive to create fun maps, just trying get as many kills as possible, haven't seen that many in over 10 hours but you'll see them, although you can always exit them and joins others.For now the game is a 8.5/10 for me, the cons being the generic kill box bases, some minor bugs(Replay function fast-forward/backward being broken) and a small variety of guards, weapons and suits but the pros outweigh them easily.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: After pumping 11 hours into the game, I can hinestly say it well worth the purchase. There are a few things I'd like to see changed/added. Right now the builders get bonuses from players being killed in their outpost but for nothing else, this highly incentivises people to build kill rooms that just overwhelm raiders if they dont speed through. As someone who was looking forward to building labyrinths, I'd love to see a change to also reward builders for other aspects, like how long it takes a raider to finish a raid. Kill rooms are fine, but after raiding for a whole evening and every single outpost being a kill room is excessive. Otherwise maybe there could be some sort of delay on trap activation if too many try to acrivate simultaneously. The most creative and interesting challenege I've had so far is one that challenege my resource management. It was a long stairwell that had bomb traps sprinkled throughout that if triggered you had to make a split second decision as they roll down the stairs but the guards at the top made it difficult to just run through. The state of the game right now doesnt push builders to be creative with their outposts which gets repetitive for raiding. As far as building goes I'd love to see some tweaks and additions, like instead of being forced into boxes, give us wall peices so we can run rooms right next to each other, or steeper slopes that raiders cant walk on but instead slide down, or pitfall traps that still count as path blocks for the harvestser but allows raiders to fall through. I also think the harvester should gave a delay or something that prevents it from immediately showing the path to the raiders, maybe a mod that makes it wait 5 or 10 minutes so that way mazes are more effective cause as of now all you need to do is follow the harvester and the maze is no issue. I'd love to see more suit custimization too, it'd be a great resource sink to help the longevity of the game and for player expression. There are also some mods that I think would help create more unique challenges, like a mod that allows you to place decals on traps to better hide them, or a mod that lets you change what type of block the hologram is so its harder to notice, or a mod that has traps that were broken repair themselves once the genmat is stolen, a mod that makes single use traps infinite but heavily raises their cost to compensate, mods that refund build space but makes infinite traps (like the incenerator) single use. More mods would add to the diversity of each trap and make outposts stand out from one another more. More traps and guards would be nice too, like a guard thats cloaked and tries to melee the raider from behind could be used to patrol mazes. Or a trap that doesnt kill the player but moves them to the other side of a wall. More raider weapon and equipment diversity would be a nice addition too.All in all I'm loving the game I just wish there was more. But as it stands for a $30 game I'm more than happy the outpost building scratches my creative it h and the raiding scratches my competitive itch. I'm looking forward to what content future updates will bring as I expect the low amount of content will be addressed and added to in future updates. 8/10 great game, looking forward to its future!

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re interested and want to try Meet Your Maker then the time is . There’s no guarantee this game will hold its audience, and this game is also very at risk of degeneracy taking root and causing everyone’s base designs to become soulless charnel houses. I’ve exclusively played solo Raider so far, and, right now, killbox bases are both infrequent and haven’t been perfected yet. The few I have encountered have been a bit fiddly in places, but the tools you have (particularly if you’ve levelled up your gear) give you ample options to take them down. Patience, using all the gadgets available, and learning from your mistakes will typically get you through tough bases. And, if you’re not in the mood for that, you can just abandon for an almost meaningless penalty and remove the map from your listings.Having said that, while killboxes are the current fearmongering buzzword for the playerbase, as someone that’s got a few Raider hours under their belt, I actually think Builders getting a bit more experienced would improve the challenge at the easier end of the base design spectrum a lot. Right now, we’re still at the stage where most bases are either a killbox or a series of corridors with traps hidden behind each corner. I’m not always in the mood for a killbox, but the other base type is overwhelmingly easy unless you deliberately hamstring yourself by attempting to blitz through it with minimal caution. I’m not sure what the midpoint between killboxes and the current easy corridor bases would look like, but I hope the community can evolve in that direction.I’ve read a lot of criticism, particularly from Builders, which I don’t have any opinion on as I’ve skipped all the building so far, but I do wonder what the Raider incentive to keep playing will be once I’ve maxed all the equipment. There’re cosmetic season rewards (which are essentially based on playtime), but other than that I don’t really know what will give me purpose after I’ve upgraded everything.Overall, I really like Meet Your Maker’s foundations, but the direction this game goes in, and how the community evolves, will make or break this game over the course of the next year or so. If you want to try it then now’s the only guarantee of a decent experience.P.S. - if you like Meet Your Maker's Raider gameplay, but want something less player-driven, then Phantom Abyss is very, very similar but with procedurally generated levels.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through it some more i changed my review to negative since there are some disgusting practices at play here.First of all: the DLC content (both the 15 dollar pack, though in a lesser degree, as well as the content you get for owning DBD on the same platform) is basically pay to win. Especially the DBD content has tiles that look exactly like the trap, something you can't achieve with the normal content in the game. The Scorched content has items that will make your game lag (the rotating clock thing, which some people spam to achieve exactly that). Cosmetic items should never have an inherent gameplay benefit, but yet they do. That alone made me change this review to a negative. besides that the game is inherently skewed towards Raiding. Raiding gets you way more ranked points, to the point that you have to have like 400 something kills in your base to gain rank points equal to one raid. On top of that your base is automatically rendered useless once you get it to prestige  10. It is no longer activatable. So your hard work as a builder creating a fun, engaging base is rendered null and void because... well i don't know why they did that it's just stupid. Another thing that is stupid as hell is that you don't gain any resources for receiving accolades, just from kills. So all that supports is the killboxes the community likes to cry about. Yes, the killboxes are beatable, yes they are annoying as hell to play through and simply uninspired and not fun, and yes you could just leave those raids. However something like 90% of the raids i undertake are those same rooms full of pistons, incinerators, sentinels and corrosive cubes. But why bother making something people enjoy raiding when the accolades don't provide the builder anything? Bad game design there. Not that you get many resources from the kills anyways, you barely make enough to sustain the uptime on your base. Adding to that is the fact that there's also no reason to buy smaller bases (they are separated into small, medium, large) all you want is a base with high capacity and most importantly 9000 genmat so you only have to pay the refresh once per day. And anything well thought out traps get nullified by raiders running the arc shield which is basically a big undo button on any mistake the raider makes. It barely has cooldown, has a base 1.5s of complete invulnerability (no it's not direction based, go figure) and goes up to 2 seconds if you "perfect block". And if that is not enough to save yourself from all the mistakes you should be getting punished for, use a flash barrier. At least you're only limited to 2 of those per raid. Yes, these things are necessary in the current environment because the devs decided to only incentivize builders making killboxes, but they are completely overpowered if those things were to be changed. ---TL;DR.Right now i'd definitely recommend waiting for a sale if you're interested (thought by that point the game might be dead, considering there's been no advertisement for it that i've seen and it's currently only at a pop of 1.5k players or so, so that doesn't bode well). Because the pay to win aspects, the poor incentives and the actual incredible grind it takes to get anywhere (especially if you want to focus on building) is just not good. ---Lastly, be careful of the community discord server. It's owned by elitist snobs that have played since beta, especially the owner of the discord server who will personally attack you for "leaving raids". No casuals allowed in there.

_childDocuments_.review: Changing my review to negative for now.The gameplay has devolved into two styles of outpost creation:1. Killboxes: Most outposts you will find have these rooms that are just stuffed full of traps and/or guards. One might argue that "iT iS tOtALly pOSsiBlE" to beat these outposts, but it really isn't worth it. If you have all the time in the world to waste on one outpost, then by all means, torture yourself with it. I'm not spending 30 minutes or more, dying over and over on some garbage smashed together by masochists who have no intention to make a fun experience.2. Mazes: The point of a fun maze has always been to find the way and get through to the end. What makes 99% of the mazes in this game unbearable is that once you get the genmat, you have to find your way back to where you started! Basically, doing a maze twice. Then even worse, you have to battle your way through second wave traps on the way out.It's also worth mentioning that I enjoyed the first 4 outposts I built, but when they deactivate for good one by one, it becomes tedious. I don't really want to make more outposts. I liked the ones I had and now they're done. Hardly anyone raids my latest outpost, so I just wonder what's the point? Put all the work into making a new outpost for very little reward. This whole system needs a huge rework!

_childDocuments_.review: I personally really like this game. It offers 2 types of gameplay -base building and raiding-. While I am more in favour of the raiding, there are still alot of problems in the current version.-Builders dont need to complete their own maps: You sometimes get nearly or fully impssible maps, where you just enter a single room with 30 traps stacked upon each other. No way to reach them with a sword, nor a way to recover your bolts.-Content: I know it's still a very early version, but having a weapon system and only 2 sword 2 ranged weapons and a shield as well as 2 armours is honestly not that much, especially as soon as you reach 10+ hours you basically already know your own preferred setup, as you dont really have that much choice anyways-Hardware: Your expandables are used, even if you die, which sometimes leads to having not enough of them and forces players to abandon missions and return later-Mission choice: As I have already written about it, there are some maps, that are generally impossible to do. If you abandon them and return to your base, they will just stay in your selection for ever, blocking that spot.I still recommend this game, especially if you are playing with friends (unfortunately I dont have any :,( ). _childDocuments_.review: I started this game around the patch notes where the dev's said they wouldn't force a map creator to finish their own map to confirm it was solvable by its creator. This reeks of some "feel good" everyone-gets-a-tropy BS. Ten hours in, that's what it is. I'd already run into two maps in the "Normal" (lowest) category that were so absurdly difficult to the point of having to give up on it. "Skill issue," you may say, fair enough. Playing today, I was kicked out of the game. A patch was being released. It turns out people having been designing maps with exploits making them harder or uncompletable. You know what would have helped resolve this before it became a wide-spread issue? Forcing players to complete their own maps before publishing them. This policy won't stop all trash-maps from getting published but it's a first step filter, a basic step that should be taken.The game dev wants to take a soft approach to policing a game that relies on players for playable content. This isn't a good decision. It's also a very bad sign for the future of the game.I've got good things to say about this game, but so long as they're taking this soft approach and not forcing players to complete their own maps first, I'll keep those positive comments gated. I have nothing good to say about it until then. SteamCharts indicates a high likelihood that this game will be the next Battleborn as long as it continues to be likewise mismanaged.

_childDocuments_.review: The negative reviews talking about how they don't like how maps "troll" the player clearly did not look at any of the promotional material for this game. The "trolling" is from map creators, a.k.a other players, designing their bases/maps to intentionally kill players. Which is the whole point of creating maps. I'm not sure where along the process of buying the game they skipped over that whole selling point, but it's silly to see negative reviews because they didn't know what they were getting in to. The game runs very well, at least for me. It has a very fun gameplay loop that rewards you for playing even if you die. Creating maps is also extremely fun because of the replay system in the game. You're able to watch replays of players trying your map, and you can see where either your base design can use improvement or where it's doing well (killing players). You have a ton of progression with 5 different areas to upgrade from Suits, Traps, Guards, Hardware and Weapons. The suits is really the only lackluster upgrade path imo, as there aren't many super interesting upgrades to invest into but I'm sure it just needs some tweaking. Also not really any customization options for suits either but maybe that'll come later in the game or down the line with an update. It's a pretty simple game, but also a very fun and addictive one. If you like games where you can create your own maps for other players to try or vice versa, I definitely recommend this especially for only $30.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Meet your Maker is a fun, base building pvpve shooter. You'll never fight another player (unless you and your co-op partner get trap madness) instead you raid player built bases for genetic material to improve the abomination of science you keep back at your sanctuary. That isn't the only abomination in this game, from the lack of things to buy and customize, from the level ups of you, your test tube messiah, and your npc level ups only giving you material and slight time increases to buff you'll begin to ask where is the content? Welcome to predatory "asym gaming" where the creators release a beta, put the full game behind several dlc walls (only one is out now but I'm confident in saying there will be many more), don't show any ingenuity or creativity in what goes in the game, and short change the players because to them the players have to make it fun. Concepts like locked doors that require keys, boss enemies, levers, leveling up npcs to unlock new items and gear, more than 5 "weapons" in the game, hell even more than 2 suits. What about teleporters? Having your bases last more than half a day irl? Nope, this dev team is not interested, just drop in some looney toons style traps and a handful of guards straight out of let it die and viola you get this game. I cannot recommend this game for the simple fact that it is not a full game. It is missing so much content and basic concepts that the devs are either highly predatory in how they plan on making it feel complete or they are so uncreative they truly believe this game is complete. Either way the future of the game as it is now does not look promising.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Game looked kinda neat, but then I seen it was made by BHVR, a publisher that only knows 2 things: Fostering hate in its community by intentionally leaving things broken in the interest of eventually fixing it with paid DLC later, essentially forcing the player to spend money on quality of life patches, and over-monetizing the holy hell out of everything in the game without ever doing anything to improve the game in any meaningful way.Even setting that aside, played like 3 maps and the game just doesn't really feel that good. Everything feels sluggish and bad, and while that's something that maybe improves after you get past the tutorial phase, I know how a BHVR game goes anyway, so I didn't see a point in investing any more time if I didn't like it right out of the gate.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: A speed runners heaven with beautifully player created mazes of traps and guards or a brutal prison layered with deceptive corridors and mind games. Being able to construct a base and watch people either run through it like a breeze or die many times trying is incredibly fun. You can upgrade traps, your suit and your weapons. You can also buy new weapons and suits to change your approach when raiding an outpost (quicker melee, quicker ranged, faster reload times etc.)Very fun game and worth the 39.99$.Hopefully they add more decorative content, traps/guards, suits and weapons, the possibilities are endless.PS: Buy different grenades and get the bubble shield from the vendor if you have trouble in tight brutal outposts. You can even get a grenade that increases your speed ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: 2 phases to this game; both are good, but could be great.1. Raiding. You pop into a random person's outpost/fort/deathtrap based on how "dangerous it is," and you have to fight/speedrun/navigate your way through the traps and enemies they placed in order to get the sweet sweet stem cells for the fetus overlord. -The thing here though is the variation between forts is kind of minimal because of the builder limitations. Improving the building system an a few ways will inherently make raiding more varied and fun.2. Building. You pop into a mostly vacant lot with only one goal in mind: Make raiders die. You can do it either through brutal trap quantities, clever placement, or even making a "loot room" that makes people self-delete on purpose so they can farm materials and XP from the self destructing traps. It's a good time.-Building is limited because you need the gatherer to get to the point and thats the requirement. So no parkour maps, no puzzle maps, nothing like that. Just halls and rooms with a handful of traps and enemies. Replacing the gatherer requirement with a "complete it yourself" option would immediately allow for more creativity.If you are like me and like being clever, you are able to watch replays of people surviving/dying in your outposts so you can see what does and doesnt work, making you a better insidious killer; H. H. Holmes style.
_childDocuments_.name: Meet Your Maker

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun. 16 hours on Open Beta and 9 right now since release. I have to agree that people who are complaining about kill boxes are suffering a skill issue (I also say this as a fun gimmick builder, no death rooms). Most death rooms you can just grapple forward through. Slow is death. Mazes though, those are wild. The game is really fun, and only gets better when more people contribute unique ideas.
