_childDocuments_.review: Only an hour into the game, but having fun with it so far. No unreal engine shader compilation stutter (thank you devs). It does have some Returnal vibes going on, but keep in mind that this does not have a AAA budget (which is fine honestly). It does not at all look cheap, the character models are high quality and the animations look good. The world is perhaps lackluster (at least in the first area) but nothing that has hurt the immersion. It does have a souls-like save system where you activate pillars to save progress and heal, which respawns enemies. But beyond that, I would consider it a 3rd person adventure game with shooting mechanics. You have to scan a lot of enemies and objects which helps you upgrade your gun, you start off with just an electrical attack and build out from there. I’m happy with the purchase and think it’s easily worth the sale price with 15% off. I will update if I run into anything that changes my opinion of this game. Performance is fine, I’m getting between 90-120fps at Ultra with a 3070 + 5800x3d @2954x1231(77% scale of my 3840x1600 Ultrawide).

_childDocuments_.review: O.G. POST = 03-27-2024:I've been playing SCARS Above from one of the recent Humble Bundles. It's a sci-fi & horror-based shooter/action-adventure/Souls-like hybrid of sorts.You're a scientist & engineer named Kate and she's trying to find out why she's on this weird alien planet, as her ship w/ many of hew crew-mates got taken down. Genre-wise, there's a more emphasis on the shooter/action-adventure stuff, as you do lots of shooting & some easy puzzle-solving, not say stat, skill and number-crunching. You will learn skills & craft stuff, as you go along - but don't expect to sink lots of points into that stuff as this ain't a RPG; this still feels and plays like a third-person shooter, more so than anything.For the Souls-like part: you do have these Big Obelisk-like things for Save points there & when you reach them (which are like Bonfires in a Dark Souls game), you heal & replenish everything and cure all diseases & issues (such as Toxicity from poison, Hypothermia from being too cold in freezing environments) - BUT it also respawns everything back (like a Souls-like does) for enemies & encounters, once you reach these Obeilisk-like things.You also have environments that you need to use to your advantage (i.e. you have an electric-gun, so shoot this at water but don't stand in water - you'll do more extra damage on certain enemies). A lot of enemies have weakness points - so you need to use the right weapon to defeat them much easier & exploit that.Game's running at 1080p maxed-out looks great & runs very well at max on my RTX 3060-based laptop, at often 50-60fps.I'm having a blast with it (SCARS Above) so far, some 7 hours in.ADDENDUM - 04-02-2024:After about 20 hours or so (some handful or so of the 26 hours, I was either away or asleep - so it's probably more like 20 hours or so that I played this game), SCARS Above is now finished & in the books as Complete. I know, most players seem to finish it in the 8-15 hour ballpark - but I was certainly taking my time and let's be real: when it comes to hard games, I'm not always great at games that also have Souls-like and/or Rogue-like elements.Overall, the game and its many levels & plot twists was very good. And there was even some awesome boss fights later on, which were tough - but eventually, I found my way through some of them and they certainly weren't easy. Some of them boss fights & mini-bosses felt like puzzles too, as you also had to figure out how to defeat them w/ the environment, situation, and weapons & items you've at you disposal too. The premise & story is always intriguing - but once the story reveals all of its hands & cards later on, after it slowly gets peeling back info like an onion, it certainly hits hard with some really good and bonkers type of awesome twists, turns & revelations.In the grand scheme of things, SCARS Above is an awesome shooter/action-adventure/Souls-like sort of hybrid & is an easy recommendation. Even more so, if you caught it recently in the recent Humble Bundle that it was in and/or can catch it in a sale.Awesome game.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting story in the beginning but the gameplay comes down to "shoot shiny spot on monster to progress". The beginning ape-fire-chest guys suck and really drag the whole thing down, and I'm FAIRLY sure the pattern of the game will continue that way if my experience with clunky games like this is anything to go by. Not a great gameplay loop or way to handle combat that CONSTANTLY happens. When I ran into my fifth rock-fire-gorilla in a 5 minute timespan I refunded the game. They are NOT fun to fight against and there are way too many. I also had to fight two near the end at the same time after the first boss and I was just like "jesus christ, man." I can't imagine what other gimmicky enemies are later in the game.Let's just say there's a reason the trailers are only the first hour of the game, I'M SURE.Combat: 2/10, gunplay feels okay but the constant swapping of elements in your gun with having to freeze enemies to even get a shot in is not great. Then you run out of freeze ammo and you're dead in the water. Elements don't swap fast enough because they're assigned to the DPAD, so by the time you swap, the enemies are unfrozen.The enemies you can just shoot and kill feel good to kill though, more of those and less elemental enemies please. Save that for the boss fights.Visuals: 8/10, beautiful alien world you're running around in, gear and equipment look great, the aliens look cool.Music/Sound: 8/10, gives a real feel of running around an alien planet, I'd liken it to Returnal's soundtrack/world-feel IMOGameplay: Movement is kind of clunky, much better with a controller. Shooting is okay, dodging is hit or miss it seems like sometimes. There are some "mini puzzles" but they're mostly solved with finding items and bringing them back to a place or shooting a wall with a certain element.Check out my Let's Play review of the game here (3 episodes):  (2 more episodes coming today)

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting Sci-Fi story and a girl scientist/astronaut protagonist keeps you engaged with the game and the world.It's mostly simple shooting and dodging around the enemies and a lot of exploring, with different elements (fire, electrical, ice) which is cool when making combos (shooting electrical into the water, freezing then melting...) :DThe bad side is the save system (checkpoints) which re-spawns all the enemies, and god forbid there is a cinematic somewhere inbetwean, you can't skip it - so prepare yourself to run through the same fields and bushes and watch the same cinematic over and over again, while you are dying from some boss repeatedly.I mean, games should be challenging, and losing to some boss is expected and it should be a bit frustrating until you win it - but respawning back at checkpoint (a couple of minutes back) and rewatching the same cinematic for the boss makes it really unpleasant experience if repeated. Maybe I am just not hard-core enough :(I would recommend the game nonetheless, exploring the alien worlds is always good fun -  7 / 10 .

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a Soulslite with an excellent sci-fi plot with a hint of body horror.As Kate Ward a scientist who is part of "SCARS" a team designated with making contact with aliens who have appeared above earth, you find yourself and the crew of your vessel lost on a strange planet. To make matters more intriguing as you navigate the hostile environment led by a strange alien hologram who appears to know who you are, every time you die... you are reborn moments later in a strange cycle of life and death.The basic gameplay of Scars Above is focused on exploration and combat, you must navigate the mostly linear alien world battling different enemies with your four different elemental weapons (which later unlock different fire modes) . The combat is simple, featuring a dodge roll, melee attacks and gun play. The basic premise of the combat involves exploiting each enemies set environmental weakness in order to kill it quickly. It's fast paced, and once you get the hang of some of the clunkier weapons very, very compelling. The exploration and story though for me are the games strongest points, you gain experience to unlock abilities not by killing but by finding "knowledge" - small purple tokens hidden through the map. It makes exploration very rewarding and you want to check every nook and cranny of the gorgeous alien world. The plot is also excellent and while it spells itself out early on it's a satisfying story with a great conclusion with a good cast of characters who are all well voice acted and realised.The game also has a horror aspect in that the plot revolves around mutations to DNA which leads to some pretty disturbing moments and body horror as the story progresses. Excellent stuff.Overall Scars Above is a fantastic shooter and while it's no where near as difficult as Dark Souls theres still reasonable challenge to be found in this great little "AA" title. The story and horror aspects only push it to new heights and it runs great and looks great on PC. Highly Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game to be played for the story, which was interesting enough to keep going to a point. But at some point the goal of being souls-like conflicts with the goal of telling a story. I get that it's supposed to be hard, and that's fine. But being set back very far (in terms of distance and having to repeat fights) when you die is a hassle, and at some point I decided it was more fun to delete the game than make another long run to the target.Also, the image for this game on the steam library page does an awful job of selling it: a woman sitting around with her eyes closed has nothing to do with the action in the game, which is performed by a woman running around with her eyes open. Seriously, it gives nothing of the flavor of the game, it just says, here's a female protagonist, in case that's your thing - but she looks kind of bored, so maybe you'll be bored, so maybe you should go play Tomb Raider again instead.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a AA-tier soft "souls-like" third person shooter with linear level structure and not much customisation options. Gameplay elements are okay and shooting has been done decently, although there's isn't much more to it than "Shoot ice monster with fire bullets, then fire monster with ice bullets". I found the setting and story to be generic and forgettable, but at least the game looks quite nice graphic-wise and having purchased it for £6 on sale, I can't complain too much about it.As of time of this review the game is a bit pricey for how short it is (you can complete it on 100% in ~5 hours), therefore I suggest waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with the concept of a "popcorn movie" - a movie where you turn off your brain for 2 hours and then forget all about as soon as the credits roll - then you understand what this game is.  It's a Popcorn Game.As a notably mediocre and forgettable game it manages to do everything competently while not offering anything that stands out or makes it unique.    The most interesting part might be the weapon you have which can fire 4 different elemental types (electric, fire, ice and acid) and the way you can combine two of them to create two additional combo effects - ice and electricity play off one another and so do acid and fire.    Most of the enemies have some ill-defined weakness or weak spot but they can be defeated with brute force as well.The various maps and levels of the game are mostly linear with a handful of obvious side paths which invariably lead to extra skill points or weapon upgrades.   The enemies all follow the same general rules.  If you enter an area with water deeper than your ankles, some snake men will jump out of the water to spit at you.  If you find yourself on a path no wider than two widths of your character, some spiders will jump out of the ground to crawl at you.   In between these recycled ambushes are bigger areas where you fight a half dozen varieties of minibosses, most of which become trivial once you find their weakness.The story is fine but is every bit as forgettable as the gameplay.   All in all it's fun way to kill 10 hours, at about the same price as watching 5 popcorn movies.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game overall. One hiccup at the beginning with a major patch that removed my save file, this wasn't anything major as I was able to find the old folder where the save was and cut/paste into the new to retrieve it. Other than that, I didn't run into any other bugs during my playthrough.The game itself I think won't win any awards but don't let that stop you from playing. The combat was fun, learning the monsters attack patterns and also what gun to use in what situation, being able to combo with elements was also great. Gadgets were fun and unique, you will probably rely on certain ones over others like I did. The story was decent, the graphics are very nice and yes while the artwork does resemble Returnal in a lot of ways I assure you the game is very different in playstyles. Overall I enjoyed myself even though it only took me roughly 7 hours to complete the game.I do look forward to see if they improve on this and continue in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Story and game-play were great. Guns were interesting and fun to use and the combos were quite satisfying to pull off.The game was not too hard even on commander difficulty however you need to be very efficient with your shots (and combos) to kill enemies fast before it becomes overwhelming. I'm guessing it is similar in lower difficulties just with more room for error.One small gripe I had with the upgrade system was that there were very few actively useful upgrades, namely the rapid reload and the better scan thingy (and of course the top 2 upgrades). All other upgrades were extremely minor and did not really feel like actual progress was made. Also it needs a system to dump excess upgrade points (can be minor like 1% dmg per point). I finished the game with 8 point after having unlocked everything.The graphics were very good but the facial animations were quite bad, however this can be easily excused by the fact that it is an appropriately priced AA game.All in all I highly recommend this game for the price-point of ~30€

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautifully relaxing to play. It was exactly what I was looking for on a weekend. I find the graphics appealing for my taste; the U4, which I believe is the one used in this game, looks really good.The weapons and attributes that you unlock during the whole campaign are so satisfying; they're not too complex but not too simple either. The cutscenes looked kind of odd; I believe they were pre-rendered and not in-game, so it felt a little bit funny and made me question why such a decision was made. It didn't stop me from enjoying it, of course; my eyes were hooked!The scenarios in this game are very interesting as well. I've seen many aesthetics similar on some sci-fi book covers that I usually read from the 80s'/90s'. Giving that feeling of a world unknown, exploring areas that look very odd to you, and making you not expect what is yet to come. Many times during the game, I spent a couple of minutes appreciating the effort made on these levels. Now to the story, which I found pretty interesting—the main theme of the game and its conclusion, along with everything else. I could see many other great works that were probably used as a base for inspiration (I might be wrong). Some enemies reminded me of Metro: Last Light, Venom, and Alien. The story itself reminded me of a couple of movies and books, too. So that was really good to see these similarities to other contents; I have already enjoyed them myself. Gameplay is fun and brings me back to some old third-person shooters from the PS3 or some recent ones. I really liked kicking some aliens with the new weapons and always finding a fun or different way of eliminating them. The abilities and the weapon upgrades make it possible for you to vary in your gameplay and combat techniques so the game doesn't get too repetitive for you. I really don't know the difficulty of the game; I played it on normal difficulty and only died once, but the game got pretty tough many times, making me almost die during these events, so it must vary from person to person. Bugs: There were only a few bugs for me; one of them was that I entered the wall for no reason and got stuck while being hit by the enemies. The second and third ones are related to achievements. I don't know if it's meant to be this way, but I got some achievements during the training sessions when you get new gadgets. That's all. It's a good game; if possible, get it on sale and have a good time. That's my quick review, without trying to spoil the game, but you'll only know if you'll truly feel the game when you play it! At least that's how I think.And good job to all the developers who worked on the game; I can clearly see some love integrated into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a game that doesn't reinvent the genre but it does what it does really well. The ambience, the action, the gameplay and the story are pretty good. I really liked the combat mechanics. Each weapon has their use and so are the tools. You can't just pick one gun and blast your way through the game. I liked that this game gives you different guns and tools that you'll have to use and switch regularly to make your way through the story. The game isn't too hard even though some fights are more challenging than others. All in all, it's a pretty solid game that surpasses even some AAA games out there.On the down side, I think the price is a bit high considering the length of the game. It only took me 10 hours to complete the game and get all the achievements.I still recommend it though but you might want to wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I agree with the general consensus on the pricing of Scars Above, all things considered, its still a solid game for what you get honestly, and I enjoyed every second I played of it. A rough 8 to 10 hour short, linear experience with some not half bad voice acting, smooth controls and really good optimisation. I can't say I ran into any glaring issues like bugs and the game didn't crash once.The story is probably what you might expect from a sci-fi game, or even something you'd see in a sci-fi horror movie where there's always some sort of body horror of some description. If you've watched a few then you kinda know what you're in for.As mentioned, although linear, the maps are generally quite interesting though stereotypical when it comes to the whole alien planet vibe, you could pretty much play science fiction bingo with the tropes you run into. Still, its designed nicely for what it is. The meat sections gave me dead space vibes for sure.I liked the elemental damage aspect, especially where you can combo for extra damage. Essentially every weapon has a use for maximum efficiency along side a rather decent selection of abilities that run on battery charges ranging from a shield that negates damage, to the ability to slow down time through a throw-able "chrono-bomb" that slow time in an area, or to temporarily stop time itself and move behind enemies to hit weak spots. I honestly love some of the design choices and wasn't once thinking "my god whats the point in this gun/ability" because everything had a well thought out use instead of just been filler garbage. There are also consumables that can be crafted using fiber found around the world or on defeated enemies that can help keep ammo topped up or recharge battery power to name a few uses.For some reason they decided to sneak in a pseudo "bonfire" mechanic like that of the souls series, and gave it some lore, but I reckon it could have been fine without it honestly. Too many games these days recycle these mechanics where it just isn't necessary .All in all an 8/10, dropping a number due to the price...again, for such a short indie experience shaving off £10 to £15 would make it much more acceptable. Its one of those situations where I want to recommend it, but only when its on sale, unless you got a whole bunch of expendable income and need something to kill time for a day or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game biomes. Good and engaging combat with enemy weak spots and different element types to use, that even act differently in different environments. Level designs are good but nothing over the top. Exploration is fun and well rewarded. Human character models, faces, and voice acting are rough but doable. The good gameplay makes up for it. So far I am liking the story and is keeping me intrigued.An indie action adventure shooter recommend for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short indie adventure game and is mechanically a third person  shooter. It's nothing special, everything you see in the game has been done before. The weapons use an elemental system that correspond with colored weak points on enemies. The levels are semi-linear with branching paths and collectibles strewn about. The premise is unknown aliens visit earth with bad intentions, you're the hero that deals with it.  I felt very meh about this game but it wasn't bad, this is soft thumbs up. bugs were minimal, all the game play systems work, the story exists and follows a clear narrative. If you're interested in adventure games, get this when it's on sale and keep your expectations low. It probably won't disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing this game i read the reviews that said this game was too hard, even on easy mode. After completing the game on normal mode, i cant say these things:Overall the game is really good, especially since this isnt my normal, go to type of game. Story is good, mechanics work well.XP SYSTEM NEEDS REWORK. . The reason for the complaints of this game being too hard is just because the character is under powered. I found levelling early game really slow but after the 2nd boss xp from knowledge cube began to increase and skill points dropped more frequent. Too frequent in fact. I managed to complete all skill with 7 skill points over at the end of the game. this game just gets easier as the game goes onIN GAME FEEDBACK FOR LOW HP NEEDS TO BE IMPROVED. I often found myself dying in boss fights because i didnt realise i was on low HP. many times i took a hit, stood doing damage, took another hit and died. with the amount of mechanics and abilities in Scar Above, the volume of the Low Health warning should be increased and potentially red border on the screen before death, as it is too easy to miss during an intense fight.overall 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above feels like an indie version of Remnant: From the Ashes. Combat feels good, enemy variety is decent and the levels are well designed, although quite linear. The game gives you a lot of interesting weapons, tools and gadgets to approach combat however you want. Combining your weapon elements with your time manipulation gear feels like a good power fantasy. With that said, it ends up making the player a bit too powerful. So if you want a challenge you should go for the harder difficulties. On normal the game is very easy. Each enemy is well designed with a very specific way to approach them well thought out, but the sheer power of all your tools allow you to simply power through all those mechanics.Definitely worth picking up at a discount, but don't expect anything revolutionary. Game is fun for the duration of its short campaign, which should take around 6 to 8h depending on how much you explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid 7/10 game with fun combat and good enough story. Unfortunately it's a short one and too often it limits you with invisible walls. However, it's definitely worth its price and I would love to see a bigger sequel that provides more freedom of exploration to the player. The groundwork is here and it definitely has a 9 or 10 potential. Scars Above definitely deserves more recognition and love especially for dabbling  into horror in a few sections which was really interesting to experience. For such a short game you also encounter a lot of different environments. To sum up, definitely worth it especially if you are a sci-fi/horror fan. Now please make a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed my playthrough of this game from opening cutscene to end credits. The gameplay is very smooth and fluid; The creatures telegraph their moves clearly through wide motions and distinct sounds; The gunplay works within the setting and the story flows quite well. It took me a while to realize it was playing a lot like a souls game with guns however the path to strength is not found through fighting but by exploring the areas. Although I couldn't put the game down without thinking about it for 2 minutes and picking it back up again I wouldn't call it perfect.The first area being the swamp and having to deal with poison from the outset made the beginning moments a slog and it didn't improve until after defeating 'The Alpha' boss (sub-boss?) and getting an upgrade from it. The 'scientific' elements of the game were well integrated to the upgrade system and it was a nice to see all the available upgrades from the start. I only have maybe one or two gripes for the game overall but I would still very much recommend this game to anyone else who, like me, sees this trailer and thinks, "wow this looks awesome!"

_childDocuments_.review: Good AA game, with some caveats. 7.5/10Good: GraphicsGunplay / Combat / GadgetsSound DesignMonster VarietyGreat boss fights with a good deal of challenge and tactics to take them outVoice Acting4 Elements to mix and match in attacks and using the environment to take down enemies and surviveProgression, finding new enemies almost all the way to the end of the game. Was surprising. Performance / FPSNo crashesDecent:Story: While the story was wrapped up, the most interesting plot point was left unresolved. Leveling / Perk System: Nice to have, but nothing special. You unlock better perks and bonuses as you play through the game.Bad: Woke - Every character is ugly as sin. Not "just a normal person" ugly, but intentionally making ugly women with weird faces and the cast of characters are all "strong, diverse and brave". Strange, considering the game devs are Eastern European.Major Bug - About halfway through the game, in certain levels you may encounter a bug that causes your movement inputs to not register. As in, you literally can't move or go anywhere. As you can imagine, this becomes very frustrating and I found no solutions online. TLDR: A good linear A to AA game. Third person shooter with great 4 element (fire / electric / freeze / toxic) battle system. Weapon upgrades, lots of good enemy variety and engaging boss battles. Would be a near perfect little AA adventure if not for a major bug (see above), ugly / woke characters, and a decent story that while being concluded, leaves the most interesting part of the story unresolved.Strong recommend when on sale. Not rushing, exploring and decently taking my time, full playthrough on medium difficulty took around 12 hours of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly great game!I love how weapons are used to interact with the world(they're just tools, after all :D ) and not only for fighting. How obtaining new weapons changes exploration and combat strategies through the game, Also, gadgets are actually useful and versatile, and not something you forget you have, like in most games. Enemy variety is also very good and persistent throughout the entire game(in 9 hours of gameplay I've seen more different enemy types, that require different strategies to defeat, than in most 40+ hours action adventures/rpgs). Very well written and acted characters(most of them at least, especially Kate), main character that actually acts like a scientist, simple, but well written story that can sometimes be creepy and terrifying, and sometimes heartwarming and hopeful. Great art direction and environment design, Great sound design and music, that appear to be very well above AA budget of the game. Only few things don't work in this game (and it is kinda baffling how bad they can get sometimes) - cinematics and facial animations (especially lipsync).  It's hard to believe that same team that pulled off rest of this game, goofed so hard on these. I guess they were low priority tasks, left for photo-finish of development. No matter how bad these can get, they don't take away from great experience that this game absolutely is, and I'd rather have engaging game with tight gameplay, great world and characters, then fancy cinematics.

Characters are highly detailed but bland and boring; the main character doesn't even sound interested in (or maybe even bored by) what's going on around her. _childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Except for the major performance drop in which a simple restart fixed, there's not much negative to say about the game. However, not too many positive things stand out either. It was fairly easy, even on the hardest difficulty. My low-mid end system could keep it at 60fps on Ultra settings most of the time, which was unexpected for a newer game. Story was...okay, gameplay was...okay.It's just an okay game. Got it as part of the "Humble Heroines bundle".
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: 6h from beginning to end. Good story, good performance. Some animation in cinematics are lacking, specially facial animations but overall good work. Graphics are good, but not ground breaking. Gameplay is good, making use of status effects is nice specially when they can be combined with environmental elements. I find that on easy difficulty the experience is more enjoyable but most consumables are pretty much never used as well as many of the gadgets and going to harder difficulties is in this case a way to ruin the story. It is a bit expensive for what it is yes, but I recommend it. Wait for a sale if you think you might enjoy it. It is a very linear game, just don't expect dark souls type of freedom even with the resurrection mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: If you like dark souls you'll like this. Even though the game 'CLAIMS' to have adjustable difficulty IT DOESN'T!!! Setting it to easy will result in you dieing just a tad slower than the medium or insane difficulty. Why bother putting this in the game? It doesn't make the game easier. I ended up asking for my money back because i couldn't get past the dang first boss so this game is no fun for someone like myself. Don't put different levels of difficulty in the game when they don't work.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is simple and there is no accumulation of resources. Consumables are made directly from a resource you only hold a little of and are constantly running out of and replenishing. Sizable amount of time is walking down hallways and holding E to interact. Dialogue is very stilted like it was AI written and never reviewed.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this is a nice game, like many other players, I did not manage to get past the first big boss and uninstalled the game after only 3 hours of play. This is very unfortunate, as I like the graphics and settings overall. Due to its insane difficulty in this regard, I cannot recommend this game for the casual players like me right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: clear, simple, relaxing, no stupid secondary mission, graphic is ok, runs well, story is good, weapon and ability are good not like other games where you have 154 abilities and 72 weapon that you will never use because you'll stick with the only 2 that you really need. if you have some free time play this game. like i said, it is relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 62 yo and really enjoyed the game. Was hard at the start with first few boss but I cruised thru it. My hardest areas were when you can get hypothermia and die while fighting due to freezing. Other than that I enjoyed it. I played on easiest setting an ach's were straight forward w/o guide. Wouldn't mind a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't very difficult, and the story and lore don't bring anything profound to the table. However it is a cute little niche gem if you're looking for an action crafting game like The Last of Us. You can ignore the souls-like tag on the game because, despite it being a dodge roll shooter, it's not a very difficult game by itself. You can expect to kill any of the bosses within one to two tries.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: A solid Sci-Fi story, interesting alien environments and decent third person shooter mechanics, utilizing elemental attacks. There are checkpoints, which you can activate and where you respawn if you die without losing your overall progress in puzzles, unlocked paths or the story, and you occassionally unlock shortcuts back to some of the checkpoints you visited. But the world is overall designed in a linear fashion. Some encounters are very difficult, some even require using the environment to beat them - but the game is forgiving enough to not hinder the enjoyment of the well crafted story and characters.Recommended for hardcore Sci-Fi fans, especially Trekkies! Mature Sci-Fi entertainment on an alien planet with alien technology. If you are fan of interesting Sci-Fi scenarios and good design for tools, ships, weapons and alien tech - this game is definately going to grab your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed the game, fantastic story, great variety of alien mobs, 4 elemental weapons and many gadgets to help in multiple playstyles, weapon upgrades on discovery throughout the game. Dying respawns at latest pillar but no loss of items. Pillars are nicely spaced throughout the game so you don't lose a lot of time if you do die. Good length of game too, Three difficulty levels. Well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: 0/10 the game ran fine ONCE.after that ive never been able to make it past the logos without it giving me a black screen- also, not supported on steam decki have no way of playing this past the 1st time i got it runninggot it working using this method+ looks nice- gameplay- everything respawns- you get nothing from killing things so just run past them- boss can stun lock you to death from full health
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. Kind of a breath of fresh air... sure it's lower budget but it's a solid game that you can tell they cared to deliver a solid product. While I can see the Returnal influence it kinda has it's own thing going and the two games really are nothing alike IMO. Can't wait to see how they evolve and hopefully enough success they can invest in better animation etc... but what's here is solid enough. Very fun and that's what matter most.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not hard, it is just frustrating. I have pushed forward until the second Construct boss fight because there were good parts (story and some of the gameplay). But this fight is just not fun. You know what needs to be done, but you have only 1 opportunity in every 10 minutes and you have to survive until that. And even if the boss is in the correct position, there are several mechanics that can prevent you to do what needed. Yeah thanks no, I value my time too much. This boss design is the worst I have seen in my 20+ years of gaming life.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Annoying save system that forces you to replay the same thing over and over again. Offscreen enemies hitting you without any indication of their presence. Your character is sluggish in movement and hit detection seems to have a massive delay. Your hit box is miles wide and you are getting hit by attacs that are nowhere near your character. Story seems to be interesting but the game play drags everything down. I don't know why developers insist on usig this "souls-like" mechanics. It doesn't work. It's boring and annoying to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be summarized as "It's not THAT bad"... Was it worth paying around $10 on sale? Kinda, it's six hours worth of gameplay that's not entirely horrible. TBH though, you could spend that time playing a better game for around the same price. Dead Space remastered or countless other games that are in a similar style to this one. The graphics are some five years behind, gameplay can be more of a jump scare and a pain than fun, and the story is from a C-class SiFi, I think the only redeeming factor is that it is cheap, but again, you can spend your time and money in many better ways than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games that actually created some curiosity and eagerness to figure out more about the story in me. While it certainly has some flaws like the stiff animations and sometimes comically bad mouth and face animations, it does not deter from the overall experience. The voice acting is very good, the graphics are nice and the gameplay interesting.Sometimes I felt like there were too many gadgets and guns and not enough game to actually try all of them, but that is somewhat of a good thing as nothing is streched too long or too thin. Another great thing for me was, that this is a mostly linear game, some side branches, but it feels refreshing to experience a story and discover on the side without open world fluff.I can wholeheartedly recommend this game, if you can accept that it has quite some flaws, but otherwise punches above its weight class!
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Its ok and that is all I can really say. The difficulty will swing wildly at times with fights. The graphics are meh, the combat is meh, story is meh I guess, everything is basically only ok. There are some basic features the game is missing that it really should have such as toggle aim and ability to cancel sprinting without just stopping or aiming. I would wait for a sale, I'd say this game should be more in the 20 dollar range, not 40.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Scars above is a beautiful sci-fi game, very similar to tomb raider. Sadly, it fails in many ways to replicate what makes the latter a great series. Exploration feels rather dull as you find yourself looking around corners for the only collectable in the game: purple cubes that gives you xp to unlock perks and the occasional upgrade for your weapon which are pretty much unlocked toward the end of the game.The combat experience is good, you're required to pay attention to your environment as well as what weapon to use with limited ammos. Ice breaking is absurdly op btw.The game is rather short, I'm someone who enjoy exploring a lot and waste a lot of time looking around every corner for collectibles and whatnot, yet the game lasted roughly 6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Fun gameplay with good pacing of receiving new tools and weapons.Game is not that long but it is ok if you buy it on sale.Interesting worldbuilding, simple story which is not necessarily a bad thing.Really like the voice acting, especially the protagonist.Just playing the game will net you 100% acheivment unlock.Cutscenes are quite horrible, some cutscenes look like they are low resolution.Dialogue animations of characters are really bad. You can obtain way more exp than you can spend on skills, i eneded up having 10+ skillpoints with nothing to use them on upon completing the game. Should have been able to spend it on increasing damage or something similar.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Played 1 hour. Game crashed and froze 5 times to the point where it forced me to restart the pc every single time. (Seems theres a bug that freezes up the game everytime you RUN into a solid object like a wall etc) and yes my pc meets the requirement, and I just came from Remnant2 and ER which runs smooth on high settings.Also it doesnt seem like the devs are really interested in fixing this issue, as i can see its the same standard answer to the MANY that has experienced this same "freezing" issue as me. Something like : "We are very sorry to read that you are obviously experiencing technical issues. Unfortunately there's not much we can do from here, but have you tried writing to our support? Maybe its your specs?"ive reported every single time the game froze, i hope it helps to solve this issue, and that the devs actually gets this fixed, cause the game seemed decent for the half hour of gameplay where it didnt freeze. But i surely cant recomend it in its current state
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the light souls-like aspect to it. I'm not good at souls-like games, but ones you can tweak on easier are definitely something I've come to enjoy. It was an enjoyable game with a good story, and a really good soundtrack that reminded me of Mass Effect 1 (and one particular part that gave me Stranger Things vibes). Overall, it was a good experience with interesting creatures and an easy combat style. I did get it on sale, but I would have been happy with the result if I paid full price. :) I do wish it was a little longer, but it did still hit a sweet spot with the game style and soundtrack, and I do like a good space game. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The story was intriguing, the character interesting, but the first boss fight, the Alpha, was impossible for me, even at "Rookie" level. I tried multiple times with multiple strategies, even went back and looked for some power up I had missed, but, nope. I never got it under 50% health before it killed me.Bear in mind, I'm no third-person shooter newbie. I've successfully finished games like the Horizon series and Greedfall on normal difficulty with no problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a pretty fun, much lighter souls experience. Unfortunately, it likes to crash while loading save files and at a few points of loading larger enemy groups . After a few runs with this issue happening repeatedly, I've hit a wall that no settings or reinstalls seem to make passable. I can see why most people haven't done the majority of storyline achievements, which is unfortunate because it is interesting. Not sure I'll pick this back up.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Overall - 8.5/10 Gameplay is decent for an indie game. In fact, I would add that it has potential to become an AAA series, if it had a wider budget, deeper story and longer gameplay. Would love to see a sequel on what happens next to the team. Some bugs, weird facial expressions but doesn't ruin the overall experience. Good work! Enjoyed this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be the most Mid game i have ever played so far.Not good, not bad. Everything about this is mid.The playtime, the soundtrack, the world... everything is just alright.well... 1 bad and 1 good thing is there.The good: Weapon mechanics and the interaction with the world is good.The bad: Holy ♥♥♥ hell the animations and ur character.I don't even know if i recommend or not. I would because in sale its ok but on the other hand its nothing special at all so don't waste your time.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a decent and intriguing sci-fi game. A hidden gem in my opinion and criminally underrated. An interesting story revolving around a crashed space crew on a mysterious alien planet. Hidden paths that lead to upgrades adding an element of exploration. Vast array of different hostile creatures and neat mini bosses in each chapter. Ending could have been a bit better but could lead on to a second title maybe? Mechanics where good although nothing special. However, the game had a good amount of difficulty and challenge to it. Felt very Remnant and Souls like in a way. The gadgets and skills where simple but effective. Also very easy to max out towards the end game. Although, after maxing out, points could have be allocated elsewhere instead of building up aimlessly.I did encounter two bugs during my play-through. One when near outer edges of the map and a water pool towards the end game. These bugs left me stuck and having to restart at the last pillar. However, I had nothing game breaking, progression loss or crashes, despite many people saying in recent reviews. Game played absolutely FINE apart from these minor areas. Nonetheless, the game is great. But it could still do with some optimisation and performance updates to iron out these issues and the clunky textures during main story scenes.I would still recommend Scars Above as for me it was a good experience, great story and something different to the usual sci-fi genre. I enjoyed the game immensely. But ONLY grab Scars Above when it's on sale. Current price is too steep for a game offering nothing to do after completion and with recent reviews it would be hard to say you would even get to experience this hidden gem. Edit: Thanks for the Jester Award, clearly coming from someone that can't get the game to work :steamfacepalm:. All the people saying this game doesn't run or work should update their PC or stop claiming they got a high spec PC. I had two minor bugs and the game ran as smooth as anything, it never dropped below 60 fps. Completed story and no crashes throughout the entire play through. Don't be fooled by these band wagon negative review bombers. They're just salty they got a crap PC build and couldn't experience this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I'm running a PC well above minimum spec for the game, and I'm running into frequent crashes and bugs. I'm glad I chose to play the game on the easiest difficulty because then it's not too bad to replay the game after the last pillar (savepoint) I reached before the game crashes, but it's kind of ruining my immersion in the story when the game locks up every 20 minutes if I look the wrong direction in an environment.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.Gameplay-wise a streamlined version of Returnal, but still very enjoyable to play. If you are (like me) playing with mouse and keyboard - don't play on normal. I don't like soulslike games for their difficulty and time-investment but even this game was too easy for me on normal.Score and story are actually really good and made me push through the game in about 6hrs total playtime.Only thing i would slightly critize is the level design. There aren't any major secrets or other reasons to step aside the main path since most things are already in massive supply. But still, that is a very slight criticism for a game that came out mostly bug-free without ingame purchases and for only 40 (34 currently) euros. If you can afford it buy it know and support these type of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: For me this would fall under a neutral review, but since it's more pro than con, it gets a thumbs up from me. What's Great:- It runs very well (240+ FPS with 4090, 12700K, 32 GB DDR5 RAM and NVmE drive)- The environment is beautiful- The voice acting is well done- A good mix of combat, puzzles and exploration- An intriguing stroy- Combat is fluid enough- Decent arsenal for the gameWhat's Not So Great:- Boss fights can be annoying. Not overly tough (minus the first one), but dying can cause grief (see next point)- No Save Anywhere/Weak Autosave if there is one. You activate pillars (save points) throughout the game and return here when you die. That in itself isn't bad, but it does suck when you have to repeat some content over and over again after dyingNeutral (Nitpicky Stuff):- The mouths don't match the animations. This is far more noticeable during live scenes than cutscenes. It's immersion breaking, but not a deal breaker- No jump mechanic. You're pretty much railroaded on paths most of the time.- Very linear. It fits the game, but it would be nice to have more to explore than an offshoot here and there from the main pathOverall the game isn't bad, and I feel the 34 dollars I spent was worth it. With a beautiful environment, enjoyable characters and a decent arsenal of weaponry, it can be a fun game. Solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it - technobabble was too jarringly stupid at times, but otherwise it was a good experience. Also, constant scanning of every crevice for power upgrades (and missable ones at that!) detracted from my immersion in the story because I wanted to be powerful and there was that alluring data cube in the background of a lot of very important and dramatic cutscenes. To dews credit at least there are enough of them that for the final stretch I was maxed out and fad 11 perk points to spare. In my opinion it would be better to give perk points for scanning creatures and progression (knowing your enemy and whatnot) - this way you didn't need to account for little Timmy who could not be assed to find cubes and could not finish the game or at least died like 100 times on every boss. And again - conflict of motivations of player is bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: A great mix of sci-fi, puzzle solving, and interesting combat.  I love that you have to use strategy and an array of gadgets and weapons instead of just button mashing.  The story and environment are engaging and immersive and the soundscape is well done.  I'm looking forward to what else this game has in store for me
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a great experience! Many different types of enemies, which some even have reactive strategies. Maybe not great, but a good storyline which I enjoyed very much. Weapon design is very cool, but the crafting mechanic involved with said weapons is heavily underutilized and feels like it was put there to fill a checkbox from some list... Soundtrack was fun, felt right at home with the setting. Overall graphics were good (besides human modesl). I liked the spin on experience and leveling done here, altho it felt rather random. Facial animations were absolutely wooden, dipping into the uncanny valley. Besides a couple of unexplained performance drops, it run smoothly. Bosses were either bigger versions of normal enemies, or really cool entirely new creatures, with at least one having a fight sequence through terrain interaction. Elemental reactions were nice, but no info was given on them, so some people could have missed out. Scars Above is a solid 8/10. Most souls fans most probably wouldn't find this up to their liking, but I wholeheartedly recommend. It reminds me a lot of "Remnant: From the Ashes" in a positive light. If you had fun there, you should have fun here and vice versa.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The Alpha Boss appears too difficult even on Rookie mode with Strong aim assist, so the game is basically over after about 3 hours of play.  Since the save point before the Alpha Boss fight requires 5 to 10 minutes of  repetitive play just to try the fight again and again, the game quickly loses its initial appeal.  The option to bypass a frustratingly difficult boss fight after several failures would have made this review a positive one instead of a negative.  Games can be very enjoyable entertainment, but not if game progression is blocked early in the course of the game and cannot be bypassed.  Some gamers may be less skillful than others or may have less time to master a game due to work or family commitments.  Difficulty levels that scale to the player's abilities or that can be adjusted by the player to maximize enjoyment of the purchased product would be appreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said the second Construct boss fight is not fun at all. It's really frustrating because of the delay on the fire weapon. I've been trying for days to get past this, at the point now of giving up and playing something else more enjoyable. Shame really as I was enjoying the game a lot up until this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Pathetic Game Design with gameplay, Poor costume design, Poor keyboard control with gaming environment. The story line of this game is non-existent. Weapons also poorly design. This game is like childish kids dodging and running around. Enemies are also one dimensional. The game thumbnail is deceptive. _childDocuments_.review: So... This game is quite something... I confess I bought it not knowing what I would get (I got it for 8€ at a sale, mind you) and it turned out to be quite a fun short adventure! The levels are intricate and have different paths for you to explore with different enemies and bosses to fight against. The skill leveling is a solid enough - you have to grab some small cube-like alien structures and you get Knowledge from it - and it has some good and useful perks. The story is cool, maybe sometimes a bit predictable if you pay close attention to some stuff, but overall cool stuff! The gameplay tho has some weird issues. I don't know if it was because I was playing with a Xbox controller but sometimes Kate wasn't moving at all or it seemed like she was glued to a specific path - like she had a specific hitbox around her. The enemies are challenging and can make you sweat! Some more than others! Overall I would give this one a solid 6.5/10, maybe a 7. It's a nice game but make sure you get it on a discount tho, cause for the normal price it's totally not worth it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game. As others stated, the save system is a little bit annoying (once you use the pillar, enemies respawn) and sometimes parts can take longer than necessary because of that. Honestly though, it ain't that bad - yes it is annoying sometimes (one part I did, I believe, 13 times or something, just bc I couldn't figure my technique out xD), but that was on me. Rookie difficulty is still challenging sometimes, so don't underestimate it - but it really shouldn't be a problem, it's also not that bad. I usually don't play single players quite often, I usually don't finish them quite often either... but this was intriguing, interesting, engaging, emotional - all in all a good experience. Would I buy it for 29,99? _childDocuments_.review: This is quite a nice 3PS, in a similar vein to Outriders.  My biggest problem with this game is that it requires very good reactions.  I'm playing on the easiest difficulty, and can't currently get past the 2nd boss fight.  You cannot actually dodge some of it's attacks.The game does require some quite well developed reactions and 'twitch' mechanics to survive.The plus side: using the environment and the weapons/tools you create to create combos and control the battlefield are quite interesting.One of my biggest problems with this game is that not all controls are definable; a bit of a problem for me, as I mainly play one-handed and can't use a controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Describing this game I would put it somewhere between a souls-like and a linear survival game. Which isn't bad, and I liked having to use the gadgets smartly to make it through the game. Also several scanning moments that made the scientist character feel like a scientist. That said while I enjoyed my time, I beat the game in just under 7 hours, and that is with me taking the time to find all the secrets and XP upgrades I could. I also won't say the story is anything to exciting or innovative, but I wouldn't say it wasn't interesting either. Overall I recommend this game if you want a sci-fi game that has a little survival horror mixed in with a souls-like. I don't regret my purchase and it was a fun time, but It is a little on the shorter side so keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game. A good story that doesn't try to explain what it doesn't have to. The weapons are different and the soundtrack fits well.It's funny to see all of the comments about the stiff animations, because as soon as you start playing, it makes total sense. Never before have I seen someone trained to survive drop off a two-meter cliff and land with their legs straight. Nothing about this ruins the game, but it was entertaining.I played on Commander (hard) difficulty -- it was tough. I'm not a phenomenally skilled player, so I'd say it's accessible. After the first two creatures, it seems like they introduce the new enemy in a boss-style format. One-on-one in an arena-type location. Then immediately that creature is just a normal enemy that swarms you. True bosses don't keep coming back.Your exploration is almost rail-based with few branching options. There are a few hidden paths, but largely when I thought I was being clever by not going toward the waypoint on my HUD, I was actually doing exactly what I was supposed to be doing.Most of the achievements are hidden, which I dislike because when you beat the game, there is no load. It wipes your game. I was so excited to beat the final boss that I ran through the next doorway and forgot to scan the body. That and one other equipment-based achievement that I didn't get because I never used the gadget. I wish the non-story achievements had been visible to me.I made up some new swear words as I played this game, and there was a fair amount of horror-esque elements. The developers weren't afraid of using the good old jump scare. The save/respawn system lets you breathe a bit easier after finding a pillar, and I liked the 'shortcut' system of moving forward without necessarily putting save points around every corner. I think playing it on the hardest difficulty really made the horror elements pop.TL:DR: Fun game. Buy it on sale, it's short (12 hours, even on the hardest difficulty and pausing while I did other things at times).

_childDocuments_.review: Sci-fi TPS with an interesting story, but lots of flaws in itDifficulty ★★★★★★☆☆☆☆ (at the beginning more difficult, later quite moderate)* good graphics* story line was good (with some lacks in the storytelling)* interesting fight system that rewards you a lot using the right weapon for the correct weakspots* 3 difficulties* enough XP cubes to unlock anything without the need to find all of them* traps and ammo does respawn over time as well* the face expressions are weird - you clealy see that they are coded and not motion-captured* only rare placed checkpoints with a bonfire system like in souls games* running passed enemies is sometime more efficient than killing them* linear pseudo-open-world* you gain still ability points if fully skilled, permanently highlighted in the HUD* you need to charge the thermal gun for firing* dialogues / logs get stopped when you trigger another audio unintentionally* combat system flaws:  1. enemies may occasionally shoot through other enemies  2. hitboxes of attacks or enemies causes you to get hit or blocked by thin air  3. (especially at the beginning) getting poisened is a death-sentence (too strong)  4. freezing in some areas is just too fast  5. controller even w/ aim-assist is still not as good as mouse w/ keyboardI am in general not a fan of soulslike games. The bonfire technique, evading mobs and focus on boss fights is just not my understanding of a good gameplay. As this game uses some of those things, or at least tries to be a half-hearted soulslike game, I did not like it.The game got tagged with open-world and Metroidvania as well, but it is in fact neither of it. Your backtravelling is quite limited and thus you have missables (like weapon upgrades). I know those tags are sometimes placed by players, but still it caused me having wrong expectations about this game anyway.The final kicker was the fact that the game just auto-deletes your savestate as soon as you finished the game. A no-go if you ask me. No NG+, no chapter select, no repeating the finale how often you want to, devs just decided to force the player to begin from scratch.Good visuals and story driven game, but paired with a very bad executed gameplay concept. Problem is that you just can't like this game even if you want to, as long as the 'little flaws' just slap you in your face every 5 minutes or so. The game made just too many mistakes to be called good for me, unfortunetally - and it looked so promising at the beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun. While I wouldn't say it's going to win any awards, it's solid. Not all games need to be AAA perfection after all! If you come into it with that in mind, you will enjoy it.STORYFORMAT: Semi Cinematic LinearThis story is fully voiced and follows a linear story style. It's not choice based or heavy Cinematics like Last of us. It's story overall seems interesting enough. The voice acting is good, and I am interested in what's going on. In general it's not going to leave you at the end of your chair.COMBATCombat involves light melee, and elemental weapons. I don't believe you get a tone of weapon types, I think you just get one per element, but I could be wrong. I'm not super far into the game. That being said, It's not a looter shooter. Elements play a huge role in the game. It makes combat fun, but for those who are looking for difficult game and can master these mechanics well, it may not be as challenging for you. If you play games more for fun than challenge then it will likely be enough fun to keep going! However while it has souls like elements, don't mistake that for it being hard. It's meant to be challenging if you don't master the elemental mechanics or don't hit the weak points. However using the tools the game gives you will make it easier. In the end, if you prefer a fun combat system that you can feel the benefits of different strategies, than this is for you. If you prefer all strategies to be equally challenging, than this game is NOT for you.GEAR/CRAFTINGSo far this is pretty bare bones. Do not play expecting any robust crafting or gear.RPG ElementsThis game plays similar to how Jedi fallen order plays in this regard. You do not gain levels, you gain "Knowledge" and when you gain enough you can get a skill point. However, unlike that game, you don't seem to loose any knowledge and you pick up purple knowledge cubes to gain it, so while actions themselves might provide this cube, it's not always gained. Therefor, going back and fighting enemies isn't beneficial as many of the smaller ones don't seem to provide any benefit. You also don't seem to be able to restore knowledge you might have lost from dying. However, since the world is so linear, I honestly can't tell if it even takes it away or not between save points. All in all, I wouldn't really call it an RPG in any way. Having skill points isn't really an RPG in my opinion, it's more of a natural progression that is bare minimum if no other progression exists.Overall the game is a fun adventure to have in between all the big hits. I would certainly wait for a sale, but if you like space, science, and want something a bit different than a typical shooter, than this is a great choice. Just keep in mind it is not going to knock your socks off!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game.  I think the developers have some solid ideas that play out enjoyably enough.  Some feedback:Understanding the enemies and utilizing their elemental weakness allows you to dispatch them very efficiently.  This is fun, new enemies start out intimidating then quickly become trivial after you've worked out a strategy which makes the player feel smart and powerful.  The bosses aren't too hard, they do require some puzzle solving to defeat which is enjoyable.  The Alluvial boss is a delight to fight, it's easily the best boss fight in the game.  What makes it enjoyable is it serves as a final test to everything learned in the first biome.  You have to use every tool you've received up to this point, and often in quick succession.  The following bosses feel like... quizzes in comparison which is disappointing.  I think the Neural Parasite was pretty close it just needed a bit more going on with the fight to be great.  The construct is meh.  Audio elements feel a bit flat, should the studio make a sequel this really needs to be improved.  There are a few too many invisible walls for my liking, please try to avoid this going forward.  Character facial animations are Oblivion-tier.  Really need to improve this.  Honestly I really enjoyed this game, if the developers can iterate further upon this game and come out with a more polished sequel, I think they'll have something truly special on their hands.  Just, uh, maybe do some marketing next time.

_childDocuments_.review: To start the video  Above shooter from the Serbian studio Mad Head Games looks like a hybrid of Returnal, Dark Souls and Mass Effect. Is it worth paying attention to such an unusual "cocktail" we tell in the review.When an unidentified space object of clearly alien origin appeared in Earth's orbit, humanity, of course, wanted to get to know it better. For this purpose, the SCAR squad was created, and one of its members was Dr. Kate Ward, the main character of the game. Approaching the object, the spacecraft of the researchers landed in an unknown anomaly. Kate lost consciousness, and woke up already on an unknown planet, surrounded by aggressive monsters and the ruins of an ancient civilization, without the slightest idea how she ended up here. Acquainted with the ghostly figure of a resident of this world, who promised to help her get to the bottom of the truth, the girl went in search of the surviving crew members.The plot, the use of a female protagonist and light interspersed with soullike elements are reminiscent of Returnal, and the visual style also gives a little bit of Mass Effect games. However, this project is not as hardcore as a roguelike shooter from Housemarque, if only because after death we are not returned to the very beginning of the campaign - no, Kate is just reborn near one of the obelisks scattered around the world in abundance. Opponents are resurrected along with her, but the player is not required to run to the monster that killed him to take experience and loot - all this remains with the girl.And in everything Scars Above is so, not special. A generic world with unsurprising biomes (there are countless times we traveled through swamps and alien complexes), the most common combat system, the Dark Souls "bonfire" system seen many times, the mechanics of accelerated weapon reloading peeped from the Gears of War series.However, I don’t want to scold the game for this: it’s well-tailored, all its elements work well, and you don’t get bored throughout the entire passage. If you need a linear action movie for six to eight hours, take a closer look at the project.Reader Rating0 Votes0PlusInteresting, stupid scriptIntense firefightsBeautiful landscapesgood soundtrackMINUSESThe game is completely secondarySometimes there are bugsMy mark 8.5

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game it is clear to me that a lot of dedication went into the game but ultimately, the developers wanted too much. Scars Above is a roughly 7-9 hours singleplayer game. It is pretty linear, has Remnant From The Ashes like fighting and some light puzzle elements. Additionally, it tries to present itself in a cinematic fashion with a lot of cutscenes. And right there the problems start - the animations are really lacking, in every aspect, from the lip syncing to the the combat animations, especially due to the very realistic tone the game tries to set. The gameplay mechanics do work properly but just on a very basic level. Neither the combat nor the puzzles are very interesting or exciting. The levels are designed competently and here and there are some really nice environments, but all in all the world you explore is pretty lifeless.Up to this point, I would say, get it on a sale, but there are some technical problems, especially freezes. The game used to freeze quite often, forcing me to replay stretches of the game several times. At some point I discovered that sprinting into objects/scenery seems to cause this and carefully avoiding that reduced the freezes. But this is not a minor annoyance, but borderlines on breaking the game.In the end, I think the developers should have cut the costs somewhere and focus on fewer features. A good example of how to achieve a game on this scope might be Mortal Shell. No cutscenes, no facial animations, but therefore refined gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: A good and simple game to spend a few hours of your life with!I'd say the game is a souls-like with a sci-fi environment, slighlty reminiscent of Dead Space but more nature oriented. Don't expect the most brain-twisting plot or really deep character development, but not in a bad way. Storytelling is direct and you can get most of the lore if you look around every corner (get the scan upgrade, really important). The maps feel the correct size and the art department did a good job with the colours and ambiance. The models of the enemies look great, the design behind them is cool and you even get some small explanation on why they look like that. Your character will explain a lot of stuff as if she was documenting it, which I found really nice. Didn't find any major bug or problem and it ran pretty well on my computer (8GB RAM, 6GB VRAM).Now for the bad stuff. There isn't much but I'd say some hitboxes are a bit misleading. Thankfully they're not the attack ones but the collision ones, enemies are wider than they appear or at least it feels like it. Fights, despite seeming a duel of wits between you and the mechanics of the game, are more like match color with weapon and shoot the glowy parts. Still, they feel nice and challenging enough to provide a good experience without getting you stuck for 2 days. In general, I'd recommend this game if you're searching for a quick SCI-FI adventure with a simple plot and a not-too-difficult challenge. I give it a 7.5/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Yikes, this one was rough all the way around. The graphics by themselves were not terrible but the character animation... what the hell happened there? I've seen stroke patients with better facial control. The characters don't show expressions so much as have facial tics , It's like they left the animation up to Chat GPT. The combat system is clunky and repetitive, the weapons and their upgrades are very incongruous with the world setting. I found the lack of a map, mini-map, or even a compass to be a very confusing choice with frustrating consequences. Personally I'm not a fan of the "souls-like" save mechanic, I find it to be a very tiresome experience. The lack of a jump feature meant that I had to restart more than once because my character got stuck.  The fact that the description for this games includes:  really makes me want to report them for fraud. I've seen more character development at the bottom of a bottle.  The story is about as coherent as an Ayn Rand novel and yet somehow worse at the same time. I've been more emotionally invested in a game of solitaire. You cannot have the main character rattle off a bunch of large words that sound fancy and go "science!". That's not how that works, it's just a bunch of gibberish that you made up hoping no one would call you on your BS. There was this beautiful opportunity for the exploration and discovery of an alien world and all the creativity that goes along with that. All of that potential squandered and reduced to a few sound clips that honestly sound like they came from a different game.

The visuals in general are really meh but the music and sound effects are awesome so it's a mixed bag. The game definitely has some jank I got stuck a couple of times and had to quit out and the character movement is stiff and awkward. The game it's slow to start but chapter IV and V were the strongest, however the finale chapter is really disappointing, it's mainly just a backtrack thru previous areas leading into a laughable reused enemy as a finale boss encounter. The combat is satisfying each enemy is kinda a mini puzzle figuring out how to kill them efficiently is enjoyable. The gadgets are well designed but clearly one is much more powerful, the "gravity field" once you get this the game becomes pretty easy. Overall for the current sale price it's decent albeit kinda short but I find this type of narrative and gameplay worth while but don't expect anything groundbreaking. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Scars Above is a game of modest scope and production value but it's fun, feels good and doesn't outstay its welcome. Features:- Souls-like player/monster respawn mechanic, stamina bar used for sprinting, dodging and melee.- "Science shooter" focused on targeting weak points, using the correct weapon and gadgets, taking advantage of the environment.- Unlockable skill tree with free, unlimited respec, some weapon upgrades.- Light puzzles and science themed mini-games.- Fairly linear levels with side areas to explore and shortcuts to unlock.- Pretty fun and interesting boss battles except for the final one which is very recycled.- Somewhat dated visually but still looks nice imo. - A more low tech (by sci-fi standards), down to earth "astronaut" aesthetic and characters. I like it but some might find it bland or vanilla. Scars Above won't blow anyone's mind but its combat mechanics are satisfying, it runs smooth and it's over before it becomes repetative. I guess it's hard to recommend it over Elden Ring or whatever but it deserves better reception than it got imho.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is good, graphic nice and story interesting.The problem is their save system; In that you have only ONE save, there is no autosave, no fallback point, no restart from the beginning of the chapter/map. The game also only save specific game states. And if you somehow had the game gotten saved in a wrong state, then tough luck, you're now locked out of progressing and there's no old saves to revert to.For an example of how to get a broken save state; In the Glacial maps, after you have obtained the two Power Sources and arrived at the two-slots door, put one Source in the door's slot and head back down the ramp to save point. Now exit the game and resume from save. After loading back up, you'll fine yourself with the single Power Source item in inventory, but with the other power source missing from the door and the door remains locked. It is also NOT possible to pick the item up again as the game objects you picked them from can no longer be interacted with!And if any dev actually read this, I will say I still have NOT resolve the issue. I'm going to stop playing unless I got a response+help from custom support. I'd also have asked for refund if it hasn't been more than a few hours already.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a little in, and for the first 2 chapters, the music and atmosphere make it mysterious and thrilling, My heart is pumping sometimes I'm not sure I can take it. It's damn scary and there's no way to really trigger the monsters that jump out in the lake.  The devs have done a Good job so far, but I wasn't sure if I was able to play through the whole game at the time...UPDATE 9/3/23; I've just finished the game. Actually, I did not find the rest of the game Past Chapter 2-3(?) as scary and learned to anticipate when creatures would jump out of the water etc. I even found myself looking forward to these moments (for the mild adrenaline rush when you jump in your chair a little) as my character had the 2 level 4 upgrades (15% more dmg and 15% more dmg resistance) so I was never at risk of dying from these. I actually enjoyed this game quite a bit. It is a decent narrative, with decent weapons, the creatures and bosses weren't overly difficult and obviously the difficulty is something that can be changed. There were some times I missed the save points or had to walk a little bit after respawning, but on the whole, it was just a bit of a nuisance, not a flagrant fail. I generally don't think that only being able to save at Monoliths enhances the experience (although it fits the narrative). Maybe when dying the devs could make it so that you had a choice to load a save game (this feature would have to be added) that saved your resources and health stats OR the choice to respawn at a monolith in which case you would have full ammo, health, and fibre,Also, I found it a bit frustrating that later in the game scanning creatures such as the Fungus-'humanoid' didn't yield any weak points and when I checked the audio and the log it really didn't provide any useful intel - more just a description for the sake of it. It would have been nicer to only have the creature with it's description, strengths, & weaknesses catalogued in your log IF you have scanned the creature purposefully.Thank you to the dev's for making this game and their time and efforts - I really did enjoy it. No gross errors and nothing is going to be perfect. I think it had a 2010 feel to it somehow, where the graphics or character models esp of the advanced alien race, aren't the best, the narrative is simple, straight forward, fun to play, provides challenges along the way, and kept me engaged until the end. (96% achievements 43/45, 2 hidden features not completed.)Well done. I'm Happy with my purchase. It was worth the time and the money. Really hope they continue to improve and develop similar games in the future!!!
