_childDocuments_.review: First, I am a casual gamer. I enjoy spending my hard won free time playing a game and having fun. My favorites are the Witcher series, I've played them all. I appreciate 2077 and AC Odyssey and others like these. I like open world RPGs with First and Third person views. I enjoy FPS as well.Now that you know something about me and my gaming preferences:Mechanics are a bit clunky. Visuals are great. Story is...fluff, but no real meat. No Map... Why no map? Anyone would make a map in this scenario. As others have mentioned the first real Boss or "Alpha" you reach is pretty tough. The scale of difficulty from what you've experienced prior to meeting it is incomparable, off the charts difficult, and interrupts the immersion. I took quite a bit of time to try an learn the timing but the aforementioned "clunkyness" of the mechanics makes it even harder. I'm not willing to dump my time into this tedious and time consuming boss fight.I don't like Souls games for this very reason. I don't mind a difficult boss this one is designed to take some time or to get the timing down precisely. Anyone playing this will die repeatedly working out the mechanic and that is where this type of Souls approach loses me.I just ended and uninstalled there. I hope you understand I had higher hopes for the game and I love the art and visual aspect of it, can tolerate the linear story while having almost labyrinthine environment where it goes above and below itself constantly, which I can deal with but outside of that...not worth it to me.Moving onto the next one. I wanna have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game good? Yes, this is a good game. It's fun to play and worth picking up if you are interested.NOTE: THIS IS NOT A SOULS-LIKE GAME.Alot of review are negative cause its a bad souls-like game. This game isn't a souls-like game.With that said, this game very much feels like this developers first game. There's a lot of things about it that just don't feel right or thought out. Three things stick out to me the most. 1.) the XP progression. You gain exp by picking up info nodes(they're playing off the idea of discovering info that allows you to level up). It's a cool Idea, except by chapter 6 I unlocked all of the abilities and was still gaining XP and ability points. I had 10 points stored up that I couldn't use. cause I was done with it. Once this started the idea of exploring for stuff just went away for me.2.) Stamina. It felt like they threw stamina into the game just cause everyone else has it. The dodge mechanic is setup in a way that most of the time you're only dodging once or twice at a time and never use enough stamina to justify having it in the first place. The melee in the game is does so much less dmg than the gun that it's almost never used.3.) Map layout. This game does a really good job, of not feeling like a hallway game, butt it very much is. Any break off from the main path is just a small area that has stuff. It doesn't take long before you lose the feeling of openness.Aside from that, and the very old looking animations in the game(faces and cut scenes look like PS2/3 gen graphics), the game is neat. I like the elemental combat a lot, but I wish it was more involved. _childDocuments_.review: Scars Above does not raise the bar for shooters, but that does not make it a bad experience. It offers a relatively brisk seven-hour adventure that does not get too repetitive. Its shooting is competent, with elemental damage quirks and decent gadgetry. The various alien creatures and their weak spots keep the combat fresh, with a few respectable boss fights. Although the beginning is tedious, with sparsely placed pillars acting like Dark Souls respawn points, it gets much easier (and fun) as it transitions into a more traditional third-person shooter. Scars Above certainly needed more creativity to break away from its generic attributes, but at least the pieces it borrows from other games are stitched together well.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like combat that feels like a quicktime event? Do you like games that are artificially difficult? Then this is the game for you! Really, none of it is difficult, none of it actually feels like combat, it's not balanced, it gives no wiggle room for how the player wants to play, and if you don't jump through the exact hoop the developers want you to jump through, you don't progress. Simple as that!Let's start with combat. One of the earliest enemies you fight is what is essentially an armored gorilla. The reason I've chosen this enemy is because every enemy in the game essentially has the same gimmick.This armored gorilla takes little to no damage, from any weapon, except from your fire based weapon. This weapon has a three second charge time before it fires what is essentially a puff of smoke, unless you hit a specific weak spot, on specific enemies, that are actually vulnerable to said weapon. Even better, once charged, the weapon only allows you to hold this charge for about another second before it releases the shot, regardless of if you want it to or not, making your timing crucial, and inserting even more artificial difficulty into the fight. The gorilla's weak spot is only vulnerable for a split second when the gorilla closes in and rears up to slam it's fists into the ground. Forcing you into a very specific, tedious pattern of close range play to deal with this enemy. Then, once you've shot this weak spot enough, the gorilla roars for a split second, which gives you a tiny window of opportunity to change weapons and fire a different, but again specific, weapon into it's mouth to do more damage. You then rinse and repeat this process until one or more enemies are dead in what feels like one giant quicktime event after another.I know what you're thinking.. Not EVERY fight can be like that, right? Okay, let's talk about Chapter 2. During chapter 2 you're caught in a snow storm, forcing you to fight several gorilla enemies that are covered in snow, making them immune to fire damage. Good news, tho! You're on a frozen lake! You can use your fire weapon to punch a hole in the ice, allowing the gorillas to fall into the water and freeze solid, allowing you to shatter them with a well placed shot from a different, but again specific, weapon. Sounds easy enough, right? Except the ice takes two shots, in the same place, to break, your fire weapon, again, requires you to charge it, and the gorillas are not just moving, but actively avoiding the places you shoot to try and break the ice, once again forcing you into the same close combat play style, the only difference is now you're aiming and the ground.Still sounds too easy? That's because it is. During one particular fight with two of these gorillas the ground is also swarmed with spiders, are the spiders particularly dangerous? No, but they will catch your shots, protecting the ice from damage while trying to play out the quicktime event.Still doesn't sound that bad? Well, do I have a surprise for you! During the quicktime event, in the middle of a snow storm, you also have to deal with hypothermia. That's right, if you fail to warm yourself up, you will flat out die by freezing to death. How do you warm yourself up? There are bushes that are interspersed through out the level that, when shot with your fire weapon, burn and emit heat for a short time, allowing you to warm yourself as long as you stand within the aura they emit, and after they're used, they're gone forever, giving you a limited time, and limited amount of resources, to combat the cold.That's right! Quicktime events where you juggle the invulnerable gorillas, can't shoot the ground and break the ice because the spiders will catch your shots, AND you get to freeze to death in literally one minute! Should you need to warm up during the fight? Good luck trying to stand in that tiny aura while juggling two gorillas and a hoard of spiders!TL;DR? The developers of this game need to resign. They haven't made a game, they've made a giant quicktime event, then, I can only assume after they realized this, inserted needless mechanics into what is already tedious combat to artificially boost difficulty. My only regret? That I really tried to like this game, and didn't refund it before the 2 hour limit.

_childDocuments_.review: The Earth is approached by a giant alien construct, and a select team of specialsts- SCARS are chosen to approach it and make first contact. After initial introduction section (where you get to meet the stereotypical crew members and learn the basics of item manipulation) something goes very wrong and you, Kate Ward, double Ph.D in biology and Mech Engineering- find yourself on a hostile planet, among wrecks of your ships' cargo and haunted by a strange alien apparition. That's where the game really begins, and its a mix of third person shooting, light exploration and puzzle solving. The shooting involves juggling 4 elemental weapon types (electric, fire, ice and acid) to match specific enemy's weakness. certain enemies have elemental weak point that need to be exposed first, and then you can shoot them for massive damage. In this sense, it's similar to the Horizon games. Some people like to say this is a "souls-like", but honestly, I wouldn't say that. There's a stamina bar, that's used for melee attacks and dodge-rolling, enemies respawn when you save at a checkpoint, and your health pickups and ammo refill, but there's no penalty for death, and only rudimentary shortcuts. You can also unlock a skill that gives you some health for  killing enemies with melee, but it's only really useful for a few enemy types, and is rather risky for everyone else. The levels are pretty linear, with some side-paths that yield either extra XP (used to unlock passive Skills), or weapon upgrades. The main path is always marked with blue or red lights, so it's pretty easy to navigate and make sure you don't accidentally lock yourself out of extra stuff. Overall, there's a lot of extra XP (I finished the game unlocking all skills, and then had enough extra XP left over to unlock 7 more skills). Sometimes you need to solve puzzles to progress, but there's nothing particularly complex. Game ran flawlessly on my Ryzen 3700X and 1660ti at 1080p Ultra; no serious bugs to report- occasionally the waypoint would dissappear, but going into the menu and back into the game fixed that. Overall, a really solid linear game with a decent story (VERY strong System Shock 2 influences), varied level design and interesting, albeit basic combat system. Easy title to recommend to anyone who likes action-adventures with some climbing, shooting, exploration and puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, but lukewarm.  It's pretty enough, with a modicum of predictable and cliched story, but the dialogue is terrible, and (with the sole exception of the protagonist) not well voiced either - fortunately, it is skippable, though missing the cutscenes means you'll miss a few contextual clues about what is going on.  Oddly mechanical character movement which I guess is lacklustre motion-capture.  Combat and crafting are on par for this sort of game, though the boss fights are tedious, relying on hitting weak points in order to do any damage, and sometime with weapons that you need to charge by holding down a button, then shoot by releasing it (button-up to shoot can be frustratingly counter-intuitive, making it harder to hit).  Also frustrating to navigate and too easy to end up wandering in circles trying to figure out where it wants you to go; it's quite linear and insists you go where it wants you to, so if you don't spot the path to get there, you can't make progress.  All things considered, it's enjoyable enough to pick up on sale, but hard to recommend at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I rip into this game, let me state this: I definitely don't dislike this game. I'm giving it a thumbs up because it's worth playing on a good discount. It's nothing incredible, but you'll get a solid eight hours of fun out of it. What I have is mainly just a bunch of small gripes that brought the whole experience down to "average" rather than "good."I got this game gifted to me for my birthday after having it on my wish list for a year. After playing through the game on the standard difficulty, what I was left feeling after a bit under 9 hours was that I'd played a tech demo for a larger game. There's a decent game here, hidden under a solid first couple hours but a very bland mid/endgame, a painfully predictable story, systems that don't really interconnect, and "puzzles" that devolve into "shoot thing with matching color." The only time the game surprised me was when the one time a puzzle required me to inspect something in my inventory and manipulate it. I hadn't done that since five minutes into the tutorial, and seven hours later I didn't remember it was a thing you could do until a popup told me to go do it. After a few jump scares here and there, figuring out how to deal with a new enemy, and then it's all just same-same. Resources were so abundant the only time I ran out of ammo was figuring out how to beat bosses. The final "boss" upset me because it really was just a reskin of something you fight repeatedly through the game, just with a bigger health bar. The typical combat "puzzle" is that an enemy has a weak point you need to hit with a matching color of weapon. Color and element are basically interchangeable terms when it comes to combat. Blue spot? Shoot electricity. Orange? Fire. Once you know what color to shoot, there's no puzzle left. Kate, the protagonist, will even talk out loud and tell you the right thing to do to kill things. And you'd better do what you're told, because you can dump every point of ammo you have into an enemy and not kill if if you don't shoot the weak point. And yet... A thing I really do love and hate at the same time is that enemy weak points are guarded. It makes total sense that a creature would hold up an armored arm to prevent you from shooting the glowing bit in its chest. It's completely reasonable that a creature turns to face you rather than let you shoot it in the back. But the enemies are often TOO good at avoiding the damage. The enemy with the armored arm is only really vulnerable when it's swinging up to attack you - and if it's doing that, you need to dodge or you're going to get whacked. The enemy with the weak point on his back can turn 180 degrees in a fraction of a second to swing at you.There's tools to fix that, like the "stasis" field that really is just a "make everything move slower for a few seconds," but the first few times with each critter type you won't have those tools, and really you can just wait for them to make the swing, dodge past them, and shoot them in the back. Or just use the cryo gun, freeze them, and line up a shot. It's just... bland.I think my biggest critique of the game, despite enjoying it overall, was that I had to take several days of a break between chapters 5 and 6 for work reasons - and I came back to the game having forgotten all the controls, and still completed the last  chapter without ever coming close to dying even once. I didn't use a monolith (campfire) the entire last chapter.And for anyone coming in with "just play it on Commander," the story won't change, there's no new items, no achievement for doing it, and the enemies don't get new moves - they just get more health and deal more damage to you. You might scrape a couple more hours out of the game because of the increased health pools though, so if you want more challenge, go right ahead and play on Commander. Now that I've complained a bunch, here's some things I genuinely liked:The unique bosses requiring you to use the environment to kill them.Body horror and sci-fi are always a good combo.The weapon upgrades actually felt like real upgrades - piercing on the lightning gun, more ammo per clip, different firing modes, tighter spread on the acid shotgun - these are good things that made the weapons easier to use.The little virtual arenas that teach you how to use the new gadgets you make were a nice, quick break from the routine, and did an excellent job of showing you what each gadget's purpose was.The Big Bad seemed appropriately threatening as the villain of the story (outside of the ending which I don't want to spoil.)The elemental combo system always felt like a nice bonus when I could pull it off.The game has solid potential, and I WOULD be interested in a sequel if they made one. I just hope they do better than merely average next time!

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the story line and had fun for 90% of the game. It was a easy 8-ish hour time waster with a creepy atmosphere and groovy world design. The elemental weapons system felt very similar to guardians of the galaxy but not in a bad way and most of the boss fights were puzzle like in a way and i found that to be an interesting change of pace from the regular combat featured throughout. I also really enjoyed searching for collectibles to level up. The biggest disappointment was the rushed ending of the game, it was like they ran out of budget or something. Without spoiling anything it felt like a lot of reused assets and less exploration. All and all if your looking for a short single player game that features an interesting world to explore Scars Above is worth buying when on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: The dreadful combination of boring and unoriginal. It constantly reminds you of better games. Mass Effect, Metroid, Remnant and Dead Space. This game has elements from all of them. They aren't poorly implemented or anything and mechanically it works well enough. But why even bother? I don't care about the story or the characters. I am not even curious about what may happen because everything is so predictable. There is no reason to continue. Alt + F4, uninstall, negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game, simple, and worth the cost. You need to have realistic expectations-it's not a AAA title. Some animations are going to be janky. But for UE4 game it looks pretty good.Gameplay has some good ideas. Elemental-based damage on enemies varies gameplay. The story is serviceable and enjoyable, but a little cheesy. It's got a whole scifi B-movie vibe and I love that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an AA title for an AA price. You have to go in expecting that. Already seen some reviewers criticising the game for a certain level of Jank. This game is on par with a title like The Chant which released at the end of last year.  I personally love a good low budget game the same way i enjoy a B-Movie and i also think that horror titles in particular are better off when they are a bit gritty and rough around the edges. It adds to the uncomfortable atmosphere.The game gets you into the action after a pretty short intro section. This section does a good job of introducing you to the game world and characters as well as some of the base game mechanics. There are things to pick up and read or listen to that will increase your immersion and understanding of the game world. Once you get into the meat of the game it plays a bit like a metroidvania title with different areas locked away until you have certain powers or tools. You progress through the story but each time you die you reset to a save point a little bit like a souls game where enemies reset. You have skills you can gradually level up and unlock as well.There are weapon upgrades to craft that make things easier. Some are more hidden and some are on the main path. The enemies are all pretty neat so far. The weapons can combo to create more damage or impact weak spots but there is an element of resource management at play as well.The game is also pretty challenging in places - and while you can tone down (or increase) the difficulty on the normal setting i have died a fair number of times - but in a way that feels fair. Some encounters just catch you out the first few times until you start to learn. So its got some really nice gameplay and combat elements woven in.The puzzle design and interaction is also really nicely done. I love the way you interact and move around the puzzle scenes. It feels very tactile. So far the puzzles haven't been too challenging but i have had to stop and think a  bit. Almost got tempted to cheat and look something up online but finally figured it out after looking around the puzzle scene a bit more for an extra clue.I can tell that this is going to be one of the rare games for me that i actually play all the way through,I haven't gotten too far in yet but so far it seems great and i'm excited to really give it some solid play time over the coming weeks.Oh. And it runs flawlessly on max settings for me which for a release in 2023 is worth recognition as well. Nothing seems overtly broken or buggy.So if you are a fan of indie / lower budget games and want to try something different from the main stream cookie cutter game factory machine then this is certainly going to be well worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable science fiction story and I look forward to any sequel that might arise.    The combat was uneven, at first it was difficult enough for me to go to minimal difficulty but by the end I was finding it a little easy.   I also wish there had been some more puzzles but I'm weird that way.  Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game was good and I would recommend it, but it really feels like it copied alot from Returnal. Even still the story was different enough that it kept me interested. The developers clearly added a ton of padding to all of the world so in most cases you are pretty far removed from any edge or even anything seemingly outside what the developers want you to touch. I know the reasons why that was done, but it does make it feel cheap and not very immersive.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful dark sci fi story with solid gunplay, immersive environments, and rewards you for thinking on your feet and experimenting. Exploration is encouraged and the devs clearly worked hard to make your time worth it. Short and sweet, can be completed in one weekend or several smaller sittings. Runs well even on moderate rigs. Personal note, this game made me say holy **** more times aloud than I expected, for the right reasons. It puts you the player into it's world and never lets go. It joins the ranks of sci fi worldbuilding greats like STALKER, Subnautica and Journey to the Savage Planet
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: I believe this is highly underrated game. It has great and mystery story of a (yours!) space craft gone missing. You need to figure out what is wrong on highly hostile plant. The game has great atmosphere, nice combat, amazing storytelling. The soundtrack also reminds me of some great ambient/space music. Maybe the game itself is not that long, ~9h for 100% completion. Pros: 1.	Story.2.	Atmosphere.3.	Combat.4.	Upgrade system.Cons: 1.	Sometimes you need to fight with ‘predesigned’ scenarios, meaning like the creators thought you would do it. If you do not, you will die. 2.	Not really challenging. This is not a cons as is, but the tag states it is challanging. (At the beginning of the game I died occasionally, most late game bosses were dead on first run. Including last one) 3.	I would suggest giving some benefits for upgrade points that cannot be used. I have maxed my skills and then had ~7 upgrade points at the end of the game that I could not spend. If you are not sure whether to buy it, I encourage to do so. I bought it for ~6EUR/USD. Worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: A soulslike with no progression other than what the story gives you. In other words you are only as powerful as the game wants you to be, and if you can't beat an enemy you can't got and level up, you are just stuck. Lies of P did exactly the same thing, BTW, it just hid it a bit better.So I dropped the difficulty to easy and I can't see any difference. I can only assume that the people who gave this game a thumbs up just really like punishing themselves or are diamond tier FPS players. If you are a normal gamer with average skills, stay away. If I'd bought it on steam, I'd have had my refund by now.
_childDocuments_.name: Scars Above

_childDocuments_.review: A sci-fi version of the Remnant game series. This game is story driven and relatively short. It's a 1-time play through kind of game but the experience was good. The combat was a little rough in some cases. The melee function can feel a little janky but it works. The outer-spacey music and atmosphere were great. Voice acting was decent as well. Overall I really enjoyed my time with this game. If they make a sequel to this game, I'll be looking forward to it

_childDocuments_.review: It wasn't bad. The negative reviews mention stuff I didn't experience personally. Difficulty was fine on the "medium" difficulty option. The game is mostly linear, you can go out of the path for a tiny bit to get some resources or . I liked the story, in a not very serious way. Combat felt good enough for what's needed. I never felt ridiculously strong which is something I prefer but it's not a game where you have the ability to farm anything to get there. It was a little bit short but it didn't feel that short. (I didn't realize it was 7 hours until I saw the steam time)The elements remind me of metroid prime but them having their own "weapon" type is both good and bad. I liked the first gun the most out of all because of this. I wish there had been more "combos" or maybe I just didn't find them all. The active abilities were fun.Overall I guess I'd grab it on sale if you think you want some linear-ish third person shooter.About the linear-ish:

_childDocuments_.review: Charming game. It reminds me of the feelings I had when I played A Plague Tale Innocence and Hellblade for the first time. Game from a small studio that tries to provide rich gameplay and story. Perhaps, a sort of AA game. I really did like everything about the game.  Core game mechanics are actually quite nice. You have to consider combinations of different elements, such as environment and weapon choice + gadgets to take down enemies. I think that was really well managed in the game. You can make the combat difficult, if you don't consider the options you have been given. I like that approach in this game.I think the game would had benefit for more richer exploration and crafting. The idea behind crafting is actually quite clever. Some good engineering small game to craft items and components would had fit perfectly in the game regarding the background story. Now items are pretty much just there to find. Also game world seems to be rather small scope. You actually run corridors and secrets are just behind different corner. I think the level and world design is probably the biggest down side in the game. Really pity, because if that had been better this would be an excellent game.I think the game pace is actually really good. There are moments when things go slower and there the emphasis is more on story and world building, then pace gets more intense and it's more combat orientated. There's a really good balance of when combat is provided and when small puzzles are offered and when everything leads to conclusion of level and a chapter.Like said, I really enjoyed virtually everything about the game. Well spent 10+ hours. With some more development and fine tuning, this would had been really an excellent game. But it's not bad at all for such a small studio.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up in a Humble Bundle as the description sounded interesting.  Given only the option to vote yes or no, I have to vote no.  If I could give this a thumbs middle, I would.  It's an OK game overall, but there's a lot of inconsistencies throughout and the game is severely missing any kind of map.Combat mechanics are good.  Different creatures are affected differently to the different weapons that you have, so you have to think on your feet to beat them.Level design is OK.  It's very linear, and it makes it very easy to get all of the collectibles in the game.  That being said, the open-world aspects can be confusing at times as the game has no map whatsoever, so you have to remember which path you've taken to get to your objective.  The story is set in the future, where you have a mobile 3D Printer that can print entire weapons in about 3 seconds flat and a scanner device that can analyze mechanisms hidden in structures, but nothing that can generate a map of the areas you've been to so you can reference paths you have already taken.  It does have a waypoint though, which at least is something.  Climbable ledges aren't consistently marked, so you might find yourself wandering around for a bit until you realize that there's a ledge you can climb up on.  Some of them are marked with a whiteish top to clearly identify it though.The story is OK.  Very straightforward Sci-Fi story, but for whatever reason, you're special because reasons.  Bad guy is using bad methods to do something good, so he needs to be stopped.  The game feeds you audio logs that spell out the reasons for things, and then has you watch a non-cutscene explanation of the very things you found in the audio logs previously towards the end.  Very little character development, if any, The story would have been better served with a twist ending.Graphics are good.  Not great, but good.Controls are OK.  I like to play with a reversed Y-axis camera, and that seemed to throw off the entire mouse in the scanning parts and the gadget wheel.Overall, I would say not to get this game unless you can get it in a really deep discount (like I did with the Humble Bundle) or you just absolutely love these types of games, otherwise, it's not quite worth it.  I do feel that the devs have some promise though.  They have good gameplay, and if they can just tweak the rest of it, they could have a really stellar game, or maybe a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: is a game that managed to surprise me and I mean that in a good way. I never considered myself a gamer, I mean I basically played League only for years but I decided to branch out and Scars Above became my first game I finished (on 100% completion too) so here's my humble opinion.The movement in this game doesn't feel as smooth as I would prefer. I think that the main problem with this is character's movement speed, whether it is attacks, dodging or running speed. I imagine the devs of this game realized that despite the large areas in the game and many enemies that will try to stop you on your every step, the game can be completed relatively fast. I mean, I myself managed to finish it in 8 hours which is not much game time, so I imagine they purposefuly set the character speed very low. But I mean, it does feel realistic, so if that's what you prefer. The guns feel very good and I enjoyed using all of them - of course, preferably in combination, because that is something you will use a lot in this game. Yes, you can combine your guns and you will have to switch to a fire gun if enemy has a weak spot to fire. But that is not all, you can also interact with the terrain in this game and use the guns accordingly, so if enemy is on frozen lake, you can shoot the ice and the enemy will fall through. That is a very cool mechanic and I had so much fun combining all the guns and gadgets, made me feel smart.There is also great variety of enemies, ready to be blasted. They all represent a certain challenge and they are all capable of making you hate them, especially if they jumpscare you by jumping out of the the water. The boss fights were fun and challenging. I liked that it's not only about blasting, but also using your brain to find advantage against your enemy. Again, made me feel smart. The one bad thing I have to mention is bugs. Sometimes the character would randomly get stuck in place, not being able to move. That would usually resolve itself after a few seconds, but other times, when I was in a river for example, and I got stuck, I had to use my cryo gun to freeze the space under me to finally move and jump out. I also died a few times to hypothermia while standing in the zone of the fire plant which was active, so I don't know about that. But none of these ruined the experience for me.One other thing that really bothered me is the respawns. When you respawn, the game resets all your ammo so you are ready to go at it again. But what about your fiber? If you fight, use heals, die and then respawn, your fiber doesn't reset so you are not able to use your heals again. That just doesn't make sense to me. Same thing if you switch the guns in your inventory. After respawning, the game resets your gun selection back. Why?I would say the world is a fine mix between Control and Alien universe. Grassy parts breath life into you and the slimy parts feel... well, slimy? Whether it is snowy mountains, smelly swamps or inside of a living organism, I always spent time looking around me and admiring the amazing textures. I had fun exploring the world and I think you will too. You get rewarded for it too so don't be lazy and just do it. Might add you some game time as well so win win? The monsters look very creepy so that's a good thing. The only problem I noticed is that some cutscenes look laggy, foggy and the expression on the character's faces are just bad.The music is okay, kinda catchy but nothing special. Some scores remind me of Mass Effect for some reason. The voice acting is great in this one, the actors really put their hearts into this. The sound effects of monsters and enviroment are also very decent.Big part of this game, of course it is. They work very well with the mysteries around you to keep you intrigued. It's simple, but it's good. The characters are rather bland, especially our main character. I think the problem with this one is, that our main character is only reacting to what the game throws at her. She never mentions what she likes, what she doesn't like, how she feels... She's just on a mission and that can feel empty. I also think the opening sequence could have been a little longer. Maybe the crew could have played some card game together, having fun before the mission starts. We would see them interacting, get the idea of what their relationships are like. Don't tell us Kate is friends with Mike, show us. But yeah, might have been a budget issues. Also, the hallucination sequence in the caves towards the finale was a bit unnecesary. Feels like you see this kind of thing in so many games and I wish the devs went for something a little bit more original.Overall, I had a great time playing the game, but it has it's issues. The game is short, it has some bugs and the characters feel bland, soulless and uninteresting, especially the MC, despite the amazing voice actors. I would give this game a solid

I crafted the cryo blaster and made an ice path all the way across the worms, but it wasn't showing I completed that portion of the quest to give me the next objective. I saved at the pillar thinking this might be what the game wanted me to do, but still nothing... so I continued on and even fought a boss, but it all doesn't matter, I'm not able to get it to say I got past the worms... even though I did. _childDocuments_.review: Neat little game, I'll recommend it on a discount.There's definitely some jank here and there, enemies blocking you when there's clearly room for you to move. One place my feet sank into the ground, wasn't stuck it just looked goofy. A bit of floating grass here and there. Cut-scenes doesn't look great by modern standards.But it's all minor things that shouldn't deter you from the game though. At its core, it's good fun, specific weapons counter specific enemies, weakspots are highly rewarded and lends itself to deliberate gameplay. The story is pretty good, not great but interesting enough to keep me engaged.You won't find much reason to replay the game, so you get the one playthrough of 5-6 hours.As I said, I'd recommend it at a discount and I do believe that the price is main reason for the relatively poor reviews. I don't think it's worth 30eu, definitely worth your time, but not the price itself. If you can pick it up at 10eu and have an afternoon free, I think you'll enjoy it.Note: If achievements is something you care about, you can reliably 100% the game in a single a single playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game that I would like to recommend for many reasons.- Interesting story, I really wanted to see how it will end. It is like a hard SF but still not so hard to think about it. Who knows maybe it can make sense in the future :)- Graphics is also very nice. There are different areas in the game and each one of them is unique in its own way. So really enjoyable environment, you will not feel bored by areas. There are nice structures, effects of using weapons can look not so great but still acceptable, Animations are fluid and didn't see any problems with shooting or targeting.- Very solid amount of different enemies which is a refresher. Some games don't have so many enemies which needs to be eliminated in different way. Boss fights are also nice and interesting.- Game is solid challenge even on medium difficulty. I really liked that also because even simple fight can bring some risk.The only negative sides I encountered are mostly around some movement problems near walls, when camera also behaves strange. There are several types of weapons of gadgets you can use, but I didn't use many, simply there was not so much use for several.A really nice game in general and should be played who likes SF, alien topics. decent challenge and unique world designs. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review:
Something strange has entered Earth's orbit; an object alien and unknowable, made out of matter that seems not to obey the laws of physics - the Metahedron. As a part of a hastily gathered group of astronauts and scientists sent off to explore it, your fate takes a jarring turn as you awaken in another world - dazed, alone on an alien planet... but determined to stay alive.  Scars Above is a challenging, immersive third-person shooter inspired by modern type action-adventure games. It takes the genre staples, such as the rewarding feeling of overcoming difficulty, and combines it with a compelling and intricate story, meticulous and lavish world design, and a living, breathing ecosystem to explore and endure.

This is a game of mystery and discovery.

name: WE ARE FOOTBALL
detailed_description: As a manager and trainer in WE ARE FOOTBALL, you’ll come face to face with the latest trends in the world of football, experiencing all the emotional highs and lows of your favorite club. For the first time ever, this modern football manager game also offers a women’s football game mode, featuring all the same functionality as well as many unique gameplay elements. To maintain and ensure the highest quality across all game modes, WE ARE FOOTBALL has been developed with experienced football management veterans such as Gerald Köhler, Rolf Langenberg, and Dirk Winter. You’ll get immediate feedback for every decision, big and small. You’ll have to plan out your deadlines effectively in the game, and will only be truly successful in the club by working together with your colleagues. WE ARE FOOTBALL focuses on real management tasks. The goal of the game is to build up the club over the long haul, including growing the team, colleagues, infrastructure, fans, and more. As a result, the football players in the game are individual personalities who spin their own stories. A season can be played through in a few hours: You’re in the middle of the action after just a few minutes. Alone, several seasons can be played through in one afternoon, and two players can even finish a season in an evening. There’s always new challenges to face in WE ARE FOOTBALL. The bigger the club, the bigger the challenge! Features: Beginner-friendly and playable without long introductions or tutorials – easy to learn but hard to master Just as complex as traditional manager games Club selection and career mode via settings quiz Comprehensive manager functionality (finances, sponsors, HR, organization, fan support, followers, IPO, sale of shares to investors, fan shares, and much more) Manager skills can be upgraded Implementation of the latest developments in football Detailed team and player attributes Modern training and realistic training planning Individual skills tree for each player Full psychological profile for each player – the team’s types need to match each other perfectly to have any chance of success Huge youth sector – manage player development even from a young age Comprehensive list of playing styles and basic rules New match engine with a focus on the ball and the players involved in the offenses with additional text commentary All matches in the game world are calculated equally Spectacular half-time speeches Expandable 3D stadium and 3D club grounds, as well as a club museum you can walk through Weekly progress with exciting negotiations and many small and big decisions to be made Comprehensive statistics section – a real treat for fans Critical fan commentary after the match Simulation of the ups and downs of major football teams Simulation of national team tournaments with changes in the market value of team players The game doesn’t include any official football licenses. The game comes with an editor which lets you create your own leagues or clubs: Any country in the world can be edited Men’s and women’s leagues Choice of official or personal database at the beginning of the game Open league systems with editable promotion and demotion rules Expandable names list per language Automatic creation of players and teams Comprehensive editors for crests and shirts Options to integrate your own graphics WE ARE FOOTBALL is future-proof: the game’s start year can be adjusted in the editor.

Features: Beginner-friendly and playable without long introductions or tutorials – easy to learn but hard to master Just as complex as traditional manager games Club selection and career mode via settings quiz Comprehensive manager functionality (finances, sponsors, HR, organization, fan support, followers, IPO, sale of shares to investors, fan shares, and much more) Manager skills can be upgraded Implementation of the latest developments in football Detailed team and player attributes Modern training and realistic training planning Individual skills tree for each player Full psychological profile for each player – the team’s types need to match each other perfectly to have any chance of success Huge youth sector – manage player development even from a young age Comprehensive list of playing styles and basic rules New match engine with a focus on the ball and the players involved in the offenses with additional text commentary All matches in the game world are calculated equally Spectacular half-time speeches Expandable 3D stadium and 3D club grounds, as well as a club museum you can walk through Weekly progress with exciting negotiations and many small and big decisions to be made Comprehensive statistics section – a real treat for fans Critical fan commentary after the match Simulation of the ups and downs of major football teams Simulation of national team tournaments with changes in the market value of team players The game doesn’t include any official football licenses. The game comes with an editor which lets you create your own leagues or clubs: Any country in the world can be edited Men’s and women’s leagues Choice of official or personal database at the beginning of the game Open league systems with editable promotion and demotion rules Expandable names list per language Automatic creation of players and teams Comprehensive editors for crests and shirts Options to integrate your own graphics WE ARE FOOTBALL is future-proof: the game’s start year can be adjusted in the editor.
short_description: Lead your football club through national championships and to international stardom. Take over an established men’s or women’s team of your choice as its manager or bring a small team into the big league.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing football management games all the way back to the original Football Manager, through the Championship Manager era and right back to the current iteration of FM. Throughout this period I have fond memories of games such as Ultimate Soccer Manager, LMA Manager and FIFA Manager, and to me these were always good stable mates to the more tactical approach of the FM series.Recently, I’ve burnt out on the FM series, I’ve hardly played it this year to be honest so I was really excited that we may have an alternative, something a little more casual and less of a time sink. So far this This Is Football is nicely filling that gap for me, and I’m really pleased I took a chance on it. It’s a great change of pace and I think that as a first release of a new franchise the devs have done a good job. Basically, this game focuses more on the building of an entire club, through the building of club facilities, sponsorships, looking after the fans etc. rather than just heavy tactics.So I’ve seen multiple reviews berating parts of game, but in my opinion anyone expecting a new football management game to be ‘perfect’ on day one is not being sensible. There are so many moving parts and simulations that interact that I fully expected that to be the case. Even the current iteration of the FM franchise has to issue multiple balance patches every year.What I think we have here is a very solid foundation of a franchise that sits very nicely as an alternative to Football manger, and competition is important to drive both franchises forward. I truly believe that the devs can build on this create a really strong product.But the most important thing is I’m having fun with this game. I’ve had a terrible couple of weeks due to the loss of my mother, and this game has successfully provided moments of respite. I’m happy with my purchase and hope this review helps you decide if this game is for you. A few things for people to consider who may be thinking about a purchase:•	The UI is confusing at first, but after spending some time with it I think I know where everything is. It certainly gives a fun throwback vibe to some of the other games I mention above. •	I really love how you can literally just drag and drop players anywhere on the tactics pitch and enjoy the more simple way the player rating is shown.•	The teams and players are not real, however it can very easily be patched with one download. Its very simple so it’s not really an issue. •	The match engine is very different to FM, I suggest watching a YouTube video if that matters to you. I wasn’t sure about it at first, but it’s grown on me. The devs have said that they are looking to develop a fully 2D/3D engine. •	Some of the German to English translations are a bit weird – it can make things a bit difficult to understand at first.•	There are a few minor bugs, nothing major or game breaking that I’ve seen. I’ve had no crashes. The worst one is an issue with young players asking for way too much money when signing a contract.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the right idea, but is in dire need of patching. There are some baffeling design choices that are unexpected from such an experienced team, and there are some additional annoyances that are easy to fix.1. Let me start with this: The game is easy. Very easy. Sadly, it is easy for the wrong reasons.Having a more accessable and therefore easier management game is not bad, but maybe the only way to challenge the more complex managers out there. But there is a basic truth to these games: Balance is important. The game gives you tools, and you use these tools, that is what a game like this is all about. If the game overpowers one tool and makes others useless, then the game becomes far too easy once you understand which tool is the only one you need.That tool is the transfer market. It is downright funny how easy it is as a 4th league team to get players that would be in the best 3rd league teams. They are cheap, they are willing, they are far better than the alternative. Said alternative would be to develop players - but forget about that. Training is just there to raise fitness levels, and young players shouldn't be trained, they should just be bought cheap from other teams.2. Player availability is something that is also a big problem, because... there are just too many good players. In this game, all countries are generally at the same strength level. As English team, you will find great first league players everywhere. Russia, Switzerland, Turkey - and not just a few, but many. The whole league is full of them, wherever you look. And some of those players will be on the transfer market, so you can buy them for 40% of their value. Which is by the way the same vaue for every league - players from a lower league in Austria will be priced identical to first league players in Italy, so do not think that you can make a better deal in smaller countries. Every country is just the same, only names are varying, but the numbers won't change. And while you can get a nice team going very fast, you do not feel happy doing that, you do not build a connection to your players, because they are not rare, it is not an accomplishment to get them. They are just numbers, and you will sell them the moment a opposing team offers you 300% of their value (which happens not as rarely as you would think when you keep in mind how many identical players are on the transfer market at the same time).3. Some small things that are annoying: No explainations about some of the features in the game. Why is my manager stressed even though he only works 8 hours per week? Why can't I scout players in a country, why do I have to scout league specific? Why does a game that wants me to play it fast paced and with the bigger picture / long term goes in mind all of the sudden have me answer press questions that I could not even answer if I would analyse the match I just played for half an hour (What do I know if the catcalling of my supporters was justified, I did not see more than some moving pictures and even those I skip half of the time! And no, I have no idea how hard the fouls were, because again: I cannot see them, I just see the amount of cards given and even those I do not keep in mind because interviews are only onced every 10 games!). Interviews feel like surprise exams, and I am out of school since more than 10 years, so no thanks, I want to play games for fun.So - how to fix things? Well, here are some ideas:1. Leagues need to get some simply variable that makes them weaker / stronger and lowers prices / wages for players.2. Players need to develop faster and more, talent needs to have more of an impact. Young players have to be weaker than they are, but need to get stronger fast, otherwise I will just always buy very strong young players.3. Development needs to also happen in lower leagues. It cannot be that a player buys a young, talented team and then watches how all those 17-20 year old players do not get stronger at all for the whole year because they are only winning every game in league 2 (doesn't even change much in league 1 though, cause: Development is soooo damn slow and unfulfilling!).4. Transfers need to get harder. There must be a middle ground between the AI saying "I only sell this player for 400% of the market value" before having a stroke and selling it 2 month later for 40%. That is just weird to watch. And again: It amkes development useless! I will not wait 5 years for my 18 year old youth prospect to reach a level that I can also just gain by buying some random dude from Greece for nearly nothing.I hope this helps the developers. I want this game to succeed, and like I said: It gets the idea right. The market needs a more casual, but fun oriented football management game. But right now, things are too chaotic for me to recommend the game to anybody.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have enjoyed this game, and will probably continue to play it for a while, I wouldn't recommend it in its current state.  There are several issues with it, and I will go into some detail about issues I have found. Keep in mind that I have played about 10 seasons in different leagues and in different nations (with different players, of course).First of all, matches certainly seem to be stacked against the human player (not surprsingly).  Regardless of the skill of your penalty takers, you will miss most of your penalties during matches, where as your opponents will almost never miss. 90th minute goals from opponents (that have never been in the match) abound, stealing wins or even draws away from you. Opponents will score on their first attack about a third of the time, your team will likely score on less than 10% of its first attacks. Red cards (or second yellows) are given for ridiculous things, like "re-entering the pitch without permission", which I'm not sure I've ever seen a card given for in my lifetime. There also seem to be commonly-used formations that do not work at all.Outside of match play, there are other issues. Recently, while playing as a English Championship club, I was able to win the League Cup. In real life, this win comes with a spot in the Europa League the next season, which is a huge plus for a Championship side because of the money that comes along with it. In this game, I somehow did not get entered into the Europa League, nor any continental competition. I realize that this is a German game and centered around German football, and I was playing in the English league, but the German League Cup winners also make the Europa League in the same manner, so this issue doesn't exist because of a difference in the leagues.Also, with the winning of the League Cup came another problem. I was in the midst of playing 5 games in 15 days, and because of the importance of the League Cup final, I pushed my players hard in the match, which went extra time, then to penalties. I did my best to substitute tired players, but the match took a lot out of them. After the match, they never physically recovered for the rest of the season. No matter what I did in practice during the week for the remainder of the season (about 10 matches), my squad of 23 players came into every match absolutely knackered. I tried resting them all week, or using active recouperation all week, but nothing I did made any difference. Two months later, when the season ended, they were still just barely making it through matches, and getting absolutely destroyed on the pitch in every match.A couple other issues I've found are having to pay for changes to club grounds on infrastructure that hasn't even been started yet (pay to "destroy" what doesn't exist, and of course, fail get the money back that you invested to place it in the first place), and not being able to ask for a raise during the length of your contract (I got promoted from League One to the Premier League during my contract, but was not offered a raise, and was expected to see the last two years of my £4810 p/w contract as a Premier League manager).While this game has some great elements and ideas, it definitely needs some work. I do enjoy it to an extent, but there is plenty of frustration as well. It does scratch the itch that I have when it comes to allowing you to run a club from the view of a chairman and manager, so I will probably continue to play it. If you are still thinking about buying it, I would suggest waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Are we Football?Let's face it: Outside of Burgerland (and even they catch up slowly), everybody loves Football. It's a real sport, so we are Football, because pretty much everybody at one time or another played it. But is this Football?I write this review in english because most so far most are german and don't help people who don't speak the language and since we're on Steam: I'm trying to help out but the first segment will sound like ancient hyroglyphs to most non-german people. Anyway, I love football, i watch it, i'm in the stadium, i'm a lifetime member of my club (1860) and i played a ton of football manager games and when i say a ton, i mean a metric ♥♥♥♥-ton of them. All of them: The entire Bundesliga Manager series, the entire Anstoss series, Hattrick (and its "we don't speak about it" sequel), Kurt and its "all grown up" Kicker sequels, english games like the Ultimate Soccer Manager series (truly the Ultimate, if it wasn't for a few dumb bugs and a lack of youth players, it would be the best of all time), the original Kevin Toms Football Manager, the later Sega Football Manager and some experiments like Teamchef and even some of the worst of the worst like Club & Country, Team Manager, Split Screen Manager....shortly: I played them all. Now, Gerald Köhler is alongside Jens Onnen and Werner Krahe (those 2 made the Bundesliga/Eishockey Manager series) one of the absolute legends of german football manager sims, he made Anstoss (up to the 3rd game) and went to the dark side of EA to make the Fussball/FIFA Manager series until it got cancelled with FM14 which was FM13 in disguise (for a full price with just updated rosters, yeah, that's EA!). And now he's back like a franchise character that can't be hold down. A new game from him. You'd think with nearly 30 years of experience (Anstoss was conceived around 1991/92, came out in late 93) he would give us the ultimate, absolutely greatest football manager there is..Well...no, if you have a turntable, put on some cheap crappy vinyl and imitate the screeching halt sound,  because it fits this perfectly.WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ HAPPENED?!You'd think this game would at least be on the level of Anstoss 3, from 2001You'd think it would have a few features from EA's Manager, considering Köhler hired a few people from that staff.But no. What you get is like the beginning of football managers. It's like Bundesliga Manager Professional (1991)But let us start from the begining: You can either choose a team directly or answer question at a breakneck pace to determine what team in the lower league would be a good start. The problem already is: You answer it, it says "3 clubs want you" but you only see 1. In Anstoss 2, 3 and every other game, you'd see all 3 offers, be able to compare them and choose but here, you basically either take offer 1 or decline untll offer 3, which might suck. This is stupid. Now one thing german football managers always sucked at was the important part: The game calculation. Even as far back as the crappy Bundesliga Manager Hattrick, most of the time, it was a random number generator that slightly takes your overall team power in consideration to compare it to the opposite team and ♥♥♥♥♥ out a score. You might win, you might lose, you never knew why you won or lose. Sega's Football Manager and even that old Ultimate Soccer Manager gave better feedback: You know if a player was too slow, wasn't good enough to mark an opponent or why the other striker could dance through your penalty area like it happened at the current Euro between Wales and Turkey. In this game here, you get nothing. Youi don't get to watch games, you don't get scenes of goals or anything ,you get no feedback at all. Instead highlights are shown as the player face with lines were the ball goes - you don't see the other team though, so you don't even know if somebody was out of position or whatever. After the game you get no stats at all either, you get a message in the newspaper that is a bout as far removed from reality as somebody who swallowed some LSD. I lose 1:2 and it says "My Tactic was perfect, the team was set up great, just unlucky", on the other hand, i win 6:0 and apparently my setup sucked, i had no "analyst" on the field and i just got lucky. WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥? If i curbstomp a team like that, nobody would call it "luck". The other areas are just as broken, You can only plan a week in advance and everything takes up hours in your calendar. You want to put some money in the bank? Takes 2 hours for no good reason. Also the games wants you to waste 2 hours to do sport on your own for no real reason.You also can't plan training in advance, you have to plan it week by week, nothing else is possible, not even outside the season. The training camp option is horrible as well. You say "Let's go to a camp" and you have to do it, but you get no feedback if it was good or bad, how players got better or whatever. Again: This is from the same guy who made EA's Manager which had futuer week planing, future training plaining and total feedback on how training went, how the camp went and all that. Even the whole stadium and club area section is just sad. In the old Football Manager games from EA you could design every aspect of the Stadium, even to the point of adding fireworks and litter. Here? Nothing, you just add rows of seats/stands/vip places and a roof and the worst thing: it looks ugly, the roof ultimately won't even cover most seats. Same with the club area, you just put down a few areas like a Gym or some "Football Tennis" area, it gets instantly built and that's it. You can't even additional pathways, so everything will just looked half-assed. So the fundamentals are totally broken, unfinished, unsatisfying and there are bugs as well. At least i hope the negotiations are bugged. Because it's ludicrous you can sell players for far more than their worth, while coercing the CPU into selling them your players for far below the market price. Even the sponsores are broken. I played a season, went up to League 2 in Germany, looked for new sponsors, now the board sponsors for the most part offered me 280,000 to 380.000 - except 2 who offered 2 and 4 million for 2 boards each. It's totally unrealistic, it made sure i went out with a profit for the entire season - and the best thing? I still couldn't negotiate more money for transfers and wages, even though i had 25 million in the bank, plus the money from those 2 offers. It's just broken and unrealistic. Also i just never actually have the feel i play a football game. Exchange the field during the "game simulation" and it could be "We are Hockey" or "We are American Handegg". Ea's Manager felt like football, thanks to the FIFA engine for games, Sega's game screams "Football!" and the older german games catched it as well, especially Anstoss had an atmosphere that made it obvious it was a "By Fans, for Fans" affair and had the mascot Pallino. This game on the other hand has the personality of a McDonald's Burger. What else is there to say: Not much to be honest. The music is atrocious, there aren't alot of sound effects, even the "games" sound weak. It was promissed to have the legendary half-time speeches from Anstoss 3 but it doesn't, except the one time you pay for a motivational speaker. I guess for total beginners to the world of football managing, the simplicity and lack of anything might be ok, it's not as overwhelming as Sega's behemoth (or any older manager), but for anybody who played the old games, this isn't worth it. Stick with Anstoss 3, EA's FM13 (both still have active communities creating current data sets) or Sega's Football Manager.Edit; Several Updates got release, which are just patchwork, they try hard to fix some of the issues while breaking other things, by now this game really is a lost cause. Updates add bugs,rarely remove any and the few "features" that get added are so small in scope, they don't even matter.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It has its issues - some bugs to be fixed and features that are missing - but I really enjoyed this direct competitor to Football Manager and found several aspects that I would love for Football Manager to take note of and possibly add their own twist to. This review is really more of a WAF vs. FM22, so I'll structure my biggest points as to which things I preferred from each game.Things I Feel WAF Does Better:- Negotiations in general are more fun and hands on. FM22 is certainly more granular when it comes to all the possible options for contracts and transfer offers, but at the cost of being a bit too opaque for all the but the most hardcore negotiators. Negotiations in WAF feel more like a minigame.- I really enjoy the passage of time in WAF, and how you need to balance your time and thus pick and choose which items you're going to address in a given week.- WAF gives you the ability to add and negotiate with sponsors directly, and I loved having direct control over this aspect.- I love having full control over both the training grounds and the stadium. In FM, your training area is a hidden number between 1 to 20 that controls how well your players train, but in WAF, you have all manner of buildings and fields with specific bonuses. Likewise, choosing when and how to expand your stadium is left up to you in WAF vs. oftentimes infuriating back and forth with your board in FM.- The UI itself feels much more accessible in WAF. While there are plenty of great skins in FM, all of them fail to achieve the kind of openness and intuitiveness that I found in WAF.Things I prefer in FM:- Attributes. For both staff and players, the single most important attribute in WAF is basically a "level" between 0 and 15 that is indicated by the number and color of stars. On the one hand, I love the simplicity and it does generate some excitement when a player or staff gains a star...but on the other, there is next to no indication of what staff/players are good at on any kind of granular level outside of a handful of skills they can unlock.- I feel much more connected to the games themselves on FM. WAF has the ability to see the stadium and plays during games, but I quickly turned it off once I realized it was just going to show me diagrams and not actual gameplay.- This is an area I hope will improve as more people play WAF, but while both games suffer from a lack of licensing, FM has a MUCH larger collection of add-ons to be able to mimic real-life teams, leagues, and tournaments. WAF has a great database editing tool that allows you to import custom databases, so I was able to play with real teams in roughly the correct league structure, but I still felt pretty disconnected calling the English leagues "1st Division", "2nd Division", and so on and without any of the correct cup titles.- Coaching licenses, work permits, cup registration restrictions, finance rules, and I'm sure plenty of others that I'm forgetting about. FM is ridiculously accurate when it comes to its depiction of the leagues, and everything I mentioned above is missing entirely from WAF. This makes WAF a bit easier to approach, but is still a net loss for those of us that appreciate really feeling like we're managing a real club.All in all, I really enjoyed my time with WAF, and would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys the genre, but after a week or two, I found myself back on FM22. I'm hopeful that this marks the beginning of a rivalry with both franchises pushing each other to be better. I definitely have room in my life for more than one football management sim.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions? Not that good but has potential.The UI is bloated and confusing, the upside is that you can delegate most of the tasks so you can just do that if you feel overwhelmed and get into it in a later date.The UI in itself feels generic and boring, did mention bloated already so you're quite busy looking for thing...you do get used to it at some point, I'm in my third season right now.A lot of quality of life improvements are due, more often than ever I found myself using the arrow keys to navigate the ListViews the UI presents just to be disappointed that you can't use arrow keys, instead I have to move and click my mouse around which is a pain and personally annoying.When setting up a Training Camp or Friendly Matches you don't have access to the Calendar, so you can't doublecheck if you're accidentally creating a friendly right before an important or busy week, only showing the date is not enough, I don't have the Calendar memorized, even if I wanted I wouldn't be able to memorize it since you don't have access to the Calendar at all.More often than ever during contract negotiations you're forced to accept the very low transfer clause players want, you can't outright remove it...only increase or decrase which takes away an action point from the negotiation per change in that one value...Things like saving formations and games doesn't let you overwrite an existing one by double clicking it, in the formation screen in particular selecting an existing formation you saved and clicking on save will NOT overwrite your existing formation, it will instead create a new one, to actually overwrite it you need to input the name on the TextBox and once you try to save it detects that the formation already exists with that name and asks to overwrite it, how annoying is that?The soundtrack lacks soul, I was expecting the kind of banger track and sound effects you'd get from Anstoss 2, instead you're left with listening to something so boring it feels like it was straight off pulled out of a royalty free playlist.CPU Opponents will quite often engage in trying to purchase your players, which I like as long the proposals are reasonable of course, keeps up the freshness of selling players and bringing new ones in for future profit, HOWEVER they almost never try to buy players you explicitly put in the transfer list for selling or loaning.As of now, can't really recommend this game, hope that with future patches it gets better, I do feel like that this has a lot of potential but is not hitting it quite right with certain choices on the UI side of things and the useability of it, Football Manager is a lot more complex but the UI is a lot easier to use and not as overwhelming, I do still play FIFA Manager with the 21 Mod Patch and that's a prime example of a clean and easy to use UI.EDITS: ##### 13.06.2 #####- Removed the portion about Transfer Budget not increasing after selling players, it increases now, maybe it was a bug or some state in memory?- Removed the portion about only doing the pre season and two matches, I'm in my third season now, what I feel hasn't really changed, the UI is bad and takes time to get used to but the game isn't horrible by any means, it's fun but not recommended in its current state

A lot of the issues players had in the beginning have been addressed and fixed through regular updates or will be addressed in future updates,It does not have official licensing but that is actually a positive in my opinion as it gives a more immersive feeling of an alternate football universe where you can lead your low-level team to international glory.Not as much depth as SI's manager with all the stats and info, obviously, but it has some nice gimmicks like the infrastructure and back-office options. And the game does not take itself too seriously so you can expect a few humorous things here and there.Overall a superb game and highly recommended if you like management and / or football games. _childDocuments_.review: I'm leaving a positive review because I would like to encourage the development of this game and others like this one.I have been a hardcore Football Manager gamer since it was called Championship Manager, and before that I used to play games like PC Fútbol (PC Calcio, PC Premier...) and Ultimate Soccer manager, so, been playing this genre since around 1995.I haven't bought any new Football Manager games since FM2015 because I don't think the upgrade is worth it. It's essentially the same exact game every year and I'm tired of the super repetitive press conferences and all the flaws the game has always had. Plus, it gets boring once you kinda settle with your tactics and just keep hiring or developing the new best player for each position. FM series doesn't allow you to play the game in the rol of a club manager, so you have nothing to say about marketing, merchandising, finances, stadium, academy and so on, which are truly thrilling parts of football that were widely covered by PC Futbol, Ultimate Soccer Managers and other games back in the 90s.To me, it is simply absurd that for the past 20 years we haven't had one decent game about football club management besides the Total Club Manager series, long dead since EA decided to kill it. So, this is what We Are Football is trying to fix, and that's why I bought the game in the first place.As many other reviewers mention here, the game  has the right idea, but it's still far from being a truly enjoyable game, in my opinion. I won't take too long reviewing it. On the positive side, the game looks nice, is not hard to play, has an enjoyable and immersive music, and has everything that Football Manager is missing: you can build your stadium, negotiate with sponsors, hire or sell players, manage the economy of your club and so on.On the negative side, the interface is just hard to manage. Everything is somewhat organized around your weekly schedule, which you have to determine beforehand. This is trying to give you the feeling of being an actual manager of a club, but I don't think this is a good approach, since club managers don't actually take care of every little thing by themselves. They are presented with different options and they get to decide, so dropping this scheduled organization would be a better approach for me, just like the old PC Futbol or Ultimate Soccer Manager did.Besides, the match engine is very lacking. Most players won't mind having a 2D layout just like Football Manager had for years, as long as they can get a grasp on their tactics. However, in its current state, this part of the game doesn't even meet the basics and is just truly lacking. Also, since the games are quite dull and hard to watch, it feels even worse having to spend several minutes for each match just staring at what is basically nothing, simply waiting for the game to end.Despite all this, however, I think this game could become something much better and is on the right track, so I'm hoping to play it again maybe a year from now and check on its progress. And I recommend anyone interested to give it a spin and keep an eye on it as a potential Football Manager alternative.Don't pay the full price for this game, however. I bought it on sale for around €26 and it still was way too expensive for what the game actually is in its current state, which is what I have refunded it. Either becomes a game as enjoyable as Total Club Manager, in which case it would be worth €35, or is sold for the right price for what it truly is right now, which to me would be around €10.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I would like to start off by saying that I never write reviews for anything, but this game has made me want to. We are Football is a great game if you understand what this game is. I feel like a lot of people want to compare this game to Football Manager and that's the wrong idea. This game does not focus so much on the tactical aspect of every match like Football Manager. WAF focuses more on the overall development of a club (ie. designing the stadium, deciding ticket prices, finding sponsors, etc). We are Football is a much more casual game when compared to FM and that is what I really like about it. I love soccer/football, but after a long day at work, I do not want to come home and play a game where I have to meticulously decide tactics for a team (I am looking at you FM). We are Football still allows me to enjoy my love of football, but not have to be so intense about my every move. If you want an alternative to Football Manager that offers a different experience, then I highly recommend WAF. However, if you absolutely love the tactical aspect of FM, then this may not be the game for you. If you want a new experience with managing a football club, then give this game a try!On a side note: WAF does not have licenses, but this can be easily remedied with the FM-Zocker mod which actually has a total of 86 countries you can manage in around the world.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the football game I've been waiting for. I've played a lot of FM, but it is a manager/coach game where as this is an owner/manager game. I also am really enjoying the skill tree for players, it is more fun and rewarding to craft a player in this way than how training works in FM. For a career taking a club from the lower divisions up to the top, I think WAF have the right game design that gives me the freedom to make investment decisions to support what they want to achieve while making the training of the next generation of players more engaging.This game also feels like a game - it's fun, doesn't feel like a spreadsheet, and has lots of depth. _childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable game not to be compared to Football Manager. As a game in its own rights it is great, yes its rough around the edges for example the gimmicky things are not needed like sabotage of a match, building things like directors house in facilities and such these things are not needed and make the game almost childish. The game would really benefit from a 3d match engine although saying that the stadium view and facilities need a graphical overhaul, stadiums at the moment just look all out of perspective with the stands and corners all massively oversized but the roof not getting any bigger as the stand grows. this game has been made great with the edition of mods to update team names/badges and updated league positions. having randomly generated players hasn't bothered me in the slightest. i think if there are any newer versions in the pipeline then they should take influence from the FiFA Manager Games of years gone by namely the EA SPORTS FA Premier League Manager 2002 game which was by far the best in this game type. the range of building and stadium types you could build were fantastic and something i would like to see this game develop into.Tactically the game feels good and it feels like the decisions you make influence a game, team talks for me seem to a be pointless task tho. moving players freely around the pitch is great. overall i think they have made a great game that is FUN and not a second job like other manager type games, season can be quick but but also take time with all the facility/stadium/sponsors and such that needs attention. i hope this game keeps going with new releases and more improvements in the right direction going forward. i know i will purchase newer versions if they come along.
