_childDocuments_.review: I can highly recommend We Are Football. It's just fun to turn a small club into a big international top club and to have all the powers in your hands, from the first team to the second team and youth team to the expansion of the stadium and club grounds to disputes with club members and much more.The overall focus here is more on the long-term development of a club, mostly through good management, appropriate transfers, youth work, etc.  It is not necessary to deal intensively with tactics and individual instructions before every game.However, if you like just that and dislike everything else than tactics and training, you are probably better off somewhere else. So you shouldn't compare the game with Football Manager, because it has a different focus. If you like original licences and want to have all the real club crests, player names and pictures, etc., I can only recommend the fan patch from FM-Zocker (just google it), which enhances the game considerably and ensures immersion! _childDocuments_.review: If you liked the Anstoss series, this game is for you!It's a well made mix between Anstoss, the EA FM and Sega FM.In this game you'll progress through a season a lot quicker than in the Sega FM and your main focus is the long term development of the club, instead of spending hours per matchday.Some negative reviews state that the match engine is bad, because you can't see the whole pitch but only the active player. While that is factually true, it's not a bad thing at all because it takes some of the complexity out of the game.Same story for the player stats. Instead of having 20-30 stats to analyse, you'll just be presented with some of the strengths and weaknesses of the players.This game keeps it simple, and that's great!Huge thanks to Gerald Köhler and his team for this game, we've been waiting for this for so long!PS: Don't forget to install a fan patch to have a fully "licensed" game (like the one from FM Zocker)!

_childDocuments_.review: While this pup draws a lot of its ideas from the older football management games (looking at titles like the old Premier Manager series or FA Premier League Manager/Total Club Manager), somehow manages to be somewhat worse than those.The ideas are there, but the execution feels cheap and unnecessary complicated by the poorly designed UI. It's not a bad game, it's actually a decent football management game, one in which you are actually a manager and not simply a bloody coach (Championship Manager/Football Manager series style). But it still needs a lot of work. As this is the first game from a new studio, i am probably more forgiving, as i hope that a new entry in what i hope is a new football management game series would solve most of the grievances we have with the game. I would love to put a recommended note there, but i can't just do it in good faith. So far now, it's a negative. But i might change it after more updates.

_childDocuments_.review: **UPDATE**So after 13 Updates it seems to be a time for an short update:The positive feedback still stays and if i could I would gibe the game an even bigger thumbs up now:1. The team is working consistently on bugs and new features. They are listening to the community and do their best to include their wishes.2.  All but one of my negative points were addressed and greatly improved.3. The remaining one being the difficulty of the game: It is still, and probably will remain, an easy game. As mentioned before this is not inherently bad; I do enjoy this difficulty a lot, but hardcore lovers of the fm franchise may be disappointed.So without any more words: Buy and enjoy it, so we can get a lot more great updates and see a We are Football 2 in the future!**Original Review:**So, first of all: This games receives a positive feedback because it is a lot of fun. And by a lot I mean a whole lot of fun. For me it is a much appreciated counterpart to the football manager, which is also great but can get a bit tedious. Let's start with the positives:+ I really like the UI. Espacially in comparison to the fm: More colourfull, more icons; just overall more fun to luck at+ The different areas you can interact with+ Personally, I really enjoy the match display. I don't need a 3d match, since it always looks and feels clunky at best+ the fast paced gameplayThe negatives:- The match calculations seem a bit off: Positioning of players doesn't feel right, Participation of a single player in a play at different points looks like he might be using a portal over the field- Player prices: I am able to sell my players at really really good prices and on the other side to purchase players at really really low prices. That makes it way too easy to replace large if not the whole team as you like and improve it- Match results: The game seems to favour you when calculating the matches. It feels to easy: I started as Eintracht Frankfurt and won the championship. Another game I got contracted in the german 3rd league which had the object to avoid relegation. Instead i achieved second place and now I am playing the 2nd league. There again havong the objective to avoid relegation I am currently ranking at 6th place just one point behind 2nd place.- Overall feedback of game elements is missing- Buildings are built instantly- The week has to be interceptable: As I am getting older my memory is getting worse; having multiple player interactions on monday how am I supposed to remember after a full week and a game what I wanted to do or what I told himFeature whishes:- Manager area. Please let me do something with the money I earn- Let me save right before a game

In WAF all you see is a ball pinging around with small details of commentary. These days a decent management game needs a match engine. FM and even FIFA and Soccer Manager have upped their game in the last decade or so and have included a decent match engine, Whilst the developers of FM have acknowledged the faults of the ME, they have listened to the fans and are making a complete brand new game for FM25. _childDocuments_.review:
As a manager and trainer in WE ARE FOOTBALL, you'll come face to face with the latest trends in the world of football, experiencing all the emotional highs and lows of your favorite club.

For the first time ever, this modern football manager game also offers a women's football game mode, featuring all the same functionality as well as many unique gameplay elements. To maintain and ensure the highest quality across all game modes, WE ARE FOOTBALL has been developed with experienced football management veterans such as Gerald Kohler, Rolf Langenberg, and Dirk Winter.

WE ARE FOOTBALL focuses on real management tasks. The goal of the game is to build up the club over the long haul, including growing the team, colleagues, infrastructure, fans, and more. As a result, the football players in the game are individual personalities who spin their own stories.

detailed_description: Resident Evil Village Gold Edition Experience survival horror like never before in the eighth major installment in the storied Resident Evil franchise - Resident Evil Village. The Gold Edition includes: - Resident Evil: Village game - Winters' Expansion additional content - Trauma Pack DLC - Access to RE:VERSE online game Note: Resident Evil: Village and the Trauma Pack DLC will become playable upon the release of the Gold Edition on 28/10/2022. The Village of Shadows unlock included in the Trauma Pack allows access to content which is otherwise unlockable through gameplay progress. Details of the service period for RE:VERSE can be found on the official website. The service period may have already concluded, so please check before purchasing. Access to Re:Verse may become available through other means at a later date. Set a few years after the horrifying events in the critically acclaimed Resident Evil 7 biohazard, the all-new storyline begins with Ethan Winters and his wife Mia living peacefully in a new location, free from their past nightmares. Just as they are building their new life together, tragedy befalls them once again. FEATURES • First-Person Action – Players will assume the role of Ethan Winters and experience every up-close battle and terrifying pursuit through a first-person perspective. • Familiar Faces and New Foes – Chris Redfield has typically been a hero in the Resident Evil series, but his appearance in Resident Evil Village seemingly shrouds him in sinister motives. A host of new adversaries inhabiting the enigmatic village will relentlessly hunt Ethan and hinder his every move as he attempts to make sense of the new nightmare he finds himself in. • A Living, Breathing Village – More than just a mysterious backdrop for the horrifying events that unfold in the game, the village is a character in its own right with mysteries for Ethan to uncover and terrors to escape from. _childDocuments_.review: First, Resident Evil 7 blew me away and has had a personal impact on me.I wanna share this on the slight chance that a developer, or someone at Capcom, may possibly see this; so that I can say thank you. At the time that I played that game, I was dealing with the personal trauma of coming out of an abusive and toxic relationship, and fear and pain were feelings that were nothing but familiar to me. I was at a point in my life where I couldn't see the light at the end of the tunnel. Pushing forward, as well as courage, were necessary steps in my life that I knew I needed to take. While I dealt with this situation mostly through therapy and other forms of help, videogames were one of my ways of finding some comfort. Ethan's story of being an average guy who has to fight fear head-on and overcome obstacles, oddly enough, has had a huge impact on me. Ethan saving his wife from the baker family gave me the courage to fight my own personal pain.Now that's out of the way Ethan returns better, stronger, and with a few more funny one-liners. From the trailers and the footage, I was very confused about what the heck was going on. Needless to say, I was so intrigued by the mystery. (MAJOR SPOILERS ahead for resident evil 7 and 8)  I could go on and on about the story but I think you get the point.The gameplay is fantastic with tight gameplay. No filler, everything is in the game for a reason. The story, is something that should go down in history from start to finish this game is a masterpiece. In conclusion, not only does Village shine on its own as a highpoint in the franchise, but it is the perfect follow-up to a game that is very important to me.  Thank you Capcom.

Later on the merchant will even offer the player special Health and Ability upgrades through cooking found animals.Upon finishing the game one can unlock Mercs Mode. This time around Mercenaries mode has the player fighting through multiple areas per stage with the store to buy from and random perks scattered through the areas in that stage. _childDocuments_.review: It's not as good as RE7, but taken as a whole, the Ethan Winters duology is a strong two-punch return to form from Capcom. The lore and series continuity is as convoluted and as contrived as ever, and I can't help but wonder if 7 could've been their chance to do a complete reboot -- it tried the soft reboot thing with a new first person perspective, a new protagonist in Winters, and taking cues from the likes of Kojima's P.T. and more recent flavours of horror (instead of originally ripping off Romero's zombie canon) but the Umbrella connection is still shoehorned in, Chris still shows up, and it still follows the Mikami formula of tension and dread in an enclosed space >> which opens up to a larger space as more puzzles and combat is laid on >> finally a climatic shoot-out in a high tech lab or some such, etc. Not that any of this matters with how loosey goosey RE can be in its own storytelling logic (and who plays RE for the story amirite).Ethan Winters is a bit more compelling as a protagonist this time around and the Shadows of Rose DLC is a nice coda to it, to say nothing of its smart reuse of 8's assets, as I felt even Capcom knew they underutilized the fantastic Castle & Beneviento maps, the latter of which gets a chance to truly shine in its redux.The Steam/PC version is a mixed bag. If you install RE Framework or similar mods to say, unlock the FoV, you may run into system instability like I did (perhaps caused by Denuvo rearing its ugly head if you have the DLC installed?). And really that console level FoV of like, 10, is inexcusable for a PC port in 2023. Playing on KB+M always feels off, while the controls on gamepad aren't great either (something to do with mouse acceleration or some such, IDK). Enabling RT will cut your framerate down by a lot, and offers subtle but barely noticeable differences to my untrained eye, so I'd say leave it off. Lack of Nvidia DLSS support, or an updated version of AMD FSR (stuck on 1.0), or hell, Intel XeSS is also unfortunate. Capcom will go through the effort of having sliders that show the performance impact of each setting on your system components -- great! -- but then bizarrely make you click RMB to back out of its options menu instead of using Esc, or bind Ctrl by default as a Use key instead of crouch -- wth??Can't say I'm optimistic for RE9, knowing Capcom's history with this series, but 8 isn't any worse than previous games and is a strong, if uneven entry.

_childDocuments_.review: Some misconceptions about RE8!1. “Short game or it’s 8 hours only.” This is straight up WRONG. The game can easily take more than 12 hours to finish. Some even beat it in more than that. The in-game timer literally lies to you, if you’ve played 12 hours, it will tell you that you spent 7 or 8 hours. RE8 has more exploration and side optional in-game content more than any previous RE game. It’s easily one of the longest RE games. It’s got a perfect length for an RE game, not to mention that it has post-game content and good replay value.2. “It’s not scary.” hella WRONG! This game has different types of horror. From RE7 type of horror, to RE4 (panicking), and to Silent Hill / PT level of horror + other types. In fact, one section in the game has probably the scariest and creepiest moment in the entire franchise.3. “It’s RE4+RE7.” This is TRUE, but it also has inspirations from almost every RE game. The game feels like it’s a celebration for RE’s 25th anniversary.I’ve enjoyed my time playing it and I think it’s A MUST BUY for every RE fan or a survival horror fan.- Easily and by a huge margin, RE8 is the best looking RE game ever. It's INCREDIBLY detailed, well designed and STUNNING to look at.- Very atmospheric, and its got a lot of variety in that aspect as well.- Sound design is also the best in the series. The intro is horrifying!- From the first few hours, you'll quickly notice how big and diverse the game is.- Levels are intricately crafted, with more ways to explore them. Really liked how the village was structured with more ways to explore and search its houses.- The game INSANELY nails the interior design of its levels; I find myself stopping every 5 mins or so just to absorb the beauty of it all.- The game's setting really makes you feel like you're playing in a horror themed amusement park.- There is clear emphasis on exploration and side content.- The game allows you to take control of your own pacing at certain sections. It’s not really a linear game. It has more freedom and exploration than previous RE games as I mentioned before, which I liked very much!- The game does a really good job of changing its intensity from time to time. Presenting different types of horror along the way, mixing them up with action / adventure elements & sequences while still being within its survival horror medium. It’s well balanced, diverse and refreshing.- RE8 has some of the highest highs in the franchise. When it hits, it hits real good. :D- NO LOADING TIMES. That's a technical marvel considering the quality of its graphics, level design and performance. RE Engine strikes again!- Puzzles are fun and rewarding.- Backtracking here is the most fun and rewarding in all of the RE games.- Music is top tier.- The merchant is cool.- The story is intriguing and thrilling.- The characters are some of the best in the series. Really interesting, very well acted and fun to watch. Not including Ethan though lol, however he's honestly better this time.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil is one of my favorite game franchises of all time, but RE8 is pretty low on my teir list.It is so slow and boring. Enemies move slowly and you are encouraged to abuse furniture to make enemies walk around like idiots. The game is also constantly taking away control from the player and making them watch some slow animation like looking at blood on your hand, or flipping a switch, or turning a crank. There are also a ton of scripted sections and/or cutscenes, and skipping them is painful because it does the crap where you can't open the pause menu to skip until you are several seconds into the cutscene (probably cause loading or something). It just overall feels like a massive slog to play through.The game is nonsensical. The story is always ridiculous in RE games, but RE8 just doesn't strike the right tone. It isn't campy. It isn't scary. I just found it dumb and I don't care about it whatsoever. Heisenberg and the Duke were decent, but I hated all the other characters. It has a lot of gore and is intending to be shocking, but the gore is so over-the-top and non-stop that it is often more comically bad than anything else. Why would I be scared of this enemy in front of me when I just survived multiple fatal wounds in the cutscene 5 seconds ago? The amount of gore goes way too far and has a very negative effect for what the game is going for.Here are some games on Steam in the same genre I would recommend over RE8:- Resident Evil 2 (remake)- Resident Evil 3 (remake)- Resident Evil 4- Resident Evil 5- Resident Evil 6- Resident Evil Revelations 2- Ghostbusters Remastered- Dead Space- Last of UsHere are some additional Steam recommendations over RE8, but these are farther away from RE8's genre:- Control - Tomb Raider (modern Square Enix Trilogy)- Uncharted- Vanquish

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village, and I must say that it exceeded all my expectations. This game masterfully combines an immersive and captivating narrative with refined mechanics, creating an unforgettable gaming experience.The narrative is intricately woven, keeping players on the edge of their seats with every twist and turn. It expertly blends horror, mystery, and even elements of folklore, creating a chilling atmosphere that keeps players engaged from start to finish.The characters in Resident Evil Village are memorable and well-developed, each with their own distinct personalities and motivations. The game's antagonist, Lady Dimitrescu, became an iconic figure even before the game's release, and rightfully so. Her imposing presence and the enigmatic nature of her vampiric family add an extra layer of intrigue to the game's narrative. And let's not forget the splendid performance by Neil Newbon, who just nailed Heisenberg's eccentric and daring nature.The game strikes a fine balance between exploration, combat, and puzzle-solving, providing a satisfying gameplay loop, . The first-person perspective intensifies the feeling of vulnerability and helps immerse players in the game's unsettling world.The addition of the merchant, Duke, provides a welcome respite from the horrors, allowing players to upgrade their weapons and replenish their supplies.Unfortunately, the Beneviento Mansion suffers from a lack of random events, that could make the encounter a little bit more startling and scary. If you played the story once, I believe you will not feel the same way. I played the game for 5 times and did every challenge, except for 3, and had fun all those runs. I highly recommend the game if you want to experience a wonderful story with engaging puzzles and mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I wasn't interested in this game but when I heard it continues from RE7, I felt that I had to play it to see what more story they would have with Ethan. There's a lot of twists and turns but overall I felt that the story was alright. There's a lot for discussions in terms of lore and what's coming for RE9.I had a problem with the game at the very beginning. The game's FoV is set to 81 and Capcom for some inane reason decided to not add a FoV slider. According to some people, this helps make the game more scary. Excuse me while I go puke in the toilet from the motion sickness. I'm used to playing First-Person games with at least 90+ FoV so having the FoV that low made me incredibly nauseous. I had to go and download a external mod made by the community called Lazy FoV and Vignette Fix from ModNexus and no more motion sickness. The game itself, in my opinion, suffers from an identity crisis. It tries to be scary but that ends in 15 minutes of the beginning. Seriously it goes from night-time so dark you can't see ahead without a flashlight to daybreak and then daylight the entire game through. You just run through the place and shoot monsters. You should play this on Hardcore because then the 'Survival' part of the game comes in full effect while managing your ammo. You can shoot at the monsters' legs to stun them while you pull out your knife for some free damage or even kill to save ammo. There are 'puzzles' in the game but they're so simple that I not sure if I like it or not. To be fair I wouldn't really want to get stuck in a puzzle for 10+ minutes when I could be enjoying the story but I digress. Simple puzzles. There's a stage in the game where you have to run and hide in a closet or under the bed. That part was pretty interesting. When I opened the closet and saw nothing inside, I tried to step in it and close the door. To my surprise, it worked and I thought, "There's going to be a run-and-hide section. Alright."Then it's just back to shooting, more shooting, throw a few explosives, and shoot some more. The protagonist, Ethan, which should be prey felt more like the Terminator instead. You don't die and you carry a couple or three pistols, a shotgun or two, a bolt action sniper rifle that uses 7.62mm, and plenty of explosives on you. I want to complain about a section of the game later on which you use a cannon that's literally welded in place with a few screws and bits and pieces of metal... more than once. Physics begone! Overall the story was interesting, the gameplay's there and it's whatever. If you've played RE5, RE7, RE2 remake, you'll know what to expect. One thing I like though is that the crafting materials have their own separate inventory like The Last of Us which was a huge problem in RE7 trying to manage the inventory. The game has its own immersion and immersion breaking things like monsters dropping money or crafting materials. Whatever. You're not provided with any military-grade weapons until you beat the game which you unlock in the Extra Contents shop: The Dragoon (Which should be a AN-94 or something of similar) and the WCX (MCX, a 5.56 assault rifle). There's also the USM (USP) and the kramabit. They're really powerful for Standard difficulty and Hardcore is about just right. For the hardest difficulty, Village of Shadows which you unlock by beating the game or pay more money, it's truly about Survival of the Fittest. I've beaten the game on Standard and I'll go back into it on Hardcore. I enjoy popping heads with the sniper rifle.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Resident Evil 8, where Capcom once again try to physically break a divergent path in their story back into line with the rest of the canon, even though everyone has been happy with the ending of certain plot points 3 games ago. Also witness as Capcom try their hardest to explain away the complete apathetic attitude and utter invulnerability of their new main protagonist in a so-called twist which sees the head of everyone who witnesses it turn 142 degrees in a direction though impossible in utter disbelief. Aside from this, behold a game which takes what RE7 does for it’s gameplay, improves on it, give you a bigger area to walk around in, more weapons to slap ♥♥♥♥ around with but still keeps pulling from its past games for every single one of its ideas. Old ideas, done very well.In this game you will be fighting the following:•	Furries•	Bigger furries•	Hammer furries•	Meth addicts•	The gargoyle gremlin from Gremlins 2: The New Batch•	Aggressive gardeners •	The Internet’s new waifus for the week•	Silent Hill’s cast off•	Raggidolls•	Your fish supper from last week•	Meth addicts hired by Facebook•	Wolfenstein’s  Supersoldaten•	A B52 bomber on legs•	Jim Carey’s Dr RobotnikThe majority of the game’s first run will be trying to figure out where the hell you are going, fighting off attacks from one or more of the above and cackling in laughter as you watch Ethan get battered, thrown and mutilated throughout. Not much has changed from RE7, it’s still first person, you still can only have 4 weapons in your hot-swap bar at any one time, you craft ammo and healing items out of stuff you find on the ground. Adding to this is a health dose of RE4 mechanics. Enemies drops stuff, ammo, craftables and money, the inventory system is a straight copy of RE4’s attaché case and there is a merchant dotted around the area that you buy things from, never explains how he’s able to move around as quick as he can (Which is even more impressive given this guy’s size) and allows upgrading of your weaponry.  It all comes together to make a game which is functionally good and works… mostly. Odd glitch here and there, but it works.The story is… typical Resident Evil. As said before, RE8 is trying to break what was done in RE7 into line with the rest of the canon. There was something said way back when in a Zero Punctuation video on a RE game, RE 5 I think. RE had a twisted mess of plot threads and non sensical stuff, then made a game only tangentially related to that mess. It sells gang busters, and the next game follows up on that, but then bogs down the narrative with all the mess from the previous games. That last game was RE4. Then e had RE5, which really should have finished off the whole ‘Umbrella’ arc, and then RE6 which was RE 6 and had Neo Umbrella and bioterrorist dinosaurs and we do not talk about it. Then, we get RE7. Fresh take on the series, tangentially related story wise to the previous games. And now we have RE8, which tries to shoehorn the previous game’s canon in like a demented baby trying to push its own bulbous head into a square hole two inches wise. You can see the strains, and the contrivances are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous. Capcom needs to make this the underline point. They have a world where bioterrorism exists. They have the opportunity to do something fresh with it. They almost made it this time but could not help themselves and had to go back to their crutches. As well as that, the whole deal with Ethan is hinted at throughout the game, but the big reveal actually had me stop playing for five minutes before saying ‘That is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid’. One story beat does have me interested in what I am hoping is the DLC and not the next main game, but only time will tellAll in all, this is as close gameplay wise as you’re going to get to RE 4 in the modern age. It’s an enjoyable game to run and re-run, trying to blast past bosses and obstacles with New Game Plus and the god like arsenal you acquire, or start fresh on harder difficulties with self-imposed rules. Aside from one or two characters, however, there is not a lot of charm in the characters that would make this a 100% RE4-like for me. Ethan is still a brick with an affinity to reject fall damage. Chris has not changed since RE5,. The internet’s latest waifu, giant vampire lady, has presence for the short time he’s around but it is short. The other bosses are given even less screen time aside from Heisenberg (Who is given about the same amount of time as Vampire Lady) and the overall antagonist is just… there, really. The Duke, the vendor for the game, is the only one with any sort of charm that you can like and you actually want to know more about him.Overall recommended game if you want something to enjoy for gameplay but don’t care on story

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is a survival horror game developed and published by Capcom. The game was released in 2021 and is the eighth main entry in the Resident Evil series.One of the things that I really appreciate about Resident Evil Village is the way that it builds on the foundations of the series while still feeling fresh and new. The game introduces a new protagonist, Ethan Winters, and a new setting, a mysterious European village overrun by supernatural enemies. The game's gameplay is a mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat, with players needing to use their wits and resources to survive.The game's environments and character models are top-notch, with the game's creepy village setting and its varied cast of enemies being particularly memorable. The game's story is also engaging, with a plot that keeps players guessing until the very end.Overall, I would highly recommend Resident Evil Village to fans of the series or to anyone who enjoys survival horror games. The game's immersive atmosphere, well-done environments, and engaging story make it a standout title in the genre.

In the initial game settings, you will be asked to pick a play style to be first person or third person. Do yourself a favor and keep it first person. Great for the atmosphere, and matches the RE7 vibes. This game is like they took the best parts of all the previous installments and lovingly put it all together in this one. The village really reminds me of playing RE4, at least in the beginning. The environments are constantly changing, there's lots of treasure to backtrack and find, and the characters are unique! Also shoutout for fixing Chris's appearance versus his RE7 look. Ethan only grew as a character in this one, quickly becoming a personal favorite for being down to earth while exceedingly out of this world. _childDocuments_.review: Due to a lack of AAA games this year due to the pandemic, Resident Evil Village is one of the saving grace for 2021. The game is an absolute classic as it succeeds in balancing survival horror, which we saw in the first three Resident Evil games, with fun and engaging gameplay from Resident Evil 4. The story was good and I appreciate how this game resolves most of the plot holes left by Resident Evil 7. One of the nitpicks that I would like to add is the underwhelming and uninspiring villains. Besides Lady Dimitrescu and Heisenberg, the other bosses felt mediocre as they didn't get a long screen time compared to the previous two. _childDocuments_.review: The first half of this game is a true horror and design masterpiece. 10/10. It can't be faulted. It will go down in video game history as a legitimate testament to the medium.After that, it gets quite a bit more action-oriented, more about combat and weapons etc- however, it is still incredibly good, and it never really sacrifices the horror and tension for the combat side of things for any longer than a short time at most.*Nothing* in this game feels cheap. Everything has a very high level of polish and you can tell that everything was designed with a lot of testing and thought involved. Each and every section of the level has amazing detail, interactions and graphical fidelity.The story is really enjoyable. If you are a fan of the RE-series and the previous games, you will most likely enjoy this one. Without revealing any spoilers, the return of Chris is great and I think that the development of Mia and Ethan's story in this game is also really well done. The character designs here are some of the most creative and unique we have ever seen in the RE franchise.It is hard to find any real complaints. Obviously there *should* be an FOV slider included at launch. I think that launching a game without one of these in 2021 is completely crazy and ludicrous. I played through almost the entire game using the community-made FOV mod and I had no problems. Another slight complaint I have is that some of the boss-type enemies feel quite damage-spongy. This might just be a problem with my combat approaches, though. I played on Standard difficulty.Overall, definitely give this game a go if you are a fan of horror, Resident Evil, and good stories. You won't be let down.

_childDocuments_.review: Update to Notice: A patch has been released, and the stuttering issue has been fixed!On to the review. This is a fantastic Resident Evil game, in my opinion. It pulls very heavily from a few other titles in the franchise, most notably 4 and 7. It uses the elements it pulls from the prior entries to great effect, and really builds on the solid foundation that was laid by 7.The story, while a bit cheesy, was really enjoyable. Some of the dialogue was a bit goofy, but I was heavily engaged throughout my time with the game and it was a fun ride start to finish. The handling of Ethan was great, and it gave him much more of a personality than he had in 7. He truly felt like a character, rather than a vessel for the player. The conclusion was satisfying, if somewhat predictable. Overall, big ups to the writing team because they did some great work. There is some fantastic info hidden in the notes, too, and it really helped build up the image of the Village, and added depth to the big bads.Gameplay wise, this is a truly fantastic successor to 7. The overall feel is much the same, but the guns felt weightier, and Ethan feels a bit less stiff during combat. Village also does a fantastic job at having you bounce between weapons, as ammo can become scarce within moments. Conservation is key, and knowing how and when to use your knife to it's fullest potential will save your behind in later sections. Enemy design and AI is more varied and well done than in 7, leading to even single enemy encounters being more engaging. There are some cheese strats. but that's to be expected of just about any game and I don't feel that it detracts from the experience in any way.Bonus content is a bit lacking, as this game has no DLC at the time of the review, but what is included in the game (NG+, VoS difficulty, The Mercenaries, and progression earned from in-game achievements/goals) are a lot of fun. The game continues long standing series traditions by giving you bonus weapons for replays after meeting some requirements, and gives you ways to unlock infinite ammo for your favorites which is always welcome. A small touch that I love is the fact that weapon progression is carried between purchase and sale, so if you sell the base handgun for room in your inventory but choose to buy it back later you'll still have the upgrades you purchased for it. Overall, the game is fantastic, and I highly recommend for both series veterans, people who only enjoyed some of the later entries, or those of you who only enjoyed 7. If you're looking for an entry point to the series, I recommend 7 more, but because you can get caught up on the key notes of the story if you haven't played 7 you can definitely start here too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was well worth the wait! The story was a very amazing and ambitious one, the gameplay was so much fun with some awesome FPS shooting mechanics, the antagonists and monster design had so much variety, I had to buy the models of all the characters and enemies as well as every single concept art in the item shop so I can admire how much work the dev team put into the character design and environments. I loved all the monsters and enemies in this game so much more than the Molded from Resident Evil 7. Speaking of which, I'll be honest, I think this game tops Resident Evil 7 by a landslide. I really hope there is DLC released in the future for this game because I WILL BUY IT. If DLC is released, I'd really love to see each DLC centered on each antagonist featured in Resident Evil Village because if you aren't aware at this point, without spoiling anything, there are multiple antagonists that are all so distinct and have much more potential that little story DLCs can be done to add more to these characters and the lore and to expand their backstories and character development, and maybe they can even add another game mode like Mercenaries, or something completely different to add more replay value to the game. I have one idea for what they can do, and I'll try to say it without spoiling anything. There is a certain "inanimate" object as a villain in the game that I'd love to see some kind of terrifying bonus mode based around (anyone who has played the game already knows exactly what I'm talking about).Overall, I absolutely loved this game! Capcom did an outstanding job with this game! If you're an Resident Evil fan, a fan of Survival Horror, or a fan of games in general, I'd recommend this game 100%! Worth every penny. And like I said, I hope Capcom adds story DLCs in the future, or at the very least, extra DLC modes. This is definitely one game I'd buy extra content for. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun little game to play. I did buy it on sale, but even if it was the full $60, i probably still would have not minded paying full price. The game is mostly survival horror, in that it's really only survival bc you have to shoot things to survive, unlike other types of survival games where you have to do more than shoot things to survive. If you're an RE fan, honestly, this game plays very similarly to some of the first games or RE7: one large environment where you solve puzzles and kill things to open up new locations and progress through the story, with the occasional entities that you can't kill until it comes time where you can kill them. And, just to make a quick note: the available screenshots should be evidence enough, but clearly the game is very beautiful and detailed.That said, at one point you actually get to play as Chris and this was just a lovely change in play, where before you were struggling to exist, with chris you can just mow them down. It was what felt like a fun little mini-game inside the greater game, and i did enjoy it. The only thing I have not enjoyed so far: the mercenaries mini-games. This is because sometimes the monsters don't spawn if you are moving through the areas too quickly, and will have to back out of the area and re-enter it. For a game that basically wants you to finish the levels with as much time left as possible, it makes it really hard to do that. The mercenaries needs fixed to ensure things spawn no matter what.Also, all those houseplants not being dead in the start of the game was very unbelievable and broke the immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: I found it enjoyable. Overall, I loved the experience. In most games, when I replay them, there are moments where I just say to myself "Here comes an annoying part." I've played this 4 times now and never really felt it like that. I just have a few critiques about this game:1. The graphics are amazing, until it comes to water and the slime-like substance from Moraeu - it turns into a blurry mess and at times, just looks like a color with no texture. Speaking of graphics, I noticed that there is dynamic resolution. I don't know if it's because I'm using Ray Tracing, but even at 1080p I can see textures pixel-ate when I move around. When I stop moving around, it becomes high definition again. It's not always noticeable, but it is more often than I'd like.2. The performance issues are quite annoying. Most of the time, I maintain a good 50-60 FPS, but there were moments where it would drop to 10-20 and would remain there until I reload the game.3. For being a "survival horror" game, it sure lacks the "horror." Don't get me wrong, it has it's moments that made me a little scared my first play through, but only at the beginning. Mainly the introduction to the Village and Beneviento. Everything after that just felt like action, especially the end. After Beneviento, all horror seemed to disappear. I thought I was playing Call of Duty for a minute. One way to counteract the horror part is to play on Hardcore or "Village of Shadows." Enemies are actually a threat on those difficulties, and it brings the terror back into the game when you're being attacked.4. When you beat the game on "Village of Shadows," you're able to get the Rocket Pistol from the Extra Content Shop. I felt is was a bit under-powered for shooting rockets. It would still take 7 shots or so to kill a Lycan on "Village of Shadows." On standard, it took 2 rockets to kill a Lycan. It was a great experience, I would definitely recommend it to a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is a game that's not to be missed. Its stunning visuals and immersive storyline will keep you hooked from start to finish. The characters are well-crafted, each with their own unique backstory and personality, and the voice acting is top-notch, adding to the overall immersive experience of the game.The gameplay is a perfect mix of action, exploration, and puzzle-solving that will keep you on your toes. The combat system is smooth and intuitive, making it easy to take down enemies. The exploration aspect of the game is also great, with hidden secrets and items waiting to be uncovered throughout the village. The puzzles are challenging but not overly difficult, adding to the overall enjoyment of the game.The storyline is one of the standout features of Resident Evil Village. It's engaging, suspenseful, and full of unexpected twists and turns that will keep you on the edge of your seat. The game also pays homage to previous Resident Evil games, making it a must-play for long-time fans of the series.The variety of enemies that players face is another great aspect of the game. From werewolves to vampires, each enemy requires a different strategy to defeat, adding to the overall challenge of the game. The boss battles are also well-designed, with each one providing a unique challenge that requires players to use their skills and weapons to their fullest potential.In conclusion, Resident Evil Village is a must-play game for anyone who loves action, exploration, and puzzle-solving games. Its stunning graphics, immersive storyline, and well-designed characters make it a game that's not to be missed. So, if you're looking for a thrilling and suspenseful game, then Resident Evil Village is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: A bloody great game. Certainly worth the "triple A" price tag without any negative catches.Combination between the down-to-the-ground combat from Resident Evil 7 and the character and equipment progression system from Resident Evil 4 is certainly the best way, if not the only way, to help freshen up the gameplay of the franchise.Replaying the game in the "Newgame+" finally feels rewarding with the continuing upgrades in weapons and the modifications with the gears carried over from the previous runs.The animations in this game is truly splendid. The realistic tactical gun animations, the grappling attack animations from all the enemies are all there, leaving only small to no more improvement to be desired.The style of the story is still the cheesy formula of Resident Evil franchise, but in no way bad.For the bonus gamemode, with how they create the mercenary mode, I really really hope for the new update/expansion to also include a roguelike dungeon crawler mode since the system is actually already there, and that I really want to keep playing with the gem they have made.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm using a 1070 which is not that old and is listed in their recommended settings.  The only way I can play at all is by turning the entire game to bare minimum settings.  Even then the gameplay is enjoyable most of the time, but there can still be a problem with "micro-stutters" that happen a lot.  I have to reboot the game or my pc to flush it out.  The game has been out for almost a month now and no patch for this.  The problem here is they put so much good stuff in the story (ignoring plot holes), the detail, the enemies, the level design, etc that I just wanted more and more.  The 4 Lords could have had much longer segments that explored more of their history and background.  What is there is quite nice, but right now it's only around 3 hours per lord (if that) and that's if you try to stretch it by being thorough. The enemies are well detailed and most have their own ways of behaving.  In addition many have multiple kill animations for poor Ethan that really look "intense". I'm going to give the Story and the Characters a bit of a pass on the "making sense" or "using good judgement" since most characters in horror games / movies don't.  Capcom did a better job at making Ethan seem more intelligent than RE7 IMO.  Traveling cross country (UNARMED AND WITHOUT BACKUP!) to a a creepy abandoned estate where people have been known to go missing; sounds like a great plan. Hey, like I said before, characters in the Horror Genre don't roll very high Intel stats.  At least here there is a bit of an excuse as to why he shows up at the Village. Hopefully we get some DLC that expands on what's going on and at least does a half-arsed attempt at answering questions and plot holes.  Be nice to see the entire cast of this little Quaint Village again somehow.  Ethan's time in it was far too short.

_childDocuments_.review: To be perfectly honest, this game so far (4 actual hours of game play time) isn't exactly what I was expecting from this series. Capcom seems to want to make the player think that they have gone in a totally different direction, making a 180 but using familiar faces. I'm guessing that by the end of the story the writers somehow manage to tie the previous game into it's lore. This game is so cool I am thinking this would have been a better stand alone title, completely removed from the Resident Evil franchise. I just don't feel like it has the spirit of the series in the early content of the story which leads to a lot of confusion, where as Bio-hazard at least seemed to reach for the Umbrella links fairly early on and it felt like a natural evolution of the series. Village plays and looks great, however, it is flawed in that it doesn't feel like a Resident Evil title for quite a while. Spoiler alert: werewolves, not zombies, are your first enemy. Yup, that's right, you face off against straight up Lycans, like out of a Gothic horror movie but there is little explanation until like a quarter of the way through the game. I'm not even going to get into the rest of the macabre cast but it doesn't feel like a part of the RE franchise to me. I still think it is enjoyable and some nice eye candy, however, don't think you're getting a true RE game, at least not in the first 4 hours or so. If you have patience you will be rewarded with some cool links to franchise lore once you get past the first major section.

_childDocuments_.review: Great follow up to ResE7 and great game in general, though it sacrifices some of what gave 7 its charm the new focus on a whole village rather than just a small rural compound allows the gameplay and the plot to be much more substantive than 7 was. Although not every plot point was perfect, the plot overall was still fantastic and I was hooked until the end, even taking the time to read most of the lore notes hidden around the village and mansion. Only 8 hours to beat the campaign on my first playthrough but the game heavily incentivizes replay with completion points used to unlock bonus content.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is definetly worth getting. Some people are complaining that it's not enough like RE7. What these people want is a "boo! haunted house" format of horror game with almost zero gameplay where it's essentially like a big interactive movie. RE: Village has parts that are like this, but does not overinvest in it. It also does not make the mistake of being too action oriented where you are bombarded by mobs constantly taking all the horror and suspense out of it like RE: 5. RE: Village I believe delivers a very balanced experience of survival horror where there are parts with a lot of gameplay and action, but it takes time to build up some suspense so when you get to the action it has more impact.The atmosphere of the game is awesome. This it does very well. It is incredible to look at visually. The controls are not the best though, but I don't think it ruins the experience. When you are running away from a giant monster you aren't sitting there thinking about how the movement is a little clunky.The biggest downside of the game for me personally was the fact that it takes a very long time to find all the items hidden within the levels. They really seem to want you to stay in each area for awhile and explore, but I wish they would of made items a bit easier to find so the pacing isn't constantly broken up by searching every nook and cranny of a room to find one tiny jewel embedded on the ceiling or a piece of scrap metal in the corner that blends in with the wall behind it.The payoff though is well worth it. The game does a great job of putting you in the setting and it's a pretty wild ride from start to finish. Once you get into the world the game puts you in you will quickly forget about all it's minor flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is a great follow-up to RE7 despite its change of tone. The gameplay and visuals are a step up from its predecessor. _childDocuments_.review: I have spent about 15.6 hrs in this game and as of today my rating is a solid 9.8/10 It adds on to the base story in resident evil 7 very well, although it does seem that capcom toned down the scares and included alot more action than we saw in resident evil 7, the first 2 to 4 hrs of the game are genuinely unsettling and i got  jumpscared at every moment. The two areas that brought the scare factor out the most was Castle Dimitrescu and the house of Beneviento (doll lady) although i do think doll ladies area was a bit rushed and i wish we had a lot more screen time for Karl Heisenberg who i found to be the most interesting villain of the game with the exception of Mother Miranda Overall it was truly a heart racing experience and i honestly reccomend it but if you're only playing this game for the queen that was Lady Dimitrescu, don't bother. The game is a lot more than just big booba lady and she is the first villain you encounter and deal with so... Ethan's story has been one of the most interesting and captivating stories within resident evil to date, and he has been one hell of a protagonist who have come to love dearly. Also just get ready to go between hating our beloved Chris Redfield, to loving him then to hating him then to loving him... Again, seriously it was a wild ride. OH and get the tissues ready and prepare for some tears to spill, because it was the first resident evil 8 that made me WEEP. If you enjoyed resident evil 7's scare factor and the action and fighting of resident evil 4 you are going to love resident evil 8. It has a good combination between the two. Plus just to add the game is stunning, the atmosphere is brilliant, the voice acting is great especially for Lady Dimitrescu, Karl Heisenberg and Ethan Winters, plus if the one thing you complained about the most in resident evil 7 was the lack in variety of creatures... you are going to be very happy with the variety you encounter in Village. Oh and don't rush the game, believe me it went by so fast. Savor it !
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give this game a thumbs up and a pretty good review overall. It is fun, the story is interesting, and the game play is creepy and intense. It has a good balance between horror and action along with all the puzzles one is used to when playing a Resident Evil game. My main gripe is the last 2 entries into the RE family are simply not RE games. They are a cross between Silent Hill and Resident Evil. Which is not really a bad thing, but I am hoping for a modern and good RE zombie story made like this one. There are many things that remain RE-like but I feel they are losing the thread (intentionally) of their overall franchise story.Truth be told I was not a fan of RE7. I love difficult games that make you think and have intensity etc. But RE7 was to me a run and hide simulator. I hate the feeling of no control at all. I am glad others like it and were happy with it but to me it was dreadfully boring. I just ended up watching cinematics on Youtube to get the gist of the story. I also was not a RE fan in the 90s. I did not play consoles after Sega Genesis. I was a PC player so RE does not have a place in my heart so when I play these games I am taking them in individually without expectations or desires beyond the series continuing to serve a coherent story line/theme. So in that way I feel the newer titles sort of fail to offer that. That being said, if you look at them as a separate game/universe loosely tied to the original titles then they are great.I do not understand the memes regarding the Lady D (I forget her name). She is not made to look attractive at all in my opinion. Her role in the game can be likened to Tyrant (whatever his name was from RE2) to chase you around occasionally and basically be unstoppable (until the end I am assuming although I have no completed the game thus far).Her character works mostly in this regard as she is fairly terrifying but that is mostly due to the fact she is made invulnerable and you know you cannot stop her. Tyrant was truly terrifying. Mostly the reason for this was his lack of emotion, and his silence. Lady D is quite vocal and exhibits a fair amount of emotions from joy, jealousy, anger etc. She also is quite vocal. Even though you realize you could not defeat her nor could you reason with her, her emotional displays like when her daughter dies, or when you read her journal she is clearly not concerned with the authority of mother miranda etc give your (at least mine) senses that perhaps she is more human and able to offer something other than what Tyrant would promise with his dead stare and stomping gait which tells you without any words or backstory that this man/thing is hellbent on killing you.This tends to detract from the horror in the game. Again this does not dismiss how great the game really is, nor does it mean she lacks terror-inducement at all. She is clearly evil and logically you know she is dangerous. The story cannot continue to have carbon copies of the villains of before. But it also makes me wonder more on my earlier point: what do vampire bug people and werewolves have to do with Resident Evil? And even if they somehow do tie this together it seems like a large pill to swallow and a convoluted arc of a story to accept the connection.I love that they brought some action back into it without falling into the pits of that awful RE5 (I believe thats what it was? The one that seemed like a straight up shooter) I only played RE4 briefly on PC years ago because my nephew was over and wanted it so I got it on Steam for him. But it seemed good and a reinvention of the previous REs that was quite welcoming. I also like the upgradable weapons, and shopkeeper addition to the game. HINT: when you first see the shopkeeper you'll notice items that cost nothing. Buy all of them and you get free items. This may be obvious to many but it appeared to me to be possibly empty inventory or a glitch in the game so I almost ignored it. You will get some free bullets and other stuff. You should never have to buy bullets in this game as you find so many (on standard difficulty) so sell the valuable items you find and save all your money for weapons upgrades. In the 2.9 hours I have played I have fully upgraded both the shotgun and the handgun through the upgrade screen.An unintended benefit of this new direction of Resident Evil is it does slightly fulfill the absence of a new Silent Hill game. It really does have a resemblance of some of the elements of that series. But at the same time fulfills enough of the Resident Evil elements to satisfy fans of the series in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is much like Resident Evil 4 in that it plays much more like an action-adventure game than a survival horror game. I did my first play-through on hardcore and ammo and healing wasn't particularly scarce at any point. Granted there are times when you find yourself short handed but they are few and far between. There is much more emphasis on shooting your way out of situations than avoiding enemies by sneaking by.  Actually I cant think of a single point where you were able to outright avoid a fight. Resources are also abundant, with almost every enemy dropping loot, which further incentives killing them instead of avoiding them. I'm not bringing this up to disparage the game, but its important to understand that this is not a traditional Resident Evil game. If your expecting a survival-horror experience like that in say, Resident Evil 2, you will be disappointed. If you are a fan of more action oriented games than Village will almost certainly be an enjoyable experience. It still features mechanics like crafting and inventory management from previous Resident Evil games, however it is more simplified than in previous entries. Your inventory, for example, is much less constricted.  The graphics are very good and, more importantly, the game ran well on my decent but not top of the line PC with everything maxed out. This cannot be said for many older AAA titles. The game is, however, missing an FOV slider which is unacceptable. Granted I didn't find the default FOV to be horrible, but being locked in without the use of mods is frustrating. Most of the voice acting is pretty good (some small exceptions) and the motion capture is excellent. Definitely don't skip the cut-scenes.  Gameplay is very fun and with a good variety of weapons and enemies. The several boss fights were also quite good and didn't feel too formulaic. The puzzles are abundant and fun as always. Another standout feature is collecting loot to sell to the merchant. There is a lot of it and it can be quite satisfying to see just how much money you can make which can then be used to upgrade weapons and purchase items. The only thing I didn't really like was the Call Of Duty campaign-like segment around the end. It isn't too long but it felt very out of place and kinda lazy. In conclusion, Resident Evil Village is a fantastic game that I highly recommend to anyone who enjoys more action-oriented experiences.  There are still plenty of scary moments if that's more your thing, but again, this is not a true survival horror game if that's what your after.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is an excellent, well - paced, and tense continuation of Ethan Winter's endeavors to yet again rescue another member of his immediate family. Having played Village immediately after completing Resident Evil 7, The Ethan Winters Saga came to a meaningful and satisfying close (albeit with enough unanswered questions to allow the series to continue).       From the onslaught, Village's excellent presentation in terms of visuals and audio design is impeccable. Story moments are immersive due to the superb animation, made possible by motion capture technology. Furthermore, Each member apart of the wide cast of characters was performed exceptionally by their respective actors, especially by that of the four lords. Enemy encounters and atmosphere are made far more tense due to the great audio design, allowing for needed tension and horror to build when needed. The variety of environments in which this game takes place in also add to the experience, in areas such as Victorian Castle Dimitrescu, the dilapidated Village, and Heisenberg's underground factory. The level of detail and polish that went into each of the environments by the team at Capcom is phenomenal, made possible by the latest version of the RE engine.       Combat this time around, when compared to Resident Evil 7, is the forefront of the experience. The gunplay is satisfying and fairly balanced overall, although continue to expect enemies to act as "bullet sponges", a staple of the resident evil franchise. Ammunition and weapon variety is increased considerably over Resident Evil 7, allowing for a more action - oriented experience. As a direct result of this, enemy encounters are less scary this time around, mostly due to the fact that they can be easily disposed of due to the emphasis on combat. Moreover, the jarring nature of many of the enemies found throughout the game also become less tense as the experience progresses, as you will see many of the same enemies due to the lack of variety. This was an issue with Resident Evil 7 as well, although this is a minor gripe. Furthermore, boss encounters are a delight and a considerable leap forward from Resident Evil 7, having mitigated the use of weak points which I find quite basic. Each combat encounter is still fairly streamlined and simple however, allowing for the game to progress at a fairly quick rate. The difficulty can be increased, to the extent of the inclusion of "Village of Shadows" which in itself is a much more challenging means to play the game.       Post launch content has been a treat as well, due to the likes of "Shadows of Rose" DLC, the expansion of the mercenaries mode, VR support, third person perspective, and more. This further adds to the replay value of Village, although this has always been a given for most Resident Evil titles.       Overall, I have had an incredible experience with Resident Evil Village and look foward to see what the team at Capcom will continue to with the Resident Evil Franchise! I thoroughly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: A Phenomenal horror/action game!If you are coming off of Resident Evil 7, it is worth noting that this is much more about the action than the horror. This game was built off the Resident Evil 4 blueprint and is amazingly similar in that respect. Resident Evil 7 on the other hand was made to specifically be scary above all else. So it depends on the experience you are after. Do you wanna be specifically scared pretty much non stop? RE7Do you want a horror game that is a bit easier to brave, for various reasons, but primarily due to having lots of weaponry to deal with the scary?RE8In RE8, just like in RE4, they have abandoned the intense darkness of their usual horror and have pretty well lit the entire map. There are some dark segments but for the most part, you can see quite well the whole game. This means surprises are less common, or rather they are harder to achieve. So action takes more of a focus. The fear here comes from needing to fight to survive, rather than being on edge due to the scenario.That still happens of course, being on edge per the scenario you are in. Just less often when compared to RE7. That was the whole game with 7... I love the level design. These areas are very fun to navigate. The idea that some mad man built these areas as labyrinths on purpose, is great. I love it. All the environments are beautiful. This game has moments of photo realism that blow my mind. I have caught myself walking past a spot multiple times purely due to how amazing it all looks. Best part of this game I think is the replayability. They always had challenges and additional modes, but now they have a New Game + mode. Where you keep everything you ended with and can continue to upgrade your stuff further. Even unlocking more stuff to potentially use. Really damn cool!

_childDocuments_.review: The best way of describing Resident Evil Village is that it's all the best aspects of Resident Evil 4 combined with the best of Resident Evil 7.That is a big deal to me because Resident Evil 4 is not only my favorite game in the Resident Evil series, but also one of my favorite games, period. Or it was until I played Resident Evil Village. While Ethan Winters is no Leon S. Kennedy, Village is truly the spiritual successor to RE4 and an absolutely perfect blend of horror and action.I will admit RE7 was a bit (or a lot) too terrifying for me, but a return to the survival horror roots of Resident Evil with a switch to a first person perspective made it a great game. Village tones down the horror enough to still have terrifying moments without feeling like you're constantly about to have a heart attack, and ups the action with a lot more guns and a merchant, The Duke, to buy and upgrade those weapons a la RE4. If RE4 was your jam but RE7 was a bit much, give Village a try.Lastly, I rarely, if ever, finish or replay a game in my library. At the time of this review, I have beaten Village five times so far and have started my sixth playthrough. Yup.

I often encountered problems where it was unable to flush properly, due to which it crashed. I monitored my resources non-stop, I even became paranoid that something is wrong with my hardware, but no issues surfaced. I managed to observe similar issues with the RE2 and 3 remakes too, which means that it's something related to the new RE in general. Regardless, I hope that this issue can be addressed in future releases, as it was annoying to have to repeat some stretches. Luckily, the game was so fun that I didn't mind as much most of the time. As with REVII, I see myself returning to this one a lot in the future. It was beautiful, fun and well-designed. And Ethan Winters remains one of the best characters in RE history, for sure. Well done! Totally recommended from me! And I am definitely looking forward to the 9th installment in the series, while hoping that they stick to this style of game play. _childDocuments_.review: Best Quote:"I'm going to murder that boulder-punching a--hole, but you're first!" - Karl HeisenbergReview:Resident Evil Village is a top-tier action-horror shooter, delivering an extremely high level of quality in every conceivable aspect.Story:Resident Evil Village is the direct sequel to Resident Evil 7 Biohazard, heavily building on the events of the previous game. However, it can also be enjoyed without prior knowledge, as the game frequently includes flashbacks to the predecessor, and any missing context only occasionally affects the understanding of certain connections.The story is thrilling, action-packed, and dark, yet also partly emotional, allowing players to experience a wide range of emotions in a cinematic manner.The characters are all uniquely interesting and fit seamlessly into the story. This often leads to genuine interest in learning more about their backgrounds and roles within the narrative.Gameplay:The gameplay is as varied and engaging as in the recent Resident Evil titles, characterized by constantly evolving opportunities. There are well-designed shooter segments with a variety of enemies and several boss fights. As you progress through the game, you can find loot, such as new weapons and treasures, scattered across the map. Occasionally, you’ll encounter small puzzles to solve. Everything runs smoothly, providing an excellent gaming experience.Graphics:Resident Evil Village stands among the most visually impressive games I've ever played, alongside titles like Witcher 3 and Batman: Arkham Knight. The breathtaking landscapes of the village, both day and night, the interior design of buildings—especially Lady Dimitrescu's castle—and the detailed character models are all visually stunning.Conclusion:In summary, Resident Evil Village is a worthy successor to Resident Evil 7 Biohazard, matching its quality in many aspects and even surpassing it in some. I appreciate that Resident Evil Village has managed to establish its unique atmosphere, giving both games their own distinct right to exist.Personally, I was thoroughly captivated and entertained while playing Resident Evil Village and can wholeheartedly recommend it to everyone.That’s it for this review. Until next time.

Even though during the first Lycan fight/interaction on Hardcore it can feel frustratingly tough especially if you're unaware of what to do to progress. Though, after that sequence the game is very well balanced in it's difficulty on Hardcore, for me Standard/Casual enemies are a bit too easy to put down and ammo/crafting resources feel a tad too plentiful. TL;DR Standard/Casual will have the game feeling like it's leaning harder towards RE4 vs. RE7, whereas I'd say the opposite on Hardcore.RE Engine shines once again, RE8 is absolutely beautiful graphically and it's art style is very well realized. Combat/gameplay is responsive and fun, Guns have a lot of punch to them and feel great (Much like RE7) which makes the combat that much more engaging and satisfying. There's also quite a lot of weapons to get your hands on, which also boosts replay-ability given the fact some weapons won't unlock until you've finished your first playthrough, some will also become available to buy in the bonus shop. So, NG+ is totally worth it IMHO, and there's also an unlockable (Unless you bought the deluxe version, in which case it's available from the start) harder difficulty called "Village of Shadows" which is very tough, but all your NG+ weapons/gear make it quite fun.Each area has it's own detailed, well realized style. Generally speaking also quite varied which I found to be a great thing, especially the way each area interconnects with the Village, which also is very fun to explore and unlock sections of. Some areas (Especially one area in particular) being scarier than others, but all of them have their own mood and atmosphere. And I personally loved all of the locations. For story/characters, this is IMO arguably the best Resident Evil has ever been, especially the last Act of the game. I never thought a RE game would make me emotional but hah, RE8 proved me wrong. Is it over the top in that vintage RE sort of way? Sure, sometimes. But RE8 does have it's darker, more serious moments, and for me it was very effective in pulling me into those moments.Highly recommended. It's a great RE game, and just a phenomenal game in general.  Though numbered reviews aren't my personal thing, if I were to give RE8 a score out of 10, I'd say for sure a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the internet going crazy over the tall lady the four villains you face throughout the campaign all have pretty poor character design. The Baron however is an incredible character and a few of the survivors you meet early on are believable and interesting.  In terms of the story the series jumped the shark long ago so every installment stretches things even further at this point. If you stop to think about the plot at all things immediately start to fall apart and make little to no sense but if i'm being honest i'm not here for plot or character design. This is a Resident Evil game. The characters are rarely interesting. The stories stopped being good a long time ago and i'm here for the gameplay and atmosphere.  I'll start by addressing atmosphere. The good news is RE8 has a incredible atmosphere. The environments are visually stunning and distinctly Resident Evil.  It doesn't do anything exceptional with environmental story telling, but you can expect to find a few interesting documents and letters to read throughout the campaign that add to the world building of the universe and aren't that bad but nothing like what's found in early installments. Overall i will say the world i wonderful to live in with a brilliant gothic atmosphere and captivating scenery. Now I saved what i consider most important for last which is the gameplay and I am happy to report the moment to moment gameplay is lots of fun. Continuing in the footsteps of RE7 this installment is first person but takes ques from RE4 in the speed and pacing of the gameplay. This game is a massive improvement over the gameplay in RE7.  You move faster, there is more enemy variety, the story and campaign moves at a very nice pace all things that Capcom from the feedback they got with 7 and it really shows. However the addition of enemies dropping ammo and lots of heavy firepower really take it more towards that RE4 Action Horror genre and away from that traditional RE Survival Horror genre that I do much prefer but honestly both are great.

It isn't a subtle screen shake either. Your screen goes ape sh*t! It is very annoying and nauseating.In conclusion it is better than RE 7 but the game has its flaws and pacing is terrible. _childDocuments_.review: , the latest instalment in the iconic survival horror franchise from Capcom, continues to push the boundaries of the genre with its innovative first person camera view. Set in a chilling, Gothic European village, the game takes players on a roller-coaster ride of thrills, intrigue, and heart-pounding action while also delivering the franchise one of its most iconic, if not iconic villains, Countess Alcina Dimitrescu. From the moment she appeared in an early trailer for , Lady Dimitrescu captured the attention of the internet: her towering, sultry frame; her sickly-sweet smile; her massive hat; her proper yet authoritative tone. Viewers were instantly obsessed, labelling her "tall vampire lady" and demanding to know everything about her, which prompted Capcom to reveal her exact height — 9'6" including her hat and heels — months before  launched in May of 2021. Lady Dimitrescu, and her murderous three daughters preside over Castle Dimitrescu which towers over the village protagonist Ethan Winters (the lead from ) finds himself in at the start of the game. Countess Alcina Dimitrescu is not the only villain Ethan Winters will need to outsmart in this sequel, but she definitely is the most memorable. From the get go  manages to deliver an intense and memorable experience that should keep fans of the series on the edge of their seats.:One of the standout features of  is its stunning visual presentation. The RE Engine once again proves its prowess, delivering detailed character models, breathtaking environments, and impressive lighting effects. The titular village itself is a masterclass in environmental design, seamlessly blending decrepit architecture with eerie ambience. The transition from the village to more fantastical locales is seamless and adds to the game's sense of mystery and foreboding.: continues the franchise's shift towards a more action-oriented approach, akin to . The gameplay strikes a balance between tense survival horror and intense combat sequences. Ethan Winters, the protagonist, is more agile this time around, allowing for smoother movement and dynamic evasive actions. The inventory management system returns, adding an extra layer of challenge as players must strategise on the fly.The weapon variety is satisfying, with each firearm feeling impactful and unique. However, the game occasionally suffers from pacing issues, with certain segments feeling too action-heavy, diminishing the sense of vulnerability that defines the series. The addition of crafting and merchant mechanics adds depth, but the inclusion of some survival elements may alienate purist fans of the franchise.: boasts an intriguing narrative that combines supernatural horror with 's signature bio-terrorism plotlines. The enigmatic Lady Dimitrescu and her vampiric daughters steal the show with their eerie charm, but some secondary characters lack development. The overarching story sometimes struggles to maintain a cohesive tone, veering between chilling horror and campy action. While the central mystery is compelling, some plot twists may leave players scratching their heads.: excels at creating an unsettling atmosphere, with its haunting sound design, meticulously crafted environments, and relentless tension. The first-person perspective heightens immersion, making encounters with grotesque enemies genuinely terrifying. The game's psychological horror elements, especially in the dollhouse segment, are spine-chilling and showcase the developers' mastery at crafting scares. However, some areas lose their fright factor due to predictable jump scares and reliance on shock value.: runs smoothly on current-gen hardware, maintaining a consistent frame rate even during intense action sequences. However, I did experience severe frame drops when fighting one of Lady Dimitrescu daughters who deploys swarms of insects during the fight with her. This swarm lowered my framerate in to single digits which was jarring.  Load times, for the most part, are minimal, and the game's visuals remain impressive throughout. Some players may also experience minor glitches or texture pop-in (as I did), though these issues are infrequent and don't significantly impact the overall experience.: is a worthy addition to the franchise, offering a visually stunning and atmospheric journey through horror. While the game occasionally strays from its survival horror roots and stumbles in its narrative execution, it still manages to deliver an intense and memorable experience that will leave players eagerly anticipating the next chapter in the  saga. With its exceptional graphics, spine-tingling moments, and a gripping sense of dread,  solidifies itself as a must-play title for both series veterans and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the best in the series, and an excellent echo of Resident Evil 4. Tons of replay value, and none of the staleness of 7. The environment and enemies make up for some really tense, and scary moments, and bringing back the sort of zany, almost wackiness of the bosses really hit me in the nostalgia. Didn't realize how much I missed that. Lots and Lots of new guns/toys to play with, and an expansive variety of enemies make for an incredibly fresh experience each and every time you triumph over a boss. Just when you thought you had a flow going, RE8 manages to throw a curve ball each time, flawlessly. This game is great for newcomers to the series, and long time fans alike. 10/10 Capcom, I tip my hat to you, seriously thanks for the amazing experience, and I can't wait for more to come.

In exchange for not as much horror, you get way more action, lots more explosions, an arsenal of weapons; fully customizable, more crafting, more exploration, and overall just more instances to be a bad ass instead of running around scared. As for how well the story is lets just say the ending is well worth it, It's definitely better than Biohazards' in my opinion, since Village wraps things up nicely providing more closure, which i feel they didn't get to do in Biohazard.
