_childDocuments_.review: This review contains spoilers!Was really looking forward to this but after finishing it once I have to say I'm a bit disappointed.The premise seemed really interesting at first but the villains you have to fight were all kinda boring and killing them off seemed a bit rushed. You literally meet the three daughters of the big lady and the big lady herself and kill them in what feels like half an hour playtime. The other big enemies feel the same way. They are introduced and finished way too fast in my opinion. It also bothers me that they toned down the horror aspect in this game compared to the last. The only section that was somewhat unsettling was in the dollmaker's house. The monster baby's sound design was pretty awesome and the overall atmosphere was great. Would have loved to see more of that in the game. Gameplay felt alright, you now have a counter move after blocking an attack from basic enemies which can give you some free space. Weapons and gunplay are fine but nothing special. I did enjoy exploring the castle and village, unlocking doors with new keys and collecting treasures and such.Storywise it is a bit of a letdown for me as well. Ethan is just a boring protagonist. Other main characters in the series weren't especially deep but they worked for what they are - cheesy action heroes - but Ethan isn't even that. He comes across as a normal dude in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up situation but he lacks any charismatic or over-the-top properties a Leon Kennedy or Chris boulder-punching Redfield had in previous titles. The explanation in the end on why Ethan is able to survive all of these injuries felt kinda unnecessary and out of nowhere. Chris's role in all this is weird too. He has yet another organization - the "Hound" group - and his previously found anti-bioterrorist organization BSAA is apparently now an enemy? It's just all presented very poorly in my opinion.I am going to play it on another difficulty at some point to see how that changes things up, as Resident Evil games are known to do. All in all, I feel like the game tries to combine many things that made previous titles great but fails to do so. The action and gameplay is better in 4, the exploration is more satasfying in 2 and 2 Remake, the horror and villains are more effective in 7 and the story feels underwhelming.Edit: Nvm, got every achievement, it's a banger

However the game is not nearly as scary as resident evil 7, but still a phenomenal game in its own right with some good tense moments and scares of its  own. Resident evil 7 and 8 together probably have the best Resident Evil story and lore to date. Towards the end of the game, Village (RE 8) ties in HEAVILY with resident evil 7 and if you haven't played 7, when you reach those story and lore tie-ins, you will be very lost as to the MAJOR twists of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Now you may look at my hours and think "how can he give it a negative review?" but this is one of those times where I wish Steam had a between option. It's a solid game with a fantastic art direction, but some people are praising it as if it's the best entry in the long standing franchise and it just isn't. The first problem is a loss of identity. Even the logo is "Village" with Resident Evil shoved into the background like it's ashamed to be a part of it, and outside of some basic tropes like collecting keys if you were to remove Chris and the Umbrella logo you just wouldn't know this is the 8th entry into Resident Evil. Another problem is NG+, it wasn't designed with this in mind with forced cinematic sections you can't skip, and entire section which removes combat and rewards with no options to turn these off slows down NG+ runs which is counter productive. Finally another big issue is the developers clearly knew the castle was the best area, as it's all the marketing focused on and unfortuently it's also the peak of the game. It never reaches the heights of that place again which is a shame to say the least. In short, it's a solid title, the village and castle are a lot of fun to explore but both are too short, and Ethan really can't carry a game let alone two. The dude has as much personality as cardboard.7/10 title. Enjoy playing but it's not Resident Evil.

_childDocuments_.review: As a die-hard fan of the Resident Evil series, I can tell you that this is a solid edition to the RE lineup. Following on from 7, RE:Village encapsulates beautiful yet tense environments with appropriate resource management and thoughtful boss fights. The story develops nicely and includes a few tantalising callbacks for original RE fans (you know which note I'm talking about). However, I found the factory area very drawn out and very frustrating in terms of resource management and pointless enemies, but each to their own. Overall, it sits at a solid 8/10 which has the potential for high replay-ability and a promising third instalment of the 'Winters' storyline on the horizon.

_childDocuments_.review: The overwhelmingly positive rating will probably speak for itself, but just in case you A) Haven't bought this game B) Actually want to know why so many people are gushing over it, here are some cliff notes:1) Satisfying Gunplay: This one's a carryover from RE7. Between the sound design, the gun's recoil animations and effect on target they don't get old very fast. The weapon selection isn't that large, but besides the clear-cut upgrades to your shotgun and pistol they mostly feel distinct with their own unique strengths and weaknesses. There's one notable exception, but saying what it is would be a gigantic spoiler so you'll just have to play the game to see.2) Solid Map DesignIf you're a fan of games that reward exploration and reading through everything you find, you'll be well-rewarded here. There are bits of lore and loot scattered everywhere for you to find. Having said that, the maps still do a good job of herding you in the right direction if you're not. 3) Intriguing StoryVillage hops into the canon as a direct sequel to RE7, expanding upon the lore established in Biohazard and adding some fun new twists. The second game's plotline isn't quite as tight as the first, but it definitely has a logical progression and a satisfying ending. If you're a Resident Evil fan you're used to not asking TOO many questions about the plot and this one won't demand too much.4) Great Action, Spiced with HorrorI will say that one particular segment scared the absolute hell out of me. I won't spoil exactly when it is, but it made me remember playing Penumbra as a kid. That's not a comparison I make lightly and is just about the highest praise I can come up with. The rest is a fantastic action game that can have some real adrenaline-fueled panic moments as you balance conserving ammunition and the horde of enemies trying to use your rib cage as a xylophone. tl;dr Just trust me on this one, it's good

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a "meh" rating, since I would recommend this game to a certain type of player, but I certainly didn't like it, hence the thumbs down.Ok, so I want to make some things clear first:- I don't think it's a bad game, in fact I think it's very well done and I can see why most players like it.- I'm not biased towards "old school" or "new school" RE. My top games are 4, 1R, 2, 2R and 7, and the ones I hate most are 6 and 0, so it's not the style that makes me like or hate a specific game.- I'll obviously talk about spoilers.So, my main gripe with this game is funnily enough what most people seem to like: the variety in horror. As I mentioned, I don't mind RE trying new stuff, but I just wish they committed to just one or maybe two styles. For instance in RE4, the horror "theme" stopped being virus/zombies and became parasite/mind control, so they took this and exhausted every single type of enemy this would entail, and the limitation allowed them to be very creative with tons of memorable, unique enemies like the blind claw, chain-saw dude (which gets an updated version in every game since), cultists etc.In RE8, it is pretty clear (even from the art designs comments) that they went more to a horror show approach with a variety of monsters, kinda like Castlevania does. I don't think this is bad per se, but I just don't think it fits RE. How I wish they just committed to the Vampire and/or Werewolves theme and created a ton of stuff with that!  When I saw Lady D daughters, the lower medieval prisoners zombies and the fly/bat thing I was genuinely hyped, but then this theme suddenly dropped and got replaced with Child's Play and I was "waa?". This means that every enemy just got it's basic interpretation of the trope and not much else. Also I know the fetus is a lot of people favorite scene, but on-rails horror where you have to hide and wait a timer just don't do it for me man, I just find it boring and on repeated playthroughs it'll be a slog (just like Sherry's section in RE2R). In the end, it feels like the fungus is now a pretty lame excuse to give Magneto powers to regular humans, and I just don't know how I feel about something that can do whatever, whenever with no rules. Cyber zombies were pretty funny though (even though it's basically Doom).Another gripe is combat. It is definitely better than 7, but I would make the point that in 7 you're not supposed to be good at combat for two reasons: Ethan is just a regular dude, and an awkward combat helps making you feel helpless in a horror game, like old school RE (i'm not saying this as an excuse, if you don't like it, you don't like it and that's ok). However, It's still so limited compared to 4, 5 and 6! I'm not very fond of 5 and 6, but the combat in these games are fun. The one I like most is 4 though, and I know it's the more limited of the three, so I know you're thinking I complain 8 is limited but praise 4 for being limited what the hell? The thing is, for me, all combat in 4 was built around the limitation of having to stop to shoot, so every enemy has a singular strategy you have to uncover to fight against. Enemy with projectiles, enemy with shield, dynamite enemy, blind enemy, OHK enemy, giant machine gun enemy, among others. So it could even have situations were you fight multiple enemy types at once, having to think about  how to tackle each situation. Am I wrong or in RE8 you ONLY fight one enemy type at a time, except for the occasional projectile dude and a few bosses? Also in RE8, my strategy for all enemies was the same: walk backwards and then the enemy whiffs, or just block, occasionally running forward. Even on bosses.And finally, I thought the story was just meh. First of all, I think it's pretty fanfic-y how Umbrella went from just being a pharmaceutical company with shady bioweapon labs, to this almost cabalistic thing that involves ancient ruins and rituals, Spencer being almost a mythical figure in search of immortality that's related to every BOW incident in the world, and Chris coincidentally always seeing the document saying that (I wouldn't be surprised if he comes back at some point, also Miranda just casually having a 60 year old letter sitting on a table for others to read). I don't get how Ethan being a fungus is that big of a deal since to me it was supposed to be pretty well established with 7, as both he and Mia clearly had regeneration. Also I think Mia got robbed of being the one to save Ethan and her daughter at the end, since I think Chris was there for fan service (but no Jill... smh).Well, I said my piece and I'm at ease, agree to disagree with most people I guess. Thanks for reading anyway!EDIT: honestly the more I think about it the worse it gets. RE never had outstanding stories, but apart from a few exceptions they usually made sense in of themselves, even all the silliness of 4 was explained in one way or another. This game though... is just nonsense.What was Miranda's plan after all? Why did she need to disguise as Mia? Wouldn't it be easier to just sneak in and take the baby, since she did this anyway? Then she makes a challenge for Ethan to kill all 4 lords... why? Miranda had no use for Ethan, just straight out killing him. Then again, why didn't she just do the ritual when she got to the village with the baby? Why divide it in four and give Rose to the 4 lords? She just makes the ritual without Ethan, and without the lords... she just needed Rose. It's not like it's magic, it's just a fungus.And then there's Chris... what was his plan again? Why just not tell Ethan outright that it wasn't Mia? It would take like... 3 seconds? The game even acknowledges this was stupid, but it sounds like the writers realizing this made no sense more than anything. Then he trained Ethan for combat... and tells him to not do anything? But Ethan did MUCH more than Chris and he was still unwilling... Did Chris purposefully let Ethan and Mia have a fungus baby? So he knew the baby was a fungus, and also Ethan and Mia? How did he know Miranda would come for them, and disguised as Mia?Ugh, my head hurts...

_childDocuments_.review: The story of this one was great, as well as the sound design, characters, visuals, and voice acting! Gameplay-wise, it is basically just like the previous game. I love how this one brings back Chris and mentions a few other characters from the older Resident Evil games (you'll see which ones if you read the documents). I also love how Duke says "What are you buying? Just something an old friend used to say", in reference to the iconic merchant from Resident Evil 4, that used to say "What are you buying?".When it comes to the characters, each one of them is unique in their own way, we have Lady Dimistrecu and her three daughters (the Internet went crazy about these), the charismatic Heisenberg, Mother Miranda with her tricks, Duke and his deals and items that can save your life, Chris Redfield making a comeback, Ethan - who was the playable character from Resident Evil 7, the horrible Moreau with loser complexes, and Beneviento with her creepy dolls.Although the game doesn't have as much horror as the classic games, it was still scary, especially with the chasing phases with Dimitrescu and that weird big baby in Beneviento's house.Overall, it was a fun game to play, and very engaging, yet still with some of the essential Resident Evil elements in it to remind us that yes, it is still a Resident Evil game.Thank you Ash, my beloved, for gifting me this amazing game <3

_childDocuments_.review: Some people may be a bit divided on this title, namely people who still desire the more toned down style of the original trilogy, but honestly for me, after having played this and it's dlc campaign Shadows of Rose, I can safely say this is one of the most solid Resident Evil entries out there. I'm not the type to replay games either but the replayability of this one has me having completed 4 playthroughs of the main campaign now. It really does take all of the good from Resident Evil 7 as well as the RE2 remake and consolidates it into an incredibly polished experience. Well worth the money, no sale needed.

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoiler Free Review*Compared to the Last Game:This game took every problem I had with RE7 and fixed them.The pacing is faster. There are more enemy types. There are more weapons, and more ways to improve them. There's the Duke. There's a Thicc, Tall, Dommy Mommy vampire. There are also werewolves. Ethan is significantly improved as a protagonist. Literally it's RE7 but better in every way. It's similar to how Assassin's Creed Odyssey is just an objectively improved Origins.Performance:Game runs fantastic on high settings, even on my aging rig. You shouldn't have any issues unless you're on a potato. Lots of flex and customization options. The game defaults to a window mode on first launch which is weird but, Capcom games have a history of doing so for me. Easy fix to full-screen, runs flawlessly. Potential Story Issues:The one thing that people may not like are the late story twists. To my estimation there are three. One involves a shift in game-play, one involves a retcon to the previous game (RE7), and one involves a retcon to the wider RE universe lore. These are all very much a case of YMMV. Personally, I liked the first two and I am ambivalent towards the third.TLDR:It is RE7 but better and with a dash of RE4. If you thought RE7 was boring then you should like this one. Highly Recommend.Update: Still holds up, excellent game.

GET THIS you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The many positive reviews is understandable because Capcom for the first time introduced a RE game where puzzles are easy as eating pancakes to solve, and it is basically an FPS game with that RE4 feel. So far I am 7 hrs in and encountered (excluding bosses) three different types of enemies, of which:- Ferals: there are only two different looking types, so they're basically all clones by the hundreds, even dress up the same.- Sewer dwellers: Now these are all exactly the same clones of each other, dressed and look the same- Gargoyle things: Totally identical as well, but somewhat acceptable here.And this is 7 hours in. It was as in RE4, after you start engaging infected enemies that all look identical, a game just does it for me, it means time and money was spent elsewhere, to the expense of immersion. Again, you get jumped at by those clones, they are all over you, taking up 80% of your screen, and they all look the same, WTF, all look the same !!!!! At least give them a different t-shirt next time or different haircut....I am playing it in Hardcore mode, the game is also easy. Did not die once so far. The game is also not scary, just once I had a scary moment where one of those sewer dweller clones just rose up from the dirty waters two meters in front of me, that was all.The boss fights are obvious, you'll beat them first try in hardcore mode. The game is also extremely horrible in terms of unlocking/explaining additional content in-game. For instance, you find exotic animals after a certain part in the game, you kill them, then you talk to the trader, the game makes you believe these rare exotic animals (or what's left of it after you toast it), that you need to sell it and get a lot of coin for it. So what do people do? They sell it. But suddenly an hour later into the game, by opening some random door of some random house which continues progress, only then suddenly out of the blue the "COOKING RECEIPTS" are unlocked at the trader, where you can learn receipts and COOK EXOTIC MEATS which give you permanent buffs and perks for the rest of the game, but guess what! The same trader at the same location did not say crap before, so all that were unfortunate enough to spot and shoot exotic animals BEFORE triggering that scene, and which sold them, are unable for the remainder of the game to learn those receipts that grant you permanent buffs, and there is no buy-back option at the trader either, I mean J.F.C., really ? So basically guys, I did not write SPOILERS in hopes you read this, because in order for me to be able to use receipts for permanent buffs, I would have had to read ahead and watch potential spoilers. How can I smell to ignore exotic animals and only kill them after a certain phase of the game which only then triggers the vendor's kitchen and cooking receipts, to only then be able to cook, so what we supposed to do, smell this in advance? Sense it? Capcom probably thinks many of us have psionic powers. All that were LUCKY enough not to spot exotic animals (and they are obvious to spot, due to noises they make etc), and only spot them afterward certain progress areas, man, hats off to you.But then again, this game is so incredibly easy, I might not even need more permanent health to begin with as I have had no issues whatsoever on this cakewalk Hardcore mode. I am actually thinking of restarting and play it in the most difficult setting, now that I learned, but no wait, best I play and finish it as it is, let's see what other surprises capcom made that we have to sense or smell in advance.tldr: 1. Watch spoilers and read a lot on the game before you start or you'll miss on MAJOR things like permanent buffs etc early on for good.2. 7 hours in, all enemies look the same unless sometimes they have clone brothers that look and dress the same.3. No scary scenes at all so far, this is more of an adventure game than adventure horror.4. Puzzles are a joke. Toddlers would do fine.But then again, I understand why such good reviews. People new to this genre have an easy time and think they're most likely hot s... on a stick because they finally doing good on a RE game without needing any guides etc in their first playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: Very different from RE7, but not in a bad way. One can tell when playing the game just how much RE:4 has influenced the development roadmap for Village. More action orriented, although with some pure horror moment (Absolutely loved the house benneviento section of the game). Some folks say the story is meh. I liked it a lot, I felt much more connected to Ethan than in RE7. In RE7, Ethan seemed like a placeholder character that was really just a human manifestation of a game camera, necessary for you to progress. There is a much higher degree of connection with Ethan in RE8. The last couple of hours of the game are intense.Visuals are A++++, and performance was great even with RT on (not sure just how much RT impacts visuals, but hey, at least you can say RT was activated). There was this one room in Dimitrescu's castle where the frames were cut in half, for some odd reason, but it was only the one room.Lots of replayability as well and will definitely do multiple playthroughs in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Great, in my opinion better than RE7, but it has the same problem as the first one. It falls apart in the latter half. When you get to Heisenbergs Factory you get that feeling like you're on the ship from RE7 all over again, which is not good. Capcom really needs to stop making all modern RE games end in a compound/factory/facility, it ruins the atmosphere and instead replaces it with the blandness of what is part of pretty much every modern RE game. The game is at its best in The Village, getting the head flasks from the Lords was also very fun, adds a lot of variety but it all gets ruined once you enter heisenbergs factory.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I have to admit I miss the psychological horror elements from RE7, Resident Evil Village is still a well made game and will satisfy fans of RE4. + Smart level design where all areas are interconnected+ Meaningful backtracking coupled with Metroidvania elements+ Great art and monster design+ Puzzles that make you think a little but don't piss you off+ Good PC port (no FOV slider isn't a bummer for me but I know it is for some people out there)- Underused characters that hardly get enough screen time to shine (E.g. Lady D)- Average Boss fightsTLDR; Fans of RE4 will love Village, fans of RE7 will feel it did not quite reach its potential!
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: As a major RE fan, this game delivered on every level. The action and combat was on par with RE 4 with some direct references to that game that made me smile a little. However this action was well paced with some slower paced puzzle sections that were the challenging. The horror and scares were on par with RE 7 so you were always on your toes. The story delivered much more than I expected which was greatly appreciated. Only real complaint is difficulty. I played the game on standard and it was a little to easy. If you are an RE veteran definitely start on hard at least.TL;DR An amazing game that all RE fans will appreciate. Newcomers to the series will also appreciate the game but may get a little lost within the story if they have no played at least RE 7.

_childDocuments_.review: Others have made comparisons to a ghost train ride and that's pretty apt. It's a fun experience as you're funnelled from encounter to encounter. The puzzles and gameplay are pretty bog-standard but that's not really what we're here for. Things get ridiculous towards the end but if you've been a fan of the series for a while then that will come as no surprise.The pacing is pretty spot on for the most part and it was nice to play something on the shorter side. This took me a shade under 9 hours to complete and that was definitely enough. Each time you are about to feel bored there is a change of pace. Some other games could take note!Game looks great but the HDR seemed to be all over the shop for me anyway. It seemed that no matter how much I monkeyed around with the settings certain parts looked washed out.Not sure this was worth all the hype and accolades it received but definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: So rather than going on about a certain lady who's height is a little above average I'm going to give a little review of what I think so far.The most simple way to explain the game is to describe it as RE4, RE7 and Bloodborne's love child. It is more action packed than 7, but less than 4 yet it keeps the great things about 4 and 7 while leaving the bad things out. It's not as much of a survival horror as 7 or the classics but it is enough to definitely warrant the name. There's plenty of backtracking and resource management but the item boxes and limited saves are gone, unless limited saves are unlocked in a harder difficulty than hardcore. So far playing on hardcore hasn't been too difficult except for one section relatively early which feels like a horde chase. If you can get through that you should be fine.While the game itself doesn't feel overly "Resident Evil"ish it does do a fantastic job with its horror aesthetic being real gothic in nature set in an old town and Romanian castle with more side areas. Coming from an absolute die hard RE fan I'm really enjoying it and think it tops 7 with overall enjoyment. My only negative is I wish the other side areas had as much detail as the castle but if my only complaint is that I want more then I guess that speaks for the game.Runs like a dream too.Overall It's a strong recommend for any RE fan or even for newcomers as it does come with a recap of 7's story as this game is set I think 3ish years in the future with 7's main characters. If your unsure, check out the demo.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Brings back memories of the originals of the series but in first person.  Puzzles don't seem to be to challenging so far but are welcome as one of my favourite elements from the older games. Not far into the game but can recommend but not at full price as the game is apparently very short.  I secured it for £15 from another vendor and must say worth every penny so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: This game has everything you would expect in a modern Resident Evil game. But there are some things about it that are a little questionable. The difficulty is probably something I've heard a pretty good amount about. I played the game on normal difficulty and I literally never died to a basic enemy once... ever. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times I really wish steam would add a "neutral" button - It's Resident Evil, it's definitely good, but not in its current form.I'm going to assume there will be a day one patch to fix the stuttering and audio issues, but as of day one, the game is virtually unplayable for many.On my RTX 3080 and R7 3700x I'm getting an average of around 30-40 fps at medium-high settings at 3440x1440 resolution. _childDocuments_.review: A fine entry in the series.It doesn't leave as strong an impression as other recent darlings--namely, RE7 and RE2 '19. The novelty of 7's first-person take has kind of worn off, and there's nothing in here as compactly intricate as RE2's puzzle-box police station. But, it's got everything else an RE fan should expect: lofty production values, slow, deliberate combat, meticulous bullet rationing, and laughably bad writing.The emphasis on exploration feels lighter here, and long segments are pretty on-rails. Almost every time you get a key, you already know where the door is. The body horror moments now come so frequently that they kind of read like gruesome jokes. The maguffin-guarding area lords have decently cool designs, but other than that big vampire lady, you get the sense that you've seen them all before (they are--no spoilers--Chucky, yet another giant fish, and Magneto). And none have anything to do with the narrative, of course. But what did you expect? RE has never tried to hide that it's just a video game.For a triple-A series that has reinvented itself so successfully and frequently, an entry like RE8 is always going to feel a little disappointing. But, some of the zombies have jet boosters and drill arms, and that's pretty cool.

_childDocuments_.review: !!NO SPOILERS!!Some context:I see a lot of Resident Evil fanboys rating this game negatively because it "doesn't feel like a Resident Evil game." So I'm going to be writing this review about how the game performs as a game, NOT as a Resident Evil game. Also I'm going to be rating it on four different aspects, the game play, the combat, the spooky, and the story.The actual review:THE GAME PLAY 8/10: The game play in RE: Village is pretty similar to other RE games as in you go around searching for different keys or items that open doors or unlock different items you need to progress. You usually find these by searching the village or by doing puzzles. The actual exploration of the village was very fun as there were many secret paths and many areas for you to search. The map is pretty big so you will spend a lot of time exploring. The puzzles are not very difficult and pretty underwhelming in most circumstances.THE COMBAT 9/10: The combat was my favorite part of this game, it was so satisfying to walk up to a zombie and blow its head off with a shotgun. The gunshots felt responsive when you hit a zombie in the head, and just overall felt good. You will be doing a lot of shooting things in RE: Village, so if you like shooting things you will not be disappointed in this game.THE SPOOKY 5/10: The weakest part of RE: Village is how un-scary it is. There were a couple parts in this game when I did feel pretty scared, but after you get all your weapons and gear nothing is very scary anymore because you know that anything the pops out at you, you can just blow its head off. I do wish there a little more spooky parts in this game but the rest of the game makes up for the lack of it.THE STORY 8/10: I really enjoyed the story in RE: Village, I felt that the devs definitely did a good job with the story. There are some emotional parts and there are some spooky parts, but the overall plot was the best part for me. It did a great job continuing on from where RE: 7 left off but at the same time it felt like its own story in general. OVERALL 9/10: I really enjoyed my time playing this game and I definitely feel like I got my moneys worth. If you are looking for a pure RE experience maybe this isn't the game for you. If you are just looking for a solid 12 hour game that you can really have fun in, I highly recommend Resident Evil: Village.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always reserved special spots for the Resident Evil series in my heart.Being one of the longest running horror franchise, it has crafted many great moments, characters and stories. Whilst RE8 can be played as a standalone game, having played the previous games in the franchise or at the very least, RE7 will enrich your experience by providing you with a much more complete story. The moment I completed RE8, I'm very confident that this is a very solid 9 out of 10 and is easily one of the best game in 2021. Let's break it down!In terms of horror, RE8 is not as scary as RE7. However, it makes up by providing you with a more unique and larger environments to explore. There are several areas in the game such as the celler and the doll house which really creeped me out. The sense of dread and helplessness is further enhanced by the fact that there are 0 jump scares throughout the game and always low ammo count. In the doll house area specifically, the game even removed your weapons and introduced outlast-like gameplay mechanic. I must say this area is the scariest area I've experienced in games in recent years. The action oriented gameplay ramped up in the second half of the game but it is highly polished and tells a great story that even answered some of my long time questions about the characters and settings. Upon completion, you will unlock the mercenary mode offers additional challenges and as RE traditions go, replayability is high with unlockable infinite ammo weapons intended for higher difficulties. Overall, I'm very satisfied with RE8 and I'm looking forward to the eventual sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think Resident Evil Village is one of the best solo triple A games that came out in the last few years, and I highly recommend it. I have nothing but praises in terms of story and gameplay. The game looks and run amazingly well. I've got a good configuration (RTX3080, 16gb RAM and a Ryzen 3600X) but surprisingly, a lot of the games that get released lately don't really run well. COD Black Ops Cold War, Red Dead Redemption 2, Cyberpunk 2077 for examples. In Resident Evil Village however, I can easily get 100fps+ with Raytracing. The game is super stable too.I've seen lots of comments about the length of the game, with some calling it too short. If you compare this to big triple A games like GTA5 or The Witcher 3, where the main story of these games can easily keep you busy for 40+ hours, and there are tons of additional contents in the form of side missions/quests, I guess I can understand why you would say that. RE8 main story took me approximately 12 hours to complete. I was playing on hardcore (the hardest difficulty available at the start) and took my time, explored at lot. If you plan on playing in normal/casual and be more focused on the story than me, you can probably expect 8 to 9 hours of gameplay.Personally it's the kind of duration I expect from this kind of solo experience, so I wasn't too surprised. What I really like about RE8 is the pace, the rhythm of the game. I feel like CAPCOM has really nailed this notion in the few last Resident Evil games that they have made/re-made. I never feel like there is any filler.  You know when you play those solo games, and you do these kinds of quests/objectives that you feel are there to just to add content ? Where you feel like it's just the same area copy pasted and you're doing the same thing for another hour ? Well, RE8 doesn't have any of those. It feels like watching a great movie. It's super intense, there are constantly new mechanics/zones/enemies to discover and that renew the experience. You constantly want to see what's next. The game also has replay value in the sense of hidden content/places in the game. After finishing the game, you can replay it with all of the equipments/unlock from your previous run (NG+/New game+). CAPCOM implemented a list of challenges to complete which can unlock a bunch of bonus content in the game, in the form of artworks, new weapons, cheats, etc. There are a lot of them, for example : - Finishing the game in the hardest difficulty - Beating bosses under a certain timer- Finishing the game using only the knifeThere's also the classical "Mercenary" mode that makes its return, which is basically an Arcade mode. You are dropped in an area of the game, and the goal is to score the most points by killing enemies. It's alright, but it's definitely not the highlight of the game.On the negative side, I thought that the difficulty of the game was weirdly calibrated. The puzzles are ridiculously too easy. You know this game for newborns where you have to put the shape in the hole that corresponds to them ? Yeah... that's pretty much the difficulty of the puzzles in this game. Fights also tell the same story, at least in the hardest difficulty settings. For example, I one-shotted almost every boss, but I got stuck at one of the intro sequences for almost an hour. Weapon damage is also super weird. One sniper shot does 10 times the damage of a single bullet of your handgun. The game also lacks an FOV slider.

_childDocuments_.review: Among re7, re2r and 3r, 8 is imo best of them all.7 felt too short, locations felt really small and, compared to 8, it felt very much like an interactive movie - which isn't bad in itself if the game has some crazy story or spectacle going on that will make use of linearity of the game but alas that didn't really happen in 7. It was just aight.8 improves on basically everything except the fact that horror elements are rather more sparse (which is not bad in itself too, just different). Big improvement in this game compared to 7 IMO is player agency - weapon progression/upgrade system is MUCH more robust than one in 7 and u will make more of your own choices on what u will want to get first, which items to craft etc. Enemies drop currency which makes killing feel rewarding. There is also a sizable amount of hidden currency items to find in the environment - that too fuels the progression system considerably. You have lots of options to deal with encounters and to power yourself up. Combat feels way better all around, there is much more weapons too.Difficulty, for a horror game scaredy-cat like me, was really great on Standard mode, I was trying my best and felt rewarded for it without the game feeling like a cakewalk. Story is similar in quality to 7 but imo a bit more intriguing. It has some very wacky stuff in it that made me go like "why would you do that" (same in 7) and i did not like such moments but overall it is cool. Characters (mostly antagonists) are neat and some plot reveals were great even though i was confused for the big part of few last hours and had trouble telling who is who lol. It is wacky, sometimes nonsensical in not really a good way - but ultimately cool. I felt satisfied with the amount to stuff to do in game, theres quite a bit of optional-exploration metroidvania elements and locations included in the game feel impactful/used how they are supposed to be used, which again, was a problem in re7 to me, lots of places in that game felt weirdly small.Music is nice, with some ultimate bangers, some tracks that get old pretty fast.Replayability factor is... mixed, there are few additional modes that u can try after beating the game and unlock more and more stuff to assert dominance on your enemies after unlocking infinite ammo weapons and that is VERY cool. But the bad thing about replaying re8 on ng+ imo is the inability to skip few lengthy walking sim/puzzle segments of the game where no actual gameplay action happens. It happens at the beginning of the game and around halfway through mostly, i wish they would just let u skip these segments on ng+ cause they are basically glorified cutscenes but alas.Graphics are amazing and optimization good.Bossfights are good.Great-ass, wacky game.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is an electrifying rollercoaster ride through horror and action that will leave you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.  I can confidently say this game delivers an experience like no other.First off, let's talk about the graphics. Wow! The visuals in Resident Evil Village are absolutely breathtaking. From the eerie village streets to the dark and foreboding castle, every corner of this game is meticulously crafted to immerse you in its world. The attention to detail is incredible, making every environment feel alive and hauntingly beautiful.But it's not just about the looks - the gameplay is where Resident Evil Village truly shines. The controls are smooth and responsive, allowing you to navigate the treacherous landscape with ease. Whether you're solving puzzles, scavenging for resources, or taking on hordes of terrifying enemies, every moment feels intense and exhilarating.And let's not forget about the story. Resident Evil Village continues the saga of Ethan Winters in a gripping tale of survival and mystery. From the moment you step foot in the village, you'll be drawn into a narrative full of twists and turns that will keep you guessing until the very end. And with memorable characters like Lady Dimitrescu and the enigmatic Chris Redfield, you'll find yourself invested in their fates every step of the way.Of course, it wouldn't be Resident Evil without its signature brand of horror, and Village delivers in spades. From jump scares to tense encounters with grotesque monsters, this game will have you jumping out of your seat one moment and nervously peeking around corners the next. It's the kind of adrenaline-pumping thrill that horror fans crave.Overall, Resident Evil Village is a must-play for any horror enthusiast, you're in for one heck of a ride. With its stunning visuals, gripping gameplay, and spine-tingling scares, it's an experience you won't soon forget. So grab your controller, brace yourself for the horrors that await, and prepare for a gaming experience like no other.

_childDocuments_.review: **Spoilers hidden**  Played with RTX 3080/ Ryzen 5 3600X/ 16 GB 3600MHzIt's the best-looking game I've ever played by a large margin; it's also one of the most fun gaming experiences I've ever had.  Some takeaways:It takes a step back from the horror aspect of RE7 in favor of a more action/cinematic experience.  A lot of people compare it to a cross between RE4 and RE7, but to me it feels more like RE4 crossed with Uncharted.  Fans of a pure horror genre might not like the change but I loved it.  That isn't to say there aren't any scary parts (there are), It's just less of a focus.The "avoiding unkillable enemies" aspect of RE7 plays a significant role in the early parts of the game, but tapers off in the second half.  In the castle especially this works really well.  Bosses become puzzles to solve where you have to meet certain conditions in order to kill them and it takes thinking on your feet to pull it off; it's very satisfying.One caveat is that the first 3/4 of the game is much, much better than the last quarter which is very disappointing in my opinion.  Ultimately the issues with the end of the game weren't enough to take away from my enjoyment of it as a whole. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: BUY THIS GAME AND PLAY IT IF YOU ENJOY HAVING FUN!I want to preface this review by saying that I've never been a very big RE fan. Had the first one on my PS1, but was too scared to play it, played RE2 and 3 (remastered), but was pulled into the franchise with RE7. RE7 was awesome, there were few things I didn't like about the game, so I wanted to put that out there due to the criticism the game's receiving over "not being a RE game".The game is absolutely stunning, and though I've seen a few complaints on FPS, I'm running it on very high settings, at around 80-120FPS, with no problems at all on a RX5600XT. Another note, the game uses a compelling sense of rule of thirds. Every single area I look at could be used as a wallpaper, so considering how big the game is, it was quite a feat to accomplish.The RE Engine is quickly becoming one of my favorites, combat is snappy and responsive, weapon animations are well made, and though the spread while moving or firing to quickly can be a bit forgiving, a sense of accuracy is made clear through gameplay. I kinda wish the weapon swapping would've been fixed, but I guess it adds some kind of culture to the game (Octo Ethan).Gameplay loop can be summed up by; New area with stuff you can't do, fodder enemies, area specific bigger enemies, mini bosses, hidden area that can be completed because of previous said new area with stuff you can't do (usually accompanied by a mini boss or bigger enemy), next zone, sell all your collectibles to the Duke, upgrade your stuff, ♥♥♥♥ your pants when you get to the ventriloquist's zone, rinse and repeat. There's a lot to do and is very well paced which keeps the game fresh. In terms of the horror aspect, I can definitely say I've screamed multiple times. But I'm also a massive ♥♥♥♥♥. Comparatively, I don't believe it has as many scares as RE7, but 8 definitely has one of the scariest (or uncomforting) thing I've ever seen in a video game. Overall, RE8 definitely felt a lot more tense, so if you enjoy that kind of stuff, this game's right up your alley.Overall, this game is a serious breath of fresh air, it's been a while since we've had a AAA title with this kind of quality, and it's definitely going down as one of the better games I've played in the last couple of years. The only people I would not recommend this game to are people who aren't a fan of horror/thriller, and anime lovers.People who watch anime shouldn't feel any enjoyment whatsoever.5/5.

They all felt distinctly different with differing themes and areas that came with their own differences in gameplay style, from Beneviento's creepy puzzle esque mansion where the player in unable to fight back to Heisenberg's factory with its onslaught of enemies and mechanical theme.Another thing that was done well was the overall story, while admitingly basic in motive and execution with it being a big fetch quest, it really allows for the game to bring out the character in Ethan, Chris and the lords, that can really make you appreciate, sympathise and hate them.The game ran good on a mid-range PC, sitting constantly at about 60fps on medium graphics, with the only noticeable dips being the headshot issue mentioned earlier and some dips while streaming to my friends during sections with lots of enemies, but the settings also allowed for a lot of customization with its graphics.While playing the game I encountered very little bugs, with the only ones occurring was a second of lag when landing head shots on the enemies sometimes. _childDocuments_.review: The good- Breathtaking visuals. Amazing detailed models and textures, awesome lighting. It's a piece of art.- Fantastic world with weird, haunted atmosphere. From the creepy, abandoned in a hurry, village to the imposing castle above it and so many other unique locations, everything will make you feel stranded and alone.- Fluid, fun gameplay with responsive controls. Each level has different approach which makes it interesting enough. Some locations prioritize action and others puzzles. The overall pace is great and never lets you get bored. Shooting is addictive and kills are rewarding.- One of the best sound designs ever in a video game. Amazing job with the environmental sounds. Every bush's rustling, every door's crackling will make you sweat. It never feels excessive. Everything is super realistic with attention to detail. Battles' sounds, shooting, enemies' roars are great. Ethan's sounds, heavy breathes, struggling makes it even more suspenseful. - A stunning cinematic experience with great flow and high quality cut scenes. Fantastic direction and photography.- Great characters design. Although mobs are a little bit boring, the bosses are pretty unique visually. The main five enemies have a weird, grotesque style that helps on creating an eerie, almost surreal atmosphere. They're all absolutely unforgettable. The Duke is such a cool guy.-  Very good job on motion capturing. Great animations. Very good facial expressions. Everything feels super smooth and realistic.- Nice, convincing voice acting performances.- The main story isn't anything special but the lore surrounding this small village is pretty rich. A combination of traditional legends, medieval vibes, modern gear and sci-fi elements make the game's atmosphere even more unique.- The "Village of Shadows", that small animation video at the beginning is pure art and could easily be a stand alone short movie.- A menu full of extras gets unlocked the first time you finish the game. It includes challenges, concept art, 3d models, videos and more.The bad- It isn't survival horror. Unlike older games of the series that you have to survive with whatever you find, here there is a shop, you can loot enemies' bodies and sell trophies in exchange for bullets and gear. The supplies are plentiful and the inventory is huge. You don't need to count your bullets anymore. The game has evolved into a run and gun action shooter which is entertaining but not exactly what you expect from a "Resident Evil". Especially the last part with all those stuns, blockbuster battles, bombarding and tank driving threw me completely off.- This cinematic approach is great for selling to bigger audiences, but it doesn't have that raw horror feeling of its predecessors. It feels too restricted, too guided. There are many scripted sequences with predetermined path of movement and others that look like QTEs. It just keeps reminding you that it's a movie and not an actual experience that you have to find your own way to escape.- Puzzles are easy with completely linear and uninspiring structure. Usually you don't need to think or even open the map cause the game automatically guides you to the next object that you have to find. A little bit more freedom is offered at some locations but it never really "opens up".- A lot of things that Ethan does make absolutely no sense if you think about them. It's like he doesn't have a certain plan and tries random things. Furthermore a lot of things seem to happen completely by accident. Luckily all the monsters throw him at the right place.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not believe what I am seeing. It feels like my eyes are playing tricks on me but no, it's legit. I had my FPS counter up the entire time to confirm I wasn't crazy.In short, this game runs like f*cking butter. Holy sh*t it is so, so smooth. Rock solid 144 FPS in my 3 hours of playing (at the time of this review) and it never dipped once. Not even from gameplay to cutscene transitions (which is typically when FPS dips occur), or even when moving from one area of a map to the next (another common offender of FPS stutters). I am nowhere even close to finishing the game but the performance alone gets a thumbs up from me. It's extremely rare I say that in this day and age with all the god awful PC ports constantly being released. I do recall hearing back when this game originally launched that there were performance issues regarding how Denuvo was implemented or something along those lines. So, I came into this game wary and with expectations tempered. Either it was fixed or those FPS drops only affected a small selection of people. Regardless, as it stands this game is unbelievably well optimized. I got this game for sale along with RE7 for roughly 60 bucks and that includes the gold edition of both of them. If you were like me and got any of those 2 games on sale, they are an absolutely steal. Yes I recommend Resident Evil: Village, it is fantastic. May or may not come back to update this review when I finish the game but like I mentioned before, the performance is so good it gets a thumbs up from me regardless.Alright 10 hours later I have finished the main game and everything I wrote before still applies. There were a couple instances where the FPS would dip for a second but those instances were so rare it doesn't matter. It's not like I expect games to run flawlessly 100% of the time without any single hiccups. This game still runs like a dream and is an absolute blast to play. In comparison to RE: Biohazard, this game is a little less scary in favour of more action. Not necessarily a bad thing depending on how you view it, but something to think about. I personally didn't mind and found the wide arsenal of guns and the implementation of a shop system quite a fun departure from what was done in 7. I really liked how each antagonist had their own area and theme surrounding said area. The game has a village in the middle and surrounding it are 4 areas that each of the lords occupy. Beneviento's was my personal favourite, though it was shorter than I expected. For a roughly 10 hour game there is a surprising amount to do and see. It certainly felt much longer than 10 hours and it's one of those games where it's so good you wish there was more. However, it's easy to miss collectibles and with the game's challenges system, it incentivizes repeat playthroughs.  On the topic of playthroughs, I finished my first game on standard difficulty. Definitely consider ramping up the difficulty if you're considering doing more playthroughs because at that point you are familiar with the game's systems and layout. I think I can count on one hand how many times I died in this game on my first playthrough. That is certainly a byproduct of the game giving you lots of resources during combat, but it's also a testament to how well the game gives instructions. There's plenty of chase sequences and puzzles to solve where it's not like my ammo or guns would even matter in those scenarios. But the game does an excellent job of nudging you on the right path to take when you're being pursued, or dropping subtle hints when trying to piece together clues to solve a puzzle. So I had a very smooth and pleasant experience with this game. Certainly part of it was the abundance of resources, but also the game itself just does a really good job of guiding the player without frustrating them. I could have all the ammo and healing in the world but if I kept dying to some chase sequence or stuck in a room for an hour it would be a very different discussion. None of this is to imply that the game is boringly easy or anything like that, it's just a solid experience all around and it strikes that perfect middle ground of challenging but fair.In short, Resident Evil: Village is fantastic and I recommend it to anyone who isn't afraid to try some survival horror.

_childDocuments_.review: Although the plot is a direct continuation of the previous game, no prior knowledge of the events is needed. There's a nice recap at the start that tells everything you need to know and still manages to keep it short in case you haven't played it yet. Three years after the meeting with the Baker family, Ethan and his family lead a quiet life. One night, after the bedtime story (foreshadowing the events in the game), the legendary hero Chris comes knocking at their door. This is no friendly visit. Before he can ask questions, Ethan gets knocked out. He wakes up in the woods after a car crash, someone or something is there with him. By following the trail in the snow, he ends up in a village.The first hour in the village is unsettling. Everything looks abandoned, there are dead animals everywhere, and whenever you enter a house, you always hear floorboards creaking upstairs. It doesn't take long until a lycan bites off a nice chuck of your hand. Lycans, which is just another word for a new kind of zombie, or werewolves in this case, are your main foe in the village. They come in a variety of shapes and sizes, ranging from fast and vulnerable to armed and nearly unstoppable. Since the reward for killing them isn't worth it, it's better to just run past them and save your ammunition. But killing weaker enemies is a lot of fun, particularly once you learn their moves. They have a tendency to jump away the moment you press the trigger, so aiming a bit to the left or right is the way to go. And you don't want to waste ammo because even a basic enemy requires an entire clip from a pistol. Sometimes I felt like the battles were staged; you rush in loaded with ammo, but by the time the carnage settles down, your pistol has only 5 bullets left.Village is the first game in the series that tries to explore the open-world concept. Unfortunately, this only works for the titular village that acts as a hub. The other stages you visit in a linear order become off-limits once you complete them. As you collect new tools and keys for locked doors, each trip back to the village reveals a new path to a secret reward or a new monster. Because you're aware that this is a video game with its own set of rules, you don't pay attention to things that don't make sense. All defeated enemies drop lei, the game's main currency, as well as materials for crafting various types of ammo and medicine. Since this is a survival game, there is a limited amount of inventory space with the ability to expand. Items and weapons come in various sizes; the bigger the gun, the more squares it takes. Even if you can rotate items to make them fit better in your briefcase, you'll still have to juggle and decide which valuables to sacrifice for that brand new antique pistol. Despite the fact that the game brings back the old typewriter-based saving system (don't worry, there are still checkpoints), it neglects to include its companion, the storage box. This means that stuff in your inventory is everything you "own" and you can't switch weapons whenever you want.Your main source of new weapons and objects, the Duke, is willing to assist you for a price. He accepts lei and buys things you don't need. He can also upgrade your weapons and grant access to a special kitchen. Here you can cook meals that give you permanent perks, such as increased health or decreased damage. However, the ingredients need to be found first. Village, unlike other games in which you collect plants and prepare mainly plant-based meals, jumps right for the meat. You'll see chickens, pigs, and other animals being slaughtered. There are also a few rare creatures. But be careful. Since meat is in short supply and can be traded, you might lock yourself out of these perks.Upgrading weapons can hurt you too. Because there's no way to save them, you might waste resources on a nice gun that will turn itself useless once you find a better weapon. You can sell it to the Duke, but most of the resources will be permanently lost. Since each of the four lords reside in its own distinct environment, you will have to adopt different approach. One environment requires you to use stealth, which becomes totally pointless in the next, which brings back the suspense and horror from the previous game. The fist level, for example, includes a mechanic that has been implemented into every new Resident Evil game: an enemy that can appear at any moment and chase you relentlessly. Except that it's almost a joke in this game. Lady Dimitrescu is so big she has to bend down to go through a door. While she's busy getting back up, you can easily run past her and into a save room, which is apparently off-limits to her.The inevitable boss fight awaits at the end. With the exception of one, they all take a lot of punishment, so you probably won't have enough ammo with you to take them down. That's why you need to run around the arena and collect valuable resources. The bad news is that bosses have several stages with different attack patterns. These hurt and you'll probably die several times before learning them. Although you can kill the bosses just by shooting at them, you'll run out of ammo long before they die in a satisfying fountain of goo. Battles feel like an excuse to waste all the best grenades and ammo you're been saving all this time. Instead, you have to pump enough bullets into their body to reveal a weak point. Even those, however, can survive a few hits from the most powerful gun and prolong the combat until it becomes a chore. Half the time you don't even know if your weapons are doing any damage. First-person view doesn't work well. Unlike the old third-person games, where you can keep the camera on the enemy at all times, here you're constantly running away from the boss without being aware of its position. When you stop to take a look, you usually get hit by something you never see coming.By completing in-game challenges, you earn CP points that can be used in the shop to purchase special and infinite ammo weapons, character figurines and even a new game mode Mercenaries. This is basically a time-attack mode in which you need to score points and clear stages as fast as possible.  Unlocked stuff can then be used in the main game.After going back to its horror roots and slow gameplay with the seventh game, Village adds more action and goes for the spectacle. I'm afraid this doesn’t sound like good news for the next main game in the Resident Evil franchise. If we take a look in the past, action came to the forefront with each new game. So, if we follow the same trend, the series will turn into a first-person shooter with zombies. That's when the series loses its identity. And there's no going back after crossing that point.  Rating: 8/10Reviewed by:

_childDocuments_.review: -My Short History with Resident Evil-Heard a lot about it but never played any until 5, and it was great fun if only because it was something that was co-op. As I grew older I've grown to love every bit of the franchise, no matter how varied. 5 remains special to me but like most people I consider 4 to be the best, or at least the most fun. I've played every mainline entry that's on PC at this stage, including Revelations. I've been drawn to similar games too like Evil Within. Resident Evil made me love survival horror.-Reviewing The Game (Spoiler free)-It's definitely less scary, while i am a veteran and i appreciate the similarities to RE4, the fact that every single enemy drops loot without fail in all difficulties removes a big question of when exactly they die. Of course there have always been other tells, audio or visual but having something so concrete removes much of the fear from the enemies themselves. Along with neatly placed documents that tell you how to kill whatever's in the next room. The franchise has always had hints like this but i don't feel like it's ever been so detailed and conveniently located. This also removes a lot of the spooks. There's some new additions to the formula with a shove ability after you block certain attacks. If you are looking for a survival horror game and not an fps with a horror dressing, play on hardcore right from the start. Obviously doing so won't entirely erase the fact that this game is more action and exploration focused. With that said, the range of environments, like most RE games will surprise you. Sometimes you will wish you could spend more time in some versus others, and a strong complaint for me in this game is just wanting more. Many of the threats you encounter are kind of isolated. There's several notable hostile NPC's but it's extremely little the amount of internal interaction they have. When you are in X persons area, they and their particular cronies are the only threat you will face. In RE7, it felt like the family was really toying with you as a collective. There was times when it focused on one more than another but it felt more unpredictable on a first time through and even replaying it, it feels more interesting being able to see them all more often. Basically in 8, the characters are just as interesting but really not built upon as much as the Baker family was. It feels too cookie cutter. I don't think a narrative/puzzle driven game like Resident Evil could handle a "pick your own adventure" approach to which threat you went toward, but if they were determined to quarter them off in their places as they did, maybe it would've been worth trying? But besides the quality of spooks, it's a great game. The story is great, and it's a decent sequel from a franchise that doesn't really do them. It's still funny, it's still surprising and shocking. But it's game-play at least, isn't as spooky. It feels like the combat really has become too formulaic in this entry. Even in RE4 you were dealing with tank controls if combat became too predictable. In this, to it's detriment, it's too fluid and easy. About the only thing limiting you is the fov, but even then enemies don't seem too dangerous when you can't see them. In the end it's a fantastic entry, a great starting point for newcomers and a great continuation of the franchise and Ethan's story. While being at times both a subtle and heavy handed homage to earlier titles in a truly endearing way. Sometimes it's cool, sometimes it's meta, sometimes it's respectful and at times downright hilarious. Even without comparing it to the rest of the franchise, it's like a love letter to classic horror aesthetics (not so much thematically though, this is still Resident Evil). The references to RE4 and 5 in this make for some interesting discoveries both in the games lore and stories about the real life development of the games. The potential for dlc and a sequel is strong. Also the mercenary mode this time around features almost rogue-like combat elements. Makes replaying it more fun despite the fact it's still kind of just a time trial in a preset location from the story.-Summary-I love this franchise, I love this entry. If you liked 7, you will enjoy this without a doubt, but bear in mind it's differences. I have no idea where Resident Evil goes next, but you will see me there.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. The only major complaint I could have is that it isn't really a  follow-up to RE7, in the sense that it's just such a different tone. It's kind of like the Aliens to RE7's Alien, or the Terminator 2 to Terminator. In RE7, despite all the pseudoscience fantasy stuff, the story was pretty grounded, and the challenges you faced felt insurmountable, like you  just barely scraped by (even though really you didn't have much trouble at all). RE8 has a lot more action and a lot more large threats, but at the same time, Ethan really feels kind of ready to face them, so some of that tension is lost. Oh, and another flaw with the game: despite having more varied enemies than 7, it still really didn't have great diversity of enemies. Most of the enemies were just the same sort of AI with different costumes, that stagger more or less when shot.But overall, it's incredibly fun. The story is compelling enough to keep playing, the setpieces are very refreshingly different with their own unique experiences, and the action is harrowing but - again - not overwhelmingly so. While the emphasis on action  does distract from the horror to me, I'm actually surprised at how effective some of the scares really are. Since the events of the game delve way more into the fantasy side of RE, there was also more freedom to set up scenarios that genuinely toy with you deeper than just a jumpscare. There are tons of secrets to find, and the map is incredibly helpful in finding them without just giving everything away. There was only one puzzle that felt a little obtuse, and unfortunately it comes pretty early on in the game, but everything else is comprehensible enough to piece together without feeling like the game is just holding your hand all the way through. It's got an almost metroidvania feel, where you have the titular village as a hub with 4 main baddie-controlled areas to explore, then as you beat a boss in that area, you unlock something that will grant access to even more of the village. It really makes exploration exciting, and again the map is helpful for finding things you've come across but couldn't access before.Performance-wise, I was blown out of the water by this game. With a 3060ti, I have moderately high expectations for what I can  run well, but at 1440p plenty of games struggle to stay over 100fps at all times. But, with very rare exception, I maintained a stable 144fps throughout the entire game! The graphics settings are decently comprehensive. I thought it was pretty cool, albeit in a mundane way, that the game has minimum and maximum brightness settings. Great for those who like to pump the brightness up a bit - you don't have to completely blind yourself in lighter scenes now.All-in-all, I could keep going, but it was just completely fun. It has a kind of slow ramp up, but then the pedal hits the metal and this game never slows down. Simultaneously, I played for an hour or two and felt like it was 8, because I was so absorbed in the game, but then later finished the game in ~10.5 hours and it felt like it just flew by. I wanted more, and yet it never started feeling like it was overstaying its welcome.I just hope RE can keep up with these last two games. If it goes back to the classic style after these, they'll have lost at least one fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rare AAA game that is not a pretty disappointment.  It's a tour de force!Some people are saying this is an unfortunate mixture of RE4 and 7; I've played both and I think it's true on the surface but this game has its own thing going.  It's definitely worth the purchase; it is a lot of fun and it's almost like several smaller games tied together by a hub.  The locations have very different play styles and atmosphere.  I suppose you could beat it in 10 hours but I've enjoyed just walking around and taking in the sights.The visual presentation is also amazing, though, there is a bug where the FPS dips (which is usually a buttery smooth 60 + FPS with everything turned up to 11 on an RTX3080; I have a 60 Hz monitor so I am not sure what the internal FPS is) into the teens and does not recover until the game is reloaded.  It's not scene-dependent and it does not seem to be the GPU overheating since the FPS recovers immediately upon returning to the main menu and then the same scene plays just out fine.  Turning some of the settings down (specifically, going from ultrawide 1440p to 21:9 1440p and leaving all quality settings intact) does make this more bearable since the fps goes down to a technically playable 30 FPS but it needs to be fixed because it is SUPER annoying!  The autosaves are sparse and it basically comes down either suffering till the next save point or losing progress.  I hope this is patched soon; no complaints otherwise.  I hear this is a memory leak specific to NVIDIA RTX cards.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village is a wonderful game.Split into four main sections, each covers different themes, so there is something for everyone to enjoy while playing. The villains are all very well written, and their battles all feel very different from each other, creating unique challenges for each fight. The story is also well intertwined with previous installations and you can tell a lot of time has gone into everything, from the beautiful environments to the lore scattered throughout the various areas. Coming straight from finishing RE: Biohazard, it takes a little while to get used to the new systems such as the inventory, but once you do it is a major improvement on the old one. The currency system is also a great way to allow the player to get new upgrades without it feeling like the game just hands it to them when they need it.The game is also not very demanding, I use a laptop and was able to run the game perfectly with no crashes or frame drops and the game still looked absolutely stunning. There is also content in game that you can unlock after completion, allowing you to replay the game with a completely different experience. As I bought the game with all DLCs, I will mention that the bonus content is somewhat lacking, such as the odd choice of safe room music you can enable, but I would not recommend using them anyway, as it breaks some of the game's atmosphere with out of place objects such as tape recorders rather than typewriters for save points, this is of course personal preference.The positives of this game definitely outweigh the negatives though, and I cannot recommend it enough.10/10, would definitely play this again.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best survival horror game I've ever played.  The graphics and level of detail are nearly immaculate and the range of environments depicted, from quaint and snowy chateaus to dark, dingy subterranean crypts and factories just took my breath away.  The characters and their designs are interesting and memorable, each adding their own horrific theme and set of challenges to overcome. Since Village does continue the story through the eyes of Ethan Winters, having a basic understanding of what took place during the events of RE7 is a must to fully appreciate the story and its conclusion.It's clear that the horror elements introduced in RE7 have been ramped up considerably, I can recall many "oh-shi*" moments ranging from jump scares to desperately running or attempting to craft supplies with what few raw materials you have while being chased by hordes or giant enemies.  I would definitely recommend to play at a harder difficulty for more fear factor, since ammo is usually pretty easy to come by if rationed well.  The combat system is roughly the same as the previous title, though the introduction of weapon component upgrades and a mini economy provide a nice sense of progress and encourage fully exploring the environment for maximum benefit, though admittedly the scavenging and certain enemy encounters become a bit repetitive at times.I bought the game when it was on sale for around 10% off, but definitely wouldn't have been disappointed had I paid full price. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hot take: Resident Evil Village is one of the best entries in the series, and it’s in my top 10 favorite games of all time. I originally played it on Series S back when it came out, but recently took advantage of the Halloween sale and picked it back up again on PC. This is one of the best horror games I’ve played and I’ll explain why (spoiler free.) Story: The story is top notch. Ethan Winters is probably my favorite Resident Evil protagonist. He’s just a normal guy. Not a John Wick esque, roundhouse kick giving, boulder punching BA. Just a normal dude trying to save his wife and daughter and doing whatever he can. I love it. The story takes many twists and turns, including a ton of jaw dropping moments and action set pieces. Without spoiling anything, the game is split up into different “zones” that encapsulate different horror themes and gameplay styles. There’s survival horror, psychological horror without the ability to fight, straight up epic action sequences, and much more. In my opinion, the game stayed fresh throughout and the story kept me engaged the entire time. The bosses are excellent. Voice acting is superb. Set piece design is A+. The roster of characters in the game is fantastic, most of them are very well written and memorable. The game is a mix of action and horror. The game is overall not the scariest game I’ve ever played, but it has one section… oh God… one section that is THE scariest thing I’ve ever played. I speedrun this game and EVERY time I get to this certain section I dread it. The finale left tears in my eyes and really resonated with me emotionally, especially as a new father myself. I was a huge fan of RE7 and RE8 and I loved the Ethan Winters storyline. He truly is the greatest dad ever. Gameplay: The combat is top notch. I will say, it is much easier on PC than console because of mouse and keyboard. Part of what made it scary on console is how difficult the aiming was on the game pad. If you have decent aim, the combat is much easier on PC. The game is loaded with puzzles and treasures that reward exploration and sharp wit. If you take your time and search every inch of the game, you won’t be lacking in money, supplies, and really cool weapons. The game is difficult, but exponentially more so if you just try to barrel your way through the game as fast as possible. Presentation/Graphics: I personally think this game is one of the most visually appealing games I’ve ever seen. Whether it’s a dank, dimly lit basement illuminated solely by flickering candles, a gorgeous castle hall, snowy forest, or a factory corridor lit by flashing red lights, the game is gorgeous and makes fantastic use of light. Textures are gorgeous. If you run the game on max settings with ray tracing, you’d be hard pressed to find a horror game with better looking textures and light effects thanks to the tremendous RE engine. Enemy designs are amazing. Every enemy looks unique and terrifying. Not only do they look terrifying, but their movement is very lifelike and immersive. Enemies don’t just sit still and wait for you to kill them. They sway  from side to side, attempting to dodge your bullets. The blood and gore effects are top notch. Exploding a werewolf’s head with a shotgun always feels nice. This game is really fun to speedrun. The whole Resident Evil franchise is consistently a good choice for speed runners because it rewards skillful play and you can really breeze through it if you commit the puzzles and fights to memory. Things you might not like: The game is very good, with the exception of a few stale segments that don’t hold up as well as the rest. (Fishing Village, I’m looking at you.) Some people might not like the B movie cheese, but those people have clearly never played a Resident Evil game before. As mentioned earlier, the game is meant to be played slowly. If you just want to barrel through a story, the game is probably not for you. Conclusion: Give this game a chance! It’s a wonderful addition to the series, and in my opinion it’s up there with RE4 in terms of quality. Hope you enjoy as much as I did!

_childDocuments_.review: After completing this game I can safely say that this resident evil is the best in the series aside from 4 and 7. The environments actually feel handmade like someone's soul actually went into it.The horror is REALLY good, much better than 7's sort of cheesy over the top campy horror. The regenerator moment for this game is in the second house and believe me, that thing is absolutely horrifying, coupled with the suspense when running for the elevator.
