_childDocuments_.review: I won't lie. As a diehard fan of this saga since the first game, i was skeptic about this game, but it surprised me big time.This game takes off what Resident Evil VII left and gives it renewed value, bringing the story forward in an extremely well narrated and well paced game.- You don't need to play any other game to understand the story even if it's the 8th in the main series. You could play RE7 for a full picture of this game story, or watch the RE7 recap you find ingame here.- I'm not one to pay attention to it, but the graphics were simply gorgeous. 10/10- The characters are well designed and some are quite likeable, even the damn villains.- The world design is stunning. Wandering off in the world can make you discover eerie and gorgeous locations. Some may induce curiosity, making you explore further and further, others may induce anxiety and claustrophobic feelings that will make you want to bolt out of there. The mix between beauty and danger is perfect, at least for me.- The feeling of progression reminds me of Resident Evil 4, in sense of tuning up your weapons until you can  get the next best thing.- The merchant is not just a "Whaddaya buyin?" guy, he has cute and funny interactions. He even cracks a joke once or twice. A real personality that brings you moments of company from time to time. - The stress inducing situations are truly ones of survival horror, where you have to manage your resources and path in order not to ♥♥♥♥ up your progress. You may end up spending one hour exploring the map trying to get some currency to buy more items because you were reckless before, or you may be able to sell some stuff to upgrade your favourite weapon to feel more secure going forward.- The story is well paced and very well narrated. The main character grows on you like a good friend or a brother and you can truly feel his dispair through out the game, with the ending being something you can truly empathise with.  - Some apparently ridicolous stuff happens during the game that arises questions by design, and the plot-twists are real.- I loved the final boss design, simply epic, can't put to words how much i loved the design.- The background music could have been better, seems like they did not pay much attention to it which is weird in a Resident Evil Game.- There is one specific plot-twist that was designed just for marketing and it shows, leaving one big plot-hole or inconsistency.- The marketing hype for Lady Dimitrescu will cause some mixed feelings after beating the game for reasons that shall be rather obvious.- The FPS for some people seem to fall harshly when the vampires are around, I had no issues with this though.- First person, i hate first person and i know this is a problem for me not for the game, but still, negative in my book. Looking forward to the third person mod.- Field of view is pathetically bad, there are mods to fix this available already that make the game much, much better.- Game is incredibly good for my taste and im sad i finished. If you like story driven games, and do not mind the first person, definitely try Resident Evil 7; then Resident Evil 8. Playing 7 before 8 wiil truly make a difference for how you feel during this game and after. The other games in the series are not needed in order to understand this story arch at all. RE:Village was an experience i did not have in years from a story perspective. Being a hardcore fan of the saga, specially the originals, this game has brought me back some hope for CAPCOM and curiosity for the future of the saga.Truly looking forward for the next installment in the series, and for now, probably busy trying to hunt down achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a Resident Evil that tops Resident Evil 4! What's there to say? It's basically Resident Evil 4, cranked up to 11. None of the formula has really changed, as far as fright factor and overall feel of the RE universe. I love this titles, where they break away from the overused T-virus thing. The revisiting of the super natural is always a refresh break, from the usual mutant zombies. The only bad thing that stems from clinging to the traditional RE layout is the "confined trail systems" aspect, that even Tomb Raider suffers from. That and the constantly overused "double back" system. Meaning, every route there is to take is visible off of the main path, but either barred, or locked, the first several times you may pass through the area, until you've either finished a particular objective, or found a proper tool, or key. In many ways this has been an annoyance, for decades. Resident Evil pioneered the model, and it was then adopted by, pretty much, ever survival horror game, including Dead Space. I'd like to see minimized in the future. Alan Wake managed to avoid this, namely by providing a number of different settings and somewhat more expansive areas, making the game feel more like it's continually moving forward, instead of used and re-used again. But I'll not complain because the game freaking hits every note beautifully. I was almost sh**ing my pants in several areas. Especially those segments where all you can do is run and hide, or wait for the boss to finish creepily patrolling a particular zone you were in, so you could move again. The game is Resident Evil 4, meets Alan Wake, meets Alien Isolation, meets Tomb Raider (reboot), meets Dark Souls...that's really not a bad combination.  The only other issue, which is probably bigger than the often re-used areas matter, is, you have a crap load of weapons you can collect and upgrade, but no place to keep them all. I would like for there to be a universal storage box, near the merchant. This way I could come back and swap out my gear, as needed. Not sell weapons, to fit other (new) weapons. That's a horrible model. If you're going to have twice as many weapons as there are inventory slots then we need storage containers, so we're not forced to ditch healing salves and ammo for more weapons. So, really? Overall? It's mostly just an inventory issue this game suffers. Especially since some items, like healing salves, don't stack but really ought to and other things that do stack, don't stack nearly enough, like sniper ammo. You're only able to hold 15 in a stack.

_childDocuments_.review: MY RATING: ★★★★★★★★☆☆ 8 / 10After the end of Resident Evil 7, I wondered how they would make a sequel to the game and what direction the series would take. All of my questions were answered with Resident Evil Village. RE8 had the gunplay and 1st person perspective of RE7, with the village theme, inventory system and traveling merchant of RE4. Upon noticing this, I was very excited to play the full game because RE4 is my favorite Resident Evil Game and RE7 is easily top 5. Village didn’t disappoint with its memorable characters, detailed zones of the game and well written plot to wrap everything together. One thing that bugged me a bit was I felt as if I was given a bit too much ammunition, making the conservation of ammo little to no worry at all. Resident Evil Village divides itself into 5 sections with the village being somewhat of a hub area. BUGS:Microstuttering after kills and cutscene audio sync issues ZONES:Alcinia Dimitrescu’s section is the beginning part with the castle. This plays a lot like Resident EVil 2 with the fear of Dimitrescu hunting you down, for better or for worse, looming over you. This seemed to be the only section Capcom advertised. All I would see is the ads with the tall lady time after time. The next zone of the game is Donna Beneviento, or as I like to call her, the doll lady. I really enjoyed this section as it reminded me a lot of the evil brother from Resident Evil 7 and his birthday cake puzzle. It felt a lot like a reimagining of Silent Hill.   After the doll lady you come across Salvatore Moreau who’s section is pretty lame. THe giant fish in the sea is a lot like Resident Evil 4’s sea creature which was cool. But the final fight of the zone was pretty lame. Karl Heisenberg really stole the show for me with his zone of the game. The enemies, which reminded me a lot of the Regenerators from Resident Evil 4, kept me on my feet the whole way through. SPOILER SECTION

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village carries the burden of following up not just the  critically acclaimed Resident Evil 7 but also the series' 2 & 3 remakes. These games all vary drastically, and their different degrees and takes on the classic Survival Horror formula prove only to make this challenge more daunting. Right at the start, Village proves itself to be of a different mettle. Taking notes instead from the ever-classic Resident Evil 4, Village instead seeks to mark itself as another Survival Horror / Action hybrid. While that may stir insecurities in certain series fans, Village itself is an astoundingly good example of how solid these titles can be.Similar to Resident Evil 4, Village bombards players with a thorough depth of mechanics, mostly returning from 4 itself. The opening combat segment alone steals its gameplay from Resident Evil 4's hard opening, a scary village, filled with creatures, and only one objective: SURVIVE. Barricading myself into the buildings, pushing furniture in front of doors, and shooting the all new Lycan (Werewolf) main enemies, I quickly realized that this game was more of an homage to the Resident Evil 4 and 5 days, of horror-esque environments with tough as nails combat and an exaggerated, fun story. Don't take those words as an affront to the horror and quality of Village, however, this game can be outright dreadful, with one specific gameplay sequence reminding me more of a Silent Hill title. PROS:-Unique, Gothic Horror Aesthetic-Plenty of gross-out body horror-Outright beautiful graphics, comparable to that of Alien: Isolation and The Witcher 3-Combination of Resident Evil 4's action gameplay with 7's control scheming-Fantastic, somewhat exaggerated story with interesting plot twists-Wealth of unlocks and the inclusion of The Mercenaries optional gamemode-1 Incredibly fun, challenging difficulty unlockCONS:-Controls can sometimes feel slightly loose-No FOV options on PC (I recommend using Fluffy Mod Manager's built-in trainer)-Performance issues with Lady Dimitrescu's daughters-A dumbed-down Mercenaries modeConclusion: Resident Evil Village is definitely a step in the right direction for the series. As much as 7 captured that same classic survival horror feeling, Village does a perfect job of meshing it with action. In my opinion this is the second best action game in the series, next to Resident Evil 4.FINAL SCORE: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has followed the RE games since the directors cut of the very first game ill be giving my point of view.After the original Quadrilogy (RE1,2,CV,3) I had lost alot of hope for RE after 4 came out, it was a huge departure from the series to the point where i flat out lost all respect for the name, it became more about action and jokes and less about horror and survival. Flash forward to when RE7 dropped, My god was i amazed, it was everything i had ever wanted in a FP RE game, horror and survival every step of the way, it easily jumped ahead of what i considered the worst RE games (4,6,Revelations 1 and 2) and became one of my top 5.Now onto RE8. This game is yet again a HUGE departure from the series in the same way RE4 was, only this time it was for the better. This game is what RE4 should have been, horror, survival, story and intense boss fights. You can tell the devs knew this and they paid homage to RE4 in many ways, but also overshadowing it by miles. Many will try and say this isnt true RE because its not about killing zombies and Wesker, but as i said, it is a departure from that all, in the first stages of RE4 development it was very close to what RE8 is, and if they had only gone with that instead of the james bond rip off that it became then maybe the series could have avoided the blunders later on.When it comes down to it, RE8 is going to forever be in my top 5 replacing RE7 just slightly, with its stunning visuals and its heart shattering horror I can safely say that RE8 has beaten all expectations and gone beyond. This is easily a 10/10 purchase without any question.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil has faced a myriad of backlash after the slightly disappointing Nemesis (which I have not personally played) but CAPCOM secures another hit and continues the success of 7 with various improvements (both under-the-hood & in design/story telling). It is important to note that this is a successor and continuation of 7 and is designed to feel that way so if you enjoy the more "traditional" over-the-shoulder format of RE, you might be a bit disappointed.You can tell CAPCOM experimented a bit with mechanics in this iteration and not all of them succeeded but boy did they have an impact when executed flawlessly and the game has a lot of those moments for me, personally. At first, I was a bit apprehensive and confused by the story but questions & ambiguity in the beginning hours fuelled my drive to keep exploring. I just had to venture deeper to understand what was exactly happening and the revelations (whilst somewhat cliche at times) did satisfy me. The story's ebb & flow was smooth, the pacing somewhat fast but the end the delivery: impactful.The puzzles are not hard (it's not like your traditional horror in that regard) but they are somewhat interesting and help break up the action to take a break and lose yourself in the scenery. Have we spoken about environments? They are gorgeous. The world isn't large enough to be considered open or even semi-open but the way the levels are intertwined with smart blocking & locks help to pique that curiosity as you progress only to go "ooh, that's where this leads". Enemy design has been meticulous and the attention to detail impressed me immensely. There's a good chunk of variety in here so you won't feel like you are fighting the exact same enemy over and over but it's just large enough that you WILL think "not this guy again". As for standouts: I think we all know and can appreciate the "lovely ladies of the castle" as one prime example.As an avid horror fan, the biggest aspect I appreciated is when the game decided "okay, you've had some fun blasting your way here, now buckle up and put your diapers on". It leaves you helpless, it tortures your senses and creates the sheer terror of a truly psychological thriller during segments of the game. I would've loved more but when they cropped up, I was both terrified & filled with adrenaline. What sets RE:8 apart from a lot of other horror games is its balance of action & horror which are designed to complement each other to provide a varied & engaging experience. There are specific sections where you will simply not be able to shoot your way through, no matter what weapons you have or how good you are. If that is a negative, so be it but for me this was nothing but a positive. It's rare to find a game that employs a risky approach of trying to meld the two genres in such a unified manner. After you are done with the story, Mercenaries mode is a lot of fun with a heap of replayability & CAPCOM has gone the extra mile to make a second run more enjoyable beyond the usual "here's a crazy weapon for the next time, enjoy".Let's talk difficulty. I finished on "Hardcore" which is the "Hard" version of RE and it was challenging but not overwhelming. There's a steeper mode beyond that if you truly wish but I actually enjoyed not having the burden of having to min/max everything and potentially spoiling things just to understand what I would be up against. I died a good amount of times for me to reconsider elements of strategy and adapt my approach beyond running into everything and gunning things down. The bosses themselves are probably on the easy side but again, the story was what I was there for primarily so take heed.The lack of a FOV slider is a big no-no for a lot of people and I cannot defend CAPCOM here. I do agree it's unacceptable at this point in time that the game requires a mod for this but hopefully with time, this will get patched in but whilst this was inconvenient, it did not detract me from enjoying the game in its full glory.There's not a lot of good "horror" games lately and whilst this may not fit the full bill of what a horror game should be, it created a VERY fun run of emotions for me and for that, I say "well done". I might be easily pleased for some standards but I would consider this a huge and welcome success in my eyes. I thoroughly enjoyed every minute and only wish there was a bit more.As for that and in closing, m8, I r8 this 8/8. Recommended purchase from me if you enjoy a healthy mix of horror & action in a first person perspective. Think of this like a love-child between Resident Evil 4 & Resident Evil 7.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4, 7. I was hesitant about RE7 years ago, then fell in love with it. This installment meshes the first person RE with an RE4 environment and item management. A perfect horror setting in gothic castles and snow, fantastic attention to detail, yellow square vases with specimen inside to rotate and conjure deep, real horror, books with beautifully drawn stills to entice you in its lore, paralyzing lighting that truly stops you in place with fear, an entire section that feels out of P.T.'s concept trailer (The Dollmaker/Hallways). It's a very good game and I can't wait to see its conclusion, replay it on hard, try mercenaries etc, the classic RE experience. Very good, exciting, nostalgic, and new. The only issue i've seen from other reviews is the FOV, some people going so far as to return it and curse the devs. I'm not sure if their creative vision was for everyone to suffer at 70-80 FOV, I feel bad that it was and I'm changing it on them, but uh... mods do exist after all. The FOV fix is one of the easiest mods i have ever used, and I only try and use mods that are this easy. Download, run, fixed (its on nexus, Lazy FOV Fix). 70-80 FOV is a bit too zoomed in, 90 is perfectly fine. 100+ is for competitive mode for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically RE 7 except more so. There is about twice as many bosses to kill, four times as much ground to cover, five times as much treasure and secrets, and twice the story arc and combat. RE 7 was an amazing game and my favorite of the series when it first came out. But this game has put that game to shame with its vast map, terrifying scares, and an ultimately amazing character arc for Ethan Winters. You feel everything in this game. Nothing ever just happens that you don't react to. The puzzles are intricate, the combat is insane, the lore is intricate, and then ending leaves much up to speculation about what the next game will be like. Truly an amazing, amazing game. Well worth the 60 dollars I paid for it. They have truly outdone themselves. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Although not a masterpiece, one of the best Resident Evil games we've seen in the last 20 years.  The environments and lighting effects are some of the best I've seen on current gen hardware, and the story is one of the best efforts Capcom has put forward to date.  That said, nearly every positive has a "but" to go along with it, with loads of missed potential.The one example I'll touch on is the second major area you get to explore.  Although it is incredibly well done, it's also incredibly short and would likely have done better to have been the third section of the game rather than the second for pacing's sake (grounding/humbling the player as they were starting to rise heading into the final section[s] of the game).  Felt like they put it that early to appease RE7 fans and it was a mistake, imo. That said, if you're looking for a step into what's to come moving forward for gaming, this is an outstanding video game and worth your hard earned $$.  If you love action / horror style games, don't miss this one.   + ProsIncredible Lighting/EnvironmentsAmbient noises are well doneStory is one of the best RE stories we've gottenMore GunplayPacing is incredibly well doneBonus mode (Mercenaries) is tons of fun and a great post game reward- ConsSome sound effects feel very "stock" and phoned in A little cheesyGunplay feels a little meh overall outside of MercsCould have been GOTY with better directional choicesTL;DR: Both old and new RE fans have things to like here, and if you've never played a RE game before, the only thing you'll miss are a few references here and there, with even a recap of RE7 existing in this game.  Don't feel like you need to play the previous titles to give this one a go.  Solid 8.5/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good way to evolve this franchise, but unfortunately I don't like everything in this game. I really like the combat system, the story and the characters, but I don't like the level design of the game after the castle part. I appreciate the fact that you can find different styles of gameplay going through the game, but I don't like how it is done. However, it's a good Resident Evil game.I'm eager to see how the next chapter of this series will improve all the good features from Village. I really like the open map of this game and I hope to see something like this in a full survival horror Resident Evil game.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Story direction, cinematography, atmosphere, and everything in between, RE Village provided and satisfied both cravings of what RE fans, even the new ones, always wished for, a tasty and balanced blend of horror, action, and survival. Gameplay was executed perfectly bringing back the fun of customization and upgrade of guns, items, and even food are in your control throughout the entirety of the game. Along with diverse side paths that you can take to become stronger through treasure hunts, finding collectibles and solving puzzles for currency, the replay-ability of this game is surprisingly high, making sure you wouldn't miss the little bits of information that brings the game to full circle.Story and direction was straightforward and easily understood through navigating the remnants of diary entries and logs that provided a better context of the environment, along with the characters and enemies that inhabit the village, the residents all has its own unique environment and character. Much like how RE7 portray the infamous family of a variety of their own set of powers and morbid transformations, the game nailed on terrifying, sympathizing, and astonishing the protagonist and its players through its odd and wonderful concept and diversity.Furthermore, it consequently created the growing curiosity of what goes around the village that was accompanies by its set of horrific creatures from a humongous vampire lady, a Van Helsing and a lot more unfathomable beings, they managed to recreate and further refined the charms that successfully crafted the elements and concepts that made RE4 and RE7 a game-changing story of the franchise. This is truly worth the try to witness how CAPCOM is finally going to the right path of development towards the RE series, this game was honestly a slap on the face to the players that they've atoned for their mistakes and will go on for greener pastures. They've proven that they will most certainly provide a fresher and exciting take to the RE universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Loved every aspect of this game, the combat was fun, the story was interesting, this is one of those games that makes you not wanna leave your chair for ages, looking forward to more like this from Capcom! as a long time resi fan this change of pace and mix or styles is refreshing, some parts reminded me of resi 4 some of 5 with a mix of a new style that 8 brings to the table honestly this might be my new fav resi game.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Actual masterpiece. Story is solid, visuals are gorgeous and  gameplay is very reminiscent of RE4, except ofc being in first person. Combat can sometimes feel pretty clunky, but aside from that, I feel as though this game has a bit of everything in it for all fans of the series and even new fans. Would recommend to everyone, so long as they're okay with being afraid here and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil Village has incredible story telling. Probably the best story telling in all Resident Evil so far. It really takes you on a journey. The main cast are multidimensional, they invoke many conflicting thoughts - do you feel compassion, disgust, should they be condemned? This game's character relationships are all interwoven nicely, swift and relevant to the performance. The game also unravels itself in a satisfying way, it knows what it wants to share and does it at opportune moments. There are somethings that feel too strongly tied for convenience but I don't fault this, it is refreshing for once to have a story that wraps itself up in 1 package.The voice acting is fantastic, best voice acting I've ever experienced in a game. I turned subtitles off for the most part to really enjoy the delivery of each scene.The gameplay is up to you, can play it fast or moderately paced. There is a lot to explore and many things in the environment to really take in.Overall this is an incredible game, seeing how history goes I'm sort of sad you know, I'm not even sure we will see another gem like this. Resident Evil Village is definitely going down as one of those games we can pick up in 10-20 years time and will still enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Embark on a quest to rescue a kidnapped daughter and end up in a remote village. From the moment you enter the village, the atmosphere is reminiscent of RE4, with each location crafted to evoke fear and isolation.The game boasts stunning visuals, with lifelike environments and characters immersing players deeper into the horror. Combat is intense as you confront grotesque enemies and towering monstrosities, armed with an arsenal of weapons.What sets Resident Evil Village apart is its captivating storyline, rife with twists and turns that keep players guessing. Ethan's journey forces him to confront his fears and make difficult choices that shape his fate.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Being a Resident Evil fan, I was interested to say the least when they announced this game. I will say though, the marketing is a little falsely done, as the marketing is mainly based around the castle, & that is only just the beginning of the game. The game actually picks up after that, but it has different flavors of horror added into this game. I don't think everyone will enjoy this game, but I think this game will be remembered because of how different it is, but Resident Evil itself is just "different" than what we expect it to be. I can honestly say I did enjoy this more than Resident Evil 7, but my taste is subjective to the reader most likely. If you want, I say pick this game up, but don't expect anything from it, because it will find a way to surprise you either way.

_childDocuments_.review: The sign is a subtle joke. The shop is called "Sneed's Feed & Seed", where feed and seed both end in the sound "-eed", thus rhyming with the name of the owner, Sneed. The sign says that the shop was "Formerly Chuck's", implying that the two words beginning with "F" and "S" would have ended with "-uck", rhyming with "Chuck". So, when Chuck owned the shop, it would have been called "Chuck's Feeduck and Seeduck".The game is amazing. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time I have ever left a review longer than a word or two, but this game really deserves it. While it's not particularly hard, with the exceptions of some bosses, it's also not immensely scary other than one, maybe two, of the levels, the story is one of the best I have ever experienced in any game ever. If you like story-heavy games this is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10I had missed out on playing RE: 7 cause I was a big baby and the game went back to it's horror roots and delivered something that blew everyone out of the water. The RE: 2 remake was another step in the right direction with their new engine and while the RE: 3 remake wasn't the best, hype was high on this one. And given how much hyped games have come to end up being on launch, I can say that Village has hit a home run.I won't disclose any story spoilers but let me put it this way, I bought this on an impulse after checking if I can run it at the minimum because I wanted to experience the story first hand and not later find it out or watch someone bumble about the game. If you're a huge RE fan from a lore respective? This game is right up your alley.Now what if I told you this game took what made RE: 4 the commercial success that is was and took what made RE: 7 great, and put them together? It gives off so many good RE: 4 vibes and this feels like the Resident Evil 4 Capcom wanted to make all those years ago, for any of you old enough to remember the early concepts of 4. Now I have a laptop and it's nearing it's third birthday so I wasn't playing this on the highest settings but the game still looks damn good and that's probably more credit to how good the engine of the game is. Yes, there are times where the game doesn't attach your HP but rather your framerate but, I didn't die because of those so I wouldn't right it off as a flaw.There's mods to remove those anyways, in case it does bother you.Again, I would say the game is perfect really but that's my own experience and it may differ. But I highly recommend it, especially if you can play with friends watching like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Here we are... the predecessor of RE7 has been around for some time now and it definitely has been a very interesting experience! First and foremost the story is captivating once again, since what seems to be a quite relaxed evening at the house of Ethan and Mia begins to unravel with shocking developments. Moreover as you progress through the game you meet some intriguing bosses who have a backstory and it was one of the few times i made a little research for game characters after i finished the game due to the fact i was really interested to find out their whereabouts! Furthermore the visual sector is stunning! They definitely took their time so as to create beautiful sceneries and magnificent buildings like the Dimitrescu castle. As for the sound and music sector i have no complains at all. The field however where this RE shines is the atmosphere. It may not be as scary as RE7 (for the most part) though there is no doubt it achieves building an intriguing tension especially during the first two chapters. Nevertheless the best and by far most memorable part of the game for me in terms of atmosphere and tension was the whole House Beneviento chapter, on account of the fact it constituted a unique experience i haven't encountered in a game for a very long time! Don't worry guys because i won't spoil it for you. You will just have to play the game to find out.. Of course there are also parts with too much shooting which is of course a striking contradiction with other more subtle sections and what i didn't like is that the boss fights are quite easy but overall despite its flaws and its weaknesses RE Village is a game with which you will pass a good time and on the whole i fell satisfied when i finally saw the credits........ Can't wait for the next RE....
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Resident Evil 4? If you say yes to this question, chances are you probably will be fine with Village as well.Village is the second adventure of Ethan Winters, this time given more of a character from his time in 7, and a lot of things have changed in the interim:* You no longer keep crafting items in the same space as your main inventory as crafting items are kept in its own inventory section, and your main items are kept in an attache case similar to how the inventory was managed in RE4. * The gun play is fine, but ammo will usually be in short supply and thus, you'll need to rely on crafting more ammo in case you ever start to run dry.  * The game is a lot more intense with enemies being abound and with more variety in comparison to the Molded in RE7, with some enemies requiring the player to change up how they're point and shooting to kill.If none of the above or the initial question of liking Resident Evil 4 bother you, then the game is probably going to tide you over for a solid 8 hours or so. That all said, I play on a computer with not insignificant parts, and there are small occasions where the game slows down to a crawl to process the enemies in the area. This doesn't happen enough to be a deal breaker, and if you have a computer that is far above the recommended specs and is powered by the essence of angels, you probably won't have this issue. But I still bring this up because it has happened enough times to me where I was brought out of the experience and there were times this has happened and I was fervently trying to pause or otherwise regain control so I didn't die at a bad time.

The Game looked amazing, the Bosses were all unique, no cardboard personality-placeholders, with few bullet-sponge fight sequences.The puzzles were few, but clever and meaningful. _childDocuments_.review: Probably my second favorite Resident Evil game after RE4. While the game retains the first person perspective and a similar looks to RE7, the game leans more in an action/horror direction. You get a wide variety of weapons, plenty of ammunition, and things move at a much faster pace. The weird "wet" look of the textures from RE7 has been fixed, too. The story is compelling, and the variety of weapons and approaches make multiple playthroughs appealing. There's a lot to like here.Is there a downside? Like the remakes of RE2 and RE3, plus RE7, it's short. I've wondered if it's some kind of limitation to the RE Engine or something, but all of the games that use it are short. It's roughly twice as long as RE7, but it's tiny compared to RE4, RE5, and RE6. Replayability helps, but I wish the main story was about 30% longer. Especially with how rapidly the story wraps up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best horror games I've played in the past decade. It's not as scary as RE7, but I really dig the Universal Monsters-style rogues gallery in this one. Lotsa variety, and gunplay feels fine. There were rumors of SJW nonsense pre-launch, and thankfully I can confirm there isn't a trace of that in the game; I'm thinking RE8 will age really well. If you're on the fence, I recommend going for it. Don't play this before RE7, though, I'd recommend getting the RE7/RE8 bundle if you don't already have it.Spectacular art design, really cool bosses, the village is memorable. Runs incredibly well at 1440p 170FPS on a 6800 XT and 5900X, max settings minus RT. Facial mo-cap doesn't seem quite as impressive as RE7 for some reason, but otherwise animations are great.Overall like a 9.5/10 for me, but here are some cons:- The puzzles are incredibly simplistic, not very stimulating. Most are sorta like finding a red key card to open a door in Doom, but the actual puzzles don't take more than a few seconds to figure out.People with weaker hardware may experience framerate drops in certain segments.- Narrative point that irks me:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. The game is exactly how it looks, a combination of RE4 and RE7 in terms of gameplay and story. The gameplay elements added from RE4 are great and the game really does align closer to the type of design introduced in RE7 and RE2R with more puzzles and exploration than in RE3R. It's a very meaty RE game and has a really great story with many points that you don't want spoiled. Easy 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 7 is, without a doubt, my favorite horror game of all time and the long-awaited Village sequel is nowhere near a disappointment. Village focuses more on action rather than the survival-horror aspect that revolved around 7, but with an upgrade in storytelling and graphics. As a fan who has played almost every resident evil game to date, I can't encourage you more to be open-minded and experience Village whether you're new or familiar to the resi series.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Although overall it's not actually a bad game, (I have spent over 46 hours playing it after-all) it isn't a good Resident Evil Game. Now this is coming from someone who think Resident Evil 4 is very overrated simply because it was fresh at the time for the Resident Evil Franchise but in reality it's a clunky arcade feeling not very good 3rd person shooter with an annoying child, so keep that in mind. That said, when it does come to this instalment you get a game that borrows alot from number 4 but, possibly due to development woes, ends up feeling more like 4 different game ideas attempting to act in one cohesive manner but missing the mark, in some areas by a lot. It's not scary in any way shape or form, still lacks any real decent puzzles and the enemies although looking good are actually somewhat 'easy'.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Another part of everyone's favorite franchise, which is simultaneously trying to preserve the traditions of the Series, and gradually abandon them. _childDocuments_.review: Awesome game - a worthy follow up to RE7. It has everything that I loved about the past few games in the series: slow burning survival horror, great tension and atmosphere, resource management, interesting enemies and boss fights, interesting story, and the Duke is the coolest merchant ever. I'm also absolutely floored by the graphics and the world-building, exploring Castle Dimitrescu was a right treat, especially in COVID times when I've only seen the inside of my own home for months.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down the worst Resident Evil game in history. Everything is lackluster to say the least. Either that or blatant copy\paste from other games\franchises. Level design is uninventive, boring and dull. The factory is only one decently designed location. Enemies are a joke, as well as bosses - they pose no threat at all, you never ever lack resources. Dying is almost impossible with absolutely broken block mechanic and the amount of bullets and healing items thrown at you. As a result there is no tension, no "survival" and no horror to be had with the exception of two decent jump scares. Controls are highly unresponsive and directly designed to induce rage into player in a futile attempt to add suspense by handicapping playable character. Dukes shop mechanic with weapon upgrades is copy\pasted directly from RE4 and is completely unnecessary, only adding another level of chores to be done to increase lacking playtime. 8-9 hours of playtime with first "blind" playthrough is a joke for 60$ game, not to mention RE game. And the game is so boring that it has no replay value whatsoever, due to the lack of interest in completing all achievements, let alone forcing yourself to play on higher difficulty. The story is a mess, it is outright stupidest thing i have ever seen, to be honest. Not to mention the complete lack of said story right up to last hour of gameplay when every ounce of lore is suddenly shoved right down the players throat. This coupled with wonky animations all throughout the game will probably induce gag reflex into many players instead of being a product to have fun with.Avoid this game at all costs. At least do yourself a favor and wait till solid discounts. This game is a joke and an insult not only to RE fans but also to the gaming community as a whole. This "game" had no chance to be anything worthy of a mention if it wasn't for the current situation with quarantine and such, with barely any new games to play with. This is a total and blatant cashgrab from untalented developer, knowing full well that this situation we are in makes any trash product sellable to the wide audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Story-wise, the game would make a lot more sense if the 5% that poorly attempts to handwave how this is part of the RE universe didn't exist at all.  "I don't have time to explain" Chris keeps saying, and he's right... he never does.  I've noted a number of things that Ethan will not do on his quest to save his daughter, but an average 12 year old would have no problem doing when sneaking out of the house.-Move a half dozen small items blocking a path-Clear 2-3 inches of snow blocking a gate-Jimmy open a wooden drawer-Kick open a rotting wooden door-Pull up the bucket from a well by pulling on the rope-Climb over objects as low as two feet fall or over gates with multiple handholds (and no barbed wire) as low as eight feet tall-Attempt to swim to safety after falling into water instead of flailing around in place waiting to dieI know 'obstacles' like these were part of the series from the beginning, but it's not the 1990s anymore.  Capcom needs to create roadblocks that make logical sense rather than insult the player.Other random things that bugged me-Ethan has a flashlight that he pulls out on his own when it's completely dark, but you can't use manually even when it is 90% dark... thanks a lot Ethan!-Some doors/gates are locked with no key, and you can't unlock them from either side, so they only serve to annoy you when going between areas you've been to before-Your map shows the locations of chickens, wells, typewriters, locked doors and treasure chests, but not which roads are blocked by debris-In the intro Ethan makes a reference to going through military training, but I guess he wasn't paying any attention, since he doesn't have any new moves from RE7... maybe that's where they taught him how to stick keys, giant crystals and crafting items into his hyperspace pocket (you can't do it with meat or lockpicks though)
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Very good Resident Evil game. One of the bests to date. I think this is due to the overwhelming influence and inspiration from RE4, which I believe to be the best game in the main series titles. This is a very close second. It combines a lot of what I love from 4 into this game. There are a few story inconsistencies in the game I believe, and like historical inaccuracies, but I am no historian so I won't pretend to be. Otherwise, I have no qualms about this game, it's a great game if you're not a super nit picky person, and just enjoy story, setting, and gameplay like I do. Definitely worth your money buying and playing it brand new. I will have to buy this game for my PS4 to play on as well! :)Edit: Also I REALLY loved the art concepts when you finish the game. Shows a lot of early development ideas for both RE7 & RE8. There's a lot of concepts they decided not to use for RE7 which I believe would have made 7 a whole lot better, but that's just my opinion :)

Here are a few notable ones I noticed:1. For a game that is clearly very focused on FPS action, the FOV is way too narrow. I completed the game on Village of Shadows difficulty and found myself getting frustrated over enemies that you SHOULD be able to notice. I understand that the developers did this intentionally to simulate a more claustrophobic experience, but there are times where this FOV is just a hinderance. I would suggest perhaps having moments in the game (House Beneviento especially) where the FOV tightens.2. The game feels too easy. So far, I have completed it on Casual, Standard, and Village of Shadows (I probably won't do it on hardcore since I have the achievement for it already). With the unlimited ammo bonus content, Village of Shadows difficulty becomes somewhat of a joke. With the exception of a few moments of course (The initial lycan attack and Mother Miranda, which tbh, was more of me not recognizing her attack patterns. It probably would have been easier.) I would definitely recommend either the hardcore or Village of Shadows difficulty nonetheless if you want a truly tense experience. 3. If Ethan Winters were a spice, he would be flour. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I played in a while. For those who like suspenseful thrillers, this is a must.Story wise, it's fantastic - it keeps you on your toes, and you want to go on just to understand the bigger picture that's slowly unfolding. The main big enemies are wonderfully done, each one of them has character - and you have a good feeling of achievement when you finally finish them off.Graphically and sound, it's amazing! From the very beginning I had many questions to what is happening. The game very beautifully sets the tone and the formed questions after the introduction make you run forward for answers.We don’t have straight answers until the very end, and only before the last fight game gives us all answers and admirably connect this part with the whole RE saga.RE Village doesn’t give all answers in cutscenes, in turn, more answers are given in notes. This is done in the spirit of the old parts, where there were no beautiful cutscenes, and all the answers had to be given in the form of notes scattered throughout the game.When I was playing the first time - I really was scared almost all the game. This game doesn’t have many screamers, in turn it casts a mood of constant anxiety. During the passage, my mood changed very quickly from panic and apathy to peace and tranquility in the save rooms. So all gaming experience may be explained as emotional rollercoaster.The game is based on Village  And it was the most scary part of the game.The last location is  and it is the only location during which I was tired from the game. When I played this game second time, only  was stopping me from playing.DLC Shadow of Rose is made perfectly in all canons of DLSs. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed RE8.  Some may not as a follow up to RE7 which was at least for the first half more of a return to horror than action whereas RE8 is a mix of different RE mechanics and gameplay.  I'm at ~49 hours as of writing this, have beat the game 5 times and have 100% the achievements which is the first game I've done this for in a while.  For me, the gameplay loop was great, the characters were fun and it's just a joy to play. Story: Direct follow up to RE7, you could read a summary on this if you wanted to but I suggest playing it.  Guy is trying to save his daughter, Chris Redfield may or may not be bad (if you play RE, you know the answer to this).  Capcom in traditional Capcom fashion has seemed to forget some elements from RE7 they found they no longer needed and shoe horned some other elements into this entry.Gameplay: Think RE4.  Game is broken into 4 main parts but as you move through the world, side areas open up, extra bosses spawn and the design of the world is solid.  Just FYI though: once you finish one of the main dungeon areas, it is done, no returning.  The village acts as a hub and opens up after each section.  The main areas also play differently with the 2nd area being really creepy for me on the first play through.  System: 9700k stock, 3080 stock, used gsync.  Used kb/m.Audio: Standard, some voice acting is silly, some is fine.Video: Lot of options, but my system ran hot playing this with settings pretty high.  I can recall ~2 areas where I would get slow down but they were just rooms that had a lot happen all at once.Game: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I am quite enamored with this game. I had enjoyed RE:7 a bit, save for a few gameplay hitches. I'm not going to lie - it took me a second to break out of my usual "KILL EVERYTHING!" mindset to embody the more survivalist style the game wants you to take. The scripted events could be frustrating. But you know what? I'm not mad. I thought the graphics were going to be a lot more rendered but the game is, by no means, ugly. It is vivid, and has a lot of detail and intricate architecture, artwork and symbolism I appreciate.Is it the scariest game of the genre? Well, no. But I was having so much fun playing it, being spooked became secondary. The ambiance could be a little bit better at times, but Village makes up for it in many different ways. This was well worth the purchase to me, the story is engrossing and the characters and villains interesting.This is a game I will definitely be playing again after my first run!

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 8 is a more action-oriented game after its direct predecessor firmly returned the series back to its survival horror roots, but fortunately it doesn't overindulge in action schlock: this is still a very spooky, very tense Resident Evil that maintains an excellent balance between frantic combat encounters and quieter moments of exploration, set in often visually stunning environments that are excellently designed and featuring some of the best and most charismatic antagonists I have seen in any media in a while. Absolutely recommended!It's also worth mentioning that the Winters' Expansion DLC not only adds a few hours of fantastic story content and enhances the Mercenaries mode with extra characters and maps, it also allows you to play the main campaign in third-person perspective instead of the default first-person; a welcome option that should make an already highly replayable game have even better replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil Village

_childDocuments_.review: Even if Village doesn't deliver on the amount of terror of it's predecessor, it most certainly is another triumph in Capcom's revamped horror series.  With an incredible new story to dive into, and a variety of ways to play that highlight all the best moments of series roots, I can't recommend this title enough.  It was an absolute blast from start to finish, and now I have to impatiently wait for the next installment.  Gorgeous graphics and scenery, a remarkable soundtrack, and gameplay that constantly felt fresh, Resident Evil Village is must play for all!

_childDocuments_.review: Bonkers resident evil goodness. The game tries out some new things for the series - the Beneviento section especially and brings in a variety of classic horror monsters to go with the beautiful Hammer horror-y setting. _childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, it's a 7.5/10 for me. Finished my first playthrough in 9 hours and 52 minutes on standard difficulty with thorough exploration.The story is nice, some unexpected plot twists right at the end, but the whole connection with the older RE games seems kinda forced, and it feels like the devs didn't really mean for the plot to be a part of the overarching story.This game starts to peak at castle Demitrescu and reaches its best in Beneviento's mansion, which was the best and most memorable and horrifying part of the game, then it devolved into an actiony mush of loud noices and explosions.The villians barely has any screen time and are not as prominent or memorable as the Baker family (It seems that the devs concentrated so much on Lady D, that they forgot about the others).Personally, I enjoyed RE7 more, and it felt like a RE game despite all the changes. This one just feels like a fairy tale, and the only thing reminding you of the fact that this is a RE game is Chris popping up from time to time.I feel like this game needs some story DLC that focuses on the villains, and more set pieces similar to Beneviento's mansion.

_childDocuments_.review: To say I was absolutely blown away by Resident Evil Village would be a massive understatement. RE Village was an experience, simply unforgettable and an absolute joy to play from start to finish. I think it's a very nice change from RE 7 Biohazard which felt very terrifying for the sake of being terrifying. It wasn't bad by any means but didn't feel entirely like Resident Evil, Village does a complete 180 and takes your favorite parts of RE 7 Biohazard and RE 4 to create what is easily the best horror game of 2021. If you are a fan of Resident Evil, this is an absolute must play and I have zero doubts saying that. I was fascinated with every facet of this experience and would gladly play it again as it has an unbelievable amount of replayability with the Extra Content shop which includes countless options for special weapons, weapons with infinite ammo, and so much more. The future of this franchise is bright and I will not be missing out on a single installment to come after playing RE Village which I would easily consider, a masterpiece. I hope you have as much fun as I did. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start with the conclusion: This game is not bad. It's fun to play, the story is interesting, the level design is good, and I enjoyed most of what I've experienced so far. However, Steam doesn't have a "meh" or a "yes, BUT" option, so if it's a choice between "yes" or "no", I'm going to go with "no" because it commits the fatal sin of a horror game: Not being scary.The game looks good, and has decent level design...unfortunately, from what I've seen so far of it (I've just completed the Castle segment, so it's possible later areas are far scarier, but first impressions count for a lot), it might also be the single least scary game in the franchise. Yes, less scary than 5 and 6. (EDIT: I've now beaten the entire game. Wasn't scary at any point.)After how delightfully freaky Resident Evil 7 was, and how well RE2Make and RE3Make managed to still capture the frightening atmosphere, Village is a huge disappointment. It feels like they're returning to the ill-advised "let's just be a generic shooter" Chris levels from Resident Evil 6 (though of course it's not as bad as 6). Honestly, the game reminds me of Resident Evil 6 a lot, and that's...not something you ever want to be reminded of.Considering the devs have actually said that they intended for it to be less scary than 7, all I can really say there is...well done missing the entire point of a horror franchise? The enemies don't even look that disturbing compared to...basically any other enemy in the series. Morpheus Duvall was scarier. The game so far feels like it has only one single trick for being "scary", and that trick is "do something terrible to Ethan's hands." Which...after the second time Ethan gets impaled through the hand, it's just silly. Ethan somehow has the durability of Superman in terms of the torture he goes through with little more than a grunt of annoyance.  By the time his hand gets sliced off, I actually cracked up laughing at how stupid this apparent running gag (running scare?) was. *And then the hand was added to the players inventory*.Other complaints:-No FOV slider. If the FOV is too low, it can cause nausea and motion sickness in a lot of people. This is well known, why do they still insist on a single fixed FoV regardless of things like "monitor size" and "player preference".-Can't unequip weapon charms. You can disable them entirely (but you have to quit back to the main menu first), but you can't just...unequip them. I have no idea why they would do this other than the feature being rushed.-Massive lag when fighting the daughters in the Castle. I assume this is due to the flies, hopefully that can be optimized in the future.-Ray tracing has a severe memory leak that cripples performance regardless of hardware.-Denuvo. Come on, please, find a different DRM. This thing kills performance and doesn't help fight piracy by any noticable metric.

_childDocuments_.review: This review does contain very minor spoilers.I will admit that this one surprised me, I rather enjoyed. The setting and mood was amazing (although, I enjoyed the more focused and singular locale of Resident Evil 7). I was surprised that the game took place in more than just the castle and it's titular Village prelude, but rather the village as a whole (the castles surrounding houses, a "factory," a home on the outskirts of town, etc)As a side note, I was expecting Lady Dimitrescu to be the main villain of the game, considering all the hype she had gotten as well as the focus on her daughters, and virtually no mention of the games REAL villain despite their appearance pretty early on in the game. I was pretty surprised that Lady Dimistrescu was simply just a side character.The gameplay of RE7 was carried over to this one, so if you played that one you know what you're getting into here. It's still Resident Evil, but in the first person. There's plenty of slow paced exploration, inventory management, moody & creepy atmospheres, and a few action sequences. I'll admit that I enjoyed the creepiness of RE7 a little more, but I loved many of the set pieces of this game (the castle is definitely the highlight of the game).The story is definitely the weakest part of this game, and I feel that it comes to the questionable actions and occurrences of the main character, Ethan Winters. To give an early game example, Ethan gets his right hand cut off, and a little while later he simply just "sticks it back on" and keeps on fighting. I know that there's an explanation for it, but it ends up feeling thin and insinuated (and that same argument can be applied to RE7 as well, as the same thing happens to Ethans left hand. Honestly, I think Ethan is the only character I have ever played as who got both his hands cut off and was still able to fire a gun with a fully functional hand).If you go in to enjoy it for it's awesome set pieces and atmosphere, ignoring some of the dumb things and weird story beats, I think this one is worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil has finally made its way into eastern lands of Europe, more specifically one unnamed village in Transylvanian Mountains of Romania. You're left off with Ethan from the previous installment now settled with Mia in his relatively modest home somewhere classified location, taking care of their very so normal baby girl. All of the enthusiasm you're experiencing in the beginning will slowly dissipate as you're thrown at the heart of swarm, unknown beasts and monsters alike roaming your surroundings like rats amidst harvest. The dreadful, sinister and abandoned looking village will entice your gaze on every single yard corner, remnants of bodies from farm animals and wasted grains paint slowly and intensively the vicious encounters you'll partake. The visual fidelity through protagonist's eyes is an experience to behold, life-like artwork and animations worthy of unique appraisal. You're provided with a powerful arsenal to choose from which allows you to annihilate every single grotesque creature paving the path to your precious daughter. Raw true survival horror experience occurs and indulges my expectations, I can attest it stands firm from previous titles in the series. There are several areas to explore each with its own theme and ridiculous but thrilling traps that will coax flight or fight responses, leaving oneself more often than not forced to improvise and adapt to each situation. The whole system of first person shooter is vastly improved from Ethan's previous adventure as mentioned earlier with lots more weapons to behead ghouls, everything feels more responsive especially when you're blocking enormous werewolf claws with your bare hands; obviously enhanced by the fact you're superhuman with fast regenerative abilities fully recovering your endurance after every encounter. OST & sound design as always is at the peak creating and augmenting the already intensified terror you're forced to withstand. The major character actors being into their roles one hundred percent strengthens the attachments and bonds you'll feel towards their personas, there's a tragedy lying in wait getting you to only empathize through their harrowing stories. Location & characters lore is well written to emulate further involvement, boosting the immersion as if you're there yourself strolling with your own feet and smelling the cold appalling environment. A worthy journey with authentic design of local tradition and culture (approved by a romanian native™) there's lots of fun things to explore, decently difficult puzzles and high variety of monsters to go decimate in most gory manners.- graphics & artwork - fluid first person combat mechanics- good replay value & mercenary mode- OST & sound design- voice actors fitting their roles perfectly- attention to detail when it comes to romanian culture- vos difficulty poorly designed- pointless character deaths as per your typical RE experience

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, let’s not waste any time or try to kid ourselves. Resident Evil Village is a masterpiece. There, I’ve said it. It’s out in the open now. In the wake of so many AAA titles being released in a half-baked or broken state, it is the very epitome of a relief to see a game with this much hype released not only working, but excelling at nearly everything.The story picks up several years after the events of RE7. If, like me, players had not experienced RE7, there is a recap available that broadly goes over the events to bring the player up to speed. It’s enough to let one know what happened without spoiling the experience. Players are then treated to a Tim Burton-esque sequence before revealing it was a bedtime story for new parents Ethan and Mia Winters. Following what seems like a pattern of trilogies in the RE series, Ethan stars as the protagonist in his second outing. Events quickly turn things sideways and he’s set upon a quest to track down his missing daughter, Rose. The search leads him to a small European village, hearkening back to Leon’s trip in RE4. Along the way, Ethan is subjected to a litany of monsters, creatures, and larger-than-life characters. In fact, aside from the stunning views Village consistently delivers, it are these characters that I found most enthralling.It’s not just the Lords and Ladies governing the town that are so engrossing. Mysterious characters like The Duke and even the villagers Ethan encounters are so completely fleshed out. Motivations are as unique as the mannerisms and models. There is a level of detail in every aspect that only helps to decorate this decadent experience. Everyone has a story to be told if the player digs enough.But, Village follows the traditional Resident Evil format. Players are introduced to a starting area that was shown primarily in promotional materials. From there, the shock and horror subside a bit before revealing secret labs and conspiracies. It’s formulaic, to be sure, but it’s a formula I love all the same. The primary reason for this is the execution in each of the areas players visit. Each has a distinct theme and story-telling method. From the Dracula-inspired halls of Castle Dimitrescu to the Silent Hill levels of creepiness in House Beneviento, each area and mini-story is nearly a masterpiece in its own right.The story moves along at a good pace without any noticeable slogs or portions that felt tired. Even after three play-throughs I found myself still exploring every nook and cranny, hoping to learn more. Much like any RE title, there is an abundance of notes to be found that flesh out the events of the world. Towards the end, certain pieces are set up for a third entry in the Ethan Winters trilogy. Not a cliffhanger, but more an aftertaste that left me hungry for more.Village was my first foray into FPS Resident Evil. I skipped out on RE7 as the demo was far too scary and I wasn’t sold on hillbilly horror in a series primarily about zombies and biological monsters. After playing through Village, I realize how wrong I was. It was shocking how well the game lends itself to first-person as well as it did third-person. While I don’t necessarily see a benefit to either perspective, the take-away I had was that neither was a detriment. The only odd thing (that I quickly got used to) was that despite being a FPS, Village doesn’t utilize the iron sights when aiming. Rather, it opts for an arcade-like crosshair system that can be zoomed in. Otherwise, the game handled extremely well with controller.The inventory system and crafting are nearly identical to RE4, so it was quite intuitive to navigate around and manage my stuff. One fantastic addition was the “bounty” system offered by The Duke. By tracking down and hunting certain animals, The Duke is able to whip up dishes that offer permanent stat bonuses to Ethan. It gave the back-half of the game a little extra life as I tracked down chickens and fish for my next feast.Combat is fast, fluid, and frantic. From the first attack by “werewolves” on the village to the mutant soldiers found later on, each encounter is tense and terrifying. Ethan has a bevy of weapons at his disposal and he’ll need them to overcome the horrors he’s faced with. The bulk of the enemies are melee-focused with only a handful having ranged potential. That being said, most of the fights then rely on them having superior numbers that must be whittled down and engaged strategically in order to survive.My first play-through was on the easiest difficulty as I wanted to experience the story and not worry about my skills failing me in a critical spot. From there, I took advantage of the unlock system and equipped infinite ammo for the starting shotgun. On my second play-through, I bumped the difficulty to normal and quickly found it was going to be a walk in the park. When play-through three occurred on hard mode with my infinite ammo magnum, the game was laughably easy. All of that tension and strategy I had mentioned earlier had completely gone out the window. So, subsequent play-throughs will lose the terror, but present a different form of fun as players become the monster beset upon this remote village.Along those same lines is the Mercenary mode. Rather than be subjected to the horror of monsters, players must fight against another kind of evil: a time rush. Racing against the clock and trying to rack up kills, perks, and points as fast and efficiently as possible is the key to this mode. Players are scored at the end of each run. Doing well will unlock bonuses for use in the main game.I mentioned Village’s beauty earlier and it cannot be overstated how gorgeous the game actually is. Pictures fail to do it justice. The amount of detail each character, environment, and weapon receives is unreal. Capcom’s proprietary RE Engine is on full display here and it truly shines. I am consistently astounded at the level of quality and fidelity Capcom is able to put into a game without performance suffering. Perhaps knowing that players would be so enchanted with the world they had created, Capcom did add a photo mode to the game. There are a number of options available, however, the end result is always tragically marred by Capcom copyright info boldly displayed at the bottom of said photo. I’ve not found a way around this and it is a shame. This single inclusion made the entire option pointless.That being said, despite taking place in a relatively small village and the surrounding area, the number of environments available was surprising. From the run-down village to dank dungeons to industrial labyrinths, it’s all a visual feast.Your eyeballs aren’t the only ones in for a treat. Ears get a special experience as well. Gunshots crack and monsters roar and howl. The surround sound options bring the horror to another level. All manner of nastiness bumps and creaks and shrieks in the dark before bloodied talons and fangs leap forth. Voice-acting is sublime with a masterful performance from each member of the cast. The accompanying soundtrack is a horror masterpiece, falling just short of the majesty that was the Bloodborne soundtrack.By now it’s no secret the love I harbor for Village. It is a perfect balance of action, adventure, horror, and grand ambiance. Seven months into the year and it is an incredibly strong contender for my game of the year. I can’t recommend it enough to anyone remotely a fan of the genres it occupies. It only helps that the game does well enough to loop in the larger world without making new players feel lost. Again, it’s a taste that will leave you hungry for more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where Steam's thumbs up/down system is woefully inadequate. It took me quite a bit to decide if I should put one or the other and ultimately decided that thumbs down is too negative for what this game offers. Yeah I would recommend this game but I have my reservations regarding it.Due to long history of this franchise and the review's word limit, it makes it difficult to put down everything I found problematic or lacking, but in essence it is lack of consistency in the design when compared to previous entries. For those coming into this series at this point, I would actually recommend watching videos and if it suits your fancy chances are you will enjoy it. The game doesn't really lie or try to overshadow its faults. It's more because I'm picky and because I expected more from people who made so many games that outshine this one in the franchise.The series in general has two major design directions (ok not counting offshoots like Survivor and such). It either follows the atmosphere/tension/puzzle/item management of games like 1-3, or it follows a more linear combat saturated approach such as 4. Games like 5 and 6 for example follow 4 but fail to capture the reasons it was well made. While something like RE2 remake captures the essence what made the original games so good but in a more up to date experience. This game simply can't make up its mind which it wants to be. It is broken into multiple sections that can be complete different ends of the spectrum. One second you might be mowing down  a horde, another you won't have a weapon and you will be running away playing hide and seek under the bed.The linearity of the level design is in a bit like RE4. Puzzles are simplified, you find a solution for each pretty close to where it is. There is little backtracking or thinking to actually progress, all backtracking is optional for resources. This isn't navigating RPD where you find different bits and bobs that open up things in different ends of the place and you have to figure out how to navigate it to conserve resources (or time). This is fine, as I said RE4 did it much like this, but this game doesn't have NEARLY as much combat as RE4 did. It has good bits in some sections, but again, that whole pacing issue just makes it a disjointed experience.Some sections are just downright bad or gimmicky. One of the opening segments is to survive endless amount of enemies for a period of time. This ends up far more frustrating because the game did not set a good precedent what to expect out of resources. RE4 did something similar but this felt like a really bad copy paste of it where the missed the point. Kind of like the copying someone's homework and not really reading if the questions matched the answers. Top down is the same, execution, not so much. I can't really go into some other segments without spoiling, but the difference in design for them is too stark. I am not quite sure what I'm playing in the moment. Am I playing an action game, am I playing an atmosphere horror game, or am I playing a resource management survival game. It's neither of them.  It doesn't always work.(I do have to point out that FoV is awful. I understand why, but it doesn't work when you start to lean on combat). You can mod this though.What does work is adoption of the upgrade system. Even if it isn't as good as RE4 (no exclusive upgrades, and guns are more tiered than sidegrades). It makes combat and replayibility good. To me that sort of thing is fun. Running around in RE4 with the handcannon blowing everything away. Same thing here. In general combat is pretty good but I'm still unsure why they made only Lycans have their heads explode on final headshots. Why not other enemies too. _childDocuments_.review: THE MOMMY MILKERS STRIKE BACKThe Resident Evil franchise has experimented with many aesthetics and styles of horror, all being based in the realm of cinematic presentation. RE 7 really tried something new with a focus on visceral horror akin to Tobe Hooper’s Texas Chain Saw Massacre. So, it was fitting for the franchise to return to more gothic, fantastical horror, but keeping in the established canon of the Ethan Winters storyline. However, does it improve upon its predecessor?.. Ehhhhhhhhh not really.Resident Evil: Village is an incredible game  with great aesthetic and familiar gameplay. Adopting a more gothic design akin to Stoker’s Dracula meets Dario Argento, the updated location of a castle and village grounds is expansive and expertly designed. It is gorgeous to look at too! The only problem I have with it is that the map feels too big for the atmosphere to be effectively scary. The brilliance of Biohazard’s map(s) was that the farm and ship felt uncomfortably intimate. The scares were more invasive instead of grandiose, but that’s probably due to the different styles of horror. However, there are moments in Hammer’s Dracula or other cult horrors like Suspiria that are far scarier than the jumpscare-y blandness of Village. Also, the horror is lessened by the reduced difficulty of standard, which felt more like easy than anything else. Despite it taking me longer to complete this one than 7, everything felt rushed and quick. The design is brilliant though. The creatively found in the characters is truly inspired with extreme levels of detail and nuanced voice performances. Even the mommy milker vampire lady  is a fully-realized minor antagonist with depth. The rest of the intrigue is kind of a let-down, but it’s a decent bookend to the the plot established in Biohazard, making a good two-parter for the franchise. Come for the milkies. Stay for the mixed bag.
