_childDocuments_.review: It was honestly hard to give this a thumbs up, even tho i really liked the game. It's beautiful, moving game with wonderful mechanics. This game is almost perfect but it has a major flaw holding it back. The art style, animations, maps and everything are incredibly beautiful. Flying around the giant trees with my cool bug mech is truly awe inspiring, It could only be improved by the ability to move my camera.The story tho short, is emotionally packed in a very natural way that's hard to explain.It's a memorable and unique gaming experience filled with charm.Unfortunately it has a big issue.and that's how janky and chaotic the combat feels. whenever anything hits you, you fly off stage super fast and are forced into a fall animation that badly hurts you and then teleports you back on the stage in a spot thats sometimes not even close to where you were. It feels so unnatural and frustrating. I can't tell you how many times i was flung off the stage and could have easily glided back on with my GLIDING robot, but was violently forced into a fall animation that teleports me back on the stage, just for me to immediately get flung again and rinse and repeat, sometimes 3 or 4 times in a row in chaotic battles. It's so mentally exhausting, in an otherwise serene and relaxing game. I honestly almost quit playing just because of this.But i still enjoyed the game in the end and cried for the ending so whatever. It's all about the journey right?!
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good. But be warned.The story is very simple.Controls are confusing later in game, so many tricks to pull off.And yes please, play with controller!:)What this game excels in is art and uniqueness. Maybe it's not well suited for very long plays, but played here and there, in bits and pieces, it's lovely.Yeah I guess playing it for hours ruins it, I did the same mistake. Maybe worth mentioning that I've picked this up after a month since I dropped it, and I checked the controls by looking at the mech workbench, relearning the controls was easier than expected.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: PROS: Neat little game. Amazing art and animation. Sucha beautiful little world to explore. Was so cool to upgrade your ship and modify it and see the difference. Fun combat even though it can get a bit frustrating at times. CONS: There were a few major bugs in the game but they did not ruin the whole experience. Also some resource grinding is in the game and backtracking in the game can be a bit annoying because there is no real time map.Overall good 7/10. Art and animation really carries the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: , what a strange setting this is.You are a girl who lives in this world of humongous plants and bugs, who, with the help of her own custom built mech, scours the land for resources to upgrade and improve her rig, in search of something she’s lost.Tranquil music and an interesting paint-like aesthetic is what closes the deal on  this beautiful art piece.However, while the exploration is functional and many times feels good to just glide and climb this intricate natural labyrinth, the combat hits quite a big rock:You cannot “kill” the insectoid enemies this title throws at the character’s mech, you can only push them off the edge of the platform you are currently standing on.“That’s fine” you might say, but on top of that you cannot push them until they are weak enough, and you have only one way to weaken them, awkwardly floating above them while dropping bombs with an extremely small explosion radius, these bombs cannot be aimed so arm yourself with a great deal of patience since many enemies will require multiple hits.And then again to make matters worse, the swarm of enemies that hit you send you flying across the screen, nullifying your progress you made against some of the other ones.And to close the deal on this incredibly clunky combat system is that many enemies are faster than you and your only way to push them off a ledge is by charging up incredibly slowly an air gust that will get interrupted from the smallest thing.This wouldn’t be as insulting if the dame didn’t lock you into mandatory combat at random points in the game.Still recommending this, but be very wary, if you want this because you saw a cool mech in the trailer, I’m afraid to shatter your hopes like this, watch something before you buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of a missed opportunity.This is a really weird juxtaposition of really great and absolutely terrible design.The world, bugs, rigs and players are all beautifully designed... and the story does nothing with any of them. The story is SO incredibly bad - the characters are underdeveloped, motivations are all over the shop, character 'arcs' are jarring - but most insulting is how little the story links to the beautifully designed world. I'm pretty sure you could run the exact same story with almost no changes to the dialogue, in literally any other setting almost seemlessly.How did they come up with such a great visual design, yet have a story that basically ignores the world altogether and does effectively zero lore or history? Combat has some really interesting ideas and great mechanics in it... but then swarms you with enemies, making any sort of strategy either useless or tedious. It gives you a tool kit and then punishes you for trying to use it.I very rarely write reviews, but after the unbelievably clumsy and hamfisted 'twist/betrayal' in the story, I felt that simply stopping and uninstalling was insufficient and needed to say something more.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Creature in the Well, but this game just didn't grab me like that one. This is one of those games that at first I found frustrating and annoying, but as time progressed, I began to enjoy it more. It never becomes great, but it's very okay. In the beginning, I found myself quite frustrated trying to skip enemies and farm resources, as if you don't, they get consumed by the bugs. And since there are so many different types of enemies to manage who are attacking you, this felt like a chore. As the game progresses, you get some tricks to make this easier, but I felt it rather annoying to have to rush in to deal with saving resources, when the focus could have been on the combat. Despite that annoyance, there are plenty of resources available and farming to get what you need is easy, though you usually have everything.The story of the game is minimal and sort of interesting. New upgrades are triggered by using your rig's abilities or killing enemies. When upgrades are identified, Annika will reminisce about her father or technically discuss the upgrade, which I thought was a nice touch. My favorite part of the game was getting the upgrades and then upgrading the rig. It felt very satisfying.The game has a very unique art style, but I didn't find it appealing for whatever reason. The character models are okay, nothing special. Sound effects are average, but the music is oddly good, not quite ambient but sort of.I played the main story of this game in about eight hours. There is some arena style combat available after beating the game, but I did not have any interest in this. I would imagine this would extend the life of the game a bit, but not as much as necessary to make the asking price worth it. It's not the greatest game, so if you have limited time and resources, I'd pass it over. But if it's on sale and you are looking for a unique experience, give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: Breathtakingly beautiful and charming. I'm not far into it yet so I can't properly judge the game as a whole but so far it's captured me like nobody's business, and there are no obvious missteps in game design or presentation.Late(?) game update: still all of those things, but the sound design is... it's weird. What's there is good! It clicks well and feels good! But there's *not enough of it*. Not enough ambiance and no voice acting. You end up with prolonged periods of near-silence. Not the good kind but the "is this bugged out?" kind. I'd ding the game a star if there were star ratings involved. As it is, it's still a recommend, but a wistful one, a "this could have been even better" one.Final update: well, it took me 7 hours to beat, and I skipped some of the grinding with ye olde cheat engine. I never found the other parts for the rig (there's a guide on the forum, looks like they're all findables, and all materially the same - you're not going to make something that behaves differently). So it's more limited than implied by the interface. But it was still a good run, and the price is appropriate for the scope.I'm prone to complaining about things so don't let my salty dissuade you from trying it! It's gorgeous and it's a presentation you haven't seen before. I hope they make a hojillion monetary units and go on to make Stonefly 2: Mercenaries.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem; the soundtrack is incredible, and gathering resources while avoiding/pushing bugs off leaves is both peaceful and enjoyable, as is customising your rig (while not entirely customizable some pieces can be changed). It may not be worth it at full price, but it is worth it if you can get a discount on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: Goregous game, love the idea of Mechs and Bugs, the world is lovely, the characters great! There is so much to love here and the price is very reasonable for the size. That said it can be a bit rough around the edges here or there. Lacks polish and some extra testing as it isn't uncommon to run into a bug here or there or search for how to progress because something hadn't been explained too well. _childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: A heartwarming coming of age story set in a fantastical world reminiscent of the Microcosmos film. The cast of characters are memorable and interesting. Sound, music and art design are great at making the world feel alive.Lots of customization options for the bug mech and plenty of upgrades to work towards. Abilities can be a little overwhelming however only a few are necessary to complete the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: I very addictive game. At least, for a gamer such as me. While the controls and the snail-like pace at which your mech moves when not in the air did take quite a while for me to get comfortable with, I'm really enjoying myself and having a lot of fun.The art style and music compliment each other extremely well. Though I'm sure for others it will be insanely repetitive, it's right up my alley.Perhaps my one major problem with the game so far is that there's no player-controlled map. Although you're given guide lights during missions that you can activate by pressing the down button on the D-pad, when roaming freely, you're on your own. I've been thoroughly lost for going on a hour now.What kind of exploration game doesn't give players a map they can bring up at will?My frustration with the lack of player-controlled map notwithstanding, this game is one I definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: Stonefly is a relatively chill, exploration game. You are either a very tiny person or on a planet with very big trees and bugs, either way, you pilot and upgrade a bug mech. It's cute and pretty nonviolent with still some fun action. You don't kill bugs, you just blow them out of the arena. The controls are a little clunky but once you get used to them, they are fine. There is no camera control which can lead to some scenarios with unfortunate blindspots. Overall recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: Charming game so far, nice unique visuals and chilled soundtrack. The story seems decent, with fun characters. So far the main thing which has stood out is the combat and movement, in a good way. It takes a little to get used to certain combos of controls. Im using a keyboard+mouse, but I understand the game has full controller support so perhaps that's easier for some. Generally its very smooth to control and intuitive. There's upgrades that can be unlocked for certain resources you acquire, and as there seem to be a few different mechs I imagine there is some decent replayability here. I'm not sure how big this game is, but for the price another few hours of this would definitely make it worth that. As I've only scratched the surface ill resist this review when I've finished, but if this looks like your thing it probably is worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Stonefly

_childDocuments_.review: Harness the wind and soar through the wilderness of Stonefly, a chill and tranquil action-adventure game about self-discovery, legacy, and belonging. Glide your mech strategically among beautiful flora and dangerous fauna, confronting hungry bugs, adventures, and memorable characters.

name: Tainted Grail: Conquest
detailed_description: MORE FROM AWAKEN REALMS MORE FROM TAINTED GRAIL JOIN OUR DISCORD & MAILING LIST TOP BUNDLE Set foot onto a world full of darkness and treachery, where danger lurks around every corner after King Arthur's demise. Roam the island of Avalon, battle your way through numerous enemies and live a story out of twisted Arthurian legends, unlike any other. This bundle contains two games from the Tainted Grail franchise, which first took the world by storm as a board game. Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon (early access) and Tainted Grail: Conquest. Both let you immerse yourself into the dark island of Avalon's setting in different ways and both guarantee a journey you won't soon forget. This bundle includes: Tainted Grail: The Fall of AvalonStep into a dark reimagination of Arthurian legends in this first person, open world RPG. Explore a world stuck in everlasting autumn, witness falling legends and make meaningful choices woven into a complex, branching storyline. Tainted Grail: Conquest A unique, infinitely replayable, story-driven hybrid between a deck-building Roguelike and an RPG game. Explore the ever-changing maps, fight with deadly enemies, and learn what happened to the cursed island of Avalon. About the Game

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I know, I played 60+ hours on this game and I still review it badly. That's weird, but let me explain.The pro :- Graphically, this game is great- Musically, I love the atmosphere- The lore of this world feels rich. I want to live great stories within it- A lot of class options (which is great, 9 classes if I remember)But (The Negatives) :- Given a class, I don't seem to have multiple ways of equal power for playing it. And therefore, when I level up, I don't feel like really having a choice. I just take the best option at my disposal- A roguelite is about unlocking new options for your next run. You need to feel more powerful or eager to try that new thing you got... Here, I unlock new cards that don't feel like giving me a new way of playing and therefore don't renew my gaming experience- When You wander in this world, it feels empty (would love a bit of decoration, broken items... some life in the Wyrd to justify lighting a candle)Conclusion:So That's why I don't recommend it. The world and the idea are great and I want to love it, but all I feel is a bit of deception and a waste of time I could have spent on a more engaging/thrilling game

_childDocuments_.review: A fun if dark story told through a casual rogue-like card battler.  This genre is becoming more common and this game does well with it. Tainted Grail has varied classes which have a unique special ability and some unique cards, distinct enemies and an interesting story that doesn't beat you over the head with it.  The game has plenty to discover and most of the classes are interesting enough to make their journeys offer their own challenges and rewards.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Damn this game is sweet. Only 7 hours in but I can see this becoming one of my favorite rogue-lites of all time. The amount of classes/cards/passives/masteries and meta progression is nutty. All the characters you meet are interesting and can change the course of a run in a big way. And there are quests to do as you play that you have to try and complete before you die. Really cool stuff here. AAA voice acting as well. Like some of the best I've heard. This is a must buy
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, a very underrated game. The story is surprisingly interesting, the world is detailed, and the combat is actually very well thought out for a card-based game. Each class is similar in a small way with the options available, but they are all unique in their approach, which makes replayability quite easy. Finished my first successful run and was excited to discover there was more. For a game of its size and calibre, definitely an 8/10 for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: There's no need for it to be free roam in the "dungeons", it just feels janky. Card games are usually laid back, where you only use your computer mouse. Why the hell do i have to use my damn keyboard as well? The characters are just copies of what you've already seen in other games but worse. The story & world feels forced in a weird way, like a story that has been done hundreds of times before. Is the setting supposed to be taken seriously or as a joke? Is the world real or not? The decks go from feeling under powered to over powered, it's rarely in-between. The torch system they've implemented (kind of like Darkest Dungeon but worse) is just straight up annoying. I played through multiple bosses but whenever i won (which was every time, strangely enough) I didn't feel like as if it was due to my own efforts. It just felt like straight up luck. It feels like it's their first published game. It's unpolished, they don't expand on parts they could to make the game better & other parts of the game just feels unfinished. I was really excited for this game so it's sad that i disliked it this much.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I really hope that more content continues to be added to this game, DLCs, other game, or something. This game is amazing! I love the storytelling, and I'm dying to learn more about this universe. It's a very well made roguelite card game. Think like a darker Slay the Spire. You get to keep certain upgrades for your future runs, and it all feels very well balanced. I think if I had one "issue" it's that while there are 9 classes, it's really 3 base classes with 2 other subclasses. They play similarly with some base cards, but have a few different cards and ultimates. I don't mind that, but some others might, I suppose. I enjoy all of them for different reasons. Ultimately, if you like games like Slay the Spire and Monster Train, give this game a shot, it's pretty amazing. I hope to see more!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for 11 hours, I can say I've gotten my money's worth with this game.  Gameplay wise, it is very similar to Slay the Spire, with a Darkest Dungeon torch mechanic mixed in.  Due to being able to move around the map freely and pick and choose the encounters you want at will, it's balanced by the torch mechanic that tick down as you move through the map.  When your light meter is high, you get bonus cards that will have very good effects when played or when discarded.  But as your light meter fall, the card effects get worse and worse until both playing or discarding the card gives impactful negative effects.   Classes are divided into three archetype decks.  There are the archers with arrow and maneuver cards, the fighers with melee attack and stance cards, and casters with summon, spell, and sigil cards.  So while there are 9 classes, three sets of three share the same basic deck.  However, each classes has its own unique cards and passives that make it play drastically different than another class in the same archetype.  Just be aware that all nine classes aren't completely unique.As you play and trigger events, you'll eventually start recruiting NPCs and activating quests.  These will add new shops to the main hub and give you permanent upgrade options.  Everything from torch duration, health potion heal amount, armor and weapon slots (for the simplistic, but more build options, rune system), and basic stats like health and armor all have ways to be upgraded permanently to make future runs easier.  The game can be difficult if you're new to the genre, but has systems in place to make it easier over time.  However, if you're a Slay the Spire veteran, this game shouldn't give you many problems even from the start.   Overall, if you like rogue-lite, card battle games, you'll most likely like this one.  It ticks all the boxes and adds some extra build mechanics on top.  It might not have the polish or style of some of the other games in the same genre, but it's got a good amount of content and replayability for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavily inspired by slay the spire, but with some more freedom of choice. There's a lot of classes, but honestly I feel a bit weird about them. Some are just difficult for no reason. There's no real payoff for playing a more difficult class like necromancer when summoner gets you through the game without any issues. When I unlocked summoner I instantly completed my first playthrough, and have only ever completed it with summoner again since. Still, the goal like with slay the spire is to deal as much damage as you can, and maybe by playing other classes you can deal more damage. Who knows.I'm rambling, but yeah, give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit disappointed after the first run, but then I started meeting new characters, and once I unlocked the 2nd class I was hooked. I'll be honest, I switched to easy after a few runs, because I have nothing to prove to anyone, and it just made it more fun for me, since I could progress faster. I managed to finish the "campaign" on all but ONE class (I tried, I just don't understand the Necromancer) and I wish there was more to do, the gameplay is that fun! The overall progression takes a looong time, but you do feel the difference, my runs later on were so much easier, even on the classes that I was most likely playing poorly. That's roguelite done well in my eyes!

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh! This must be the most boring and tedious deck-builder I've ever played. The tutorial already sets the mood: Have fun grinding down a giant bag of hit points. And the whole game is like that (afaict)!You constantly have to light candles for no good reason, curses get shuffled into your deck, there's barely any source of healing - it's like the designers did everything to create the most unfun experience they could think of.I mean, it's possible it gets better at some point, but the beginning is such a slog, I'd rather not waste more time with this when there are so many better games that are fun right from the start.The voice-acting may be good, but they speak so slow, and the 'story' being told is so generic and pseudo grim-dark, I quickly couldn't stand it any more and just quickly clicked through it.The graphics aren't bad, but quite unsuited to this type of game. Why run around in a 3D environment if it serves no purpose? And the UI is sluggish with long load times.Apparently, there's 9 different classes in this game, however all but 1 is locked. Why?!Okay, I've explained why the game is boring, but I didn't explain yet why the game is also bad!To explain this properly, I have to explain some game design basics about randomness.There are 4 ways to include randomness in games:1. No Randomness:    Basically Chess; it's like basic nourishment: it fills the belly, but it isn't terribly exciting.    It's open information and completely deterministic, so you know exactly what you're getting.    The advantage is that it rewards strategic planning and it's well suited for tournaments.    And I can definitely see the appeal _if_ you have a regular gaming partner who is at about the same level of expertise as you.2. Input Randomness:    An example for this is your typical deck-builder:    At the start of your turn, you draw a random subset of your deck.    So, while you may not know which cards you'll get in a turn,    once they're in your hand, you can reliably plan your turn.    This kind of game rewards tactical thinking over strategy,     but it's not without strategy since you know the content of your deck and you know which cards are in your discard pile.    So, you can make an educated guess what you may draw next and take that into account when you plan your current turn.3. Output Randomness:     This is how many tactical skirmish games work:    You can freely choose which actions to take on your turn,    but these actions don't have a guaranteed outcome:    E.g. you may decide to attack with a 70% chance to hit your target,    or you may decide to take cover, granting a 50% chance to avoid being hit, etc.    This doesn't give you the planning security of input randomness, but it still allows for some planning:    You can take the actions that give you the best chance to improve your situation,    but bad luck can make short work of the best planning.4. Both Input Randomness and Output Randomness:    A combination of 2 & 3, e.g. a deck-builder with card effects that are random.    In other words: randomness on top of randomness:    You don't know what you'll be able to in you next turn,     and you also don't know if your actions will have the desired effect or not.You may have already guessed it: 'Tainted Grail' is an example of case 4.Your starting deck has 4 types of cards:1. Block2. Attack3. Buff4. Debuff1. Block: Unlike in most deck-builders, these don't block a certain amount of damage during your turn.Instead, they block one attack completely, regardless of the damage it would deal.This doesn't sound so bad, until you realize you don't have any control over _which_ attack it blocks.It will simply block the first attack in a given round.So, if you have a minion that'll attack you for 4 points of damage and a boss dealing 20 damage,if the minion attacks first, you'll block 4 damage, and the take 20 points of damage from the boss. Yay!In other words: You have no control over which enemy gets blocked.2. Attack:You have a choice betweena) dealing a random amount of damage to an enemy of your choice,b) dealing a (lower) random amount of damage to 3 random targets, andc) dealing a (very low) random amount of damage to an enemy of your choice choice,    and also lower his armor rating permanently (if he has any).In other words, even if you get to choose which enemy to damage, you don't know how much damage it will take.Say, you choose to attack an enemy with 10 health remaining, hoping to take it out.Your attack deals 5-15 damage. So, you have a 50% chance of taking it out.3. Buff:This doubles the damage you deal with the next Attack you play.However, since it costs an action point, the net effect is identical to playing two attacks.Using the only hero available from the start, there is one corner-case where this is a better option:Every attack improves your 'ultimate' which is theoretically usable once per turn.If you don't use it for a long time, it eventually deals more damage than your regular attacks.And that's the one case when this buff is better than playing a second attack.4. Debuff:For a whopping 2 action points, you can choose an enemy and stun it.This is similar to a targeted block (yay!), except it also delays actions other than an attack,e.g. if the enemy is preparing a devastating effect.I already mentioned the 'Ultimate', there's one other thing to mention for the complete picture:You starting hero makes an enemy vulnerable after attacking it 4 times in a row,allowing you to deal double damage for a turn.So, where does this leave us?Unfortunately, in most fights, there's little to choose:- blocking is usually inefficient, because you cannot use it to block the highest source of damage.- stunning is inefficient because it costs 2 actions.- attacking random targets is inefficient because it doesn't help your hero ability- reducing an enemy's armor is worthless if they don't have any armorSo, you're always trying to do the same thing:- choose the highest available attacks as often as you can    (substituting an attack buff in case you haven't drawn enough attack cards).That's the game (at least initially)!Now, given this is a rogue-like game, theoretically, it might eventually get more interesting.But are you prepared for the drudgery to reach that point?To compare games like 'Slay the Spire' with 'Tainted Grail':Just imagine you're visiting your drug dealer of choice to get your favorite poison.And lo and behold, he has a new drug in his sortiment:It costs 100% more than the drug you usually buy, but the first three times you take it,all it does is make you vomit. And after that there's a chance it'll make you vomit, get you high, or both.Now what do you do?Buy the drug you know and have a reliable high or try the new stuff?

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a deck builder game to follow through my wonderful experience with Slay the Spire and this one does the job. _childDocuments_.review: I got early access to this game with my purchase of the board game. First, this game is in a very early state. At the time of this writing, you've got a couple of hours in the campaign - though you could probably get some more out of the Conquest mode. The game is VERY clear about the current state and includes notes and explanations about what's there and how that compares to the planned experience. I wish more early access games were some forthright. So far, I'm liking what I'm seeing with the campaign. I actually like it more than the board game at this point. (The board game places such a high emphasis on resource management that it distracts from the narrative and decisions that should form the basis of the game. So far, this adaptation doesn't suffer from the same issue.) While this has the same basic starting premise as the board game (The heroes are gone, and you're what's left. It's up to you.) this experience seems a little more finely focused. It's not just a copy of the board game.Setting the board game aside, this has some real potential. It looks great and has great atmosphere, and the sound and voice acting are solid. The card-based combat (different from the board game) is actually quite enjoyable. Outside of combat, there are plenty of interesting decisions to be made that seem to have a real impact on things. If the ripples from these decisions really do have an impact - and the density of decisions in the rest of the game matches that of the opening hour or so - this should be really impressive.As for the Conquest mode, I'm definitely intrigued, and I like the idea of being able to play a whole new mode separate from the campaign. That said, it seems punishingly difficult in its current state. Combat is far tougher than in the campaign, and you seem to start of weaker - not a good combo. At the moment, it feel like things need to be made significantly easier or you need a lot more hand holding with regards to how you are expected to progress.If the premise of a grim and dark variation on Camelot (Kamelot) appeals to you, give the game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost deleted the game during the first hours, as it was too hard and I kept dying during the first boss battle. Playing on an easy mode helps a bit. It is a good card game, not great though. It's slower than competitors, cards have limited combos, and overall gameplay is not so great. The UI feels a bit clunky and rushed like they used default assets from Unreal Engine. Would like to see a unique interface, better cards UI (art is amazing though), and more animations. Also, it wasn't necessary for this game to be in 3D.The game's strongest points are the music and the overall style and ambiance. Danheim and his Nordic folk songs single-handedly carry boss battles. Also I really liked the dark style and narrative of the game, which soak the player with emptiness and despair. Overall, it is a good cardbattler, however I suggest buying it only on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, blending RPG with Card game elements. Decent story, but what is great is the addictive gameplay and deck building choices with a bunch of classes to pick and upgrade and a lot of cards to customize your deck through playthroughs. It also has great replay value. On the negatives its the grinding required to reach the "true ending"(i wont spoil but you dont miss much even if you dont reach it, kind disappointing) the OST although having some nice tracks they get repeated a lot and because of the huge re-runs required they can turn tiring and boring quickly, i just played youtube music on the background after a while. Also you can get screwed for a whole playthrough and its rest runs with some choices, that was a big yikes cause i was locked on from some NPC quests and couldnt finish them despite having done all the rest to unlock the true ending.Give the game a try if you like card games and RPG with strategy feels with choices that matter.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid roguelike with a couple unique twists on the genre.  The production value is notably high, it seems like.  Pretty quality voice acting, decent Arthurian myth inspired story and lore, and way above average graphical fidelity for the par for the genre.  My main issues are the combat is often imbalanced and the pacing often doesn't feel right.  Combat is usually way too easy or but then at times it surprises you out of nowhere with being insanely hard.  Additionally some classes it feels satisfying to play the right cards at the right time, and other times it just feels like you have to go through the motions of playing the cards because that's just how the class works.  Which leads to you not really feeling too in control of the playthrough, so much as just doing what needs to be done, without much decisions in how you influence your character build.Pacing is kind of wonky throughout the experience.  On your first couple runs you'll be figuring things out and taking a lot of new information in, and somewhat struggling for resources.  But then with subsequent runs, think will feel boring at times because getting a couple key upgrades will make it feel drastically different with how hard it is to balance resources.  Wyrd candles noticeably feel hard to balance early, then seem to become so easy later that it becomes an insignificant tacked-on feeling mechanic.  A few of the mechanics, actually, feel kind of tacked on.  Like, they feel okay in the sense of lore and the world, but gameplay wise they don't add anything meaningful other than pointless fluff (the various different items and consumable, notably).Additionally it can feel pretty grindy at times.  There is a decent handful of enemies for maybe several dozen hours of play, but after that, it starts to just feel repetitive with the enemies and their predictable attack and action patterns.  So this makes the necessary fights to acquire resources to upgrade the town and your characters mostly like a chore.Still giving this a positive review as there's a lot of things this game does that are fairly unique to the genre and do feel pretty satisfying.  And checking the update history for the game you do see the developer does care a lot about the state of their game, making lots of quality of life and balance changes.  I feel like with a little bit more attention and culling of non satisfying game mechanics, this could be a really stellar game.  Main thing I'd like to see them do is to just work out some of the classes so they feel more fun to actually play (Apostate and Necromancer notably felt like a chore to keep going to finish the run).

_childDocuments_.review: Well,I felt it was somewhat short - as I realize its a slay the spire sort idea so not going to gripe - took about 2 hours to do a good run.The classes do not really seem to vary that much to me - as it stands they got 5 of the 9 classes in game.The idea is basically you walk around a map going into random battles - there does not seem to be any importance in choices you make outside of leveling. The game is pretty sparse with explanation.The music is great!The art is meth - it seems like some very generic assets that are somewhat dressed in garbage.The battle system feels like its not nearly random enough to really matter - my general tactic was "stop all damage and whittle down my foe" by the end of the game I had to put in zero effort to walk over the majority of fights.After you do so - your hub gets upgraded and you do it again.Going to say 6/10 for now - its not terrible but not really worth full price. - atleast not yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a good card battler but not as good as I hoped.I was about to give up on this game after a few runs with the starting character. I did well in my first run and then I got stuck. The starting character isn't very flexible, mostly just a damage giver. Worse, I couldn't make any progress and wasn't able to unlock anything significant.I switched over to another class (summoner I think). Suddenly the game became much easier, maybe too easy. I think this is a significant flaw in the game - the starting class should be reasonably capable, not the best but not useless as it is in Tainted Grail.The game is definitely designed for grinding. There are lots of permanent upgrades to unlock but in many cases they take an absurd amount of resources to upgrade. You would have to play dozens of runs to unlock some of them. Unfortunately there isn't enough variety in the game to make it interesting to do that many runs. Once you beaten the "true boss" you've pretty much seen it all. A good card battler which I can recommend, but I was hoping for more given it popularity and high ratings.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I like this spin on the Arthurian legend with a giant heap of "weird". Atmosphere & setting are interesting, it really has a believable vibe of ruin/apocalypse imminent/"♥♥♥♥ this i'm out".  Music and visuals are creepy and unique, lots of crazy chanting and screaming type music ahahaha I was quite pleased with it and felt like it was complementary to the world.  Combat system has a lot of potential, you get a bunch of cards to use on a turn by turn basis and you can build your deck to suit your strategy.  Game still needs a ton of work, but it feels like there is a solid foundation and that there is a clear and unified vision in place for a final product.  What is available right now is a very limited "teaser", but is enough to allow the player to get a feel for the systems and a hint of what the full game could be.  I am interested enough to return periodically, or for the finished product.

_childDocuments_.review: On one hand, very nice looking game with fun classes and interesting combos!   Very much a solid copy+paste rogue-lite card builder following so many before it!On the other hand, the developers decided that because this is a "rogue-lite" game, you must grinding for endless hours replaying the game over and over and over in order to unlock more fun...Ultimately, if they reduced the grind in many areas of the game I think it would be worth recommending.  As it stands, I estimate I'd need to invest 30+ hours of grinding out the same few levels over and over and over in order to unlock any meaningful progression on the account.  For example, you unlock most of the buildings or "features" pretty quickly.  And each of them effectively require a different currency to upgrade what they offer.  The issue comes where the buildings you care about most and offer the more enjoyable changes to your runs, will maybe result in ~3 currency drops in a run... and you need 15-30-50+ for one upgrade.   If a run takes you say ~15-30  minutes?  You can do the math but likely see that you have to grind A LOT to unlock stuff.Compare this to other rogue-lite games I've played where if you beat bosses, you straight up get new items to use (this game isn't like that from my experience).  Those other games do have currency, but it's ONE currency that you choose to use wherever you want.  This game has MULTIPLE currency types, one for each building, and you don't get equal drops of that currency every run.  Some of the currency you have to actively and specifically grind for (often at the expense of others).

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more recent patches made the first boss almost impossible to beat. It used to be a golem which while hard was possible to beat since killing the little golems gave you strong attack cards. Now the first boss has a tank which absorbs nearly all damage and gives barriers to all the other dudes. Since it is the first boss you are not very strong and do not have the cards to beat needed to win. Before this patch the game was a lot of fun (although challenging for sure), now I never want to play because the boss is too hard. If they get rid of him I will gladly play again. (I got the game from kickstarting the board game and have played all the different versions)
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Good deck builder with a surprising amount of story and featuring some fantastic voice acting.  Good classes, options and ways to build up over time.Only cons are the areas you explore are bleak and very basic looking (boring) and I've run into some annoying bugs in combat which caused me to have to restart fights after getting stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: A solid deckbuilder in the vein of Slay the Spire, but in a grimdark setting. You have a hub village which you gradually fill with NPCs, which unlock permanent character upgrades that persist from run to run.Basically a single run consists of you playing through 3 stages, collecting cards, runestones for armor and weapon slots and passive skills, beating the boss of each stage to unlock the next - very similar to Slay the Spire. Once you beat all 3 stages you fight the final boss. The final boss never dies but you have to survive for 15 turns and do as much damage as possible to him in that time - the damage you do determines your final score, which is used for ranking on the leaderboards.All of the character classes play much differently from one another and are divided into 2 main groups of 3 classes each. Warrior group classes are solo and rely on themselves for damage and healing, Mage group classes use summons for combat and healing.In my experience a single run takes close to 3 hours to complete, which is much longer than the 40-60 minutes a typical Slay the Spire run takes.All in all, it's fun to discover and explore the world, unlock new skills and cards and see how broken or OP you can make your build. But all that said, it is very much in early access and is still missing a lot of balance and polish passes. I do not recommend the game at this time due to the EA nature of the game, and its many bugs and poor optimization, but once it is a complete product hopefully it will be polished enough to whole-heartedly recommend.PROS:-original grimdark setting-fun, addictive core gameplay loop-runestone system adds a lot of diversity and strategy to builds-sense of exploration and discovery-music is superb-shows promising potential of being a great gameCONS:-movement controls on the overland map are a clunky mess. game would be better served having a 2D overworld map to traverse, the 3D environment does nothing to enhance the game-speaking of the 3D environment, the game is very poorly optimized and very demanding of resources for what could easily be a 2D game. GPU is often at 100% load...not even Cyberpunk2077 on Ultra does that to my GPU! This kind of load for a muddy, not very attractive game is unacceptable.-the game screams EARLY ACCESS with many typos, spelling mistakes, inconsistent or missing dialogue/voicework, NPCs under construction and balance issues popping up all over the place-similar to the atrocious movement controls, the camera is an even bigger mess. It doesn't auto-follow the character and will often glitch out, centering itself in the middle of the forest leaving you unable to see or move your character-Wyrdness mechanic seems half-baked - I find there's little reason to burn wyrd candles
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10What is nice- gameplay is good. straightforward roguelike, card game, deck building and rpg. balance is ok. improvement can feel too grindy, to get to the "decent" drop take some time and probably some will feel bored already.- characters are good. "classes" and "subclasses" feels pretty unique yet have enough similarities between each other. cards are interesting.- enemies are ok. it can got boring over time. need more varieties.- story is ok. story is interesting but clearly the gameplay feels superior.- sound is ok. voice is good. music is good at the beggining but it got boring after some time. need more dynamics.- visual is ok. environments, characters, cards, monsters, and effects looks good but got boring after some time. need more varieties or dynamics.- visual performance is good using middle low end graphic card.What can be improved- improving ui, visibility, descriptions, details, etc. there are times i am not sure what will happen.- more enemies is needed- more cards- more characters is nice- while understandable it will get a bit faster later, the amount to grind for the improvements feels too high at the beginning- bugs. some visual bugs happens. not annoying but still it just happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Fwoah this game is GOOD. Massive amounts of synergies and options to pick from in deck building, and it's legitimately engaging, challenging and very fun. Aesthetically it's way up my alley, that alley being dark fantasy, and it brings back hardcore memories of Diablo 2 (especially the class selection screen), the grimness of grim dawn and the gore/bleak feeling of Soul Sacrifice (Vita boiz).Gameplay is layered and purposeful - all mechanics have a specific intent in how they function, and the sense of urgency that wyrdcandles provide to just running around is wonderful. Music is appreciably bassy and a strange mix of Slavic folk music that is really catchy. Very good sound/music.The best part for me is aesthetics, really. The game has clear identity in its design - it's really well lit and tonally consistent. No jarring colour distortions or odd use of overly bright lights. It's all moody, well crafted and coherent, and has a very unique look to it that sets it apart from other dark fantasy types.It's just a really damn good game all round. It's consistently great and fun! The ONLY downside is some optimization issues at launch, but they're minor at best.Otherwise, top, TOP recommendation, particularly if you enjoy dark fantasy settings and turn based card combat. The layers of gameplay in here are exceptional and all classes play very differently.Ace game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: This contains some small spoilers that are game play mechanics which I was not aware of when I bought Tainted Grail. If you don't want to know stop here! Just know the game has some nice replay mechanics. OK, small spoilers ahead...So far I am mostly loving this game. One huge thing I was not aware of is that death opens more options. You will unlock a new class each time you play through to your death until all nine are unlocked. Also some items can carry over from run to run. Plus upgrades to your village carry over after death. Some currencies carry over also. This makes the threat of death less frustrating since you will most likely die before accomplishing your first goal... at least on regular difficulty. Just remember it's a learning experience and a gateway to better things! Plus each death holds the possibility of a better next run with varying blessings, passives, cards to add to your deck, and rewards to be enjoyed. How many variants I have no idea at this point? This goes without saying but I will say it anyway. You will like and/or dislike classes. I think so far for me it's pretty much split down the middle. I got the farthest with a Sentinel and a Summoner though I still have a few to unlock. The flip side is you will need to play as each class at least once to unlock everything in the game? The other negative is the twisted dark world the game takes place in. So you may not like it at all or like me want to take it in smaller increments. Over all I don't mind dark worlds just as long as there is great game play to keep me engaged! My final point is that I've only played a bit more than fourteen hours at this point and I feel I have already got my money's worth... since I bought during this current summer sales event!  Very enjoyable game in my opinion!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelike, gritty and dark. Some NPC's are more wierd than dark themed, which is not my preference.However the game easily makes up for it with the deep combat mechanics and progression systems, which are definately my cup of tea. I have not played this game for more than 3-4 hours. But the amount of clueless negative reviews needs to be watered down.Surprised you have to start over in a roguelike? what?!Surprised a rogue like is Thumbs up from me
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks very nice graphically. The UI and controls are good. Controller support is good. Most everything else is not good in the game.First, the deck building is slow going. You don't feel like  you have much choice in what you are doing with the deck. Resources to manage the deck are extremely limited as well.The map element of the game is pointless. The map has no meaning other than just a time sync to watch your character walk around. There are no interesting locations or paths really. Just a way to activate the next encounter. No interesting decisions with the map. The quests have no real guidance, just randomly you wander and maybe you run into them.The worst part of the game to me is the stupid candle system. These burn out really fast and are extremely limited. This prevents you from exploring the area as you may want to. You are constantly having to activate another candle and they last almost no time as you wander the pointless map system to get to the next encounter as fast as you can.Overall, just a poorly done rogue like/deck builder system. The encounters are somewhat interesting, but since you have such limited control of your deck and no time to actually enjoy powering yourself up before you are forced to run along before the stupid candles run out, it just is not enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly well-rounded and fun rogue-lite deck building game with a unique atmosphere delivered through rather good graphics and backed by a truly great soundtrack. Would recommend a look to anyone interested in PvE deck-builders at all. My main concern yet to be answered would be just how the difficulty scales and balance of the various classes, as I did complete the first run I set out on successfully. Looking forward to challenges ahead as the "mystery" unveils!Shout out to Jorbs (and the devs for promoting through him), as that's how I heard of the game in the first place!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Cool roguelite deckbuilder with some unique takes on the genre. Highly recommend for fans of Slay the Spire, Monster Train, etc. I have over 400 hours in STS across PC and mobile with I don't know how many A20H kills. Tainted Grail was worth the pickup. Folks who don't care for the genre won't be convinced, I don't think. Note I've reached difficulty #11 in the main game mode, and haven't touched the other game modes. Can't speak for how it is later on. Pros - - Ton of build variance. Lots of classes with subclasses different enough to feel unique. Insane amount of cards, plus the powerups you pick up along the way.- No other deckbuilder I've played handles combat like this one. Playing as a summoner feels like the fantasy Magic the Gathering always wanted of being a mage casting spells from their spellbook. - Satisfying wombocombos- Freedom to fight as much or as little as you want, rather than set amount of encounters.- Great voice actingCons - - Little bit janky. Stutters a lot even while running on a 3080. Sometimes need to click a few times to select an enemy. Sometimes controls don't always behave as expected, like pressing Escape doesn't get you out of an NPC interaction. Nothing so bad as to make it unplayable.- Soundtrack is tiiiiiiiiny. The few songs they have are great, but they get old when looped so constantly. - The overworld gimmick feels pointless after the first few runs. Torches are too easy to come by.- Some encounters kind of feel like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if you go into it not knowing that the enemy in the group is build specifically to punish you for whatever you may be lacking at the time. You'll definitely remember for next time though.With a bit more polish this could be up there as one of the best in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun roguelike deck builder! It plays similarly to Slay the Spire, but with an enjoyable dark fantasy setting, interesting characters, and great 3D graphics. I only have about 20 hours in it and haven't played on the high difficulties, but it feels quite a bit easier than Slay the Spire. That said, there's still some challenge, particularly as the difficulty increases (kind of like Ascensions in Slay the Spire). One of the biggest draws of this game is that it has 9 classes that are all fairly unique (although they are bucketed into 3 "factions," which gives them the same base cards as other classes in groups of 3). I still have 2 classes that I haven't tried, but all of the ones I have played have distinct play styles that make each run really fun and interesting to build around.If slay the spire gameplay with a souls-esque dark fantasy setting sounds like a solid combination to you, I definitely recommend picking this up!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed this game. It has brilliantly replayable. I've played 51 hours and I have yet to unlock all unlocks for just one class. What I love: It has great variation even if you run the same class after a previous run. The story and side stories are still unfolding with 51 hours in. A mistake could cost you a defeat but once you understand the class and combinations it can be really satisfying going from brink of defeat to winning a battle. I've completed the main story with one class and since then I've had a better understanding of the game and moved onto other classes and enjoyed the learning process for the class. It is very casual player friendly. Saves can be anytime, I've just popped on for 30 minutes this morning and closed it down. The music is brilliant in this game because of it I have started to listen to Danheim which is now a favourite. The graphics for this type of game are ace. I don't think I've come across a roguelite with better graphics yet. I appreciate how it's one character you're playing at a time in comparison to a party. During the steam Sale I was looking for something that could compare and I really struggled and stopped searching. Two things to note: at the start there is a learning curve but it isn't too steep to deter away from. The game says 10 classes, kind of yes and no. I'd say there is 3 classes (possibly 4, I've not really touched the last unlock) with subclasses. For example there is a range class with 3 (maybe 4 subclasses again not played the last unlock much at all). A further example of this is one character works best when saving attacks for one big hit in comparison to another which does better with many hits in a turn. They do play differently to one and another with enough variation to feel it is a different class.100% I'd recommend this game if you like roguelites with lots of combinations, more realistic graphics in comparison, great music with lots of replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the demo in a couple of hours.  I own the tabletop version, and like it a lot.  This is a good interpretation of the tabletop game, with decent graphics, turn-based card-centered combat and an interesting story (at least so far).  Aside from combat, there is exploration and several opportunities to make decisions in interacting with NPCs that feel like they will affect the main story.  Overall, I am interested, and looking forward to the full release.The combat system at this time is pretty well-designed, but overall the combat in this demo is very easy.  I won every fight I was in, and never really had to worry about the outcome if I made good card choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I typically love difficult roguelike games like high ascendance slay the spire or trials of fire. That being said, this game isn't really difficult as much as it is unbalanced. It is frustrating to absolutely decimate the first two areas and then suddenly get 1 shot by the first enemy in the third area. I think some numbers need to be looked at before this game officially releases. Also, this game has quite a few annoying bugs that ruin a game that COULD be good.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful time sink of a deckbuilding roguelite RPG set in a dark medieval fantasy world with King Arthur folklore as its central theme. One doesn't need to be well-versed in medieval mythology to quickly become immersed in Tainted Grail's grim world, as it has a magical sense of appealing to nostalgia, invoking memories of games like Diablo II and Gauntlet. Strategy plays a large role in bending the RNG to your will, but the game reminds you often enough that you aren't truly in control - and without completely shattering your little gamer soul. Each death brings new opportunities, making them less frustrating and more exciting. Pretty cool game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun. The deckbuilding has a learning curve, but after that i had a blast. I reached the point where i had my first "real" playthrough. You get more of the story after each playthrough, because you meet new people. It is a bit of a grind to unlock all classes and villagers, but after that it is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Deckbuilding roguelike with good variety, fun mechanics and a strong theme.3 major archetypes (Archer/Soldier/Summoner) split into 9 classes, each with a unique play-style and a good set of cards.Relatively well balanced, probably on the easier side where even on the higher difficulty you win the vast majority of your runs. Although I will say that the summoner archetype does seem much weaker than the other two, maybe I'm just bad at playing it.Most of the time the once you get past the first few fights the game gives you so many passives you start to snowball out of control. Which is both fun when you can play the yackety sax and do really broken things but it does kill a little of the challenge.The surrounding story and lore is also pretty neat. I wont say much about it because I skimmed through most of it as I prefer gameplay.Overall I enjoyed my time playing it and would recommend is to anyone who likes deckbuilding games.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: It tries to have some cool ideas; and to a degree, it kind of does - but on the other hand, the gameplay is extremely repetitive within your class. Worse however, is: it just takes too long to play for what it really is.Additionally, there looks like there's a handful of classes - there isn't. Each of the 'classes' actually belongs to 1 of 3 main archtypes, which utilize the same starting cards and discoverable cards; the only difference within those different sub-archtype classes is their charge ability - and even then, they mechanically overlap a bunch still.Like, it's not the worst game, but after having played it for a bit - I actively don't want to go back and continue playing. There isn't enough variety between runs/decks, and the core gameplay (map exploration, as well as combat itself) is such a slog at the end of the day. Sure, I like discovering the story in the repeated playthroughs/encounters, but that's not enough to make me actually want to keep playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I can"t suggest this game for 2 reasons:1: balance (or rather scaling) is horrible. If you make somewhat logical decisions, you will scale far far harder than the enemys most of the time. As a result, if you survive the first half of a game, is is extremely hard to lose.2: progression. There are random encounters that give you choices. Many are a 1 time thing, and unlock permanent stuff after. You can actually fail a questline if you make a wrong choice, and as punishment the rewards of that questline will be forever locked from your current savefile. The most powerfull quest reward you can miss out on is a certain flute. A consumeable that recharges after every fight, can be carried into every run and gives 2 block that turn.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: It's great! I must say that after a weekend with Tainted Grail I am undoubtedly hooked up. I really enjoy the creative mix of roguelikes, RPG and deckbuilder. A very interesting design choice with the quest log persisting through separate runs - it gives you a constant sense of progress. One thing that irritates me is the UI - cards are so big they sometimes cover your minions when playing Summoner or Bloodmage. It's a minor detail however. 10/10 nevertheless
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Campaign is short for now, they have promised to expand on content as the board game version production nears completion. The conquest mode is fun but a bit aggravating at first as the descriptions from events and items are lacking often leading to the end of a run in frustration because the consequences were not well outlined making the entire mode have very steep learning curves. Plenty of bugs and glitch's in both the main story and conquest. Do not attempt to draw your entire deck in one turn as the only thing you can do is end the turn without playing any cards. Hopefully they will continue to improve of their content.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that I LOVED this game.  All of the classes play and feel significantly different and the graphics and sound effects are top notch.  You basically just run around in the same little area over and over but, honestly, I didn't even care, I loved the combat so much.  There's some story and some questlines and they are very good carrots to keep you on the treadmill but, again: the gameplay and combat is so flippin' good, it almost doesn't matter.         They have a terrific engine here and should keep expanding or make a sequel or something because the only thing missing in this game is MOAR game!  For realsies, though, it is on sale right now for $8 ... if I were you, I'd tear out my back pocket getting the money for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly deep card builder.  Especially considering all the other elements in the game.  The classes are different enough that trying them out until you find your groove is the best way to go.  I couldn't put it down for five hours straight.  For me that's a lot!  I recommend Tainted Grail.  It was worth the two coffees I didn't buy to get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: TG is the type of game i've been waiting for. It has features that break new ground and is the type of sleeper hit that people are going to look back to. Like Slay the Spire which gets mentioned a lot in comparison, TG is so much better in many ways, except maybe for the hardmode type challenge.It really brings many things together in a flawless, fun and atmospheric way; a roguelite card builder rpg with many character archetypes set in a dark fantasy story world. Just amazing.There are a couple downsides though. The character balance aspect is always going to be hard if not impossible to get exact but the heavy handed way it's been handled for Necromancer for example is unfortunate considering the way they changed Apostate, it just all seems arbitrary if not lazy.The biggest downside for me is the fact that there could be more variety of areas and corresponding monster types. Adding dungeons for example would be great to keep your attention for longer without it seeming like the same thing over and over just with different backgrounds. Another problem is that the difficulty should ramp up more as later areas are a faceroll if you build right and/or get lucky. I understand that this is a roguetype but this could have been avoided with less rng char progression.Overall a much needed example of the creativeness that can be achieved, unfortunately pioneering work is never well known except maybe in hindsight.So much value for what you pay, very highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game to turn my brain off to while enjoying the awesome soundtrack playing in the background. It's not nice to newer players like myself who aren't so veteran to the genre of deckbuilders, but if you persevere you'll eventually get there! That said, most of the ability to last until the end comes from unlocking all the newer cards until you can make some real broken combinations. The only gripe I have is the art: I can't buy a little PDF of it as DLC. I would love to have it for my own tabletop roleplay games, I'm a fan of dark fantasy style like this has.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: 1. despite being pretty and an interesting take on arthurian myth the game is poorly optimized and has no consistent framerate.2. The gameplay feels rather repetitive in campaign mode just doing different tiers of corruption. I did the first 4 levels of corruption which makes you basically clear the run 4 times and die. It was mostly the same save for a few new cards. a couple classes. But the runs themselves are largely uninteresting since individuals spend a lot of time fighting weak/dumb enemies like rats that are tedious and don't offer interesting engagements/fights. 3. character creation is limited.4. deck building is shallow compared to aeon's end, mystic vale, dominion, clank, and slay the spire.I recommend slay the spire over this but if you're burnt out on slay the spire, then consider a board game or a digital board game like aeon's end on steam first before trying this.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Brief:Give this game a shot if you enjoy rpgs or card battlers.  There are so many systems you'll be playing for a long time to come.  It's a pleasure figuring out just the right combinations, unlocking more complexities and story as the hours stack up.Too Long:Huge Slay the Spire and Monster Train fan.  Watching this 1 on Twitch (and reading some forum threads) I wasn't sold, looked a bit boring.  Boy was I wrong.Sadly, for the developers, this game took just over 2 hours to turn from fair to interesting and another hour to really start enjoying it and getting hooked.  The game takes it's time unlocking core components of it's upgrade/loot system which I feel are essential to it's enjoyment.  Additionally the initial cards and class you start with are fairly basic.  Also the first tutorial fight is stupidly long and a poor representation of the typical combat flow/challenge - hopefully people don't think it represents the game and bail prematurely.  Around 2 hours in I finally was unlocking some real interesting cards in the then unlocked Summoner class along with the runestones and some town npcs with upgrade mechanics.Once you've unlocked some of the town merchants, classes, runestones, and items you begin to experience the joy and complexity of Tainted Grail's system.  The cards, classes, and runestones have some excellent synergies you can exploit to destroy your enemies.  With all the gear, systems, and classes you'll get many dozens of hours of play out of this title.  This enemies in this game have many variants forcing you to deversify your strategy far more than I've seen in other card battlers.  Some enemies grow stronger each time they are hit, some are immune to stun attacks, some grow stronger each turn, some grow stronger as there are more of them, and so on and you take on multiple enemies in each battle.Throughout all this there is a very odd story being weaved with the oddest of characters.  I've now played 3 classes and each plays completely differently with different decks.  My last 1 an archer went from me disliking it to enjoying it as I unlocked more cards and discovered the synergies in them.  This happens again and again with the classes as you adjust to their uniqueness and figure out strategies that will work for you.  I'm hooked and jumping in to try the next 1 now, so many to unlock and so varied, it's great.This game went from meh to addictive in the course of a few hours, hopefully it does the same for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! If you enjoy games like Slay the Spire, you will very much enjoy this game. The combat mechanics are similar with more powers and abilities. There are way more classes to choose from and you get a bit of story element. Awaken Realms really went all out to make a superb game, and for a board game company, this is saying a lot! (Also you should play the Tainted Grail Board Game, it's fantastic, although different experience for sure)
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, great game, terribly bugged.To give you the quick rundown of the game: Imagine Slay the Spire (just a lot less RNG) with Diablo-like flair. While I played I had a great time with it, but unfotunately the game is so buggy that I don't think it's ready to be played yet.Both of my first two runs ended with the game softlocking on me. The first time I somehow got stuck behind a NPC, the second time the portal that was supposed to take me back to town bugged out and just didn't move me.To sum my experience up: Reporting the bug via the "Report Bug" menu failed with "Could not send bug report". That pretty much is the state game right now. I think that Tainted Grail has great potential and a solid foundation to be an amazing game if the devs can iron out the issues it has. But for now, don't buy unless you want to playtest the beta version.If you still decided to give it a go after all, here's a a quick guide how to play:First off, shift makes you sprint which really speeds up the game. Secondly, never press F to interact with stuff, always click on things. Pressing F on the portals is how you softlock your game. If you did it anyway and you bricked your save, just alt-F4. The game saves fairly infrequently and just hard-restarting the game is a pretty good way of undoing f_ckups.The recommended starter class sucks. I don't think it's supposed to clear the game without a great deal of failing first. After you're in the map quit your run and restart as Necromancer. I'm unsure if the Necro is super overpowered or everyone else is really underpowered, but with this game you gotta take what you can. The Necro has the insane advantage of being able to heal itself while doing bonkers amounts of damage.For starter minion take the crab thing, it's the key to victory.Your basic combat goes like this: Sacrifice your crab, use barrier on yourself to offset any incoming damage, dump your remaining mana into Ritual on your crab-spirit. Every time the spirit attacks it becomes stronger. Use your golems to soak big hits and Fae to heal back up. Your ultimate can really boost your damage output, so use it regularly. You can double-up on the -100 armor ability quite freely as it's close to impossible to die as Lich.Once you beat the three side-areas you get to fight the last boss. On all subsequent playthroughs don't fight the "real" last boss, as you'll not unlock higher difficulties for beating him.Congrats, you mastered Tainted Grail and you're ready to rinse and repeat until you get bored. Feel free to experiment with the other classes now that you know what's going on, and be surprised how terrible they are.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest: I am no expert in these card games and i probably will never be. So i can't really judge how good the game is in terms of balancing, requirement for thinking all possibilities through and arranging your deck. What i can say is, that is very atmospheric to me. The music, visual art, sounds and story-writing is well done including pretty good voice-acting (most of what you read is being read out loud). Most of that is done in sketch-like form, which isn't an issue for me. It fits the game very well.So far i had my fun and not too much difficulty in proceeding. In the end it has rogue-lite elements anyway, so i guess you just have to play long enough to unlock options that make the game easier for you. And there is a lot to unlock. I'm yet not sure where it's going to in terms of difficulty and complexity. Up to now I completed one run (after a few game-loops and unlocking stuff) and now have the option to play the next diffculty. And I am still motivated to see what's coming next. There are many, many passive abilities, cards, runes, helpful items. Maybe to much for some people who prefer to be limited in their possibilties to force them thinking stuff through, but as said I have yet to see where this is going to.Also there are 9 different character-classes you can unlock. But I haven't tried any of these yet, instead sticking to the initial class for now. Should be worth to try out the others too though. Considering the fact that i got the game on a discount for a few bucks, I can say that it's well worth the money to me. So if you are into this type of game, give it a try. I doubt that you will regret it unless you expected something totally different.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Was a little skeptical because I hate card games and I hate rogue games, this game is both those things but also not. I first tried the rogue play and died basically right away, several hours later and I had to pry myself away because I kept wanting to progress further and further. _childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good StS-like deckbuilder with a few new twists and takes.  The standout addition is the setting, lore, and overall vibe of the Arthurian version of purgatory you're tasked with saving (by Death himself, of course).  The voice work and writing are both surprisingly excellent and really make you want to keep plugging away.  A few of the classes are quite unique and interesting in their own ways as well.  The downsides are poor graphics performance (for not anything special) and a decent amount of grind (you cannot win a run without at least a failed runs to unlock 'the good stuff').  Overall, 9/10.Be warned: if you want to get all of the story, it took me about 50 hours of play, but could've been 30... if I had realized earlier that a good chunk of the story requires you to wander around without a wyrdcandle lit to trigger specific events.

Characters are actually 3, not 9 - 3 warriors/summoners/archers , with the same cards as others in group, but slightly diffrent twist, to them (unbalanced for such similar archetypes, although necromancer is the best one i've seen in games). Game often crashes my pc with bluescreens and freezes. Today I decided to stop playing it, till it gets fixed, last update(today) I lost my 36h progress due to game corrupting my save with no way of backup, forcing me to start over grinding up all characters unlocks (terribly unnecessary feature), all village npc, storyline, resources, cards.. etc. As much as I enjoyed the game, I'm not going to risk losing almost 40h of gameplay again. _childDocuments_.review: tldr; If you do well in Slay the Spire/Monster Train, you might not enjoy how easy this game is. This game is way easier than both of those.Solid game, with a decent story, interesting mechanics, and unique classes. But, simply put, the game is too easy. And this isn't me trying to big flex on anyone. EVERY class can become very powerful very easily, after only a few smart choices. You don't even need very many upgrades to your persistent village area; such upgrades only make you even more overpowered. And while the ascending difficulty system may help with this eventually, it doesn't feel like it solves the issue.I truly believe that any veteran of Slay the Spire or Monster Train can breeze through this game, as well as both the false and true final bosses.Overall, I feel no excitement from the game, and no clutch moments that made Slay the Spire/Monster Train fun. I just feel like I'm going through the motions of a deck-builder without any of the thrill. I suppose you could say the fun of the game is from how broken you can make each class, but I'd rather fight for my life than lifelessly mow down opponent after opponent.I'd only recommend this game to people who just can't get enough of deck-builders, or that can overlook how easy it is. Maybe even to people that haven't played any other deck-building rogue-likes, but even then I'd probably just recommend them the other two games mentioned above instead.If you want to see for yourself, I'd recommend you buy the game and see if you can beat it in your first run. If you can, you should then refund the game, because it doesn't get much harder afterward.
