_childDocuments_.review: Deciding between a 'thumbs up' and 'thumbs down' was very hard for this, but I think the mechanics used for a deckbuilding rogue-like fell into too many of the same pitfalls that other games of the same genre do. I think the game can be fun for ~10 hours but once the grind starts there is no real reason to continue.Pros:Interesting story, atmosphere, and general feel for the world. Multiple classes each with a different ultimate, way of generating it, ability you can reliably use every turn, and passive ability to start with. Cons: Too easy to build decks that combo out on turn one. In other games this can incidentally happen with luck or planning, but in this game in particular it feels like that's a mechanic built in. There are far too many passive abilities that can reliably give you more energy, cards, and power on Turn 1/2/3. It makes the game uninteresting when the game actively provides an incentive not to interact with the enemies/bosses. My first Boss 3/Boss 4 kill was done on turn 1 before they could have a turn.There are many card options for what you can add to your deck, but many of my runs that are successful I add very few actual cards to my deck. Many times the cards you are offered are "OK" and side grades to your starting cards or very situational. But you don't take them because you don't want to reduce how often you draw your good cards. With that said, the cards that are good are... extremely good. Especially the 'quest' cards that after meeting a particular condition you get an extremely OP card you can use once a fight.The archer classes don't feel particularly well thought out or rewarding. Having a common card type that actively reduces your ultimate charge feels particularly bad. If you are actively using these Quiver cards, the chances of actually using an impactful ultimate is very low.

_childDocuments_.review: “Cuanact is dying, its barren fields provide little food and its crumbling walls offer no protection. As the power of the guardian mehnir fails, the wyrdness creeps ever closer. Twisting places, breaches and even space its self, despite this the people of the farmhold refuse to leave. Instead Lord Yvain lead four of their best on a desperate mission to Kamelot. They promised to bring back help, they never returned. Now those left behind are growing desperate, they will try to bestow the burden their fate on someone else, new heroes, with even slimmer chance of success.”  There are two game modes currently, the Tainted Grail Campaign and the Tainted Grail Conquest. Currently the Campaign is just a teaser of the story-driven experience where your choices will affect the fate of Avalon. The Conquest mode is for hardcore players, slaying beasts while developing your village and skills. You will die plenty in Conquest, and each time you fail you’ll begin back at your village with what you first started with. Selecting to continue will open a window asking you to choose a slot for your game saves (there is three slots) after which you’ll be able to create your character. The options of your character consist of Gender, Skin and Hair Colour along with Hair and Beard Styles. Once you’ve chosen your characters look, next you can choose your Class and Rune. Currently though there is only one class you can choose, a Warrior (more will be available in the future). You have the choice of three Runes, Brawler, Guardian and Berserker. The Brawler Rune focuses on inflicting heavy damage against single opponents. The Guardian Rune is an energy-efficient rune which focuses on sequencing cards into advanced combos. The Berserker Rune is a high-risk high-reward which gains more power the less Health points you have. Once you’ve done deciding hit Create will start the game. Beginning a new quest, you find yourself in a clearing standing beside a huge Menhir statue, ruined buildings around the edge of the clearing. To one side there’s some tents around a camp fire and nearby is a Milestone. There’s only one path leading out of the village, however, surrounding the village is a strange blue fog … the Wyrdness! Entering the Wyrdness is a very dangerous environment to be in, things won’t always be as they seem on the map. While in the Wyrdness you’ll become weaker, engaging in combat will become much harder than normal but the rewards should you survive are more profitable. Stay too long in the Wyrdness and it will transform and corrupt your body and mind. You begin with a Sword, Leather Armour, WyrdCandles and Travel Map, the wyrdcandles will allow you to move through the Wyrdness without any problems. However, the candles only last for a short time, so after leaving the safety of your village you’ll need to find a Milestone. These mysterious stones light up and hold the wyrdness at bay, runes are inscribed into them. Some say that Merlin invented the runes, while others believe they hold a darker notion. If you find a Milestone you can activate it by carving your name into it, this will disperse Wyrdness around the Milestone. It will cost you One Health, if you have enough wyrdcandles then you can light one and this will increase the Milestones protective range from the Wyrdness. Once you have activated a Milestone, you’ll be able to travel between any other activated Milestone.  This will then allow you to move about and search the surrounding area without any problems. In the top right corner is a mini map which will detail the current quest path with red dots. The map is partially covered with a fog of war and will become visible as you make your way around the area. Also, on the map you’ll uncover new Milestones, Buildings, Enemy’s and Loot (Hidden Wealth and Chests).  As you make your way throughout the map, you’ll come across some enemies. You will see the enemies and be able to hover your cursor over them to get some details on them. Moving towards them will instigate combat which will open the battle screen. Along the bottom centre of the screen are your cards for your current turn, on the right side of your cards is the Energy Count and End Turn. In the opposite corner are your Combat Quick Slot items and your Weapon and Armour stats. The top left corner is your Rune Ultimate status, this will increase during combat and be able to use it once its full. In the top right corner is any Passive Skills you currently have.  Tainted Grail is a turn-based and you will go first when combat starts. Each turn you’ll have cards placed in your hand from your deck. Every card has in the top left corner the Energy Cost to play that card, there is also some information on the type of card and what it does. While in combat if you hover your cursor over the enemy, you’ll gain some information on their behavior such as if they’re immune to something. Above the enemy are some Icons, these will show what their intent is to be on their next turn. Keep an eye on the icons underneath an enemy’s health bar as you can gain valuable information to help you towards victory. Upon defeating the enemy you’ll have the choice to pick one of three cards to add to your deck. If you don’t fancy any of the cards you can skip the process and gain some gold instead. You will also get the chance to choose one of three new Passive Skills and again should you wish to skip a new passive skill then you’ll gain some gold. You will also gain some Experience Points, Gold and may be some random items to help you on your quest. You will come across some characters who you can interact with and maybe they’ll join you in your village. These characters will take over one of the ruined buildings, although they will require some resources to rebuild them.  When you die and you will die, your game stats will be displayed, Total Wealth Gained, Total Wyrdshards Gained, Total Damage Dealt, Enemies Killed, Rounds Fought and Total Cards Played. You will then have the options to carry on or to quit. If you carry on you will find yourself back in your village, you will have lost any items you had collected before dying. However, any character who you have added to your village will still be there as would any pathways you may have unlocked. If you decide not to carry on then you’ll lose any characters or pathways unlocked and start from scratch. The Campaign Mode takes place in Cuanacht, the Wyrdness is closing in around the city. You will have to complete quests and protect Cuanacht. You will have the choice of playing as two characters, although currently they play the same. The campaign story hasn’t been completed yet; you can play for a few hours currently. After which you may find some bugs, unfinished work and story. The game is in Early Access and they plan to have the campaign completed when the game comes out of early access. Positives + Fantastic graphics + Good story so far + Two game modes  + Choices matter Negatives - No achievements currently - No cards currently The Wyrdness is spreading across the land, soon it will envelope everything unless you find a way to push back the Wyrdness and save everyone. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Once again I am hunting for a great roguelite deckbuilder and this one came across my eye. My first impression was that it's very grotesque and gory, but after a few runs, you get used to it and there's a fun game in all this dreariness.The story starts with your village getting destroyed but then upon you dying, you return to life but notice that time seems to be stopped or stuck in place. There's this strange stuff known as the Wyrdness that you are stuck in. People don't seem to notice that time has stopped and strange things are happening. In order to break out of this nonsense you have to defeat guardians, save people who have things they need to get done, and bring some of them back safely to your village. Can you break free of this cycle?As stated before, the game is very gory and grotesque. It takes some getting used to, but it fits the theme and setting of the game. You start off as one class and slowly unlock more as you play more and more runs. Just like other roguelite deckbuilders, don't expect to get crazy far on your first few runs. Once you level up and unlock new cards and classes, then the fun really begins.Each class has their own special cards and an ultimate ability. They each gain charges for the ultimate in different way. Some gain it by dealing damage, some get it by taking damage, etc. It's important to figure out the gimmick of each one so you can maximize their effectiveness and know what cards to add to your deck. Some classes are definitely more easier to play than others. Some take awhile before they get stronger and more viable like the Summoner class. It's nice that there is variety to keep you on your toes to increase the replayability.If I can be completely honest however, I think what kept me hooked on this game was the storytelling and the worldbuilding. Throughout the game you will run into a lot of characters. Some will join you in your village so you can buy permanent upgrades to your character. Others will usually have a side quest for you to do to help them live out their lives in the Wyrdness, or escape it. A lot of the stories were really nice and kept me wanting to replay runs so I could see how the individual stories ended.I unfortunately do have some gripes with the game. The map movement outside of combat was a lil clunky and really hard to see if you don't have the Wyrd candles to help you see better. I wish it had just some fog of war or something, but be mindful that it may strain your eyes a bit when you are exploring without the candle. While there are many classes to choose from, the majority of them are just "echo fighters". They are copies of another class just with a slight variation. Like one fighter class works by you dealing damage, while another fighter class is the same thing, except it works by you blocking and not getting hit. Only some of the cards and the passive abilities change so it makes the gameplay sorta stale after awhile. Lastly, there is a lot of stuff you have to get to get the "true ending" to the game. Unfortunately due to how same-y the game feels after a couple of runs, I didn't have the urge to push for the true ending anymore, but I did save a lot of villagers and completed a ton of runs before I stopped.Final verdict? This was a super fun deckbuilder game. Despite the gameplay growing stale after awhile, the story and good writing kept me hooked for a lil longer. The aesthetic takes some getting used to at first but it's worth it for the fun combos and overall package you're getting. I think the asking price of 20 is fair for the amount of gameplay you get for this game, but if you're on the fence, getting it on sale is just as good. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! As a long time rpg fan, I only recently discovered I like the "roguelike deckbuilder" formula a lot, and it was the excellent Slay the Spire that got me the message.Tainted Grail is by no means inferior, on the contrary I find it far more charming, deeper and richer.I never played the early access (I prefer playing games only post release) so I started directly from 1.0. The game has a diablo-esque atmosphere peppered with Witcher-y and Lovecraftian elements, with some Gothic roughness thrown in.The game boasts a ton of classes (9!) divided into 3 archetypes (warriors, rangers and summoning-focused mages), with each sub-class covering a specific variety of playstyle.I'm not going to spoil much about the lore, the classes etc. because part of the charm of the game is the joy of discoverying bits and pieces by yourself in a cyclic journey of challenging unearthly horrors (my only advice: if you unlock a class but it seems clunky and hard after trying it out, go watch 1 or 2 video guides about it, you'll be surprised...).The game flow is divided among these things:- the chosen class gives you a certain preferred playstyle and potential to grow;- the (upgradable) hub is used to rest and recuperate and to strategize about how to spend your limited resources according to your situation;- the nonlinear dungeons alternate between combat encounters and events/exploration, where you'll spill blood and make obscure decisions about all the many NPC you'll encounter;- the combat relies on a bit of luck (which cards are selected from your deck and what card upgrades you'll be rewarded with) and a lot of strategy, there are MANY ways to tackle situations by combining enemy patterns (all attacks are telegraphed to allow strategy), cards of various types, passives, consumable items, permanent upgrades, helpers, runes, crafting, barriers, armor, summons, etc.- there is no "stress" in building your deck because A) you can continously get new cards and everything can work all right (but you can also limit your deck and discard cards if you want) and B) you will accumulate a ton of passive abilities that will shape the way you play your cards, and as far as I know there is no upper limit, as many as you can get.Really, if you like a dark atmosphere and are remotely intersted in deck building rpgs (there are so few of them yet!), THIS gem you just cannot miss!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I am on the borderline between recommending this game and not, don’t get it wrong, it is a decent deck-builder but compared to something like Slay the Spire, it feels off.First of all, there is the grind. The whole game revolves around the cycle: start a new game -> get as far as possible -> collect resources during your run -> use them to unlock perma bonuses -> die and start another game. Process is the standard rouge-lite but this can take a lot of time, especially if you wana try all the classes, because the more you level one of them, the more you will get stronger cards for that class. There are 9 in total so either stick and level up one of them, or take your time with multiple or all of them. By this point you might see where boredom starts building up, starting runs with the same class, over and over again, just to get some bland upgrade for it. Die and repeat.Speaking of the perma upgrades (which are shared between all runs and classes) you buy with the resources you gather; I have to say, they are too bland. You get stuff like +1 to attack/defense, extra slots for runes (which I found the most useful), a few bonuses for consumables and some other minor passives, that’s about it… Well, since it mentions that is also an RPG; I gotta speak a bit about that. There is a level up system which gives you the choice to pick a passive, there is also up to 6 runes (3 for weapon and 3 for armor), you need to unlock slots for them (you start with 1 for each) and (depending on the rune you equip) they provide the best bonuses. AND that’s it! That is the whole RPG elements you will get; no skill tree, no weapon/armor you can equip (you get some consumables though), nothing you got used to from other RPGs. Even StS has those relics you can get, BUT is not labeling itself as an RPG.Anyway, a positive, what keeps the reruns fresh is the story, every time you make progress you unlock all kinds of NPCs or events which help growing your small town, you also get to complete different quests and quests chains which lead up to saving those NPCs as well as others you run into.Another positive is the atmosphere, it builds a dark fantasy setting very well. Ohh and you can customize your character.In the end, the game is decent enough to give it a try but get ready to grind off your class and those bonuses. And if you do not get bored in 2-3 runs with the same class, and actually do not mind the grind then all the power to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Tainted Grail is a lot of fun. There are a whopping 9 characters and the metaprogression is very rewarding. It is difficult at first, but once you figure out how to use each character properly, it is incredibly satisfying. The intriguing story and immersive graphics make it easy to sink a lot of time in the game. I highly recommend the game for players who enjoy deckbuilders. The cards and synergies are pretty awesome, but difficult to master. For beginners, this game might get a little overwhelming because the simple block and attack mechanics are much weaker if you don't build the synergies well. The game punishes you, even early on, for not utilizing the character's full kit. The first character, in my experience, is actually very difficult to use when compared to some of the others. Still, if you stick with it and follow along with the game, the metaprogression will do a ton to make the game easier. You just have to find the right NPCs. In conclusion, Tainted Grail is a challenging and intense deckbuilder with many fun and unique characters that grant the game lots of replayability. Difficult for beginners but awesome for deckbuilding veterans. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: You died and then spawned in another dimension. The goal is to find and save all the missing villagers to rebuild the village and figure out how to save Avalon from the curse of Wyrdness. During the journey there are many random encounters that either help or harm you. Every character has a little background and story to tell, most of the dialogues have a deep meaning and the voice acting is top notch considering this is an indie game. I also love the dark fantasy/ gothic atmosphere, it is definitely one of the things that pulled me into the game and kept me playing. The soundtrack contributes to that a lot as well.Though Tainted Grail is a card game, it actually plays like a typical turn based RPG game. You can move in an open world area and choose which fights to do, in the order you want to do them. Skipping fights is also an option. The character can level up, use consumables and his stats have an impact in fights. Attacks, buffs and summons are played by using cards. I like the variety of classes and their designs, there is also a bit of character customization. As someone who isn't that good at card games, I'd say that the RNG is perfectly balanced and well thought out. Most tough fights are a fair challenge as long as you figure out some of the hidden gameplay mechanics. The procedural generated levels and events make it a bit immersive too.

_childDocuments_.review: Death slough with reskined same-ish champs.Three main stays of the classeswarrior, archer and magic user. each has flaw(s) and a theoretical way to be played.warrior: cards can hit hard. Best built class towards new players. Stack Hp buffs and Buy potions. Put up with the death and get to bezerker, I had fun with the life drain it does fall off as overkill doesn't always give you the full Hp refill.Archers: death by 1000 cuts, this archetype felt so action-to-damage starved. Plenty to do, nothing getting done. I suggest aiming your build toward on kill effects or towards stacking buffs and using free arrows. The lack of actions in the early game severely hampers set up builds.magic user: you summon stuff and it fights/blocks/buffs/debuffs for you in one of three styles and requires you to manage the creatures with your action pool. Skulls and concentration oil are your friends. The necromancer felt the most fun, the druid did better against bosses and legends.The Stagfather is a D*ck and hold onto your candles, using them before you go into fight can help change battle in your favor.Over-all this isn't a game meant to be fun. It is a patience test in disguise. Some heroes have no early game viability but to get their stride you need to survive to late game or die multiple times, I suggest the later, just kill the first three battles and die, repeat till the cool and better abilities are unlocked and hope they appear in the current run. (the worst offenders being the way-finder, apostate and druid). The action/energy pool you get is best described as stingy and makes you choose between damage and set up, often rewarding neither skill, memory or ability, only dumb Rng card luck and overwhelming cheese.bosses are huge health pools that do allot of damage. most summon brutes or defenders to Debuff you. champs without a hard punch attack or an adequate action/expenditure scheme will find themselves struggling,The Npcs are best ignored, they're supposed to help you make your deck stronger or allow you to use items. I think the idea was there, however the currency exchange system is paced very slowly and requires hard grinding for little reward.perseverance, a good guide and the willingness to cheese everything without shame is needed to enjoy this game.4/10 will update as I play more,Current boss 3/?8/no/1-13

_childDocuments_.review: Best game I've played in a while.  If you're a fan of rogue lite's, I feel confident saying you'll love this one.I'm not normally into card games, usually playing more strategy/crafting/exploration stuff.  Surprisingly, this has most of those elements.  The rune process is super basic crafting, but the gameplay is highly strategic, both in the way you play cards and build your deck, as well as how you explore the world.  The meta-game unlocked after each play-through is remarkably deep and unfolds both gameplay elements and story that are each exceptional.  If I had one criticism it's that it doesn't feel super balanced.  But given the variety of characters and the huge variability in which they can each be played, it's not surprising that some avenues feel a tad OP.  To that end I would suggest playing it soon, before the internet broadcasts all the min/max guides, although it stands to reason the balance will be improved with time as well.Overall, even in it's current state, I'd rate this one 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Tainted Grail: Conquest, where Death isn't the end, rather, he's your boss!Tasked with punching, gouging, clawing and biting whatever goes bump in the night, lurks in the shadows, and bursts out of the mist born from your darkest fears, Death sends you on your merry way to gain the strength you need to be a reliable pawn in his little chess game.  Your only refuge from the fighting is your village, which you will slowly upgrade as you unlock new NPCs and bring them what they need to help you on your way.  As for the rest of the world?  It's constantly changing, warping and twisting.  Outside of the safety your village provides, only truly powerful beings will remember you even exist, if they can be bothered to remember you at all!Each of my runs tends to last about an hour and a half.  You can save and quit at any point to come back when you have more time, so you don't have to do it all in one sitting.  As you fight enemies and explore the world, you'll gain access to level-up rewards, event encounters and loot.  Things like adding/removing cards to your deck, gaining passive skills, asking the Gods for power, etc.  Use whatever you can to help build your character up from your basic starting point.  With 9 unique classes to pick from across 3 archetypes, there's a ton of versatility in playstyle to grab anyone's attention.I can't end this review without mentioning the music though!  Absolutely love it!  I'm waiting to see if a full OST will be released here, or if I'll have to pick up the main album used in this game off of Amazon later!

_childDocuments_.review: Am I enjoying this game? Yes. Would I recommend it to you? No way.The combat and the deck building parts are fun. The voice acting is also good. Everything else is whatever. Out of the 9 classes available only 4 are fun. The rest are either boring as heck, underpowered, or both. Running around in 3rd person between encounters is a time consuming chore. Village upgrades are unexciting.But the worst thing is the "final boss". The "real" one. So, yes, I'll probably do enough reruns to finish the story-line. But if you're looking to experience The Flow, entering the state of seamless oneness with the game, as you had before in Slay the Spire or Monster Train, you need to look elsewhere. Tainted Grail does not have it.

_childDocuments_.review: Tainted Grail has a lot to like about it. It leans hard into a sort of Celtic mythology horror that you don't really see too much of, and unlike a lot of roguelikes, it places emphasis into the story as much as into the mechanics.Invariably a game like this ends up getting compared to Slay the Spire, so let's do that right from the off. The design isn't quite as tight as STS, however the mechanics still hold up by themselves pretty well. Graphically, it's a massive upgrade, and the atmosphere is great. Music's decent as well, and there's one boss fight track with chanting that really hammers home the brutality, danger, and mystique of the setting.I don't have any real complaints with the game, honestly. Performance is a takes a dip here and there when you kill an enemy. By hour 30 you've pretty much seen all the narrative elements, and despite it claiming that it's story-rich, there isn't actually that much to go around - but I liked what is there! The voice acting really drew me in in a sort of mysterious, almost Disco Elysium level of narration (but with Brits instead of Australians).For saying that the game is less than £16 (at time of writing), it's extremely good value for money. Like, the quality/cost ratio is very, very high. It probably won't convert anyone who doesn't like deckbuilders, but those who are at least open to them should enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Overall, this is a great game.30 hours in, it's time for the review:This is a roguelike deckbuilder. If you played slay the spire, this is exactly the same kind of game, but with lots of cool new ideas.The visuals are not what I would expect for a game in this genre. Roguelike deckbuilders usually have simple or cartoonish graphics, but Tainted Grail decided to go for a darker setting. Yet, this game is beautiful to watch.Each of the three factions feels incredibly unique, and the subclasses are also very distinct. I feel like this game will take hundreds of hours to master.I've encountered a visual bugs and one gameplay one. Nothing major that I couldn't resolve by restarting the game.Difficulty-wise, the game relies on ascencion leves, i.e., every time you beat the game in a difficulty level, you unlock the next one. The game suddenly got really punishing at difficulty 5, though it might get a lot easier when I unlock more NPCs, which I intend to do at difficulty 4 for a couple runs before venturing into difficulty 5 again.

_childDocuments_.review: The people who cooked up this game clearly tried to merge: 1. Dark Souls (all of ‘em), 2. Slay the Spire, and 3. Diablo (all of ‘em) into a single game.  It kind of works, better than expected, but the end results are simply not as good as Slay the Spire or any of the Dark Souls games – to its credit it does play better than the Diablos IMHO but that is the least of those games by far.  If you ever wanted to play Dark Souls as a shorter “time loop” deck builder ala Slay the Spire, this is probably going to be the best offering in that mixed genre for quite some time.In terms of the story and the setting, I feel it is a little overbaked and overwritten especially the dialogue.  Tainted Grail wants to be Dark Souls, but both Dark Souls and even Slay the Spire know how to “say more by saying less;” too much bumbly dialogue and needless backstory is more of a burden then an immersion factor.  That said the goat who helps orient you is generally done very well, which is important as especially at the beginning you get a lot of him.  One significant and repeated writing failure:  multiple times for no discernable reason or motivation is frankly terrible.  One could counterargue that this game really doesn’t need plot at all to work and be fun, and I would agree, but if one then bothers to put plot in it is going to be judged, and if it is bad it just shouldn’t have been put in.  The intro and setup are good, but the major twists from there are just random and unexplained in a way that only 12 year olds and certain Hollywood writers that have failed-upwards think is acceptable writing.Tainted Grail’s devotion to maximizing “grim dark” occasionally moves into a slightly cringy “trying too hard” category.  That said the art is really good IMHO and successfully fulfills their “Grim Dark” aspirations. This goes for the music too, though there is one legendary boss track with angry chanting that definitely has moments in the “trying too hard” category and was occasionally cracking me up as a result.I have an army of little nitpicks, but I’ll just mention the bigger ones.  First it is pretty easy to get enough cards in hand that the cards cover your energy counter which can really ruin things at the most critical of moments.   Second wandering around in the world on silly little hard-to-see jaunts between encounters is clearly a step back from the clean concise “move directly to the next accessible point of interest” from Slay the Spire that they are copying.  It feels like the developers of Tainted Grail were starting with but trying to improve on the “Slay the Spire” paradigm there, but their approach actually makes the world feel smaller than it would via a “Slay the Spire” world traversal approach if done properly, and their approach also slows down the pace of the game as the action and interaction are now broken up with what feel like janky, awkward, slightly-slow walking interludes.  Walking around in the mostly static tiny-feeling world has such a different feel from the rest of the game that it really is a bit of a set-back to the immersion and aspirations.My whining and nitpicking aside, overall Tainted Grail is definitely fun, interesting, and well produced; the strategy and play I find immensely satisfying with very high replay value.  I had to play it for a while before I fully appreciated the richness of diversity across the full range of different class play styles – it is one of the few areas where this game has actually beaten Slay the Spire in design at its own game and this is quite commendable and key to its replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best games I have played in years. Not an expression. Been a lot of games over the last few that I thought, "That looks good!" - and it was meh. OR "that has potential, I will give it a try" - refunded. This game came out of nowhere. Wasn't even on my radar really, and it's been great so far. Combat: Satisfying. You use cards, but feels way more strategic than most of these card battlers. Also, you have so many classes that you can play however you want. Which spices things up quite a bit. Graphics: Dark, gloomy. Some will like it, some won't. However they aren't cartooney or pixelated. So if you are looking for something that looks modern...here you go. Sound: Music is great. Voice acting is well above average. Writing is okay. You can get into it, but if you want to skip over and just keep playing...I feel as if you don't miss anything important. I don't really have anything too negative to say, except I want a fullscreen mode instead of borderless windowed. Definitely worth the price if this is your kind of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very very good game! Deckbuilder and Turn based strategy lovers should play this game.A dark fantasy game with lots of different stories, characters and choices. Highly addictive, joyful an suprising. There are total 9 specialized heroes in 3 main classes which gives you 9 different experience and strategy. Moreover, a complex strategy is created with Passive Abilities, Cards, Runestones, Items, Enemies, Upgrades, Trades, Randomness, Wyrdness and damage ranges. Every moment you should make a choice considering also future events. Furthermore, game has not only high replayability but also necessity to play again to unlock tons of new items, abilities and cards. When you die and you start another campaign with all your previous upgrades and story continue where you left. In addition, game increase the level of difficulty according to your accomplisments to give you a balanced experience. You can also manually change the difficulty.The philosophical and psychological content of the stories and structure of the new world is very good. Dark humor and jokes are fun. Sounds and musics are very good. Suprisingly first class game. One of the best game in this genre is Slay the Spire (2017). I think the developers enhanced it and made us a very solid game. _childDocuments_.review: This game shows a lot of promise and as a Finished product this game could really push the single player deck building Genre,as of posting here are Pros and Cons with the game.Positives:. The Game Has a Town building Aspect to it which is its rogue lite element. Unlocking New armour, Weapons, trinkets and skills will help you overcome the odds and carries on through to your next playthrough.. The branching paths in the areas of the game so far is littered with events, characters for your Town and enemies Both Weak and strong. its pretty unique for a single player deck builder, giving quite a lot a room for strategy between building your deck, tackling groups of enemies in a particular order and interacting with events.. There is a Torch mechanic in this game, Fighting enemies in the wyrdness as they call it, means you will take more damage but you get more rewards or fight in the light to make the fight easier.. Multiple events and characters have been fleshed out with some good voice acting and the dialogue is well written.. The Deck building element (For the warrior) was great, an assortment of different blocks, Debuffs, attacks and talents with room for variety of different types of decks.. The enemy difficulty seems very balanced with room to make the game even harder hopefully in a possible ascension mode not yet available as of this review.. Replayability at the moment there is just the Warrior with 3 different sub classes to choose from with a promise of more Characters available down the later.Negatives:. The thing that hurts this game the most is the Music, especially the battle music at the moment it is the same track for all regular enemies and it sounds very dull and monotone.. The enemy models could be better, they're not terrible but certainly not great.. At the moment most of your skills when cast look the same, no special effects or different animations for some of the better moves you have acquired.. Enemies could have more varied debuffs and buffs for the most part they either give their allies a barrier or try to flood your deck with useless cards.. Consumables such as potions and damage battle buffs seem to acquired too easily in the current build and i wish they were more scarce.. Content:  Obviously with this being early access, between the campaign and endless mode There quite a bit of stuff missing. I would say currently there is at least 15 to 25 hours of content.with the right improvements this game could be something really special. I have never seen so many different elements thrown into a single player deck builder, between the gold, character gear, consumables, area exploration, town improvement and interactive events there so much strategy to this game.Hopefully with enough love and attention to detail this game could be one the greats in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me for a surprise. The narrative and the voice acting gives life to the world and brings an overall great deck building and roguelite experience.Initially, I didn't like the flow and progress of the game; however, game's mechanics grew after the first three or four runs. 9 classes to pick from that unlock over progress, each with their own card base. Difficulty choices increase as you clear each run. You eventually unlock an additional boss near the end, which is a comparison of damage in leaderboard score. Lots of replay value  for the small purchase price. I've played 30 hours at time of review and still have not completed the game's main story -- involving the saving of all villagers from the corruption (wydrness described in game).If you like deck building card games with some strategy, this game offers that and then some. Good pickup for single player enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering this is in early access its looking very polished and stable. Runs smoothly on my 5 year old machine and I have experienced no technical issues with the game. There are two versions of the game to choose from at startup but I have only been playing the "rogue like" Conquest version of the game because I have found it so addictive. It involves overhead third person  exploration of the Wyrdness where you are balancing your survival resources to judge how far you travel to try to recruit useful people to improve your village or meet other situations and make choices that effect how the game plays out.  Enemy battles are played out with a card based, deck building mechanic - this seems a bit simplistic at first but once you start coming up against tougher opponents you realise that it has lot of tactical depth to it. Its also very atmospheric with quality voice acting and beautiful artwork setting just the right tone for immersion, Its early access, so there is plenty more to come and I am really looking forward to how its develops through to the finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I suck at reviewing things and I know I won't do this game justice, but if you liked Slay The Spire & old school RPGs then you need to try this. Sprinkle in some early Diablo vibes from the dark ambience and some of the music and you've got yourself a hell of a nice game. Plenty of cards, plenty of characters, but most importantly, everything is polished and immersive (in my opinion, anyway). The world feels more real than it should. I don't know how to explain it. I don't want to spoil any surprises, but interactions that you take for granted may suddenly become entirely different as you progress. Some developments may also be in part because I'm playing as a different faction but the world definitely feels alive in its own strange realm. Looks to me like there's a significant amount of content that's saved for after the first "Loop" and that isn't readily visible in the journal (like events / npc storylines etc).Just play it, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels extremely janky overall which never allows you to get into a flow state, you are constantly fighting the camera, its strange torchlight system or looking at the weird map layout. As many other reviews have stated this game should really have been 2D like most deckbuilders, because combat is great but outside combat is HORRIBLE.Deckbuilders have this ability to make time fly, but this never gets there because you are constantly fighting the game, the aesthetic is also terribly bland, its basically Grim Dark shorthand mixed with Unity asset-tier 3d models that just feels like it has zero originality. The Quest system also adds nothing because each run is random, there is no continuity or stakes because you might not see a character for awhile, meaning its just a bunch of fetch quests.The story starts of strong but then basically becomes background noise to wandering around in the dark and dying to samey encounters. The balance also doesn't feel well calibrated, your character goes from a weak pushover to a juggernaut as soon as your build comes together without any stages in-between, this feels really janky and more like you are exploiting the combat system instead of developing your character and winning through strategy or tactics.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: A great deckbuilder with some great ideas, very straightforward if you played a deckbuilder before and an overall great time waster. A few issues keep it from the being among the greats though.Classes are overall boring and very similar. The mages all summon things, the archers rapid fire things, the melees all hit like trucks. Maybe your mileage will vary, but i found the first class to be the most consistent and quickest to win with. It seems the other classes reward long drawn out fights, while the Wyrd hunter is just gogogogogo.Despite being a roguelike, it doesnt "feel" roguelikey. Cards are very similar in design regardless of class, and events get stale quick. The side missions are neat, but its not like you need to do anything special to complete them, just play and the occasional progression with a decent reward at the end.Overall though, fun game. The lore is VERY interesting to me, and the story takes a neat turn after the first completed run. $20 is fair, and they seem to be expanding on the Wyrdness with an FPS game in early access currently. Only thing i actually want is workshop support, considering the animations are so limited and the exploration ripe with possibles, workshop support should have been a priority in my opinion. Missed opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with deep conversations that take place in a dark distorted arthurian reality, Tainted Grail is an amazing card game for player who like psychological atmospheres that make the characters question their own existence. _childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Really glad I stumbled upon this one! Engaging (albeit lofty) plot, the classes are diverse enough to warrant thorough exploration of each of their builds (really lending to the infinite replayability its roguelite-ness provides), gorgeous setting, interesting characters and mobs, and I love the map exploration aspect of going from encounter to encounter. It was a breath of fresh air in this nascent but heavily congested genre to not click a room on a map to progress, but instead you chart the most efficient course to make fullest use of your candles. Plenty of unique aspects that you can invest into and grow stronger, like the card drafting feeling runestone system and the mastery trees as you level up.And there's a doggo you can pet. Highly recommend, some of the most fun roguelite action I've played lately!

_childDocuments_.review: Tainted Grail: Conquest is honestly one of the best deck builders Ive played in a long time. Aside from the actual card-play, which is fantastic, the meta-progression is engaging and impactful, on par with some of the best Rogue-likes to date as well. Each run you feel more powerful, and fall deeper into the world as you meet with NPCs and further their questlines, similar to a Hades style progression. Its got a horror-fantasy feel that I immediately fell in love with. The art, music, and voice acting all comes together beautifully. The in-between fights sections feel like there could have been a bit more, but with the amount of content here Im really not complaining.There are 9 different classes to play, from 3 different factions, and they all feel totally unique and powerful in their own way, each with their own set of Passives, Masteries and Ultimates. The difficulty feels appropriate, and scales well as the content evolves with NGs. I absolutely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys deck builders, Rogue-likes or just fantasy in general as the atmosphere is really spot on. Excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: After 23 of ingame playtime on this game, I will list the pros and cons.Pros: Amazing story with a bunch of voice acting added in!Multiple different stories with different options.A repeat gameplay that changes with each time you die or kill the final boss. Great class system that has a bunch of uniqueness and game style. Difficulty determines rewards and xp bonus. The more runs the more likely you will receive loot drops from upgrades and difficulty. I love the darkness/gothic theme through out the whole story line. Gameplay is smooth and unforgiving.Cons:\Some build are just absolutely silly, doing about 10k+ a turn. The grind of repeating events will eventually ware on you and make you question why it's stuck in a constant loop. Defeating the final boss doesn't really feel like a challenge at the very end and was a let down for me. Some of the content may put people off with how dark it gets.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I usually don't like "slow" rogue-likes that takes too long to complete a run. This one certainly does but the biggest reason for that is that it has a lot of storytelling to do. The world of this game is quite nice, some kind of mad afterlife where all kind of monstrosities exist and I enjoy listening to all the voice-acting that brings this world to life.On the gameplay side, this is a very good deckbuilder. There are 3 main factions with different set of cards. And each of these have 3 playable characters for a total of 9. All 3 characters of a faction have a different ability and passive and a different set of bonus perks to pick up when leveling up. And to be honest, it's kind of impressive how unique the 3 characters of a faction are while still using the same set of cards. Every character has to be built in a unique way and has a lot of potential to grow in power through new perks and cards.My biggest pet peeve about this game is the camera in combat. Instead of being fixed in a position that allows you too see everything, you can move it around freely, and it never fits right. Zoom in and units UI will cover eachother if there are too many. Zoom out and your summons will be under your hand of cards making them hard to target.Otherwise I'm having a lot of fun with the game. It's very well made.

(Which works, it's just a pain.)  Also, the in-game documentation isn't the best.  I still have no idea what lighting the milestones does, and I've just been turning them into candles, but don't understand why I wouldn't do that.  But overall, the complaints are really minor.  I'm a big fan of the roguelike deckbuilders, and this is one of the better ones.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite fun and sometimes unforgiving rogue lite card battler.  8/10+ Nice graphics and soundtrack (3d card battler is always welcome)+ Addictive and has usual "One more run" formula+ 3 factions and each has 3 classes that play bit differently+ Grim and dark, creature design is interesting as well+ Gameplay in general is done right, there are some bugs with certain abilities etc., nothing that cannot be resolved in a patch or two. Some bugs were already resolved in last patch.+ I haven't completed the full story, but I'm very close. It's is nothing spectacular but it is interesting and fits with rogue lite mechanics quite nicely- Game has some optimization problems, I can run many games (indie or AAA) that look better and run better, this one is overusing GPU a lot and FPS can be all over the place. Devs have acknowledged this and are working on it- The Wyrdness filter/fog ruins the game if you ask me. Each biome looks more of less the same because if you don't have lit candles, whole screen will get foggy/blurry. Personally and don't find it easy on the eye.- Meta progression is slow in some aspects and in later runs doesn't really motivate you to play that much (ofc this is highly subjective)- Some classes are unbalanced, some are way too OP. Having OP class would be fine it it weren't so easy pick certain passives and cards for that same class.I have 43h clocked in per Steam, although I feel I played more. I'm starting to get bored now even though I haven't unlocked everything fully. _childDocuments_.review: Do you not have this yet? That is a mistake, quick, fix it, add to basket and check out.Why? Okay, I will attempt . . . Do you enjoy deck-building card battling roguelikes? If so, this is a standout top tier example in many respects. Variety, theme, haunting thematic visuals and audio (terrific audio!) and longevity. It can be compared to Slay the Spire, Roguebook, Griftlands and other similar games. It has some absolutely stand-out features that make it special though. These being . . . *Role Play & Village Building*A huge hook of this game is that the meta-progression from run to run is first establishing your own village and then satisfying the unique desires of the people that settle in your village. The people that settle all become vendors of some special range of bonuses and items, requiring their own special currency earned in-game in various ways. In a fantastic twist that I have not seen in any other similar game, the quest-lines for your villagers, and other non-village NPCs, carry over between runs. Some quest lines have six or more stages, and you may advance them from run to run. This does not take up any 'busy work' as  you do not need to track, and the journal provides a very effective recap.*Darkly thematic visuals and audio*I was initially irritated by the need to walk around a 3D world. It felt unnecessary and I preferred simple node-to-node movement seen in similar games. However . . . the visuals are just gosh dang gorgeous and especially when you operate *without* a Wrydcandle, meaning everything is being distorted by the in-game effect of "wyrdness". It really does upgrade the immersion factor, and the audio is a beautiful match. You absolutely have to listen to the cultist chanting and tell me it is not spooky creepy awesome!*Enormous variety and replay value*There are about a dozen character types to play and these each have a huge range of cards, and a huge range of passive abilities, and huge range of runestones that can add extra effects, and a huge number of consumables . . . .and this adds up to provide amazing variety, with lots of very viable and different styles. There is a flipside, which is that moving from one character  type to another presents an initially steep learning curve. How the heck does this one work? This really adds to the interest over time though, as it feels like playing a very different game.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid entry into the grossly overpopulated deckbuilder genre, this game manages to capture a lot of the elements of Slay the Spire, looks infinitely better graphically, and fills out a lot more design space. The runs do tend to take a bit longer than a Slay the Spire run, and the roguelite elements make the difficulty a little harder to suss out, you do gain power in between runs, but with the amount of classes, several of which have multiple passives to choose from at the start, you'll definitely be able to find a LOT of depth here.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So let me begin this with a disclaimer.I break every game I touch. Eventually.This one broke super fast. My runs end because I let them.So.. the game is beautifully made, in the sense that the ambient horror and gore of the blastest environment conveys a real sense of "well this places is ****ed." from the very begining.The music that accompanies it could only be described as a deep and primal mix of chants and percussives of both metalic and organic nature.Choices have consequences, as they should, and those may or may not be to your detriment.Healing is.. something you have to aquire and regulate carefully until you are able to aquire a modicum of minor healing through passives or actives.Several of the mechanics given to you can absolutely turn the tide of a battle, one way or the other. I accidentally saved the first boss from me and was murdered as punishment.The voice acting is entertaining in it's own regard and the lore, along with it, together create a superb compliment to the visual panorama of gore and despair.Defer back to my disclaimer.This game is, in my experience, one that is punishing only if you fail to turn yourself into a raid boss through deck building, passive selection, and intelligent slotting of runes.10/10 - would recommend. sterling example of the deck-building rogue-lite genre. Got during summer sale, but, in hindsight, would totally buy at full price knowing now what it is. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for awhile. The game seems unfinished. Almost 2 years after release and you can still talk to guarded NPCs without first fighting the enemy by staying just outside the aggro radius. Needless to say, getting benefits from NPCs without risking anything destroys the balance of the game and should be avoided unless you want easy wins. And speaking of balance, the devs aimed too high with the number of classes. Sure, there are lots of characters to play, and some of them are really interesting, but some cards are absurd, while others are laughably bad. If you make a mistake and pick a bad card, you're pretty much stuck with it because card removals are very rare. There might be an argument that some cards could be good if there was more enemy diversity. Seems like every fight goes pretty much the same, and there aren't really any enemies that punish turtle builds so you can just stack defense which leads to very boring gameplay if you want to win. Will I play more in the future? Maybe, but there are better roguelikes more deserving of my time right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Filled with magnificent artwork and story telling, but unfortunately hampered by an atrocious graphics engine, poor balancing, and thematic inbreeding.Balance is all over the place depending on class and enemies you encounter. Some enemies will be significantly tougher for some classes to what feels like a plain unfair extent. The same goes for bosses. This does not seem to be an explicit design decision rather than an implicit one by having a few too many classes.The graphics engine feels outdated, choppy, and unnecessary. This can largely be ignored, but those cool 3d-models for enemies sort of fall apart when the animations look cheap, and the different classes look too samey. In this case, simpler would definitely have been better.The thematic overlap between classes is too apparent. While the three summoners have a different behavior at their core, and different playstyles, it feels cheap when you essentially get the red/green/blue flavor of the same class. Time could have been spent adding depth instead of breadth. This would probably also make balancing easier.However, in spite of all my complaints, you'll probably enjoy this game if you can look past the issues described! If you think you can't I'd suggest spending your time/money on Slay the Spire/Monster Train/Banners of Ruin/Griftlands instead.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - if you like card battlers, dark and moody atmosphere, and enjoy brutal combat, worth the purchase; even if you don't solid 8/10 game.Dark, gothic atmosphere - although heavily viking / Norse / druidic influenced - and visceral, card based battles. There are plenty of classes to unlock, including cards, as is typical of the genre. Less typical of the genre is a persistent character you create that walks around the game world, complete with unlockable cosmetics.You will gain levels if you win fights, and this earns additional cards - although you may decline to take them - and every few levels you gain a new passive. Some of the passives are weaker than others, of course, but nearly all of them enable or enhance your playstyles. There are also of course events around the map that can harm or help you.There's also a village where NPCs you've saved end up living. They will help you in your quest, ranging from a blacksmith who sells runes (items slotted into your weapon or armor that add a bonus), to a ghost who gambles with you.On the note of armor and weapon - these are static. Whatever your character uses, say a staff if you're a necromancer, that's all you ever have. The runes are what change your weapon or armor bonuses throughout play.You will die or complete a run, and like most in this genre, you lose your deck, nearly all items, and most progress. What remains are unlockables, saved villagers, and certain event rewards (e.g. a flute you can earn if you play an encounter the right way stays with you forever between runs).Overall the gameplay is quite fun. Issues at present primarily are around balance. Some of the classes are, imo, far too weak to bother playing (looking at most of the archers and wizards). Some of the enemies are abnormally strong given either other enemies in that act, or the act itself. Also some fights feel far too lopsided as certain classes (e.g. a heavily AoE fight with any of the characters who have no AoE at all, and no, "deal 3 damage to 3 random enemies" doesn't count as AoE).If you enjoy Slay the Spire, Griftlands, or any other card battler, this is an easy purchase. If you don't, or you are turned off by potentially brutal difficulty, avoid this one.

Summoners with the exact same summons only reskinned, attack animations recycled, and the sheer draw this damn game has on my cpu despite looking like someone took Path of Exile and zoomed all the way in on low settings is hillarious.Despite having "300 abilities!" I saw them loop but of a different color in each class I unlocked. Oh here is a "New ability" just like the old one only BLUE!!! Like 5% minion damage every card played working for both the Summoner and Blood Mage which is EXACTLY THE SAME F*CKING CLASS ONLY THE BLOOD MAGE SACRIFICES ITS HP AND IS FAR WORSE! AND NO YOU CANNOT "Upgrade" YOUR CLASS. ITS BY LEVELING BY KILLING THINGS. NO POINTS INTO STATS...NOTHING...RPG MY A-S-S.In some sick way I can say this could fall under false advertising but I don't know since they could stretch "300 unique passives" to be whatever the hell they mean by unique as in "You only get this ability on this class because its the blue one! The green one on the other class does the same but you can't get them both!"If you play the game you will stick to summoner because it's broken and the first class is so terrible it can't even make it to the second level 80% of the time out of sheer crap mediocre damage cards with essentially 0 defense because 1 block means NOTHING when you fight 3 enemies half the time. And sure you can even walk around the enemies to talk to the NPC's in the game but THAT SHOULDN'T BE A THING!!And the unlocks like the vendor giving better trinkets? I doubt I could unlock them all in under 400 hours and thats not like 1 unlock per hour...Thats ONE 1/100 MATERIALS NEEDED TO UPGRADE ONE NODULE THAT CAN MAAAAAYBE DROP WITH RNG ONCE PER RUN IF YOU DON'T GET KILLED BY CARDS SCREWING YOU OVER!Oh and a 68-80 HP pool in a game where the second level enemies hit for 27-377 which I saw hit a golem of mine is utterly ridiculous.This screams cashgrab and it sure did mine *unless steam gives me my refund which it probably wont*. _childDocuments_.review: So I'm a total novice in this genre and don't really have any similar games to compare it to, but I've played TCG games like Hearthstone and MTG Arena. What attracted me to the game was honestly the screenshots and the way other reviews described the atmosphere - and honestly they were spot on. The game has a very mature atmosphere (and by that I mean it features existential horror, dark myths and general creepiness - not porn) and some sick music that repeats often but never feels repetitive. For art style think of a mix between Diablo 1/2 and Warhammer Chaos with some Dark Ages mythos thrown in (witches and wendigos et al) and for the music there is a very strong resemblance to the Witcher 3 in tone and choice of instruments - and that's a good thing. Story seems like it should be good although I'm a little early on to really say, thinks are fairly vague at this point but all the characters you meet are definitely.... interesting, and the game gives you plenty of sidequests and permanent resources to progress so you probably never have a run that felt like a total waste of time.As for the deckbuilding part, I have no other games to compare it to, but I like it. Some classes definitely feel more powerful than others but it will also depend on your personal tastes. Some classes like the Wyrdhunter (the starting class) are sort of "OTK" heroes where you will spend several turns just sustaining yourself until you fill up your ultimate meter and draw the perfect hand to go in for the kill with massive damage, other classes are summoners where you progressively increase your board presence whilst keeping yourself shielded until you overwhelm your enemies, and other classes use bows (I have one unlocked but I have yet to play it). There's still a bunch of classes and NPCs and cards I haven't discovered yet, but as someone who got the game on a whim for the story and setting, that's what will probably keep me coming back. So far I have zero regrets about my purchase and there is a good amount of polish here for the price (all lines are voiced and pretty well too for the most part, artwork and visual style are top notch). Good job devs. If you are a fan of the genre and the setting appeals to you, I imagine you can't go wrong with this one, and even if - like me - you have no previous interest in the genre, you might still love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most underrated rogue-lights I've ever played. Awesome soundtrack, great gameplay, a surprising amount of quality lore and good replayabilty with a lot of unlocks. Each class plays very differently across 3 archetypes. This game deserves more attention, don't miss it if you enjoy games like Slay the Spire or Monster Train.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been on my wish list for a while and I finally gave in and bought it. I was not prepared for how much I was going to fall in love with this game. For being early access, it shows soo much promise for much more to come. All the current characters available have different play styles that let you tailor different builds for them, making every play through different from your last. There is some limited character customization but it looks like they'll be adding more to it in the future; but overall it is still nice. They reward you with more cosmetics to tailor your character's appearance to your liking. Overall, a solid 9/10 right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Refreshing and unique take on the roguelike deckbuilding genreLOTS of classes to unlock, each class feels very uniqueCombat system is very refinedUnique monsters with interesting interactionsNeutral:Survival elements that contribute to combat but during exploration just seem tacked-on. Cons:Incredibly grindy. Really needs tweaking/re-balancing of ingame currencies. Quests are interesting but 'exploration' is effectively nodal....but without the nodes, feeling overly complicated. Needlessly "souls like." Missing that "one more run" factor. So, why do I still recommend the game?  Becaus the sheer # of classes, well-refined battle system along with a unique setting a unique monsters makes the game genuinely fun imo. I just wish the currency wasn't so grindy and the game was more thematically balanced. But some people may LOVE the grind and the utter dreariness (plus I think it's worth playing even with those flaws). Long Version:Refreshing take on an overdone genre (don't get me wrong, I LOVE roguelike deckbuilders, but the quality is starting to go wayyyyy downhill).   This one, however, at least tries to do something new by giving you a gritty survival, "eldritch horror" themed deckbuilder.  No, it is not a 'horror' game, and there are no jump scares (i hate the horror genre), but the game is filled with creepy woods, graveyards, mutated forest beasts/trees, and (tbh) creative monsters that aren't your typical fantasy/tabletop rpg fantasy baddies. the deckbuilding is straightforward and refined.  The classes feel very different, which is something I always want to see, and there are MANY classes to unlock. The difficulty is brutal.  If ever there was a 'souls-like' (i hate that phrase) deck-builder. This game is it.  I actually really don't like how grindy the currency feels, tbh, and that seems to be a recurring theme. Also, the game seems to be missing that "just one-more run!!" factor, at least for me.   Roguelikes (whether a deckbuilder, or any other subgenre) should be so fun that they allow the player to get lost in them for hours.  But this game has such a grind to it that after 3-4 runs or so I'm exhausted and want a break.  Sometimes just 1-2 is all I can take. Also, thematically, the game doesn't balance the dark, eldritch horror theme well with, well, anything else really. There are no light elements, no humor, no hope in the game. it's rather dreary all around, which is kind of a downer.  Grant it, this is eldritch horror, not gothic horror,  but I do think some balancing thematically is necessary--or else why do I want to keep coming back?That said, if you want something fresh, that is well-polished, and challenging, this is your game.  This is not another "Spires clone."  No, in Tainted Grail, you will definitely sip something unique and at least fun for a while.

_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Really Good Game, a mix of RPG and Deck Building Rogue-Lite elements in a lovecraftian setting with fully voiced dialogues. Game's got a lot of memorable and enjoyable characters and the combat and deck builduing elements are pretty good. Only real complaint is that the classes aren't all that different from one another and some feel downright bad to play in my experience, will return once I got more gametime though to make a final assesment. _childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This game has several classes you can chose from with no gender lock, the story is grim and mysterious and i enjoy the combat(card battle) and the adventuring around a level to discover whats around sense its different from each run. and i dont want to spoil anything but the game does get easier once you unlock stuff and understand the flow of combat  and how the classes work But then it gets harder again once you defeat the final boss and go into new game plus where the enemies start useing more abilitys.

_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue-like done right. I typically bore of die-and-restart mechanics fairly easily, but this keeps me happily coming back. Each run you progress toward new classes which change up the abilities and strategies entirely, keeping combat fresh. The soundtrack is also wonderful, especially for the boss battles. Definitely worth the price. Only complaint I would have is the combat can became quite cheesable depending on your class/strategy, and it can make some encounters fairly easy. I beat the last 2 bosses as a Warden taking zero damage. However, this does require a good deal of strategizing, and is super satisfying when it all works out.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a MUST Purchase, -First I have not played rogue-like games I have watched slay the spire just never got around to playing it, I also Have not played the board game that this is based off-Ok with that out of the way, this game is incredible, for 19.99 it exceeds what anyone could expect of a game for that price, the voice acting, writing, story are all top notch, very entertaining characters and I rarely get into a story these days when I play a game but this is done just so expertly.the classes are fun and unique, and the combat is progressively more challenging, (certain random boss encounters) nearly lead to instant death some times.I bought the game a couple days ago and have already sunk 20+ hours and have really been enjoying the necro, zerker, and sentinal so far excited to unlock and try my characters through future runs, if you have 20 bucks laying around this is a great lil game to put on this
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the worst optimization I've seen in a game.  It's a real shame, because there is a good game in here.  This is a fun take on the Slay the Spire formula, with some good new ideas of its own.  Unfortunately it's a stuttering mess that sends cpu and gpu temps through the roof.  At launch the devs seemed like they were working on some fixes, but over the last couple months nothing has been patched except some extra language support.  When it came out I had a gtx970, and the game would run (poorly) on low/medium, but even then it was heating my system up far beyond acceptable.  Now I've upgraded to a 3070ti, and while the game does look better, it still has out of control temps and constant stuttering/frame drops.  Do not buy this unless a solid optimization patch is released.  This genre is very saturated these days;  there are plenty of other deck builder games that don't run like garbage or turn your pc into an oven.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: A good challenge that unlocks harder modes to test yourself.   It is slay the spire like.  Each game is a few hours and is around 30 fights with 4 bosses, with some mini type bosses.  What separates this from other card games?They put a lot more thought into replay-ability than any other game in this genre.  There are quests you complete that can take several runs to complete, which unlocks more things.  There are also several types of currency you collect that are saved between runs to unlock more upgrades for the vendors in your town.My biggest critiques are that there are several hero's and the base one feels way overpowered compared to the others.   Certain hero's have a very difficult time fighting certain enemies and your better off avoiding certain fights, which also means you have to memorize the head pictures of enemies so that when you walk up to the fight and it shows you their mini image you know what to expect, which is a pain to remember all of them and their abilities.Overall a fun and challenging game that is worth playing just to experience one of the most replayable games in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Unpolished, unbalanced, and unfinished. This appears to be some kind of paid beta for the real game, which they intend to release as "Tainted Grail: Fall of Avalon", at full price for people that buy this now. This, of course, is not noted on the store page. Would not have purchased if I'd known this in advance.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I really like it so far. I just completed a few runs and unlocked some characters and I can already see some interesting strategies and builds in the few classes I've used. Each class feels very unique.  The graphics/music/voice acting/world map are all very good. I would highly recommend this game if you like Slay the Spire or Monster Train.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: The stylish graphics gave me classic Diablo vibes. The gameplay is easy to grasp and interesting and the soundtrack sets a nicely foreboding atmosphere for this deck building roguelite. There are various classes to play and the many unlockable cards and skills and different game modes that bring in variation for many hours worth of gameplay.My only gripe is that some of the card descriptions are misleading. For example, while a specific class uses a "gain barrier" card for creating an additional shield of hp that remains until it's broken, another character gains this barrier ONLY for the duration of ONE round. Also, there are cards that have a flip side, but for what I can tell, there's no way of reading what says on the flip side before the card comes in play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool roguelike that is quite different from other card battlers, with how it uses the class system to introduce different combinations of cards and abilities.The mediocre mobile-game aesthetics and frankly unnecessary overworld navigation (that offers very little beyond what you get from a choose-your-next-level system) are less ideal.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I've not followed the development very closely, but a few updates ago, this game had a fun combat system that used different types of runes to combo them together, it was very novel and fresh.The game I played today is jut an imitation of Slay the Spire. It does it competently, but still feels tired and threaded. It's sad to see a game with a fun and original combat system turn itself into an unimaginative copy of another game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Tainted Grail is a great game. Game play is like Slay the Spire, Monster Train, and other card battlers. But the loop is more like Hades in that the player is building up a village, there are quests, dialog, a story, new classes to unlock, new skills and cards, and progress carries over from each run. I like the dark aesthetic and the lore, but it's the battles that make me want to do another run--that and the feeling of constant progress. I find the difficulty to be about right. Deaths come from my own mistakes, and I feel better prepared for the next run. Graphics are nice, but there is slight stuttering and choppiness with loading when going into a battle but nothing that detracts from the game. Heavy metal horns up for Tainted Grail.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are good, theme is creepy and fantastically so.  Voice acting is excellent.  Gameplay is fun.  You don't beat this game quickly.  You *will* die early and often for a few runs.  The good news is that every run unlocks additional classes, cards, and features of the game to make future runs easier.Each class also plays differently from the others in noteworthy ways.  In fact, some classes, like the Summoner and Blood Mage, superficially seem very similar but play actually significantly different from each other.  There's a lot to unpack here and it's a joy to go through the process.  :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: My first deckbuilder game and i absolutely love it. In many ways it reminds me of Dark Souls. It has nightmarish atmosphere, death being a part of the story, challenging boss battles and feeling of great accomplishment after winning, NPCs with wicked backgrounds and quests, phenomenal art style. And the music... it has to be one of the best OST in games. It pumps so much adrenaline during combat, think Witcher 3 mixed with Hellblade, simply amazing. Highly recommended even if you think you're not into this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Great roguelike deck builder that pulls you in a grim, Arthurian/Norse atmosphere with a fantastic soundtrack. Your village grows across each run which adds a nice rpg element. It's in early access, so expect a few glitches here and there. But it's clear the developers are working on it continuously - every time I login I see another fix/polish. Recommended.P.S.: It also has a short campaign (still in development). Play that first to get acquainted with certain mechanics (e.g. "wyrdness").
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Darkest Dungeon's clone. Not as good, but not horrible.The game is complex (at least complex enough), fun, atmospheric. I actually liked it slightly more than Darkest Dungeon just because I find the gameplay much more fun.Cons - the writing is a bit simplistic, the story and the writing style resembles Thea a lot, which is extremely annoying. Writing feels like "what if Thea, but in Arthurean setting." One thing about the atmospheric part, Darkest Dungeon genuinely felt like a horror game, good writing and good intro, interesting dialogues play a very important part. This game, unfortunately, lacks all of it. There are encounters with interesting dialogues, sure, but overall they aren't particular important, they barely influence the gameplay and they feel like an afterthought. Bottom line, if I were to introduce someone to the genre, I would have recommended Darkest Dungeon over Tainted Grail. It is hard not to appreciate the efforts put into this game though, and at the very least the technical implementation is not bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: I mean all I really have to say is wow. This game is an excellent combination of Deck-building, rogue-lite, and RPG...which is something I never expected to say.The mechanics are different enough from others (ie. Slay the Spire, Monster Train) to really let Tainted Grail stand out on its own and be a unique, individual game. The aesthetics are gorgeous! A lot of time went into the art for each card and each enemy.The story is very entertaining and it actually makes me want to talk to each character multiple times, and the voice acting is very well done!If you like StS or games of similar style, this is a must-have.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Very impressed with this game.  In the style of slay the spire.  My personal favorite in the genre is monster train.  I've played many others but Tainted Grail stands out.
