And sound design! And Presentation!Mechanically the game is solid but the writing takes this 10 levels beyond that!If you enjoy worldbuilding and quality cRPGs, this game is a must-have!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Decent rougelike gameplay.- Runs are mostly less that 2 hours so losing each run isn't so bad.- You can mix and match the cards from the different classes to create quite lethal combos. My favorite was using Blood Mage (with its minion auto-level ability) with cards that increase attack and auto-delevel, making a loop that can increase the minion's attack to 1K+.Cons:- The candle burning mechanic is annoying and I'm still not sure what burning the candles even does, it's never properly explained. Because of this mechanic, you are incentivized to rush from mob to mob before the candle burns out without fully taking in the world and game atmosphere etc. - Lacks replayability, probably because its so easy once you figure out the mechanics. Compared to the classics in this genre like "Ring of Pain", "Slay the Spire" or even "Monster Train", I don't feel any drive to do more runs to unlock more stuff etc. - There seems to be a story here but all I was able to grasp were mostly undertones regarding King Arthur mythology. Kinda wish there was a more coherent plot to set this game apart from other roguelites.Overall, 5/10. Not a bad game but not one I would recommend either. The aforementioned games: "Ring of Pain", "Slay the Spire" or "Monster Train" just do it much better and I would rather spend my time playing those games instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is amazing and straightforward, though it has a lot of variety it doesn't try to make it overly complex or difficult, yet it still manages to give you a challenging way of discovering how to build your deck. You might think that you will get overwhelmed by all the RPG elements and currency but that doesn't happen. Difficult-wise the game is also pretty fair, it provides a challenge for every type of player from beginners that only want to enjoy the game as a casual player and know more about the lore to higher levels of difficult for those who want to test their limits. Graphics and design are great together with the soundtrack. Fair price and provide a lot of replayability.If you enjoy card games, give this one a try and you will be surprised!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enoughThat I can overlook overflow of bugs.As the game asks you to leave review after killing first "last" boss, I can say that the game is a buggy mess, but this mess is ambitious and fun.I am not a fan of drab aesthetik - everything "sucks", black and mad. In the end you are told that we played the "bad guys" side the whole time, but it is not an exuse to have 75% of the game be "Broody black with pinch of spilled guts".The game asks you to keep playing more cycles, but I feel exausted after 2 runs.1st run ended after starting second zone, because of bug in perk interaction.You see there is a perk, that gives you +300% damage on the 1st hit of the next turn, if this turn you played 2 cards or less (on starting class). I built my character around that, and even killed 1st boss in the 1st run.After killing the boss I got to choose 1 free perk, and I choose one, that activated on the same condition, but granted +100% damage on the whole of the next turn, thinking that it will have nice synergy.Litlle did I know, that currently this perc interaction is broken, because while this perc have same counter, they count cards each on they own.So - 1 card played - 1st perc counts it and 2nd perc counts it. If I want my bonus, I can't play more than 1 card a turn, and I did not have "I win" card, so my build and run ran down the drain in 2-3 normal encounters.Second run was wih summoner, and with a bit of thinking, a lot of reading, and a lot of patience, I cleared all 3 areas and 4 bosses (and recruted bunch of NPC).In the time of 1,3 runs (7 hours by steam count), game crashed on me 3 times, while I played with minimalest grafic options possible (exept resolution - I played on 1280x720 and you can go lower).Disscussion indicate that corupting save (even auto one) is a problem you can face, some loot can dissapear, and you can softlock game if you will moove slighly not the way devs intended (as example if you tried to use more than only mouse for interactions with a game, or even tried to drag and drop reward loot, intead of clicking "take all button")Music is cool, nothing bad to say here.There are 9 classes (card packs + passives packs), and even by playing only 2, I can say that they were distinct enough, and with some variety of possible builds inside a "class".Voice acting is good, but due to desing choises of devs, it dosent make me want to explore more of this "grimderp" universe. I am not runnig to see more stuff, because I already know that I will find nothing more than more "grimderpness". There is just no humor here, and this direction is just not for me (Yes I know that comparing it with Hades is not fair, but come on, I feel like this is movie DC universe, with nothing emotionally pleasing in sight).Mechanics are fine, fun and complex, when they work as intended (see bugs).All in all could be a lot better, but ambition, that I see under the rough surface makes me want to suppot game, so I can see at least intended game as is "presented", and not as it "is".If they will make DLC, instead of fixing the damn game, or will focus all of their attention on the other game that they are making, instead of fixing this one, this will be the last game, I buy from this team.With your ambition and vision, you bought youself some wiggle space from me, lets see what will you do with this trust.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: What a surprising breath of fresh air. A game which not only feels complete thanks to the expected quality of life designs, but also shines with both quality and quantity of content. However I've only finished the game once and have yet to touch everything. The storytelling and accompanying voice acting & art really ties everything together, making the theme work and the game even be a bit immersive. Oh, also the battle music is bumpin' and goes with that grim-dark vibe. All characters I've met has been VA'd, and greatly so, bringing the characters to life, and I really want to underline how much I'm enjoying the writing - in a lot of media it is so shallow that I'm just looking at it, seeing my own reflection and feeling my wrinkles grow; in Tainted Grail the character design and dialogue is interesting and mature, and even the dialogue options given makes it feel like the Player/protagonist is naturally reacting to the situation and even put some thought into it.The game is somewhat daunting and the battles takes longer than in similar games, however the well-presented story and balanced gameplay (i.e. the power level is about where I feel it should be) sells it and keeps me going.I'm a long-time gamer that likes to spend his time either exploring interesting mechanics or experiencing great stories, and I don't want to be rude, but I'm just still so surprised over how curious and moreish Tainted Grail turned out to be!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game so far, really enjoying it. The atmosphere and gameplay have been excellent. The sky is the limit for future potential in this game. If you enjoy deck building and dark fantasy, this is a must buy. I'm also very impressed with the work done so far by Awaken Realms Digital as a company and team. Other Early Access game developers need to take note, the amount of communication and progress I've witnessed since purchase on this future master piece of a game is truly impressive. I wish you all the merriest of holidays and I hope you all receive fat bonuses and lots of praise, well deserved and well done! Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a roguelite RPG, it a has a really nice and complex turn based combat with cards.The amout of content and replayability is quite impressive, with 3 classes and 3 subclasses each, along with several quests with different possible outcomes that usually take several runs to complete, giving you even more reason to keep playing.A lot of times similar games have little to no story/lore, but this one is actually packed on both, and it is very well writen and voice acted.about 21h in I believe I'm still quite far from unlocking all classes meta progressions (and at early access I only have access to 6 of the 9 subclasses), and even farther from finishing all the quests, so this probabbly will still be worth your money even if you only plan to finish all questlines and not keep playing just for the increasing difficulty levels, card and perk unlocks and all that roguelite stuff.So far even in early access all bugs I encountered were minor and animation related, had one softlock which a reload solved.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Exceeded my expectations by a long shot. Definitely up there with my favourite deck builders right now. Pros:  - Good voice acting and writing, paired with a story that fits a rogue-lite game. Worldbuilding is pretty solid for a deckbuilding game. The first time round I definitely enjoyed listening to the stories but future encounters are kept short for re-runs. - Lots of freedom of choice. You are very frequently given the option between 2 or 3 things which makes tailoring your build easier. Rerolls are also fairly cheap. - A large variety of enemies that have many different behaviors that allow for interesting interactions. They don't just feel like stat-bloated versions of weaker enemies. - A large number of unlockables as you progress. - Cards scale well (from cheaper weak hitting cards to more expensive heavy ones). Damage is based off of a % of your base damage (in contrast to say Slay the Spire where a 0 cost attack will scale with strength the same as a 3 cost attack). - Well explained tool-tips on cards and hovering enemies. - Decent quality models and artwork. - No major bugs so far - Cheap, considering the amount of content and replay-ability - Interesting mechanics (leveling up, passives, runes etc.) that combine fairly fluidly without being overly complicated.Cons: - Definitely some issues with optimization. Game runs relatively smoothly most of the time but has frequent frame drops when transitioning or loading battles. - Animations feel a little clunky and repetitive. A lot of cards use the same animation. - UI is passable, but definitely lacking. - The overworld feels rather bland and scarce. It's not particularly fun to explore, just walking from one battle to the next.I would definitely recommend it at it's current price. Quite frankly, I'm surprised it isn't more expensive.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Games in dark fantasy settings are a little bit like games about the zombie apocalypse: There are so many, you really have to be doing something special to stand out. Tainted Grail definitely pulls it off. The art, writing, and well executed mood alone are worth the price of admission. I'm not usually one for deck builders but I'm enjoying this one. Take that for what its worth.Now I don't often write reviews, but what motivated me to write this is a super minor detail. A button.Being a roguelike you die a lot. When this inevitably happens, you are given two buttons. One lets you start again, and the other that says 'I need a break' which takes you back to the main menu. As someone who will compulsively play a game, deprive myself of sleep, and then have to deal with being braindead at work the next day - this 'I need a break' button is a good nudge in the right direction when it gets late. So many games design systems to target the reward centers of your brain in order to keep you playing as long as possible. Though this game is addictive, I appreciate the devs for choosing not to go the full Skinner box. It shows that they have respect for their players.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Had a blast with this game! I also played and enjoyed: Darkest Dungeon, Deep Sky Derelicts, etc.Tons of content and replay-ability. If you like tactical deck building, rogue-lite elements, and gothic atmosphere - this game delivers. Lots of fun stuff to explore and awesome and always-surprising combinations and synergies to be found across the many class types. Story is well-constructed (weird) and non-intrusive, but also quite fun to explore and ponder some of life's bigger questions, if you're into that sort of thing, as well. 100+ hours well worth the price! Kudos to devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: If there ever was an EA going in the right direction, you might have found one here. Basically what you´re getting into is a 3D Slay the Spire in a dark arturian fantasy/mythology realm, hence the Grail. So less Comic, more grit, wicked indeed °|So what was all the fuzz on top about ..Well, originally this was meant to be one title with two game modes - "endless" roguelike & CRPG campaign. Due to the success at the start and in EA the development team finally decided to split those games into two titles - this one here, the roguelike & this one - the fully fledged RPG campaign, which will see the light of release sometime next year.By that time, according to the roadmap, T G - Conquest should have reached it´s full release already. Now, if you backed Tainted Grail early or had purchased the game before 11/27/20 you were promised to receive the sibling title, you´ll never guess.. Development is constant & I have high hopes for these ones. This development team actually seems to have a plan. Heck, they are giving the whole thing a complete graphic overhaul to make a decent looking game into a great looking one! Plus they lowered the price after deciding to split the games .. Who does that ?!Bottom line; If you are into TurnBased, CardBattling & the like and a little gritty mythological challenge doesn´t scare you -  - I can´t imagine you´ll be disappointededit4: EA ended like a week ago - promises fulfilled, check! on to Avalon.. ; )

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 2Changed it to a negative review as they senselessly increased the difficulty in weird ways. All classes are now available.... NOT-you get one to start the melee class that uses multiple hits to build ultimate (forgot the name)-All other classes are unlocked in a random order by end of run xp gains-The berserker no longer heals when killing  things with his ult, making him 10k times less survivable-You can no longer return to town (at least in the tutorial level I haven't passed it yet) to heal or buy more goodies, the teleport feature for wyrdstones no longer exists-The boss of the tutorial zone summons minions every 10 hits, their damage is multiplied by the number of minions out. Since the only class you got is based on multi hit cards, which target random enemies, you will easily get 2 or 3 minions out even accidentaly the first 2 rounds of combat if you built your guy how he should be built. -After failing multiple times to down the boss ( 3 or 4 runs of simply just dying with 0 excitement as I can't play a class I'm actually into) I unlocked my first class... the druid... yaaaaay another class I don't want to play, at least he's not hit based? Idk I've never played him. the ENTIRE tutorial level feels like a scripted wipe you have to relive until you unlock another class by... dying. Womp freaking WompThis is sad because they added a lot of new cards and  stuff which feel good. Too bad I'm forced to play in ways I don't find enjoyable. =====================================================================UPDATEThey have tweaked or even overhauled many aspects of the game and it's working better than ever. Decks feel better and they did away with gear and replaced with a runestone system that works much better. ======================================================================A Wyrd take on Aurthurian legend that isn't a bad experience for 20 bux if you like slow moving deck builder roguelikes. Playing the Roguelike mode atm. I've downed the first of 3 bosses.  Classes need balancing I found the guardian to be rather hard mode compared to warrior. Haven't played mage yet and Druid is still heavy testing phase. The game aesthetic is pretty but I'm not sure why they bothered making it look like you have free control of your character as there is no "open world" to explore at all it is very path based and may as well be set up similar to Darkest Dungeon but top down you know? So far the card games are neat and have fun combos and such I'd like to see more ability to edit your deck. Gear is like non existent. When you spawn in initially you get one regular shop guy that has one armor and a sword for sale and until you complete a quest and gain 4000 Wyrdstone (20 hours in and I have like 400) you won't get to expand that at all. You'd think once you find your blacksmith you'd get more. Well you do, one more weapon and one more armor option (for the blacksmith they are randomized per run, the item vendor always sells the same armor/sword) So, assuming they are an upgrade you have all the black smith has to offer until you get thousands MORE wyrdstone. You can get this from downing bosses or fighting enemies without being protected by the wyrdcandles. You get like 5 -15 a fight if that. The only way to heal is Healing potions or any random event that may offer a bit of healing (often risky). Which is rough to start but about halfway through the first "leg" of the map you are downing things efficiently enough to keep enough potions stocked to keep going.  Then once you got things seemingly in hand you open up the second leg (this is after I have killed and looted everything I possibly could on the first leg) and you're back to getting your ass beat. harrrrd. Enemys go from (literally) *trivial* and *easy* to *talesworthy*... there was no "medium" anywhere lol. It feels like a pretty game with some Heroes of MnM in its heart. Minus the gear, units, skill trees, world, etc. That said I did play it for like 20 hours straight for some reason. I'll likely play it again its just hard to justify  that kind of time played and so little actually shown for it. No fancy gear or anything. I got a legendary card that was bad ass but you lose that when you die so woooop woop. Usually a good roguelike will have you "building" something up between runs and so far I haven't been able to expand anything beyond simply getting my Blacksmith (1 new wpn and armor and offers no other reason to be there) and my seamstress (sells nothing just wants you to upgrade her ♥♥♥♥ for... you guessed it... thouuuusands of Wyrdstone). I feel like I'm not even experiencing the game reallly.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit rough around the edges and needs some optimisation, (the framerate is pretty bad), but it's really enjoyable and has a unique setting and style. The different classes, or at least the 3 I've tried so far, all play completely differently. The story and characters are intriguing and I like the idea of 'wyrdness', which is a similar mechanic to the light/dark of Darkest Dungeon, but with a less obvious impact on the gameplay (at least as far as I have seen).It's one of those games where you slowly learn how to play, develop the best (or preferred) combat strategy for your class, understand what you need to do/collect, what you can avoid etc.Every run is different and you slowly gain NPC's in your village and earn currencies that persist after death that are used for upgrades. You also unlock cards, passives and classes after each run to give you more choice, power and flexibility for the next one. The better you do in a run, the more points you score, meaning the more you can unlock. Apparently you earn cosmetic items as well, but I've not done so yet. There are also quest lines for the various NPC's. Each one is a unique character so I'm looking forward to seeing what happens to them further down the line. The overarching story of the 'wyrdness' is also intriguing, with its links to Arthurian legend.Combat is interesting and challenging and generally fair, although I have walked into a couple of fights where I was steamrolled in the 2nd round. But, playing well and planning how to mitigate damage and which enemies to prioritise is always rewarded. Some encounters are significantly harder than others though, so you need to be aware of what you are walking into. It can be frustrating to walk into a fight and know you have zero chance to win, even though you managed to defeat the last 10 encounters without losing even 1 hp. Probably this is where having a 'get out of jail free' item in your inventory would save the day. I've not yet experimented with some of the more arcane items available....A really fun game at a reasonable price that just needs a patch or two to add some polish, optimisation and clarity. Looking at the road-map, that's exactly what the devs are planning to do. I wouldn't wait for a patch though, it's very playable right now. I'd love to see this game do well!

_childDocuments_.review: not a fan of card gamesnot a fan of rogue-games, no matter if they are "light" or notbut i do love Tainted Grailimagine Diablo, Soulsborne and Path of Exile had a love childboth the visual design and the plot ooze athmosphere and moodit also helps that the voice-work is spot on and the soundtrack is a mix of The Witcher and more mainstream nordic-sounds. it just bangs.the only downside are the somewhat lacking sound-effect, they lack some "oomph", but that's just nitpicking.when it comes to gameplay the game is a card-game, but also a Diablo-rpg-clone. your village stands for the permanent progression (there's more permanent progression) and ties together story, gaining power and actual gameplay goals in a "just one more try"-manner that many other rogue-lights fail. tbh. this is the first rogue-light progression-system i can live with.you pick your character amongst a wide array of chars, which are quite well done and would even be great in a hack'n slay or action-rpgpassive effects, active "ultimate abilities" and actual card-decks create unique classes that actual grow during each run like they would in a normal rpgwhile playing you not just unlock more upgrades and support-items/abilities for your village but also totaly new cards for subsequent runs. so yeah, while each run starts you kinda fresh both the story and the actual gameplay support real progression, both in a lore sense and in actual "power-gain".battles vary between the more standart trash-mob combat and quite interesting boss-battlesthe wyrd mechanic is also interesting, kinda like light worked in Darkest Dungeon; while you do not get benefits for running with maximus "wyrdness", it ads unique cards that often offer ups and down for playing or not playing, which ads another strategic layer; also certain enemies gain or lose special skills depending on the level of wyrd.all in all i realy didn't think this game would be for me, but after a friend's recommendation i gave it a chance and boy am i glad for it. i cannot recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Slay the Spire meet Diablo.A diablo style town and questing environment merges with a slay the spire style card game to create an interesting card game with unique cards and a few twists on some classic types of characters.The game in normal mode is a bit unforgiving at first. Once you get a few of the losses under your belt and have earned a town character or 2, things start to get easier. Once you've filled the town and beaten the big boss you find at the end of the 4 acts. The replay ability kicks in, you've unlocked a new character, and added some new skills and cards to the available list, or found a few quests you didn't complete.Quest items and town environment are shared across all characters on the save slot. _childDocuments_.review: When The Witcher and Dark Souls had a baby, it came out as a deck builder.In general- Challenging, and unforgiving. Completely consuming in its macabre feel, between the lighting, soundtrack, and general dismay about you, you can't help but be drawn in. The game play- Interesting process to actually building your deck. It's a marriage between RPG's and deck building. Some aspects could use work, but the dynamics check out, though some parts aren't self explanatory. Story- Holy crap, there's an actual story! So far so good!Replay value- Keanu stood there for a moment taking it all in. "Whoa." From the get go, you see a massive variety of different characters. Between those and the options you face as you build your deck, it's not likely you'll ever have the same run. Some aspects don't change, you basically unlock one thing or another, then it becomes available from the start of your next run. It doesn't take away from the replay value, I feel. Mostly because you're gonna die. Then probably die again. And again. Have fun!If you like deck building, dark fantasy, and a challenge, pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine, but due to a combination of traits, not as good as some other deckbuilders. Slay the Spire is incredibly straightforward and thus elegant. Monster train is complicated, but it does all the math for you upfront so you make informed choices. This is neither; it is both complicated and inelegant in how it presents the outcome of your turn.The dreary Souls-like aesthetic is... okay. It does it well in presenting a consistent theme, and the story is one of the stronger aspects of the game. A few core classes with several variants on each class makes for lots of playstyles, but for some reason I'm just not that enthusiastic when I nail a combo, which is crucial for deckbuilder engagement.That being said, if you love deckbuilders, it's a a perfectly fine game. it's well-balanced with lots of replayability and scaling difficulty. I got it in a Humble Bundle and it was worth my time.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Deck Building that lets you become quite OP on some classes. I am Currently Difficulty 9 and rising.Voice acting was pretty decent, eventually there was just too much dialogue and i just wanted to get my run over with so i'd skip a few and listen to a few.You can practically play the entire game one handed using the mouse since it uses point and click as well as WASD. I prefer WASD because you can step close enough to some NPC's and trigger their dialogue/event before bothering to encounter the enemy. Decent amount of classes to unlock and cards and even some cosmetics.The 3 Factions are basically Bow classes, Melee Classes and Summoner Classes, 3 of each.Bow has 2 of the funnest classes, Apostate and Sentinel. Zealot as well, but i have barely played this class.Apostate is borderline broken imo. It is very easy to build damage and practically 1-2 shot most enemies, sometimes even bosses if you got the right setup. If you like big numbers but long set up time, this is the class.Sentinel is more balanced, you basically shotgun blast the enemies with a bunch of arrow cards and its ultimate skill. Quite satisfying to play.Melee has Pathfinder, which is basically a tank that build damage each turn he's not hit. Wyrdhunter who uses multi-hit cards to build up his passive and ultimate for big damage. Berzerker that needs to be low HP to do good damage.Summoners are Blood, this ones my fav of 3 summoners. Blood loses HP to summon and promote his minions. His minions attack each turn and overcharge (activate a stronger attack basically) on every 4th promotion and die, they also promote automatically each turn. Have to manage HP as a resource.Druid type of Summoner can promote his minions and make them stronger, but if they get hit, they deal their level as damage to the PC. and i haven't played Necromancer.The game gives out tons of upgrades as you do a run. You'll be choosing new cards, and passives often, getting items for use in combat and even a Flute that you can obtain from a Pied Piper who can change what it does, you keep this flute between runs and can use it once per combat. A Dog/wolf companion if you followed the quest right.The Village stuff gets upgraded as you play and you can complete runs on higher difficulties with enemies having more stats and annoyances for extra gold, which is used to upgrade combat items. Eventually you'll have some decent upgrades and a lot of runs can become easier, you'll have more options and gold to spend on returns to the village. Definitely the best part of this game is coming up with broken builds. The worst part of this game is the optimization. It's pretty bad, this game has no reason to run the way it does.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this as a gift from my friend.Few games as of late are able to hold my attention, stir my imagination, and challenge the tactician in me. After facing defeat, it's fun to go back in with a different class and build, and tackle your encounters in a new way.I highly recommend giving this game a go if you like turn-based, card-based combat games. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR : recommend on sale not on full price!If everything was on par with the quality of the storytelling this game would be an easy recommend. They really nailed the aesthetic of the dark and corrupted fantasy world where everything feels a little familiar but also wrong or uncanny.The game itself is fun too, very reminiscent of slay the spire, however the balance is way less tight. I felt like I was breezing through the difficulties after understanding how the enemies and bosses work - and some classes seem to be strictly more powerful and/or easier to play than others.The second issue is performance, the game looks okay on higher settings but it just has no right to put so much stress on a high end system as it does, the optimization was clearly not ironed out properly. So the best way is to play on the lowest settings, but on lowest the game honestly looks horrible, and even then it's not running proper smoothly.Lastly, lack of content. I finished the game with 100% achievements after 30~ hours of playtime. It's really weird how they didn't put a lot more achievements for specific classes, difficulties and unlocking all the cards and collections and such. I have a lot more things to collect and I only got to difficulty 9 while playing so I'm not even sure how high it actually goes - but without corresponding achievements I just don't have an urge to keep playing, but that's more of a personal issue.All in all good game with lots of missed potential, so I don't think it's worth it on full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Tainted Grail: Conquest is a deck building roguelike with light RPG elements set in the dark fantasy setting of Avalon. TG:A has 9 classes that are unlocked gradually as your complete runs. These classes can be broken down into 3 play styles of melee, archer, and summoner. The 3 classes under each of these 3 play styles share a lot of cards between them but differ in execution. Some of these cards are not unlocked until after completing runs with that class encouraging repeated runs. Some classes are more interesting than others. I personally found the 3 melee classes the most fun to play whereas the archer classes did not distinct enough from one another.In addition to class specific cards, there are cards granted by NPCs and vendors, sometimes requiring the completion of a task or quest beforehand. These quests and NPCs are where the RPG mechanics come into play as you are given a handful of dialogue options when solving various dilemmas in Avalon. Unfortunately, these choices never felt very meaningful as there was often a clear right choice with the wrong choices being downright punishing to your character. These NPCs were well voice acted (in most cases) and the dialogue was written well enough to make repeated runs feel distinct enough for a good while.What did NOT contribute to distinct repeated runs was the exploration and environmental design. This is by far the weakest element of TG:A. Once you've gotten enough experience/cards/stat increases to complete a full run you will see that a full run consists of 3 wings each with its own boss fight and then a final boss fight. These wings have branching paths, but there isn't an choice involved as you can clear an entire wing (and often should to ensure your level is high enough to face the later fights). The game uses a system where you have a limited number of candles that ward away the wyrdness (penalties in battle) that in theory encourages path planning but it doesn't take long until upgrades make the mechanic meaningless. Additionally, these environments are just downright drab and ugly to look at. I understand they are going to dark fantasy setting, but the majority of the wings are just desolate, muddy-brown, vistas. They serve merely as a means to present the combat encounters and NPCs to the player. The monster and character design is well done, however, with some particularly unsettling looking creatures whose design often encapsulates their unique abilities well.Music is also fantastic and fits the atmosphere perfectly. There was one particular boss theme, Reida, with Nordic chanting and a throbbing bass line that gave me goosebumps. It was the kind of track that sticks with me long after I've played the game which is the highest praise I can give to a song in a game.I'd recommend TG:A if you are looking for a great deck-builder roguelike. The RPG mechanics the game advertises aren't anything special enough to write home about and story elements become gradually fewer and farther between leaving you with just the core gameplay loop. While the "exploration" itself is not good, the combat is addictive, varied, and fun enough to give you a large amount of replayability, which should be the ultimate goal of any game of this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a great game and I hope it keeps getting updates, expansions, etc.Mild spoilers. I found the game a bit too hard or a bit too easy depending on which class used. Which is awesome in a way, because I don't actually like rogue-lite games much. But I love the deck building, exploring, RPG parts of the game. I found that the Wyrdhunter was so difficult that after 4 or 5 runs I just got frustrated with it and gave up. _childDocuments_.review: If you like deckbuilder roguelikes this is a must play. It perfectly embodies the phrase 'easy to learn, difficult to master.' Story: I think this is probably the weakest point, but its still pretty good. The concept and setting is very unique and intriguing, and there are several NPCs you recruit for your town (and others you just meet in the wyrd) who have fairly interesting plots. The conclusion of these plots can vary and may alter future rewards. For example, at one point I made a pact with some cultists and now I occasionally come across shrines where I can offer *ahem* meat for rewards. The NPCs you meet set up the atmosphere very well, however, the main story feels a little underrepresented. It gets introduced well within the first couple runs, but afterwards falls by the wayside. Perhaps there is a satisfying ending that I haven't reached yet, but the main story really isn't motivation for booting up another run.Music: very good. The sounds and instruments used are unique and suit the setting well: tribal, mysterious, suspenseful and energetic. After looking into it, I was surprised by how few songs are actually present in the game, because the music never felt repetitive.Gameplay: this is the reason you should play this game. There are three 'classes' each with three 'subclasses'. Each class has a unique pool of cards (barring a few special cards that can be acquired by special means for every class). Then each subclass has a unique ultimate ability and method of generating ultimate points which may fundamentally alter your play style, plus a few unique cards to support their unique playstyle, and unique starting skills that dictate their playstyle (for example, Watchers of Tuathan have cards that flip over after use so they have a different effect next time you use them but the Apostate starts with a unique skill so that flipped cards stay in their hand rather than going to discard). For example, while the Summoner and Necromancer both belong to the Moonring and thus share ~90% of their cards, the summoner usually wants to keep only one or two summons out on the field at a time to make them the ultimate powerhouse. Meanwhile the necromancer constantly cycles through summons, turning their dead summons into ghosts and their enemies into ghouls, and occasionally turning themselves into an almighty lich. There is an incredibly wide variety of enemies, and one of the most important tactics for beating a run is recognizing what kind of enemies your build is capable of tackling to level up, and which you are better off avoiding all together. Nothing is worse than trying to fight a group of Wisps that ignore all damage below a certain threshold with a character that specializes in many small chip attacks. There are many ways to increase your power: the most obvious is normal deck building. You also have a selection of items (consumable and reusable) which I find myself using an astounding amount of. Even in other roguelikes, I find myself hording and then never using consumable items, but something about the design of this game has me using consumable items more often than in just about any other game. Level ups provide passive skills that can reinforce a play style while level 10 and 20 mastery skills offer skills that can radically alter your play style. After over 40 hours of playtime, amounting to around 30 runs, there are still several tactics I know I've slept on, and even for my favorite class I know there are tactics that I've only just begun to take advantage of. And the attitude of the developer is very promising. We just received the first major update, which includes three(!) new modes for free, and the developers really seem to listen to community feedback.

_childDocuments_.review: I was disappointed I didn't buy the game before it officially split into two products, but it takes two minutes of research to figure out why that was necessary.  Turns out I'm the bozo since I should have owned this long ago on account of it being a really solid roguelite deckbuilder.  I was initially scared away by the early access related lack of polish and problems that I'd seen around the forums, but realize that my lack of faith would eventually be replaced by a lack of getting the second game for free lol.  So it goes.  A grim-as-♥♥♥♥ tale of King Arthur card battler was not something I knew I needed in my life but this game seems to be fully my speed.  The VA work is top shelf so far and the goofy 3rd person controls will hopefully be sorted out a bit before release.  Not a dealbreaker, just not very effortless in current form.  Lots of comments about how this is a good game for people that like Slay the Spire but that's just a bit broad.  If those comparisons are invoked because both games have...ya know cards in them, then sure that's accurate.  But Slay is a bit more symbiotic with its approach to the cards and at no point is STS trying to be an RPG which allows itself such freedoms.  But 'being an RPG' is what Tainted Grail is actually nailing pretty well.  So it really is like comparing two very different things.  I'd say this is a better fit for people who are into Bard's Tale 4 or Operencia: The Stolen Sun, more than a card game only like Slay (or any of those).  But it would make perfect sense if someone that liked STS liked this too, though.  Can't wait to see the finished product here soon.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best rougelites I have played. There are number of neat permanent upgrades you can get that transfer over runs giving you satisfactory feeling of progression without overdoing it. Everything in this game is voice acted which helps to build atmosphere and immerse you more into the game. You will encounter number of unique and interesting characters many with their own questlines to pursue. Visually the game is very pleasing.The combat is similar to Slay the Spire - you have a recycling deck of cards and you encounter manifold different enemies each with their intents. The game offers you lots of varied factors to keep you entertained for a long time. To start off you have 3 main schools. Different schools have their own deck of cards, abilities and each school has 3 classes - each with their own unique passives, ultimate abilities and even some cards. Depending on what class you are playing with you get very different playstyle and fresh game experience. On top of that you get many random upgrades to diversify your runs such as combinable runestones, consumerables, neutral/quest cards, passive abilites etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Three of my top fave genre's are: Grim dark, Rogue-like, and Deck-building. Tainted Grail Digital combines all three of these with wonderful twist of their own. The developers added their own unique vision to it.For any fan of at least two of those genres this game offers something fun. The Conquest (Roguelike) is the one most developed for now and has already given me many hours of fun game time. The Campaign has been completely remade from scratch compared to the alpha demo and you can see major improvement in development in less than 6 months. In those 6 months they not only remade the Campaign, they also added Conquest.While this game is currently in Early Access, as a backer of the board game (which I enjoyed massively) I personally see a good and unique game coming out of this in the long term.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I came to this expecting another Slay the Spire clone. While it certainly has its roots there, this is a solid evolution of the emerging genre. You have the roguelite elements, the card selection, the character powers... but you also have deep (and difficult to obtain) permanent progression elements. If I had a con, it would be that they're too expensive for what you get... but at the same time, it's also a pro, because it's definitely not handed to you. Those progression elements (passives, especially) really make me feel like I'm developing something unique every run, rather than just putting together the optimal card set and hoping for the best.However, there are two elements of Tainted Grail that truly stand out as being all it's own:Music. Wowza. The music is dark, grim, a bit futuristic, and really meet the theme of the chaotic elements of the Wyrd so well. It's not like anything else I can think of, and it's perfect here.Top billing goes to story, though. As an older guy, I'm a little fatigued of story after a lifetime of playing RPGs. Somehow, the story here though is just brief enough in chunks, and... weird enough... to keep my full attention. All the NPCs have their stories and quests, and there's an interweaving that I'm still catching on to ~30 hours in. And I'm captivated. Every time I run into an NPC in the game area or the town when they have something new to say, I'm hungry for it. I still have quite a ways to go there, but I'm truly enjoying the story in a way I haven't in a video game in a very long time. It's brilliant.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a number of favorable reviews about this game, but I honestly cant understand why. I gave it more than a fair chance to wow me. The whole game is set in a small map with 4 paths - there is no changes to this limited field of play at any time. You have 9 players to choose from, but basically the idea is to kill the 4 bosses in the 4 paths only to find out when you win that it was some kind of cosmic joke Death played and you have to respawn from lvl1 with no skills and do it all over again. There's a "true boss" hidden away but it requires a complentionist mindset to unlock and really wasnt worth it to me. Im shocked a game this limited exists and even for $8 i cant help feeling ripped off. Never imagined I'd be happier with a random loot box in a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've read a few long form reviews to see if I'm missing some late game weaknesses, but they all seem to confirm what I've thought since the first few rounds I played:This game is fantastic.I would go into so much detail why, but I'd rather just give the short version - the developers hit all of the right notes with this one.  I've seen some say that some classes aren't balanced, but of the ones I've played, understanding the mechanics, making sure there's synergy with your passives and deck, and finding the strategy that fits your play style is key to successful runs.  And if you're not successful on a run, go through another time, unlock some more stuff, meet more NPCs, and keep refining your approach.It may not be the game for everyone, but if you watch the trailers and think, "This looks pretty good. I wonder if it's actually good and worth buying..." The answer is an emphatic "Yes" from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl,Dr; if you like deckbuilding games, get this. You owe it to yourself!Gameplay -10- In depth, with many creative mechanics and ideas that I haven't seen in board games or other deck builders. Balance is very tight, with only a few exceptions.Story -7- The narrative is gripping and compelling. Various NPCs in the field offer quests that you can complete, and every run through feels like you're accomplishing something.Writing -9- Amazing, dark Arthurian setting. Each dialog is written like it's from a full length, well edited novel. Graphics -7- Only ok, but the art direction is stellar.Audio -5- Voice acting is great, the main female narrator is very good with ranges and inflections. They do reuse her quite a bit, though. Sound effects are present but nothing crazy, music is good. Loses points for some dialog having a garbled mumble sound effect, I assume these are placeholders for more voice acting.Bugs -10- None that I've seen in 7+ hours of gameplay.Content -7- It takes about 3 hours to do a full run through, and there are tons of classes to try. I'm sure the game is going to keep getting bigger and bigger as time goes on too. This section has me the most excited for what could come in the future!If I had any complaints, it's that it needs more hotkeys, as it's a bit mouse intensive atm. It's also hard to select specific monsters or characters at times, but these two things are minor issues really.The game has insane potential - each class plays completely differently from on another, each with their own unique passives that change how you play. Every fight is interesting and brings new challenges to the table.
_childDocuments_.name: Tainted Grail: Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very close one for me, I think if I had played this before games like Spire I would have given it a much kinder look. It runs kind clunky with animations, and there isn't much to look at, everything is sort of grey and brown. Some of the character feel much too similar, and you unlock cards so slowly. The same is true of Spire, but a run of Spire takes 40-60 minutes if you're just moving along normally.Runs in this game take forever, and there are, in my opinion, too many options for upgrading that just don't do much interesting. You run around these areas, you clear all the monsters, then you fight the boss. There really isn't much reason it had to be structured the way it is, the same thing could have been achieved with different sets of branching paths with choices and rewards and it would have trimmed down a ton of the meandering. You only get cards on level ups, not after every encounter (barring certain rewards that give them after fights) so your deck doesn't really feel like it's progressing very fast, and that means you don't really get excited for the next fight, because your deck isn't that much better than the last one. All in all, I would recommend this game when it goes on sale, try a few characters, and then see if you want to keep it. The devs have obviously put in a lot of work, I just found playing it a chore more than a treat.

I just like messing around with the undead. Either way they really are one in the same. It can be challenging but still fun. I like the npc's and the side quest. The voice acting is great! Sounds to me like the actors really tried to play the part. The music is on point to me and the graphics are not to shady at all! Again, this is not some huge dungeon crawler. It's a deck builder card game with some RPG spice. I Like to play this when I am on the road or staying in a hotel for a night or too. (I'm a truck driver). _childDocuments_.review: Overall, Tainted Grail doesn't bring much new to the table that other games have brought before it. What it does, however, is blend turn based RPG elements and Rogue Lite gameplay quite well. If you enjoy a challenge and repeating yourself until you get it right, you'll love conquest. Your decisions have consequences as you build up your personal village. While it's difficult, the game feels rewarding and does in fact reward good decision making. If you rob a shrine, yeah, you're gonna get cursed. I haven't played much for the normal campaign so I have no insight on that, but I would recommend this game if you're looking for a dark, difficult Rogue lite RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like Tainted Grail; it has a really nice dark fantasy vibe, story telling is on point as is the voice actors delivering the lines, and in theory I was excited for a deck-builder that tried something new. In practice, however, so much of TG feels hollow or unfinished. The enemy designs are creative but the models look rushed and suffer from clunky animations. The game's tutorial is near nonexistent, so the player has to sus out what the game wants them to do, all the while introducing mechanics layered on top of each other that are rarely highlighted. At first I was concerned this would lead to difficulty and frustration, but I was surprised to find all this chaos was in the player's favor (for the most part) but lacked any sense of accomplishment. The helter skelter of the game's lack of balance didn't encourage me to continue, unfortunately, as it just began to devolve into a grinding sprint for permanent upgrades. Nothing really feels cohesive and it feels better suited as an Early Access title with room for fine tuning, IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me say this game is fun and I am looking forward to a full release of this game, but it still needs a lot of balance work.  I like the idea of an adventure card game like this in the vein of a Slay the Spire meets Diablo type game.  This is a really fun and unique concept.  After playing all the available classes, I feel all of them need some work.  I have some general suggestions about the game, and some specific ones that I really think will improve this game.GENERAL SUGGESTIONS:(1) In battle, the camera angle starts at a weird position.  It should be rotated more to the back of the player about 20 degrees for the following reasons:     - When more than 4 enemies are present the fifth enemy on the right can't be seen, and causes surprise attacks     - When using the Druid and you have multiple summon creatures, the info for your creatures will overlap each other and makes it hard to read.(2) When encountering enemies on the map, there should be a confirmation screen that pops up to accept or decline the battle.  Several times I accidentally go too close to a creature that I wasn't ready to fight when I was just moving around the map.  Some type of ambush type of mechanic is okay, but no one likes to accidentally start a fight from a missclick.(3) The fast travel system is kind of hard to use.  When using the portals, clicking an arrow to go from portal to portal is kind of annoying.  It should bring up a map of the entire area and you can click on the portal you want to go to.WARRIOR SUGGESTIONSWarrior classes are all underpowered.  The following should help a bit.(1) The energy charging for the Ultimate ability charges waaaay too slow.  With the Guardian and the Berserker, the battle was usually over by the time I got 3 energy to use it at the lowest level.  Energy should be retained at the end of every combat so it can build up.  I had a run with that ability, and it made the run much much much more fun.  This should be a default characteristic of the warrior.  Kind of like he always stays mad like The Hulk.(2) Attack cards are too weak and don't scale very well into the 2nd and 3rd Tier battles even with stronger weapons.(3) Warrior has a severe problem with multiple enemies because its attacks are too weak and they can't absorb a whole lot of damage.  Their attacks should do more damage and/or hit more enemies(4) Their cards cost too much for what they do.  I think maybe increasing the warrior's base energy to 4 would really help these classes in general.(5) Warrior should have more 0 cost cards (particularly with attack damage) and maybe a 0 cost attack that is always in-hand every turn like the Druid's 0 cost card that activates a summoned creature.  that would go a long way to helping the warrior seem more fierce.(6) The Berserker's Ultimate should charge when blocking attacks.  Since it doesn't, the fight is usually over by you being dead and charge is maxed out or being at 3 and the battle is overDRUID SUGGESTIONS:(1) The Druid, particularly the summoner is too strong.  It's fun to dominate the game, but it is currently too powerful.   This class is kind of a glass cannon, so toning down the damage output may make the class too weak.  I think toning down the damage of the Abomination's attacks might be good.  That thing just facerolls most battles with multiple enemies.  (2) With the Golem summoned creature, I found it to be underwhelming.  It doesn't 0 damage and is exclusively a damage sponge. it should have a little bit of offence capability.  With it only being a damage sponge, it kind of makes it somewhat useless because it is more beneficial to take down the enemies quickly instead of chipping away at their health while the golem takes the hits.  In fact, I kind of skip over any Golem related upgrades because damage output is more effective than damage absorption.(3) If the Golem is going to be 100% defensive, maybe give it some damage return or poison or something like that so it outputs some damage when it is attacked.

_childDocuments_.review:
Avalon is dying. King Arthur is long gone, and Knights of the Round Table are in disarray. Guardian Menhirs, the only thing that makes it possible for humans to survive in this remote land, are going dark. Your village chose its best and brightest and sent them on an epic quest to reach Kamelot, find the Grail, and save the land.

You were not among them.

They've never returned, and now it's your turn to lead a band of unlikely heroes, the only ones this land can still provide. These ordinary people set off far too late, under-equipped for the task ahead, and with little hope of success.

Tainted Grail is a dark fantasy open-world RPG with fresh turn-based exploration and combat. It is based around deep, immersive story from one of the best and most innovative board games (biggest Kickstarter project of 2018!), but introduces a whole new experience crafted directly for PC.

name: Gleamlight
detailed_description: Welcome to Gleamlight – a 2D action game that will take you through an adventure traversing a beautiful, transient world. Immerse yourself amid the beautiful stained glass artistry as you navigate without the reliance of any standard game UI, while tracing the world’s mysterious unspoken story. What will you, as Gleam, sense and feel through your travels across this beautiful, yet fearsome world of glass? ◆A World Made of Glass The world beautifully unfurls before you with lush trees, boulders of all sizes, and various paraphernalia, all in the form and shape of glass. Prepare to explore this fantastical world where light warms the glass and darkness stains it with bitter cold. ◆A Game Without UI The game has been designed to immerse players into the world and story without being obstructed by any standard game UI, allowing players to organically enjoy the action and tension of defeating enemies and traversing the world. ◆An Unspoken Story The story behind what happened in this world, and what is to come is up to you as the player. Discover and piece together the story through your adventure, and save this beautiful, transient world of glass.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no real reason to spend money on Gleamlight when even the most mediocre platformers on steam offer better content for a fraction of the price. It's clunky, poorly designed and generally a slog to play through.It's Very sad to see a game i was looking forward to fall flat on its face like this.There's not much to like and much to complain about, so i'll separate this into categories.The game looks fine in screenshots, but in motion you realize the animations are very rough.The environments look pretty good, but they tend to hide stuff they really shouldn't (enemies, switches, spikes...).Unresponsive and clunky. Inputs will sometimes not register and some things are completely unintuitive (you can't drop through a platform unless you stand completely still). Your attacks are frustratingly slow as well.The game overall is easy, since every attack you land regenerates some of your health instantly. It's hard to die unless you get combo'd by a bunch of enemies, which will happen in some areas.The music is forgettable and somewhat repetitive but it fits the game's atmosphere well enough.The sound effects, however, are weak. Enemies make little to no sound, despite being bulky machines.You can get your first ending withing the first hour of playing. You can then replay the game in the opposite order (going from the end to the beginning) to get a second ending. Once that's over, you can .It feels kind of insulting for a nearly 20$ game to recycle its entire world  and make you go through it in reverse only one hour in. That's something NES games would do, and that trend died with good reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly lackluster. 6/10.It's impossible to not compare this to Hollow Knight as it's obvious where this game's inspiration came from. My major gripe with the game is the combat. As it is, you leech HP from enemies with every attack. This was an incredibly bad move by the developers. It is quite literally impossible to die as long as you spam your attack. I cheesed through the first boss without moving at all and the 2nd was more of a goose chase than a challenge. Gleamlight also lacks any sense of purpose for the player. You start in a cave and move left to right, killing enemies and jumping around along the way. There's no explanation about the lore through either notes or NPCs. The premise for the story is that you get punched/mugged by a crystal guy and you now have to chase them. No context at all. Even after killing the first two bosses I found myself asking who are these people and why am I killing them? Graphics and soundtrack are fine on their own. Enemy appearances quickly get repetitive but the backgrounds still look nice, and while you'd never intentionally listen to the OST, it fills the game with white noise well enough.Overall, Gleamlight just feels uninspired. Despite the initial criticism of it being a Hollow Knight clone I wanted to give it a chance and now I've ended up thoroughly disappointed. If you just want something to tie you over until Silksong releases, I still wouldn't recommend playing this even if you plan on refunding it.

_childDocuments_.review: So.  "Gleamlight."  A wildly misunderstood game.  If you want a TL;DR review, this game is too expensive, but the game itself is a perfectly good little linear action platformer with a subtly dark plot (for lack of a better term), some fun story twists, decent bosses, and a short but satisfying run time.  It's worth a play . . . if you can get it on sale.Now, if you want a little more depth, please continue on.So, there appears to be a lot of negativity born of misinformation about this game, so let's clear a few things up right off the bat:1) This game is NOT "Hollow Knight," nor is it ATTEMPTING TO BE, no matter what a vast majority of so-called "games journalists" (or enraged fanboys who didn't play it) claim.  Anyone who thinks that either didn't actually play this, or didn't actually play HK.2) This game DOES certainly share some of HK's artistic style (simplistic character designs, black outlines, fast arcing sword slashes, caves with crystals and spikes and shadows, etc.), but these visual elements were not created by that game, they predate both games by DECADES.  And especially with the outlines, those are inherent to the stained glass aesthetic of "Gleamlight," which honestly gives the game a more unique flavor than most detractors are willing to give it credit for.3) This game is NOT a "metroidvania" (and seriously, that word is atrocious and always has been, can we, as a gamer community, PLEASE finally come up with something less stupid??), and again, it is not attempting to be one.  It's a straight action platformer with minimal power-ups, no power-locked gateways, no branching exploration, and no map, a straight linear path that (mild spoiler) you have to repeat three times to truly finish the game.  Yes, there is "backtracking" as a result, but only because you're repeating that linear path more than once.4) This game is short.  INTENTIONALLY SO, I firmly believe.  Because it is a linear path spanning only four "levels," and the game requires you to repeat them to finish the story, and there is limited environmental differentiation or enemy variety, the designers clearly set out to make a game that didn't overstay its welcome.  It is not overly difficult, attacking enemies heals you, it is not easy to get lost, dying spawns a checkpoint IN THE SAME ROOM, it is not particularly deep as far as story is concerned, and thus it is very brief (I finished it and got the true ending in about 3.5 hours).  This is a GOOD THING, mind you.  If it had been long, it would have been a SLOG.  Keeping it short kept is mostly enjoyable the whole way through.5) This game is a year old.  That is to say, it has received multiple bug fixes and minor QOL improvements since its release.  Yeah, a lot of the negativity is from people going in expecting something this game wasn't ever supposed to be, and that's on them.  However, I've noted that a couple reviews have noted bugs and mistakes when the game first released, and to that, all I can say is "well, it plays completely solid now, I had no problems!"  I figure people should know this by now, given that it's a standard videogame industry practice nowadays, but *shrug*.  I found no technical issues.6) This game . . . is DEFINITELY overpriced.  $20 for a less-than-4-hour game is kinda ridiculous, not gonna lie.  Me, I got a Steam Key from an independent online retailer for only $5, and THAT was TOTALLY worth it.  So . . . your mileage may vary, in terms of cost/return analysis.IF you go into this game WITHOUT the silly preconceived notion that it's a "Hollow Knight" clone (which I will stress, IT IS IN NO WAY TRYING TO BE), what you will get is a tight, short, fun little platform hack-and-slash with powerups that make combat progressively easier and faster, some fun (if not super complex) bosses, a few interesting "twists" (the game fakes you out with a "game over" credits sequence . . . TWICE.  Make sure you look up how to get to the REAL final boss) along the way,  It's got a dark, foreboding atmosphere and environments that help to subtly tell the minimal story, and the whole thing just works.  Not a major time investment, not a lot of replay value, but if you stop treating it like something it's NOT, you will find that it's actually really good at being what it's SUPPOSED to be.You want Nintendo hard?  Get "Dark Souls."  You want metroidvania?  Play "Bloodstained."  You want dozens of hours of gameplay?  Join an MMO.  You want a cheaper game? . . . Find a coupon. *LOL*  But if you want a fun, low-stakes, semi-gothic fantasy dungeon crawl with a pretty art style, solid controls, and plenty of action? "Gleamlight" is by no means a bad game, and I enjoyed my afternoon with it!- J

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be the outlier on this review page. I do recommend this game HOWEVER, I recommend it if you go into it without expecting HK 2.0 or a sequel or anything at the same level and polish as it. So far I played roughly 2 hours and got to the end of the first major boss. I will highlight my thoughts.It has a beautiful soundtrack and art style. The setting is nice and feels dark and mysterious. However its UI and menu is clunky as hell. It tells you and explains NOTHING. Which is both a pro and con. Some mystery is fine, but not knowing what the new attack you learned is can get annoying. The aiming of swings is off and you don't hit at angles you'd expect to. and be prepared to die a lot, but there is no penalty. Every floor has an entrance and exit, it has spots you respawn at if you die. you will die because you cant see your health. Some things will kill you by touching you and the next time will hit you 100 times and you wont die. Each floor is the puzzle, you find a button to hit or thing to kill to move on and open the end door. It is fun, however you have to treat it like its a puzzle/platform with some "I want to be the guy" challenges (aka that floor will fall and crush you, but you don't know it until it does). I do find it fun in its own way and I hope it gets some love and polish because I see the potential in it to be good with some tweaks and updates. Its like Dr Thunder to Hollow Knights Dr Pepper; its not as good side by side, but if you are thirsty it still is nice to quench your thirst and doesn't have any less merit as a drink because it took some inspiration from another. So in conclusion, if you go in with a certain mindset its fun but just janky at times. Hopefully the Devs will fix some of that and make it hit the potential I am sure it can hit with the right love and careUPDATE 8-22-20: Today I went to play after not for a few days and my save file was gone as well as my in game achievements. :/

_childDocuments_.review: Had this game on my wishlist, appeared to be a cool 'Hollow Knight-like' platformer so I was looking forward to it.Played through the game, but the credits rolled after the 3rd boss, I was confused and almost refunded. However, I loaded my save again and there were about 6 additional bosses after the first set of credits. The boss design wasn't bad, some of them were kind of frustrating. Also, trying to get back up through the last area again after reloading your save is very frustrating. Graphics and OST are nice. The combat isn't bad, but I wish there was a little more to it. It's hard to recommend this game for it's story, since it's veryyyy passively told with no dialogue.In my opinion, this will be a good game to speedrun. If you're looking for some boss fights and platforming, this game will do nicely. I think $20 is still a bit much due to only having 9 bosses and reused areas, but I'd definitely recommend picking this one up when it's on sale or if the price gets reduced.Update: A few days after launch we have found additional endings, secret areas, and several hidden bosses. This game offers a fun experience trying to get all the achievements, but afterward it's even better to speedrun since there's no dialogue to skip through, just platforming, boss fights, and multiple endings to run for.

Playing it to the first end took we about an hour and some people might conclude the game here saying thats it but if you reenter your safefile after the credits the game continous. Now the player simpy goes back the whole game again while more and stronger enemies are appearing. Im honest playing that was kind of boring cause i already had the kill achievments so i could just rush towards the "final" boss which is actually pretty easy to fight after this i had the apocalypse ending done. Here i also did not know how to advance further and finding help on the internet proved to be pretty challenging too. But after some research i found out that now i have to do a "pacifist" run which means playing the game again without killing an enemy. If this mission succeds a secret passage gets opened which brings the player to another enemy spam section and afterwards to the true final boss. After defeating him in an i would say average difficult fight the player returns to the start once more and is able to free the child to trigger the good ending. All that said it was pretty annoying to experiment with the keyboard in order to find out what abilities i got after the boss battles i mean some help from the game would have been nice but the games description says it wants to be like that so i can not really judge it for that. Next would be the controls while they also were on an average level and sometime took too long to realize the input (that mosly happend when i wanted to turn around). I also want to quickly mention the 100 deaths achievment which i found to be pretty annoying i had to farm it after i had everyting else because i just didnt die enough. Another negative thing would be the spamming of the credits occuring an minimum of 3 times troughout an 100% playtrough.After all i would give the game a 4/10 when it comes to everything together  i just expected more playtime (i had 4,6 hour btw) and stuff to do as well as challenge for a game of this price category the game would be pretty ok if it was in an 5-8 buck area insted of costing solid 17 bucks I hope my review was helpfull lovely reader

_childDocuments_.review: Got this on sale a while back to give it a chance, because I hoped it wouldn't be THAT bad, but it is. The art style looks pretty good (when it's not moving), but the areas, abilities, enemies, and bosses are all uninteresting, and the game is incredibly short and repetitive even with its multiple endings. Comparing this to hollow knight or any other metroidvania isn't exactly fair, because this isn't a metroidvania - it's a basic, linear platformer. And gleamlight is bad even by basic, linear platforming standards.If this game were free I would give it a pass, but $20 is absolutely ridiculous. At the same cost you could get, for one example: bloodstained curse of the moon, muri, and crowtel renovations (all 3 of which are better linear platformers on their own). Even during a massive sale I’d avoid this one.(Steam might not be displaying it on here, but I got a refund)

_childDocuments_.review: 1.5hrs long if you take your time. The abilities unlocked had no rhyme or reason, and 2 or 3 of them are completely pointless. If this was a demo, it would be a 3 out of 5, but since I paid for a full game, I feel like I've been left  empty handed.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly not sure why this game is rated so poorly. I will agree that it is not a metroidvania and should have that tag removed. But for an action platformer, it's quite enjoyable. The game itself is pretty short even for going for both endings. The art is absolutely a dream to look at. Music is pretty good as well. The game does make the assumption that you'll play it a second time and maybe that's off putting for some. But I could tell at the end of my first full playthrough, I'd be playing again to unlock the rest of the game. I've played other games like this, so it's something I'm familiar with.The downsides for me are the following:- Dreadful controls at times- 0 recovery window after getting attacked- The price for such a short game- The world and its lore could need expanding to make the story actually a storyDespite these downsides, it's still an enjoyable game if you get it on sale like I did. It's not like HK and it's not worth 20$ for it's length. But the game does offer an experience that is worth putting a few hours in if you need something to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Gleamlight

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I had heard of it through Hollow Knight. I made the mistake of not reading reviews before purchasing and spent my $20 on it. At first, it seemed like a cute little magical game. The controls were my first complaint. I'm a PC user and it was weird figuring out how to move let alone attack. I had to change all of my controls to be able to do anything. When I left the first area and encountered my first enemy, It seemed to be decent enough. The enemies are unique at first but that leads me into my second complaint, none of the enemies are very engaging or different from each other and don't really tell much about the area or the story. They are all dark, red, disformed crystal creatures. Next, the fights. One thing I have to give the game is that the health system is very unique and interesting, with quite literally TAKING health from your enemies, and it being transferred to them when you get hit. However, this doesn't save the fights as they are slow and not very engaging, they're all around boring. I also noticed that the game isn't very good at telling you what to do, as I got stuck in an area for a bit because I couldn't figure out how to get out of it. This is my first review on a game on this account, at least for a long time from my knowledge. So I will close with saying that this game seems like it has potential, but all around it isn't good right now. If you want a better game, I suggest Hollow Knight of course since it is $5 less and has HOURS worth of game play while from what I've heard from others, this game has a couple hours worth of game play at best.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this nice looking game in the steam sale.It looked very beautiful and interesting so I tried it.The movement kinda nice, with you being able to cancel nearly all your mobility abilities, but not the platforming.It is NOT a metroid vania. It is an action platformer.You run through lots of corridors spammed with enemies.In one of the screens you have to jump up small blocks while six enemies attack you through walls, sometimes diagonally.The platforming is rather frustrating as you don't have coyote time (or very little) while jumping.The game has barely a story and no dialog. The enemies are stupid and get stuck a lot of times. Sometimes it seems like they just give up and stand there looking at you.It is very frustrating to play and you will die through a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. On the other hand the bosses are surprisingly easy and I often first tried them except for one that was aggravatingly difficult for all the wrong reasons.Overall the game plays more like a demo than a 17€ title.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10This is arguably great ideas executed poorly. The art is beautiful. The main character is charming enough. There is a “multiple endings” system that is kind of interesting. For the title menu and boss fights, the music is great… the rest of the game is bland and silent. But despite growing up playing tons of basic platformers without much story/narration…unfortunately this one just felt bland. Credit where it’s due, there have been QoL improvements since I first tried this on PS. But, fair warning… if you go for the trophies, this game becomes tedious fast. I’ve played the game front to back, back to front, rinse/repeat afew times to get all endings… took a couple hrs. Final trophy? “Die 100 times” If it takes about 5min to die each time, that’s 500min / 60min= 8.3hrs. …. Uncool. I’m sure they won’t see this, but total credit to the artist on this one though… I’d love to see their next project!

_childDocuments_.review: Hollow Knight might be Gleamlight's greatest curse. Developer DICO created a beautiful stained-glass graphic style for their platformer. Only that, on the very first look it's reminiscent of Hollow Knight, which can create specific expectations.		The truth is that Gleamlight plays nothing like Hollow Knight. It's much more simplified, shorter, without any metroidvania elements. It's an action platformer with a very basic gameplay formula.	The problems arise with various in-game mechanics being directly at-odds with eachother. The so called „unspoken story” might feel like narrative is non-existent. Gleamlight tries to convey it's plot through presentation. Unfortunately the inconsistent gameplay focusing on backtracking and re-runs of the game makes it really hard to get engaged. The poorly designed combat system is the final nail in the coffin. It devoids Gleamlight of any challenge and depth.	I see glimpses of passion and artistry within DICO's team of developers. I'm going to pay attention to their future projects. Regrettably, as for Gleamlight...   	I do not recommend this game.If you are interested in a really thorough review then check out my video about Gleamlight:
