_childDocuments_.review: How this got "very positive", I can only guess is down to troopers fans being a little over generous? It's a "mostly positive" at best.Pro's first...1. It looks nice. It really does look and feel like Starship Troopers from the 90's. 2. It's quite satisfying annihilating hordes of bugs with a well placed few units.3. It's challenging (but see cons)4. The music and sound effects are good.Con's...1. It's short. VERY short. Even if you take your time, it's done in a solid day of play. Not great for an "RTS".2. No multiplayer.3. No skirmish or scenario generator. It does have a whopping...TWO bonus levels, but they are fairly weak.4. It's not really an RTS. There is one central strategy, really. Edge forward, suppress and don't linger too long. It's also quite linear Which also removes a lot of strategy.5. Unit variety is pretty limited and not very exciting. Granted, the movie pretty much had two unit types, so they at least bolstered it up from that!6. And the biggest flaw for me (and everyone else, it seems) The scorpion bugs. They are the laziest game mechanic I've seen in a long while. Very large health pool, and really high damage. They can all but one shot your toughest units and the game just spams them at you to artificially hike the difficulty. Rather than being a challenging mechanic, they are frustrating and irritating. Sure they have counter units and there are tricks to beat them, but it doesn't make them any more fun to fight. The game just forces you to suddenly micromanage more.7. There are bugs...the crap, game ruing type. Sometimes units will fail to select. Sometimes they decide to just not fire at the enemy, and promptly die! 8. It can also be difficult to select a particular squad, even when your troops are spread out a bit, so using the ctrl + 1,2,3... function is HIGHLY recommended.9. It's predictable, meaning once you have the single basic strategy down, you can walk the game.10. Lacks camera rotation. Not a massive issue, but it would have been nice!If it were £10/15 I would happily to recommend it to Troopers fans, (but not to real RTS fans) but at £20+ don't bother, it's far too basic, short and outright infuriating at times. even as a fan of the movie, I'm not wowed by it and I doubt I'll replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive Starship Troopers fan - I loved this game. Is it the best? No, did it satisfy the need to kill some bugs? Yes! Massive shout-out to the devs for allowing me to relive some Starship Troopers memories. I just finished the campaign and a few scenarios - at the 18 hour mark. The campaign was enjoyable, albeit short. I would recommend this game for some simple man v bug blitzing. It really has the base of a great game,  but I think a few things were missing: 1. The music - I appreciate it may not be possible with copyright or something, but this game feels like it misses the core Starship Troopers vibe by just a touch. If the devs could get the OG Starship Troopers sound track, I think it would make the world of difference. 2. The cut-scenes were great, but felt a little shallow at times. The "go to war" should absolutely be a "Would you like to know more?" moment. 3. Don't let the bodies disappear! I want to see the physical signs of my labour!Some other reviews have had some awesome suggestions around different combat modes that should be expanded on - aka. Space, sector based planet siege, more grunt vs grunt. These all make me so excited and I would 100% go for these.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, its a ST game. It does everything ST. But there is soooo much more potential for this game. It just comes off as.... average. Compared to other slitherine games...Good first:1. Its starship troopers.2. Maps are fairly big, and game doesnt lag even when theres 100's of bugs on the map3. good progression system4. good for those of us RTS players ( Starcraft,, C&C ) who are used to spell casters, microing,, etc etc5. Fairly lengthy campaign.Make a coffee because here comes the bad:1. Game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Linear OMG. Its nice and challenging to play it all the way through, true. Yet there is absolutely NO replay-ability. Finishing the game doesnt grant you the ability to unlock ALL tech when you replay missions. Its literally replaying the exact same mission with the exact same tech.... but maybe with a higher difficulty.. Although I havent had any sort of incentive to play it on a harder difficulty,,, I didnt unlock anything...2. Omfg another desert planet. Feels a lot like " how can we replicate the first movie without actually using the first movie planet ",, well, this is exactly how you can do it. Whilst the cityscapes offer a bit more tactical play and various height adjustments, overall the maps are so bland and boring..... luckily there are bugs to kill otherwise you would go blind..... We could have gone anywhere or to multiple planets,, yet we get bogged down in a 20 mission campaign on the same damn planet.. for 12-15 hours ( i left my PC on today with the game loaded while i went out and had lunch for 2 hours lol )3. There are 10 something unit varieties, all with their own tech tree to unlock when they " rank up " ( only once ). HOWEVER.... There is literally no reason to use all of the tech. You can win every map with Rocket Troopers and basic infantry.... A fleet commander if you want to re-supply unit counts in the field or have a bombing run. The balancing is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥, and even when you unlock the BEST units in the game ( powersuit mobile infantry ), you can only use them in ONE single map and its not even the last map... Its nice to have variety, but there also needs to be > versatility <, but there is none. Just make mobile infantry and rocket troops and win the game. Mobile infantry upgrade to the shotgun anti-bug charge ability and rocket troopers upgrade to the napalm rocket strike to block choke-points etc etc and kill armoured units ( because literally nothing else can kill armoured units.. ) and done, easy.4. There is no map editor or mission editor, therefore there is no way to use all the tech you unlock. This is dumb as ♥♥♥♥.5. its basically a tower defense game with the option to push out and attack the spawning points,, realistically.All in all,, buy it if you llike starship troopers and cross your fingers for the developers to release more content. Otherwise give it a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR : a mix of Company of Heroes and a tower defense. Not a bad game, but feels unpolished and lack crucial features.I played the entire game in highest difficultySTR has a lot of renowned franchises, and ST:TC has a hard place to earn.The mechanics are very similar to the Company of Heroes series (and somewhat W40k : Dawn of War series)I would usually write a review with + and - but it feels wrong here. The game is not bad at all, but it just feels shallow in every area.Graphics : i wasn't very inspired by anything. 2 biomes is very little. Units don't shine either.Unit variety : only 10 (i count 3 mechs for 1), and you can win with 4 of them.Macro gestion : inexistent. Having more varied units means you have less turrets and mechs, that's a bad idea. The tech tree is replaced by a timer (and only exist in a few missions), you get no upgrades.Micro gestion : there is little micro since it is meant to be a tower defense.Bug variety : is rather fine, though fliers are mostly absentIA : inexistent, the bugs will just spawn waves at you until you kill them. They do not try to turn around flame grenades or fortified positions. They do not try to repopulate hives even though scarab tooltips say they are meant to.Map variety : bad. The game only features a quite long campaign (37 hours to complete, a few missions are hard, some are tedious). No procedural maps, no sandbox scenario.Multiplayer : none. Probably something to expect on that side, but should have been in the base game.General feeling : OK. You were promised bugs to kill, the game delivers. Don't expect more or you'll be disappointed. If you want a better STR, look for older ones or pay season pass and pray it gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: Would you like to know more?An absolute joy of a game packing all of the cheese you came to know and love from the 1997 movie. Simple controls for an RTS game, a genre I love but am terrible at actually playing. But the apparent simplicity hides a clever game: positioning your troops well is rewarded, with forming good kill zones, but failing to keep it in control means things go south FAST. One squad being overwhelmed by the Arachnids and you can suddenly be looking at a frantic leapfrog retreat, or a complete failure of your defensive lines. At first, I questioned the fact this game has no PVP, but the longer I played, I understood. The Bug threat is designed in a way that would not be even remotely balanced in the hands of a human player. I would absolutely love a coop campaign, or a coop horde defense mode, however. Each one of your units is good at something specific, and can be hard shutdown by one bug variant, or hard shutdown them the moment they appear. Knowing how to choose your troops and their special abilities for the situation is of utmost importance.The only criticisms I have so far: is that sometimes unit pathing derps out a bit, requiring another move click; right clicking to attack specific targets is sometimes finicky (you generally don't have to do that on a hordem however); and that when you have several units selected, pressing the special ability keybind only activates one of the squads, and you have to manually re-select to use the other squads' available cooldowns. Overall, great entry game for the RTS genre, and an enjoyable time overall. And remember: The Bug Stops Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Well, where to start. The game basically only has a campaign with two scenarios to play, but the campaign is pretty long and the missions are varied. From the bog-standard "defeat all enemies" to escort or even a stealth mission - the game offers a relatively wide variety. Missions that require you to clear bug nests usually also become gradually more difficult with modifiers to the bug lairs that get added over time during the mission. For example causing lairs to spawn more units before emptying out or adding tougher enemies, thus requiring you to overhaul your army with different units to combat the bugs efficiently.The "resources" you have are war-support, dropships and supply. War support is gained by doing objectives and is used to build turrets or buildings that allow you to call in specific troops. Every unit except the standard trooper needs a respective building. Supply is generally found on the map or in abandoned outposts and is used as a population capacity. Neither supply nor War support are up in the conventional sense, but held in reserve. Losing troops refunds the supply costs and losing turrets or higher end troops refunds their respective war support costs. Dropships on the other hand... serve a weird purpose and most missions don't offer ways to increase their numbers. These serve in three capacities. Most missions limit you to three of them.1. Bringing in new troops.2. Reinforcing existing troops that suffered casualties.3. Disbanding existing troops.Since dropships go on a short cooldown after being used, using them for 3. is not really.... useful. It is easier to just throw the unit you want to disband into the nearest bug lair since disbanding it via dropship does not give any benefits compared to just letting them die.Since it's Starship troopers the enemies are kinda limited in variability, but they did a good job in distinguishing similar bugs from from one another. For example the Warrior bug comes in three varieties. The normal warrior, large squad size and low durability, the Tiger bugs, low squad size but decently armored and a smaller version of warriors, which I forgot the name of, coming out of nests as a group of swarmers defending a position with very low durability but a very big swarm.  Similar are the Terran units, every unit can fill one niche. Even the standard troopers are good if you need anti-air and the elite-specialisation makes all of the Terran roster more versatile. I've only ever felt that the sniper team under performs a lot for taking the same unit space as a combat engineer team with flamethrowers. My only complaint balance wise apart from the sniper team is the, imho, overtuned scorpion bugs, which are way too tanky on higher difficulties for their damage output and numbers in which they show up.The narrator reminded me a lot of the movies too, which is good. Mission objectives and the in-mission dialogue are also very Starship troopers, even the tutorial sets it up pretty nicely. Every mission intro is also like a TV-News segment, which is a nice touch. The biggest complaint in general I have is one of a missed opportunity, but hopefully that will be implemented later. There is no survival mode at all.I also haven't encountered any bugs apart from the ones you shoot at, or on higher difficulties get eaten by.All in all, it is pretty good.If this convinced you to give this a try, I hope you are wiling to do your part for the Federation!

_childDocuments_.review: Dr Bright here for another review.  This time a game I've waited for with baited breath for a long time and to my knowledge there is only two other Starship troopers games in existence...a FPS and another RTS and both sadly not on steam.I've only played a couple of missions so far and I've enjoyed what I got my hands on.  Its a more squad based RTS then it is a base builder, though some base building elements exist.  Units, instead of being built in buildings are dropped near comm stations by dropship, which also send in reinforcements to heal a squad when some bad luck or a pathfinding hiccup gets a squad partially turned into bug chow...and the bugs are vicious.  They will do all they can to munch on your minions like the bugs have the munchies and your men are all skittles.  Luckily your men have a nice pile of weapons, from the basic rifleman and engineers to plop down turrets to marauder power armor...and you'll need it as the bugs come in a nasty selection of flavours, such as the regular warrior bugs to the tanker bugs.The game has a few little hiccupts but its nothing to really worry about and the very few bugs I've encountered are barely noticable.If you're a starship troopers fan, then this game is for you and even if you aren't its pretty decent too.The doctor most certainly recommends this game so sign up.Service guarantees Citizenship!

_childDocuments_.review: Why? Because I like Starship Troopers, it was a great movie, wished there was a game after watching the movie back then.This is a good game, hope the dev add more story campaign and Achievements.I would buy those expansion campaign in DLC as long the story and hopefully additional new units along with it.Starship Troopers: Terran Command is a real-time strategy game based on the classic 1997 sci-fi film of the same name. Developed by The Artistocrats and published by Slitherine Ltd., this PC title puts you in charge of leading a Mobile Infantry squad against an alien enemy known as “the Bugs”. With its faithful recreation of the movie’s aesthetic, engaging tactical combat system, and plenty of content to explore, Starship Troopers: Terran Command is a great way to experience the Starship Troopers universe.The game begins with you, as commander of the Mobile Infantry squad, being sent on a mission to investigate an abandoned base on one of the Bug’s home planets. After establishing a foothold in this hostile environment, your task is to build up your base and defend against wave after wave of relentless bug attacks while also using special operations teams and airstrikes to further disrupt their forces. The strategic layer is nicely done, allowing for different tactics depending on what resources are available and how powerful the enemy forces are. You can focus on defense or offense; expand your base by constructing new buildings or deploying troops directly onto field missions; deploy air strikes and artillery barrages for area damage; use special ops teams to infiltrate enemy bases for reconnaissance or sabotage objectives; upgrade existing structures or research new ones that offer enhanced defensive capabilities like turrets and walls. As you progress through each mission, you will earn XP which can be used to unlock more advanced units such as tanks, power armor troopers, mechs, heavy weapons specialists etc., giving you access to even more tactical options in battle. Gameplay-wise Starship Troopers: Terran Command plays out like any other RTS title with basic resource management mechanics intertwined with combat scenarios across multiple maps. The core gameplay loop consists of gathering resources (in this case it’s “morale points” instead of resources), building/upgrading structures within your base/base camp (such as barracks, research labs etc.), recruiting soldiers from these facilities into squads then taking them into battle against bugs in various locations across the map where they must complete certain objectives before returning back safely (or not). On top of all that there’s also an additional meta-game element called “tactical decisions” which involve making snap judgments about various choices presented during key moments throughout each mission - do I send my troops forward towards an objective? Or retreat back? Do I divert all available personnel towards defending our territory from encroaching bug forces? Or launch a preemptive strike against them first? These decisions can have both immediate consequences but also affect how future events play out too so it pays off greatly if players take time between missions to think carefully about their strategy ahead rather than just rushing headfirst into every fight without considering potential repercussions down the line! Graphically speaking Starship Troopers: Terran Command looks quite good despite its age – character models are detailed enough although some textures appear blurry at times due mainly because it was developed using Unreal Engine 3 rather than 4+ versions released since then while environments look suitably alien and foreboding when viewed close up but slightly bland when zoomed out further away from ground level perspective . While cutscenes unfortunately rely heavily upon pre-rendered 2D images instead of 3D rendered scenes which could have been much more immersive thanks again probably due limitations tech wise back then plus there isn't really any voice acting either aside few lines spoken randomly by characters during dialogs but overall visuals seen here are still quite decent.The sound design is also quite good, featuring a mix of sci-fi inspired score composed by the talented Marco Beltrami and more militaristic tunes that play when your troops are in battle against bugs with each theme fitting its respective situation perfectly. Sound effects themselves aren't anything particularly noteworthy but they do get job done just fine so no complaints there either. In conclusion, Starship Troopers: Terran Command is a great game for any fan of the original movie or someone who enjoys RTS titles in general. The strategic layer offers plenty of depth while combat scenarios can be both thrilling and challenging depending on how you approach them. Graphically it’s somewhat dated but still looks good enough to pass muster plus sound design really helps bring atmosphere needed for such type experience alive even further thanks to its combination between futuristic music and traditional military style tracks playing during battle scenes which all adds up nicely together into an enjoyable package worthy checking out if you have interest genre as whole or simply want something different from usual options available nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Starship Troopers, a film that came at the wrong time and was widely misunderstood at the time of its release. It's an overtly cynical and over-the-top criticism of fascism made in the 1990s when fascism seemed as distant a threat as WWII. So, if you're going to make a game about it in 2022, you have to go for broke, because fascism is a real threat again, and the 1990s-style inclusive warmongering fascism in the film now appears slightly more optimistic than the path we're currently headed down.So if you're going to make a Starship Troopers game that is both relevant to the times and true to the source material, you have to *go for broke,* not half-ass a few "Would you like to know more?"s throughout the cutscenes. You need to demonstrate the wrongness of the world of Starship Troopers while providing a compelling gameplay loop. The humans are not the heroes in Starship Troopers, and a game about the Federal Republic's Mobile Infantry should remind you of that at every available opportunity.Terran Command does neither. It half-asses the gameplay loop with a same-y RTS structure, and its cutscenes and voiceovers seem to suggest that the creators of the game either aren't in on the joke that the humans are the bad guys, or didn't care to explore that central aspect of the story.To be fair, the bugs look great and are perfectly reminiscent of the film's CGI, which surprisingly holds up even today. But--there are probably a dozen better RTSes to play even if you love the film. And if you love the game for what it is, you should probably rewatch the film and think about what it's *actually* trying to say.That's gonna be a no from me, dawg.

_childDocuments_.review: Courage, Duty, Honor!We call upon our troopers, in this our darkest hour,Our way of life is what we're fighting for,The flag that flies above us, inspires us each day,To give our very best, in every way!It's a good day to die,When you know the reasons why,Citizens, we fight for what is right,A noble sacrifice,When duty calls, you pay the price,For the Federation I will give my life!You will not find many good RTS games on the market. But be aware, this game is not a classic RTS. No base building or resources collecting. But it is single player RTS. How often we can enjoy such things this days?Is it the best rts game out there? No, but honestly, was the starship troopers the best SF move ever?Nope, but we still enjoyed it. Here is the same. It is a very decent game, with a cool campaign. Game is really based on a move (the first one not the abomination sequels movies).We have even a reference to the animation movies (Power Suit Troopers), where logic in the Terran and bugs military was on a better level.  Surprising just a few game bugs in the game filled with bugs (sometimes units can get stuck on corners when ordered to move). But nothing really annoying. If because of this you will loose a local battle, no big deal. They are just a canon fodder. You can always order reinforcements. Sound: Deep inside I was hoping to hear original voices. But the new cast is ok. Cool thing - units voices are changing during underground missions.Story. Cool, we have a tutorial reference on Klendathu. Then is a new story on one planet. Instead of a mission biffing you have "Do You Want To Know" mission preparation. Really cool.Achievements. For people who likes them. 100% are working. Even more, for every mission you have 2 achievements and you can see them in the game menu during the mission. No need for any guides. Just open menu during a mission and you can see possible achievements. Really nice. You can find few additional ones (like kill x number of bugs) but it is impossible to miss them. Scenarios/workshop. Usually I'm avoiding them. But one achievement forced me to start a scenario. But no regrets. I played ambush on Whiskey Outpost (planet P). Sadly, history did not repeat itself. No survivors this time.... What else. With a mission progress, Tier of the battle increase. Mean more bugs. Sometimes it is easier to clear bug caves on a lower level. The power is in the number. And bugs have numbers....Units: When achieving elite level, you can choose a special ability. In the beginning I thought, it is just a grenade, or  incendiary grenade. I will be not using it. I was wrong. It is really something that you need. You can stop an attack with few  incendiary grenades. And to win you need few types of units. You cant just build on type. Like I said. It is not the best game ever. But I played almost 30 hours and I enjoyed them all. I managed to finish the main campaign, get 100% achievements and I had a nice time.Just do your part, and play the game. Remember, Service Guarantees Citizenship...

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the actual Starship Troopers (1997) film this game is a great tribute to the saga. It's a very good and modern RTS with one of the best level designs I've seen in the genre. Despite minimal to none base construction (only possible to build specific buidlings in specific locations to advance the unit tech tree) it follows Company of Heroes "capture base stations and strategic points" style to get resources. The mission campaign despite relatively short (10-15h) is very well made and can grab it's hooks into the player. There is a good progression of difficulty and very unique missions to undertake. There is also steam workshop support for player made missions (the community has already made incredible maps including some remakes from the popular film) and despite not yet present, a mode focused on replayability it is planned to be added  sometime in 2023. There are also some official challenge maps that range from Spec Ops missions, to a experimental wave survival mode. A great game for RTS fans, go out there and Kill some Bugs!

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little hesitant to grab this game but after seeing the reviews posted and noting I didn't really have anything better to do, I went ahead and made the executive decision to get this time. I'm glad I did. You'll see some reviews by try-hards saying this game doesn't have this feature or that whatever. You can safely ignore these guys, like the people of the opposite sex probably do, and let them fire rants and salt into the gaping void of internet entitlement and wish fulfillment.  I'm an RTS guy and I like huge battles, setting up engagements, losing units but getting the goal accomplished. This game delivers what I wanted to see in an RTS game centered around fighting the bug hordes. Are there things that could be done better? Probably, but maybe you should look at yourself first and ask yourself what you could be doing better, with your life in general, before you ask this game. No, battling the Arachnid hordes won't stop the inevitable existential dread that creeps up in your thoughts from time to time before you drown it out with Monster Energy, overpriced restaurant food and Tik-Toks with slowed down versions of popular songs. No it won't fool the angel of death when she - yes "she" - inevitably mows your mortal soul to power the holiest and unholiest of the celestial engines of war that we mortals are completely unable to comprehend. It will, however, be a game that is entertaining, delivers what it promises and actually has a pretty decent atmosphere and story to go along with it. Also the developers seem to have plans to add content, so that's good too.

_childDocuments_.review: If you really like Starship Troopers and either have it already or it's on deep sale then maybe get & play it.I went in knowing I wouldn't like the lack of this feature. It's the reason I didn't buy it before. (I bought this via Humble subscription) All the best / most popular RTS's have tactical pause for a reason. That reason being micromanagement required in games of the genre. The first few levels it's not that big of a deal, relatively casual, but on missions a little bit in where you have more than a few troops of varying types against hoards of bugs and you need to micro their movement and all their different skills as each troop type has different skills and two different skills to choose from when a unit hits max rank, so that's even more needing to select just the right unit in a split second.One of the replies I see to this is "But then the game would be too easy!" That's what I call "false difficulty" if me not being able to control the game is where the difficulty comes from and I consider it a bad game.BUT! There's other mechanics to partially make up for this... that the game also fails to implement.A big part of the micro management is getting all your units to where you want them and in having certain units be in specific places relative to others. When you right click you can drag toward a direction and it will place a line, always a straight line, of your troops sort of broadsiding the enemy. I'm not sure how it calculates which unit goes where but I don't think I have control over that either. The game does have line of effect blocking so soldiers won't shoot if another blocks them generally, with exceptions.You can spend some time telling all your units to get in a specific formation with flamethrowers just barely in front and in the middle of riflemen units with snipers and grenade launchers behind them, but as soon as you need to push forward it's a straight line they'll end up in. They move together relatively well, pathing is pretty good, but I can't tell the engineer/flamethrower dudes to stay in just barely front of the riflemen or whatever. You can't save formations where they try to stay roughly a certain space away from each other. I'd have a few different formations I'd save where I'd say specific classes should be at certain locations and use them for various situations like when there's enemies only to one front or from multiple.Attack Move command is even more atrocious! Unlike the regular right click and drag which way your troops will be facing & broadsiding, you hit A then left click and whatever way the game thinks they should be facing at the end of the move is how they will you have no choice. But wait there's more! Along the way to the location if a troop encounters an enemy they will start attacking and moving toward the enemy even past where you told them to go, and in the case of engineer/flamethrower dudes who come in groups of 3 they tend to run ahead to get into attack range then quickly get swarmed and killed by bugs as they run ahead of all other units.There's multiple reasons I disliked Warcaft 3 and it's because of  levels. You know the ones. The ones where they give you a set few number of units and expect you go through some cave system or whatever and they're to make their game more like how DoW2's gameplay is but it will never be because it's not balanced like that. Many, but not all, of these levels end up feeling just flat and frustrating not fun .Almost all skills are on a cooldown timer AFAIK, which is nice.As I've said before in this review there's a variety of unit types that feel like they each have their place. Each type has one ability to start with and your choice of one of two skills when it hits max rank. There's your standard grunt riflemen who have assault rifles and a grenade special skill. Engineer types have flamethrowers and their special skill is to build different turrets (I've seen machinegun, rocket, and grenade) but that requires a special type of points spent for each placed. Laser riflemen with energy based guns whose special I forget but it might have increased fire rate. Snipers who have higher range with a special that makes them move and shoot faster. Grenade launcher dudes with of course grenade launchers can lob a volley of grenades. Rocket launcher guys also obviously have rocket launchers and their special is a higher damage rocket attack. You also have coms guys who allow you to reinforce anywhere I forget their weapon. And commanders... inspire others or something I forget about this one. That's what I've encountered so far.The mission's story is what you'd expect from Starship Troopers and it's enjoyable in that way.

_childDocuments_.review: "Starship Troopers: Terran Command" is a true-to-the-universe and quite fun real time strategy game, with heavy emphasis on company-level infantry tactics.Playable content:- 1 tutorial mission.- 19 campaign missions.- 2 special scenarios.- units from Star Ship Troopers 1, Starship Troopers 3 and Starship Troopers: Invasion movies. The Good:- solid mission & character writing (as far as Starship Troopers logic goes).- FedNet propaganda reels. - developers managed to honor the universe quite well in terms of map design, unit design, voice overs, dialogues, etc.- units are unique and fun. - the game can be quite challenging, sometimes presenting players with difficult decisions which may or may not pay off.- decent mission variety, even though the core of gameplay is all the same.- non-linear approach to many missions allows for some creative decisions.The Bad:- for a game heavily emphasizing interplay between different units, it lacks some basic features which could have been useful, namely a "formations" menu to determine how groups of different units should position themselves on the battlefield. Its absence makes the game heavy on micromanagement... maybe too heavy at times, even though that's basically the name of the game.- no ability to build and repair some of common structures (like heavy machineguns on towers or gates) located on many maps, making them irreplaceable once lost. - no multiplayer or other features beyond campaign and a couple of special missions.- the price is a bit too high for a game largely limited to campaign. Conclusion: good game, especially for fans of Starship Troopers movies. But best purchased on sale due to its limited scope.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey there,Firstly, I would like to say, I love the starship troopers franchise. It is basically an unadulterated viewing of patriotism and violence gone mad. I killed a bug, have you? I'm doing my part, are you? Would you like to know more.Basically the idea of any game regarding the Starship Troopers franchise has to be be one thing and that is, atmospheric. If you don't feel like you are in this crazy system with nothing but runaway testosterone and blinding loyalty and pride and everything for not just your country or planet but your citizen status, well, you are doing something horribly wrong. This game fails on basically every single level. The amazing music you would expect to find in this game is just not there.The outrageous lines are just not there.The atmosphere is just not there. The graphics are what you might expect, nothing amazing but nothing so terrible that you could complain about it.The unit control is clunky and at times, not responsive. The game is entirely rock-paper-shotgun. Everything requires your attention.Unit AI is dreadful. Back to the good old days of your left flank and right flank switching when you move for no reason.Repetitive nature and one set of scenery.So lets get started with how it feels to play.You get in, you expect some crazy drill sergeant or somebody to come at you with some verbal abuse and colorful bug killing metaphors, instead you get colonel happy pants. No introduction, your learn how to play mission is dreadfully basic but so is the game. You get told simply what to do and you just go through the motions, no surprises, nothing. Since this is technically your first mission, its a bit strange that you are being told how to do things when you are in charge already. Probably means you can't skip it if you don't want to repeat boot camp each time you play. Nothing feels dangerous at all, your unit composition is just kind of bland. Nothing really has personality. Here is your standard troops. . .yippee I guess. Here is your other standard troop. . . woop? Here is your blah blah blah. You get a handful of specialists but honestly, I don't really know why. The balance is pretty terrible. Get a fleet liaison and call in airstrikes which kill weak bugs and half the hp of strong ones. So exciting, now sit back and wait 30 seconds to do it again. . . *sarcastic* hooray!The wide range of troops feels pointless, they all have their niche since its rock-paper-shotgun but most of them aren't worth getting. In maps where you need a big army fighting along a long front, you can't hop from one battle to another and use abilities. So it becomes tedious. Units don't have priorities so will regularly be shooting the wrong things. An armored unit is hitting you from range, well, I got rocket launchers and they are attacking the weak unarmored horde that are being wiped out by the units that are getting slammed by the armored units. . . . great. . . guess I have to hold their hands as they cross the road as well. There just isn't anything that makes it fun about doing it. As for the commands, they don't always work. Tell a unit to throw a grenade and there is a chance they just bug out and don't do it. Or tell them to attack a bug and there is no line of sight, they suddenly stand there and do nothing even if they are attacked by other things. The end tier marauders are both amazing and pathetic at the same time not that you get to play more than a couple missions with them. The giant mech suits of death are fun but also not that practical. Takes about 3 shots for them to die from the right enemy and so you need to guard them with an army to make them practical and if you have an army to spare, its better to just throw in another 2 rocket infantry for the same supply. As for bugs, this game has them, not just the creepy crawling ones you get to shoot but units not responding to commands, not using special abilities but my favorite one must be a logic one. You order 2 or more sets of rifleman up a small corridor with move attack and they will try and leapfrog each other, constantly removing line of sight to allow for the squad next to them to shoot until they just run straight up to and in to the enemy. You can set formations, directions etc for your teams but whenever you order them somewhere, its back to close line. You also get unwanted camera movement, unit icons moving randomly, hard to select units on the field. Ooh and not so much a bug but whenever you get orders or they give an in-game cinematic, it slows time, not stopping it, just slowing it. Which means if you are in combat and you need to do something, you can either cancel the exposition or suffer the consequences. I once lost 3 squads to bug plasma while I was being told an enemy attack was on its way and I needed to hold that position. . . .which was now decimated. As for the icing on the cake, the video clips are basically non-existent. Its some picture and half the time, the federation flag from the movie. A cap trooper walking on and some very unenthusiastic narration. Also, the interactions with the command structure as well as the overarching plot. It is plain and simply dreadful. Even when I'm doing the end missions, I feel like there is no gravitas behind it, just another day at work and nobody cares. They hint at things but then don't go any further. They constantly leave you outside of the loop and that is it. The morality of the command is to just let everybody die because they don't matter. The federation might be bastards but they aren't wasteful. They aren't going to order multiple squads of troops to stay and defend a position with no strategic, tactical or well, any value whatsoever when they will be overrun and there is a way to escape. Half the missions feel this way. Just pointless. Like whoever made the game just came up with 1 mission he wanted to do and then the rest were there to pad the games run time. This game is a masterclass in how to not do something. It takes all the source material and fails it completely. The game itself is pretty much a one map repetitive game through multiple hours of repeating itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it and wow, this was some LEGIT RTS. Unit balance was pretty solid, the art design and sound design were great, acting was hammy in the right kind of way for Starship Troopers, bug design was true to lore, gameplay rewarded good micro and good positioning, playing it on 4/5 difficulty was a real challenge with only a couple restarts but battles and missions really had that sense of desperation that just vibes with the theme of mobile infantry.There were a few things that I felt weren't great balance - the mk2 troopers' melee ability is basically useless since it sweeps EVERYTHING, friendlies included (make this not deal friendly fire like basically everything else doesn't.) The combat engineers are almost impossible to level because they're so short range, require a lot of kills and block line of sight for your damage dealers. They feel worthless against nearly every bug. Make them transparent to your other units, so they can stand in front and actually do the job of stunning. The fleet liason needs more range, they're a PAIN to level up and their level up skills aren't as good as the default one.Rifle troopers need something that sets them apart. They're brutal with shotguns, but the short range grenade pack is a liability and once you get mk2 troopers they're kinda worthless.And the marauder bombardment needs to do more. I'd like to just see more skills for marauders.Overall though, this was super satisfying. I loved how most every unit had a really clearly defined role and tons of micro opportunities, you never felt safe even with a deathball of the right unit composition, I liked how they encouraged you to be at several places at once.Even if you aren't into starship troopers, this is a SUPERBLY designed RTS that rewards thoughtful play and quick thinking. Please god make more planets and campaigns. Even if the unit compositions don't change at all. Maybe even make the bugs playable and add in multiplayer similar to early 40k dawn of war. This has the bones of a truly great multiplayer 1v1 or 2v2 game.

Some abilities seem useless at first but most have their uses, there are counters and counters to counters, it's all about understanding your enemy, and your units.Something this game does that no other game does, is the lack of multiplayer, not even a 1v1, you don't even get to play as the bugs! _childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend it ... it's crap.It's one of those games that insists on choking itself while deep throating it's source material, and paradoxically screwing up the theme in the process.The voice acting is atrocious. It's milking the whole "Would'ya like to know more" bs in the most bland and uninteresting way, possible and the core gameplay loop is beyond effed.Their idea of difficulty is essentially doubling your damage output on easy, or subsequently taking half away for the difficult option ... and relies much too heavily on unit micro-management. Pausing the action would have been a good idea in order to set up some tactics.I get the whole "more meat for the grinder" stuff, but the whole point of the books was that even though humanity is essentially stuck as a fascist parody of itself, picking fights with aliens on the far side of the galaxy for no good reason other than to enact some sort of effed up manifest destiny crap while also getting rid of some undesirables, and when it all turns into the massive cluster♥♥♥♥ of "oh man... those guys are actually waay more fascistic, prepared and have a lot more expendable individuals than we have " thing is held together by the struggles certain people face in that universe. This game misses the point entirely... which is weird since the gameplay is geared towards that hero-based branch of RTS games.... so that whole leveling up after you kill some ♥♥♥♥ mechanic is complete garbage because it's temporarily mission locked stuff in the beginning, and so for absolutely no reason other to make sure you lose some units before that idiot of a CO of yours figures out it'd be a good idea to requisition you the proper counter-measures for the scenario you are in. ... which you probably won't have in the next mission.oh... that CO is the guy who's voice actor is so out of it, muting the game and reading the subtitles makes the experience 10 times more enjoyable. He also decides to force you disobey some " stay there and die for zi greater good " bs orders that make no sense and is subsequently removed from the picture (temporarily i bet because i started writing this review after having to save scum the following mission since it's a crappy escort mission in which you can't lose any unit... by which i mean... it's ok if you lose a unit... but can't lose a squad. ... which brings me to the lack of care that went into designing their scenarios.)Oh... and it glitches like nuts.So yeah... a glitchy game that sucks off the memes associated with the source material, slow paced, inconsistent, weirdly thought out, with no real point to it other than " let's basically play some missions which look like that one movie ".... oh ... and it's so brilliantly designed that when you do get stuck having to save scum a stupidly designed escort mission, both the bugs and marines behave in unpredictable RNG ways. For example, that escort mission I mentioned has this situation in which it pits you against two tiger bugs which are blatantly impervious to pretty much anything short of a grenade to the face, and the only guy in the squad that can lob them randomly decides to forget he's got an unlimited supply while the two snipers get their feet bitten off by bugs while this insipid bastard figures out how to tell his prick from his elbow. I got past that point by essentially save scumming the exact same sequence of events because there was a chance this prick could fire off a damn grenade at the right time... and it took 12 tries to do so.Oh... and your entire squad of however many riflemen stop shooting at the incoming horde of bugs to revel in the glory of that one guy who throws a grenade wihich has an effective range that's so unbelievably badly thought out, that if you do decide to lob one, the enemy is so close that half your squad will get mowed down while they remain busy staring at the guy instead of shooting the enemy.There's also this other mission that basically spawns an endless amount of bugs if you decide to go back and cover your rear in the by taking out a specific bug nest, and only if you have units past a certain point, and after which, when you decide you're bored and want to move them, the horde just ... sort of forgets about it.Immersion breaking ♥♥♥♥ like this is abundant a.f. If you're a fan of RTS games in general, this isn't for you.If you're a fan of ST ... and you can stomach this crap .. you're probably not a real fan.. you just like shower scenes.And if you're a fan of that movie... ... you're better off seeing that movie again instead of playing this.I mean... like why the ♥♥♥♥ would you go through the trouble of pissing away half the money you can make on a game on royalties to the holder of whatever IP you wan to use... go out of your way in blowing the fan-base with trailers and dev talks and whatnot, telling them the reason you've decided to use the property is to bring the universe alive... and not profiting of of the fact that you know for a fact that your slow paced piece of crap  which'd go well past it's "2 hour game time till you can return it" before revealing itself to be a boring piece of junk which will inevitably disappoint and further ruin the IP.Why... for money of course ... well ... ya got mine... enjoy it... but for the price I paid for this piece of crap, I'll squeeze every last drop while taking a dump on your game.This game is nothing more than a lazy cash grab at best, and if you strip away all the Starship Trooper stickers off of it, it's a bad RTS with half the functionality cut away, bad voice acting, and stupidly designed missions.

_childDocuments_.review: After about 11 hours of game play and blowing through the Campaign, I can definitely say this is a must buy with a huge asterix on it...The Story is fun, cheesy and captures the movies propaganda feel to move the story along between missions. The Voice acting leaves a little to be desired, but its not the worst I've heard in a game before. Before this came out, I watched a few videos of gameplay footage so I knew I wasn't going to be getting 'Starcraft' and more Dawn of War 2. I would've liked if this game had more of a base building aspect to it but that maybe that's something they can do if they make another game. Visually, the game looks great and there's a good variety in maps and missions, considering this takes place on a desert bug planet there isn't a whole lot you can do to make each map super appealing but a lot of the mountain maps, city maps and even the underground complex type maps are fine.There's a ton to see from all the starship troopers movies in this - so if you really liked the CGI movies you'll enjoy seeing the Powered Suit Cap Troopers in the late game, the Marauders from Starship Troopers 3 pop up, and even the pulse rifle troopers from the second movie appear. There's a TON of different bug types as well to fight - you might recognize some of them from the old first person shooter game like the Tiger Bug.Now for the downside of this - there is only the campaign and two scenarios to play.That's it, once you beat them, you've essentially beat the game and there isn't too much in the way of replay value unless you want to play at a higher difficulty. This game is in serious need of a free play mode or something where you can play on all the of the maps against waves of bugs or something, I'm talking like a game type where you defend that fort on Planet P against the massive horde of bugs or something.On top of that it feels like the AI is pretty cheap in some places. A lot of missions have you clearing out bug lairs and things like that which will spawn waves of bugs to take out your troopers, but a lot of the time they'll drop a special type bug like the scorpion bug that will incinerate anything as soon as it pops up out of the ground. I played on Medium for most of the game and there were some very unforgiving missions where RNG played a huge factor.all that being said if you like RTS games and are a fan of starship troopers, this is the game we've been waiting for, if they add the free play feature or something I would say this is the essential Starship Troopers game until we get a proper first person shooter that's not an ARMA 3 mod.

I can say that "I am doing my part.", and I recommend without a doubt that anyone who has not gotten this game should get it as well. And always remember "Service Guarantees Citizenship."Anyway serious talk, I love this game, it's an interesting take on the rts genre and does it beautifully. The game mechanics are smooth and not hard to wrap your head around. Every unit bug, or human fulfills a different role and are useful/annoying no matter what mission you are doing. The story is great and spans 19 whole missions so you will spend a good bit getting through it. If I had to complain about anything, it would have to be the lack of content after the campaign. The two extra missions are cool and all, but I still wish there was more and am hoping they add more in the coming months. I also wish the game had a unique multiplayer where players play bugs, or humans in an nearly endless war of attrition. I think it would be a great take on an rts multiplayer. Having player controlled bugs attempt to dislodge human defenders, or Humans attempting to clear out Bug Hives on a massive battlefield would be amazing. Aside from those two I think the ability to make custom mission through and editor would be nice as well although It can come much later than other things. I'd also like to see the ability to gain more supplies and war support through other means other than objectives. Like calling in supplies to fill and empty depot with war support and vice versa.Anyway that's how I feel about this game and what I hope to see in the future. And as always "A good bug, is a dead bug."The 2024 Update:Since my attention has been brought back to this review, here's an update. I will be going over the base game and the DLCs in this update.Base Game:I still recommend the base game, it was and still is a fun experience you can sink many hours into. The addition of extra scenario missions, and the mission editor help fix the content issue that game had originally since you can always find a new mission to play via the community. Couple all this with the modding scene, and I can say that Starship Troopers Terran Command is a great game.Raising Hell:I won't sugar coat it. Raising hell is not the greatest dlc ever. Honestly it is a rather large disappoint from my perspective. The new campaign doesn't hold my attention that well, combined with how short the campaign is. I think they could have done a lot better with the story especially if they had shifted the attention off the Mobile Infantry onto the Mercs. I think the Campaigns ending was bland and uninteresting. It would have been more interesting if we had several more missions focused on the Merc's point of view. That alone however, isn't why I rate the campaign so poorly. Outside of the campaign the units are abysmal. Although they have rather unique designs for the units, they always end up falling short except for the Frag Mercs. The frag mercs are the only salvageable unit in my opinion. Their unique design and concept make them a fun unit to micro within your force, and the unit itself is fairly powerful. Aside from that the Rifleman Mercs are a decent concept, but generally perform poorly compared to normal Rifleman squads. The Merc officer is essentially just a tactical officer. The Engineering Bi-ped is another salvageable unit that does its job well. Finally the shredder merc is in my opinion the worst by far.  The fact that a mission revolves around their use is a massive blow to the campaign as the Shredder does not do well in my opinion. It does awful anti-air damage, which is supposed to be its primary role. Although it's deploy-able mode is unique, you have to use it all the time for shredders to actually work. Outside of their deployed state, they feel like they fire bean bags at the high hp flyers you're supposed to use them against. All in all, they suffer from a lack of damage, and the investment you put into them isn't worth it since a normal rifle squad could do the same thing at a lower cost. Aside from those, the Power-suit Officer and Incinerators are nice to have and are decent at their roles., The Personally I rate the Raising hell DLC a 4/10. Urban Onslaught:Urban onslaught is a major step up from Raising hell. Although the story isn't amazing. It at minimum held my attention while I was playing the campaign. The units hold up greatly as well. The Police squad is an interesting take on a rifleman squad and serve the role of a front-line rather well. The only issue the Police squad has is the fact it's phased out by the Riot Squad. The Riot Shields squad is a very powerful unit. It works similarly to the Frag Mercs while being a larger squad, and a very tanky squad at that. Due to their ability they can tank any source of damage in the game while coming out of said damage with only scratches. This makes them the best front-line in the game, and I found myself relying on them for most the campaign. Technicians are a new Engineer unit with a variety of interesting and useful emplacements. The squad itself however performs rather poorly as they trade the flame thrower for a taser. I do not recommend using them for combat unless you're forced to do so. The Cyclone, or the Hover Tank is a fun vehicle to have. It is fast, and deals decent damage. Personally I would not spam them as they work better as a simple IFV that gives your squads an extra bit of firepower. The Peacekeeper biped helps serve as an alternative to the Radio Operator, capable of placing landing zones while also being a decent support unit with its grenade launcher. The Pegasus, or the Gunship is rather underwhelming in my opinion. I had trouble finding it useful as aerial bugs easily countered it. If you aren't facing any form of bug air support, then it is an easily abuse-able unit that can shred basic bugs and deal hefty damage to larger bugs. Lastly the Rainmaker is an incredible unit. It serves as the first real artillery unit you have outside of turrets. It is useful both deployed and undeployed. Although I personally found the text for its elite drone ability broken, the unit still performed very well. The Rainmaker is in my opinion the second most powerful unit this dlc adds behind the Riot Shield Squad. Lastly the J.A.C is rather underwhelming, it severs as an alternative to Rocket Troopers, but it feels like the Rocket Trooper was nerfed so that this unit could be an alternative. J.A.Cs can't fire over other units leading to issues when attempting to design fire lines in tight areas that include them. J.A.Cs do have a jumppack which can be used to scale terrain for better vantage points, but I found this ability nearly useless. There was simply no place where the ability was actually useful since I simply couldn't scale certain terrain, or there was no terrain to scale. On the final mission the jump ability isn't even use-able. The J.A.C is simply disappointing in my opinion and I would have preferred Rocket Troopers 9 times out of 10 if they had the range. In terms of level design I liked the Urban Onslaught levels although the Bridge one did end up as an awful slog that took over  an hour to beat on brutal. The final mission suffers as well and personally I think it would of been better if they treated the final hive similar to how they did the super hive from the starport scenario. I rate the Urban Onslaught dlc an 8/10. It is a fun experience, the new units are fun to play with, and the story, although not amazing, wasn't so bad I hated playing through it.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through on the hardest difficulty and had a really good time. Quite a few missions felt like a real tug of war and I had to fight for every inch of progress. Took 15.5 hours to finish on the hardest difficulty. You can no doubt finish the game alot quicker on lower difficulties but I felt like Brutal is the only way to get a true sense of being overwhelmed because you do less damage which allows the bugs to close the gap before they are killed.Theres no base building so its just controlling units. You do have to select platforms to upgrade to buildings in order to unlock units throughout the mission but thats about it. The story is more akin to the movies instead of the book. Its entertaining and cheesy and I loved it. I've noticed there are references to the movies. The overall theme follows the movies as well.There are a good variety of units on both sides. Theres a select few units that are alot better then others and theres a a couple units that are direct counters to certain bug units. Theres a good variety of bugs to kill although there seems to be a problem with their spawning priority. The majority of the time I spent fighting 3 types of bugs and the AI would rarely or never spawn tankers or some of the lesser units. The last Starship Troopers game was in 2005 and the fact it took this long for someone else to mess with the IP is disappointing because there is alot of potential. Its a good, fun, simple game that lets you kill all them bugs. I hope it does well enough to warrant content updates or expansions because I would definitely purchase it. I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Obligatory TL;Dr:  Great game, its not done, hope they add features later.So I conquered it.  I had a lot of trouble stopping playing because it is addictive and fun.  I look forward to the game being completed.Here is my in depth review:There are two universes of Starship Troopers.  There is the book version, where powered armour is the standard.  Troopers die  in training when they fall off mountains learning how to use it.  Training is hard so the Mobile Infantry consists of a few, elite soldiers.  The armour is thick and allows for large jumps with massive firepower.  It is also where the term "Mobile" in "Mobile Infantry" comes from because troopers move, "on the bounce" and scale mountains with ease.  There is only one game that used this universe and that was "Starship Troopers: Terran Ascendancy."  The movie universe is the useless plastic armour that cant stop bullets or claws.  Helmets don't fit right and often go over the soldiers eyes and give them the iconic look of covered eyes and the chin strap pushing their lip up.  Waves after waves of infantry march against the bugs.  This game follows the movie universe but with mechs.  In this game, to beat the bugs you have to weaken bug holes then attack then main bug nest in the middle.  However, the single player campaign only gives you set units in a map to accomplish this.  What winds up happening is back and forth to your base to fix units, back out, do some damage, back to base to heal, then rinse and repeat.  On one mission when I unlocked power armour, the built up quarters meant lightning bugs would hurt me so bad I couldn't finish off the nest before i had to go heal.  While I was healing, the bug nests would respawn.  Basically I had to go back and forth to the nests until I weakened it enough to eventually take it.  On other missions, they would wipe out my troopers, who moved very slowly, and I would have to rebuild the army.Rebuilding the army:To rebuild, you have to have drop ships available.  Drop ships have a timer of 1-2 minutes before they become available to bring one unit.  This means you can make 1 unit every 1-2 minutes every time you get wiped.  It is slow.  The tempo goes make army - go get wiped but cause enough damage to the bug hole to make progress in killing it so your next wave of infantry can take it down.  No sense running - your troopers are painfully slow until you get to the powered armour troopers who are quite zippy.Unit balance:There are a lot of rock paper scissors elements.  Laser troopers kill almost everything, but short range so they get killed by spitters.  Rocket troopers kill spitters and armoured guys.  Lighting bugs kill everything, including frying your mech, so you have to have rocket troopers available.  You'll need radio operators to respawn your squads because they get wiped out so quickly.  You will require a cross section of soldiers, not just a fleet of battlecruisers like in SC2.AI:This game is designed for micromanagement.  You must move every squad individually.  If you attempt to attack move a group across the map, they will die.  They'll trip over each other, get into fire paths, not shoot, and be eaten in seconds.  If you expect anything other than that, you will get frustrated.  Move every squad in leap frog formats,  Be prepared for multi-prong attacks on bug holes.  I really enjoyed this feature, despite the scolding it gets from other reviews.  It is a unique feature to the game and adds a lot of neat mechanics.Graphics:Yup, awesome.  Great job there.  Felt good, explosions were fun, i enjoyed them. 10/10.Music:I didn't turn it off the entire 14 hours I was playing.  It fit well with the gameplay.  I often turn off music that is distracting or drowns out the voices/warnings/commands/whatever of RTS games.  I did not do that here. 10/10.Overall:As i stated at the start, I look forward to it being completed.  There are bugs (programming bugs, not just bad people eater bugs).  There are no achievements.  There are no unlocks like in There are billions, SC2 Co-op, and Warhammer RTS series.  You get unlocks based on the mission you are on and that is it.  Upgrading unit health, damage, speed, reducing dropship respawn time, and reducing time to escalate battle tiers would all be wonderful upgrades.  If Age of Darkness can add these after release, I'm sure it can be done. There is a single player campaign with no freeplay, skirmish, or multiplayer.   As of June 20, 2022 the only thing you can do once you conquer it is replay the single player campaign.  If you turn up the difficulty you will not get any achievement or e-pat on the back.  That's not to say it's not fun, but it does lack a feature that an immense amount of other titles have.Are these features going to be added in the future?  I don't know.  There is no publication about it from anyone.  I hope so.  Slitherine is not a small indie company and this game could make a bazillion dollars.  Obligatory TL;Dr:  Great game, its not done, hope they add features later.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's a thing.If you played the original Starship Troopers Terran Ascendancy, then this one will be familiar to you.In fact, I am honestly going to say at the outset I preferred the original Terran Ascendancy to this game.   Both feature squads of infantry that are good at something, weak at others.  However, the original (Terran Ascendancy which I will abbreviate to TA and this one Terran Command, which I will call TC) had a system where you kept the same troopers over the length of the entire game.  You got to promote them, give them different weapons to round out the squad, and over all their stats improved with experience, or they died, and you were sad you lost Dizzy who you named and had from the first mission.Terran Ascendancy has the BOOK mech suits, both Command, Scout and Marauder.  It is a real privilege to finally have a trooper capable of wearing one, and he greets your orders with "On the bounce Sir!" including actually bounding on jump jets.In TC, you get numerous squads, but always new ones that start off green, gain experience, upgrade, then vanish at the end of the mission so there is no continuity with your army.  Just disposable troopers, much like the movie.Then there is the micro management. Oh god, the micro management.   I am not a fan of micro, never have, it's called Strategy for a reason.  I can put  up with a single click to activate perhaps one special ability per squad.  But TC has at least two micro skills to use per squad.   So you'll find yourself being rushed by various enemies, some of whom you can't even get to out of range, and you are going from squad to squad clicking to activate a special, and in some cases clicking again to tell them where you want the special to go.Lets average it out, 1.5 clicks per squad, at least 5 squads, and this isn't even counting moving them.   You can see how this gets very annoying very quickly particularly on higher difficulty levels.  Now add to that abilities of the Tanker bug for example, it shoots fire.  But then that fire stays on the field as a corrosive area for several seconds, so if you don't move your squad out of it, even after the original casualties, it will keep killing troopers in that squad until you move them.  So...click to move them.You might have Mortar Bugs launching plasma way behind the bug wave, thankfully you get a little purple circle to tell you where it's landing...click to move your troopers out of harms way.Of course naturally you might have Flying bugs swooping in as well, the most effective way to kill one of them is with Mk2 troopers special ability, activate and click on the area, despite how quickly they move.Then your rocket troopers who are best at killing things long distance, or heavily armored will target the closest thing, usually warrior bugs...so click to make to force them attack the target of your choice, don't forget to move them out of the way of the mortar plasma.  Oh yes, keep them from the tanker puddle of fire, also be careful the Mortar bugs aren't out of range or they'll run forward into the warrior bugs and get eaten.You can probably see by now how micro will add up to just a plain headache, even after extensive control remapping, game mouse short cuts, and such.So with almost all mission, you aren't going to zoom down and just naturally enjoy a little cinematic action with the troopers on the ground.  Oh no, it's stay up high, and click for dear life gentle gamer.Everything will be quite manageable until you get to Valley of Death scenario where all those clicks happen at once while being surrounded on both sides.   And it goes up from there of course.Do I enjoy the game?  Yes, I kind of do.  It's like how I prefer Book to the original movie (And maybe Invasion), both are enjoyable in their own way.  I just like the book more, and I just like Terran Ascendancy more despite it's age.It's the little touches that I think are missing, to make it a much better experience.  Such as in T.A if you had a squad of troopers mowing down warrior bugs, and one happened to charge at the squad, the trooper the bug was aiming at would scurry back out of the way to try and avoid the charge, making the squad more dynamic, and interesting, sort of like in the movies as troopers kept shifting when they were pushing bugs into a corner. Where as in this game, TC, the troopers will happily stand in a flaming puddle until the entire squad is dead.  The troopers have no personality at all.  No real good lines, the music score seems a little..blah compared to the excellent score of the Movie it's based on.  It's pretty much a game by the numbers, painted and filled in, but with no true art to it.  Perhaps my view was skewed by the original Starship Troopers Terran Ascendancy, but that is how it for meWhat I do like about the game is it's not to bad as far as squad management goes.  You will find out rather quickly Attack Move is your friend to keep your troopers from running right in and getting eaten up.  In fact it is so useful I made it the default left click after I pre-programmed my gaming mouse.  Now I Ctrl left click to force a move instead.I most certainly love the fact you can put your squads in a formation, such as plain gun infantry at the front, snipers and rockets just behind them, and they will stay in that formation as you navigate up the map with your attack move, which makes them halt as soon as an enemy is in range and begin firing.  Make sure to hold down Left Click and rotate the formation till it faces the correct direction for best results..ala Ground Control (Still the best rts of them all) It could probably do with a bit of tweaking, but it is a good feature more RTS's should make use of.I think others have mentioned before, that a little AI tweaks might go a long way to improving the micro problem, as well as giving the troopers personality.Overall, I shall likely finish the game out, it's what I'd call..light enjoyable no thinking entertainment.  It's like the Cat Meme Youtube of gaming.  If you like a bit of rp, or depth to your gaming, perhaps it's best to look elsewhere.Starship Troopers Terran Ascendancy is on a few Abandonware sites now, look it up, I promise even as old as it is, it has far more heart then this title.Overall I'd give it a median score, say 3 out of 5.  Or if you are percentage based, a good solid 66.6666666%. If you like just plain uncomplicated clicky fun, this game is for you

It's not imaginative.  I waited hopefully for this and am wondering what in the world did they actually have to improve/fix that caused such a delay?  I'm a pretty big ST fan.  The book was incredible.  The movie, even though lots of people were critical, was fun.  30 minutes in and I'm not seeing it.  Given that Steam will only give me a refund with less than two hours game play, this just isn't enough to justify my time or money.  At least not yet. Although I'm disappointed they did not seem to reference the book or the old game at all, please don't think that to be the focus of my review.  I tried it.  I was unimpressed.  I'm asking for a refund.  What a shame.  Perhaps I'll try again down the road, but I don't expect that to happen.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugs ..! BUUUGS!!!Had to get that out. Seriously, it's good. It's a little rough, some missions need some balancing but all the bugs are fair, your units are effective and operate well together. It's a rock, paper, scissors sort of combat. Rocket troops for big single units, E-Pulse for armour shredding bug squads, standard Morita bois for staggering and slowing enemies. You have the tools, just need to use them cleverly, tactically. It can be frustrating but the best part of the game is that no one unit is overpowered. Every unit can be overwhelmed and countered, it's up to the player to use the right tool for the job.Positioning, composition, anticipation. Great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun base game with potential to become great!Could definitely use some balancing for both resources for players & enemy units. At times you want to do more but simply can't due to resources or time constraints imposed.The endless swarms of bugs that come your way really seem great & make you feel like you're in the movie. What doesn’t though is the number of  larger or unbalanced bugs that spawn endlessly e.g. Royal Guard, Scorpion, Spitter and/or Plasma Grenadiers, when masses of these start spawning in your mission, the game loses some appeal. The spawn rates just don’t seem balanced at all, endless warrior or tiger bugs, no problems. But grouped masses of scorpions I don’t feel should be happening. Some of these bug types should be a little more unique/limited?Trying to push hives or defend a base without the ability for certain units to target specific bug types as a priority soon becomes a drag as well. Especially when, as above, you can't have units target spitters or scorpions first your entire front line is evaporated. Please add this feature!!Otherwise though I enjoyed the campaign & hope further features & modes get added, without additions to gameplay the replayability isn’t very high.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just a good straightforward RTS. Good unit variety keeps the maps from becoming too stale despite the somewhat samey objectives.Clearing hives can be a tedious slog though. Still, even if the missions are hard to lose outright they present compelling challenges and if you rush in without a good plan you "will" just get chopped up. All in all i think there's 25 euros worth of game here, especially since the RTS genre is so sparse these days. Looking forward to the DLC!

_childDocuments_.review: Fifteen missions in at time of writing, and so far ST:TC is proving to be a fun, occasionally tough, but satisfying RTS.There's no base-building to speak of, which is a downer; instead the focus is on capturing pre-built command posts to act as reinforcement stations. Resource caches and secondary objectives give you access to Supplies to recruit units, and War Support, which is used to build turrets and base upgrades to unlock additional unit types.This is a very "caster heavy" game, with everyone having at least one ability they can use on a cooldown. These can range from throwing grenades or firing incendiary rockets to launching distracting flares or buffing allies. Each unit has different strengths and weaknesses on top of this, meaning that success relies on getting the right mix of troopers to clear out the hostiles.Tonally, this is fairly true to the movie - though a lot more cynical. It's less Starship Troopers as it was, and more what idiots like Verhoeven wanted Starship Troopers to be. There are not-so-subtle hints that this is a nation run by Stalinesque individuals and that the Federation higher-ups don't care about people's lives beyond their immediate value to the Commissariat. It is honestly rather tiresome to be facing an unstoppable horde of mindless killing machines while being told you're working for the bad guys - well excuse me for not wanting the human race to be devoured!But questionable narrative choices aside, it's otherwise a gung-ho dive into glorious Man-vs-Bug conflict. You get a lot of cool toys to play with, a huge variety of bugs to make those toys feel inadequate, a lot of bug holes to nuke, and a whole host of last stands to gloriously perform. Service guarantees Citizenship!
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: While I agree there could/should be something like a skirmish mode, the game has a real Ground Control feel to it and so far I'm loving it.  The fact that most of your units can't just fire through clusters of friendly units really makes you think about positioning and lines of fire.  You don't generate resources to spend, you have a fixed amount that you can sometimes supplement and use that to determine which units you call in.  It's best if you keep them alive so they gain veterancy and another ability.It's not a macro base-builder where you harvest resources, turn them into units, and just right click and forget about them, micro is the name of the game.I hope it has good post launch support because I want more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a lot, despite that it's not very long and doesn't allow for multiplayer campaigns.  It's a neat tactical RTS game that is more focused on combat and less on resource gathering/management, like what you'd see in games like StarCraft or Command and Conquer.  Being that the campaigns in this game are exclusively about squad and platoon level infantry combat, and being a former infantryman, I really appreciated what this game had to offer.  Factors such as elevation and terrain, types of enemy you're facing on a campaign and the proper management and use of units you have available (you have to be smart about how you deploy your forces) very much come into play in this game.  Maximizing each squad's arcs of fire and setting up proper kill zones are key.I also liked how the game, sometimes in a very 'tongue in cheek' way, played proper tribute to the satirical themes present in the Starship Troopers films.Overall a good game.  I highly recommend.
