_childDocuments_.review: Keep in mind, this isn't from a big team. They didn't over sell their game, in fact they even reneged on a few things to make sure they could deliver exactly what they did. Even with their communications to the public about the game being very far and in between they kept the promises they said they were able to keep.After reading a lot of the negative reviews people seem to have missed what the devs have said this game was going to over and compare it to other games of the same genre made and financed by much larger teams/studios; however, what was delivered by The Artistocrats was nothing but stellar.The campaign was fun, engaging and kept me going to see what the next part of the narrative would be. Was it a thrilling epic- no, but then again it didn't need to be. The story segments that were spoon fed during the intermissions between missions was comical and delivered much like the news would've been from the satirical film of 1997 and it hits it mark. The real story came from the dialogue between the characters during the missions.The gameplay is incredible even on brutal. Bear in mind I was master ranked on Star Craft 2 during both base game and Heart of The Swarm. Its not super micro intensive but enough to keep your brain going instead of just making a death ball like every other RTS and just stomping the opposition. Elevation and clear lines of fire were fun to manage. The tunnels where you can barely fit two squads side by side were fun to figure out to optimally work your way through. Its a very nice RTS with both simplicity and some advanced features to utilize.  Arguably, some things need some balance tweaks- looking at you scorpion bugs- but its by far nothing that is enough to deter any from the experience this game provides. My actual complaints with the game are, much like the comment above about the scorpion bug, nothing that takes away from the experience of the game. The most glaring complaint is the turrets- when you build them they get a trooper attached to them that holds a rifle and is incredibly close to the turret. My issue with this comes from the 2000 game, Terran Ascendancy(TA from this point on) where the trooper who mounted a turret had an actual animation for mounting the turret. Granted the troopers in TA were their own entity and not a placeholder in Terran Command (TC from this point on) so I can understand it, but every time I see that trooper not mounting the turret I get slightly triggered. My other complaint is whenever you go to reinforce a squad, a drop ship comes down. If you have to order that squad to do anything after issuing the reinforce, the drop ship just leaves without unloading the trips. I wish the troops would offload when the ship touches down and going to meet the squad. Again, I realize this is likely a balancing thing for if they did this the Radio Operative and Fleet Liaison would have their usage minimized.Now, again team that worked on this did renege on some things, and other things are rumored to be in the works. As of this review on 06/20/22, we are lacking skirmishes, survival/horde mode, and the possibility of co-op.  We might even get a planetary conquest later on down the road, but I wouldn't hold my breath on it. If just Skirmishes and Survival/Horde makes it will be more than happy. Co-op would just be the cherry on top.Overall, this game was everything I wanted it to be with the promises given by The Artistocrats during the development of this game. They hammered out an enjoyable experience that I was able to blow a weekend on. I finished the game with around 18.5 hours into it. Granted this was on brutal, doing the extra challenge missions, and not rushing through the levels.  Going into this game with the knowledge of what was promised and not expecting anything outside said promises I am extremely happy with the product I received and I hope you will be too. Get out there and do your part for The Federation.

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasantly surprised by this RTS. The store page looks like another fairly generic affair; however the game uses sight lines, spacing and elevation to create a remarkably engaging experience. The unit roster feels thoughtful and even the basic grunts stay effective into the late stages of battles if used intelligently. There are no resources, so players are encouraged to be aggressive. If your attack gets butchered well, call in the shuttles for the next wave in true Starship Troopers fashion. Be warned that this game has a few rough edges here and there and can feel imprecise at times. The campaign took me about 12 hours to finish on the standard difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played a "good" game? A strictly good game? Starship Troopers is that type of game.It's a good RTS, it's got a good selection of units, each with their own good abilities and veterancies, and good fun levels but it excels at nothing it does. As far as RTS games go, it doesn't really bring anything new to its genre outside of its setting.The campaign suffers from a lack of great characters to get attached to, largely because of the voice-acting which is just not that great. Even the propaganda reports, a very cool concept failed to get me hooked as the Announcer was just...generic. It's good but not memorable. There's a very good selection of levels and scenarios to playthrough which is a big plus however none of them escape the feeling of being glorified skirmish missions due to a lack of central progression.Yes, you unlock new units as you play but those units don't get stronger, there's no upgrades and there comes a point where you just get objectively better units that invalidate more than half of the roster by virtue of being stronger and cheaper.Each unit has a basic ability, a way to select which enemy to prioritize, better stats as they level up and another special ability at level three, which only really matters for the early game units. Which, it's important to note can be dismissed to obtain better ones which is an appreciated feature.Most units do have some genuinely great abilities but the gameplay it's compelling enough for them to properly spice things up. Except two of the late-game marine units which are fun by virtue of being utterly broken overpowered. The Third Level upgrades on the other hand are rather useless since there is almost always an objectively superior one which invalidates the ability to choose between three.The enemy selection is great, with lots of enemy types but fighting them largely resume to...sitting your units in a good position. Some may enjoy notion of not having to micro but you'll still have to worry about moving your units back from the mid-game and onwards artillery strikes. Later game you will unlock some more fun unit types that can you can... watch as they mow down through the enemies swarms with barely any resistance. The RTS element was simply not that engaging to me.The "Micro" Missions especially suffer from this basic "hold this position" type of strategic gameplay which the game fails to make compelling. Which is not to say that the macro, aka big, missions don't have their own problems. They can largely be resumed to get a base and destroy the hives just like you did the other 10 missions beforehand. The few times the formula is changed do work pretty well though.The base-system which is your main way of getting troops is neat but on a lot of maps it can be skipped as it's simply more effective not to worry about having to defend another base (or any base) as long as you have units.I don't remember much about the music but I do remember some bad sound design, especially in terms of atmosphere. The game fails to build a proper atmosphere and especially in its later half, also fails to build tension and suspense since you're already used to just, careful positioning or simply a-moving if you use the again, objectively broken units. Performance was good, there's no crashes, graphics are good and so are the combat effects, which is a plus. The game would have benefited from the super-zoom games like Company of Heroes have to see the combat up-close.I think a way to speed-up the game could improve it quite a lot.If you have an RTS itch, this game might scratch it, in the same way a bland meal might get rid of your hunger. I think it can be improved, I'm willing to change my opinion based on the expansions but the vanilla game is worse than vanilla, it's  just bland. Some leniency should be granted since it's their first game and there are some genuinely great concepts but the execution fails for most.I can't recommend the game, unless you're particularly interested in the setting it provides or want to support a smaller studio. There's better games on the RTS market, and almost all of them are older titles.I also cannot say the game should be avoided, after all, it's just...good.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Not a terrible game by any means, but one that won't be installed on your computer for very long. The campaign is quite long and has a nice variety of missions, but there is no 'skirmish' mode like on similar games, you NEED to play a story mission, though you can replay any that you have previously won. Units will occasionally mess up their pathing the most annoying issue with the game is that most infantry units can't see through other infantry. While units are stationary that isn't a problem as you can set them up where you like and take advantage of raised positions, but when you order units to do an attack move 50% of the time they will merge into this giant blob of soldiers and they get destroyed because no one can see through the other units. The bug varieties are also really lacking, they could have been SUPER creative and made nightmare fuel bugs to kill, but the drones, warriors, 'tiger' warriors and royal guard are all the same model repainted and their size changed, and those are 50% of the bug unit types and 90% of what you will be fighting.What the game DOES do right is capture the vibe of the original movie. That might not seem like a huge positive, but that is why you are looking at this game, right? It doesn't break any new ground, but it does make you feel like you are in the world of Starship Troopers. Your soldiers aren't 40K Space Marines, they are fragile little humans that go down in one or two hits, they need massed fire or rockets to take down anything but the most basic bugs, the story is bleak, as soon as you think that your boys and girls are catching a break, something else happens or some troops need to hold the line with no hopes of survival so that you can extract a Fleet Officer. And the news channel/propaganda in between missions is PERFECT. The exact same nationalist, story spinning style as the movie.TLDR; Wait for this bad boy to go on sale if you enjoy the movies.

_childDocuments_.review: A Starship troopers strategy game that does precisely what you would expect. It even surprised me a little. While the game may not tactically be complicated, it's focus is more on you as a player making sure you have your force consistently set up for a wave of bugs.I selected the difficulty below maximum and it feels just about right. The idea is to keep a consistent firing line so that your units can absorb a wave of bugs at any moment, because if you leave a gap, about 6 bugs can take out one unit in less than 10 seconds, once one goes down it can snow ball and within a minute your whole force could be at risk of being wiped out so retreating before it's too late is something you'll have to judge very quickly.The unfortunate part about the campaign are the 'tunnel/cave' missions. They feel very uninteresting compared to the other missions. As the campaign progresses the mission get more consistent and fun but those early tunnel missions grind the gameplay to a hault when compared to the levels where you'll have to face hundreds of bugs at once.The price seems just about right too but I would recommend getting the DLC on sale as that does feel like it should be included in the game. Never the less, the game does what you want and the developers did a great job keeping the gameplay in focus. It's not a lazy cash grab nor filled with any glitches, it does just what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, it's a decent game with a promising road map ahead of it.  It's fun, it's engaging.  It has a decent story.  But there are problems.Personally, I'm a Starship Troopers fan.  A BIG fan.  When I was a kid, I watched the movie so many times it used to put me to sleep.  I've read the book, watched and own all 5 movies, AND (this is the important part) played the game Starship Troopers: Terran Ascendency.  A great Starship Troopers RTS game.  Any new RTS Starship Troopers game will be compared to any old RTS ST game.  And the old game is better than the new one for several reasons.* Terran Command has WILDLY swinging difficulty.  It can go from so easy you don't think about it, to enragingly difficult mission to mission.* The unit special abilities are not optional, they are REQUIRED for success.  Even on the easiest difficulties, you are required to micro manage every single unit's every single ability and their cooldown timers.  These special abilities are so necessary that they need their own individual hotkeys.  In addition to this, some upgrade abilities are so good that it's only ever worth it to take one over the other.* There are contradictory gameplay mechanics that need to be fixed.  The game sets up a great LOS system.  (Most) Every unit needs a clear field of fire to shoot at the enemy.  Most units can't shoot through / over other units.  BUT most every unit has a very limited range they can shoot.  Hence the contradicting gameplay mechanic.  If I have to micromanage a battle line, then it doesn't make sense for soldier that can fire a bullet reasonably accurately over a thousand yards to only be limited to start shooting at 50.* Marauder implementation is very lacking / uninspiring.  They are NOT good enough to be worth the extra effort to get them.  There are bugs that EASILY destroy them, but the marauders aren't even that good compared to other bugs out there.  It's not even a rock-paper-scissor system.  Mobility wins battles, and the one Marauder is NOT better than the 1 squad of troopers, plus rocket launcher, plus 4x HMG emplacement replacement cost.Now, these problems don't make the game bad.  But fixing them will change the game from Good / Good Enough, to Great.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game announced, I had really mixed feelings and wasn't sure if I like the concept of an RTS where you just constantly mow down hordes of bugs. My initial skepticism only grew stronger as I watched gameplay trailers and previews, which seemed to reinforce my belief that the game would turn out to be dull and uninteresting.And then I decided to actually try it out and suddenly realised that the game is pretty fun and engaging despite how it might appear. I've got to say that I am a fan of the franchise, so that might make me biased, but I appreciate the game's references to the movie and all these corny propaganda-style cutscenes and dialogues. The diverse array of weapons and units at my disposal further added to the enjoyment, and discovering the inclusion of different Arachnids from different movies and cartoons was an unexpected treat.Having successfully completed the main campaign, I can confidently assert that I find this game pretty good. Despite my initial uncertainties, this game managed to surpass my expectations with its entertaining gameplay, charming tie-ins to the movie, and an array of captivating features. Its straightforward mechanics, coupled with suitable graphics, culminated in an overall positive gaming experience. For the future, I hope that the developers might consider incorporating an Arachnid campaign to further augment the game's appeal. In the meantime, I still recommend it to both fellow fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this title. It reminds me a lot of an old Starship Troopers RTS released in 2000 I enjoyed as a kid. Definite recommend, especially at it's current price point.Would you like to know more? The campaign took me around 25 hours on normal difficulty which I think given the game's price point is a fair length. The game itself does a great job of capturing the feeling and aesthetic of the films and overall the presentation is great.The game does suffer from a few issues. Firstly the game really could do with a pause ability as the amount of micro you need to be able to do is pretty wild on later missions. Especially when multiple places on the map demand your attention at the same time. I also found that the camera didn't zoom out as much as I'd like making it harder to get a wider view of the map. Lastly the game's tutorial is almost nonexistent so the player is pretty self taught. My pro-tip is to learn where the 'prioritise enemy type' button is and become close friends with it.All-in-all though I really liked this game. The campaign story was interesting and really fit the universe well and I enjoyed the between mission cut scenes.  The missions themselves were mostly fun and varied. Voice acting was pretty good and so was the writing. I'm definitely hoping we get a new campaign or two in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, been waiting a long time for a good SST RTS.  I'm not a developer so I am speaking from a gamers point of view.  It feels and sounds like a high end tablet game.  For a PC, it falls short of most of the RTS games out there now.  Maybe later some things will get better, or maybe a SST2 will be a little more up to par with modern RTS games. - Camera pan would be helpful, as in be able to rotate your point of view (if you can do that, I'm an idiot and haven't figured it out yet!) - Mechanics similar to Company of Heroes or Iron Harvest would be nice. - It's a Satire, but the game sounds like a really well structured joke, maybe tighten up (and add more) the troopers comments and leave the satirical narrations for certain parts, and not make it sound so deliberate.  Sounds forced, too much like you were trying to do this. - As I said in the intro, the sounds seem cheap for a PC game.... - Make some of the special abilities automatic instead of micro-managed - Make some of the movements a little more automatic instead of micro-managed, I.E., bugs get too close to a unit they back up and also fire while moving.  Have the troopers form defensive semi circles instead of just a block of bodies, and allow units to move when their line of sight is blocked, - Also, when you click to kill enemies further down your map, the troopers stop on the spot.  Literally stop, and don't move towards the target you clicked on.  Would be nice if they would move towards the enemy you've clicked on to kill. - Allow snipers, flamers, other special units to be attached to infantry units. - More "defend the fort" type missions - Allow us to prioritize which enemy to shoot. _childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers: Terran Command is a very competent squad-based RTS. If you like that sort of thing, and especially if you're a fan of the book or the film, then you'll get your money's worth. I'm just past the halfway mark and the plot so far is good, Excuse the inevitable pun, but I haven't found any bugs, and the missions are very well-designed - there's plenty of variety and they mostly don't to the whole 'build up a big army to take on the big bad at the end' schtick. However, for a modern RTS the range of units is relatively limited, with each having particular specialisms that you will have to use at various points, and they need constant micro-managing. There's no base-building beyond a limited amount of structures that unlock new units, there is (as yet) no skirmish mode, but then the only factions are yours and the bugs, and you don't get the cinematic cut sequences you'd expect from a bigger budget title. Nevertheless, it's great fun. Maybe not a game you'll play for hours at a time, but one you'll want to see through to the end, and the devs clearly have a lot of potential so it's worth investing some cash to support them. As a fan of these sort of games I'd say it's well worth buying - I doubt you'll be blown away but you certainly won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: There's five things plentiful on the battlefield:1. Bugs2. Bullets3. Jank4. The desire to Know More5. The desire to Know More about why I can't rotate my cameraTerran Command plays like a water-downed version of the original Warhammer 40k: Dawn of War in the most loving way possible, where the focus of the game is on utilising terrain and careful unit placement to defeat mass hordes of bugs.Despite some scattered pathfinding issues, this game is shockingly easy to pick-up-and-play.  Gameplay is unfortunately plagued with incomplete or nonexistent animations, frequent graphical glitches/bugs and overall lack of polish. The lack of polish can be forgiven, especially for an indie team, but Terran Command is also borderline unfinished with a complete lack of a skirmish mode, survival mode, or any other sort of classic RTS mode to add replayability and no multiplayer whatsoever.But despite its jank and so-far missing content, the game  like the movie when you play it and makes you feel like a MI commander. Even the  encourage you to be risky and bold... your troops are literally FREE! They just cost supplies that you  when they die! Sure you could use rockets like a nerd, or you can send wave after wave of your own Mobile Infantry at that hive until they run out of bugs!The bugs have the numbers, and so do YOU!

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers is a pretty unique RTS, made by a small studio so people should temper their expectations, the theme of the game with cutscenes mirror the first Starship Trooper film with the satire news broadcasts. The way the characters talk and act is typical of that universe and it feels genuine and funny at times. The game uses a "line of fire" mechanic, so most units will not shoot through each other so the player will have to be side by side or to be at an elevated position, even though this seems terrible at first, it makes sense and helps the game a lot and makes it feels satisfying in every small to big battle!Talking about the theme, one mission entails rescuing a prisoner whos crimes were for "unionising". The reason for rescuing this guy is so that the federation can broadcast his execution of Fed Net on all channels which made me laugh at how ridiculous it was (but in a good way). There was another mission that greatly disappointed me, I am not sure if more content was cut from the campaign but it was either that or an easter egg for the fans. In Starship Troopers 2, the bug the film focused on was the control bug. This bug was used by the bugs to be inside of a person and use them to try and infiltrate the Federation and destroy their leadership and learn secrets/war assets.  Now at the start of the mission the Psi Ops officer kills one of his marines and tells the player that he does not trust anyone and wants biological tests to prove they're fully human. So initially I thought the campaign would shift to destroying this plan by the bugs and having interesting missions were you may not be able to trust your marines or others in the federation. But no, sadly after the mission and cutscene nothing was said about it and it was swept under the rug. I am hoping if they do campaign DLC that they focus on this as even though the second film was awful, the premise of the bug is very interesting and different.The AI is mostly competent although occasionally it will bug out and your soldiers will stop shooting completely or the bugs may stand still, hopefully this is patched quickly as it can take you out of the game especially at harder difficulties. Speaking of difficulties, I played the campaign on 3 stars (normal) and it seemed balanced until a couple of missions near the end that were frustrating at times so on the hardest difficulty it may be a bit imbalanced unless you're an RTS veteran.The campaign overall is good length, around 20 missions overall. Some missions are short, some are long. The missions remind me a little bit of Starcraft II where the shorter missions give you specific units to work with throughout the mission without any new units (unless the mission gives them to you throughout) the campaign does a good job overall at introducing units as at the start very limited units are available to player. This is good and keeps the campaign fresh and interesting. After completing the campaign, I looked for more content and currently there isn't much. There are challenges to complete that are mission length scenarios but sadly there are only 2 at launch.Prepare for a lot of dog fighting, very satisfying when you prepare a kill zone to crush the bugs. Sometimes you will lose troops and that is OK. The death animations are great but sadly the player will not focus on them much due to the chaos on the screen.There are 12 different types of enemies encountered in the game, they all have a various series of ways of interacting with the player. Some are purely more bullet spongey than others, some like the famous tanker bugs have their own mechanics in the game where the player has to micromanage.Overall there are around 11 different types of units too (with some variations in the later missions) most units, like the bugs have their own mechanics. An example of this is the engineer. This unit creates their own turrets (3 variants) that use war support. Overall it keeps it fresh with the different amount of units available. Fans of the film, it is a MUST buy, it does the franchise justice and uses units from other films, games and role playing game lore. It does have its problems but overall with certain bug fixes and additions it will definitely be worth the £23.79 price tag. Again the game was made by a small team so people should not expect AAA cutscenes, gameplay etc. The devs have said they are adding game modes/challenges in the future. 7/10 overall and if you're a fan of the films then its a 9/10 due to the theme being great. [/b]

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, it is probably the best new RTS i've played in a few years, up there with Iron Harvest for quality and maybe better due to the low pricepoint. It's a single player only game, with a pretty long campaign that lasts for about 12 hours with some replayability if you enjoy horde defence modes. In addition to the campaign it also has two challenge missions, i only mention those as they aren't mentioned in most reviews and I assume most people missed them as they are in the scenario selector and there's not a lot of reason to go there. Both of them are good. As for the game, it's 100 percent starship troopers, it takes from the three live action movies and the two animated movies giving it a good variety of units. The missions are varied but mostly follow the David Gemmell plot model of defend area X or move to area X with little deviation. there is a limited amount of tactics but 90 percent is form a firing line and let the bugs come to you. It's very satisfying.  The bug hunt missions in the caves are probably my favourite as you have to be careful ow you move up your firing line and always cover each unit, its the most tactical the game gets. the game does desperately need some extra bits though, skirmish mode, map editor, and horde mode (which would just be skirmish mode again really) but for a 25 euro game its really hard to complain about such a high quality product. Strong recommend. Or in other words, SERVICE GUARANTEES CITIZENSHIP !!!

_childDocuments_.review: I've had lots of fun with this game. The atmosphere is spot on for Starship Troopers. The scenarios make sense and in a classic fashion the federation views your troops and expendable tools. The game can also put a serious amount of bugs on screen. When you are getting overrun you can see it. It can be a lot of fun to plan how you are going to hold the line then beat the bugs back in order to destroy their hives. I like all of the different types of units. What really adds to the longevity of the game is community content where you can play missions/scenarios other people have made. By biggest gripes with the game are:The most challenging bugs to face are the scorpion bugs but they're also extremely annoying to fight against. They are not fun to fight, they are just frustrating. They are the arachnid's equivalent to tanks, complete with a cannon. There are no physics in the games besides the hopper (flying) bugs. All the bugs and your troops collapse from a death animation which after a while gets stale. The unit dialogue gets a little repetitive too "Yes sir." "Move it!" "Get your gear and roll out!" for every little movement and you have to click a lot because moving your troops across large areas is treacherous. So you can't just click once and be done or they'll be slaughtered. The dialogue is fine the first 100 times you hear it but then you start to wish they spoke less often or only when the movement was substantial. In the end though these are relatively minor grievances to an otherwise fun game. If you are a fan of Starship Troopers you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: In short very fun game took me 12,3 hours to complete the campaign on 4 start/hard difficulty.Not played the 2 challenges yet.Will replay on brutal/5 star.I assume 10 hours on normal and 15-20 hours on brutal difficulty for the first time players.I give it 8.0 as it lacks many quality of life such as shift queing commands and some polish and content.With quality of life+some more content patched in it is a 9.0.Pros:Nice art style,fun to play nice story,good animations and upgrades,both bug and enemy models are well done.Very micro heavy,with light RPG and light base "building".Many soldiers skills,certain weapons are good or bad againts certain enemies.No macro cavern missions are very well done.Cons:1 tutorial mission,19 campaign mission and 2 challenges as of yet for 25 euro.No RNG maps or skirmish.Only presets for gfx options,no advanced graphical tweaking like AA,AF can be changed individually.Most other RTS games have more content.-Lack of quality of life most RTS game has.-Small for me but no STEAM achives or trading cards.-Scorpions are very overused elite bugs in missions they appear,and take good dmg ONLY from rockets.-Non armor piercing deals almost no dmg to armored targets like scorpions.Of course it makes sense but the dmg % is very low,lower than piercing to fortified in Warcraft 3.Rockets mans in masses are forced due to massed scorpions in many late game missions on higher difficulties.-Difficulty only affects dmg dealt,nothing else-slight skill or weapon balance issues.-The fort mission has insane jump in difficulty over the previous one.Overall if you are truly a fan Starship Troopers go buy it,otherwise I would wait for a few patches and buy it on a light sale.If content gets added,I will update this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Fun missions-Difficulty balance feels just right (I played at 4 stars)-A lot of heart-The pre-mission cut-scenes are in the style of the propaganda reels from the movie-Cool/nice looking pre-mission/main menu art-The micro heavy design/anti blobing mechanics match the setting-Game is reasonably good looking (especially given the smaller size of the developer)-I never felt like I wasn't having funCons:-Not a ton of replayability at the moment. The year one map editor freeLC and DLC should solve this, but at the moment it is just the 15-20 hr campaign and a few challenge missions.-Location variety was all right but not the best (I suppose there is only so much you can do with a desert planet).-If you are really into macro heavy RTS games this game doesn't really have that-Settings and menus are a little limited/rough around the edgesConclusion:A fun little RTS romp, with well designed/balanced missions, and a whole lot of heart. _childDocuments_.review: Warm it all up! Everything you've got! Come on, you apes! You wanna live forever?The 1997 film was absolutely iconic but does the game live up to these cult expectations? The re ignition of this game no doubtfully created huge nostalgia for those of us who had the privilege to watch this in the late 90s.Now 25 years later, a creative and collective mindset has brought the big screen to RTS gaming, which I tip my hat off to. If someone asked me if a Starship Troopers game would ever be released now in this age I would have laughed.Albeit a game it is but simply a version specifically based on the Terrans as the title suggests. There is a number of single player missions some hard and some easy. I mean there is no real in depth RTS strategy like Starcraft or Age of Empires, absolutely no comparison. You do not do much building, nor gather resources but concentrate on specifically the mobile infantry, tactical resources that are given to you and management of your forces are vital against the arachnids.You have a different array of units but these develop further into your missions as time progresses. You definitely must be strategic in your movements, utilising unit special abilities to outsmart the bugs at times or face being defeated. Using ground advantage and offensive machinery is also beneficial in this game. Some units can build turrets etc. Exploration will greatly help you, as numbers are a big thing in this universe.The arachnids are as you expect them to be and of course the different types of bugs are present in the game.This game also couldn't be complete without its satirical fednet cutscenes. How else would I be able to keep up to date with the war in Klendathu without the militaristic propaganda machine! would you like to know more?However this game is not without its bugs (no pun intended), I did find myself very frustrated at times. For example the strength of the arachnid forces and your army when clearing bug holes (volitile and slow) and at times the infantry wouldnt fire on arachnids when commanded to. I did find some of the missions was the same and repetitive, specifically fighting on one planet instead of other scenarios and some of the storyline dialog was I guess 'acceptable' including the limited infantry punchlines. Dont expect Michael Iron side or Casper Van Dien to suddenly appear and start spitting fire.I did also feel the arachnids were predictable in their movements and that the AI wasn't fully utilised to act as the hive would. Negatives aside, I do think the game has much improvement to go and a big future to build upon. Coming from legendary games in this arena is a big ask and big shoes to fill. This game is definitely not on this level, but then again it has not been created as such. It is however still fun, it still brings alot of memories and is good for an introduction into the RTS genre.The devs are definitely improving and fixing and updating as they go. Keeping a close eye and even releasing a road map to show the future. I do believe this game will be much better and polished gem as time permits.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is "almost there"  The music is ALMOST good, the sound design is ALMOST enjoyable.  The AI pathing is ALMOST functional.  The map designs are ALMOST good.  The game play ALMOST feels good.  But unfortunately the game falls flat on just about everything.   The guns sound wimpy and the voice acting isn't very good.  The maps are kind of boring and your units constantly get stuck on corners.  There are no original designs in the game, with literally everything coming from the 3 original movies, traitors of mars, and the old strangelite FPS game.  But apparently none of that came with a license for the music, leaving the soundtrack feeling hollow.The resources aren't.  Yes, you can choose what units to deploy, but instead of spending resources, you just have a unit cap, which can be increased a few times every mission.  And should your unit die?  No worries, you can just build a new one instantly (And I do mean instantly).  The bugs feel sluggish which really takes away the tension as you can just run away as long as they aren't too close.  And IF the unit dies, the ONLY thing you lose is the unit's veteran status, so there isn't much of a downside at all.  But the REALLY disappointing part is that the game ONLY has a single player campaign, and ONE single player scenario.  There's no Co-op.  There's no multiplayer at all.  There isn't even a skirmish mode.  You get 20 missions (19 campaign and 1 scenario mission) and THAT'S IT.  There's almost no replayability to this game unless you want to grind the same scripted mission over and over again.Overall, I'd give it a 2 out of 5.  There's the potential for a good game here, but it'll probably take some serious DLC and modding to get to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game. Does a good job of riffing on the original films, and the gameplay elements are sufficient, although theres nothing particularly novel about any component of the title. Many of the levels do pose a good challenge, but sometimes its from wonky soldier AI - for example snipers rarely opt for high value targets and its a mess to try and wrangle them in the midst of a skirmish. One thing that would have really taken the game up a tier or two is if you were able to play from the bugs' perspective. Would have been MUCH more interesting. Granted, they probably would have had to do some footwork on flushing out the background of the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: It's exactly what you think it is.Like Strategy?Love the Mobile Infantry?Hate bugs?Then you'll love this.All the units have a fair amount of utility and I love how you're actually suppose to keep these guys alive. They level over time and unlock new abilities that can really effect the outcome of a skirmish. So unlike C&C you don't just sit there spamming units. You work with what you have. it's all about positioning and superior tactics. There are occasions where you can steam roll enemies but more often than not you have to proceed with caution, keeping line of sight clear and watching the flanks. it's a tense, drawn out war of attrition where you will spend most of your time holding your ground until you can make a counter-offensive manoeuvre against their nests. I could rave for hours about how much fun I've had but I don't want to reveal everything. Jump in and enjoy, citizen.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm going to be brutally honest here and say this game has its faults. Yes, the game is actually really good; if you're into the Starship Trooper series, however, if you're not, you're likely going to avoid this one until more is added. Anyways, the game's campaign took me 9 hours to beat but that was on easy (Cause Scorpions are lethal), so give or take another one maybe three hours on the higher difficulties if you're doing the side objectives. Scenario wise, there ain't much... just replaying many of the same missions you beat in the campaign save for two "Challenge" operations at the bottom. Still, would I recommend this game? Yes. Despite it's flaws, it's still an overall, fun game. Is it worth the price? Well... debatable. Graphics? Not bad, but bodies don't stay and disappear into the ground which kinda sucks. Gameplay wise, pretty fun as it has you think a little more tactically and utilize each unit effectively in order to come out on top. Now, a few issues I do have is how unbalanced the game does feel at times on the higher difficulties - I know, that sounds weird to hear from someone who beat the game first on easy, but some enemy units are just literal tanks when they shouldn't be and one hit units that are supposed to be YOUR tanks, so it makes all units feel as squish as your starter units despite being "elite" which sucks. Another issue is the lack of any ST violence... I mean, there are some cool death animations, but nothing like a guy being cut in two or limbs being cut off... just dudes falling and or dragging themselves away until they die. Blood is fine and stuff, but yeah, overall, wish the bodies would stay as well so you could have a bit more immersion on that front.Also! Should note, that one thing that bothered me is how the player is the MC, but we don't actually get acknowledged at all for our efforts in the game, and despite all the victories we win for the Federation, we're not promoted, honoured, or given anything beyond the rank of Lieutenant... which you start as and stay as. You also get to name your Division, your squads, etc, but none of it matters as your Division's name is never uttered or shown in the gameplay, and your named squads don't carry over to aid in future operations. So, the naming feature, while cool, is pointless, and you don't feel like you're the main commander but just some individual doing all the hard stuff while the CO gets the praise and story focus XD. But yeah, all that said, still recommend this game to any who love ST's and enjoy killing seemingly endless hordes of bugs!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Starship Troopers fan and an enormous RTS fan, but I tend to like basebuilding games like the classic Command and Conquer and DoW, that being said, this game was really, really fun. It looks great, plays great, and I was really impressed by the studio. That being said, after beating the campaign and scenarios, here's some pros and cons. Pros- Looks great, plays great. Didn't have a single crash or stutter. It's pretty well polished, tells a fun story (if not particularly inspired), the art looks amazing (dear God please sell prints or an art book). The unit variations are interesting and all of them have their own specific uses. I like the upgrade tree, but I wish there was some more useful ones. I found myself picking the same exact upgrades 99% of the time. For what I can remember, there weren't any game breaking bugs or anything that made me ragequit about. Like I said, the game presentation is amazing, everything looks, feels, and sounds great. I cannot get enough of mowing down Warrior bugs with the arsenal provided, which again, is great. This game is very infantry and unit focused. There is some good micro-ing to be had if you enjoy that sort of thing, which I normally don't, but it feels like they did it right. Cons- Some stuff is kind of unpolished (my specific issue is that for me, the TAC bombers made no sound at all.), some of the pathfinding can be weird. Human enemies are insanely difficult to fight. I feel like some of the bugs are a bit too tanky, for example the Scorpion Bug is insane, both incredibly powerful and really hard to defeat, I feel like that should've been switched with the Tanker bug. Some of the unit unlocks are a little late in my opinion, only getting power armor troops towards the way end of the campaign. Other than that, my main issue with this game is that I want MORE. I get it, the game is $30 and has been out a day or two, but what about some skirmish maps or something? It's got some pretty good replayability, but both a pro and a con are I want more of it. All in all, I'd 100% purchase again, please dear God release some DLC or something soon, I need another fix.

_childDocuments_.review: This game mostly follows the continuity of the 1st film ("Starship Troopers" 1997) and has a tiny bit of the expanded background from the 3rd film ("Starship Troopers 3: Marauder" 2008). They definitely nailed the satirical style and feel of the first film here.The RTS elements are simplified. You don't have to worry about resource collecting. You just have a supply limit and you choose what units you want. Replacing units is free and only costs you Time and Micro. Your micro is mostly spent on positioning your troops and utilizing their abilities for maximum dps against the incoming bug swarms.When Attack-Moving, sometimes your units will run past enemies that are hiding behind corners and will just get annihilated . Attack-move should always prioritize attacking but in this case it doesn't. This can get really frustrating if you are pushing multiple objectives simultaneously and it requires a lot of additional  to compensate for it.I finished the campaign in 10 hours. That's mighty thin. There are 2 DLC packages that would bring the playtime up significantly but you're left with the sour taste of having to buy DLC for the game to feel full. The saving grace is that there is community content that is easily accessible within the in-game menu.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great title for what it is with a fair asking price. While not being as deep as some might have expected or wanted the surface level mechanics of the game create a believable and fun Starship Troopers experience. The Voice Acting is perfectly cheesy and over the top as is expected and for the most part the game hits all the right highs that one would expect.Unfortunately this experience is also hindered by a laundry list of bugs and features that seem half baked at best. _childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write steam reviews, however having played over 14 hours of the game, I feel like I want to take the opportunity to - partly to document my experience in the hopes that the developers will try to fix some aspects of the game, which would make it genuinely very fun and enjoyable, as well as partly to help inform anyone still sitting on the fence for the game.The Starship Troopers setting is actually done pretty well overall - everything feels quite organic, whether it's the different types of troopers you can command, the buildings and maps, the campaign's narrative and characters - not to mention the bugs themselves! This is nice, because sometimes when working on a game adaptation, studios will try to fit the setting around the game, introducing a load of "stuff" that ends up feeling out of place, but you never really get that here. The first thing to say about the core game mechanics here is that they're not sophisticated - in fact, they feel extremely casual. That in itself is no bad thing; not everyone is looking for a "Wargame" strategy experience - and even if they are, they're likely to also be open to a more casual experience, which doesn't require large amounts of micro-management and won't heavily punish you for small mistakes.The problem is that, inexplicably, Terran Command does do those things.  The separated "fire and manoeuvre" mechanic that the game puts forward is by all means an interesting and meaningful concept - the issue is that the actual implementation of it really is not, or not consistently enough. To name just a few problems with it: ...a rule which they will obey, ironically, with the same kind of lack of autonomy that you might expect from a bug possessed by a hive mind. Want to send your troops anywhere except the immediate vicinity? Better check which route(s) they take then - because they might not be the same as others! This happened to me in a mission where I selected a collection of 6 different units at the same time, who were all approximately in the same place - only to find that two of them had gone the *wrong* way around a set of impassable terrain, taking them straight through a bug hive, because the game calculated that was the fastest route for them. Hilariously, when doing so, those units will actually just mindlessly run past or even into the bugs, not stopping to engage them at distance (remember, they're not allowed to run and shoot). You might argue that is what the "attack" move is for - except you don't expect to have to use attack move when you order your troops to go back to their base. Small oversight's like this one - calculating the routes for the grouped units individually, rather than collectively - combined with the rigid "fire and manoevure" mechanic lead to endless problems and massive frustration, which ultimately just takes any semblance of fun out of the game.First of all, you have no choice on how units will position themselves with respect to one another - this is decided by the game, based on the units composition that is selected. Normally, it will do this by positioning the troops that are capable of indirect fire behind the ones that are not - i.e grenade launchers located behind the guys with regular rifles, parallel to the line of fire. Ok, pretty sensible. How about perpendicular to the line of fire? Good luck trying to work it out, as I have no clue how the game handles this. Many times, I've had units that were on the right flank, run over to the left and vice versa, when changing the angle of the firing line, resulting in the centre getting blocked and no-one firing - goodbye units. Oh and about controlling the forward facing direction of your units - the game automatically adjusts this depending on where your mouse is relative to where the troops are now. Want to move a firing line backwards? Congratulations, your troops now have their backs to the enemy, by default, unless you can yank your mouse around to get them to face the right direction! The real cherry on the top is the way the campaign constantly features set pieces where your units will turn a corner in a canyon, or crest the top of the hill, only to have a previously unseen (due to LoS) group of bugs attack them from the side, leaving you unable to either back up effectively or reorient the line - and when I say constantly, I really do mean constantly. The campaign is 20 scenarios, which probably equates to roughly 20 hours - that's not an hour per mission mind you - many of them can be completed in half an hour, or less in fact - however, others can take between an hour to even two hours, simply because you have to go through, triggering all the ambush attacks where your units get slaughtered, only to reload the last checkpoint and cheese it on the next go, because you know it's coming. So the "strategy" is basically cheat to defeat. Honestly, the worst part about this is that it would be so easy to fix - the Total War games have spent literally decades refining exactly this kind of system, to the point that the perfect answer is already there - but we get this terrible system instead.Units will only ever engage an enemy if it is within their line of sight, in range and not obstructed by an obstacle. Therefore, if they're attacked by anything with a ranger greater than their own, they will literally just stand there and take the punishment, until they're wiped out. If a unit next them is attacked by an enemy unit out of range, they will also just stand there, doing nothing. If you order a group of units, some of whom have direct view of an enemy, others whose view is obstructed, the latter will just stand there doing nothing, making no attempt to move to a position where they are able to fire.Units have no ability whatsoever to determine any kind of priority when it comes to choosing which enemy units to attack. Therefore, a Mech will quite happily blast away at Warrior/Tiger bug units which are doing little to no damage to it, completely ignoring the Scorpion bug unit that is able to kill it in 3-4 shots. Rocket troops, that are able to counter the Scorpion bug, will quite happily blast away at the Warrior/Tiger bugs that are too fast for them to hit, whilst the Mech next to them turns into a ball of slag. Basically, any engagement that involves Scorpion bugs means micromanaging your rocket troopers - and if there's more than 4 Scorpion bugs at a time - which happens on a number of occassions - good luck, because you're going to f****** need it.To be honest, I think I'll stop there, because I honestly don't have the patience to write out all the other problems with the gameplay mechanics. Hopefully, some of the other reviews will capture these.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom Line Up Front (Overall 8 /10)- A simple, yet fun game worthy of investment. Probably the best game representation of the Starship Troopers universe yet- Plays more of a Real Time Tactics than a Real Time Strategy game- Excellent artistic style and game environment really shines- Easy at first then the missions get challenging past Mission 5- Very basic base building mechanics- Lacking features of most modern RTT / RTS games such as a 360 degree camera, skirmish mode and multiplayerDevelopers, if this game had multiplayer, skirmish, 360 degree camera and the ability to play bugs this game would be a masterpiece. Gameplay Loop (6/10)- Only giving this score based on the fact that there are 2 DLCs at the moment and there is a lack of skirmish and multiplayer- Few mission varieties but it suits the game universe- Campaign is nice and lengthy especially with the DLCs- Achievements are not difficult to obtain but definitely a good challenge in some missions. Might need a few replays to succeedGameplay Mechanics (7/10)- Very few controls to learn the game- Some units will not conduct their special ability on first click (most prominent one is engineers using the demo ability)- Needs some unit micromanagement (sight lines and unit special abilities) to be efficient in a mission but it is not tediousPresentation (8/10)- Excellent artistic style and eye candy- Some of the unit explanations can benefit with a rotatable unit model when you view their stats- Captures the vibe of the Federation very well- Little to no glitches, gameplay or graphical bugsSound (6/10)- Some gunfire sounds could be a bit more punchy- Some arachnid sounds could also use a bit more volume to convey presence - Voice acting is bearable and relevantHow this can be a 10/10 game / Developer wishlist- Introduce the arachnids as a playable faction- Introduce Multiplayer- Introduce Skirmish- Introduce a 360 degree cameraSpecsIntel I5 13500KRTX4070Ti80 GB DDR4 RAMSSDSamsung 4K TV 60 FPSGame is on the highest graphical settings with VSYNC ON - consistent 60 FPS no issues

_childDocuments_.review: As I start the game, I am washed over with anticipation, I have been ready to join the mobile infantry since I saw the movie as a child, to see the galaxy, do my duty, and kill as many bugs as possible.  	The opening of the game starts off with promise, telling me I have Fednet news so that I can learn more, I eagerly click to start the game as I wish I could watch Fednet clips showing me the story of the game and giving context to where I will be, the galaxy is a huge place and there are millions of troopers, we can't all fight in Rico"s Roughnecks. 	I start my 1st mission, Big K - The worst and most disastrous mission the Skymarshal has ever led. I remember the movies, the hundreds of soldiers, and drop-ships that are lost as they descend to the planet's surface. In the game, however, I am met with a soulless and monotone voice that repeats the reporters' words from the movies. "It's an ugly planet, a bug planet." The voice sounds like a radio personality, reading a radio ad to the midnight shoppers at a grocery store. 	My 1st command comes available to me, an infantry rifle squad, nine troopers who easily dispatch the few warriors who approach my landing site. The combat starts off easy, the troopers automatically shoot and destroy the warriors easily, not much strategic or tactical planning is necessary so far. My ally troopers do the same, static positions set around the drop site, not moving a muscle even as a blue bug bomb explodes on a trooper unit, some die, but not many. I don't know if I am on Big K, or if we went to a local park. The announcer's voice speaks to me as if he has no idea what emotion is as if we are not supposed to be watching thousands of our fellow troopers die in front of us. He leads me to my next objective, helping guide me through the mediocre tutorial, as the bugs try to "force" their way into my troops at a brisk speed walking pace. I don't know if they are rushing to defend their home, or trying to hurry to catch the ice cream man before he drives off. The mission ends. I am greeted by a sliding screen of pictures as I hesitantly prepare for a new campaign. The music fills my room, it sounds like the generic music from most 1950s old military movies, once in a while I can hear music from the movie that I remember, but the other times I feel like getting some green army men and setting them up to create a diorama of an action scene, so far I think that would have more action than what I have felt so far. When I click on New Campaign, I am greeted with Kwalanshiand and my difficulty that I set to Brutal, I need much more excitement and toughness that What the prologue gave me. I choose my division: the 3rd Marine Division, the same one that I served in. The same narrator's voice greets me, this person I will now call Scab. I get a cut-scene about big K and why we need to be on the planet that we are heading to. Another voice comes up, nothing memorable, and the same soulless direction is given. The mission starts, a small OP greets me, buildings that look like they come out of a toy box wrap around a road that leads through the end of the southwest map, and continue north through a small town and to the same what looks like the same type of metal fort that Rasczak dies in. Some Allied NPCs marines surround my two squads of riflemen, the objective is to join up with the advanced team. 	What advanced team?	Where are we on the planet?	Why are the roads blocked off?	Why is there an OP out here? 	Why are we out here?	Who is my commander? My Rico in charge of these troopers? We move Northwest, killing some Chariot bugs, I click on the glowing Icon and I am taken to the worst info screen I have ever seen. Most Star craft fan made maps have better graphics and information, and why does the music sound like it is being played through the free airplane headphones? Who is this guy who keeps speaking? The next battle is numbing, my troopers saw tougher battles trying to get through the chow hall. The mission progresses to the point of a narrator asking what type of half-assed operation is this? I ask the same one. We arrive at a settlement that is roughly 30 yards north of where I started, within eyes view of the troopers who were still standing there. The no named voice who I will call Plastic gets "mad", saying either the civilians refused to leave or they weren't cleared out, maybe we should ask the guys who are standing right around the corner. Continuing east, twelve feet we find a company needing help, we "rush" over by right-clicking once and completing the battle. These bugs are not a match for me, as I write this and play at the same time. I gain control over a few extra teams, the new unit of Engineers can throw an Incendiary Grenade, a Demolition charge, and carry a Blazing Spear (Flame Thrower), but I still don't see my MEDIC!  (Zim Voice). I have to capture a Radio Station so I can talk to the fleet, and I can reinforce my casualties ( I have none from my own brilliant strategic mind). As I capture the radio tower, OH NO A MAJOR BUG OFFENSIVE INBOUND! I "quickly" arrange my guys west of the Radio tower by some buildings, a concrete barrier, and a burning car and within seconds, the great battle is over - No trooper dies. Go North the voice tells me, but I am an explorer and the vast, mostly unpassable map gives me the ability to recon one area before I continue with my main Mission, I find nothing. I get to the base, secure it, have a few seconds of combat, and, it's over.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If the description on the store page is something that you think you would enjoy, you will enjoy this.You pretty much know what you are getting with this.  What you expect is more or less what is delivered.  It is nothing ground breaking, but solid.  It would have been amazing back in the late 90's.  That is not a knock on the game because it is striving for that genre.  It is just to give you an idea.  I'll address a few negative comments that didn't make much sense or apply in my opinion:1)  The storyline makes sense - I think the only way the story would be hard to follow is if you were not following it.  It is not an epic story, but the narrative fits into the theme from the movies quite well.2)  The game is based off the movies and not the books - It does not claim to base off books.  It is clearly from the movies.  So to get the game knowing it is not based off the books just to write a negative review that it is not based off the books is non-sense.  If they did a poor job basing it off the movies, that would make sense.  But they did not do a poor job.  3)  Yes there are mechs - I think this is another book and movie debate.  I never saw mechs in any movies, but know they are in books.  Either way you do get mech action in the game.  They are valuable and used sparingly.4)  Variety - The mobile infantry kills bugs.  That is the theme.  For a limited scope, I would say the missions could have a bit more variety but doesn't do a bad job at this.5)  Choke point conflicts are small portion of game - chokepoint combat can get boring and repetetive, if that is the only form of combat.  Lucky for us, it is not the only form of combat in this game.6)  Not the typical amount of bugs (programming variety) you would expect with today's games on release date, but there are some.7)  I have not seen any commitment to post launch content.  Could be wrong on this, but I know some people would like more than the narrative campaign.  Once again, the game does not mislead you that it is more than the campaign.  I do wish they would come out and clearly state what the plans are (if any besides patching).8)  The right amount of hand holding - in the beginning missions there is hand holding, but not much after that.  Most people playing this game are going to be very familiar with RTS style and strategy, but I agree with the decision that the initial missions should accomodate new players as well.9)  It is probably priced right - Once again, if i knew more about post launch plans I could answer more clearly.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels good overall, if one is a fan of the movie-verse for Starship Troopers, they'll get exactly the right feel and vibe from this. Managing troop types and numbers is a good juggling act, and the strengths and weaknesses are straight forward enough to easily grip what you need and where.There is one big issue however and that is with the pathfinding, there is a "Troops won't shoot through eachother" mechanic to encourage the player not to just blob their troops and move smarter, but there are pathfinding issues that make that impossible in some places. Even while moving across open areas troops will tend to bunch up on their own and be unable to shoot because the units too close leading to substantial loses from one or two enemies that the troops couldn't shoot at.I recommend the game, but know that this is an issue that I hope is addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m old enough to remember when the original Starship Troopers movie came out and it was cringe, with at times bad acting, but at the same time strange in a sense that it was borderline between satire and glorification of national-socialism. I personally took that a satire with grotesque and exaggerated fight against space travelling bugs (I mean, hard to take such a plot seriously really), but you are not here to read about the movie aren’t you?The game, well, just like the movie, I liked it, it is true to that satire and exaggeration of all nazi stereotypes (for younger readers nazi is short for national-socialism) of ‘do or die’ and never think about the orders for mobile infantry is not there to think it is there to kill bugs. Of most importance though, behind all these there is a solid old school RTS with a classic rock/paper/scissors formula mixed in with a good roster of units with an insecticide tendencies. The game itself is not hard, however if you fail to properly compose your troops you will be mercilessly annihilated by the arachnids. And I have to say, slaying bugs and setting up defences and counter-offensives was fun, it was the type of the game I wanted where I am engaged, but not overly concentrated add some cool unit specs (you can choose between two different skills upon unit promotion) and there you go, the formula for creation dopamine is achieved. score 7/10 – good adaptation of a movie into an RTS with a military command codex that would make Stalin and Hitler proudFor more grumpy reviews follow me as a curator at

_childDocuments_.review: Never turn down something goodbecause...IT'S AMAZING!!!! I'm the happiest I've ever been doing my part! Would you like to know more?Ok Amazing is too big a word but it's legit and pretty good, though if you're looking for Starcraft and CoH2 levels of strats and variety then this ain't it chief. With that said the lack of variety is held up by the maps and abilities each unit has as well as the scenarios you are given.To give you an idea of how various the units are you haveRiflemen with 12 dudes and 10 health eachRiflemen with 6 dudes but grenade launcher and 10 health eachRiflemen with 14 dudes but energy and 30m instead of 60m and 10 health eachRiflemen with 2 dudes EXCEPT they have radios/the same rifle but with an ACOG/Rocket Launchers that act as mortars/Flamethrowers and 10 health eachLook you get it Everyone is doing their part and you will more or less end up having freak accidents involving a grenade or rocket because you skipped knife trainingBug wise it's a bit more varied minus the Warrior sub-types like the Tiger and Drone, they get actual 'Vehicles' like the Tanker and Plasma bug and his bigger Plasma brother who'll wipe out you whole army cause you decided to bind everyone to the same button, then you have special cases such as the Chariot who is useless, Spitters and Hoppers who deserve to die like the filthy Xenos scum they are and the list goes on with the last 2 LEGIT existing to counter all your important guys who aren't withing range of the 12 dude firing squad.Map wise they actually play a lot with verticality, LOS and more importantly not flagging the other squad. What do I mean not flagging other squads? Squads can't shoot through each other UNLESS they are one of the select few who can, they're on another level or they have an arcing projectile such as grenades or rockets and I didn't tell you but most of you units are infantry and I kid you not about the health thing you could throw a pebble at them and one unit could die from it.  *ahem* MEEEDDICC!!Speaking of units from the universe's best Mobile Infantry force they all have an ability in addition to a 2nd ability they work up to from a choice of 2 usually consisting of straight damage with little to no utility or an ability with a LOT of utility and possibly no damage giving every unit a subclass instead of guy with gun. For instance the Rifle squad has a rifle and grenade but then can have a 10 second shotgun mode that tears through bugs or a 6 second demolition charge that does A Lotta damage however the trade off for abilities is that using one causes both abilities to recharge.Campaign wise it feels like a Starship Trooper movie and is even told in a similar manner some of the lines don't even feel like they were done seriously. Map wise it follows the attack these locations with some bases between but also defend your bases from another wave of bugs, depending on the map it can be one giant wave with specials or local bug hives are beginning their attack meaning if you haven't destroyed the hives yet you don't need to worry about defence OR it'll be a story map where the game tests you on small unit tactics instead of the bigger base defence missions.All in all 9/10I'm doing my part!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Now finished the first out of three campaign after 20 hours of game play. This RTS game is a masterpiece.  There's a story, there's bizarre humor alá: the movie. There is even political commentary baked into the story and the game play. My favorite part is the side mission of wasting your troops to link up with a camera crew, in order to unlock a powerful but almost garbage unit painted in parade colours, only to bring with you to the main objective. The Federation wants it to have screen time on Federation broadcast. And the federation will get it, at any cost necessary.-------------------------------------------------Great hidden RTS gem. True to the movie lore. Accurate unit designs. High difficulty level and interesting mechanics. Base building mechanic is module building a call-in point. Gameplay is a combination of Command & Conquer / Starcraft and Ground Control.Fun missions with a lot of variety in objectives and functions. One mission has you clearing out a mine with limited ammount of units. Another has you repairing a factory while clearing out bugs. The other has you strategically falling back from hordes of Arachnids to a huge base and defending it until you are evacuated. There's a story, there are cutscenes, there is dialogue and the game is actually difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the campaign fully on highest difficulty, it's not easy. The no build tunnel missions are especially hard on this setting. The challenge and gameplay is there and it's quite fun. Gameplay, I'd give it a B+. There are times where I'm fighting against trying to target arachnids that I should be able to target, but because they are in some attack animation, or because targeting is maybe animation dependent, I miss. The units walk too slow at times to have fun with positional movement - which is what this game is trying to convince us it is about. The power troopers at near the end of the game, walk just the right speed to change positions often and effectively. Doing a 7 squad, 4-5 hive takeover is fun as you're pulling units back and forth. Medics would make it even more fun I think, as right now if you're out of health, the best you can do is run back all the way to base and reload. Or maybe I should have gotten the fleet liason to do that, I did not try that. The liason can set drop points near your troops to reinforce I think.Campaign mission design is good. Good variety, good phases, all mostly pretty fun. Mission design I'd give an A. The story really took away from it though.I wish they made the story a bit more than what it was. I would give the story a C+. There's no clear goal and not enough character build up. Things just happen. It borrows emotional beats from the movie too much, though the last mission's emotional resonance was good-but because the movie's was good too.

_childDocuments_.review: At 21 hours I just finished the campaign and I really enjoyed it! I think the demo gave an accurate example of the game you'll be playing and it is what got me excited about the game. It looks like there are 3 more "scenarios" that I can play that I'm looking forward too.I enjoy RTS games, I really like StarCraft I and II, but I'm not good enough to play them in multiplayer, so I only care about the single player experience.The novel mechanic of having a line of sight in order for your units to be able to shoot their targets is nice and forces you to care more about the position of your troops where I would otherwise default to my usual strategy of building a giant army and steamrolling them in a direction and not care who is where.The small downsides are: - sometimes your units can get stuck when trying to walk around something- Could be a me thing, but when sometimes I'll try to click on a unit ability and it won't trigger so I have to click it again, which is annoying mid fight- In order to heal your units you have to first use the ability that allows you to select a location of where to heal, and then pan the map to one of those locations and choose it. I wish there was something like in Iron Harvest where you can just push a "retreat" button and they will auto choose the closest one so I don't have to move my focus away from the fight.Other than that I just flat out enjoyed my time playing the game, and these issues might be resolved in future updates. Some of the mechanics in the game is its downfall, crossfire is one of these. The game forces you to micromanage crossfire between troops to prevent friendly fire(which is a bloody headache especially when moving the troops across the battlefield) that can be solved with troop formation (like found in AoE) and a bit better AI.Troop AI gets the job done but rather clumsily. _childDocuments_.review: Its a real-time strategy game that is, overall, more forgiving than what would be the average for the genre. That, however, does not mean that the game will always be easy. Towards the end of the campaign missions you may find that some aspects of the game you had found to be forgiving earlier had, in fact, been situational to the earlier missions. Certainly a fun game, and I am a fan of the universe and setting. To a degree, micro managing units can be significantly beneficial, however, it is considerably less intensive, and not necessarily a requirement outside of the hardest difficulty.The game is not polished and needs some bug work, but it is not so significant as to break game immersion, more so just enough to cause frustration depending on the timing. Sometimes trying to use a units ability will be met with no result (pressing q to use the q ability simply does nothing, or clicking on the ability simply does nothing and the unit will continue their regular actions). This can happen by either not loading the ability when requested (press q for air drop and no air drop overlay appears), or by not summoning the ability (press q and the overlay appears, but when placed no landing zone is used, and the ability is still available as if it had not been placed in the first place.)  Given that keeping your units at full strength is crucial for their performance, glitches preventing this from happening, even momentarily, can be seriously detrimental to your progress.Sometimes when a unit is given an order, the unit will act very strangely. For example, flamethrower units told to attack move will sometimes ignore enemy units close to them in order to run at a unit further away. Sometimes attack move will result in an unexpected path of movement. Commonly the order of your units in your firing line will randomly change without cause when moved or attack moved, requiring you to re-organize the units to your desired formation multiple times when making moderate movements. For some units attack move will cause them to move closer to the enemy than their maximum range, especially in the case of fleet units. Fleet units have a very short range, so when attack moving with a group they naturally move to the front lines when they're more of a support unit, which is fine, but they may be the only unit that will continue to move towards the enemy already within range until they are literally touching them.Although I do not think this is a bug, it is worth mentioning that attack move when used in small spaces with large numbers, generally results in none of your units attacking as they move due to breaks in line of sight from overlapping units. Occasionally this may result in a small group of enemies completely wiping a large force that should have easily dispersed them. Might not be a bug, but it feels sloppy.Luckily, the auto-save function allows glitches such as described above, frustrating though they may be, to only cause minor problems. The consistency of the glitches, however, is still very common.Overall, if you're a fan of RTS games, or of the starship troopers universe, it is still worth a buy in its current state. I would hope the game is updated to address some of these issues in the future, but it was a great way to burn about a 24 hours worth of game time on the campaign alone.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 7/10.Great graphics, max bugs (and minimal programming bugs). Satisfying in places where you're just mowing down everything around you.  Captures the spirit and feel of the propaganda machine of the FedNet.Spoilers follow:Cons: Too many stages where you have a set handful of units and have to micro your way around indoors.  Nonexistent story and character development.  Bare minimum of references to canon.  Simplistic gameplay, when you get stuck it's usually because you're expected to use unit abilities in a strict order.  No shower scenes, singing Sky Martials or new canon.To get 10: I'd love to see some kind of story-driven between-campaign stuff. If only they had the budget or rights to use live-action footage like the old AAA titles of the past, or slice up and include scenes from even the terrible ST2/3.  Even a Visual Novel style approach to introduce characters and interactions between/during gameplay would be welcome.  Get some characters to care about in there even if it's a carbon copy of the original (3 school friends drafted, follow their campaigns etc).  As it is, I couldn't remember the name of any of the thumbnails that have been barking orders at me for 15 hours so far. Gameplay: Get some named elite units in there at least, I'm  not asking for Johnny Rico, or a chance at having Carmen pilot a random drop ship, but  but killing off a developed character would be totally a ST thing to do, and caring about a few grunts amongst thousands of cannon fodder would be nice.  Oh and more content, map editor etc...Solid game, a must for fans and the best ST game yet.  Potential for sheer greatness with more content and polish.

_childDocuments_.review: An asymmetric single player RTS.RTSes are rare these days and this game certainly filled the void after my second run through Iron Harvest. This is not a AAA game, but it is very well executed within the constraints of its budget. It looks and sounds good. It also excellently uses the license of Starship Troopers (movie(s), not the book), drawing heavily from its over-the-top militarism and ever present propaganda. Even cutscenes between missions are done as motion comics styled as heavily biased news reel and visually inspired by propaganda posters.  The game is single player only and only playable as Terran Federation. This makes sense, as it is heavily asymmetric, reminding me of They Are Billions. The gameplay is based around proper positioning and use of special abilites. Working with line of sight is crucial. The game has a decent path finding (most of the time, trying to use abilities beyond their range is unreliable) and rudimentary ability to keep and angle formation during movement. There are some features that would significantly improve gameplay and may still be implemented later: an active pause and command queue.  I had a great time with this game. I had done my part. Will you do yours?
