_childDocuments_.review: I'm doing my part! By leaving a proper review!TL;DR: Game good. Devs currently active and planning more content. PVE only, stop asking for MP. Buy and support. Would you like to know more? Then keep reading.As of this writing - you get a full campaign of over a dozen missions which includes units from all 3 movies and the two Japanese CGI movies. The OVA and Roughneck Chronicles are NOT included. There are currently two Extra Scenarios which allow access to the full roster. Be aware - this is NOT Early Access. This is the core game, around which more content will be added. I participated in the demo and Beta. This is a small studio and they have released a good product within their timeframe and means. Devs have stated they intend to include more content in future. Gameplay - Are there Bugs? Of course, there are Bugs. This is Starship Troopers! Know your enemy! Jokes aside, the game runs well. Terran units work well and generally aren't idiots if enemies are nearby. That being said - hotkeys will save your life. If you're the RTS gamer who doesn't hotkey, some of the missions will be nigh impossible for you. I get definite Starcraft and Command & Conquer vibes in terms of the combat mechanics. Not much in terms of base building, which keeps the focus on combat.Maps are large enough that you may have to fight on multiple fronts rather than just blob and push forwards. Also, units have a line of sight mechanic. So, Squad 2 will not be able to shoot through Squad 1 if they are lined up behind each other and bugs are to the front. This is a good challenge since it requires thought in unit movement and placement. Leave a squad isolated, they will be swarmed and killedThere are multiple enemy types and there is some rock-paper-scissors mechanics. But all units can kill all enemies - some just take longer. Rifle Squads are take a long time to hurt Plasma Bugs, for example. Or Snipers can outrange Spitters.The gameplay bugs are trivial and barely noticeable. Post-release, I've only seen one instance of Arachnid pathfinding getting confused and one instance of clipping. The lost Arachnid did eventually get out of the confused path and start heading towards one of my bases. The clipping issue was solved by killing the offending Arachnid. So, again, Music & Voice Acting: Passable. Could be better but that's trivial compared to the gameplay being nearly flawless. They know how to put corny lines in. My current favorite is "If we ain't dying, we ain't trying!" No, there aren't any cast members from the original 1997 movie reprising their roles. No, there aren't any hero units currently. Maybe in the future. General Rico is only mentioned in passing.Visuals: Good for what it is. Arachnids are Arachnids, troopers die in gruesome ways. It is easy to tell apart all of the Terran units and generally easy enough for the Arachnids. I sometimes confuse Tigers with regular Warriors, but that's only when the two are mixed in large swarms.If new content comes, I will add more to this review.

The voice acting is crap, and the whole game has a "this is a 2016 RTS" feel in the worst way possible. _childDocuments_.review: Will we ever get a strategy game that simulates the Iraq war or the Israel/Palestine conflict?  Nope, never.  Can't do that, it's offensive.Buuuut.... Here's a game where you're sent to a desert planet, to capture strategic mineral resources.  You're attacked constantly by enemies that spawn from places you're NOT allowed to attack until Command gives the all clear, Your Command is a bunch of incompetent idiots that hide behind a woman in order to avoid responsibility for their boneheaded decisions.   They will constantly tell you that you're doing great when they order you to almost certain death.   Whenever a soldier gets killed, you're expected to just airlift in replacements and continue on as if nothing happened.Your opponents are armed with suicide bombs, blades, and poison.  Often they will not die when shot, charging at you in a blind rage.   You are expected to stand behind walls and shoot them as they approach, giving no warning and no quarter.  You are also expected to call in air strikes from afar, and use walking tanks, which can't handle ambushes, so of course they have to be screened by infantry...Would you like to know more about Iraq?Review changed to negative in order to better reflect late game play experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game.Its stupid how much I enjoy playing this game. I like the movie, I prefer the book, but this game is just unbelievably fun. The developers did an excellent job, for the most part. Pro's: - Stupid fun to play- Great variety of unit types and abilities for each - Missions are varied enough to keep you engaged - The promotion/reinforcement system actually makes the player   care about their basic infantry units...they're not just cannon fodder- Actual strategy required as enemy abilities scale with the player- Impossible to "kite" the AI, for the most part. Con's: - There is only one campaign...this game could have several without feeling repetitive, ala Age of Empires. - No online/multiplayer options - Some minor AI pathfinding issues/ glitches- No cutscenes and very little narration...not much of a storyDEVELOPER Recommendations:- Expansion campaigns should include planet hopping/multiple locales - Be able to place units in two control groups simultaneously- Do more with bases...one suggestion would be an armory where you can include   an equipment level up system...so the units level up and gain abilities, but also be able to spend supply/war   support on upgraded equipment. Barrel Rifling = +3 tiles range, Lighter Armor Aloy +2 speed, Heavy Armor   Aloy + 2 armor (or more HP) etc. - Removable Structures from Deployment Pads...so only holding one position can swap unit types, but never   have all units available at once unless you have all radio towers secured - Also, the tanker bug needs to be buffed with more armor/damage and the scorpion bug needs to be nerfed, turrets should get at least two hits from one, otherwise engineers become totally irrelevant in late game. - Add a Horde Defense Mode, just a fully walled base with increasing supply/war support after every couple waves as they become harder waves. - AI needs to better prioritize enemy targets, snipers should automatically target spitters, not drones while spitters are doing damage to the place. - Add an Internal Hive mission/mode...no reinforcements, just 2 squads of power troopers. two squads of riflemen and two teams of engineers (power troopers that can be repaired with engineers) with 2 war support  and only regular machine gun turrets available (all the units that can enter a hive currently...the challenge is to get to the center of the hive for a brainbug...if you run out of troops before that, you fail)

_childDocuments_.review: Dizzy: Rico, I'm dying...Johnny Rico: No Diz, you'll be fine.Dizzy: But it's OK, because I got to have you.Overall this is a good game, but it does have some issues.The great stuff is that the sound and graphics are great and it really sounds like you are fighting a army of bugs. The story is written well and I like the subtle tones in the writing such as calling prisoners "Patriotic Volunteers" when you send them down a mine full of arachnids.The bad stuff is primarily with the difficulty and the mapping of unit movements. The difficulty is based on damage which is not bad, the higher the difficulty the lower the damage you do. The problem is that certain types of bug can only be effectively hurt with a certain type of Mobile Infantry, so you can have moments in missions where you can not  kill a bug quick enough before the other types kill you all. As for the movement issue of units, most Mobile Infantry units can not shot through each other and fire while moving, but when moving they take the quickest path to the destination you send them. So you can have a firing line of ten units in a sewer level and when telling them to move down to the corner the first unit closest takes the corner first and starts shooting a bug and the other nine Infantry units take the same exact path and now none of them will shoot or move and they all will be eaten, even in "Attack Move".So overall it is a good game, not the best, but it's okay, because I got to have you.I also recommend you use Wemod on the higher difficulties just for the resources to span units and then try to kill all the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game a lot of time. But it came with many defects. It has to go back to the shop before it is decently playable. My issues with the game are: (1) Reinforce: What a mess. You have to mark a place in the ground, then hit the stupid button and then after several tries, you get the reinforcements. This should be a simple halo around a special character/base. The current method is exhausting and prolongs the game unnecessarily. The whole routine is boooooring. By the way, The officer should be the one with this perk to avoid wasting time. The radio guy is absolutely useless (very difficult to use). And the HQ pistol officer is another distraction that wastes very limited resources. (2) Special perks: There is no way to use them. it is already too complicated to move the units around. This should be a passive item that gets activated. Clicking them is boring. (3) Units priority fire: This is waaay too crude. Rockets waste their time with non heavies and let the Scorpions move around. It doesn't matter if you have a perfect formation of units, the rockets won't do their job. They have to be micro-managed. (4) Formations: Too messy and have to be micro-managed all the time. There are many games to copy this from. There should be several formation types like Circle (support units in the center); and Chevron (arrow or spear). And more units to have several platoons attacking. (5) Snipers: They are useless. I had several costly setbacks because I used this idiotic unit. (6) Game pace: Too slow and forces the player to waste an unreasonable amount of time. (7) Turrets: There should be more, since the available amount of units is small. So there should be a way to leave defenses in your bases. But no, the game forces you to move and the insects take your base while you are in the map since you have a few units. This is an opportunity wasted for complex battles with multiple platoons all over the map. (8) Robots: I got exited when I saw them, but then got extremely disappointed by their horrible performance. It takes forever to get them, they are too slow and get toasted y Scorpions in milliseconds. Better to replace them for key control areas in the map like artillery bases, that if the player opts to control, they rain fire on the entire map, but have to be defended.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely enjoyable homage to the 1997 Starship Troopers movie (No not the book, and that's okay; some people can simultaneously enjoy two different types of media, and if you're on of the weird haters of either who thinks everyone should have the same views as you, well you're a mouth-breathing gremlin). In ST:TA basically role-playing the Federation from the movie, and if you do, this is a great experience. Walls of unsupported infantry blasting away tracer fire at endless Arachnids that twitch and spasm as they are riddled with bullets. Having a squad of Mobile Infantry swamped by bugs on a hill, blasting away with their underslung shotguns, and calling in a TAC strike in on them because, well, they're doing their part and they will be remembered as Heroes of the Federation. GloriousIt's a old-style RTT, I say RTT rather than RTS as this is a squad management game, with the beginning missions having maybe three or four, and the later ones a dozen at most. You get MI riflemen, snipers, engineers, powered armour troopers and, everyone's favourite, M11 Babar "Marauder" battle mechs, among others There's limited elements of base building, but engineers can build turrets to satisfyingly hold choke points (a brief moment of silence to remember the two MI of the tower gun at Whiskey Outpost...). Units are brought in via dropship at node points that are captured, and infantry are reinforced for free in the same manner - in the true tone of Starship Troopers, units wil die, so meh, call in more! The Battle of Big K supposedly saw 300,000 dead, so you're doing okay if you lose a few units. The graphics are decent enough, the MI models are pretty decent. There are a few janky animations (the soldiers go from a "ready" position to firing in a weird snappy animation). The bugs, on the other hand, look great. The tanker bug in particular creates the appropriate sense of "oh ♥♥♥♥". The terrain is relatively simple, being a desert planet but there are a lot of good assets, burnt out vehicles, busted forts - it's very well models on the movie. The lighting, however, is very good, with scuttling shadows in the dark looking great. The cut scenes have a really nice aesthetic, played as propaganda videos for the Terran Federation. The game can be challenging. You will of course see the "I beat this easily on Brutal" threads in the forum, and good for them, but for the average playing it's challenging, and some missions are trickier than others.  Level designs are nice, with multiple paths and ways of achieving objectives on most of them. There are a few "tunnel missions", (think the power plants in Command and Conquer Red Alert). If you hate those, tough luck, but I actually found them quite enjoyable - they definitely bring the chittering hordes in the dark vibe to the game. There's a few balance issues with things like scorpion bugs (urgh), but I'm sure that will be ironed out eventually.Voice acting is good - I enjoyed the main characters and the classic ST story. Likewise, sound is decent and meaty with the retort of weapons (there's a lot of that) and the screeching of bugs. The game isn't too long - the campaign and scenarios took about 10-12 hours. I played through the campaign twice and enjoyed it both times. I really hope that there's additional content in the future with additional scenarios. Overall the game is an excellent addition to a genre that really saw it's heyday almost twenty years ago (oh man, I feel old), and a really loyal depiction of the Paul Verhoeven movie. So remember; the only good bug is a dead bug, and everyone fights, no-one quits!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit-Original game is fun, DLC has been made idiotically difficult. Avoid the DLC. When it's more chance and luck than planning and strategy, you know you have gone ahead and killed the Goose that laid the golden egg. Why would you do that?Original review-A word of advice before I talk about what I think about the game.This game is not a classical RTS. Base building is not focused for example on unlocking research tiers and using that to unlock more powerful units. You don't have resources that you can use to purchase units in the classical RTS sense- in game resources constitute of tiers of battle and unit logistics which sub for old school RTS concepts like currency and raw materials, but are earned very differently. Now moving since that's out of the way, first the good bits. This game is a lot of fun. To the point of being addictively so. There is good balance in how the story unfolds without overwhelming first timers to the franchise. It isn't too deep, but hits all the right spots. If you have seen the movie or Read Heinlein's book, you will instantly recognise the source material.Each mission brings in something new and it's satisfying to continuously unlock new units which allows you to really experiment with your squad load-out and approach victory in different ways. Squelching them bugs when you are at a numerical disadvantage but hold a tactical advantage feels just about right for a committed citizen of the federation.While the unit leveling mechanism is rather limited, it doesn't detract from the gameplay. If anything, the game encourages you to use special abilities wisely and cleverly turn the tide of the battle in your favor. Bugs flanking you? Get your elite rocket troopers to block one side with a firestorm missile launch and funnel the bugs into killzone where them critters run into the muzzle of your troops impressive armament. Now for cons, which IMO don't detract from the quality of the gameplay but are annoying nonetheless.There are minor bugs related to squad animations where your units get stuck in motion and look like they're suffering a seizure. Sometimes units appear through the terrain if you pan the camera too fast.There is a huge amount of micromanagement required from you and while this fun sometimes, it would be nice if we could set some default actions for the units like holding their ground or have a balance between aggression and defense. All too often tactical units which need to be in the back line end, end up in the front and get slaughtered because they aren't supposed to be there, but in the heat of the battle you've selected all your units enmasse to move them to a specific point or to attack a specific location. You can number code units or groups of units but in the heat of the battle, selecting each group through a number on the keypad is rather tedious for a largely point and click game. Also some of the instructions aren't really clear (for example clearing bug hives) and require some trial and error before you perfect it. I get that the game doesn't want to babysit you, but when there is a tutorial (of sorts), these little things that are important within the game context can be helpful especially at higher difficulty levels.Lastly, not a game bug, but this game is too short, needed more content for such an excellent game. I Will look forward to either a DLC or a sequel where we take the fight to bug homeworld and crush them once and for all!

The more objectives you accomplish, the more challenges are being introduced "more difficult bug times, bugs spawning more, etc, etc", it just gets old too quickly about 15 hrs in.If you want to really enjoy this type of game, I suggest playing easy mode because the animations are cool, as well as the immersion is top notch and the maps are well designed in details.I will try this game again if the devs start to patch some things and actually play test the game.I recommend you grab this game only if it is less than 30 bucks, it is at the end repetitive and wears out about 15 hrs in.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a yes, but with reservations.The game is enjoyable enough; glitch--free, well made, it doesn't have an overly difficult learning curve, it looks good, the voice acting is solid, there is a good variety of community content, and it's a decent representation of Star Ship Troopers...mostly.What it is lacking is passion and punch. It just feels repetitive and somewhat lackluster.  There aren't any tense moments, there is no attachment to units (but in the meat-grinder world of SST, that is fully acceptable, it's just that a loss is only a tactical moment, not a regret of losing a cherished squad or character), or any real doubt as to the outcome.There isn't anything wrong with it, but there isn't anything overly right with it either. I don't look forward to playing it, but I also don't look at it as time lost when I do. I will say that after six or so hours, I'm losing interest in it and will probably shelve it for a bit.I don't regret buying it, I'm just happy that it was on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: i pre-ordered this and tbh i was very happy with the game on release there are little to no bugs what bugs there are are minor things like troops when standing still sometimes will have a member of the platoon running around trying to get to his allocated spot or sometimes not engage a enemy within range unless told to do so at first i thought i must have given them the order to hold fire but it happened a fair few times on different levels with different units. If your like me and have persistent dead body's because that's what we are playing for really lets be honest then a dead bug or trooper will now and again remain in his idle pose (found a guide since its not a option in the base game) The story is ok it has that same level of cheese from the movies but as a whole it takes from all of the Starship troopers universes from the movies to the book to the older games and i believe a board game?!? This game really nails it and can not be faulted What needs work is at some parts minor parts like the trooper who cant stand still  however 1: There needs to be more replay value be this challenges or achievements or new game modes as once you have done the campaign there is pretty much nothing to do than play it again at a harder difficulty which does not net you anything other than a imaginary blue peter badge.2: As a keen RTS player i had a fairly difficult time at the start but soon got the hang of it but will admit i struggle on higher difficulties this is (arguably) down to some of the enemies such as the scorpion bugs which while yes manageable with the right troops they are still down right annoying most times a hive can spawn said scorpion bugs faster than your troops can get to the hive and within seconds start decimating you from range greater than your currently deployed troops whom may be in the middle of clearing said hive only to retreat at half health  into the waiting claws of the scorpions that have just spawned.3: No multiplayer: i'm not asking for player Vs bug although that would be cool, but co-op would be nice even within the campaign some mission its tough to manage several assaults on positions all at once what with how necessary it is to use troop abilities to survive the onslaught so a friend helping out would be niceAll in all i do enjoy it as a fan of the movies i am happy with my purchase i can not fault it for it had a very enjoyable playable launch and even got a copy for a friend but i was kind of expecting more.

_childDocuments_.review: There's little to say about this one. The RTS mechanics are shallow as a puddle. You can call down units and have units cast abilities on long cooldowns. No resource gathering, no base building (aside from a token building slot system that acts more like an upgrade than a base), essentially no strategic element, this is a lot closer to DoW2 than Starcraft.That's not inherently a bad thing--I'm not really a fan of CoH/DoW2-like RTS games compared to traditional ones, but some people like them a lot more. But I think even with that preference, this doesn't quite cut it. Your units move  slow through vast maps. At least 60% of your playtime will be watching your little apes jogging around in the empty desert and tunnels. Unit abilities can make a difference but there's no thought in using them, you largely just spam them when they get off cooldown.The flavor is right, at least. The mission briefings are done as Federation news broadcasts that invariably sugarcoat the awful situation on the ground, papering over your doomed soldiers with banal slogans and empty patriotism. The few voiced characters also sell the heartless machinery of war you're a cog in, though the voice acting is strange. Very strange. I'm not entirely convinced the characters weren't voiced by a text-to-speech program.Ultimately what kills it for me is the pacing. Every mission is slow, painfully slow, as moving takes ages and combat is mostly a case of standing around hitting the "shoot more" hotkey occasionally. I think I got about halfway through the game's missions before getting tired of it all.Only buy if you're desperate for a starship troopers fix and it's on sale for $5 or less.

The maps are poorly designed and remind me of an old command and conquer game. There is no story worthy of the name. The voice acting is terrible. Avoid or buy when it's $1.99

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Good RTS, if you like the genre for playing campaigns buy this one.After playing through the campaign and scenarios I have to say its a realy good RTS.An RTS that purely focus on single player and does that that very well, something that has been missing for decades in the genre.The units fit well and each has its place for tactical reasons, the endgame units are extremly powerful and fell good as a reward for getting to the end.The mission design is one of the best in the last decades, it has everything from "base building" and non base building offensive and defensive missions, to indoor and survival mission over escort and multi staged missions. I normally hate indoor, escort and survival mission but they are done too well to complain about them. The indoor missions have refill points so you don't have to play perfectly the whole time, the escorts are eighter imbeded in other mission styles or only a short part of multi staged missions and the survival part also is mostly part multi stage missions or has very reasonable short timers, no "survive 30min" bs where you clear the map in 10min and than have to wait because the mission says so.For the setting, I watched the first movie a long time ago but wasn't a fan but even if you don't like the setting and humor the game is really fun to play. When you are a fan of the films than you will definetly enjoy the storytelling and humor and there are scenes that you will recognise from the movies (I assume that there are also scenes in from the movies I haven't watched).

_childDocuments_.review: FEDERAL NETWORK RELEASEOur boys and girls in the Mobile Infantry protect the galaxy from the Arachnid menace, and now they are available on YOUR terminals and personal devices!Starship Troopers: Terran Command is an RTS set in the Heinlein-inspired world of the Starship Trooper films. Set on the fictional Kwalasha, players will command their own regiments of the M.I. as they fight to push the Bugs off this valuable industrial world and secure it for Terra.Focusing on combat, you will command ground elements of the M.I. inspired by all three films, from light infantry to Marauders and the modern exo-armour of 'Invasion' and 'Traitor of Mars'. Against you is arrayed the full force of the Bug race: Warriors, Spitters, Tiger Warriors and even Plasma Bugs. All that need to be put down by your heroic troopers!While rocky to start with, the beginnings of the Year One roadmap have seen valuable improvements in the user interface's comprehensibility, balancing of how effective certain units are against others and - especially a problem early on! - unit path-finding. While some viewers might bemoan the lack of achievements or multiplayer capability, the Year One roadmap issued by the Federal Council assures viewers that future updates are pending that will expand replayability and content.So join up, citizens! Do YOUR part! There's a war going on!SERVICE GUARANTEES CITIZENSHIPWOULD YOU LIKE TO KNOW MORE?

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little bug hunt RTS in the "real-time tactics" subgenre similar to CoH's main campaigns. Not a base-builder game.Missions are surprisingly challenging and fun, starting out quite simplistic and easy but quickly ramping up into some tense challenges. _childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game for what it is. The mechanics are fairly simple, but fun overall. The game is fairly cheap, so don't expect a fully fleshed out AAA RTS experience. Nevertheless there is probably a dozen-plus hours of content here that would be worth at least a second playthrough.A word on difficulty. The game is VERY easy (IMO) the first 3 difficulty levels, and even hard difficulty isn't too difficult until things get really hectic. The very hardest difficulty is IMO the most enjoyable in that it will punish you for not playing smart. That said some later levels where you can't get reinforcements easily are punishing on very hard difficulty. You have the option for each mission to adjust the difficulty, you might want to step down the difficulty on the mine missions while leaving it very hard for others.I also advise you learn the keyboard commands. There is no pause for this game, so when battles get a bit large it is useful to know how to quickly tab between units and select grenades and other special abilities with keyboard shortcuts to.
_childDocuments_.name: Starship Troopers: Terran Command

_childDocuments_.review: A great RTS in a fabulous series. The combat is great with each difficulty not only making more bugs spawn, but do things like lower the damage of your units making strategy a key part of every fight. The use of high ground and true sight lines make positioning and proper unit types key throughout the campaign. The introduction of a custom map maker along with challenge levels make this game shine after the campaign. The DLCs are fresh, adding new planets, new bugs, new mechanics, and new units. I've played this game's campaign through 4 times and still go back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current form I cannot recommend this game. Yes, it is early access and yes, it does have the look and feel of the movies. The maps and animations look nice. What completely ruins the fun is troop management and especially movement. It is impossible to change the formation of the squad, which leads to them standing in each others way in the most stupid way possible. In combination with the very narrow ways (for such a clumsy force) of which the various maps have a lot - which is strange, as most of them are on desert planets, your men get killed.For the first six or so maps you just give the attack order and let your men do the rest, which is quite boring. Sometimes triggered events occur, which leads to enemy units appearing behind your lines and start destroying you scarce resources and building, leaving you stranded, as you cannot train new troops. But movement and room to maneuver is not the only problem, as the controls are very clumsy, slow and often not work properly. Also, you are supposed to place units like snipers on elevated places. Most of the time that is not possible. Or, it is only possible after passing enother chokepoint where you just kill all the bugs. Since all the bugs are dead when you arrive at the elevated position, there is no need to place the snipers here any longer. Stuff like this happens all the time. Currently 5/10 - not recommendable

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a bad game by any means. Unfortunately for me though, it takes a great game to really hold my attention nowadays. I was hoping for a Command & Conquer and StarCraft hybrid of sorts, with a Starship Troopers theme. This game is simply too linear and too restricting to keep me interested. It's a series of capture-the-flag type of missions over and over again where you can only grow your military presence and strength in primarily predefined ways. It's not the open concept, gather, build, expand, and conquer type of RTS game that I was yearning to play. I've only played the game a little over 3 hours and I already feel like I can see exactly how the remainder of the game would play out.I absolutely loved the movies (especially the first one), but the game just isn't interesting enough to keep me coming back for more. I will say some of the fort defense missions are pretty darn fun, but they are too few and far in between. I picked this game up on sale so I can't complain. I'll say it's good enough to justify the $22 I spent on it, even though I won't finish it.I'd only recommend it to perhaps younger gamers who are big fans of the Starship Troopers movies. If you're young then you probably haven't played as many games as I have, and so your expectations and standards might not be as high as mine have become over the years. If I had to score the game, I'd give it a 6/10. If it weren't so restrictive with regard to where and when you can build and expand, I would have increased the score to a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. The mechanics are well balanced and every unit and every bug type has its place in the game. That is no real problem for me but some people might see this as a critic point. I played 18 hours to finish the campagne and the scenarios.Some levels of the game a really much harder than others but you always can restart and adjust the difficulty settings like you want.The only real critic point I've got is that some mechanics are not directly understandable even though they are shown in game. _childDocuments_.review: About 20 hours to complete the main story and a little longer to complete the two challenge missions. Overall I liked the game. The first half of the missions I was playing on the 4 star hard mode. But after the half way point the missions get much more difficult. I had to go down to the 3 and 2 star difficulties to complete the missions. It is a unique RTS game with the bug enemy and the Starship Troopers world which is awesome. The game does get a little repetitive, especially on the harder missions that take time to take out all of the bug hives. A lot of the levels have the same objectives. Take out a bunch of bug hives while securing more bases. Some levels are unique though, such as capturing a fugitive and dealing with a prison riot. My favorite level would be the final level. The big down sides are the fact that you cannot play as the Bugs and there is no multiplier or procedurally generate maps vs AI modes for more replayability. If the Bugs had playable missions and multiplayer then this game would get a couple more points. But I do believe for what is included the $29.99 asking price is fair. Positives: Starship Troopers World. Unique RTS against Bugs. Some Unique Missions. Various Units. Good Campaign Length. Cons: Many Repetitive Missions, especially the ones that are longer. Only Humans Campaign, No Playable Bug Missions. No Multiplayer. No procedurally generate maps to play. Very Little Replayability. 6/10 - Slightly Above Average

_childDocuments_.review: Early impressions are surprisingly positive. On the previews it looked like a dull and primitive corridor army crawler (which is the strategy game equivalent of a walking sim), but the actual gameplay is much more interesting, with hordes of Arachnids flowing from multiple directions while you need to push for objectives, capture bases for reinforcements (yes, there is some simple economy here) and keep your soldiers alive against an unending tide of bugs.Some aspects of the game seem "cheap" (barely servicable graphics, lack of audiovisual impact, mediocre unit animations) but the love for the movie makes up for it: The tone is spot on, gameplay replicates the lore well, and I think there are even some book-inspired mechas later on. I am a bit torn on the music as it sounds cheap but does its' best at replicating the original movie's soundtrack and I find it hard no to commend it for that.I'll edit the review later once I do my part.

_childDocuments_.review: Couple reasons why this game is worth it overall. First of all, more Starship Troopers is never a bad thing - it's classic satire anyone can enjoy ironically or unironically. Rarer than you might think, and the game embodies it; not just in tone but in gameplay too. The RTS gameplay perspective itself lends another layer into the Federation's MO and ordering around a bunch of apes are satisfying. They move fast, pathfind in clear reasonable ways, and the line of sight physics are welcome.There's also the simple fact that we don't have too many campaign-driven rts games outside of Starcraft (which has messy consistency so it barely counts) and Relic games - namely Homeworld. This game doesn't have deep great writing, but it does have personality and a clear narrative, which is something.Some problems though. Mostly in balancing. The developers have a very limiting view on what "difficulty" means. Hardest mode just means bullets showered, the core bug AI is predictable as is any mission structure that relies to heavily on scripted "gotcha!" moments. Simply put, don't play this if you're an RTS buff... but do play this if you want a solid starter entry.Beyond that, it's reasonably priced and it's fun - what any person wants really from a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, its nothing super innovative and special. However, It is a great addition to the franchise. You don't get to see it alot in full (except in one challenge map) but the progression control/scale is well done, prevents you or the enemy from going OP too fast but definitely has a reward/punishment factor for strategy and efficiency.Many updates just keep making it better!

_childDocuments_.review: For a measly 30 dollars, this game delivers a good Starship Troopers experience. The campaign is fun, for the most part. It's a solid RTS experience, it captures the source material well, and takes some particularly interesting mechanics such as requiring firing lines for your riflemen because you can't shoot through allied units.Now, for the negatives:-Clunky Movement: The game is not *difficult* but it is tedious at times. Some units will stop and attack when in range of an enemy during an attack move, other times they will stop, fire, move up, stop, fire, move up, and rinse and repeat until they're jumping into bug maws. This wouldn't be a particularly bad thing if melee damage was not so utterly devastating to your units. Your units are slower than enemies, which means if you need to run away, you're going to leave one unit behind to die off, because you CANNOT escape the enemy. Other units, such as rocket teams and marauders, are constantly getting stuck on corners and have to be manually controlled to get unstuck.-Babysitting: I don't mind a bit of micromanagement, but when the game is designed around micromanagement while also having really clunky unit controls, you're essentially doubling up on the player tedium. This gets especially nightmarish whenever you have to defend multiple areas or attack one area while defending another. I understand it's needed to some extent because of the barebones base/resource building, but I think it's worth mentioning it's a bit too far in the wrong direction.-Trimmed Down Strategy Elements: When it comes to base building and resources, this game is skeletal when it comes to RTS. Base building is limited to capture points with set slots for what units you can recruit, and resources are tied to map objectives and the occasional capture point. This does put the focus on the bug shooting, but it does leave something to be desired. The only real building you do is placing turrets from your combat engineers. I would have liked to be able to construct more, as well as have more intricacy with resource allocation. If you combined the base building and resource gathering of They Are Billions with this game, it would be phenominal. One of the last maps has a system where killing enemies increases your available resources, and I think that should have been a baseline feature. I like having some gameplay/counter play with resources, like having a more vulnerable position that generates more resources for me, risk/reward. There are very few maps that actually utilize this. On the more difficult maps, I just let the enemies take my points that I wasn't interested in defending because it cost me nothing, and that's a negative consequence of the simplified resource system. Losses are essentially nothing, because your resources just determine the maximum number of units you can bring, and you can always replace them with a minor cooldown to transport ships. In some cases, your defenses can be so solid that you essentially stalemate the enemy with no real victor.-Infinite Respawns: The nature of the game essentially gives massive bonuses to the defender, both bug and human.  Humans have defensive turrets, can recapture any lost point, can respawn any unit that dies, and can hold a defense while "healing" a unit on the point. Bugs, on the other hand, can be an absolute nightmare. A hive with 3+ tunnels attached to it is essentially invulnerable short of extreme overpowering on the player's part. You'll often find that when you're trying to clear out a hive, the defenders respawn so frequently that you're fighting more by the time you finish a wave. If this map spawns the scorpion unit, then you are in for a nightmare of a slog. My personal feeling is that replenishing bug caves should be halted, or at least slowed if there is a military presence nearby it. There comes a point where you're moving the needle by centimeters until you're finally able to get that goldilocks moment of having a 0 strength hive to clear out before the next wave spawns. If you're wondering why I didn't just clear it once my army strength was higher, it's because my game was bugged and if you ever sent in an army in there and there was even 1 enemy group left, your entire army will die in there regardless of being stronger. I lost a 4.0 army to a 1.0 hive because the hive just didn't take damage.-Units: Experienced units should be an investment, and a detriment if lost. Veterancy unlocks a choice between one of two abilities to equip the unit with. Usually there is a correct choice and a wrong choice. I also disagree with a shared cooldown on every ability. I think there should be more tiers of veterancy, all of which improve a soldier's output as well. The only units that really mattered to me if they were veterans or not were rocket troopers, and snipers. Everything else was disposable. I think there could be a bit more unity variety as well. I'm not sure why Marauders have 3 individual units whereas power troopers are able to change their weaponry upon veterancy. I think it would make more sense for marauders to start with the grenade bombardment ability, and then upon veterancy select between flamethrowers, gatlings or howitzers. Again, I really want to stress that veterans should be a significant investment and reward. A minor nitpick as well: Rocket troopers should really have an aoe. I know they're already basically the must have unit, but I absolutely hate how often they miss single targets because their big warhead has zero splash damage.-Balance: Good lord what masochist created the Scorpion unit? The units for the most part are reasonably balanced, but this thing is a blight upon civilization. It would be fine as a strong high priority unit, but the problem is that they often spawn *en masse.* I've gotten into the habit of having a sacrifice unit for Scorpions. So I just sent the dead men to their graves while my rockets do their best to focus fire one by one. There's some rebalancing to be done across the board, but these guys are a glaring thorn in the side.-Campaign Design: The campaign is generally fun, and I enjoyed them keeping the starship troopers motif well. I did, however, have a few problems with some of the design for the campaign. There are some questionable design decisions for the campaign.  Having an ambush that you need to hold fire until the right time, but then putting the tutorial for hold fire in the mission AFTER that. There were also several times where secondary objectives just had no value. Like literally no value, or even a detriment. Said ambush was one such secondary objective. It's a difficult fight that you can choose to do. And as a reward for doing it you get nothing. I think the missions need a second look over to make sure the objectives are handled appropriately. Generally speaking, main objectives should just be for victory, whereas secondary objectives should be more difficult things to do with actual risk, but also yield rewards for doing them. I'll also note that the no-build missions are probably the lowest point of the game. I do not care for these kind of missions, especially because the lack of a way to replenish lost troops means you could very well be unable to finish the mission, but not know it until much later on. I'm sad to see that an actually helpful AI partner was saved for the very last mission.  I would have liked to see more missions involving AI players. I also think it's rather bizarre that bunkers and special heavy turrets that cannot be built also cannot be repaired by combat engineers.All in all, it's a good game. Worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers: Terran Command is a very faithful continuation of the Verhoeven's classic. As a game however it fares far, far worse, alas. The jank, the bugs (hehe) & the lack of the very standard quality of life features will have ruined this game for anyone but the most hardcore RTS fan. Here's the silly me thinking I could get back into the genre by picking it up. Unfortunately I am not a hardcore RTS fan. Never been. Never will. All the way back in the 90s I played some of the legendary OG Warcraft 2 & Starcraft, some trash like Krush Kill & Destroy (Yes, it was the time of the capital "K"), & even the criminally underrated, ahead of its time diamond in the rough: Total Annihilation. I finished neither. But I did finish X-COM: UFO Defense which guess what, was a strategy game, but not an RTS. It too was ahead of its time by two decades. Such was the style at the time in the 90s, kids.I am convinced that RTS as a genre, whilst not being dead like the immersive sim, is still a very niche genre overall. There's a single culprit to blame for it. You know how there's always a meta to basically every game out there, right? Well, for RTS as a whole it's the actions per minute metric. It all comes down to that simple number. Now, I reject that notion, just like I reject being forced to perfectly memorize boss patterns in From Soft games (it's okay, I adapt to beat them in my own ways). It's just not for me. Sadly, such is the case here. You have to micromanage your idiot troops like toddlers. Running through fire to get an entire squad killed? No problem, boss. We have it. Flocking like morons into a single square meter just to die from an AoE attack? Sir, yes, sir!If that weren't enough, of course the game bugs out all the time. The pathfinding is broken, especially for an army of more than 3 squads. They will either get stuck, or more often take separate paths to your designated destination. They will freeze in the aforementioned square meter surrounded by aliens to be slaughtered mercilessly. I'm not even talking about being able to shoot trough walls, that comes with the job. All of this is but a tiny sample of the ever present jank.For some reason special abilities can only be used by a single squad... I'm sorry, but why? There's no formations that were a standard feature twenty freakin' years ago in games like Perimeter. If there's one thing this game needs more than air is battle formations. The troopers just loosely follow a staggered column. By loosely I mean very loosely. But there isn't consistency even here. The pulse rifle troopers are all glued together in a rigid square, making them the single most useless unit in the game. Yes, sometimes pulse rifles is all you get, so you have to make due. Dear god.The game tells you, the player in the first mission is that it's about positioning troops. You break formation, you die. Only it makes it impossible to keep your troops positioned. It's like herding cats. There's no hold position button. So they'll just run off to do something stupid and hence get themselves killed. At a midway point in the main campaign the game throws AoE attacks your way. Guess what? No disperse button either. How am I supposed to hold my positions like that without micro managing every single squad? That takes a very special kind of person, mind you. Most of those people are in South Korea playing Starcraft on esports. I'm neither Korean, nor an RTS esporter. I want my strategy games be about strategy, not about clicking and pressing buttons real fast. Is this so much to ask, game?The campaign goes off the rails in the second half. The DLCs fare better, but even then it's a coin flip as to whether it's gonna be good or crap. This of course sours the whole experience. I really want to like this game, I really do, but I have an upper limit of frustration & baby sitting my soldiers in real time is an instant disqualifier. If you enjoy ApM gameplay, then by all means, be my guest. I in the meanwhile am going to go hit my head against the wall a couple dozen times.Now, I said in the beginning that the story is good. Yes, it is very good. The only reason why I dragged my feet to finish this holy mess of a game at all. Now, why did I say it was the continuation of Verhoeven's classic & not Heinlein's? Because the former understands the source material better than the latter despite not being its original author. Kinda in the same vein as Mary Shelley & her Frankenstein. That is if you read her radical feminist preamble that completely misses the point. Death of the author & all that. The author's interpretation is just one of many.I've read a rather amusing review here on Steam about how the game "disrespects the source material". I'm not sure if the author was serious or not, but let's assume they were for a moment. Because it betrays them quite a fair bit without them even realizing it.People who regurgitate the all too familiar phrase "service guarantees citizenship" uncritically and hence unironically are missing the obvious external implications for it being a blatant con. The war is waged in perpetuity by design. The "arachnids" are the perfect enemy for a fascist state. An overwhelming external (?) threat that replenishes its ranks faster than they're eradicated. A colossus that shrugs off every federal attempt at hurting it as no more than a mosquito bite. Yet the "superior technology and tactics" shall surely prevail over the uncivilized hordes.We've heard all of this before more than once. Only now we don't even need to unperson each other anymore. They're just bugs that ought to be squashed. Who cares how this war started, who started it. There's no question about it: a good bug is a dead bug. All the intellect and obvious high levels of consciousness? Let's ignore that like we always do.But fret not, there's also traitors among us. Union leaders, mercenaries, people at the end of their rope financially, bug infested (?) humans. Everybody is out to get you, brave citizen to be, who's afraid of their own shadow at every hour of every day.The idea that this world is a utopia because there's gender equality is about as silly as the idea that "communism is when the government does stuff". It's only a utopia if one agrees to the premises. In other words it is a fascist's wet dream. Verhoeven understood that. Heinlein in his novel has created a fascist utopia. Whether on accident or by design. Having read his "magnum opus" Stranger in a Strange Land, or how I like to call it: The Wacky Adventures of Space Jesus on Earth, I tend to think it's probably the latter.Now, you may say that the aliens bad. Aliens might indeed be bad. But that's not the point. I don't need them to be good for my argument to work. There's no shortage of straightforward alien bad media in which they come home to destroy us. You won't hear a single objection about those from me. The point is that the aliens in this universe are the perfect enemy for a regime in a constant need of external & often internal threats. It's their Iraq & their Afghanistan to be waged war in perpetuity in. It's a pretense for something greater. And let me tell you, that greater is not for your benefit or mine. Fascism thrives on fear like a demon that subsists on suffering. Do not let fear control you.Wow, I'm being extremely political lately. First Lost Judgement, now this. How could I not though? Both these properties are highly political. To not speak on their implications is a crime in & of itself. Emotionally I felt dirty by the end of the Gehenna (DLC) campaign. What one of the protagonists does by the end & how it contrasts with the heroic music playing at the end of the mission. It almost made me want to vomit. This is good. I like media that challenged me, that tears me out of my comfort zone & beats the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. This is the best kind of media. This game in my opinion should have been an animated series. The story is that good.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Star craft 2 single player campaigns. I also really like AoE2 and AoE4, Grey goo, the various Homeworld games, Supreme commander/FA, C&C/RA, Ashes of the singularity. This starship troopers game is well worth playing. The tactics are much about positioning. Also about order of objectives. If you mix Ashes (replenishing troops + timing/concentration of force) with Company of heroes (positioning), but with more humor, I guess you get this game. The tutorial is a bit long perhaps, with maybe 5-7 missions being very attack-move-ish. But at around number 7 or so I had to pick up the pace a bit. So far, I haven't yet really had to rethink any of the obvious tactics, so I guess its been a bit shallow so far, but I have not played at the highest difficulty so far, and am only at perhaps map number 10 or so (8 hours in). Apparently there are around 20ish maps. So there is enough challenge in the game for me to have fun at least. 2.5 out of 5 for the depth of the game mechanics so far, but I hope that will increase to a 4 before I'm done.The atmosphere/voices and mission stories are great (in a stupid way, keeping true to the spirit of the source material). 5 out of 5 for the atmosphere.Many of the reviews I found of this game, both on Steam and on Youtube (e.g. IGN) were unnecessarily critical. We don't get a lot of games in this genre anymore. And if you like this genre, specifically sci-fi RTS, you can't really afford to miss this game. Get it. Play it. Enjoy it for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the greatest RTS that came out in a while.Every campaign goes through a satisfying military campaign exploring the glories and perils of battle, while revelling in the satire of the setting and explicitly showing that the federation is not good and none of this is desirable. Each campaign also explores the relationship between a new cast of interesting characters and how they influence each other in extreme circumstances, which provides personal engagement and really makes you care about what is going on not only gameplaywise but also emotionally. It has been a long time since I was genuinely surprised by characters in a rts campaign…It is refreshing to just get a finished, polished game for your money from the premiere, it is even more satisfying to get solid dlcs providing straight up new content in good quality and quantity (instead of some shi tty micro transaction shop like some rts do). It is also very nice to see creators providing extra missions outside of the dlc campaigns with the updates, that’s a nice touch that shows this is a work of someone who cares, not calculated investment of some pencil pushers.The gameplay is solid and innovates the rts formula in an interesting way, providing an extremely satisfying gameplay loop of positional warfare against the endless bugs. There is a bunch of unique units to play around with, and both the formula and level design allow for variety of tactics and combos. Experimenting and coming up with new (mostly dumb) things is very fun, and very much supported.I don’t think it is endlessly interesting like StarCraft2 endless depth and possibility, but for playing a solid dozen mission campaign from time to time it is very fun, simple as. The game has no coop and pvp but I see them as unnecessary to this game, I would not play it much I think, I don’t see how you could bend the formula enough to fit them.The art style is solid, and pleasant. While the models are on the simpler side, animations are lacking and the effect are not crazy, it is all very readable and flows nicely in combat. Also, the bugs look good and that the most important part for me.The sound effects are distinct and solid, that’s all. But the music and voice acting are STELLAR, some incredible work there! (Eli Harris, I’ve cried tears of joy because of you…)Also, my favourite detail:So in the first campaign we are on a desert planet (cos movie, you know how it is), and through the first few missions it looks like it’s going to be boring: endless rocky desert with some houses and walls here or there. But the designers drag you from desert to mines, to bug tunnels, to night missions, changing environments and colour schemes between missions or even during missions so it never becomes boring. Masterful use of limited assets and location types to change up the visual language of the game while reusing most of the stuff they made, that is genuinely impressive. Really! To the point when towards the end of the campaign you’re in the desert canyon again and your glad to be back in the comfort of known environment again… but you were fighting a war on a desert planet all the time! How cool is that!Also, also:Do you want to play as the bugs? Check out “The Defence of Fort Rico” in the stream workshop or ingame “Community Content” menu. The provided editor is superb, and if your hungry for content even after finishing the game you can find fully fledged CAMPAINS in there!That’s what I like to see, so that’s what I’m buying. _childDocuments_.review: The game offers 19 main missions divided into three types: attack, defence and missions where you have only a small group of soldiers at your disposal, we can call them stealth. Attack missions require clearing bugs on a map or capturing bases. Defence requires you to withstand big waves of insects. Sometimes attack missions change to defence and vice versa. When you play stealth you must complete certain objectives, but you can’t call new units at your base or you have limited support. All missions are well-designed along with the environment. Before starting, you can choose difficulty but it only changes the damage multiplier of your units. After the fulfilment of all primary objectives, there are also some secondary ones, you will get short comic cutscenes that move the story further. It is a good addition otherwise the story is told by three main characters during a mission. I would like to see some stats at the end of the mission too, not only the winning message and short cutscene because you have no idea how many units you lost or how many Arachnids did you kill.All of the mission types have one thing in common – clearing bugs’ hives. While your soldiers are defending the captured point, another group of units must clear the entrance by depleting Arachnids. Some hives are connected by tunnels that you should deplete as well. You can see the strength of your infantry (green text) and bugs (red text) when you hover the mouse over the hole. If red is more than green, it’s a suicide mission for soldiers. Once the tunnels are clear, you can focus on the main hive, but keep in mind that Arachnids can always respawn, so don’t forget to check the red bar above the tunnels. I think the devs make this system well and you must prepare a good tactic on each hive if you want to successfully clear it.In most RTS games you call units from the side menu and they come to the battlefield or you recruit them in buildings. In this game, you have small bases where you call units from the command centre and they will land on the ground at certain points in your base. You have two resource types: Supplies and War Support. Both can be raised by completing objectives or capturing some equipment around the map. For basic soldiers, you just need Supplies that work like population limit in other RTS games, but for stronger units, turrets or new buildings you need War Support as well. The selection of units is good, from regular soldiers armed with rifles to skilled snipers, officers and even heavy mechs, there's a unit for every situation. However, I have to admit that the MK II Troopers with their assault rifles and grenade launchers seem a little overpowered to me. A few groups of them can easily wipe out a horde. It would be nice to rebalance it, so players will try to combine more unit types and the unique skills that can gain from clearing Arachnids. Additionally, while the pathfinding system generally works well, there are some situations when units get stuck on obstacles or in narrow places. Some improvements would be good. Pathfinding is important here because there is some micromanaging of units that is nice. They can’t shoot from behind through other soldiers. You must check their lines of fire because If you have a larger group of infantry, but in the wrong formation, they will end fast, especially if some strong Arachnids appear like Tigers, Royale Guards or Tankers.The game has an Editor where you can create your own scenario. The UI is a little bit outdated, but you can make the same missions like you played in the main campaign. Of course, there is Steam Workshop support, so you can download many nice creations made by the community. I tried The Infernal Crossroads, and it was crazy, there were so many Arachnids everywhere. Also, there is a remake of missions from the old Starship Troopers Terran Ascendancy.

_childDocuments_.review: It is so nice and refreshing to find a game that simply works and does what it promised without compromise. No microtransactions, no nonsense always online servers causing single player lag, just... no nonsense.Starship Troopers: Terran Command provides you 19 campaign missions and 3 scenarios at the time of this writing. The missions are fully voice-acted, there are cutscenes before each mission to further the story and the game nails the feel of the Verhoeven movie universe with every sentence uttered, every mission briefing provided. They even managed to make the flashlight guns from the second movie into some semblance of a fun weapon and they remembered Starship Troopers: Marauder exists.I encountered no issues, no bugs, no crashes with the game in my time playing.The only two points of critique I could offer is that the missions could be a tad bit longer because I do enjoy just seeing waves of bugs crashing against a defensive position and being turned into chunks by superior firepower.And I would have liked a little more information on the HUD regarding the status of the bugs, and attached to that more hit feedback on tougher enemies such as Tigers to show whether your Riflemen are doing damage. The biggest enemies have health bars to indicate it but again, just a few signs of damage or deflection on the bug carapaces would have been nice.If you are a fan of the movie setting, I don't know why you wouldn't already own this game.If you want to play an interesting RTS campaign with reasonable amounts of content, pick this up maybe during a sale.

So all in all it's an enjoyable game, and it really brought life back into a franchise I wish never died, but it is lacking. There's rarely a loss condition in any of these levels. Enemies wont retake their old bases, your units spawn instantly so long as you have an available drop ship, and most units can create landing zones so even if a unit dies, you can spawn and then drop them back to your front lines rather quickly.For a 30 dollar game, it's not bad. I've definitely bought games that were equally priced and delivered far less content. *cough Democracy 4 cough* So yeah the voice acting is horrible, and yes it's a little simple, and I would have loved to play this game with friends. But I'm happy to fan boy at just the aspect of someone bringing back a franchise that no one ever dared to continue even though it was a cult classic. Maybe this could be the start of something more?

_childDocuments_.review: Terran Command is a pretty fun Solo-Focused RTS. It's simple in its mechanics and plays kind of like an improbable mix between Dawn of War 2 (You control just a few squads/Vehicles, each with abilities and veterancy) and napoleonic warfare (strong, strong emphasis on line battle, as your units cannot fire through each other, safe from a few exemples)The Starship Trooper aesthetic is spot-on, with each mission having a FedNet propaganda presentation often contradicting what you discover once loading, and every unit basically acting like Helldivers with no sense of self-preservation and unwavering morale.It may become a bit repetitive after a bit, as you are limited to 1 faction (Mobile Infantry) and 1 biome (Desert, with some Urban environment in a couple of missions), at least in the main game. It's kind of the same for the missions, usually revolving around cleaning up Hives and Nest in-between waves of bugs. However, the addition of an Editor is pretty interesting, as I tested a mission where you played as the Arachnids in kind of a reverse Tower Defense fashion.So, yeah, I recommend, pretty solid game :D

_childDocuments_.review: Starship Troopers lands a good 4/5 game. The Score, Graphics, and Presentation are generally pretty strong, although sometimes there is a missing voice line here or there, and a smattering of animations can look silly; additionally, there are some visual bugs (haha) which can make unit icons appear somewhere other than where they are momentarily, but these resolve quickly and aren't gamebreaking. The units and level design are thematic and comprise a large variety of different mission styles. With the exceptions of scripted cutscenes (obviously), it never felt like things were scripted, at least that I noticed, to happen in a way that was contrary to the game's mechanics. There are several RTS tropes presented, all in ways that feel thematic and make sense. However, I would change two major things which hold the game back as it currently stands. First, the game really needs to have a form of target selection automation. Currently, troops appear to target the closest units. It would be nice to have the ability to either select a general category or a specific bug type to be a Priority target. It fits, thematically, with the game, and it alleviates many of the problems the game has with excessive micro hurting the game when it tries to expand its scale. Snipers seem to be the absolute worst about this. They have long range and are your de facto answer to Spitter Bugs and serve as a solid ranged defense against Hopper Bugs. As it stands, though, they constantly get baited by Warriors (or, worse, Tiger Bugs because they stand no significant chance of hurting them) who stand no real chance of pushing up into your E-Pulse troopers. Second: The Underground, Confined, or otherwise Limited Reinforcement Missions feel like they don't fully explain their mechanics, which could be a sticking point for players and which I only figured out by accident. External Doors, Staircases, or certain cracks in tunnels can provide reinforcements to your troops, but some only work once. Even after figuring this out, which ones work which way is never clear. Fixing these two issues would dramatically improve the quality of play for the game and fix issues present in several mid-game missions which felt like they were anticipating these sorts of mechanics or player knowledge of mechanics and were much, much harder to complete as a result.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr Version: I don't think this a fun game because the tactics are oversimplified, I'm not hooked by the story, and the promise of new troop types and new enemies isn't enough to motivate me to complete such a linear game.Essay Version:I was expecting a modernization of Starship Troopers: Terran Ascendancy, but my impression had me shaking my head in disappointment and boredom within two hours. It's kind of like Terran Ascendancy with an increased polygon count and post-processing effects such that it is visually acceptable in the second decade of the 21st century. Oh, and better gore. However, as far as gameplay goes, it lacks what I consider basic elements of a single-player RTS.Now, I know I've only played a few hours but unless there's a huge engaging plot twist somewhere down the fragmented storyline, I pretty much get the whole idea of the game: I'm in tactical command of the ground forces of a highly-militarized society which finds the continued existence of the giant bugs unacceptable, but the Federation is unable to defeat them directly on their homeworld, so my theater of operations is restricted to one planet conveniently free of canon conflicts with the film. Perks of the game include getting to watch my troops kill bugs, getting to watch bugs kill my troops, and getting to use new troop types for the aforementioned purposes as they are added by the story, which is progressed by completing whatever objectives are given in each mission, displayed in the top-left corner of the screen, and are often something along the lines of "Don't lose your command center," which translates into "defend the only position where you are allowed to build and deploy new troops while simultaneously completing the other objectives," which might be something like "Clear bug tunnels (x/6)," with 'x' being however many targets (locations clearly marked on the minimap) you have neutralized. The promise of new unit types, enemies, and new variations of the same desert/underground scenery are the rewards for progressing the campaign. I've already completed at least ten of the fairly brief missions so I assume there are a lot of them. Thing is, I don't really care to see the rest if all I'm going to get is new unit types. Troops go from recruit to Elite over the course of single missions but they don't even carry over to the next, so I'm not sure why the developers bothered to let you name each squad or building, and the last time I saw the custom name of my division was when I was naming it.Anyway, so, the story. There isn't much of one outside of the actual missions, which are story-driven, as emphatically promised by the developers, but unsophisticated and uninteresting. Various recurring characters constitute the human aspect of the classic Starship Troopers flavor. For example, you are effectively characterized and voiced through what seems to be your second-in-command, who exists as a voiceover character most notable for his passive frustration with the Federation's flawed strategic priorities while simultaneously promoting his absolute acceptance of everyone's expendability. The 2D cinematics (in the same style as the illustrations you see on the Store page) barely tie the missions together, although they often provide some flavorful exposition and dark humor. However, I find it entirely inadequate.Strategy and gameplay are lacking in a very similar way. The missions are extremely linear. No replayability beyond replaying the mission using a different combination of units or physical routes to your objectives, and even those options are few. There are no automatic formation options on a squad level, but with multiple squads/units selected, the automatic formation has each squad/unit stand side-by-side in a simple line, which is the only formation you need anyway because it maximizes crossfire support while making your flanks (which are weaker because the squads have more width than depth, so even though each member of the squad can fire in any direction, getting attacked from the side means your flank isn't as strong as your front and rear) more difficult for the enemy to exploit simply because it takes longer to reach them because they are farther away. The more troops you have firing on your primarily melee opposition, the longer it takes for them to reach evisceration range because there are more bullets hitting them, and the faster it kills them. For other formations, or in small canyons, tunnels, and corridors that the algorithms think are too narrow for squads to stand side-by-side, squad units must be positioned individually. Aggressive/defensive stances are equated by a few commands: "Move," which moves your units to a position, at which point they will immediately open fire on any enemies which are in range unless you have the "hold fire" option activated, which I guess is most useful for sneaking by enemies spotted at the edge of your field of view and still outside of aggro range, and the "attack move" command, which causes your units to halt and open fire on any enemies in range en route to their destination. The "attack move" command is really nothing more than a quality-of-life option that automates the process of halting, firing, and ordering them to move again. The only other tactical mechanics are utilizing elevation to expand field of view and be able to shoot past friendly squads between them and the enemy, as well as using impassable terrain to slow down or bottleneck non-flying enemies. I know I made my explanation overly drawn-out and complicated, but my point is that the tactical game, which *is* the entire game, is unrealistically simple and logical. The rest is all unit-type-specific special abilities. So just move, engage the enemy with normal and/or special abilities, and watch the not-especially-spectacular action until one side is victorious. If you win, you advance a little towards the objective until you're stopped by more bugs. If you lose, you deploy some new troops and pick up where your old troops left off when you got them massacred.If you really love the Starship Troopers flavor, you'll get that for sure, and it will probably motivate you to finish the game. But if you're like me and are primarily motivated by the opportunity to dominate the numerically superior enemy on their own turf by masterfully coordinating a perfectly equipped crack squad that even includes some veterans you've managed to keep alive since the first mission, like in Terrran Ascendancy, you won't be much better off than if you were playing the RTS minigame in Space Rangers 2. I know I've barely played the game, but after more than ten boring missions with no reward besides a handful of new enemies to counter with the new types of now-relevant troops graciously and conveniently unlocked by the admirals and generals seemingly tasked solely with restricting my tactical options to limited unit types and generally ensuring even simple objectives are more of a hassle than they need to be, I'd rather just read the spoilers about whatever else Starship Troopers: Terran Command may have waiting for me than experience any more of it myself on the off-chance the game actually does get good, eventually.Maybe if they added a non-linear strategic campaign that includes building and preparing invasion forces and occupational conquest, and/or expanding the tactical game by implementing persistent stats and equipment, this game would suit me. But as it is, this game is inadequate in almost every area. I do hate to leave a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: The "roast'em n' toast'em" part of the game is good, apart from that this game has two things that anger me endlessly. If you click by mistake on the ground, instead on a fast moving bug to attack them, they will happily run to their deaths without a second thought, and without shooting a single bullet. Sometimes they will even just stop shooting and start looking around before getting dismembered, LOL.The marines are most effective while standing in long straight horizontal line, since they can barely shoot from a second row, usually they won't. They are absolutely useless when clumped together. A lot of times is impossible to have them positioned in a long horizontal lines because the scenery does not permit it. All that while the enemy is endlessly tirelessly spawning colonies of bugs, and some special ones are really hard to kill. All that while on the other side of the map for example you must be hyper-vigilant so the bugs don't cross the bridge. And your army size can also be quite limited. In short, the game is very difficult even on medium difficulty. It requires lots of patience and  strategy. Yes, I still recommend this game to anyone who loves Starship Troopers and/or RTS games, as I do. But you've been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: “If we can use an H-bomb--and as you said it's no checker game; it's real, it's war and nobody is fooling around--isn't it sort of ridiculous to go crawling around in the weeds, throwing knives and maybe getting yourself killed . . . and even losing the war . . . when you've got a real weapon you can use to win? What's the point in a whole lot of men risking their lives with obsolete weapons when one professor type can do so much more just by pushing a button?'Zim didn't answer at once, which wasn't like him at all. Then he said softly, 'Are you happy in the Infantry, Hendrick? You can resign, you know.'Hendrick muttered something; Zim said, 'Speak up!'I'm not itching to resign, sir. I'm going to sweat out my term.'I see. Well, the question you asked is one that a sergeant isn't really qualified to answer . . . and one that you shouldn't ask me. You're supposed to know the answer before you join up. Or you should. Did your school have a course in History and Moral Philosophy?'What? Sure--yes, sir.'Then you've heard the answer. But I'll give you my own--unofficial--views on it. If you wanted to teach a baby a lesson, would you cut its head off?'Why . . . no, sir!'Of course not. You'd paddle it. There can be circumstances when it's just as foolish to hit an enemy with an H-Bomb as it would be to spank a baby with an ax. War is not violence and killing, pure and simple; war is controlled violence, for a purpose. The purpose of war is to support your government's decisions by force. The purpose is never to kill the enemy just to be killing him . . . but to make him do what you want him to do. Not killing . . . but controlled and purposeful violence. But it's not your business or mine to decide the purpose of the control. It's never a soldier's business to decide when or where or how--or why--he fights; that belongs to the statesmen and the generals. The statesmen decide why and how much; the generals take it from there and tell us where and when and how. We supply the violence; other people--"older and wiser heads," as they say--supply the control. Which is as it should be. That's the best answer I can give you. If it doesn't satisfy you, I'll get you a chit to go talk to the regimental commander. If he can't convince you--then go home and be a civilian! Because in that case you will certainly never make a soldier.”― Robert A. Heinlein, Starship Troopers
