_childDocuments_.review: If steam had a normal rating system i'd give this game a 3 out of 5. The game is super fun especially if you like starship troopers, however the way your units behave drove me bananas during a lot of missions.The units in this game are a weird mixture of all the things that annoyed me playing 90's RTS games when i was a kid, combined with a lot of "modern" concepts like line of fire and lot of special abilities.The only two commands you have with your units are move and attack move (they do just that).while in attack move they do engage the enemy, however they won't co ordinate their position to allow other units in the same group a clear line of fire (which is a big concept in this game, your units wont engage unless they have a clear line of fire). instead you get a huge mess of units in which only 1-2 have a chance to attack. clicking on the enemy directly will cause only the units who have line of fire to attack, they wont attempt to spread out automaticly, you have to micro manage it. also while in attack move they somtimes won't engage and instead move right in front of the enemy before attacking/standing there and getting butchered.The game is also super fast paced and lacks a pause button so getting a good position on the attack is near impossible.The game works well when you have a single small army. large army on the attack becomes a moshpit fairly quickly and the bugs will annihilate all your support units because they somehow reached the front line. Managing 2 small teams on the attack was nearly impossible for me and iv'e been playing RTS since the 90's so i think i have a little bit of skill.other that those frustrating moments, the game is really fun and i enjoyed it.Buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the devs missed out on an enormous opportunity by making a game that just outright lacks ingenuity and is just a grab at nostalgia from the SST movies. The entire game just feels like a mod that one guy made in his spare time, not something that has been in the works by a dev team for any notable amount of time. Other than being tied to the SST franchise, there isn't anything this game brings into the RTS genre that hasn't been done already. If you want to spend $40 for some SST cut scenes this is your game. - Bare-bones RTS with repetitive missions, no skirmish/multiplayer modes, and pretty lackluster combat. - Bug movement speed is a brisk walk compared to the movies.- No Tech tree or base building.- Only able to replay the bland Campaign missions.- The cut scenes seemingly took priority over gameplay.- Be prepared to restart multiple missions as the objective log will not progress at key points. - Even though this is a pretty gruesome universe there is little to no blood textures and your soldiers will borderline T-pose    and fall over once killed. - Difficulty has no affect on bug spawn rates and numbers. It only affects your troops damage output by reducing it. - Tankers/Plasma bug target finding is countered by just running in a circle.- Numerous ability and interface bugs during combat.- Units are unable to shoot on the move, and raise/lower their weapons between each shot causing them to bob up and   down like some kind of whack-a-mole game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, tower-defence-esque RTS. The fun:- Watching bugs die by the dozen.- Setting up defensive perimeters against swarms of bugs.- Having that feeling of just barely holding out against the bugs.- Music has some suitably 'epic', but cheesy, tracks.- Loved the propaganda videos at the start of every level.- Campaign is fun, if somewhat brief.The weird:- Not much replayability (no multiplayer, only two 'challenges', no 'skirmish' mode, no 'last stand' type mode, etc.).- Sound design is average (some weapons don't sound great, units don't feel like they have 'weight').- Campaign story is pretty much just the plot of the first Starship Troopers movie - it's good fun, but nothing spectacular or memorable.The bad:- Unit balancing feels a bit off - some abilities / units don't have impact / some abilities are just flat out better than others.- Scorpions are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - they turn some scenarios from fun engagements to just annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (for context - Scorpions are tough, armoured, ranged, single-entity bug units with a sort of splash attack. It's fine to deal with them in small numbers, but some scenarios spawn these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things by the dozen).Overall - good fun, recommend when it's on sale.

And now to ♥♥♥♥ on the power armor units... they seem to only be able to kill the most basic teir 1 bugs, and you have to use them and only them when they are introduced.. are you fighting only teir 1 units? oh nonononono. They can take a beating though... which is pretty much all they can do, and ffs don't go after the hives out of order on their mission. I know you can normally kill hives in any order you want... but go for the wrong one first and you unlock more powerful units to all the hives... and now you can't take out any of them, of course this wouldn't be an issue if you had any better units are your disposal... but no stuck with the poopy unit.Overall still a fun game despite me wanting to cry about having to play a couple of missions with crappy units.Edit; had to come back and edit this... the power armor units only suck until they become elite... and then become a good unit.

_childDocuments_.review: The game really punishes you for trying to split push, you need to have all your eggs in one basket making a death ball go around the map. there you go i just spoiled your whole game play later on in the game. the only strategy is playing leap frog with your squads.It looks good, adds to the world building, though idk what is truly cannon in this franchise, but unit control leave so much to be desired.Also the insanely... I don't feel like that got the point across, let me try again. *ahem*INSANELY poor pathing. Told a squad to move up and around this rock, what would be like idk 5m adjustment to a north east movement, turned into a 35m hike around a Boulder (It's not just a Boulder *sniff* its a Rock!) to get to the commanded spot, I found this happened a lot on multiple maps with multiple objects (Boulders, Vehicles, Random things with round edges). i would even hold down the mouse button to make sure the squad wasn't landing on the object. Yet they would go on a hike, away from the bugs like Cowards.Also many times squads wouldn't fire till the bug was slaughtering one of the members, Idk if i spawned some kinda pacifist squad or poor coding. I thought it was like maybe a LOS issue but the Wars come in packs of 4, and they would shoot the stragglers in the pack but only after the fastest bug attacked them first... So that lead to some... Annoying game play.Honestly there needs to be like a Meh button, if its on sale get it, it'll be fun I can't imagine these issues are as punishing in lower difficulty as it is on high, but on high difficultly these mechanics were brutal and only lead to grinding game play instead of strategic play.

_childDocuments_.review:
Starship Troopers - Terran Command is a thrilling real-time strategy game set in the Starship Troopers movies universe. Take command of the Mobile Infantry and do your part in the war against the Arachnid threat. Build, develop and control your armies to strike an effective balance between tactical superiority and strength in numbers. Ensure that human civilization, not insect, dominates the galaxy now and always!

Planetary Campaigns
Fight for control over an entire planet in the campaign mode, where the storyline and missions develop according to your choices and achievements on the battlefield. Remain obedient to the demands of Terran Command no matter how costly or ruthless to benefit from exclusive unit types and special abilities, or follow your own path to glory to become an irrefutable Hero of the Federation. Develop and customize your forces through a detailed technology tree and upgradeable leader characters that can be assigned to your units.

Tactics & Numbers
While the Arachnids can rely on virtually limitless numbers, the Mobile Infantry must develop effective tactics to overcome this imbalance. Deploy your units at strategic locations to cover vital choke points and gain superior firepower through tactical use of elevation levels. Be wary, however, that battle mechanics such as True Line of Sight and True Line of Fire also allow Bugs to lay ambushes around every corner, as they are well known for their use of surprise attacks and deception.

Units & Abilities
An expansive range of unique units, weapons, and special abilities are at the disposal of MI commanders. Infantry squads armed with Morita Assault Rifles and MX-90 Fragmentation Grenades form the mainstay of your forces. Rocket Troopers deliver deadly payloads with pin-point accuracy while Engineers are vital to shore up defensive positions with MG turrets, barricades, and minefields. As a campaign progresses, technological breakthroughs unlock the true potential of the Federation's arsenal with Power Armor infantry squads, TAC Fighter airstrikes, Marauder mobile suits, and many more developments optimized for spraying Bug ichor across the battlefield.

Key features
- Dynamically generated campaigns for virtually limitless replayability.
- Dozens of unique unit types, each with their own special abilities.
- Terrain elevation, True Line of Sight & True Line of Fire provide deep tactical gameplay.
- An extensive technology tree to develop and customize your forces.
- Persistent leaders can be attached to units and upgraded throughout the campaign.
- Heroics, explosions, gore, and Bugs. Lots of Bugs.

name: Paleo Pines
detailed_description: Welcome to Paleo Pines, a charming island known for its friendly dinosaurs, quirky townsfolk, and mysterious past. Here evolution took a different path, creating a world in which humans and dinosaurs live together in harmony! Set out with your dino companion, Lucky, to uncover the island’s secrets and discover new dinos. Your arrival on the island is met with welcome curiosity by the local townsfolk who can help you on your quest (and just might give you more work to do!). Together with Lucky, build a thriving ranch, assist local villagers, befriend adorable dinosaurs, and unearth the island’s lost history to build your cozy dino sanctuary. Set off on a lively adventure with your dino pal, Lucky, who you’ve known since she was just an egg. Is she the last of her kind? The other parasaurolophus are missing, and it's up to you and Lucky to uncover their whereabouts. Explore Paleo Pines, a charming island filled with friendly townsfolk and hidden corners. Build a new home, make friends, and unravel the island's lost history. Get ready for a journey filled with delightful discoveries alongside your trusty steed Lucky! Set up your home base on the island as you go about your parasaurolophus quest. Paleo Pines is a place where you can express your individuality and creativity; no two ranches are the same! Build square pens, or not (although the locals might have something to say about that!). Use decor to build a romantic garden, give your ranch a witchy vibe, or go full-on-farmer with rows and rows of tilled soil. Furthermore, customize your character as you like with a variety of features, curate a colorful collection of clothing—with different items to be found in each area—and change your style using the wardrobe! The island of Paleo Pines is a dino lover’s dream! A collection of cheeky dinosaurs roam the wild areas waiting to become your friends, as well as ranch helpers. Coax them near by mimicking their calls with your flute, then seal the deal with a tasty treat and trustworthy nose boop! Gain their trust by creating cozy pens and learning what keeps them happy. Dinos move around and some are harder to find than others, or may appear only under special conditions, so new discoveries await you as you explore the island. As your ranch grows, you’ll soon have a dino haven for all your new friends. Check out the Dino Journal to learn all about the creatures that roam the island. Farm to your heart’s content, growing crops all year round with (and for) your dino besties! Start out planting and watering by hand, but earn your new friends’ trust and they’ll help you deliver a roarsome harvest that you can trade with the townsfolk. As your ranch grows, you’ll learn that each dino has a special farming skill to help you with your tasks. With a bit of love, care, and attention to detail, such as matching soil and season, you can grow the highest quality produce in all of Paleo Pines. Soon you and your dino ranch hands will be the talk of the market! There's plenty to explore out in the wilds of Paleo Pines, from the flowery fields of Veridian Valley to the high canyons of Ariacotta. Make the most of each day by venturing throughout the lush landscapes across the island, each with their own charm, collectable items, and dinos to discover. Take a leisurely stroll through green meadows, foraging for wild crops as you go, or hop on your trusty dino mount on a hunt for hidden corners. Pause to watch wild dinosaurs playfully interact with each other, right before your very eyes. You'll never run out of things to find or dinosaurs to befriend! A quirky (but friendly!) array of townsfolk on the island can’t wait to meet you and help you on your quest. Granny might have a stubborn side, but get to know her and she’s an ol’ softie. Building friendships within the community is just as important as building friendships with your dinosaurs. As you ride dinos, farm, and explore, you will come across new characters, each with their own story, items or knowledge to share, and gossip to exchange. Help them out day or night by completing quests, opening up new areas, and visiting the stores and community hubs. And who knows—they may even gift you something to spruce up your ranch!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a bit of a mixed bag in it's current state, but overall I do recommend this game. The overall aesthetic is cute as heck, down to the lil scale texture on the dinosaurs. I love the research notebook aspect of the game, its a nice touch and really adds to everything. However the game has a good handful of limitations and quality of life changes that would improve it greatly. Firstly my biggest gripe is the damn jump button. Either add a jump or don't, don't give us whatever that stopping midrun and going "yippee!" bs is.  Like, it honestly drives me up a wall to be running, and then force of habit use my spacebar only to stop midrun and do a stupid lil yippee. It completely ruins any flow you may be in and adds nothing to the game. I get that the lack of jump is to avoid platforming over obstacles, but like, you could just make the spacebar do nothing. I would love the option to turn off jump entirely. Customisation options are also very restrictive, There isn't really any long hair options and it would be nice to have more color choices. Additionally I would really like to be able to change the clothing color on the character create screen instead of each clothing style only having one color choice. right now it feels like you can pick from a few very cookiecutter options as most of the clothing pieces don't work with eachother well and only work with one/two other pieces each. It would be nice to be able to feel like your character is more personalized.Overall the game is a cute and cozy romp through a colorful little world of dinosaurs, and I highly recommend it to anyone whose willing to overlook a handful of issues and focus on the core gameplay loop. This, a warm blanket and a cup of tea would make for a nice fall evening.

I wasn't even a dino person and I'm in love with them!!Some controls feel a bit awkward compared to other similar games, but the joy of seeing cute dinosaurs in the wild and having them in your ranch made me get used to the game system fast.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say the graphics in this game are adorable, and the story line is great, but the game does have room for improvement. First, I wish resources like stone, wood, and fiber were more accessable, some quests require hundreds and the grind can get very annoying. Second, I wish you could enter and customize your house, having house furniture outside looks wrong. _childDocuments_.review: I have watched this game develop for 4 years. It has such a great concept and a fun idea, but it is poorly executed. Despite the 4 year development time, it feels like it was put together in only 1. In short, the game would be better if they post-poned the launch until they had done more. Below I have my issues, my good points, and my recommendation. (Note: I started my save file with the progress I had made in the demo.)=Issues=- The general quality of the models and textures is.. okay. To be honest it reminded of Roblox both during the demo and at launch.- All of the characters suffer from "same-face-syndrome." Everyone looks the exact same, the primary trader is the exact same as the player-model. The game's art style feels like it's trying to be two different things. - The character personalities attempt to be distinct, yet they all just wind up being the same or annoying. there is no drastic differences between the characters. I find trouble being attached to any of them.- The sound design is.. something. I feel like I've only heard three songs in the whole game (Title theme, Day Theme, and a Rain Theme). On top of this, it feels like every character has the same voice actor (including the dinosaurs). The dinosaurs sound like people more than they do creatures or animals.- There is no way to remap controls. While this may not be an issue for some, I use remapping the controls as a way to learn how to do certain things.- There is no good of explaining specific features. For example, It took me going to the discord server and asking online to figure out how to change a pen biome. Upon going to the vendor who supposedly had the supplies, they did not.- The game's progression is feels extremely quest heavy. As a player who wants to focus more on farming and taming dinosaurs, it sucks that most of those features are locked by quests rather than exploration.-The balance between dinos is lacking. For example: In Dapplewood and the Valley, there are 5 waterer/sprinter dinos but only 2 stomper dinos (both of which are locked behind stomp-able barriers)=Goods=-The game has fantastic dino designs. The melanistic and albino variants are amazing to encounter randomly. The taming and friendship methods for the dinos are fantastic as well.- The farming mechanic is fun! You can cycle through crops throughout the season based on soil types and it's a fun system. This is the only farming game I've ever enjoyed the farming system in.As an end note, I would wait on buying this game until changes are made. It has the ability to be great, but it isn't. Right now, I'd say both you and your wallet would have more fun in a free, well-made Roblox game.Edit: It has been over a year since i made this review and from what I've seen not a lot of changes have been made. It still feels like a poorly made roblox game that lacks substance. It would do well with some better stories, better quests, more areas, better bug fixes, better pricing, and not locking things behind paywalls and labeling it as "dlc."

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing and casual farming game, simular to Stardew Valley to some extent. However, there is still diffrences and two of the most glaring ones beeing 1) The artstyle! Paleo Pines artstyle is absolutely adorable and wonderfull, a treat for your eyes and it fits the relaxed tone its going for. 2) The dinosaurs! Yes, these adorable creatures are everywhere and I adore them all, specially some of the smaller creatures can be absolutely captevating!In diffrence to ark your dinos are not tamed, they are befriended by bribery and soothing words. If misstreated they will leave you so tend to your new friends carefully.In diffrence to Pokemon your dinos can and will not fight for you, they will however help you with your farming or traversing the world. Pros: A cute, cartoony artstyleA relaxed playstyleNo fighting (some arguments between npc's)Easy to understnad the controllsAdorable and super cute dinos!Easy to recognize npc'sThe carachter creation part is simple but effectiveCons: The quests are some times frustrating due to no questlog with informationThe map is stationary on you, you can not switch between unlocked maps to planThe map have no markings, you better remember the name of every place!Would I buy again: Yes!

_childDocuments_.review: The idea is great, but the execution leaves much to be desired.Tl;dr: The game lacks content and offers very little once the novelty wears off after the first couple of hours. There have been no major content updates either (save for one coming up that adds a couple new color variants to existing dinos), it's definitely not worth the 30EUR price tag. It feels like a demo, the most I would pay for it is 20 EURs, but only if you really like the whole idea.I really wanted to like this game. I spent around 15 hours on the demo, going through  multiple save files, looking up tricks to get the most out of the 13 days I could. Those first couple of hours left me wanting more - more dinos, more quests, hidden things to find and maps to explore.I got none of that in the full version and after 30 hours, I got fed up with the gameplay loop of take care of farm → go to town for fetch quests I may do → look for rare dino colors → tame if I find any, but otherwise back to farm and sleep → repeat.The dinos are great, they are cute and round and adorable, the animations are smooth and satisfying. The color rarity system is fun as well, I enjoyed looking for new helpers quite a lot. But that is about all I can praise the 1.0 version for.Dino species, while they look interesting and fun, have no real variety gameplaywise. At least a third of them are small farm helpers that could take care of your farm for you - however, in my 30 hours, I've only unlocked the seeding ability and have yet to access weeding or harvesting. There is very, VERY little variety in the dino skills as well, and with 4-5 dinos, you have access to all of them, which makes collecting more pointless. The only reason to get them is to look good, which just wasn't enough for me.Farm gameplay was pretty standard, the soil type rotation is a fun mechanic. Dinos helping is a great concept, but we run into the above mentioned problem of only needing more dinos for the same role on lower levels. Once your friends reach level 10 and above, even that becomes obsolete.The quests are BORING. All of them are fetch quests, and I couldn't be bothered by them. They felt like a chore I needed to do in order to progress in the story.Speaking of, the story itself was just as bland and emotionless. It felt as if the devs used up all their time and ideas in the first few cutscenes for everybody. All the characters are pretty much a simple, one dimensional archetype (the geeky scientist, the nice crafter or spunky old farmer lady), which wouldn't be an issue IF the interactions didn't feel forced and soulless, like a second thought they needed to implement so the game could have a bit of flavor.Because the maps certainly don't do much. The plains biome accessible in the demo was the only open-worldish map we could try, as the forest and desert biome were only added in the release version. This biome was a bit boring, but while playing, I was like 'yeah, sure, this is a good tutorial biome, it has that cool pond I can't do anything with and that secret garden I have to bring stuff for, but I really want to see what other places I can visit!' Now I have to add that you can run through the whole plains, even after destroying the couple of roadblocks to get access to some of the dinos (and NO other content) in less than ONE in-game day, using no stamina on your starting friend Lucky. You could run through the whole thing and see all the little landmarks and locations in about 5-10minutes, but for the daily dino scavenger run, it only takes about 2-3 minutes.Aside from the plains, we only have 2 other biomes, both of which are exactly the same size, if not smaller. So my problem with this game: while it sounds good on paper, and the dinos are indeed a fun thing in the beginning, the lack of content or engaging gameplay and the small areas make for a game that gets very boring, very quickly. Add to this the ridiculously slow pacing of getting the first item needed for the small farm dinos in the middle of the second season, the whole game is just sluggish and uninteresting after the novelty wears off.As a last thought, because I know a lot of people don't care about it that much, but the graphics are very poor as well. Even the dinos look unfinished (looking at you, anky and your weird roundish head with random edges), not to mention the environment and textures. This aspect too could use a lot of improvement.It feels like this is still a game in development and is definitely not worth the full price. There is no news of any upcoming content updates in the discord either, not to mention the whole problem at launch when you could only get 10% off on steam instead of the promised 15% (though this was not the devs fault). In it's current state, I just can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I'll get it out of the way, the dinosaurs are absolutely adorable from the designs to the noises they make when you try to befriend them. _childDocuments_.review: I'm torn.  I love the feel of this game, but it falls short on SO much that could be done.  The events feel laughably bad, and very unenthusiastic.  The representation of the dinos falls short on things such as MLM or nonbinary, but have an overabundance with WLW type.  I'm very happy they have the representation, but it cannot be falling short on one leg to uplift another.  If you have the representation of MLM/Nonbinary, it's on inherently ugly dinosaurs, or done in such a bad way that's showing a lack of love. (IE. Corythosaurus, Proud Pansy // Carno, Proud River - why are nonbinary and gay folk only represented on ONE SINGLE DINOSAUR that barely shows the color scheme?)The recent DLC bundles are $4 a piece- only one being (in-game) year-round, and the other being a time limited one?  For the DLC event to be just as hodgepodge, slammed together feel like the rest? _childDocuments_.review: I am so in love with this game and I have been going on and on about it all day to my friends ❤️I want to send in my feedback on everything I love love lovedddd about this light-hearted dino farmer game ^^Some of my friends are real dino-brains so it makes me smile whenever they see a dino in-game and try to guess what species it is before I interact with it. So much fun to see all the creative designs while still being recognizable and fitting into the world.Most farming games I tend to feel pressure to prepare for winter but the farming in this game feels very fun and lively. It makes me feel connected and rewarded by thinking about what crops to plant and when without stressing out over the time day by day.I was so worried that there would be a limit to how many little friends I could have but that was not the case and it filled me with excitement thinking of all the ways I could arrange a big farm with different colors and shapes of dinos! Even now with only around 12 dinos I feel like I have so many little buddies to take care of so having almost 50 in total is an insane goal to work towards! Speaking of colors, gosh I just love all the color pallets!! It's so much fun to stop by a herd of colorful dinos all walking, sleeping, and playing to see each one stand out so nicely in a crowd. There really is a pallet color for anyone and the many choices it presents are all so wonderful. I've also seen many people already start "shiny hunting" ultra rare colorations like albino and it makes me think of doing the same for fun.I am excited by the idea of updates/dlc that add more to the game but even now I am entirely satisfied with this lovely little dino game and hope to have many relaxing nights after work to play with Lucky and all my other dinos ❤️I could go on and on and on but yeah, 10/10 game, you get exactly what you pay for and I love it

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute game, and I love how the animals are depicted as how they truly were (Stylized, but the animals with feathers have feathers, for example.) I recommend it, I really do, but it has issues.The characters look so bad, they make really awful sounds. I hate hearing their voices. The only tolerable character is Granny. Everything else looks great!There are so many little things that drive me crazy, tiny little obstacles that become mountains as you encounter more and more of them. Much of the game is made to waste your time and keep you playing, like a modern live service game, which I am...not a fan of.For example: You can't use dinosaurs until they become helpers, but it can take days upon days of time for this to happen, which means you can't access specific areas of the game you need to progress. Inventory is dependent on befriending a character that isn't even there half the time, instead of a backpack like a normal game would give you. I honestly enjoy this aspect and it's refreshing, but why is she not always there?The devs seem adamant to continue to add more colors to the game instead of QOL improvements or actual fun, sustained gameplay and that seems rather suckish. _childDocuments_.review: i do really love this game, the dinos are super cute, its chill like stardew with the farming and it just feels fun to continue. i do feel like it was worth playing and i highly enjoy it.they have a unique taming system and i find it super fun that dinos help you farm with their unique abilities, i like the chanced variety of colors of dinos, overall a fun and cute game to chill to. really easy to get lost into for hoursBUTthere is so much that feels wrong with it at this moment.>stamina doesnt refill anyway, not eating or waiting, makes it a terrible time when i cant do anything after the limited points are gone> very tediously confusing layout of the map, making dreamstones and fragments of artifacts just annoyingly hard to find, even with a wiki open to tell me where they were i didnt find some of them.>after reaching the stuff at the desert the game just becomes a grinding slog, just kind of a boring grinding game of planting, cleaning and wandering around for rare colored dinos.>theres never enough dreamstones to be happy, like i just wand some cute dinos but i never have enough to add the great dino in without it immidietely leaving>just everything with making a dino a helper is super tedious for what feels like no reason, like one of my dinos had everything they needed always clean pen, but left my farm after 2 days because of no reason? aside from it "prefering more pen mates" like im always fearing my dinos leaving because of the weirdly specific conditions i have to balance with such short day cycles>the npc quests only have 3 types, get me this resource, find my lost hat or give this thing to another npc right next to them, gets super boring but i need to do them to improve character friendship>no direction or goals, aside from 'find other parasaurs' theres really nothing, even in that questline i dont feel like it was directioned well, i just had to run around until i found it >VERY annoying pathfinding issues, like when activating a thing the character or dino will spin around or glitch around until they finally go to the right point for activation, the character movement is super slidey and weird so its hard to grab anything. also the watering dinos have a ramdon spray that sometimes wont hit the same square in the middle of the perfectly watered area multiple times even when right in front of it.dont get me wrong, this is a good game even though i listed a bunch of small flaws, at this point it is nit picking because the game itself is still a successful one. but there are some features that could be made a little less annoying for player retention.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:*Dino mount system is pretty great for farming/exploration.*Cute Dinos, you can pet them all.*You can change game speed to be faster or slower.*Soil type system along with season changes can encourage you to grow different plants in cycles.Cons:*Overly simplistic in many ways. Once you've played through 1 year and unlocked the 3 areas, you've done it all.*Sometimes collision just happens. Sometimes on objects that never existed.*Controls can be clunky for even smaller dinos with important farming functions but massive turning radius makes them frustrating.*UI bugs, sometimes the menu just don't work or keep scrolling up for no reason.*Why is there a furniture placement system? Am I just going to put furniture on... grass? No pathways, walls or carpets. No extra buildings to work with. Rotating items just slightly offsets them in a direction.*Side-quests have precedence in conversation over main quests, some require you to get something from 2 seasons later and will not be available until you pass 42 days to reach it. My main quests are in limbo until I have to arbitrarily give someone 3 turnips because they want to talk about their main quest.*Some dino's farming functions are locked behind requirements that are too deep into the game and there is no way to figure it out. Ground tilling, crop watering and harvesting are unlocked relatively on pace but cleaning your farm areas is weirdly time gated. I STILL do not have dinos helping me plant seeds are 34 hours of gameplay.*(major gripe) Collection of dino patterns and crops are an absolute nightmare. ALL crops, ALL dino patterns, ALL discoveries are in their respective SINGLE statistic. There is no catalogue, there is no collection, there is no way to mark off what collectables you have other than search all 3 areas+farm+towns again and hope you run into the missing pieces.Gameplay gripes that don't ruin it but are really annoying:*Character turns around and faces the camera for no reason when I'm trying to apporach soemthing o interact with it. decorating/placement of items and interacting with anything you can interact with is just awful.*There is no way to select how many items you want to withdraw. If you press confirm, it fills your inventory and you have to put away all the excess stacks.*You can't split or select quantity in menus unless it's a shop.*If you hop on a dino, it removes it from your party and you have to quickly pull out the flute to re-add them to the party.*Collecting items in the 3 areas is a headache, there is no way to tell which items you've already collected and each item has a total count for ALL areas together (3 main areas+town+your farm)*There is ONE SINGLE STAT for how many variations of all dinos you have... tamed? discovered? I don't know and doing so is very costly and tedious to the point of frustration.*No rebinding keys cool I guess.*controller works okay, for some reason some functions are just not available given how little keys you really need (not many at any time)I paid 45AUD, it really doesn't feel like it's worth the price. Get it on sale for sure if it's at least 30% off. Otherwise I can't see myself paying this much for a clunky farming sim. Cute dinos sure but everything around it just makes it frustrating. Overall, it just feels okay. I finished the 'main goal' from the start of game after 1 year cycle and it gives me no incentive to come back.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point I've played part of the demo, didn't finish it and have now played several hours of the actual game now that it's out. First off...................the dinos are super adorable! The noises they make are cute. They have very useful skills (I'm loving the one I have at the moment that can water all my crops, saves me tons of energy!). The hearts that appear when you pet them are so sweet! The character create section is well done. The choice of hair in the demo was unfortunate but the full game has much better options (or at least a couple that I actually want to use). This section is simplified and frankly a breath of fresh air in said simplicity. The clothing is cute and I find them acceptable. Energy runs out fast but when your dinos energy runs out you can still ride around on it and forage or just explore or just enjoy a relaxing time wandering around for no reason whatsoever so that's great. I got a little frustrated trying to forage at first but that was because I didn't know that the spawning of forage stuff is random but now that I do know that I can relax and enjoy the game now knowing that the thing I'm looking for will eventually turn back up  - where I found it previously or in a similar area. I really like the little chores/side job you can get and do from the billboard in the town and that they give different rewards not just money (shells). They are nice and not stressful. It's a little annoying that you can't make money fast (well I haven't been able to) but so far I always have enough for food for my dinos and I am constantly finding herbivore food out in the wild so I'm not stressed about money at the moment and it's not like there's a bunch of objects or whatever that I absolutely HAVE to have so it's fine. The NPC characters are wonderful so far. There isn't a single one so far that I hate. Their personalities are very good and I've grown fond of the choice of characters the developer's chose quite quickly. The area I've explored so far is beautiful. There literally was a beautiful rainbow that I got a picture of with me with my dino and it's just gorgeous with the rainbow and the hills and the trees and everything it's just fantastic! The night sky is lovely and just everything looks good so far scenery wise. My graphics are on like the highest setting so take that into account. Overall at this point in owning and playing the game I'm enjoying it. It's simple enough, directions are straight forward enough, and everything seems less complicated than some other "similar" games I've played. 5 stars at this point! P.S. Only being able to get a certain amount of dreamstones and owning only so many dinos is a let down but I'm still enjoying and loving the game despite this actually disappointing and seriously terrible decision (I'm sure there is a very valid reason for it but that doesn't change my feelings on the matter).

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game.  I've put in a lot of hours trying to get the achievements and just can't force myself to finish them.  The questing system in this game is quite possibly the worst I've seen.  The only way to increase friendship levels is to do these mindless quests.  The worst being to go find a hidden object with the tiniest missable marker you can think of.  It's seriously got the worst questing system I've ever had to suffer through in any game in any genre I've ever played.The NPCs just kind of exist.  There isn't really much to them at all.  The only thing they are good for is selling items to, even then they rip you off.  All shop keepers only accept certain items, so there is a lot of mundane travel in between merchants.    Crafting does not take place on your farm and inventory is tiny.  Which leads me to my next gripe.  It's incredibly irritating trying to cook stuff, but need to use 4-5 inventory slots for one recipe.  So you end up having to run back and forth from your farm to the random cooking pot to cook.  You have a tiny inventory with no long distance access.  So you end up running around with 5 different poppins to tame, a few food items for taming, then the full set of wood/stone/fiber/forest wood for doing quests.  So when you do turn in one quest then your inventory is full.  God forbid you accidentally run over an item that auto picks up and fills that last open space.  Then it's all the way back to your storage again.  This is only slightly alleviated by npcs automatically sending items to your storage if your inventory is full.  It seems like I am in a constant battle to manage inventory space.My last big complaint is the dino AI.  If you are using a mount to get around on your farm, it almost always immediately sprints off when you dismount.  This is a small thing, but oddly infuriating when you are strapped for time.  All in all, they are going to have to do some serious quality of life improvements to this game.  The cute factor doesn't cut it when there are so many downright infuriating things to deal with.  This is supposed to be a relaxing fun game, however for me I just end up aggravated the whole time I'm playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Words cannot express how deeply I wish I didn't feel the need to give this rating. I've followed Paleo Pines since it was a concept on Tumblr, both because of my love for farming sims and because I have been a dinosaur nerd since I first went to the museum and saw the skeleton of one of those amazing animals. I had high hopes for Paleo Pines- because honestly, how many games are out there with dinosaurs in them that don't depict them as rabid, wild-eyed, scaly, Hollywood horror monsters for you to simply shoot? Paleo Pines is different, and for that at least I'll wholly give credit. But unfortunately, in a desert of FPS dinosaur shoot em ups, this poor oasis...has stale waters.Pros:-Dinosaurs. Full stop, that's the sentence, there are dinosaurs and they're adorable and they're in a game where I can pet them and make little houses for them and feed them treats like particularly spoiled cats.-Dinosaur designs. To be more serious, the different patterns and colors are an utter delight. Imagine how excited I was when I was crossing the bridge to get to town and ran face first into an albino psittacosaurus? The noise I made could have roused the dead with how excited I was.-The mechanics are well thought out, that there are different dinosaurs that can help you with different farm tasks is imaginative and fun, and the fact that I can bring multiple dinosaurs with me on any given outing so I can just hop off of one and directly onto another without backtracking across the map? A+!-The world itself, though rather large and somewhat empty, is still beautiful.Cons: -Missing tutorials and information... there were an alarming number of times where I was truly at a loss for how to complete a task or how to get a dinosaur to perform its actions. I had to google the psittacosauruses, was sent to reddit, and from reddit, was sent to the Paleo-Pines tumblr, where I finally found out that the core mechanic of the psittacosauruses, one of the first three dinosaurs you encounter ingame...cannot be used until you complete several quests for an NPC that (for me at least) did not show up until the Paleo-Pines version of summer)-Inventory size... You get a 4x4 inventory. You cannot expand it. Different quality crops take up multiple inventory spaces. Your dinosaurs cannot help carry extra things. -The NPCs. Characterwise they're alright, but they don't have schedules- or at least, not consistent ones that you can find in-game. Different NPCs spend different days in different locations. The Seeds Grandma will spend an entire day at her seed stall and cannot be found at her house at any point, but then the next day the opposite will be true and she will be at her house and will not come within a mile of her stall. This especially will make quests where you have to deliver an item to a person while they're at a certain location even more of a pain in the tail.-The NPCs continued, this game does not have a quantifiable friendship system from what I can tell? I may be wrong about this though, which is why I put it in a separate bullet.-You can't cook at your house. I didn't even know there was a cooking mechanic until I happened upon a cooking pot by a lake while digging for clovers. I still have no idea how to cook, trying to click on it just prompts my character to say I should learn how to cook. Special Con because I still can't quite wrap my head around this:-This is a fantasy/farming sim... that you cannot craft in. You can find all the wood, fiber, and stone in the world but lambed if you know how to use them to make a fence post. IE, THE most common item you need for your farm, to make paddocks for you dinosaurs. So much of my money has been spent not on seeds or equipment, but on fencing and troughs.Look; truthfully, nothing in the world would make me happier than the devs making me eat my words and improving the game to a degree that I'd be ashamed to have ever doubted them. I want that with every fiber of my being. So, if in the future, I need to come back to this review and chow down, I will do so with unfettered, unabashed JUBILANCE. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the farming aspect of the game. It is lucrative and makes it easy to buy fencing and gates for your farm. Questing is fairly straightforward, mostly gathering quests or recipe demands, research journal requests, and lost/returning items. There are some NPC friendship quests that can lead to shop discounts which vary depending on friendship level. Dino interactions are based on utilizing your flute to mimic the dinosaur of interest: melodies dependent on how long you hold the note for to attract the dino's attention. I think it is pretty unique because each dino has a different sound. Once interacting you can feed it something you think it might like from your inventory. Each dino will have different preferences. To befriend a dino you have to feed/soothe the dino's meter until it is in the dark green area, then feed it a Pippins treat. A prompt will either state that it trusts you, then you get to pet it and befriend it, or you need to feed it more poppins depending on if it liked the flavor or not. There are many different color variations between dinos, some rarer than others. If your farm is too full, you cant release them to the wild and access them again with Mari's help. To keep dinos happy, Dreamstones need to be used. These are found in the map areas you explore. I've collected most of my decorations through exploration or completing quests from the town quest board. I enjoy the pen crafting, it can be buggy on occasion but you can check your journal to see which of your dinos need attention. Getting money for feed is taxing early game if you didn't start farming early. So try to plant as soon as you can for easy money and dino food treats. When you meet Avery you'll eventually get the option of having your smaller dinos help on your farm which makes it even easier to make money/food. Graphics and gamestyle is relaxing and playful. Easy to grind through in-game days. Especially if you're looking for a certain dino. The vibrant variations are generated randomly, unless it is the Harvest Day Event, then there is an increased chance for rarer dinos that evening/day following. Event days are also the only days you can spend festival tickets for decor items. Which is significant if you achievement hunt.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest review from someone who plays a lot of farming sims.I only bought this game because of the dinosaurs. Having the dinosaurs act as different kinds of tools really makes it stand out against other farming sims. The game feels very much like a game in early access with how little there is to do in the game. The lack of crafting, customization, and very limited bag space are some major negative points. The limited bag space is probably the worst aspect about the game, I haven't come across an opportunity to increase my inventory slots so I'm not sure if this will change later on down the road. I do hope they intend on adding more content down the road, because as it is now I don't think the current amount of content justifies the price point. The game has been enjoyable though and I do recommend it for people who like farming sims and want something a little different. I think that the price point is a little too much for what you're currently getting in the game.Positives:-Dinosaurs-Dinosaurs with variety-Dinosaurs can be used similar to tools-not super complicated-The OST is really niceNegatives-lack of crafting-lack of customization on the farm-not being able to go inside your house-not being able to customize your house-no minimap for direction on the overlay (I am directionally challenged IRL and in game, I love a good minimap on the overlay)-no clock on the overlay (Sometimes it's hard to tell what time of day it is due to the weather)-lack of character development with the NPCs-not being able to add personal inventory space.-lack of a toolbar to easily switch between tools-You can tell that they put a lot of effort into the dinosaurs and the environment, but it feels like the people in the game are a little meh? I don't know how to describe it.Eitherway, a cute little game. I'm glad it's finally out and I hope we see some content added later on.

_childDocuments_.review: i was really, really looking forward to this game. i REALLY wanted to love it. but i can only say i was disappointed.the dinosaurs are ADORABLE, but interaction with them feels very formulaic and soulless. the designs of the humans are, in my opinion, very unappealing when it comes to style. i dont remember a name of a single npc, their dialogue and personalities are flat and boring.you need a specific sort of finite item to keep dinosaurs, and there are a finite amount of them in the game. this means you will only be able to have persistent access to a small fraction of the dinosaurs species in the game, let alone the different colour variations. when building a pen for these dinosaurs, you have a follow a very specific criteria that reminds me of what it was like to build enclosures for animals in Zoo Tycoon 1 was like, if you remember that. it's like following a recipe instead of being able to add your own creativity and flair.even though farming mechanics are one of the last things i pay attention to in games like this, as i personally focus on character interaction more, even i felt this was lacking here. farming never progressed from being a dreaded chore into a comforting flow with a good pay off. it never gets rewarding, just something that you have to get "out of the way".this game could be a good for younger children or just for a few hours until you get bored of it, but not at the current price.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible! Everything I've wanted and craved from the cozy farming genre1. DINOSAURSThe star of the show! AESTHETICBright and lively, warm and welcoming: Paleo Pines feels like a dream world you've stepped into, reminiscent of childhood memories and a strange yet euphoric nostalgia. COMMUNITYStrangely enough, Paleo Pines has a deep sense of community that really comes through with the fesitivals and the mannerisms of the townsfolk. Even though I obviously don't exist in the Paleo Pines world, the townsolk manage to make me feel as if I am a part of their tight knit community...and always strive to be the best neighbours they can be!  It's almost as if we've been lifelong friends and they're always there to help. Definitely heartwarming <34. MARLOMarlo. _childDocuments_.review: If you like the demo in all its clunkiness, you will probably like the full game since it's just more of exactly the same thing. But it does get repetitive and grindy.I played with a controller, and there's plenty of issues with any kind of "precision" work. Even just picking up items is difficult at times. Inventory management is cumbersome, switching tools is annoying, and the small dinosaurs that are supposed to help with discovering items never did anything other than get stuck standing somewhere and disappear until you get back home.So in summary it feels unpolished and buggy, but not so much that it's unplayable. _childDocuments_.review: I have been following the development of this game for a while, it's great to finally be able to play it! I have things I very much enjoy, but there are also some issues that I hope will be remedied in the future.Please note that this review may contain spoilers for things such as game mechanics (or lack thereof), and if you haven't played this game, you may find it confusing to follow.-The dinos in this game are adorable. Their designs are all great and despite the cartoony and simplified art style, they are surprisingly faithful to our current understanding! It makes the huge dinosaur nerd in me super happy.-It's very fun to explore and discover new species and colorations of the dinos! Seeing my ranch fill up with all of my paleo pals is very satisfying. Some of the color combos are so pretty!-Growing/managing my crops is fun too, and figuring out what treats my dinos like best gives them a touch of individuality I was pleasantly surprised with!-Cooking food with the crops I harvested is very satisfying, and it's cool that they give you buffs!-The flute mechanic for befriending dinos is so cute. The more complicated songs you have to repeat back to them add a fun little challenge to the mostly laid back gameplay.-Cute music!-The main feature I feel that is missing is the . We're able to harvest all of these resources, but all we can really do with them is sell them, turn in minimal amounts for daily requests, or pay someone else to make something. This isn't always convenient, especially when the NPCs (aside from Corlan) stop selling things as soon as it hits sunset. The days aren't long, which isn't a bad thing, but especially when you're exploring the further areas you unlock later in the game, there's no way you're making it back to town in time to snag some needed supplies for a new dino friend you may have made. Crafting is a staple feature in these types of games, so the fact that it is absent here is quite strange to me.-In the same boat as my previous point, it's strange that we cannot turn our produce into herbivore food for the dinos, or even just put crops into the feeding troughs. I could understand the latter because of balancing, but it's strange we have to go into town to buy special food to feed our dinos (because the snack mechanic does nothing for the daily amount of food they need in their troughs and is only really for gaining trust and affection) when we live on a farm and grow food ourselves.-In the wild, we can occasionally find herbivore food laying about, but not carnivore food. The only way to get carnivore food is by buying it from Corlan, basically. A fantastic way to remedy this would be to add in a fishing mechanic! Not only could that provide a source of food/treats to our more carnivorous helpers, but it also brings the potential of being able to discover and document fish in your journal, just like your dinos, landmarks, and recipes. This could also pave the way for aquatic dinos/fishing helpers.. (wink)-In the future I hope the game gets expanded to include more areas and dinos! (especially the ones that were designed but cut before release!!)-Breeding mechanics! Little baby versions of these dinos would be so cute.-Dino personalities! Just like each dino having an individual favorite snack, a randomized pool of personalities would add even more individuality to each friend!-I find myself and my dinos getting caught on invisible geometry both on the ranch and out in the world fairly often. Not just when I'm near objects either, sometimes I'm just out in the open and I'll get blocked by an invisible wall. This happens to the playable character, while riding a dino, and to dinos when they're free roaming.-The NPCs are pretty basic, I wish they were a little more complex as characters. I think it would be more motivating to complete tasks for them if you could get to know them and care about them more.-Some of the game mechanics are not self-explanatory or even mentioned in the game. I've seen quite a few reviews on here where players have talked about having no idea what to do/how to do stuff and I have to agree. It does not help that quests logged in your journal are often very vague to the point where the only way to know what you're supposed to do is by googling it, as there's no way to click on the quest for more info.-The map isn't the greatest, it can be hard to tell what's where. I think more defined pathways would help, as well as the ability to pin locations on the map. Maybe at least being able to zoom in for a more detailed map of whatever area you're in. (As a note to readers, there are some pretty nice intractable maps on the Wiki!)-The seed pot, which is needed for dinosaurs with the Tender skill to be able to even use their skill, isn't accessible until way later in the game. I saw some people even saying it was by chance when Avery gives it to you, but I'm not sure. Regardless, it takes a while to get a hold of. I didn't even know it existed until I googled how to use the Tender skill.-It is weirdly difficult to get turnips, which are needed to progress the main quest at one point.-The daily quests are very repetitive, there's not much variety so they get kinda stale after having to give someone a hat for the 30th time.This game has a ton of charm and it's clear a lot of love was put into it, and while I am mostly enjoying it, it definitely could use some polish because in it's current state it does not feel finished. Despite the flaws, I recommend this game, as it's still quite fun and I hope that the support encourages the developers to continue refining and expanding this game!(P.S. if I have said anything incorrect please feel free to let me know!)
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for exactly 1.8 hours, I am requesting a refund. I was so excited to have an adorable farming game, with my favorite subject matter of all; DINOSAURS! Cute and accurate ones at bat! Maybe it's because this game seems a bit more for kids, who are easily entertained, or maybe it's because I have played so many fun dino games, but this just wasn't all that I was hoping it was. On my one point, if it's because it's more for kids, I really hope not. There is no real guidance system, and the controls, at least for PC seem clunky as hell. Why not just give us a hotbar for us to see our "equipment" that mind you takes up inventory space. Why not just make an equipment scroll reel? Anything, but having to go into your inventory and selecting the equipment every time you water your plants, and yes I understand if you scroll through you can select an item but that even seems random with no rhyme or reason. I wish there was more guidance on here, some helpful hot tips in the corner that are toggable, anything! The map is weird, the whole journal function seems scuffed, why can't i Just see my quests in a hot bar? Why can't I click on my quest and get a more DETAILED instruction? I have to google search practically all the quest to figure out what area to go in, and yes maybe that's because I skip through the dialog, but how many people do that? Are you supposed to remember exactly where you were an what the NPC said the next day you get on, am I supposed to be taking notes IRL, while taking notes in the game? I'd also like to mention as far mention there are crafting benches everywhere, but as far as I know, no crafting. Also, you have a house that you can't even decorate. WHAT'S UP WITH THAT?! Such a shame when there could be so much more content and opportunities by just adding some simple functions or more things to do.I do want to say the visual are beautiful for the dinos, and I want to say ONLY for the dinos. I wanted this game to be so good, but alas it was not what I wanted. The world while beautiful, seems empty, half baked, and not all that adventurous. I wish this would've been what I was PINING for, but as far as the state it is in now, I don't see that happening. :(These are just the things I noticed playing for 1.8 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "Maybe" option instead of just yes or no. This game is cute! The dino models are fun and cute, the human models are nice if not a bit uncanny. The game play...however? Not great. The cooking mechanic is basically just empty material thrown in to give the game some taste. The quests are hard to follow and have little value, and on top of that there's no way to see the dialogue after, you just get the tiny useless hint given to you. It's basically impossible to do anything until you can get each kind of working dino but of course you first need to get all the poppins (like taming treats) to do that, which puts you several in game weeks in. The farming mechanic is nice, but honestly hard to get the hang of without looking stuff up on the wiki. The house is basically just a glorified storage and save point. And there's decorations, sure! But its hard to make any kind of garden/walking place/outdoor area etc etc without screwing up all the dinos and your own pathing/walking ability. Which speaking of, your dinos will run away from you if you get off of them in the ranch! You get off? GONE. Half way across the map! They also can't do turns and will just not go forward if theres a turn in fencing. In conclusion? It's an ok game, not great. I'm honestly super disappointed. But the dinos are cool, so there's that.

_childDocuments_.review: I was all on board with this game at first. Love dinosaurs, love farm sims, love creature collection, and this game has all three. But the more I played, the more I kept thinking that I'm not having that much fun.The farming aspect does not feel very rewarding. It takes too much time and stamina (both yours and your helper dinos) and all they are for is selling (money is pointless but I'll mention that later) and giving to dinos as treats. You can't turn them into herbivore food or anything, which makes no sense to me. A potato is considered a "treat" but not "food", and yet a pile of nondescript leaves is a nutritional meal. I'm only making a mountain out of this mole hill because the devs have made it clear that these creatures are meant to be treated as friends/partners, not pets or tools (this has been used as a reason why pen management and creature limits are a thing), but we can't feed them our own produce as food? Note that I purposefully did not mention cooking as a use for farming goods, because cooking in this game is quite possibly the most worthless and frustrating mechanic here. Plus, all foods (raw and cooked) degrade over time. Worst idea I've ever heard in my life.Next issue: money. What is it for, exactly? Aside from buying poffins every now and then, there's just nothing worth spending it on. There's no house upgrades, hell there's no house decoration at all. Can't even go inside, might as well not even have a home. There's no farm upgrades, no fun toys or enrichment to make your dinos happy, there's nothing. I just don't understand it. I thought these were our partners?The NPCs are the most generic-looking, boring ensemble that I have ever encountered. I would also call them unmemorable, but I'll definitely remember them as being one of the most dull cast of characters you could think of. Couldn't name any of them though. There was a yeehaw girl with a raptor I think? The quests they give out suck too, unless you really love repetitive fetch quests.Keeping and managing dinos is an absolute slog and extremely frustrating. As I mentioned before, you can only have so many, limited by Dream Stones or whatever they are called. There's only so many you can get, so if you're wanting to get one or two of each creature, you're outta luck. Don't even think about collecting and keeping all the colors, it's not possible. Sure you can tame a new color, then release it to log the color in your journal, but that really sucks. Even building pens for dinos is a massive chore, all species has a specific size of pen they like, and they can get pretty big even for a single dino. You can combine species into one pen but then you have to do some weird math wizardry to get the pen size right or the dinos are unhappy, and even then most dinos prefer being with their own kind or by themselves.The holiday events are just... you could remove them from the game and there'd be no impact. There's no fun to be had, no cool seasonal items to collect, no memorable moments. At least the most recent Halloween event follows the same tradition of being a giant nothingburger. No, all the interesting stuff is paywalled behind a DLC. The trick-or-treating, a seasonal quest, decorations for your farm, costumes for your avatar, gotta pay for it. What, and I cannot stress this further, the ♥♥♥♥? Is this for real? I expected nothing and was still disappointed.The only thing that can potentially save the game in this state is opening up modding so talented players can actually make this game even somewhat an enjoyable experience because right now the ONLY thing this game has going for it is how cute the dinosaurs are.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is a fun little dinosaur farming simulator! In an age with farming sims out the wazoo, its all too easy for them to end off bland and generic. Paleo Pines manages to bring something fun and fresh to the table with its adorable dinosaurs! The music is quite pleasant and very fitting for the game. Below I shall list points about the game including how important I feel they are ^-^+++ Dinosaur Models are top notch.+++ Sound design is good.+++ Almost everything about the game looks great- I don't really like the player models themselves, they just feel less refined than the dinosaurs to me+ There is a reasonable amount of outfit choices- There is a lack of colour choices for said outfits, it would be awesome to see new colours for the existing items!+++ Overall gameplay loop is quite fun, exploring the map and checking the rarity of the creatures is quite entertaining (to me anyway.)-- The games tutorials are lacklustre, leading to you having to figure out stuff on your own. In some games, learning to do things on your own is good. In this game it can be frustrating until you learn the mechanics on your own, especially when there is no indication of what you are meant to do at times.- Side quest rewards seem to be randomly selected along with the quest itself, this leads to quests that require giving more of the same resource in exchange for less reward. Not a big deal but it can feel a bit funny at times (such as getting 80 shells for 3 fibre or 35 shells for 5 fibre from the same person on the same quest-board on the same day.)++ Cleaning up the farm feels satisfying and rewarding.---- Probably my biggest upset with the game, there is nowhere to put extra dinosaurs. This game desperately needs some form of the Pokemon box system. Maybe it could be a ranch where you send friends that don't fit on the farm. For a game all about collecting dinosaur friends, the current system discourages you from it instead. I have passed on dozens of rares, and 1 ultra rare (It was an exact duplicate of one I already had) just because I have no reasonable space for extras. If I grab an uncommon I'll just replace it with a rare/ultra rare later so why bother? It leads to me only going for ultra rares or a rare if it has a new ability for the farm. I should never need to release my friends back to the wild and lose them forever, in a collection game that is the worst thing to make the players do. If they were to add/fix any one thing, it would be this. I don't have an issue with the limited dreamstones (The farm has a limited size anyway), but we should have some way of keeping the friends we can't fit somewhere where we can still visit or see our collection.+++ Developers have good transparency with the community, which is huge.-- I've had some optimisation issues, the game will randomly become crippled with lag visually and audio-ly that isn't caused by the system (game doesn't even surpass 15% of my gpu, cpu, and no more than 25% of the ram) I have found changing the graphics settings from high to medium, playing for about 5 seconds, and then returning them to high fixes the issue for the rest of a session. // I won't put a minus because it is a small studio who made the game and it is difficult to implement, but this game would excel with multiplayer!Overall a fun experience, I look forward to what the developers add and fix overtime!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I really really REALLY wanted to give this a solid review.I had been following the game for a while now and was excited, as Parasaur are my favorite dino's and oh look a game thats centered on them?? SIGN ME UP!But since I started playing I have been having 20% fun and 80% griping. Its that bad.It feels like the game is lackluster for one, like its not fully fleshed out.You constantly have to go to google or the wiki to understand HOW to play the game as it feels like half of any tutorials there could be are just... Missing?We have no way to tell what dino colors are rare or not until they are caught.You have to friend a dino, get it to follow you home, and then "level up its trust" with NO physical indication of how far that "trust" is with the dino in order to even ride it. I have played for 8 ingame days and STILL cant get a dino to trust me enough to ride to PROGRESS THE ACTUAL GAME PLOT. Oh and finding dreamstones, I have found ONE large one, and I have 3 dinos total so far. Which means the last dino will ALWAYS be mad at me cuz it "cant sleep right" And I have looked up guides, I have searched every single inch of the beginner area, NO LARGE DREAMSTONES. I can have one of the NPC's make one, ok but you need a "biome" themed pen for that. Wheres the tutorial on how to make pens into biomes cuz now I have to google ANOTHER thing??? I may come back to the game and try again some day, but the game itself has frustrated me much more than been a cozy and relaxing game at this point to the point where I dont even recommend it to friends anymore, thats how annoyed I am with the mechanics. I also have a friend who played the demo, and they said a bunch of things from the demo are missing in the finished game, so maybe thats where it went wrongAs of right now, I dont have the patience to wait 10+ days to progress the literal plot of the game due to not being able to make a dino "trust" me enough without the ability to see what "trust level" I am even atI have a friend who has been playing for 8 hours and has JUST gotten the same dino's trust level up enough to put a saddle on it and progress the plot of the game, 8 REAL HOURS. Its too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: Some opinions may change with further gameplay.OVERALL THOUGHTS: 6/10I've followed Paleo Pines development for many years on social media. I'm not a 'cozy game' person or a farming sim fan to begin with, I came here for the dinosaurs. My problem with cozy gaming is a lack of substance, which I have to say is the case here too. Then my problem with farming sims is a lack of instruction, which is VERY MUCH an issue here too. However, if you're just here to wind down or are already a fan of farming sims  with a good understanding of their similarities, I can't imagine you'd have any issues here.Pros:- The dinosaurs are cute, varied, and fun. Their skills are very helpful and a fun mechanic. Finding dinosaurs with really rare colors is very exciting and enough to get me out in the field day after day.- The environment is very pretty. It is a really nice looking game! I did get lost a ton in the valley at first, but I got the hang of it after the first week.- The act of befriending dinosaurs is pretty well thought out! The flute mechanics are fun and the meter provides a real challenge at times.Cons:- The controls are pretty clunky. When you're building fences your own character gets in the way. The press vs press and hold system gets annoying. Foraging is harder  than it should be because you have to stand at just the right angle. Yikes!- The human characters are... boring. Maybe you'll start to unlock their tragic backstory after awhile and they'll have some interest but truthfully I can't find a reason to like them much. I wish there were more dialogue options.- The absolute lack of instruction, or suddenly receiving instruction after figure it out yourself after too much trial and error. I should not be having to google how to do the most basic things on my farm. Some things I figured out slowly from  reading the journals but others completely lack an explanation of control schemes. This has made questing much more slow-going than I'd like.Honestly there's a lot of mechanics I would have liked to see more of in this game. The fact that you can't craft is really a shame. It's like they needed a reason to make players actually want to go to the market so they decided 'special orders' were the way to go instead of letting your character craft on their own.A breeding mechanic for even rarer or breeding-only colors would have really knocked this game out of the park for me also.Despite my complaints, I really do like this game, I just wish it had a bit more going on. It's just niche enough to get me into a genre I don't play though.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxed, comfy game with the most adorable dinos you've ever seen! With so many farming sims out there that feel honestly kind of stressful, Paleo Pines does a wonderful job of being very stress-free with a more "go at your own pace" style to it. The pastel color palette of the game is also super pretty and very sensory friendly as well as the sounds being sensory friendly, which I absolutely appreciate as an autistic person. Overall, very pleased with the experience so far and will continue progressing through the story to find even more dinosaurs (especially those pride flag inspired rare ones !!).
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: If you find yourself pining for Viva Pinata the way I do, then just go ahead and buy the game right now.This game is deceptively big and in-depth, while keeping the UI and controls simple, and the micro-managing to a minimum. It truly is a relaxing and chill experience that still rewards you for exploring, asking questions, and thinking through your next steps.I have a handful of gripes. They are all minor, and unobtrusive to the experience as a whole, but would be nice fixes to see anyhow. The controls are elegant in their simplicity, but I often find myself pushing them to their limits. Sometimes it can be difficult to select which dinosaur you're communicating with the flute, and the most frustrating thus far was trying to till soil with a dinosaur. It's very clear that using a dinosaur to till is meant for making broad strokes without the stamina investment, but I was trying to till a handful of specific spots because I was out of stamina already and had seeds to plant. Trying to till one specific tile with a dinosaur is honestly a nightmare, and I do not recommend trying to do so. But then again, if I was smarter with my stamina for that day, I wouldn't have had to, so there you go if you wanna talk about rewards for planning.What really stands out to me is just how masterfully the game comes together. It spins a lot of plates at once, and it never feels overwhelming, or like it's throwing too much at for doing so. I'm already 16 hours in, and I feel like I've barely scratched the surface. Yet every moment has felt like the right amount of engaging. Not too much, not too little. The game really does succeed at making the present the most comfortable place for your mind to be, and that's a remarkable thing to capture in a video game.This is an easy recommend. It's cute. It's fun. It's relaxing. You can tell that it was made by people who actually like making games. Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I'm only sixteen hours into this game and it's brand new but I'm already massively in love. The animation style is cute, the dinosaurs are cute, the taming mechanic? So cute. I'm having a blast, the progression takes time but doesn't feel tedious, and the story is engaging enough to keep my attention. I have only one real gripe at the moment. There's an invisible wall in the middle of my farm. My dinos run into it and either get shunted super hard to one side or stop like there's an obstacle, but there isn't. _childDocuments_.review: This game lacks content for the price it set to be. "CUTE DINOS" by itself won't sell.Let's start by talking about the first hour you're in the game. Break it or make it for new player. After accepting a quest from the post board, it can not be cancel. The quests themselves, some require materials from the second/third season. Some players were stuck not knowing what to do about the dinos they already recorded while asking them to recorded it again by npc for quest. Don't get me started with the find my lost hat at this location.For a creature collection game, most games allow you to catch the creatures you see. In this game, it uses poppins, 5 at that. If the creature you encounter doesn't like the poppin you currently have, you're out of luck. Bye, bye ultra rare dino. You'll have to wait to unlock a new poppin. Imagine, you're only allowed to catch pikachu with a fast ball. That's how this feels.END GAME has it's own problem.Update: Let's talk about "end game". This game isn't a ranch nor farm. Ranch has breeding or animals that produce anything besides poop. If you turn your property into a farm, you'll be punish for it. If you have 200 three star watermelons 2 days before summer ends, you won't be able to sell them all before the season ends turning your three star into a two star the next season. There are only two NPC that your crops can be sold to who has a limited amount of money. At best, this game is petting zoo with a side garden.Now that you sold all your crops for money (daily cap). You can now buy some decro with additional materials (wood, forest wood, stone, sand stone).  Sadly, they also cap this to a daily respawn. There is no cave where you can farm unlimited resource or npc to buy off from.There are so many restriction to dinos. Pen size, dino type: loner-pack-herd, number of dreamstones, your property, happiness/unhappiness. There are other issues to the game and the first "massive update" to the game is more dino colors.This may really discourage new players from continuing. If you can get past this and other things, this game might be enjoyable for some hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved dinosaurs since I was a little kid, and I want to like this game, but the developers' questionable priorities have showed me that it's just not worth it, especially at full price.As others have pointed out, the premise is basically Animal Crossing/Stardew Valley with dinosaur taming.
