_childDocuments_.review: (Spoiler Free): This game officially soared to the top of my all time favorite games. I have always loved farming games (I've logged almost 300+ hours on Stardew Valley combined across Steam and my Switch.) But this game officially captured my heart.I adore dinosaurs and to see this game with it's adorable and rounded art style which I LOVE) and the accuracy of the dinosaurs made me love it even more. The only bugs that I have personally come across are in the footprint tracking quests where it doesn't register that I'm interacting with the dinosaur. I was still able to complete the main story without doing that part, so it didn't affect my gameplay at all. I do not understand the negativity surrounding this game in every comment section I've come across. This game is a joy to play and I would HIGHLY recommend if you love dinosaurs and farming games. _childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying Paleo Pines so far, but as of right now, I cannot recommend the game in its current state! I love dinosaurs and farming games, and in terms of style, I absolutely adore the art direction of the game. However, I've played a lot of farming sims, so I have to be critical of the flaws this game possesses. There's a lack of direction concerning quests and learning the main mechanics of the game. They teach you how to befriend a dinosaur, but not how you properly house them. How big does their pen need to be in reference to the game's placement grid? What is a dreamstone and how does it work? If I have to open the wiki to figure out why the pen I made isn't valid only a couple hours into the game, it indicates that the game is missing better explanation. Key items for quests that you have to find can also benefit from better highlighting, something like a search area for "Find This Item" quests would be great. In addition to this, a minimap somewhere on the screen would be helpful, considering the sizes of the areas, and maybe to better indicate where you can and can't walk (lots of invisible walls or hills that look traversable but are out of bounds).I also find it strange that you can't craft many of the essential items you need to care for your dinosaurs, such as kibble and fences. Kibble is arguable the most important factor in dino care, and you have to keep your dinos fed so they don't run away. But the only way to obtain kibble for carnivores is buying it, and it's more expensive to purchase than herbivore kibble. You can sometimes find small amounts of herbivore kibble on the ground, but it's not sustainable once you have 3+ dinos. Rope Fences are also important for housing your dinos, and your only way to obtain those is to buy them as well. There's a lot of emphasis on spending money, and not many alternatives to buying everything you need. I should be able to craft fences with the 3 stacks of wood I have sitting around, and maybe if the game had fishing, we could turn fish into food for carnivores? And turn crops into herbivore kibble?There are smaller, more scattered grievances I have, like the journal not recording dino colors, fertilizer not being able to be placed on already growing crops, a lack of a clear NPC schedule, clunky and unintuitive decorating system, general balancing, and more, and while there's a lot I really love about the game, interaction with dinos, the flute mechanic, the lovely animations and art style, it's not enough to ignore the nagging feeling that the game seems very underdeveloped in a few, very foundational areas of the game. Hoping to see some improvements in the future so I'm able to recommend Paleo Pines in confidence!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite fun and relaxing, it's the sort of game for those who just enjoy cute and peaceful aesthetics and don't mind repetition or a lot of waiting. There are repetitive parts to the game and it can become quite boring however the range of dinosaurs and their colours makes up for the back and forth. There is some figuring out needed especially when it comes to farming and the main quests. The main quests tend to not give much information on what you are required to do and can be a lot of trial and error especially when certain quests require certain dinosaurs or even friendship points with certain NPC's that isn't clearly told to the player. The game sometimes bugs out and requires you to save and then quit before loading back in. Other than the glitches that can be solved with reloading and the tedious quests that don't give much information on how to complete, the game for the most part is pleasant and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: This has been on my wish list since 2022 and I finally snagged it on sale, about a year after it released. And like many games that I say "that looks cool, I'll add that," it ended up being a disappointment. This is NOT a $30 game AT ALL. This is borderline unfinished. Getting myself motivated to play this after the first go was very difficult, but I gave it an honest try. My experience of 2.6 hours and half a month in game: Immediate frustration and confusion at the controls and then disappointment upon seeing the human NPCs (why are their names the same color when speaking? They couldn't even so much as make them distinct??). I kept getting lost in the map because all the hills and bushes looked the same with very few landmarks. I needed more cash because everything was very expensive but the only way to earn money was to grow crops, which took days, and the only thing to do in between waiting was smash debris and do quests. But the quests are fetch quests and some were even "grow a bunch of crops" quests... and some involved picking plants I never even found despite scouring (dandelions). After a while I just started waking, watering the plants, then sleeping, so they'd grow and I could finally get money to buy things. Bought a$100 ($100!!!!) pastry to befriend a new dino, just to be rejected when that dino didn't even like them. Got frustrated and called it a night because I just wasn't having fun.Pros:- Cute dinos and pretty environment. You get to ride the dinos which is awesome.- ... I can't think of anything else.Cons:- Unpolished, clunky controls and UI. Why is the character on a grid when walking but when moving a dino forward you can turn smoothly? That was a clear choice made and it was a bad one.- The human characters look kinda... unappealing and samey. They look cheap and uninspired, just uncanny to look at.- It's in the same genre as Stardew Valley but... not very fun. Slow grinding, boring surroundings, flat characters, fetch quests with little reward, items are too expensive, you can't skip the eating animation when trying to befriend dinos... etc.Overall I wish I could say "meh" instead of no. Because really this game, from what I've seen, is just... meh. It's a little cute and riding dinos is fun. But everything else is just unfinished, unpolished, uninspired. It's missing that special something to make it worth playing, and riding dinos, especially with such poor controls, is just not it. There are way better games in this genre out there :(

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute game, and one that I very conditionally recommend. It's functional, and the theme carries a lot of weight for me, but the game itself seems to have a bit of an identity crisis.It has all sorts of dinosaurs to collect, and rare/ultra rare color patterns for them for even more collection potential...but limits the number of dinos you can have on your ranch, and the leveling system emphasizes sticking with individual dinosaurs, not switching them around. And your ranch is a huge mess to start with, but clearing up the mess takes so much energy that clearing enough space for, say, a new pen can take several in-game days.The farming is functional enough, and the dinosaurs do actually help quite a bit, as tilling and watering don't seem to be as stamina-intensive as space clearing.There are some skills that really emphasize the need for a glossary or something; I had to go to wikis and forums to find out, for example, what "Discoverer" and "Tender" do.The cooking mechanic is...bad. Just for starters, you can't (as far as I can tell and have reached) have a cooking spot at your ranch, there's just a pot out by a lake. You need a significant number of each ingredient for a recipe, and given how slow earning money can be, the benefits of cooking a meal are often worth less than just selling the produce. Furthermore, recipes seem to be earned at a snail's pace.The NPCs are...there. They don't really have much in the way of character, at least compared to something like Stardew Valley, and everyone is friendly to you from the start; there are no real antagonists, and no 'jerks' that need to warm up to you; the closest thing is one that is, at worst, a little bit weird. That's fine, but ONLY fine, which is a running theme with the game.So again, that's my review. A lot of negative, but for me, it's functional, and the cuteness and concept help make up for a LOT. The non-launch-sale price is a bit much, though; I really hope that this game gets updates and otherwise expands so it could justify that price.

_childDocuments_.review: I am extremely torn to say this. I am still planning on playing it to completion because of the ups of the game, but I _cannot_ recommend it, at least not at full price. While it is on sale, $15 or so, definitely worth the money. At $30, you can get a lot, lot more gameplay and polish out of other indie games. It really hurts because I want, with every fiber of my being, to love this game. I think the dinos' designs great. I love the concept. I think the farming is decent. I think the music (while slightly limited) is enjoyable. I think the exploration is fun.* I think the variety of things to collect are great! **Just... It has some pretty crushing flaws that keep me from giving it full marks. The smallest critique is that the humans kind of look like old wooden dolls brought to life. It is the tiniest, because that's just a personal preference thing. The other things, though, I feel the reviews even address, outside of mine.The game has three areas, three seasons, and one town. Already rather small for a farming sim going up against things like My Time at Sandrock, or even its older, less polished predecessor, My Time at Portia. There is an acceptable amount of the focal aspect of the game: dinosaurs. Huge marks on that one, for me. It's what I came for, and I'm here for it. However, the variety is primarily carnivorous theropods, raptors, thyreophora and ceratopsians. So, while there is a lot of variety, they all are branches of four aspects of the very vast quantity of dinosaurs out there. While they are in the code--there are no sauropods, the only hadrosaur is the mascot, etc. I do like some things they left in details-wise, such as both Compsognathus and Archeopteryx both appearing in the same area (as fossils have been confused for one another, before) and how it addresses whether dinos are loners, pack or herd varieties. It really does seem like they _care_ about the game. Again, part of why it hurts so bad that I can't recommend it.** There are many other things to collect, which is nice, but there is no difference between carrying several of them in replacement of others, besides one aspect of individual dinosaurs' charts. I can go through most of the game on carrots, onions and potatoes, without ever collecting another crop. Further, while the farming works fine and does what it needs two, it does mean that not much farming is truly necessary, barring a couple cases I will address in the following section.One of the two hugest issues, glaring, and a major part of the not recommending to others, is this: there is a lot of waiting, for waiting's sake, in the game. I don't mind it in some ways, as you shouldn't get everything immediately, or it'd kill the playtime. However, some lore-based quests have you waiting for one crop to grow, or one person to appear (who may only appear once every five or six thirty minute game days.) This doesn't really add to the fun, especially if you are at a lull on other goals at the time. In fact, sometimes it added tedium that legitimately had me debate dropping the game mid-playthrough. The other time it really bothers me is when it is fully RNG-based waiting. There is a place you can repair that requires an item: Pampas grass. It is insignificant, inconsequential and a decorative prop like many others. However, it shows up so infrequently I only saw it around three times in a full game year. If you don't have enough money to buy all you need on that day, you just get stuck waiting again, with no guarantee it will show for weeks.* The other huge issue, and the one that had me almost stop a stream, one day, is that, while you can refer to a wiki, I was trying to play blind, and then... some of the quests give you so little direction you have no idea what to do, where to go, or what you need, or when you need it. Some are like "find [x person]," and while you can infer which region (i.e. which of the 3 I mentioned earlier) they are in, the area is narrowed down to "not at their house" and nothing more. I spent at least a game week, I think, looking over the same map, walking circles, only to not find them, and on occasion, since it had been so long, forgetting to bring the necessary item, which may outright not make them spawn at all. It was deeply infuriating, and felt pointless. These seem to be the only times a person does _not_ appear on the map screen (which makes sense in-story, and on the gameplay meta, but feels confusingly arbitrary from any other context, especially player-side.)There are other things, such as recipes, which you just literally have to guess, unless it is one you are outright given. It can be any from 1-15 of an ingredient, for multiple ingredients, with no hints or guides, to my knowledge. It might have them, but, frankly, outside of achievements, the cooking feels almost pointless. They give buffs, which is cool, but they feel entirely irrelevant to every other aspect of the game, besides temporary perks. Similar with decorating. You can't decorate an inside, so some of the furniture seems odd, since it is outside-only. Everything is snap-to-grid, so precising decor, even matching the way they are used in places such as town, are off the table. Also, it just didn't seem as compelling as something like My Time at Portia, which added perks to decorating your house that influence gameplay, sometimes a noticeable amount. It is a necessary aspect of a game like this, but it just feels rather uncompelling in this circumstance. None of the furniture, to my knowledge, does anything unless you can sit on it. I never even bothered cleaning my whole farm out of scraps and rocks.The mission board missions (to get resources and, more importantly, money, though you can also farm and sell if you prefer) feel very redundant, because they are literally find or deliver [journal, hat, lucky trinket], or bring [usually common resource]. Little else happens, and that limited variety of item names that appear makes them feel extremely cookie cutter. The three environs are decent for what they are in what I will conclude my major criticisms on. However, they are vast enough to get frustrating to explore (see: above) and small enough to feel like big play rooms. They have fixed, designated spots most dinosaurs appear (with a few changing during seasons, or moving somewhat wildly across the map to add a hint of welcome flavor.) There are houses you can sleep at to, I suppose, keep your exploration to a certain area, less interrupted. However, since you need to go tend to your dinosaurs and crops, you still are going to have to return home every day, anyway, so it feels a bit superfluous. The shops are _mostly_ predictable, except the person who makes outfits, who is the only one who can expand your inventory, and requires fiber and money, which might mean you have to wait a bit between purchases, even days, to try and get a pocket upgrade. The characters feel pretty classical NPC with a few boxed up dialog, minimal lore-based reward for friendships (though there are item and recipe rewards,) and I didn't even do much shopping outside of three of the stores, even still, two of which I could avoid for ups of a month. Why I really wanted to love this game, but only ended up liking it is 1. dinos, 2. farming sim and 3. heart. The game has heart. It just feels more like a concept demo of a fuller game. You can, if you really press, get 30-40 hours out of it, but sadly, a lot of that is literally waiting or walking in circles. BUT it has heart and charm. I could see a fleshed out, polished sequel that takes the criticism to heart and addresses it being something I'd gladly recommend at the same price. This is the hardest thumbs down I've ever felt it important to give, because I love what there is, it just isn't much for the $30 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: After some time playing, I would not recommend buying this game at its current state. It needs quite a few quality of life improvements and polish. Decoration is tile based and leaves a lot of empty space between items which makes everything look clunky. your energy bar depletes fast with the only way to restore it being to sit down, but the way it refills is so slow it's not worth it. Just going in between mounts can drain your entire stamina. You can make food to eat but that doesn't restore stamina, it just gives you friendship buffs. And the only place to make food is halfway across the map. After 20 hours there's no in farm kitchen/cook pot. Inventory space is abysmal. You can apparently upgrade it by 3 slots at the most, but, after 20 hours, I have no clue how to do that. With how much food and poppins you have to collect for befriending dinos plus tools you only really have 3 spaces in your inventory to pick up any of the dozens of foragables, building materials, or quest items. There is a reason why every other farming sim I've played has upgrades of 10+ slots per upgrade. I mean with the 3 different quality crops you get,  farming day can take 2-3 trips to the village to sell. A fix for this is either bigger upgrades or maybe having some sort of dino operated cargo? Like a wagon for huge amounts of inventory or even just saddle bags?And yeah the selling is a bit of a nightmare. Each item has to be sold at a different stall and you can only sell 5 items at a time. Once again there's a reason why most farming sims has a selling box on the farm. I understand wanting to break away from formula but the quality of life that's being sacrificed is way too much. Character customization has to be only 1 step up from none at all. While the models are cute (before they move and the teeth clip through the mouth every single time) the options are too small. You can't even have freckles or glasses and I see them being used on the main NPCs. Honestly, this game needs major quality of life improvements before I can recommend in good faith. The bones of an amazing game are there, but it feels like I'm a play tester for an unreleased build. For 30$ it's not worth it. For 18$? I still couldn't recommend. Wishlist instead and keep a close eye on development logs

_childDocuments_.review: If Stardew Valley and Ark had a one night stand, you get Paleo Pines. _childDocuments_.review: So I wanna say I followed the development of this game on and off for a while and I really enjoy some of the models and some of the gameplay. However, there is a heavy lack of content and I'd even argue some elements do not get as much love as others within the game as well. I'll break my thoughts into parts, as many before have mentioned the characters all look sort of bland, and this is true, besides Agami Zara, and Marlo, many of the characters have same face syndrome in their designs, even the main story characters such as Pippin and Mari. And the only other character that looks different than the others is well, Freya but only her body is different. This goes for the player as well, I understand wanting to keep the character gender neutral which I respect, but having one single body type and few other ways to adjust the look of your character makes them fall sort of flat. This also goes for the animation and sound department of characters. The player has one sound from what I have experienced, and it's an input that does nothing but make you jump and say "yippie!." The npcs have maybe two to three, with Avery being the only character to have ones you can actually really hear. As well the main npcs are so boring, they sort of just stand in one spot or walk about aimlessly, talking to them doesn't feel fun or engaging. I have not talked to a character once outside of quests and shopping and had more fun playing than watching the ingame cutscenes that sort have characters just blabber to each other. A fix to this issue is quite simple, I've animated before and simply pushing the animations and expressions could really help flush out these characters. Stardew Valley has me more engaged with the pixel characters more than this game by simply having their characters have individual, unique and to the character's personality expressions and actions. If Mari research dinos why does she just walk around the field? why not have her writing notes under a tree next to a herd of dinos? or have her sitting on a hill over looking a pack of carnivores. Have her explore the other regions if she's such a researcher.Next is the dinos themselves which if you look at the community board on here, you'll notice a pattern. One thing I've always disliked in games with dinos, animals, anything of the sort is when the same love is not shown for each creature in the game. This is apparent when you look at the wiki or community tab. If you look at the diversity of colors for the Trex, compared to the Dilo, it's not too different. But then go to the Stego and the amount of colors and patterns fall off. I understand they are adding more colors to the game, but only popular dinos are getting love which to me is like, why even HAVE the others in the first place? Some dinos even only spawn in one spot and only in that spot, for Trex it makes sense, but why make the Baryonx and the Megalo spawn in the same spot interchanging from time to time? Many other dinos were planned as well, including some special ones for the npcs, such as an Iguanadon for Marlo. The only two that actually got their dinos I believe, are Owynn and Mari. The others got replaced with much more lackluster versions. As well, some models are clearly stretching from time to time, and just like with characters, lack animations. Watching the dinos moving in their pens gets boring as they don't do much besides walk, run, eat, and sleep. which instead of animating them laying down, many just tuck their head forward or back and sleep. Some Dinos even become useless after a certain point, once you clear all of the large spots for gathering, there's not much else to do with clearing dinos except for on the farm where the little piles show up. Yes, materials appear in the wild, but it's sad to have to carry an Anky out to the forest for forest wood, and have a much of other wood dinos just doing nothing. The "CUTE DINOS!!!!" feeling wears off rather quickly, especially with just how little the dinos do and the very limited amount of programmed personalities that really don't change much. It would be interesting to have dinos with complex personalities that add depth to keeping them at your farm. such as ones that are extroverts, to where no matter their pack or loner need they are noisy and get more enjoyment from being visited or interacted with, but become sad without enough interaction. Or an Aloof Dino who's more distant and low-maintenance often wandering around the farm, they may also be harder to tame due to this. This personality diversity would give players more incentive to engage with dinos, allowing players to be able to have multiple dinos being tamed and say, oh my extroverted Trex needs to see me every day, my Aloof Ourano is more likely to enjoy being left alone with food and clean pen, and my Adventurous Proceratops can come with me on my travels today. This could even give homestead dinos a "requests" mechanic allowing you to fulfill little things dinos wanna do every so often to grant a bonus to exp, materials gained, or maybe even blessings of good luck or harvest of some sort. Enrichment toys would also be a fun way to have dinos engage with their living spaces, and some dinos disliking certain forms of weather and temperatures. Adding a simple large shed for Stegos to hide beneath during the rain, or a platform like goats irl have for Troodons to jump on would help breath a bit of life into the pens.Currently the state the game is in, there is no drive to go out and explore besides completing the history notes, finding rare dino colors, and decorating your farm, but even then, decorating your farm may even become lame since well, the dinos don't do much. Characters aren't fun to engage with outside of leveling up friendship for better rewards or shop discounts. Overall it feels like a full game demo more than a full fledged game. The reason people say the demo was fantastic and the full game is lackluster is, everything there was to experience, was in the demo, nothing new was really added besides access to other areas, more days, and more dinos. I really want to love this game, I love the style, though it needs some polish, I like how the dinos feel to use on the farm, and I like most of the colors. But with the lack of content and the sort of repeating cycle I've found myself in. I feel no drive to play. I tend my farm plot, race about the regions to see if any ultra rares are about, then go back and sleep. It's not a terrible game, there is content, but once you get use to the gameplay loop, nothing breaks it up. It doesn't allow for players to immerse themselves after they've noticed how most of the dinos follow the same patterns. That's how I feel about Paleo Pines, a lovely idea, with a lot of holes that just need to be filled.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit; Apparently there are more dreamstones than I have been led to believe! Which is my bad, sorry about that. All of the articles I was reading and information I could find had told me there are only 24 dreamstones. If this is true that there are more, then I do reccomend the game slightly more, but overall still can't recommend, especially for $30. Here are *some* of th gripes with it that I wish would be changed/were done differently.  Yes, it is nit picky, but all these things overall combined really do hurt my experience and enjoyability of playing this game. • The NPCs feel empty and unlikable. The NPC that sells the player dinosaur food and buys the player's produce (I can't remember his name, Cor something?) has the dialogue line of "You'll be back" which to me just doesn't feel very friendly. Mari and Owynn aren't too bad, just a bit awkward. Same for Pippin. The only character I find to be actually likable is Agami and Marlo. The rest of the characters just feel forgettable and pointless.• Every "class" of dinosaur function the exact same. I was really excited to have gotten my first deinocheirus, thinking it would water my crops vastly better than my gallimimus, considering it's size and rarity. I was wrong. The watering is the exact same between each of the dinosaurs, which is honestly a bit disappointing. I see no purpose to seeking out the rarer dinosaurs other than just to have them to be cool. In this way there is no upgrading at all. What you start with is what you have forever essentially.• The game is very difficult to navigate at first. The quest line to get your first styracosaurus bugged out the first time I fed it a crunchy poppin and it did not trigger it to allow me to continue until I fed it again, leading me to be confused and frustrated on how to actually get one. This may be my fault as I did not pay much attention to the characters dialogue, as, again, I find them very uninteresting and boring. • The inventory system is an absolute mess. Trying to get to the item you need requires you to scroll through every single item in your inventory before you can get there, or opening your inventory and clicking on the item. Both of which are a hassle. This game could have really benefited from an item hot bar or an item wheel of at least your tools. Now that I am later in the game and don't have much use for the tools I only keep my book shovel and flute on me, so a hot bar would probably be the best option. • I wish the book had recorded colours and their rarities as well. I would have loved to fill out the book with every single dinosaur variation! It would also help the player remember which dinosaurs they've already discovered, saving them the work of befriending a dinosaur only to realise it's the same uncommon colour you released just yesterday. It's easy enough to remember and figure out what colours you have and haven't seen before early in the game, but once you have all the areas unlocked and you're ultra rare hunting it becomes quite difficult to remember all the different colours for each dino! This being said I am not sure if the colour rarity should be discoverable from just writing about it in the book. Perhaps make the player need to befriend it to be able to record it in the book? I am unsure. • The building system feels very clunky annoying and difficult to work with. As some other reviews have already said, you can't turn your camera or move while in build mode, so if you are in the way or want to move to another area you have to leave build mode and reenter it somewhere else. Not fun. • The story line is boring and forgettable. What am I doing again? Why am I doing it? Do I really even care? No, I don't. I haven't been given any reason to care.• The maps are small and also very clunky. Invisible walls everywhere. Wanting to leave the path? Good luck, you're going to have a very hard time. • The gameplay loop is incredibly grindey. Wake up > water seeds > scoop poop > feed dinos. Next day, harvest seeds > sell them for next to no profit > spend all your money on seeds and food that will barely get you by. Living paycheck to paycheck right now and I don't even have that many dinosaurs. It gets boring fast.• I forgot cooking even exists until reading someone else's review. -----------------------------And now that the bad is out of the way here is the good! • The variety of dinosaurs is lovely! There are so many to choose from and gather and it's quite fun discovering all the species! Also the colour variations are to die for. I am a collector type of person so the idea of gathering one of each species in the ultra rare variety is very appealing to me!• The graphics are absolutely adorable. The dinosaur models remind me of games I would play as a child, bringing me a nostalgic feeling that makes me feel warm and safe. The little happy dance the galli does or the wiggles the para do are heart warming and I love hanging out with them!• The decorations themselves from what I can tell is super cute! I am really bad at decorating and I'm kind of dumb when it comes to decorating so it is a struggle for me thus far though.-----------------------------dumb dumb original unedited ignorant review: <s>Very cute and fun game, but extremely disappointed with the amount of dinosaurs you can keep. As far as I can tell you can keep a total of 15 large dinosaurs (including the one you start with) and 9 small dinosaurs, for a total of only 24 dinosaurs. For a game boasting to be a dino sanctuary and having so many types of dinosaurs and different colours, I had expected to at the least be able to have one of each species. I had hope to collect one of each gallimimus and psittacosaurus, but if I were to do that I would be unable to own any other dinosaurs (at least, for the small ones). This is absolutely saddening. The promise to be able to collect dinosaurs and fill out a sanctuary was the main attraction for me, and due to this reason I hate to say it but I can't really recommend this game. There are enough farming games already for that aspect to be able to make up for the dinosaur restrictions.</s>

_childDocuments_.review: Some context: I have been following this game since it's announcement, have been in the discord server, and am a massive dino nerd and farm sim fan. I'm leaving a review not out of spite but as caution to buyers since this game costs full price.The concept of a dinosaur farm sim is fully utilised with perfect dino integration, giving each class of dinos useful and dynamic abilities to aid you through the whole game, encouraging you to use them all during your day-to-day. It is obvious the team has a deep respect and love for paleontology, having professionals of the field in their team and community, and anyone can appreciate that level of dedication.Unfornately, this is the only noteworthy thing to say as the game feels empty as far as gameplay. I've been waiting for a game like this for years but in it's current state there's not actually very much to do. Even the little things seem to be overlooked or completely absent. I can count the things you can do on one hand: Farm vegetables, tame dinos, do fetch quests. Oh, and if you're lucky there's a holiday where you can click on stuff (yippee?). As far as progression, you essentially clear paths to get to new areas that don't offer any new gameplay features.There are massive genre-defining staples missing such as proper NPC relationships (not talking about dating, there's not even a proper system for friendship), crafting systems, unique resource collecting, resource sustainability, and even fleshed-out farm customisation.The world feels really small because of all the invisible walls and odd geometry and the movement can be slippery at best and clunky at worst. The gameplay loop also feels immediately predictable. The only thing keeping me playing is the dinos, but ironically I hope that's the last thing they update (we already have a lot and they are adorable).Buyers beware unless you want to explicitly support the devs because there really isn't very much here... yet. I hope the dev team keeps it up since there is great potential here!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is really good, really cute and over all a great experience. Is it worth the 30 Euro pricetag? No. 20, maybe. I can say I've been quite addicted to this for a bit. I like the exploration, although it's easy to get lost and I wish the game had a minimap.The game has a good chunk of quests, so you won't be lacking in things to do, although some of the quest descriptions tend to be a bit lacking. For example, you need to fix an entrance to another area at one point, and you need to collect planks and rope. The quest does not tell you exactly how much of each you need or the extra wood and stone needed. So you collect what you think is enough only to return and not have enough at all. Same with the cooking quest. The quest log doesn't really explain to you exactly what you need to do or where you need to go. The game concept is super unique, and a good change from the 'regular' farming games like Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley etc etc. Having dinosaurs help you water your crops? Heck yeah, give me that. I like that you need to pay attention to each dinosaur species specific needs for biomes, pen size and other dinosaurs in the pen with them. Great attention to detail.I do wish the dinosaurs had a bit more personality, though. They like different treats and such, but I feel like that's about it. Genders would be a good change and possibly breeding in the future? Would be super cool to breed for rarer colors!All in all, 8/10. I really enjoy the game, and even 10+ hours in, there's still quite a bit to do. Graphics: 7/10. Adorable style, though I wish the lighting was a bit better. Gameplay: 9/10. Super cool concept and executed well.Character customization: 4/10. Definitely needs more diversity and a few more types of clothes to pick from. Price tag: Wait for it to go on sale, or find a code on a website that sells it for less money. 30 Euro is a tad bit much for what you get.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I really did.  I will say, I'm 30 years old, love dinosaurs, love farming, love cute things -- so this should've been right up my alley!  The more I played, though, the flatter and emptier it started to feel.  There are things that I felt needed a little brief tutorial that I didn't get from the text dialogue.  I wish I was able to craft things on my own without the need of NPCs -- ESPECIALLY fences and gates!  It seems like this game wants you to balance the ranching and the farming aspects it has to offer, but it feels punishing if you have too many dinos over crops (why do they stand on their own poop and hide it!?), and painful if you have too many crops over dinos (that can help, whose watering patterns make sense?  How can I water 90% of a row 5 times back-to-back before having to stand on the unwatered patch AND STILL MISS IT?).  I don't know, maybe there's just something I'm missing to understand the balance and how to be lucrative.  I'm sure going into your third year of play, you'd be an expert on crops, fertilizer, rotations, etc., but it just feels off to have to rely on opening your book with every decision you want to make.  The dinos, I get it, but the crops?  The seed packets in your inventory should have a tooltip to tell you the soil type they prefer; it'd be a neat QoL improvement in my eyes.  Another thing is that I definitely don't understand how to make a dino you've "tamed" trust you so you can put a saddle on it.  If it got explained in one sentence, then that's terrible.  What affects this stat?  Do we just have to sit and wait?  Sitting what felt like 20 days with something I couldn't use was driving me absolutely insane -- it had an upgraded sleeping patch, it had a partner, it had tons of food, its biome was right... I pet its face every day and had it follow me back to Dapplewood, threw poppins in its face, shoved snacks down its throat, yet it resisted being trusting of me for so long that I had completely forgotten why I tamed it in the first place.  Or would it be charming them since we're using a flute like the pied piper?  The loading screen tip that says advanced information can be found in the help section of the menu is... half-true.  There is info there, but it doesn't really help much.I have a relatively new PC, or at least one I feel should be able to run the game on Ultra settings without too many issues.  However, there were many times I'd be running through Dapplewood and my frames would start dropping.  It only seemed to happen at night and/or if it was raining.  I never got into the desert area to see if it had any optimization issues, as I started getting bogged down and bored, especially with the having to rely on traveling NPCs to craft items for you.I don't necessarily like the player customization options; I wish there were a few voice/pitch settings and a few more hair styles.  I feel like my character didn't have the same style as the dinos, which isn't a terrible thing, but definitely something you notice as time goes on (or at least I did).TL;DR: I really like the aesthetic of the game for the most part, but there are too many mechanical/technical things that hold Paleo Pines back from being a great dino farming+ranching game.  It feels like the game is trying to appeal to younger gamers (like actual kids) and older gamers (nerds like me who really fell in love with Stardew Valley, for instance) alike, and in wanting to attract both of those demographics it falls short in a lot of areas.  I believe there's a demo -- if you really want to try the game, play through two and a half in-game months there first, then you might have the ability to get through the parts that lost me.

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw a buyable DLC with an event, and a few days ago an official statement on Instagram about their financial problems, stating a "Paleo Pines 2"(loud sigh), telling people to go buy their merchandise and plushies.... Yeah, I knew this was gonna happen.I never wrote a review so this won't be perfect, but let's go.After following it's development for some time I knew this will be something for me to just relax and have fun. I got this game last year and was not wrong, it was a blast... Until. But first here are my pros:1 - Great style design, the dinosaurs are so cute and yet remain pretty scientifically accurate, which is very important to me. Their sounds, animations, really bring lots of character into them and I grew a great bond with my Baryonyxes.2 - Soundtrack is amazing, I love the OST on rainy days. It does sometimes gets repetitive, that's the only thing that could be changed.3 - Exploring is very nice, I personally like getting lost in the forest, makes me feel like I'm wandering around with my dino rather than constantly looking at coordinates on the map.4 - Gameplay, foraging, farming, taming dinos is fun, I like that dinos have their own abilities for each thing, but it's very clunky, so see you soon in cons.Cons:1 - Gameplay, foraging, farming, taming dinos. All of these things could've been done 100 times better. Targeting in this game is terrible, whenever I wanted to make a field with my Styraco, I'd need to turn 180 degrees and try again because game would not focus where I wanted it to focus. To forage anything you need to get off your dinosaur, making it tedious rather than fun, a dinosaur with new "Forager" ability would fix this. Focusing dino to tame is as well at times just not working, the flute just doesn't catch the animal. 2 - NPCs are so bland it's unbelievable, all of them are nice to you, give you things to begin your gameplay, you don't feel any connection to them, you don't make FRIENDS with them. Furthermore, they're so annoying with the long tiring conversations, at some point I just skipped thru everything because the game just didn't keep me engaged (eg. shorter talking, more animations, scene views changing etc). Not even to mention that some NPC are just gone from the plaza for DAYS leaving you with an unfinished quest.3 - The story. My main issue here is that I felt no connection or importance of the story whatsoever. The game throws Lucky at us, says "this is your favourite and most loved dino" and we don't even get to choose her name, colour, or even species. We're on a quest to find Parasaurolophuses because they're so important to us and Lucky, but I stopped caring about it... Almost immediately. I believe they made it like that just to pour their player's money into making plushies and merch rather than develop the actual game.4 - Before I forget, the cooking pot. To cook anything you have to get out into the wilderness and cook there, instead of being able to BUY a cooking pot for your ranch. There's no reason why we shouldn't be able to buy a pot.5 - Inventory is way too small. Imagine running out all the way to another region, you gather things along the way, filling up your slots, and you run into 5 other things you need. So what, you gotta go back to your ranch, put everything away, and then run for the things again. Solution? A single storage chest in every region so we don't have to run around like headless chickens because we got no space or forgot a single carrot.6 - Game about collecting dinos... Has a limit to collecting dinos. I love Baryonyxes, and I want every single one of them, but I can't because theres not enough space, not enough dream stones, 7 - Spawn rate of dino colors is terrible, I'd get a rusty/shamrock Bary like 20 times, but never a different skin, the same goes to other dinos. Solution? Breeding system.8 - The biggest one... Lack. Of. Multiplayer. The way I would have 300 hours of gameplay with my partner if this game had multiplayer, imagine all the couples buying this game to play it together? The devs or publisher just shut it down to cut on budget and time, just like they did with many things such as polishing the game, making free updates (we got ONE new dino in 1 year span, I am dying lol), not adding more useful abilities to dinos, developing more in depth NPC relationships (where is my romance option?), not adding MORE NPCs, making the tutorial and unlocking small dino helpers/ariacotta canyon (I still don't know how to unlock these two and I'm 50hrs into the game lol), 9 - Paywall event in a DLC with little to no content, and in today's times, a paywalled DLC with new gameplay is just a slap in the face to the community, especially when we got NO free updates the whole year. Just a single crocodile.10 - Some animations. Why isn't there a mount/dismount animation? Or why is my runner dinosaur sprinting in a 300% sped up animation rather than just running like a normal animal would? There could be much more animations during cutscenes, but there's not, welp.11 - If "Paleo Pines 2" is happening the Dev's attention will shift to that game, leaving Paleo Pines dead for good. No more free updates, no more ANY updates, just slightly 1 year after release, that is WAY too soon. The developers should be focused on base product, on fixing it, polishing, adding new content that players paid for, to further extend it with new attractive features like multiplayer, so that new people will be interested in it. They should not run to a new game and ask for more money, not only is it greedy and disrespectful to their community, but also because this exact same situation will repeat. Game development is not easy, and people working in that genre should know very well how to use their resources, if they won't, they'll end up making posts on reddit, instagram, steam and everywhere asking for "financial support". The merch and plushies made tons of money, over thousands being sold, an800% and 500% of them being funded, each plush costing 30$. They have no idea how to leverage their resources.I'd like to reccomend you their post here on Steam "Paleo Pines Needs Your Help", there's lots of comments making good points on why making a new game is wrong and that they should focus on THIS game.I would love to support this game, but there is no guarantee that If I support it all these issues won't repeat, and right now it seems like there's a big chance for repeatance. Both the developers and publishers of Paleo Pines chose the wrong steps, instead of focusing on their game.Shame we won't get new updates from marketable plushies.

_childDocuments_.review: [Note: I do not hate this game, if I did I wouldn't have so many hours on it, I'm just frustrated with the current state of it.]I originally had a positive review for this game, but after heavily thinking it over, I don't think I can recommend it anymore, even though I do enjoy it when I play sometimes. I'll start with the biggest complaint lately:*Most news updates are them spamming their merchandise or begging for reviews. The last time they did an actual patch was several months ago, and the last time they added actual content, they only added one dinosaur. Which leads me to:*Due to the extremely limited skill set the game revolves around, the dino kinda blends together with the rest of the colorful mush. The game essentially boils down to choosing what flavor of logging/rock breaker/bush slasher you want.*I used to tell myself I like what I'm doing, but lately I've been swearing twenty different curses in my head every time a quest NPC pisses me off. NPCs have EXTREMELY unpredictable schedules. Oh I'm not talking about their daily schedule, that makes sense, I'm talking about the times Avery, Pippin or Orani decide to f*ck off for the day you just so happen to want to talk to them. See any quests for Avery you want to take to make him friendlier? Better check the journal to make sure he's actually here that day so you don't have two quests blocking the journal for the next week. My latest complaint goes to Owynn. This bastard is hoarding one last fruit tree seed, the banana tree, from me, and I couldn't figure out if I was even doing the requirements to get it from him. Turns out I am, but he only gives the banana seed  . No wonder he won't fork over his precious banana seed. Speaking of which:*Why are fruit trees treated like a rare commodity in this game? For most of them, there's only a single seed in the ENTIRE game, with a few exceptions, and some of them do not appear in the wild such as the aforementioned banana, so you have to get these stingy, annoying mfs to like you enough to hand over their piece of the fruit tree Triforce to even log it in the journal.*Limited dreamstones aka dinosaurs. Now I don't really have a problem with this, as the game gives you an option to convert small dreamstones to large dreamstones and vice versa (and trust me you will do this at least once because the game is about 70-30 with the ratio of small to large dreamstones it gives you), but it made a lot of people upset. This is also a hard limit, as I recall hearing some who tried to glitch or hack more dreamstones in had the game completely sh*t itself, so don't try it. They say the reasoning is to prevent lag, but personally I'd rather have the option to totally lag out my game than be limited, the lag is part of the endgame experience y'know? Although the farm is so damn tiny you wouldn't really be able to fit more dreamstones anyway. Trust me once you establish more pens, the farm is not as big as it looks.*The map is entirely useless. All it shows you is where you and NPCs are. No dinosaur locations, no artifact locations, not even quest markers. The maps are also just a painting of the area rather than a Skyrim-esq sky camera, which would be fine, if it wasn't for your map icon being a red circle and directional arrow. The circle does nothing to tell you where you actually are, it doesn't contrast with the map well and is hard to see, and the pretty map painting that's not all that accurate doesn't help. On this subject:*The game tells you absolutely nothing useful, most of what I've learned is from experimenting or other players. Did you know you can tell where an NPC is if a line in their 'locations' list is in bold text? Did you know the Helper meter for dinosaurs isn't actually a level up meter and is just displaying how much Helper 'EXP' you've gotten that day? Did you know you can raise dino friendship faster by taking them for a walk in their wild habitat or playing their friend call to them? Why does my dinosaur still not love me, I tamed them in Triassea and now it's late Cretumnus, how many times do I have to pet you? *Some designs are just straight up hideous, the humans being the most apparent. I thought I could look past it, but everyone else is mentioning it so I don't feel as alone for thinking they're creepy and unappealing. Another design I really don't like is the Triceratops. It looks like a bath toy. I was interested in replacing my Styracosaurus with one, then I actually saw it and noped out of there.*Glitches. I haven't had any CTDs or major problems with quests, but I have experienced several audio bugs. Mainly, sometimes the game randomly decides the entire map is Ariacotta Canyon and only plays that music no matter where I am, including during rain. At one point the Megalosaurus had a de-synced animation where the player would just stop animating after the first loop and float there while the Megalosaurus moved (they did actually fix this one). It's easy to get stuck on obstacles with bigger dinosaurs/while sprinting due to bad turning rates, and if a dinosaur happens to spawn a little too close to the invisible boundaries, they will be completely deaf and won't listen to the flute. I found a solution for this is to scare them out into the open.*Passive aggressive developers. There were two things we were requesting, namely the ability to change the speed of the day cycle and for the shop NPCs in the later part of the game to come out earlier or be more consistent in their schedules. For the time changing, they did implement this which was nice, but they originally named the slowest speed 'Lazy'. I find it silly to get offended by a game mechanic's name, but it did feel kind of rude since the original day speed was rather cramped for getting things done and we just asked for speed options. They've since changed it to 'Casual'. As for the NPCs, I forget how they worded it when they changed them to always be awake as soon as the day starts, but it was something to the effect of 'Now the NPCs have no lives so they can sell stuff to you early birds' (not as rude as this but essentially what they said). Thanks.The game is very cute and relaxing, a very unique concept, but it has several problems that have not been addressed or just barely addressed, and their constant nudging for us to buy merch when they haven't updated the game in several months is rich. They literally ran a campaign for their Makeship plushie twice. One wasn't enough money ig. At the end of the day, this is one of those few games where I  . My farm is ugly, there's things I wish I did better, but the absolute tedium of unlocking poppin flavors, unlocking areas, doing very slow quests and having everything being order-only purchases  I just never want to go through that again. They added an option to skip the prologue and get some free stuff, but it's not much. A farming game that isn't replayable feels like a hate crime-(Also in the Steam Points page, their profile backgrounds are nearly identical to Stardew Valley's point items. Really beating the 'Stardew Valley clone' reputation there)
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really nice, and I'm always a fan of cozy games, but Paleo Pines can't really hit that farming game niche for me!Its a very beautiful game, but at this point, its extremely bare bones, and more of a "dino pattern collector" than a farming sim. There's very little that motivates me to play in the game. I got all the dinos i like. My farm is pretty neat, and tidy, and im guaranteed to get all of my daily quests done. I'm just waiting for the season to pass! On top of that, the game over-explains certain functions, while others are left to be understood by the player through guides. It was overwhelmingly hard to understand how to tame other dinos, and the "treat taste preferences". After a while, the slog of having to re-discover the pattern of dinosaur i wanted, just to scare it off, and THEN use up all of my treats to unlock the next treat quest was just miserable I have great hopes for this game, and maybe I'll amend my review in the future, but at thus point, i'll be finishing my cosplay and shelving the game for the future

_childDocuments_.review: A severely-needed change in the bloodthirsty monster depictions seen from most prehistoric genre games. It may be lacking in content, but the devs have been continually adding new things from community feedback and fixing bugs as they show up. The excitement of exploring new areas, decorating your farm, and discovering adorable archosaurs in a rainbow of colors makes up for the game's downfalls. _childDocuments_.review: If you're like me and you don't usually play farming simulators because you think they're boring repetitive; Paleo Pines is a farming simulator with a very unique twist, you farm with dinosaurs and they all have their own unique abilities. This game is relaxing, The farming is very satisfying, the characters/dialogue is well written, the story isn't too deep, there isn't too much dialogue and the art style is so cute! The end of the game is also very satisfying and leaves the player wanting more.However, there are a few things that make this game a farming simulator and not a cozy game: - inability to craft anything, even basic things like fences and gates for Dinosaur pens.- Not being able to order Dino food from Corlan, having to run back/forth between the Pebble Plaza and the ranch, just to buy food is tedious and a waste of in-game time.- Fetch quests (find this hat, find this trinket, going back and forth between different characters multiple times for one side quests).There are bugs here and there, but the developers are doing a very good job at fixing them, communicating and are open to suggestions.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not want to be exceedingly harsh on this game, but I feel I must be brutally and unfailingly honest so that potential players/buyers know what they are getting into and signal the developers behind the game that there are problems that need major fixes. As I do on a lot of these reviews I will break my points down into a positives section and a negatives section. With that, here are my thoughts on the game after 80+ hours of playtime.Positives1. The game is exceptionally technically polished for the most part. Loading times are reasonable and often tolerably short. Also, being able to change how far you can see off into the distance is a good call, something more games should implement by default and often forget to do.2. The art style of the characters, animals, and environments, while somewhat cartoony and childish-looking, is pleasing to the eye. The world, regardless of the time of year is beautiful, vibrant, and colorful. I just wish there was more to explore than just three zones (grasslands, forest, and desert).3. The dinosaurs and other prehistoric life feel alive and unique from species to species. Apparently, there was a paleontological consultant brought on for the designs of the animals to make them as accurate to current science in terms of appearance and design as possible, which is a plus. Despite the cartoony art style, I can confirm that each animal does feel authentic in this regard. Feathers are also properly given to dinosaurs where they should be (pretty much all theropods that should be feathered are, Psittacosaurus has its characteristic quill sail along its back and tail, etc.). Overall, the animals are fantastically modeled and designed.4. The named characters within the world all have their own personalities. Also, through completing quests related to the named characters, you can build your relationship with them which has differing effects (shop discounts, additional overnight sleep points, item rewards, etc.).5. Different creatures have different abilities that help with farming, ranch maintenance, and navigating obstacles in the environment.Negatives1. The day and night cycle is way too short. A single day goes by in like less than half an hour. This means that you only have so much time to accomplish all the tasks you want to do for a day before the game literally forces you to go to bed. I think the day-night cycle needs to be greatly extended because as it is, it makes it extremely frustrating to have to pick and choose tasks (some of which like tending to your creatures by restocking their food, cleaning poop, watering crops, harvesting crops if they are mature, weeding crops, clearing respawning debris, and other such things have to be done on a daily basis which eats up valuable time). Yes, I get this is a farming simulator, but you should be able to accomplish all the tasks you want or have to do in the same single day-night cycle. Even if the day-night cycle of each day was like an hour or two, that would be a vast improvement.2. Shop owner characters can often not mind their stores randomly when you really need them to be there because you need to buy something or complete a quest objective. This becomes especially egregious when you open the paths to the forest and desert areas up as such NPCs will often vanish without a trace for a day or more, so you can't buy things you need from them or complete quests related to them until they show up again.3. The quest system in this game is very rudimentary and weak. Most quests in the game are simple fetch or delivery quests, which when they bombard you with 10+ at any given time, can get extremely repetitive, boring, and mindless very quickly. You also have no good way of distinguishing main quests from simple fetch or delivery quests as all quests are in the same tab in your journal. This can make it hard to concentrate on specific objectives. Some quests also require you to obtain specific items or other conditions that you might need to wait multiple days, weeks, or sometimes months on to be able to complete, which is infuriating. Tutorials too at times can be extremely vague and confusing.4. There are some bugs in the game that need immediate attention. Firstly, when completing objectives where different named NPCs come to your ranch in a sort of cutscene, this can randomly cause all your creatures to scatter and wander about your ranch outside their pens. To correct this problem, you either need to herd all your creatures back to their proper enclosures with you flute or else go to bed to advance to the next day. Second, I think the Music of the Night subquest related to the main quest to find more Parasaurolophus other than Lucky can cause a game-breaking bug where you cannot complete that subquest and advance the game. I was in the desert one night taming some creatures to bring back, we didn't get back to the ranch in time, so the game forced me to bed, going to the next day. It then triggered the interactive sequence where you are supposed to play music near the tablet at the entrance to the desert canyon to attract more Parasaurolophus, only it did so at the ranch. My game then went to a completely black screen where I could still hear music, but couldn't do anything. I forced closed the game using the Steam overlay and then restarted the game, which seemed to fix the problem. However, I have come to realize that quest may now be completely bugged out because every time I have gone to the entrance to the desert at night to play the flute, nothing happens. Suffice to say, I really do not want to have to restart my second playthrough because of this bug and I am afraid my game's progression is now completely broken because of that issue.5. There were approximately 11 species cut from the game's launch (Amargasaurus, Apatosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Dimorphodon, Diplodocus, Pteranodon, Pterodactylus, Quetzalcoatlus, Sarcosuchus, Spinosaurus, and Tupandactylus) which explains the lack of sauropod dinosaurs and pterosaurs. The developers have apparently expressed the desire to add these species back in later, so hopefully that does happen.6. As others have stated, there are several things that point to missing features. There are resources like wood, stone, and fiber, but no real crafting mechanics. There is no fishing. There is no aquatic traversal. There are no additional areas to explore outside the three already mentioned.7. The Dreamstone system is, I'll be blunt and unashamed to say, infuriating and senseless in its design. There is only a certain amount of them (45 in total) period. I'm not even sure at this point if you can even tame one of every creature in the game (there's 38 unique species in total). Some have claimed that it's due to engine limits or because the devs wanted each creature befriended to feel unique. To that I call their bluff. Players should be allowed the freedom to tame as many creatures as they want, they should not have to sweat if there are enough dreamstones to accomodate all the unique species, and if this game had been designed properly, it would be able to handle such things.Overall, while there are aspects of the game that are fun, there are things that feel unfinished, the quest system is extremely weak, there are game-breaking bugs present, the hard cap on how many creatures you can befriend is utter lunacy, and the day-night cycle is so short and the tasks so repetitive that it feels pointless at times. This honestly feels like a big-budget mobile game at times. I do think the game has some fun elements, but for right now, my review remains neutral, leaning slightly more towards the negative until some of the major bugs, glitches, and other problems are fully addressed to my satisfaction. To potential buyers, I would wait until some of these things are fixed. To those who have already bought the game, we need to continue to make the devs aware of these problems in our reviews so they can be fixed.

The character model itself is kind of janky as well with the run animation. You can’t craft at your “farm” and the vendors only have a limited number of currency. _childDocuments_.review: Yes, I recommend, but it's not a recommend for all.I have been a fan of dinosaurs for 40+ years.  I am a HUGE fan of farming sims.  This looked to be the perfect game for me and parts of it are.  The dinosaurs are great.  Their different looks, colors, and calls.  I enjoy the different things they can do on the ranch and it's kinda of interesting how we befriend them.However, as much as I adore the dinos and the first time I played the demo I was so happy I cried, this could use a lot of help in the game department.Not enough tutorials or ways to check passed info.  I get so confused on so many things.  What little is in the 'help' section doesn't do much after your first week or two.  I've had to either go to the Discord or Google for help with what feels like basic things.  I don't like that sometimes info is told to you, once and then you can't review it ever again.  I've got severe memory issues so I do sometimes forget what I was just told.  Even if I didn't, it'd be nice to have a place to get an idea how to do things again.  Like cooking, I still feel sort of lost on when to pull the food off the fire.  Nice to know I've mastered 'glop'.The quests get very, very boring.  I hate walking in circles looking for the small 'interact' icon when someone has AGAIN lost their hat.  No joke, had a series of quests today where 2 different people lost 3 items.  Owen, who never wears a hat, lost his hat two places.  We have dinosaurs that specifically help us find things, but they can't help with this, why?  My mornings are spent running back and forth between Pebble Plaza and my Ranch to get the items someone is requesting.  And I can't just bring things I'm hoping to need because the inventory is so small.  At one point I was getting a more interesting quest where I needed to observe a dinosaur but that seems to have vanished again.On top of that, you can easily get quests you cannot complete (giving something to an NPC you've not met you or realizing you can't get a an ingredient in the current season) and as far as I can tell, you cannot abandon any quests so they just sit there in your book.I know the quests are optional but they're they are the best way to make money (shells) especially if you're not spending your entire day farming.  Couldn't get a berry bush to grow because was missing fertilizer, took me a bit to figure that out and figure what it wanted.  Didn't know the dino assigned to planting (once I unlocked that through a quest two in game months in) wouldn't plant if there was no fertilizer.  Can be a little overwhelming with 3 different fertilizers.I never know if I'm doing enough to keep my dinosaurs happy.  Several I've still not found their favorite foods.  I'm not saying I want to be allowed to ignore them, since that's the point of the game, but half my day is quests, trying to figure out farming and the dinos before I even get a chance to explore.So many of the areas that are blocked off are blocked by more than one type of material.  So when my smasher is leveled I break stuff and then I need to find a slasher.I'm starting to really not like the music.  It doesn't feel varied enough and, for me, just kind of sticks out while I'm running around.I'm guessing the player character has so little stamina so you can rely on your dinosaurs but with all the time off my dinosaurs looking for hats, the energy amount feels extra small.I will be taking a long break from this game, something that makes me bummed but I'm so frustrated and bored it can't be helped.So yes, I recommend this game, I ADORE this game, but it feels very unfinished and if you're not ready for what it's asking of you, you won't have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 50+ probably closer to 100+ hrs in the demo on this, if I didn't have other life things to do I'd spend all my time playing the heck out of this game. Indie devs yes, does it show all the effort and love they put into it? yes. It's a great chill relaxing game, quests are mostly optional (board) story seems short sweet simple. Most hours are basically me running around looking for ultra rares and stockpiling on items that I remember to get from the map XD my anky/para/styr/wue are all 15+ levels and are the mvps of clearing the map. I was so bummed during the demo I couldn't find any ultra rares (outside of psitt aka taco) but day 2 of loading my demo save I got a melanistic arch which made me so happy then got a portals scel the next day. Lots of hours are going towards repairing stuff and making sure all the villagers are happy in my run XD If you encounter a audio bug via the dinos (like styrc tiling) just redo the action that is continuing after using it, to make it stop the sound from playing outside the action. If you get stuck in terrain best to just reload the save when entering the area do not think there is an unstuck option. Great game, might frustrate some kids with the songs at first when learning the song of the dino (the wood dinos in particular) but there's sights that say their favorite food and the song each dino uses and the colors that are rare.Highly reccomend joining paleo pines discord and checking the pins the community is very helpful ^_^ edit: happy with the new controller input prompt on the flute

_childDocuments_.review: I ADORE this game. I love farming sims and Dinos and this is the perfect combination of both. They've done a really great job of giving a variety of content without making the game feel weighed down to play. With all the different areas to unlock and explore as well as rare colors for dinos to find, it's just the thing to kick off my fall gaming. I greatly enjoyed testing this game and I look forward to playing the full release and finding everything they added to it.  I know there were some small hiccups in the release plans, but that doesn't bother me any. I would've paid full price for this game, (and I intend to buy it again on the Switch for my kids anyways), as this is so obviously a labor of love that I will be enjoying for quite a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played 310 hours on the game, so I hold a bit more weight than most who would play for two days and write a poor review. There may be some with more hours as well... but at least I played it, actually played it.The game is designed for kids who love farming and dinosaurs, its not one most adults would look into, Take that into account first, its a relaxing game with simplicity built into it. Adults are going to get bored of it as there is no blood, action, violence or penalty, but its not made for those seeking an Ark fix or anything similar to Jurassic World Evolution. If you are not looking for a very simple, easy game, do not get it. That easy.The game is slowThe music is relaxingThe  dinos are colorful and varied. Quests are really simple (Fetch and observe)There are no penalties (You can be out all night and nothing happens, there is no death or starvation or harm)Easy memory game for taming dinosCute graphics. Small map.Limited taming.The game is not for if these bother you, go play another dino game. Theres plenty of dino and farming games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of different dinosaur games but honestly this one is one of my favorites. So far...The game is relaxing after a long stressful day I can unwind and enjoy cute chibi dinos that sing and interact with you. The game is easy to follow and provides you with all the information you need to advance successfully if you actually pay attention, I have been playing since its release and still have things I can do! _childDocuments_.review: The game is really super cute. The idea to combine a farming game with dinosaurs seems random at first, but what can I say? Dinosaurs are cool, and the dinos in the game are animated and modeled really well and cute. The game is fun, you have a lot of options to create the pens of the dinosaurs, tons to explore and to discover. My little one of 4 years loves dinosaurs and obviously loves this game. If you look for an inoffensive game to play with small and very small kids, this is ideal. There is effectively nothing that is "bad" in here, the worst thing that can happen is that you forget to feed the dinosaurs one day. Everyone is happy and friendly and even rainy days are kinda sunny.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game a lot, but I don't think I can recommend it in its current state. It's just missing personality.Don't get me wrong, the dinosaurs are really cute and it has some really interesting concepts like crops changing the soil texture or being able to have your own day where villagers bring YOU gifts. But I just think the cons are too numerous for me to recommend this game at full price. I read a lot of the reviews on launch and decided to buy a key, and I'm very glad that I did.None of the NPCs are fun to talk to. Literally none of the dialogue was worth reading imo and I ended up skipping the majority of it later on. The villagers' personalities are pretty bland, even with their different catchphrases or whatever you want to call them. They're just one-dimensional with nothing else to them. You have the nerd, the cowgirl, the theater kid, the geezer, etc. and none of them are anything other than their surface personality trait.It's also not really rewarding to befriend them. On top of them not being likable enough to talk to them every day, there's just nothing to incentivize you to get close to them. You don't get new dialogue, you don't learn anything new about them or have a cool event trigger, you just gain a discount on their store (if they own one) and the ability to sleep at their house (if they have one). My mistake, your incentive for befriending the NPCs are your 8 or so hidden achievements.There's no crafting. You just buy everything. There's nothing interesting happening with money or resources; you either find it on the ground or farm enough crops to buy it from the store. You'd think that with all the wood and stone you find, you'd at least be able to craft fences and maybe buy recipes from the NPCs or something.The quests really suck. I mean, REALLY. You either have the same 5 quests on the community board, or you get a story quest that you just can't complete because you're waiting for another event to trigger. I'm currently stuck on Mari and Owynn's (yes, Owynn with a Y and two Ns) pie quests because I apparently need to wait for an event in year two to gain the ability to make pies. In the time I've been waiting for that to happen, I beat the main storyline. It was kind of disappointing that I basically beat the game in year 1.Trying to do community board quests also really sucks because some of these NPCs just disappear. They're not in a location that isn't the plaza, they're just unreachable. Avery is the worst offender because he disappears to "far off lands" for days on end. Orani is the second worst because most players didn't even know she existed for the first season or so. She doesn't seem to have set days where she visits the plaza, she's just there sometimes. At least she's always reachable once you unlock the third area. Orani is not, in fact, always reachable in the Archeopelago. Sometimes she's just gone. She's probably  but I haven't gotten there yetOne of my biggest gripes with this game is that the character customization is AWFUL. I mean seriously, I don't have a very unique or uncommon hairstyle, but none of them were even close. Imagine all the hairstyles that people complain aren't available in games. That's the hairstyle selection for this one, but without any of the normal ones. You can't change your face shape or body type, so your character just always looks like an androgynous child. You also can't have facial hair which.. Is just really odd. Like did they not expect their player base to have beards? In cases like this, I usually just make a random character rather than trying to make myself. But that led me to another speed bump: the clothes. Even after looking at the catalog of clothes from Orani, it's almost all cottage core crap. There's nothing casual or even really gender expressive outside of a dress. The clothing styles are all the same (sweaters, overalls, and corduroys in browns, maybe greens, but mostly warm tones) unless I wanna wear something that's just.. Not from my culture. I'm not asking for a full punk rock outfit but like, can I just wear some jeans or a black t shirt?Finally, there aren't any consequences in this game. You know how in Stardew Valley, you get penalized for passing out or expending all your energy? That doesn't happen. Deplete all your energy, stay up past midnight, deplete your dino's energy, it doesn't matter. Wrong biome and number of dinos in a pen? That's okay, they just won't become helpers. Unhappy helper dinos? That's okay, you can make them your helper again. Release a dino and regret it? No worries, just call Mari to go get them for you. I get that it's a cozy sim, but this is just baby mode. I already paid for it, so I guess I'll squeak out the last of the achievements

_childDocuments_.review: I am sooo frustrated by this game!I love creature collectors and the prospect of rare/shiny hunting, so thought I would give this a go. I felt like it was really slow to begin with, with not much direction as to what to do or how to do it, but interesting enough to keep me going. One of the first things you have to do is build your friendship with a particular dino to progress the main story, and I was heaping friendship on this stupid dino for in game weeks before it was friendly enough to do it's job, only for it to take a poop in it's pen and drop out of being my friend the next day because it didn't like living with the poop (lol).When I finally unlocked the next area, that I had worked weeks for, it was... small and underwhelming. _childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: It's true, this game isn't full of quests and epic adventures. There are no intricate skill trees, no time limited events or exclusives. And that's what I love most about it. If I want a fast paced, grinding game, I can take my pick from hundreds. But a nice, calm game where the stakes aren't the fate of all things and where you can absolutely screw up without it ending in devastation? Yeah, not so many. I originally purchased this game to check on how child friendly it was, and it is that - provided the child can read fairly well - but what I found kept me playing was just how low stakes it is. Some may call it boring, I personally find it soothing. Sometimes you just want a non idle game where you can take your time & enjoy wandering the map and making discoveries. If you want a game that's relaxing, while still managing to be rewarding and is easy going, with a charming soundtrack and adorable characters, you should give this one a go.
