_childDocuments_.review: 🟩 Pros:+ Lucky (your first dino) is cute as heck+ The maps are decently sized, with three settings to explore+ Dinos roam these maps, they’re based on their real world counterparts, and come in a variety of colours (where my Triceratops gang at?)+ The gameplay loop is in line with other farming sims, so if you’re a fan of the genre, you should have a good time+ You can save your game WITHOUT having to go to sleep and end your day🟥 Cons:- Character animations are poor- The characters in town (outside of the main characters) serve no purpose other than making the town feel alive- Crating is a chore - Why can’t I do this from my inventory? Why do I need to visit an NPC in town?- Romancing characters isn’t an option, and while it’s not a big deal for me, I know that this plays a large role for some- Exploring is exciting at first, but quickly becomes dull as many areas are empty voids- Exploring without a minimap adds to the frustration- No mail system to send and receive items, doing everything by foot (or by dino) is tedious🏷️ Suggestions:~ Look at my list of cons and improve on these aspects, because at present, it feels like a budget version of many farming sims which have come before it
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is a fun and engaging game as a fan of both farming games and prehistoric animals. My only gripe, and it is pedantic, is that some of the scientific information isn't 100% correct, but that doesn't make or break this game. Paleo Pines is carried by a nice atmosphere, charming music, and a soft, cute art style. It's easy to spend a few peaceful hours in this game just taking care of your dino friends, finding new ones, and farming crops. Definitely recommend this game for dinosaur fans that want a break from the more grungy and survival or action-focused games like the Isle, ARK, Saurian, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: If you are coming into Paleo Pines, expecting "Harvest Moon with dinosaurs" you'll likely be disappointed.This is because Paleo Pines goes by its own formula really. Nothing quite works like it does in Harvest Moon and in my opinion, that's actually a good thing!Instead of upgrading tools to better you farm, all of it is dependant on your dinosaurs and your friendship towards them. I like this choice. Dinosaurs here can't be hoarded (even though I really want them all, they are incredibly adorable!), but have to be cared for so they decide if they want to help you are not.This never gets tedious but still brings in the choice who to befriend, because your space is limited as is your time. Again, this isn't a bad thing, because I like the idea that you have to choose specifically who to keep around, instead of dinosaurs becoming merely collectables.Even if you end up sending someone back into the wild though, fear not! You can always find them again. A great mechanic that makes it less painful to let a new dino friend go if the farm becomes to cluttered!Not to mention, the dinosaurs themselves also feel very alive and seem to do as they please on your farm, when they aren't helping you out. I absolutely love that!As for things not related to dinosaurs, It has a rather satisfying gameplay loop that feels organic. You integrate into a little community of Paleo Pines and despite most quests being small ones from the towns questboard, over time the characters will grow to like you when you help out, unlocking other, bigger events in turn.It makes the game relaxed, you can take your time to get a feel for everrything and there hasn't been a single point where I felt rushed to do things really.The town itself houses a handful of NPCs but I think that every one has its place and the small number helps the game not feel overwhelming. Each of them is unique and very fun to interact with!Day length is actually something I usually fear in "timed" games, but it oddly works out perfectly in Paleo Pines. I can do quests, scout the land for new dino friends or harvestables, work on my farm and interact with my dinosaurs, all without any sort of stress. Tl;dr: If you like laid back, relaxing and cute games and dinosaurs and farming, I can just highly recommend Paleo Pines. Go make some cute dino friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: After 90+ hours in this game, I have some thoughts.I had a lot of fun in this game, especially in the beginning when everything was new and fresh and I was just playing to farm and catch dinosaurs rather than play anything else, and I had a really good time. Once I set my sights on completing the game, that is where the fun ended and the woes begin.If you want to treat this game as a slice-of-life farming simulator, then this is the game for you. If you want to actually complete this game, you are in for some major frustration.The Good:• Good and fun game, neat mechanics• A must play for dinosaur lovers• Farming is generally fun• Catching mechanics for dinosaurs is fun• The dinosaurs are cute, props to the design team!• The ultra rare spawns are fair despite being sparse• The quests are cuteThe Bad:• The human designs are GOD AWFUL AND UGLY. At first I thought my character was supposed to be a child due to proportions, but then I met two other characters in the game who are clearly adults. One has full face stubble and the other has massive breasts. The latter is weird because everyone looks like toddlers so it looks like a toddler with massive bazingas. She even has a romance storyline quest. I did not need these toddler characters to have a romance in my dinosaur game. Strange decision by the devs.• 100%ing the game is tedious. FINISHING the game (all character quests) is tedious. Achievements are also locked behind 100%ing the game. REALLY tedious. I have one more questline left to not just complete the achievements, but the GAME. What started out as a good experience has quickly turned into: rush through this day, see if this NPC wants to talk. No? Okay repeat.• NPC quests are slow. Just like mentioned above, NPC quests are timegated with no clear indication of how long I need to wait before checking in with an NPC. This means the end of the game is just dragging out instead of finishing on a high note.• Resources don't respawn in a meaningful capacity, particularly wood. EVERYTHING in this game requires wood. Building, cooking, quest lines. I diligently went for every wood spawn I could throughout the game and I STILL was barely chugging at the end to have enough wood for every quest and cooking recipe. •NPCs teleport. I will find myself running toward on the map only for her to literally teleport in front of my face to the other side of the map and then I have to trek to go talk to her. This isn't a bug, the NPCs are designed to be in certain areas around certain parts of the day. However, some quests only trigger when that NPC is in a certain spot, so if they teleport, you are SOL and must try again tomorrow.• There is no schedule to tell you when a merchant NPC will be in the towns that day. It makes me have to run my ass and waste time to go see if they're even there and memorize what days they're not.Bugs I ran into:• When cleaning up dino poop, they will try to 'show' you where the poop is. However they will KEEP trying to show you meaning they bump you out of the spot as you're doing the animation and you have to readjust to clean the poop. Very annoying.• Dinosaurs do not always respond to your flute. You can't direct them to tasks or tame them without the flute. This is most egregious in Find Dinosaur from Mari, but I have experienced it with wild spawn dinosaurs as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very much enjoyed this game and overall recommend it if you enjoyed Stardew Valley, ARK (for the aspect of riding dinosaurs, this is a comfort game yall), and My Time at Portia. I do have to say, there is too much comparison to Stardew Valley in the reviews. This is its own game, don't treat it like another.I do 100% recommend playing the demo before playing the full thing to decide if you want it. There will be a Christmas sale on steam soon so I'd get the full game then. I paid the full $30. The reason I say try the demo is you may be like me and really enjoy the game despite there being a few negatives that would normally be a make or break for me with games. While I do love this game I do have some criticisms.Positives first: -Even on low graphics this game is still very visually pleasing. -Very low stress game and good to wind down with (even more so than Stardew)-Very cute and adorable models and they're all very well made. Even the human models with your character and Pippin aside (looking a little uncanny valley lol. Small eyes with big heads) look very adorable-Decent game mechanics (some can be worked on)-Go at your own pace you're not rushed even to do missions -You can go a day without paying attention to your crops and they'll be okay so theres no stressors there eitherNow for my criticisms. If you can get past this stuff like me, then this is a great game.-All non ridable dinos have only two abilities. I think it would be nice if some of them could harvest, till, and water passively. This however is a personal preference.-Unable to rebind keys. This is slightly annoying as someone who's slightly more lefthanded dominant, but I can deal with WASD-Again, personal preference, unable to scroll out to see more of your surroundings.-This game has the ONE mechanic I hate in Stardew Valley. You can only save at your house. Tbh, this is THE MOST annoying part of this game-No color adjustment settings for colorblindness.Now I have seen a lot of people talking about the motion blur and I get motion sick SUPER easily and have not experienced this. My settings are resolution scale to the max, maximum FPS is off, quality is low, and FOV is in the middle. Maybe this will help others.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, slow paced - a perfect cozy farm sim with adorable dinos!So far nothing in the game feels like a punishment if you don't do it optimally or at the right time, etc. which is a definite bonus in my book.The player character customization is bare bones and quite lacking for a game like this (no different body types in the year of our lord 2023??) but while that can be a deal breaker in many cases I'm not super bothered since honestly I'm here for THE DINOS.Which there are more available species than I expected, honestly - though I deeply feel the absence of a big sauropod of some sort. I mean, isn't that the quintessential fantasy riding dinosaur? Wild that one wasn't included with launch, they're so iconic!Otherwise, a very adorable dino-focused cozy farm sim. Definitely worth picking up if you like any of those things.

_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Soft and pretty dino game for farming and dino fans alike, plus the art and sounds the dinos make are cute! Though I wish the story of the game was more alluring and there was more you could do with your dinos, after completing the main quest it just felt empty and not much left to do but collect rare dinos and build your farm the way you like it. The characters in the story didn't pull me in or make me have any feelings for any of them. I never really interacted with them besides just doing chores for them or buying things I needed from some. The events you would have with them also was very lacking and boring as well, I never even really noticed some events happening until I just came across them randomly when I was gathering items or hunting dinos. If you love farming and collecting dinos it's a really nice and relaxing game with lots of collection variety but it's just lacking in interactions in terms to like stardew valley is with your neighbors/villagers you share the area with. The story being similar as it felt very simple and short, a bit tedious as well but that's just me. I'd still recommend it, especially for its simplicity, the art/environments, and a nice kids-like game to enjoy. I really hope to see more in the future with this game if possible too!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a very chill and fun experience. There is always something to do from tending to and selling your crops, cooking meals with your produce, and decorating your ranch. The only downside to the dinosaur aspect is that you are limited on how many dinosaurs you can keep in your ranch. On the very good side, the dinosaurs are very cute and nicely designed. I appreciate how the game used more modern portrayals of dinosaurs instead of imitating designs from popular dinosaur media such as Jurassic Park/World.There are many minor bugs in the game, but so far, I have not experienced anything game breaking. And the game has a very active Discord server where any concerns about the game are sure to be heard. I would definitely recommend to game for anyone who likes dinosaurs and wants a chill escapist farming game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a great and cozy game. It doesn't require much thought so it's nice to play when you just want a chill game with minimal effort. The world is colorful, and so are the dinos! Questing could be better though, especially when asked to walk a hat from one person in the plaza to another person that's only 50ft away... The system for befriending dinos is very cute a different, although the calls can come a little fast so I recommend an online guide that tells you the calls if you want to make it a little easier. There are also different rarities of dino colors for every species which is fun to try to find and collect your favorite one! I haven't finished the game yet, but the story seems very very simple. Which isn't a bad thing for a simple game like this. It focuses a lot less on farming though, and much more on dino collecting. So if that's what you want then this is a great game for you! I would say some of the controls though are a little wonky, so I find it slightly easier to play on PC with a controller. Controls, story, and questing could be improved a lot. The dinos, befriending mini game, and map are great! I really hope they add more dinos too. Overall score: 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill/relaxing game. It has farming/community building similar to Stardew Valley, there are a lot of dinosaurs to befriend, and the game has a pleasant art style. Unlike other monster catching games you befriend new dinosaurs by repeating their call on your flute and soothing/feeding them until you can befriend them with a Poppin. I am happy my favorite dinosaur made it to the game, but I'm a little surprised the Spinosaurus didn't make it in. It also would have been cool to befriend Pterodactyls and other flying dinosaurs and to be able to fly around to the other areas of the game very quickly. Would be great if there wasn't a loading screen between our farm and the main Plaza. Most of the NPCs I got to know also didn't seem all that interesting either.Overall I had my fun with the game and it's fun to watch the small dinosaurs automatically help your farm on their own once you unlock the small seed pot, but I kind of wish there was automation for other parts of the farm like watering, harvesting, and maybe even a lil dino that auto sells the crops you give it. Unlike many of the other dinosaur games I've played this is definitely one of the good ones and if you find it on sale I recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 7/10There may be some very minor spoilers in my review.I got this game after a friend talked about how much they loved it. As a fan of Stardew Valley, I'm enjoying it well enough! It's sometimes hard to feel fully invested, though, and there are some aspects of the game that seem unfinished. It feels, sometimes, like this game was put out before it was 100% ready. For example, there are (crafting?) tables and telescopes placed all over the valley, but you can't interact with them. I don't really know what they're for. Additionally, unless I just haven't figured it out yet, it doesn't seem that there's a way to split stacks of items in your chest or inventory. This makes it a little frustrating when you only need a few of an item, but end up taking a couple hundred instead.Aside from that, there are supposed to be 45 dream stones, according to the achievements, but it seems that to me (and the Paleo Pines community, too) that there are only 23 that are currently reachable. Maybe there are more that no one has discovered yet, but it does seem a little strange that half of the dreamstones are more or less un-findable. With over 35 available types of dinosaurs- all with a wide variety of color variants, and each one requiring its own dreamstone- only having access to less than half of these stones forces you to be picky about which dinosaurs you actually tame. Perhaps this is intentional, perhaps not. Just an observation. Aside from this, though, the color design in this game is beautiful. All of the areas are fun to look at, even if they're areas with limited color palettes. The artists did a fantastic job making everything bright, beautiful, and fun to look at. Additionally, the dinosaurs are very cute and the wide variety of colors makes "window shopping" for dinosaurs exciting, and adds an element of suspense when you're waiting for a rare variant to finally spawn. It's also fun that they've added some pride flag inspired color variants to some of the dinosaurs. Having the dinosaurs act as farming tools is a unique and creative way to separate this game from other farming sims, and it's a cute way to tie the farming aspect into the game a little more. I have found it to be a little difficult to remember that this is supposed to be a farming game, however. It's easy to get wrapped up in the excitement of discovering and taming new dinosaur friends without realizing they're supposed to help make your farm more efficient. This isn't necessarily a downside, but adding more to the farming could help bring this further into the "farming sim" category. To me, it feels more like an exploration game, at heart. This is exaggerated somewhat by the fact that crop seeds are very expensive, and it can be a little difficult to get enough money for everything that you need in order to progress. I usually find that by the time I've finished buying the materials I need for taming dinosaurs, building pens, or completing quests, I'm all out of money to buy seeds.There are times that I feel like I'm on the edge of boredom- only JUST captivated enough to want to keep playing, but feeling that I'm starting to lose interest. This tends to be the case with a lot of farming sims, in my experience, but adding new areas and more dinosaurs- as well as more easily discoverable dreamstones- could help remedy this. There are many points where you're forced to dismount your steed in order to write notes in your journal or collect items from the ground. This halts the flow of the game-play somewhat, and can be very tedious when there are many items that need to be noted or collected. Adding the ability to collect or take notes from the back of your dinosaur would help this a lot. Overall, while it's easy to get tied up in the minor complaints, this is a fun game with a cute, unique, and creative concept. Due to the dreamstone, telescope, and minor game-play issues, this does feel like a semi-unfinished game, but I'm hopeful that the devs will continue working to implement more over time. I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys exploration or farming sims, but if you're still on the fence about purchasing it, it couldn't hurt to wait a few months and see if any expansions come along. Might make it more worth your while.

Once you've played through the first year, you've basically played through them all. My main gripe with the game however is that the endgame is locked behind a convoluted scavenger hunt that had me running around the map for hours looking for that  piece i needed for a quest, before I eventually folded and found the map on the discord.Other issues include dinos getting stuck on objects they're interacting with, me losing dinos that were following me because they got distracted, performance issues that occurred the longer I played, and trying to figure out 'what the hell did this npc want again?'. The game needs  QoL updates, particularly one for the journal/quest menu, more explanations of the game's mechanics in the help menu, bug fixes, npc interactions, etc.Overall, I recommend if you like dinosaurs and you're sick of the movie monster treatment they usually get. _childDocuments_.review: Sadly this game's only achievement is cute dino visuals. Everything else is lacking in all aspects. - Characters are bland and sterile. Even an AI would write better text than that. It's as if they were straight up copied from child movies. Hell, to think of it, first city is literally My Little Pony characters.  - Quests are literally "get to this place and grab this" or "bring me X amount of this". Nothing else. - Dinos have similar skins. If you want something unique you are in trouble - stripes, blank, white stomach. There's barely any difference in them. - For some its not a problem but for some it is. There's a lot of LGBT stuff in the game up to the point of a non-binary kid and pride skins for some dinosaurs. It would be better to have at least a tag on the main page as a warning. - Locations are soft-locked with invisible walls so, while looking vast and free, you'll end up running in maze when you try to get off that 10 cm hill. - No jumps. Nor you nor your dinos can jump. For main character they get the weird "Yahoo" animation instead. (???)- Lack of actual tutorial. What is the harvester? What do small dinos do? Whats the point of leveling your dino? In many, many cases you would be forced to look online for different information regarding "what the hell is this". - Bugs. There are many, many, many bugs from visual (on ultra settings half of the dinos have white lines on their skin at the spots of texture connections) to game breaking where even the main quest line can't be progressed further. - Lack of actual gameplay. All you can do is tame/take care of dinos, farm crops and do a bunch of "get this" quests. No fishing, can't go inside your own house, can't interact with your dinosaurs any other way than "pet/sing/ride", no breeding, no baby dinos, forced "pack/herd/loner" dino types so you can't have an actual "wild-like" pen with a herd or a big pack (because a pack is only 2-3 dinos max).- Weird, weird, WEIRD construction mechanics where enclosures don't get recognized if they share the wall so you have to rebuild the gates, gates not seeing the right enclosure and instead making your farm an enclosure (???) and much more. Overall for a such huge price I completely don't recommend this product. It would be fine if it was an Early Access but even then I don't think it would get a high enough quality to be worthy that price. Yes, developing prices are rising but this game's style and amount of mechanics is way too low for a such increase.

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, but the actual game play is awful. If you want a life sim, there are waaaay better ones than this available.Pros: Dinosaurs are cute. That's it. That's the only pro.Cons: -No NPCs properly explain how anything works. Whoever did the copyright for the NPCs failed with this. They start to explain, then never mention it again. If you mis-clicked and didn't read it. Too bad, too sad. They're not going to re-explain.- There's no schedules for the NPCs, they just show up whenever they want. They have stalls. Put a board on the stall to show when they are there.- Nothing prompts you on how to get new poppins. Pippin just decides if they want to offer something or not at random. And if it is based off something, they haven't specified it in game (see the 1st Con).- The cooking is horrendous. The 'tutorial' dings when the food is ready, but when you go to actually cook, that ding is nonexistent so enjoy your worthless gloop and wasted 10x, 15x, 20x items. Also you cant cook at your home, you have to go halfway across the map, away from your inventory, so hope you brought the right stuff.- Why does food not revamp stamina? It should at least re-up my own at the bare minimum. The same dinos appear in the same locations. Adding in a perk for more earthy or fragrance is pretty worthless. - Gardening and build mode all relies on a grid system. This is fine for gardening, but not for building. You can't turn your camera or move it in anyway in build mode. You're frozen in place, facing the same direction. So if you're building a pen and need to turn or go behind your character, you must exit build mode, move backwards, re-enter build mode and *hope* you gave yourself enough spacing or your character decides to face the right direction. It's so nit-picky and irritating that I dread having to build any new pens.- Shells - this is the currency. You get shells from selling items. But only certain NPCs will buy certain items. But they won't tell you which ones go to which. Just run round and hope you had the right NPC. - Seeds are super expensive, but crops sell for 2 shells. WHY EVEN BOTHER?! Cause you can't cook your own dino food. You're forced to buying it. And it's also hella expensive! Good luck earning enough to get the crops and dino food.- Feeding the dinosaurs - some dinos eat one of their food preference a day. Others eat multiple each day. Does it tell you that anywhere? NOPE. Have fun figuring out who eats how much of each thing when they want you to put different dinos in mixed pens. - If I have to rely on a wiki to do everything little thing in the game, the game is broken🤷‍♀️ They either need fix the copy writing or fix the user flow for the quests/story line. Either way, it's broke and not worth $26.99.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically write reviews for games but having read some of the other reviews for Paleo Pines I wanted to add my own as I have a few thoughts that I don't see others talking about.I've followed Paleo Pines since the game was originally conceptualised and have eagerly been awaiting updates on the games progress since. Now that the game is out I can confidently say I finally have a dinosaur taming game that I love and I hope this game helps to inspire more like this.I highly recommend playing with controller, I see a lot of people in reviews saying the controls are clunky, and I don't think clunky is the right word. The game has finicky inputs at times that sometimes require you to be standing in certain spots to interact. I have experienced very little trouble with this while on controller, but with some of the larger dinosaurs for things like tilling the ground you may notice it.The game has a bit of a slow start, you need to go through a couple days before you can really get into the fun of taming and even then with your initial farm size you will only be able to tame so many dinosaurs at first. This slow start may turn some away from continuing and thats fair enough. If you feel like it has your interest though and continue on, the exploration and discovery of new dinosaurs and new colours and patterns is rewarding. I found myself excitedly exploring the second area of the game running up to each new dinosaur and wondering what they were and what roles they'd have on my farm. There is the downside of limited dinosaurs however which was disappointing to find out about but I will mention here that you can send dinosaurs back to the wild and always get them back, its not ideal by any means but it does allow you try new stuff out with the comfort of knowing they're not gone forever its kind of a storage system (and is literally called dinosaur storage).In my opinion if you're here for a farming game you may be left disappointed and a bit unsatisfied with whats there, I think this game appeals more to those who want a game about taming dinosaurs. The farming though fun is very simple, use a hoe, plant seeds, water, harvest after a few days occasionally weed and switch up soil type for higher quality and higher output from crops.The dinosaurs do add some fun twists on this but the focus is a lot more on the taming and seeking of unique dinosaurs, the story also revolves around this as well.The game could use some expansions in some areas which is worth pointing out, this game does not have a true crafting system (you can make custom orders using your materials but its not real crafting). There is also no way to get carnivore food outside of purchasing it, others have mentioned a fishing mini game would be good and I agree I love fishing mini games. One other thing i'd like to see is a section of the journal that has record of different dinosaur skills, I had no idea that some of my dinosaurs could plant crops or that slasher wasn't for cutting down trees, its small but would be ideal over having to look at the games wiki page. I have my fingers crossed that these might be added in the future but since these are features currently missing I thought it worth mentioning.In short, if you're here for farming you may not be totally satisfied, if you're here for taming dinosaurs and taking care of them this might scratch that itch at long last.

_childDocuments_.review: I've now fully played this game and got all the achievements, so here's my thoughts! Overall, I found the game very enjoyable and it's great for anyone who likes farm sims or dinosaurs. The game will appeal to people who like organizing and decorating a farm, and people who are "collectors" who enjoy finding different colored dinosaurs of all kinds. PROS:-The art style is adorable-Wide variety of dinosaurs, from the classics everyone would expect (triceratops, t-rex, stegosaurus) to some less well known critters. All of them are so cute and come in a wide variety of colors so it can be hunt for exactly the one you want.-Unlike some farming sims, growing certain fruits or vegetables isn't limited to a specific season; your crops just won't be as high quality if grown out of season. This means you aren't stuck waiting for several seasons to pass just so you can grow crops for a quest. (The exception is fruit trees and bushes, but these can still be bought from a vendor if you're lucky). -The map keeps opening up with new dinosaur abilities and many things (dreamstones, artifacts, etc) are cleverly hidden, so you can keep exploring for a surprisingly long time given the maps aren't huge. -Farm can be as hands on or as automated as you like depending on how many little dinosaurs you have to help you plant, water, and harvest. CONS:-Cooking is pretty frustrating, especially if going for the Mastery achievement. "Mastery" isn't gained from cooking the meal just once, you have to cook it several times, sometimes up to 10 times. Additionally it is entirely possible to enter the ingredients for one recipe and get a similar but completely different one. This requires tons of ingredients and a lot of luck. At least some of these are automatically mastered when an NPC teaches you the recipe (except all of Avery's, for some reason?)-Watering plots of land with dinosaurs is a bit hit or miss. It's nice that they can cover up to 25 squares but their aim can be pretty abysmal. You can be standing right in front of 1 single dry square and water 3 times in a row and never hit it, but water the plants all around it multiple times over. -Some NPC quests seem to be unnecessarily padded out, making them take far longer than they need to. The most egregious by far is the quest chain associated with the achievement  which takes an incredibly long time for seemingly no reason. I spent a full in-game month camping the NPC morning, noon and night waiting for her to offer the next part of the quest, with literally nothing left to do, before she finally offered it (despite already being BFF rank with her for quite some time). It took an additional 21 in-game days to finally complete the quest because of  A lot of this could probably be cut down as the padding seems unnecessary. WHAT I'D LIKE TO SEE:-Option to pay shells/in game money for 'express' custom orders -Dinosaurs with some additional skills for more variety (dinosaurs that fill holes, weed crops, act as pack animals to carry more stuff, etc)-Removing the flute and journal from the inventory. They are both essential core items for the game, so it's unfortunate that they take up 2 precious inventory slots. -More maps! Perhaps Pippin's swamp? There's some caves mentioned as well. The most fun part of this game is exploring, it'd definitely be nice to be able to do that more. -Possibly the option to convert small and large dreamstones to the other size. Towards the end I had tons of large dreamstones I wasn't using, I would've liked to get more small dinosaurs to help with crops. Overall I enjoyed the game and had a ton of fun with it. There's definitely some things that can be improved, but it's a great to pick up if you like dinosaurs, farming sims, or both.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'll admit that I'm not the most educated or experienced person when it comes to these kind of casual, life sim farming games. The closest I've truly come are Minecraft and Animal Crossing.I wanted to give this game a try due to the fact that it has dinosaurs in it which you can tame and ride. And to be fair, the cute designs of the dinos, the interesting capture/tame mechanics and the cozy atmosphere seemed like a winning package, at least at first. Most games like this I understand tend to start out slow, but this one especially felt like there was very little meaningful to actually do, and when you combine that with game mechanics that don't do a great job explaining themselves, vague side quests and rather limited resources and no reliable ways to easily get more, this game just isn't really beginner friendly. I'd say stay away from this one unless you're a veteran of the genre who doesn't mind having to put in some extra work early on.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "Reccommended but not /really/ reccomended" like a neutral. Because while the game is incredibly relaxing and cute and I love the style, it also feels VERY unfinished. There are only a handful of NPCs who don't offer much depth aside from One (1) character so far, the festivals having their own unique currency to buy decorations was a neat idea until you realize you can only get maybe 10 tickets per festival, and cooking requires so much of the ingredients (15 onions and 10 each of carrots and potatoes?? what's the reasoning here) and the tool to cook is SO FAR AWAY from home base that it's really not worth it for the first year, so far. With no way to replenish energy other than sleeping it leaves you relying on your dinos to do every single chore, but the mounted controls are clunky and once dismounted on the ranch the dino leaves your party immediately and ai/pathing causes it to sprint off, which can only be stopped with a VERY fast flute "hey you" and "follow me" but more often than not they're already zipping halfway across the field by the time you've brought the flute out. You have a house and supposedly a bed that you sleep in, but it's all done with a menu from the ladder door of said house, yet there are a decent amount of indoor furnishings on offer at the carpenter's shop for you to have him build for you. As well as a calendar in the journal but no way to actually check each day individually if it isn't the present day, which makes planning ahead finnicky if you forgot what off days for the various shop npcs are. ESPECIALLY because your initial bag is SO small, and gathering resources at first is VERY difficult so each trip out has to be carefully planned for or else you just end up wasting a day.While it seems like I do have many complaints, it's because i feel like this game can go far and become a staple of the farming simulation Harvest Moon/Stardew Valley type of games. I hope that the devs keep working on it, and improving upon the solid skeleton it is right now. There is much to enjoy about Paleo Pines, the enchantingly cute art style, the calming music, the premise of a peaceful dinosaur farm (even scooping the dino poops is entertaining enough), hunting down Ultra Rare or just personally favored dino colours, and I will continue to enjoy it further, with the hopes that eventually future updates will resolve all of the 'unfinished' feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable dinos to tame caught my attention immediately. There is a good variety of dinos as well. The farming includes crop rotation, which a lot of games in the genre do not. And the way it is implemented is pretty damn good.Your character has no personal improvement as far as I can tell. You do not have skills to level up and your stamina bar never gets bigger. HOWEVER, this is not an issue and works game-design-wise because you tame dinosaurs who will be able to do the things that would drain your stamina, and their stamina DOES increase as you level their friendship. My only real complaint is that small dinos all have the same abilities. They only plant seeds on the farm and help discover things when exploring. While larger dinos can plow fields/water fields/clear debris/harvest crops on the farm and sprint/cut obstructing plants/break boulders/smash logs when exploring. It would have been nice for the little guys to have some more things to do.I would gladly buy a DLC that adds new areas and more dinos along with a separate or continued story. But what I think could really shine is if the devs made a successor game that has a bigger scope from the get-go. More dinos, more areas, more friends along the way. They did great with this game, and I think they could take what they learned making it and make more amazing games in the same vein.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: They say that this game is the perfect blend of Ocarina of Time, Jurassic World Evolution and Stardew Valley.Well to that I say "SHENANIGANS!"Now I'm not saying it's a bad game. For what it's doing and what it has it's actually a really unique and interesting game. But you don't need to make up stuff to make it look better. The only similarity this game has to Ocarina of Time is that you can play a flute. The only thing similar to Jurassic World Evolution is that it has dinosaurs. And sure...it's a LITTLE like  Stardew valley but not enough to make a comparison. If I had to compare this game to something I'd say it's like My Time at Portia but with dinosaurs and no building.The game is above average I think. Probably only worth 20-25 dollars, not 30 so I'd wait for a discount. Because I mean.....it has no voice acting. It's U.I. is very badly designed, it's really slow in the beginning and it doesn't teach you a whole lot so you find yourself kinda stumbling around those first couple of hours.But the idea of using dinosaurs as tools is really interesting. Your dinosaurs leveling up is interesting. I love dinosaurs so that's a plus as well. And for what IS there it actually for the most part feels pretty decent and looks pretty decent. And besides the lack of voice acting, it sounds exactly as you'd hope and expect it too.So...yeah thumbs up. It's a good little game. Not amazing or groundbreaking, but if you're desperate for a new farming sim game then this one is a pretty safe bet all around. Just know what you're getting into.If you'd like a more in-depth look at the game then please check out the video review on my YouTube Channel (link below).Otherwise, thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello! This is my first Steam review so here we go!I found out about Paleo Pines from the YouTuber BestInSlot and followed his updates on the game's release. I played about 25 hours a bit after it was released and it was really fun. I took a bit of a hiatus from the game due to an overall gaming burnout but a flame has been rekindled. I have been a fan of dinosaurs since I can remember. I'm also a fan of cozy farming games like Stardew Valley, and this game is the best of both worlds. The publishers at Italic Pig seem passionate about Paleo Pines and I can't wait to see what future updates or new games look like! I just got done playing on a new save file for the last 5 hours and I can say that I'm having even more fun than before. I will say though, the character designs are middling and the begging customization choices are not good either. I'm not too taken aback because I'm, to be honest, ONLY here for the dinosaurs and I'm sure most players are too. But it can't be helped to call out the human designs. I love the dino patterns and colors. I like there is LGBTQ+ representation without it being forced. It also has nice scenery and good graphics for the art style.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, but don't get your hopes up too high when playing it. The world, cute and innocent, feels very refreshing and unfamiliar at first, but as you progress, the true cracks start appearing. The only things you can really do in this game is do meaningless quests with flat NPCs (where only two of which are actually decent in terms of character, namely Marlo and Pippin), briefly farm (this is made moot when you level up the tender dinos), and tame dinos. That's really all there is to it. There is no fishing, water-crossing dinos, mining, or really anything else. It's a good game to sit and relax back with, but it can get boring very quickly, especially once you figure out how to rotate your crops and make bank. Most late-game is, unfortunately, just going to similar spots to see if there's a Ultra Rare albino dino somewhere, not much else.Also, finding the Parasaurolophuses (which is the MAIN big quest, mind you) has a very weak reward and feels empty and hollow. Don't get your hopes up for something exciting, it's a disappointing let down.When it launched I bought both this version and the Switch version, and main the switch version, which is notoriously a buggy mess and lower quality(as is usually with switch), but to find out that some of the bugs that are present on switch are also present here is a letdown.It's the little things that add up into a shallow experience as a whole.All in all, as long as you don't expect much from this game and enjoy cute dinos, it's an ok game. I have hope that they will expand upon the game in the future. I recommend getting it on sale or later on if they decide to add more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: As a dinosaur lover, I eagerly anticipated the release of this game and got exactly what I was hoping for: a menagerie of species with adorable designs, sounds and animations, each with different food items they like and dislike. As the game progresses, the tasks your prehistoric friends can help you with - from travelling across the land, searching far and wide, to harvesting crops, finding useful items, tilling and watering, and so on - becomes increasingly indispensable. Simple are their needs, and true is their friendship... so long as you give them a suitable enclosure, and keep it clean! They also sport a variety of wonderful colours and patterns; which one(s) you might find in a given area varies from day-to-day, and there are many delightful uncommon and rare variants. You'll want to routinely perform tasks with your helpers once they've come to trust you, as they'll level up and gain increased amounts of stamina as a result!In terms of the map, each of its three regions (valley, forest and desert) are adequately sized for their purpose, and populated by more-or-less unique species (some of which you won't find anywhere else, and will only turn up at certain times of the day)! Each zone is replete with little areas that are easily missed or overlooked, but almost always reveal a pleasant surprise to the careful explorer.Nothing in this game is threatening - all is simply wholesome, gentle fun. Your dinosaurs won't eat you, nor will they ever attack one another. The world of Paleo Pines is that of innocent childhood adventure, and it brings me back to some of the games I used to play with my dinosaur toys when I was little.Cons: While (at least in its at-launch state) Paleo Pines can appear a bit limited in comparison to certain other games in its genre, and there is certainly a degree of repetitiveness to be found in its gameplay, the greatest shame is how shallow and pointless interactions with its NPCs can be. For those characters who don't just wander around its main plaza with simple on-interaction (or in-passing) comments to make, serving as its main cast and/or as vendors, conversations with them will often constitute simplistic fetch quests, resource exchanges or barely consequential dialogue choices. It takes a long time to befriend each of them, and it can be difficult to ascertain what gifts they like to be given. That being said, they're still likeable and do serve to make the world feel a bit more lived in.My greatest con - and again, this is in terms of how the game is at launch, having only received a couple of small updates - is how few dreamstones of each type can be found in the game. These are a vital requirement in order to keep dinosaurs happy, without which they'll become unhappy, leave your ranch and return to the wild (don't worry, there is a way to coax them back again later). The issue isn't that there's a limited number, but rather how unfortunately small that limited number is! Oftentimes I've gone out into the three regions of the game's worldmap and stumbled across a dinosaur I'd loved to have taken home with me, only to know that I can't. From what I can tell, the amount of dreamstones that are present in the game mightn't stop you from being able to have one of each type of prehistoric beastie (there are 38 species in the game, and 45 small and large dreamstones to be found), but it does prevent you from having colourful herds or packs of them all.Lastly, it's a shame that certain dinosaurs (such as sauropods, of which even smaller species such as Europasaurus or Magyarasaurus make no appearance, nor sauropodomorphs like Plateosaurus), including famous theropods like Spinosaurus, aren't available to be befriended - in some cases as a result of apparently being cut from the game. The same goes for pterosaurs, despite how charming it would have been to watch them fly around above the worldspace; and though it would have been lovely to have found more Permian reptiles in the wild, the only one to make an appearance is Dimetrodon! Perhaps such animals will be implemented later, but until then their absence is a bit of a shame. Though it may not fit the dinosaur-centred theme of the game, it would also be a treat to have an expansion with Ice Age mammals, or a coastal region to explore.All in all, Paleo Pines is still a game I'd recommend to friends and family, and I'd give it a fair rating of 7.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this game for under an hour and so far it has been more enjoyable than most of the newer and bigger "cozy" games. It doesn't feel like the intro and tutorial are designed just to keep you playing for past the 2 hour refund mark. This game and the characters have so much personality. I haven't played long enough to confirm if there is combat, fishing, dino breeding or townsfolk social/romance aspects. I'm sure these are mentioned in the store page's literature, I didn't look. I wish I found this game sooner.

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game asap or put it on your wishlist for sale notification.  Cute! Colorful!  Dinosaurs and adjacent creatures (and also dimetrodons!) _childDocuments_.review: So I originally posted a positive review of this game, but as I've continued playing, the initial wonder of the game has lost it's charm and the issues with this game are glaring. Generally, the game is just quite shallow. There are only three areas to explore, most dinosaurs have shared skill sets, and for a game that everyone seems to keep comparing to the likes of Stardew Valley, the human characters are incredibly flat and boring (and also look like cabbage patch kids rejects). Like, sure there's a friendship system in the game, but it feels completely hollow, seeing as how the only way to increase friendship is to give them gifts on their birthday and do quests for them, which usually boil down to: "Fetch me this item.", "Give this item to another character.", or "Go look at this dinosaur." and even when you do this, it never feels like anything has actually changed. They're still just as friendly with you as before with no real change to their dialogue. Also, the festivals in this game. Much like the NPCs, they're boring and feel hollow. There's nothing particularly exciting or interesting about them, and the limited decor items you can get during them feel just as bland and disappointing.This whole thing is an incredibly painful disappointment, the concept here is phenomenal. I played the demo like crazy before the game's release and i had such high hopes. The dinosaurs are adorable, the world is cute and colorful (if small), but the execution feels like it was rushed. Paleo Pines feels like its in early access, but it has a $30 price tag. The devs at least kinda seem to care about the game as a handful of small bug fix and QoL updates have been trickling out since the game's release. I really hope this game gets more in the way of actual content rather than just getting new dinosaur color palettes. Also, side note: In their intro video on steam, they proudly display a GamesRadar review saying that the game is "...the perfect blend of Jurassic World Evolution, Ocarina of Time, and Stardew Valley." And like... what???While I strongly disagree with everyone comparing this game to Stardew Valley, I can at least kinda see where the comparison is drawn. J.W.E.? Like... there's dinosaurs. So. A bit of a stretch but ok I guess? But Ocarina of Time??? How? In what way? That's a nonsensical comparison. The only thing in common Paleo Pines has with OoT is that the main character plays a flute as a little minigame. That's it.TL;DR:This game is an agonizing reminder that a game can have a A+ concept and art, but still absolutely blow it in the execution. If you wanna buy this game, maybe wait until it gets some new content or if it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game, sans a few issues that, for me at least, have made this game stressful.First off, you have a limited number of dinosaurs you can have on your farm at maximum. This seems to be especially frustrating early on, as I've reached my limit already and cannot get anymore Dreamstones to get more until I move onto another area. However, I've learned that there is a set number total, and the max you can have is apparently too low for all the colors and species in the game, which is unfortunate.Adding on to this, the journal is made so you can catalog and track the dinosaurs, and other discoverable things, in the game. However, as far as I can tell, there doesn't seem to be a portion that tracks the different colors you encounter, or even tame. This means that the limit on dinosaurs you can have is even more felt, because you are also unable to look at them in the journal to feel as though you've accomplished it.Secondly, there seem to be a lot of... Artificial blocks from progression, I suppose? There doesn't seem to be a direct way to progress the game how one might like, such as with gaining new types of dinosaurs, you have to just wait for a quest to show up. Which, as far as I've read, doesn't seem to have a set, known way to trigger. This means you miss out on some events, because you don't have the quest yet.Thirdly, and this may be my own personal issue, but I found a few of the tutorials lacking. Events and how to befriend and raise trust on the dinosaurs particularly, which is unfortunate because they are major portions of the game, particularly the latter one. While it gave me a very simplified explanation to tell me what to do, it didn't give any details, and from looking online, most of the things I've read about it also are rather vague, just stating to 'continue doing these actions until it works'. The combination of these things has made this game turn from very relaxing to almost frustrating for me, as some of them almost feel like they're slowing down the game on purpose. However, I don't find it relaxing to play very slowly, and the forcing of it and vagueness ends up feeling more stressful, and I end up having to leave the game to play another in order to relax and calm back down.All this aside though, I would likely recommend this game to others. It's extremely cute, and I really love the visuals, the music, and the dinosaur species that are in it so far. I find the characters mostly charming, and I love how a lot of the actual mechanics function once I understand them.These things are the ones that are making me wish to come back to the game and play it again, despite the other issues making it frustrating to do so. I wish at least they'd offer up maybe an explanatory area of the journal, and a colors page for the dinosaurs. These things would fix the most frustrating portions for me, and give me something else to read and look at.So yes, again, I would recommend this game. I just would also give people a warning about it and maybe offer them some more detailed information if they decided to get it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll update my review when there's more updates.This is a game that I was looking forward to, I had followed the development of the game since it was just a silly idea made into an actual game but I can't shake the feeling that the game we have right now is nothing more than an early access of something that could be great.A game that advertises itself as a cozy farming sim with dinos, I guess you get that. The dinosaurs are cute, the farming is there and the aesthetic of the game is really pretty, the world feels nice to traverse and explore and you are always eager to find different dinosaur colors to add to your ranch, there's also some cool mechanics such as the farming soil changes depending on what you plant on it and dinos having special skills to help you with farming and exploring. Given that, I can't think of any other positives so I'll have to state what I think is lacking in the game.Reminding that this is a farming sim, I found it weird that there's no "winter" season, only a springy season, a summery season and an autumny season, maybe I'm biased for enjoying the winter the most, but I'd love to see what would be the work around of farming in the harsh cold season and see the world covered in snow, maybe even having to make special shelters for the dinos, a warmer bed or something.Still in the season talk, I didn't notice too big of a change in terms of seeds that you can plant between spring and summer, and the wiki isn't helping me fact check this considering the first seeds you get are carrots, spring onions and potatoes, all stated to be from different seasons but I can still plant them all in summer so idk.The village doesn't feel like a village, there's only like 4 npcs, sometimes an extra one, that you can buy stuff from and sell stuff to, but the construction npc can only buy from you construction materials like wood and stones, the vegetable npc sells the dino food and can only buy from you vegetables, the seed npc only buys and sells seeds, it feels redundant, it could all be sold in a shipping box like every other farming game out there. There's barely any seeds to buy in the beginning with but I hope that more get unlocked the more you play.There's no crafting mechanics. If you want to get fences, you have to go to the designated npc to get them and a gate, and a feeding trough. It feels like a chore, something that could be done from your farm since that's where you get most of your wood and stone.For a game that requires a lot of back and forth from farm to village to get money, has a decently sized world to explore, many dinos to tend to, farmlands to water, I feel like the game would benefit from a multiplayer co-op experience. Having your friend travelling with you on dinosaur backs, racing to the coolest wild dino out there, splitting daily tasks and such. I'll hold onto hope for a multiplayer update or mod, but until then, with the very lackluster cast of npcs, the game experience is somewhat lonesome.Honorable mentions on features that feel like they're missing:-move seasonal events-house interior-breeding (but exploring for the different color dinosaurs hasn't gotten tiring yet)-more customization like different fence materials, etc... (but maybe I'm just too early in the game)-fishing (i mean why not)I don't want to touch too much on the pricing choice because it appears to be a very sensitive topic, but for what the game is at the current state, I still think the game should be treated as an early access instead of a full release.I still think the game is fun, but it will be short lived. I'll hold on and wait for further updates. Until then, I can't recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the cutest, most lovely, well made Dino game I have ever seen and have had the honor to play. The graphics are wonderful and beautifulThe art and animations are fantastic.The story.... ohhh the story is just amazing. You really start to feel for the characters and get immersed in their own story. _childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I want so badly to recommend this game. It's cute. I played the demo and was tentatively excited.I can't. There's some tedious issues I can't with along with a lack of explanations about certain functions and shallowness of the entire thing.NPCs teleport and there's no real way to find their schedule. The game really wants you to use your journal, but we don't have the ability to see shop hours... Because there's no clock. I haven't seen one yet, at least. Every now and then, I'll see a tiny pop up that says "Midday" and like, okay? What is that? How long does it last? Is there a point at night I'm going to pass out? TELL ME.Running as a human character costs stamina for some reason. A way to waste time because if you like to move fast like me, then you are forced to slow walk if you forgot your sprinting dino. Just let us run. It doesn't go nearly as fast as the dino but it means I don't get caught in a slog that makes me immediately save and quit the moment I get back to my farm out of annoyance.There's only one inventory upgrade because the devs say that's "part of the challenge", but more difficult AND more chill versions of this type of gameplay let you get more upgrades than that. This is further compounded by the fact that all your gear is in your very tiny inventory if you need it. So you have to go to storage, put stuff away, and it is so tedious.There's no key remapping. There's only like 10 NPCs you can build friendship with. I haven't even met them all. Cooking? I was going to try it out more, but then I couldn't find a way to get a way to cook on my farm/ranch thing. So that means, if I want to cook anything, I have to clear out my inventory, get everything I need from storage, leave my ranch, go all the way to a single cooking pot at the lake. EXCUSE ME? ARE YOU SERIOUS? That's not game play, it's time sink and waste for so very little reward.This game could be great. I don't know if I have faith, though. I really want to. I adore the entire concept of the game but the execution has been lacking. I've seen people in the discussions asking for quality of life improvements, settings about the stamina thing, the NPC schedule. The responds have been... not promising. Like they really want to stick to their narrow vision of what the game needs and not hear what's driving their players kinda crazy. I would never say they need to change their entire vision, but compromise might be nice. I would take stamina to run as a human if the stamina regen wasn't so slow I could go cook dinner and come back to see it's not full yet. It's only 50 points of stamina! Give us a real clock and schedules about where the NPCs will. I won't care about their teleportation if I could figure out what time it was.In it's current state, I just can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. I love dinosaurs and I was so excited when I found out there was going to be a cozy game where you could collect and ride dinosaurs, decorate a farm, and dress up your character. I got the game, played it nonstop for two weeks, and I have barely touched it since. This is 100% a me problem. This game STRESSES. ME. OUT. I grab pretty dinosaurs when I see them and when I get back to my farm and realize I have no space, I panic. I don't want my sweet digital dinosaurs to be cramped and unhappy, so I grind to clear space and make a pen for my newest baby. If I have to put my dinosaurs together, I get very sad because they are very sad. The other thing that is probably a very big me problem is I absolutely DESPISE farming in cozy games, which makes the genre literally impossible to play (CURSE YOU STARDEW VALLEY). I am broke all the time in this game because I never touch my farm. I sincerely wish there was another way to make money. Every time my dinos get hungry and I don't have money, I feel like the worst parent in the world. Also, the dang food stand should be open at all hours. I can't have my meat eating dinos starving because the person that's supposed to sell me food is "sleeping". YOU SLEEP WHEN YOU'RE DEAD I NEED TO FEED MY BABIES!!! Anyway it's a good cozy game that's perfect for my fellow dinosaur lovers and if you're not like me and don't hate farming and don't get unreasonably stressed out by seeing dinosaur shaped pixels unhappy, I deffo recommend picking this game up. Now they should make a version with dragons and no farming. Let me run a coffee shop or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a disclaimer. If you're looking for a super in depth collection/management/farming sim - look elsewhere. This might seem like a criticism but there's something nice about a game where you aren't swiftly bottlenecked into optimizing your farm and nothing else. I like the variation here; typical farming sims have the problem of either monotony from manual labour or total automation, but Paleo Pines fixes this with your new dino friends. But like I say - it's simple. It's not as complex as other farming sims, and that works to its advantage in some ways, but if you'd like something more substantial, this won't quite hit the spot.It would be great to have more areas to travel in in the future. Perhaps a large update or even a DLC if needed, to add more dinosaurs and different ways to use the farm. Overall I have a lot of fun with this - it's not something I'd play all the time, mind you, but it's fun to switch off and go wandering with cute creatures, and satisfying when you manage your crop rotations well and get good yields. Marlo is my bestie, btw.
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Friend gifted me this game in exchange for an art piece (that i still need to do... oops). 100% recommend this game for fans of calm farm sims and pet collecting! If you aren't a fan of dating aspects in some farm sims this is def also a game for you- avoiding possible spoilers but marriage isn't a feature in the game so theres no need to pick a favorite non-player character to spend your life with; aspec's rejoice! Reminiscent of original Harvest Moon game(s), Animal Crossing, and even a bit of Pokemon, even if that's a stretch! Long lifespan and plenty of gameplay. Terrific possibility for themed save files as well! Even if you aren't usually a fan of dinosaurs, this is a terrific game for folks that really only know what a T-Rex and Triceratops is; maybe you'll even memorize the name of new dinosaurs! Queer friendly as well; there are pride flag dinosaurs to find!! Whimsy, calm, silly and fun. Only downside I can really note that I've seen from other fans in the Discord server; the in-game map is hard to read and track where the player is, especially for those that may have colorblindness. Definitely could benefit from additional accessibility features for those that are colorblind and/or hard of sight!
_childDocuments_.name: Paleo Pines

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 2 bad DLC (paywalls a festival) + 2nd game announced instead of fixing this one? Not a good look given the game's history is pretty much just "buy my merch!!" Don't bother with this game or devsI had a lot to say about this game from the jank in which it controls movement to how absolutely infuriating it is to actually progress (NPCs will just go MIA for ingame months), but it seems reviews do indeed have a character limit and I went well beyond it. I'll have to shorten this a lot.Tl;dr: Do not buy this game. This is like breeding for a shiny in pokemon but somehow even duller and that's almost the only thing to do. You will be following the same route and checking the same spawns for a dino if you're the color collection type. If you're not, your gameplay will be agonizingly boring as there is so little else to actually do. There are so many issues and annoyances I would never, ever recommend this unless they're all fixed (which I doubt given what I've seen).Mod support would very likely save this game, but the devs are against it which is another reason I will never recommend this game.....t's doing the same thing again and again with timegating and insane jank to controls and how stuff works.Gosh I love and hate this game. I have many more hours on a friend's account and did end up getting it for myself on sale, but it was only because I got tired of having to borrow it if I want to play. It was very begrudgingly done.I'll start with the positives:-Sound design is absolutely great minus volumes on some things and maybe a few sounds not fitting. Many share sounds, as expected, but it's still cute. Some environmental noises can be too loud, like rain on a tarp, but I do like the fact such sounds exist there to begin with. Lovely touch. Also the "yippee!" makes me laugh each time I hear it.-Dinosaur designs are ADORABLE. There are some personal gripes I have about some designs, but those are nitpicks I personally dislike and won't go into. I adore most designs and I found myself especially fond of the tyrannosaurus, the dimetrodon, and carnotaurus. I loooove those guys so much. I wish ceratosaurus had more patterns because his current one isn't great, but if he had a better one he'd be in my top favorites for sure.-The fact dinos can roam from their enclosures is great! I wish they did this more, actually. It's fun seeing them wander around the ranch and adds a lot of charm.-You can pet and feed dinos and they will play cute animations when you do so. They're simple, but very charming.-Dinos have special abilities to help with stuff, though this can be a mixed bag as some unlock...way too late.-The environment design is charming for the most part. My favorite biome also feels smaller than the rest which is a bummer, but man...the forest area is LOVELY. I adore being in there and wish I could put my ranch in that area instead. Absolutely charming.Now for the cons which can be incredibly large in many cases and are why I can't recommend this game despite enjoying it (Ark syndrome™):--This one is a big one: the amount of dinos you can have at any one time is harshly limited. This is a game that pushes you to collect colors and different dinos but it won't let you collect them...it's...horrible. The excuse given is that no more than 45 can be in one area or the game starts to lag, but as SO MANY have pointed out, you could just add another ranch OR another area to the current ranch that goes through a load screen. Most every area is a loading screen anyway...why not....it's terrible.-It's clunky. Like horribly janky. Like I despise playing this even as fun as it is. It just feels wrong with how many steps you have to do to do certain things and sometimes if the character doesn't line up JUST RIGHT you end up not getting the response you want. Trying to flute toward one dino and another BEHIND THAT ONE somehow gets summoned instead happens a lot too. Trying to pick up something and your character decides to just not turn around/go to far/etc. They let you pick up stuff from mounts (selectively) recently, but it is way too limited. Dismounting and remounting to access/pick up certain stuff is tedious along with the notebook not registering stuff. I could go on.-In that same line, the fact you either have to carry a ton of items around or risk being unprepared when you see a fancy dino SUCKS when the inventory is so small.-The fact some NPCs can just vanish when you need them or aren't where they should be so you CAN'T BUY STUFF FOR ENCLOSURES AND DINOS. One character in particular that anyone who has played this game has wanted to throttle with their bare hands is especially guilty of this. I missed a window to make ALL SMALL DINOS have ANY use at all because I didn't realize I needed to talk to him more or something so my tiny dinos were just useless for ages. Also the quests involving him really take up space. Why have him asking for quests when he won't show up for like another ingame month?Need to buy something to make a pen? Too bad! The owner of that stall is out somewhere you can't get to.Need to order rope for a quest that prevents you from seeing dinos? Nope! She's IN THE AREA YOU ARE TRYING TO UNLOCK like 90% of the time. Finding her is a nightmare and you better pray you have everything you need when she's there. Also after that, you get to wait more ingame days for your order. Nice. Animal Crossing felt less forced than this. People have said this feels like padding time to prevent refunds and frankly I agree with that. It takes FOREVER to get to finally taming dinos and if you skip the tutorial then good luck figuring out the wonky systems they have. Most still aren't explained (like tender dinos which to this day have discussion threads about them).-THE QUESTS. They are so bad. Timegating is strong here too and everything is just fetch quests. I could go on but character limit.-Some small animations are cute, but most are lazy at best. Movement looks incredibly lackluster + no mount/dismount anim.-Some dinos have a few patterns while some have just one and it's not that great...which leads me to...-There is no mod support. For a singleplayer game. None. People have been asking for it but from what I can tell and have seen, the devs are very much "their way or the highway" types and you can see it in how they interact with the community. I'll never forget on twitter seeing someone make a mod for Jurassic World that put Lucky in it and the devs acted disgusted by it until adding 7 HOURS LATER (after people called out how trashy such behavior is) that they're actually happy about it. Uh huh...seeing your community pour their heart and soul into something then stomping on it is not great behavior. I hear nothing but unpleasant things regarding the devs and suspect mod support will remain nonextistant which is a shame as it could really liven things up. I really didn't want to buy the game because of this especially...-On a similar note, unlike the dinos, the human designs are atrocious. Personality wise and design wise, they're painful to look at and interact with. The closest one I come to liking is the guy who's gone most the time and caused me the most headache. Hearing distant "yippee!" is great, but it won't save these little gremlins for me.-The friggen social needs of the dino pens. Allosaurus, a renowned pack hunter, is a SOLITARY DINO....??? WHAT. This makes creating nice enclosures such a hassle because now I'm limited on dreamstones AND space because of space needs and dinos not wanting to have buddies. This should be togglable in some form.In the end, while I know this is a lot, it's because I wanted to love this game, I really did, and a part of me still does...but it's so marred by horrible choices, devs, gameplay, and design all throughout. I could never recommend this unless so many things get added and changed. Sadly, with what I've seen, I don't see that happening.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 5/10 - Don't love, don't hate, just kind of boringCasual farming sim games are an easy escape that I can get lost for hours in without realizing how much time has actually passed. Paleo Pines... fails at capturing that same hook and, honestly, it's just a 'meh' game. Can you have fun playing this? Sure. Does that fun wear off after an hour? For me, yes. The following are issues that I found with the game at my current play time (I wanted to get to at least 10 hours before review but...):What it got right:-Dinosaur helpers (amazing concept)-Designs fit for the general atmosphere they're trying to sell-Decent character customization (handful of choices - could definitely expand)What it got wrong:-Inventory space starts off real bad-Farming doesn't feel right (lots of click and holds to trigger animations that feel like pointless slowdowns)-No personal crafting of basic items (like fences, troughs, gates)-Item crafting is done through an NPC which requires in-game currency for all items (not just decorations)-Cooking is locked behind a quest chain of waiting days to grow certain crops-Cooking can only be done by going to one random pot in the middle of a forest?-Cooked meals don't restore a lot of stamina and costs more than it's worth-Main character feels like an afterthought with no leveling or upgrade system-Controls on mouse and keyboard are -Taming system feels off-World/town feels empty with only a few people to trade/chat with while everyone else (3 people) just run laps-NPCs don't have much to give outside of the same talk to them, deliver item, talk to them again quests (how many times can you lose your hat?)The game has a lot of potential and I'm sure I'll chip at it here and there. I can only strongly suggest watching some gameplay videos to see if this is something you want to get before buying. Steam really needs a neither option for recommendations for games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: A fine dinosaur game for children - which is not the criticism it might sound like as kids deserve fun games too. While steam discussion forum comments imply that the devs see this as more an all ages game, in truth it does not have the depth that the "Stardew, with dinosaurs" impression gives.It has many attractive systems, from town interactions to farm sim to dinosaur raising, but for its width these elements are shallow. And yet the game is charming, it is presented well, and it's nice to see parasaurolophus given central focus for a change.But the game is charmingly presented, and the dinosaurs are definitely the stars of the show around which each system revolves. For its simplicity, finding and befriending dinosaurs IS fun, as is learning how to keep them happy on your farm and learning how to best use their abilities to help you at home or in the wild.So for kids, it's a no brainer: they would love this charming game about befriending dinosaurs. And for adult players, they might enjoy it too if they can look past the simplicity of it.However, there are no glasses on character creation and as of yet I have not been able to find glasses with the seemingly only clothing merchant. Resolution scaling can be reduced to base 0 to simulate glassesless and makes a surprisingly compelling N64 experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very cute game, although I think the start up is rather slow. I think There could be more Patterns added, and That'd make me happier as the current patterns all seem very samey. I'd like a reason to collect a clear favorite Dino. Improvements to the game can definitally be made, but it's still quite enjoyable.Relaxation: Average. CUte music. Cute Dinos. The humans aren't as cute. I Have zoned out wandering around collecting things the past few days. I want to build an adorable park.
