_childDocuments_.review: On paper, Paleo Pines plays more or less like every other cozy farming simulator to come out in the last five years. You’re yet another kid sent to another farm to spend another summer toiling away in the hot sun. You’ll till the land, water your crops, trade with townsfolk, and spruce the place up like you did in Stardew Valley, Everdream Valley, My Time at [fill in the blank], etc.  But videogames aren’t made of paper, and Paleo Pines isn’t made like your average farming sim, because each of those fun if familiar farming mechanics are reimagined here through the ridiculous and wonderful filter of dinosaurs... because why not? Why manually plow your fields one cube at a time when a Styracosaurus can lower its horns and knock out a row in seconds? And why refill your rusty ol’ watering can every few minutes when a Gallimimus can regurgitate dozens of gallons of H2O on command? It’s a fun twist to an always satisfying (if done-to-death) set of gameplay mechanics, and Paleo Pines ends up standing out from the crowded cozy crowd as a result. But, while befriending new dinosaurs through a musical note-matching mini-game and unlocking new biomes with your hard-headed friends adds some spice to these pines, a few underwhelming design decisions add a bit of suck. For starters, Paleo Pines is less open world and more a collection of instanced boxes that are stitched together with loading screens, fussy pathing, and no jump? Ugh. As a consequence, I always felt restricted when exploring in Paleo Pines. Thankfully, some of your mounted minions can absolutely haul, and the more you use them the quicker they’ll level up and the more stamina they’ll get, meaning after a few hours you’ll be able to figuratively fly from one end of the map to the other and back at will. Which is a good thing, because Paleo Pines mandates this kind of backtracking through disappointingly grindy, fetch-questy objectives. Bring me five potatoes, take her ten carrots, find my missing notebook, take him this present—it's uninspired stuff that only seems to exist to clog up your comically tiny inventory and add artificial length to a game with no real plot. And, while the handful of folks you’ll meet along the way are all pleasant enough, they’re merchants and vendors first, characters second. But who needs ‘em? You’re not here for cavemen, you’re here for dinosaurs, and Paleo Pines delivers dozens of them, from skittish Psittacosauri to chonky Stegasauri. After befriending each through song and snack, you’ll lead them home and construct a pen, though the game's static building mechanic roots you to the spot and makes this process a bit of a chore. From there, it’s all about maintenance, cause fail to feed or clean up after your dino friends and they might skip camp and return to the wilds.  As for style, Paleo Pines is a pretty if dated-looking little game that mostly makes up for its low-res textures with bright, fun colors and adorable 3D models. Nice and simple (if repetitive) music and cute, funny low-budget dino sound design adds silly charm to a game already bursting with it... but nothing here really wows, and I can’t help but think that Paleo Pines would run fine on my PS3. In the end, Paleo Pines adds up to an addicting if clunky little spin on the crowded cozy farming genre. At $30 for 10 to 15 hours of relaxed playtime, I think it presents decent value, so I’ll give it an aggregate MEGA score of 2.82/5 (full scoring breakdown available in video form) and am happy to answer any questions you have about the game or my review.  Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the dinosaurs, stayed for the dinosaurs. An easy and fun game to play and unwind with after a long day at work.There are some differences in opinion in the reviews I've read. I think it comes down to why you want to play this game. If you are looking for the next Stardew Valley, this game is not that. However, if you're here to scratch an itch for collecting cute things, you'll probably have a good time.14 hours in, the farm decorations are bare bones, the friendship system is easy to overlook and character customisation is minimal. It also took me a couple of hours to forgive the slightly clunky controls. This hasn't stopped me from enjoying the game.What I appreciate is the surprisingly large roster of dinos (expected about 10, got 35+), colour and pattern variations, lovely animations and endearing behaviour (come back here Lucky, I'm not finished with you yet!). I also like the soil type mechanic for the farming as this isn't something I've come across before.I'll be playing this game for much longer yet.

_childDocuments_.review: if you enjoy games like Stardew Valley then you will love this game! I friended a T Rex and brought him home. How many other games will let you do that? This game is awesome! If you like farming, ranching, exploring, or dinosaurs then this game is for you. It is so worth every penny.I've been playing for a while now and I can say that this game doesn't get boring. I have completed the main quest, which doesn't end the game. You can start over any time you'd like and use what you have learned to get different dinos or different colors of dinos. _childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is a great concept, but the game doesn't feel as immersive and in-depth as I expected from an almost full priced game to be.Mentionable areas for growth:- You can't enter homes - not even your own home - meaning you can't decorate or get to see the personality of the characters.- There is no option to romance!! Meaning no getting married or making a family in this game. I mean, the fun part is getting to really know your partner right? And I think for this genre of game being able to at least romance is the standard, and is so for a reason.- The movement when watering crops feels clunky, namely it's difficult to water 1 specific square tile of crop at a time and gets frustrating fast.- The map isn't helpful, I'd like to know where exactly I can find somebody without the icons overlapping.- The building in the game is also not as intuitive as I'd like it to be, it took a while to figure out, I think the POV they chose is good but the controls don't really flow with the design- I'm surprised they didn't take tried and true qualities of past successful farming games and implement them into this game, or at least deliver a decent amount of new features that haven't been in a farming game to make up for the lack of features.This game feels like it should be for early release price, but for now I think the gameplay does not justify the cost. It's an amazing idea and I hope some of these suggestions get to be actualized in future updates; for now keep up the hard work, devs, you've got a great game in the works.

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is a pretty fun game overall. Its mainly a farming game which is a bit overused yet really well done and the main focus of the game, at least for me is taming and collecting different dinosaurs using foods and poffins, which are used to tame the dinosaurs. You need to get different dinosaurs to get into areas to get more dinosaurs and more things to care for your dinosaurs, these dinosaurs also have skills and abilities to help you farm, complete tasks and you are able to ride them. After the tutorial (which doesn't explain everything to you) the game gets quite repetitive and feels like to progress, its more helpful going on the wiki or on a fellow player's guide to know what to do to progress, especially because that's pretty much the only way you are able to decide what dinosaurs you want, at least for me. I would recommend the game to others and its quite addicting (especially with dino nose boops!) for its chibi design and cutesy concept with little dinos to interact with.I'd also like to mention that the majority of items feel overpriced with the majority of your foods going into taming new dinosaurs and selling them doesn't gain much, I wish that currency was easier to get and things more clearly explained. Also, in early game if you decide to collect as many dinosaurs as you can with your extremely expensive poffins, the majority of dinosaurs are unavailable to you because they require different poffin flavors, wasting your precious poffins which costed around three times your salary. Dreamstones are an entirely new issue with it being hard to get them and if you manage to get your dinos with poffins they will need one, and they usually leave no matter what else you do in my experience eventually, I searched on the wiki for their locations and still struggled to find any in the beginning. Plus, you need to get enough trust with your dino so they can actually be useful, such as being ride-able, scouting for items and such which takes forever and if you mistreat them then you have to try again, the only exclusion to this being your gifted Parasaurolophus, Lucky. I came into this game looking for a dinosaur ranch game to have fun with but its quite difficult being engaged with the game after awhile and prices are extremely high, for example, a single gate costs 100 shells at the start and without the whiteboard feature being explained, that's pretty much all you have.Has a few issues but I generally like the game and recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game over the course of the past week since it's initial release, and suffice to say I'm hooked. I've grown up playing a variety of chill park and farming simulators, and I'm a dinosaur lover. I played some of the original Harvest Moon games (which eventually became Story of Seasons,) Zoo Tycoon, Jurassic Park: Operation Genesis and several others. You'll find Jurassic World Evolution and its sequel in my library.The artstyle is wonderful. I can't say that the human NPCs stand out to me, but they aren't as important as the dinosaurs, which are the game's selling point. The designs of these ancient beasts are cute and colorful, and balance being scientifically accurate with an appealing cartoony style. The mechanics are simple and fun and easy to grasp.However, having put over twenty hours into the game now as of this review, I can definitely say that the game could have used more time to cook in order to feel 'full.' The dinosaurs themselves, I felt, were absolutely nailed. However, as a farming simulator and cozy game, the game itself feels empty and like it has so much untapped potential.You can't customize your house beyond an exterior paint job. You can't even go into it at all. There's little variety in the customization of pens and farmland. There's plenty of space for you to work with in case you want to have a huge menagerie of dinos—but in my case personally, I felt very little incentive to go out and tame dinosaurs once I had the abilities I needed to clear specific obstacles. After you have what you need, taming specific dinosaurs more or less is unnecessary except for certain quests (if you care for the simplistic story,) or to simply fill out dinosaur entries or find a rare skin to have as a trophy of sorts.The NPCs themselves are flat as cardboard and scarcely memorable, and there's little indication of a friendship system. Apparently you get prices lowered if you befriend shopkeepers and specific items from others, but beyond that, there's nothing that really motivates you to go out of your way to say hi to a specific NPC every ingame day.I think my biggest issue is that you reach a point where you've basically done everything way too early in the game. I'd unlocked every area, cleared just about every obstacle, and cleaned out my farm in its entirety by the third season of the first year. I would have liked to see more areas outside of the valley, Dapplewood and Ariacotta.I should also mention that unlike in most farming simulators, the main way you're going to make money throughout the game is crops. Yes, its a farming game, but foraging hardly nets you anything unless you're looking for truffles, which you can only dig up at the end of the year. You cannot fish. You cannot craft. There are areas and pieces of furniture that feel as though they were meant for something that was cut from the game, such as the tables and telescopes set out overlooking the wild dinosaur packs and herds.This game has me hooked and wanting  though not in a very good way. It definitely needed more filling out, with more content, more dinosaurs and prehistoric animals, more places to explore, more features, etc. I'm hopeful that the devs will eventually be able to add whatever was cut from the game and more in the future.For now though, I recommend it, especially if you're a dino lover who enjoys simple, cozy farming simulators. I would wait until a sale though or until/if more content and DLC gets added, because the current experience doesn't feel like its tapping into its true potential.- Lucky is actually insanely useful throughout the game and not just a replaceable starter- The dinos are well designed, quirky and colorful. I love looking for different skins- The dinosaurs are your 'tools' and have unique abilities that save you time and stamina both on the farm and in the wild.- The days feel long enough that you're not rushing to do everything you want to do, but short enough that you aren't bored by the end of them.- The NPCs are horribly bland- Progression is quick. Unless you have set challenges for yourself, you'll have done most of everything by the end of the first year.- There's little incentive to do much else once you've unlocked the areas.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first discovered Paleo Pines, it seemed fun, cute, and exactly the casual game I was looking for.Unfortunately, this game was not for me, and I can’t recommend it.Positive:- The dinos look and behave really cute.- The music sounds nice and adds value to the game.- There are many color varieties of dinos you can discover and befriend.Negative:- Although you can collect different color varieties, it’s limited by the amount of dreamstones you can find in the world. Without a dreamstone, you can’t keep a dino, so you’re not really able to “collect” them.  Apparently, you can replenish a dino's stamina by feeding it the right treat. My bad.- The overall story lost my interest quickly, and I ended up button-mashing just to move on.- The NPCs weren’t engaging; their dialogue felt boring and clichéd, so I didn’t feel like talking to them more than necessary.- Some tasks and controls weren’t intuitive and weren’t explained well by the game.- The quests were mostly “fetch this and bring it to that specific NPC.”- There’s no option to enter or decorate your house.In summary, the aesthetics are nice, and the dinos are cute, but the overall gameplay wasn’t fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this project since the original artist first posted a concept drawing with a farmer and an Allosaurus. I was extremely excited for it and watching the project grow has been great. However I have my gripes that I hope the developers will take into consideration and make adjustments in the future. Minor mechanic spoilers? I'm not going to talk about the story much if at all.-Dreamstones. I've yet to finish the game and don't know if the dreamstones will be explained but the fact they're required to own a dinosaur and are very limited is disheartening. I understand the need for a sleeping area but I'd much rather the dinos build their own nest than have a mechanic that limits the amount of dinosaurs I can own at a given time.Better yet I would rather the locations you find large clusters be used to mine from, with a limit on how fast it regenerates based on size and takes up so many in-game days.I understand they don't want you to abuse your dinos and get too many in one pen but there's other factors into their happiness that I believe prevents that (i.e. keeping the pens clean, food stocked, interacting with them daily, etc.)-Carry capacity. You're stuck with such small pockets and you don't receive a bag or backpack to increase your carry capacity. At the very least I wish you could put saddlebags on the dinosaurs, maybe have it deplete their stamina faster if they use their skills while encumbered? I would have very much loved a wagon the ceratopsians could pull as well. I feel that's a missed opportunity.-Searchers. I love the idea of my tiny little dinos helping me locate items in the game! However I wish it had a fetch mechanic alongside it. It's already blatantly obvious with the sparkles that you can harvest from nature but I think it'd be better if the searchers could also fetch if you'd like them to. -Harvest/Pickup. For the love of all things holy please let me harvest from the back of my dino ;; or let my dino harvest and give it to me while I'm riding them. The constant mounting/dismounting I do in this game is appalling.-Quests. There are quests in this game but most of the time I see a lot of stuff that's off-season in the requests by the NPCs. I think some edits there are much needed to keep with the season.-NPCs. I just think the human characters could be better animated. There was an argument between two of the characters and after one would finish talking, their face would return to a smile. It took me out of the scene and overall I just dislike the art direction with the humans. I'm also disappointed it's not like Stardew Valley in relationship building/romancing. It's easy to develop a relationship with these characters in just buying their stock or the required interactions, there's no gift giving other than birthdays and it doesn't feel all that beneficial. -Music. It's redundant and I found myself turning it off to play Animal Crossing/Stardew music in the background instead. Would I recommend this game? Absolutely. Am I disappointed it's not more complex in the farming/game mechanics as Stardew Valley? Yes, but I also recognize it ISN'T Stardew. I hope this game continues to grow and improve. I hope it gets an overhaul in a lot of places. Top notch dinos but it's just lacking in a lot of areas.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. And in some ways, I do. _childDocuments_.review: So ... where to begin ... After 100 hours on the game, I have finally finished the main point of the game i'd say ? (finishing the main story and gathering all species of dinos ???)But there's clearly alot to be worked on, this is a bit tough for me, cause I have been waiting for this game without spoiling myself at all, so no hype really, just wanted to have a relaxing time surrounded by dinos ! But sadly this relaxing time lasted for like 10 hours or something.As you go in the game, you'll notice a big lack of Quality of life, an omnipresent clunkyness and an extremely boring storyline with very stereotyped borderline flavorless NPCs. The only good thing about the game are dinos and their design really, and the map is pretty too.So let's do it.--The Good Points--- Dinos are cute and attaching.- The taming is cute and unique.- Exploring around with your favorite dinos are kind of rewarding with the leveling system.- The Ranch is fairly large, so you can manage your pen as you please.- The ingame book (kind of a portable wiki) is fairly well done and handy to collect all the infos.- Has a good Art Direction overall for the dinos and background.- Feeling the progression of your exploration of the map by seeing dinos migrating all over your already explored spaces, is actualy nice and feels natural. It fills up the world quite nicely.- Not too many bugs for me, beside invisible walls in the ranch (some people got some serious crash issues with progress loss, so I'm not doing too bad on this side.)- Devs are reactive and working hard to solve the bugs.--The Bad Points--- The characters look dollish and almost completly out of the general Art Direction, they do not blend. And trying to make them look somewhat like yourself if you have straight hair or blond air is litteraly impossible cause there's no straight haircut or blond color.- Your character is too slow and has 50 stamina points forever, unlike your dinos, you don't level up.- The "housing" system is extremely basic and very lacking, you cannot even put an item on a table. Or a lamp on a fences of a pen. Getting rid of the items you've put on the ground is even worse, your character half of the time will not look at the thing you want to remove, and the special item to remove multiple items in one click will only transform the item in little boxes on the floor for you to pick up afterward one by one.- Ressources like Stone and Woods becomes quite limited once you've cleaned your ranch and unlocked all blocked path on the map.- Caring for your dinos becomes a HUGE chores as you get more of them, even with only one exemple on each dinos, it's litteraly a chore in-game day.- Quest management is a pain and you can get soft-locked for a whole in-game years or in-game month very easily. Having some quests asking you to bring one specific item to a character in a specific location, cause it's where you got the quest is non sense.- Some quest like "find the item" for an NPC is extremely poorly thought as you cannot even see the item on the ground, you'll see an interaction floating dot if you luckily stumble on the said lost item.- Farming is an endless chore, it takes an average of 4 in-game days to grow something fully, to sell it for not much unless it's a cabbage or a salad.- The in-game yearly events are extremely basic and don't add much to the game except some themed decoration for your ranch, even the minigames don't feel like games.- The NPCs relationship system is very random and uninteresting cause these character don't bring anything to the atmosphere, and their questline even more so, those kind of things can also get you soft locked quite easily.- The whole cooking food system is useless, completly, it takes too much effort with too limited ressource to even consider using it as intended.- Watering the plant with dinos can be extremely random if you don't make a perfect small square of plant crops.- Alot of dinos have the same utilities and purpose so getting them all really feels like a material need of sort.- Main Story line is cute, but don't bring ANYTHING to the game. It's cool that you want to find the Paras so your friend Lucky is not alone anymore, but once you have found them, it doesn't bring anything since you had one since the begining. Not to mention how dull and empty of suspense the "plot" is.- And at last but not least, one point that makes me fear a bit, is that their discord has a "Positive Feedback" channel, so I hope they're not too closed to objective / bad feedbacks.- A huge lack of quality of life in many aspect -~ No other way to manage your item stacking beside splitting them in half.~ You can't recover your own stamina even if there's a food system.~ The automatism in the farm system is welcomed but far from enough, and easily forgettable or easily soft locked due to NPCs non sense.~ Your Dinolist is quite unreadable.~ Having to interact, then pretend to tame, then make a dino get bored so he falls asleep in front of you to check if he's a rare or ultra rare color with your book hoping that another dinos don't bump into him and wake him up before you reach him is very long and annoying.~ Interactions with dinos are ponctuated with alot of blank moments between several actions which make things quite slow.Conclusion :So yeah, overall it's a cute game with a good potential if only it had more than one beta just before the release of the game. But sadly, that cute and relaxing looking game, becomes quite the frustration nest as you go and get more friend dinos... The game left me with the feeling that their devs as passionate as they seemed to be, did not play their game entirely, otherwise everything wouldn't have felt like a chore in the end. The game feels unfinished, and the devs did say that there are alot of thing they wanted to implement but didn't have enough time. (Flying dinos, swiming dinos, there even had some unused models.)So yeah, my review will be there and, will get modified when things get better ! I really hope it'll get better, really.The project is kinda unique and appealing to any dinosaur fan, and could become an actual very good starting game for kids or adult who likes dinos or anyone that want to discover them.Hope that helps, take care y'all !

_childDocuments_.review: Just a heads up, this game is poorly optimized at the time of release, and can cause your GPU temp to skyrocket. I have experienced this, and some other players are reporting the same. By default the max FPS is set to unlimited, so before launching the game I recommend limiting the FPS elsewhere (e.g. Nvidia Control Panel or GPU tweaking software), or go to in-game settings as soon as you launch it and set the max FPS there.I have played this game for a full in-game year (63 days), discovered almost all the dinosaurs and the crops, met all the townsfolk, so I feel I've seen most of what it has to offer and feel comfortable enough to give a review.It's a cozy and wholesome farming/life sim with dinos. Aside from the usual farming, chatting with townsfolk and exploration seen in this type of game, it has dinos who can help you with farming and exploration. The ultimate goal is to set up and customize your farm/ranch to your liking while listening to your dinos' needs and helping the townsfolk with everyday problems. I am barely done decorating my ranch, and I can see myself spending many more hours playing it. There is a demo that lets you play the first 14 days, so I highly recommend giving it a go.What this game is / what it does well:- An unique approach at farming. Most farming sim sees animals as livestock, but in this game they're not your property nor pets, they're your friends and can actively help you.- The cozy wholesome aesthetic. Everything is bright and soft, They've nailed the design on the cute and cuddly dinos. You can of course pet all of them.- Each dino species have different skills. They're well incorporated into both farming and exploration, and no dinos feel useless.- Rare dino colors. Every dino in the wild has several rare color variant including albino, melanistic, and other special colors, and hunting for them can be addictive.- Amusing writing. Some townsfolk have quirky yet very on-brand dialogues ("I'm as busy as a Baryonyx" and many others), and funny item descriptions that gave me a chuckle (Spring Onion "Once picked, it's a sprung onion", Mango "Man come back").- The sense of progression. The game slowly introduces new and helpful mechanics in terms of farming, so it's not overwhelming at first. As you befriend different dinos, they can help you unlock new sections of your ranch and new areas to explore. What this game is not / what it doesn't do well:- Lots of bugs at release, some are minor, some are game-breaking. Anything minor from your dinos stopping following you randomly, characters getting stuck in geometry, a glitchy UI element that can't be closed by any means, to major ones like the save corruption that reverts your ranch data to the first day, and in-game date resetting back to day 0 of year 1. For the two latter bugs I recommend not having more than 20 manual saves and going back to previous saves if the bug appears, but the real cause is not known yet. Hopefully the devs can fix this quickly.- Unintuitive controls, and no key rebinding. Splitting a stack of items is tedious. Tilling exactly where you want with your helper dino feels awkward. Waterer dinos are good for watering crops, but it's difficult to predict which tile the water goes.- The game's sometimes bad at explaining mechanics. I don't know if I was being dumb, but I couldn't figure out what certain symbols in the UI mean at first. In order to "discover" and see the info on crops, you must first plant the seed and examine it, which the game didn't explain. You can house both herbivore and omnivore dinos in the same pen, which the game also didn't explain. Thankfully there is an in-game help menu that shows most of the stuff, and anything you plant/place in your ranch is can be removed afterwards, so it has rooms for trial and error.- Silly repeatable quest system. In one quest this person asks for 3 potatoes, but in the same quest board on the same day the person rewards you with 6 potatoes for some other items.- The map seems small and lacks in variety. There are only a few biomes to explore.- You can't see nor decorate your house interior.- Does not have breeding mechanics.Despite the flaws and the lack of contents, I feel this game takes a shot at a niche idea (farming with friendly dinos), and succeeds in realizing it very well. The devs haven't promised any future content yet, but I'm hoping to see new map/biomes and dinos that were cut during development (sauropods, pterosaur, and many aquatic dinos).

_childDocuments_.review: I recently bought Paleo Pines and I've become obsessed with the game already due to many factors, including the adorable/refreshing dinosaur designs; the interactive town folks with different personalities and great sense of humor; and the endless amount of quests, which lead you to develop better relationships with other character as well as increasing your farming success. Every object/item you encounter in the different biomes have a purpose, so don't ignore them! Nevertheless, some of the negative aspects in the game, which I hope the developers will improve later on, are the storage size and the personal stamina of your character. While I understand that by using the dinosaurs you will not spend as much stamina nor storage in certain items, it would have been nice to have a way in which I can level up and increase my own stamina and storage. Another factor to consider in the game  is the lack of a crafting system. I understand that via missions you are able to obtain the money to buy all the items necessary to create new pens and improve the decor of the farm, however, some people may prefer to craft on their own items/objects instead of going all the way to the town to speak with Marlo. I do not find any of these factors incredibly detrimental but it would be wise for the developers to take them into account in the future.Overall, I am very grateful to all the hard work the developers have put into the creation of Paleo Pines. This game has definitely become one of my favorite games in 2023.

You get to grow different treats like vegetables and fruits to feed to them as they become helpers to do different tasks around the ranch. I enjoy the graphics and all of the cute dinosaurs I've already discovered in my game play and cannot wait to encounter many more. From first viewing of this game I knew I would enjoy playing it. The Poppins similar to baked muffins are delightfully crafted with  five different tastes as Crunchy,Spicy,Juicy,Earthy and Fragrant. It is a game of chance and trial and error in getting the wild dinosaur to try one and then allow you to befriend them. Currency of shells, for collecting and trading wood,stone and grown crops you've harvested on your ranch are never ending if you can find dinosaur helpers to clear the land in order for you to farm. Best of all just enjoy the timeless adventure that this game has to offer and collect lots of dinosaurs.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I feel terrible not recommending this but I honestly feel like it wasn't play-tested and that they clearly didn't have many, if any, experienced game designers on board for this project. I have been following it for years and was more than excited to start playing, but it just falls so so so short. It could have used more time in the oven.I'm not sure where to start exactly with my problems with this game because its really just a bunch of little things that make the game un-fun to play. First, I guess, is your character is remarkably slow. the run speed should be your default speed and sprinting should not take up so much of your energy bar. It takes WAYYY too long to get from one side of your farm to another.Second, watering dinosaurs... I'm not sure if there is any logic to how they water plots, if there is I certainly couldn't find it. Many times I'd stand directly in front of the crops I would want to water and my dino would just... miss.. and repeatedly rewater crops I'd already watered!! Like I said, small things that just add up to become real irritating.Third.. cooking in the game is almost completely useless! I feel like many mechanics were added just to have them, without there being any actual benefit to them existing! Same with the festivals and seasonal events... theres one minigame that can barely be called a minigame for each season.. I mean, filling up a pile of food...? The easiest game of hide and seek known to man?? At least the race is fun, I guess, but its insanely short and takes like 10 seconds to complete it. and you can't even re-do it til next year. (also the fact you have to cook things 3+ times before you see the rewards the meal gets you is insane. like what thought process went behind that?? no one wants to waste every crop they've grown repeating a recipe...)Fourth.. and I know I'm not the only one to complain about this, but limited numbers of dreamstones??? the one GREAT thing about this game (i'll get to it later) is the dinosaurs and you're telling me I can only have 46?? and thats only once you go through all the friendships and bs that you even get them all! Theres so much space on the farm, no reason dreamstones shouldn't be craftable...Fifth, NPCs are boring, dry, their quests are bad and uninteresting. I'd attribute a portion of their lack of personality to the art style tbh but even the writing doesn't make me feel anything towards these characters. Also, another mildly annoying thing: some NPCs aren't accessible for DAYS at a time, and other NPCs will not allow you to accept OR turn in requests unless they're at a specific location. In some scenarios it makes sense, but other times you're telling me I cant give Avery 20 pieces of wood the entire week+ hes at pebble plaza because you can ONLY turn in the quest when hes at the canyon?? I had that quest for like a whole in-game month. It was, as I said, mildly infuriating.Now, the game isn't ALL bad. Like i genuinely loved the bit about the dinosaurs. They clearly put a majority of their efforts there and it shows! They all have unique animations and speeds and skills... and the relationships you form with them do feel personal! I loved getting to meet all the different types of dinosaurs! but unfortunately you cannot get very far at all if you just want to focus on the dinosaurs. There's no way to feed the dinosaurs without money, no way to get money except farming, and no way to farm without getting irritated by minor bugs and inconveniences.There's so much that needs to be altered in this game to make it worth playing, I'm writing this review 10/20/23 so hopefully by the time you're reading this, many updates will have come out that will make worth it. But as of right now, I'd wait on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Paleo Pines is a farming simulator where you obtain and train dinosaurs.I quite like this idea and got it because I love dinosaurs and watched their development through TikTok and other locations, so needless to say, I was very excited and was not disappointed. I loved going out every day to do quests and seek out the dinosaur colors I wanted, as well as grind to expand my farm and complete the game's story, but that's just it. The story. After you complete the story and even before, the game eventually becomes an endless grind where you're always doing something or some days not doing anything at all. There is no factor to interrupt the monotonous gameplay loop, like fishing or fighting. I always found myself wanting more, but the gameplay doesn't change throughout the entire game. There are no races or competitions to provide a need to obtain dinosaurs, and the only need for them is to go around faster, unlock areas, obtain resources, and farm easier. That's it.I've gotten myself to the point of trying to 100% the game, and even that is a chore. You need to BFF most neighbors to get the dreamstones and trees required, plus you need to farm for multiple in-game years to get all the food required to get the recipe mastery achievement. It's to the point where I dread opening up the game because I know I'll just be sitting there tending the farm, cooking, then sleeping to get more crops to grow or get to a different season to harvest hazlenuts and other seasonal materials. This game is a chore and a real grind once you get through the story, and I do hope more content gets added, like a DLC to venture into the swamp or a new mechanic to break through the monotonous grind.The dinosaurs have no different personalities other than minor stat differences when it comes to speed between the species. An example of this is that a dilophosaurus is faster than Lucky. Leveling up your dinosaurs is fine, but slow. The issue with the dinosaurs is that they're all the same, other than the tasks they do and their minor stats. They don't have any personality or special interactions you can do between them to make a further connection, rather than the color and their use. I can't connect with my dinosaurs at all, since they all feel hollow. They feel like robots since they have no personality or charm other than the color and model themselves. I want dinosaurs that have personalities where one isn't the same as another. Give me some that are exciteable and like to run, so they're faster than others of their species, or ones that hate rain and don't want to go out during a storm. I want personality.Once you get through the dialogue of the quests, you're left with no directions other than what the journal tells you, which isn't anything but the items you need. An example of this is the quest for Marlo, where you need to find him at night to give him 100 fibers. If you miss that dialogue, you won't know you need to do that, so you'll be confused and lost until you take a moment to look up the answer and location. You shouldn't need to do that, and it should tell you that information in the journal so you don't forget it. I spent a whole year in the game on that quest because I didn't know that. This is the same for a couple other quests. It's a common issue.In summary, the game is a grind that feels endless, and even once you beat the game, that grind is never done. The dinosaurs have no personality and serve no purpose other than the task they have assigned to them. The 100% achievement is horrible and genuinely the worst experience I've had trying to get that for a game. The quests aren't logged properly in your journal for specific times you need to find them. I don't recommend this game if you don't enjoy endless repetitive tasks, but hopefully the game changes somewhat in the future.This feels like a bad horse game.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys cute dinosaurs and relaxing farm sim games!I adore the artstyle and graphics of this game. The world and it's creatures are super cute and the game's visual style just screams "cozy". The music in the game is also pretty nice, not a major aspect of the game but support the relaxing vibes of the gameplay well! And don't even get me started on those cute little dinosaur noises!Talking of dinosaurs: They are the main selling point of the game. There's a big selection of them available and a LOT of different color variations of each dinosaur! I personally like to "shiny hunt" the ultra rare color variants and everytime I find an ultra rare color it makes me super excited!The basic gameplay loop is pretty simple and I find the easiness of farming relaxing! I absolutely LOVE that the dinosaur friends - both big and small - actually can help you at your farmwork! These dinos aren't just cute but also very essential and helpful to run your farm!The NPCs have some nice personality to them and some of them struggled with stuff that personally resonated to me. Especially Marlo's storyline sticked with me and resonated to me a lot.The biggest beef that I had during my hours of play was the fact that there's a lot of collectibles in the game, and I have no way of checking which items I've already found and from where, which made it frustrating to hunt the last remaining few with internet guides.Overall I really recommend this game for anyone looking for a cute and cozy farming sim with the dinos being the focal point!

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute, but otherwise disappointing. I was extremely hyped for this game's release, but I ended up losing interest very quickly. The gameplay is repetitive to the point of boring, the crafting system feels clunky and unoptimized, and no fast travel means that you're wasting a lot of time traversing the (admittedly small) map. Then there's the stylistic issues, namely the human NPCs. I think all of the design effort went into making the dinosaurs. Which is understandable! They look great. However, I feel like more care could have been put into making the human designs look more appealing. Right now, the human characters look like they were ripped straight from a low-budget, cocomelon-esque youtube video. Compared to the lovingly crafted dinosaurs, its incredibly jarring and really took me out of the game.Overall, there's just...no substance to this thing. I think it falls into what some call the 'paper-doll' problem that a lot of cutesy-style games end up having. It's a pretty game at first glance and might hold your attention for a few hours, but there's nothing underneath. IMO, if you're going into Paleo Pines expecting the vibes of Stardew Valley or Sun Haven, just save yourself the disappointment and pass on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall score for the initial portion of the game (24 hours in): 5.5/10. Initial review at 8 hours: A very cute game, lots of expressive dinosaurs, and a generally good atmosphere. Nothing ground-breaking, per se, with controls being a bit finicky and some glitches likely to affect your early launch experience, but it's a good premise with quite a decent amount of depth with a tad bit of difficulty with its slower progression and time-based approach. Edit at 24 hours: There are a lot of quality-of-life issues which does make the game tedious in particular ways, lacking the ability to manage stacks by individual amounts being something which dropped my review score on its own, alongside the tiny inventory and inability to drop items from your inventory, meaning you will invariably be stuck unable to get an item you really need until you go back home, empty your inventory, and return. It's cute, and once you understand the loop, it's pretty satisfying to find new dinosaurs. Overall, following the initial tutorials, you're sort of forced to learn diegetically through randomly trying things to actually progress, like finding Slashers and Stompers, or how Tenders work since the character who introduces the mechanic is close to 16 hours in, by my recollection, and I've still yet to encounter all localities and all people, and a lot of it still feels random in a way that I'm basically biding my time through, or tedious like actually working through the main questline, which is about the only follow-through I can follow to try and progress into the next area.This isn't a bad game, between its dinosaur designs and what is a reasonably good gameplay loop, but it probably should have been playtested a bit more, between glitches and general progression grinding to a halt several times.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I want to give this game a bad review? Absolutely not. I love the visuals, the cute dinosaurs, the vibrant and eye-catching color the entire world has. I've had SO much fun. You can see how much time I've put into this game. But still...Am I going to give this game a bad review? Yes. Despite the fun I've had, if someone looked me in the eyes and asked me, would I recommend this title to them? I couldn't. Not with the game as it is now. Not with how much it costs. This can change depending on just how much support the developers want to give this title as time goes on, but right now? No, there's titles y'all are better off playing instead. Paleo Pines' only draw is its dinosaurs, but if those don't pull you in.... Absolutely nothing else will.TL;dr - For what you're paying, you're getting very little. Only play this if you love dinosaurs and ARK isn't giving you the cutesy cozy vibes you want from said dinosaurs.Pros:+ VISUALS. The only aspect of this game that truly feels like there was any love and thought put into it. Dinosaurs are amazing, as I've already said. The game is super nice to look at, at all hours of the day. (Night time might be just a bit too dark though, and with the VERY limited display settings, that might annoy some people.)+ USEFUL DINOSAURS. Every dinosaur you befriend for your farm comes with a couple skills that make life on said farm easier. I especially love my stompy Carnotaurus and speedy Baryonyx. This game was 100% built around dinosaurs being your main tools around the farm, and I love that. There's just one sticking point with this and I'll elaborate in the cons section.+ RARE SKINS. The vast majority of my time in this game was spent 'shiny hunting' for ultra rare dinosaur colors. It was a bit undermined when a certain festival basically gifted me an all-black Carnotaurus within my first ten hours of play time, but the other dinos I found were found legitimately, and it was an actual rush each time I saw them in the wild. I absolutely love that this is a thing in the game, though I really wish that the Ultra Rares amounted to more than just 'Albino' or 'Melanistic' for like 80% of the dinosaurs.Cons:- PRICE. I paid less for this title because I got it basically at launch. But... $30? That's a hard price point to sell this thing on. The lack of content in this game makes itself very apparent, very quickly. By the end of the game's first month (There's only three in the game.), I was already running out of things to do, and that's not very good when the developers are wanting half the price of a AAA title for their game.- SHALLOW CHARACTERS. Aside from the dinosaurs, you aren't going to be playing this for the characters. There is no meaningful development as far as I've seen, and I've been playing for over 60 hours. You start off friendly with the villagers, you end things friendly with them. Developers say they do not plan on adding a romance aspect to the game either, so already, that's one big feature that most people look for in these types of games gone. Sure, the lack of it isn't a deal breaker for some, but in a game that's already starving for content, this isn't helping things.- CLUNKY UI AND CONTROLS. Who on the development team decided that by default, we only have 12 slots in our inventory? Who added onto that then that the only expansion for your inventory only occurs once  (to my knowledge, I've only done it once), and it only adds 4 slots? To a game where your own tools like your journal take up space? I just want to talk to them. Also, some dinos' controls and handling is a real chore to work around. Traversing the map on some of the bigger dinosaurs is laughably slow, and there are MANY arbitrary barriers on the map that stop you from going where you want to. Want to climb up or down a very slight hill somewhere in any of the zones? Oh, no, you can't. Walk around it instead in your slow as molasses Styracosaurus, please. Also, no jump button, game? Really? I have SO much to say about this, but this review is already an essay. Oh, but I could go on ALL DAY. - UNDERCOOKED PROGRESSION. Might be a nitpick of mine, but outside of unlocking abilities through more dinosaurs in your roster, you never really 'feel' as if you're getting any more efficient as a farmer, even as your dinosaurs gain levels. Sure, their stamina bars might get bigger, but Sprinter dinosaurs don't get any faster, Waterer dinosaurs do not water more squares than they do from the start, and Stomper/Smasher dinosaurs do not see any increase in strength, since all obstacles only take the skill itself for them to break. Befriending your dinosaur only consists of bribing them just enough to convince them to let you put a saddle on them, but there isn't anything more to it. Oh, and you can't change these skills. For example, if your favorite dinosaur of all time is a Rex, but you aren't a fan of how slow it moves, you're out of luck. You're forced to use something else that can actually move, instead of your favorite. - DREAMSTONES. I only include this because it irks me so much that in a game about making friends with all the dinosaurs, you realistically can only have a few dozen on your farm. I believe there's only enough dreamstones on the maps combined for about one of each type? What if you want a herd or something? Guess you're up a creek without a paddle, then. Yes, there is an NPC you can go to to 'track down' the dinosaurs you release into the wild should you want to see them again, but it's not the same.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fine game. I'm not super impressed by it, but that's more because the game feels like it doesn't know what it wants to be, chill, cozy and cute or yet another grind fest. It's both. The dinos are absolutely adorable, I mean I never thought I'd have to tame a tame by feeding it daisies and yet here comes this game. The rex is a carnivore. A carnicore that you buy carnivore food for, which is more expensive than the herbivore food. You tame this carnivore, this rex, by feeding it flowers..So the only issue I have with this game is the grind that it is to earn shells, the ingame currency. Yeah there's clothes and stuff you can buy to customize your character, I did not buy any, not because i didn't want to, but because they were ridiculously expensive and so were various seeds and all my dinos literally ate up whatever shells I managed to earn, cause the food is rather expensive too with how much those dinos eat, and you have no way of cooking that food yourself. There's also tons of furniture and decor items you can buy for you farm and the dino pens, which I also didn't buy much of for the same reason. Tried growing all the crops I could get my hands on, but it didn't help any with the shell earning when rebuying seeds cost most of what was earned selling the grown crops despite them having 2 or 3 stars.My biggest complaint is actually about the dinos though. One you have a slasher, smasker and stomper, you don't need any of the other dinos at all. once you got one of each, the rest of whatever dinos you befriend are really just food drainers, increasing the cost of shells you'll have to spend on food for them. Yes, they produce fertilizer for you, which is great for your crops if you care to up their quality, but that's it. The little dinos I find utterly useless. You can get them to plant seeds for you, but be careful with it cause they might eat them. You can also take them with you to scout for maqterials scattered around the world, sounds useful, sadly it isn't. If they find any, they make a little noise, little jumpy jump to alert your attention to it and then they run over to it to show you where it is. Issue is, after their little noise they'll stand and do nothing for quite some time, then they'll run over to it. Second issue is, they gotta be so close to this material that you can see it perfectly fine yourself. In order to see my little dino do this, I had to find something for him to get alerted to myself, then move closer and closer to the material for him to be in range of it. We were sitting literally right next to it before he reacted, made his little noise and then we proceeded to sit their for another 10 or so seconds before he ran over to it while I sat there going "It's right there, buddy. Go on, you can do it, I believe in you!" positive reinforcements and all that. I finished the game, Lucky got herself a sisterbrother - cause the dinos don't actually have genders - who shockingly enough is much bigger than she is. Imagine my horror when I realized I had been riding around on a child during the entire game, I am so sorry Lucky. All in all, great game, except that in my opinion food for the dinos should be basically free, or at the very least the game should allow you to grow/find ingredients and such to make food for them yourself. Then I wouldn't care if any other dino I have after I have gotten my 3 main utility dinos aren't anything but adorable food drainers.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited about this game after following it for a very long time leading up to launch via TikTok. I think the art style is adorable, the concept is there, and it could really be a great game. Unfortunately, I just don't think there's enough here to make the game FUN. The "plot" or quest lines of the game are very basic fetch quest type errands that will have you running from place to place on the map. Unlocking and taming new dinos allows you to access new areas, which is great! The interactions, animations, etc. of the dinosaurs are fantastic and a major selling point of this game.What really kills it for me, though, is the tediousness that permeates through every single task. To expand your pen, be prepared to be fighting with fence posts for extended periods of time, readjusting all of the gates, reintroducing your dinos to the pens, etc. The button mapping/user interface of the game is not intuitive and feels very laborious and clunky to use. The inventory size is just too restrictive for what the game seemingly wants you to do, which is always have multiple snack types and poffin types on hand for different dinosaurs. I found myself loading the game up, realizing how much unenjoyable tedium was needed to accomplish anything in the game or to get new dinos, and would just quickly exit out of it.It breaks my heart to write this review! You can tell the devs really have the makings of something unique and enjoyable here, but it just isn't cutting it for me. I am a big dino lover and an almost 20-year veteran of farming sim games and this just isn't it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game... sort of. I like this game, I really do, although I admit that I have a few reservations about it and things I feel people should know before spending money on it.1) This game doesn't quite feel... finished. I'm not talking about the bugs (which are present and vary from funny to game-breaking), I'm talking about the quests. A large part of your time is spent doing quests/requests that are posted on the bulletin board in town, as this is needed to boost your friendship level with the villagers, and that's required for more story-quests. But there's only a handful of different tasks: item requests, lost item (which is a hat or notebook), and giving an item from one npc to another (which is again a hat, notebook, or I believe a pendant or something, it's been a bit). You have to do a LOT of these quests, and they get INSANELY repetitive. It doesn't feel finished. There should be a far bigger variety of these quests that'll take up a huge part of your gametime.2) Devs are unclear how much content we can expect to be added in the future, which is a big problem for me. There's no roadmap, no estimates - it only became confirmed that they were going to add more dino colors to the game when they posted a "flash contest" on the discord for people to give them color ideas. Before this point, they wouldn't really answer if they were going to add any more colors to the game - and this lack of transparency also means that I'm not confident that they will be fixing the quest issue as mentioned earlier.To be clear, I'm fine with games that have room to grow. I'd even say I'm more permissive than many people I know for games publishing before they're fully polished, and I'd be completely fine with my 1st issue if there was a clear roadmap and transparent communication from the devs. But there's not, and that really impedes my trust in this game. If these things don't bother you? Go for it. But if this also gives you a bad feeling... maybe wait a while longer before getting it, and see if they've added updates that fix these issues. I hope they do, because this game is incredibly cute and has Incredible potential. It just doesn't feel done, and I'm not pleased that the devs don't see the fact that it's a bit underbaked.EDIT: Upon reflection, I've changed my review from "do recommend" to "don't recommend." While I have a fun time playing the game (for the most part) I just don't know if I could honestly say I recommend someone spend money on it in this state. I really hope that this changes.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember having spent hundreds of hours just with the demo of this game back in 2007 when my internet was still piss poor and somehow found mad tracks on a compact disk.There were only 3 tracks: Training Day, Foosball and Fast FoodSending rockets to my opponents while they are taking a speed bump and getting them off the track on Training Day was my speciality, Foosball was Rocket League but even nastier and funnier, and I think I probably found some hidden shortcuts in Fast Food.The game went quite under the radar and even finding a digital copy of the game was hard (I'm not talking about the wii version or the shady russian iso) but now it's on Steam, multi-languages, with an handy remote play feature to play with your friends (since there's no multiplayer for the PC version).I was worried to never be able to play mad tracks and keep it as a distant souvenir, but now a part of my childhood went on Steam, fully functional and on top of that with achievements. Guess it's time to be 12 again.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that's a surprise release!I enjoyed Mad Tracks quiet alot on the 360 back in the day and also playing it via backwards-compatibilty on the Xbox One. A silly Fun-Racer that provides races and minigames that can get really chaotic at times which makes them even better.You have three types of cars (slow, fast, sports) and three difficulties to chose from some choices make levels harder others make them more easy.The game offers an adventure mode, which unlocks new levels, as well as an arcade mode where you can play in multiplayer or on your own, both with bots available.Online multiplayer seems to be absent on PC, but you can play with your friends via Steam Remote Play if you want to.Both DLC packs are included in this version as well.A few graphics options which cover the basic needs of a PC Port are available and there is no FPS lock.Great Racer that shows it's full potential when played in multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't pretend the game is good, because it is not. What I will say though is that Mad Tracks holds a very special place in my heart because I played a ton of it as a kid even on a German copy. I didn't understand a single word but that did not keep me from spending absurd amounts of time playing it. I even sent the developers an email once thanking them for the game and begging them to make a sequel. The dev studio was probably no more by the time I sent it but I did not care. It was like sending a letter to Santa. I replayed it now purely for nostalgic purposes which did allow me to have more fun than a regular person would in Mad Tracks. If you have the ability to wear rose-tinted glasses in the game, then buy it. If you have friends that are willing to put up with whatever game you toss at them, then you'll have fun for a few minutes. If you have neither, Mad Tracks brings nothing new to the table and is shoddily developed with heaps of jank, terrible design decisions (I'm looking at the stupid friction engine mechanic), minigames that are locked behind a wave of races and events, a short career mode that can be finished in less than three hours and achievements that have no business being as tough as they are. This is not an easy 100% by any means. I spent upwards of two days trying to get two achievements in particular that required an unreasonable amount of luck and patience. Under any other circumstances I would not recommend this game, but I will give it a thumbs-up for the sheer nostalgic value it holds for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Mad Tracks

_childDocuments_.review: There are *many* play modes, like table soccer with cars, pool, throwing stuff of a table, etc., but they are novelty gimicks - after scoring first place, I have zero interest in returning to them. What has replay potential, are actual races. Problem is, the game is unfair and has a couple of really annoying effects - first is 'bullet time' at random moments, which completely throws off steering - if you are doing a difficult turn with a jump, you quite likely will go off track. And here's the problem: it's a vechicular combat game, but if, as a result of either some 'weapon' or a collision you are thrown off your course enough to stop, let alone fall off the track, you have no chance of catching up - the time penalty is too large. This does not apply to bot cars though: you could have hit most of them on your way to pool position, but they are magically always on your heels. This made the arguably best track, which would otherwise be real fun, a frustrating experience of hundereds restarts (I kid you not).

_childDocuments_.review: Apparently this game dates back to 2000's , and it certainly feels like it.The game balance is wack. When racing against bots, being in first place doesn't have the same "Blue shell" risk to it and there's no rubber-banding, so if you get far enough ahead, there's almost nothing they can do to stop you. On top of that you can stack items until you have 10 shields and nothing can touch you.The non-race single-player missions have their good moments, but most of them are pretty simple and forgettable.The music is pretty good, though when trying the same mission over and over it became grating quite quickly.The biggest flaw in this game is that there is no way to choose which items are enabled while playing solo. This became an issue when trying to go for an achievement to get a 1:15 time on a race. All the guides only had the starting items, the boost and the rocket, while I was stuck doing attempts with all items on and never getting the boost consistently, since I had cleared all the other content before trying this. I managed to tough it out but it soured my last moments with this game and the first 20 seconds of the song it played in that mission.Apart from that, 100%'ing this game is mostly out-of-the-way collectibles outside of the track, for which YOU NEED TO CHANGE THE SETTINGS TO DISABLE AUTO-RESET, something I didn't know was a thing until looking up a guide. This game also has a weird obsession with making you replay the same mission over and over, as one achievement requires you to win one race 5 times in a row against hard AI, while another wants you to play another race 20. TIMES. IN. A. ROW! Why? What's the point?

_childDocuments_.review: Mad Tracks is a micro machines racing game from 2006, and it plays like one.Graphics are rough, difficulty settings are whack, mechanics are not fleshed out.HOWEVER, with all that said, it's a pretty fun party game (especially for solo play). Besides traditional racing, there's time trials, elimation, control point, hill climb, collectathon, soccer, foosball, billiards, and a ton others. It keeps the variety up for basically every event. Yes, some are just bad. Yes, some are dirt easy. Yes, some are incredibly difficult to get gold medals.Remember, it is a micro machine game. You have to be a child or a brain off adult, and I am a brain off adult. It's (mostly) relaxing, simple and you can watch a movie while playing. You can do this with other (better) racing games too, but for the variety and the price, this one is hard to beat.P.S. If that doesn't sound fun or you're looking for a challenge, you'll hate this game lol

_childDocuments_.review: I would probably rate this game 4/10 maybe 5/10 if I would play splitscreen with friends a lot and find it enjoyable.For single player the campaign does give a sense om making progress and could take some time to do if you play every stage at hard difficulty. Otherwise your looking at about 90min+ to finish with all gold medals.As an achievement hunter this game has some challenge to it, not the best kind but atleast it feels good to finish.Playing the same map 20 times in a row is kind of stupid as an achievement. Everytime you leave you will hvae to reselect map and difficulty. This makes the achievement of winning against 5 hard level NPCS on "Speed Racer" (idk 100% the name) 5 times in a row annoying apart from the RNG.The speed run achievement "Ultra Fast Food" is a good challenge, the only thing is that it suffers from the same problem as the other challenging one; its RNG.No matter how well you play you could lose 10 times in a row due to not getting enough boost power ups.Overall the game has apart from racing some interestign gameplay so called "minigames".You go bowling with your car try to land as close to a hole as possible and play a retro version of Rocket League to name a few.It is relatively easy to handle the cars, but a bit frustrating on some of the minigames.It has its moments, but overall the gameplay feels dull and not very enjoyable to me.It might be worth to pick up at a good sale but there are a lot of better cheap games.While I do recommend it, it is more a neutral score on my part.//ECE//

_childDocuments_.review: To start out brutally honest, there's not a lot of game here and everything can be completed in a day or so. I'm glad I got this cheap as part of a bundle. Yet when viewed as a short and inexpensive game, I can easily recommend this. After playing both, I feel like I understand now what Party Crashers (released 10 years later but with some suspicious similarities in feel and weapons) was trying to do and be, except this game did everything better.The standout gimmick here is how the cars run on a power source which recharges when not in use. When you let go of the accelerator for a sharp turn or when you're midair after a ramp or whatever else, the engine's meter fills back up. They call that power source spring-energy from pull-back friction, but the engines may as well be running on magic; you don't actually have to drive backwards to power up the engine, though doing so will supposedly recharge faster.Weapons and powerups are where these combat racing games succeed or fail, and this one has great and useful stuff scattered around the tracks in yellow mystery boxes. Each item you pick up is added into your inventory, with your currently selected item visible on the car's top, and you can cycle through your inventory and use them with a button press each. There's a slightly long cooldown after using an item, so you can't spam anything.Various kinds of auto-homing missiles will send opponent cars flipping or turn them to a block of ice, the poison crates reverse steering for anyone who hits one, the oil slick is good but not too powerful, and the headlights blind others for a moment. The excellent shield both deflects attacks and pushes away other cars and objects, which is very useful in certain events. An electro field drains motor power from other cars while the spring fully restores your own engine power. The offense-focused time warp greatly slows down everyone else for a couple seconds, which can be countered by using the excellent boosters. I liked how some powers were extra good at canceling the effects of others. Only the barrels felt kind of pointless, but I could see them being a lot worse if they were heavy.The game starts with a single-player Adventure Mode against CPU opponents at difficulty settings of Easy, Medium or Hard. There are 46 “events” where you can medal from first to third place, and beating some of them unlocks powerups across the whole game. As an aside, you actually might want to avoid certain powerup unlocks while trying to medal certain races or get certain achievements because a limited selection can be easier, though this doesn't seem to be an intended strategy.Many of the events are traditional races where driving skill and reaction speed can get an easy win, while the rest are a wild mix of styles including collectathons, checkpoint hunting, and casual activities like darts, marbles and golf. There's a bunch of bobsled-style races where your power doesn't recharge and instead you can only slide down while taking care to avoid a spin-out. My favorite events (not counting all the races) involved pushing the most items of a table, navigating a tower maze to get as high as possible before time ran out, and climbing a steep hill while objects roll down as hazards.Next is Arcade Mode, where you can play any unlocked event and have some freedom to adjust options including adding more players for a multiplayer race and choosing the car type. The weight of the cars makes a big change for some races such as heavy cars being easier for icy bobsled races. Sadly this level of customization also makes obvious the things you can't customize, such as choosing what weapons will appear.Finally, Battle Mode has some interesting potential for when you have a group of players. Each battle strings together several events in a row and one player wins the whole battle based on their scores in each event. For some strange reason you have to unlock the battles by finding special items in specific events, so just look up how to do so online.These odd flaws in the game get more obvious the deeper I go, so let's dive into them. For example, the way the Adventure Mode events board works is a little awkward, where you unlock races if you medal in a connected race; there's not much reason to have them connected in this chaotic web and the lack of structure makes finding events difficult. I also wish there were more of the fun ones, like at minimum three with increasingly difficult tracks.For a long time, one event in particular called Cannon Man did not seem to be working for me. The goal is to boost off a jump and land on targets for points, but I was landing at the 100 point bar and getting only a few points – and then one day the event suddenly worked. The other worst events are anything spent bowling for vases because you only get more vases if you break all the ones out there, as well as the Foosball table because getting a gold medal perfect game is very dependent on luck.Also, I tried customizing the controls early on and that didn't work at all (possibly because they were the default buttons for Player 2 which couldn't play Adventure Mode) and then every time I started the game after that, it would be on those non-working controls which meant I needed to go set the controls back to default. For this reason alone, I would say don't mess with control customization at all.Despite its occasional janky flaws, I really enjoyed this short game. The cars feel good to race and the large human environments make for a fun background. Whether from being frustratingly tough or high-adrenaline thrilling, every race does seem to be unique. This could also be a pretty great party game for a group of racing fans – once someone has unlocked all the items and battles, of course.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, it starts off promising, but this'll be a pass.First the good: the sense of speed is really something in this game. You'll be speeding at whatever the toy sized equivalent is of Mach 10 during the racing parts. It also feels really good when the tires are on the road, giving you plenty of grip to turn on a dime. The game has a lot of potential to is. The music and sounds are pretty good, too.Now the bad: First thing... lemme ask you something: what's the one thing you want to do first in a racing game? ...Accelerate, right? So why is there a mechanic that makes you take your finger off the gas? I understand doing that to turn tighter, but the way the game works, as long as you're not flying through the air, you'll turn really easy, so there's never a need. The "battery" is literally an anti-fun mechanic there to slow you down, for some reason. (Unless the RNG gives you the battery powerup. Then you can recharge it like 2 or 3 times all the way and at once.)Secondly, speaking of flying through the air, most of the things that you get hit with will send you flying in one way or another. God help you if it sends you up, because you'll likely end up off the track. When you do that, you have to manually reset your car, but it won't put you where you fell off. Nope, you go back to the last checkpoint you managed to hit. So it not only sends you backwards, you also now have to accelerate, which despite being able to go fast in this game, the acceleration isn't the best (which will make you hold the gas down, which the game punishes you for doing too much) On the flipside, you can use this to cheat in some of the bajillions of mini-games they've got going on. Like, if you get hit with the mortar and go flying way up in the air (which is unavoidable and not fun), you can cheat to snap right the frick back down.The only other thing I've gotta say is that most of the tracks in this game... aren't actually racing. It's mostly mini-games. You'll be pushing balls into goals, dodging obstacles, throwing your car at a targets. Now, dodging is easy enough, just keep moving. The target mini-game was actually fun and easy to get used to. The ones that involve pushing things, though... no. The thing here is you'll be throwing yourself into reverse a lot to adjust your direction, but with how the camera is constantly fighting you, it's really hard to do so. (Also, side note, for the time trial tracks... why does the game give you offensive items when there's no one else racing?)Anyways, I only got passed the first half of the game before I realized I'm just not enjoying this. It's a shame, because it started off good and it looked pretty fun, but man... maybe if half of the mini-games were just more racing bits, that would make the game a LOT better.

_childDocuments_.review: Teaboy's Basic(ish) Reviews....I read a lot of reviews when looking at games on Steam, and it quickly gets tiring – those who write involved, down to the micron scale reviews, although helpful, end up like looking at War & Peace when you’ve only got time for a quick 5 minute dump!  This is middle of the road and to the point – not easy for me as I tend towards sesquipedalian loquaciousness!  Vociferously Verbose?  Alright, verbal diarrhoea.  (Although I hate panning a developer’s work and all the time, effort and love they put into designing these – it is their life after all – this is my honest, personal opinion of my level of enjoyment.  Sorry devs!).  A note on time played:  My Steam clock does not seem to work properly, indeed, it even minuses time on occasion!  Plus, I have a tendency to wander off and leave games running at times, so time played may not be entirely accurate!  Teaboy’s Tonsil Titillators or Toenail Titbits!  (Rating)  Tonsil Tickler (Totally Tops):  The frenchy of which you always dreamt!  To quote a master, “She’s got a tongue like an electric eel and she likes the taste of a Man’s tonsils!”.  An absolute masterpiece and joy to play.  The Tits (Terrific):  Everyone loves playing with these!  Not THE best bit, but such fun on their own you can be lost for hours....mmmm.  What most games you really like score – perfection is so rare after all.   Torso Teaser (Taker of your Time):  It’s a flat stomach....sure it’s nice to look at, run your fingers over, slobber on a bit, sometimes that bellybutton gets your motor running....but it's just basically the corridor between the two ‘gaming rooms’.  The definitive ‘Meh’ - the middle ‘sideways thumb’ option for which everyone on Steam cries.  Todger/Tadger & (scroTum) Taters (Tedious):  Is it an ‘a’ or is it an ‘o’?  Who cares!  The meat can be fun to play with for about 5 minutes of your entire day, the rest it just hangs there and generally gets in the way of doing something else.  The main problem of course, is the two veg sticking to your inside thigh.  This is what this game feels like – the occasional/rare bouts of fun, the rest bobbing like a 19th century British Policeman (now you know why!).  Toenail Tornado (Total Toss):  A playthrough so appalling it’s like being trapped in a Turkish sauna with the ugliest, hairiest, fattest, sweatiest beast of a neolithic hominid who’s trimming his toenails using pliers and the splinters are reminiscent of a scene from the Normandy Landings.  My god how did this get released!?  Teaboy Touts (Score):  The Review:  Todger TeaserA mixed review due to a mixed enjoyment.  It is a '5 minute play' style game, at least for me.  I tried completing the map (all racecourses) in one playthrough but 3 were locked with nothing telling me what I needed to access them (that I could see - the icons were minuscule).  Small game, VERY basic, as in start/stop/fire weapon.  That's your lot.  Camera (view) options are a bit naff but not terrible.  Control of vehicle is fair, but you get one car per flag you drive under and only four flags.  I'm a Brit, so I just did them all under that flag.  So pretty much zero vehicle choice.  It's a small game for a small price - I don't even remember getting it anymore and I don't go for racing games so most likely  a bundle.  If you like micromachines type stuff, then this will tickle your fancy....for about 5 minutes.  I fancied a change of pace for a bit so flicked through my (getting stupidly large) library and thought I'd give this a go.  It is fine for what it is - can't mark it down for doing what it is supposed to do.
