_childDocuments_.review: 20$ for 100 hours of fun~. If that's good for you then you should buy this game but if you value your sanity then you should not.The game is really fun at the beginning but once you get used to the combat, the skills, the map and the movement and once you gain some rating and meet other people who are also used to these things then you realize that the game is completely luck based and requires little to no actual skill and the only way you're going to climb is through patience and macro play rather than killing people which is completely and utterly disappointing. It IS a typical battle royale  , gear matters too much and getting gear is luck based. Ganking is even worse than normal BR cus of perma stun/stagger mechanic so you essentially can't move when outnumbered. The damage is stupidly high and you can get 1-2shot with 10min+ queue/wait time for the next game. It's horrible. The final circle is a complete joke. It shrinks to the point of disappearing and on high elo there are 5+ people alive when this happens so you're not even having a "skill based 1v1" exchange or anything it's just luck .. just like its combat, the combat system is based on light hits, focus attacks and counter hits and each one of these counters another one but the parry system is complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ as it is delayed and ping plays a role on how parry works and you actually have to use it earlier or it won't work but if your enemy decides to cancel his focus attack then he can just hit you with light attacks and you die. It's essentially a "mind game " (which is the deceptive way of saying its a 50/50). It's complete luck. If you watch top players duel they are dying the same way as plebs do, the only difference is their movement is more fancy and their fights are faster but in the end its the same "rock , paper , scissors" type of gameplay which is not skill based. Combine the RNG combat with the RNG gear and the ganking/outnumbering ( which is out of your control and is essentially rng ) and you have yourself the most luck based game i've ever played in my life. You can finish top 5 three games in a row then have three games where you're 60/60 , last place, because you got stunned randomly by terrain before you could even get a weapon because for some reason these devs thought it would be a good idea to put random stun lanters all over the place which trigger whenever they want. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The game actually has desync. _childDocuments_.review: Naraka is a sick game that is held back by what I can only assume is a severe difference between what two video game communities want from their experience. I played a lot on launch and came back for around 5 hours after it went free to play and what I'm about to talk about was a problem back then and is an even bigger problem now. As I think a lot of people have pointed out in the reviews is the bot issue. What an average game to me and my friends looks like is walking around bored out of our minds massacring bots for like 10 or 15 minutes, then suddenly finding a fight of 20 people and getting instantly massacred by those people. In the last match I just played I realized why. The game has an actual MINORITY of real players. My friend and I found this out and I have a clip of it recorded because we walked around and killed some random team and then we started to walk away from their loot and a group of 6 bots spawned in literally directly in front of us. Then the bots instantly parried me by reading my inputs and reacting to them in an inhuman amount of time because the bots were on a harder difficulty. I know this because these bots only spawned in when there were 12 players left. That's right, TWELVE PLAYERS LEFT and at LEAST HALF of them were bots that hadn't been spawned in yet, so you couldn't interact with them until that point. And since they were in the final 15 or whatever, they had purple armor, purple weapons, and the ability to instantly read my inputs and parry me. This was in a RANKED match too.So if anyone read this and felt vindicated by this feeling of "why am I just walking around and finding NO REAL HUMANS" for like 10 to 20 minutes at a time, now you can understand why. In this part of my comment I'm going to speculate a bit so bear with me and try to understand I could be wrong about this. The reason I think this is happening is because the majority of the player base is from China, and in their culture being bad at ANYTHING is heavily stigmatized. They don't want what Americans want, they want to load in and feel good about being able to smash bots into pieces and tell their friends "yea I'm super good at this game check it out I have a high kill/death ratio" whereas us as westerners are told that being good at something isn't virtuous, but overcoming a struggle is virtuous, and we want to go in to a ranked mode and fight other players and win some, lose some, learn, and improve over time. That way if we get good, we EARNED it and it's something noteworthy and cool to show off to your friends. This whole problem has caused all the North American player base to abandon ship, and only exacerbates the problem since now there are almost no real players to put you against when you do queue up. Chinese players LOVE that about American servers, because the more bots the merrier. Expect to load into lobbies with about 15 to 20 real players, half of them will be Chinese players with VPNS connecting to US servers. Ever wonder why Chinese players cheat so much but Americans HATE cheaters? Maybe my speculation can give you insight as to why.As a final note, I wanna say I actually love this game. The core combat mechanics are pretty cool, simple enough but with enough depth that it can feel pretty good to mess around with. The graphics are awesome, I personally love the style and outfits and weapon skins and I loved making my character, Tarka Ji (the drunk guy) look like Jackie Chan so I could pretend to be the drunken master. The characters and unique abilities are fun to use, they genuinely feel interesting with different play styles. _childDocuments_.review: HERES A REVIEW THAT DOESN'T CRY ABOUT THE MTX SHOPSSeriously, just don't buy the cosmetics. I don't get the issue. Game is fine, just learn the game instead of crying that you died to things you don't understand. Tips:Light attacks will block/parry other Light attacks. Focus/Charged attacks (blue) will give you flinch resist against light attacks and can break someone else Focus/Charge.Counter (red) allows you to block any Focus/Charged attack (blue) which allows for a followup, disarming the opponent.Counter (red) can be interrupted by Light attacks.You can feint your Focus/Charged by hitting C (also Crouch when held). While Crouched you can do a low attack. If you're met with light attack (left click) spams there are 2 ways to combat this. Try to spam dodge out of it, left click attacks are typically horizontal while right clicks are vertical. Side step vertical slashes, back step horizontal. Or (best way) is to understand when their Focus attack comes out. Every 3rd attack is a focus attack so remember the animation of the 2nd attack for a weapon, then parry in the window between the 2nd and 3rd attack, allowing you to parry the third Focus.If you're playing against someone that's timing your 3 hit light combo you can hit C (crouch) to cancel your combo. So for example you'll do your 1st and 2nd hit then hit C breaking the combo making the next attack the 1st attack of the combo. You'll also do a slight lunge/slide attack when coming out of a sprint. The main use for this is sliding Focus attacks. One very nice technique is dodging (space bar) out of the way, immediately going into a sprint, then holding left or right click for your Focus attack. You'll then charge your Focus attack while sliding in the direction you were using it. I'm sure I'm missing more but there are quite a lot of ways to combat different situations and how you go about each fight will change based on your weapon. Tactics will change based on the weapon you and they have so keep these in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's a shameless cashgrab battle royale with every garbage monetization model possible AND it's b2p. Battlepass, loot boxes, cash-only skins, $20 buy in, 3 different DLC tiers. I wanted to get that part out of the way before I got into why I actually can't stand this game: every match has bots in it, and I'm not talking about the first 4 or 5 games they make you play with nothing but bots that literally run in place (which is absolutely insane to me, this teaches you nothing about the game), but even in ranked matches it seems like about half the lobby is filled with bots. I know this because I've sat and watched one of them repeatedly climb up a pole over and over again when I'm right under it in a bronze 3 ranked match.After looking it up, I guess you eventually get to the point where they stop flooding your matches with bots once you climb to a high enough rank, but I'm not looking to play a BR filled with bots, if that's what I was looking for I'd play warzone. The actual gameplay is pretty fun, I like the melee-focused BR approach and is something that's sorely lacking in the genre right now, especially after The Culling hurt itself in confusion years ago and eventually got shut down. There's a lot of technique that goes into fights when you start getting into the nitty gritty of it with animation cancelling, counters, weapon frames, really deep stuff like that, but unfortunately nothing in the game bothers to go that far into combat. The most you'll get is "press LMB to attack, press RMB for charge attack, press both at the same time to counter a charge attack", just the basics.I want to like this game and I've been begrudgingly trying to climb ranks to eventually get to the fun part, but I just can't bring myself to trudge through another 20 games filled with bots to get to the real people. Oh, and when you do eventually get to play against real people, there's a non-zero chance they're going to be lagging all over the place and hits won't register. No region lock makes this game a real mixed bag when it comes to quality of fights when you're up against people across the world with 200+ ping.TL;DR: Good idea, bad execution. Garbage business model, one of the only BRs I can think of that makes you pay to get in just to pay every other step of the way. No region lock, so expect to play against high-ping players that might have an advantage over you in combat. You've gotta put at LEAST 2 hours into the game before you start seeing real players, and even then you're still gonna have lobbies filled with bots presumably until you get out of bronze. There are too many prominent games in the genre to accept a standard this low, unless you're like me and are really just attracted to the melee aspect of it.

Collect an arsenal of classic gear, things that go 'pew-pew', maybe a thing or two that goes 'BOOM!', and some things that go 'BOING!', and definitely a thing that goes 'SCRATCH'. Does this smell like chloroform to you?
short_description: UnMetal is a 2D stealth action-adventure that pays homage to the classics with a healthy dose of humor and satire. You play as Jesse Fox, who is definitely NOT an elite commando, under arrest for a crime he didn't commit, and must escape a covert military base using his wits and fists.

_childDocuments_.review: I hid this review in the only safe place I had left, my ass.Honestly though, this game was an absolute treat to play. The game play is very authentic NES/MSX Metal gears, and is varied enough to stay interesting. There's even a couple of vehicle sequences that never felt overly frustrating and stayed fun. It truly felt authentic to the games its parodying with its very good mix of stealth/action and problem solving.Of course the other question on peoples' minds; "How is the humor?" Its done pretty well, nothing goes overly cringe territory, the game is just goofy enough to be entertaining but never goes too overly dumb. The game also explains any of the extreme silliness very well by wrapping it all up in its ending, it was pretty clever.This game is not going to last hours and hours but I've come to appreciate short games that don't wear out their welcome and remain entertaining throughout the whole thing. I completely recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Just a quick review of this little gem.Heavily inspired by Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake from the MSX in character design, general aesthetic and gameplay, UnMetal already has some very witty humour and I am barely an hour in. I loved MG2, quite possibly my fave in the series next to MGS3, and this seems to tick the same boxes of puzzle based exploration, sneaky combat, and challenging boss battles.My only negative point really is that, if you are familiar with Metal Gear 1 and 2 (again, MSX, not the NES titles) the bosses are pretty much carbon copies, albeit with some humorous additions. I'm hoping that won't be as true going forward, though this may also be true of various plot elements.Also, as MGS1 was essentially a 3D remake of MG2, expect some similarities from that title also.Though being a parody it is going to hit some of the same notes, and that's fine.Fun for sure, much more of a puzzler than the later Konami originals, but I think all the better for it.8 fights in a minefield/10
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a hard task to create something that pays homage to a beloved work, as no matter what happens it will always be compared to that original piece, often unfavorably. Against these odds, UnMetal manages to straddle the line of being both a parody and an exceptional example of a top-down stealth game more than able to stand up to such scrutiny. While the game’s inspirations are obvious, it’s the fact that it also stands out on its own merits which makes it special and worth playing for anyone longing for a retro experience or clever, enjoyable writing.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, so it's extremely cool to see a Metal Gear fan-game that takes so much from that title specifically. Things like puzzles, weapons and bosses but with original looks, functions and/or personalities. This game certainly doesn't take itself too seriously, when I saw the first few cutscenes it reminded me of old animated MGS parody videos.A lot of the puzzles make sense and are pretty enjoyable, especially when you've played the original Metal Gear games.The game has a good length and a fair price considering what type of game that it is. I can tell that this one will have it's replay value for me because I intend to find all of the "secrets" in the game among other things to complete.Overall, this is an excellent homage to some of the coolest games in my favourite game series: Metal Gear!PS. Mike is the best character in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Old school stealth game that every true mgs fan deserves to play. And if you like 2D adventures than this is for you too. The game is hillarious in a positive way. Unpredictable yet fun and engaging story with a massive plot. A variety of items, weapons, and equipment that you can combine and use to your advantage. A level up system  with a twist. You get to choose what skills you get through the game, which makes you play the game again and pick that other skills you didn't get the first time, for a whole different experience.Variety of unique bosses, each with their own strengths and weaknesses for you to exploit.Use you wit in this funny adventure story of the hero that saved the world. Or did he? Find out and have fun while you're at it.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I am sneaking behind a building in the middle of the night. Reaching a new screen, I spot a guard. He clearly has a cold, as he sneezes every few seconds. Every time he sneezes, a range circle appears around him. Curious about the meaning of this, I silently step on the circle. The guard sneezes. I say "Bless you!". The guard hears me and shoots me dead. This, I think as I laugh uncontrollably, is going to be one of the greatest games I've played in quite a while.That was my experience with the demo of Unmetal, and the moment I swore I'd buy this game on launch day, which I did. Playing the actual game I can attest that thankfully the demo is not misleading and the game stays in line with it. As you might have imagined just from the screenshots, this game is a clone/parody of the Metal Gear franchise, particularly the original first two MSX2 titles and MGS: Ghost Babel for the GBC.The most notorious thing about this game is the writing. It feels as if Hideo Kojima had handled the Metal Gear franchise to Jim Abrahams of "Airplane!" and "Hot Shots!" fame . It's zany, over the top and absolutely hilarious. But fortunately it doesn't just stay there. They didn't just slap some funny writing on a mediocre game. They actually bothered in making a fun experience as well. Unmetal recreates the style of classic 2D Metal Gear masterfully, while also adding a few more gameplay elements to keep the experience fresh.Just like in those classic games, stealth is your main weapon. But fortunately, being caught doesn't result in an instant game over and just causes an XP penalty. In keeping with the tradition of the franchise, Bosses are brutal, but not cheap, and you never feel like their attacks were unavoidable. Adding to the gameplay there are a few elements of graphic adventures, such as item combination and dialogue choices that directly affect your experience, which certainly adds to the replayability.From a technical standpoint, the game really shines. It takes the classic look of the old games and gives it better resolution and a higher range of colors. Sound and music are amazing, and every character is voice acted (at least in English and Spanish, no other language has its own set of voices for now).But honestly, the humor is really fantastic. I find myself picking certain dialogue choices just because I figure I'm likely to get the most amusing answer, even if it ends up making my experience a bit harder. You'll do the same, I guarantee you.Edit: I finished the whole thing. This might actually be my game of the year. It is absolutely fantastic through and through, to the very end.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: An old-school Metal Gear parody that manages to both subvert and outperform any expectations I had walking into it. Yes, there are jokes, foul-mouthed humour and much breaking of the 'fourth wall'; but behind all that swagger there's a modern indie stealth game that demands to be taken seriously.Each mission has a theme running through it. Each boss has a unique strategy you have to learn. Each guard you can KO without alerting them has some XP you'll need to level up and learn new skills.If there's something that sticks out as a negative for me, it's that you can't quite tackle each scenario any way you want. There's usually just one solution, one path or one choice to make.I can't complain too much, though. Not with all the laughs I had getting to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I came across this game through the Discovery Queue and got it during one of Steam's giant sales. I expected a silly little metal gear parody, which it is no doubt. What I was NOT expecting was that it would ALSO be a really well done, fun stealth-action throwback game with a great soundtrack. Generally, parody games are playable enough while being carried by their humorous premise, with most of the jokes just being variations of "Remember when [HERO] did THIS?!" or somesuch. UnMetal surprised me not just by being funny, but being CONSISTENTLY funny, and actually being "Laugh Out Loud" funny a lot of the time.The gameplay was also a huge surprise, in the best way. A lot of MGS fans have likely played the Christmas-themed parody "Merry Gear Solid: Secret Santa." It's a decent little game with a goofy premise, with neither the gameplay nor the parody aspect quite making it to "memorable" status. I had this in mind when I started up. I had my expectations blown away when the game played absolutely beautifully, merging the best aspects of NES nostalgia and modern QoL gameplay improvements. It not only controls well, and implements the controls and functions smoothly and intuitively, but is also a ton of fun to play.Long story short, this game is fun, hilarious, and MORE than worth the full price paid. Now, if only we could convince the devs to just make a fully modernized recreation of the original Metal Gear games with this engine... I know, I know, it couldd never happen... but, like... I'm just SAYING it would be so awesome
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game.  This game is funny, clever and hard. However, it doesn't know when to end the joke. It is like cousin who tells the same joke over and over. My main gripe with this game are horrendously long sections of insta death grinds and the painfully lengthen ending of the game. The first 75% of the game had me a laughing with delight.Rolling with the ridiculously over the top stuff. The challenges were tough but mostly fair. Then around level 7-9 it just becomes a grind. I am forcing myself to play, just to see the end. Initially, I planned to replay the game to see what other options. I won't be now. If you are a fan of metal gear, this game is worth the ticket price but know it peters out towards the end.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I'm surprised how funny this game ended up being. I was concerned it was just going to be reference based humour, and while there is a bit of that its otherwise genuinely hilarious. It feels like the sort of thing Lesley Nielsen would star in.Gameplay is pretty solid too. Very good stealth mechanics that hearken to the original Metal Gear. It often tries to change things up with escape sequences, boss fights and other set piece moments, these can be a bit hit or miss, but even the ones that don't land are short enough to not overstay their welcome.Definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly funny parody that stands on its own as an enjoyable and challenging game. Some frustrating trial and error puzzles and later boss fights can really test your patience, but the overall campaign is a solid ride with a surprising amount of gameplay quirks and variety.And to put the cherry on top, its humor not only recognizes its absurdity, it uses it to create and justify ridiculous scenes that serve the overall tone and keeps the whole game exciting and fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal has a lot of charm going for it. Refreshingly affectionate toward its inspiration and never overplaying its humor, with base gameplay that nicely mimics the old 2D Metal Gear games with some welcome tweaks. But the experience is brought down by frustrating boss fights and trial-and-error puzzles on the bad side of old-school design, which is compounded by a bafflingly bad lategame level design decision and a post-credits twist that will make you wonder what the point of the story was. UnMetal is a net positive experience, but a handful of bad decisions hold it back from being a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest; I believe UnMetal has a very distinct vision, one that developer UnEpic Fran has delivered on with gusto. Unfortunately, I don't believe that vision has made for an especially entertaining experience and, for many players, will fast become grating. UnMetal is a 'Hot Shots'-esque pastiche of Metal Gear Solid, albeit one with a far simpler storyline. Resembling the NES original and playing like its PSX sequel - initially at least - the opening stages are familiar inventory-juggling, patrol-avoiding fare that hint at an enjoyable retro demake. Sadly, the further you play into UnMetal, the more this idea becomes diluted; bu the seventh mission, I was genuinely fatigued. The comedy, while a welcome reprieve from the straight-faced MGS series, fast outstays its welcome, dragging jokes on for long enough that the punchlines are at best predictable, at worst utterly tepid. Eventually, they become intrusive, pausing the game for minutes of awkward shtick before divulging mission-crucial information. UnEpic, the first game in the 'Un' series had similarly dim humour, but it was never this insistent. Fran is arguably better suited to a more natural, serious style of writing, as demonstrated in the superb Ghost 1.0. While players tire of the writing, however, the game is slowly tiring of itself. Frequently, UnEpic drops all pretences of being a stealth game and decides to change genres entirely. An arcade shooter. A choose-your-own-adventure book (complete with instant failures, I would add). A Jetpack-esque submarine adventure. Such variety wouldn't be an issue if they weren't so often a chore. One section tasks the player with reviving any enemies they kill via a slow revive animation. The section is poorly justified via a lame comedy exchange earlier in the chapter, but dedicating an entire section to this torturous, stop-start style of gameplay means the joke is only ever on the player.UnMetal is a game with a vision. For those that recognise that vision, it might even be called a success. But I can't imagine many people sharing a vision so schizophrenic, so player hostile and so mistakenly sure of its humour.UnEpic Fran is an incredibly talented developer who has an otherwise commendable track record. UnMetal is not an example of shoddy workmanship; rather, it's an example of a developer taking a swing and missing the mark quite spectacularly. Play Ghost 1.0 instead.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I like Fox, I like Mike, I like the other Mike, and I like the music. The game has a charm to it and the pixel art is decently done. (The consistency of the artstyle in cutscenes can be a slightly off, its the 1970s? but the US military is wearing UCP from the 2000s? Little things like that.)The gameplay can be a frustrating depending on your objectives for the chapter, though its still less frustrating than the actual two MSX Metal Gear Titles. I can commend Fran and his team for streamlining the mechanics compared to MG1-2. (Wish I could prone though, go under tables, something like that. Fox is trying to be covert after all, at least we get a combat roll. The abilities Fox DOES have are solid, heh.)Some of the jokes and swears fall short of their intended humor. But for a game originally written in Spanish then translated to English the dub is serviceable. I think I like Mike's various deliveries the best, the Drill Sargent is a close second.I'd like to see more of Fox's adventures in the future, but the after credits sequence kinda ruins the whole thought of that for me, its a good joke to end on though. Credit where it's due.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed this game. The dialog can go on a bit long at times though which can drag. Also the humor is hit or miss and there is a lot of attempts at it. Aside from those 2 complaints the rest of it is pretty good. The graphics are 8 bit style and they are done well. The music is fitting and some of it is really well done. _childDocuments_.review: This caricature of the original Metal Gear (1987) concentrates on sophomorical humor, simple puzzles, and a slight upgrade to the pixel graphics compared to the ones of the past. Honestly, if the repeated schoolboy-leveled jokes were not a issue for some, then the sudden, instant death scenarios strewn around the game and the limited (quick)save options presented will be.

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun and funny at first but it wears off after a few chapters. The comedy gets old and running through countless screens to retry a fight or silly chat to make sure you get it right 10 times is just annoying. I think if they toned it down a bit on how silly it tries to be and made some of the tasks a bit less complex, it would be more entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Kept you waiting, huh?Yeah, you did. But ya know what? it was worth itUnMetal is a parody/love letter to the Metal Gear franchise that I know and love. It's a flawed but enjoyable experience with a fantastic sense of humor that got several laugh out loud moments from me.The stealth system of UnMetal is a lot of fun, though does leave a little to be desired. Instead of forming your own strategy as Metal Gear would frequently allow, frequently, UnMetal wants you to figure out what the game wants you to do. While I don't think either approach is inherently wrong, I do prefer when I have several options and can figure out what to do for myself. You do have a variety of different weapons, but several are just objectively more useful than others and oftentimes are only intended to be used in boss battles and such.None of this is to say the stealth of UnMetal isn't enjoyable, because it is. There's also a wide range of boss battles and other mandatory action scenes. Bosses can be quite challenging and punishing if the player panics and tries to act too quickly without formulating a strategy.UnMetal also features a rather hilarious dialogue options system that can alter the levels layout sometimes or perhaps get the player killed in an amusing way if you make the wrong decision.However, for me, UnMetal's biggest drawback is it's bleed effect. Not because the effect itself is necessarily a bad thing but just because of how often it happens. Almost every time you take a hit from anything, you'll start bleeding and have to use your (thankfully unlimited) supply of bandages to patch yourself up. Not a bad idea if this was a randomly inflicted effect, but it happens way too often for my liking.The game's scanlines also could really use an option to turn those off.All in all, UnMetal is a solid love letter to Metal Gear (pun intended) and well worth the price of admission to me.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This game somehow captured all of the absurdity and absolute chaos of the early MG and MGS games into one neat package. The stealth gameplay is okay, certainly passable for an indie title. The visual and audio design pay homage to their source material with great respect. The tongue in cheek jokes/dialogue (which is fully voiced might I add!) are hilarious and reason enough to play the game. If you have even a passing interest in metal gear, this is a MUST PLAY. This is to metal gear what Kung Fury was to 80's action films... which I guess is a good thing. You can use a broken toilet bowl to save your progress any where in the world - 11/10 for that alone.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Great game (in many aspects) !What I enjoy the most is the way the story unfolds by Having protagonist Jessie Fox The map starts with a plain blue coordinate paper, then gradually adds boxes, trees, guards, even time of the day to be consistent with the content as Jessie speaks. The whole process is like watching how the level is being built, quite unique and interesting.UnMetal has 10 chapters, each contains a fairly big map, the later ones are much bigger. I'd say this is a half action half click and point game, the player needs to have good skill and a creative mind. Dealing with various enemies requires precise timing and good control,  then a sharp eye and to search the floor thoroughly for essential items, for they could be on fainted guards, in random boxes, or well hidden inside unimpressive items. A good example is when asked for a pair of encrypted radios, I easily acquired the crypt radios but was not sure how to decrypt them. Turns out and the work is done. Speaking of the combine system, kudos to the idea of combining a Y branch with an eye patch to make it a sling shot.I can't say I know the MGS franchise well, but the memory of Phantom Pain is still fresh, and unMetal reminds me of the game. Various items can be picked like cigar butt and eye patch reminds me of the game, not sure how a cigar works but once the eye patch is equipped the player can only see half of the screen. Besides, the protagonist Fox looks just like Snake, the devs are paying good tribute. The fights are challenging. Game has several mini bosses, but it is the regular guards who bring me more trouble. First of all, even if Jessie has a gun he needs to use it wisely, as the game does not allow killing so the player must use one medkit after hurting an enemy. Sling shot or fists are better choices, however if an enemy spots him an alarm will be raised, which calls a team of enemies on site from all the directions searching the area and all the doors are locked down before they think it is clear. The AI is high, I rarely escaped an alarm lol. Good point is it is not much too hard to deal with both regular enemies and bosses, auto and manual save points are not far, players can almost always make temporary saves at will.Besides fighting, player also get to do stealth, submarine driving, work out the way of a maze, detect mine fields (I like this part, it reminds me of Splinter Cell), in various environments. In additional are so many good jokes, like  The story is solid and well built. The nano suits and holographic image, the story is full of ups and downs, heroic but feeling very authentically real, making me feel like watching a James Bond or Jason Bourne script. I especially loved the last part where enter the room X to trigger . Those little ideas are brilliant, and fun.The only thing I'd complain about are the bugs. Yep, I encountered 2 game-broken bugs and had to restart the entire level, one time a box with a mission object won't break, the other is I run out of the map and can't get back. I usually do not keep playing any games with game breaking bugs, but UnMetal is well worth my time to play the level again.Last, I enjoyed reading the behind-the-scenes artbook before the boss fight. Really beautiful work, I wish to get a physical copy of the game. The ending after the credits is a surprise. :) Game is a gem, I would love to play again some time later.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal is a weird game in the best possible way.The protagonist has been captured by the US Army for coming to their base with a Russian helicopter, and must now explain how he ended up here. The game is therefore a flashback of his story, as he tells it. This weird setup soon become very interesting, as the game reacts to the narration and our protagonist doesn't seem particularly reliable, leaving us to guess as to what is real or not. I'm usually not fond of dumb protagonist, but this one works great, it's dumb enough to be funny, but serious enough to not get into the way of what is a surprisingly fun stealth game. It's not particularly deep, but it's engaging, and varied enough to stay interesting for the whole game.Overall, UnMetal is a fantastic experience. The story, gameplay and characters mix together into a unique game, which doesn't overstay its welcome, it was a great 10H

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal is a hilariously fun and addictive 2-D stealth game! Harking back to the past of old Metal Gear on NES, it is an ironic take on the MGS franchise. I literally beat the $#!% out of someone in a bathroom stall! MGS V / 5

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal: the zany Metal Gear game you should be playing	Austin Powers is a parody of spy thrillers like James Bond. In that case, Unmetal is a silly equivalent to the beloved Metal Gear games during the MSX era.  Unmetal wears the Metal Gear franchise of yore on its shoulder like a badge of honor.  While there are some missteps along the way, the game is nevertheless a fun, hilarious, absurd, and thoroughly enjoyable ride from beginning to end.Story:	Players take on the role of Jesse Fox, a civilian who has been arrested for a crime he didn't commit (a statement our hero constantly reminds us of).  The story is told through a series of "flashbacks" as Jesse narrates his yarn to others.  This type of narrative structure is exceptionally clever in how it is executed within the game.  For example, several "choose your own adventure" moments allow you to change the story as it develops.  All are silly in their own ways and can change the structure of the actions in numerous aspects.  One instance in a sewer gives you the option to choose between whether there were rats present.  In choosing option no, Jesse narrates a silly alternative that is worth selecting.  Having Jesse be an unreliable narrator brings a lot of replay value in trying different outcomes. Furthermore, it establishes itself as what the crux of the story really is.  A silly parody.Gameplay:	From the start, the game is designed in the style of past metal gear games.  From a top-down view, players move Jesse as he sneaks, fights, and punches his way through an interactive environment.  Much like the story affects the gameplay, the same can be said when playing the game. Specific actions done by the player may cause a cutscene to occur with humorous dialogue thrown in for good measure.  As the game is focused on sneaking, players need to adhere to the old-school rules of being undetected and take out enemies.  In return, you receive experience, which allows you to gain skills to assist you on your adventure upon leveling up.	No metal gear parody game would be complete without boss fights, and Unmetal delivers in that respect as well.  Whether you are fighting some rando human or something big, the boss encounters offer tons of variety that nothing feels stale.  Even on normal difficulty, many bosses are a challenge. As a result, you may die a few times before you find the right strategy for success.  But the battles are fun in their own right and offer a needed change to the gameplay that allows you to use your arsenal. Level Design:	The game comprises ten levels ranging from a military base, jungle, sewer, and dock, to name a few.  The attention to detail to each level is genuinely spectacular, whether it is the movement of trees in the wind or the animations of characters and objects.  The areas feel lived in and set the level's mood; it’s a bit of a shame that they can be a bit small, and some levels go by so quickly you don’t really get a chance to enjoy them.   I really appreciated the developers hiding an Easter egg in the behind-scenes making of the game.  This adds a level of depth to how and why certain aspects of the game developed.  Likewise, the game hides many secrets that improve stats if the player is observant. Limitations:   	However, not everything is perfect, and the game does have a few cracks in the lens. For example, inventory management can be a bit of a pain. You will often cycle to your inventory screen to use an item, bringing the game to a bit of a crawl.  While there is an option to shortcut four items to the right joystick, I found this unresponsive at times.  Such as during boss fights, more often than not, you will be using the inventory screen to accurately select the item you need.  At best, it is a minor hiccup to the fluidity of the gameplay.   One genuine criticism lies in the occasional difficulty spikes that occur.  Regardless of the difficulty setting, there are times when the game throws the kitchen sink at you. For example, one particular boss fight involving a helicopter requires you to drive a vehicle while trying to dodge incoming fire and not hitting the embankment perfectly.  Just getting hit once causes a game over, and you have to repeat the experience again.  Two others are in the form of puzzles and one mistake, and it's game over, requiring a lot of trial and error.  One puzzle, in particular, has "almost" no information to correctly figure out the solution, and that can be tedious.  Thankfully, the game autosaves before most boss fights, or you can use a portable potty (the game's alternative save system).   Additionally, the zone of the proximity of the enemy's field of view is a bit questionable.  While the game gives you a mini-tutorial when encountering a new foe, it is sometimes difficult to know where the enemy's view began and ended.  Sometimes you can hug a wall underneath a camera to avoid detection. Other times, you can't.  Or you need to collect items from boxes that may or may not be within view.  Another instance of the trial and error issue I was discussing earlier.Conclusion:	Unmetal is definitely a game worth playing!  Despite the flaws in difficulty spikes, trial and error gameplay, and some inventory management, the game was a blast to play.  It would be even better if there was a new game plus option to bring your fully decked out Jesse into battle, but that is splitting hairs at this point.  The game is a slide-splitting zany parody with truly clever jokes that consistently land.  While flawed at points, the gameplay still excels in its own rights. It delivers that tactical espionage players look forward to with laughs along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal is quite obviously a Metal Gear parody. The jokes are stupid, but often funny, reminding me of movies with Leslie Nielsen.Even though it may seem like "just a parody", it does have more to offer: very nice pixel art and animation, good music and sounds. And pretty Solid gameplay that consists mainly of sneaking, exploring and fighting bosses. There are also some mini-games and occasional gimmicks that help to keep the gameplay fresh.The game can be challenging, but isn't very hard, although you do die quite a lot due to many things that kill you in one hit. Some of the jokes also result in your unexpected demise, which you can prevent after reloading. This doesn't mix well with the save system that leaves a lot of room for improvement.Despite that, it's a perfectly enjoyable experience. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Overall UnMetal is a really good love letter to the original Metal Gear games, and ultimately manages to stand on its own. As the game was a mostly positive experience for me on every aspect. Here aresome specific negatives about the game: - Even though the dialogue is mostly great, there are times when there's just too much of it. Some scenes go on for a bit too long. (And I don't mean certain jokey scenes that are the way they are on purpose.) - Couple of the segments towards the end of the game were just the most unfun (haha get it) I've experienced in a game for some time. They felt unnecessarily frustrating.- Couple of trial-and-error -type of encounters, that get stale fast. But luckily they are short.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good parody of Metal Gear games. I found myself pausing the game just to laugh. But more importantly, it's a good game too. I think I would still find this game fun, funny and engaging even if I wasn't someone who has been playing Metal Gear games since 1998.Edit: About my playtime, I bought this game on the Nintendo Switch so I can play it on the go. I have way more playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game expecting a cheap parody, but the gameplay is way more solid than it has any rights to. It's also very varied, revealing new gameplay mechanics until the very end - no levels feel like filler. The boss fights are also quite creative. The game was very satisfying to beat. Also gave me quite a few laughs.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I had to somehow get out of a stinky prison cell. I prepared a good trap for a guard. I fooled him that I hang myself, he came closer and punched him. Yes, I could kill him, but I'm not a killer, am I? During my whole escape, I didn’t kill anyone. My favourite weapons were my bare hands and a slingshot. Yeah, you hear the slingshot. I crafted it, and I know it’s sort of childish, but three shots of depleted uranium balls are enough to say goodbye to someone. How do I get those balls? Easy, I just punched some crates and voilà. I figured out that smashing various objects is good for relieving stress, finding useful items and even uncovering hidden rooms. Soon, I encountered imprisoned Colonel Alan Harris. I hacked two walkie-talkies that got from guards so we could talk to each other. The Colonel helped me a lot. When I got lost, he gave me advice on what to do.On my way to freedom, I visited ten locations, each offering different challenges. I had to create different tools by combining items from my inventory in order to progress. In some places, I also had to choose between bad choices or... another bad choice. If I thought it would be easy, I was wrong. So if you have to escape from prison, think twice about what you choose on your way. I met many guards who were easy to beat, but I had to be careful because one bad move could set off an alarm that would cause a lot of trouble. Thanks to humans, they invented the WC (yep, I mean toilets) and a potty, both of which can save my progress. What an original idea!The regular guards weren't my only enemies. Some guys looked like bosses. One threw grenades at me, another tried to shoot me in his office, a crazy guy used a tank TANK! to stop me, and many more. I have to say that each of them was original and used their methods to stop someone who was imprisoned for a crime they didn't commit, but they all have one thing in common. Each of them had their own way of fighting, so I had to learn their moves and find their weaknesses. Some were easy, some were hard and they almost got me, but I overcame them.

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is a retro-style action-adventure game developed by Studio Unepic and released in 2021. The game is a parody of classic 80s and 90s action movies, and it follows the story of a former soldier who has been wrongly accused of a crime and must escape from a high-security military prison.One of the standout features of Unmetal is its unique art style and humor. The game features pixelated graphics that are reminiscent of classic games from the 80s and 90s, but with modern animations and effects. The game's humor is also a highlight, with numerous references to classic action movies and pop culture.The game's gameplay is fast-paced and action-packed, with a range of weapons and gadgets that the player can use to take down enemies and solve puzzles. The game also features a range of stealth elements, which can be used to avoid detection and sneak past guards.The game's storyline is engaging and well-written, with a range of interesting characters and plot twists that keep the player engaged. The game also offers multiple endings, based on the player's choices and actions throughout the game.However, the game's difficulty can be challenging at times, especially during boss battles and stealth sections. Additionally, the game's length is relatively short, with the main story taking around 4-6 hours to complete.Overall, Unmetal is a fun and entertaining game that offers a unique and humorous take on the action-adventure genre. Its retro-style graphics and engaging storyline make it a must-play for fans of classic 80s and 90s action movies. However, its challenging difficulty and short length may not be suitable for all players.

_childDocuments_.review: represents something that I honestly have not encountered much of in my days of gaming: the genre parody. Now when it comes to film, we can talk all day about excellent parodies like Naked Gun or any Mel Brooks picture. These take the conventions of a popular genre and turn them on their head while also maintaining the spirit of what is being satirized. So, just as  is both a comedic satirization of both  and the greater space adventure genre so too is  a parody of both Metal Gear and the larger stealth action genre. However, a comedy can be funny and maybe have some of the finer technical aspects of film-making glossed over. The same cannot really be said of a game; you can have the most hilariously written game but if it is not paired with fun and engaging gameplay there’s going to be issues. Luckily  succeeds in both fronts. 	At its core  is able to provide satisfying stealth action gameplay while also utilizing its game mechanics to further enhance the games comedic satire. This game is fun to play but more specifically it is fun to master. Perfect stealth is encouraged through the earning of experience when enemies are taken down without being detected. This is a great touch and encourages players to perfect their strategies in each level to get the most benefit. However, you could also say that perfect stealth, especially in the later levels, is demanded as it is the only viable strategy. I’ve seen this brought up as a major point of criticism but I believe the game is correct to prioritize stealth gameplay. Combat is at its best in  during its boss and other designed encounters. Bosses give you a singular target with a unique pattern to maneuver about and fight while designed combat sequences allow for a balanced encounter that lets the player utilize force. This has been the case of nearly all Metal Gear games, combat is not encouraged between bosses and designed alert phases because fighting your way through isn’t the point and  follows that design principle brilliantly. We’re left with a game that’s fun to stealthily weave through that still has an intense fight with a nuclear submarine that puts your reaction times to the test.	But that’s not all!  uses its gameplay to make jokes too! This was especially fun to see. There are plenty of moments in which the game utilizes its inventory and combination system similar to that of  in order to deliver jokes about the absurdity of what is happening in game. Mixing ‘Chloro’ and ‘Form’ to make chloroform, combining four C1’s to get one C4 and it goes on. These are small things but they show an effort to bring some of the parody into the gameplay itself as opposed to having it all maintained in cut scenes and dialog.	If I had to guess the largest point of criticism that could be leveled at this game it may be difficulty. On hard I found this game to be frustrating at points but never unfair. Save and checkpoints are frequent and you are never far from throwing yourself right back into a boss fight. So, I found it to be a quite rewarding challenge to memorize patterns and perfect my own skills to take these challenges on. Some may take issue with the classic style of stealth gameplay it can be simplistic but what is presented is nothing short of very well curated. No area is dull or un-interesting nor is any one segment of the game particularly worse than any other. It’s a good time, I especially enjoyed the barracks stage with a group of jogging soldiers roaming the base. Alright there is a weird segment where you have to pilot a submarine that’s unlike any other part of the game but it isn’t very long, I still don’t really get why it’s in the game though and probably does weaken the overall experience more than it adds. 	Alright the gameplay has me sold because I’m a nerd who can appreciate old MSX metal gear and it’s good but the main selling point for most people here is probably going to be the comedy. Don’t worry the game is funny. Yes, some of the jokes are groaners. Yes, some jokes go on for too long. But this is comedy it’s going to be highly subjective to individual tastes. My favorite parts lay mostly in the way the game is being framed.  is a story within a story and events and logic change based on player choice at certain points as the story is being told. It feels as though Jesse Fox is laying down tracks as the train moves down them and that’s exactly what’s happening. I find this premise quite funny and the ultimate payoff satisfying. Take that and then add in plenty of nods and references to other genres and movies and sure not all of them are as hilarious but there is an admirable vision that I believe is executed on well. Perhaps decreasing the amount of direct reference humor like the drill sergeant for instance would help keep the game more cohesive but overall, the game does not rely heavily on those types of jokes. The game sets out the goal and executes quite well on what somebody would sound like trying to manufacture a Metal Gear type plot out of thin air and for this I’d recommend it.	It’s likely that no other game will come in the Metal Gear series and in a way seeing something like  gives me some form of joy in the sense that it’s good to see someone create something so clearly inspired by it. Sure, there is room for improvement, stealth could be a bit more in depth similar to MG2 with the addition of crawling but I can see that probably wasn’t the point. Sure, you could trim some of the fat and less critical jokes and segments but there would not be much to cut. I can say the same about some of the  games not every narrative beat is always necessary nor is every section uniquely fun. Piloting a submarine may be a bit goofy and a different type of gameplay but so is piloting an RC missile through vents to blow up a generator in a room with the US president. So, in a way I love this game for the entirety of what it is and I think every fan of  should definitely give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rank A- (85-88%)Great game - play this if you can!!See my profile for more details about my reviews.Additional notes: Fran strikes again with another great game. After using and abusing the Metroidvania genre in unEpic and Ghost 1.0, he tackles the very unique genre of MGS, and especially the first two in 2D. Good chance, I had done these 2 and MGS is my favorite of the 5 games. In other words, I am the perfect target for this parody and love letter to the genre. If you never cared for it though, I wonder if the game could get you interested. I read some negative reviews complaining about the lack of action and the presence of "too many puzzles"... these people obviously never played the whole series of MGS. If there is ONE game that gives back a lot to MG1&2 while adding some personal quirky and ludicrous content like in unEpic or Ghost, this is unMetal! Obviously it is not a masterpiece, obviously it is sometimes very trashy (too many swearwords!) and bad taste (the acorn running from squirrels with Benny Hill music...). But so many jokes are good, and the gameplay is so rich and impeccable. For the price, and for 20 hours of good gameplay and funny story, this is one great little game!

_childDocuments_.review: I will say I have been really excited for this game, and I will say, the first couple of chapters delivered on the awesome gameplay and hilarious humor it showed on the demo. After the first couple of chapters though, you start to see the game's true repetitive mechanics come to play. For all the chapters there seems to be a theme of tasks that you need to do and pretty much repeat them till you find a boss and kill them and move on to the next.  You can't kill anyone which, sure it adds a challenge. But it becomes almost impossible to use the handgun when swarms of enemies encounter you. Speaking of the enemy, once you're seen, it's game over. There are very few times you can get away, and when you do, you're often wasting medkits on yourself and enemies you've downed. This repetitive pattern that is throughout the whole game really takes a toll on the player.Everything I've experienced is on the Normal difficulty. I'm sure there's going to be some GeT GuD nerds on here but honestly, if you say you didn't die to the point where you closed the game out and had to return to it at a later time, you're lying or were playing it on easy. I was really excited for this game but just can not bring myself to give it a good review. After the first 8 hours it was tolerable, now it's just annoying and the story isn't really funny anymore. You can see they definitely ran out of content.

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal follows in the footsteps of Fran's other work and presents a solid game that flips the formula on the basics of the genre that it's presented in, but does it with fantastic humorous writing. There's careful crafting of the jokes, ranging from stupid yet laughable to clever and gut busting. It definitely understands the material that it's parodying, using the tropes of the genre well while crafting a unique experience. Let's be clear: while the gameplay and other elements of this game are good, it's the writing that is the shining star and deserves your purchase. It uses the pace to surprise the player with gags, but it also keeps an underlying story underneath that's still worth following. Characters are stereotypical but not at the same time, leading to a unique experience that's going to stick with you in the first few hours (of what I played so far), and I'll want to come back to it until its complete.The gameplay, while not on the level of the writing, still is able to use the comedy and tropes of the genre well and keep you invested while still feeling like you're a sneaky soldier. It takes inspiration from Metal Gear (NES), and while it's not trying to be anything ground breaking, it's able to use slight shifts in the mechanics to help vary the experience and keep you having fun. The stealth system is basic but works well enough (even if it's not the most precise). Sound design is well put together and gives you the information you need, and boss fights while coming down to basic patterns will make you appreciate the absurd situations you're put into.Really, in the first two hours I played, I started turning off my Reviewer brain and just was enjoying the experience. Let me tell you, for a game to do that, it's got to be something special, and Unmetal understands how to let the player have fun. It's not flashy, it's not shiny, but you know what: it's Fun and that's all you need.

_childDocuments_.review: I first heard about this game a couple months ago and was interested when I saw the retro NES Metal Gear style game play. I played the demo and loved the humor in it. I was excited to give it a go when the game came out and it did not disappoint. The gameplay is great. My only complaint about it is that at times, it's hard to get right up behind somebody to punch them if you're approaching them vertically without alerting them. It's probably more to do with the 2D design than anything else but I had to knock a slight point off for that. Fortunately, after the first few chapters, you get chloroform which you can hold from a greatest distance so you won't run into that issue again.The story and humor is really where the game shines. At the end of the day, the gameplay is more reminiscent of a NES game that feels really polished and a bit modernized. The humor is what kept me coming back for more. There's a good amount of stupid humor and they even troll the player big time. As an example (minor spoilers), the first chapter has a few sections where you're retelling your story and you can pick how the story goes, 1 guard vs 2, a sleeping guard vs an alert guard, etc. The game trains you into thinking you can pick the easier option for some encounters. Well in chapter 2, there's a moment where you can choose how many tentacles the boss has. You can pick 2, 4, or 6. Naturally, you want to pick two because it'll be easier but the game tricks you to say "2.... DOZEN tentacles!" and the fight becomes way harder than it needs to be. Every mission had several moments that actual made me laugh shaking my head even if it lead to a game over screen. I didn't care about any of the game over screens because it was always hilarious leading up to it.Overall, this is probably my indie game of the year when I really wasn't expecting it to me more than just a fun game play for nostalgia reasons. Absolutely top notch, I think everyone should give it a go, especially if you liked the old school Metal Gear style games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had been on my radar since around June last year, when it was originally going to release. UnMetal is an all-around solid title: The gameplay is fun, the story is hilarious, and it exudes quirky charm as a love letter to MSX/NES Metal Gear and that era of gaming as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: "Because no one threatens  to tell the truth."One of my favorite tropes in gaming is the Unreliable Narrator. When it's done well, a narrator messing with the story can make for a really interesting, twisted story in a way that isn't possible otherwise. In video games, it works even better, because it allows the gameplay to change dynamically as the narrator remembers things, makes corrections, or makes things up.  is one of the finest examples I've ever seen of this type of game, sitting alongside  Jesse Fox weaves a creative, layered, and over-the-top story, twisting the game world to his whim, with an all-timer of a bait-and-switch at the end.In terms of overall gameplay,  is largely the same as  and  with a bunch of modern quality-of-life features added in. You do  need to select the right keycard in your inventory, thank goodness. You'll sneak around and perform takedowns on guards (and drones, and fish people (yes, really)), avoid being spotted, fight a boss at the end of each chapter, you know the drill. It's solidly executed, although it can feel a bit hand-holdey at times. If you've enjoyed the Metal Gear games, especially the 2D ones, you'll feel right at home here. Also, fitting in with the shifting narrative, you'll be given dialogue choices with a direct impact on gameplay at several points.Be warned, however, that the gameplay can boil down to trial-and-error sometimes. You'll get a number of game-overs from one or another of the game's practical jokes. Fortunately, the game is also pretty generous with its manual and automatic save points, so you should never lose much progress. Still, if you're the type to get easily frustrated, this might not be the game for you.Speaking of practical jokes, I have to talk about the game's humor. Obviously, UnMetal is a parody of Metal Gear, and a piss take in many ways. It's full of references, and much of the comedy hinges on those references and shout-outs. What this means is, while it's  funny to people in the know, it's not very accessible. That said, you can enjoy the non-referential jokes if you're not as media-savvy as the intended audience.Also, the game is fully voice-acted! I just felt the need to mention that. Some of the lines are a bit stilted or disjointed, but on the whole, it adds to the experience. The characters are so much more lively than they would have been otherwise. I'm also pleased at how the F-bombs have been toned down compared to . I don't normally complain about profanity, but it was overused in  to the point of being distracting. The dialogue in  still leans on F-bombs too much, but not nearly as badly, and the military setting makes it feel more organic. is an unabashedly fun and funny game that delivers a unique story in a way few other games can. No wonder I keep coming back to it.  for fans of Metal Gear. However, if you're not familiar with the stealth-action genre, you may want to try a different title first.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a soft recommend. One of the first three console games I ever owned was the original Metal Gear. Years ago when I saw this, I wanted to get it but was suspicious about it being a "nostalgia bait indie cash grab" game. So it sat on my wishlist until recently. I also appreciate parodies, but the humor didn't really click with me, somewhere between dad jokes and cheesy puns.Gameplay is similar to Metal Gear, but unlike it, UnMetal has several parts where the puzzles suffer from Moon Logic, wasting the players time. There is no explanation for some of these puzzles, with no motivator for why it should be solved that way, and I enjoy puzzles. Again, most puzzles are trapped in moon logic solutions.To expound on time wasted even further, there are several parts in UnMetal where the MC is faced with responding to questions with just 3 words to choose from. There is no context for where the words will lead (and I mean NO context at all), and is a big waste of game time going through and finding out that each answer/response could be wrong. This is peppered throughout the game, masquerading as humor, and is a complete waste of time going through a needless process of elimination to get the correct answer set up, and moving on with the game.If you can get past moon logic puzzles and meta gaming a series of correct responses, then there is gem to be found for $5, but I wouldn't pay more than $10 for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, this is a difficult review to write, because I wanted to like this game so much. So, from someone who just wanted an old school Metal Gear experience mixed in with some of the toilet humor and pop culture references from Unepic...this game just isn't fun.Some sociopath developer of this game decided that slowing down your progression with near constant interruptions would be a good idea, so that you never actually play long enough to get a hang of the controls. Then, you basically get to die a ridiculous amount and essentially just learn how to beat the game (not PLAY the game) by sheer trial and error. Then, instead of even allowing you the ability to perform any action to progress in any sort of freeform manner, the game places constant restrictions on you and basically puts your whole experience on rails. All of this serves to only frustrate you as a player, to the point where any "jokes" just land totally flat.It's not the funny Metal Gear combined with MacGyver that it could have been. It's a sociopath's idea of what a game should be in that you have to do exactly what they want you to do at all times, while telling you "jokes" to make you feel better about constantly dying to gaslight you into believing you're having fun when you're clearly not. And trust me, if you get this game in its current state...there WILL be a point in time that you hit like a brick wall, where you come to the sudden and unquestionable conclusion that this game just is not fun. It comes around the 48th GAME OVER screen from you dying in one hit (as usual) from something you had no prior experience with in the game. Do yourself a favor and hard pass on this one. They would need to retool the game entirely to make it actually fun in order to make it even remotely likable first.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give this game a negative review, but I do feel it's justified. This game started out super strong; I laughed my ass off for the first two hours or so. The gameplay was good, the inventory items amusing and the story was keeping me invested for the most part.Unfortunately, much like a bad comedy movie, this game starts forgetting to be funny and just kind of starts being a regular game without the humor about four or so hours in, and it quickly becomes kind of boring and stale. It becomes too concerned with making you run around getting this and fetching that to get through the next hurdle rather than sticking to hilarious dialogue and story events.I had super high hopes but at this point I just got bored and even after sticking with it for a while, things didn't improve all that much so I just threw in the towel and uninstalled it.That said, I did enjoy this just enough to check out the developer's other titles and they have enough positive reviews that I will likely purchase Ghost and give that a try next.

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly not that great.The pixel art is very nicely done and the game itself is polished, I have encountered no bugs during the time i played.The combat mechanics aren't bad, using ranged weapons just takes a little getting used to. The boss fights are completely manageable and usually have some unique gimmick to them, which makes them less boring.The jokes range from being okay to being outright unfunny, though that's just a personal opinion.The gameplay loop however, consists of being told exactly what you're supposed to right away and then just ticking off boxes on your list of chores instead of being able to properly explore the game and its' mechanics. The items you get range from useful things like med packs to being completely gimmicky and kind of useless.With this fairly linear game design and a barely engaging story, likely due to the fact that it's just a parody, the game simply doesn't feel worth playing to me.If you are a fan of the old metal gear game, you can give this game a try. If you aren't, then I simply cannot recommend this game to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is many things. Firstly, it is agreat homage and excellent parody to those original stories of Metal Gear, back before Hideo Kojima started to believe his own hype and be weird for the sake of weird. The graphics are smooth, the music is simple and effective, and the ambience with the levels seems solid. Then we get to the problems:The humour, though originally brilliant, gets tedious and repetitive by LVL 4 or 5. It breaks the tone and flow of you playing the game. You can't go two screens without a joke or reference from our unreliable narrator. Some of these are incredibly funny, and others are just reddit dad jokes. Mostly, the humour works, but it will bully its way into gameplay and make things very staccato-like. Secondly, there's the tedious gameplay. From an extremely fragile submarine that handles like a Trabant with parkinsons, to a wait-a-thon flaming tile platform, there are ample moments engineered to eat up your time, frustrate you, or simply bore you to death. Then you have the stealth, which though semi-competent, once failed will drag you into unrewarding combat. In Metal Gear, you often have the choice between sneak and shoot, but not in this game. Because of a promise to a doctor, if you kill someone, you have to provide healing with one of your own medi-packs to the enemy. There's no killing; the game is about you crawling through a screen to get to the next joke, then the next, then the next. By the end, I started to hate the humour for what I had to do to reach it.Lastly, true to the original MG, you're often hopping between your screen and the inventory, flip flopping through cumbersome controls as you brute-force puzzles. This really should have been handled better: nostalgia doesn't hold up to the scrutiny of modern day experiences, and the rose tinted goggles soon wore off.A fun idea, a wonderful experiment, and then tedium and trite results.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ Superb!UnMetal is an absolute delight for fans of the Metal Gear Solid series, offering a brilliantly crafted parody that pays homage to it's beloved source material. You embark on the adventure as the protagonist Jesse Fox. From the humorous fourth wallbreaking dialogues to the exaggerated characters and situations, UnMetal successfully encapsulates the essence of the beloved stealth franchise while adding it's own unique humor.Every interaction, cutscene and dialogue choice is brimming with hilarious moments that will have you laughing out loud. The game's self-awareness and ability to poke fun at the tropes of the genre, while still delivering a compelling story, is a testament to the developer's comedic prowess.The graphics evoke a nostalgic feeling, reminiscent of classic games from the 90s. The attention to detail is impressive and the animations are smooth, adding an extra layer of charm to the overall gameplay mechanics in UnMetal are well-executed. The controls are tight and responsive, making sneaking around enemy bases and engaging in intense combat encounters a joy. The game keeps the pace high, throwing new challenges and puzzles at you frequently, ensuring that you're always engaged and aspect that deserves special mention is the voice acting, which is superb.

_childDocuments_.review: A fine game with a lot of effort behind it with some bad design decisions mixed in.I really love 2D Metal Gear, which is probably why this game fell a little short for me. While I love some parts of this game, others really drag down the experience in my opinion. It all works, it all functions quite fine, some parts just overstay their welcome a little. Personally I think this game could have done with some pruning. My first playthrough took around 9 hours and I think about 3 of those could have been cut out entirely.I felt that the cutscenes in this game dragged on for way too long and the dialogue itself, while funny in places, was nothing to write home about. It's very much self aware, this is played for laughs multiple times but if I'm being honest it started to annoy me in the last 2 to 3 hours of the game and I could never really get invested in the story. Which seems like a problem to me, because there is just so much of it. There's obviously a gag about Metal Gear having long cutscenes in here, but personally I think it falls completley flat. Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake for the MSX has a lot of dialogue but not nearly the amount this game has. MG2 is also around 5 hours shorter. But let's pretend the comparison is not invited and judge it on it's own merits.The gameplay is a mixed bag for me aswell. Movement is very smooth and fun, the shooting works just fine and I really liked the inventory system. That being said I have mixed feelings about the stealth mechanics. Some sightlines seemed a little undercooked for me. Getting caught is usually either a game over or a healing item tax. There's no chase, no hide and seek. The level design rarely allows you too outwit the AI by finding a clever hiding spot or simply lose them in the corridors. There are items and weapons which can help you take out guards, however there are no items which help you to hide from them. Due to this every room becomes a simple game of "How was this room designed to be beaten?". During my first and sadly only playthrough I felt that the game offered very little in terms of player expression and creativity. Everytime I thought I outsmarted the game a text box appeared and told me: "Sorry, you can't do that yet." Lastly I thought that the leveling system felt completley tacked on.I really wanted to love this game. But I'm afraid it's just gonna be that one playthrough for me. There isn't much reason to revisit it as far as I'm concerned.Still if you are into 2D Metal Gear, I'd give it a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Parody games usually miss the mark. The humors normally awful and the gameplay is barely competent. I remember being excited for Pyst starring John Goodman when I was a kid, only to realize that it was a poorly made barely interactive mess where you clicked Mr. Goodman's belly to make him fart or something. UnMetal is a real game made by people who actually care about games. Their fondness for the first couple Metal Gear games shines through as they adapt a lot of the mechanics from them in new and interesting ways. Many of the boss battles are awesome, and on hard mode some presented a decent challenge.The gaps in action are filled with high quality comedic writing. I laughed at almost every story choice option I made, and I can't wait to replay it and see what the other ones were.So yeah shut up and nab it. I missed the preorder for the physical Vita edition, I hope there's a Switch physical version just so I can buy the damned thing all over again!

_childDocuments_.review: An intentionally cheesy satire of NES-era Metal Gear games with frequent interruptions by an unreliable narrator. I understand that it was released with a lot of balancing issues and bugs, but was a generally enjoyable 12 or so hours by the time I got to it. There were a few areas of frustration, but if I had figured out that porta-potties were re-usable before the 9th mission, or had used some of my "cheat" items, that would have saved me a lot of aggro. If you're on the fence, just watch someone on Youtube play the first mission. If you're not annoyed after that, you should be fine.+LOL'd on more than one occasion. To tears once.+3 difficulties, with a 4th unlockable+Frequent save points+Can reduce difficulty after death+Lots of optional challenges+Speedrun mode+Replayability for dialog options and completion+Can replay levels to pick up anything you missed+Nods to other games, fran games, 80's movies etc+Lots of nice little touches in artwork, animation and special occurrences~Same voice actors as previous fran games~Frequent unannounced points of no return~Couldn't find any purpose to Perfect and UnPerfect ratings~Foul language that an old man like me felt unnecessary for a retro game~Very easy to die, especially on bosses~Some troll mechanics~A few subtitle errors~Occasional dips in quality of humor~Game frequently stops you for silly cutscenes which I've seen people complain about...as if this is a pure action game.-The doctor's eye color changes between scenes. Yes, I was looking at her eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty...Good..A callback to stealth action genre with it's own spin! Tight and easy to understand controls mixed with a story that has branching options. Sometimes you get funneled into one direction, but choosing the wrong option comes with laughter more often than not.There's of course the choice in making things harder or easier in between Jesse's storytelling, and even an achievement for using the worst choices! There was a point where i actually picked off a trail of soldiers running around but an alarm went off and that soured my mood, where i thought i could get a ton of xp for just going out of my way to challenge the obstacle... BUT other than that;I would recommend this to any metal gear fan for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has more soul and personality than any game in recent memory. It elicits that kind of indescribable experience that only a game made by a very small team can create. The story is fantastic, it's funny and doesn't take itself seriously, yet still gets you curious to see what comes next. The gameplay is good, the basics are simple but new stuff is added every level, it keeps you guessing. Though it's here that I do have a bone to pick. I don't like trial and error - and this game does it a number of times, especially in the latter half of the game. Meaning there is no way to get past some areas without dying a LOT. Luckily the game is very generous with its saves so it's never a big setback, but it did irk me whenever that happened. Anyway, this is a great game for when you're in the mood for something lighthearted and fun that you can sink an hour or two into every evening, for a week or so. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with UnMetal.
