_childDocuments_.review: I played 5 hours of this game (up to Chapter 4, around halfway through the game) and it was more than enough for me to leave a review. I can say with certainty that this is one of the funniest games I've ever played in a long time. It pays homage to the original Metal Gear games for the MSX2 and NES while simultaneously parodying it, as well Metal Gear Solid, in the most hilarious way possible.The voice acting is spot-on (making fun of David Hayter's rough and rispid voice for Solid Snake), the comedy timing is beyond perfect, and the pixel art and soundtrack really captures the essence of classic Metal Gear. The crafting / combine system is quite engaging, and the leveling system rewards stealth gameplay.If you're a fun of pixel art games as well stealth, I strongly recommend trying this out. If you're already a fan of Metal Gear, you're in for a plate full of references, as well meta-jokes akin to The Messenger. This game was truly a harbor of love, and it shows. I've finally finished the game, and it was worth every second. It has a few boss battles and sections that are a bit annoying and overstay their welcome, but overall my first opinion still maintains: one of the funniest games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the Metal Gear series and after playing the hilarious demo I just had to buy UnMetal instantly. And I have not been disappointed, not at all. I'm still in the middle of it, but I can already say that UnMetal is far more than a "satire" of the first two Metal Gear games. The allusions are all there, but so is the gameplay and the overall style, you could say it's a very successful and, most importantly, original imitation. The humour, I'd argue, is one of its strongest points and I'd go so far to say that you have a game that is on the same level as the Monkey Island games, a solid (no pun intended!) combination of witty dialogues, absurd situations and well working gameplay. The voice actors do a great job, too, the art style is neat and the game has tentacles. Lots of tentacles. You should just grab this, test out the demo before if you are unsure, but it's really worth it. It's been a while since I had so much fun with a game! Jesse Fox is awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: The setting of this might be a parody one but the gameplay is solid stealth-action. You sneak past the guards when they're not looking, ambush them from a corner, distract them with coins, lure them in with sounds (by punching a wall in a convenient place), put them to sleep and drag away the bodies. The levels have variations: in one level you find a flamethrower and burn down waves of mutant critters, in another you sneak past sleeping dogs, dodge turrets and cross minefields, and another yet has you construct fake guards to replace the real ones you take out while the camera is pointed elsewhere; and the last level before the final boss area introduces several new types of enemies, and each must be dealt with in a different way (you can even pick a preferred enemy out of two available options for the first floor).The bosses on hard are really tough to deal with – especially if you don't pick speed and health perks over punching mastery, and/or don't find secrets (which often contain a permanent health increase). And yes, the game is visibly different between hard and easy difficulty – on hard you are constantly pestered in the docks by boat patrols armed with miniguns (which only appear once or twice on easy and seem to be equipped with a handgun), while on easy the bosses, er, go easy on you, and even the drones during the last boss fight wait for their turn instead of swarming you and showering with bullets from all directions.In addition to visible achievements (one of them being "beat the game on hard"), every level has a "perfect completion" challenge (requiring you to find all the secrets and gain all EXP – most of which is gained by taking out sentries without being discovered) as well as a "UnPerfect" one (these have additional requirements which are specific per level and in some if not most cases can only be achieved on Easy).Edit: there's also an "Iron Man mode" now (which can be enabled at the New Game screen); it disables autosaves along with your ability to save – except by using potties (which now cannot be reset), thus limiting you to 5 saves . Since you can enable it along with any difficulty level, that gives you 3 extra playthroughs that you need to prepare and plan for carefully. (Especially choosing where to use your potties… I.e. you need to identify the 5 places where you're most likely to die, on each difficulty.)

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is a slapstick parody of Metal Gear but PG, so no killing because Jesse Fox isn’t a killer.This is a stealth game through or through, or at it is mandatory to be stealthy to earn more points to upgrade your character like being able to carry more healthpack or to move faster. Speaking on that, I highly suggest first playing this game on easy mode, because there are plenty of times you wanted to just kill someone, but it’s game over once you commit to it. Plus, there’s a lot of trial and error to sneak past enemies and not be spotted, lastly, some boss fight like the one in the sewer level is quite challenging to defeat, so you've been warned. Other than that, Unmetal was a whole lot of fun down to Jessie being a bro with his no-killing rule or some in-game jokes like him explaining in an interview why he is punching a crate to smithereens. Plus, there are a few unique silly mechanics like distracting enemies with a penny or sacrificing your health pack to heal an enemy you just shot, so you can punch them until they’re unconscious again,  (at least they appreciate the healthpack). Experimenting with mechanic are the fun part as well as enemies are the joke with the way they responded. Comedy is subjective so not everything is gonna land especially toward the end, but I can at least promise you this game would at least chucker 10 times if this is your sort of genre, or play the demo if you want a few laughs because this game is long.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are at the age of about 30+, »UnMetal« might have gotten your attention due to its graphical similarities with the top-down »Metal Gear« games (MSX2, NES, GameBoy), and »UnMetal« plays very much like those: While escaping from your prison cell, which you were thrown into for »a crime you didn’t commit«, you explore your surroundings and stumble upon files about an imminent terrorist action you then try to prevent. Sneak around your opponents, distract them, knock them out with your bare hands or even shoot them (but with a catch), use mine detectors and nightvision goggles, disable surveillance devices and so on. In contrast to the aforementioned »Metal Gear« games, »UnMetal« follows a rather humorous approach while referencing iconic scenes from its inspirations. To get a first impression, I recommend playing the free demo.Generally, I always play games on the normal difficulty level, which I consider the way the developers intended the game to be played. This level provided me a decently balanced experience of challenging gameplay without frustration due to too many tries needed to meet its requirements. At the same time, it never felt too easy to finish the various chapters or boss fights, especially when trying to find all the secrets and/or get each achievement. The hard difficulty mode has the exact same quantities – at least it felt this way – of enemies, ammo, and health kits you can find throughout the world; its main difference is the amount of damage you can take, respectively the damage that enemies deal to you. Most notably, the boss fights get significantly harder, yet they stay fair and manageable.My playtime of 24.5 hours are continuous playing with no screen absence for more than a few minutes or even multiple hours. It equals three playthroughs, one per difficulty level (excluding »Ironman« difficulty level), and 100% of the achievements. Your very first run might take about 10–12 hours, assuming you want to be intrigued by the story and don’t skip the dialogues.There is no native Linux version of this game (yet), but I can confirm that it plays extraordinarily well and out of the box with Proton in its most recent version. I had no issues at all, no single crash, tabbing out of and back into the game works flawlessly. So if you are interested in this game and are planning on playing it on a Linux system but hesitate due to a lack of a native version, fearing compatibility issues, there is no reason not to buy »UnMetal«. (However, controller support was not tested, but I don’t expect any issues in this respect, either.)I had a lot of fun with »UnMetal« and it made me do something that hardly any game accomplishes these days: stick to it until the end and beyond. Having played the majority of the existing »Metal Gear (Solid)« games, I can doubtlessly state that »UnMetal« is a passionate homage to that series, enriching it with the developer’s own ideas instead of just copying the original games. It felt absolutely worth its price and the invested playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sometimes compared as a combination of "Metal Gear Solid" and "Hot Shots". It is true.Sure this game is not the most beautiful one, but it redeems a lot with the fun gameplay and even better dialogues executed with brilliant voice acting.This game is played through in about 8-9 hours and I enjoyed every single second of it.The boss fights can be tricky so if you only want to enjoy the completely ironical persiflage of 80's military movies (from said Hot Shots to Full Metal Jacket) you should play it on easy mode.Take your time, let guards talk while you explore the levels. This game really shines on this.If you can live with pixel art and want some entertaining hours, this game will be for you. I would even say it is better than Unepic, which was fun already but not so much of a parody as this one.Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Unepic, you'll love this one!This game isn't meant to be taken seriously, but it was taken very seriously by its creators. It's polished, well designed, and has one of the best post-credit ending cutscene I've ever seen in a video game.Fair warning though there is not much depth to the gameplay, if you buy it that's for the parody and the story sides of it.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, you should just buy this game on principle because it's such an awesome idea, BUT if you insist on more persuasion than that:- This is a literal must have if you are an older gamer like myself that played and LOVED the original Metal Gear on the Nintendo.- This is one of the most genuinely funny games I have ever played.  I've played a few games that are *funny* buy I have already laughed out loud more at this games humor than any other game I have ever played and I'm just 2 hours in!  (FYI I played the demo a lot before getting the game so I probably have about 5 hours of game play total.)- The perk choice when leveling up is rewarding imo and improves on the formula of the first MG on Nintendo that it is an homage to.**  "Wish I knew when I started"  = When you get the gas can, make sure to combine it with the lighter immediately, it's basically an instakill weapon!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, has some replay-ability since it has a nice achievement system and secrets to find in each level. The humor is cheeky and if you're a fan of metal gear you'll probably smile at the references and other nods. The only thing that I'd dock a point for here and there is that there's not really much in the way of music/atmosphere and it oftens feels like there's a bit of dead air on some occasions. There's also a couple places (the 2m time trial a few levels in, finding the torpedos for the sub) where I think it's a bit too easy to get stuck for a while that kills some of the enjoyment, but besides that and if you can get yourself there then you'll have a good time. Oscar Mike... Leonard.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: A much better game than I expected! The core of it is very simple "use coins to distract, ambush guards from behind" gameplay, but generally each chapter, they come up with some interesting new mechanic or weapon to add to Jesse Fox's challenges. These even culminate very well in boss battles that always feel like a unique application of some new concept, and are genuinely challenging a lot of the time.For a pixel game, it doesn't trim on production costs - involving quite a lot of custom voice acting and artwork for short-lived scenes. Many of the jokes it puts forward are of the "silly situation" vibe more than the laugh-out-loud variety, but it works very well. And, what keeps it moving forward is that it's not FULLY reliant on humor - it's telling an actual earnest story of a hero's escape. In that way it's even kind of similar to Metal Gear, rather than just being a direct parody.I always looked forward to the ideas it was going to put forth in each new boss fight, even when it found some inventively humorous way to suddenly kill me, and a lot of the challenges felt really satisfying to overcome. Definitely worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing UnMetal! It might at first just seem like a parody of Metal Gear games, but it spins the whole idea in new, funny, stupid, amazing ways. I actually prefer this much more than the originals! Jesse Fox is now my hero and I devote the remainder of my life to punching all objects I come in contact with in hopes for loot to fall out.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough. Even if you're not a fan of the old metal gear games, this game has a ton of charm. Constantly funny, plenty of quality of life features, clever use of mechanics, great art style...it's really the total package for such a low price. My friends and I spent a good eight hours cruising through this and I'd gladly play through it again for the laughs.

_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Great Metal Gear parody. Good pixel art. Decent soundtrack. Sometimes funny, sometimes not.However, the way AI behaves can be quite annoying: they choose to move in a somewhat-random-somewhat-fixed direction, so going for full stealth/XP can test your patience. Damage is based on the sprite position, which is awful for many boss mechanics: you can dodge missiles by moving horizontally but not vertically. Just slight annoyances, but other than that, it's good.10/10 ending that had me chuckling for a solid minute.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Goofy Metal Gear clone that doesn't take itself seriously. Surprisingly it made me laugh up until the pizza segment, then everything just kinda fell flat. The whole "two doctors" thing was a drag.I think the voice acting could have been delivered better. I get that Jesse Fox a satirical take on Solid Snake, but after a while his "cool guy" impression (or whatever it is) started becoming irritating.Gameplay wise, it was fairly easy, though there was one moment involving a certain antenna that I needed a hint for because nowhere does it mention anything about . Other than that, there are a decent number of times where the game doesn't tell you what to do, but things just "click" like the X door scene, or even the pizza segment that I wasn't much of a fan of, but appreciated the game not assuming I'm stupid. I found those moments more enjoyable than the moments where Fox or another character would monologue what to do. As for the things I didn't like, one was the labyrinth because the map felt inconsistent, the other was the final boss and his  Overall it was decent.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great parody game that has excellent writing.The writing could carry the whole thing, but thankfully the gameplay and sound/visual design are good as well. Plenty of jokes and moments where you can choose your own version of the story, with each choice often having unexpected and humorous complications. There are also quality-of-life design choices that make tough sections much more manageable, and secrets hidden in every stage that can have unique items with significant bonus effects.Easily the funniest game I've played in a long time, and one that you can tell has a lot of heart put into it.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I give it a 5 outta 5 stars! Great pixel graphics, the perfect parody to the stealth genre while paying homage to it's number 1 title in stealth games: Metal Gear. Features a cool story and the humour was absolutely hilarious in my opinion, especially considering it's a video game. Very challenging too. Plus fun enough with just the right amount of comedy and different choices in story to make a person who's a fan wish to play through it one more time after completion, but that's about it as far as it would go for it's replay value. Overall... I thoroughly enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Does not work properly on 4K displays. Would not recommend purchase till fixed if using 4K.Patch 1.05 did not fix the 4K issue on my end.Edit:I fixed my 4K issue.1. Right click on unmetal.exe, select properties and then compatibility.2. Click on the box at the bottom labelled "high DPI settings" Leave program DPI unchecked.3. At the bottom will be "High DPI scaling override"4. Check that box and select Application.This fixed my issues in 3840x2160 full screen completely.No more black bars on side or bottom in 4K or 2K full screen.Proper windowed resolutions showing up in menu. Game works perfectly.I highly recommend this game, once I was able to play properly, I cant put it down.The Snakes and States of Matter would be proud.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Really funny but a bit tedious.Humor is subjective, some people will have a great laugh at Unmetal, some won't. I personally found it really funny, the characters particularly Jesse Fox is charming, and it is worth a playthrough.PROS:++ Practically every line in the game has voice acting. This is rare for a retro-inspired game.+ The game has a great self-aware sense of humor.+ Intuitive inventory screen and management, ability to hotkey items is really good.+ Solid stealth gameplay, no respawning enemy B.S, guards don't wake up.+ Some multip[le choice segments give you a creative way of adjusting the difficulty to your liking.+ You can't kill anyone, so the gun is OP but you have to heal everyone you shoot. It's so refreshing to play a pacifist in a game nowadays.CONS:--Boss fights are pretty tedious. The 1st one can kill you in one hit, later on bosses resort to spamming grenades/rockets at them, they are not too fun to play besides 1or 2.- Having to punch practically every crate on the screen to get key items becomes tedious.- The blasted submarine section. This is where i caved and turned on Easy mode.- Antagonist very "Meh." - The music is very uninspiring for the most part.- Graphics are not the best for a 2D game.Overall, i give Unmetal a solid 7 out of 10. If you like Metal Gear 1 and 2, you will be sure to enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kinda neutral about this game. It's a good game if you want a mgs clone but only if you ignore the weird game design choices. I'm not into pick the right dialogue choice to progress and ♥♥♥♥ you, now start over since you chose wrong game design. I understand what the dev was trying to do but that's not a thing in Metal gear. I kinda wished that the game allowed you to write notes in the game because I kept screwing up in the second to last chapter and dying because I couldn't figure out where to go using the map. Also, it really needed to not copy all the crappy parts of the MGS series either. Long cutscenes that go on and on and interrupt the gameplay flow to have another long cutscene isn't what I want to do in a game. And it really need to stop with overly long funny jokes/gags that didn't really need to be there. The stuff that made the game great were the  interrogator pointing out the absurdity of some of the things that happened. I liked that it borrowed from the MSX Metal gear games which I loved and didn't have old timey game design. Allowing the player to switch difficulty on the fly is always a plus in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for November 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before December 6th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.An attempt to inject humor into the original Metal Gear. On paper, this should be fine.  Someone has taken the outdated NES Metal Gear and modernized it, giving it a different story and humor.  And if the humor on the screen is working for you, ignore the rest of what I’m about to say and check this out.  I’m sure there’s an audience for it. However, for me, I disliked everything about this.  The humor was painful as was the story. They said “I was sentenced for a crime I didn’t commit” at least four times.  We get it, it’s the A-team, it wasn’t original the first time you said it.  The game constantly stops for well voiced, but awful cutscenes that try too hard to feel needed.  The graphics are average at best, but the gameplay just never felt fun.  Even the boss battles felt weak. I can’t recommend this game, like I said, if someone loves the humor here, which is why I’m trying to show it, maybe they’ll get a kick out of this but the humor here disappointed me, and the rest of the game made me dislike the mishmash of different features and ideas that never worked together. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the game kinda wears off after 2 hoursWhat I personally disliked most is the ridiculous amount of stealth gameplay required. It completely kills the fun, when on every damn corner there's either a guard, beam, sensor or camera that sounds an alarm (and alarm means game over)And then to top it off, once you've finished the game, there's no NG+ mode. So if you miss anything in a chapter, you can only replay that single chapter as your character was at that time. I guess screw everyone who didn't find every secret, get max XP per stage or collected every item.Another thing that ticked me off, was that in each stage there's a gold medal that you can pick up. What the developer doesn't tell you, is that if you don't pick it up then you don't earn the achievement for completing the chapter. Couple this with a ton of niche achievements, that have to be built up over all the chapters, then the lack of NG+ is even more infuriating.Save your money and time

_childDocuments_.review: An homage to Metal Gear that stands on it's own merit. If you are expecting outright Metal Gear fan service, you will be disappointed. Lots of gratuitous swearing in the dialogue. A very fun casual play-through.  Overall, an enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: The more you play it, the more it looks like an unfinished product of a contest entry.The gameplay ranges from jank to serviceable. The game resembles a Click & Play project riddled with mechanics clumsily copied and pasted from other games, which often don't fit well together. For example: You can move in 8 directions, but you can attack/interact only in 4. This makes controls resemble The Binding of Isaac, but it is not balanced around it in any way. Enemies, on the other hand, shoot quick projectiles with great accuracy. It plays into the theme of the main character, but it is often not fun to play. You might not notice this on easier difficulties, because this makes enemies have less health and attack less often and less accurate. But then the core gameplay becomes so easy that I felt like I was skipping it.I wanted to do the challenges that the game kept proposing, so I never used the quicksave system. But for anyone who isn't a tryhard like me I wouldn't recommend doing that. It is pretty clever and actually fixes a lot of issues the game has. But there are situations where you can't use it or it doesn't help, so this all seems often undercooked.But this would all have been fine if not for the story. It is extremely shallow and doesn't not provide any payoff whatsoever. In fact, one could say that the Steam description page is kind of a false advertisement. The "pays homage to the classics" part is certainly only true for the gameplay. The "crime he didn't commit" part of the story is never explored in any way. Actually, we don't get to know who the main protagonist even is (besides his name), how he got in the game's setting in the first place, how he is related to the story, or who the antagonists are or what they want. Even though the game's title implies a pastiche of MGS, it barely references anything related to Hideo Kojima. It's bizarre, like watching out of context C-class action films in another language and out of sequence. Many of the items highlighted in the game's description are single use comedy gadgets with no real gameplay value. I don't think the crowbar is in the game at all, I 100%ed it and never found one. There are other, more interesting items to interact with in the game, which are strangely omitted.The jokes themselves are sometimes really clever, . But they often overstay their welcome and turn into cringe running gags, which feel like some hermetic inside jokes of a group of buddies you don't even know, being made in your presence over and over again.I had a lot of fun with this game and it's challenges, but I can't recommend it due to these flaws - I suspect that, to really enjoy it, one must have a certain type of gamer tism like I do.

_childDocuments_.review: The jokes were funny, but would do better in other content.  Mainly because this game was tedious, the gameplay is not intuitive. _childDocuments_.review: A hilarious, beautiful homage to Metal Gear full of humour and geeky references, pulled down by annoying design in gameplay progression. It’s by no means bad and was made with love and charm, but with so many exceptional games out there, I can’t recommend it.-Art, animation, aesthetic, and setting were all fantastic. Great pixel art, moody environments, with generous variety among the tools and stages encountered.-All of the voice acting was top notch, even minor characters. My favourite is Mike! Fox was a bit grating, but I give it a pass as it was done with an intentional affectation.-Gameplay:  Here’s the big stinker. The game trolls the player constantly in what’s intended to be “so close but so far” jokes, but the laughs are short-lived as you’ll find yourself spending hours backtracking and doing other tedious, trial-and-error tasks to progress. It made the game unfun such that I ended up just watching a video after getting fed up a few hours into the game.-Length:  The above is also where most of the game’s length comes from, so it wears out its welcome long before it concludes.-Story:  No deep plot, but it definitely got plenty of laughs out of me.-Sound Design, Interface, Character Design:  All solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is a parody game. The parody aspect of the game is well done. I liked the writing and the humor. It made me laugh out loud a few times. Unfortunately, this fun is ruined by horrendous gameplay. The game consists of %50 cutscene/dialog, %40 beginner's traps that are guaranteed to kill you in your first time and finally %10 actual gameplay. The gameplay itself is okay. The stealth mechanics are good and the game rewards you with XP for playing stealthily. If you let the enemy see you, you don't get an XP and I think for encouraging stealth this is really a good mechanic. Now, let's take a look at the rest of the gameplay. First of all, the game gives you a gun, but you are not allowed to kill anyone. What's the f*cking point of giving a lethal weapon then? Give me a tranquilizer gun or something. When you shoot an enemy, you have to heal him before he bleeds to death. I have never seen such a stupid sh*t before! Secondly, you don't get a second chance to fight back against some enemies. Dogs and ghosts for example. The player can make mistakes especially if it's the first time playing. You don't have to punish him with death for his mistake, at least give him a second chance. Especially for a parody game this is unacceptable. Finally, I want to talk about beginner's traps that made me want to swim in a septic tank rather than playing Unmetal. These traps are designed to fool you on your first time playing. You are going to die and repeat the whole section because of these annoying traps. For example; in one part, dogs are sleeping, and you have to silently sneak around them. I started walking, and General called me from the radio and dogs attacked me. Turns out, I was supposed to call the general before sneaking. How in the name f*ck I was supposed to know that? And there's section with the drill sergeant. You have to choose the right dialogue in order to win the duel. Which option you are supposed to choose is not clear and you are going to fail that part at least three times. Jesus f*cking Christ that part almost made me uninstall the game. And also, in one part of the game you have to enter the base. I go to the door, talk with the guard and again game gives me three choices. I try every single one of them, and I die each time. Turns out there's a pizza box in the trash bin on the corner of the screen. I have to go to the corner of the screen to get it and then it is not enough. Then you have to choose what type of pizza is it? I died again because turns out you have to examine the pizza and learn that it's pepperoni pizza. And that's not enough either. Let's take the sh*t scale to the next level. You have to get the fire extinguisher and use it on the pizza to cause steams to rise from the box. After all of this bullsh*t, you can finally enter that c*cksucking base. How was I supposed to know all of this on my first try? It's pure trial and error. This trial and error concept is repeated through the whole game and ruined the game for me. There aren't clever puzzles to solve or riddles to answer. Just trial and error gameplay that is designed to waste your time over and over again. Dying again and again and repeating the dialogues again and again really became boring and frustrating. The writing and the humor is good and entertained me in the beginning but the whole gameplay ruined the experience for me. Unepic was good, but Unmetal left a sour taste in my mouth.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and funny game. Never really loses its charm or humor throughout the game. It's trying to copy a bit of the Metal Gear games but without the extremely serious tone. I think it's definitely one of the better games i played in the last few years and now I am even more interested in the other games from this developer.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, but it is not without its numerous warts. The level of self-awareness is usually right on, but sometimes floats into "stupid" territory. That's tolerable if you're willing to give it the benefit of the doubt. There were enough genuine laugh-out-loud moments with cleverly framed jokes that I'm certainly willing to deal with a couple of eye-rollers. The game does fall into the usual indie trap of "REEEEE VIOLENCE BAD" but the gameplay in general is more than good enough to make up for the unnecessary narrative disconnect. And the game is generally meant to be comedic, and I am disinclined to be super tough on someone who might not want to making violence and killing into a silly funny matter. So we'll give it a pass on that front. The one thing that really burns me out though is the downright obtuse difficulty scaling between normal gameplay and boss fights. It tracks 100% with the silly parody game to have boss fights that require some lateral thinking and involve some slightly cartoonish elements. Especially when the game is a parody of Metal Gear, which... Let's be honest. Metal Gear is not a poster child for gritty realism. But the regular gameplay leans toward the casual side a lot of times, relying more on being strategic and patient. Which again, tracks well with what it's supposed to be. The boss fights turn often into a bullet hell MLG grind where you almost have to know "the trick" to cheese them, and then you're still barely scraping by at the end of your sixteenth or seventeenth try. This inevitably means that if you adjust the game difficulty to where the regular gameplay offers an exciting challenge, the boss fights will be impractically masochistic, and if you adjust the difficulty such that the boss fights offer an exciting challenge, then the regular gameplay becomes trivial or even boring. Fran is a talented dude, and I'm going to tell you to buy this game as long as you can deal with the bosses being an utter slog.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like here; Sneaking around is fun, combat is fine, the game is pretty funny. But it has a few flaws that are so big it really ruins the entire experience. Way too many sections require you to do something in perfect order and if you don't pick the right option you die and restart the conversation or section at the beginning.  I truly cannot fathom how the creators play tested the maze section and thought "yeah, lets make this maze very long, poorly designed and if you die you have to start it all over again." it's one of the worst design decisions I've ever seen. Same goes for multiple conversations, it's all random chance and if you pick the wrong dialogue tree, you have to do it all over again. The game is also too long and has way too much dialogue. The dialogue is funny but at least let me skip it if I can read faster than your characters are talking. It's so tiresome to sit and watch endless cutscenes over and over again. If this is on sale, maybe give it a chance but it's laughable they released a game with this much fat and time wasting in it for 20 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the demo on Steam Next Fest I thought it would be a parody on Metal Gear (NES), a welcoming expirience since the  choice in that genre so abyssmal. Turns out it's an actual game with its own story and characters loosely based on original game from Kojima.At beginning I had a great fun. Lots of dialogues, rich graphics, smooth animations. I'd say I have no complaints about the technical side, everything is fine. The problem is in plot, characters and humour.The humour is... poor. The more I went through, the less the game could offer. At first the main character (mc) talking in a Batman voice and remarks about the way the mc managed to do somehing unusual were funny, but that's like 95% of all jokes. At the end I can't even say if it's a comedy game rather than an average top-down action with funny side remarks. Speaking of game mechanics, they are dated and frustrating to use. There is no  way to shoot at more than four directions (but enemies do it without any problem). Stealth mechanic is unreliable. Enemies may spot you behind their back. The alarm is turning on immediately, but there is a split second moment when stealth is already broken, but other enemies aren't alerted, in that case no bonus for stealth take-down. Also, to reach the melee range, there is an awkward sneak mechanic of frequent little steps which counts as "slowly but quiet walking", instead of, you know, the actual slow walking ability.The plot is plain and boring. The villain is not someone's brother separated at birth, there is no traitor in disguise, no surprising twists. Come on, if you are ripping off the Kojima game, you have to include something like that. Otherwise what is the point.Mc starts with the goal to escape the enemy territory, at the end he escapes. The game is extremely lengthy, with a few chapters where nothing interesting happens. Would be much better if chapters 5, 6, 7 would be gone and the game would be a little cheaper. Last thing, the aftercredits scene is horrible. I said earlier that there are no twists, but actually there is one. Would be nice if I didn't see it, but here we are. Anything doesn't make sense now and I suffered the repetitive, poorly made gameplay and uninspiring plot for nothing, bravo.Thinking about that, if it wasn't the obvious Metal Gear setting and vibes, I wouldn't be interested in this game in the first place after playing the demo. For me it looks like the dev intentionally ripped off the old game to lure more people to his otherwise unremarkable product. Shame.

_childDocuments_.review: A few months ago, I got the chance to play the demo for UnMetal, a 2D stealth action-adventure game developed by @unepic_fran and publisher Versus Evil.  The few hours I got to play UnMetal left me feeling very optimistic for the full launch of the game. UnMetal seeks to pay homage to similar 2D stealth games, most notably the older Metal Gear Solid games, both parodying and emulating the best and most cliché aspects of the genre.  I was also a big fan of the humor in UnMetal; Jesse Fox may not be as edgy and hardcore as the Snakes are, but he more than makes up for it with his humor.  Now that the full game is coming out and I am able to fully experience Jesse Fox’s story, does UnMetal live up to my high first impressions? Despite not having a lot of experience in stealth games (or being very good at them), one of the things that I enjoyed the most from the UnMetal demo and now, the full game, is the comedic and small Easter Egg type items laying around the levels.  It’s clear that the developer put a lot of care and passion into creating a parody/homage to games of the genre.  I mean, for crying out loud, you get to be a giant wedge of cheese!  What stealth game lets you do that?  The stealth mechanics are definitely hard, especially for someone like me who prefers to have a fully loaded assault rifle holding down left click as monsters and bad guys turn into red mist in front of me.  Don’t worry though, UnMetal also has boss fights sprinkled throughout the game to help alleviate any potential fatigue from constantly sneaking around. UnMetal forces you to survey and scour the entire level as you pick up both joke items (seriously, toilet paper?) and items that you will need to progress, such as rope for climbing down sewers or a key to open a locked gate.  It can be a little annoying at times when you get the feeling that “I totally already looked through every crate and corner of this level and I still can’t find (blank).”  You will need to backtrack a fair amount, especially if you’re not thorough.  Getting caught is really punishing, too, since enemies can deal lots of damage and healing items are a treasured commodity.  There are exploding-shooting parts to UnMetal but be prepared to hoard items and do a lot of panic rolls; those parts can be some pretty hard on the highest difficulty settings. Because of all this, I am actually glad to say that UnMetal continues to build on what was a very enjoyable demo into the full game.  Obviously, stealth games aren’t for everyone; it takes a certain amount of patience to watch a guard walk his predetermined route half a dozen times before deciding to kill him.  However, I do think that UnMetal is a solid game in its own right, an impressive feat considering that there seems to be only one guy behind the development.  Whether you pick it up because you miss the old Metal Gear Solid games, want to support an indie developer, or thought hey, I kind of like stealth and this game looks funny, I believe anyone who buys UnMetal will find a great title that they will enjoy.  Even if you’re not into stealth, like me, UnMetal’s story, its quips, and wit make it a fun time, arm and leg not required.   9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Time for another unpopular opinion. I think the Metal Gear Solid series is overrated. That's why a title like UnMetal (UM), which lampshades those games, is something I'd possibly enjoy. After all, it's the ridiculous, goes on forever story that really made me turn off from what the games tried to offer. Either way, I'll have to try UM to see if I like it more than the series it's based on.Taking inspiration from a stealth-centered title, most of the time you'll need to sneak up on enemies or dispatch of them quickly. Once they raise the alarm, you're more or less screwed. While moving through hostile territory, you'll be scrounging for supplies, some of which are specifically needed to complete objectives. These will update in each chapter as you come across various obstacles and problems. However, UM doesn't always telegraph information well. For instance, when trying to encrypt the radio, I didn't realize the computers could be broken. It's hard to complete an objective when you don't realize what can or can't be used.Another issue I had was pinpointing the tone it was going for. It's obviously not super-serious, and some scenarios are odd and bizarre, but it's like the developer didn't want to cross a line in the sand and be too absurd. Maybe it's going for action movie logic, which also tends to irk me. After all, Jesse often finds stuff that winds up being useful, but only to someone who happens to know how to jury rig trash into weaponry. For example, you come across a flamethrower with a crucial part missing, and luckily enough have everything needed to make it functional, when it'd already be weird that you could identify any of that stuff on a flamethrower. Thank goodness you didn't use that gas to drive away from there.The amount of inputs in UM makes the control scheme feel busy, as you can take so many actions at any given time. On the one hand, the gameplay isn't that advanced, so spreading things out so much seems a bit overkill. Conversely, most controllers have the buttons available to map things this way, so why not make use of it? Overall it works, I just found it a bit clunky.An American being arrested for a crime he hasn't committed? Sounds like something that could only happen in America. Jesse Fox will tell you all about it, because like most Americans, he enjoys talking about America. And himself. That's somewhat like the vibe the game's writing has for it. It can be a touch repetitive, leans toward the outlandish side, and there's no way you should believe a word Jesse says. Due to the heavy emphasis on the game's story, you might expect a decent amount of cutscenes or clips to show some of that action. However, much like the Metal Gear series, a large chunk of the story is told through dialogue between two characters. At least in UM's defense, they're a small developer without the sort of budget to animate so many videos. Looking at the gameplay itself, there's a decent variety to the environments, as you escape a military base, dive into the sewers, and traverse a jungle. Because Jesse is lying through his teeth, certain hurdles he encounters don't seem plausible, but otherwise the locations have a decent level of detail to them. Unfortunately, the NPC sprites are missing their faces though. While playing the game I didn't notice the music very much, and when I checked out the OST the reason was obvious. Many of the notes and sections are on the subtle side, as if it's trying to sneak around too. Also, oddly enough, a few sections come across with an eerie tone, like they had a different game in mind when composing that part.A big part of UM you may not expect is the voice-acting, as all the lines are dubbed. That meant Jesse Fox's actor had many lines to record, as he's the protagonist. I'm not trying to hate on his voice-acting, but it has the timber of someone who wants to sound cool, like a kid trying to intentionally lower his voice. The problem has less to do with his delivery, and more to do with an unreliable narrator, who loses his credibility quickly, so I think he ultimately did his job well. After all, I wouldn't make the same complaint about the voice-acting of the military officers.🌟 Toilets aren't the only way to save. Certain events trigger them too, such as watching an important story moment play out.🌟 It's a nice touch when a game is fully voice-acted, and there's a decent amount of dialogue in the title too.❌ There's no way to know when the AI will function differently or a dialogue choice will give undesirable effects. For instance, choosing 2 tentacles actually creates 2 dozen instead, or knowing which guards will chase down a coin or ignore it. Mere developer whims.❌ I don't see what all the fuss was about with the noose, considering everything else he claims to have witnessed, “Right, you spoke with a dead guy, but what I really want to know about is where you got the noose.” ❌ They failed to put the UN in fun or funny, but it at least had guns.🔍 Good timing makes boss encounters much easier. For instance, in Chapter 3 you know he's going to stop and fire in the middle of the hallway, so you can wait for him to get there and fire early.🔍 If you're having trouble, you can reduce the difficulty to easy. Aside from one achievement, there's no special reason for staying on harder modes.From the reactions other people had, I thought my feelings toward UM would be stronger. It'd either be an uproarious, compelling experience, or have weak jokes and lame gameplay. Instead, I found it more middling than anything. I thought the narration and choices made by the player altering in-game situations was a cool idea, but that didn't make up for how the rest of the game plays. Throughout most of the game you have limited combat options, and pretty much always make the same choice: ambush an enemy, shoot them, or use the new gadget you made because plot. To be fair, the writing could have been a lot worse, but it also wasn't really funny. When it started turning into a story being told to another person about telling a military guy a story, I thought they got too far ahead of themselves. Ultimately, I think the game was average or a little below, and I started getting tired of it after a few hours, especially as it starts feeling like filler in a tall tale. I don't find the number of positive reviews aligns with how many people actually beat UM, so I wouldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the type of game that requires a middle of the road score and not just a thumbs up or down. I'll give it a thumbs down to make it stick out from the pack, but it's not a bad game. In fact, some parts are excellent such as the writing and jokes. Some of it tends to be goofy and try-hard at times but especially in the beginning, there's a lot of genuine laugh out loud moments. If you're a stealth action type, you'll enjoy the clever gameplay as well.The issue for me is how the game gets obnoxious with how it treats the player. The twists and turns the devs think are clever or funny are more annoying and obnoxious. For example, the main character is an idiot and does things that are ridiculous, such as saying "he's not here" when an enemy asks for someone, giving away his position and activating the alarm. The devs are going for a subversion gimmick but it's more annoying than fun. The game is full of those, especially once you hit the mid-section. Much of the challenges come from the protagonist's moronic nature and it's grating. Some parts will restrict you from doing something "just because", essentially.Stealth action fans and those who don't mind trial and error gameplay should pick this up. Others, wait for discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has its moments as a cute parody of the old Metal Gear games, but it's held back by infuriating fake difficulty. The main character, Jesse Fox, is an unreliable narrarator, and at times you get to choose what he says happened in the story. There's a moment where you're fighting a boss using a flamethrower as a weapon, and about 75% through the boss fight, a dialogue box pops up. You are to choose whether the flamethrower falls apart, or explodes. Me, being an idiot, thought the game would do something funny or entertaining for picking the "explode" option. This just immediately killed me and made me have to start the boss all over again from the last save point.. Unfortunately the game has a few situations like this, where you would assume the choices are harmless, but instead will just cause the game to immediately kill you.Death in this game is NOT forgiving, either. Apparently, despite being a 2021 video game, is has the 90's video game outdated death punishment concept. You know, the one where you have to repeat sections of the level and get back to where you last saved. During something like a boss fight, this very much pisses me off. I don't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ need to replay the level to that point unless I reload my game, just let me try the boss again from the beginning, especially when the boss's attacks instantly kill me.Game starts off as a really cute homage and parody, but where it doesn't know when to let go of the past, it REALLY doesn't know.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, this is more like a  game, than it is a parody or a reimagining, the problem lies in how far you can run with such project before calling quits and demanding a change out of its structure, sorta like a joke going for too long if left unattended. What about the rope? I'll tell you later.the problem is, this game isn't about combat, puzzles, story, codec, dialogues or pretty much anything.  it's a game about "stealth"But WHAT REALLY is "stealth"? Is there even such a genre? Even in comparison to what MGS franchise essentially was, if we remove the broad understanding of the genre "stealth", when it boils down to describing each of the franchise's entry it would be something entirely different than the one in the past:MGS1 is some schoolkid's 'joke-wad' or 'troll-hack' of metal gear 2 MGS2 is a neat arcade that hates itself more than it hates your guts as it lusts to show off its cool technical features. 'Sons of Liberty' has a liberating gameplay.MGS3 is some weird janky immersive beat-em up with secret and subtle rpg elements (which get improved upon in PW)The rest are too far off from their roots as games (but not as an experience) Now, where does UnMETAL fit into all of this? It fits into 'stealth' in a sense of having to wait for a platform to come down in a subpar generic platformer game. A true understanding of the stealth roots, for sure. Besides that, you have your typical "swamp section from MG2" where you move frame by frame, and that was a really good joke, but then the game removes the stealth aspect entirely (still retaining stealth perks for some reason), and becomes an action game with inanimate objects as enemies and enemies that serve as a walking wall for you to open with the right tool (which is everything the original MG did, but having the idea of multipurpose items never got its own debut in UnMETAL). Oh, also backtracking was made purposefully evil. Good. Very close to MG-MGS1 so far.Call me a villain or something, but i think it's fair to compare games from 35 years ago, surely we're not that below common sense and general progress, are we? Mechanic wise, i think MG1-2 are still better. There are some life-improving self implementation like homing-fist, being able to jump out from cover rather than time your hits with the next passerby moment, and a very unique to UnMETAL feature - dragging bodies and coin toss. Although there is no real need to drag anybody, since enemies never wake up, you beat them up so hard they become biomorts. You can't crawl like in MG2 anymore, and it's now reserved to a roll, which you can utilize to avoid projectiles and go underneath holes instantly. Which is essential, since everything tends to one-shot you on normal, and you are usually left with zero health and a countdown to your death (upgrades merely add more seconds to it, besides the health ones there are also extra bullets for a gun you will never use, even for a boss fight, after initial unlock) So there's no more slowly crawling through a vent with a very dragged out exposition playing in the background or masking loading times between transitions! Because there isn't any! Or i didn't notice. I don't think i've noticed myself playing this game until it was too late, even. Nor did I notice I've switched it off into background at one point to make myself a sandwich. But yeah, as its own experience, how does it perform as that? Well, here's the upgrade system for a replacement to the usual ranking system, i'll ask you a question and tell me what's a better alternative fit for stealth:Better punches throughout the game or run faster when no enemies are around? Heal faster and more often, or once but better? (you still have to wait a long time to regenerate) deal more damage with that one weapon you don't really need OR get a fist-homing attack? Deal +5% damage this or deal +5% damage that? Even the upgrade system is a joke within itself, a subtle satire on how game developers create artificial progression systems wherein all of their other mechanics contradict that there is more way than one, which can be truly played. If you're having a worse experience, you're gonna be hit with the 'Homing Attack' gang to remind you, that you are playing wrong.From the first to third level, inventory system slowly becomes useless, not even guards drop anything up from that point on, so why not get rid of it entirely, or is the purpose of having every interaction off actual possible combinations kill the player, that important of a feature? I guess i'm just stupid, and this is obviously a joke too. Besides the idea of having to collect some of the most bizarre and useless tools, you as a player, need to deliberately collect useless gag items, and look for punchlines to use them in a joke, like Coconut-Jim once said, "player is his own director" (i don't know whether he said that, he looks like a dolt that would) so in fact, you have to collect jokes yourself, and wait for it to pay off, and some do, some don't. This is the true purpose of the inventory, to remind the player that there is, in fact, an invisible pocket for all of his sucessful jokes at one point, and to entertain a crowd, unlike grenades in the actual mgs title, he would have to use them at one point. Then throw them all away into the recycling bin, lest they become a meme.The rope? Ah yeah, well don the noose, because symbolically, after the 3rd stage, the game actively looks to start falling apart, introducing broken mini games and horrendous boss fights that would be better off left out of the whole experience, bosses part also fitting for a game that was made 35 years ago, but why? We can defend literally any mistake if we'll take it out from the past, or would that be like, complete contradiction on why history exists at all? Out of all ideas that were interesting, only the idea of making up lies on the spot was the redeeming one, but even then, it doesn't drastically change the experience of having a single room filled with either cows, or sheep, and like real jokes, they were ether hit or miss, since some would outright kill you, as you would get shot for being a liar, not the most creative-ish improvement over Alpha Protocol.Uhhh ehh what else...The music makes it look like you're playing an adult motion picture, which is quite fitting for mgs as a whole. This game is a joke and you act as its punchline. If the intent of this game was to remind of how horrendous MG-1-2 is, it succeeds at that. But without this context, it's an utterly miserable experience. It lacks a touch of sharpness from No One Lives Forever, it doesn't have the fraction of genuine stupidity of its predeccessor, nor is it really a celebratory pastiche akin to the Tom Fulp's 'The Room Tribute' game. It's more of a collection of gags from Sunday Funnies wearing a skin of a thing that now is the most misconceptualized phenomenon of the modern culture. Play this if you are one of the 'Arnolds' from MG1. You are 'Dirty Duck man' at best, man.

_childDocuments_.review: People say this game is like Metal Gear, and maybe it is in some of its most superficial aspects but gameplay wise, frankly it doesn’t compare to the metal gear games I know, I don’t know if people are comparing it to the ones from NES, frankly I wouldn’t know because I haven’t played those.As for the game? Is a very boring and badly paced experience, or at least it was for me, there are a number of cutscenes interrupting the gameplay, most of which repeat the game’s trope of telling joke after joke, it gets tiresome after a while…Then there’s the gameplay which frankly is quite counterintuitive, simplistic, and boring. I don’t know if I would call good game design having a game have to tell you where to go and what to do in the form of cutscenes, I feel as if this kind of design is a cheap solution to not put in the thought, nor effort in actually developing a compelling gameplay experience, which since this is a video game, should really be the focus of the experience…Yet you have people here and even so called “professional critics” venerating the game, the game got great scores despite the focus being put into joke after joke, cutscene after cutscene, stuff that none of which really has to do with the gameplay, it should be a secondary aspect to the experience, not the main focus as far as games are concerned.I also couldn’t stand the fact that I had to revisit area after area, waiting for the game to actually let me progress after I had done a completely unrelated task than the one evidently designed to lead me to progress further in the game, and that’s not even taking into account the terrible inventory system. You get a multitude of different items to combine, some others are just there to make a cheap pun or a silly joke, but the ones that serve to be useful, sometimes have the strangest combinations all in the sake of trying to make a dumb joke, your game design shouldn’t bear the consequences of you attempting to make a joke, humour is not an excuse for bad game design, having to combine a stick with an eyepatch in order to create a slingshot isn’t clever, nor is it fun, specially if you have to do this on the spot, in the middle of a freaking boss battle…I gave up at the start of the second chapter, I couldn’t stand a dumb joke about baby piranhas coming out of a failed insemination attempt, and afterwards, when I was locked in a room, having to bear yet another dumb conversation through my radio in order to get out of said room, I just tapped out, gave up, there’s a ton of other games that are frankly better and actually use the potential of the medium in order to create an actual compelling gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest; I believe UnMetal has a very distinct vision, one that developer UnEpic Fran has delivered on with gusto. Unfortunately, I don't believe that vision has made for an especially entertaining experience and, for many players, will fast become grating.UnMetal is a 'Hot Shots'-esque pastiche of Metal Gear Solid, albeit one with a far simpler storyline. Resembling the NES original and playing like its PSX sequel - initially at least - the opening stages are familiar inventory-juggling, patrol-avoiding fare that hint at an enjoyable retro demake.Sadly, the further you play into UnMetal, the more this idea becomes diluted; bu the seventh mission, I was genuinely fatigued. The comedy, while a welcome reprieve from the straight-faced MGS series, fast outstays its welcome, dragging jokes on for long enough that the punchlines are at best predictable, at worst utterly tepid. Eventually, they become intrusive, pausing the game for minutes of awkward shtick before divulging mission-crucial information. UnEpic, the first game in the 'Un' series had similarly dim humour, but it was never this insistent. Fran is arguably better suited to a more natural, serious style of writing, as demonstrated in the superb Ghost 1.0.While players tire of the writing, however, the game is slowly tiring of itself. Frequently, UnEpic drops all pretences of being a stealth game and decides to change genres entirely. An arcade shooter. A choose-your-own-adventure book (complete with instant failures, I would add). A Jetpack-esque submarine adventure. Such variety wouldn't be an issue if they weren't so often a chore. One section tasks the player with reviving any enemies they kill via a slow revive animation. The section is poorly justified via a lame comedy exchange earlier in the chapter, but dedicating an entire section to this torturous, stop-start style of gameplay means the joke is only ever on the player.UnMetal is a game with a vision. For those that recognise that vision, it might even be called a success. But I can't imagine many people sharing a vision so schizophrenic, so player hostile and so mistakenly sure of its humour.UnEpic Fran is an incredibly talented developer who has an otherwise commendable track record. UnMetal is not an example of shoddy workmanship; rather, it's an example of a developer taking a swing and missing the mark quite spectacularly. Play Ghost 1.0 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal is a 2D retro pixel top down action/stealth/adventure game with a 1980's comedy/military/action film theme.  Gameplay consists of managing your inventory to solve puzzles, stealthing around, beating people up/shooting them, etc etc.  The game design itself is quite deep and rich and showed great potential, but incomprehensibly the developer threw all their hard work into the trash when they decided not to bother doing proper graphics or anything, and just phoned it in with lazy, ugly 2D retro pixel "art" instead of proper graphics.  It's 2022, you know, not 1991. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.  The developers didn't design the game for modern gaming PCs, as such the game resolution caps out at 1080p, a very low resolution that became mainstream back in 2006 and became obsolete when 4K entered the mainstream in 2014.  The game simply won't look right on modern gaming displays due to this failure on the part of the developers.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.UnMetal has the laughable, eye watering price of $20 USD (for a 2D pixel game!!!), for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games, let alone the sheer number of free games available on Steam.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is undoubtedly designed for old-school Metal Gear fans. The similarity in gameplay style, combined with additional content, voiced dialogues, and unreliable storytelling, makes the game more engaging.The core story is fair enough for an action-hero-against-villain-military game with both stealth and mandatory hard fights under certain unconventional conditions. However, it becomes more interesting and is elevated to another level of complexity by being elaborated on by the protagonist himself in more than one event in the near future. This element sparks doubt and curiosity, making the story more addictive.The gameplay is also commendable. In addition to elements derived from old-school Metal Gear, including stealth and action-packed sequences, the item combination system occasionally gives players a chance to test their brains to make progress, not just their reflexes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is beautiful. It's satire but it manages to be a great retro game that feels classic in everything in a good way. _childDocuments_.review: Context : I like to play some short games between my playthroughs of long and challenging cRPGs. UnMetal was quite entertaining and funny.  Although it is not a serious game, it is mostly stealth missions (not easy), with some hard bosses or "boss challenges" at the end of each chapter (that you cannot succeed without dying a few times), and the story has some pretty good twists!  Also, every one of the 10 chapters are very different and it was all-around fun. Some "bosses" took me 10 to 15 attempts, but it can be done, once you practiced it many times. I managed to get 33 of the 40 achievements in one playthrough. It took me about 15 hours, but most people report finishing in around 10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Got it on sale for 5 dollars USD. For that price, it's a great game. Took me about 10 hours to complete the story on medium / normal difficulty. Some of the game moments totally upset me, however the thing is... It did so in a way that brought me back for more, to try again because "I know I can do it" and I must say... Good fun! Simple yet clever story with enjoyable writing for my sense of humor. If you like difficult old school games AND appreciate a campy comedy vibe, then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: A spoof on Metal Gear with dashes of other video game references presented with loads of humour.Do you need to play Metal Gear before you play UnMetal?  No, but you'd definitely get much more out of the game if you played maybe the first two Solid games.I didn't know what to think going in, but I was surprised how much fun I had with UnMetal.  The gameplay is exciting and the mechanics all work extremely well.   I had a couple hang-ups with puzzles and missing some destructible environmental pieces, but a little perseverance went a long way.  I played the game on Normal difficulty after toning it down from Hard.  I usually play my games on Hard or Ultra difficulties, but UnMetal has that old school difficulty which felt right for me on Normal.  Luckly, you can turn down the difficulty mid-game If you find things too tough.The presentation is exceptional with solid writing and excellent voice work.  I played with an Xbox controller and I thought the default control scheme was perfect. A truly fantastic gem of a game.  I'd highly recommend it to any stealth genre fan and especially those who've played the Metal Gear Series.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this expecting a revamped 2D Metal Gear like the ones from the MSX (knewing the author also made MSX games before). I *did not* know this was a remake of his older MSX game called Prisoner of War, which I remember when it was released and it looked awesome, but I had kinda just completely forgotten about it (even though I still have a working and plugged MSX2+ here :D )And if this was just a revamped 2D Metal Gear I'd be happy... but it isn't. It offers a lot more than any of the 2D Metal Gear games ever offered, with variety on the gameplay. The game always seems to be throwing new mechanics and gameplay features at you, so it never gets tiresome. Also the game length is perfect without ever overstaying its welcome. The last 2 levels *do* feel a lot like the MSX Metal Gear games (with Rooftops, Basement and stuff), and that was actually great.There are also secrets to find out and probably a lot of stuff I've missed (I mean... I never used the Radio's Channel 3?????)Difficulty level is good enough. You *will* see the Game Over screen a lot of times, but... if you played the origina Metal Gear back in the day, you also did it, so you know what to expect (and checkpoints here are really fairly spaced, much beter than how it used to be back then :D ) There's also a huge dose of humour (I laughed a lot, it seems some people didn't find it funny) and references to Pop Culture (I know where you saw that "Cat Joke", ok? And The Goonies is my fav movie ever :D ).Graphics are exactly the kind of thing I expect from 2D indie games, they don't "try" to look retro and fail, they just look good while being at a lower resolution. Soundwise the game is awesome, none of the BFXR sound effects we usually see on indie games, and the voice acting (at least on english, didn't try the Spanish one) is excellent. This actually has a huge production value for such a small indie game.Controls are great, it plays fine and it's a lot of fun. My only gripe with it (and others pointed it out) are the trial and error sections where you have to try to guess a correct answer without any tips or clues, and it's all about dumb luck or just "die and try a different answer again". Fortunately there weren't a lot of moments like this, but they were enough to diminish the experience. Overall, I recommend the game a lot. I had loved Mini Ghost, but this here is an even better game. Can't recommend it enough, awesome game.(But seriously, what with Radio's Channel 3? :D )

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic writing and solid game mechanics make for a great game that stands on its own merits, but coupled with the parody angle and really great Monty Python/Leslie Nielsen absurdist comedy it should be a cult classic hit. A blend of MacGuyver x Metal Gear, every level gives you a few new tools and puzzles to tackle, keeping it fresh in a hard-to-put-down game. Fantastic even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Great metal gear clone.  Disagree with negative reviews focusing on the humor and purported uneven challenge. Cut scenes can sometimes get lengthy, but are easily skippable if you already watched it (or if you are just one of those weirdo gamers who don't watch the cut scenes ever).  I thought the challenge was fine, never unfair, and progressively harder but never got extremely tedious or anything.  I mean you will die, but it's easy to learn from mistakes and I never got stuck on one part or boss for hrs or anything, which I mark as a good thing.  And while the game is set in stages, most are not linear and there are a fair amount of secrets to be found.  There was also a leveling system for stealthy takedowns which I thought was a nice add.All in all great game, especially if you like the old school metal gears.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a serious spiritual successor to the original top-down 2D Metal Gear games on the NES/MSX, but this is actually more like a parody game (albeit a full-featured one) you would play on NewGrounds. And yet despite saying this, it is not a bad at all.- The retro-pixel graphics are pretty and the system requirements are low, allowing a smooth 60FPS+ experience throughout the game.- The writing is passable. Despite the plot starting off as an extremely bog-standard "you're a POW and need to escape the evil military general's stronghold" shtick there are a few twists and turns (along with Jesse being an unreliable narrator) that keep things fresh. You start wondering what crazy stuff the game is going to throw at you next near the end due to the unpredictable off-the-wall humor.- Since the plot is technically a story that is being retold to the player through Jesse, are several points in the game where you are allowed to choose the challenges you face like a choose-your-adventure book. This is a cool way of taking advantage of the medium and allows for some extra replay value to see how differing choices influence the gameplay.- The controls are easy to learn and responsive.- Overall the game has a ton of personality and it's clear the developer wanted to show his love for old school Metal Gear and 80s action movies.- If you make a sequel please tell Jesse's English voice actor to just do a generic gruff voice instead of the unbearably bad David Hayer impression.- The evasion mechanics leave something to be desired. If you are spotted the game will enter an alert phase, where infinite waves of guards will spawn in to search for you, and the only way to stop it is by staying out of sight. Only...there are no places to hide. No vents, no lockers, no nothing. This means you're almost always better just quickloading if you are spotted, as avoiding the endless stream of guards is just dumb luck and relies on their AI not stumbling into you.- You're not allowed to kill anyone. Each time you shoot a guard you are forced to burn a first-aid kit to stabilize them, otherwise they die and the game is over. It makes sense in the context of the story they set up, but it would have been nice choose this optionally instead of being railroaded into it. This compounds with the lack of meaningful evasion mechanics listed in point two, and makes defending yourself in an alert phase near impossible.- Once you get your bearings the game is pretty linear with its chapter-like structure. Some more free-foaming elements and the ability to backtrack/unlock new areas (be they required or optional) with your new gear would be nice.Not all the jokes land and there are some small segments of trial-and-error frustration, but it's overall a pretty good experience and I enjoyed it. I think the asking price is pretty steep however, and that something closer to around 10 USD would be a bit more reasonable. If you can grab it on sale like I did, it's worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with some really funny humor. It's definitely both a love letter yet a fun parody of the original two Metal Gear (non-Solid) games. It's pretty well polished, but I do think it could've done with a little more explanation on certain things, or for the codec to be more directly useful/conversational about what the player might be stuck on. Has a lot of fun dialogue for different situations that the player might've picked.The story itself is relatively "lacking", but that's not a bad thing. It feels more like a vehicle for humor and the game itself more than something to enjoy in itself. But just letting you know in case if you hate stories that exist for that reason.My personal biggest con in the game is that there are some "secrets" in the game that you kind of need if you want more HP. You find them by punching certain spots. I didn't really know that until almost the end of the game so the bosses were rather difficult, having so little HP, but the game is still doable even with the smaller HP.I'd also recommend going "Normal", rather than "Hard". Normal is pretty difficult enough for a really solid challenge, and Hard feels rather hard. That said, I never used the pottys (whether the game didn't explain it or I just missed the explanation, I don't know) nor found many secrets, so that's all it could've been.
