_childDocuments_.review: - As the title implies, this is a love letter to old school 2D stealth action games. Hell, the main character even looks like Solid Snake- It's got the pixel art to match those old games, though it does look considerably nicer than either Metal Gear or Snake's Revenge on the NES- The music is pretty good (especially during the boss fights), but the best part of this game's audio is the voice acting. The performances were really well done all around, especially Jesse Fox and The Colonel- The story isn't anything new for the genre. You've been imprisoned for a crime you didn't commit. In trying to escape, you find that the organization keeping you hostage is building some sort of weapon. You've got to stop the bad guys and get out. This should all sound very familiar- That stereotypical narrative is spun out into a pretty funny frame story where the main character is trying to impress a date, at least- The dialogue is hilarious. I was consistently chuckling to myself the whole time- Even though it's a parody of the early days of the Metal Gear franchise, it's all done in a pretty friendly way. It does a good job poking fun at the silliness of those plotlines and their overly serious tones without stooping to outright ridicule- If you ever played a top-down stealth action game from the NES era, this is basically the same thing. Gather weapons and tools, sneak around, knock out guards, and try to avoid open firefights unless it's a boss- There's a few other quirks beyond that usual formula (like having to stabilize guards after shooting them since you promised the hot doctor you wouldn't kill anyone), but the mechanics are pretty easy to get the hang of- I wish the bosses had been a little more creative. The final boss is pretty cool, but the bosses leading up to it are kinda forgettable- If I do wind up replaying this game someday, it'll probably be for the humor more than the story- I wasn't expecting this game to be as entertaining as it was. It was a very enjoyable throughout its entire 10-ish hours- This was an excellent Steam Deck game. Pretty easy to pick up and put down whenever, but I didn't really want to put it down- . A genuinely funny game with some solid 2D stealth gameplay. In many ways, it doesn't feel like a new experience, but it's just so entertaining that I didn't really mind
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Got it as part of Humble Choice and spun it up as a break in between larger games. A meme game but it does it well - the retro graphics are awesome and the game play is simple yet doesn't get tiresome. Humour, parody and easter eggs are paced evenly and don't become stale. About 10 hours in length (I left it on the menu for a while).Definitely recommend if you are looking for something short that doesn't overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through Unmetal on a different platform, and now I am playing it through Steam.Would I say this is a good game? No.I would say that this is a fantastic game, and one of the best I have ever played.I am a huge fan of the original Metal Gear...before it went "Solid". This plays so much like it, that I feel right at home. But the story, and the humor are spot on. I really doubt all the references the younger generation will get, like the A-Team or The Goonies (even Bryan Adams), but they hit perfectly for me. Everything is so well written, and there are parts where you have choices on how things will turn out. Sometimes you end up making that game harder when you think you are making it easier.Unmetal is the perfect example of why indie games are outdoing AAA titles. I really hope that they keep making more games at this caliber....all indie creators. This game is a treat in every way.Stop reading and start playing it!!!P.S. The Ungear up ad......so perfect, and brings back so many memories of when I first found out about Metal Gear.Edit: Just so everyone is aware...there is a lot of bad language in the game. I just wanted to mention this in case this is something that bothers anyone reading this review.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game if you skip the gameplay :)You'll get most of the game process through first two hours and the rest of the game is worth to be seen because of amount of references, jokes and a script itself, but playing it feels repetitive and exhausting the further you go.Overall I would recommend to buy it and watch the longplay or play it on a steamdeck, as the game itself feels worthy if you're into games like MGS series and 90's/00's movies :)
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really like point & click games, and this one totally tricks you into think it's NOT one of those... but it is. Still, the grfx and and way you move around really gives you some 'adventure/action' feel to a P&C. The humor is nice and it really doesn't take itself too seriously. It has tons of tropes and parodies to other games and media. SOMETIMES it can drag on a bit and the cut-scenes can be a bit TOO long, but that's probably another parody of Metal Gear Solid. Only REAL downside, is the main character's voice. I know it's a MGS David Hayter thing, but it just never grows on you, sadly. Otherwise, it's all pretty fun and quick to pick up and play.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: The storyline is full of humor and offers a fun parody of the classic Metal Gear games with retro graphics. The controls are smooth and the boss battles are entertaining. Easy to just pick up and play and I found myself laughing at the humor multiple times. The comedy is reminiscent of classics like Hot Shots and Naked Gun.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting homage to MSX and Nintendo era Metal Gear that masterfully emulates the retro gaming experience while keeping it fresh. _childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Humor is relative, I know. It's a good thing then that I'm the type of idiot this Metal Gear spoof was made for. _childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal is a clever game with good comedic value, it fools you/predicts you a few times and even makes fun of you for it. It makes you think about what you're doing for the rest of the game if there's something simple you missed. I looked up a walkthrough twice while playing, I wish I hadn't, because both times it was something stupid yet simple that I should have known, if you get stuck, think about that.I was able to predict the very end but and you likely will too when it happens. Expect to play some bosses over and over again, the patterns are difficult but they are all possible with repetition.Minor spoiler below about the amount of missions there are because I think if I knew how many there were I wouldn't have felt the game went on too long.Cons: - I don't think the 'secrets' were easy enough to find, one plot point is never answered, and the weapons live a little bit to be desired.Overall, it's funny, worth playing especially given the Metal Gear references for fans of that series.8/10***************slight spoiler below that won't ruin the game, about how many missions there are*************......There are 10 missions - I just felt like if I knew that I would have more happily sat through some of the dialogue towards the end, around mission 7 or 8 I started to skip some parts, so just know that it will probably end soon once you get bored of the slapstick script.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: great stealth action game, i also found it to be funny especially if you like meta jokesi haven't played the original metal gear games so i don't know how much of it is copiedthe bosses are mostly simple fun puzzles and on normal difficulty were usually just hard as they should bethe none boss puzzles are also fun the mostly everything works well, the default controls are a bit wonky but changeable
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Solid stealth gameplay for a few chapters, then it stops being fun very quickly. The no-kills limitation imposed on you at the midgame is laughable game design. Every time you shoot a guard, you have to expend a medkit to heal him or get a game over. Meaning if I get spotted, I can fight with my fists and certainly get killed by the reinforcements, or I can gun everybody down, not have enough medkits to heal everyone, and get a game over anyway.Escaping isn't an option in most places so the only thing you can really do after being spotted is just let the guards kill you, every time. For the entire back half of the game. A nice thing about Metal Gear is that it doesn't expect you to 100% stealth it, and it actually gives you the tools to fight your way out of a bind. Shame that Unmetal didn't catch on to this.The story and cast are bland and mostly serve as a vehicle to deliver the game's long, grating comedy scenes with endlessly recycled punchlines. By the last chapter it's so creatively bankrupt that it resorts to "Japanese people have funny accents" as a joke on its own. What an absolute mess. Would have been a hit if it was on Newgrounds in 2005.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love-letter to fans of action movies, satires, and Metal Gear Solid. It looks and plays like the old-school 2D Metal Gear games and is chock full of references and tropes. The Hunt For Red October, The Terminator, and even cheesy 1980s pop rock and King of the Hill. It is filled with secrets, choices to make, and an entertaining story. The language is harsher than what you'd expect from a game like this. There is replay value to be sure, to unlock all of the secrets and see all of the different dialogue choices. The art style holds up well and the animations are smooth.The game is not for everyone. Sometimes the writers don't know when to let a joke go, and there are a few setpieces where the gameplay elements feel like a hindrance. Some puzzles have very roundabout solutions, and not in a good way. Remember that really obscure puzzle solution from Metal Gear 2 where you had to pick up an egg, incubate it to hatch an owl, and then have the owl hoot so that a guard thought it was night time so they can leave the front gate? That's a solution that most players were not able to to figure out due to crazy moon logic, and this game has puzzles and setpieces just like that. Personally I think that should have been left in the past.Overall, a solid game that I would rate as a 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Oh this game is fun, silly and a delight to play.The whole premise is a parody of metal gear solid and it's done in such a silly but great way even my girlfriend laughed at some of it. I managed to complete it in one sitting, if i wasn't bad at some parted could of done quickly easily a 4 - 6 hour for a regular gamer.I loved the music, the artwork and just the fluidity and ease of the game, i actually struggeled to find secreted like i think i only found 2 through out it all.If you go in, just remember...we're not assassins...we're just a civilian

_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal is a true definition of one of those games that I suck about, but oh my god how I enjoyed it. The game is an amazing Metal Gear satire, with a story full of jokes and awkward moments. The 2D artstyle is really cool and helps the game vibe. But you clearly understand that the game is not old and that the developer made a tremendous effort to make the game look old but have quality of life features like voice acting on every line.Gameplay speaking it is a pretty fun to play, it looks like optimized for controller but it can be easily played with a keyboard (the way I played it)... but as I said in the start it is one of those games that I suck about. The game bosses are a complete pain and, although I have manage to crawl my way through out the game, so far, after countless hours, I couldn't defeat the final boss. Maybe "Mike" can help me out, ahahah..To summarise it is a game that I fully recommend. Whether you're a fan of stealth games, 2D style games or even Metal Gear, this is a game to try.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal achieves its goal of serving a humorous homage to the games for the creator's childhood.The gameplay is enjoyable, with every stage having it's own mechanics and look/feel. The boss battles are also all distinct and bring some welcomed change of pace, but the fact that you can't skip the bosses' splash screens got really grating, adding unnecessary friction between the boss attempts. The voice acting is well done and a very welcomed addition, enhancing the character's personalities and humor. That being said, I found the humor to be very hit-or-miss, often relying on the use of "♥♥♥♥" as a crutch. My favorite jokes were those directly tied to gameplay, such as the times when you get to choose the outcome of the protagonist's narration. The rare occasions where the game comments on your actions were also a standout. Some sections, such as the minefields or the death labyrinth near the end, just slow the pace to a grinding halt, bringing just frustration and not much else. If this was game was about 20% shorter, this would have been an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal is a top-down, 2-D stealth and action game. The graphics are pixelated. But, the characters (during conversations) and map designs are nicely done.It doesn't take itself too seriously. The story is narrated by the protagonist, and all the action takes place in the past.Some of the jokes fell flat, and the story felt amateurish at times. But I did laugh on a few occasions. All the actors' voice work is excellent.I liked some of the soundtracks. The sound design is serviceable.The gameplay is good. The weapon choices are limited. That is understandable since you need to do stealth takedowns most of the time. That is a good idea. Because the more takedowns you perform, the more experience you gain. This helps with levelling up and unlocking different abilities (a light RPG element).You also have to collect and use different types of resources, as well as combine them, to get through some of the sections.There are some game-design choices that may feel unfair and frustrating at times. You need to select dialogues in a particular order to progress. If you make the wrong choice, the game is over. As a result, you must rely on trial and error. Some of the boss battles may require a few tries. So hold on and don't rage-quit. You will get through eventually. The Vs (versus) splash screen pops up every time during boss battles, which is annoying if you die so many times (and also restarts from the last checkpoint instead of directly putting you against the boss). They have gone overboard with cutscenes. It may break the flow of the game. That could have been kept at a minimal level. Also, I was dissatisfied with the ending.It took me around 12 hours to complete my first playthrough on normal. I have played it again on hard to get the remaining achievement(s).Overall, I have enjoyed it for the most part.I would recommend getting this during a sale or through any bundle if it's available.My verdict: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with my time playing Unmetal, although it's not one I imagine I would play through a second time. I enjoyed the humor of the game, but someone who does not enjoy this kind of humor would not enjoy this game. The humor in the game is far better than the videos here on steam might indicate - I would suggest watching some gameplay videos prior to playing.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little stealth game.It has a mix of unique game characteristics that we don't see very often:- Very good stealth gameplay that's not slow or annoying- Good humorous story. Parodies are often cringe, but this one is an exception (for the most part)- Accent on non-violence done right- Cool retro graphicsThe game is not perfect.The biggest flaw is the same one from Thief 1. It's like the authors didn't have enough fate in their own stealth gameplay, so they added a bunch of extra gimmicks (driving sequences, explosive shootouts etc). I'd rather if they somehow deepened the stealth elements instead.Also, the story felt a bit over-explained near the end. Like the authors became too impressed with their own lore. The ending wasn't as clever as they thought.I finished the game in 14 hr, during one sitting pretty much. High recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This game really surprised me. I've never actually played any Metal Gear games, but I could immediately see this game was an homage to them. I was just expecting it to be a lot more bland than it actually is. The story is great and full of humour, and the campiness of the dialogue is actually a good thing. Gameplay is great too, and it's just the right difficulty level for me. I don't mind dying a few times here and there to figure out how to progress to the next area. But I haven't gotten to a point where I'm stuck on an overly hard part and quit out of frustration.The only complaint I have is with the CRT filter. I get that some people like the retro look of it in games, but other than thinking "Oh yeah, this is how games used to look" I'm really not a fan of it. It just makes games look worse than they need to since we obviously don't have the limitations we used to with technology. I wish the developers would've given us an option to turn it off.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty hilarious game. Many are comparing it to Leslie Nielson, I'm personally going for Topper Harley from Hot Shots, at least moreso in tone. Maybe it's fresher on my mind than Spy Game. Hilarious either way.The game is somewhat simple, where to knock out guards and advance, you must do a 3-hit combo, finishing with a roundhouse kick (nice touch). You get points for doing so stealthily, of course, and there are silly scenarios lined up and down the game. I've made it to chapter 5 only, and it hasn't filled out with repeat material yet, don't expect it to. This is a simple escape game in terms of the basic commands being hit, roll, and shoot, mostly, but you also have an inventory system where you can combine scraps you come along and string together materials to aid your escape.Bosses feel a bit generic at the end of the day, but still challenging while holding a unique theme. I've been searching every nook and cranny, yet have come up with zero game secrets over the first 4 chapters. I don't expect the secrets to be hinted at this point, so a guide is probably necessary to find them.All in all, while this is a pixelated game, the game is completely voice acted, and done well, again with the Topper Harley vibe described earlier. This is done with a narration based on interrogation from an officer, too, so you get a bit of funny snarkiness throughout as well. This package has been a pleasant surprise at every turn, despite otherwise seeming like what would be an over-simplistic game. Strong recommend for the Indie hunters out there, and still a recommend for anyone who needs a game to tickle their funny bone a little. This might genuinely be my favorite comedy to date, which is partly because of how dry the comedy field feels in gaming, but this is no slouch. If any game will scratch that comedy itch, it'd be this one right here.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: The controls take some getting adjusted to and the voice mastering can be a bit wierd at times (too loud or too slient from one scene to the next), though in any case the game stays fresh to the end, always throwing new or varied mechanics at you and providing fun diagoue to listen to. It's a rather unique experience I'd recommend.

_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what you'd expect from the title and the look of this game. The voice acting is surprisingly full and well acted, the art-style and motion works really well alongside it and the gameplay. I also really like the crafting mechanics in the inventory too, it's really clever and funny how they relate to both the gameplay and even the narrative.So far, so good. Really enjoying this title. I'll probably come back and give a more polished review... I dunno. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is a game that does not take itself very seriously, it will do whatever it wants to try and make you laugh, breaking any logic and even making the main character stupid for a bit. Expect jokes ranging from game design tropes of stealth, subverting choices given to players, or some flat-out scenes where some characters are unaware they are in a comedy game and play it straight.All these jokes will help mix up what would normally be a simple stealth game with each mission being quite varied and never overstaying its welcome with new gadgets and obstacles to overcome. Boss fights are equally fun and funny, with one being a dialogue fight over Texas, that I will never forget. If you are ok with simple stealth that will throw some curveballs of difficulty in some boss fights and sometimes getting lost at how to progress. These minor gripes in a rather well-paced game will be quickly forgotten as they did for me.If you’re on the fence I have some highlights down below to see the vibe and if you don’t laugh at the reason for how he breaks out of jail in the beginning, the game’s humor is not for you. _childDocuments_.review: It's hilarious and the Mike joke was great every single time. Really well done. Gameplay manages to be fun, while also being funny and holds through to the end. I thought all the items were great; lot of them funny. The save system is xD bosses were all good. It's challenging enough too, but just enough. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice game, all problems from other reviews either don't exist or were already fixed.- Humor in the game is nice. It's not something you're gonna laugh too much, perhaps chuckle or smile in a couple of places - it's just a bonus to a game with good gameplay. I don't get why some people think it's repetetive/dull. Most jokes are repeating gags but I don't really see a problem with that. And some jokes are *really* ingenious.- Story is as good as any action movie story, except it's not taken very seriously.- Gameplay. The game has pretty much 3 stages of the main gameplay loop:       * Neutralize guards. You have to get rid of guards without making them raise an alarm/notice something's off. It's really fun considering there are a few types of guards, tools, different maps etc       * Puzzles. Puzzles in this game are rather obvious. It's usually combine item X with Y, read a sign, break a crate while camera isn't looking. They also usually have some sort of a skill element to them, like when avoiding traps. It's not much but it's generally enjoyable.       * Boss battles. This game has a fair share of boss battles. They're generally fun although simple. They're pretty much the only place in the game where you have to do your usual skill focused dodge&shoot.What could be made better:- I'd love to get some optional stuff you can craft with the items you gather. There are tons of items without use and it'd be a great rewarding element for people who tinkered with them. The only optional craftable item is molotov which is just a reskinned grenade you can get early on.- It'd be also nice to get more sandbox/open interactions on maps. Some of them are fairly open but there aren't any optional locations aside of secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I was recommended this game and I am SO glad I pulled the trigger. It is a brilliantly fun game. It felt nostalgic, but not old - tricky, but not impossible. I completed the game on normal in 30 hours, but I still have a lot of achivenments to complete, so will be playing again. If you want a game that makes you smile and laugh whilst you throw coins to distract guards, then punch their lights out - this is the game. 10/10 - will play again.tl;dr - If Metal Gear Solid had a baby with Monkey Island.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This game is intense and rooted in the original Metal Gear, it has great satire and references to other games, TV, movies. The comedy and intense action is paced just right. Controls are solid and the mechanics are fun and interesting, Jesse Fox has to be my new favorite character coming out of a indie game, he's witty, smart, sneaky, kick ass and a bit dim in some places but a really great character with great story that you never know is real or not even at the very end. This deserves a sequel and I have a name...how about "Unmetal 2: Fox's Revenge?"
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: A lite metal gear parody done in the old MSX style. Pros: Great pixel artGood controlsDecent stealth mechanicsJokesCons: Biggest gripe was some of the dialogue that dragged on for WAY too long. I get this is poking fun at Kojima, but let's not take it too far. Jesse's made out of single ply, unscented, unpatterned toilet paper; and you die from a couple of hits. The medkits heal over time and you're likely to get hit again when trying to heal. Basically the motto of the game is don't get caught, don't get shot. Overall ruling: 21 hours for a full clear (2 full playthroughs). I got it on sale, so the price is right. Go ahead and snag it.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and silly, Some of the things in this game will throw you for a loop and wondering where you'll go next. It'll have you at the edge of your seat for completely unexpected reasons.The stealth mechanics are pretty sensible, and forgiving/exploitable with little to no consequences.Boss fights and events were pretty straightforward, didnt feel the need once to whip out a strategy guide.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a tight blend of metal gear solid for gameboy color and link's awakening on gameboy.If you enjoy the metal gear games, there's  a good chance you'll appreciate the game play of this one.As far as challenge goes: On the action side this was an enjoyable and pretty easy game to play through, there wasn't a single time where I sat down with the game and couldn't figure my way through at least a few parts of it. There are however a few situational and conversational scenarios that are a bit frustrating, but if you enjoy doing some trial error/detective work the solutions eventually become apparent.I'm personally a big fan of the Hideo Kojima games, but in the states I think I might be a minority in the fact that I actually enjoy the off the wall/philosophical narratives, easter eggs, and themes of the Kojima team's games.This game's narrative completely exchanges that layer of philosophical depth for a super silly absurd 80s action parody. I'm not saying this is bad, I'm just saying upfront, don't take this game too seriously it knows it's silly and embraces that goofy side. Half the time it cracks me up, half the time I cringe a bit, probably won't play it again, but glad I did once.Nice work to the devs!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: If you like metal gear games you'll have fun with this game. Very clever game/level design, fun story. Jesse Fox is kind of a knucklehead douche who seems to end up in the wrong place at the wrong time. He narrates the whole game as you progress and make decisions Jesse will chime in with the appropriate dialogue it's pretty cool and usually funny. The game doesn't take itself seriously which I like as well. It was one of my favourite games of 2021 to be honest. I hope there's a sequel one day.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: A stealth game with a lot of humour, but not a simple game. Some bosses can present a real challenge, especially on hard mode. The pixel art is great, the level design is very varied and constantly presents new mechanics so it doesn't get repetitive at all and the voice acting is a real marvel. Infiltration is simple and rewarding.The fact of testing objects at random to see if the creator has had in mind some nonsense is wonderful, and spoiler: he has taken it into account. In the 15 hours it took me to complete all its achievements, it made me laugh on many occasions and the good times it gave me were priceless.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Metal Gear, this game is for you. I've played every entry in the series, including the original MSX titles this parody is based on, and I can assure you this game is a love letter to the franchise.What surprised me most was how challenging and thoughtful the game design was in Unmetal. You won't just be laughing at the dialogue; the actual items and scenarios themselves are genuinely funny. This is definitely a game I will be re-playing. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is a great indie game, and I am pretty intrigued by this realization : I found it good roughly for the same reasons than everyone found Undertale so good, even though it's in a very different genre! The surprises, writing, and little innovations scattered through a classic gameplay loop make it very fun and allows the user to be sucked in the experience, despite the technical limitations of the game. And that's what makes it a bit like Undertale : both games transcend what retro-pixel games usually do with great touches of modernity, humor and creativity.You keep being pleasantly surprised and entertained by the wacky ideas and the jokes, which all somehow blend well together into a parody of Kojima's famous franchise.Unmetal a good moment that you should definitely try, unless maybe if you're deadly allergic to the old Metal Gear games that it parodies.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Jessie Fox is everything I wanted from a Metal Gear game, and an outside player combined. A very funny and charming game, which benefits from previous tropes and mechanics from other games. It didn't innovate much beyond expectations, but the story telling itself was very appreciated. Segments to obtain player input to choose the difficulty, narration which clues you in on reality, and of course a explainable reason for all the wild nonsense we witness throughout the game. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift and I'm really glad I did!It's well polished, well written, and overall, a well designed game that was a joy to play. The controls felt appropriate and responsive, the story was quirky and interesting - really it's hard to find much wrong with it. If I had to be nitpicky, I would say the non-lethal ranged weapon (uranium balls) was something I used less than I'd have liked as the other options I had were superior, but that's about it (though I only played on medium - hard might require more usage of it!)All in all, a great experience that I can wholeheartedly recommend and that I can definitely see myself replaying in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Doing a good parody is hard. You should have a really good understanding of the source material. You should imitate the original work you intend to mock, as closely as possible. And this is what Unmetal masterfully achieves. It’s a perfect parody of Metal Gear Solid games.Unmetal plays as if the characters, dialogues are all taken directly from the Metal Gear Solid franchise (more so from the original Metal Gear titles), albeit in a more exaggerated and hilarious way. Without spoiling anything, it is a very complete story from start to finish and the laughs never stop until the very end. Unmetal is a must-play for all Metal Gear Solid fans. I think it is a must-play for all the Kung Fury fans, as the sense of humour gives very similar vibes. It is also a remarkable video game and easily one of the most underrated games of 2021. Just make sure you have played at least one MGS game in advance, so you get all the jokes.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Played this after UnEpic and both the Ghosts - nice to hear some audio cues and motifs again. In my opinion, UnMetal definitely has the best storytelling of all three, but sadly also the worst gameplay. Indeed UnMetal felt, at times, as if a story I was invested in kept me from playing a game I didn't even enjoy.The first half of UnMetal is a precious, little gem. Every time you think you have it figured out, UnMetal does something you did almost, but not quite expect - particularly when it commits to its own gags and schemes, instead of just dropping pop culture references. At times I was chuckling, at times I was plainly laughing my heart out. This part is also why I'd still recommend UnMetal.Gameplay in the first half of UnMetal feels like some sort of tutorial, and you keep waiting for the moment that the game opens up and lets you take the reigns. However, that moment never comes. Instead, UnMetal continues throughout its second half exactly as it had started: Short, railroaded gameplay sequences and small, funny snippets of dialogue that almost overstay their welcome.Worse, even, that gameplay mechanics are not up to par with general writing. Levels are tiny and mostly linear. Puzzles are trivial and still have their solution spelled out at times. The more "modern" gameplay features need more polish - such as tolerance frames for surveillance cameras or a visual indicator for hold-to-choke range. UnMetal wants to encourage stealth (which earns XP), but still gives you a gun (which expedites your medkits to keep downed foes alive). Even then, gunplay feels worse than in the original NES Metal Gear - you can't shoot at an angle, but your enemies can. Last, but not least, the worst offender: There are a lot of cheap, for-the-lulz, one-hit deathtraps at the expense of the player. The first few were fun (), but it grows old a good ways before the end of the game - more so since some of these traps can't be figured out without trial and error.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: A sometimes frustrating but mostly hilarious game with a fun, creative storytelling style which I am not sure if I've seen elsewhere in a game to date.  There are some frustrating sections using the old school unforgiving trial and error mechanic but in almost every instance where this is at play success brings a sense of accomplishment and another great joke / bit of story progression.  I probably laughed more playing this and had more fun with it than a great number of much fancier looking big budget games.Highly recommended retro romp worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game thinking this gonna be something on style to first metal gear solid. I think this way surpassed my expectations. Story = great, gameplay = fun, memes = a lot, A LOT. I had one of the best laughs playing this, enjoyed the inside jokes, laughed on my own stupidity as narrator points out something obvious that I haven't thought of. This game is amazing. <3You should buy it Mike
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: If you are reading this, then you know what kind of game this is and you know you want to play it. Buy it now!Seriously, it's a good game. It's a light espionage stealth game with a pack of action and funny jokes. If you know the references and easter eggs, you'll enjoy it a tad more, but it's not essential to have a fun time with this game. The visuals are great and fit the game perfectly, even the scanline effect adds a lot to the overall feeling of the game, a very nice detail.Something I really enjoyed were all those interactive decisions which change the game as you play through, they make the game very replayable and fun. I actually never have seen it implemented so well in a videogame, it's brilliant.There aren't many downsides, they mostly depend of your tastes and how you play the game, but sometimes the difficulty curve is a bit high where you need to take very specific actions or you'll die. This leads to a lot of repetition of the same segment over and over, but it's fun and challenging so I can let that slip.Bottom line, if you like top-down view games, this is an easy recommendation. Have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't aware Fran had a new game in the works and only heard about Unmetal the day it released.Immediately went to grab it and play through it all, and immensely enjoyed it. Currently replaying it to hunt for secrets and challenges.The Metal Gear (Solid-less) parody works very well (having played them quite extensively back in the day, it hits the nostalgia chord just right) and this story told by Jesse Fox was quite enjoyable, with him always tossing absurd, wacky or totally random bits at the military officer who's getting his testimony and his girlfriend.The gameplay is just what you'd expect from a game of this genre and works very well, with a twist that Fox hasn't killed anybody throughout his entire journey to escape the situation he ended up in. Meaning that yes, you don't kill anybody and should you try, you will have to save them or face defeat. Also, you are rewarded for being as sneaky as possible, so forget going in guns blazing.It may not be the greatest game in the genre, but it's close enough. That was very enjoyable and I would urge you to check it out.(Shoutout to the Grenade Guy, )

_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is unique in the sense that it is a comedy parody of a game yet still manages to deliver the solid experience of that of which it is making fun. In this case the games in question are the old MSX Metal Gear games from before the series took the jump into 3D.You play as Jesse Fox, a man who was imprisoned for a crime he didn't commit, who has tasked himself from escaping captivity in the most non-lethal and environmentally friendly possible ways. The game is played from a bird's eye perspective and at it's heart is a stealth game where the player tries to avoid detection from the guards whether it is by sneaking past them or quietly knocking them out.For the most part gameplay is simple and intuitive. The basics you learn early on are very rarely strayed from until much later in the game where extra elements such as security cameras and trip lasers force you to utilise gadgets to hide yourself.Occasionally you will come across a boss fight. These can range from good to tedious. They will usually call upon the player to use weapons and tactics that are likely to be only used to their full extent for a particular boss strategy. I guess this is meant to give more of a puzzle element to the fights  but the odd one or two will test your patience as they rely on luck or trial and error judgements.The only other criticism I could make is that Fox can be a bit too slow to use health items (even with the speed upgrade) which makes them essentially useless in most boss fights. I'm a little unsure of how ideal the levelling up system was implemented on the other hand. Gaining enough XP to grow a level gives the player a choice between two skills or upgrades. Its sometimes a bit of a blind choice but not game breaking so I can't complain too hard.The rest of the game pretty much achieves all it intends. The look and sounds perfectly capture the 2d Metal Gear aesthetics while the script, which can be a little cheesy at time, does have plenty of funny jokes  and moments. Some of the more offbeat humour can be a result on the very light RPG choice elements given in the story where you may think your making it easier on yourself only to have the exact opposite effect much to the bemusement to the people Fox is telling his story to.Overall if your into comedy games or want a Metal Gear experience (that pokes holes in that series' serious take on the genre) you can't go wrong here. I found Unmetal to be a thoroughly enjoyable experience.Also as an added bonus I played through the whole thing on a very low end laptop so ideal for those looking for something that doesn't require a super PC to run.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Gear on NES was one of my favorite games and I enjoyed unepic and ghost, so I even preordered this game. So far I finished only single walkthrough on hard difficulty, so perhaps my impression of the game is not complete. The gameplay of most of the game is actually quite similar to that MetalGear, but with few tweaks, and tuned to be more stealthy. It's nice, but I wouldn't mind more shoot-n-run. And later in the game there's a lot of pieces where you have to learn the position of guards and cameras to stealth successfully, so it becomes a bit to much grindy. Again, maybe this happens only on hard difficulty. The biggest downside in terms of gameplay for me were the bosses. At least half of them felt with too much artificial difficulty, and not really exciting fights, especially if you compare them to the bosses from Unepic. And also ghost labyrinth. Seriously, ♥♥♥♥ that part. If it was some sort of sidequest, it was ok, but as a part of main story that was super annoying. The writing and is on the same level as in unepic_fan's previous games. By this I mean that it's fun, but don't expect it to be serious and well, the word "unepic" is in his name. The game has full voice acting, which is really nice and adds a lot to the characters. The only questionable point for me was which exact crime Jesse didn't commit. But maybe that's a DLC material.All in all it's nice game. Gameplay is not boring and varies a bit throuhgout the game, dialogues and story are nice, but... But, the game also feels a bit short. I finished hard while streaming in around 12 hours, and that's all, I mean there's no much more content. It's not that short, but I wish it was longer. Anyway, I still recommend you to buy it and support this dev, he delivers 3rd time in a row.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of the Metal Gear series my whole life, I figured this would be fun for a bit of a chuckle and see just how much Metal Gear could be put into a game without being slapped with a cease & desist. What I got instead was a fully fleshed out game and while it does nail the Metal Gear feel, it's also unique in its own right. This is one of my favorite games of 2021 and one of the best parody games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Good sense of humor is an essential ingredient for a great indie game that's pleasant to play., and I'm glad to say this game has it.However, on the later parts the game tries to be what it's not — a boss battle game. _childDocuments_.review: In the world of gaming, one of the most cliche and played-out premises is the stealthy one-man army, shamelessly copied from the Metal Gear franchise. But, the recent release of Unmetal is able to break the mold and deliver a fresh stealth experience full of wit, personality, and of course: cheesy action scenes.Unmetal is a top down stealth-action game parodying the popular Metal Gear franchise. From secretive government plots to clandestine military bases, Unmetal hits every beat expected from a Metal Gear ripoff, but puts a spin on each one every time, often making fun of the ridiculous situations and logical leaps commonly made in contemporary games. The humor is consistently spot on, and if you have experience with the games it's parodying, I guarantee you will be buckling over with laughter.When it comes to gameplay, it's the standard Metal Gear romp: Sneak around and silently eliminate guards while trying to stop the bad guy’s evil plot of world domination. Sometimes, the game will mix things up, for example: Giving you a gun but if you shoot a guard you have to patch them up with one of your very limited medkits because the main character doesn't kill people, or running through a sewer with a flamethrower while being chased by a horde of squirrels (no, I’m not making that up). Occasionally I got stuck doing the same screen over and over again, trying to take down the guards in just the right way that none of them see me taking out another one, with the most recent save point being upwards of 10 minutes of gameplay behind me. Aside from these rare occasions though, Unmetal is able to consistently keep gameplay fresh without compromising fun.At certain points throughout the story, the player is given a choice that can drastically change the situation they’re in, but often the player isn’t given much context on what each answer actually does. On paper this might sound annoying, but is actually really fun. For example, upon entering a room deep within a secret military compound and was immediately prompted with the main character saying (in his discount Solid Snake voice) “When I walked into the room I noticed the presence of…”. I was then given a choice between the letters GRD or the letters SHP. Due to my lack of knowledge on what these letters represented, I chose SHP. To my surprise, the room suddenly filled with sheep. It was funny to say the least. Very similar encounters happen often throughout the story, but I’ll keep their details in the dark because most of the fun is experiencing the shock of what your choice delivers.Unmetal puts a fun spin on an over-saturated genre, and is consistently able to keep me engaged, in a tense state of panic, or laughing. If you’re in the mood for some cheesy drama or lighthearted parody, Unmetal has you covered.

_childDocuments_.review: YES! YES! YES!This game has some issues with mechanics as bossfights can be a bee in your bonnet, but! And this is a big stinky but. The writing is amazing. The game almost killed me... TWICE! I spent 15 minutes in horrid gigglefit so that friends I was streaming the game to, were quite rightfully worried. The game is illegally funny. Like all Leslie Nielsen movies copulated with Hot shot movies. This game took month of stress off my shoulders and probably lengthened my life by 50 years if old sayings are to be believed.This game is small and not very long but it is one of the best games of 2021 for me. _childDocuments_.review: I own the game on both PS5 and Steam.Both versions work fine, But I have to admit that sitting next to the PC, I can view the pixel art far better.While Konami abandoned the Metal Gear franchise, Unepic games brings out a hommage to the beloved stealth action genre that goes the extra step beyond the original (Metal Gear 1+2) introducing new gameplay mechanics and mix it with a the great humor, I last have seen on Lucasarts and Double Fine adventures. So it s not only for Metal Gear fans (MUSTBUY!), but a good story based action game in general.Speaking of story, the story is told in a flashback. The main protagonist is under arrest and interrogated. Telling the story of his escape while you play it. This is extremly well done and one of the core aspects that make the game so great. The character forgets to mention details, can t remember until you discover a secret, and even is interrupted by other while telling the story. This changes during manifest in the visuals and the gameplay. Really a fresh idea. The first game that does this, to be honest.Story, Gameplay and variety is also pretty solid. Bosses are also fun and can be quite challenging!However the game over screen still is not as Metalgeary as it could be. :DI would LOVE to see part 2 being in production.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: As a MGS fan I could not let this one slide under my radar.An excellent parody of the Metal Gear series. It's more than just a handful of jokes, gameplay is also very good.Obviously the game makes many references to the og Metal Gear, but it also uses other sources for time to time (for example Full Metal Jacket).
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Tho i'm positive in general i feel the game is not exceptionally good.There is way too little sense of exploration and discovery. It feels very very linear.The boss fights are either easy or boring and there are way too many of them. The game relies way too much on dying in boss fights. With al lot of bosses i got sick of going through the 'continue' routine too many times as i learned the patterns. And in the end, when you know the trick the bosses are almost trivial. It's a cheesy way to program bosses imo.I also feel that not enough was done with the spaces/environments you travel through. The levels are generally quite small and the progress is linear. I didn't get the feeling i was alone on a mission in hostile territory, like in the original metal gear games. It didn't make sense as a coherent place and as i traveled along the path i only saw fragments of the place i wanted to explore. The game is structured as a story that constantly progresses and that leaves very little place for going 'the wrong way' and finding something interesting. Give me a serious base to explore, damnit!The game also seems to replicate some of the flaws of the original metal gear games. The problem is that these flaws are done for a joke but reappear constantly throughout the game. This makes the game worse because the joke becomes old very quickly and then you're left with something bad in your game.One such example is the face animation in the codec. The animation is done with a 'block copy' moving part of the face up and down. This was a fun joke and reference when i saw it the first time, but for the rest of the game it just looked bad.Nice level graphics. Not so nice graphics for the portraits and cutscenes.Nice music and sound effects, tho i'm getting really really sick of the 'continue' music because the game relies too much on retrying.The controls are in my opinion too complicated. On the pc you need 5 separate buttons for all the stuff and that already has one button mapped to a double function. It's a bit overkill.Fortunately the game is not very expensive and for the price it is a nice game.If i had to give it a number between 0 and 10 i would say somewhere between a 6.5 and a 7.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game a few minutes ago and here are my thoughts. For a parody of Metal Gear, this is the best and funniest game that I have ever played. The Stealth system in this game is extremely enjoyable and some of the puzzles are either really simple or some of them are a little challenging to get through like for example the final boss.

_childDocuments_.review: So first things first. Not only did I get UnMetal for free, I am also a part of the Versus Evil (Publisher) Herald program and if you download the free voice pack DLC and use code "Drogith", you can hear my voice lines in game. I was never paid for any of the content I created for UnMetal, I was literally just so enamored with it I had to do more.Now that all that is legally out of the way, I LOVE THIS GAME. From the moment I played the first chapter in the demo months ago until finishing the game just recently, UnMetal has been a knock your socks off laugh fest that harkens to the movie Hot Shots and plenty of titles from the 80s and 90s. This MGS style of game flips everything about that genre on it's head with whitty one liners, smooth combat, and plenty of Easter eggs that you can just randomly find... Like what happens when you combine a lit cigarette with gasoline?It only took me 3 days to fully complete the game (I knew chapters 1-3 from early access), but every step of the way was filled with pure joy... ESPECIALLY when I found out where Jesse got the rope from! Instant classic and already built for speed running!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I saw an ad for this game, watched the trailer, and decided to buy it. Needless to say this game did not disappoint. Not only is this game a Metal Gear Solid parody but it also contains many funny (Full Metal Jacket) dialogues. For those familiar with the British humor, it even has a Benny Hill reference (pure joy) The game is actually very fun to play, with many different game mechanics. First game I played in a long time where I would find myself to play it on repeat after each time I die, just to kill the boss, or beat the level. I highly recommend adding it to your gaming collection, money well spent, and big respect to the team who developed this masterpiece. Thank You!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is a very funny and entertaining game. Despite being a parody of Metal Gear, it stands on it's own with it's comedic takes, varied gameplay and bosses. The graphics are evocative of the classic Metal Gear games for the MSX2 and the soundtrack reminds me a lot of Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater. The stealth mechanics could be a bit more fleshed out. But for what the game was trying to accomplish, it was ok.Overall, i found it a very enjoyable game. I wish it had a map editor. It would be nice to create and share our own maps.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Quite simply: Solid Snake meets Archer. Well worth the price. A simple but engaging old school puzzle-action game; good level design, with lots to do and easter eggs to hunt, and all lovingly faithful to its source, right down to the over the top macho dialogue and excellent voice acting. Humour is just the right balance of satire and tribute. You can only love something with a passion to take the pi## out of it this well. This should be a required purchase for all Metal Gear/Syphon Filter/Splinter Cell fans.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. This guy's best work yet. The satire is perfect at poking fun at everything. Only a couple of annoyances in the game like not supporting anything above 1080p (come on man it is 2021). The upgrades are funny, dialogue is funny, some hidden funny stuff depending on some choices, some great boss battles, etc. !00% worth a buy and at a great price.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially Metal Gear if it was directed by the guys who did the "Naked Gun" movies. Unepic_Fran and his team have crafted a hilarious, challenging (although sometimes frustratingly so on difficulties above Easy), and ultimately fun homage to the classic top-down stealth games. Great characters, great sound, great gameplay variety, and a narrative that's as funny as it is engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good sign for a game when it doesn't even try to take itself serious... while proving that yes, they  care what they're making  what they're spoofing.Stealth-based action works quite fine, but what really took me was the plot. No, really. The plot is one of those "the protagonist is telling his own story and we're not sure if he's lying or not" kind of stuff, but it works out surprisingly convincing.The game is retro-esque, and by that I also mean that the difficulty is "retro," as in "trying to exploit your coins" kind of difficulty. But maybe it's just me.tl;dr: Sneaky, action-packed, tongue-in-cheek, and surprisingly narrative. If you love some old-school graphics as well, this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most fun i've had with a game in awhile. As i saw others comment, this really does feel like the Hot Shots version of Metal Gear Solid. Luckily for me I love both those franchises.Great soundtrack, great humour and controls really well. The visuals are easy on the eye too, unlike what i found with the Castlevania GBA recent re-releases. I find pixel art hit or miss but the (camera?) view and sprite sizes work really well here.I never got into playing Metal Gear 2 although I always wanted to, now i realise I love this kind of game play. I might have to load up my MGS3 disc again!!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: UnMetal is a fantastic 2D Metal Gear Experience with some great potty humor. I was always excited for every single cut-scene waiting to see the next twist on the plot done in the most off the way way possible.. The choice options look simple in the beginning, however the dev's get real creative with them after the intro stage (Just wait until the Trash boss). I highly recommend this to anyone who was a fan of the old school Metal Gear titles or MGS1 on the PlayStation. Replay ability comes in a few flavors: There's hidden secrets in every chapter. Choices do make a difference in gameplay progression. Level up's are also a huge factor in playstyle and fixed skill choices per level, per level up. For Example: Level 2 you can pick between faster punching, or faster movement when not alerted. You'll never get the opposite skill on level 3 or higher. I only have 8 hours in, streamed it from beginning to end. But I plan on doing at least 20 more playthroughs 10 for completion sake, and at least 10 more casual ones for fun.Side note: I really did enjoy this game. My original paragraph review got deleted from a missclick and I still took the time out of my day to retype it just because this gem of a title deserves all the praise it can get. Please support the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing ! I finished it in about 12 hours (playing offline, which is why Steam reports 20 minutes). It's really funny, story is interesting and lots of hilarious gags are breaking the fourth wall so often.2D graphics are really beautiful, animations are great. Gameplay feels way better than expected. A few moments would be a little frustrating, but it's worth hanging on to it ! A must buy, on my top 5 of best indie games of all times !
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy UnMetal, and I was very hyped about its release but the game becomes extremely boring really fast. Jokes are repetitive, tedious and sometimes not even remotely funny. The idea had potential but insted of this we got a repetitive and dull experience that will be easily forgettable
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Been 2 months since I finished the game and I am already considering a replay. It was so good and I really, really hope for a 2nd game.------Unless something radically changes after the 3 hour in mark... I can't say enough about how much I love this so far. Perhaps I am the exact demographic for this game? I just might be because the things that people are saying they don't like about this game I completely love. I think it helps to be a big metal gear fan. I think it also helps to have grown up playing all of them. I think the best analogy would be to say this is OG metal gear + deadpool + the nice quirkiness (boxes anyone?) of MGS. It's campy and ON POINT. The choose your own adventure piece is hilarious. If this game stays like this for another 40/ 50/ 100 (unlikely but I'm old) hours I will be completely happy with it. Brilliant so far and I will update if it somehow burns my house down.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece!Finished my first run in ~10h, any casual or dedicated player would enjoy playing it. It was filled with jokes and humour from the first frame to the post credit scene, the cinematics were awesome!!This game has :- Multiple Choice scenarios (I mean, it doesn't really change anything, but the dialogs are really fun to listen :) )- Nice inventory management (assignable shortcuts, different weapons, item crafting and so on)- Level progression (with skills to help you during your run)- Secondary quests (to find funny and helpful secrets)- Challenging yet fun and intuitive gameplay (easy to learn, and some boss are still challenging - several difficulty levels asw)- A nice story-telling (I've never seen any game with this kind of scenario narration, I loved the idea)- Wonderful artistic direction (It's pixel art indeed, but it has its own style, and I find it beautiful)I was bound to love it as I'm a fan of the Metal Gear games on ZX Spectrum, and I hope you will like it too if you decide to try it.Whether you're a "casual" looking for a little game to play over the weekend or someone who wants to get 100% success on everygame, this game deserves to be in your library :)
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly a parody of Metal Gear, the humor and over-the-top dialog/story worked on me. I put it right next to Blood Dragon for games that are sure to cheer me up.The game's challenge and occasionally poor checkpoints can work together to make the experience a tad frustrating, but this is mostly due to my refusal to use the quicksave items.I think you get exactly what it says on the tin: If it looks like you'll enjoy it, you probably will.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well done parody of the OG Metal Gear games that were on the NES. I never really played those games but this gave me an appreciation that i never experienced for those games! Points well deserved for that :)- Controls are simple to figure out if you're playing using a controller or mouse & keyboard- Graphics look really well done for a retro style game (Feels like a remaster of the old Metal Gear games on the NES)- The comedy is really good, took me by surprise a few times on a couple of sections that i am not going to spoil.I highly recommend buying this if you enjoy parody games or even enjoyed the OG Metal Gear games back in the day, trust me you will get a good laugh out of this hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: The best Metal Gear parody I've played and its also better than anything konami would make started with that metal gear survive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!Be prepared to die a lot on your first time playing through.  There's always a strategy with the boss fights or else they can end you pretty quick if you don't realize it sooner.

_childDocuments_.review: You can combine a lighter and a gallon of gasoline in your inventory and immediately explode. 10/10Honestly it's a really good game. The sense of comedy is flawless. _childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the game isn't for me I just put a thumbs up to support the dev because I really like his other games and want him to do more. In general the humor is good similar to the first two games but it completely lacks the sense of freedom. There is no skill tree or open world, you just follow a scripted tube throughout the game with some secret areas sprinkled in between that are honestly  a little too hard to find. It was an interesting experience and I do not regret buying it but I hope that the dev goes back to his roots again after this
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: The language used by these guards is great. I think the writers of this must have been in the military. Great tribute to the old school games. Not a perfect game, but the quality is there. No bugs encountered. My only wish thusfar is to have the controls be a little tighter, and the game over screen to speed up. Some areas you will die quickly and repeatedly. I will be replaying this a few times for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, i was hyped for this game since the day the trailer dropped out.Truly a love letter for every mg(s) fans out there, with a special touch of comedy and parody for one of the most beloved sagas out there. The game pretty much plays out like a "scary movie" or "hot shots" movie would play. Story, gameplay and presentation is certainly inspired  by earlier MG games, but then everything is comedic and goes to greatly stupidly levels on things. It's a very fun game, even if you aren't a MG(s) fan yourself, you'll still laugh at the gags and easter eggs the game brings.Thing is, even if it we cut out the inspiration on MG, the game itself  for what it represents is amazing, and you can get that a major ton of work and care was put into it.I can't put into words how much fun i had with it. I can't remind the last time i laughed off so much playing a video game. I camped at eastsoftAsia to grab a phisical copy for the vita, but got no luck with it, and they went out of stock :( And there was no news when it would launch on PC, so i kind of went the "skull with an eyepatch" way of things to play it at the time, but today I stand here happy has an officially proud undeluxe edition costumer for this amazing game. And like myself, many more will do the same.It's one of those products that it simply cannot go unnoticed and unrewarded.You deserve every single penny for what this game offers, and i can't wait for your next work
_childDocuments_.name: UnMetal

_childDocuments_.review: Unmetal is a metal gear msx2 spinoff where it borrows the game's pacifist action gameplay more than the tactical espionage of stealth. Like most versus evil titles, Unmetal leans quite heavily on satire and comedy. The game's difficulty is on par with older game's difficulty where normal offers sufficient amount of a challenge while hard really ramps the games difficulty quite significantly. Overall, while alot of the humor in the game fell flat for me, the overall gameplay was quite enjoyable. I highly recommend this gameIf your searching for a metal gear inspired game that focuses on the stealth aspect of the game, I recommend Volume. For more challenging MGS games you can also try out Intravenous along with Unmetal.

_childDocuments_.review:
In 1972 a crack commando squad threw you in prison for a crime you didn't commit. You promptly escaped from a maximum-security stockade to the underground trying to survive from these soldiers of fortune.

UnMetal is a 2D stealth/action game (with a bit of humor) where the goal is to escape from an enemy military base. But what started as a simple break out ended up being an inside operation to prevent a massive attack against the NATO.

_childDocuments_.review: So, after a few hours im really pleased.Let me tell you why:Monster trucks are a very American thing, and from Ive noticed, a very "first motor sport" vibe to it. For anyone who may not have any regular exposure to Monster Trucks, its important to remember that these machines arent racing cars. They arent rally cars, not Nascars, not Dragsters, etc. They are heavily glorified stunt vehicles. Vehicles meant to do high speed, at short distance. Trucks equivalent to hyper active puppies. This game requires you to think about the unique movement and durable nature of monster trucks, but at a level they could never hope to achieve.The real life "Monster Jam" events require you to obey and confer to the rules of MT, giving an "extreme alt sports" feel to the game. In the same vein as Tony Hawks Pro Skater, Taco Apocalypse, or Rocket League. Its a unique way to think about the movement of a vehicle, because really only MT's have this kind of movement. IF you have played Redout, you would be at home, if not, and you dont know what im referring to, its the four wheel steering in MT's. Youll be using both sticks on a controller to perform otherwise "normal" turns and maneuvers so it may take some getting used to. Because, as i stated earlier, these machines were never really meant to perform at this level.And yet, the game allows you to do this extreme level of movement and speed. its filled with real labeled trucks, a very very mixed soundtrack and makes you rethink how you as a player would move and control a vehicle in a "racing" game. On top of that, it offers a New Game+ mode so you could grind the crap out of this with a friend, or maybe younger family member.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine, but it can be easily improved by removing the powers/passives (including boost) and freestyle event beacons. Let the trucks represent the absurdity that makes Monster Jam awesome, not some magical fantasy elements! Remove the aforementioned aspects and replace the maps with realistic ones, and you got yourself a near-perfect Monster Jam game. Don't over complicate it! Keep it realistic. Also, the different trucks should offer significantly different driving experiences. It would be neat if the different trucks were tuned to match their real-life versions (eg Avenger being very loose). It doesn't have to be perfect. Even arbitrary differences between the trucks would make the game significantly more replayable and less mindless. Another idea to really ramp up this game's quality is to copy Wreckfest's systems of upgrades and tuning. The upgrades would also satisfy progression in place of the current leveling mechanic. I get that Monster Jam doesn't prioritize games and are just looking to release some quick fun, but I truly think simple decisions like those I've explained can turn this game into an actual good game that hits a broader audience, not just something for those attracted to the Monster Jam logo. From PSP to console to mobile to PC, I've searched for a satisfying monster truck game. Its unfortunate that after all this game satisfied, it disregarded one of the only things that made the other monster truck games fun -- realism.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: For monster truck fans, this second Monster Jam Steel Titans is something that will make your hands tickle.With no fewer than 38 unique monster trucks, some of which are also based on real monster trucks, with which you can refine your best stunts.The monster trucks also each have a special ability that you can use to your advantage during a race.In addition to the wide range of tricks that you can do in the game, there are other activities such as racing or even exploration,In addition to the competitive jams, you will also be able to go out in a kind of open worlds,here you can indulge yourself without limits and you will also have to watch out for hidden objects, each area in the open worlds has 5 of these objects hidden and when you find strings of 5 you will be rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: +Great physics and graphics, if you are familiar with the behavior of the CRD Monster Truck in BeamNG you will find little flaw in this, but it is Forza-esque "simcade" in that you have lots of assists on tap, making it easy to learn and hard to master.+Responsive controls, advanced options for separate rear steering and manual transmission+Decent wheel support, good FFB+Fun variety of racing and stunt modes+Great trick scoring and combo system+Huge hub world and colorful graphics make it feel a bit like a '90s 3d platformer but you are a monster truck.-Cannot reassign controls easily-Missing effects like watersplashes -Odd sticky collisions with other trucks-Not all objects are breakable -AI is very fast by itself but not smart enough to race other trucks very well making some events more challenging than they need to be-Truck special abilities make the AI's inability to overtake worse-Early game events are a boring slog (drag racing in a circle?), AI is quite strong, your truck starts out slow, and the races are short, but it picks up later-Checkpoint races have overzealous cut protection and often just ruin your race resetting you before you even have a chance to return to the trackTo configure the controls on a steering wheel, the only way I've found possible is finding UserWheelInput.ini in "AppData\Local\MJST2\Saved\Config\Windows" and manually changing the numbers minus one to reflect the button labels reported in the Windows Joystick control panel (0 = 1, 1 = 2, etc.).Also, as a bonus, if you make a shortcut to MJST2-Win64-Shipping.exe and add the "-vr" command line option you can play with your SteamVR-compatible HMD. The menus and HUD are broken in this clearly unfinished mode but the meat of the game is still fully playable and lots of fun. Hope to see this as an official feature soon.Overall a great budget racing game with surprisingly detailed physics. It does nothing really new or exciting aside from being one of the few games to have even vaguely realistic monster truck racing, and suffers a bit for it's lack of polish and direction. It's hard to tell whether it's for kids or the old veterans of the MSN Gaming Zone, but it is definitely all fun, and the inclusion of real life arenas along with the fantasy hub world means you can play pretty much however you like.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

Trucks look pretty good, environments are pretty bad.-The AI is HORRIBLE.-Stunts aren't physics based, just kind of happen when you meet the right conditions.Disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I didnt really like the game to be honest. I got bored of it very quickly. The gameplay was fun for half an hour but I didnt think there was much too it, you do a list of events that are presented to you in chapters, whilst the rest of the game is just exploring a small map in freeride. I cant say I found the game to be all that interesting, the trucks are cool and all but I just didnt enjoy it much. The controls are a bit weird and not exactly ideal. I was using my xbox one afterglow controller and I had to use the D-pad down arrow to look backwards, which makes it almost impossible to do when your in the middle of a race. One of the first things I wanted to do was change this right away and the game wouldnt even let me because there didnt seem to be an option?Something else I could not stand about the game was the addition of powerups. The one I always had was called "Boost" as you can imagine a bit like nitrous, the truck would go super fast. The problem for me it would go so fast to the point where it would send me off track, so generally I preferred not to use it, which then gave the other AI trucks a slight advantage. I noticed one of them had quite a useful powerup that gave them some kind of shield that would just shove everything else out the way. Whenever this happened it would be rather frustrating because most of the time you would not land on wheels and end up having to restart the race again. I just felt like the powerups sort of ruined the game a little bit and I would have preferred it without them.Overall a disappointing game and a waste of money. I cant say I would recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is an improvement over the first Steel Titans, its just still not up to par with what a Monster Jam game should be.Firstly, the huge offender is the physics. They are WAY better than the first game, but still are under developed. The problem is the monster trucks don't feel heavy. They constantly bounce around like they have helium in their tires. This isn't necessarily a problem for stadium events, where the good aspects of the physics truly shine. However, when you are navigating/racing through the open worlds, the uneven ground and bumps send your truck tumbling CONSTANTLY. Also, why does hitting breakable props slow you down so much? It feels like the damn props are heavier than the monster trucks! Utterly baffling...Secondly, this game is for kids. You can easily tell by the collectibles and open worlds. They really played into the fantasy aspect for these monster trucks, which I guess is cool. However, as an adult, I much prefer the more realistic environments of the previous game. If you aren't into the fantasy aspect like me, then you might as well avoid this title.Thirdly, the game doesn't look that great. The reason why is this was also developed for the Nintendo Switch. Because of this, we end up getting a more stripped down, basic looking game on consoles and PC. This is an Unreal Engine 4 game and it just looks so bare and boring!I'm very disappointed in how far Rainbow Studios has fallen, and they continue the legacy of half ass Monster Jam games we have been getting since the early 2010s. If this studio makes another Monster Jam game, I expect much better than this...
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

_childDocuments_.review: The inconsistent difficulty completes kills the fun!!!I don't even care about the constant visual glitches, or stupid hard to reach collectibles.Playing on EASY mode to just enjoy the main game, and it's anything but!Arena races, Arena championships - can lap others no problem. Wreck, or spin out in a 3 lap arena race? Still no problem to win!Then you do the outdoor world races, and it's like it's locked at Hard mode?!? If you spin out even one time during a 5 minute race, you mine as well restart, because you're LAST.  Over shoot a checkpoint just slightly, and have to back up, hit it and keep going? Oh well. LAST PLACE. Screw This.
