_childDocuments_.review: Not for those with ADHD.It absolutely kills me to leave a negative review on an Obsidian game. I've been a huge fan ever since New Vegas, and Pillars of Eternity 2: Deadfire is one of my favorite games of all time. I love both Obsidian and their team and the work they've done over the years. I can tell a lot of heart and soul went into this game, and they deserve a ton of respect for trying to make something unique as opposed to something more commercially marketable.All that to say I truly WANTED to love this game. But the game doesn't respect your time. It is a walking simulator with a few conversational choices scattered throughout. I simply cannot bring myself to open it up again. All of the world-building and character building gets completely forgotten about the first time I'm left wandering around walking in circles trying to find where I need to go. The idea of trying to start the game to continue through it again is agonizing. I'm now much less interested in playing the game than I am in simply finding out what happens. I'll likely look up a condensed Youtube video that summarizes it, because the draw of making the choices myself is worthless when those choices are gated behind a slow walking simulator. I just want to see where the story goes.If you are the type of person to get easily lost, or forget directions, or get frustrated at having to walk around through multiple loading screens back and forth to find NPCs just to start the next dialogue chain, this game is unfortunately not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game for everyone and despite the murder mystery trappings it isn't really for fans of those either. At least not the more traditional whodunnit murder mysteries where finding the killer is the main focus. That isn't what Pentiment is about. Much like How The City and the City, Mare of Eastown, and The Name of the Rose are about way more than the murder (or murders) the plots revolve around, Pentiment is about way more than just the murder you become embroiled in. It is about how seemingly throw away actions can ripple throughout small communities, about how no one person can truly shape history, how the pull of socio-economic factors are inescapable even if they are imperceptible at the time, and how the past can never truly be displayed "as it was." The murder is just the jumping off points to explore these themes.Its a game where choices matter but not as much as you think they will, much closer to real life.All in all if you like medieval history, post-modernist literature, and thoughtful murder mysteries this game might be for you and probably be extremely your ♥♥♥♥, but if you aren't into those things it might not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly beautiful game; the art direction is gorgeous, even if (like me) Catholic Marginalia isn't your favorite aesthetic and Gregorian chants don't set your world on fire, you are made to feel every inch of it in a way that (coupled with the ludicrously well-researched historicity) grounds you firmly within the narrative and made me feel thoroughly invested in nearly every role-playing decision the game puts in front of you.The writing is what you'd expect of Obsidian, which is to say: excellent. Authentically funny when its trying to be, deeply moving during its big emotional beats, and manages to invest enough personality into its characters that I never forgot who anyone was or what their relationship to the town was.It's slow, that can't be denied. Even the pacing of the cinematic animations seems deliberately drawn out, and though the map is helpful you'll probably find yourself running around a lot, which doesn't feel great. That said, they do an admirable job of filling the walk-around portions with flavorful character interactions, which is helpful in a mystery story.That mystery is probably going to be the biggest bone of contention for people who are already on-board with a Walk-N-Talk. It's tactically vague with its verdicts, and you're left feeling like there's more going on than you necessarily have a shot at uncovering, at least in a first playthrough. Personally, I kinda like that, since historical mysteries rarely have super concise conclusions, and it doesn't lead to any fail-states you feel like you should have been able to enjoy.Definitely not for everyone, but as a fan of Disco Elysium and Hell On Earth, I loved almost every single second of this one. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet (there seems to be three acts, I'm on act 2), but I wanted to share my thoughts anyways. If you like text focused click and point games you'll probably like this. Every act you seem to take on a new character, from a different perspective, impacted by the previous choices you've made, in a medieval setting.Main criticisms I have so far: I'd like a way to skip text if you're going to tease that there's multiple endings through achievements (so the replay isn't frustrating; I can't find a way to do this but it might exist and I'm just not seeing it) and a way to skip cutscenes (not just the opening segment). It's also not clear during the first act that you can't do certain actions during meal times and the night, especially since  which can be frustrating. The saving system is also barely usable, it needs to be fixed ASAP.That being said, those are the only criticisms I really have right now. The art in the game is unique and interesting, the dialogue is realistic (there isn't voice acting but I wouldn't want there to be), and it genuinely feels like I have some sense of choice in scenarios where I ultimately don't have a lot of choices ().Edit: I've now finished Act 3 and I genuinely don't see the criticisms that other people have on the third act being drawn out. _childDocuments_.review: Obsidian Entertainment has got to be one of the studios I least expected to make a basically interactive Umberto Eco novel. They definitely have a great love of fiction and narrative, although it has previously extended to mostly fantasy and sci-fi settings in a roleplaying context, but I feel there is an undeniable dedication and reverence to history in this game. I'm not big on historical accuracy, but it feels like an elegant and well researched introduction to an important era of european history.The narrative design feels incredibly cohesive and flows rather naturally, albeit stressfully sometimes, as you have to trust your gut when you prioritise what threads to follow in the limited time you have. Players looking to explore all the plot has to offer will likely have to make peace with playing the game multiple times to uncover all its underlying images poking through the layers that conceal them.Although not one of my favourite games, it's a good game nonetheless, but I'm infinitely more interested in Obsidian as a studio when they pursue titles of this complexity with such lovingly crafted care, so I hope they keep that trajectory going forward.

Fans of Kingdom Come Deliverance will probably like this game. I'm probably less than halfway through the game but I am very glad I bought it. _childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Disco Elysium: Renaissance Bavaria editionLook, this game is good. It has a unique art style and an excellent way of making your decisions meaningful, which I think is what all adventure games need. The ramifications of your decisions may be a bit bryptic, but not to the point of not making sense or betraying your intentions. It also explains a very mature story in a serious manner, and lets you experience the lives of the characters close to what they actually experience, without sugarcoating hardships of peasant live in the liwer renaissance (well, maybe a little)An here comes the but, because there needed to be a but: But, the story makes you wonder a bit aimlessly during most of the game. Not like I want quest markers (you have them if you look for them), just that the main characters seem to have little idea of what to do themselves, and instead just decide to spend time on advancing quests that spend time when they stumble on them. As you have very limited time slots to advance the story, you'll feel that the game hasn't let you investigate enough before railroading you into the next story bottleneck, and forcing you to take story changing decisions without having had the chance to unveil all the secrets. I mean, that feels like real life, but I have real life at home already, I wanted to have not-so-real-life in my game.Finally, I'm dreading replaying the game. The idea seems to be to start the game a second and third time with different backgrounds (similar to Disco Elysium), but the dialogue is very slow and difficult to skip because of the (otherwise beatifully made) annoying text effect on the dialogue boxes, and I fear to see how the story will crack when seeing what part of my decisions is actually reflected or not on the consequencesI picked it shortly after launch, and if you're an avid point and click adventure gamer I guess the full price is okay. If you are just looking for something to fill time, pick it up in half a year when the first discounts start
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Pentiment reminded me of reading a book. More precisely an historical fiction novel.You are Andreas Maler, a 16th century artist, who is staying at the fictional town of Tassing, Bavaria, doing work at Kiersau’s abbey as part of your university education. Your time there gets disrupted when a murder occurs and you immediately step in to solve the mystery in order to save a friend, but in doing so you uncover an even greater mystery...Andreas is an Illuminator of Manuscripts; he participates in the creation of all kinds of documents. The game takes place in a time setting where the Gutenberg Printing press is starting to make possible the printing of books and texts in general for everybody, a domain which was previously exclusive to the church and those with the knowledge.This game has a great deal of research an investigation mixed into the narrative. In the end credits, the amount of reference books puts to shame any other game in recent memory. If you have any interest in the time period this is one very special game.That being said, it is important to note, that this game really plays as a book, in more ways than one... Pentiment doesn't have spoken dialogues, only text (And there's lots and lots of dialogues). Each text is written (in a way) like the person who is saying the words is also writing them... Each character will have different styles of text, different forms and colors, and even will make more or less mistakes while writing their own dialogues according to the degree of knowledge they possess. The story is long, with a decent amount of twists and turns, but it does have some slow sections (which set the stage for what it is to come) and so, it demands your attention. You don't have to know everything and remember everything but not everything is on display for you to see. There are in fact, some optional objectives and dialogues which you may miss if you take some main activities that demand time to complete.Even then I would say that the choice to make all dialogues text only could be a very deliberate artistic choice. While it does take more effort to read all text it does create a sense of " being inside your head, in your own created world”. This is why, Pentiment is the closest I've been to reading a book (while playing a game). You read the words, you even see the pictures on the page. But the rest is created by your own imagination. In that sense I would say that even the graphic style for Pentiment is very much in tone with what you could find during that time period, but also of what you could find reading a book....The visuals for Pentiment have some decent amount of animation (specially towards the end sequences) but it mostly remains like a picture you could find in an illustrated book.... that and the fact that there are no voices (mostly) lets you create the character's voices in your head, and maybe even other elements from the story.It will take some time according to each player, but if you stick with the game and keep playing it you may begin to use your imagination (and your visual memory in some strange way) in a way we only do when reading books. That perhaps is the real treasure of this game.All of this of course means nothing without a good story. Pentiment's story doesn't disappoint, it is a good one, it plays like an Umberto Eco's video game adaptation, albeit not a perfect one. There are some slow sections here and there that could've been avoided perhaps or trimmed a little, even if the game clearly doesn't intend to be flashy like a modern fast pace game and play like a slow burn big novel.I liked this game, and even would say it is one in a thousand, very special and very rare and very good at what it does. But it definitely needs some time and dedication (like any good book) and you'll definitely need to be in the right mood to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unique. It is more point and click style and does not have combat. The story is extremely rich and I have not found another game that goes in such depth regarding history. It is set in 16th century Bavaria. I am german and can assure you, they did a very good job capturing the culture and customs.There is an excellent "documentary" on youtube, on how the game was made. The devs give insights into the creation process. If I recall correctly the game director used to work on big titles previously. He had studied history as a young man and wanted to create this game as a passion project.I can recommend this game to anyone who does not get tired of reading and does not need combat gameplay.P.s.: If anyone knows games like this, please let me know.

_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent art direction and design combined with phenomenal writing, interesting characters and a story with strong themes. The game side however is a bit weak, with the gameplay essentially being boiled down to walking around, talking and choosing where to spend your somewhat restricted time, making it more of a visual novel with dialouge options than anything else.I still thoroughly enjoyed it, and it is well recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "yes, but" recommendation. The game is strongest when it leans into the history. There are genuinely beautiful sections with period music and paintings, and the costumes and settings are beautiful. It's a lovely period game, with rich attention to detail -- the setting is so much more than surface dressing.But the game itself is a bit tedious -- take away the setting and there's so much running back and forth between the same locations, just to check to see if any of the characters have anything to say. The first three hours this was charming -- the next 11 it started to feel like a lot of padding between beauty, decisions, and story progress. There's a lot of just-OK elements like this -- like the painfully awkward sound design that had this terrible clop clop for footsteps that never stopped for 14 hours of playing.Hopefully, in a future game, they'll focus more on the magical parts of the game. For some reason, there's very spare with the music and the artwork, even those those sequences were reliably fantastic. (They thought we would sit through a flash mini-games but not more singing?!?) Similarly, I loved the glimpse of rooms in far off cities when you write letters to them. Overall, I think I thought about 7 hours of this game was exceptional -- but the 14 total hours I spent overstayed its welcome a bit. (This feels especially long for a choices matter game, which ostensibly wants you to replay it.) I think this view is shared by most players, since only 20% of people have the finishing achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is very much the kind of game that will not appeal to everyone - it's text-heavy, its version of agency doesn't mean that you can change the story drastically, it requires you to be (or become) interested late medieval/early modern German history, society, culture, religion, and it requires you to keep up. If you like it, though, you may very well love it. I mean, how many games are there that tell this sort of story and that show this kind of love for history and big, philosophical ideas - all while presenting us with a vibrant, fascinating cast of characters? How many games are there that respect the player's intelligence and curiosity to this extent?
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A more detailed video review can be found here: I'm yet another former student of History that will tell you of how much detail was put into Pentiment. I touch on a lot of historical elements that would take me a bazillion characters to write, but what I can say is that Sawyer did his degree proud. His ability to take all the knowledge and personal connection and form it into what is Pentiment is nothing short of worthy of applause. But what is even more important is the overall quality of the writing, which absolutely makes this Obsidian's best game. Yes, even better than their RPG classics. Deep characters, with relevant story arcs, excellent dialogue with plenty of food for thought withing their intricate lines.The branching choices mechanic is as good as you'd expect from the authors of Alpha Protocol. The moral dilemmas are on par with Knights of the Old Republic II. All wrapped under a story that's intimate, not epic in size. You're not saving the world, but only peering through the life of a small village lost in the Alps. The stakes are not at all high, but you're invested in the fates of these villagers from the end of the introduction.Buy it. Play it. Enjoy its variety of choices and consequences over multiple playthroughs. At its launch price, this game is an absolute steal.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Currently in my second playthrough and I do love this game. Played this first with a friend and then we kidnapped another mutual friend for the second playthrough. The subtle foreshadowing, the different personalities and crimes that need solving are so fun! And MAN does this game come right for the feels in later parts.It has a lot of charme and I love how much thought and heart went into the making of this. The art style is phenomenal, the dialogue is great and your actions and choices do be having consequences! I love the development of Andreas as a character and the way you can see his influences on the abbey and the town even years later. There's also humor in it and the game knows how to play its strengths. It also definitely tempts you to replay, as you won't be able to see everything the game has to offer in a first playthrough.I did encounter some bugs, especially in Act Two, that made a part of the main mission sorta hard to put together but managed fine by googling how to get around it. Anyway, this game is definitely a recommendation from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully told mystery story set in Bavaria in the period of the northern renaissance, Pentiment surprises with its dedication to its time period without the excessive modernisms that "historical" videogames often fall into (constant swearing, edgy messages about religion, obsession with pointless violence and political correctness). It nostalgically reminds me of the old Sierra and Lucas Arts adventures of the early 90s, without sharing their often moon logic or obstrue mechanics.Simply put, Pentiment is immersive in the truest sense of the word, it lets you get transported to the late middle ages and renaissance and occupy the minds and beliefs of its people. I can't recommend it enough to everyone with even a passing interest in history.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is one of the greatest games I have ever played, From beginning to end I was completely immersed in the time period and setting. The writing and art direction are something to behold, and every character is both interesting and believable. Every time I booted up the game I was waiting on the edge of my seat for what will happen next and I'm certain I'll be doing another playthrough one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game. There is clearly so much love put into every aspect: the art design, the characters, the dialogue, it all fits together seamlessly into a story that will really stick with me. One of the few games that made me feel really a part of the community it portrays, that I really knew everyone in town, even the minor characters. The age progression is beautifully done and lends to that feeling as well. Strongly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: How did this game fly under my radar? I'm amazed that I didn't hear about it until now. It's fantastic. I'm having a difficult time deliberating over choices and they have a really interesting impact on the story. It's beautiful, thoughtful, and very well-crafted. I nearly played it all in one sitting.Some people think the pace is too slow. I agree that the third act is where it starts to drag, but I like that the game asks you to really consider what you're doing with the time you have. You get many opportunities to take in the atmosphere. Personally, my only complaint so far is that sometimes I click through too hastily and accidentally select an option because my mouse was hovering over it. The auto-save feature is lovely and makes the stakes higher (I can't just go back to before a bad decision), but it is a bit bothersome when I make unintentional mistakes.Otherwise, this is quickly becoming one of my favorite games I've played. If you like mystery stories, adventure-style exploration, history, and art, I think it's absolutely worth trying.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A gem of a game.I'm enthralled by the story, I care for the characters. The pacing is amazing, as it give you not too much space to be idle, and forces you to take decisions and live the consequences.It manages to be both a great investigation / adventure game, with a pitch perfect ambientation, and a relevant game for the universal and contemporary themes and dilemmas it presents.The art direction is masterful, the dialogues feel true to life.Only a minor note.It is a bit too didactic at times, as I feel compelled to make use of the hypertexts to read everything, even when I know what the referenced terms are about.Maybe, that compulsion comes from not having enough info at the start about what matters and what not in gameplay, and it leads to a lot of zooming out and back in the scene that, given the UI, feels a bit unwieldy. In a way I would have preferred a leaner interface. But I understand the reasoning behind the "lore" referencing, and the means to present it to the players, so I forgive that readily.All in all, I'm enjoying it immensely.9,5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is huge labour of love. The art design, aesthetic choices, storyline and the amount of research that went into this is amazing. Played it on my Steam Deck which it is perfect for. If you're only slightly interested in medieval history and like reading this game is for you. Gameplay wise there really isn't much to it but that's not the point. So if a slow game with a lot of reading isn't for you, I wouldn't even bother.Choices matter in how people act towards you later in the game, but the story will stay the same. This might be where the critique may come from that it's linear. The story is so well crafted in how all elements come together that it never bothered me. Pentiment is like reading a novel. Umberto Eco's The Name of the Rose was a huge inspiration for this game so if you're a fan of that genre, you'll love Pentiment. It's also a beautiful way of seeing how rural life was in that time period. The relations between clergy and the different classes are beautifully shown through story and dialogue.All characters are fleshed out and well written, I started to care about everyone in the town and you'll get really invested after a few hours. The music is beautiful and accompanies the scenes perfectly.One negative for me was the save system. I would've liked to go back to a few checkpoints to check other outcomes or simply because I didn't have the chance to play for a few weeks so I could refresh my memory but that wasn't possible. After the game is finished your savegame is also gone. Minor annoyances of course, and I understand how this could also be a design choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant and unique multi-generational murder mystery set in a Bavarian alpine village and monastery of the Holy Roman Empire during the earliest decades of the Protestant Reformation, with visual art directly inspired by period manuscript illuminations and woodblock prints.  I was genuinely moved by the story at several points, and if the setting sparks your curiosity, the in-game glossary and journal provides enough information for a graduate-level seminar on Bavarian Renaissance culture, art, and spiritual practices.  Absolutely not for everyone, but if anything I said sounds even remotely interesting to you, you'd be doing yourself a real disservice to ignore this game.  I bought it on sale, but I absolutely would recommend buying it even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is an interactive story that deals with the changing values of society, especially in relation to the church, but also impressively shows how modern inventions and knowledge change the way we live - for better or worse.Pentiment asks some important questions. What do we want to preserve from the past? How do we want to remember it? What is the truth and what is a lie? And is it even useful to always tell the truth?Pentiment gives you the freedom to make important decisions and takes the time to work through the consequences.You are rewarded with a beautifully written story and extraordinary attention to detail when it comes to the visuals.Even though the amount of reading is enormous in this game, I would like to give it a clear recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A game made specifically for J.E. Swayer, by J.E. Sawyer. And that's what makes it more interesting than a majority of games out there. Fitting for a game about playing as an artist, the passion and artistry shines through. That fact makes it an entirely unique experience and it's why if you're a fan of narratives in games you owe yourself to play it. The fact it was made for one person means there likely won't ever be a game like it, and so it makes it an entirely unique experience worth playing for yourself. I promise if you don't learn something about yourself, you'll most certainly learn a lot about history.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is a masterpiece of its genre, and yet few in my circles have even heard of it. Anyone who enjoys narrative experiences with a rich environment and complex characters in their games should play it.From the unique art style to historical details that few will pick up on all of, this story is a rich exploration of life in a time and place many of us are exploring for the first time. Pentiment cleverly uses chat bubbles to "trick" a player into a reading-heavy experience. It works. I wanted to soak in every line of dialogue the game had to offer, but the limited number of conversations you're able to have in a day add a real sense of urgency and replay-ability at the same time while fitting neatly within the story. This game has an unbelievable amount of depth to it -- think of movies that have made you excited to go back and watch a second time, now that you know what you know. i'm intentionally being vague about the story itself here, because I don't want to spoil it or paint anyone's impressions of the characters and story. You simply have to experience it for yourself.The only complaint I could think of is that some "meaningful choices" purists may find Pentiment falls short in some ways. I disagree, but can understand how some arrive at that conclusion. Your choices *do* have a considerable effect on the rest of the game, but Obsidian does choose not to tell the player "hey, you were right/wrong about this," which I think makes the story more interesting. Endings with few stark differences may leave some feeling that way, as well, but I am willing to accept that in order to experience the ending Obsidian wanted me to see.A first playthrough of Pentiment seems to run most people around 14-16 hours. I've yet to dive in a second time, but I definitely intend on returning. I got Pentiment on sale, which made this the best bang for my buck on steam in ages. If you love a good story, you should pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game. Not just the art (which is fantastic) or the music (which is wonderful) or the historicity (which is remarkable) but the whole. On its face Pentiment is the story of an artist in the early 16th century of the Holy Roman Empire, and the impact he has on the village of Tassing, but it's so much more than that. It's a story about how art shapes us, how we are the stories we tell ourselves and how that changes the world around us. TL;DR if any part of the sentence "A Renaissance artist tries to solve murders in a small alpine village." appeals to you, play this game. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to describe Pentiment in one word it would be "beautiful". Not just in the visual style, which IS very charming and executed in fine detail (how many games make text rendering a jaw-dropping experience...), but also in the sheer love for humanity that suffuses the story. I've cried while playing games before, but this is the first time it occurred because I was happy for certain characters. I hadn't even realised how much I'd grown to care for them up until that point. The feelings really sneak up on you, like it does in real life friendships.Not that it's all sunshine and rainbows. There was plenty of turmoil and heartache in the early 16th century and this game is nothing if not dedicated to history. You'll probably spend the first couple of hours looking at random historically accurate things and thinking "hey, maybe living in this time wasn't so bad!" Just know that the devs are winding up to smack you with an extra dose of reality. But you'll thank them for it, I promise.I will say that marketing the game as a "murder-mystery" where "choices matter" might be a little misleading. It's an accurate description, but this is a narrative adventure first and foremost, and those two aspects occasionally take a back seat in service of that narrative. I don't see it as a bad thing - quite the opposite, it's rare to find this clarity of scope and purpose - but it might be offputting if you're after something else. This is not the kind of game you should try to optimise or win.Finally, I see a lot of comparisons to the Name of the Rose, which is fair enough because Pentiment is not shy about its influence. I want to specify that if you read the book but found it hard to get through, this game is for you! It has many of the book's best aspects while being a lot more accessible. Sorry Umberto Eco, but Josh Sawyer et al. are my new best friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. Somehow I was expecting more. Was expecting branched choices, puzzle style like monkey island and yet some people claimed this is like disco elysium. RPG elements like D&D it's non existing, unlike disco elysium. So comparing this game to disco elysium it's just  dumb. Still recommend it for the art style and story is really interesting, despite dragging towards the end.  7/10

I had little idea what I was getting into and was very satisfied by the story ending. The characters are well developed and full of surprises. _childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: The story is nice, the dialogues are wide in scope and the design is great!The gameplay is simplistic, though. Another drawback is that your decisions simultaneously matter as they shape the story, but also do not matter, because nothing really affects your character.I liked the game and it is as good as one in such genre (walk and click/talk) could be, but would not play something like it again.

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere of this game is something that I was craving for a very long time.One of my favorite movies is The Name of the Rose and to my surprise Pentiment gave me cozy, nostalgic feeling, similar to the one when I first watched film adaptation with Sean Connery. The art style is beautiful, really charming for a medieval nerd like me ;). You feel like you are immersed in a visual novel!I really like the way they presented pagan traditions, still alive in a 16th century christian village.The main mystery is gripping, the dialogues are well written, and the ending touched me deeply :).
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: night of the woods for a different kind of nerd, characterization is a bit too dry for my taste, commendable effort for all the research done but the gameplay is too linear and doesn't manage to fool you into thinking the world's larger than it really is.if the idea of dropping historical references to the holy roman empire gets you going then you'll enjoy this a lot
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is a real find for fans of detectives and historical plots. This visual novel with quest elements plunges you into the wonderful world of the late Middle Ages in southern Germany of the XVI century, where the old Christian worldview and modernization processes collide.I would like to point out that the game skillfully weaves historical events and facts into the narrative, creating a deep and fascinating picture of the past. Many characters with their own stories and motives add depth to the game world.The game's plot, which takes place in three acts, gives the game an interesting structure and creates a sense of suspense, especially in the first two acts, with time constraints that force you to decide how to spend it. This perfectly emphasizes the mystery and detective atmosphere.In addition, the dialogues in the game characterize the characters well and help creating the atmosphere. Although the gameplay is not the strong point of the game, it doesn't hinder the immersion into the fascinating world of Pentiment.The only drawback, as I already mentioned, could be the third act with its less interesting ending and the lack of a time limit. However, this is only a minor downside to the overall picture.So, Pentiment is a game that can intrigue and captivate you with its detective story, historical depth and atmosphere. I recommend it to anyone who is looking for an appropriate mix of history and mystery in the world of video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, the art and historical detail is masterful. The only game I've played that comes close to capturing this level of accuracy in a game is Kingdom Come: Deliverance, but because this covers a different period and perspective of Medieval Europe, there's so much to learn.I won't spoil the story, but the game has some issues, to the point where I disagree with its overwhelmingly positive reception. The purpose and impact of your decisions is not well choreographed. There are plenty of situations where my decisions resulted in the exact opposite outcome from the one I wanted. I wasted plenty of time (maybe an hour in total) trying to cover every potential option I had since the game did not always clearly communicate when all of my options had been expended.There are 3 acts, and the first 2 are very well done. The third is disruptive but never delivers on any advantages that the disruption promises. By that, I mean that the story established in the first and second acts would have been significantly more effective if it was allowed to conclude in the way it seemed it was going to. Instead, the third act introduces a variety of plot lines and story decisions that neuter an otherwise beautiful story. I don't regret finishing the game, but it promised something different and better than it delivered, which keeps it from sticking out in my mind as a game I would ever mention when listing my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I was captivated from beginning to end. A true passion project through and through. You can tell the love that went into making this, the careful attention to detail and the precision with which everything was written. I've grown to care about the characters in this story as if they were real people and become invested in a fictitious community in a way that I haven't in a long time. Pentiment is a beautiful game which deftly demonstrates the uniqueness of video games as a vehicle for compelling story telling, even education, without ever feeling heavy-handed or contrived. I loved every second of this game, and find myself with a hole left in me after finishing it. It was a refreshing splash of vibrant originality, and such an unequivocal labor of love that feels almost anachronistic in this day and age. I only hope that this game was enough of a financial success for Obsidian to encourage them to continue to break the mold like this in the future. Games like this deserve to exist, and I want to believe in a future and a world where we reward those with the fortitude to create unique and potentially polarizing new things.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing little gem. Great dialogue, and the art is really good, especially the characters. Its not a full-fledged RPG like all other Obsidian games - it's not meant to be one.No voice acting makes the experience all the better. Like reading a book, you don't have a fixed point of reference on how a character sounds like, which allows your imagination to take hold.Having now finished it, the game is an emotional roller coaster. I grew attached to so many side characters that otherwise SHOULD not have that much of an impact. But the art and the dialogue and the setting just made them feel alive.And all that emotional buildup culminated in the very last scene at the end of act 3. And I can't stop thinking about it and all the characters.I dont think I've ever seen a game's story make so good use of the 14 hours it took me to complete it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fascinating game, but only play this game if you're prepared to read...A LOT.The story is fantastic and I would consider it riveting. There were times where I had chills and just couldn't stop playing. I was constantly in awe of how my decisions early on affected things consistently even into the last moments of the story.The art style probably the most stylized and most beautiful I've ever seen. The attention to detail is insane, and even small choices have effects that you notice later in the game if you pay attention.The game also includes a TON of accessibility settings and features that make it easier to consume, especially for those who don't normally enjoy reading or have trouble reading.On top of all of this, there is so much replayability and the sound design is fantastic, adding a captivating atmosphere and making the world feel even more alive.Overall I'd recommend this game to anyone who enjoys story driven games, it is definitely a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: You'll be amazed by the intricately crafted dialogue and calligraphic expression throughout the entire story. Details such as typos being fixed, font changing on learning more about the speaker, to inc splatters and scratching from a feather to signify volume. All of which makes Pentiment's dialogue one of the most realized mechanics yet to be seen in any story-driven experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is one of those games that has such a niche premise that when I heard of its impending release I was simply glad it existed, even though I wasn't sure I'd play it. But I'm glad I finally came around to playing it, as it truly is a game like no other. Pentiment both shows what kinds of stories video games are capable of depicting, and elevates the medium as a whole.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good point and click\mystery solving game. But it’s not the usual “find the pieces, stick them together and go to the next phase. If anything this game reminds me of Pathologic (If you know what I am talking about). The game don’t handholds you, you have a journal which tracks a lot of things but you have to connect the dots and do the detective work without objective pointers. You have to remember what to do, who to talk and there is no crazy item juggling. There is also some kind of “reputation” system which will influence if people will or not trust you when the dices are rolled and the knot pulled.The story spans on a large length of time, you will see characters, choices and consequences evolving during all the game. There is no immediate understanding if you have done all right or you didn’t get anything about what you were supposed to do. The games goes on and you will see what happens.The choices you make for and with you character have a lot of importance and there is a lot of material for another playtrough, just to see everything unfolding with other choices (or doing a better job if you screwed up badly on your first try).The style is peculiar but it’s a far cry from very avant-garde games like A Procession of Chivalry. The miniatures drawing is ok but nothing to scream for. It adds to something that is already well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful work of art, and the care for detail and historical depiction which the developers put into this was astounding, right down to the font choices for the dialogue, and the way the text shines for a second like ink would. simply amazing. The story is also a beautiful one. This is a great relaxing game and the bulk of it is dialogue. There are a few simple mini-games too. It was a real time travel into the age of Christendom at the dawn of the Reformation, so a lot of dialogue choices were about how one might go about handling discoveries of that era. I'm sure it has quite a bit of replayability too as the player makes a lot of choices, like what background the character they are playing has, which in turn allows one to discover things which that background would allow them to understand. If you love art, beauty, good story-telling, and history you will love this game! The ending scene along with the haunting score brought me to tears, it was so beautiful!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not into texts games but this one is different.Visual style matching its theme, multiple historic layers, society tensions, religion, murder investigation, believable characters with own personalities and goals, relations & gossips, actions with consequences later on...You can play very poorly and still finish the game rushed, but what feels great is everything you learn and undestand about this coherent tiny universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. The rendering, the history, the multiple story lines, the characters - all really well done. I never thought I would be emotionally impacted by a game, but I actually felt quite sad and tears welled up a few times. I would recommend this to people who never game but have a strong interest or knowledge of middle ages European history, especially art history. You'll really enjoy the well researched references and beautiful graphics. I also really love the sense of humour and "realness" of the characters. I've never played through a game multiple times before (new to gaming!) but in this instance I'm looking forward to revisiting this world and making alternate choices to see how things play out differently.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a very hard review, describing how much I adore this game without spoilng anything.First, the settings is adoreable. Located in a late-medival town in the 16th century Bavaria and brought to live with an incredible pretty artstyle, the world suck me into it in the first 30 minutes. The characters are non flat and one-dimensional, you want to know more of every character, why they act their way and how they are related to the plot.Second, the story itself, divided into three parts , is with its twist that left me sitting in front of the screen like "OH CMON", but made me feel like I HAVE to know what happens next in our small little town and how things develope.Third, I usually don't want to read a lot of text all the time, but Pentiment made me do it, and I enjoyed it very, very much. Each little piece of dialog is written  rather neatly and presented in small portions, sometimes combined with a bit of game-world interaction.Fourth and final, you can't see everything and have to decide on priorities. While I am usually the completionist when it comes to main story lines, it made me feel my choices had an impact on the world and my experience was rather unique. I know I missed out on some parts, and sometimes had regrets with how I made my desicions. It made me think about my choices sometimes for a long time before committing to any important decision and then delivered.Do I recommend Pentime: Absolutely!Is it for everyone? Maybe not, BUT: GIve it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Pentiment is three things:1) One of the most beautiful videogames of all time2) Easily one of the best written videogames of all time3) An almost unparalleled labour of loveI loved my experience with Pentiment deeply. The writing had me entertained, both laughing when it was funny and sad when it was upsetting. Not many games can straddle that line with such skill so deftly, and especially not when the subject matter is such well-researched history.No other game has had me hand-wringing over the choices I made. Pentiment is largely a mystery game, with the protagonist Andreas Maler attempting to solve a crime of murder. But the game gives you good reasons for every suspect, and you are forced to act upon what you know despite not having perfect knowledge at any point. Then you must live with your decision, and that alone can be tough.What compelled me the most was seeing the town of Tassing change over time. You see families change and grow over time, suffering both losses and experiencing joys as well. And lastly, if there's anything the game is saying it is that love is the most important part of being human, and that the people of the 16th century were just like us, even if their reality was vastly different to what ours is.I'll be thinking about Pentiment for a long time, and I'll be coming back to it again, of that I am certain.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic historical pint & click adventure game. Long text heavy narrative, 20 hours, with none of the typical boring point & click pixel hunting. There's no inventory and the puzzles are self contained. (not many). My favorite Obsidian game since New Vegas and the story is almost as good as KOTOR II. Renaissance era story right around Martin Luther's nailed his theses and the incipient reformation. I REALLY ENJOY how it respects the era these people lived by having the characters believe in religion strongly without being bashful. There is also a technological change underway with the printing press making the monastery scribes obsolete. The monasteries preserved and developed philosophy, art, books, and theology after the fall of the Roman empire. This game touches on all of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game but I quit when it turns out you CAN'T solve the first murder, you can just condemn one of the suspects! That's incredibly frustrating.Not to mention that you can't talk/do everything because some actions move time forward and you have about 3 days to solve the murder, and by solve I mean find someone to blame.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Just wow. A truly beautiful, choice-based, point-and-click game. The story-line kept me hooked the entire time, and when you thought they game was coming to a close, it kept going. I can't even put into words the impact that this game has left on me; I never wanted it to end. The story has left me with the most bittersweet feeling. I will definitely being playing through this again to get the full grasp of the entire town's stories. Please play this; you won't regret it. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: A bit slow at first, but the way all the characters reconvene and re-connect with you throughout this game is truly endearing and a testament to great writing. Most games are quick to write-off or throwaway character development once a plot-point has convened.The medieval manuscript artistry also adds such a fun flair that is refreshing to play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This is art! This game shows that games are a work of art as well. I thank the Xbox for providing funds for this game to exist. Sure the gameplay is mostly adventure-quest like and  very little about RPG elements, yes the plot twist with L.A. Noire style a bit frustrating, and yes, it is a game that not many people will enjoy due to the amount of text and its difficultness. But the atmosphere, the art-style and the look at the historical changes in one small town are amazing. Despite all the clunckiness and tediousness at times I really enjoyed the atmosphere and historical depictions of the everyday life of that period.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed Pentiment's focus on storytelling and narrative choice. The art style is unique, and beautiful, with lovely details throughout. The gameplay is simple and consists mostly of navigating conversations, but the story is compelling throughout and just long enough to not overstay its welcome. If you're a fan of narrative heavy games with a distinct style, definitely give Pentiment a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, interesting story, and your character's background choices feel impactful. This is not Ace Attorney or Professor Layton, but a very cozy murder mystery. There are a handful of activities but most of the game is simply sticking your nose into the business of a not-so-sleepy Alpine village.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made story game, especially fun to play if you are interested in the late medieval era and the style of artworks from that period. Looking forward to doing another playthrough to see what the different choices would have looked like. Would highly recommend trying, especially if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautiful and compelling story games I've played in a long time. The artwork is STUNNING. All of the characters felt so relatable, so easy to connect with. The subtle clues and hints keep you searching, right until the end. The final sequence made me tear up, as so few things can these days. Buy this game; it's entirely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This hidden gem is an absolute beautiful experience - whether you are not really into historical narrative-driven activities, you are going to love the illuminated medieval transcript-like art. Besides from the interesting story and character development as an investigator, the way this game is written has astonished me. The writers certainly have humor which I appreciate most. Recommended buy! Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very enriching and thought provoking! Especially if you allow yourself to have patience with it and suspend any frustration with a couple semi-janky game mechanics and if you really immerse yourself into the culture and time period as best as you can. A couple things could've been smoother but I found myself overlooking any technical flaws as I sunk deeper into the world through the eyes of Andreas Maler (and eventually Magdalene). I am no history buff but with my constant Googling during my play through I learned so much historical context about not only 16th century Bavaria but also surrounding Europe and how the aristocrats, relgious insitutions, and peasantry all were handling the transitions in culture and innovation of the Renaissance.  The atmosphere, the monastic and folk songs sprinkled throughout, the illustrated scenery as you walk through, around, and beneath Tassing, watching and interacting with the lives of the villagers and seeing the changes throughout the decades, and being able to tailor your decisions in a plethora of morally gray scenarios are just some of the reasons that I enjoyed my 20 hours of playing this game. Pentiment is clearly a labor of love, of dedicated research and story building, a relic programmed into a point&click game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: It's a magnificent thing, and this story will be lingering in my thoughts for quite some time.Pentiment takes Obsidian's expertise in branching narratives, role-playing, and building evocative worlds, then packages it all up in an exciting and unique way.I was devastated when it was over, and I'm still not over that ending. But now I'm looking forward to playing it all over again, this time with another Andreas.Maybe one who speaks Latin, studied law, and spent his wandering years in Switzerland.There are some bad choices and disastrous consequences I'd like to avoid this time too. That's the beauty of being an artist: you can always scrape the parchment clean and start again.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the greatest story of any game I have ever played. Plot twists written I could have never expected, impactful themes of trauma and forgiveness, beautiful art and meaningful characters. I wish I could play this for the first time again. First New Vegas then this? Can't wait to see what could be next.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Adored this.From start to finish, I was completely absorbed.  Every step I took, every decision I made...absolutely gut-wrenching choices and constant guilt.  Ending was okay, but the journey was worth every moment! Beautiful visuals, lovely music and sound effects when called for.  Pretty good story and dialogue overall.  Will give it a year and run through it again.  See how it changes things :)
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: When you're in the middle of this game it's pretty fun. A little bit of a simple walking sim, but the art is great, the town of Tassing is fun to get immersed in, and there is TONS of replayability with how you build your character's background. You are an artist who gets wound up in a medieval-murder-mystery.***SPOILER ALERT***=====================================================================Unfortunately as you progress through the story you find out that it was always hopeless to find the actual killer on your own accord. At the end of each chapter the game commits an "Idiot Plot" where something insanely dumb happens that could easily be avoided if someone did *one* simple thing, but nobody does. That's when you realize you're being subtly railroaded.Peasants revolting outside of the library with torches? Made a character that who loves books too? Well, your character is going to just stand there like a mannequin and watch a peasant slowly... casually... toss a torch on the books ===================================================================Final act, you find the murderer. The murderer starts slowly, feebly, pushing up against the supports of the structure you're all in right in front of you. At first your character gives a half-assed push in protest, but then he goes back to just standing there watching it happen.If you're going to railroad the plot, don't make it something so easily avoidable! Not a single torch from the only peasant angry enough to burn down the Library, and not a lazy push against a pillar from an old man you could easily overpower. ===================================================================Also, the main conflict of the first two acts ends abruptly and annoyingly:The whole town is suffering from excessive taxation from the Abbot, so you're inclined to believe he's a greedy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (and may even be responsible for the murder), but when you find out who was *actually* responsible, the guy gives you a sob story about how he's been donating the money to needy people in a distant land. And while you're sitting there thinking "Wow, this guy has been stealing from the Church, causing the Abbot to demand more taxes, which caused the peasants to resent the Abbot and spark a violent revolt, what a prick! All we need to do is tell the peasants that it wasn't the Abbot, it was just this one guy, so send him to jail!" But what is your character's only response to him? "I never knew you had such a tender heart of Christian charity..." WHAT?! THIS ♥♥♥♥♥♥ WAS STEALING FROM THE ONLY PEOPLE YOU KNOW. PEOPLE DIED BECAUSE OF THIS!Then, the guy who embezzled the town's money for years , so like, what happened to the importance of this money going to charity?? When you ask him why he cares so much for the off-screen people you never meet, you know how he justifies it? He shares a religious kinship with them, not you, not the town, so he feels right taking their money.===================================================================I thought I was being given enough clues to solve the mystery, you're not. You're forced to pick two of six innocent people to be charged with murder and 'live with the consequences'. You can't be clever on a second play through and catch the killer quicker, it's impossible. You're just supposed to sit there as the writers jerk off to their own Red Herrings. I guessed the main villain on a hunch in Act 1 (You can tell how the character's facial expression doesn't match the crowd's, and how he's always antagonistic to you, or how he doesn't have an alibi), and I would have been elated if the game let me win like that. Instead it gives you three wrong answers, and when you pick one it basically goes: "*BZZZT* WRONG! Look what you've done! That person's family is going to die now!"===================================================================My mistake was thinking the investigations were solvable. What you're supposed to do is 1. Falsely accuse innocent person in Act 1: Their death reverberates through the rest of the game.2. Falsely accuse innocent person in Act 2: More reverberations3. Do busy work until the game straight up gives you the answer. No critical thinking required.4. Enjoy the endgame mural showing the happy families of the people you  falsely accuse.For your 2nd play though you get to ride the same railroad, but this time you can choose to falsely accuse someone else and see how  family suffers from your decisions. COOLI'm wrote this minutes after finishing the game, so my disappointment is clouding the fun I was having in the first act. The game gives you the impression that you CAN find the real killer, and while that illusion lasts it keeps you engaged. You think that on a 2nd playthrough you can find the real killer with better decisions, but you can't.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I just finished the game and must say I´m stunned. I had an awesome experience. The intricate art design, the minute details in the animation, the overall atmosphere, the writing, the music and the themes... Everything fits nicely. I don´t want to get into the plot because I think that is something everyone needs to experience for themselves. Although the games story takes place in the 16th century, I see a lot of relevance in it for people noways: What is the meaning of life? What do I want to live for? At what length am I supposed to question the status quo and society´s order? Why am I supposed to accept a political order that I was born into?  - a lot of the big questions in everybody´s life. The choices you make concerning Andreas´ character an career `feel´ relevant and help shape the experience.I really cannot give any negative criticism at the moment. I will play this again, for sure! Recommend this game to anyone who is interested in history, art related themes, philosophy and those who are looking for `the special´ in games; something more than just pure entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I adore detective stories and history, especially Medieval times, so when I heard of Pentiment and "overwhelmingly positive" reviews, I was eager to play it. Unfortunately, it turned out a huge disappointment.First, pluses: beautiful art, interesting beginning & a good hook of a mysterious murderer sending notes.Now to the minuses (which form a majority of my experience):One of the worst things is that you are unable to actually save your progress and return to a specific point before making a wrong choice or some mistake. I had to restart the game as I thought choices you make are important (sadly, it's not true and whatever you do, it does not affect the ending that much if any).Another disappointment: extremely long, boring dialogues. Basically, you are clicking 1 mouse  button most of the time and reading, reading, reading... and hardly getting to the point of the long conversations. Don't get wrong, I adore reading books (for instance, I loved Eco's The Name of the Rose which Pentiment reminded me a bit), but a video game is not a book, right?Another huge minus is the part where Magdalene steps in: what started as a potentially good plot, ended up as a girlish story with making cookies & dealing with annoying Otz. By the way,  Sabine & August were awfully disturbing as well as Andreas' complaining. And, making him (players) to actually say a prayer as if there were not enough Christian stuff already?!When I finally uncovered who was the Thread-Puller (kinda strange author's choice, i.e., not convincing for me), I had to admit that enough is enough. The last chapters were both boring and annoying, and killed all the vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I found the story pretty enthralling. I liked the setting. Some of the characters were interesting. I kind of felt like I'd like to get more in-depth into the world of this game, but it's sort of streamlined for you to follow the main quests. I don't consider that a criticism - it's just that I liked the world so much that I wanted more, to be able to really live and breathe it. If you're interested in a game that is something more than a visual novel, where your choices have a bit of impact on the story and world, but that is heavily story and reading focused, then you may like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: The writing in this game is absolutely amazing, I never thought story set in a small town in Bayern could be so captivating. The obscure historical references were all annotated, which really shows the love the team had for the project, and I think Josh Sawyer's love for pre-modern German culture has a lot to do with it.Finished the game on Christmas eve no less, big plot twist at the end, the groundwork was subtly laid, perfectly done.10/10 would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start my review of this game, I want you to know that I have uploaded the final 3 hours of my playthrough on my youtube channel (  ).If you want to watch some uncut gameplay from this game without commentary, I got you covered. So, with that out of the way, let's begin. This game is special, without a doubt. When I saw the trailer for this game during the Xbox E3 showcase last year, I immediately went : " This game is going to be worth my time for the creativity it exuberates alone."It's games like this, that break the monotomy most games fall victim to, you have to keep an eye out for during set showcases, because they usually end up becoming hidden gems. Games that were less popular when they released, but are in the end better than most of the popular ones that released during the same time or after it. This game is an hidden gem. I firmly believe more people should play it. It's one of the more creative video games I played in a long while, and an example of what the team at Obsidian Entertainment is capable off. Let's talk about the art style they used for this game first, the first stroke of creativity the game assaults you with. The entire game plays like a medieval painting, and I love that they made this choice. Not only will this game age extremely well ( again, making this game even more of a gem as time goes on ), but it immerses the player into the game from the moment you start playing it, and it will not let you go until the credits roll. In my entire playthrough, I have not seen any visual bugs. The game runs extremely well, with my laptop getting a solid 165 FPS without fail ( with a Nvidia Geforce RTX 3060 ). Why mention this ? Because the fact that a game releases finished without bugs or issues is a rare thing these days and it deserves my praise every time I encounter one. It reminds me of a time were this was the norm, and not the exception, which as a gamer is a sad thing to think about in this day and age. The story is what you can expect from the talent at Obsidian Entertainment. I'm a writer myself in my spare time, and I like to think I know a thing or two about good writing ( it's the reason why I play games in the first place ), and this game gives you an excellent mystery to solve with a memorable set of characters and excellent dialogue. I especially liked the moments when the story goes inside the mind of the main character. Those moments provide both background information on the main character, as well as some thoughtful conversation with characters living in set character's imagination. Those moments get even better as the story goes on, as the main character's emotional state gets reflected by those imaginary characters living in this city in his head. It was inspiring to experience from a writer's perspective. As for the story itself, I'm not going to spoil it here. I recommend going into this completely blind. As for the setting, the story takes place in 16th century Germany, at the time when Martin Luther started questioning the values of the Catholic Church, and when the effects of the printing press ( one of the most important inventions of all time ) provided a whole group of people, who previously had no access to books, with the knowledge that books can provide, and an incentive to learn how to read thanks to Martin Luther. You play as Andreas Maller, an artist who's in the employ of the local scriptorium, while he finishes his master piece in order to become a master back in the city where he grew up. During his employment for the monks, someone gets murdered at the abby, and a friend / mentor figure of Andreas gets blamed for the murder. It is up to the player to figure out who truly murdered this person, which sets a chain of events in motion of conspiracy and mystery surrounding the abby and the village located next to it. Throughout the story, you get to solve 2 murders, while you live through the stories of the villagers and the monks at the abby, all the while trying to solve the mystery of the Tread-puller, the person responsable for the murders you're trying to solve, and who pulls the strings behind everything that happens in the story. I really liked this story. It provides you with a good mystery, while the story of the village and the abby plays out based on the choices you make, and your conclusions to the murders that took place. The identity of the Tread-puller took me completely by surprise, which is what a good mystery needs, and the twists and turns of the story kept me hooked to this game from start to finish. The only bad thing i can say about the story is that near the end you play as a different main character for a while, and the story grinds to a halt for a moment, becoming quite dull for a few hours, before picking up again with a surprise twist. That's the only bad thing I can say about the story, as the rest of it was excellent and I'm glad I experienced it. The team at Obsidian Entertainment have not disappointed me yet with the stories they tell in their games, and that's an achievement worth mentioning. As for the music, which is a part of game design that people rarely talk about, but is in my eyes a crucial component of games, it is good, with a lot of medieval festive music, a lot of latin/german singing and vocal performances ( which to be honest I'm a little biased to, I love me some good vocals ). All in all, it fits the setting of the game really well and further adds to the immersion ( it's also good to listen to on it's own, the soundtrack is available on Spotify, and I have listened to it several times already ). All in all, I'm really happy how this game turned out. This is definitely one i recommend you buy at full price ( its not even half of the cost of a brand new AAA game ) if you are interested in playing through it. I can already see myself going back and replaying it in a couple of years, just to experience it all over again. Super well done, and congrats to the team at Obsidian Entertainment for releasing this gem of a game. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: NGL This is up there with Elden Ring, and Baldurs gate 3 in terms of its art direction. Probably in my top 5 games of the year. If you like history, Illuminated art, and complex relationships with a small 16th century Bavarian town at the tail end of the middle ages, this game is for you. Play it after you've hit a youtube binge on European history.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't know what to expect even after I've read several other reviews. I have to say I'm very pleased with this purchase and thoroughly enjoying the game currently.It has a good and rich storyline,  many possibilities and takes place at an interesting place and era.It also has replayability as your choices come to a certain outcome but the next time round new choices lead to another.Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: Cadfael, or The Name of the Rose, but as a Choose Your Own Adventure.Be prepared for soul-wrenching decisions at every turn!  And yes, every single thing matters!  I have to say it's also quite a lot of reading, including some pretty front-loaded exposition!  Are you familiar with the politics of 16th century rural Bavaria?  Well, you're about to be.  All this stressed me out initially, and it's not even really my genre, and I was honestly a bit overwhelmed at first.But the depth of this world pulled me back in, over and over.  Beautiful, honest, and audacious.  This game is a masterwork.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally play this kind of a game, but it was really one of the best i've ever played. I did everything, explored everything, I exhausted every dialogue possible. It's an absolute 10/10 and as a history teacher, I would love to have this in my class to explain to kids via an extremely informative and fun way this time period. Martin Luther, this is for you bro.
_childDocuments_.name: Pentiment

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits me in all the right places... I have a degree in Fine Art and Art History coupled with an absolutely passion for the late medieval era so when I meant to start it and just play a few minutes over a cup of coffee this morning, it is no surprise to me that it is now noontime.This game hits one of my favorite moment in history, but especially in the arts - the end of the Medieval era and beginning of the Renaissance period - and it gives me intrigue, rebellion, murder mysteries and coquettish maids bathing in waterfalls.  The visual style of the game is amazing and the art direction is superb and obviously well researched. i find myself loving even the smallest details in the world environment for the references to illuminated manuscripts and early printing. Seeing the tintype used when the print-maker's family speaks, for example, is just perfect and gave me such a smile.It is not for everyone, but those of whom this game was designed in mind for, will absolutely love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a great fan of narrative adventures, though I have not played as many as I might like.  However, it becomes immediately apparent that Pentiment is among the best that has ever been made.Pentiment does what all great stories do: it invests you in its world and the characters it portrays.  It makes you interested in the history that is unfolding, in part because so much research went into making it as accurate as possible.The illuminated artstyle and manuscript dialogue are very compelling and help to immerse you, and the story is an absolute masterpiece.  I found myself caring so much for so many; building conclusions that were sometimes dashed, coming to opinions that I would then have to reconsider.  The families are so special, the events are gripping.  There is a lot of modernized wording and thought added in to help the audience, but as a history buff myself, I felt the game paid a great homage to a time when so much change was sweeping through Europe.If you are a fan of historical fiction, of murder-mysteries, I wholeheartedly recommend this.  Know that you can and will make mistakes, but the world grows from those choices, and for every despairing winter you face, there will still come the bloom of hope in spring.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game.Here's a checklist to figure out if you'll enjoy the game:[] You are a raging medieval Europe nerd.[] You love slow-burn visual novels about relatable characters.[] You are not particularly worried about interactibility or choices mattering.[] You REALLY are a medieval Europe nerd. It's not enough you liked Kingdom Come: Deliverance.If you only "kinda" like these elements, it's not enough. This game is niché, just like other reviews say. It's nothing like Disco Elysium (my god... that's the worst comparison I've seen) The writing is not even on the same level, not in the same universe as that game.I love how much passion and effort was put into the trivia, visuals, music, and accuracy. But it's not fun. The game is so booooooriiiiiiing. Things happen so slowly. 90% of the characters have nothing interesting to say nor do in the story. Only thing they have going for is set dressing. They are there to create this "relatable village" atmosphere. It sure works, but the game feels super super poorly paced and meandering. It barely has a story, more like world-building, with vague themes. Nor has it anything clear to say.The writing is dry, painfully so. If the dialogue would be at least colourful, witty, or otherwise interesting and clever, I think the game would be a joy to "read" just on that alone. (Look at games like Roadwarden). But this game reads like an essay. It's written like one. It's a wikipedia article reformatted so a 10-year-old understands it. It's not "bad", but... It's not particularly great either.There's plenty of aimless running around, plenty of "choices"/"sacrifices" to make that impact very little. Some characters have different lives, some dialogue calls back, but nothing really matters. So you will be here for the ride. And the ride is like that Spongebob clip where the rollercoaster is just a loop with 1 small bump. That's quite accurate visual for the pacing of this game.I personally found the game incredibly dull in all aspects except the artstyle. The story is long and meaningless, the dialogue is lifeless, the choices aren't cool, the pacing is just bad, and the themes are barely there. The game overall has a terrible case of TELL, not SHOW. Very important things happen off-screen and then the resolution is just dumped in one dialogue. It's not good. It genuinely is not well done.It's not a bad game. But it's not great either.

_childDocuments_.review: A game for true lovers of history. This game never ceased to charm me, with so much love and research carefully put into every corner of this game. The art, story, and characters make for a massive world that unfolds in such a small town. A true appreciation for history as it was, this is one of the only games I can think of that comes with a bibliography (with books and articles that I will certainly be adding to my reading list!). The only game I can think of that even came close to exploring medieval/early renaissance life this much is Kingdom Come: Deliverance and I think this game surpasses that one just in terms of the atmosphere, setting, and research. The mystery aspect is thrilling, with limited time to piece together as much as you can before you're out of time and need to name the guilty party. You'll never have enough time to fully figure out everything, encouraging multiple runs. With minor amounts of character customization that unlocks different paths/dialogue options, it really seems like the devs encourage the player to play through it once or twice.With that said, this is a surprisingly long game. I thought that it was done on 2 or 3 separate occasions but it just KEPT GOING. And that's not a bad thing at all. You certainly get the bang for your buck with this game, even at full price. My first run took about 16 hours and, while I was fairly thorough, I did not exhaust every possibility.  Before I bought this game, I read a couple of reviews saying that the ending was unsatisfying and I couldn't disagree more. I won't say too much to avoid spoilers but I think the ending ties everything up nicely.Overall, an amazing experience. Incredibly sweet and heartfelt, with a true love for history, how history is made, how history is remembered, and how people lived. If you have admiration for medieval history, whether that be great academic interest or a casual enjoyment, I would recommend this game. So much charm and love sprinkled on top of an incredibly robust and sturdy base.
