_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a little work. Let me explain.I've loved most of the Rainbow Studios games since I started playing ATV Offroad Fury, through the MX series intro with Unleashed. This game stands out as a different style on how they wanted the player to feel. It comes across as though they wanted to create a more "realistic" feel with the vehicles in this game, and honestly, I love it.The 3 vehicles you get to play in the game (as of right now), are the Motorcycles, which range from 150cc 2 strokes, 250cc 2 and 4 strokes, and 450cc 4 strokes. The second vehicle you can select is a 450cc ATV, and the last one is the UTV (kinda a sporty side-by-side like a Polaris RZR if you know what that is).The game itself feels like Forza Horizons had a butt-baby with an MX game. It definitely feels a bit more sluggish, and less responsive on turns than most of the franchise in the past. But once you start to work around the little nuances of dual stick steering, or how bad you'll get thrown off in ruts or digs, or even corners, the game is one of the best. Speaking of dual stick steering, it seems a few people playing do not understand so let me clarify a little (this is in reference to MX only, it doesn't matter as deep on the other 2 vehicles). The left stick is for your main turn, basically left or right on the handlebars. Up and down on the left stick is seatbounce, to gain a little more height on your jumps, at the sacrifice of distance. The right stick is lean, to tilt your character left or right, and help you dig deeper in the tighter corners, or lean back for a wheelie over some whoops. Like any MX game that I know of, gas and brake in the air is to lean forward or back to do a flip, so make sure you aren't holding down those unless you need to rotate. The last thing that's really necessary, is the clutch. A slight tap of the clutch when 80% through a tight corner, or at the tail end, will give you a little bit more traction and really help assist you to get that bit of speed you might need in something tighter like supercross.Once you break down the game into individual vehicles, you get a little more complex on controls, but nothing that's too hard to learn. MX has one of the most responsive feels, but as the engine size gets bigger, you definitely feel that weight in corners. ATV feels very fun, it's the most straight forward of the 3, and probably the easiest. And the UTV is arguably the most fun, but also the hardest to learn and get comfy with, it's a freakin boat. It should also be noted that the 3rd person view feels really slow and slightly clunky, but I'm sure there's some people who enjoy that more. But I play exclusively in 1st person, as it feels MUCH better, and almost fits the "realism" part of the game I enjoy so dearly. It should also be noted that you should almost immediately be upgrading your vehicle, as it gets harder to hit jumps and actually land them properly, without adequate power.All of this good aside though, there's a few very blatant problems. Luckily they aren't game breaking, just annoying.Firstly, in 1st person, going over any jumps or bumps, your character tends to throw their head up and to the left, probably coded in to help you see where you are landing and what's ahead of you, but for the slightly bigger whoops, or if you case a lot of jumps, it gets kinda disorienting to get thrashed that much without control of your camera or any settings to dampen the effect.Second and definitely the one you will notice most, the audio needs an entire rework. Getting your MX going above 2nd gear, you'll hear the bike re-start its throttle sound, so it almost simulates revving your bike really snappy and fast, it doesn't sound natural at all. And it only gets worse, the faster you go.The 250cc 2 stroke, the 3rd bike you get. God I want to love 2 strokes so badly, but this specific bike ruined the entire experience, until I shut all the sound off on my system. The exhaust sound will leave your ears bleeding compared to other vehicles, and sounds terrible. The only way I can describe it is gargling spoiled milk. Putting frozen beans in a blender. Putting spaghetti in an upside down lawnmower. You get the point, it's terrible. I think it wouldn't sound so terrible if it wasn't clearly the loudest vehicle in the game, by a longshot. You hop on a 250cc 4 stroke and it's really tame. You can even hop on the 150cc 2 stroke and it sounds fantastic. But that god forsaken 250cc 2 stroke is like microwaving bologna in olive oil for 40 minutes, at deafening levels.Speaking of things being really loud, the freakin music, of all things. It's really quite good when you are free riding and exploring, as the sound is almost attached to your player or just background like it should be. But for some reason, it's like the Dev team wanted to make dynamic stadium speakers, like you would have at a real MX event. You go into the Campaign mode or really any race for that matter, and you get music blasting at levels that will make you flinch with every percussion or beat. You could throw your headset across your house and you'd hear the music fine, unless it's an endurance style race, where the map is huge. In that case, the music is usually either glued to the start and finish, or to the crowds. But good luck with that tinnitus on the smaller maps. I'm sure your friend's jet engine fan blowing into their mic, is more quiet than this music.Oh and there's a third thing that I cannot stand. The maps "Vallis Wind Farm" which has an A, B, C, and D variant. Normally, the map is fine. On MX you might struggle a bit as you need to understand how the rhythm of landing jumps works, which I got stuck on because I didn't know you could upgrade the bike to help land more jumps, or to get more power coming off of a botched landing. But once you get into UTV's you'll for SURE hate the map. They decided it would be a bright idea to stuff 8 freakin vehicles, each being about 2x the size of a golf cart, on a single lane map, where even ATV's struggle to not hit each other. It's immediate congestion right off the start, and god forbid you get the holeshot through the start. You have to wrestle this machine, as it fights you to stay straight on the landings, and as you go over countless jumps of all sizes, hoping and praying that you won't just barely budge the stick to the side a little too far and have every other driver pass you while you respawn. It seems like changing difficulty does nothing to help you as, to assist my pain, I set steering to 1 stick, difficulty to very easy, and made the rider physics not pro. But it feels identical to any difficulty, or any setting. I even race it in 3rd person to help see what the heck is happening, but even then it's a tense struggle. BUT on top of all of this, there's literally 7 other guys with their foot through the floor, bricking the gas like they left the oven on at home. It's a nightmare to try to land straight or to control your vehicle and try to get a 1st place win. BUT IT DOESN'T STOP THERE...You have to complete map variants A-D MORE THAN ONCE. The game is measured by seasons, so when you get to the next year, you have to run it again. Off the top of my head, you have to race the set of 4 (A-D), 4 times through the career, PER VEHICLE. Granted, the ATV and MX are much easier to grasp, but still, it gives me the heebie jeebies even thinking about trying to 100% get first place.Fourth, and minor at that. The snow maps, there's specific sections of it like the starting/ finish line, or the huge left 180 corner, where I get horrible lag. I have a 1080ti playing on 1440p monitors, and other than this one specific map, I get zero other stutters or hitches in the gameplay.TLDR. The game looks beautiful, it plays great (once you get the controls down), and it's definitely something I would recommend, as long as you have a controller and are alright with first person racing. But it has its issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to begin.One of the biggest things I dislike most about this game is how boring it is literally. The career events are so painful and tedious to play, the customisation of your bike and rider etc. The menu could use some improvements and so could the UI, the camera angles are not very good and slightly odd. I always seem to find myself falling off my bike its not exactly what I would call fun, there is not like any sort of rewind or instant reset, the actual reset the game gives you forces you to press and hold a button, for like maybe 5 secs and then by the time you do reset, all the AI opponents just slight shot past you and the game will just respawn you like exactly where you were, so say for instance your climbing up a hill or something your not going to gain any speed and then it becomes annoying and quite frustrating.Considering the cost of this game with all the DLC. _childDocuments_.review: MX vs ATV Legends might seem like a fun game at first glance, but upon examining the game further in more detail you might come to the realisation that it needed a lot more time in the oven. The premise is there, but the execution is very poorSteam Curator Page:+ Cleverly laid out stages+ Good amount of stages+ Split screen+ Multiplayer- All sale category vehicles behave the same- Upgrades make little to no sense- AI is rubber banding hell- Audio design is mostly broken- Graphically not impressive at all- Hub world feels like a waste of time- No official ultrawide support (DO NOT change out from full screen)- Stretches image on UW monitors instead of black bars- Cannot replay tutorialMX vs ATV Legends feels like a rushed product. Starting off with the good. The design of all the stages is done in a great manner. When the game is taken at its core, the racing CAN be a lot of fun and it does not feel repetitive thanks to the healthy amount of stages there are to play on. Some tend to partially repeat when used between the different vehicle types but each vehicle will bring its own challenge to stir things up.Continuing on to the negatives, my main gripes with the game are the driving mechanics/ handling and the AI rubber banding. Even on the easiest difficulty, the AI will tend to ignore the laws of physics and blatantly rubber band and slingshot past the player. I am well prepared to face the harsh, but fair, reality that I suck at this game. However, the only time I notices that the difficulty was affecting the AI's behaviour was only during the MX portion of the game. UTV and ATV races ignored the difficulty and  there was at least one or two AI units that were driving incredibly fast. This is less blatant in the easiest difficulty, but it is still present. The driving mechanics are also not perfect. The handling is incredibly funky and very arcade style. Getting the jumps right takes a lot of practice and unfortunately, according to my experience, it is impossible to repeat the tutorial. A very close third is the horrific experience I had with the audio design. Sound effects seem to be properly rendered, but the balance of the audio is way off in most cases. Usually the music is too quiet and will start blasting at either random intervals or specific parts in certain stages. Having my bike at full throttle and full revs on the tach on the bottom right results on my bike's engine making flocculating engine noises with it revving up and down. That is not very accurate and contributes in the poor audio design of the game.The menus feel clunky, the upgrade menu of the vehicles is not explained very well. For example, Cutch boost VS clutch speed upgrades in the UTV as shown in the video. What is the difference? I can at a glance see what the end result will be on the bars next to the vehicle, but that still does not provide any values, or any form of feedback explaining what each upgrade offers and takes away. In the case of the UTV, I added so many upgrades to it that the bars were literally off and past the charts. Car still handled like butter wheels on ice though. Fans of the series might disagree with me on this and I would love to hear why, if you do. Please, give me some feedback in the comments of the video explaining to me if, and why, I am wrong with my outcome. Did I miss something? And did I miss it because the game did not do a good job at explaining it to me? Am I missing the point because I am so far past it? Or are my complaints valid? I am well aware that his might blacklist me from ever receiving keys by THQ, a publisher that I hold near and dear to my heart because they helped bring the Darksiders series (1 and 2, 3 was subpar) to the world. They have helped bring Wreckfest to the world. Spellforce, Remnant FTA, SW Jedi knight, ELEX,  Pillars of Eternity... The list goes on when it comes to great games they have published. This is not one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Review based after the v1.08 patchPros:- Supercross tracks are all good they knocked it out of the park with these- Pro national tracks are very well done the ruts and braking bumps are placed in right locations- Physics are an improvement you have to brake instead of pinning it on every corner- Seems like the dev team is listening to feedback already and trying to improve game- DLC content- Online racing is intense you can bang bars and race close without crashingCons:- Customization is lacking from previous games (No graphics kits, less parts, barely any gear)- Nationals tracks leave a lot to be desired thrilled they went with more fantasy on some; however the roughness and where they placed it on the track just doesnt work well at all.- No leaderboards for laptimes, no voicechat, and no custom lobbies online- Tuning needs reworked I understand having pros and cons most people are running the same setup- Game seems to crash quite frequently on PC- Bike sounds could be way better not sure why this is so difficult- Career mode is cool and how you have a compound and level it up. The whole thing just kind of feels empty you get new sponsors and they never really seem to do anything. Good idea with the career just bad execution.This game has a good foundation and they have improved in some areas over the previous installment however core features of the franchise are just missing which is unacceptable in my opinion. I'm really looking forward to the content they come out with in the future for this game. At this time I wouldn't recommend picking it up unless you are a diehard fan. The racing online is a blast PC seems to have a small player base that is usually active at night.

Worth $36 on sale, sure, but I feel like if it was really polished like a game with a release date that's been pushed out until summer of 2022 should have been then I would rather have waited even longer and paid another $30 for better quality.  The audio is a mess, the first 125cc you get sounds amazing idling and pretty good while riding (especially while in first person view) but revving with the clutch pulled in sounds like a toy weed whacker! The music I eventually shut off because even on the lowest setting it would randomly start blasting out of nowhere. In the tutorial it's even worse. The menu does not look great on a 34" curved ultrawide, it's like it's stretched to fit terribly. Gameplay is fine though otherwise. Graphics are beautiful and the terrain looks really good! Deformation looks good in first person. Speaking of first person I feel the physics and the way the bike handles with pro physics and dual stick control on is fantastic, I switched back to third person for a bit and instantly wanted to go back to first, it's so good. The game makes it easy to ride around and finish races but to actually win on a normal difficulty you really have to ride the bike correctly with body and bike control and hitting jumps perfectly. It is a bit of a learning curve but ohhh man does it feel amazing when you hit a line perfectly! The tracks in this game are a ton of fun! If you're trying to absolutely send it off everything in a stock 125, you're bound to crash, so you definitely have to learn the tracks and hit lines with a bit of thought put into them if you don't want to eat it and actually place on the podium. I wish there were name brand vehicles from the start or unlockable through play without having to buy them as DLC packs. I hope some of the little things will be polished in the near future. As of right now it's worth it on sale if you can stand to make it through the tutorial and if you like to ride in first person view!

_childDocuments_.review: This is certainly a good *looking* game, but I'm having problems actually enjoying it: the biggest problem is the inconsistency of the tracks, the lack of balance, and the fact that the AI bikes "cheat".The core problem is that motocross racing is not just about "going fast." It's about managing your energy and tackling obstacles on  a course to maintain your speed.So let's start with the tracks: I ran the first race and pretty easily beat the AI bikes on the medium difficulty. On the second race, I found myself having to run sections over and over again, because the track had whoops and jumps that were simply impossible to sail through, due to the poor handling of the player bike's preload/seat bounce system. On a real motocross bike, you can compress the front forks or the rear shock by appropriately leaning and managing the throttle going into a jump Do it right, and you can sail further or rise higher on a jump.BvA tries to implement this, and it seems to work to a limited extent, but this is where "the AI cheats" comes into play.You start the game with a smaller bike (a 250 2-stroke, if I recall), yet the tracks are sized for the larger, faster bikes. So you can't actually make the doubles or fly through the whoops like you could on the bigger bikes.Except that the AI bikes don't seem to care about that. They will sail over a double and make a perfect landing, even though they are traveling the same speed as me. I can run the same section, preloading, seat bouncing, or doing both - yet get the same basic result. Looking at the path the bikes are taking, it seems like the AI bikes are basically taking a pre-recorded run - then just playing it back at a slower speed. So they make every double. They go through the whoops with no problem. They nail every turn and basically can't be pushed off their course in a collision... yet the player bike can attempt the exact same path and speed, yet constantly crash or fail to make jumps.For this reason alone, I'm saying "don't buy" on this game. And that's disappointing, because I enjoy off-road racing games and riding ATVs IRL. But the races in this game are just not enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam noticed that I keep playing this and asked if I wanted to update my review. So this is an update - the original is below.The game is still meh, but since I paid for it I want to try and get my money's worth out of it. As you play through the career the difficulty increases because they stunt you from getting as many holeshots. CPU racers are able to immediately jump off the line and accelerate to speeds you aren't able to reach, and the difficulty increases because then you are stuck in the pack and any tap to your vehicle and you're folding up like a lawn chair. You fall off when you are in the pack and you will lose 7-10 positions every time, and that's where the challenge is. The atrocious physics are still present and accounted for. You still get those bounces after landing jumps some times that send you off to Mars, and regardless of how you are positioned, you will always land, turn as flaccid as Leonardo DiCaprio does around women his own age and proceed to slowly drop off the bike. It's unavoidable. Oh and the camera is terrible too. The desert levels with the cave that drops will make you wonder how a camera this bad made it past QA and into a finished product that customers pay for. At this point I'm 20+ hours in and I still wouldn't really recommend it. I don't expect to be great at everything I do but this game just keeps being frustrating for reasons I don't have any direct control over. There aren't very many MX or off-road racing games out there like this unfortunately, but if this is really the best that is out there than I would say save your money. It's like they could have either gone for an arcade feel or realistic but somehow managed to miss both of them completely. ---ORIGINAL REVIEW---So if you like MX or ATV racing games, there's really not a lot out there, so far that reason it's hard not to recommend this game. But man this is such a frustrating game, and it is so inconsistent! Sometimes you take a jump and land it perfect and it still kicks you off the vehicle, or even worse, sometimes it sends you way up into the air for a second 'jump' which you then get kicked off the vehicle for. Sometimes colliding with another rider doesn't do anytihng to you. Sometimes a vehicle grazes you and you turn into a wet noodle, sliding slowly off the vehicle and losing at least six or seven positions before it graciously allows you to reset. Sometimes you can do half the race off track and its fine, some times you go off track and it immediately resets you where you are. When you reset, you start from a dead stop, which is just brutal when there's no real consistent explanation for it. You will always lose at least 3 or 4 positions from having it reset you, and you will be lucky to gain even one of those positions back so you might as well restart the event, in fact if there's one consistent thing about this game it's that you will restart every single race at least a dozen times before you even finish a single lap. You get a bad start off the line? Restart. Someone knocks you off your vehicle before the holeshot? Restart. The lousy game physics knock you your vehicle when you land on a jump? Restart. Go off-track in the wrong space? Restart. Lather, rinse repeat. When the game clicks, everything runs well and it's really enjoyable. But sadly it's more restarts and frustration than it is racing.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan since the Xbox 360 Reflex, this is a nice improvement. A lot of the negative reviews about traction, AI, and overall gameplay are likely to stumble through a minecraft world set-up. You can tune your bike according to your play-style, adjust AI difficulty in settings, and have an improved experience over previous titles. It's a fun Arcade-style MX/ATV/UTV game. there is no additional launcher, the graphics are a huge improvement from previous titles, and the compound is pretty sick.My only cons...There was some serious rubber-banding when loading in. Almost like severe server lag, but on single-player. I'm sure it was assets loading in, but i do periodically experience it on lengthier trails.  Another would be the bails on hard landings. Sometimes a hard cut on a berm can force you to bail. Mostly it's when you land just after the end of a long triple. Most times your suspension would hold it, but dude and his ankles just fold. All-in-all, it's a good game.  It has some quirks, but isn't enough to ruin the fun of it. I'd say it's a 10/10 on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been back and forth on this game.  At first I hated it, was pissed off they sold this crap to me , then I persevered, played on.  After completing the career mode and riding the vast free ride maps, I found there are some things I liked. As I got better, I noticed things that were dog sheet.  When you are going up hill, its like they tied a piano to the bike, if you get a little air, the bike jumps straight up and starts going backwards, amd a bunch of AI go flying by( in the tunnel), or if you contact a bail, another rider, over or under jump...the bike goes to first gear. Like from 4th, and suddenly 1st.  I can't play in 3rd person, kind of like All Out, have to be in 1st, the bike still doesn't seem right. game crashed a lot, I click send report over and over. joystick shifting, no re-mapping of controller, I don't seem to be able to turn fast enough on sx tracks to be fast and consistent. I went from hating it, to liking some of it, to I just don't want to play this anymore. I enjoyed All Out, so have gone back to that.  I know people are hoping patches will be the answer, I don't think there are enough patches to make this any good.  There's ridiculous money needed to spend to get all the DLC, which isn't worth it because the base game still has issues. I have played many dirt bike games, so not my first rodeo, I'm very disappointed in this purchase, I know there are people reviewing as good and would recommend, but I question what their experience with the history of games is. I'm not saying you can't have fun, I know I could have fun with Pac Man, but soon get bored of it. _childDocuments_.review: *Post Update*Bikes now feel a lot more grippy and not like you're sliding on ice. UTV racing still feels like a joke, not in the way they handle, but being rear-ended constantly. My first UTV race, i had to check if i was playing Wreckfest. _childDocuments_.review: So here it is, I know many of you have been curious on how I would review the game and this is my thoughts after 20+ hours and finishing the MX series. 1. Game is not perfect, there are many bugs that need to be fixed. Mostly for me the random stuck in gear after upgrades or new race, the name/number not showing correctly after being added, and oh my...the amount of game crashes are insane. 2. The lack of items and real life products are really a worry I have that much more DLC is coming soon. Most other MvA games had much more to offer and with the MESX games you really have a lot to choose from. 3. The rider motions in the game and the whip/scrub physic could use some work. Once you get good at it you really can throw it around, but it is still vague compared to past games.But now onto the good!1. This game has some of the best elevation and track design of any game, period. No matter how much you want to hate on the game you cannot tell me the tracks are amazing and really well scaled to the speed/style of the game.2. Makes you work hard for the part of the career you want to be at. So many have asked for a game that makes you work hard to go from the start of racing to pro and then when you finally have it so many complain that it takes too much work to grind and make it to pro. I get it, the stock bikes suck, but it is so worth it once you level up and build your bike and progress.3. Graphics imo are some of the best we have seen. They are really stepping up the game. So overall I would give this game a solid 7/10. Main reason being that this is a step in the right direction and I really think that once they update the game more and work out the bugs it will be back to how we enjoyed these arcade MX games like we did as kids. Order up that Pizza Hut, get out some SURGE, and call your friends over. Just have fun and enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd wait 6 months or so for them to fix most of the issues/missing content. The tracks and free ride are by far the best part of the game, really well designed and filled with booters and great elevation. Physics are good and bad, they get better once you tune up the bikes a bit, at release they slid around corners a lot. Since then they have already patched the game to give the bikes more grip in corners.Scrubs feel great, whips not as great. For some reason the bike doesn't come back in the air by itself when running with pro physics, but turning off pro physics makes it easier to bring it back. Go figure.The game has an actual career, with a linear set of events you can go through for each individual type of vehicle. Only really been playing through the MX career but it has a good variety of events. The game sorta has a story of you helping an old motocross rider save his farm. _childDocuments_.review: Are you tired of feeling disappointed in yourself all the time? I know I was. That's why I bought this game and boy let me tell you, its been amazing being incredibly disappointed in something else for awhile. And for the low price of $39.99, you too can feel disappointed in something else!For the real review..Overall: I understand this isn't a Simulator, not everything is going to be "Realistic". However; this game is pretty terrible considering the amount of advertising and how they are literally sponsoring a portion of the AMA National Motocross series. I would expect a much more polished game. CONS:-Upgrade system is a joke. Parts are for show only, no reason to buy them for performance. I'd wouldn't mind the "Tuning" options if it was a combination of tuning and parts to increase performance. But its just tuning.  -Preload/seat bounce doesnt feel consistent in any manner. Sometimes you'll clear a jump, sometimes you wont despite taking the same line, at the same speed, doing the same maneuver. -A 125 with some "tuning" is faster than a stock 450, yet still can barely clear the 700ft  jumps unless you're a master at their poorly designed controls and physics. -You cant really rev it out in the air to prepare to land and get power to the ground, it feels like each landing you just bog out for 1 second before there's power again. -Audio makes no sense, noises hardly correlate to whats going on. Putting around a 2 stroke and it sounds like im blowing out the top end.-Dumping the clutch for quick speed works randomly, sometimes you get a boost, other times you just bog out.-Crash on the MX course thats nothing but 350ft doubles with 60ft take-offs? Might as well restart the race because you aint ever going to get enough momentum to hit the next world record sized jumps.-I know all of these games are the same, but for the love of god can I just play all the stock bikes and all the stock modes without "earning" them for 5 hours in silly races and tutorials? Maybe I just want a have 450 so I can go mess around, maybe an "Arcade" mode versus nothing but Career. -Last one, bikes look really stupid. This isnt a performance thing, I just hate how they look. I'm on this spaceship looking bike that can barely clear jumps at full throttle. I imagine the OEMs (honda, yamaha etc.) are probably contractually tied up with the ME Supercross / MXGP Games, and they probably have to avoid making something look similar but come on... Pros:-Trail mode on MX is actually really fun, I like mode quite a bit because its like wide open desert/dirt roads, then they mix in what is as close to single track type technical turning/gullleys/canyons as you can probably get in this type of game. -I dont mind the UTV mode, in first person with custom camera it can be fun to feel like youre drifting the corners. Just turn the sound off because your UTV will sound like a dying whale the entire time. -Supercross isnt terrible, its actually more fun than the Motocross modes. Still needs a lot of work though.-The ability to explore the large ranch is pretty fun.-Hydroplaning is fun once you have a good bike. I dont recommend this game as it is now unless they drop it to $3.99 during a steam sale or fix all of the glaring issues that are outlined in these reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: If you look at the playtime on the negative reviews, most of them are a half hour or less, don't believe anything they have to say.The game gets significantly better once you get better bikes with upgrades, unfortunately this is usually just passed the 2 hour return window depending how much time you spent free riding the crappy 125 around the compound.I do recommend this game however I feel like it released in an incomplete state. I would have been happier with my purchase if it was labeled as early access to be honest. Pretty severe lack of polish all round. People's complaints about the physics are more or less cancelled out once you're on a bigger, upgraded bike. Yes, it's still a bit too slidey, but, if you tune your suspension all the way soft and your tires for the most grip, most of that issue goes away. Also learning good throttle and brake management is key. You don't want to slam on the brakes into corners and go full throttle out of them. You're better off feathering or easing on each. I got much faster when I learned this and the game immediately became way more fun.I do think they specifically need to adjust the traction on berms/ruts. I am fine with sliding the back out into a berm, but once that back tire hits the inside of the berm, it should hook up and go, not slide right over the berm. Ruts also give the opposite of the desired effect. For some reason, they slow you right down like you're stuck in the mud when really you should feel the bike get down into them and dig in for traction. So far, you seem to get punished for getting your bike perfectly into the ruts instead of rewarded and this should be changed. Audio is also mostly horrible across the board and it almost sounds like all the sounds were just placeholders and they didn't have time to complete the audio before release. 2 strokes are literally missing a sound file or something for max revs so the bikes go completely silent when at max revs which is really weird. Bike sounds need a rework all around and the whole game needs the audio mastered because the volumes are all over the place.I do have high hopes that the devs will continue to support this game, listen to the community and make the most requested changes. MX vs ATV All Out is SUBSTANTIALLY better than it was on release and that's because the devs listened and implemented requested changes. Still not my favorite, I prefer Legends physics to All Out's, but still far better than release. I feel like the same will go for this game, the devs will improve it over time without a doubt.Overall, the game is VERY fun once you get used to it. High fun factor, high skill ceiling. Momentum and flow are everything. Story mode is cool and a nice change of pace from just doing random events for no real reason.Tracks and environments are exceptional.Sound track would be good if it was properly mastered.Overall, I think a lot of the game's criticisms are warranted but are also highly exaggerated. If you're a fan of motocross and arcade racers, you will find something you like here if you just give it the chance.

The racing is hilarious (watching the AI whiskey throttle off track and go flying/ragdoll into space is too good) and with the right camera setup feels fast. The new custom first person camera is one of the best I've seen in any arcade MX game.I didn't know that the upgrades were in the "Tuning" section of the garage, so if you're struggling with races definitely prioritize upgrading your bike. Before upgrading, I thought I was playing the game wrong (casing every jump, missing corners, etc.) but after upgrading everything on track seems doable now.Seriously, go set up a high FOV first person camera, upgrade your bike, and go explore one of the insane new free roam maps. Rainbow isn't pumping out the same bs every iteration like Milestone, they are actually trying new things and it's worthy of supporting.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up doing MX in real life, and enjoying MX games as a child, such as Excitebike 64, Pure, MX vs ATV, etc., This game looked like a promising breath away from the super paywalled games like the Monster Energy game(s) and MXGP. However, it was not. Initially, I was hopeful and excited. Unfortunately, while this game felt like it might be okay at its core elements, there are too many details that make it unbearable and frustrating.1. The audio/music experience is annoying. I felt like I couldn't get the music loud enough without the engine sounds overpowering it during racing, even with the music at 100% and the engine volume at 10%. Then, randomly during racing, the music will get so loud it's unbearable. Furthermore, the inability to choose what songs actually play is a feature I feel like should have been a no-brainer. I can think of MX games from the PS2 era that had that feature and it was great. I don't like some of the music in this game and I have zero control over it. Kinda sucks.2. When I started some events, I forcefully got put on the starting bike, even though I had a tuned-up and selected Kawasaki. Why would I purchase a separate bike and upgrade it just to get stuck with the starting one? I tried to figure out why I kept getting put on the starting bike even when I clearly had the Kawasaki selected when I started the event, but could not seem to find any logical indicators as to why. I thought maybe some events were locked to a certain CC, but I couldn't find the CC listed anywhere, so it didn't seem like that. It's frustrating when you are being passed by AI riders in straights because their top speed is faster than yours and you can't do anything about it, especially when you have another bike that is better but the game won't let you use it. Maybe there is some logical reason behind it, but even if there is, it should be stated somewhere.3. I was feeling experimental and switched the transmission setting from automatic to manual, just to see what it was like and maybe what the game demanded in terms of gear shifting. I couldn't really find any significant difference between the two. The rider still shifted up and down gears automatically in both modes. I didn't seem to have any extra controls (I tried to check the controls/keybindings menu to see if there were any controls listed, and then realized this menu doesn't exist). I didn't see any kind of tutorial or mention of the manual transmission mode either. So, to my knowledge, there was no difference between automatic and manual, other than I could hear the engine revving on the upshifts a little more, but I didn't have to really do anything. Pressing the clutch didn't seem to have any effect other than throttling myself, so there was no point.4. Lastly, the riding mechanics are pretty smooth feeling compared to some older games, but it also feels impossible to really hit anything correctly. I started out with the dual-stick handling and got decent at it, but it's hard to not get sideways hitting jumps and I end up losing all my speed in a lot of turns because I end up over-leaning and it spins the rider around. I couldn't preload, seatbounce, or scrub consistently either. Could I probably get better at them over more playtime? probably, but I feel like it's a mish-mash of too many inconsistent suspension mechanics and it's ridiculously hard to have the speed and power at any given moment to actually jump and land anything properly. Sorta like others have said, the bike is too heavy considering how much speed you can realistically achieve to be able to jump and keep your speed most of the time. I switched to the single-stick handling mode to see if it was any better, and it felt about the same, I was just doing less.I could have probably tolerated the riding experience and just tried to upgrade my bike far enough to out-stat the other riders, but the music and bike issues were the nail in the coffin for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played damn near every MX game, and my honest opinion is that this game feels like it wasn't finished yet. The tracks are fun and the game plays decent enough. However, you could thumbs up this review if you agree. The bikes feel like bouncy balls. there are times when you land perfectly and the game feels good, but more times than not, I feel like I land my bike and it bounces up in the air like a golf ball on the pavement. On top of that, turning is pure chaos, you take the inside berm and can fly over the top of it and there is no penalty, you will still carry enough speed to stay ahead of your opponents. I appreciate the arcade-like gameplay as opposed to the Monster energy game I've been playing recently, but come on. a little realism on the tracks is still wanted in an arcade-style racing game. If you are looking for a good ♥♥♥♥ around game to play with the boys, I think you'll enjoy it enough because of the large tracks with giant jumps to hit. But if you are buying this in hopes of a solid dirtbike racing experience, you won't get that with this game. If simulation style racing is what you are after, I recommend Monster Energy Supercross or MXGP ( but even they arent perfect). Overall, I think the game needs work and I'm not sure if we will ever get updates to correct that. I paid $35 for the game ( 4th of July sale  ) so I will be keeping it, but if you are reading this and the price is $59.99 I would reconsider your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: When the career mode AI racers have no smarts and the multiplayer is a me first marathon (with exploitable quirks), this game is still leading to some disappointment. Although the mx vs atv game selection has been around for a number of years, this latest title feels a tad far from crafted perfection & is appears to be more worried about the style,  the wow factor and the high speed. Of course your tuning is more simple, and the game has a touch of arcade (and seems to be targetted for the younger bikers out there) but when you hope on one of the few vehicle types like a dirtbike, atv, or a UTV it has a way of capturing you and forcing you to do better. Make yourself a better racer & properly utilize it's rider & bike functions. The bikes them self feel a bit better then they were and overall the game has some slight improvements versus previous hours and updates. I can say things are looking up, seasons roll by new content is added here and there & options they change to suit the game better come around. _childDocuments_.review: After playing through a bit more, it's a lot more fun. Once you get past the jank it's an okay game. I would like to see the developers continue to work on this to make it the best MX vs ATV game yet, although it doesn't have a lot of features that I loved from older games.If you're looking to buy this game, wait for a sale and make sure to get track pack and a couple vehicle DLCs if you want the full game... Higher-ups fault not the devs.Bugs that should be fixed:- Reversing/Moving backwards in first person on bikes causes your body to clip through the camera.- Fix/Improve the bike sounds, they are horrendous at times, and the awful clipping bug.Suggestions for improvements:- Vehicle flooding timer bar like in Untamed- Map for the compound like in All Out- The display for the UTV's is very low quality in the Garage menu, I'd recommend moving the camera back or upping the quality of the model displayed if there is a higher quality option.- In the audio settings there should be a track-list of the music played so you can remove songs you don't like and just listen to the ones you like. Untamed had this as an option and it seems pretty simple (from a outside looking in player, I don't know how the music system is set up) and a very nice improvement for people like me.- The helmets do not have straps to keep them on, please model it and add to the helmets <3- Improve the compound, it feels empty and soulless unfortunately. Make some of the roads that lead out loop back in, the amount of times I've just tried to chill and ride around and accidentally rode out of the playable area following these roads is quite annoying. Turn some of the main roads to a more gravely texture to differentiate it from the dirt mix. Add creeks and little bridges over them to add a greater feeling of bliss in nature :)- Make it more clear that tuning is where you upgrade the engine parts etc, I was super confused for a while trying to find where to upgrade. I and many others think of tuning as only like gear ratios and things like brake bias.- Revamp the tutorial to include the garage and alter the checkpoint system to just be apart of the starting tutorial because I found it boring and clunky. Thank you!Suggestions for Additions:- Track Editor. I'd love it to be in the normal game, but it can be a DLC but don't make it more than $5.99 if you guys have any control over it, I don't know the structure of Rainbow Studios.- Split-screen mini-games like Untamed had, those were super fun and don't seem to hard to code in :) Might be something fun for you devs to work on and be creative with!This is a suggestion for the career mode that might be a lot of work, but it could be an improvement.Personally i hated constantly riding to the NPCs that don't even move their mouths when they talk. It's fine to have that sometimes but almost after every race.I'd rather have a GUI in between the races where you are in a trailer and you can select over to a laptop to read and hear audio messages from the NPCs. Then when you are done your series you can talk to the NPCs in the compound. So then we would have less loading screens and less annoying driving to the NPCs then opening back up the GUI, there would still be some. I see what you the developers were going for, but it needs to either be overhauled or fixed into a GUI like I have suggested :)(I will edit when any are fixed or added and put a check mark next to it)I hope with the next game we can get more vehicle types again like some of the older games, Untamed and UnleashedRemember, I only made this review because I love MX vs ATV and I want to see it improve and succeed. Love all you devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, ignore the reviews with a few hours or less.. they haven’t played long enough to get the hang of the game and give it a fair review…Secondly, I almost gave up in the beginning and refunded the game as I was cracking the sheets early on, trying to get the hang of it..I am so glad that I kept with it!!! This game is awesome, the tracks feel like dirt bike tracks and ride like it too! Plenty of difference tracks so you don’t feel like you are doing the same thing over and over.Keep in mind the first bike with no upgrades is crap.. you will crash, you will flat land, you will under jump… BUT, once you earn some money you can upgrade the bike, get better and have a nice flow.Change the settings!!If you want a better feel for the bike and want to be in control, go to gameplay settings and change:Airborne Throttle: User Input (use the throttle to control the bike in the air/ don’t hold throttle flat all the time in the air)Pro Physics: Enabled (gives you full control of the bike)Once you stop treating the game like a simple accelerator/ brake race car game and treat it like a dirt bike, it will get much easier.I never use first person view in race games, but this is a must for this game, it feels like an actual dirt bike and is completely different than third person view.In first person you can really see where you are going and spot you lines and use the track. (the game really feels like it was developed for first person view)In third person I slide out everywhere and under jump, in first person it flows nicely and feels much better.All the buttons/ controls have a purpose and you need to use them all!!Mainly use Preload (right stick down) to get over jumps and use both Preload and seat bounce over the massive jumps until you get the hang of it.Keep in mind there are two brakes, front and rear.Front helps balance the front of the bike in the air and rear helps bring it down and cutting into corners.Rear brake into hard corners and clutch tap out of corners!Use your clutch, its there for a reason.. Clutch tap out of tight corners, clutch tap up steep hills, clutch tap on a slow landing.Don't forget to lean into corners!Lean back and get that front wheel skipping over the terrain!!Just slowly get the hang of the bikes and then worry about coming first place and making the money to progress.

_childDocuments_.review: After reading the rest of the reviews I've come to the conclusion that all of these people are just trash gamers who want an easy experience.First let me get my only gripe out of the way. The sound, and particularly the mixing with the music, needs a patch. Engine sounds are synthetic but nothing different from beloved titles like Forza Horizon 4. Motoheads are sound ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and there's no getting around it. Luckily given All Out received a sound fixing patch back in the day, I expect the same to occur here.As far as the physics goes, I think this expands excellently on the physics of All Out, and fixes a bunch of issues by slowing things down. The heaviness of the bike feels real, and the sliding allows easy scrubs off jumps.What I gather from the other reviewers is they haven't bothered tuning their bikes at all, because whips can be sped up significantly by tuning your chassis, and sliding can be significantly reduced by tuning tire traction. It's as simple as that!People don't actually play the game before giving a review eh? Coming from a person who's held many top5/top10 times on the All Out leaderboards, I can tell these other reviewers just don't want to take the time to learn how to enjoy the game and be quick. You cannot just huck your sticks left and right and expect to be successful. It takes time to learn how to both control your slide and whip aesthetically. The point of a free whip is that it's not supposed to be easy. I personally wish the hardest difficulty was a little harder as a good tune can easily outpace the best AI. All Out received an AI upgrade midway through it's life cycle and I expect the same to happen for this game.The rest of this games strengths are as follows:- Vast open world scale with excellent detail- Excellent outdoor track design- Simple yet effect progression through story mode missions- Fantastic free whip physics unlike any other moto game I've played- Great sense of speed in every vehicle- Killer soundtrack (Finally a game soundtrack with a little bit of testosterone)- Engaging supercross stages that are scaled very well.- Decent customization with real brands- Actually good voiceovers for story characters- New and fresh gamemodes (Trials engages the same part of my brain that Dirt Rally 2.0 does and I love that)- A preload mechanic that takes skill to master + a not-so-OP clutch boost mechanic- Terrain deformation that won't ruin a track in just 2 laps.- Graphics that hold up to modern day titles (cannot speak for the console editions or your brother's shoddy PC)- Bangin' price (especially on sale)At the end of it all, every mx vs atv gets review bombed because there's a cult that just wants rainbow to remaster mx vs atv reflex. Reflex was a great game and I enjoyed it, for the record. But they're not going to do that. Ever. I'll happily play Reflex modded for the rest of my life.For the rest of you that want a new challenge to conquer, while scaling the massive open world stages, this is the game for you! For the rest who want a casual experience I would recommend Monster Energy Supercross. They make one every year, it's basically a subscription! LOLTake care yall

_childDocuments_.review: PROS: + Graphics are really solid. While not staggeringly photorealistic, the colors pop really well and it's fun to look at. It might be my favorite visual style in the series so far. + Gameplay is fun. It feels like All-Out, mixed with Unleashed. It's very arcade-y, very videogame-y, but fun. + Track design is AMAZING this time. Really feels like the good ol' days of MX games. Lots of crazy jumps. + Lots of tracks and a lot of variety. + The career mode is actually pretty fun, it doesn't feel like such a grind to unlock tracks. + All the game modes, including the new trails mode are fun. + Base game is $35 at launch.CONS: - Customization is sorely lacking, especially with the rider gear. There's only a few brands to choose from, each brand only has 1 or 2 color variants, and you cannot change the appearance any further than that. Easily the most bare-bones customization in the series. - While the physics are fun for the most part, the cornering needs more work; The bike tends to drift to the outside a lot and it can be difficult to pick lines and follow-through. Adjusting the Tuning does help a bit, but I still think it could use a bit more work. - The FPS camera constantly drifts to the right on SX tracks (It's mostly fine elsewhere). I really like the FPS camera (a first for me) and the customizable settings are great, but it feels unusable in SX. - The audio is mixed like a commercial; the music can sometimes be stupid loud even on the lowest setting, while the bike can barely be heard at times.FINAL THOUGHTS:This game is fun, it does not feel like a cashgrab. If it was $60 I'd have a lot more gripes with it, but for what you get, I think it is priced fairly. However, it will not blow you away. It's not Reflex 2, but it is a welcome entry to the series, and I do think this game will have a much longer life than any of the yearly Milestone releases. the base track designs alone made it more fun than All-Out for me. All of the issues I've listed can be patched out or improved upon, and I really hope Rainbow does so. I'm looking forward to seeing how it is improved upon.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure glad I didn't listen to all of the terrible reviews!  Get past a few issues that will be patched ASAP and a few janky animations and this game is incredibly fun (and rather relaxing in free-roam).  Let's get the bad out of the way immediately: the audio - turn off music right away (it'll get patched), manual shifting - leave it to automatic for now (it'll get patched).  Other than that, turn on pro physics and dual-stick steering and you're good to go.  First-person view seems to be a must (for me at least), playing in 3rd-person made the handling feel completely wonky.  I had some weird flickering ground shadows that I simply needed to update my graphics drivers for and that was fixed.  Some people are saying there isn't a free-roam, there sure is:  Exhibition > Quick Play > Freeride.  Many reviews seem to mention the physics or the handling: you can re-run all the career races for as much cash as you need and then simply begin TUNING your bike.  Add as much grip or slip as you'd like.  The progression in the game comes from the idea that your first ride is pretty weak and you get to improve it (and others) as you earn money by racing in the career mode.Tutorial was a breeze and took maybe 15 min max.  This is an absolutely solid racer that still may need some fine tuning (starting animations with the elbows is hilarious) but for it's current price of $35 it's a steal if you're into the idea of free-roaming and racing some simply amazing tracks.  There are two huge free-roam areas currently in-game, (you can free-roam the race tracks as well).   I'm hoping they expand on the racing tracks but also on the free-roam areas - apparently we are going to get 22 new tracks this year.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of the MX vs ATV series ever since I was 5 years old playing Unleashed on the PS2. Fast forward a few years, Reflex and Alive came out on the PS3 and I played those titles to death, Alive especially. The graphics were fantastic at the time and the physics were perfect. Since then, I have never found another motocross game that could compete with Alive (especially when combined with the Stewart Compound DLC).I bought MX vs ATV All Out last year, played it for an hour and immediately lost interest because the physics were just too different compared to what I was used to with Alive. Not to mention, I just don't play games much on my PC so I find it hard to get into anything as is. Recently, however, I bought a Steam Deck and thought I'd give All Out a try again. I still wasn't a big fan of the physics in All Out but gradually got used to it and really started enjoying what felt like the first solid MX vs ATV title in many years.Legends came on sale a couple weeks ago so I thought I'd scoop it up for 50% off and see how the latest and greatest MX vs ATV was. And I have to admit, I am very impressed. So much to the point that I *almost* like it more than Alive. Yes, the physics are a bit weird, strangely in the opposite direction as All Out. All Out felt way too twitchy and I couldn't hit scrubs and whips anywhere near like what I could in Alive on the PS3. But in time I got used to the twitchy physics for the most part. I then came over to Legends and wow, do the physics ever feel unnecessarily heavy in Legends, especially compared to All Out. It's probably more of a 'realistic' feel but it's still just too heavy, Alive's physics are still a little better for sure. Important to note though, the overall feel and handling of the bikes and physics in Legends noticeably improves after maxing out the tuning on each bike.Now, this game is packed with a ton of great tracks and locations. And the design for the most part of these maps is really excellent in my opinion. The graphics are also stunning for an MX vs ATV title and the game plays reasonably well (40 - 60FPS) at Medium to Epic settings on the Steam Deck which is a nice surprise. Customisation is by far the best we have seen in an MX vs ATV title. Yes, you do have to buy OEM bikes (if you want them) but price-wise it isn't terrible for all the bikes you get with each bundle. And my favourite part of all is definitely the first person view. It's just fantastic. I'm not sure why, but the overall physics of the game feel better in this POV. Legends is the first motocross game I have played where I find myself preferring to use first-person for most of the game play. It's fantastic.One of my gripes with this game is the soundtrack. Of course, no one expected it to be a banger playlist as in Unleashed. But man some of the songs in this soundtrack really suck, like just non-stop screamo metal. And you can't skip them either, like you could at least in All Out. This is a pretty easy fix, you can just disable the soundtrack and play music (like the Unleashed playlist if you're old school) on Spotify in the background or something. But sometimes it's just nice to know the soundtrack in-game is bearable, this one isn't half the time.I like the career progression but I think having to talk to the 'characters' after every single race is a bit annoying. I shouldn't have to go locate the mechanic on the map and listen to him say 2 sentences about how he's sad that "we don't hang out anymore" before I can go to the next Supercross race. I get the intention here but it just seems like a lot of unneeded filler to make it seem like there is more of a story to this game than there is.All in all, I think this game is really quite solid and better than some of the reviews make it out to be. If you're a big fan of motocross and the MX vs ATV series, give this a try. Especially on sale, it's really a no-brainer. You'll like it.

_childDocuments_.review: MX vs ATV Legends (Legends) is an arcade style offroad motorcycle/4-wheel ATV driving game with a large amount of outdoor terrain to tear through, jump over, or crash into. On an Nvidia 3080 the graphics are beautiful and the game maintains a high FPS. The physics are there, but on medium difficulty at least, the physics are very forgiving. Alas, all is not well though. Legends is published by THQ, a premier game publisher, and it appears that Legends was released in an incomplete state.Upon starting, Legends present the player with the option to play the game with or without Steam support and also to play in VR. VR flat out doesn't work, not with Vive or Vive Pro, anyway. Some video output in VR is achievable, however, the controllers don't do anything, and several different SteamVR error messages pop up. Frequently the HMD would show one frozen graphic screen in the left eye and another in the right eye. Another major problem with Legends is the total inability to remap any of the keyboard or controller controls. Playing non-VR as a left-handed player and being forced to use WASD is galling. The game uses WASD for the acceleration and turning and keys like IJKL for leaning/pivoting. Also, QE are used in jumps, and probably some other keys, though there is no guide in the game for all of the various controls. It is incomprehensible to understand why Legends doesn't support control remapping. There are several graphics quality options and the usual sound and music options. For game play settings, there are several options relating to control operations, and even some custom camera positioning.Legends game play starts out by presenting the player with several tutorials. In fact, when the game is started, the player is dropped on a motorcycle with no introduction and is apparently supposed to know to drive somewhere. Getting used to the controls takes some time and expect to crash frequently in the beginning. As this is a sandbox game half the fun is performing insane jumps and stunts, and in this area, Legends delivers. Ride the trails and make jumps or go overland and ride right over a rocky cliff. Legends also has a split screen mode, like as might be found at an arcade. In this mode, it is assumed that one player will have a controller and the other would be using the keyboard. Though it might be possible that two separate controllers would be used. Legends has bike upgrades and there are various 'missions' to undertake. There is a garage and various deadpan NPCs scattered across the map. Legends looks like a lot of fun, but there are a lot of headaches to playing it. Hopefully the developers will add in controller/keyboard controls remapping and fix the VR issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the reviews I have read and watched, I found this game to actually be quite good. The physics feel great, the tracks are the best in the series, the free-ride areas are massive and fun to explore, the first-person camera is PERFECT (I cannot go back to third person after trying it), and the tuning system is much less of a mess than it was in the past. Additionally, the career is quite substantial and enjoyable to play through.The only really, really glaring flaw this game has is its absolutely abysmal AI racers. I am not amazing at MX games, just somewhat decent, but on the hardest difficulty, "G.O.A.T", I finished every race in the career (yes, even the 450 races) on a 125 bike just to handicap myself and still placed 1st on my first try on almost every race (there were only 2-3 exceptions throughout the entire MX career). On your home track, the AI literally all ride up to the same point and just stop moving completely by the second lap, almost every time. They don't even try to get unstuck - they just sit there, parked.Overall, it's a fun game in its current state. I've played every game in the series apart from Supercross/Encore, and I believe this to be the second best (with the first being Reflex by a large margin). I did not play the game before v1.19, so I was not around to experience the shoddy launch physics and crashes, but as of now the game is quite worthwhile (especially on a $20 sale).

It reminds me of an EA game and their micro transactions.The trails in free roam at the farm are not trails, they are generally flat and wide paths. The sounds need a lot of work. If you don't believe me, look up a video and hear for yourself. I did not try the multiplayer so I can not speak on that.The AI also needs a lot of work. _childDocuments_.review: Decent arcade MX game that we'd all expect from this series. Amazing tracks. It does have some day one flaws but I can look past them for 35 schmeckles. The flaws are the audio. Fades in and out, blares music, bikes sound weak like a lawn mower. The game punishes you for trying to bark corners, without throttle control you blow ruts and slide the rear out and drift. The bike mods seem to do little to nothing to the actual power, traction or handling of the bike. If you get the IRL bike packs they're way bigger than the stock bikes so your rider will glitch through the seat and look like a child riding their dads 450. This series really shines with the modding community of bikes, skins and tracks though. If they can work out the traction some and in air physics to free the bike up some this game will be solid. Right now I'd give it 2/5 stars. It's still better than a milestone game like MXGP or MESX and I'm comfident the modding community will give this game real replayability with friends and solos alike.

_childDocuments_.review: 270hr Review Here!TL;DR: The improvements from the initial release date have been exceptional and consistent from the developers. The team has really listened to the community about making changes to the gameplay while at the same time, adding more content. The tracks have good flow and it's easy to pick up for newbies. Now go ride, Gary.Gameplay physics: 8.5  / 10I tend to like more realism but for an arcade racer, this hits the spot. More improvements are being made here with every patch based on community feedback.Tracks: 9.5 / 10The tracks are incredible and fit well with the bike and rider abilities. Best tracks ever created for the MX vs ATV series imo.The DLC AMA tracks are 10/10Customisation: 5 / 10While they've added a lot from initial release there's still more that need to be added. Dev's in the discord mention that they're looking at a custom graphics mechanic for the bikes and they're constantly sorting deals with companies to bring in more varieties and colour options for bike and rider. Sounds: 5 / 10Still not great at all... ultimately still being worked on with a supposed revamp coming for season 2 later this year.Overall features and options in the menu's: 5.5 / 10There's still a number of standard racing game options they're missing like custom championships, server browsers, career progression, rider stats and levels (think prestige systems) that is missing but a number of these have been considered or are being worked on for later release.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for MX vs ATV Reflex, this isn't for you. If you're looking for good old fashioned MX vs ATV arcade racing, this is the game for you. The bikes feel kind of heavy like Alive did, but other than that, the ground physics feel very similar to All Out. The tracks are very well designed, and the free roam environments are very well made. Don't listen to all of these negative reviews with .5 hours played. They're playing on a bone stock 125cc bike, no tuning, no upgrades. Of course the bike is going to handle poorly. Play the game, unlock bigger engine bikes, and enjoy the game. MX vs ATV Legends is a very good arcade racer, and feels like a new experience, and if you go into the game with the mindset of expecting something new, you will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unpolished, but something good hides underneath.Pros:- The dual stick mechanic feels great. Sliding into corners, boosting out of the corner with clutch, and use preload + seat bumping to launch off a triple feels really great.- Ground physics generally feels good.- Nationals and Supercross tracks are well designed and are a blast to ride.- Tuning system is OKAY. Wish you could tune during a time trial mode / free mode and not just in the garage. Tuning is not well explained in game (what is handling?)- Game runs well and looks really nice.Cons:- 250 2-stroke sound is headache-inducing bad. I have to turn the engine sounds all the way down. The 4 strokes are tolerable but not great.- A.I. unfortunately sucks. I easily beat the hardest A.I. only after a few hours of gameplay. Not having a challenging A.I. is going to seriously dampen the longevity of this game for everyone, unless the online community thrives.- Trails (the checkpoint) tracks are mind-numbingly boring, especially the desert themed ones. Twice I have caught myself thinking about work problems while slogging through these (again on hardest difficulty, winning by 50+ seconds. I promise I suck at this game, the A.I. is just that bad.)- Tracks and bikes are locked behind completing the career mode. I wouldn't mind that if I could just focus on Supercross and Nationals only. The trails tracks are just a huge buzz-kill and are unfun, and there are way too many of them in succession.- Air physics need some work, but are tolerable at the moment. Scrubbing and whips feels pretty clunky. I do like that you can bring the nose down a bit in air, that is a fun mechanic.- Can't rebind keys :(- Some bugs that I'm sure will be addressed soon, like manual transmission not working (stays in automatic no matter what setting I choose).- A seemingly pointless Parts and Sponsorship system. I have zero incentive to interact with these systems at all. Why not make them interesting by tying them into the gameplay loop somehow?Fans of MX games will probably be able to overlook the problems and will enjoy the National and Supercross tracks. _childDocuments_.review: Video Review:  Steam Curator: MX vs. ATV Legends is the seventh installment in a storied racing franchise that pits off-road bikes against four-wheelers and side-by-sides. Let’s start with the good!  THE GOODWhen it comes to driving mechanics, Legends nails the basics, delivering intuitive and responsive steering, clutch, throttle, and stance controls that render realistic results much more often than not. The result is a consistently thrilling racing experience that’s easy to learn and hard to master. But don’t worry, you’ll have plenty of ways to figure things out, as Legends features a nice blend of game modes, including 16-player multiplayer, local split screen, free ride, and a beefy story-driven career option complete with tournaments and sponsorship challenges. These modes take place on well over one hundred different racetracks ranging from claustrophobic super cross competitions to massive, desert wind farms out west and frigid mountain peaks in the east. Speaking of snow, note that the weather effects in Legends are static—not dynamic, as I’ve seen it so-often advertised. You'll never drive through a sudden rainstorm, for instance, as the environments here are all prerendered. And gorgeous, admittedly! Really, despite each race’s high stakes, it’s easy to get lost in the scenery, as Legends boasts excellent lighting and above-average environmental textures... from a distance. THE BADLook closer and you’ll realize that there’s more style than substance to much of the visuals in Legends. For example, the dirt trail your bike kicks up is mostly cosmetic—there’s inconsistent, largely surface-level terrain deformation that doesn’t seem to have improved much since Reflex 10+ years ago. Rider animations, meanwhile, look stiff (at least, until the hilariously bad rag doll physics kick in) and it took me hours to realize that the disturbing double-jointed elbow-popping at the start of each race was actually the revving of engines. As for music, the selection of songs here is fine, if a little all over the place, but it is HORRIBLY mastered—music cuts in and out, has random volume spikes, and drowns out vehicle sound FX on the lowest level. I couldn’t turn it down enough, so I turned it off. Not that the sound design is much better. Vehicles sound okay, but the same choppy audio problems persist, here, and some of the stock sound effects are downright bad. Sadly, these quirks aren’t unique to the style of Legends, as the longer you play, the more you’ll realize that, despite having the foundation necessary to become an excellent, addictive racer, Legends currently lacks depth and polish across the board.  For example, the game’s economy is just busted. I was able to afford Tier-3 parts for all three vehicle types, thereby maxing out their stats, within a couple of hours—a task that would take weeks in other racers. And, because each unlockable vehicle has the same starting stats, I feel no incentive to save up for them. This all cheapens the overall experience, and mind you, Legends is not a cheap experience! Launching at $40, I can’t help but feel like this game is underbaked and underdelivers on features that fans of the genre have come to expect. THE REST Speaking of expectations, I expected exactly nothing from Legends’ story and received just that. The plot is super generic, you know, win the races and save the farm kinda stuff, and is punctuated by surprisingly low-res cutscenes. There are a handful of thinly-written, one-dimensional characters scattered about who inject some decently-voice-acted enthusiasm into the story, but I would never recommend this game on story alone. I don’t have much to say about the game’s simple U.I., so let’s wrap up with a few words on playability. The load times in Legends are decent, the game boasts excellent camera controls, and besides those animation anomalies I mentioned earlier, I didn’t encounter any noteworthy bugs.  THE ENDSo! In the end, MX vs. ATV Legends delivers on what matters most: racing. For that reason, I can recommend it to fans of the genre. But, for everyone else, I would definitely wait for a significant sale. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read, I have only played about 4 hours. Now that has been stated, let me get into the review. First and foremost, I believe this game is just fun. I play MX vs ATV games for the arcadey fun, for sim racing I will play MX Bikes. In my opinion this game has a great balance between fun and challenge. The physics do take time to get used to, but once you do they feel fairly nice, although slippery. I find that it is very important to tune your bike before judging the game, as without it the bike is fairly slippery, and not great to your preferences. Personally, I believe one of the best parts of the game is the track design. Each track is developed very well and is extremely fun. The nationals are my personal favorite, but in this game they somehow made me enjoy supercross and even the trails mode was super fun. Now that is out of the way let me get into some of the flaws; The first major one being how unironed this game is. The music goes from super quiet to super loud randomly, which is a big problem if you like game soundtracks like I do. Another flaw is how slippery it could be. It isn't too bad but it takes some getting used to. The customization is not very good in my opinion, due to there not being many options or even graphics kits. Personally I do not care about this but it is preference. I feel the biggest flaw is that at the time of this review you cannot create private multiplayer race lobbies with your friend, or choose what track it is. All of these flaws can be fixed, and I am sure they will be fixed, as All Out had a pretty sloppy start too. Now I will say some features I hope that they do release: Tag. Tag was a super fun game mode for me and my friends. The 350 MX Models; These were always my favorite bikes in all out. This is just my personal review so i hope i helped people out. TLDR: At the time of this review I give the game 7.5/10. I have a crap load of fun playing it but it needs to be ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Rainbow Studios and THC Nordic Team,I hope this message finds you well. This feature would certainly help increase server activity, as I've noticed that the maximum player count on a supercross track has been only three.Furthermore, I wanted to propose the idea of porting "Untamed" and "Alive" to PC. _childDocuments_.review: MX vs ATV Unleashed is one of my favorite games ever and I have been hoping that magic would come back someday, but it doesn't seem like that will happen here.  The physics strangeness that all others have mentioned in their reviews is a real thing, the most unpleasant aspect I found was that it seems impossible to get back into a rhythm if a single jump lands short. Aside from that, there isn't much to hook the player into with the Career mode from the start:  You race, you go back to free roam and visit a static "team member" who is about 100ft away, then go back to a race.  It's neat that there's a free roam, but I couldn't find a way to open a map to save my life and nothing was in the controller bindings.  If you're going to have a free roam in a racing game, give that free roam a purpose and introduce it to the player immediately!  Give the team members a purpose, give me something to work towards in free roam, or just a map so I can see what's out there.  Without anything to entice me to go wander around, I'm simply going to just go to the next race, and since there's nothing to entice me to keep searching for answers in the game, I'm simply going to just go on to the next game in my library and hope that someday that fun Unleashed was able to provide for hours and hours comes back.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can look past the glitches, Legends is a good arcade racer. The grind isn't bad, the weather effects are incredible, there's a lot of assist and customization options in the settings, and there's no rubberbanding. What kneecaps this game is the outdated physics/animations & AI. There's little traction and bikes have a tendency to stick to each other like magnets. Bots are skilled in supercross and certain tracks, but are morons in almost every other race style or vanilla stock track. ATVs are as crappy as always in this series, races devolving into bumper car matches. In UTV races, you can even lap the competition they suck so bad. MX vs. ATV Reflex still has better deformation and general ragdolls and physics. In Legends' defense, this isn't an eyesore, possesses slightly better AI, and has way better maps and a far better control system than Reflex's godawful Kb&M set-up and crash QTEs. There's a good amount of content, but the DLC monetization model is EA-levels of slimy. Brand-name bikes are behind a paywall, and they've resold the same tracks and bikes a few times.Edit: The game is constantly being updated, so expect changes every couple months and occasionally to break. Online is dead. So you probably shouldn't buy it if that's all you want.
