_childDocuments_.review: Very long review, but I feel like my review might offer a slightly different viewpoint from some of the others.-- Background --I very much enjoyed ATV Offroad Fury 3+4 (had 2, didn't really click with me as much) on ps2 when I was a kid and they were a couple of my favourite games ever. I spent so much of my free time playing these games inside out and it's a gaming experience I don't think I'd be able to replace with anything else. That said, MX vs ATV legends certainly doesn't replace them.Now, I haven't really played these kind of games since then. I got ATV OF4 on my steam deck last summer and had been enjoying it thoroughly, nostalgia and all it still held up great. But a few weeks ago I got looking around at what had really happened since then with these kind of games, and I was led here. I saw plenty of terrible reviews of this game's launch but a few had said it improved greatly, so I watched a few videos and decided (while the game was on sale for a large discount) to pick it up with the track DLC and all the bike/atv etc DLC.-- General thoughts and setup --After beating the MX career in around 31 hours (and most of the achievements along the way) I have some mixed opinions on my experience, but overall, I enjoyed the game! I am basing my experience off of the ATV OF games from ps2 era as well, so I don't really have the same attachment to games like reflex that other people mention often.The first thing I did was change the control scheme to single stick because I was struggling with the double stick (default), separating bike steering from rider leaning just because it's not what I'm used to. After that, the game became a lot more familiar feeling. Other reviews mentioned the AI is way too easy so I also set it to G.O.A.T (hardest difficulty). -- Career --The MX career starts you off on 125 bikes and feels very awkward, the bikes are underpowered for most tracks even after getting all level 3 upgrades and you'll have a hard time flowing over jumps smoothly. Getting to 250 almost completely alleviates this problem, but you'll still have to ride well to make some of the bigger jumps. 450 made me realize that the tracks were designed around it, everything just started flowing naturally and felt right. Overall, the career was fine except for the pointless forced "return to compound" where you have to ride up to an npc in the lobby map and listen to 1 line of dialog (usually amounting to 'great job kid!', or having to take a sponsorship for a few thousand credits). The interrupts were tedious and added nothing at all to the experience, they would have been better to not be there at all. Sorry to the voice actors.-- AI --As far as AI goes, they are complete garbage at the highest difficulty. I haven't played a single other atv/mx type game since like 2007 and I crushed them easily, except for a few maps in the 125 category where it feels genuinely impossible given your weak bike. It feels like the AI cheats in those events and gets far better air time. Except that once you hit 250 and beyond you will have massive 30-60 second leads by the end of the race even with semi sloppy riding (crashing here and there). Compare this to ATV OF4 on expert, you have to drive near flawlessly and dirty to keep the AI from catching you -- it felt like a genuine challenge and was far more enjoyable.Additionally, in some tracks the AI is completely broken. Rawlings invitational comes to mind when you unlock the upper sections with birch logs everywhere. The AI will just stop dead and do nothing at that part. Some supercross tracks are also dangerous, the AI will fly everywhere or not turn for corners, tossing blocks everywhere and missing the track. This isn't incredibly common but you do notice it when you return to certain tracks.-- Vehicles --For vehicles, the base game offers almost no bikes to you (you get a 125, 250 and 450 from Rainbow, THQ and "Gold Edition", these are the only manufacturers). All the vehicles in a class are indentical in stats before tuning and exist purely cosmetically. The DLC bikes are the same, but they are all unlocked immediately when you own the DLC. I would have preferred to buy them with ingame credits during career because the career currency became meaningless from the start when I realized every bike I would ever want to use (branded ones) were already free for me to use and they all ride indentically. Compare this to ATV OF4, different bikes/atvs in a class would have different stat spreads that would favour different kind of tracks, meaning you could still get use out of multiple bikes.-- Customization --For bike customization (both parts/visual customization) there is very little here as well. Compared to ATV OF3+4 where you would buy parts for your vehicles to raise/lower their stats, and tires for different terrain, MXvATV L simply splits bike stats into "tuning" and "parts", where parts are entirely cosmetic (offering around 6-7 parts for each category, half of which are generic THQ/Rainbow etc). Tuning is a 3 level system to the left and right, but in my experience I found that upgrading everything 3 levels to the right made the bike the best in basically every scenario. Compared to ATV OF4, where tuning allowed to adjust max speed at the cost of acceleration, suspension hardness at the cost of stability, etc, where you could configure your bike differently for supercross vs high speed flatter nationals etc. In MXvATV L, you pick what bike you want and buy all the lvl3 upgrades and it's the same with every other bike, and you crush the competition in any race. It is possible to colour parts of your bikes and some clothes on your rider (depending on what ones you buy) but it is very limited here. Don't expect anything like ATV OF where every colour can be customized to anything. Often times the only thing that changes on the bike is an accent colour, and the rider can generally change any colours, but there are very few cosmetics that allow this. Most are color locked. This isn't really a massive drag but I enjoyed customizing all the colours of my bike and rider to match in ATV OF, it's not really possible in this game and will look messy.-- Tracks --I can say I generally enjoyed the tracks the game offers. The DLC tracks are great but aren't included in the campaign -- there is a mechanic where some events along the way can be swapped between two series and you only have to complete one to progress, it would have been nice when owning the DLC to see a DLC series alongside these if you wanted to swap them in, but for now you can only play the tracks in exhibition mode, or online.The terrain deformation can be a bit jarring to race over in some tracks, it's like the ruts are made out of cement and you bounce around everywhere once they're set in place. I'm not sure if this is the usual for the other games that had it too, but ATV OF had none and it was something I had to get used to, but otherwise wasn't too detrimental.Some of the pathing on tracks is broken (random full respawns riding close to obstacles without crashing), sometimes you get told you're "off track" right in the middle of the track, but this wasn't game breaking, just a minor annoyance.-- Other --The physics feel fine to me, some recent reviews hate them but I don't understand the issue. Unlike ATV OF you preload jumps by pulling down on the stick and releasing, instead of pulling down and pushing up. After getting used to this I honestly preferred it because it was easier on the thumbs.Performing tricks is pointless, because during events you get 0 points or rewards for doing them and it doesn't even say the name of the trick on screen or any indication of a combo. Your rider just kinda... does the pose. I can only trigger 4 air stunts (R1+stick+L/R/U/D), I don't know how to do more or if there are more. There are ground stunts too, but sometimes tricks just don't work at all or instantly crash your rider.

_childDocuments_.review: Legends is THE most BUGGY game I have ever purchased. If you join a match online, you will likely not be able to hear your bike (bug), and your camera will also likely be positioned within the playermodels head (bug) where all you can see is the inside of the playermodels head. Lets not mention that the bikes sound like garbage and the engine sound often cuts out randomly after each shift. I've talked with many avid players of this game who mention how they constantly get taken out or pushed around by other riders, while those same riders are essentially impenetrable to being hit or pushed. In other words, hit registering in this game is messed up bad. The physics are also quite wonky and are practically unrealistic. Most people land directly in the banks of corners after a giant triple sideways while sliding which just looks completely unrealistic. Sadly, no one even plays this game. I've played for about a month and have only seen the same 20 people play every day with a few new riders who barely last a single round before leaving. I can't really blame new players as they just don't know the countless unintuitive little secret tricks that avid players use to win. Competing in online matches is unfair as there aren't any real regulations on how people should play. For example, everyone has a different camera angles, graphic setting, bike size, bike tune, and bike DLC. Its truly bizarre to me as a player coming from competitive games like CSGO to see a game allow for third person and first person players to play together in the same matches. _childDocuments_.review: After putting in almost 40 hours and finishing just the Motocross career with doing maybe half of the ATV and UTV careers, I think I'm ready to give my verdict on this game. This game has a great foundation that you can have plenty of fun in and it has hours of gameplay. It's the things that it tries to do on top of that foundation that don't really take away from the experience but don't really add much depth to them either. The actual *racing* is fun. The physics are just right and give you a great risk vs reward. Balancing your speed on a knife's edge of going as fast as you can without going too fast that you can't take a corner or wipe out on a particular rhythm section. This was enough for me. The game is fun. If you want to know more about the different aspects of the game, read on.This game has been something I sit down and play when I have some spare time just to listen to music and throw down some laps. It's the actual riding where the game shines. Rainbow Studios knows how to make the game feel good to play between the physics and track design.There's plenty of content here with a number of different tracks and races during the main career. Going from small engine bikes to the bigger/faster bikes was a nice progression and the track design is fantastic. How you race a track can change based on how much power you have on your bike. There are certain jumps you can't make on a 125CC bike that you can on a 450CC bike, as an example. So your speed and how you ride the track change. As mentioned above, the actual physics are great once I got used to them.  The "game feel" is great, now I'll touch on the stuff that isn't quite as good.The AI feels a little bit like set dressing because even on the hardest difficulty, I found them rather easy. Once you get ahead of the pack, you can typically run away with the lead. Because racing itself was fun, this didn't bother me too much. I often just made it a game to see how much of a lead I could have by the end of the race but it is something to note. There are a few bugs still in the game that can be frustrating when they come up. There were a very small number of times AI racers teleported way ahead of me in a track such that it was impossible to catch up and I'd end up getting 3rd or 2nd instead of the 1st place I was clearly running away with. As I mentioned though, that was rare. There were also a few instances where I didn't see myself collide with the top of a jump or a hill or something as I was going over them by my rider would crash regardless. Again, this was fairly rare. The game has a system in place that lets you upgrade your bike, but I was able to purchase the "best" parts fairly early and just kept it the entire time, so I didn't really get anything out of this system. The cosmetics are fine. Nothing too special, there's a decent bit of customization but this game doesn't let you play dress up with all of your favorite gear brands, if you were looking for that. This didn't bother me, as the customization present was more than enough for me. The story here is nothing to write home about, but I wasn't expecting hard hitting story here either. What's there is just to tie races together and give you a visual representation of how you are progressing through the career. Again, it's fine. I actually like that the farm you are on gets upgraded as you go along to add more jumps and tracks and trails.So where does that leave me?In summary: I'm not sure the current mixed rating is justified. This game has a solid foundation and racing itself is fun. They've ironed out most of the bugs (minus a couple here and there). The feeling of speed this game has and the "flow state" that you can enter as you rip around the track is addictive. I prefer this physics system over the slower feeling games of the MXGP/Monster Energy Supercross series. The track design is fun and adds some strategic depth to the game as you try to pick your lines. It's the extra features that they have added onto this one that don't really add much but don't take away from the game much either. I think Rainbow Studios should be proud of this game. They remain one of the best studios in this genre and still provide a fun motorsports game. I'd love to see them iterate on this game, as I think they could take this foundation and build something truly great on top of it.

Playing on PC with XBOX Elite controller. Bike weight feels great, especially in the air. Handling manners on the ground feel great, making it easy to thread narrow trails at high speed. The absolute shining gem of the game though is the level design. The outdoor trail and invitational races you'll get to in career mode are hands down the most authentic-feeling dirtbike riding I've ever done in a video game. Exploring the massive amounts of trail in the more open-world levels is great too. First person camera is all I've used. Camera is adjustable, and easy to fine tune. Wide FOV makes the first person mode completely usable, especially in SX. To me (riding dirtbikes since I could walk) this game plays really well, and is extremely entertaining. The bad? Bikes are not very good until they're modded. No pre-race screen to change bikes/settings once you load into the track. Bike sounds are terrible. Sound of the bike is not connected to the throttle at most times. Music replays the same few mostly bad songs in repetition.  Small glitches, etc. The point is, I think the small stuff can be patched and made better, but the core of the game is great. Maybe should've been baked a little bit longer, but hey I'm here for the ugly stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial buildBig problems with MX vs ATV Legends1. The sound of the 2 stroke, so far.I've only ridden the 125cc and 250cc 2-stroke in game, so far. So this may be better with the 4-strokes, who knows.The problem: The sound of the bike is not in sync at all, with what is happening visually or with the controller.Ex #1 - After crashing, the sound of the engine is silent for the first couple seconds once you get going again. Even when twisting throttle and the bike starts moving...no engine sound at allEx #2 - The silly wind-out sound when you hit the bike's top speed. The 125cc bike has a top speed of 70mph. When you get to 70, the bike gets quiet with a sort of constant rpm sound. I understand they are trying to convey that you've hit the rev limiter, but the sound of the engine should absolutely not go nearly silent.Ex #3 - This one really makes it difficult to ride becasue riders/players use the sound as a sensor as to what to do next. If you are riding a fast outdoor track with the throttle wide open, never letting off over jumps and rollers, you'll get the "on the ground accelerating and switching gears" sound even when in the air. In 1st person view, this is horrible because you do not know when you're in the air or touching the ground.2. The throttle responseIf sitting still on an uphill, you pull the throttle and many times the bike does not respond at all. It should at least rev. Pulling the clutch would cause a rev in reality. This game has very poor ties with how an actual bike responds.3. Manual shiftingThe default buttons for shifting up and down are the left and right sticks, pressed down. This is next to impossible to use because you'll nearly always be moving the riders weight or steering the bike in directions you do not want to go, when trying to switch gears. Terrible terrible button assignments. Note there is no controller button assignment feature, so you're stuck with this horrible design.Remaining issues after 7-1-22 update1. SoundPartial throttle gives lower volume version of full throttle. This is not what a bike engine does when fed less fuel. It's cheesy, please pay more attention to the sounds of the bikes, as it plays a major factor in first person play.Dead silence while holding full throttle and jumping. This happens at times, but not all the time.Still have the 2 seconds of silence after a crash, but holding throttle (bike moving).2. Button mapping needs to be added, badly. Nobody wants to manually shift with the two ticks/down. It disrupts steering and balanceAfter completing a career, here are more complaints.1. The bike sounds in this game are an all-around joke. The 250 2-stroke sounds like a snowmobile. No gearing sounds, half throttle is just the same sound as full throttle, but quieter. Extremely weak in the sound department.2. Sand feels like frozen dirt. There's no sandy feel to it at all3. Where is championship or series mode? I have to load the pro motocross tracks one at a time, weak.4. The AI is so bad. I can win a career while single jumping every jump on every track.5. Popping the clutch does nearly nothing6. The ridiculous interaction between my bike and the AI bikes. IE: They come up behind you and steer you off the track. SillyThese, along with my earlier complaints below, make this game a HUGE disappointment.Addition 3 to my list of complaints about this game.1. Floatyness and bouncingNot sure if the devs of this game have ever ridden anything on 2, 3 or 4 wheels, but bikes, quads and SxS's do not bounce and they do not float in the air as if riding a track on the moon.2. The AI is too easy to beat. I have played "All Out" for years and I still cannot beat the AI on "All Time" setting. With this game, they are no challenge, which makes it boring.3. cannot get over the bike's non-responsiveness after casing a jump, or from a dead stop. The clutch doesn't seem to do anything at all.I've played too long for steam to give me a refund, so I guess I am keeping the game, but I sure hope they fix some of these things.ATT DEVS, I work QA for a software company, and I'm here to tell you, this game would never have passed QA testing as it is.07-22-2022 updateOH MY GOD HIRE A SOUND DESIGNER!1. They "fixed" the sound of the 250 2-stroke sounding like a snowmobile, but the sound is not in sync with the shifting, on any bike.For example, if you set it up for manual shifting (which doesn't work in-race, more on that, below) then ride in a single gear without shifting, the sound is that of the bike repeatedly shifting. That is NOT realistic at all, and again kills the feel of the ride.If you are in a single gear, the bike will wind-up, stay at peak RPM. It will not sound like it's changing gear endlessly.The sound needs to match the changing of the gears, particularly in manual shift mode.2. When setting up manual shift, not only did the bike still auto-shift when I went to a race (I used lorettas), but the settings menu from within the race, doesn't even show the mapped manual shift buttons.3. The AI are still pushovers, way too easy to beat.Imagine playing space invaders and a single shot clears the board. Is that fun? No!

_childDocuments_.review: Had a crash to desktop after an hour and was about to refund. The first hour isn't fun at all. The tutorial is annoying and it takes a while to get into the controls. But after giving it a second chance, the game turned out to be fun. Trails mode, the open maps, is the part where the game shines. The tracks are long and fun to ride on. I have no issues with physics and twin stick controls. I would say it's more arcade like, but fun to bash the tracks.Not everything is great. There are a few issues, of course. NPCs are pulled out of the worst job simulator games. They just stand there, solid as a rock, with no personality. I would have liked a garage or barn, where all of my team is. A place to walk around. But this is far to amitious for this game.The graphics are nice, but not on a top level. The game fights with pop ins sometimes. First Person is a blast and the camera setting I recommend. Customization could be a bit deeper, with more items. The most annoying section is the audio to me. No matter who was responsible for the mix, I hope you guys do overhours. At one point the music began blasting out my stereos, that I was worried about waking up the entire neighbourhood. Then it cuts off the music entirely in the middle of a song, just to continue very qiet. Music off is the only solution. Bike engine sounds cut off on full speed. You have delayed the game. This is not acceptable!So after all, I can recommend it for what it is. A fun motocross racer with great tracks, OK graphics, and OK price. But it needs fixes. If the audio and some minor bugs are fixed, I'd have no problem with it.I know this review is a leap of faith. But despite the audio I have fun playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played almost every MX game in existence (300h in MX Sim included). Do not let the bad reviews get to you, guys! So much negativity here, just chill people. If you want realism, play MX Sim or Bikes. And you’ll never get a Reflex 2, stop crying and just play Reflex instead. Leave actual constructive criticism. The game has its flaws, but I think it’s a good step forward from the bounce-fest All Out was.Pro- track and environmental design is KING!- career mode is great- game feels more heavy and slow, which is good, more grounded- learning curve (it seems that’s where most other reviews fall short, they don’t play long enough and at least try)- sliding is not that big, you just have to get better controlling your bike and let off the throttle lol- first person feels so satisfying to play- terrain deformation is good- it’s meant to be a fun arcade game, and that’s what it deliversCon- yes, customization is pretty lackluster- sounds could be better- physics are sometimes inconsistent- no changing of controls option (there is not even a controller map, which had me press random buttons for manual shifting)- track pop-in is bad sometimes, really weird glitching- the rider does not turn back in the air (gyro would be great, even in real life you get kinda turned back on your own)Tips- bike tuning does a lot for the handling- dual stick is your friend, much more fine-tuned- do not expect to be the best right away, learning by doing- first person is really the way to go, just give it a tryOverall, I think it’s solid and a better foundation for updates than All Out was at the beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: Never in my life have I played a game with more frustrating handling and physics than this. I love a good challenge, but this game just doesn't even hit the mark. The MX bikes feel like they never even touch the ground. You nearly float all over the place it seems. The preloading mechanics don't even work worth a damn. You'll land short on most jumps with a nearly perfect approach and preload while the AI somehow clear everything with ease, sometimes at the same speed as you. The tutorial is long and doesn't even teach you anything. There isn't even a button map in the menu to show you any controls once you get past it. Graphics and world design seem cheap, almost procedural, and yet they were made by the designers themselves. The only way to get other bikes is to pay for the manufacturers packs, when they should've just come with the game because there's a serious lack in other vehicles in the base game. Pulling off a successful turn or jump isn't even rewarding feeling. Just relieving because you don't have to restart the race just yet. There's a tragic lack of life in this game. As a rider myself, this game takes away from the thrill of riding anything off-road. Please do yourself a favor and do not buy this game, even on sale. It's such a waste. Hyped up for nothing for months on YouTuber early access reviews. Thanks for the refund, Steam. Do better, Rainbow Studios. :(

_childDocuments_.review: Life in a nutshell. If you want to have an experience, it is one. There's a warning in the beginning of the game. DO NOT TAKE IT LIGHTLY. This game will give you everything in the warning. Lots of gore, lots of potentially traumatizing scenes that will stick with you, and an overall horrific experience. It is tagged "horror", "dark" and "cute" for a reason. That being said,It is so symbolic, engaging, and overall mesmerizing. I played it in one gaming session (1.5 hrs with breaks) and it is just a phenomenally well made story that relates to life so damn well. Seriously, this is top notch story telling, visuals, sounds, applicable to real life through symbolism and context, trippy as hell (cuz life is trippy amaright), and ♥♥♥♥, I couldn't recommend this more.It is not "senseless gore" if you can look past the visuals and see the bigger picture; the puzzles, the very well thought out scenery throughout the game, the interactions with things you have in the game; the story. The visuals and audio just make it more horrifying in a trippy way.If you have been recommended this by someone and are on the fence about buying it, and don't mind being a little traumatized to maybe see the world differently,  do it. Worst things worse you support an exceptional small game studio that makes awesome stories.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute banger.One of the creepiest, most messed up games I have ever played- part puzzler game, part horror experience.Absolutely not what you would expect from most studios, but absolutely what you would expect from Amanita.Shades of Cuchel, only a whole lot more messed up.Didn't think that was possible?Think again.You are playing in a world of night terrors.They call them nightmares, but these are far more bizarre than "normal" nightmares. Night. Terrors.If you like Chuchel, and aren;t squeamish (lots of blood and cartoonish gore), you will probably like this as well.Full price?Sure- it's one hell of an experience, a 3-4 hour ride through h the darkest parts of human imagination.On sale?Yes. Snap it up.Keep in mind, in case you don;t bother reading game descriptions and developer warnings- this is absolutely not suitable for anyone with seizure disorders set off by flashing bright lights. Because they are a huge part of the game, and there is no way to turn them off.Deaf/HoH players- the audio does set a mood and set atmosphere for hearing players, but since there is no spoken text, and no real sound cues that you have to pay attention to- yes. This would be fine for Deaf and HoH players, not so good for people with certain types of vision issues (it was a tad difficult for me while my Map Dor Fingerprint Dystrophy is flaring, making my eyes very sensitive to bright light).No need to worry about language localizations except for the menu and credits, since there is no voice acting or written words in the game itself. Absolute banger, Amanita.  Feeling angry with myself for not playing it sooner- it's been in my library for quite some time (bought shortly after it first launched). Replay value- you'll know how to get through all of the puzzles and interactions, so yes and no. It is worth replaying just for the creepy factor, if you are into that like I am.

_childDocuments_.review: As cursed as cursed can get. It's an excellent, unique experience worth the small admission price. Psychedelia, surrealism, cuteness, and twisted horror.I chose this game as the first game to play after not properly playing any single-player game for at least eight months, and I couldn't have chosen a better one. This game captures what I love about games in general, and it's the unbounded human creativity in a medium capable of creating unforgettable interactive experiences. This game got so much love put into it, and it's simply an excellent piece of art.Although only the left mouse button is needed to play through this beautiful 2D puzzler, interactivity with the scenes is very rich. It allows for the progressive unfurling of incredibly twisted imagery as you solve straightforward yet brilliant puzzles. You must often wait and watch things unfold on the screen after interacting with something, like in a real dream. The cursor appears again when you know you can interact again. Sometimes the puzzles get challenging and even frustrating with the unskippable repeating actions, and at other times the interactions seem cumbersome and lengthy (edit: this was caused mainly by my 144 Hz monitor, there was a bug in the game that's fixed now), but it all feels seamless because you get captivated with the visuals.There are no texts or voiceovers in-game, with only the protagonist reacting with various sympathetic vocalizations. The game heavily relies on excellent sound design and music, which makes all interactions very entertaining. That's what we are used to in games by the Czech studio Amanita Design. The exciting new aspect here is the horror. Even though the imagery can get seriously creepy, it's all adorable and funny, as you'd expect from a little boy's nightmares populated by many bizarre characters. It's a unique non-conforming experience, and I loved it for that as it felt so fresh.Like in dreams, the story is indeterminate and open to interpretation, which I love about this kind of game. It touches subjects like bullying, traumas, childhood, and of course, nightmares full of toys and overcoming one's fear to get them back. The ending is surprising and makes the game even darker.I've never tried any drug in my life, but I'm sure this could work well as some sort of twisted stoner comedy/horror because it's extraordinarily imaginative.Please note: Happy Game is not a happy game.+ unforgettably detailed art style, characters and interactions, very original sound design and captivating synth/freak-folk music, unique cute horror experience- very short (2 to 3 hours, small replay value), unskippable scenes might annoy you a bit, using only the left mouse button can prove laborious and monotonousI've unlocked all achievements! 11 of 11 (ez 100%): Překlad recenze do češtiny:

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this new game made by Amanita, and I just got curious about it, especially knowing it was a short experience.Even though I recommend the game, it's more because I think that overall it's good and creative, but to be honest I enjoyed it less than expected.Starting with the good, the atmosphere is on point, u have these creepy vibes mixed with a warm/calm feeling, the aesthetic is creepy as u would expect, and the sound design is great.Overall it creates a nice fantasy and the situations you will have to resolve are many and different, even though following a specific theme based on the current "stage", that makes it feel more cohesive and immersive.The solutions to the "puzzles" are easy but "funny" to perform, and I think it was good that the game didn't take a hard path with them, it would have ruined the pace.That said, my biggest issue is that it is too abstract and it tries too hard to be weird. Starting with the title, it feels like they wanted to look cool, and then u start the game and it says "happy game is not a happy game", ugh, kinda edgy and cringe, I was not expecting it from the same studio that made Machinarium.And this is a feeling I have about the game too, it tries maybe too much to be creepy just for the sake of it, and even though is the point of the game, it put me off a bit.I've to say that this is also because, coming from Machinarium, I expected more while this feels like a bit banal. Not that it isn't original but it feels like the typical "look at me I'm weird" game.I also think that the first part was better done, where the first "stages" gave me a better sense of progression and involvement, while the last ones felt like it was just a lot of things put together.The second half is also less interesting puzzle side, where basically u have to do very very little to progress.I'm really interested in reading some thoughts on the meaning of this, it's not easy to grasp, and even though I have some idea, I don't feel like getting it as I would like it.Maybe is something about faking happiness? Or like child abuse, where parents show a happy face while underneath they are corrupted? I'll see about that.To conclude, Happy Game is a nice and fun attempt at doing something provocative, even though it ends up trying too hard, but for a game that it's just 2 hours long, I won't really think about playing it or not too much if you are into these kinds of experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros and cons are down below) If this comment is going to be useful - drop a like so it could be useful to other people as well)Check out the gameplay (1st dream) here:Advantages:1. The art style is the most obvious advantage. It's unique, it's macabre, it's spooky and it's pure nightmare fuel. An unforgettable experience.2. It's easier comparing to other Amanita games which is an advantage here as it's not a puzzle game, it's an experience. You won't get frustrated trying to solve puzzles, you'll naturally progress enjoying the visuals and having fun.3. The level design is pretty interesting and thematic, leaves room for you to interpret the game.Disadvantages:1. Even though, you have freedom to interpret the game, it still feels like there's no story or conclusion. I really didn't see the point in progression other than experiencing new visuals that are, undoubtedly, gorgeous.2. It's very slow. I would personally enjoy the game a lot more if it didn't require you to repeat the same slow action from 3 to 8 times in a row. That feels like dragging out something that wasn't meant to be so long in the first place.3. Constantly flashing red screen is a big no for photosensitive people! Be careful if you are.Overall:I would rate the game 7.3 happy faces / 10 because it's not really a game. It's an experience that's gorgeous but slow and feels more like walking simulator. _childDocuments_.review: is NOT AT ALL a happy game. It's dark, macabre, gory and it's pretty much the antithesis of what we're used to when it comes to Amanita games. Yet it's still an Amanita game, and it has mainly the same style and design, and it's undoubtedly a piece of art like any of their other titles. In  you follow the adventures of a little boy trapped in his nightmares. Hideous monsters will hunt you down, creepy toys will surround you and the screens will overall  be covered in blood spots and other gooey substances. Unlike other titles from Amanita, the gameplay focuses less on solving puzzles / finding out the way all the contraptions work (which by the way, now take shape as scary, unfriendly creatures) and shifts towards experiencing the game as an artistic creation, in a more cinematic way. Solving the puzzles will require you to summon your dark side, since you'll be pulling heads, eyes, tongues and any other tuggable parts from all sorts of creatures. For those easily disturbed a warning is in order, since some of these puzzles involve not only putting together decapitated toys, or on the contrary, tearing them apart in half, but also beheading bunny-like beasts with a bladed guillotine or throwing them into the meat grinder. There are also a few scenes with flashing lights that could be bothersome for more sensitive players and the game warns in the beginning about these two aspects.Although  is grotesque, it all sounds worse than it is. The art style and overall design is meant to convey a horror-like experience, but not a frightening one. There’s some sort of innocence in every scene, perhaps springing from the fact that you - as the little boy - are meant to approach these puzzles in a more or less candid way. Even if you’ll be tasked to do some ghastly things, the game is specifically designed so that you’ll end it with a clear conscience and a clean heart.There are no jump scares and the content isn’t deranging enough to give you nightmares, but it will clearly leave a mark on you simply because playing  is a truly unique experience, full of some bizarre charm - one definitely worth your time, but considering its shortness (1-2h) perhaps not entirely the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: You wont find anything over the top here, no high scores, no complicated or overly terrifying material. What you will find however is a message, some meaning, something personal, and for some of us, a mirror into our deeper selves.This is not your average game, Its short, simple, yet beautifully tragic. For me personally, it doesn't seem like a horror game at all, but an artistic expression. For real art comforts the disturbed, and disturbs the comfortable, this is one of those games.Once you have completed the game, here is where you'll find the message in it.Its not a happy gameIf you do plan to acquire this artistic piece of innocent suffering, I would implore you to buy the art book along with the game as it adds more meaning into what we otherwise might not notice.Happy Travels

_childDocuments_.review: Flashing lights. If you're sensitive to flashing lights skip this game.Happy Game is not a typical cutesy Amanita title, it's a dark and creepy horror game. I don't like this genre since it does nothing for me and HG was no different. It's still a good game for what it is and you can feel Amanita quality while playing, but I kept thinking that the developers must have switched their usual recreational happy drugs to something heavier. The story, visuals, audio are all the highest quality as always, but it's one of the shorter games and gameplay is more like in Chuchel rather than Machinarium. I can't see myself ever coming back to Happy Game, but I'm sure it will find an audience. I'm still waiting for a proper sequel to Samorost and/or Machinarium.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually found this game to be a bit tedious. It's nicely polished and clearly love has gone into it, and I wouldn't say it's a bad game by any stretch. But to me, the gameplay wasn't particularly engaging, a lot of the gore and weirdness seemed to just be there for the sake of it, and there wasn't much of a sense of an overarching plot, or tangible stakes to get me to care about what was happening on screen. The aesthetic of the game is well-realized, but it falls a bit awkwardly in the middle of a horror-lite game, a fairly played out "cutesy gore" vibe, and something like Salad Fingers, from the old days of flash animations.For some people, this will be right up their alley. For me, it didn't quite resonate. I'd say give the trailer a quick peek, and unless you're immediately hooked on the visuals, maybe pass on this one

_childDocuments_.review: You play a boy who goes to bed and stumbles from one nightmare to the next. Most of the time there are positive things like bunnies, smileys, teddies, clowns hearts, etc. That are corrupted or become collateral damage themselves. Every smile in the game seems artificial and tortured. The very red-heavy color scheme and art style contribute perfectly to the strange, dark and gory experience. The whole game, including the controls, is kept very minimalistic, but that fits the content. Nightmares don't explain themselves either, they just get straight to the point. The gameplay and puzzles are, on the whole, simple, intuitive and macabre. Or who hasn't cut a bunny in half with a guillotine? Or actually doubled. Complicated thing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a happy and lovely game. So nice that after completing it you will put a smile on your face and want to commit homicide (especially on bunnies, just in case). Mesmerizingly terrifying visual. Sheer nightmare fuel, but in a charming and nice way. It's psychedelic, but not frightening like your usual horror game. "Happy game" feels like a drug trip, everything's colourful and beautiful and joyfully kills each other. Awesome soundtrack, it really adds a lot to the atmosphere of unrestrained violence. DVA clearly knows how to make proper music. I used as much as one brain cell to solve puzzles, but sometimes this lonely brain cell became completely dumb for an entire minute and made funny dial-up noises while trying to connect to other brain cells (but never succeeded). However, this game failed to scare me. For me that's a story about finding peace and sparks of happiness despite all obstacles and suffering. A story that was told in a very freaky way.The description says it all. Flashing lights and cartoon violence can be disturbing if you're too sensitive. So be aware.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to say this is a bad game - the art style is fun, the music is delightful, and the concept is interesting - but it's not the game for me. I got bored with the puzzles multiple times because it seems like there are several 'puzzles' that aren't so much "figure out the solution through problem solving" as they are "figure out which piece you can wiggle and then just whip your mouse around wildly until SOMETHING finally happens".  Some of the puzzles were genuinely fun to solve! I particularly enjoyed the bit in the second nightmare with the hearts, because there were so many fun ways to interact with the environment and I actually got to do some trial and error there. That being said, a vast majority of the puzzles were repetitive or frustrating, and I wound up zoning out a lot because I was being forced to redo puzzles I'd already solved with no satisfaction or reward.The art style was fun, and I liked the cartoonish gore, but as the game stretched on I kept waiting and waiting for any sort of storyline that would add weight to the gore. When I realized there wasn't really a plot and everything was just kind of weird for weirdness's sake, it got to feeling cheesy and silly instead of disturbing. By the time the end of the third nightmare rolled around, I'd lost all curiosity and just sort of wanted to get the game over with.The lack of any sort of substantial storyline also meant that the frequent long, unplayable scenes I was forced to watch were incredibly boring and uninteresting. They weren't so bad at the beginning, but the further you get into the game the more of these scenes there are, and in a game with no plot, back-to-back cutscenes with walking simulator filler in between is dull. Again, it's not a bad game. If you're into weird, psychedelic imagery for the sake of just being weird, or you're more interested in the admittedly unusual and fun gameplay mechanics, this game might be for you. For me, though, it felt a little like waiting for someone to get to the point of their story and instead getting two hours of tangents followed by an extremely lackluster ending. I know it sounds weird to say, but I honestly think this game would benefit a great deal from being shorter. A lot of content felt incredibly padded to me. Even just increasing the walking speed would have improved the pacing of the game substantially.I don't regret giving this game a try and I don't plan to refund it. It's clear the people who worked on this game were having fun with the simple mechanics of point-and-click, and there were some moments that actually engaged my interest. Overall, though, my main impression of this game was that I left it even more bored than I had been beforehand, which is impressive because I was bored enough to buy and play a random game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was as if Isaac had lost his mind, began to smile continuously and hug his mother's leg instead of throwing flies and tears at her. Amanita Design studio, previously known for its incredibly soulful and emotional projects, is releasing a new game, which by its name alone promises a lot, a lot of happiness to the player. And for them this game is a serious way out of their comfort zone. So serious that at first it is even perceived shocking, gradually revealing the original idea of the developers. Immersion in children's nightmares cannot be painless, you need to be mentally prepared for this and in addition to the very essence of children's fears, the game also actively uses more obvious tools to put pressure on the player. The game does not hesitate to choke you with sparkling sound, convulsively flashing light reflections, cartoon violence and nervous tension. It all works very effectively. Using a huge number of tools, the game, however, does not turn into an anthology of frightening sketches, but maintains integrity and harmony.The puzzles in the game are quite simple, but at the same time very funny (as ironic as it may sound). The timing is very tightly packed, which is quite usual for the games of this studio, so the game can be completely completed in 3-4 busy hours. The game is so eccentrically tearing its visuals apart that it is even difficult to form an unambiguous opinion about it, it is not for nothing that everything here blows with experimentation and surrealism. And the same applies to the plot, which at first glance is quite easy to read, but at the same time gives a wide scope for interpretations and fan theories."Happy Game" sets up experiments, expanding the scope of consciousness and constantly pulling the strings of the player's nerves. Emotionally, this is the most difficult and pressing project of Amanita Design studio, clearly demonstrating that these guys are capable of anything. Smile and be happy!

_childDocuments_.review: is a short  with puzzle elements. You follow the story of a child who falls asleep to a horrible nightmare. You, as the player, control him and the environment around him in an attempt to make him "happy" again.The environments and the creatures you encounter change per "section". However, there seems to be an omnipotent creature watching over the child. This being has the form of a giant smiley face and it follows the boy around. It seems to control the environment or it at least has an effect on it. The game is essentially divided into . In each section you try to regain something that was taken from the child in it's past. Each area has a different feel to it. The different parts of the game also play themselves differently. Don't be shy to try to walk a different path than what the game is leading you to by the way. Sometimes you can find secrets and achievements like that.The first section has the child mainly be in a dark area with no light in the background. This area is mostly controlled by colours like black, white and red. You will essentially not see any other colours in this first part of the game, only very rarely at most. The different puzzles here are divided from each other pretty clearly. The puzzles are all pretty fun in this section I'd say.The second section is by far the best part of the game. Not only is it very colourful, but there also is an interesting mechanic where if you walk into a direction for a while you will basically loop around the map once and you'll be back at your starting point. The puzzles in this section have multiple facets and require numerous steps to be completed. They were all very thought out and a ton of fun to solve. The last segment of the second section dials back on the more open puzzles and rather reminds you of the puzzles of the first section again.The third part is a bit dull and short when compared to the first two sections. Here the colours are washed out and muddy and the area generally looks pretty dead. There aren't that many puzzles here and they are basically shorter than the ones from the first two sections as well. There isn't really anything memorable about this section apart from the ending of this area, which is also the finale for the game.Some thoughts about the ending and the story in general: The art-style is one that I personally don't like very much but it does fit pretty well to this game, since it mostly seems like it is a drawn by a child. Sometimes there are some very detailed drawings in here as well though. One thing that might be worth mentioning is that the game sometimes blasts you with saturated strong colours (mostly red). Sometimes there is some sort of flashing effect as well so people with epilepsy should probably stay away from this game if they are prone to getting seizures. This game features really terrifying creatures and environments which have been done so well by the artists for this game. This game doesn't rely on jumpscares but rather unsettling imagery.There isn't much music itself in this game, but there's one melody which repeats throughout the game a few times (It's also in the trailer for this game). The melody sounds very good in my opinion and it fits to the game in a sense that it is basically playing as a distraction from all the bad stuff that is going on in the background of the game which the child ignores.The sound-design of this game in general is great though. The noises just fit perfectly every time and they build up the creepy atmosphere pretty well.The price of this game is a bit high for it's ~2 hour gameplay. So if you want to test out this game I would recommend waiting until it goes on sale. Some other thing I saw being mentioned in the reviews for this game is to just refund it when you're done with it since it only has 2 hours of gameplay. I wouldn't recommend that because you would really be doing the developers dirty then. If you played the whole game and finished it in under 2 hours I would say that you just keep it in your library even if you could refund it. This way you can support the developers. Overall I give this game a score of 8.5/10. The only negative things that come to mind are that the controls feel a bit sluggish and delayed sometimes, especially when you are moving the child. The other negative thing is that the third section of the game really felt dull in comparison to the other two parts which ultimately dragged the game down for me. In the end I just got bored, luckily the third area of the game was relatively short though.Everything else was really good though! So if you wanna check out a unique horror game you can try this one out.With regardsM U R D E R E R (aka Lord Dominator / kennymccormick20)

_childDocuments_.review: I personally did not really enjoy this game. While the art and music is competently made, the controls feel very sluggish and you stop caring about the game before the halfway mark in what is already a very short game.Even though this is a point and click game, getting anything done is painfully slow to the point where my hand was getting tired. You will hold and drag  for most of this 2-hour experience, often doing the same puzzle multiple times in a row. You may figure out that you need to feed someone a carrot. Slowly pull it out of the ground, give it to your character, drag your character to where he needs to stand, then drag your carrot to the bunny. Great, now do that 2 more times, then walk for a while, and feed some new ones.This is how most puzzles work, do the thing, many times in a row. In one part, you have to do the thing you need to do over 10 times in a row after you already figured it out. It is not fun. Dragging items in this game is also so painful to do. You drag and drag and drag only for minimal changes to happen. Some puzzles had me drag an item for so long I thought it was bugged. I kept dragging the mouse, but the thing I needed to move only moved a centimetre at the time. You should not have to drag your mouse multiple times your screen length to open something up, especially when you have to do it many times in a row.The reason anyone would want to play this game, has to be for the art. The disturbing art is well made, and is very interesting. While it was fairly obvious from the start this would be an edgy game, I think it lost its flavor about halfway through. Yes, everything will flash red, and you will lose your toy or whatever. It's cool the first 10 times, but after that it gets kinda boring. It rarely changed things up, just going for edgy after edgy, but when everything is edgy, nothing is. You may think the game has some fun edgy tricks at first, but you're only going to get impressed so many times before it gets old. The game should have changed up the pace more, like it does during the  segment. Idk man, overall the gameplay is lame, the art is cool, but the execution is not the best. It tried to make itself seem more disturbing by spam-flashing red every time you do anything. I don't struggle with epilepsy or anything like that, but it got annoying. I rate this game Chewing gum you've already been chewing for a while / 10That said, I did finish this game, I can see that the devs have put in effort, so I will not be refunding it. There is talent here, hoping for something more genuinely disturbing next time.

_childDocuments_.review: Happy Game is a point-and-click horror game made by the mad lads at Amanita Design.  Like many of their previous games, it is a colourful, highly imaginative game with unusual puzzles that thankfully usually just require some out-of-the-box trial and error to explore what you're expected to do to progress to the next screen.  Unlike any of their previous P and C games, this one is freaky as heck, consisting of a series of three long, grotesque nightmare levels where a terrified young tot tries to get back his ball, stuffed toy, and pet dog respectively, with each level and indeed the entire enterprise being orchestrated by a malevolent smiley-faced demonic entity.  It is dark and bloody and incredibly unnerving.  And it's also a pleasure to play because of the design chops of everyone involved.Positives:-Gameplay-  As I said above, while the subject matter is grotesque and gruesome (sometimes comically, usually disturbingly), the game itself is a pleasure to play through (even as you find yourself unnerved and chilled) because of the simplicity of the controls.  No galaxy brain solution, inventory based conundrums here, just (mostly) intuitive puzzle design.-Music- Creepy.....like clown at midnight dancing under a streetlight juggling knives creepy.....nuff said.Meh:  Some of the puzzles took me a while to figure out, but that's mostly because I'm not as swift in the brains department as I used to be.  I may have gotten close to being frustrated, but I never actually reached that point, and I never had to consult a walkthrough.  Oh, and as another minor kvetch, some of the achievements were a little obscure, but since you can chapter select and there's good achievement guides out there, snatching up any of the wild and weird ones should prove no difficulty.Negatives:  None.  Highly recommended (but not if you don't like disturbing imagery and demonic/monstrous threats towards adorable cartoon tots.....then stay VERY far away).

_childDocuments_.review: If you're an Amanita fan, this is a must buy. As usual, they deliver excellently crafted animation in an interactive format. My overall experience of Happy Game was a little mixed. Amanita have departed from their signature cosy aesthetics in favour of a strongly early 2000s influenced cartoon horror makeover - taking noticeable influence from David Firth (Salad Fingers), Pon & Zi, Jhonen Vasquez, etc. I grew up loving that stuff so I expected to like this more, but unfortunately I had a strong sense that Amanita's new coat of paint was simply that - a style for style's sake with no meaningful concept behind it. It feels almost like playable fan art. It's not a bad game by any means, it just didn't feel fresh or exciting to me as someone already familiar with its influences. Still 100% worth a play if you like an atmospheric, interactive art experience - however I would recommend waiting til it goes on sale if you're not certain about buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that "Happy Game" is not for the faint of heart. Amanita Design, known for their charming and whimsical adventures, takes a sharp turn into the realm of horror with this one. If you're looking for a bright and cheerful experience like their previous titles, this ain't it. But if you're like me and enjoy a good psychedelic horror with a touch of madness, then buckle up!The game revolves around a young boy's nightmares, haunted by creepy-cute monsters that are anything but cuddly. The art style is spot-on, delivering stunningly creepy visuals that play with your emotions. From terrifying bunnies to toys with bloody innards, the imagery is both disturbing and captivating.As you progress through the game, you'll find yourself dragging and swiping with your mouse, interacting with the nightmares in a tactile way. I The world reacts brilliantly to your actions, adding a sense of life to the nightmare landscapes. It's strangely satisfying to tear those monsters apart limb by limb.The puzzles in "Happy Game" lean towards the easier side, so you won't likely get stuck for long. The gameplay revolves more around finding the right triggers and interacting with toys and objects. The second act was particularly unique and challenging, featuring small spherical worlds where you must set traps to fend off a giant bunny. However, I felt the third act had a weak start and couldn't quite match the horror and intensity of the first two.In terms of length, "Happy Game" can be completed in about 1 to 2.5 hours, so if you prefer longer games, you might want to wait for a sale.As a fan of psychedelic horror, I found "Happy Game" to be a real delight. The unsettling visuals and eerie soundscape create an immersive nightmare experience. It's my favorite Amanita Design game since "Machinarium." But, fair warning, if you were hoping for challenging point-and-click puzzles, this might not be the game for you.In the end, if you enjoy diving into the dark and disturbing aspects of childhood fears and the fragility of innocence, "Happy Game" will not disappoint. It's a memorable and unnerving journey, but proceed with caution, as it's definitely not a happy game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what to say after beating this game. It was quite a ride, nothing made sense, there were parts that were terrifying and yet it still made me laugh. If you like games that make you say "What the hell was the developer thinking" or "What was the developer taking", then this game is for you. I enjoy weird games with crazy art styles, and this game checked all the boxes. The ending did feel a little drawn out and it felt like they were running out of weird ideas to shock you with. Other than that, I would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita Design has better games in their catalog that are more interactive, have a longer playtime and don't rely on the "I'm 14 and this is edgy" shock value, which to be fair is probably the main selling point of this game, but all of that falls flat if it's really just for the shock value and not really a story. Maybe there is a story or deeper meaning, but all I could figure out was childhood "trauma" and how it felt for the child versus how it looked in real life. But I'm open to suggestions as to what the story and images mean. Also the game is very short, within 2 hours you can get 100% if you didn't miss any achievements on your first playthrough.But let's not dwell on the negative aspects and say something positive! Something I enjoyed and kind of expected was the creativity! Although I do not really like the "edgy" stuff without any real meaning, they went all out and made some pretty sickly designed monsters and scenery! The overall "puzzles" are simple but fun and some of the random stuff this game throws at you was actually unexpected! The game allows you to replay all parts of the game after finishing it, giving you easy access to scenes where you might have missed an achievement.The game is divided into 3 chapters. The second one was my favorite because of the tonal clash of the colorful scenery and the actual gruesome stuff that happens during it. Chapter 1, despite being an introduction, felt the weakest, and that's really not a good thing, as it should draw people in to play more of your game.Also, please... PLEASE don't hide an achievement behind a terrible physics system!6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I suppose it was inevitable that Amanita Design would make a terrible game eventually. But I was hoping it wouldn’t happen.Happy Game is the newest point and click adventure game from the Czech based Amanita Design, known for their inventive visuals, wonderful soundtracks and playful gameplay. They’re also usually known for cute and wholesome, if weird, titles and even the odd exceptions like Pilgrims from 2 years ago have a more mischievous rather than mean darkness to them. Happy Game is meant to be their first outright mean and twisted horror focused adventure. But in reality it’s more of a trite edgy and teenage angsty one, lacking any creativity usual for their titles.The demo for the game set the tone, as it felt like a really crappy creepypasta made by a 13 year old turned into a Newgrounds flash game, with edgy visuals, flashing and rainbow patterns that most game designers avoid as even those not seriously affected by epilepsy get nauseated or at least annoyed by those. Yet, the trailer promised more variety and I expected that the opening would just be intentionally misleading and the game would become really inventive, sinister and uncomfortable in a good horror sense. I thought we’d get CHUCHEL, but horror instead of a comedy.No, it remains as basic, obnoxious with its visuals (and even occasional tinnitus sounds) and uninteresting throughout its mercifully short length. DVA did deliver a few nice tunes here and there, so I’m glad at least that’s a positive. But otherwise, the game is just not fun mechanically with some of the sequences taking forever to finish. And has no interesting ideas, unless you’re really into the lowest common denominator creepy things. If you want creepy and unsettling adventures with a young boy, replay LIMBO instead. Or heck, Little Nightmares has more creativity than this game, even though it's not extremely inventive itself. And if you want a good Amanita Design game, pick any but this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the artwork and design of the game. They succeeded in making a very disturbing game, the player definitely feels like being in a nightmare as they traverse through haunted levels trying to navigate and put an end to this madness. It has a great atmosphere , but for me this is where the good things about the game end. You can finish this game with all of its achievements in about 2 hours. Roughly half of this time is spent in cut-scenes, and the other half is actual game-play. The puzzles are simple, most of the time you are just dragging your character or other things around. Oftentimes you just have to test random stuff to understand what you have to do , but it ends up being the same thing. You just have to pull or rotate something until you get it right. There is variety in the different areas you visit and all the wacky and cursed characters you encounter, but there is no variety in your game-play which quickly becomes tedious. I am a fan of the studio so I wanted to play this game, but other than the artwork, I don't find anything else interesting about it. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone else, besides fans of Amanita that want to play all their games.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Unique, surreal world. A combination of crazy, colorful situations with trippy design. Simple, yet artistic 2d graphics.- Cool audio design with weird, funny sounds. Characters' voices are hilarious.- Well designed, peculiar creatures and an adorable, cartoonish protagonist with some smooth and pleasant animations.- Despite being a point a click it has not a classical playstyle. You're not collecting items or solving traditional puzzles. Your main goal in each screen is to find what's interactive and how it works, which can offer some interesting, unexpected outcomes. Also, it's nice that you don't just click but you use the cursor in multiple ways, movements or speeds. All these make the gameplay interesting, but have some issues too.- It's both creepy and relaxing, both evil and innocent. All this splatter and deaths along with the protagonist's happiness create a unique atmosphere.- Good sense of humor. There are some hilarious situations.- Nice, calm music.The bad- Everything that makes the gameplay interesting and funny also lucks logic and sometimes can get annoying. Clicking all over the screen, trying to drug things or do actions with different cursor speed until something works can be silly. A lot of times it doesn't even bother of giving you any clues to avoid it.- Shallow story. You just do things because they're there and you know it's a game, without having to fulfil a specific purpose. It's like they throw in there random ideas that lack coherence.- Too short. Usually, I don't judge the length of a game, but it ends abruptly leaving you a feeling that you played something unfinished.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's environment has an odd mix of nostalgic childhood joy and bloody, morbid terror. There are no jumpscares, only unsettling visuals and noises. There's lots of blood and gore and various images of decapitation and dismemberment. It left me feeling deeply disturbed. Achievements aren't too hard to get, and you can always go to the level select screen to teleport wherever you need to go if you miss something. However, there isn't much replay value. Some puzzles can be confusing given how abstract the dream logic is. I wish there was some kind of hint system. There's a bit of a story going on, but everything is so abstract and dreamlike it's hard to tell exactly what the lore is here, even after seeing the ending. I would recommend this game to horror fans who are looking for something scary that doesn't fall into traditional horror tropes. Definitely not for sensitive people or children!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has an affinity for weird, unusual games, I really wanted to like this one. After a few levels, I started to feel like the game was going nowhere, mainly because there was no story told, and there was not any reason for the things that were shown. I didn't know why I should care about the main character and what was happening to them, and the drag-and-click mechanic got boring after a few levels.That being said, I was expecting something more from this game and it left me quite unsatisfied, so I don't think I would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).Happy game is a short and casual 2D point and click game with simple puzzles that rely mostly on placing or activating objects or characters in the right order, and the latest release by Amanita Design. When compared to older games from the same company it seems far easier and simplified, and aesthetically and conceptually, it seems like a game from an alternate reality where the same developers decided to use their talents for evil, and created this monstrosity.The story is about a small child and their nightmares that usually involve something they loved and lost, and it’s divided into 3 chapters. As you solve each scene, the story progresses, and this progression and the story moments blend seamlessly with the gameplay.When compared to the older game we see the major differences in the art style and overall look of the game. It uses the same hand drawn illustrations with the same level of creativity and quality, but with a more vivid and impactful color palette with some chapters featuring a lot of red and black, with very disturbing and grotesque characters and scenes, filled with lots of violence, cannibalism and dismemberment, and the still cute and fluffy look of the characters don’t seem enough to tone down.The animation and movements of some NPCs are also manic and weird, often with a lot of flashing lights, colors and images, to really exacerbate the unsettling and dark ambiance.   The music and sound effects change between calming and relaxing to unnerving and frightening as something bad happens, with lots of weird eerie noises coming from the creatures you find. Overall the music and sounds work very well together with the art style of the game.Regarding gameplay, as I mentioned, the puzzles are far simpler than previous games and in most scenes there are just a few interactable elements and the solution is often the easiest, most logical option. The very few times I got stuck, I was overthinking the problem.  11 Achievements. 2,5 hours Easy. Easy. There are no missables since you can pick past scenes right at the exact moment where you need to perform a specific task. Happy game is a short casual P&C game that has the same art and music quality of past Amanita Design games, but with much darker and grotesque themes that are not for everyone and definitely not for children. It’s creative and original but probably just for a very niche audience. Currently being sold on a bundle at Fanatical.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew this game was going to be weird, but boy did I underestimate exactly how weird. If you ever watched Happy Tree Friends and liked it, you'll definitely dig this game. Pros: - Pretty simple point and click. Some puzzles make you have to think a bit outside the box, but nothing is overly complex.- Great graphics. Super creepy and Tim Burton kind of vibes. - Story is crazy, but great. This is one of those games where you just don't want to stop playing when you finish a section because you NEED to see what happens next. Really made me get attached to the main character and want all the best things for him.- 10/10 music/audio. So happy I got the bundle with the soundtrack!Cons:- No in-game volume settings. The game is pretty loud, and while you can manually adjust via volume mixer, as a streamer it's better/easier to have in-game options to adjust this on the fly as needed.- No in-game settings to switch between windowed/windowed fullscreen/fullscreen. When playing, my mouse kept going off the screen, causing me to click on things on my other monitors. This resulted in me accidentally banning a viewer of my stream (oops) when trying to interact with something on the far right of the screen, and also caused me to encounter a game breaking bug when accidentally clicking off the screen at the same time as a progression scene. (luckily I could just restart that section)Overall I really enjoyed this game. While I'd hate to put the poor kid through more trauma, I really really enjoy the craziness of his dreams and would love to see the addition of some DLC with more nightmares at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me worried about Amanita Design. Happy Game has the basic single-screen puzzles of Amanita’s kid-friendly iPad game, Chuchel, crossed with the 'visual subtly' of a Sonic horror fan game. The game isn’t scary or really even that creepy, just weird and off-putting. The overall experience is more akin to being an inattentive parent flipping through their emotionally distressed child's sketchbook. You’re less concerned about the imagery and more so about the one expressing themself through desperate and contrived depictions of ‘horror’. There’s little to no build-up or clever escalation, only a tireless stream of smeared faces and severed limbs. Flashing lights aren’t terrifying, they just give me a headache. What’s there to be afraid of when there are no gameplay stakes, the story has no meaningful structure, and every problem is solved by a click and a drag? I’m not sure what prompted Amanita and all their talent to venture into the world of creepypasta, but I hope they’re all doing okay.

_childDocuments_.review: One of Amanitas worst. The puzzle mechanics are tired, the sound design is annoying (apart from the trailer song) and the visuals aren't really anything to call home about. You could argue Happy Game is a horror side scroller instead but when you compare it to something like LIMBO, INSIDE, or Little Nightmares... not even close. The world moved past meandering Flash games a long time ago. It's time for Amanita to do the same.

_childDocuments_.review: It might be a me-problem, but the entirety of this game fell flat for me. From the point of view as point-and-click-adventure it got rather boring and tedious extremely quickly, and the true horror was dragging the little whiny nitwit around while thinking "Are we there yet? Are we there yet?" on a loop.From a visual standpoint the game is nifty... for five minutes. The "psychidelic nightmare" theme gets old extremely quickly and after two scenes/levels it boils down to the following: Something's head is going to come off and/or somewhere turns out a bleeding smile and/or something's limbs are going to stretch to unreasonable length.The soundtrack... was. There was a soundtrack for sure. I didn't hate it (unlike in the previous games which DVA provided the OST to, where it got on my nerves extremely quickly), but it was one of the most unmemorable experiences of game soundtracks for me.If the game resorted to jumpscares, I would have at least felt something. After finishing the game to 100 %, there were only two moments where I got at least shocked for the moment, which were the hands coming out of the ground for the first time, and running into one of the deerpeople who appeared out of blue.That is not to say the entire game was bad. The changing Happy Wall I actually liked, and I had great fun building stone cairns (though it happened several times that the stones got stuck in each other and that was rather annoying). However, I am not going to recommend a supposedly horror game just because you can walk into a wall repeatedly and put stones on top of each other.
_childDocuments_.name: Happy Game

_childDocuments_.review: You most likely will see this review with a big red "Product refunded" on top, so let me preface this review by saying that Happy Game  indeed a very good game, but the thing is, there's so little of it. Maybe I'm spoiled, but I expected a bit more out of it. Happy Game just ended so very soon and just so abruptly, like, you finish the 3rd level, it plays a little cutscene and just... ends. I don't really feel my purchase was justified, so I will be refunding it. And it pains me to do so because I like supporting independant devs, but here I just dont know.That being said though, you  play this game. Pick it up on a sale or something. The art is beautifully freaky, the puzzles are pretty nice and there's a message to think about at the end. Just don't expect a very long cinematic whatever-the-hell, Happy Game's short. Sorry Amanita Design.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly did not enjoy this game. After many Amanita Design games I've played, I walked into this expecting to solve some nice puzzles, think hard and enjoy the graphics. I don't feel like any of those things happened for me.At times it almost felt like I'm just here to click the mouse a few times so that the story can continue, it didn't really feel like I'm the one in charge of what's going to happen. The puzzles were way easier then I expected and many times it felt like I just have to figure one thing and then repeat it again and again. The game is all done in just 2 hours, most of which you spend just dragging your character to move forward, with obviously no replayability, so that's also a shame. I expected more of this game tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: + Unique+ Grotesque+ Gorgeous Art+ Fun Puzzle+ Haunting Themes- Some puzzles aren't very clear and have simple solution- One particular input is a little too pickyPoint and click gameplay that never really gets uncomfortable. All of the movement and puzzles make sense and come pretty naturally.The soundtrack can be cute and then unnerving. And then cutely unnerving. A world in a child's dream. It tosses between delusions of grandeur through the lens of a naive child and the horrors of reality. Bright and haunting. Rich and bloody.Artistry that is very unique to the gaming world. Beautiful and rich colors in one scene and then stark contrasts in another one. This game was one of my favorites to play this year. It is almost in masterpiece status for me. _childDocuments_.review: Happy Game is a strange and unusual game that seems to be an odd mix of visually "scary" images and puzzles. I don't find the gameplay or visuals to be exciting or scary. The puzzles are pretty bland and mostly involve you walking/pulling/clicking around a bit. Audio and music start off semi-enjoyable but become old quickly. The gameplay is moving your character left or right and clicking on various items throughout the game. The story appears to be of a boy who falls asleep and has nightmares. Otherwise, I'm not even sure a story serves any real purpose and would have been just the same without any. It's a really short experience around 1.5 hours. I have some more time due to going back for achievements since it's very easy and quick to do.I found I was bored rather fast, around 20-30 minutes into it, and wanted to rush to the end. I'm not sure who the target audience might be for Happy Game, it seems like a mix of edgy disturbing material you would find teens from the '90s were into. If you remember Stick Death I can see some of that in this game as well. Overall I do not recommend, save the money and the 1-2 hours to go do something else. I got this game on sale and still feel it was overpriced for the experience it offered.

The puzzles are basic & the drag mechanic is so broken & clanky that I was stuck with multiple times at the beginning just because it wouldn't grab something when I tried the first time. I mean the grab & drag mechanic is really bad, needs to be sped up as well. The few puzzles you run into while traversing this very short game are boring. The only cool part was seeing the creepy stuff...but this was not fun to play. I was too annoyed at the grab mechanic to enjoy any aspect of the game. Art style is enjoyable & the atmosphere of some of the settings are interesting. Interesting characters, boring game though. Not worth the price, games too short.
