_childDocuments_.review: An artsy game with very little art or game present.  Gameplay primarily involves walking slowly and spamming mouse clicks to throw paint around to either 1) see where you're even going or 2) force puzzle solutions to do what you want.  There's intentionally very little artstyle present in the game because most of the game is designed around being eye-searing white, and that combined with the lack of FoV settings gave me actual nausea.  Not worth $15, especially for a game that's under 2 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: You are Monroe Finch, its probably not spoiling it but you play as a young boy, exploring a kingdom created by a young prince, with a paintball gun. Simple yet innovative puzzles abound in this game which tells a story of love, laziness, fear and loss. It kept reminding me of this 70's children's toon  .You walk about in a scene where you have to throw black balls of paint in order to uncover the obstacles and trigger machines, and as the balls change colour and effect, also trigger machines and plants that move. It's a bit parkour at times, but actually not hard at all.Eventually the world goes black, and the black balls of paint, really have no effect. You (or rather the young Monroe) must fight for your life to escape many terrors as you traverse an immense maze of a city. Oh, and did I mention, all the while you are following an incompletely-drawn swan who helps you, just a little. Sometimes there are imperceptible wind chimes that guide me, almost as in a dream, but this is no dream for Monroe.Immensely satisfying game, puzzle learning curve development is perfect, difficulty and scale are too. If you enjoyed Before Your Eyes, you will love this title. To find similar titles check out one of my lists here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this expecting the same quality of quirky and immersive story telling that I got from What Remains of Edith Finch. What I got instead was a clicking simulator. The gameplay is not married well to the story. The unique mechanics are either used once in passing and then forgotten, or stretched to its utmost to the point of exhaustion.Buy this game if you enjoy watching plants grow, because that is what I spent half of the game time doing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals and audio are great. Gameplay is unironically walking simulator. If the walking speed was doubled or you were given a run button it would maybe be a very slight recommendation. But the walking speed is so damn slow I literally didn't even want to explore. I would see a collectible just across the room in plain sight and literally think "nope too far away, not worth it"Also, the story isn't particularly compelling and the "puzzles" are trivial.Felt like I had enough after about 15 minutes, only played another 30 minutes to see if it would change in any significant way, and it didn't. Full playthrough based on other reviews seems to only be about 2-3 hours so I think I seen more than enough to know I'm not missing anything, and neither are you. Watch the trailer, see the cool visuals, and then go buy a different game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this as a big fan of What Remains of Edith Finch (from the same developers). The Unfinished Swan is a beautiful and well-crafted experience. Everything works well and you can really tell a lot of thought went into every detail. THAT SAID, it is a bit too "artsy-fartsy" for my taste: the story is (deliberately) simple and it didn't really grip me. This could be excused if the gameplay was extremely interesting, which it isn't. It does feel somewhat satisfying to use paint to reveal your path, but that's about it. The game tries to throw some variety to this main mechanic, but most of it ends up feeling dull after a while - or even downright annoying (I'm looking at you, vine sections).I can see this game appealing to more sensitive souls than my own, but if you're looking for something as engaging and fresh as What Remains of Edith Finch, you won't find it here. I recommend other walking simulators such as SOMA and Tacoma.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing "The Unfinished Swan". I played another Giant Sparrow game called  which I liked a lot. Maybe it is because I'm comparing "The Unfinished Swan" to that game but I didn't enjoy it as much."The Unfinished Swan" is way more gameplay-oriented than "What Remains of Edith Finch". It starts very unique and caught you off guard. The gameplay mechanic is simple yet special which makes for a memorable journey. It's riddled with puzzles but they are not frustrating hard and you can pass them relatively easily.Yet it doesn't offer much in terms of story. It's a simple one and mostly just an alibi to put you in the game. The gameplay itself has a very simple mechanic which for a gameplay-based title is not that helpful. "The Unfinished Swan" tries to give some diversity to the gameplay but in my opinion, they are either mostly not that different or just one-time use.You might enjoy "The Unfinished Swan" as a simple, indie game more if you are not expecting much about it. Unlike me who had played "What Remains of Edith Finch" as Giant Sparrow's previous title.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry for my poor English.In my opinion the greatest advantage of What Remains of Edith Finch is the guidance for players,accurate ,clear and very easy to distinguish.As a player I never felt lost or confused in any part of the game,the guidance could always keep me in the right track.I always believe that Edith Finch is the best game in guiding players,which is why i felt disappointed in this product.Surely there are scores of obvious marks all the way,like foot prints,golden units...But by contrast,the same patterns of the scenery made me easily get bored.Monochrome -I know that's the style you chose- but it merges every buildings and structures together,makes the swan hard to be seen(because swans are white),confused me with the path beneath me.And the worst part is,the high contrast stings my eyes...I don't like the balloon idea either.It's as conspicuous as the guidance marks so I often hesitated between keeping on the main track or turning my head to collect the balloon. That is OK in exploration games,but it's more disturbing than joyful in a game with a constant guidance system.===============================Following complaints are about Chapter 3.Who the heck considered traveling across an extremely dark place and an extremely bright place over and over without fade-out effect to solve a puzzle is a cool idea???Who came up with such an idea as using sudden flash to represent being shocked in an extremely dark place???I feel deep pity for those players who have PSE.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend the game at this time because the keyboard controls cannot be rebound.This game has no rebinding of keyboard controls. I expect fully released PC games (i.e. not early access) to have this for lots of reasons (e.g. accessibility, AZERTY keyboard users, personal preferences/comfort).Controller support is good, but not everyone has or can use a controller. I've tried AutoHotKey, reWASD, and similar solutions, but they all have drawbacks.I look forward to revisiting the game and this review when keyboard control rebinding is fully supported.

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short puzzle painting game. At first, you use paint to reveal the world to you. I thought this was an interesting concept & it was the main selling point for me. I thought that the whole game would be like this. That each level would add another color to paint with & reveal other details, but that's not necessarily the case. I still enjoyed the painting(?) mechanic as well as the storybook type of game play. The game took an odd turn at the blueprints part. I felt like it didn't exactly fit in with the style. I recommend unlocking the hose to help out with collecting the balloons for the achievements. There's one balloon in particular that was frustrating to get in the dark chapter. It's stuck in a dark cave that's not visible on your first play through. The balloons in the dark are practically invisible & will require you to play a level several times with the balloon detector. Overall, I still enjoyed the experience & recommend getting it if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Don't play this game at night, way too bright (if you couldn't tell). Also I jumped down by following some footprints at the beginning of the game, and I don't know if this in intentional, but I jumped down to something and kept falling and could see passageways and something else. At that time a loud white noise was blasting my earphone at at least like 80 or more decibels.Such a shame this was made by Giant Sparrow, very disappointing, I heard good things about the game. I will definitely refund and will not risk losing my hearing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A strange FPS puzzle game that tells the story of a painter's child.It takes about 2 hours to finish and isn't very complex.+ Minimalist but decent graphics.+ Some fun interactions with the paint and the environment.+ Great voice acting.- It's not difficult.- Personally, I find the story to be disappointing, even more so after playing "What Remains of Edith Finch" by the same makers. A much better story.- The turning keeps glitching, sometimes being sensitive, sometimes not. It looks like it's triggered by cutscenes.I'm kind of meh on it. It's not bad... Just not great either.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Removed from the context of What Remains of Edith Finch, The Unfinished Swan struggles to stand on its own. The main mechanic of using paint and water splattered to navigate through mostly minimalist levels is a fun idea. However,  as the game progresses less interesting mechanics get introduced (looking at you platform building gimmick!) meanwhile the story never seems to get out of first gear. Unless you love Edith Finch and want a tiny helping of additional story I wouldn’t recommend The Unfinished Swan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: rings at the tune of a simple tale for children, but one that can deliver a message.Splash color to reveal the path… or so you think.You have the simple ability to throw a paintball to interact with your environments but the game stays fresh by switching up the experience without changing the main mechanic you have.You’ll see yourself using splashes of paint to solve puzzles, those range from using them to reveal a path, to push stuff, to attract climbable vines, and so on.The premise of tis fairytale-esque thing is: Monroe’s mom has a quirk of never finishing her paintings, and one day the subject of her most famous piece, the titular Unfinished Swan, goes missing so Monroe in search of it enters a kingdom of wonder and whimsy to reveal the secret behind this bizarre disappearance.Gameplay is often halted to deliver story instead of having a flow between the two, and the story is often just text on a wall…In the beginning and end cutscenes there’s a very weird stutters that ruins them as it feels someone is just shaking a blurry picture in front of your face.Short, cute, has a good message, and it’s a classic, price-to-length/content ratio could use some work but as it stands I gladly recommend it, especially on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why I bought this on here since the achievement system isn't like Xbox's achievement system where once you unlock an achievement you get gamerscore. Definitely platinumed this on the ps4 and ps3 back in the day. Fun, neat, and good little story to it. Haven't played it yet it's worth it I think.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10The Unfinished Swan is a remarkable game like no other. It's more like a dream than an experience. A dream that is fully white like an unpainted painting, and you are the one that going to make it come alive with colors. That is why The Unfinished Swan is a special experience that can't being forgotten.+:A beautiful dream like a storybookSpecial gameplay that is very enjoyableStrange level design that also has good challengesPleasant music with good sound designArt design is simply beautifulGood narration with a good narrator
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this sitting in my Steam library for a while, waiting for the whim to strike me to play it, and I'm glad it finally did.The Unfinished Swan is a lovely game. The art is striking, and does quite a lot with a very limited palette -- especially important given how much of the game is about revealing the landscape with your ink. The narration is beautiful, too, and really sets the mood of the game.Occasionally the climbing mechanics felt a bit wonky, but honestly that was such a small part of the game that even in the climbing-heavy sections, it didn't really affect my enjoyment, and it certainly wasn't game breaking.The one thing I will say is that it seems to suffer a bit from small game pacing. The opening is quite lush and the first two chapters feel detailed. But the third chapter starts to feel a bit rushed; there's some really interesting mechanics introduced but the game doesn't sit with them at all, or do much with them. The final chapter is almost a walking simulator with some minor interaction so you still feel like you're playing the game. Now, I get why this is, but it frustrates me so much when indie games do this. I would have preferred that the game either not introduce new mechanics after the second chapter, or be just a bit longer and have some attention to the new dynamics. One of my pet peeves with small indie games is when the openings are quite detailed, but the more mechanically complex later stages feel thin and underdone. Nevertheless, this game is charming and I'd recommend it to anyone who wants a few hours of engaging environments and very lovely art.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Do yourself a favor and immediately reduce camera speed and mouse sensitivity all the way down. The default settings induce such motion sickness (since you're in undefined space) as to make the game unplayable.Once that's resolved, the game is creative and unique. Worth a play if you can stomach it, especially if you've played Edith Finch since they're connected, but look for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, I'd say about a 8/10. Visually interesting and neat puzzles, though something I wish it had was a sprint button! At least as a post game unlock.  Either way, though, the game is only about 90 minutes and maybe up to two hours if you use a guide for the final chunk of collectables.  The slow move speed didn't really entice me to replay to find the ones I missed.  Worth a first playthrough, though I'd recommend a sale seeing as the game length isn't particularly meaty nor the gameplay replayable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: First, I have to say that Annapurna can do little wrong in my eyes, and I absolutely love their other Giant Sparrow title (What Remains of Edith Finch), to which this is sort of linked.This game is good. But it's not Edith Finch good.The mechanic for the opening chapter is wonderful and innovative. Ironically, the richer the visuals become, the thinner the game feels. By the end, it's a perfectly fine little puzzler, but not all that complex.It's certainly worth the price if it's on sale, I'm not sure I'd pay over £10 on it, as it's very short. It's charming, whimsical, family-friendly, and occasionally surprising.But if whimsy isn't your thing, it might not grab you. Not a must-play, but worth a few hours of your time if this is your favoured style of game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept, decent execution. The game's story is pretty mediocre even though there is a nice message at the end. Also it's very short, it only took me 3 hours to 100% complete, and the rewards you get for doing that are pretty much nothing. I really wish there was a mode where you could walk through several unique maps and splatter them with paint to your liking, maybe with the ability to change your paint color so you could paint an area how you'd like? That would be a pretty good 100% complete bonus, rather than the prototype level.Overall it's fine but I wouldn't recommend buying it unless it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A great tale unfolds entirely through visuals. No book, short film, or narration could transport me to the places this short game did. The story is simple, yet the mechanics of throwing paintballs to reveal or conceal things make the experience of playing this game unforgettable. In fact, it's not a game; it's a short experience told with you as a moving piece.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant concept, very well executed. The first level in particular, when I discovered what I was supposed to be doing, was one of those "WOW" moments that tells you you have a unique game in your hands! The story is cute and has some depth. The gimmick (you shoot balls of liquid for different effects) doesn't overstay its welcome, changing every one or two levels for different effects. It's short and sweet -- maybe a bit too short -- so I wouldn't pay full price (but then, I never do =)
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The first mechanic of the game (throwing paint balls in a full white background to discover a way to path) is excellent! Too bad the rest of the game doesn't continue on this way: after the first level, the throwing balls are just used to make plants growing on walls or to turn on the light. There are no other mechanics based on the colour! I feel the creators missed to develop their start idea.Despite this disappointment, the game is pleasant to play and very beautiful. I especially like the design of the city.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Not a perfect game but ended up being significantly better then what I expected of it.Biggest complaints are are the length of around 2 hours to complete (first play through without looking up anything and collected approximately half the collectables by my estimate - pretty much quality over quantity in this games case) and the night time level which changes the game play from 'take your time and explore' to 'say in the light or die' (having the paint type change to one that temporary emits light would have solved that neatly)
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty fun and short puzzle game that anyone can play. Its gameplay mechanics are simple and enjoyable while not getting stale through the duration of the game, though it's the execution of the gameplay that truly makes it interesting. The visuals complement the gameplay with equal simplicity, accompanied by excellent direction that tells a compelling story through both the speech and the scenery itself.Just a good game all around.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I love the concept for this game as it allows the player to reveal the level. That's how it started out, but then the theme quickly dissipated. The game ended up adding shadows to objects, which I thought was a really cool progression. After the shadows, it seemed that colors were just added to most of the objects. I wish the progressive addition of color continued throughout the game, so it built on itself between levels. A small gripe I have is not giving the sniper rifle toy until the player has found all the balloons. With the sniper rifle it makes hitting balloons much easier, but it is a fun toy to have. Giving the sniper rifle once all balloons have been found feels kind of pointless because finding all balloons was the last thing I did. There is an achievement that utilizes the sniper rifle, but it is very quick, so players are not able to experience the sniper rifle much unless they feel like replaying a level. Although there were some things that I griped about, I think the game is still fun and has an enjoyable story. Make sure you drink some water when you play!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, whimsical story-led video game. It's not quite worth the standard $20 in my opinion (I'd say $10 would suffice), but it was a sweet game. Personally I'd say the story is a bit back and forth, sometimes it seems like it will lead a certain way but diverts to something maybe unexpected, and not necessarily in a beneficial way. The music and voice acting is lovely, and the different game mechanics with the paint can be fun, though a few times it just made things more frustrating rather than fun.Overall, if you like first-person adventure games centered on story (walking-simulator, I suppose) then give this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I finished it and got all achievements (some are a bit frustrating).I recommend it. However, you should attentively consider a couple things, if you want to play it:- overwhelming whiteness and brightness, general lack of clearly discernible contours and other factors, found especially but not exclusively in the first levels, can give you ocular migraine;- this game is bad for you if you suffer even a bit from Acrophobia. You will go up A LOT; dangle from under bridges, and other funny things. Falling from any height can't "kill" your character, but still it feels very bad.For these reasons, I can only play it a bit at a time, before it gives me anxiety and a headache. But I still like it.Funny trivia:
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game on my PS3 when I was younger, and it's so nostalgic to come back and play this mighty peaceful game again over 8 years later. I'd recommend this game, and it's awesome that this game is fairly inexpensive - (I'm one to talk, since I bought it when it was on sale for 5 bucks, but still.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: is a relatively quick adventure puzzle. There isn't anything particularly hard about the game but it can be extremely disorienting at times. I must mention the game isn't without it's charms. The story and narration are very engaging. In fact, you may have picked up on the connections to . A lot more depth is added to the storyline once those connections are made. The game is definitely worth the $4.04 I got it for in a bundle, just don't give up on the first level, The Garden, it does get better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: From the same people that made 'What Remains of Edith Finch'; The Unfinished Swan is equally surreal and artsy but this time is more of a puzzle adventure title than a story-rich walking sim. The game revolves around a core mechanic of splattering paint to reveal the world around you, and each chapter mixes this up slightly to keep it engaging over it’s fairly short run time. Like many of these types of games (simple puzzle games built around a unique core mechanic like 'Superliminal', or 'The Stanley Parable'), it has a faint impression of a tech demo moulded into a game rather than a fully fledged game but nonetheless I enjoyed my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: First chapter is tricky to navigate and might be a little bit unpleasant to play through, but the game gets nicer and nicer the longer you play. It's a cute story, the world in it is creative and fun to walk around. And collecting achievements for this game is also fun and not painstaking like with some games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, just like What remains of Edith Finch, it is the ending that hits you hard. This game is split into 4 chapters with 4 just being a credit sequence. 1 and 2 are lame and honestly boring, Chapter 3 is amazing and really shows the creativitiy of the developers. I would say get this game but only when it is on sale for $5.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I would say it's a nice game to play, if you get the game on sale. The storyline is sweet & keeps you playing to figure things out. I like that the game doesn't penalize you for making an error. It's a fun world to see unfold & a fun way to spend a day or few hours in. I don't think you can get all achievements in the first go around ~ so if you're going for achievements, you'll need to play it again and I highly recommend getting some toys in the Toy option to help make the game play quicker the second go around. Also, there's a good site that has some tips & walk throughs of game to help if you're going for achievements or you get frustrated but you really don't need it for first time playing it... just have fun exploring it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished Swan is a game that I go back to multiple times. Not only is it a game that is so simple in mechanics, but it is a game that is simple in story. It is a perfect game for when you just want something quick and easy to play and I recommend this game for younger audiences.When looking at the gameplay, it is generally super simple, you just walk around the world, throwing paint/water balls and solve tiny puzzles to progress in story and in the world. Anyone can play this game and quickly get the hang of it, there is nothing overly complicated about this game. If you have young children as well, I also recommend this game because the style is also simple. The cartoonish feel of the artwork and how simple the story is can keep children entertained until the very end.The story itself is also so cute and heartwarming, but also has a deeper meaning. Everyone can take something away from this game, young or old. It is a story that I find, despite being in my adult years, so simple and encouraging. I recommend this game for people who don't play video games often and want to get into them, those with young children, or those who just want something quick and cozy to play. Giant Sparrow has also done some amazing work in What Remains of Edith Finch, another game I heavily recommend for more mature audiences, such as teens and young adults.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super fun and charming (assuming you are in to walking simulators). It has an engaging story and some fun puzzles to keep things interesting. Plus the paint splatter mechanic is pretty unique. Though I will be honest and say that 15$ is pretty steep for a game this short. It's abut 2 hours to beat and maybe an extra hour if you get all of the collectibles and achievements. Wait for it to go on sale for 10$ or less, and then I'd say it's it's well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. It's so scenic. I enjoyed the creativity, and loved that I had to explore to understand the world and gain a sense of my surroundings. I adore the storytelling component, it made me feel like I was taking part of a fairytale, which was so exciting. I would recommend this <33
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game had an incredible start, I really enjoyed the first levelhowever the gimmick of being in a plain white room and needing to paint it to see was quickly discarded by the 3rd zone and became another generic puzzle game with throwing paint to push buttons to open doors.The later levels were either fully lit with shading or mostly darkness were you basically had to jump around randomlyremoving the need to paint hardly anything.My other main issue was the performance in some levels. Despite having a good computer I was still getting 15fps in some areas with super laggy mouse inputs.

_childDocuments_.review: Completionist info at the bottom. Mild spoilers in this review. Rating 8/10The Unfinished Swan is a charming game which tells a very cute story. If that kind of thing appeals to you, you will have a good time with this game. However, if you are looking for really anything else, this game is likely not going to be your thing.The Unfinished Swan is a self-described “interactive children’s book” and this is about as perfect of a description as you could ask for. The player plays as Monroe, a young child whose mother has recently passed away. Monroe is given one of his late mother’s unfinished paintings, his favorite, the unfinished swan. One day, Monroe wakes up and finds the swan has escaped its painting and, upon chasing it, the player finds himself in a mysterious painted world through which Monroe/the player chases the swan who always remains one step ahead.The design of the game is really its strongest selling point, even, in my opinion, above the narrative. It is, as was already implied, reminiscent of a children’s storybook, but with the added delight of three dimensions, which is a unique and pleasant experience. The different vistas of the game are very striking as the game transitions from painted forest to enormous castle to dark forest. Each area is unique and memorable, albeit quite short. Mechanically, the core gameplay is standard and, arguably, boring. Actual movement in The Unfinished Swan doesn’t extend much past simply pressing WASD and the occasional left-click. But to criticize the game for this would be narrow-minded. This game is, fundamentally, an interactive story, and little effort went in to any sort of dynamic movement system. Instead, The Unfinished Swan does have a few tricks, gimmicks if you will, that it introduces from level to level. These include growing vines, moving light sources, and buildable blocks, all of which play a part in different levels to various degrees. These additions keep the game from getting too stale while adding a little bit of a challenge to the player, elevating the game from being a walking-simulator to an actual puzzle game.Finally, the story of the game is well-done. While The Unfinished Swan has more gameplay than many similar games, and therefore doesn’t have to rely on its story quite as much as other games in its genre, much of the final impact of the game comes down to how well the story is executed. The story, and its conclusion, determine the taste which is left in the player mouth once the game is finished and forgotten. And I think the flavor that remains after this game is sweet. I said before that The Unfished Swan is a very cute game, but perhaps charming is a better word. Its story is a very human one, surprisingly deep for the limited time the story has and, by the end, the player who is playing this game for its atmosphere will be left satisfied by it.And really, that is all there is to say about the game. It is a charming experience which has excellent visuals, some interesting mechanics/puzzles, and a satisfying story. It is a short game and shouldn’t take much more than a lazy afternoon to complete. But be warned, the story and world might stay in your mind a good while longer than that.Completionist Information: (Difficulty – 4/10)(Fun – 6/10)(Time: 2-3 hours)The Unfinished Swan is a quick game and has a level select which allows collection of all of the game’s collectibles, which are balloons, easily and quickly. Doing this, however, will essentially require two playthroughs of the game as the player is likely to miss balloons in every level unless you are being very careful, which I don’t really recommend. When playing through just for collectables, you can go very quickly if you know what you are doing and the chapter select is quite robust/extensive.The hardest achievement is one in which you must basically play the first level of the game completely blind for the most part. This is more tedious than challenging, but if you follow a video guide closely, it isn’t too bad, just annoying.Overall, not an overly fun game to complete (it’s not really made for challenge anyways), but also not that bad either. Fine all around.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: There was indeed a swan that required additional work. 10/10This is a re-release of a game that originally came out for PS3 back in 2012. The core mechanic is cool and well executed, and it's backed by some good narration. It doesn't have quite the staying power of What Remains of Edith Finch, but it feels like the devs recognized that and made the game significantly shorter and simpler to match.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game similar to The Room but far simpler, will take you about 3 hours to complete if you follow a guide and maybe about 10 hours if you're doing it blind,Achievements are easy except the minimalist one which is a bit tricky. Would recommend if you like to get easy 100% completions and puzzle games.Definitely buy when it's on sale and not full price
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Short little narrative experience with a minimalist but compelling artstyle. Despite the fact it's all about throwing balls of paint everywhere, it mixes things up, but isn't particularly challenging. Allegorical story that you might (or might not) like, depending how much you relate to it.Bought it on sale and I'm happy with it. I don't think it quite holds up for a full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely adorable!It has a very unique style, and a very special visual design. The voice acting is great too. I am not sure what to say about the gameplay. It is not exactly boring, but neither is it exciting. It is a very simple puzzle-solver, where the puzzle-solving is not meant to, nor does it, distract from the main focus that is the art design (and the special way of interacting with it). But I am very happy that it is not longer than it is, as it would have gotten boring quite quickly. The game is good though at presenting new tweaks to the gameplay rather frequently. So overall, an enjoyable experience. A good game to help you take your mind off things, to relax and maybe to reflect on things. The story is very heartwarming, especially if you end up playing the extra levels as well. An unexpected profoundly deep game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: when i first started I thought it was a worse version of what remains of edith finch, but by the end, I think i loved this game even more. I had such an amazing time going through the game and unraveling the story.  The presentation as well as the puzzles are insanely unique.ps I got the minimalist achievement before I played any bit of the game and it was actually really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A patchwork of okay mechanics over an okay story. A bit overpriced for a game I was glad was over.It seems like half the game design went into replayability, which makes no sense for a short story game. Collecting all the hidden balloons allows you to purchase special upgrades? Why would I keep playing after collecting all the balloons anyway? (Why even keep playing after I beat the story regardless of balloons?)This game really doesn't have much exploration at all. The levels are pretty narrow paths. And for most of the game, you don't have paint; you have rapidly disappearing water. Who would want to go through these levels a third time just to get them briefly damp while using the special upgrades locked behind getting all the balloons? I was hoping for better from Annapurna.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels unfinished. I don't mind games being on the shoter side, but this game is full of ideas that lack growth and development. It's only four levels long, and its mechanics peak at the second level in terms of creativity. If you find it on sale, it's a well-made experience with some cute storytelling, but don't go into this expecting a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to rate this using the 5-star system, I'd have to give it a solid 4. A unique idea and a cute world, there is definitely a lot to love about the Unfinished Swan. But to anyone who is hoping to find a game reminiscent of What Remains of Edith Finch, you might be a bit disappointed. Don't get me wrong, the mechanics here are unique and creative, but they can get pretty annoying from time to time - I experienced a few glitches. But if you're just looking for a feel-good story, this is a great one to experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: An artistic game with different game mechanics and gameplay. The music is relaxing and beautiful. The game overall is very good and I liked it. Of course, there are some negative aspects as well. Looking at the screen for a long time can hurt the eyes because the game is predominantly white. If you want to do Achievements, take a deep breath and remember to be patient because you will have to play the game over and over and your eyes will be screaming for help. In addition, this game is a reference of the game "What Remains of Edith Finch". It also has a much broader story and setting that is great and artistic. The fact that these two games have a common point made me extremely happy and I liked it very much. If your eyes won't bother you, I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's a walking simulator with just a bit more- the canvas mechanic is neat and the game is short enough with enough permutations on the mechanic that it doesn't overstay its welcome. I didn't really get drawn into the story that much, and there's not really much special in the graphics/ost department (except the awesome space-bending labyrinth made possible with some scenery duplicating sleight of hand). If I had to place it in the walking simulator pantheon it would be below Journey but above The Vanishing of Ethan Carter. And way above Dear Esther.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I'm home from work sick with the (non-spicy) flu and wanted a game that felt dreamy, low stakes, and something.. methodical, maybe? Like an Unpacking feel - I wanted to slowly unfold the world around me. It met the prescription. The story feels a bit hollow but coming in entirely blind (just picked it because it was on sale) I was very charmed by it over all with the highlights being first when dropped in and not knowing which way was up, then being hunted' tone shift, and making your own pillars to jump on as the game came to a close. Wish the latter especially had continued on less linearly - too simple but kind of soothing, like the Unpacking feel I was aiming for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished SwanPositives:+ Nice artistic look+ Good idea+ Some nice levels+ Good sound and music+ Nice voiceover and voiceacting+ The puzzle partsNegatives:- So-so story- Some parts are challenging to navigate thru (you see almost nothing)- They could have done so much more with the idea- Some parts are repetitive and not so much funTo be honest this game was a tad disappointing.Maybe my expectations were too high, but I felt like this game was a missed opportunity.Dont get me wrong, the game was good, but it could have been great.I still recommend it though, because it had its moments.Total Score: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I know, this is one of those games where the main focus is the narrative and it's mostly a cake walk with little to no challenge. There is some credit where credit is due, however; not only is the story kind of cute as you basically take the perspective of a little kid going through some storybook to uncover the lore about the world he was brought into while throwing ink/water around to uncover the paths as he goes through the story of the world. I could be wrong about the plot; I haven't touched the game in a little bit.The art style is actually pretty neat and it varies based on what chapter you're in, and there are some unique elements that you don't usually see in other games, but unfortunately there isn't much to say about this game, if you're into story-driven games with a little bit of uniqueness in them, I say give this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Really good for the imagination. The creativity and potential at your own will keeps me engaged. The story is cute and meaningful too. Game can be finished in a single sitting but there's always a little more to see or something you may have missed. The collectables add to replayability.Recommend for a cozy experience
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: So, I initially heard of this game as a prequel for What Remains of Edith Finch and expected a kind of addition to its story but in the end I got something completely different... but also extremely interesting. To begin with, the game's graphics, music and aesthetics are just majestic - I think you could have already guessed it by the screenshots. All those things create a sort of fairly tale experience and it is pretty close to what the game's plot wants to be. Speaking about it, I wouldn't say it is something outstanding or unique but despite it's initial simplicity in the end it gives you something to ponder on. The gameplay is far from complex but it doesn't need to be: the game gives you simple puzzles that do not really make you think but rather guide you through the wonderful world of The Unfinished Swan. The game also adds new mechanics and gameplay changes in each new chapter which prevents the walkthrough from becoming boring. You can finish the whole game in 2-3 hours (maybe in 4-5 if you go for all achievements) - it is not much but just enough for this kind of a game.In conclusion, if you liked What Remains of Edith Finch and want to try another more abstract game from the same developer or just like unusual art-house projects I recommend buying it. However, if you are looking for something with a deep gameplay and complicated puzzles you better skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I'm genuinely shocked at how this game was able to take a perfectly white area and with only a few splats of paint by the player provide enough information to navigate and explore an area. The sound effects were perfect as well and were essentially required to pull it off. The story was great, the way the game eventually elaborated on the character's abilities was also a lot of fun, and the combination of the two was nearly flawless!The only concern is that this game is not particularly accessable by nature. I find that especially sad because I think this deserves having as many people as possible playing.The Unfinished Swan is yet another fantastic example of how games are an artistic medium that deserves respect and admiration!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it. A simple but enjoyable narrative puzzle game with platforming elements and even hints of horror (especially if one suffers from arachnophobia) at one point. Took me two hours to finish it so it's short, but well worth playing. Wait for a sale if you're unsure about the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: An artsy game with the tone of an innocent bedtime story. Simple and rather short, but generally well made.The people complaining about how all the game is just throwing black paint onto nothingness didn't make it past the very first area - obviously there's more to the game.But if you're prone to getting motion sickness or headaches from games, I guess beware.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: In a bizarre, sanitzed combination of Paint It Black by the Rolling Stones and Mad World for the Wii, Giant Sparrow deliveres The Unfinished Swan, the first entry in the Edith Finch Extended Universe.All jokes aside, Giant Sparrows first game may not be as great as Edith Finch, but it's artstyle and children-book told story are very lovely regardless. The Studio really shines at Storytelling and Enviroments and there are not too many indie titles that do so in my opinion.Unfortunately i wouldn't call these guys masters when it comes to gameplay. Very basic puzzle elements can be found in this title along with some collectibles that unlock tools that feel more like Development leftovers. The gameplay isn't bad, it is more than serviceable, but i think ditching elements that are found here later for What Remains of Edith Finch was  the right idea.Still, if you like WROEF and ever wonder what happened to Milton in that game i can happily recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast! (Literally, as a main aspect is to launch balls of paint that splatter on impact). The story is compelling, the architecture is wonderfully neat, and the concept itself is innovative!Edit: Other reviewers stated they felt motion sick while playing. I can say I definitely didn't have that same experience, so don't let that deter you completely!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Following a quick storybook intro, it starts off with a blank cursor over an intensely empty white screen. There is some reactive sound to player commands but absolutely nothing to see. The game very nearly feels broken, until you discover the right trigger and start throwing black paint balls that reveal the scenery and single path forward, and essentially define the rest of the journey.Gameplay evolves from base mechanics to keep fresh and avoid repetition. Water balls tint the environment in light blue but dry out rapidly. Velocity of throws pushes light objects and enables simple environmental puzzles. Activate switches to enable traversal, grow vines to climb and reach new places, push and activate lights to repel darkness. Create volumes in later chapters.Find and collect optional balloons. Not all of them colored, some hidden but most in plain sight. These can be traded for toys but have little value except for the detailed concept art that can be unlocked.More interestingly, discover additional narrative entries in the world by shooting bright golden letters peppered throughout the levels. It reads like a live storybook about love, loss, creative discovery and chasing desires, and leaving some form of legacy after a whole life's worth of unfinished accomplishments. Cute story, creative, simple, well achieved.The game does present a beautiful art direction, but it is nonetheless harshly monochromatic and heavy on contrast and brightness. It feels a little too much at both ends of the spectrum, from blinding light to total darkness. While not actual motion sickness, the game did make me feel faintly unwell during longer sessions. Best played in short amounts and in a properly lit room.Overall, I found The Unfinished Swan very imaginative except for the typical collectible chase. I would have preferred discovering more animated story beats to know more about the King and the Boy and their intriguing respective paths.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This game has such a neat premise and the paint splatter is a good mechanic. I don't want to give it a negative review, but I think it's worth mentioning that I could only make it about 10 minutes into the first level before I got so nauseous that I had to stop - nothing to do with the content but I guess due to the frequent turning in 3D space? I've only encountered one other game where this happens to me so I wouldn't call myself prone to motion sickness, but based on a quick google search it's not an uncommon occurrence with The Unfinished Swan :( Just a heads up
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game!It has a lot of unique mechanics that you've probably never seen before. But it feels like they only touched each mechanic a little bit and then moved on to the next, without realising the potential behind it, so the three chapters feel a bit disconnected. The storyline ties it all together, with great storytelling. I enjoyed finding the little story-bits and hearing more of the fairy tale. And the way they implemented the credits is marvellous.As someone who loves achievements, I aimed for getting all in this game. After you play through the game once, you unlock a helpful device for getting all the secrets. I could find all balloons without external help. Only one of the 10 achievements is a bit harder and requires a guide and some training. It took me maybe one and a half hours.This game is not for someone who wants an intricate puzzle-game. But if you're looking for a game with interesting and creative mechanics and storytelling, I'll definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Other than the story, I really liked this game. The story is good and all, but idk if it was just me, it felt like it was the skeleton and some of the organs of the actually story. Kinda like sometimes there was the perfect amount of story with the perfect amount of detail and other times both were lacking. The game itself ran smoothly and can't recall a time I had issues with long load times, glitching, lagging, or the such. Loved the majority of the chapters and their mechanics but unfortunately the game is rather a short one. Would have loved to have experienced more of everything is white and you have to paint things black to find your way through. Overall a great short game that I thoroughly enjoyed and ran smoothly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: this is... a weird one. kinda hit deep as someone who just got into animation and has no clue what hes doing. pick it up and play it... i think. also very unique game design with paint splats showing more of the world to you. also, dont over think things, just go with the flow as the path really is that straight forward
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny how reviews for games vary from gamer to gamer; each person has their own unique identity and abilities and the way a given game is structured will resonate with some and not with others. I played the Unfinished Swan in just short of four hours, all in one sitting. The first 15 minutes or so feels kind of tentative and a bit slow but the story and the environments really start to kick in after that. This game is short but frankly I was amazed by it's content. The Unfinished Swan is really an exploration & adventure game with a steady dose of excellent puzzles along the way. It's a process of discovery that's very memorable from start to finish. Games like this, that are as good as this, seem to be pretty rare unfortunately. I'm thinking here of a game like "Sable," for instance, although Sable is much longer than this and has more to offer overall. If you're someone like me, with respect to new releases, where you're like "Oh, great, look: it's this week's new top down shooter 'action-adventure' game, with an emphasis on combat featuring Souls-like difficulty...how original!!"--if you tend to have similar thoughts, and yearn for more mind blowing magical mystery tour experiences like Sable or What Remains of Edith Finch, etc., then you really should give the Unfinished Swan a try. And now is the perfect time, considering the Summer Sale!:-) A real treat, and the story, though simple, has something to--I hate to use the word "teach," but for want of a better word I'll use it--has something to teach everyone who plays it. 10 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Stunned, Neat little story to go with although pretty simple gameplay, but the way the environment changes to engage your feelings and thoughts and a few puzzles dotted through can make you have certain eureka moments. A good hour and a half to two hour of gameplay without going for all secrets, Well worth it if you can pick it up on sale, otherwise it depends on the player.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game on PS3 when it first came out and instantly fell in love with it. It's completely enchanting and magical. Visually it is lovely and gameplay is unique and relaxing. Since I switched to PC shortly after I lost the ability to play it since I could only access it while I paid on console. I have been waiting for this to come out on Steam and funny enough didn't even notice when it did, someone close to me mentioned it and it made me so happy. Playing again brought back all the joy that I experience the first time. I cannot recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly beautiful, soothing, and pleasant.  I was continually impressed with each new permutation of the mechanics, and none outstayed its welcome.  In this era of "games as service," I deeply respect the courage and artistic integrity it takes to make something gorgeous, simple, and exactly as long as it needs to be, and not give in to the endless bleating from both consumers and corporations to add more for the sake of adding more.  This is a very beautiful game, one that does things that are only possible in an interactive medium, and we should always praise and encourage people exploring territory that only games can discover, executing ideas that only games can represent, and giving us totally unique interactive experiences like this one to counterbalance the vast number of games that care nothing and do nothing for games as an artistic medium.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: (To provide context for my review, my system specs are Windows 10/RTX 2080/i9 10980HK)- Very interesting art style throughout, though some areas (the city and palace in particular) are more inspiring than others- The music is fine; it didn't add or subtract from the experience- It's a simple, bittersweet tale about family and overcoming loss- Despite the dark parts of the story, the game's mood never feels depressing or mournful. I feel like the themes could have been explored a little more- The game controls fine, but that's because all you can do is walk, climb, jump, and shoot- The central mechanic of firing paint or water to progress is neat. The twists they put on the simple mechanic are creative, but I feel like the idea could have been explored further- I don't think I'll be replaying this one. The balloon collecting wasn't fun enough to warrant another playthrough- The game ran flawlessly the whole way through- After finishing, I was left wanting a bit more. Is the "unfinished" thing a gag? Whatever the case, the experience wasn't as fulfilling as I had hoped it would be- . Get it on sale if you like the art style. It's a short (2.5-3 hour) game that looks pretty and has a few cool tricks but will leave you wanting more from your experience
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, before I recommend this game, here's what it is not:It is not a shooter.  It is not an RPG.  It is not a massive, thousand hour adventure.  It does not contain adult themes/language.Now, to why I love this game and highly recommend it.  It is based on a really cool mechanic of using a "magic paintbrush" that can throw blobs of paint around a conpletely white world.  At first it is disorienting, but quickly becomes very fun as you literally paint your own surroundings.  Later levels move away from the absolute white aesthetic, by adding more shading and eventually colors.  But there are several fun unlockables to pick up as you progress and it definitely merits a second or perhaps third playthrough.The story is of a young boy whose mother has died and he begins exploring one of her unfinished works, only to find a realm created and run by a painter king.  I won't spoil the story, but it is definitely interesting and open to several interpretations.This could also be a good game to play with a child that approaches the theme of death in the family in  a relatively safe and mild way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: It's short and cute. _childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Some people will call this game a "walking simulator," which is a term I have chosen to completely and totally disregard.  The meaning of the term has been lost since it was introduced a decade ago.  It used to refer to a type of adventure game that was focused on interactive and immersive story telling, often with few to no game mechanics.  These days, people throw it around and it's used as a synonym for "boring."If we were to abide by the original meaning, I would classify The Unfinished Swan as a walking simulator.  But it's not a pure walking sim; the game has several mechanics through the course of the story.  I don't want to spoil them, but I do want to give massive respect for the incredible feat of programming that is the growing vines mechanic.The story being told in this  (the term I prefer to walking simulator) feels like a fairytale.  I think they did a great job of making TUS fit that theme.TUS also boasts what I believe is the most ridiculous achievement I have ever done in a video game.  I decided to get the most I could from TUS and achieve a Perfect Game.  To do that, I would need to get the "Minimalist" achievement.  The blank white icon for the achievement says it all: it requires navigating the first level level, which appears as a pure white screen, without using more than three ink balls.  Sound is the only indication of where you are.  A truly demented mind came up with this achievement.  It took me 45 minutes and carefully following a video guide before I reached the end.  Whew!I'm grateful that this game was ported from PlayStation to PC, though I'm very disappointed that since it runs on Gamebryo engine, I was unable to experience it in virtual reality with vorpX.  I was able to enjoy it on my monitor at 4K, and though the original game is old, it looks nice and crisp on PC.  Really great that we have it here, now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: HOLY SMOKES! Santa Monica Studios NAILS it again. The Unfinished Swan is a story about a boy following just that. However, the art and play style is simple yet novel. Just like many other Santa Monica Studios famous titles, you will feel a curious welcoming to the world as you learn how to interact with it. There will be mood-setting music that is simply Spectacular and it will carry you up and down and far away. You will feel curious one moment, optimistic the next, determined, in awe, and afraid. In the end, you will walk out the door wondering what you just experienced. Personally, I feel a bit of a joyful sadness since my Journey is at an end with this title.I HIGHLY recommend The Unfinished Swan. Oh, and you'll find reference to at least one other famous Santa Monica Studios titles in this game.I get that other people weren't sure what to expect with this, but it is really really good. I hope that you enjoy it too!

_childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished Swan is very cutesy and fun walking-sim with some puzzle elements. I enjoyed the world-building, uniqueness, and aesthetic of this game. It presents such a interesting and compelling concept from the beginning and really does a good job at telling a simple story visually as well as aurally.I also felt kinda frustrated by some elements. The cutscenes were at a much lower framerate than the gameplay, which was strange. The story after in chapters 2-3 is fairly unimportant to the overall message and story and felt tacked on. _childDocuments_.review: Journey through a wonderful tale as Monroe, a young boy recently orphaned and left only one of his mother’s many unfinished paintings: an unfinished swan.  Waking up one night and discovering that the swan is no longer in its painting; you begin an epic journey through the blank canvas into another world.  Using your only tool in your travels you will paint, grow, and move items to bypass all manner of obstacles as you travel through strange and wondrous realms to reach the end of the story and the start of your own.The Unfinished Swan is a first-person puzzle/platforming game set in a lovely artistic world.  The game has the feeling of a well-loved children’s book and as such you progress through chapters of the story with additional pages to the tale found throughout the game.  Each chapter lets you use your only tool, a paintbrush, to progress through the world, overcoming various obstacles and progressing the storyline further.  Some minor platforming is required, but nothing too difficult.  Quirky scenes, a fun narrated story, and a beautifully simplistic world make The Unfinished Swan a fun diversion and a joy to play.While fun; the game’s mechanics seem to have no cohesion throughout the game.  For example, in the first chapter they are used to reveal the game world to you, while in the second chapter the mechanics are used to develop a way to move forward over various obstacles, and in the third chapter they are utilized mainly for security measures.  Additionally, in the third chapter, another mechanic was introduced that completely different from the rest of the game that didn’t seem to fit the rest of the game at all.  Sadly, the mechanics didn’t feel related—just something to do.The achievements are relatively easy to attain except for one which requires a bit more effort.  Achievements run from completing chapters of the story to collecting items along the way.  You may replay the game from chapters and subchapters which makes the collecting much easier than having to play over again.  Overall, getting all ten achievements was fun.While I did enjoy The Unfinished Swan I found it a bit too short and it had a feeling of being itself unfinished.  I enjoyed the world, the music, the story, and the gameplay, but wanted much more.  However, even with that said, I still recommend this game for those who like puzzles, fun stories, or for those who are looking for a short game that’s easy to learn and play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Before Reading: Don't buy this if its not on sale, not worth 15 Dollars. This is worth 5 or 10 at most. Details at end of review.This game is a pretty fun half of a game. The design and art-style are both a little above average and the game mechanics and ideas being presented are detailed enough to make the story interesting and/or involved. The introduction can make the game feel like a tech demo with how simple it is, but surprised me with how creative the next evolutions of the mechanics were. I meant the word "half" in the sense that it feels like there isn't enough to warrant a 15 dollar price tag. The time to beat each level is good, there just aren't a ton of levels. This game does enough good things that it is enjoyable to play, but enough half-hearted things that its a good tool in getting the player to think about even cooler mechanics that could have been implemented, aka aspiring game developers.Overall, I would just say to try this game out if its on sale, but don't get it at full price. Because of almost no replayability, aside from achievements, the game needs about twice the amount of content than current to warrant a 15 dollar price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally released by Giant Sparrow and Santa Monica Studio in 2012 for the Playstation 3, The Unfinished Swan saw a PC  release in September 2020. The story follows the adventure of Monroe, an orphan who discovered a mysterious little door which led him to a world of imagination. The gameplay involves exploration with evolving game mechanics as the narrative progresses. Intentionally the mechanics remain fairly simple for the entirety of the game favoring enough innovation to be exciting, but not so complex to distract from the narrative. Similarly we see very early versions of the camera adjustment later featured in the Giant Sparrow release What Remains of Edith Finch. The art direction is minimalist, the narration done by Juli Pari is very well done and features Terry Gilliam as the King which I thought was a nice surprise. I began The Unfinished Swan originally looking for more answers from the game What Remains of Edith Finch. After finishing both games I can definitely say that each game stands on their own entirely, and the cameo of the young king as an easter egg in What Remains of Edith finch is just that, an easter egg. Originally I left this game a bit disappointed since I was hoping to earn a new perspective of Edith Finch but after spending some time with both I have come out with a new appreciation of The Unfinished Swan. Before moving on to spoilers for the story of The Unfinished Swan I will leave a short rating of the main elements.Gameplay 5/10Graphics 7/10Story 7/10Sound Design 8/10Voice Acting 9/10The Unfinished Swan blurs the line between the adventure and walking simulator genres. At many points the exploration feels open and I think that Giant Sparrow have done an excellent job with the level design. There are lots of examples of attention to detail, as well as clever subconscious player motivation. However while many of the interactions of The Unfinished Swan feel fluid, providing a natural extension of the main ink throwing mechanic, there are too many examples of poor implementation to give The Unfinished Swan a passing grade. Most notably the vine growing mechanic felt slow compared to the rest of the game resulting in lots of waiting, and I think that the forest section of the game could have used a bit of work. Similarly the nursery felt like it had lots of untapped potential which could have been explored in it's own chapter entirely. The balloon finding secrets could have been streamlined, awarded to the player automatically. It's current implementation is clunky; most confusingly of all a majority of useful features are gated behind finding all of the balloons. As always I'd like to give a few thoughts on the themes of The Unfinished Swan. I think the storybook narration fit the aesthetic feeling like a fantastic unofficial Shel Silverstein story in the process. While I feel that What Remains of Edith Finch and The Unfinished Swan may have originally had more through-lines towards the beginning of Edith Finch's development, I think both games stand separate now.

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: so.....i'm not sure what to say!  i loved the controls, really simple, music good, voices good. oh and the art work is great. i don't think i finished the game, and i guess i can't. i even tried playing the last few chapters, but i still never finished, i don't think. looking at the game chapter by chapter, there are a lot of fun, innovative chapters. but overall, i was lost, ,not really having a game plan or knowing where i was going or why. it was different, that's for sure. i read some reviews where people finished in 2 hours, and i gave up after 6.7 hours. :D   so i did have fun, but it's always a bit disappointing to not be able to finish a game. i shouldn't blame the game, i guess, as i imagine a lot of people found it easy.so i'll give it a 3.5 out of 5 based on how innovative i found it. and i'll recommend it at the good sale price of around $8.00 USD. i just wish i could have finished it.

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Edith Finch, so I had high hopes for this one. I think if you're looking for a simple happy walking simulator with some nice story, this is probably just fine; but don't expect the beautiful experience of Edith Finch. This is pretty much a walking simulator, and after the main mechanic gets old (and you get RSI from clicking so much), it wears thin pretty fast. I love the idea of revealing the world with the paint gun and that works really well; it's just not really enough to base the entire game around. My girlfriend literally fell asleep watching me play this, and even though I've almost finished the game I don't really want to invest another hour to finish it off.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game from a demo in Best buy years ago and was finally able to get and experience this unique game. All the puzzles in this game are simple yet satisfying and the story itself is quite intriguing as you follow the journey of the protagonist. This was a great investment of both time and money and I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Short yet beautifully sweet game. So, instead of that, let's talk about...There is . Which wouldn't be that big of a dealbreaker in a single-player game because AutoHotKey exists, but  How did they even manage to do that? _childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished Swan is an absolute delight of a puzzle game that everyone should play, not just puzzle fans. The game has a beautiful minimalist design which combines wonderfully with the tightly design puzzles that never ask too much of the player but are still satisfying to work out. The balloon collecting side-game (which in any other game would be an annoying element) is an invitation to branch out from the straight forward path and explore every nook and cranny of the surprising intricate maps. If I have any complaint about this game, is that the tone of the game is a little unsettling at the very start. Despite the childbook story opening, one can't help but wonder if they've accidentally walked into a horror game as they slowly explore a desolate, silent landscape. Once you realize that the exploration is meant to invoke curious wonder and not dread, the game became extremely fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and short experience told like a child's book. Despite it's simplicity, some of the decors are breathtaking and the contrast of colors in very clever.Still, it's an inferior experience compare to Edith Finch but since it was released before it proves that the devs got better, can't wait for your next game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This could have a been a vaguely interesting, short conceptual demo. Instead, we got an exceptionally boring and pretentious high-budget console exclusive with a celebrity voice actor. I've waited so long for this to come to PC, because I loved Giant Sparrow's , but this game is just objectively bad.The game is very short, and yet within that limited time span nothing of interest happens. The levels are simple. The "puzzles" (I am being very generous calling them that) are at once trivial and tedious. The game is famous for its visual concepts, which are creative in themselves, but the minimalistic graphics do not do justice to the ideas. And that's it. There's nothing else to the game.I often enjoy "walking simulators" even when there is no significant gameplay. However, here there are just ... concepts. Well, there is a story that tries very hard to be delightful, but is instead disjointed, nonsensical, and inconclusive. Terry Gilliam's excellent voice acting (used sparingly) is the only thing that keeps the thin narrative from being downright annoying.Skip this.

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished Swan a pretty good game that can be finished in around two and a half hours, which for me is the perfect time that it should last. The story is divided into four chapters with each one having its own different mechanics for gameplay, so if you're worried about being blind the whole game and having to throw around paint for its entire duration you're good. There was one mechanic in the second chapter that involved growing plants that did overstay its welcome but besides that the new mechanics that were introduced were enjoyable. Don't come into this game expecting a story like the one in What Remains of Edith Finch. The Unfinished Swan's is a much more simple one that plays out like a children's storybook with you exploring the world of a painting as a child who has travelled into it. I feel inclined to mention the chances that you might get motion sickness if you play The Unfinished Swan so be wary if you're prone to it, and especially don't go for the "Minimalist" achievement because I, as a person who isn't afflicted with motion sickness got dizzy after a while.Overall, besides a small amount of flaws, The Unfinished Swan is a fairly solid game. The only advice I'd give though, is to not go into it expecting another Edith Finch as this is a completely different game, so you might come out disappointed. Besides that and the motion sickness issue, I still wholeheartedly recommend The Unfinished Swan because it's relaxing, story-based, and perfect for drinking hot cocoa while wrapped in a blanket at 11PM.

_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This is a FANTASTIC game!  And yet, it almost doesn't feel like a game.  Its interface could not be simpler, and its style is just beautiful and takes you to a place that's peaceful (thank you, soundtrack which I almost never otherwise pay attention to), and gameplay that lets you explore but never punishes you.  There is no way to make a mistake, or lose...it just might take you a little longer to get from A to B...and therein lies the fun!I am recommending this game to everyone I know and I hope to be gifting it to family and friends. If you want a game that's relaxing and yet rewarding, that does things differently and in a genius way, THIS is your game!I simply can't say enough good things about it.  Oh, and if you're playing, do yourself a favor...every so often look BACK at where you've been...it almost always look like a gorgeous piece of art!  And how many games can you say that about?
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: Another beautiful art game by the makers of Edith Finch. If you like art games, you don't even need to hesitate on pulling the trigger on this one. It is more than worth your money. They take the novel idea of "painting" the world around you to progress and it is incredibly well done. My only annoyance stems from the fact that there is mouse acceleration for KBM players; but this issue only pops up if you turn off Vsync.
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the first time I write a review after not even finishing the first gaming session (though I expect it to be possible to finish the game in one go).This is truly brilliant! I've played plenty of interesting puzzle/adventure games and I can tell from the first glance this one is going to be in my top favorites, even if it won't get much better than a few first levels. The mechanics feel fresh, which is surprising after seeing as I thought so many. I'm not going to spoil any of that, just as I didn't want to learn too much about this game and just jumped in instead. The game not only looks interesting and very artistic, it makes you feel like a part of the creation of this beauty by utilizing game mechanics. It's really up to you (to a point) how some parts of this world would look. Don't expect design or painting in the usual sense, but more of a "final touch" that you can make to the masterpiece. But it's not just that. The story telling is so beautiful too! I like all about it: the story itself, which immediately presents you with drama, adventure (escapism, if you please) a place to interpret the story your way and in a form of a really good old fairy tale. The voice acting and sound quality is so great it really brings me back to childhood.But enough of words, see it yourself! Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Unfinished Swan

_childDocuments_.review: The Unfinished Swan is a videogame about exploring the unknown. The player assumes the role of a young boy chasing after a swan who has wandered off into a surreal, unfinished kingdom. The game begins in a completely white space where players can throw paint to splatter their surroundings and reveal the world around them.
