_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, but on sale. If you have a controller. Firstly I'll say to play the demo first for yourself and see what you're getting into with it. I really wish more companies would do that. I really appreciate that they not only put out a demo for it but HOW they did it. The hour time limit didn't count toward the time that I spent in the story cutscenes which was actually really refreshing. I hate when you actually DO get a demo, and it's an hour long and has 30-40 minutes of cutscenes and dialogue in it so when you are done you only got about 20-30 minutes of actual gameplay. When I was through with the demo and closed it out I had over an hour and a half and I didn't spend a lot of time in settings, I went straight into the game and came straight out when I was done so that was how long the game let me play. So not sure if that was intended, but if it was, a giant kudos to 3DClouds, Team17 and crew for allowing the potential customers to actually play the product. Now onto the meat of the review. I enjoyed the game, but there are some big issues with it that I found frustrating. There is a HUGE grind wall, there is a Preston Garvey factor in the late game that made me want to beat Capt. D. Morgen to death, however combat can be insanely fun and I found myself giggling madly as I would kite a ship around into a tentacle trap in the environment and then unleash my "welcome to hell" skill to finish them off. The devs have mentioned adding quality of life support so maybe they're going to address some of the grindfest that exists, but man it is tedious at times.  My time logged is basically because I wanted the equipment from the fishing missions (not as fun as it sounds) and so I had to drag myself all over the map dozens of times trying to find the spots to get all the fish for the equipment for my other ships. Pros:*Pretty game*Combat can be insanely fun*Story isn't too bad, you can play as either the son or the daughter so you're not locked to the same character*Sid Meier's Pirates vibes all over the placeCons:*No/Limited Keyboard & Mouse support*With as much customization as you have for the ship, you never can get a super close look at it which is a shame*Can't change the direction of the camera when sailing (or it didn't work for me) makes the dashing skills a pain when moving south. You run into things because you can't seen them. *Fishing section is an absolute grind and feels incomplete. None of the ports actually have any of the fish in demand, they're always selling at a loss, so I never sold any of them until...*The port capturing game is to King of Seas what the settlement guarding mini-game was to Fallout 4 and Capt. D. Morgen quickly becomes the King of Seas Preston Garvey with "XXX invasion ships have been seen off xxx and will attack in 6 minutes!" messages popping up roughly every 10-15 minutes. And you HAVE to go to take care of those because even if the port is fully leveled up and maxed out they can be easily captured back by the merchants. That means the ~200k gold you sunk into fully upgrading that port is now lost because they don't know how to handle cannons. *insert Justin Timberlake blank stare meme* Normally you would say "well then I just won't capture anything else, problem solved!" Well no I'm afraid not my friend because your pirate friends will do capturing (for which you get messages for as well) and then those ports will be raided, and so on, and so on....And you can't turn that off. Any of it. The saving grace to that is that it's very late game so hopefully other players won't encounter it for as long as I did because I was being OCD with ship parts, but my god. TLDR: This game feels like it is a one ship at a time updated version of Sid Meier's Pirates so if you really enjoyed that one I'd snag this one on sale unless you really love the demo. The game needs work, but there is a lot of fun to be had unless you don't have a controller. Then you're left without a paddle.

_childDocuments_.review: My mini-review for 'King of Seas' features in my Indies of the Week video here:'King of Seas' is an action roguelite primarily played from a top-down perspective. You play the as one of two characters, both heirs to the throne. The king, your father is murdered, and you are blamed, so take refuge amongst pirates, as you seek to clear your name.  The majority of the game is spent aboard your ship, a meagre sloop to start with, as you navigate the treacherous seas and complete quests. You are able to dock at ports to buy supplies, upgrade your ship and speak to the locals.  The dynamic world is procedurally generated, so expect surprises with each play, whether it’s a kraken’s tentacle grabbing you from below or a volcano erupting from above. The wind can be your best friend, or worst enemy, and you will need to manage your sails to survive, one button opens them, another closes them.  Combat requires strategy as you attempt to outmanoeuvre enemy ships and claim their bounty. You fire cannons from both flanks, and can equip skills and talents to suit your playstyle.  The game is quite slow to get going, with initial objectives rather rudimentary and the world itself a little empty. However, once you get your sea legs, develop the story, upgrade you ship and discover hidden treasure, sailing the seven seas becomes quite an addictive experience, partly down to the roguelite elements of the game. 'King of Seas' is a highly polished experience. The graphics are gorgeous, particularly when docking on islands and using the camera zoom feature to bring you closer to the action. The music is suitably nautical, and the script full of intrigue and betrayal.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love King of Seas. I truly did - I played the demo over and over again loved it so much I pre-ordered it (something I rarely do for any game). Unfortunately having now played the official release the demo I feel didn't paint a fair picture of just how "grindy" the game actually is. Yes, it's an RPG. Yes, it's expected to have some grinding to it, but there is such a thing as "too much", and considering other reviewers echoing the same I'm clearly not alone. Perhaps if the grinding didn't involveso much getting x amount of x items to x location over and over again I'd enjoy it more, but the rate at which is does it makes this game feel more like a Pirate trading game than a pirate action game. On the plus side when there are battles they feel fantastic, and intense. If you're willing to deal with the grinding aspect of it, it might even be for you. After a couple hours though, I needed to request a refund (something I also rarely do). If you're interested in getting this game I'd recommend watching some let's plays to see if it's something for you before you commit.

The Gungeon has become a paradox and is collapsing! Blessed by the magic of the Sorceress, your gun will change rapidly as you ascend the Gungeon. name: Ageless
detailed_description: Lost, confused and alone. What will Kiara do when she suddenly finds herself with the power to control the age of flora and fauna? An ability that was bestowed onto her by a magical obelisk. Traverse a puzzle-platforming world unlike any other, full of myths and magic. Embark on an emotional journey where you will be faced with tough choices and must confront your inner demons. Follow Kiara as she is thrown into a world of wonder and heart ache. Manipulate the age of animals and plant-life as you find your way through intricate environmental puzzles and defeat the merciless bosses that stand in your way. Become Ageless: Equipped with a mystical bow, master the art of becoming Ageless. Dash off animals and plant-life to navigate through interesting puzzles and intricate platforming challenges. Unique Ageing Mechanic: Play with the laws of nature to control the age of animals and plants in order to progress through exciting levels. Not your Average Fairy-tale: In a tragic story of loss and personal discovery, Kiara must decide if she will use her newfound powers to face her inner demons or run from them. New Worlds to Discover: Explore new areas filled with unique plants and animals as you progress through the game. Each level is hand drawn to pixel perfection to create a beautiful world.

_childDocuments_.review: As it is, I cannot recommend Ageless to others, which is a shame because it's a very good idea, and it has good execution... in parts. I bought it because I saw someone play and because it reminded me of Celeste (which is admittedly a large shadow cast on this game). In any case, here are my pros and cons:Pros- Adorable art style- The player character controls tightly- The aging mechanic adds a lot of variety to the puzzles- The music ranges from good to great- The story and characters are fairly engagingCons- The game is littered with glitches, which become more and more apparent as you go further in the game, and often time can mess with the gameplay severely. Even the achievements are bugged- While the player character reacts tightly, the rest of the world can be very janky, leading to some puzzle solutions only working some of the time, even when taking the exact same steps. A large problem in a precision platformer, especially one in which the environment plays such a crucial role- The difficulty varies wildly from one puzzle to another from the second biome onward, with some puzzle taking me 10 seconds while others would take me up to 20 minutes right afterwards- A lot of the difficulty is due to things being placed awkwardly and hard to shoot at, requiring tiny jumps or seemingly pixel perfect placement which, rather than give a sense of accomplishment once beaten, is only frustrating, not helped by the combination of a lot of shooting while jumping or falling already- Story feels very rushed, with it going by leaps at a time. An example that stands out to me is when the protagonist discusses the deuteragonist with a NPC, saying that she knew him, but doesn't know who he's turning into; all this despite having only talked to him 4 times- Related to the above, the game is rather short, with only 5 different biomes to explore, and lacks any kind of postgame or bonus levelsShould the developers take steps to fix at least the glitches, janky environment and awkward placement, I would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% achievement No. Yes (6 achievements). No. is a puzzle platformer where you can increase and decrease the age of a lifeform. Different lifeforms have different stages of their lifetime in addition to different behavior. There are 5 main areas in total, featuring different lifeforms in each area.- Different lifeforms in each area give a fresh perspective to the game- Optional, harder levels to solve- Time-limited levels can be annoying to finish- Some levels require you to execute actions with precisionsIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650The visuals are alright. It uses 2D, sprite graphics with very little detail on the characters. Backgrounds have more details though, and the different theme in each area gives a variation to the mix. Personally, I liked the last area the most because of its mosaic presentation. However, the dialogue font looks out of touch with the rest of the game. I'm not sure if it's because the game fails to load the proper font or not since I'm not seeing the same font that is presented on the store page.The main character has a unique, relatable personality. It features a character that is not confident in herself, and although her negative perspective on things can be annoying sometimes, it works well on the ending. The subtle message will make it easier to reach more people, especially those who have the same personality as the main character. There are still some flaws in the storytelling, but it's not the main meat of the game anyway so you shouldn't worry much about it.The game is a puzzle platformer at its core with a focus on aging and de-aging lifeforms. Each lifeform has a specific usage on each of its life stages, allowing you to reach the previously inaccessible areas. Some lifeforms will also try to kill you, although they can still provide help in some way. The game features 5 main areas with different lifeforms, changing the game mechanics to some extent.Optional, harder levels are available in each area. The game is mostly linear, although some optional paths will be able to be reached as you progress, allowing you to tackle a harder level. You need to familiarize yourself with the existing mechanics to solve them, and it can take a while before you manage to do it since you need to re-learn everything in each area.The time-limited, "boss" levels ruin the game. It makes it hard to concentrate, especially since some areas have a very tight time limit. People who think fast might have no problem with this, but those who don't will be forced to do things by trial and error. Moreover, there is one problematic area that warps you to a place that you couldn't see on the other side, and since checkpoints in these types of levels are quite scarce, you are bound to redo the same area several times if you happened to be stuck.I finished the game in 13.1h. The game is easy at the beginning, although the optional and last few levels can prove to be problematic. Some solutions also might look impossible at first, but these kinds of solutions are usually not the intended ones. Most puzzles are of medium difficulty, with some requiring you to do some actions in precision. Luckily, the levels that need precise actions aren't at the same level as difficult puzzle games, although you might need to redo the level several times to develop muscle memory to solve them.The game doesn't save at the latest checkpoint. This can be problematic when you activated a checkpoint in the optional levels.Despite having a unique concept, I didn't feel anything special after playing . I feel like playing other puzzle platformers, which are mostly caused by the annoying time-limited levels and the different mechanics in each area. While I found the unique mechanic in each area a good addition to the game, I never feel like mastering the control. I always end up making mistakes whenever I wanted to age or de-age a lifeform and had to suffer because of that. The game is still good though, but I won't recommend it for a full price.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10I really like Ageless and I hope that in the future it'll find its target audience. Here are some remarks I made while reading other reviews:- If you feel like some levels are impossible: there is always an easier solution for every level and you've probably just overlooked it. I think the creators have really understood how to make a great and unique puzzle game that makes your own efforts feel really good. On the other hand I didn't have any problems with hit boxes or other character movements, so if you do then it's possible that some levels are nearly impossible.- If you're going to say that "this game is only one level repeating" or "bad story". Have you even played Ageless more than 2 hours? Did you even complete the tutorial? I don't say that you should've but don't act like you know everything about the game you haven't even played. There is so many different and interesting mechanisms during the journey and for example  is really rewarding in my opinion.- This last part goes for that one anonymous person who said that Ageless is too girl-gamer oriented: I'm sorry that this didn't resonate with your overflowing masculinity. Let's hope that in the future every game will be purely about WWII and that the only girl characters will have only as much personality as clothes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially Celeste Lite. It lacks a lot of the polish and fine detail of Celeste though, such as just talking about the character’s mental problems in the first minute instead of weaving an intricate story that doesn’t directly rely on that. The core gameplay is that the main character gets the ability to age living things up and down, and then she can become “ageless” thus the name and springboard or air dash off of any living object.  It’s an interesting concept though it feels like it’s a single note game, and there are just different enemies per chapter. There are a lot of difficulty spikes here as well, and oddly enough not in bonus rooms but on the main path.  However there are parts where Ageless feels awesome, but there are also a lot of parts where Ageless needed to get its controls or puzzles to be a little more developed. Pick this up if you loved Celeste, or just want a good platformer, though I would recommend getting Celeste over this.   If you’re not a fan of platformers, you’re probably not going to enjoy this one, even though it has a unique concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: In Ageless, you take control of a young woman named Kiara who is currently aimless and looking for a purpose or at least something that will let her get unstuck. A reason to keep moving. So she went to a place called Pandora to search for a Gate that is rumored to grant Gifts. The rumor foretells that if you find Pandora’s Gate, you’ll be granted a Gift that you need, not that you want. Well, it’s been three years since Kiara first started looking. The only thing keeping her from turning back is the fact that she already sunk in three years of her life searching, so she might as well continue or die trying.On the day you join Kiara on her journey, she comes across a huge gap that she tried to jump, either thinking she could make it or was just too distracted by her thoughts, that causes her to fall. When she comes to, she’s greeted by a young man named Vi who ventured into Pandora to look for the Gate. For Vi, he went out to get a Gift in hopes to help his gravely ill little sister that will die any day now. Vi already got his gift of being able to create portals and is heading out, but he assured Kiara that the Gate is close and maybe come visit his town. Well, funnily enough it was really close and she is gifted the ability to age or de-age plants and animals. With this new ability, she sets out to journey through a mysterious world to help Vi, his little sister, and anyone she may come across out.Each area you’ll be traveling through will require you to go through multiple puzzle rooms that you can’t continue before solving them. This will require you to use your newfound skills, platforming skills, and your knowledge of each aspect present if you want to move to the next room. The most important aspect is Kiara’s gift. To age or de-age something, you’ll need to make sure you have the arrow you need drawn and aim it right at them. Depending on the plant/animal and which age stage they’re at, they’ll interact with the world differently. The first animal you’ll come across is this ancient Rhino. A young Rhino is harmless and just wants to eat plants, but aging it up to Prime will transform it into a charging Rhino that can charge through weak walls and kill you if you’re not careful. Early puzzles are pretty easy, but they become harder as you go on as platforming becomes tougher (partly since you’ll need to be precise and fast at times) and figuring out what you need to do with each plant/animal in the room takes longer.Kiara can also become ageless, which will stop time around her for a few seconds. In this mode, if Kiara is touching something that she can age, she can actually launch herself with the energy that is given by de-aging it. This lets her jump distances that she won’t be able to without it. Since what she’s touching launches the opposite direction, you can also launch what you’re touching if needed, though make sure you’re not going to launch yourself into spikes. Don’t worry if you do die, you’ll just respawn at the last checkpoint (which is put at the beginning of each room).If you’re worried about this becoming stale, Ageless does a good job at keeping it fresh. Not only will each area you go to differ based on aesthetics, but what animals and plants show up, how those animals/plants react to the world, and the gimmicks that it has. The next area you go to, Remnant, is a lush forest with gates requiring you to collect three butterflies, dolphins that you can ride during its Prime, and a plant that you can bounce off of or fire thorns depending on the age. One of my favorite areas appears late in the game, but I will say that the gimmick tied with it involves becoming a ghost to bypass walls or enemies.Ageless offers players to play it with a keyboard and mouse or with a controller, with no listed preference that the game might work better with. “But why mention this since most games offer this option” I hear you thinking. Well, while this is going to depend on your preference, there are pros and cons depending on which one you’ll be using that will affect gameplay more than some other puzzle platformers. Considering that the main mechanic is using your bow to age or de-age something, using a mouse will give you more control. Using a controller won’t give you as much control and you can easily throw your arrows off by slightly moving the stick right before releasing, but time does slightly slow down while aiming and you can see the path the arrow will take rather than only the reticle you’re aiming with. Personally, I played the whole game with a controller, with the occasional use of a mouse as some puzzle rooms are more difficult to complete when using a controller.There are collectibles that you can find and try to get. Most areas have Relics hidden around, which are just yellow capital A’s, that you can only see when you’re in ageless mode. Some Relics will be in a main puzzle room, while most will require you to enter a hidden room. To get to these, you have to first figure out how to solve the room puzzle (or find a way to get to Relics placed in required rooms), grab them in ageless mode, and make it to a checkpoint before you die. Each relic you collect will color in one more aspect of a diorama of that area, which you can get to through the overworld map. You can also use the overworld map to check on how many Relics you need left per area and select which part you want to jump to (though you do need to guess where you possibly missed a Relic).All in all, I enjoyed my time with Ageless. It was really creative building a game around aging and de-aging animals and plants and it keeps it up with each area. The story, while not delved into as much here, is engaging and has some surprises throughout. The only frustrations I had was how precise and fast you’ll need to be with some puzzles, as with those puzzle rooms I often knew what I had to do, but I was just slightly off. So if you’re someone that avoids puzzles that require you to be really precise, this might not be for you even if many puzzles don’t require it as much. For those that play with a controller, or thinking about buying this on the Switch, another con comes in as the aiming can get in your way of completing puzzles.If you’re at all interested in Ageless, but not exactly sure if you’ll like it, you can still try out the demo before committing to a purchase. The demo starts right after Kiara receives a Gift and ends once you finish Pandora. I certainly would not have picked this up as quickly without the demo.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: As one of those indie darlings I was really looking forward too, I have to admit I was heartbroken here.  With a cool mechanic and premise on board, I truly expected this to be one of my faves of the year.  Unfortunately, with gameplay and control mechanics that seemed to try and cater to controller and keyboard/mouse platformer players, it ended up missing the mark on both.  The puzzles were extremely easy in some areas, only to be frustratingly specific in the next.  It created this chaos in a balanced challenge that ultimately forced me to give up on entirely on taking different paths. Aging and de-aging plants and animals is an incredibly novel idea, but when forced to make direct shots while mastering the game's platforming, it became a chore.  Although only logging just under a couple of hours into Ageless,  I got a clear idea that this was not a game I could wrap myself around.  Love the simple pixel art and pleasing, if not memorable, soundtrack, but there was too many faults that I just couldn't ignore here.  Great concept with a messy execution.  With a little bit of polish, this may be something I can jump back into.  As is, Ageless definitely feels like too many unrefined ideas.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about half way through, but I've found the controls to be very frustrating.  Specifically wasd feels too imprecise for how "tuned" some of the puzzles seem to be.  That or I beat some of the puzzles in the wrong way...  Normally I don't mind the platforming being very challenging, but for whatever reason in this game I just find it to be frustrating.  Further some of the puzzle solutions aren't telegraphed / taught before hand and are just thrown into an already challenging situation.  Specifically  As far as the story goes it seems interesting and touches on topics that have depth to them.  I intend to finish this game, just going to have to take breaks when the controls get too frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: After a bit of bowing and wall jumping, you'll get a bow and dash jump, and then you need to master timings... to spend much more time collecting hidden relics. Naturally, Ageless is a platformer game where you use the ability to change some 'live' objects to get yourself further. The fate of those supposedly 'live' creatures is not of your concern, of course. You just have the power to use them to your liking. Hmmm... It's not a bad game, it doesn't look bad, but... it's losing the catch after only a short while. So, in my very subjective opinion, it's not really that much engaging, mediocre platformer which I got as a bonus in some bundle. I can give it a 5.9/10 mark, but I doubt I'll start it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, and I was pleasantly surprised. The controls feel on par with what you'd expect from a precision platformer, and the gameplay was good throughout: with some creative uses of its core mechanics, some unexpectedly dynamic boss battles, and a good enough system that it's sometimes possible to find seemingly unintended solutions to puzzles.My two gripes would probably be the narrative, which feels a bit rushed until about the halfway point (sidenote: I wish there was more of a bridge between chapters, instead of essentially being teleported to the next area), and that some sections can toe the line of overstaying their welcome - though I don't think it ever quite crossed it.Ageless isn't revolutionary, but it's a good time for fans of platformers in general, and of puzzle platformers especially.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a better score, so I had to write this review.Ageless is puzzle platformer which is more puzzle than precise jumping. The main mechanic, aging, is very cool and made me very excited every time I started a new world to see the many life stages of it's inhabitants, but it doesn't stop at that: as the game progress, it becomes even more interesting, with some extremely cool mechanics that created some very clever puzzles. While the difficulty tend to fluctuate (even in the last world some puzzle were extremely simple), it very rarely gets annoying. The platforming also tends to be pretty easy once you figure out the puzzle, with very few rooms were the precision needed feels aggravating.What I liked most about the game, though, is that the puzzles give a lot of freedom. Too many times, puzzle games tend to be very strict in their required solutions, which tends to be very frustrating if you're missing something: this makes the player feel like they have no freedom to experiment and stops them from being creative. Ageless isn't as strict: every puzzle has an intended solution, but, thanks to its mechanics, many times the player can find a different and sometimes even better solution. This can make the player feel very clever, making the game very satisfying.The game is not perfect, as the controls might take a while to get used to them; the story is a bit simplistic and underdeveloped, but it still makes the game better than without it and never gets in the way for too long. There are also some weird things, like the "voice acting" which can feel a bit annoying or the fact that one area has an extra collectable that isn't counted by the game, but they honestly just give more charm to the game. The only issue that annoyed me was the later bosses, which can feel very try and error and make any mistake too costly.In conclusion, Ageless is a very cool game: it has some very interesting mechanics that keep the player engaged and the level design can lead the player to outsmart the game, making the experience very rewarding. Music and graphics are also well done and contribute to make the game very charming and fresh, deserving a try by any puzzle and platformers fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Unlikable characters, frustrating, unprecise, lagging(to sit on a fish you have to be in ideal position, eventhough game says just to press "E")  controls, sometimes bad level design, poorly executed bosses(the tree one straight up killed me few times after respawn). Overall not really worth your time
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this game needs a review.If you want to play this game for the story rather than gameplay, get Celeste and forget about this one. If it's the opposite, however, get this one on sale or borrow it from a friend (and then play Celeste if you want)I actually liked this game, but honestly the mixed reviews are well deserved.The gameplay is pretty good, even more so if you get the relics in case you're looking for a challenge... the physics, however, can be quite annoying: they feel wonky ( wonky) and it can take a while to get accostumed to them. The mechanics are quite simple, even if they look a bit strange you grasp them in no time.The level design, now  is where it gets interesting, and the only reason I'm actually recommending the game: The level design is , no level feels useless, very dynamic, sometimes action packed and sometimes a stop and think puzzle, no single mechanic is left unteached and none are without a relic challenge, with each passing chapter bringing you a new change in the mechanics, even if the base is the same.So, everything seems good so far, but the game mas  reviews, not good ones... well, the wonkiness in the mechanics can be quite the make or break, but even above that there's something even worse... the story.I'll cut to the chase: The story sucks. A lot. I've seen lots of good stories, average ones and even bad ones. This spans from novels (very few though) to light novels to story rich games. This game doesn't have a bad story per-se, but it's at best average. I'd personally give it a below average, only because the bar  be that low. It's too simplistic, the character development feels terrible and rushed and the ending, while it technically makes sense, it feels like they just threw the entire story out the window and axed whatever build-up they had. Cringe inducing but passable at best, horrible story at worst. It's not even a matter of saying it's "messed up" or something of the like, it's just... bad. It just sucks. And to make matters worse, they tried to tie up loose ends and ended up leaving everything hanging, just without those previous loose ends.tl;dr If you want to enjoy gameplay, it'll be worth the while. Story? Run away and don't look back.EDIT: On the time of writing this review the game had mixed reviews, hence the first sentence.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Got it with HumbleBundleDont let the childish artstyle and dialogue fool you - this game is very hard/precise.The frequent savepoints make it bearable.On the second boss fight (I am stuck in second phase) there should be more.Some relics (collectibles) are ridiculously hard to get. Sometimes its the players fault for using the abilities wrong, but often its just unforgiving placement of spikes and janky mechanics.I recommend it to masochistsMy left hand hurtsEdit: Your left has to do so much at once -on top of holding/pressing left/right not 0.1 sec too long/short or guess what, you just hit a spike.When you are in timeless mode you sometimes have a different hitbox than in normal mode - this makes you fall off ledges.Some jumps/sequences are so hard you just resort to "cheesing" the encounter by switching the creatures age - which sometimes is also wanted from you which makes it a bit confusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a solid concept that it sticks to and evolves with new ways to play with its ageing mechanics that some players will be genuinely surprised at how smart the puzzles become. But, I cannot help but feel the game is missing that final polish, that spark that puts it on the same pedestal as Celeste and a few others. There are some irritating issues with the controls, which spoil what would otherwise be a quality puzzle platformer. I can say that fans of the genre will entertain with what Ageless delivers, and anyone who enjoys a challenging game, if sometimes frustrating, will find something to like here.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless is a puzzle-platformer where you use special powers in order to change the ages of living creatures to help you along the way. The game is fairly light on tutorials, and expects you to pick things up quickly, which is a boon and a flaw at times.Some more advanced mechanics of the game are left unexplained for you to learn through either trial or error, or a walkthrough, and it adds even more to the frustration of the puzzles with how reliant they are on precise aiming at times.The real amusement in the game comes from the writing, and how enjoyably bad it is. There are quite a lot of lines of dialogue that are just so far out there that I couldn't help but laugh, and I'll be honest, it helped me get through the game.The game has collectables in the form of "Relics", that add colour to some dioramas in Relic Island, but as far as I am aware, they do not affect anything else with regards to the story and, imo, they're not really worth getting if you don't care about 100% completion.All in all, this game is frustrating, but you'll get a few laughs out of it if you don't take it seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Got as part of a bundle.  It's been a while since I've rage quit a game.  There's a difference between challenging and punishing.  At times this feels punishing.  A prime example is the second boss: You need to keep moving constantly, which causes issues because there are also stationary things that can kill you if they hit your finicky hitbox.  As you move through the stage, you need to immediately have an idea of what part of the puzzle you will do next.  While also dodging attacks.  While also not touching the spikes.  While also not drowning after expending a full five seconds of oxygen.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The game is okay. It is by no means worth anywhere near $15.Pros:-The music isn't bad-Interesting puzzle mechanic-Visually appealingCons:-Floaty controls-The bosses aren't bosses, they're tedious obstacle courses-Janky hit boxes make the game very frustrating when completing puzzles-In the Vestige stage the boss frequently won't appear at all-Cut scenes go on for way too long-The sound of Protagonist speaking sounds like a whining five year old, making every cut scene even harder to get through-Story is confusing even when watching through the cut scenes-Uses the same puzzles over and over and over again-Artificially difficult-Roughly 60% of the game is just trying to complete the Relic puzzles (Hidden items you are highly encouraged to obtain)-No reason to play more than onceI would be fine if the game was free. A dollar even. But as of now, it is still sitting at a steep $15 price tag. Please polish it up and maybe it would be worth $5. Please don't get this game until they cut the price down. _childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless is a story driven puzzle platformer where you must alter the age of animals and plant life around you to progress. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend it to others, which is a shame, because it has some nice features, especially the idea of alteration of animals' ages. The difficulty varies wildly from one puzzle to another with some puzzles taking me 10 seconds while others taking me 1 hour. The controls are quite glitchy and have weird interactions with the poor environment, which may lead to some puzzle solutions not working all the time, which is problematic for a precision platformer. 5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Charming Aesthetics, Challenging FrustrationsAgeless offers a visually delightful experience with its charming graphics and intriguing mechanics. The game's art style complements its gameplay, drawing players into a world where the mechanics themselves become a key part of the appeal. Additionally, the storyline weaves an entertaining narrative, adding depth to the overall experience.However, despite its visual appeal and engaging story, Ageless encounters significant hurdles in its gameplay. Some levels become excessively frustrating due to either bugs or an overreliance on pixel-perfect precision. This can lead to a sense of unfairness, causing more irritation than challenge.Moreover, the boss battles exacerbate this frustration by requiring players to flawlessly execute pixel-perfect actions from start to finish. This design choice can become incredibly aggravating, as any minor mistake forces a full restart, testing the patience of even the most dedicated players. It feels punishing rather than genuinely challenging, detracting from the enjoyment of the game.Regrettably, these gameplay issues overshadow the game's positive aspects. Despite its endearing visuals and engaging storyline, the frustrating levels and punishing boss mechanics make it difficult to recommend Ageless to others. Unless one has a high tolerance for these specific types of challenges or enjoys masochistic gameplay, the overall experience might not align with most players' expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a Celeste inspired puzzle game, where the main protagonist shoots magic arrows to age or de-age creatures to solve puzzles. All around a brilliant concept! However there are some issues...Like many other puzzle games there are great puzzles and then there are some less than great puzzles, ageless is no exception. There were some puzzles I really liked and there were some puzzles that were very sooooo annoying.In general usual puzzle stuff, when it shows you the new mechanic it’s easy, then once you know it, it gets harder. In general the main path through the game is normal difficulty with hard points here and there. Most of the difficulty is due to the millisecond timing and the pixel perfect aiming. The boss's also sucked.A lack of polish is very prevalent, there is a lot of fine tuning that still needs to be done. There are a lot of graphical glitches along with many game breaking bugs.I think most of the negative reviews are because of the price because for most people price = expectations. I think for $18, people expect a little more. If I didn’t receive this game in a bundle I would have never bought it.I enjoyed my time with this game, I really liked the main mechanic. However in the game's current condition I would say wait for another update, then buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game dries out pretty quickly. It's got a somewhat interesting mechanic and then it pads it out for so long. There are so many puzzles that feel really vague and I end up solving them in ways that feel incorrect because they don't always give you much guidance on how to approach them. The characters feel like typical tropes with the way they talk and sound, but the main reason I dropped it is out of pure boredom. Not a terrible game, has some good graphics, but becomes a yawnfest pretty fast.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually write reviews for two reason: the game is surprisingly good or even exceptional and I have to say something about it, or the game is so bad that I feel the need to caution other people against wasting their time or money.This isn't either of those cases. But currently the game sits at a Mixed rating, and I think it deserves more.Let's get straight to the point: this game isn't perfect, far from it. As others have pointed out, the story isn't great (but by no means bad,) and the generous collisions, rather than the controls, make things frustrating at times. There are some quirks to the controls too, but nothing you won't get used to in 20 minutes tops.The pixel art is pretty, but... it's a bit over the place. It seems like a collection of vaguely cohesive assets that come from slightly different games. Art direction is definitely the weakest part of this game's presentation.The puzzles themselves is where the game really shines. After the tutorial, you will obtain a bow that can shoot two types of arrows: one that ages living things, the other that makes them younger, and each of the multiple stages the creatures have behave differently in relation to both the character and the environment. You can also enter a state called Ageless, where everything but you freezes, and if you touch any living creature, you can boost away from it in any direction by consuming some of the creature's age. You will have to use these powers to manipulate life around you and reach the end of every screen.Each of the several areas has its own unique creatures that behave in strange and interesting ways, and new mechanics are introduced on top of this enemy variety, like teleporting or death/rebirth. And there are A LOT of levels, both mandatory and optional. Some of these rooms stretch the various interactions between your character and the environment to the extreme, pushing the limits of what you thought was the extent of programmed functionality. I was surprised by "oh, so this and this together do that" several times throughout the game. And just wait till the last area, where !Now, yes, bosses are chases for the most part, and I usually hate those in games... But for some reason they worked for me here. I think that's because the bosses themselves feel like chains of puzzle rooms, just longer ones and with less checkpoints; a natural extension of the puzzles you've done up to that point rather than a curve ball.In short, this is a game that I would recommend only to puzzle-platformer lovers, as it's quite long and hard, but some of the ideas and interactions are just brilliant and need to be seen if you're into this sort of stuff. And if you already like the genre, you'll have plenty to chew on with Ageless. If you go in knowing that it's much more puzzle than platformer, and that it could've definitely used some more time in the oven, I think you'll have a good time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the generic title and arthouse-fodder gimmick fool you. This game has great visuals, great music and overall great gameplay. It doesn't overstay its welcome and constantly throws new gimmicks at you. Be warned, though, even some mandatory puzzles as early as midway through the game will have puzzle game newbies stumped. My only quibbles are that some of the controls are finicky, some of the timing is nearly frame-perfect, and some things are unintuitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice puzzling platformer, however there are a few major issues remaining in the game.- Delaying the ability to fire arrows for the purpose of animations is a mistake in my opinion. If puzzles are designed to be solved with quick actions then you should not delay a player's actions for "cool animations".- Boss battles should be tuned for the level of progress the players have made in the game so far. As it stands, only 12% of players have finished the first world and only 6% of players have finished the second world. The 2nd world boss in particular is unforgiving and there is a section that was basically hand crafted to be solved only a single way instead of allowing the player to climb the boss' arms.- Vestige has a section in the game where only 14 relics are tracked, when there are actually 15 relics to be acquired. The fact that players have to go out of their way to figure out which relic wasn't tracked isn't a nice experience.I enjoyed the game, however I cannot recommend it to most players since they would probably not make it past the 2nd boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The ideas that aren't lifted from other puzzle platformers get a few moments of intrigue before they become overused. Otherwise, Ageless is worth very little of your time. The game is shrouded in inconsistency and bursting with weak puzzles that are only challenging in how unreliable it is to execute their solutions. Like stale bread, it’s dry, hard to swallow, and representative of something much better.I constantly considered abandoning it out of boredom and mild irritation only to reluctantly continue playing due to the same sympathy that drove others to post consolation reviews. The ideas change, but polish and ingenuity remain bog-standard throughout. Take a glance at the achievement statistics for some perspective on the game's retention.Ageless doesn't entirely deserve its startlingly low steam rating, but I can't in good conscience recommend something so unabashedly unremarkable. Sadly, receiving it as filler for a Humble Bundle seems like the most appropriate context to find Ageless in.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I was talking to a friend about this game and I'm pretty sure I said I liked it and hated it in the same breath, accidentally, which really sums it up. I love the concept, and the relatively minimalist presentation, as well as the lack of overly complex UI, HUD and in depth systems; it knows what it is, and doesn't reach beyond that. At the same time the controls don't feel quiiiiiiite precise enough, some of the hitboxes are completely off and while a minor flaw, the text boxes for the 'story' are massive, way too jarring for what they are trying to convey. Solid maybe on this one, worth a try but only if on half off or better. I wanted to love it and will probably play it through as it seems quite short, but found it way more frustrating than anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Hmmm... the idea looks nice and pixel art is cool, BUT the game wants you to to stand pixel perfect A LOT. I was in a position where i couldn't do something just because i wasn't standing in the pixel perfect spot that was  required to hit some baby rhino... I've tried for 10 minutes, than went back to previous screen and came back, and than i was able to hit it from the first try.... Later i die in the same screen and the frustration of finding perfect spot starts again... this made the whole experience of a potentially very good game into a frustrating pixel perfect garbage! There are some games that require this kind of precision, but usually its part of their core game play and its kind of fun and challenging. This - this is just a pure frustration. Not recommended at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been a great little game. I like the visuals, the idea is great and original and there are a lot of different puzzles to solve.The problem is that puzzles quickly become time sensitive and you must be very precise to pass them. Just that would still be alright for me, as it's a challenge I'm ready to accept. But the game lacks proper psychics and especially has a lot of bugs with inputs. I've seen discussions about different problems and many times I died because the game didn't take my input so didn't do the action I wanted to do pressing the right button. I couldn't take it anymore as a challenge is one thing, but dying over and over again because the game can't work properly, it's too much. Too bad, I would have liked to finish this, and maybe one day I will if it gets the patch it's really needing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good puzzle game. But there are some parts of the game where you are forced to speed run from a boss. In these instances you will realize how annoying some glitches are such as riding the dolphins. When you approach the creature to ride it, the toggle button appears. However you may press the button 5 to 6 times before the action occurs. This is not a one time occurrence but almost every time you attempt to engage with the creature. After posting on the message boards, the developers still have not fixed this problem. If the developers ever fixed the bugs and glitches it would be a much better game. Until then I can not recommend this game and I will no longer play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Far too reliant on absolutely pixel perfect platforming and precision timing. Not even the slightest errors are allowed in the beginning and that's before you even get to the intense chase part (which you encounter very prematurely in the demo too). It has beautiful, emotional music and a wonderful aesthetic, atmospheric and pixel art in general but it's way too frustrating to play. There are checkpoints in every area so far but that still doesn't stop it being immensely unforgiving ironically.Also, early on in the first world, you can permanently miss a relic if you choose to smash a wall and go right, instead of using the animal to boost upwards. It's somewhere early in Act 4 and luckily I was able to replay it and get it anyway but the lack of indication of this a risk nor a method to get back was also very frustrating.I really wanted to love this, but I cannot recommend it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: cannot recommend, way too punishing in few places. Difficulty skyrockets out of nowhere. Devs should review those places and either make it easier for everyone or add an opt-in easy more. For the most obvious example, second stage of boss for Remnant is a punishing nightmare with almost non-existent margin for error. You have to nail the whole of it in one big sequence under time pressure, no checkpoints in-between. Some might call it challenging, I definitely call it punishing beyond any reasonable expectation. I passed it (as evident by the achievement), but it took me maybe 60+ attempts to do that, and when I did, it felt more like a pure dumb luck. I would consider myself ok-ish at platformers, I shudder to think what experience would I have if I wouldn't be.It's made even worse by the fact that some of the actions glitch very frequently, like mounting a level 3 fish (dolphin), while some other actions (jumping on plants that kick you up) can be very counter-intuitive - in order to trigger jump you need to move in direction of flower, but if you don't let go of that control immediately at the right moment and your jump is in the opposite direction, it will get messed up.I was always wondering how people can get so frustrated with any sort of game as to throw controllers or break keyboards. Now I think I understand them a little better.Update: finished it, including getting all relics. Still wouldn't recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst the game is interesting, there are issues that need to be addressed.1. In the Remnant boss fight there are issues of the boss attacking before your screen has returned to your checkpoint.2. I would also recommend (for those who try find everything,) that you split the relic count between the sub worlds, so individuals can find their missing relics easier.3. I also just have to draw attention that this game, while interesting in concept, feels a bit heavy handed with the message they are trying to convey.Even though I enjoyed the concept, I can't recommend buying it the way it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to leave a brief recommendation as a counterpoint to the negative reviews. This game is a really good puzzle platformer with unique ideas and mechanics. I cannot share the common criticisms in the reviews at all. The controls are fully functional, the platforming is tight, the aiming system works fine both with controller and mouse. The difficulty and learning curve is fine. There are a few reviews of people with less than an hour or two in the game complaining about pixel precise alignments etc. These people are, no point in mincing words, just wrong and didn't understand the room they were in and missed a mechanic or alternative way to progress, which is pretty normal and even encouraged to exist in a puzzle platformer. I can confidently say, 5h in and not really getting stuck anywhere, that no room required an absurdly precise solution that the controls didn't support.  I find it a shame that the game went far enough under the radar that a few of those reviews bring the rating of this little gem down so heavily.It shines when the various mechanics combine and open up the solution space dramatically. I'm playing together with a friend and the amount of times we found quite different solutions from each other is surprising. One optional room stands out where after a back and forth of ideas we ended up with six different ways to solve the puzzle, all distinctly different from each other. The game isn't a masterpiece and has some minor issues, none of which have detracted majorly from my positive experience. Sometimes it's a bit unclear how close the ageless dash needs to be to a target. The escapes are a bit trial and error because of the time pressure and checkpoints being more scarce, but aren't a massive difficulty spike and fulfill their function of changing up the gameplay for a bit as well as progressing the narrative. The biggest problem for me is that I missed one relic in an area, know which one it is, visually, in the relic garden, but can't do anything with that information to find it. The best thing I could do is check back every single room which I'm not interested in doing.All in all, this game is way better than its small and mediocre reviewing would indicate. In the indie puzzle platformer genre which I'm quite fond of, I'd rate it 4/5, under the absolute highlights like Celeste which I'm sure was a big inspiration, but it's definitely a good game worth the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: What the hell is with those incredibly nitpicky negative reviews? It's a cool little game, with smart, original puzzle design and charming visuals. It's well worth your time. It could use a bit more leeway when it comes to timing in some areas, and the controls could use some tightening up, but that's it! People can be so unreasonably negative when it comes to games included in Humble Choice or Kickstarted games.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: played so many side scrolling pixelated games, they all mess up the recipe somewhere; too hard, too cliched, too filled with nonesense or mindlessness, too slow, too repetitive. This one somehow gets all the ingredients and portions right. Challenging but achievable. quick paced. smart mechanics that are easy to learn and use and don't get too old too quick.I have zero investment into the game world or lore or anything, but it's fun dumb fun, so keeping it.sucks that it doesn't have cloud saves.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Take Celeste and subtract 3 from the score.   9/10?  This is 6/10. I recommend it to people who enjoy this genre and want more after playing the heavy hitters.  Its fun...but its also like playing Street Fighter 2 in the year 2021 when you've gotten used to games like Street Fighter 4 (or presumably 5 but I haven't played that one). The controls feel 'fine' but worse.  Jumps are floaty.  The control scheme works but the flow and polish just isn't there.  The graphical art style is a big miss for me but mileage may vary.  I found puzzles to be very good early on but as they demanded more and more precision I found myself getting more annoyed than having a good time.  I ultimately didn't finish the game but I understand the appeal and would genuinely recommend it to fans of the genre as I said.  I'm NOT a fan of the genre in general...so my enjoyment of Celeste stands out as an exception and not the norm.    I can only assume others will cling on to this game a bit better than I did. _childDocuments_.review: Initially I was very charmed with this puzzle platformer. You play a girl who gains the power to change the age of plants and animals, which also changes their behavior. A young tree can be used to catapult yourself through the air for example, while older trees can lift you up with their roots. This mechanic works very well and is used to create some clever puzzles in a beautiful pixelated game world.Sadly the controls and hit boxes aren't as good as they should be (at least on the Steam Deck). As a result, I often knew how to solve a certain puzzle, but it still took me lots of tries to execute it correctly because my character did something else than I intended.While this is only slightly annoying during the puzzle sections, this becomes a huge problem in the "escape" sequences where you are being chased by fast moving deadly objects. Not only are these sections ridiculously difficult compared to the rest of the game, but they are also very frustrating because of the controls and hit box issues. While I loved the escape sequences in the Ori games, they made me uninstall Ageless out of pure frustration. Such a shame...

_childDocuments_.review: In my quest to 100% the achievements for each game in my library, I quickly stumbled across Ageless. I believe I had received it in a past Humble Bundle or some other bundle because I do not recall purchasing the game standalone. To be frank, the $14.99 price is absurd. The game has no where near enough content nor is polished enough to warrant that price tag. Pick it up if it ever goes under $5 (and only if you like the concept).The game itself is a fun puzzle platformer, however the fun quickly disappears when you run into one of the game's many mechanical bugs; movement is sloppy and choppy, so expect to die often when you shouldn't. Coupled with some rather gruesomely precise puzzles, you will quickly want to pull your hair out. The disparity between "levels" is massive; one second a puzzle will be a simple jump and the next it will be a complicated set of moves with no room for error. Furthermore, end stages for each world have to be completed in a sort of marathon; when you factor in the rough controls, these stages become extremely tedious. Overall, the game has charm and a cool pixel art style. The concept behind the ending is quite cool. Some semblance of a story is there, but it feels like I'm reading a self-help book half the time. Also, do yourself a favor and turn down dialogue, its painfully obnoxious. The characters just moan incessantly.Anyway, I'd only suggest buying this game if you want to smash your keyboard or monitor (or both). If you like puzzle platformers this may be a game you'd like, but heed my and other users' warnings about the quality of controls and mechanics. If they were to fix the aforementioned issues, the game would still be a no for full price, but a for sure grab it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: === First look === [90 minutes in]At very first the game seems like a cheap clumsy platformer. IT IS WAY MORE THAN THAT.DO NOT LET THE FIRST MINUTES GIVE YOU THE WRONG IMPRESSION. AT FIRST I THOUGHT THE GAME WOULD BE PLAIN AND BORING, BUT I WAS WRONG.Somewhere around 15 minutes to half an hour the game begins to unlock it's potential. The game has really cool unique puzzles. Most games do puzzles wrong. This is not one of those games.The puzzles feel like Portal all over again. You get to experiment with new stuff and come up with creative solutions. I love that feeling.Absolutely recommended thus far.The story seems to be picking up too.I will admit movement sometimes feels a bit clumsy. But when you get past the first part, that doesn't matter so much, and you'll start to get the hang of it anyways.DO PLAY THIS GAMEIf you love Portal // unique creative puzzle games, and you are in speaking terms with platformers, you will have a good time with this one.=== Update === [3 hours in]The game continues to be great in my eyes. That portal-esque feeling of solving puzzles your own way is just wonderful. Priceless to me. The story is... alright. Graphics are rather pretty. Not much to complain about, really. Lacks some polish I guess, but in a way that just makes the game more authentic, and it does NOT bother me in the slightest.=== A rant about Portal === [4 hours in]What made Portal such an amazing experience for me is how intentionally broken game it is. There are literally millions of ways to break the game. Clitches, short-cuts, bunny-hopping, skipping stuff, forcing the mechanics to go crazy, combining them in ways that make no sense, taking items where you should not, building a tower out of bodies, making your own weird challenges ... just doing stuff in ways the devs never meant it to be done. You get to come up with something yourself. There are no correct solutions to the puzzles, which makes them more natural. And even when there are correct solutions, that just means it will be ever so much more satisfying to find one that definitely isn't the correct one.Why is this relevant? I think Ageless achieves the same feeling. I can do whatever I want, I can break the game and it's puzzles in so may ways, and love breaking them every time. Granted, you could argue that here it is probably less intentional than with Portal. The game breaks since it lacks polish, not because it is meant to work that way. While that certainly is true to some extent, the end result is the same. This game makes me really happy, and I love it.=== Update === [7 hours in]The game is a gem. Ageless gem hahahahahaa. No, but seriously. I love this game. I absolutely get why some people might not like Ageless, but I do.The game continues to add new mechanics (to break) in nice ways. Maybe it's just me, but I love breaking puzzles and the whole game in creative ways.The story still is a bit lacking, but tolerable, and at points kind of cute in a way.

_childDocuments_.review: Lives may be threads, but you determine which part of that thread each life is on.To see Ageless in action, watch my gameplay video. Your power is to choose what part of the lifespan every living being is in. Is it young? Is it old? Will you steal a part of its life force to empower yourself? Ageless's plot is one of generic introspection (at least to start), but its puzzle mechanics are a breath of fresh air. Each room presents a new challenge. Some are easy. Some are painfully difficult to execute. And plenty are optional for the casual player while demanding the best from completionists. And the music is soothing.I'm not sure if it's the controls, or if timing is tighter than it should be, but Ageless is painfully difficult at times even in its first level.  Each room includes a checkpoint, so you're quickly back to your next attempt, but something in the combination of control and difficulty make Ageless intimidating to get into. Left Trigger rewinds time, Right Trigger accelerates time, and X enters Ageless Mode where you'll either exit via X again or dash via A. On paper it should be fine, but the speed with which these mechanics are introduced, combined with unforgiving timing windows, kicks Ageless to the timeless difficulty of older games right off the bat.There's a good game here for players willing to explore it, and timing is so tight that I would love to see a speedrun someday.

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless looks like . The story is very like. But Ageless fails to nail the one thing that made —and other high-profile platformers—really stand out: the controls. And it’s a shame, really. Some of these puzzles were very well designed. There are a lot of gems here, especially in the more difficult side objectives. The gist of it is the following: levels have animals and plants which you can age up or down, each age group having different properties and effects. And Ageless lets you figure things out. And it works. There are many clever puzzles, interesting solutions, and fun mechanics. The first area, by far the most basic, for example: you can age a plant up or down, raising or lowering a platform. There’s another plant that is eaten by the animal. The animal starts as an egg, ages into a tiny creature which slowly moves towards food, then into a rhino that chases you, breaking walls in the progress, then becomes fat and slow, destroying platforms below it. There are other mechanics that keep interactions fresh. You can stop time, dash out of every creature and plant, de-aging them in the process and propelling them backwards. The Titan area has teleporting, which is also used in clever ways. The Spectre has zones where you can die and come back to life. All of these are used in novel and fun ways. The final area has… timed puzzles, which aren’t very good, especially in levels where you can’t really see everything in the same screen.The bosses were fun and tense. I enjoyed them for the most part, though I’ve noticed a lot of people complaining about them, so your mileage may vary. They seemed to be harder than even the side levels, so if you hadn’t been completing them as you go along, they might be a little frustrating.And that’s it for the good.There’s lots of strange flaws. Wall jumping sounds weird, and I’m sure the devs noticed it. If you do it fast enough, most of the audio just won’t play. The dolphin animal in the second world is incredibly annoying—you seem to have to spam a button to mount it, regardless of whether the prompt is on screen. This makes puzzles in the final section of the game, where all the mechanics come back, a lot more irritating. The final area is probably the worst part of the game, too. A lot of the triumph over finding clever solutions to puzzles is lost, as the insect from the final section can be exploited whenever it is on screen—some puzzles end up with a lot of unused elements because you can pretty much skip them. The timed puzzles where you have to throw the guy around are annoying and not a very entertaining ending to a game with such great puzzles. It left a sour taste in my mouth. But the worst sin of all are the controls and movement. The controls are so floaty and inprecise. Controller aiming is annoying and weirdly sticky. It’s an unforgivable flaw—platformers need to at least adhere to some standard of control and feel. Ageless’ gimmick isn’t that it’s floaty and has weird hitboxes, it’s the interesting, well thought-out, puzzles. Of course, I’m sure it’d be too much work to test every single puzzle if they tweak the movement. Ageless isn’t a twitch reflex fast-paced platformer, as some people seem to think, but there are some tight jumps here and there which could break if movement changes. But it’s the only way this game would get a recommendation from me.This isn’t to say that I don’t think there are people who would enjoy the game. Some of these puzzles are really interesting: Ageless offers a bunch of byte-sized aha! moments. But I don’t think most people, myself included, would have a good time with it. The story could have at least intrigued you to continue to go just to see what happens, but it's really uninteresting.Nevertheless, Ageless feels amateurish. It’s janky and doesn’t feel that good to play. The ending levels felt tacked on. And while the puzzles were good, I don’t think it’s enough to save it. I’m interested in what this studio comes up with next, I think this had potential. Maybe spend some more time in the basics. Then—and only then—go all out on the crazy levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Watching footage of this game I was really hyped to jump in, I thought it might just be misunderstood by the current mixed reviews (68%). This game is not what I hoped it would be at all, and I'm really disappointed by that.PROS:+ The controls and character control decently wellCONS:- Ageless tries so hard to copy Celeste that its hard keep playing because it just feels better to play Celeste in every way.- The UI makes it look like a mobile port at times, and a wall of hieroglyphic gibberish at others. - The levels are either frustratingly easy or frustratingly difficult, absolutely no in between. The lack of "coyote time" (as dubbed by Maddy Thorson, one of the creators of Celeste) is a huge influence on what makes the platforming feel lesser, and it's so disappointing that its missing given that it would be very easy to implement and drastically change the game feel. - The story is a huge letdown so far, it differs from Celeste in that instead of giving the message of all the strength you need being within you (symbolic of Madeline's abilities sourcing from herself), Ageless denies that and says you need outside help from a mythical gate to get superpowers in order to overcome your fears.Overall, just not that great or new at all. The gimmick of aging and de-aging things isn't used that creatively at all so far, its just been the same puzzle copied and pasted for 30 minutes. I don't think I'll keep playing to see if the puzzles get any better simply because the game had its chance to impress meTL;DR: Just go buy Celeste instead, or if you already own it, go replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is one of the best games I've played in a while. It feels like a cross between Celeste & Toki Tori 2. For those who don't know Toki Tori 2 is a metoridvania where you don't have any particular movement abilities of your own, you advance by manipulating the various creatures around you. This game has a high degree of difficulty and optional collectibles like Celeste and a focus on single-room challenges that are pretty hard, though this tends far more towards the puzzle side with very little execution challenge for most puzzles once you worked out the solution. Rather than using your own mobility you advance by manipulating the various creatures in the environments. You have 2 basic abilities: a dash (which can activate in proximity of other creatures) and a bow that will either make a creatures "younger" or "older" which changes how they perform. For instance the creature in the first area has a young stage where it will move to eat a plant if you grow the plant, a prime stage where it will bum-rush you and destroy blocks in front and an old stage where it will crush blocks underneath it. As you advance the different stages has their own unique forms (2 creatures/1 creature & 1 plant for every area). The game has a really good progression of puzzles and challenge that towards the end is quite a challenge, the optional collectible challenges were also mostly good (a few cases of "I didn't know I could do that") I had to look up a few solutions on a guide but not many. I had really good time. I had to take some time for this because later down the line they got very challenging indeed.As for the story: pretty basic,it does the job well enough, but don't play it for the story. Anyone who liked Celeste on a mechanical level will probably find this a very good game. A few negatives: This games take on boss fights are not great. They are usually some variant of timed puzzles with far fewer checkpoints than the regular game. There are only 4 of them (5 if you count the last area, but that one is mostly fine because while it's still timed it has proper checkpointing)

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless is one of literally thousands of console ported 2D retro pixel platformers polluting the Steam store.   This particular platformer has you jumping around underground through various die-and-retry obstacle courses and other platformer puzzles. They chose to use obsolete retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.  It's also worth noting the pixel "art" here is really bad.  Like, it's worse than decades old games like Commander Keen, and Apogee at the time weren't using pixel "art", that was literally the best PCs at the time could do.   No excuses for Ageless having such bad visuals. Speaking of excuses, I really hope they have one for charging a ludicrous $15 USD for this console ported bundle worsening garbage.  You can buy all the Commander Keen and Duke Nukem platformers for less than that, they have more content and better graphics, despite being decades older.  It's just impossible to recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Precision Puzzle PlatformerFully compatible with the Steam Deck.I wanted to love this game.  The pixel art is cute, if a little rough.  The pacifist ethos is admirable (the only time you "kill" anything is to reset enemy states).  But in the harder rooms the puzzling tends to require a level of precision that the controls can't quite handle, leading to a disappointing tedium until the controls and targeting do what you're actually trying to do.  Add in some baffling design decisions (why do forest enemies take 2 hits to transform?), and a painfully tedious 4th "boss" (beat 7 rooms without dying while fighting the loose controls and brand new gimmicks that are never seen again), and you're left with a game that's only OK when it could have been great.I don't regret my time with the game, but I think this one is mostly just for pixel platformer purists.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid indie puzzle platformer with a simple but decent art style. The core mechanics are unique and lead to some very interesting puzzles that offer a good degree of flexibility in how they are solved. Though the controls can be a little difficult to get used to, the auto-aiming and slowing of time when you aim makes it reliable and consistent once you get the hang of it (i.e., you won't have "cheap" deaths). _childDocuments_.review: Definitely not a game for me, but it is functional, and not as difficult as I saw some claim.The positive I can say definitely is the interesting uses for animals you find, depending on which age you select for them, it's a highlight and sometimes it felt like puzzles could have more than one solution, The music is also nice to the ear, pretty competent composition.The controls are unpleseant, I don't want to think how much worse they'd be on a controller, it's a 2D platformer where aiming is important, but not in a combat sense, your power to change beings' age is an arrow being shot, a thing that also has a short windup, timing of which doesn't really bring much satisfaction in gameplay. Besides that you have a jump and wall slide, pretty standard, but challenges involving those feel finnicky more than anything else, since you're in puzzle rooms, you just kinda squeeze yourself between hazards and onto platforms, and hope for the best. The worst part comes up with your special form, which you activate for a short time, and as soon as you touch another living thing, you are in a static state, completely breaking your flow, and a chart of directions shows up, where you push yourself in one direction, while the being is pushed in opposite (while also reversing its age by one). Now if you also add plant jump pads, being small, and directional in different angles - it all mixes into a really unsatisfying, unwieldy and inconsistent at times, experience. Not to mention you sometimes bug out in environment, or a dolphin ride prompt straight up doesn't work 50% of the time.Well, I sure hope the saving grace is going to be story or visuals, but both are a nope from me. Story is trying to be uplifting, but it's filled with exposition and spelling out feelings, talking to yourself like a schizo. None of it is gripping, and lore intertwining with the see through characters, doesn't save it at all. Visuals are pixelated hard, enough to border on ugly in my opinion. Some slight vfx touches like traces are sprinkled in, and bouncy resizing adding fake life into some of the animations. Nothing that blew me away. Voice acting doesn't exist, it's just grunts and moans, some more annoying than others (unfortunately, in case of the protagonist - more). While I don't think it's a bad or horrible game, for a guy who is not a massive fan of the genre - I could not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I joked while watching the trailer "ermagerd, pixel art platformer with wall jumping, just like Celeste", but honestly, it looks like this game is quite clear about its inspiration. Without spoiling much, it definitely feels like that sort of game, but a lot heavier on the puzzle aspect, with what feels like some nods to Ori and the Blind Forest's escape sequences.I'm not sure if something has changed since people wrote reviews about it being buggy 2 years ago, but I only encountered a couple of glitches in my entire playthrough. I like challenging games, and this was definitely one of them. Kept me interested enough to play through the whole thing (100%, achievements, etc) in one sitting.My only complaints are: - While playing with gamepad, your aim snaps to targets, and I don't think there's any way to *not* do that, making it hard to lead my shots- The relics, while an interesting challenge to collect, feel extremely pointless. Would have been cool if you got more than some colour added to some voxel statues.- Might've been nice to give another shoutout to Celeste by showing what part of a stage you are missing a relic in, instead of having to scour the entire level for a single missing thing.
