_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I don't remember how this game ended up in my Steam Library but I finally got around to playing it and I think it being Mixed on Steam is not giving this game nearly as much credit as it deserves. To preface this review, I will say that the game isn't perfect by any means. Now I can't attest to controller controls because I played on keyboard & mouse but precision and hitboxes can be a little janky at times which is frustrating. The movement and abilities presented in the game should give you a freeflowing satisfying movement system, which it does at its best, but at its worst it will repeatedly cause you to mess up puzzles due to the games own collision issues. With that inconvenience out of the way though, I think my only other issue with the game could be that it gets a bit repetitive at times, but I think that's just a nitpick if anything. To start off with the things I enjoyed about the game, the gameplay systems are incredibly original and refreshing. Each area has a small amount of creatures you can use your ageing ability on but by the time you've mastered all the different ways you can utilize their different stages of life, the game throws the next visually distinct area at you full of new creatures for you to learn how to master. It's a nice gameplay loop and I found myself playing until the end of an area, then waiting until the next day to dive back in and grind through the next. The story has a lot of very fun worldbuilding in it and without spoiling anything, the area called Spectre, has a reallly really fun/cool gameplay/story section that I found to be very appealing. The story can be a bit surface level at times with it's themes of self help and mental illness but I don't think it was ever trying to be anything other than what it was so I don't find it to be an issue.Bottom Line: Ageless isn't perfect, but I think it has enough good going for it that it's definitely worth the play-through (I 100%ed it on my first play-through at just under 12 hours). I am definitely keeping my eye on these developers in the future because I think that this game, despite its flaws, really showcases the talent at One More Dream Studios and what they could be capable of in the future. If you like puzzle platformers and are looking for one with a unique gameplay system then I would definitely check Ageless out.(Between a 6 and a 7)/10 - A fun game with a lot of promise with a few glaring issues. Fun if you're looking for a short, lower budget platformer

_childDocuments_.review: Okay...a reluctant thumbs up here because I applaud the effort, even though it has some solid misses.Ageless is almost creepingly similar to celeste: the graphic design style, the overarching story, the difficulty. The main hook here is that you can shoot arrows that increase/decrease the age of living species. And that somehow lets you propel through the air if you aim it at yourself...But video game logic aside: celeste is a masterpiece, so there's plenty of room for a simile. But what all negative reviews correctly point out (and for some reason only a handful of positive ones): it gets frustratingly hard in not a good way. Often, what you need to do is pretty clear (the puzzles are okay and even good), but the game relies so much on pixel perfect execution that it's discouraging rather than challenging. And to be honest: the shooting arrow mechanic would've been great for a strict puzzle game, but it has to share its experience with a development team that wanted some celeste difficulty as well. And I feel that drags it down more than anything else...

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Boring and repetitive, despite having good ideas. Could be great with a much better execution.The controls are very annoying and very rarely feels right. Especially if you play on controller. Very hard to make any sort of precise movement with that set of movement.Puzzles are fine but that's really all you do, just very long series of mostly easy or annoyingly tight rooms. The quite bad hitboxes don't help with that.The gameplay progresses way too slowly and mechanics players can figure out in the couple first rooms don't get used until much later, instead reusing the same ones until you get sick of them.I already mentioned it but the difficulty is all over the place, there is no curve, it's a roller coaster.The basic idea of aging and de-aging stuff to progress is pretty unique and I'd say they make good use of the gimmick and it never feels irrelevant. The way the dash works feels quite bad however, despite it being used in smart ways in the level design, it just feels... off and unrelated to the concept of aging / de-aging.The story is also scattered very thin along the whole game, giving you not nearly enough incentive to keep playing it. When playing it, it's pretty obvious to see why only 14.6% of players makes it through world 1, there's nothing to keep you hooked on long enough.The story itself is really unsubtle about its themes, which could've been decent with better writing and way less space between each cutscene.In the end, this game feels a lot like Celeste and yet seems to not take enough inspiration from it which would've made the game much more solid.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot and would recommend it if you like difficult puzzle platformers. While it isn't as polished as the big names in the genre it features some unique mechanics and ideas. Throughout most of the game you only have 3 tools: ageing arrow, deaging arrow and the ability to stop time. The game stays engaging by introducing new environments, animals and plants to interact with frequently. At the end of the game the puzzles get quite tense as you often have to beat rooms under time pressure. It took me ~14 hours to complete this game with 100% achievements.Reasons why you might not like this game:The controls can be quite finicky, aiming the arrows can get frustrating, mounting a dolphin only works after pressing the button multiple times etc.The second boss is quite buggy, it has issues with camera position and it can get locked in the wrong attack patterns.The game has random difficulty spikes for both the puzzle and platformer parts.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle game with a good mix of problem solving and side scrolling mechanics to get through different levels and areas. At first I thought the mechanics were going to be too simple and boring but as you progress you get more mechanics that change up the game and how you solve the different puzzles. Each area also has a unique set of mechanics that keeps the game from getting stale. I really like that the size of the puzzles are essentially one screens worth and after you get through a puzzle there is a save point, no pointlessly doing the first part of the puzzle 100 times to be able to attempt/practice the end part 3 or 4 (looking at you super meat boy!). There are also longer sequences at the end of each area that provide a bit more difficulty and use the mechanics for that area in fun fast paced ways. Typically I ignore the stories in most games but this one has a surprisingly deep plot that has a lot of moral ambiguity and highlights the hard choices that we have to make as humans in an imperfect and sometimes brutal world.  Even with how small the game is and the short nature of the story I've actually gotten into it and have some emotional investment that I wasn't expecting at all when I started the game. Overall a solid 4.5 stars from a gamer that's finding it harder and harder to find games that capture my attention and are fun for longer than 30min. I got this game through a humble bundle and am not sure I would ever buy a game like this for more than $10 without knowing how much I'd enjoy it. After playing it I'd probably go up to $20 to support the creators. I also have not experienced any glitches mentioned in the other reviews and I'm about half way through.

_childDocuments_.review: So. Ageless. Probably the most difficult review for me to write yet.Let's get the obvious out of the way. Ageless is a story based puzzle platformer, whose storey resembles the famous celeste. It tells the story of an young woman, named kiara, who struggles to find her place in the world, and goes to a supernatural journey of self realization and acceptance.The journey, sadly, is a bit of a mixed bag. The visuals are quite decent. The worlds and mechanics are diverse and different from one another. The story and gibberish voice acting are not the best but compelling enough.But I still have several issues with the game, the first being is the controls. They're just not precise enough, and the developers made some weird decisions regarding them. Like the fact that you can't move at all when you're drawing your bow, which was really annoying at specific instances. There are a lot of small annoyances like that in the game.Then there's also the difficulty fluctuations. By and large, the puzzles are well designed. Hell, some of them instilled me with the "OHHHH that's how you do it" feeling, which some of the best puzzle games do. But it's also amazing that some of the puzzles in the endgame are easier than the one at the middle.At the start of the game, I was really enjoying myself. I even collected nearly every extra collectable (I collected more than 60 of them!). But by the end, I skipped them all.Overall, ageless is ok. It has it downsides, but it's still a fun experience.And if by any chance the developers will read this review, I really think you should continue making games. You clearly have a lot of potential. Just because the first try didn't pan out too well, it doesn't mean you shouldn't try again. I'm looking forward to see your next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: ✔️ Interesting puzzle / platformer mechanics that may not seem like much in the beginning, but really gain in depth over the course of the game.✔️ The progressive increase both in puzzle complexity and in execution difficulty is very smooth and enjoyable.✔️ Really cute pixel art graphics.✔️ Nice ambience music.✔️ The story is enjoyable and touching, even though it doesn't have an incredible depth.✔️ The game saves very often, which makes interruptions easy and failure not too frustrating.❌ A few bugs here and there, like the level not resetting correctly on death or music stopping playing. I've only got one game breaking bug once, but since the game saves often it wasn't a big issue.❌ While I found that a joystick offered a more enjoyable experience, targeting with your powers using the joystick proved pretty challenging at some moments. The snap helps, but there are still some tedious moments because of that.❌ The end part of the story felt maybe a bit rushed. Not catastrophically so, but I would have enjoyed a bit more development on the last part.❌ The game doesn't seem to have any accessibility / difficulty settings, and it might have benefited from some.Overall this game is a great puzzle platformer, and I definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys this kind of games. Obviously inspired from Celeste, it pales a bit in comparison but remains a pretty nice game on its own.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This was very challenging for me. I like challenge in my games, but I'm not the biggest fan of the genre, so committing time to get good enough to enjoy this wasn't really something I wanted to do. That being said, it seems like a fun game. The ageing mechanics are pretty good, the puzzle style environments were well designed in my opinion and I enjoyed the graphics. The only thing I disliked were the noises the characters made during dialogue scenes. It's obnoxious, but if you're into platformers this seems legit. I especially want to thank the developers for taking the time to actually design a useable keyboard and mouse interface. So many of these indie platformers force you to use the strangest keys and combinations. This felt good to play without a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This puzzle game is simply not fun enough to warrant a $5 price, let alone $15. The puzzles contain a lot of tight timing, and that combined with the janky movement is awful. Even ignoring the sub-par puzzles, the story/exploration is extremely lackluster. Also the game crashes a lot for some reason.I had no drive to complete this game, and considering the mixed reviews, I can imagine that many others feel the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are fun, challenging, rewarding, and frustrating at the same time. Almost quit a few times. I had to pause and then come back again and again because it was so stressful at times. Not recommend for hot-headed people of course! The graphic is okay - kind of. I do not personally like the graphic like this but gave it a try anyway, and it was kind of fun. So, it is forgiven and became kinda cute. The mechanic is good. I only hate it when it requires a perfect run for bosses and some puzzles. You really need to die and repeat over and over. and over and over. until you get it ( if not already quit). I am quite new for this genre of games though. But I would recommend you to give it a try. At least it proved me wrong that the games with this kind of graphic are too childish. I am about 60-70% in the story at the time of review. Enjoy the experience so far. Not sure if I could finish it before I can't stand the frustration or not though. Hahaha.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this game. I was expecting a Celeste kinda game and instead I found a great puzzle platformer. I must say that that platforming feels quite nice, but the bow controls are clunky and there seems to be some bugs. The story well, it's not the best, but the scenarios and the mechanics included in each compensate making it a great experienc. Died a few times enjoye the puzzles and overall great chill game. 7.5/10 :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Its disappointing to put a thumbs down for that game because I had a great time with the vast majority of puzzles through the game, but coming to the hell elevator where failing a challenge would undo your most recent success trying to force you to succeed through 6 challenges of understanding, timing, and at times accuracy and speed felt like a terrible terrible way to reward the player for coming this far.Once I saw myself regress twice I just alt-f4ed and uninstal. A really awful design decision that leaves a sour taste in my mouth and makes me feel like I shouldn't trust that developer in the future. Really disappointed and sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the normal levels and the collectible hunting, but hated every boss level. The extreme lack of checkpoints in these encounters make them incredibly tedious to go through. I don't know, maybe some people like having to repeat a large number of areas every time they make a mistake (potentially redoing a single screen dozens of times), but I'm not one of them. It's a shame though because I really found the mechanics interesting, and the puzzles are a great treat. There's no feeling quite like finally figuring out how to get a collectible after many attempts. Heck, I also enjoy any specific screen during boss encounters because they're a nice combination of frenetic and logical. I just really wish I don't have to repeat them more times than I really have to.

_childDocuments_.review: Liked:- Challenging platforming- Good variety of mechanics without being overwhelming- Some problems have multiple solutions, encouraging creativity- Lots of optional challenges to demonstrate mastery- Interesting story, but story doesn't get in the way of gameplayDisliked:- Some challenges felt convoluted or overly precise- In some areas, failure means a significant setback- Physics occasionally felt inconsistent, making strategizing difficult
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a good story and idea, the main premise being that you can age and unage things. The issue I have with this game is minor - it's puzzles are sometimes too strange and it's sometimes easier to just cheese the puzzle than try to figure out what it seems to want you to do (I will admit I had to go through walk-throughs for some of these, but the walk-throughs I saw also seemed to cheese some of these puzzles). This doesn't happen very often though, and I had a lot of fun playing this. One other issue I had is sometimes the mechanics just break -  but it isn't too much of an issue as it'll fix itself once you shut down and start the game back up. Overall, I find the game interesting, the mechanics are fairly smooth, easy to use and the story is pretty good so I'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels a lot like Celeste in a lot of ways, but the gameplay is more geared toward puzzles than platforming.  The game so far is thankfully slower and demands a lot less precision than Celeste.  I would recommend this to anyone who wanted to play Celeste but is turned off by pixel perfect platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think ageless deserves such a low review score (65% positiv reviews atm). Thus, I write a short review.Overall I'd recommend the game. I feel like it deserves a positive review score around 80%. It's not a masterpiece like Celeste or Portal but still good. More details:Ageless-is more a puzzle game than a platformer (platforming challenges are pretty rare I'd say [for example boss levels]).-has extremely good music which I (sadly) rarely recognized while playing the game.-has a fair learn curve for the mechanics. Not everything is fully explained by the game itself but in such situations you just have to rethink a few mechanics you already know.-has good controls. Only the wall jump felt sometimes a little frustrating.-story is good but couldn't create an impact. It feels extremely rushed.-is not a masterpiece but was fun the most time.Small additional cons:-some puzzles felt like I didn't solve them as intended. -minor bugs (2-3 in my playthrough I think which could be solved by leaving the level and continuing the story which puts you at the exact point where you left)-aiming and shooting arrows feel a little frustrating sometimes (with controller)
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: This game has way too many negative reviews. There is certainly room for some polish, but the mechanics are actually solid and consistent. The first world is mediocre, and the first boss is awful. The game exponentially improves after the first world. Puzzles are interesting. Each world has its own unique gimmick. Aging concept is very well implemented. Definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the reviews I have seen only seem to sum up the first world of the game. I was surprised to see that the game mechanics were used this well all along the game.To me the only let down is that the game expects perfection from us, but doesn't always deliver back to the player. Because if I am asked this much, I also expect the same in return. Unfortunately, the control response, the enemy hit-box and some other minor elements will sometimes prevent you to perform smoothly to feel satisfied. In its whole, the challenge, graphics, story did convinced me, and I would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: It could use a few bug fixes, but the main block is the cool-down on the freeze-time ability mixed with the timing of certain... "puzzle"(?) mechanics. It's got the ambition to hit the Celeste sweet-spot, which is a good ambition to have, but it misses the mark. It appears to be the first game from the dev, so hopefully they've learned from this game, and I'd be interested to look at their next trip out, but this one doesn't work for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle platformer where you play a girl with the ability to make things older or younger. It's okay but I found the controls to be a bit too imprecise, and some of the puzzles require specific timing where if you fail, you have to go aaall the way back to the beginning of the puzzle and do it all over again which ended up being too frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Ageless

_childDocuments_.review: Ageless is a story driven puzzle platformer where you must alter the age of animals and plant life around you to progress. Play as Kiara, a young girl who braves through heartache and loss as she journeys across a mysterious world to discovers its secrets and herself.

name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator
detailed_description: Join our Discord Upcoming features About the Game Features: Unique visuals inspired by medieval manuscripts and medical books. Hyper satisfying physical interactions with ingredients and equipment. Sandbox style gameplay where you have many different avenues available, and it’s up to you to figure out the best way to complete each task. Sell your potions to the townsfolk while roleplaying as a noble artisan, a greedy weasel, an occult dark master, or whomever else you may wish to be! Work with all sorts of ingredients Leaves, flowers, berries, roots, fruits, minerals, and a plethora of mushrooms are at the ready for your mortar and pestle. Just like espresso, the fineness of the grind matters! Learn the art of potion making Concoct your potion plan. Grind ingredients and carefully mix them in your cauldron. Heat the coals. Boil and stir. Add the base: water, oil, or… something else. Congrats on your first potion! Was it easy to learn? Now try mastering it! Experiment and invent new recipes Carefully plan your route via the Alchemy Map to combine different effects. Be mindful of common sense: you won’t find a market for a poisonous healing potion… right? Or would you? Sell potions Every day customers will come to your store looking for solutions to their problems. You will face consequences depending on what you decide to sell them. Attract guilds, befriend notable figures (or feud with them), gain riches and influence - and one day, you may even decide the fate of the whole town. Buy ingredients or grow your own Every alchemist needs ingredients. You can buy them from traveling merchants: it can be pricey, but successful haggling may save you some coin. Or you can just grow your own! Get creative with customizing Want to give a special appearance to your best potions? Go ahead! Change bottle shape, label type, icon, and colors. You can even give it a custom name and label description. Carefully arrange your unique potions to showcase them on your shop’s shelves and tables… or carelessly throw them around - we’re not gonna tell you what to do, just have fun!

You're in full control of the whole shop: invent new recipes, attract customers and experiment to your heart's content. Just remember: the whole town is counting on you.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game during the Early Access period and again after its official release.The game is quite enjoyable and relaxing. You will assist many eccentric customers in finding the perfect potion to suit their needs.As you progress, you will encounter some customers who become increasingly particular about their requirements, so you will have to continuously improve your recipes.The endgame (around chapter IX-X) can become grindy and painfully tedious. The developers have already confirmed that they will make improvements (you can check them out in their Discord),  but for now, it makes no sense to complete these chapters as they are too monotonous and dull. Although I love this game, in my opinion, this is currently the main issue.

_childDocuments_.review: i WOULD recommed this game, it is good, but its been ALMOST A YEAR since the last news on the promised update, and as they have been part of many a sale, i HIGHLY doubt that that update is ever going to happen. sad really as i enjoyed the game quite a lot and most of my problems WOULD be fixed IF the game EVER got updated. if it miracuosly dose happed before the heat death of the universe i will change my review.

_childDocuments_.review: [edited review]I'm changing my review from a not recommended to recommended a year later. since the release, i saw potion craft regularly getting updated and patched and recently decided to check back in to see what has changed. did all the updates make a noticable difference? the answer is a very clear yes. wow, they really put in the effort to improve upon their foundation. i'm not even salty that i had to restart from the beginning again because it seems like they made some core changes as well. a lot of what i was annoyed by early on has been fixed and evolved. making money is much easier now with more haggle options, ingredients are more varied and less difficult to come by, the characters feel more alive, the shop takes on a personality of their own depending on the customers you chose to serve, more meaningful progression with the room at the bottom, .. really, i'd have to think hard to find something to complain about at this point now. also love that they added steam achievements <3 i guess imma go get me some carpal tunnel still with how much i still use the mortar but it finally feels like it's worth doing so - even at full price. if you enjoy brewing potions and alchemy, i'd say this game implemented the concept the best :) nothing else i've played has come close so far. i hope they will continue to pour so much love into this project as they have in the past year, i'll be around. [old review below]it's okay, but wouldn't reccomend it at the price this game is sold currently. the fact that it's still EA is very noticable. i got bored / stuck after like four hours because people keep asking for the same kind of potion i haven't discovered yet. so i was like, sure. guess imma just go explore the map only to waste a load of ingredients on finding nothing at all for a few days, ending up with a situation where not only can i not brew the potions i already know, because i spent all my ingredients trying to find the ones i don't have yet, i now can't explore anymore either, because what's left is the top section of the map and the game kinda refuses to give me anything but ingredients going down and righti think this would be so easily fixed if we could choose not to open the store some days. since i'm forced to answer to every customer before i go to sleep, i feel obligated to do what they ask instead of find new potions since otherwise my reputation is just gonna suffer endlessly cuz i have to decline everyone or let the garden be a more valuable assetanyways, i hope the game will continue to improve and if you're still reading, i'd reccomend you check back on this game at a later date, or at least wait until it's on sale to try
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: It's just a wonderful chill time, perfect to put on and unwind with for 10-15 minutes. The way potion making works is an intriguing notion. This hits a sweet spot of being reminiscent of a mini-game in some bigger AAA product, but it's just a bit too elaborate for a mini-game. It's just become a good way to relax for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: get's boring way too quick. definitely not worth original asking the price, get it on sale and it's actually worth it.1. the game lacks a challenge or even incentive, there's really no goal to chase, and where as it does make it very relaxing, it also makes it very redundant. no lore, no plot progression, and nothing that interesting 12 hours in the game.2. after the first few weeks and unlocking and finding all the new potions the gameplay just becomes annoying and tedious. 3. the fact that you can just make as many potions as you like in a single day, how easy it is to get money after a while, and how the mileage in the game is just "craft all these potions" makes the potion brewing almost feel like paperwork.you can't fool customers with the wrong potions, you can't decide what plants to grow in your garden, the ingredients you'll get sold is fully RNG, customers are fully random, and there's nothing to do other than make the next big crystal, which is just annoying and tedious work. in the demo this game was amazing but the full game doesn't offer much more than that much more really, just more potions.i wish there were more interesting subplots , like the fisherman or the hunter. and how they come in with interesting requests, or basically any other additional system in place on top of the potion crafting itself to keep it interesting.the games core is very fun, it just lacks all of the bits and bobs that typically make indie tittles shine.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Cute graphics, decent UI, very original and clever approach to alchemy mechanics, so many loving little details. As of the time I've played it, Potion Craft is an early access game with the major mechanics settled. The major mechanics are very playable for a good 5-6 hours while you figure them out (and longer, if you are slow at learning things like me). Beyond that point, I feel like the game is going to benefit enormously from ongoing development - maybe more of a story, more goals, etc. So it doesn't yet feel complete in that there is nowhere to "go," really, but the mechanics themselves are such fun that the game feels worth the price of admission.I personally am very fond of repetitive games that I can play to keep my hands busy while I watch TV, and I can see this game being one I frequently pop into while Star Trek is on the other monitor, even if the developer does nothing else from here. I like it a LOT.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing! I truthfully cant describe how good this game is. I love every part of this game and cant get enough of it. It is very simplistic in its game style and design yet the complexity that can go into the game is amazing. The ability to (almost) fully customize your game play is astonishing and makes it a different experience for everyone. I especially love the customizable potion book and the freedom of creating you own recipes. Potion Craft is a fun mind numbing game that will definitely keep your attention for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, I've been looking for this type of art style, and potential gameplay.However, I quickly found myself feeling like this was a job, very grindy and repetitive. The game simply doesn't feel fun after a couple of hours. I only kept going because I am very stubborn.I can't recommend it at this price, perhaps it will get better.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sort of in the middle ground with this game. While it is mostly cool, and the minigames are great and addictive, i feel that it is a little unbalanced right now. I'm in my ~20th day and there's no way i can make the amount of money needed to buy the stuff in the basement. My popularity level is stuck at 3, and i can't make the necessary potions to gain another level. The materials are never enough, and customers always ask for the hardest potions on the east side of the map, and i feel like there aren't enough materials to go there, most of them go west, or up and down. Besides, the path they follow is way too weird and random, so it's hard to create a simple potion to reach the furthest places. The garden falls short as time advances, since potions require more and more materials, and the things you get on your garden aren't as many as needed. I have to buy everything from the merchants, and each time i do that, half of my money is gone. Then, when i sell the potions, i can't make enough to cover the amount spended, so i'm losing money most of the time.Of course, this being an early access, it will change sooner or later, so i think this could be an amazing game some day. The minigame its cool, and i love the interaction with all the tools, the short conversations with the characters, and the art and music are fantastic, so i believe it is definitely worth it.Edit: After a couple of hours of playing, i've changed my mind, it's stressful as hell. Its supposed to be a relaxing little game but i had to ragequit after the fifth customer asking me for the same potion i can't make because i don't have enough blue flowers that are the only material that goes to the right of the map. I hate it, i'll wait until its more balanced.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 4~8 hours game is fun and interesting. The late game is pure tedium and achievement hunting this game was insanely painful. Trying to get Popularity Level 15 is just not fun because at that point in the game you have every recipe for every potion saved and its just clicking through menus. The customers with requirements for potions only make it worse because you lose double the popularity you gain on average by turning them away. So it's just a complete slog. Another annoyance I ran into was through bad RNG I was constantly short on many of the gems that make the high tier potions possible (mostly frost sapphires). My final big late game annoyance was remaking previous alchemy machine salts is just SO ANNOYING. I would have dropped the game if I didn't add a mod that allows you to save the alchemy machine recipes. I understand it's a feature that's intended to be added, but its not in the game now so I can complain about it.   Hopefully future updates eventually arrive and change my opinion.  TLDR; Early Game Good, Mid-Game Good, Late Game Atrociously Boring

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game already, I do wish that there was more to do and a bit more customisation, maybe a world map to go and shop for certain materials or the ability to go into caves to try find more cloud crystals or earth pyrite, but thats only because waiting for the dwarf to show up can end up taking a while which makes the game feel slower.Also, it would be good to be rewarded for experimental potions, maybe theres guilds you can build a reputation with that would lead to large supply n demand etc. These are all ideas though, this game is fantastic and is still in development. Looking forward to seeing where this game goes. I can see it being a more niche version of games like nintendogs and stardew valley lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft is not just the worst repetitive and grinding game of all time but also obviously unfinished product. Although it's not an earlyaccess game, the dev still keep posting regular announcement for updates because this game is yet too empty. This game has 10 chapters but the only first 4 chapters contains original missions, and the rest of chapters are copy&pasted from those.First it's not a detailed simulator game, what you going to do is moving your empty bottle icon to a potion icon on the map by using ingredients that each have own direction like some ingredient only move your bottle north, other does south. And also that's all about game.Your main goal is unlocking achievements and those are mostly creating a new potion so you keep explore a new potion on the tasteless map for many hours with very few new experience. The another mission is fixing your alchemy machine, to do that you also gather bunch of specific potions so you keep exploring over and over, and even fixing the machine doesn't affect the game balance that much, no satisfaction and reward.It's been over 18 months since the game released, still there is very few contents and material to play, instead the game gives you so much same repeatable task to buy(waste) your time. No need to wait any updates in the future, find other games. One of the worst games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: (Edit: It's funny, I came back to see if there had been any content updates from the last time I played and realized that the developers have been working on updating this game for almost a year with no new update. There are features shown in the early access that didn't even launch with the game.)It was fun for a bit, then just extremely tedious. You feel like you need to unlock everything, but then you realize "what's the point?" For example, a salt that costs WELL over 25 unique potions that spins your bottle... just so you can craft potions more efficiently? So you go back, re-craft the same potion using new ingredients, then save the recipe so when another person comes by who wants the same thing you can craft it instantaneously. You start the game selling potions to half considerate people and end the game selling potions to half considerate people. I spent hours just to realize that I was back where I started. I didn't learn anything lore wise and there were no unique characters. Only references to other games like The Witcher and Deep Rock Galactic, and jokes like "make my bust bigger" or "make my thing... bigger".

_childDocuments_.review: For the first time ever (except dragon's crown), a game with crafting mechanics that are actual mechanics. If you're like me and have been dieing for a game claiming to have 'crafting' mechanics to actually execute them in an exceptional manner, just buy it.Bonus points if you're the kind of person that kind of phases into organization and small things like that, since you basically create your own recipes in the book.General gameplay is basically trying to optimally maneuver your potion flask through obstacles to discover and trigger various effects on your potions.Some small tips to help anyone that may be confused about UI bits and any future issues one may come across. Anything I think might be too 'spoilery' for those that like to figure their heads, I'll be sure to black out.1. The compass points you towards the focal point of the potions in their direction (example, life points to health potion. death points to poison)2. The whirlpools 3. Whirlpools cont. 4. Recipe book pages CAN be discounted, but you may still want to buy a handful in advance to be safe.5. Be sure to thoroughly explore  That way you don't get stuck like I did for several in-game weeks.6. Any truly disastrous, unsellable potions can be sold to merchants for 0 gold. Otherwise they can't be removed.7. Adding to a recipe BEFORE you apply the potion effect can let you save an optimized path for further exploration (useful when finding unknown effects)8. First bartering tier unlock is quite good.9. Don't waste stones. If there's anything that anyone has questions about, ask away. I'm nearly fully completed and have enjoyed nearly every bit of time I've spent in the game thus far. Can't believe there's already more content in the works, too. Can't wait :D

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this could aspire to be even more than they are, as it stands, it is a pretty simple gameplay loop. Your job is to find the most efficient recipes, save them, and keep stock for special orders, you buy bulk ingredients (I would), then sell for profit. Super simple stuff, but it is a little bit empty in terms of shopper variety. You should be able to put potions up for sale.The game kinda is complete, but you could have more alchemy machine recipes. The enchanted tree could use some improvements, it seems pretty random to me. Being able to target a specific crop would be nice. One day we might have a game that kind of combines trades in the economy into a much more ambitious project, sort of like combining this with a game like recettear, then adding the smithy aspect and city building. Adventurers improve based on how well the economy is doing? Sounds a bit like majesty in there, sadly, that's not what the game is.More capacity to actually use your own potions beyond selling them sounded nice as well. Maybe even as part of the alchemy process itself? Having to have high enough temperatures that fire shield is necessary. Being able to use wild growth in your enchanted garden. Using acid to melt down two ingredients into an emulsion that can be used in some way. The ability to make potions with the alchemy machine itself. All the things that could be!

_childDocuments_.review: is exactly what it says on the bottle: an alchemist simulator in which you craft potions. "What's so special about that?" you may ask. "Many games have featured the art of alchemy, most of them don't go far beyond simply combining two ingredients and clicking a button to brew." Well, that is where  absolutely shines.As I'm sure many other reviews have mentioned,  doesn't simply ask you to combine ingredients at random to try and brew. Rather, it uses one of the most ingenious systems I have ever seen for crafting in video games: an "alchemy map" that players must explore to find different effects for their potions. Alchemy ingredients create all sorts of varying types of paths on the map, letting the player quite literally navigate their way through potion-making. Different combinations of grinding ingredients and stirring concoctions just right (all of which is achieved through gesture controls that seem perfect for a tablet) allow for more refined and valuable potions. It truly is an inspired piece of game-design and is a joy to work with, making the discovery of new potions quite literally a course charted by the player.All of this is, in part, to service the endless amount of callers that players receive at their humble abode, looking to buy potions for every conceivable purpose. Additionally, as with most places of business, the player may reserve the right to refuse service to anyone, serving either the well-to-do crowd or the ne'er-do-wells, which increases or decreases the player's reputation. More money means the player can more ingredients, as well as more parts for the alchemy machine that lies crumbling in their basement, the repair and use of which can allow the player to create their alchemical magnum opus.All of this is presented in an incredibly user-friendly interface, with light, folky music and a delightful hand-drawn art-style. There are no pressures and no timers (even with customers waiting at the door) so it is indeed a very relaxing experience. The simple joy of exploring the alchemy map and figuring out more effective and potent tinctures is bolstered by the customization options for recipes, allowing the player to choose different bottles, labels, iconography, and colors for their creations, as well as naming them whatever they wish. It's incredibly cozy and dabbling in a little end-of-day alchemy is a lovely way to wind down. is not quite the perfect mix, though, and does come up a little short in the end-game department. "The Alchemist's Path", which is essentially a checklist of recipes and the only real impetus to do anything in the game, can become quite a grind to complete near the end of things. It also does not offer anything beyond an achievement for your hard work. On top of this, the game changes very little throughout that time, with maybe one small surprise that broadens the horizon slightly but nothing more than that. In this way,  does feel a little undercooked, though at time of writing, developer niceplay games does appear to have plans to expand upon the incredibly solid framework they've laid out.That all being said, the positives outweigh the negatives and if you like your games light-hearted, cosy, and simple with a healthy dose of ingenuity, then I absolutely recommend ; it is sure to intoxicate.

_childDocuments_.review: This recommendation is based on simply what we have right now, I'll be happy to change my recommendation once the game has been updated upon. If you want to support the devs to continue making the game, that's great!Just for context, I fully completed the demo that has been available up until this EA release. Potion Craft has a lot of great mechanics and style points going for it, but I don't think they have updated or changed enough stuff since I played the free demo to justify paying for it at this moment. The game feels like it's progression just isn't there. The economy is very strange and unbalanced in the beginning of the game. Everyone seems to want the highest quality potions at all times for even trivial needs, but the amount they're willing to pay for them is almost always less than what it took to make it. After making it 4 chapters into the alchemy challenges and leveling up to around 15 I didn't really feel like I was better at alchemy, just some background numbers like how much the potions were selling for were shifting slightly more in my favor. It still took a bunch of ingredients to make those tier 3 or multi effect potions that everyone wanted, and you rarely have all the ingredients you need for an optimal brewing that doesn't require 100's of gold in ingredients.I also honestly just do not like the haggling system as it is. I find it pretty repetitive and feel like I am forced to do it with every customer to get close to the appropriate price I should be selling a potion for. I feel that if it were dialogue based instead of this clicky minigame I would be more inclined to take interest in the customers, my reputation, and read what they were telling me rather than parse through their initial text to just see what they need. It is also worth mentioning that while the music in the game is not bad, it becomes very repetitive as there is no variation, so I eventually just turned it off. I'm sorry if I'm sounding harsh, I really do like this game and find it very charming. Like I said before, I find the art style, mechanics of grinding potions, and maneuvering the potion map to be very fun and relaxing. I hope with a few updates to the economy of ingredients, gold, and skill progression I can change this review and recommend that others buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game to have a unique take on crafting mechanics. So many games have crafting systems (I know that in this game it is technically brewing but shhh) there is one and precisely one way to craft something; one set of ingredients, put into one interface, that normally does the whole crafting process with a single click. This game lets you create, for example, a potion of healing by combining any number of ingredients as long as their total effect lands you in the zone of restoring mana. The game smartly limits your access to ingredients so that you need to forge the same potion but with different ingredients in a different order. This mechanic is the unique mechanic that all the other mechanics and loops of the game revolve around: the experimentation with your ingredients to turn a profit. The haggling and dialogue systems are simplistic but serviceable. There's an entire system of the game that seems like it'll take a lot of time and money to unlock which might be the sign of late-game content.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first good alchemy simulator. Whilst other games have tried to simulate alchemy, they've done so without a specific aesthetic and a clear vision. Unlike the alternatives, Potion Craft doesn't have you running around in a 3D world haphazardly chucking whole ingredients into a cauldron. It offers a rich, complex, open-ended crafting system and a beautiful medieval aesthetic. There are countless ways to brew each potion, and the game rewards you for taking the time to experiment and find more efficient recipes. The economy also feels fair. A smart alchemist can end up with a huge surplus of coins and ingredients, whilst more haphazard play can lead you to deplete your supplies and be forced to turn down your customers. Reviews that complain of the game being punishing, or too difficult, or running out of ingredients, just haven't approached their alchemy thoughtfully enough.

I ain't getting those back.Look it was fun to begin with, learning the new tricks, exploring new areas, strategizing and optimizing the recipes and potions, yeah I enjoyed it to start.  But  it really quickly turns into a chore...Here's the main fallback in my view.  There's hundreds of different ingredients, meaning countless possible solutions to make any potion you want for your customers.  Many recipes will use 10, 15, even 20 different ingredients to make your potion, after you painstakingly stir and mix and tediously path to your desired potion.  It's fine the first time, but then you need to make more of the same potion and you're missing 1 of the needed 15 ingredients, so you can't use your quick-create button. Instead, you spend 10 minutes making the SAME potion, tediously, and then enjoy repeating this for the VAST majority of time you spend in this game. _childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft has been able to create a really interesting mechanic of crating potions that was challenging, but also fun and interesting! This takes something that would normally be a mini-game within a larger game, and puts it front and centre. The potion making turns into a puzzle and a little journey that you take the potion on in order to make it! But it also makes sure it doesn't wear out its welcome by giving the player ways to save past potion recipes and automatically generate past ones they have made! This makes it fun to try to make the perfect recipe, so the repeated creation of potions never gets bland!As well as boasting a strong potion making mechanic, Potion Craft also has quite an enjoyable game outside that. There is a nice way to get ingredients, with a relaxing little garden to pick herbs and flowers from, as well as traders you can haggle with. You can also use alchemy to get new ingredients for potions! You run a potion shop where customers will give you hints as to what potion they want instead of outright telling you and you have to figure out the right one. Most of the time it is pretty obvious, but sometimes I just had to guess. Interestingly, some customers will accept different potions and pay more or less depending on how well it fits their situation. You can also get a reputation for giving evildoers potions vs giving regular people potions!If the gameplay wasn't enough, Potion Craft also has really a really art style, atmospheric music, and really nice feeling controls! The way that you can manually grind, stir and drag ingredients and potions is so satisfying! You can also customise potion recipes and potion appearances! I was surprised that I was able to get 34 hours out of this game, the way it looked, it seemed it would be quite short. If you can ignore the high price, considering it's an indie game, it's quite a fun game to get addicted to for a couple days.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy the cozy atmospheres of medieval taverns, the pleasure of recipe building and optimizations, and the convenience of a game that can be paused at any moment - don't hesitate to try Potion Craft!The art for this game is beautiful and the concept is pretty simple - combine herbs to travel around a map and generate potions for customers. In your spare time, buy herbs from merchants and brew potions in the basement to work your way to creating the philosopher's stone! I've had this game for almost a year now, and played it on and off through the year. I will say that it's easy to play this game, but difficult to play . I've held my breath more than once as i tipped the water bucket, hoping and praying I create a  potion instead of a regular potion. I've scoffed at customers for asking for unreasonable amounts of an herb i don't normally use to make their potion, and I've practically weeped trying to balance my stores of herbs with my insatiable curiosity for those hidden areas of my map. Looking back from the top of the learning curve feels good with this game :)Even though I've felt satisfied enough with the current features, I'm impressed by the dedication and creativity of the developers. What exactly does this game need that it makes my computer lag and heat itself up? Only at reducing it to the lowest frame rate (30) was it able to run smoothly on my laptop. When I checked the options the option it was on was 240 fps. Why does the frame rate need to be so high at a default? It boggles my mind.

With its relaxing yet rewarding gameplay, Potion Craft is a magical experience that will keep you coming back for more.**Improvement Suggestion for Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator**While Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator is a delightful and engaging game, there are a few areas where it could be enhanced to further elevate the gameplay experience:1. **Expanded Ingredient Variety:** Introducing a wider range of ingredients with unique properties would add more depth to the potion-making process. These events could offer unique rewards and recognition for skilled potion makers.6. **Enhanced Shop Customization:** Allowing players to further customize their alchemy shop with decorative items, themes, and functional upgrades would enhance the sense of ownership and personalization. This could include aesthetic changes as well as practical improvements like expanded storage or faster brewing times.7. **Multiplayer and Co-op Modes:** Adding multiplayer or co-op modes where players can collaborate on potion-making or compete in alchemy challenges could significantly enhance the social aspect of the game. _childDocuments_.review: A very good game for the price, relaxing but weirdly engaging at the same time.I started to feel that "Zen" level of concentration that comes from other activities like playing an instrument, working with tools... or practicing an actual trade, which is what I felt like I'd learned by the time I finished playing. The game recreates that realistic vibe through the physical experience of using your lab instruments. You can stir rapidly or slowly, but with the movement of the mouse and the animation onscreen it's easy to forget that you're not actually stirring. You can pulverize ingredients methodically or even violently with your mortar and pestle, but again, the translation of mouse movement into onscreen action gives a sensation like you're actually working in your own laboratory.Things start out simply enough, and the mechanical underpinnings of the game stay pretty much the same, but challenge and complexity continue as you progress through the game. This comes from a few different factors. Initially, there's a scarcity of effective ingredients to work with. As you progress further, your toolbox gets bigger but your objectives on the alchemy map get more and more difficult to reach. And as all of those pieces finally fall into place, the game generates new novelty through the sometimes-exacting specifications put forward by your customers - combinations of effects, including/excluding certain ingredients, limiting the number/type you can use, etc.By the time I got to the VERY end of the game and picked up the last couple of achievements, I kinda just wanted it to be done with... But, then again, there are so many games in my library that I never 100% finish because I feel like it's not worth attaining for the level of effort involved. This was within reach, so I went for it, and I certainly enjoyed all of the hours I put into the game short of maybe the last 2-3 that I did just for the sake of being a completionist. Maybe there's some room for improvement in the gameplay loop all the way toward the end of the game? Either way, I'm not too concerned.Maybe my only other complaint is that Potion Craft has ONE single music track on a perpetual loop - listening to a 2-minute loop for 30 hours can be tough to manage in large doses. But they've mentioned that that's something they're already working on, so by the time you pick up the game and get to the 10-hour mark maybe your head won't be ready to explode and you won't need to take a day to cool off.Overall, I enjoyed my time with the game, and I plan to revisit it once they add some of the new features they've hinted at. But that's not to say that Potion Craft doesn't already feel complete in its current state. It was fun, it will be the next time I pick it up, and I feel perfectly fine recommending it at the full price listed.On a side note... If you like dark humor, feel free to start catering to some of the more questionable people who visit your establishment and asking you to do questionable things. I got a good laugh out of some of the ridiculous explanations customers gave me for a bunch of their potion requests.

_childDocuments_.review: While I had fun at first, the tedium quickly rears its ugly head as you reach the later milestones.Potion Craft is a fun game in concept: Exploring alchemy map, finding new potions, using very different ingredients to get similar results. At first as you're exploring and mixing potions, you're having decents amounts of fun as most potions takes 3-5 ingredients if you're optimizing, 6-9 if you're using bad ingredients. However, as the game progresses, you'll have potions so far on the base map that it takes literally 10+ ingredients just to get there, and sometimes even special ingredients to let you go through danger zones on the map.Then you have the alchemy machine, which at first seem deceptively easy, until it requires you to make compounds of 3-4-5 potions in specific concentration just to make ONE product. Then, you either need to use that product to enhance your alchemy, or to continue your main game objective: Philosopher's stone. Note that once it's used, it's gone.In the later levels, that means having to do every difficult recipes with compounds twice over to both get the tool to improve potion making AND to advance the objective. This, for a lack of better term, is incredibly tedious and IMO is absolute padding on the game's meager features.Though, one of the worst part IMO is the RNG of ingredients. You might have several thousands gold in the bank, bartering and trading like a pro; but it won't matter because you have an RNG supply of ingredients you can't really control. Your garden is RNG every morning, and the sellers are RNG and usually comes once every two days if you're lucky. This means that saving recipes is almost pointless as you'll eventually run out of a key ingredient and have to make your own sad way back to the potion you want to make. Then you can save spare recipes, but then you're using ingredients you might need for more potions. GAH!This game would be much better if you could just outright buy the ingredients you need at a steep price instead of RNGing it all.In final, I'm between recommending this game on a deep sale or skipping it. I just think the game gets very tedious early on.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a serious risk of becoming addicted to this game. The gameplay loop is extremely simple: gather ingredients, make potions, sell them, gain more money for more ingredients and more potions. Despite its simplicity, the game manages to keep you entertained by gradually presenting you with more and more complex requests for potions, adding objectives each chapter that guide you into making the right potions at the right time, to the end goal of creating your magnum opus: the Philosopher's Stone. At least, that's the game's official objective. If you're like me however, the game will quickly devolve into an accountant simulator. You will start calculating the price to brew each potion by summing the price of the ingredients, you will haggle like your life depends on it and you will only buy ingredients when they're on discount, all of this with the final goal of maximizing your profits. You will also quickly realize that some potions are more profitable than others. With some of them you will hardly make your money back or even lose money, it's up to you whether or not to satisfy your clients' orders or lose reputation in pursuit of that sweet sweet positive cash flow. If you're like me, you will organize your recipes maniacally, you will make spreadsheets with ingredient prices and brewing cost calculators, you will lose sleep over the best way to brew a potion, using both expensive and cheap ingredients in order to achieve balance and use them all in equal measure. You certainly don't want to accumulate ingredients just to end up never using them, do you? That's a waste of money. If you're like me, you WILL use the annotation function on each and every potion recipe, annotating the brewing cost, the selling price and the selling price after haggling. You WILL keep a ledger containing the costs of crafted items and you WILL calculate the price of each and every grain of the salts you use to make potions. For some reason sun salts are much more convenient to use than moon salts, i'll have to look into why that is. If you're better than me, you will quickly realize all of this is not healthy, it's true that there are no wrong ways of having fun with a game, but the game cannot become a second job. You need to scale back, cut down the hours you play or even uninstall it. It's not good for you to keep playing. Uninstall it. I beg of you. My every waking hour has been consumed by the potion game. I eat and think about potions, shower and think about potions, do chores and think about potions. I sleep and dream about potions. Potions. Prices. Sell. Buy. Must increase my profits. I have to. I have to make a better spreadsheet. I need to organize my recipes in decreasing order of profit. The recipe book must be appealing to the eyes. It's a must. I shall optimize every single aspect of this game or my life will never be complete. "Potion seller, i only want your strongest potions". Well guess what, peasant, my strongest potions aren't fit for you. They aren't fit for anybody. The potion you want is not profitable to make. It requires too much moon salts. I will not sell you my strongest potion for my strongest potion is not profitable. You will get the weak potion. You will like it and i will squeeze every last gold coin you have by save scumming my way through the haggling minigame. I am a god of time and commit no mistakes. Never. If i do, i alter reality and load a previous save game. I cannot waste money, i cannot waste ingredients. I. Must. Profit.But the game has also flaws. First of all, it's extremely resource heavy. Why is that? There's no reasonable explanation why this game consumes so much ram and GPU resources. Secondly, there's some stutters here and there. It would be fine expect for when you're haggling and a random stutters makes you lose money. That is annoying.There's also some quality of life improvements that would be much appreciated. Like automatically sorting the recipe book, allowing us to better place recipes by disabling the snap mechanic and so on. Small things but that would really make a difference in optimizing and streamlining my potion making routine in order to maximize the gold i make every single day.Finally, we need shelves. I want to stock my store to the brim with potions and there's not enough space on the counter, i want shelves, give them to me. Please send help.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this game is fun and I spent my morning playing it, but it really needs more content. I expected way more control over what happens in your shop because I mean, the description literally says, "You're in full control of the whole shop." Which is a lie.Let me tell you why:You have zero control over which herbs you collect because you aren't growing your own, you are simply harvesting whatever you find in your garden and buy from whatever vendor happens to stop by. You can't mix and match different herbs to create your own which the description also states. You can only create what the game allows you to, which isn't experimenting at all. You can choose from different potion abilities to create your own. Example: "poison/acid." However, that isn't really experimenting, it's more just combining a few things that your customers aren't even asking for. The lack of experimental potions is disappointing because that's one of the reasons I bought the game. To wrap up the review, I feel like the game was only fun because it's basically alchemist themed "Dealer's Life" which I played before on my phone. So, is it fun? Yeah, you'll get a few hours of game play but it gets annoying and you'll soon realize there's a lot about the game that needs revamped. Is it worth the price? No. I got it on a sale and paid $11 for it, and I still feel a bit gypped.I wish there was a "meh" recommendation, but I'm giving it a thumbs up just because I was able to burn 3 hours playing.

Customer asks are easy to pick up on, haggling is simple enough given that you can choose the difficulty.Some potential QOL changes that I would like to suggest though, since these were some of my pain points with the game:- Blank pages in book be stored separately than pages that have been written to. It's difficult to find new recipes when they're hiding under blank.- When purchasing from merchants, seeing a count of "X of this item in inventory currently"A suggestion (which may be a HUGE stretch but) I'd love to see Twitch Chat integration where chatters can randomly be chosen as clientele for the next day.That said though, I absolutely adore this game. _childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft is a really nice and chill game with a very interesting take on alchemy.Unlike Skyrim or any other RPG with an alchemy system, this game doesn't just ask you to toss together 2 or 3 ingredients to make a potion, instead this is almost like an adventure game, where you have a map and each reagent gives you the ability to move in a certain direction. It is a really interesting system that I'm not sure I've seen anywhere else. At times the game has frustrated me a bit, but in a way that a mad scientist trying to hit his goal kind of way. My main complaint is the sheer repetitiveness of the game, beyond that it has a recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun alchemy shop game. Basically you bounce between a mini-game of adding herbs to explore a map of various effects, organize your recipes and another mini-game to haggle for potentially more or less sale prices. There is a moral compass duality going on where you sell to people doing something "bad" or "good" and you will get more customers like that, but otherwise there are no other effects on the game nor narrative to follow.One con to this game is the chapters and content seem well paced until the very end, where there remains only 1-2 more objectives and they take hours of grinding (repeated activity without anymore exploration or creativity necessary). It seems like it would have been a better decision to end it earlier or otherwise include additional content to make this section more enjoyable. The customer requests can also seem mistranslated or confusing--for example someone might ask to go "fast" but what they really mean is more dexterous.Very fun for what it is, plays well on Steam Deck/controller though I recommend keyboard/mouse for efficiency. I also would say if you like this type of game to check out Strange Horticulture--it is more fleshed out and less of a mini-game/more of a story.

Obviously there is more to it, you're decisions matter to an extent. This game is one for the relaxing and curious mindset, as I've found myself playing this game, I've had the feeling to put on Sword in the Stone, dress in wizard attire, and have a goblet of the finest juices at my tableside. Can't promise you'll get the same side effects, but there is always promise.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe this game is little lacking. I played this game when it was a demo too, and now I have played it for 10 hours. I love it because topic and atmosphere what I'm looking for but I think there are two major problem. First, after a while no new customers come that is their stories and demands are same. Personally, I am fond of customer stories which are kind of a riddle. It's because you try to understand which kind of potion the customers want by listening them but a lot of time stories and solutions are easy, and it ruin the fun. Second, the game is too repetitive. There is a saving mechanic for solving this repetition problem but it isn't enough. When you repair the lab, you have to travel the map again, and I couldn't find an easy way to do that. In conclusion, I have a suggestion: little events could solve or decrease the two problem. For example, after you wake up you see a notification. "While you were sleeping, someone broke into your house, and steal some of your potions and herbs." After that we can try to learn who broke into our house by questioning our customers while selling them potions. I think some events like this might increase the fun and decrease the repetition. Thanks for that beautiful game. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but needs more content.As the game is now, it has promise. As an early access, it has enough content to give you a good taste of what the gameplay will be like.Ideas:It could do with giving you more herbs each day, as you have to find where each potion is on the "potion map" and at early game, unless you know, you're going to waste a lot. I found that on starting over, I did far better, but in my first play I did really badly.The bones on the map are really irritating, An ingredient that let's you go through them for one potion would be really cool. Alternatively, A level up trait that makes the potion more resistant to them.The music is nice, but could do with more variety, a few tracks would make it feel a bit less samey after a few hours. Alternatively, you don't really need sound for this game, so you can mute it and turn on something else.An option to apologise to customers for not having the herbs, as opposed to outright refusing them. Only available if you cannot actually make the potion. For a mitigated reputation loss.A sandbox mode would be nice, give you an infinite amount of herbs to just play with and experiment. Would be useful for finding things on the map so you can memorise them, without having to google them. When more content is added, I'll try to remember to update this review. But what I see so far, I like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game lets me live out my fantasy as an apothecary owner and alchemist! It's deceptively complex, with tons to explore and surprising mechanics. I love that the NPCs change based on your reputation, it brings a whole new challenge (especially if you intentionally ruin your reputation to see what kinds of stuff more nefarious customers ask for). It's highly addictive, satisfying, more extensive than meets the eye, and I CANNOT wait for more!

_childDocuments_.review: Make some potions.Sell some potions.Yell and cuss as you fail your ten minute ultimate potion.Actual review:I love the alchemy system, it's very interactive and for all the screaming I do there are many times I manage to pull a failure back from the brink which is extremely satisfying.  Dialogue isn't really repetitive yet, but it is very basic.  Would love to see (and would pay for) an expansion that adds more story/character interactions/insane potion combinations that take you forever to complete.I think the only thing that really stands out as kind of bland is the ingredient farming, having it more interactive would be nice.  Adding "fertilizer" you can craft from potions to make it produce more plants of a certain element or type would be neat.  Every time I go to that screen I wish something would surprise me, but I'm far more excited by a merchant showing up with one new type of mushroom lolEstimating that it'll take me 10-15 hours in all, unless there's more after the "chapters".  Either way, highly recommend this as a relaxing game that focuses more on making the alchemy aspect fun and interactive, but is light on character interactions and story.Update: And I was wrong.  Up to 17 hours and still quite a bit more content left.  On top of that I'm excited to see that this game will have further additions as well as the enjoyable content in the Discord!

_childDocuments_.review: 100% Yeeeeeeeee to brewing potions, and you're also doing alchemy recipes for your clients! :D It also teaches you to become more patient, not just a mixture of creative and painstakingly precise with the potion's journey on the map. It forces you to evolve your mind and train your thoughts with your book. Feedback?------- Though I wish there were a few ways to mark each essential recipe (for what alchemy machine-based recipes require), the same way for ingredients you may/would need later shortly would also be appreciated. Game Developers, I'd suggest you consider including a mechanism or an organization tab where the game lets you have pages be separated for empty blank ones and filled/written recipe pages to have a less complicated time navigating around through the book by either cursor or arrows/letter buttons to use perhaps? :)It makes sense to have a lot of backups (a lot of blank papers/either wholly or partially polished recipes for various purposes (tiers of strength, order of ingredients inside those 5 icons, and availability of your ingredients)!There's a need to make it easier to keep track of it (too many recipe pages or blank pages can become overwhelming for people who might need help organizing or keeping track of something; keep that in mind!).I'd also love to see more spicing up (puns intended) herbs/plants and possibly even a few new expansions or lands to explore outside your backyard instead of constantly staying inside your home/store and relying on other merchants to do the work.I also wish there was a way to clarify vague requests, just enough to understand what clients are asking you. I did have a bit of a hard time understanding what a few clients were asking me, and unfortunately, I annoyed a few of those clients over it. Some requests were vague, and sometimes, the other half used euphemisms (making it trickier).The last suggestion is to include a flexible tiny shortcut option to the journey pathing between the start and end (of a potion) of every interaction between an ingredient and another ingredient. It'd make the alchemy brewing feel less long to go through using a mouse.

_childDocuments_.review: I like cozy and relaxing sim games with cute art styles and this seemed to fit the bill. Unfortunately the game gets grindy and unappealing very quickly. What I thought would be a few slight ramps in difficulty or complexity or even a new level of crafting just turned into more of the same thing except annoying. There are positives here, I really enjoyed the first three to four hours and was going through parts of the game and customer requests quickly enough. The art style and music are also nice, the character's designs are cute and the references to other media is adorable. Unfortunately having a unique art style and soft fantasy tunes didn't keep me for long after I got to very unappealing section of the game. You just run out of ingredients for things constantly and if you want to experiment to make new things or see the map you end up out of luck because you just don't have access to certain things due to RNG and vendors. There are a lot of great concepts here but they just don't work together or it was easier to overlook them than spend the time dealing with it. That and the promise of more content which still hasn't been mentioned is odd. Its not for me at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator as its name suggests is a potion crafting game where you manage your own shop, buying and selling the potions that you brew. Playing it so far, I am loving every aspect of it including the gameplay, visuals and music which all fit well together. In this game and in your shop, you have various rooms including a garden where your ingredients grow daily, the kitchen where you brew the potions, the basement with exciting gadgets, and the front shop where you greet the customers in the town. The main sections are the kitchen and the front shop. In the kitchen, you have various tools to brew your potion including the cauldron, bellow, and mortar. By mixing and matching the ingredients and how you use the tools, you can brew various potions for the specific need of the customers. In the front shop, you are greeted by various people who tell a little story, and from that you find which potion they require. It is quite fun to read what they did or what happened for them to arrive here. Furthermore, there is a neat, little haggling option system where a minigame comes when selling your potion. Here you can either slightly raise the price of what you sell or lower the price of what you buy depending on how it goes. All in all, the gameplay portion is very entertaining as there are a lot of combinations to discover with the potion making.The visual aesthetics is very pleasing with the olden medieval look of the game, the texture and designs of everything, and the colours used. There are numerous amounts of ingredients and potions, all with their unique design which keeps the game more alive. Though the game already does this by the endless mix and matching, and discovery of the potion world. There is also an “Alchemist’s Path” chapters section where tasks are set out, which earns points going towards unlocking the next section which there are several of. The graphics also goes very well with the music that is played which is some charming and relaxing medieval like instrumental.The UI is friendly and simple to use with various section for things such as the potion making, ingredients and recipe portions. Controls are straightforward to use with mainly using your mouse to navigate through the game.The price of the game is well suited and fair to offer, with the game having great aesthetics and fun gameplay. Overall, it is a solid game and worth checking out if you want an entertaining potion making game or a nice simulation. I do recommend it since it has been very enjoyable so far and I’m looking forward to seeing what gets added and expanded in the future.

THE PRINCIPLE OF CAUSE AND EFFECT: "Every Cause has its Effect; every Effect has its Cause; everything happens according to Law; Chance is but a name for Law not recognized; there are many planes of causation, but nothing escapes the Law."It explains that: "Everything Happens according to Law"; that nothing ever "merely happens"; that there is no such thing as Chance... only law unseen.VII.) THE PRINCIPLE OF GENDER. "Gender is in everything; everything has its Masculine and Feminine Principles Gender; manifests on all planes."This Principle embodies the truth that there is GENDER manifested in everything — the Masculine and Feminine Principles ever at work.
