_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game, and I unfortunately did not return it on the hopes that it would become something I could enjoy but even after the major update, I still kinda hate it. My issues with the game won't be everyone's issues. One, I hate the haggle feature. I'm an older gamer who, let's be real, never had great reflexes in the first place. I don't want to do timed things. Period. Even the stirring feature is irritating to me because if I accidentally move my mouse too far, I can mess up a potion level. So the haggling is next level. On the easy level, it's fine (though not enjoyable to me), but on harder levels it's just too anxiety inducing for what should be a chill game. My other, bigger, main issue with the game is that it seems to punish exploration and experimentation, even as it requires it for progression. It's so easy to lose massive quantities of ingredients on wild goose chases, to accidentally "die" and reset back to center, to think you figured out the combo for a potion only to have it be something else and then not have the ingredients left to make the one you needed. Some of the whirlpools spit you out at seemingly useless or weird positions. Every time I try to play around and have fun with exploring the map, I just end up extremely frustrated, broke, and ingredient-less. The game is also very repetitive, as mentioned in other negative reviews. I don't always mind this in games, I love to grind, but the lack of a truly rewarding mechanic and the difficulty creating new potions makes the tedium...well...tedious. I love the artwork, and I love the premise, but sadly the execution of this leaves me wishing I could get my money back.

Empty pages could be removed from the book and instead replaced with a button that allows the player to add a new page.* The popularity requirements become ridiculous later and seem to be mainly for artificially lenghtening the game.*  Selling should become more automated with time, especially regarding the easy potions. For example, adding a shelf where customers can automatically pick up and pay for their requested potion, should it match.Overall, regardless of the criticism, it still is a fun and unique experience for some hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little puzzle game with a simple and satisfying mechanic for creating potions. Add ingredients whole or grind them for a different effect, carefully consider how finely you want to grind an ingredient to nudge your path this way or that, and then stir and dilute until you reach a perfect mix. Finally, boil the cauldron to lock in your potion effect. The potion map's hazard zones force careful use of rare ingredients, or you can brute-force your way through with larger numbers of cheap and common herbs. There are no timers to pressure you so feel free to take your time pondering whether to add Hairy Banana or Red Mushrooms, or plotting a route through several effects for a special health restorative sleep potion.

I cant experiment with so little ingredients per day, can't skip to the next day without seeing all the customers first either. merchant prices are too expensive and I can't turn much of a profit. There should be some sort of "foraging" option where I can visit enchanted garden locations and pick ingredients that replenish on a timer rather than day-by-day. It would also be nice to see merchants anytime for normally priced merch and then they come to you with discounted merch but I can understand if that messes up the balance of the game. So far, if I want to make money for the day, then I'm making health potions, poison, etc and using all my base ingredients. I'm on level 13 and im already kind of anxious to try doing anything more with my ingredients because I dont want to waste them all and not have enough for the customers. Leveling up alchemical ability only makes more "exp books" show up on the map and not anything else. I feel there's a lot of potential there for more potent brews (like a larger bottle icon or let me make strong brews and not have to perfectly center the icons), or better abilities like to forage more ingredients per plant in the garden, or even propagate the garden with a particular ingredient and then using quick grow or bountiful harvest potions to enhance them or to make certain plants grow or even crystals grow. Through exploring the brewmap, what if there was an option to unlock travel to different biomes with enchanted gardens in them that I can travel to? Like If I go all the way down on the map, I can unlock a cavescape with crystals, going all the way in the poison direction is a mushroom rich swamp, all the way left is a desert, and to the right is a forest etc.

_childDocuments_.review: I do think this is a fun game, clearly I enjoyed it enough given I've 100%'d it. However this game is very grindy if you want to 100% it. I've played this game since beta too. The early game is very fun as you have all the exploration you could want however it is held down by the struggle to get enough ingredients. I think the mid game is best I greatly enjoy the oil map exploration and the flexibility you have with more ingredients and money. Also I loved creating prefect recipes and customising the potions. The late game struggles though. One of my fav parts of interacting with customers is the little story bit you get, the fisherman the brewer the merchants telling you about their lives. In the end game you've run out of things like this and regular customer interactions feel like a slog cus it's all the same stuff you've heard before. I do like the additional requirements they add though. The alchemy machine stuff is fun but after sun salt it gets very grindy and loses it appeal. Plus finishing chapter X and Philosopher's salt are very underwhelming. You get 5000 Philosopher's salt with an effect that's just sort of fine. By the point in the game it's not very helpful and you've probably gotten very good at understanding and using the potion brewing mechanics like whirlpools and adding more base making the salt not that helpful. Plus the reward for finishing Chapter X is exp points which you definitely don't need seeing as you will have maxed out all your skills by the time you do Chapter X. It would have been nice to having something actually useful. A garden upgrade or whatever. Also the fact the save recipe function for salts and rocks isn't working is annoying cus you have to do it manually. I don't think I will boot this game up again after this cus there's nothing left to do. I feel like this game would benefit from the NPC's being just a bit more interesting. The fellow alchemist becomes useless pretty quick once you don't need paper anymore, I feel like it can't be that hard for him to congratulate you on academical progress. Overall, fun game with a super cute art style but grindy.

_childDocuments_.review: Looked interesting at first, but gets boring and repetitive after about 5 hours and just annoying by 10 or so hours.Not to be pedantic, but the 'alchemy' of this 'potion craft simulation' makes zero sense. Not like "I don't get this" but as in, "this is stupid."Most of the customers are basically criminals that either want to kill someone, or escape justice, but I'm fine with that.Magic tree giving you herbs once a day. Sure, why not.But to craft a potion you use ANY AND OR ALL available herbs and mushrooms and leaves etc  to explore the maps to get to the "craft me now" spot.And if you want or need a level 2 or 3 potions, or a combo potion, it's even more tedious and wasteful as you are chucking stuff into the pot to go in circles just to a few pixels away from the same point. Madness!Then you 'save' the "recipe".Then another customer wants it, but you are out of 1 or more of the many herbs you used, so you can't make it, so you skip (taking a reputation penalty), or you delete the saved 'potion' and find a next set of ingredients to get you to the spot  (any will do).The chemistry version would be "As long as you are at your desk, it's fine. Blocks of lithium, concentrated hydrochloric acid, sure, toss it in the pot with the rest, what can go wrong?"It's just too annoying.What I think it should have been was to explore to find the missing pages of the alchemy book to unlock them, then experiment to see what works. Instead anything and everything dropped into the cauldron works, just so long as the winding route around the (hard to read) map gets to the 'finish potion' stage.One to miss.(Reviewed as at v0.50)

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this one, but I can't in its current state. I bought this game two(ish) years ago in early access. The basic gameplay loop is satisfying, the artstyle cute, but at the time it felt like 50% complete . In the two years since, the devs have:With the 1.0 release and the 1.1 QoL release, this game now feels...about 55% complete. The basic gameplay loop is still there, but that is all there is. There is no story outside of the needlessly grindy 'quest' towards forging various salts (far too expensive for what they do and never necessary for actually doing things) culminating towards forging the Philosopher's Stone (insanely grindy, during my two 15 hour playthroughs I gave up well before coming close to getting the stone).The devs have been promising all of these features in development and just fail to deliver. I would love to see this game get the attention it deserves, and if the devs actually implement what they've promised I will easily recommend it. But I have my doubts.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not think I would like this very much, as I tend to like story games, but here I am, sweating the tiny degrees as I add water, wondering which way the foggy parasol mortar and pestle treatment moves the upper cap path, zooming past the boneyards on high-speed-stir, mapping the swirlies so that I can teleport  to save on ingredients. It's a little like cooking, and people stop in to tell you what they are up to as you help them (and occasionally haggle). I also like the music, so it's pretty relaxing. The little guide lines are really useful in lining up for a max strength potion. Warning: "big experience book" is FOUR books in a single clump, not five. Do not despair! You'll find some up in the NE area, got to wriggle through a passage in a bone wall to get there, though - fiddly, but that will show you new useful effects up there as well! From other players, all of the 4-book clumps are outside the first ring of bone walls, so you have to look for the gaps to complete Chapter 4.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: Game feels incomplete, doesn't feel like it lives up to advertising, gets boring the more advance it gets, and is very light colored which sometimes puts a strain on my eyes. I have mixed feelings on this game. I had fun for a while and have some friends that love it. But this game isn't finished and you can tell. First, there are some requests in the game that you just actually cannot fulfill. Sometimes customers come to me with special requests and I cannot do it based on what the request is and where the potions location is on a map. It is not the end of the world and would not turn me away, it is very rare, but I feel like that could have used a little more QA. Next, there are features shown in the game that you just can't use. For example one tab advertises to upgrade your shop tools. I was so confused as I could not figure out how to upgrade anything. Well I looked it up online and people were saying that it is an incomplete feature. Then when using the alchemy equipment I tried to save the recipe as that option is there but I noticed I could not select it. I again looked this up online and again it was noted that this was another uncompleted feature. Lastly there are the maps. Some potions are much harder to make on certain maps. They eat up a lot of ingredients and personally I don't feel like it makes sense to try and make them for customers when looking at potion selling cost vs. ingredient cost. I only make those potions when I have to because I am trying to make one of the key items I need to meet game requirements. There has been talk for a while of a third map that would definitely add to the game and make certain potions more practical. However I see many threads discussing that this has been coming for over a year with no updates. As it stands the two maps do not feel like enough, and I feel like this leads into the game feeling more repetitive and incomplete as the game progresses to more advance potions. The third map point leads into my other complaint - I also find some of the advertising misleading. To advertise you can grow your own ingredients doesn't make much sense to me. Sure, there are ingredients growing in your yard. However you have no control over what grows and don't interact with growing ingredients besides clicking to pick the daily randomly generated plants. The haggling system also isn't that extensive or interesting in my opinion. Just some quick clicks of a button if you need more cash. To call this a sandbox game is also a pretty big stretch. Also the whole "Sell your potions to the townsfolk while role-playing as a noble artisan, a greedy weasel, an occult dark master, or whomever else you may wish to be!" comment feels like a stretch too. This would literally just be you role-playing that is not a feature of the game. Sure if you sell to sketchy people your rep goes down or up. That does not align with the advertisement. I really wanted to love this game. I had fun for a while and if this type of game interest you I would for sure buy it on sale. It just doesn't feel worth it to finish the quests in game when it gets so repetitive and when you can see where it is lacking. Some of those "upcoming" features they advertise really felt like they should have been in the game upon release. There are areas you can see/click that just aren't completed. If they ever add those updates I'd happily come back and play more. But for now I just feel like I've reached a part where I get it and there isn't many more interesting things to be done. It does have a lot of potential and I'd be excited to try again with updates in place. Also one final note - I did recommend it to a friend that bought it because I thought she would like it a lot more than me. She ended up having to return it due to having a hard time reading the light colored map. I agree it can make my eyes sore after a while. I wish they had a different more visible color scheme option even if it breaks from the aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately this gets repetitive and boring by Day 3. There's no real rhyme or reason to the direction of potions on the map that, if you haven't discovered something yet, makes it very hard to infer what someone is asking for and where it may be on the potion map. It's a clever idea, but sometimes you just will not have the correct ingredients to go the directions you want, and the vendors show up so sporadically and randomly have ingredients that are both higher and lower cost than average, further limiting your available buying options. Your garden just is not sufficient for this purpose.If the whirlpools made any kind of sense on the map it would also be helpful, or you could mark them to where they go, it would be much better as a mechanic, but as some warp you to unique ares and some warp you an inch, it really is not an interesting mechanic either.You are also in general, penalized for exploring the map on your own, as if you don't have the ingredients to make a basic healing potion that someone wants because it's the only ingredient you have gotten in the past 4 days that goes to the right and you wanted to see what else was that direction, you lose reputation. Can't really recommend the game, it's close and the ideas are almost fleshed out, but somehow just don't work together the way I'm sure the designer wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: A good friend of mine purchased this game for me.Potion Craft is an incredibly chill, conflictless (so far) game revolving around you, an alchemist and potion salesman, brewing up concoctions for the local peasantry and warriors for everyday use, from healing potions to rodent poisons and other miscellaneous brews. The game involves learning how to most efficiently use herbs and fungi grown and bought with correct use of the mortar and pestle as well as experimenting with your ingredients to find cheaper, easier ways to brew potions that previously required a lot of effort material-wise. The game, while in early access, has very clearly defined methods to playing that are very easy to catch onto, and feel satisfying to execute in normal gameplay. Perfect game to wind down with after a long day.Not too complex, yet innovative enough to warrant buying. It's cheap and fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Before you buy, PLEASE watch a video of the gameplay because I don't think I would have bought if I'd known how the gameplay loop works. (It's not bad, it's just personally not for me.)I really wanted to like this game - I was drawn to the simulated act of picking plants, grinding them, adding them to my cauldron, and selling potions to customers. But I noticed a sharp drop off in the Steam achievements, with about 50% of players completing chapter 1 of 10 and 1% of players actually finishing the game. I imagine that most people drop off because unfortunately, a lot of the game is a repetitive grind. Pretty much my biggest problem with it is that it feels. so. repetitive.The game started out great, beautiful artwork and fun mechanics. I enjoyed exploring the map. But then I learned that exploring the map consumed materials rapidly, especially as I traveled further from my starting point - which, by the way, is the same no matter what. You always start at the same point in the map, and by mid-game, you have traveled over the same areas over and over again. It was fun to fulfill requests at first, but then they became repetitive too. Unlocking alchemy seemed promising and I was hopeful as I created the first materials (Nigredo), until it turns out that it just requires the same gameplay but with even more grinding. Now I don't mind grinding when I think the effort is worth it, but this game didn't offer enough "newness" to keep me engaged.Another problem I have is with inventory. I never have enough of a particular plant, which is alright - that's what vendors are for! Except you have no guarantee that any particular vendor will be available when you need them. Which is still alright as long as they appear often enough - except most of the time the herbalist or mushroom guy aren't carrying what I need! My garden will not stop giving me more of a plant that I already have 100+ of, but yields like 3 of another plant that I have 0 of. Lack of control over inventory (being unable to grow or buy what I need even when I have the gold) contributed a lot to my frustration.Overall, this is a game for some people who enjoy the gameplay loop, and I still think the early game is fantastic. It just didn't have much to offer me past the first few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got a ways to go but I am so here for this! _childDocuments_.review: Really interesting and has a ton of potential. I love the game. This is a pure crafting game, with the shop part being there to only add value and perspective to the crafting part. Hopefully they expand on the shop side to make it a more important part of the game. When the shop becomes more valuable to the player, they in turn care more about the potions they make, and with more investment in their potions they care about the results they get in the shop. It's the two systems synergising that make these games really fun, so I hope they invest more effort into that gameplay loop. I do really like the NPC interaction.Most of its problems are because features aren't implemented yet. For example it's really only viable to craft potions consistently with the original four plants, because they're the only ones that spawn in bulk, since the garden mechanics haven't yet been developed. Things like that.Hopefully this goes somewhere great. I'm really enjoying to so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, cool concept, cute visuals, and fun to play. I enjoyed it enough to 100% it, but while the beginning is fun, past mid game it gets extremely tedious. I would give this a middle thumb rating if I could, because while the beginning is indeed fun, the mid to end game is frustrating. You will have plenty of recipes for certain potions, so that you don't have to spend minutes making the exact same potion over and over, but they only work if you have the ingredients for the recipe, which you have absolutely no control over, as your enchanted tree, which gives you ingredients every day, is completely random on which ones you get, and the merchants that sell you ingredients, also completely random! Meaning that you may have to simply delete one of your recipes because you haven't been given a certain ingredient in weeks. There is also an alchemy machine, which you use to make the ingredients for the philosopher's stone, very cool concept, until you get into it, you have to make a ridiculous amount of super specific potions that only work for making the stones, which in of itself takes quite a while. But, because these potions are super specific, they require a lot of ingredients, which goes back to my previous point. On top of that, you have to hand insert all the potions you made, as there is no recipe to instantly make the gemstones. At one point, I had to make a salt to help make the potions I needed, I had to go through cooking things up in the alchemy machine... 15 times!! It took like 10 minutes just to finish making the salts.Finally, the final achievement, in which you have to get to level 15 alchemy level, took me 5 hours of extra playtime, just giving potions to new customers, and taking reputation hits when people would come in for legitimately impossible orders.TL;DRI am conflicted on whether to give this a thumbs up or down, I like the game, but it gets stale pretty damn fast. This is all coming from somebody who loves to 100% games, if you are a casual player who will pick this up, play until you feel fulfilled and leave, I highly recommend it. But the 100% grind is so mind numbing and tedious that I had to push myself to make it all the way
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game with some simple but satisfying mechanics. First few hours give your the satisfaction of exploring, and I insist on this sense of exploration. Your try ingredients, get where you want on a map, in order to "join" new effects for your potion. Rewarding and addictive. BUT. The true problem comes after those few hours, because if you want to finish the game, meaning creating your Magnum opus, everything becomes super grindy. Like, super very awfully grindy. Few new mechanics have been announced and could help, but right now they are missing. Overall the game shines from a good gameplay base but suffers from lack of content. Cruelly. I wouldn't recommend it in it's current state, but would revise my judgement if improvements arrise.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the idea, but the execution didn't excite me. I think what bothered me the most in the early game was that buying ingredients just didn't make economic sense. So, I felt rather locked into using the four basic ingredients over... And over... And over.The saved recipes did save a bit of time, but I quickly found myself not selling potions that I didn't have recipes for, because I just couldn't be bothered. Especially healing potions, which pay absolutely nothing and hence only serves getting reputation. (I didn't have a recipe for it, because it almost isn't worth the ingredients put into it)I think the best way to put is that this game felt like a minigame, except it's the whole game. And it's a slow, repetitive minigame.Perhaps it could get better in the future with some more ways to manipulate the brewing process and whatnot, but it just didn't do anything for me at present.

_childDocuments_.review: Rewarding medieval potion crafting game.  It take a while to get how to play but once you get the hang of it you can make progress fairly quickly.  You have to move around an alchemy 'map' by adding ingredients to a cauldron.  Each ingredient has its own path on the map so you build paths by combining the ingredients.  The 'effects' such as healing, poison etc are hidden around the map and when your path reaches them, you can add that effect to the potion.  Later one you make potions with multiple effects.  Experience points are also scattered around the map as book icons and many of the ingredients have paths designed just for gathering these icons.There is a haggling system but I never got into it.  Merchants will appear from time to time and offer you ingredients or equipment.  If you run out of certain type of ingredients you can get stuck having to wait for a merchant to have what you need.  There is a 'garden' next to your workshop that gives you a few basic ingredients each in-game day, but it isn't enough to sustain completely.  After you make a fair bit of money you can buy large amounts of ingredients, but the ones you need might not be available in the needed quantities.  I always run out of ingredients that move up and right.  There are plenty of ingredients that move down and to the left.  I really liked the visual style of this game and enjoyed playing about 20 hours so far.  It started to feel grindy in the second half of that, but all games of this type feature grinding to some extent.  It is quite rewarding to brew a perfect potion, as they strength of the potion is determined by how precisely the potion marker matches the marker on the alchemy map.  If you get it centred perfectly you can make a tier 3 potion.  It takes a bit of patience to get them exact.The later part of the game shifts from selling potions to fixing your alchemy machine and assembling more complicated recipes with multiple potions, and multiple effects in each potion.  I stopped at this point as I got tired of waiting for the merchants to offer enough ingredients of the right kinds.  I may come back to finish it sometime.  There are seven in-game chapters, and I finished 5 plus some of the 6th in 20 hours.  There are no steam achievements, just chapter breaks in the game.Overall I would highly recommend this to anyone who likes the idea of alchemy, herbs, folk medicine or medieval themes.  It's nice to play a medieval themed game that isn't centered around warfare or the succession of royalty.  It has a relaxed pastoral feel with a beautiful wood-carved style.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: In this game you craft potions with ingredients to sell to customers. But your crafting is like a chessboard, and your ingredients your chess pieces - each with their own unique movement style. You need to experiment and work out how to reach a location/potion effect in the most optimised way to be cost efficient, but also your potion strength is controlled by how accurately you line your potion up with the effect. If you enjoy gathering resources, crafting, and finding satisfying solutions, then this will be a relaxing game for you to sink some hours into.

_childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft shows excellent promise as a shop management game, with a unique medieval inspired art style and sandbox crafting systems that places emphasis on player ingenuity. The gameplay loop consists of harvesting ingredients from your garden, crafting and selling potions to your customers, buying supplies from traders and experimenting to perfect and create new potion recipes. This is all done in a solid physics engine where potion bottles clatter and flip when you toss them and minerals give a satisfying crunch and crumble under your mortar and pestle.In it's current early access state, the game runs well and I personally didn't notice anything broken, though some users have reported running into bugs, and has about 10 hours of progression content followed by an endless grind. The developers also have an extensive roadmap of content they want to include in the final game, which will add further depth and replayability.If the game looks like something you would enjoy, you probably will.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no reason for this game to be as addictive as it is.  The concept is simple, there's goals but no real story (other than the one I developed in my head as I played), and there are no clever puzzles to solve or monsters to fight.  And yet, I love this game.   There is something satisfying about crafting custom recipes and figuring out the pathway to find new ones.  I enjoyed figuring out how to get where I needed to go using ingredients I had on hand and there are moments of surprising tension as a potion nears an explosion point but can be saved with a delicate hand.  This is not a game like any other and fits nicely into a gentle, almost meditative space in a gamer's library.  Don't dismiss the seemingly simple premise of this game.  You'll find time flies by once you start.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the general lack of instructions regarding certain things like what whirlpools do and just exactly how those crafting machines work, this game is basically a crafting exploratory game. Explore the map to find unknown potions, figure out how to make those potions with the least amount of ingredients, how to make the highest grade or combined potions and satisfy customers who sometimes make special requests.Once beyond the main menu, instructions are generally pictorial which can be a bit puzzling. However, a large part of this game is all about exploring and experimenting. All the herbs, mushrooms and crystals have a designated path so being creative in path building to the target is a necessary requirement.Most strategy is involved with the customers and making money. Though money is not the main focus, it is needed for alchemy machine upgrades, ingredients (herbs, mushrooms, crystals, and especially the much needed potion recipe paper) that need to be purchased. There several merchants that stop by on a regular basis (one merchant per day) who offer specific items. Which items, when, and how much is purchased is all part of the overall game strategy. It is possible to haggle with both merchants and customers (which is explained in-game) but can be difficult for those with slow reflexes. Haggling is not required expect for one chapter list requirement.   There are ten chapters total, each with a list of requirements to complete. Any requirement from any chapter once completed is recorded. This can be accessed at any time so progress can be tracked. Achievements are game play based and most, if not all, can be achieved while playing. The two reputation achievements are the only ones that need special attention and most likely some grinding.  Throughout the game play there are progress points earned which can be used to increase money received from customers, increase the rate of map clearance, increase number of level point books and haggling ability.Highly recommended for crafting buffs especially since there is no grinding needed for progress, only creative thinking. Plenty of crafting to do, lots of exploring needed and enough strategy to keep busy and not be bored. Easy enough for all with focused requirements for progress. Worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game in October of 2021, and had some fun, especially in the beginning. Towards the end, everything became kind of repetitive, so i quit playing, hoping for some sort of update that would add more depth to the gameplay. Since then, there have been roughly a dozen or so of announcements from the devs, 3 of which talked about/announced new features (save states, a new haggle minigame, and an autohold feature). To be fair, there was an event and new textures, but i don't really care about that. All 3 of these "updates" seem very minor, something that could have been done in a week, not 2-3 months each.Anyway, my point is that the communication & progress from the devs has been staggeringly bad, epetially considering how popular the game is- steadDB estimates the game has sold at least 200k copies, which should be more than enough to pay for a couple of full-time developers. Yet we've seen seen almost nothing in terms of progress. Did they just take the money and run?Don't buy this game. You'll have fun for a few hours, then get bored and decide to wait for more features to get released- which, for now, seems like it'll never happen.

_childDocuments_.review: So it needs some improvement, but it's pretty cool so far.I think the tutorial needs a bit of fleshing out (skill points, didn't know I had them until I amassed like 20; reputation vs popularity; the fact that potions fail if you touch certain spots on the map, and that the strength of the potion relies on how close you can get to the icon, stuff like that). It's pretty difficult to have enough ingredients, the later in the game it gets, so maybe a way to grow more, or get a whole lot more gold to buy stuff, since I found it very challenging and while that made it a puzzle that was interesting in the beginning, it started getting frustrating after a while because there's no way to make certain potions more than once every few days. One big issue is that the haggle mechanic is either broken or I misunderstood how it works. No matter what I do, if I haggle, I get a bad deal. And that's if all the little gold icons are on the left or the right or literally anywhere other than the starting position before you click something. I'm not sure if you need to get your haggle skill higher, since I only put one skill point into it, but it's not clear to me if that's why it's not working.I did have a lot of fun though, and will be playing more of it. I think as long as the developers keep working on it, it will turn into a pretty good game! Graphics are cute, there are some fun easter eggs in there (I spotted a witcher and someone hunting down a guy with a strange scar on his forehead who owns an invisibility cloak, as well as a certain mage with a mushroom covered hat, so far). I'm excited to see what the calendar and other mechanics will be like.

_childDocuments_.review: This one-of-a-kind simulator will charm you with its delightful aesthetics and unique gameplay. Set in medieval times, you take on the life of a rookie alchemist managing a potion shop. You must try and satisfy townsfolks’ needs and desires while honing your skills as an alchemist and as a merchant.Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator is the first big project for developer Niceplay Games. It was published by TinyBuild which is quickly becoming quite a hallmark in the growing world of indie gaming, with titles such as Hello Neighbor and Graveyard Keeper under its belt. Welcome, new alchemist!The game greets you with a bit of background information before guiding you directly to your new potion shop, which will serve as experimentation ground, as marketplace, and as your home. The short and sweet tutorial will hold your hand through the first few steps: how to get ingredients for potions, how to create potions and discover new recipes, and how to interact with townsfolks and sell them your goods. Before any of the narrative even begins, you will be enthralled by the sepia yet vibrant visuals. I cannot get over how uniquely beautiful the aesthetics of this game are – not only are they clean and very pleasing to the eye, but they also create a soft and immersive ambience. The graphics and the soundtrack work together in conveying a soothing medieval setting, and altogether enhancing the gameplay through improving the simulator aspect of the game. They capture you and suck you into the little world they create. This game is a true work of art. The user interface is also exceptionally clear – we do not get lost in the various components of the game and menus. Everything is very intuitive. Step 1: Make potions!Most of your in-game time will be spent crafting potions, and it is by far the most innovative, creative, and riveting part of the gameplay. It is quite simple and intuitive at its core: you drag and drop some items from your inventory into a cauldron, hold the ladle and move around to stir, then heat it up to create a potion. Ingredients in your inventory are acquired from your garden (you grow your own flowers and mushrooms) or purchased from various merchants that pass by your store on occasion. You may also choose to put ingredients into a mortar and crush them with a pestle before putting them into the cauldron, altering their effects. This is pretty fun in itself, but the real fun runs one layer deeper: there is a potion-making map, that you uncover more and more through trial and error. Every ingredient you choose to mix in has a specific trajectory in which it will drag your recipe on the map. You may also add water to strategically dilute your potion, dragging your recipe towards the center of the map. This is like an exploration mini-game, perfectly embedded into the crafting/simulation game! The map itself even has obstacles that affect your potion if your recipe goes through them. The map seems to be quite extensive, and the recipes numerous and diverse, especially considering they can be fused (e.g. a poison potion can be fused with an explosion potion to combine their effects!). One more thing that particularly caught my attention: the customizability of potions design. While it does not affect gameplay whatsoever, all potions you create are highly customizable in design. You may select from hundreds of pot shapes, sizes, labels, symbols on labels, and colour combinations. I caught myself spending so much time customizing all my potions to make them look cute and unique!Step 2: Make money?Every day, there will be about ten people at your doorstep. Most of them will have a request for you that you will try and fulfil with a potion that satisfies their needs, which they will then buy from you. This is how you’ll be making money and increasing your popularity and reputation. Some of the people that visit will be merchants from which you can purchase a variety of special goods (ingredients for potions, recipe book pages, etc.). In both situations, you may choose to haggle with the visitor, in which case, you will be given a little reflex mini-game, where you have to click on a bar at the right time (think of it like timed attacks in Paper Mario or skill checks in Dead by Daylight) as many times as possible. If you succeed, this results in a better deal for you. I think it is neat in concept but haggling becomes repetitive quite fast – so much so that after two hours of gameplay, I decided to just not haggle anymore. It wasn’t worth the hassle for a few more coins. I hope that the full version of the game develops haggling further, because it is a good idea and should not be ditched, but it is too repetitive and insipid in its current state. Interactions with fellow townsfolks are interesting and sometimes colourful in flavour text, but they would also benefit from a bit more depth and variety, as they are currently quite flat.Wait, there’s more?It is noteworthy that this game also features an RPG element – you acquire experience which allows you to level up one of four skills that improve your alchemist or merchant qualities. Your character also builds up (and loses) reputation and popularity through certain interactions (haggling too much, selling a dangerous potion to a sketchy person, etc.). There are many achievements to keep track of your progress and to have concrete longer-term goals. These details are fantastic additions to this simulator. There is also an absolutely beautiful garden in your store that provides you with daily ingredients for your potions.While I have absolutely nothing negative to say about the visuals and the soundtrack which made me fall in love at first sight, as well as the potion making, the game in its current early-access version lacks depth in certain of its mechanics and would benefit greatly from further work. This is mostly evident in the merchant aspect of running the potion store – haggling, most notably, and adding personality and variety to the recurrent townsfolks – but also in other tiny aspects of the game aside from the potion-crafting. It would be fantastic to be able to tend to the garden or just interact with it more than merely clicking on plants that randomly appear daily. Your own room is also quite insignificant: in its current state, it never changes, and all it does is serve the purpose of allowing you to start a new day (and thus refresh your plants and clients). It could change as your store grows, it could also be where you write recipes, where you look at your achievements, etc. You could also buy furniture for it and seeds for your garden. The leveling aspect as well as popularity and reputation are a bit inconsequential as well. Some of these side elements feel too much like an afterthought, in this early access version of the game.Final remarksAll in all, however, Potion Craft’s shortcomings are outbalanced by how brilliant the potion crafting is – which is perhaps why the social aspect seems so lacking by comparison. Everything other than the alchemy itself feels underdeveloped and like it has a lot of untapped potential. Once again, let us also keep in mind that this is a review of the demo version, so we can expect many improvements. And I have to say, even in its current state and in spite of its flaws, I would be buying the game. It is incredibly relaxing yet engaging, clean yet vibrant, simple yet deep. Everything is just so… pretty and captivating. Potion Craft will attract you with its artistry and hook you with its potion-making gameplay. You will keep wanting to create more potions, try more recipes, customize more pots, and explore your crafting map. The other stuff is far from perfect, but that is not why you will be playing the game anyways. Potion Craft is, after all, an alchemist simulator, and it does serve that excellently.

_childDocuments_.review: I was NOT expecting this game to be so immersive. Whoever came up with the potion-making mechanic is a GENIUS. It preserves the excitement of discovery while also giving you just the right amount of direction to make you feel like you're actually progressing based on logic rather than luck or brute force. I love when games allow you to discover them authentically, without the need for background research (googling feels like cheating to me); this makes the learning experience--which is, and should be, an important part of this game--feel immersive and exciting. This game falls right in that sweet spot, like Return to the Obra Dinn and Hollow Knight (and unlike Minecraft, which I still love, but the Minecraft learning experience is significantly more community-based rather than integrated into the game itself). However, after 5h of play, the game does leave me with two questions:(1) What is the role of Reputation?  Popularity is well-specified, but I'm not certain what Reputation does. I think having a better reputation improves the prices merchants offer you, but I'm not sure yet. I think it could be cool to have different "alignments" as an alchemist where seedier merchants will give you better prices if your reputation is worse. It is also incredibly easy to lose reputation points (you gain rep points 2-3 at a time, but the max I've lost off a single sale is 30), which makes sense, but just be aware. (2) Are the "book points" you earn from completing parts of the Alchemist's Path the same as the experience points you get from picking up books while making potions? This is probably a stupid question that will be answered with more play. I think both of these questions will be answered as I accumulate more playtime, but I look forward to the release of the manual in the full version. It could also be cool to be able to buy or brew different fertilizers for the enchanted garden that encourage different kinds of plants to grow. 5/5 stars. I absolutely love this game--can't wait for the full version!!

_childDocuments_.review: I really have to give this game a thumbs down.Is there enjoyment here for those that just want to pick it up and play for 30 minutes to an hour from time to time? Yes, I’d say so. Is there enjoyment here for those that want a game they can complete from start to finish? Absolutely not unless you’re into masochism. Why? The game is just is a massive chore to get through by the end. You will experience the entire gameplay loop within the first 10 minutes of play, which consists of adding plants to a cauldron that aid you in travelling in different directions to reach specific points on a map to create a stock of potions you on-sell to customers; then repeat that same gameplay loop for over 30 hours until you reach end-game. It’s a massive, massive grind of a game. To add, there’s no story at all beyond a little blurb at the beginning about how your shop came to be. But there is what is called an ‘Alchemist’s Path’ where you have 10 chapters to get through with each containing mundane goals including creating specific potions, creating salts that add different elements to your travel on the map, and reaching a certain level of popularity amongst customers. It has to be said that every character (or customer) that passes through is just as lifeless as the one that preceded them. None of them have any backstory, and you’ll see each character model hundreds of times over; all with similar banal requests in relation to what type of potion they require. That’s it.If you like, have a look at the global achievement statistics to get a good idea on how many players have completed Potion Craft. Of the 10 chapters, the unlock rate for completing each subsequent chapter tapers downwards all the way to where only 1.1% of players have the achievement upon completion of chapter 10 at the end. 1.1%! Sorry, but that tells you more than what I can express in words.The game is technically quite sound to play and it runs well without any problems or bugs, and the core element of using plants with different directional output to traverse the map is quite a good idea, too; there just needs to be a huge overhaul in the game design to remove the ungodly grind and make the game fun for people to actually complete. Overall, you know what they say; less is more. If there were to be a Potion Craft 2, perhaps the developer could take inspiration from similar games such as Strange Horticulture or Papers, Please where there is a much more condensed experience and a story woven in with memorable characters. Because as it stands, Potion Craft outstays its welcome; and then some.

_childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft fills a similar niche for me to MineCraft's Thaumaturgy mod. The focus on progressing and unlocking new recipes is a fun challenge. It's incredibly satisfying to dilute and mix potions to be the best that they can be. The alchemy machine being used to make the different crystals and alchemical reagents is also pretty fun since it gives you a reason to keep brewing manually when the efficiency of magic paper makes brewing obsolete. That said, there are a few things I see flaw in with the current iteration of the game. (Early October, 2021)At present this game becomes monotonous pretty quickly. When you're able to save recipes the game becomes incredibly simplified and the lack of variety in the content becomes more noticeable. The frequency of merchant visits mixed with the strength of haggling for bulk purchases is absurd. I am buying out every person that shows up offering to sell me anything every time they come. You make more money than you can possibly spend. I have hundreds of gems and 10s of thousands of plants and mushrooms. At six to seven customers a day each asking for one potion, I cannot offload enough product to consume this many reagents. Magic Paper is a big contributor to this game becoming monotonous, since you only have to craft a perfect potion once to ALWAYS have it available. Combined with the broken reagent economy Magic Paper is far to common. At 200 Gold for a permanent autocraft of any recipe you want? Why brew potions manually or by order when you can just craft 20 of each instantly and not use any reagents for a week or two? It might be less overpowered if these papers had a finite amount of uses before the paper gets consumed. At present though actual effort is temporary but P A P E R I S E T E R N A L. Finally, there's little reason to explore the alchemy map at present once you've found all the different flavors of magic gogurt. All the potion effects are closer to the center than the edges, and as such the only real reason to explore the outer 50% of the map is to collect XP Bubbles. This becomes doubly pointless when you'll earn plenty of XP from bartering, regular brewing, and perk-sourced regenerating XP orbs that respawn each day. All this in mind, I do recommend the game because it is enjoyable despite these flaws, and it's still in early access so who know's where the game will be in a year or two.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;A fun game which contains more then I thought it would. relaxing and challenging at the same time.9/10 for me. (ignore my playtime, I played offline for about 30 hours or so).The detailed review:You make potions and sell them to adventurers, townfolks, good and evil people for different purposes.The game contains several mechanics and inner games, complementing each other, which you need to progress in, in order to finish the game (potion discoveries, potion creations, selling to people which has haggle mechanics which I liked and is quite challenging at high levels, and alchemy machine creation and operation which gets very complex at high levels).The way it works is you have a potion "discovery" map, the different potion locations are hidden from you, and the map is full of obstacles which you cant not see until you encounter them.You navigate this map by brewing different plant and mineral ingredients into your cauldron, anywhere from 1 to infinite amount of ingredients, each one moves your location on the map based on a specific path unique to that ingredient, and you can take part of the path or all of it, and also use water the center yourself a bit in relation to your origin point.Overall it allows for pinpoint exploration on a fairly large map that is not so easy to navigate with all the thorny obstacles.You discover potion formulas on the map over time as you progress in discovering it and then you can make that specific potion you discovered and sell it.There are maybe 30 potions or so, each unique, and you can create mixed effect potions, with 2 or more effects combined.The customers come to your shop every day looking to buy potions to solve their problems. some are for good purposes and some are for evil ones, and you can decide to sell or not to sell, which affects your overall alignment as good or evil and which progressively affects the types pf future customers who show up at your shop.At the same time there is a morale mechanics at work, which is part of your advancement in the game, based on how many potions you've discovered and sold, whether or not you've haggled for prices, your advancement with the alchemy machine and what you create with it, and this affects how many customers per day you get, which allows you to sell more potions and make more money.You get the ingredients daily from your garden which grows them, which at first is all that you have, but as time passes, sellers start to appear and sell you ingredients, and you rely more and more on them, and you need to prioritize what to buy and try to haggle with them for better prices.might sound a bit complicated, but its really quite easy when you get into it.The game requires patience for potion discoveries, some strategy for potion creation and sale and some very quick reflexes for the advanced haggling mechanics,I've played it for about 30 hours, and i'm not done, I estimate im about 60-70% away from full completion, and i paid 9.99 for the game on sale, so I got a about 50 hours worth of playtime for 10 euro (about the same in Dollars) which is a good and fair price.Recommended.Hope this helps someone make up their mind (:

_childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft is a good game for those who enjoy simple, time-killing games. If you're looking for a challenge or a game to grind for hours, this probably isn't for you. The game can get repetitive very quickly, because not much changes day by day. I personally don't mind any of that, but I know a lot of people will.(Skip the part below if you'd like to go into the game blind, although I don't recommend that)In Potion Craft, you take the role of an alchemist. Every day, you go to the garden to collect materials to craft potions. Sometimes, traders will show up at your door and offer you items. Once that's over, you start to get customers. Customers will rarely tell you exactly what potion they'd like. Instead, they tell you what they need the potion for, and it's up to you to decide what to give them. You'll get more money for potions that best fit what the customer is asking for. I'd also like to say that this game has one of the best crafting systems I've seen in all of the games I've played throughout my life. Potion icons are spread out across the map. Crushing and dropping ingredients into the pot will push your potion in a certain direction. Once you're touching a potion, you can fully stop there, but if you want to make the best potion possible, you'll add 1-2 extra ingredients to give the potion a tiny nudge in the right direction, and water it down to push the potion towards the center. If your potion is perfectly aligned with the icon, you'll get a level 3 potion, which gives the highest rewards in terms of popularity and money.You can also choose to deny people potions. If their intentions are bad, denying them will increase your reputation. This along with many other mechanics are what makes this game good. I just wish it weren't as repetitive.Overall Score:7.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I started out loving this game; it's quite decent at what it sets out to do, which is as its name suggests, a potion crafting simulator. The thrill of discovering new ingredients and optimizing potions, however, quickly wears out. After a few days of play it simply becomes a slog of repetitive mechanics while venturing through a map where the excitement of discovery has plateaued. The addition of oil as a new base is a nice refresher, albeit a very temporary one. If that was the only criticism I had, however, I would still recommend the game as it was still quite enjoyable for however long you can bear the repetition, as with any sandbox/simulation style game. The main gripe is how the developers dangle these new mechanics which seemingly promise drastic changes to the game. After they hiked up the price, I was excited as I thought that it meant the update was coming soon. It has been probably over a year now and the only features they added were small fixes and features, while the elusive major update still loomed with no set date. As of now, the only things I do in the game is recreate old potions for the same customers, who very occasionally ask for a niche potion that I have to make from scratch. The alchemy set doesn't really add much to the game as it is essentially a disguised grinding mechanic. With all the potential it has, the late-game has essentially boiled down to a glorified Cookie Clicker. The one background track playing over and over also does not do it any favors. I do hope that the game developers focus more on replayability instead of novelty, as the game really has potential to be a casual game to play just for a few minutes. However, knowing that there really isn't a financial incentive to do so, it is just a pipe dream at this point.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Just a cozy little crafting game. Not much to say about it, unfortunately - nice visuals, simple gameplay, short completion time. The atmosphere of being alchemist starts strong - first few hours looks promising, but it just halts into points grind from there. Mechanichs seem very barebone, they could've gone so much deeper with them, but once you've unlocked all basic stuff that's basically it - you won't see anything more. Potential is there, yet they decided to stop right at the gates. Still worth trying
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I really really want to recommend potion craft but the complete lack of major updates since launch has given me no reason to play since I'd already put alot of time (well over 3 hours I'd say) into the demo. everything about this game is great, everything has those little details that dont add alot on their own but put together they improve the experience by a ton. but again the lack of anything new to do or work towards is the pull of the trigger for me
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Have you had an urge to leave society, live in a cottage alone, and collect plants to brew into potions? Well, you're in luck, because that's literally what this game is! You play as a young alchemist - that is, someone who uses the science of mushrooms, herbs, roots, and even special stones, to make special brews - who is starting a new life in a new town, and has a lot of work to do. Word gets around fast in this town, so how well you make potions and sales reflects on your overall reputation as a professional. You even make a few merchant friends who want to help you by selling and trading the goods you need to keep your doors open and your cauldron full. If you play your cards right, you can be the best alchemist in the land!The game is only very recently released, but I'm madly in love with it! The only thing I haven't been able to figure out is how to finish building the machine in the basement - I feel like I was supposed to finish it forever ago and just... haven't. I also didn't notice a huge difference on Haggling after upgrading that perk, but I'm also terrible at it, so maybe I'm not paying attention when I should be. There are still several features that are not in the game yet that I look forward to seeing and playing with, But this has my support so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome idea ! Really good game design. I think this has a lot of potential. Had a lot of fun ^^A few feedbacks before the game launches fully;-I don't get what I can use the machine for. It's a long and hard quest to craft the first recipe in the machine. (Nigredo) And when you finally craft it, seemingly nothing happens. And I can't seem to use Nigredo for anything. So there is no motivation to use the machine for further research. (Maybe also telling a tale about the philosopher's stone being a big deal or letting the player know how it can benefit them in-game would help)-Currently the rythm is pretty good, but at times I feel like it slows down so much to the point where I can't explore anything new for days because I never seem to have enough materails. I'm not sure how you could fix this but maybe more of the most basic materials(windbloom, waterbloom, terraria and firebell) in the enchanted garden or the merchant would make it so much more fun because the player will be able to explore more recipes and open up the map more. This can be done since I think you'll have multiple maps in the final build. -Reputation system should have very clear consequences I think. And it can be harder as well. I can stay at 100 reputation consistently. A guy wants a Charming potion. I give him exploding charm potion, probably literally killing a girl somewhere xD (It drops my reputation, which is great that you guys tought of this. Awesome xD) But I go back up to 100 rep in the next 2 customers.Overall I think this really succeeds at what it's trying to do, and it's a lot of fun ! Good luck <3
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I really want to like this game but as of now, the development seems to be dead.I bought the game when it became available in Early Access in September 2021 and I have to give props to the devs for the concept and aesthetic of the game.This is a very soothing game, perfect for unwinding during short breaks.Sadly, the game is pretty barebones as of now, which means that after a few hours you will have seen/done everything the game has to offer. This is fine by itself for the pricetag but it does leave a bitter aftertaste because it could be so much more.Sadly, the devs have stopped posting any kind of gameplay updates after the Early Access release and have only produced behind the scenes concept art and ideas on their social media channels.This is such a shame really, because the game got nominated for the Steam Awards, which shows that the game has potential down the road.TL;DR: Feel free to grab this if it's on sale but be aware that there might not be any further updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Unique potion making system that makes you feel like you're actually some sort of alchemist combined with a simple but enjoyable shop simulation makes Potion Craft a great experience!The tutorial sets up the main mechanics and gives you a set of objectives, but otherwise leaves you to experiment and learn how things work on your own. While this could be frustrating for some players, I felt that the few things the game didn't outright explain were minor enough that it felt good when I figured it out on my own. (With the exception of the Talents, that should've been explained.)Creating potions is the core of this game, and essentials boils down (hehe) to choosing ingredients to "move" a target around this giant map of possible potions. If you land your target on a potion you make it, simple as that! The game then adds some challenges, and other mechanics to give it more depth, and I've found that I really enjoy the process of trying to figure out how to make different potions, and then figure out how to make them more efficiently, or with a higher quality.Potion Craft seems well made with decent polish and runs well on my computer. The art isn't high definition, but looks great and has a lot of interesting details and character. I enjoy seeing all the different ingredients and characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: When something is made with love and heart, is easy to know just by looking at it.Potion craft is beautifuly made with care and passion, its still in early access, but you can feel the potential and the good will of the devs with this game. The full roadmap seems amazing and I really hope to see content beyond it, like stories DLCs and more recipes, with more mechanics too. The only Con I really found is that music is really repetitive and I've muted it with only one hour of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever wanted to be an alchemist of sorts, this game is for you!Potion Craft is an incredibly relaxing puzzle game, and has you fill the shoes of an alchemist starting up their own shop in a small town. _childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This game used to be wonderful, honestly, it's still great. Problems with the game arise when the dev team adds new content. Their development philosophy is "chill instead of min/maxing" – when they say this it means “Progression doesn’t matter, and things will be just as difficult and tedious in the end game as they are early game.” This is easy to see when looking at ingredients. Simple recipes used to be easy to make and, there was a method to the madness. Now anything you want to do is costly and time consuming. You can’t just save up money and resources then mess around and discover things. If you wanted to play a game that gives a good sense of progression (Doesn’t make you do tedious things constantly / Allows you to experiment and have a good time) you won’t find that once they leave early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy Moley, I'm a Wizard!!I haven't played an indie game with mechanics quite like this in a very, very long time.  It's nice to find a game that gives you the same level of joy and wonder as during the golden years of indie games.  You can brew a great deal of potions, and the game combines economics, time management, organizational skills, and of course, Alchemy.  Though it's early access there is still a great deal to do, taking somewhere around 15-23 hours to finish the early access build.  It seems the dev team plans to roll out updates consistently, so there's a lot to look forward to.  Really fun game.  It's great to compare notes with your friends. _childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so simple in its design and thus surprisingly addictive in the same way Game Dev Tycoon got me hooked. I have started over a few times because there is replay-ability. You can focus on being good or evil by choosing which customers to help and which to turn away and depending on who comes to you, the majority of the potions they want are different. Furthermore, you can craft various potions in an endless variety of ways and save the recipes. Customers will sometimes give you a challenge to make them a potion with only so many ingredients or using a certain type, which increases the strategy and puzzle-solving. I usually hate puzzle games, but this one is really fun because of how open-ended the solutions are. It is fun to find a way to make someone's request work; it feels like an accomplishment. I also like that you have to figure out what potion would meet the customer's needs. The balance and progression are just right. You can also design your potion bottles and the label art to be unique to each potion and/or each time you play, making your potions feel more like your own, personal creation. I recommend going onto Nexus and downloading some mods that improve the game even more, like the mods that help you organize your recipe book and the ones that add more ingredients. But even without mods, this game is incredibly fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing little game. I truly want to see much more of all the fun stuff you can play around with in the final version. It forces you to be resourceful at moments, but rewards you with helpful shortcuts for that same resourcefulness. Great mechanics, creativity, and gameplay - just lacks a little depth after a while.Great fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Key points at a glance -✅ Gorgeous artwork✅ Nice music and sounds✅ Neat crafting mechanics❌ Gets highly repetitive very quickly❌ Core gameplay loop just isn't that funThe game is upfront about what it is and the screenshots and trailer accurately depict gameplay. Sadly, even for a casual game it feels incredibly shallow. There just isn't enough fun to be had.There are a bunch of interesting mechanics in the game (for the first couple of times, at least) all portrayed with the most beautiful art. However, once you've mixed a few potions, gathered herbs, sold some of your remedies and retired to bed to start a new day you've seen a lot of what the game has to offer.Ultimately, there's nothing fundamentally wrong with the crafting. The game just needs more interesting and fun gameplay around it because that's where I find it lacking. It's a simple and very pretty looking game so if that's enough to keep you happy then go for it, otherwise I cannot recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is trying so hard to be a good game. i wanted to love it SO badly. i honestly think the design is gorgeous, the concept is sound, and the writing is clever. the sound design is nice. it manages to feel rather immersive at times, too.however, what makes the game suffer is thus: the mechanics of brewing the potions are SO unforgiving. you are barely given any guidance apart from the very brief tutorial (meaning i had to google most solutions when i got stuck). they don't explain what half of the tools do (ex. i had to google what the ladle did, as it isn't included in the tutorial). but most of all, there simply aren't enough ingredients available in a given day to allow for practically any mistakes. especially as the potions get more complicated, the first time you attempt to brew something is often a nail-biting experience of hoping to god you won't fail, because if you do?, you waste absolutely everything you just put into the cauldron. (also the fact that manually resetting makes you lose everything just adds insult to injury. sometimes i simply begin with the wrong ingredient, or forget to crush it first, and i'm forced to lose it.) i understand this is meant to be ... "realistic", i suppose, at least in regard to "if you put it in, it's gone", but then make failure not to easy to stumble into (the skull-ans-crossbone areas will kill you QUICK) or give me more ingredients so i can recover better. if i was provided with more ingredients day-to-day from the garden, if there was less pressure from loss, and/or if ingredients were less expensive to purchase? this effect could be mitigated. as it is, this "cutesy, cozy little potion game" has somehow made me rage quit more than anything i've played in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of promise judging from the core gameplay loop we have in Early Access right now - it's surprisingly addictive, and the potion mixing is simple but very satisfying. Only complaint I have is the single music track that loops throughout the entire game gets kind of repetitive...Looking forward to seeing more!
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game for a collectibles freak like me. Chill and rather easy, although looking for an unknown recipe on the map can be tiring.Edit: after 16 more hours I change my mind. I'll never get tired. Well, maybe I will when I finish everything. But for now I can't stop playing. Easy one of my favourite games (still - for a collectibles freak), I just hope it will expand in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, for a few hours.For now, the game is too empty to be really enjoyable. At first, the game is exciting, you learn to make potions, discover new potions by exploring the map, new paths to move through the map... But at the 3-4 hour mark, you get to a point where you are just making the same potions for the same clients all over again.And then alchemy comes, i consider it could be a refreshing and fun mechanic, but for now it has huge design flaws. The first recipes you make are pretty simple and easy, the same potions you made before, but with interesting and different combinations, the problem comes with later recipes.The late game recipes are obtained in the point where you have already done everything else, and don't offer anything new to the game. Each recipe can take about 11 potions, each one of them increasingly harder to make, taking up to four hours to make all the recipes. It really feels like WORKING to progress, as you are still doing the same thing you have been doing since the beginning, but without anything new, and a much higher difficulty (difficulty here meaning more tedious work and more time consuming). Gameplay really needs something new at midgame, get another way to make potions different from moving on a map, other way to process ingredients, but not the same over and over.And the potions you make at the alchemy table doesn't work for anything else, are potions designed just to be hard to make (or easy, depending on the difficulty). They could be potions that you could save for certain clients, for example:1.- The guy that wants to have creative dreams wants a  or a , a 3+2 combination of the two is more valuable, if the alchemy table asked you for that potion, you could save it for that client.2.- The guy that wants to bypass or fly from an enemy needs a  or a , same thing before, the progress could help your gameplay insted of making it tedious.To end, i must say this bad rating is temporary, i enjoyed the game, but i got really burned out at the end. It was way too early to release the game, i want to see what it ends up becoming. It looks ASTONISHING tho, the art and the way you interact with everything is unique, but it feels like they had put too much time on the artistic part, and very little on the game design and gameplay part.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: i was going to be charitable and just not review this game, then i remembered i payed $15 for it.this is very fun in the early game -- its a unique crafting mechanic, and a well thought out one. it *is* good for what it is. but if you keep playing, the novelty will wear off at some point. and then you're left with... what?the goals are repetitive, theres no story (the "chapters" are just collections of tasks to do for the achievement, and once youve unlocked everything theres no purpose to doing it.). the balancing leaves something to be desired; once youre at the higher popularity levels, refusing a single customer -- even if their request is *impossible*, which they sometimes are -- will lose you double what youd get from helping them. past halfway, the game is just grinding. but its grinding that doesnt *lead* anywhere.there are a few features that seem outright missing. the only way to discard potions, for example, is to melt them down in your alchemy machine to make a new undestroyable item. reportedly theyll be adding in garden upgrades -- which is great, but i feel like that shouldve been in the initial release. the garden right now is essentially useless once you can afford merchants.overall, this feels like... more of a game *mechanic* than a full game. and its a great mechanic, sure -- but it needs more.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: The only time this game is fun is when you've got potion recipes and you're doing the haggling mini-game. Making potions themselves was kind of fun at first but by late-game it's tedious and frustrating.I was able to do that for many hours and just while the time away, but when it came time to make something I didn't already have a recipe for, I was annoyed. It's a shame, this had so much potential in early access but it looks like the devs have given up on updating it and have made no major changes in a year and a half, despite a lot of dev logs  some great things.Skip this unless the devs start working on it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very fun the loop is enjoyable but i see myself getting less excited as i progress. Im not quite sure how to explain it but at around the 10 hour mark I feel like i understand the basic tricks, the types of customers, the best way to arrange the recipe book, i became a master negotiator. I now feels all little samey. Hopefully new content and updates will keep me engaged for longer. So far a 9/10 game really close to reaching 10/10 if there were was a little more variety in customer types and vendors and a collections tab to store achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Before reading further, you have to know two things:- I LOVE crafting in videogames, I crave for that kind of things. 99% of the case it's extremely underwhelming, but I can think of a few games that do it right. So a game that makes crafting the main gameplay loop is going to hit all the right spots for me.- This game is in early access. As of right now, even if you take your time like I did, you can finish it in under 20 hours. You can see in the game what the developpers have in mind for the future of the game, and tbh it looks like it's going to add a lot of content indeed.That being said, this game is incredible. By far the best crafting game I've seen in my life. I was sold after only a couple potions, but the depth of the potion making keeps going on and on. Being able to customize your potions with labels and names make it super personnal, and it's recommended (once you have enough bookmarks) to have a variety of "ways" to create each potion, as to never be unable to make a potion.One of the best things imo was the very natural progression (even if it was a bit quick) from "I can make three basic potions a day :)" to "Okay, I have 3 pages to instantly make every potion, and I buy everything the vendors offer at all times".The "shop" part is something that can be improved upon, but considering the base that presently exists, I think the devs are going in exactly the right direction with it.Even if the devs never add anything again (which they definitively will), I would 100% recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft , to me, is a game where the novelty wears off quickly. I put approx. 22 hours of time into the game but eventually dropped it because of how tedious it became. I wish I could like the game more as the art style and concept is wonderful, but the game feels forgotten about now. The Beginning (1-5 hours): You spend time familiarizing yourself with the ingredients, and recipes, & the customer requests. Everything is new and sparkly and you have so much fun! Learning the in's and out of potion making is a great process. This is the space where you have so much hope and feel like you'll be obsessed with this for weeks. Although, at the end of hour 2 you've muted the music and put something else on. Listening to one track on repeat is too much. The Middle (6-15): Things are starting to slow down, you unlock harder and harder recipes, it's getting monotonous but with recipes you learn how to make things more efficient and less time consuming. 'Haggling' with merchants is a chore, but there are still some interesting and new ingredients out there. You hope you can unlock the tool upgrades soon. Middle Pt.2? (16+ hrs): You get tired of everything at this point. You are no longer reading the requests, just keywords, you angrily given them what they want and move on. You are praying for merchants to show up so you can finally get more  ingredients that you can't grow yourself (90% of them). Rapidly you are developing carpal tunnel in your hand and you realize there are no upgrades for your equipment at all. It was never put in the game. The objective of the game became too tedious and complex to manage and eventually you give up. If you are still really interested in this game I would suggest waiting for a sale. In it's current state it feels closer to 5-10USD, not 20.
_childDocuments_.name: Potion Craft: Alchemist Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Potion Craft is a neat, niche game, but it can definitely get tedious very quickly.
