_childDocuments_.review: A delightfully cheerful game about music and color. It’s simply fun to snake around and figure out how the many unique worlds work. The order in which you can explore each world is pretty open-ended. It’s nice to simply wander around without a ‘level select’ screen in the way as well as being able to move on and keep exploring when you come across one of the game’s trickier puzzles.Since the game is committed to minimizing direct communication for the sake of maximizing its wordless cuteness, it can be a bit difficult to know what exactly you’re supposed to do. Spending a few minutes cluelessly dithering around and feeling a tad dumb takes away from the playful atmosphere of it all. Although, I wouldn't be surprised if I'm just really good at missing Hohokum's cues. Either way, more time spent dithering meant more time enjoying the soundtrack, so I can’t really complain.
_childDocuments_.name: Hohokum

_childDocuments_.review: The glowing review I wrote still stands but as I have played more I have run into some bugs that mar the experience a bit. Sometimes animations replay several times in a glitched manner which left me sitting there confused wondering what was going on. In one instance, in the hat level, animations did not progress leaving me softlocked and unable to finish the level, exiting and returning erased my progress for that zone. Fix the bugs and I will edit my review.In Hohokum you take control of the "Long Mover", a multicolored worm-like creature that looks suspiciously like a sperm, and wander around a set of beautifully illustrated interactive worlds. I first saw this game at a friends house and I was intrigued by how strange and colorful it was, I sat there for an hour or two and zoned out to the little dioramas I stumbled into. Later I bought the game for myself and had a blast completing it. I bought this as soon as I saw that it was on Steam and I hope to see it get steam deck functionality soon as well.While not entirely obvious, The story of Hohokum is  You slip through portals to travel to different levels and sometimes there are little interactive transitional zones as well. Each level has its own "theme" and/or story (For Example:  and ) and as you interact with things you find a worm friend hiding in each level. The main objective of this game is to find all of the other worm guys but it really is a game like Flower, Abzu, Journey, etc. where its great to just zone out and enjoy all the pretty colors. There is also a side objective where can you open these eye things scattered in each of the levels by touching them. The levels are connected in these branching paths like a tree so if you ever get lost just look up a guide and you can find your way around that way.The music in this game is great as well, its very relaxing and fun.All-in-all Hohokum is a unique little zen-game that you can just put on and zone out to some pretty colors and funky landscapes. I recommend you check it out if you are into that kind of stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Hohokum

_childDocuments_.review: -- UPDATE -- Ok, so I gave it another go, and I think I mostly get it now. You're a snek and you travel to different places. If you solve whatever puzzle is in a place, you unlock a new snek bud that hangs out in the Home area around its little portal. However, I still don't love it...some of the puzzles are kinda fun, others I never would've figured out in a million bajillion years without a guide. Achievements are even more obtuse than the puzzles. Navigating between different areas was a complete mystery until I finally looked up a map. Overall, I was usually too frustrated to enjoy the intended "chill" atmosphere, so I'm gonna go ahead and stop trying to love this game. :/--- ORIGINAL REVIEW ---I...don't get it :( I want to get it. It's colorful verging on hypnotic, and there's lots of areas to explore. Little dudes jump on your rainbow snek and ride around making silly noises. I really, really wanna love it!!!But ultimately I was quite lost on what I was supposed to do. It's a virtually text-less game, and it seems like you're supposed to discover the puzzles organically by just wandering around. While I like that in theory, it somehow wasn't intuitive to my brain. After a half hour or so of aimless wandering, I'd kinda had my fill of just enjoying the pretty colors, and a hint to get me started would've been really helpful.I also ran across a number of bugs that really affected game play, and they appeared very reliably no matter how many times I left and came back to an area or restarted the game. And because the game is so hands-off and quirky, it took me quite a while to realize when it was actually broken versus just a puzzle I didn't understand.Overall, it's very pretty and would probably be amazing when you're high, but I just had too much trouble with it to give it a thumbs up :/
_childDocuments_.name: Hohokum

_childDocuments_.review: Even though they added the required for the game to run on PC, it is not worth to buy it, because you are going to be paying for a far worse experience, allow me to explain.I am not sure this is caused by a setting for refresh rate (and it would be really dumb if it was) but some of the worm friends are simply impossible to retreat, on Hector's world you can do everything available on it and the cutscene will not trigger like it does on PlayStation, it  get stuck, and therefore you cannot finish the game, there is likely another world where this is also true, but I stopped halfway through after noticing this, in hopes I can still get a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Hohokum

_childDocuments_.review: Playful puzzling-adventure romp in an enigmatic, colourful world awaiting your explorations. I absolutely LOVED this!!It's a 'cult classic'(?) from the Play Station era, apparently. Fairly recently ported to PC.It's vibrant and childlike (not childish!) and fun and favours exploration and experimentation and an open mind.But may have rather a high threshold for new players going in blind - I saw it described as 'maybe too obtuse for its own good'! And, yeah, I can see that ;-)Not difficult in the gameplay as such, no QTE or platforming or arcade or shooting or anything like that. Pleasant and wholesome and do-it-at-your-own-tempo and VERY nice-looking. But yeah - can be bewildering:  am I,  is going on here,  is the purpose or goal of this whatever it is... The game Steam forum is pleasant and helpful (and there's recently a completionist guide on the game forum, too, for the 100%-ers out there). For myself, I was very happy that a web search turned up an old 'paper guide' from 10 yrs ago when it was PS-only. Especially happy for its basic tree diagram of the structure of the world connections, which was such a help in getting my head around it enough to actually manage to get INTO the game and understand where I was. (I'm working on a 'newbie Guide' for the game, based on my experiences and bewilderments with it, but it's my first Guide ever, so may take a bit of time still to get there...Setting it in writing here, will hopefully push me along ;-)).It's great fun, and I love games that reward pattern recognition and open-ended exploration. And cheerful. Music is lovely,  and fits the various worlds.Plays fine on mouse :-). Despite game saying controller recommended. Or you can play on KB if prefer (and keys are rebindable). Be warned that there is NO MANUAL SAVE, and AUTOSAVES ONLY on LEVEL COMPLETION. After completing a level ('world') it will be reachable in a short-cut through a sort of level select mechanism that you will have to figure out for yourself. Or you can go back to anywhere 'the long way round' at any time (this will make more sense to you once you're in the game)TIP: There can be a tendency to softlocking in a couple of the 'side-room dead-ends' in the DOT world, but a quit-and-restart will get you back into the game. May be smth to keep in mind in that level/world, though, so that you do your explorations BEFORE starting in on the puzzles or achievements. As it won't autosave your progress if softlocked but you'll be back to level start.I'm not an achievement hunter at all, but got 8 of the 12. Most are attained through exploration and trying things out, but a few require some speed and accuracy, and one is a classic speed-run. Which is why I didn't manage those.

_childDocuments_.review: A very goofy but fun game for what it is, travelling the multiverse as a weird sperm/kite/worm creature. Fun but chill music plays as you explore many worlds and this soundtrack just adds to the game's atmosphere and unique aesthetic.Nearly every world has it's own unique puzzles/challenges for you to discover and solve, the world's that don't are connecting worlds that house other portals but even then the backgrounds they have are trippy af and relaxing to stare at.The game is kinda short but for the small price-tag, it's more than what I expected!
_childDocuments_.name: Hohokum

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is designed to be open-ended, even though there is a way to "complete" the game.  For example, there doesn't exactly seem to be instructions, and you kind of learn how to play the game as you go along.However, the visual design is striking (and, at the same time, peaceful).  So, even if you don't make formal progress zooming along in a colorful world with interesting sounds and rumble feedback is a unique experience!In terms of being goal-oriented, I am not sure if I would recommend emphasizing completion.  For example, I think it would have been very hard for me to "complete" the game without additional assistance.  However, at the same time, I think my first playthrough would have been shorter if I didn't have a goal, and I am not sure when I would have curiosity again to explore the game.So, with that being said, to try and balance looking up details with understanding what is needed to accomplish tasks, you can "complete" the game by .  This is accomplished by completing .  If you look up more details, then that ruins some of the surprise.  However, I found certain "required" tasks otherwise hard to determine and/or complete.  For example, they are not all immediately obvious (at least to me), they are arguably not necessarily the most fun (but some certainly are), and they certainly don't represent everything that you can do in the game.However, I hope this helps you with deciding what you would like your experience with the game to be like.

If you want a short and sweet audiovisual experience where you can relax, it's perfect for you!Gameplay: 8/10May seem aimless at first glance, but this game is all about exploration and discovery, and it's very fun to find everything these worlds have to offerVisuals: 10/10Incredibly vibrant and stunning 2D environments with tons of artistic varietySound: 9/10Stellar music and pleasant sound design, headphones recommendedStory: 8/10Oozes charm and childlike wonder despite not using a single wordValue: 9/10Will only take about 4-5 hours if you know what you're doing, but if you play it completely blind and just immerse yourself in the discovery it has the potential to last several hours longer. _childDocuments_.review: At first the surreal atmosphere looks awesome, however the game play quickly makes Hohokum very boring.The only things to do are find all the portholes, open all the eyes, complete the optional missions some maps have ( which reset if you leave ), and acquire all the achievements. Eyes can be hidden behind objects, and some are invisible.  I've spent way too much time in individual maps going back-and-forth, in a search pattern from one side to the other, attempting to find all the eyes. This game play mechanic sucks all the fun of exploring the worlds, and instead creates a boring & repetitive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Hohokum

_childDocuments_.review: While I appreciate  ambitious commitment to redefining what a game can be, I rather liked how they were made already because this is a "game" that so deeply lacks purpose, vision or a clearly defined goal. You spend hours coasting around as a celestial worm that draws coloured squares, organises weddings or saves swimmers from the trip to the pool. I just don't get it. If someone asked me what this game is about, I couldn't tell them. Over 2 hours of play didn't bring me closer to understanding it, just more frustrated that I didn't. So I quit. It's colourful nonsense, perfect for a toddler maybe.

name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7
detailed_description: Five new incredible party games to bring the fun! 1. The say-anything threequel Quiplash 3 (3-8 players). Get big laughs answering the quirkiest prompts. 2. The collaborative chaos game The Devils and the Details (3-8 players). Can you survive the daily torture of human life? 3. The drawing fighting game Champ’d Up (3-8 players) . Can you take down the heavy favorite? 4. The on-the-spot speech game Talking Points (3-8 players). Just keep talking whether it makes sense or not. 5. The pop culture guessing game Blather 'Round (2-6 players). It’s a good fun time experience. Play using phones, tablets or computers. No extra controllers needed! NOTE: The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is in English only. NOTE: The game is local multiplayer but can be enjoyed over streams with remote players. How to Play Remotely Players use any web-enabled device (like a smartphone or tablet) to join the game and play along. When playing with remote players, you can use a video conferencing tool like Zoom, Steam Broadcast, Google Hangouts, Discord, and more to connect with others! Just share your screen while on a call and make sure you look for prompts to share audio.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great pack with a unique assortment of games. All of them work over the web, which is a big plus.- Quiplash 3: It's good ol' quiplash. Can't go wrong with this one. The prompts are good, and there are custom packs if you get bored of the defaults. The last lash is always the same- every player gives 3 answers to a prompt. I'm not a huge fan of this, but meh. It's quiplash.- The Devils and the Details: This is my favorite, simply because of the chaos it creates. Players yelling at each other to finish collaborative tasks, scolding the selfish players, and freaking out when there is an emergency. It can get a little old, but the wide variety of "scenarios" keeps it fresh enough.- Champ’d Up: Head-to-head drawing game. Pretty fun even if you suck at drawing. Playing multiple games in a row allows for comedic callbacks, since the game lets you "tag in" drawings from previous games. It gets pretty silly.- Talking Points: This is a close second favorite. Players have to bulls**t their way through a wacky presentation. It's fun to make up something as fast as possible on the spot. Lots of improv is involved. I wish there were more images to choose from- when images repeat it gets a little less funny. The custom mode is pretty fun if you have creative players. The scoring system kinda sucks.- Blather 'Round: This is the one I have played the least, but it's interesting. It's not as funny as the other games, but it's still very entertaining to try to deduce what the word is. It's like charades with words. Seems to have good replayability. Overall, awesome pack that is well worth the asking price. Plays great over Discord or IRL :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Jackbox Party Pack in which our group felt all 7 games were "winners".Quiplash 3 - The "Thrip Lash" is, finally, the perfect structure for the final round of quiplash.The Devils and the Details - Mechanically has the potential to get the most repetitive, but you'll be having too much fun shouting at your friends to drive you to the dentist to care.Champ'd Up - A drawing competition where only one player knows the prompt. The game shines in it's last round, however, when you get a random prompt and have to pick one of your previous drawings to fight for it. This gets very special with repeat plays, as the game keeps your entire roster of drawings around as long as you select "same players".Blather 'Round - "It's a Spicy Box Place". "Taco Bell!" "HOW DID YOU GUESS THAT?"Talking Points - A classic improv game. Give a speech, with no idea what your next slide is going to show. Creates some truly special moments when the assistant selecting pictures and the presenter psychially align. Also you can mash upvotes and downvotes, which is very satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: As always, Jackbox brings hours of laughter to my group of friends.Favorite game: Champ'd Up.The drawing tools are expanded from those of previous entries, such as Drawful, allowing for more creativity and freedom in drawing. The fun really kicks in when you draw the challenger, using only your opponent's drawing as a reference point. I definitely recommend using the extended timer so you don't feel as rushed to get your drawing right.Least favorite: The Devils and the Details.This game just doesn't flow well for my group of friends, but I still recommend trying it for yourself. It doesn't have the same format as most other Jackbox Party Pack games (Prompt, respond, vote), and is much more continuous and at times hectic. While there is a bit of competition, it's mostly a cooperative game. While this could definitely be a big drawing point for some people, it wasn't very fun for us.The brain game: Blather Round.This game is essentially word charades. You choose one of three things (person, place, etc.) and have to vaguely describe it by filling in the blanks of a sentence using a list of terms the game provides. As the round continues, you can form more clues in the same manner while other players try to figure out what you're describing. Lots of fun, and if you're like us you'll end up playing it multiple times in a row and forgetting to try out the other games.The chill game: Talking Points.A much less competitive game, but that's not a bad thing. You take turns giving presentations on material you've never seen before, and while you're briefing each slide, another player is creating the next slide. Forces you to think on your feet, and even for a group of people who all hate giving presentations, we had a lot of fun.Ol' Reliable: Quiplash 3.If you liked the previous Quiplash entries, you'll like this one. The only real changes are the ability to choose your avatar, and the new final round: Thrip Lash. In Thrip Lash, you give a three-step response to the prompt, with each step being revealed one at a time. We found that some of the prompts in Thrip Lash were weak, but overall it's a solid addition. You also have the ability to create your own prompts in the menu.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Jackbox in years. Quiplash 3 continues the high quality of that game, even if little has changed aside from the final round. Champ'd Up is possibly a contender along side Drawful for best drawing game. Blather Round came completely out of left field and is one of the most popular Jackbox games among my friend circle now.Now for the less glowing critique.  I personally really like Talking Points, but it seems to be massively unpopular among those who I have played with, and I understand why.  It requires a performative personality and a sense of improvisation that isn't for the shyer folks in your group, and may end up with some people feeling left out.  Also, the scoring criteria isn't super clear and seems to be heavily weighted towards those who go later.I have not had much experience with the Devil and the Details yet and while it seems fun, it is almost impossible to play virtually as it is too hard to coordinate in a video chat when all voices end up drowning each other out.  In person, I can see it being a fun collaborative affair, but COVID has unfortunately put the kibosh on that.Champ'd Up and Blather Round alone make this the best Jackbox since #3 and the one probably most in the spirit of the original games in terms of accessibility and straight of fun.  Time will tell if the two games I mentioned as weaker will be more viable once in person gatherings are a thing once more, but regarless the pack gets a strong recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 7 comes with some good games, it is not my favorite though.Quiplash 3Always a classic. Always fun. In Quiplash you come up with the best punchline. There are no noteworthy changes except the art style.Devils in the DetailsOne of the few co-op Jackbox games, but with a twist: there is still a first place. For me, doing chores virtually is even worse than in real life. On the plus side is that you do not have waiting times.Champ’d UpThis game can be really, really funny. You draw multiple characters and give them names to win in certain categories. Later, you use the same characters to win other categories, which can lead to hilarious combinations. Talking PointsThis Party Pack does not only have a game where you do chores, it also has a game where you do PowerPoint presentations like you are back in 7th grade. Do not get me wrong, it can be hysterically funny. Just make sure that everybody in your group feels comfortable giving a speech. Otherwise, it can get awkward.Blather ‘RoundI got this Party Pack only for this. It is like a trivia game, where one person chooses computer-generated hints. It can be a magical moment, when you already gave up because the hints you could give were not so good, but then somebody guesses correctly at the last second.Keep in mind that you play with one smartphone / tablet or web browser per person. If you want to play with your friends online, you can use Steam Remote Play or Discord. It is still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is one of the best Party Packs that has come out recently with 5 different new and unique games that are great for parties and streams. Since this is 5 games in one I will review each one individually.If you have played any previous Jackbox games you probably know what Quiplash is. In it every player gets prompts with fill in the blanks that you try to create the funniest answers you can. And then everyone votes on which answer they thought was more clever or funny and then the person with the most points at the end of the game wins. This version of Quiplash has some unique rounds to spice things up along with obviously an abundance of new prompts. Also you can make your own questions in the game if you want and whats really cool is you can actually play other players custom made questions in a featured content tab so that is awesome. And the artsyle is this really cool looking claymation vibe and so overall this is probably going to be a lot of players favorite game in the pack.In this every single person is on a team of devils trying to do everyday human chores to fit in. So the gameplay consists of there being a huge list of chores on everyone's phones and when you do them there are small and simple minigames you must complete to get points for the family. This game overall has a very interesting and unique premise but my problem with it is all the chores you are doing kind of feel like actual chores. I think if the minigames had been a little more fun almost like little Warioware games this could have been incredibly fun but every single task you do consists of you doing the most mundane things ever like looking through a phone book for a specific phone number to type in so it kind of makes the game fall flat a little in my opinion.This is stupid fun and honestly one of my favorite drawing based Jackbox games ever. In it each player draws and names a champion to fight others and then gets to create another champion to fight another players champion. Then the rounds start and each person votes on who they think would win in a fight and in the later rounds you can tag in your other fighters which is awesome.And one really cool feature about this game is if you continue playing with the same players across multiple games when it comes time to tag in some of your other fighters you can actually use your fighters from previous games which is super cool. Also the music in this game is way better than it has any right to be.This is one of the games that you kind of need to have the right group of people to play because it’s less of a competition and more just a fun little experience. In it each player will give speeches kind of like Ted Talks to the other players and when its your turn to give the ted talk another person acts as your assistant by choosing what the words you have to read are and what pictures accompany your power point.Everyone can like or dislike your speech at any time and that is what determines how many points you get but overall you should just be playing this game to give hilarious speeches to your friends or family and it is pretty fun when you get a group of people to really commit to this game.This is kind of like a game of charades almost. In it each player chooses a word from a list of 3 and it could be a person, a place, or a thing and when it’s their turn they try to form sentences with a very limited amount of words to give the other players hints. The entire time the other players are trying to guess the word and sometimes the person who is giving the hints can even include the previous guesses in their hints. So say someone said the hulk but the real word was a different super hero the person giving hints could make a sentence saying “it’s very similar to the hulk”.And if someone guesses the correct word then they along with the person giving the hints gets points and if they used any other words from other player's guesses they get points as well.And so overall this one is really fun because I haven’t really played a charades like game in a Jackbox Party Pack and so it is a very fun and unique experience.And so overall I absolutely loved this party pack. I loved 4 out of the 5 games and the one I didn’t like I didn’t hate I just wasn't a super fan of. If you are a fan of previous Jackbox Party Packs you will definitely enjoy this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Another year, another Jackbox Party Pack. My friends and I are huge fans of this series and return to it numerous times throughout the year. Usually, with each new Party Pack, you get maybe three good games and two bad ones, so I was interested in seeing if the latest would keep up that trend.Quiplash 3 was a good bit of fun. It’s by no means the strongest game in the pack, but it takes the already solid Quiplash formula and delivers the best version yet. You basically answer a series of prompts with what you think is the funniest and best-fitting answer and those answers go up against others in a series of rounds until you get to the multi-answer finale and all the points are tallied up. It’s pretty simple really, but the Jackbox team has done a great job with all the creative prompts, the visuals and music, and just the overall presentation.This is something you’ll see extend to the other games in the pack as well, they’ve really upped the visual side of things this time around. Regardless, Quiplash 3 is a solid first game for the pack and one my friends and I will be returning to.The Devils and the Details is easily one of, if not the most, chaotic games I have ever played in any of the Jackbox games. It plays very differently from the rest of the pack, being a co-op survival game of sorts where you each play as a member of a family trying to complete certain tasks before the end of each day. However, each family member has a personal score and it can be increased by completing selfish tasks that harm the rest of the family. This creates this cool dynamic where you’re both trying to help out the rest of the group while also trying to stay above the rest.The actual tasks are divided into individual and group tasks – with the latter being where the chaos comes into play. They oftentimes require you to instruct another player, but when you have seven or so people playing at once, it quickly becomes a mess of players shouting instructions at others and trying to get everything done by the time limit. It can get very loud, but that’s the point of the game and I quite enjoyed the change of pace compared to the other games’ comedy-centric focus. It may not get the laughs, but it will definitely get the communication going in a chaotic fun sort of way.Champ’d Up ended up being my favorite game of the pack. Every pack has a drawing game, and Champ’d Up not only expands on the drawing tools offered in the previous packs through colors choices and an undo button, but pits drawings against each other in a very cool way. You’re basically tasked with drawing something against another drawing without knowing the category that the two are competing in – only the original drawer knows the category. This can create some very cool matchups and the worse your drawing skill, the funnier it becomes.This was one of the two games in the pack where my group literally couldn’t breath because we were laughing so hard at some of the drawings, and the way the game facilitates these matchups just makes it all that much better. Jackbox always seems to knock it out of the park with the drawing games and Champ’d Up is no exception.Talking Points is the game that had the most laughs from my group. And not just regular laughs, but the kind where you find yourself wheezing. It’s a presentation-style game where you have one player presenting on a topic they know nothing about and another player feeding the first player new text and picture slides for their slideshow. As the presenter does not know what slide is coming up next, there is a ton of adlibbing involved, but that’s what really makes the game shine. You gotta somehow link together all of these unrelated images and lines and it can lead to some pretty funny moments.For example, I pitched my presenter an image of a squirrel, then sausages, and then house keys, and he managed to weave it together into this werewolf narrative that had the rest of the group dying. It’s definitely the simplest game in the pack in terms of its design, but it’s got some top-tier execution and provides a solid foundation for a simple, yet fun party game – the type you can just bust out with any group and get to playing.Blather 'Round is without a doubt the weakest game in the pack. It’s not outright bad, but it definitely doesn’t click like the rest of the games do. It’s basically a trivia game played using word charades. You get a word and have to convey it through a limited set of other words and player guesses as they come in. What my group found was that a lot of the prompts are simply too hard, even the ones marked as “easy”. For example, I would get something like Bikini Bottom, which you would think would be at least somewhat easy to pitch, but the clues are so abstract that half of my group was guessing oceans and lakes and such and the other half was guessing coastal cities.Of course, just like the other games in the pack, this is all going to depend on the group you play with. Blather 'Round is just the type of game that is better played among those that like trivia games (and this is coming from someone that does).The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is yet another solid addition to the series, definitely one of the better ones. It’s got some really good highlights – most notably Champ’d Up and Talking Points – but some other fun additions as well – Quiplash 3 and The Devils and the Details. The only one that didn’t quite stick was Blather ‘Round, but even then, it’s not outright bad like the usual bad game included in past Party Packs. If anything, this might be the most well-rounded pack yet.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: By far, in my opinion, this is the best Jackbox Party Pack I have ever purchased, and played, thus far. Through Sub-category, reviewing each segment, as the entirety of the game.1.):The third one in the series, this is a game of wits/clever commentary within about a minute to answer gap, per round. You are given a category, to fill in what you feel would be or not be the best answer for that category, and you generally compete against other people, each person in your party having their own category, besides the one(s) you compete with. 👍This game is really fun, and they even have separate episodes in the options to choose from, for folks who may be getting married, for children and/or a sports team. Overall, this game has a lot of re-play value, and is especially great for friends or family you are close with. Bear in mind too, that you can include an outside audience, if you so chose to do so. :) 2.) :You start as a 'devil' family, over-going daily chores as a family, sometimes having to involve other parts of the family to complete tasks. However, be aware, also, there is one task that is in red, and causes trouble for the rest of the family, and if the person so chooses to pick that task, the other family members have a chance to stop the devious motive. 👍This game is especially fun with family and/or close friends. However, I do feel it could be repetitive, were it to be played too much. 3.):Get ready to show off your creative and/or possibly not creative but hilarious skills of drawing. Each round, you are given a subject of which what your drawing would be deemed the "champion of [random category]" The first part of each round, a person is given this prompt, and then, the second part of the round, the player is given the other player's champion, and has to create a worthy opponent for this champion, pay mind, the second round person involved is not aware of what the first person round's drawing is the champion of, and have to base it off of the drawing. 👍This game is great, especially with the drawing mechanics, and choices between different pen styles, and different colors. The avatars chosen at the beginning of the game are fun. My family has found it to be quite hilarious, even creating "champions" that make a comeback in following games, and we have a lot of fun, creating new champions. However, this game may not be for everyone, especially if they lack the desire to draw. But even, if you feel you do not possess the ability to draw, it can still be a fun game, for everyone. 4.):This game is a true pop culture game where you are given a category [people, places, things, etc] and it may or may not involve time eras that your party have knowledge there of. However, that does not lose it's charm. You have to make your party guess what it is that you are trying to tell them (the subject you had chose at the beginning of the round) and when they guess, you, the person in charge of the subject chosen, may also use what the other players clues to guess the subject to what it is you are trying to reveal. Whoever guesses the subject, also earns points.  Anyone involved in the cluing toward the subject, if the main player chose your guesses in the category round, also get points. 👍No matter of different time eras and possibly not knowing what the subject may be, this game has a lot of fun and cause people to be in cahoots about it. The ultimate goal is to guess the subject. Whether you like to be clever, and/or immature about things, this game is full of fun. 5.):Imagine trying to sell a product, or making a powerpoint about something. This is exactly what the game is. You are trying to convince your audience that your item, is the best. However, it doesn't necessarily have to be this way. You are given a powerpoint, and an assistant (*ahem* another player in your party) to help you with the powerpoint. You create the context, and your assistant gets to choose a powerpoint slide that is given by the game, that they would feel would fit most (or possibly not fit most) to your speech. You can draw on the photo, creating more hysterically lasting memories. Each player gets to make a comment at the end of the powerpoint, and vote on which one they felt was best, at the end. 👍I do not feel this game may be for everyone, however, it can grow quite hilarious, depending on the party you play with. Clever-minded to immaturity, this game is overall fun.

_childDocuments_.review: No disclaimer about the fact that I'm European this time around. This Jackbox Party Pack has a Filter for US-Centric content, to make it accessible to the broader audience around the world. Definitely a welcomed addition. You might still note that all of those games were played with the aforementioned option turned on.- YES, GET IT AT ALL COSTS!!- A classic of the Jackbox Games.- The best of all.- Simple and fun.- Infinitely replayable.Schmitty's back for some more Quiplashing. The concept of Quiplash just never gets old. It's easy to understand in 2 sentences, it's hilarious and moreover, its third round FINALLY was improved with THREE answers to input in a prompt. This leaves space for even more creativity and laugh moments. The "make your own" mode is still there even. I think they've really hit the spot here. My personal note is .- Developed from what was an April Fools' joke.- Cooperation game with a tiny bit of deception.- Interesting concept of interactive tasks on phone.The cooperative game that will really get the interest of Jackbox players. It is fun in its own way (perhaps different from the rest of the series). There is a complexity to it. It marries cooperation and individualism very well. It has many challenges and the theme is just well made. It is however barely playable on a browser or so I'm told, so try to play it on your smartphone. A mic might sometimes be required. It must also be better if played with all players in the same room. Personal note is .- The best drawing game ever made by Jackbox.- Hilarious battle of drawings.- Leaves space for creativity.- AMAZING SOUNDTRACK!Everything is in the lines above. The concept well detailed and easy to understand. Despite being a drawing game, it proved absolutely hilarious and accessible. So many twists. It has an infinite replayability. The universe is absolutely awesome. Nothing else to say, that's in my top 3 of my favourite games from Jackbox. Most of my friends approve as well. Personal note is .- Will definitely please the fans of Patently Stupid.- Can be tricky to understand at first, stressful if first timers are talking first.- Can be quite funny once people grab the concept.- Room for creativity pretty much everywhere.Met with a bit of mixed opinions at first in my own sessions. Despite that, if people understand it and are able to improvise, it can prove to be very funny. The speaker and the assistants' thinking and cooperation is what will make their presentation hilarious. It is best played with a mic. It has to be a lot better if done in front of a big screen with all players in the same room, like Patently Stupid. I have to try that out one day. Personal note is .- Very tricky, even with the US-Centric filter on.- Satisfying when you find the answer.- Requires players making others guess to think a lot to succeedThe less funny game of the pack, but not a bad one. It basically calls for some basic trivia and guesswork. That said, the concept is easy, it's using it that isn't as the host of the guess. Could definitely benefit from some additions in terms of possibilities when creating a sentence. My personal note is .The best Jackbox Party Pack EVER CREATED. To this day, as 2020, I can only recommend that you get this pack above any other. It is the funniest, most accessible and replayable pack Jackbox has ever made. Very good Job, developers, this one will probably be the most played and requested one until - one can wish - The Party Pack 8!

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the best Jackbox to date. Quiplash 3 fixed the only issues I had with the final round of the game feeling pretty hit or miss. The Devils and the Details is extremely hectic and Champ'd Up is another great drawing game. Talking Points is a perfect spiritual successor to Patently Stupid and adds a good amount of chaos to it. _childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: The most recent entry at the time of writing, and also by far the best pack. 4 out of the 5 games in The Jackbox Party Pack 7 are exceptional party games that knock every other instalment in this series out of the water. Champ'd Up is an endlessly entertaining game about creating characters and putting them head to head to compete in strange and specific tournaments, and is the best game in this pack. Quiplash 3 is the most recent Quiplash, and is probably the most famous Jackbox game, a simple but very effective game about answering prompts and voting for the funniest answers. Talking points is a great improv game where you present a power point presentation while your partner makes it at the same time, using quick thinking very important. The Devils and the Details is a very chaotic coop game where you complete as many warioware-esque microgames as possible to blend in with human society. Blather Around is the weakest entry, essentially just verbal charades, but you can ignore it's difference in quality due to how great the other 4 games are in this pack. I would strongly recommend this pack above each other one in the series, it's easily the best in the series, both for someone brand new to Jackbox, or someone who owns and has played every previous on before. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: I believe this is one of my favorite of the Jackbox Packs, with all five being unskippable and all bringing their own fun to the table. Each are good are being interactive and keeping everyone's attention. Blather 'Round is pop culture trivia presented through keywords given by another player which presents a challenge and funny moments. Talking Points is really fun for IRL play as you can stand up and give a presentation and somebody else being in track of your slideshow creates really great improv. Quiplash is a classic and is very fun. Champ'd Up is an awesome take on the drawing genre and imo is better than TKO. Devil and the Details is the only meh game to me, but I still enjoyed playing it. It's just a little dragged on and confusing sometimes, so I don't play it often but when I do it's fun.Overall, this pack is very solid with each game having something new to add to existing formats or having a whole new format to experiment and play with.

_childDocuments_.review: They're all pretty good Quiplash 3 is just Quiplash with new promptsThe Devils and The Details is a pretty good co-op/competitive game where you need to get as many tasks done as possible to contribute towards a goal with an option to take selfish tasks that give you more points but can cause a disaster. Some tasks on phones can be annoying if you swipe down too hard and refresh ur page by accident.Champ'd Up is where you get a prompt to draw something and another player will draw a competitor to match without the prompt which can be fun.Talking points is do a silly TED talk and can be good if you like the speech based games.Blather Round is where you get a famous person, character, story etc. and have to describe it using the ingame prompts and it can be hard but it really depends on how quick your friends can be to catch on.Overall i'd rate this in the top 3 jackbox games with 4 and 6 :)

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox Party Packs come in all shapes and sizes, and include a number of different games within them. So I'll break down this review based on types of games in this pack:CO-OPERATIVE PLAY!This pack includes some AWESOME cooperative play games. Devils and the Details is a crazy fun game where you work together to complete random challenges. It involves a lot of yelling so make sure your microphone is working for this one!But the real star of the show is Blather Round, a creative take on the classic Password. You basically try to describe your prompt using awkward language (e.g. you might us "sad liquid event" to get people to guess Titanic). I've played this game with family, friends, and even random strangers online, and it is always a blast. Worth the price of admission 👍🏼FUNNYQuiplash is a lot of fun, a great game to play with friends. Basically you're just trying to give the funniest or most amusing responses to prompts.DRAWINGChamp'd Up is a high energy game where you draw and name characters, and vote for the best ones. I still like Drawful a bit better, but the music and the whole vibe of this game makes it stand out.TRIVIAThis party pack is not the best game option if you just want to play a straight trivia challenge. For trivia heads I'd recommend looking into Party Pack 5 or 6 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I have played every game at least twice and i've tried to be as unbiased as possible.Quiplash 3: Honestly, just some good old quiplash but with a cleaner art style and better music. One of the stronger games in the pack but like what do you expect, it's quiplash.The Devils and The Details: I honestly love those chaotic games where you're just shouting at your friends and this game just perfectly encapsulates that. I think my friend group are just ♥♥♥♥♥Champ'd Up: Literally just a better version of tee k o. A nice setting and im so glad you can see what you're going up against in this game, it makes it make way more sense, a pretty nice drawing game overall.Talking Points: One of my favourite games in the pack, it's bascically improv patently stupid and i LOVE it, i cant tell you specifically why though, it has a nice clean aesthetic and a laugh.Blather round: I went into blather round not thinking I would like it because i'm not really a fan of trivia games in general, but this one is a nice change of pace to just chill out and play at the end of a jackbox nightOverall, one of the best packs, a strong 8.5 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Best pack by far.Played through all of the games with a discord server full of friends for 2+ hours. Each game made us laugh and was worth the time playing.Quiplash 3: It's Quiplash. All you need to know. _childDocuments_.review: My tier list of these games:Champed upHas awesome art and music. _childDocuments_.review: Word Spud.Lie Swatter.Civic Dodole.Zeeple Dome.Joke Boat.They've been waiting for a year for their new member.They will have to keep waiting.There are no bad games here.Champ'd Up is a real treat for people who love to draw, and even people that only draw black and white stick figures can join in and stand a chance. So much unintentional humour - and a lot of fun to be had by trying for some humour if you can guess your opponent's prompt and make a deconstruction of it. You get to keep your drawings for the next game if you play with the same players, too! Compared to Tee K.O., it feels like a better flow because you draw two things at a time and every drawing is used at least once, possibly more because there's four drawings and six rounds per person (and again, they can be used in the next game.) Also includes the best part of Bracketeering with none of its bad.Blather 'Round is like Taboo with less control, and hilarity when someone guesses Oedipus off of "They are tragic; They feel the mommy." Or a rush to type Atlantis after the hint is "it's a not tall liquid civilization."Devils and the Details is designed to make people talk over each-other and get frantic. I need more time with this one to say much about it.Talking Points is a chill game where people probably don't care about the points. It can be cute and/or wholesome. It has a "free mode," but I don't see why you'd want it unless you use it to make custom restrictions.Quiplash is Quiplash.

_childDocuments_.review: This pack is a winner! The look of the Quiplash 3 is great, the returning feature of making your own questions maintains it as probably their best game. I also feel like the new final round has a very different feel, which is a good reason to move between 2 and 3. The pack has more to offer than that though. I was really looking forward to Blather On (like a mad-lib Charades) and it feels like a great fit for smaller groups or those who aren't as interested in competition. Champ'd Up may feel like the t-shirt game from a previous pack, but cultivates it's own feeling as you build your team over multiple rounds. I haven't played The Devils and the Details because I'm waiting until we can have a group over to play it. Communication between a large group over a video call just sounds like a nightmare. I'm looking forward to it though.The only one I don't particularly like is Talking Points. I enjoy the performative nature of Patently Stupid, but this doesn't have the same creative spark. _childDocuments_.review: As someone new to Jackbox as a series, this one definently hooked me! Had so much fun, even with my small group of four friends on Discord (the game can support a minimum of four players). That said, this game, like the others as I've heard, has hits and misses. I'll go over every game now.Quiplash 3: Simple fun boiled into a game. This game is a favorite among'st everyone and rightfully so. The simple act of pitting two quips together and picking the winner feels so much better than something like CaH, which I find fun as well. In Quiplash 3, you must write a quip to fill in the blank of a question asked by the narrator. It gets worse though on round 3, Thriplash and its 3 quip format never is really funny and we've even sometimes just skipped over it to get to the next round. Although, I hear others like it, so its probably our preference. Overall, 6/7.The Devil's and the Details: I hear people ragging on this one, and I see why, but I think its still a nice little game to touch on every once and a while. You must complete simple (extremely simple) minigames to increase your family score by the end of each day. You can also perform selfish tasks to increase your score. While the family score keeps the team alive, the game is decided by YOUR overall score, so you have to pick your tasks wisely, as some aren't worth the points. This one is fun, but maybe not a repeat play depending on what type of person you are. The style is very charming, reminds me of Hazbin and Helluva Boss. 4.5/7Champ'd Up: This is very situational laughs, although, its contained some of my hardest guffaws in the whole pack when people know how to draw their champs. You draw champions against another players underdog fighting for silly titles. I prefer Tee K.O. but this is fine. In my opinion, it requires your friend group to be very creative, but I'm sure my friends are just bad, although this isn't a good quality for a party game. I do sound like I'm talking bad here, but its a very fun game if you play well and you will at least chuckle a little in the round. 5/7Talking Points: I hear so much hate for this one... I have literally no clue why, this is EASILY the best game in the pack, and probably the hardest to explain. Players start by filling in 3 different talking points and they are sent out. Players pick which of the other players ones they wish to speak about. One by one, each of them, assisted by another player to bring up pictures for their presentation, must publicly speak to the group and just keep talking. The goal is to just keep talking about whatever is on screen and create strange stories and silly motivational speeches. This one has had me laughing HARD every round, sometimes multiple times. Most of the pictures are amazing, but sometimes if you end up with a bad assistant, you'll struggle. Other than that tiny detail, this one is a blast for everyone who can keep talking, you probably should inform new players on this detail, since most of my group just read the titles and hardly talked when the pictures came up. I love this one though and at least someone will enjoy this. 7/7Blather Round: DISCLAIMER! Don't get this with a group of 4. This is probably the most annoyingly hard game with fewer than 5 players due to the nature of it. This is charades with words. You get a pop culture name, and the other players have to narrow it down while you give them hints off a board. This one probably can be fun, but its only fun if a lot of people are guessing at once. I feel the guessers should have more time. As it stands, its ALWAYS a flat minute no matter the player amount. It's overall fine, and other people seem to like it. 5/7Overall, all the games are pretty solid, even TD&TD is good on the first few plays. This one is great for new people to the series, and allows some of the older fans to have a great time too. I'll be back again for Party Pack 8! 6.5/7

_childDocuments_.review: First of all let me say that I'm a sucker for jackbox games but I'll still give an honest review.This is pack is a good pack and has some interesting stuff which can be fun and not so fun. The 5 games included in this pack are:-Quiplash 3-The Devils and The Details-Champ'd Up-Talking Points-Blather 'RoundI'll go over each game equaly.First is Quiplash 3:If you do not know what type of game this is let me explain. At the start of a round people get to input some funny things to get some chuckles with some jokes. They can be fill in the blank prompts or something you have answer. After answering the two prompts the people with the same prompt get to go against each other and the person with the most votes in their answer wins that round.This game is as always okay and can be fun if not ruined by some jokes, but if you have some good hitting jokes it can be fun.The new triplelash is fun if you have a good prompt because you have to give this question 3 answer at the same time.Now its time for The Devils and the Details:I personaly like this game a lot but so far not many in my friend group don't as much.In this game you are a family of devils who have work together by doing simple tasks and getting enough point to win the game. These tasks can be from: Doing the dishes to mowing the lawn and many other things.But there are also some other thing at stake because there are also some thing called selfish tasks. If you do these you can get big points for only yourself which will not help the family score. But you only get these points if you are not stopped before its to late.Ive played this game with some friends of mine and we agree that this game can be a lot more fun with a full group. Because if all 8 slots are taken there is a lot more chaos and scream at each other to either get some help doing a task or trying to stop someone from doing a task.Next is Champ'd Up:In this game you have to draw a specific champion like 'The champion of Cuteness'. After you draw your champion someone else will get your drawing and without knowing what kind of champion it is have to draw an underdog to try and win against the champion.This game is really fun. You get enough time to draw and name you character and even the characters that "Draw" these champions are nicely made. Not really much to comment on.Next is Talking Points:In TP you have to give a talk about a specific topic made by another person (which are fill in the blank statements). In these talk one person will give the talk and another person the, the assistant, will create slides by choosing text and an image to talk about.This game can be really funny if the assistant can get got slides and text. Not all of the time will you get a good looking presentation which is a bummer. Ive had talks which were really funny because the person talking got really go images but so far every time i got to be an assistant my choice of images were really dumb and bad.And at last but not at all least is Blather 'Round:In this game everyone needs to choice a prompt like a: person, story, thing or place. After choosing your prompt you need to create a small sentence trying to hint at the prompt. These sentences are really simple because you get to only choose from a specific word list.So for example I choose the word 'Minion' and with the sentence 'Its a BLANK BLANK' i have to choose words to try and explain/hint at the word i choose.After the first hint i get to try and make as much as hints possible trying to make people guess easier what my word is.After playing this game me and my friends find this the best game in the pack. Its easy to learn (like really easy) and if you get it right it just feels so good.In one game the first hint got shown and the first guess was immediately the right answer.Over all this is a ery noice pack. Games are fun and easy to learn and over good to play.Now for some scores:Quiplash 3 - 6/10 - Fun but still the same game though.The Devils and the Details - 7.4/10 - Can probably be really fun in a big/full group but still fun.Champ'd Up - 8.2/10 - Easy drawing game and challenging.Talking Points - 5.8 - Need to be lucky to get some funny stuff.Blather 'Round - 9/10 - So easy and so fun. Best one for sure.And in the end i give this pack a: 8.2/10.-Worth it-

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Jackbox Party Packs. IMO pack 3 and 7 have the most great games. Devil’s in the Details just doesn’t offer enough player interactions — too much time is spent managing your own stuff and there’s not enough time socializing. As we all know, the social aspect of these games is what makes them fun.Quiplash 3 is probably the best Quiplash. I like the simple “thrip lash” final round, it just works. Blather ‘Round is a relatively fun guessing game. Champ’d Up is a lot like Tee K.O. and that’s not a bad thing — always fun to see peoples’ hilarious drawings. And Talking Points is great fun for the more extraverted folks. All in all probably my favorite party pack, but again, 3 is excellent as well. If you’re like me and don’t want to buy every single release, I highly recommend 3 or 7.

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is considered by many to be the best pack, and I'd even argue that there's no truly bad games featured here.First off, there's no trivia game. It sucks because some of the most famous/popular jackbox games ARE TRIVIA GAMES. YDKJ, Fibbage, TMP, none of that is here. If you want a good pack featuring a trivia game, I'd focus on 3, 4, or 6.You get two prompts, you answer them in funny ways, and then you're put up against somebody else to see who's was funnier. The open response style makes this game great for inside jokes with friends! People tend to dislike the final round (Thriplash: answer with three short responses instead of one long response,) but I actually prefer this over the final rounds from earlier games. Also I HAVE to mention the clay-mation style, it really helps make the game stand out more, and it looks awesome.9/10You complete small tasks by swiping, tapping, holding, etc. The game shines when you have to actually communicate with other players, whether it be through telling them that "left" does not mean "straight" when driving a car, or yelling at them to stop trying to sabotage the family score. The game is absolute chaos and it's fun because of it. Given, it does get repetitive.7/10You receive a champion title (i.e. Champion of Disappointment) and you need to draw + name a character that fits the category. Then your character is sent to another player, and they need to try and create a new character without knowing the original category. The two are put up against each other and people vote for the best one Quiplash style. I want to praise this game because either this or Drawful: Animate probably have the best drawing tools in the entire series. Not much else to say, just a really solid game.9/10So this might just be my inner theatre kid/improv bias, but this is probably the funniest jackbox game (if played with the right people.) To play, you and another player are set to improv a presentation based off whatever topic the speaker picked. The second player has to select text and images to pop up for the speaker so they can tie them into whatever they're talking about. The comedy in this game mainly comes from the shock value, but it thankfully never overstays it's welcome. My only big problem with it is that the Awards Ceremony is honestly really stupid.9/10It's word charades. You pick a topic, then use a combination of premade senteces and a list of words to describe it, in hopes the other players will be able to guess it. I don't know why, but me and my friends actually got a really good laugh out of this, even though it's the only game in the pack that ISN'T meant to be funny (there is an arguement that Devils and the Details should be here, but I digress.) This game has a large community of people that dislike it, and I can't blame them, but I personally think it's a great mix up from the more comedy-focused games in the pack.7/10In my opinion, the overall best pack. The lack of any trivia, social deduction, or more team based games is disappointing, but if you can get past that then you'll be left with a pack that has very little to dislike.Average Game Rating: 8.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with each game:The Devils and the Details: The best one in my opinion, I love doing the chores they tell me and my friends what to do, and me and my friends screaming at each other the directions was amazing.Champ'd Up: We weren't expecting this one to be fun or good because we normally don't like drawing games, but holy lord do we love it. It gives us a prompt which is what I didn't like about most drawing games, and the drawings we made were very funny.Quiplash 3: It's quiplash... that's it.Talking Points: Us improvising a presentation with no knowledge of what the slides are, are amazing. We, at first, thought the game was only fun if you're good at improvising what you see, but the third time we played this, we were laughing so hard, because of how we just said, "♥♥♥♥ it," and just said what came to mind. I won that game because my mom went into my room and I screamed, "WELCOME TO MY PRESENTATION!" and made my friends cry from laughter.Blather 'Round: Probably the worst one, but not bad. It's hard to describe things when your choices are so limited, and it made me and my friends not wanna play that one as much. (That's our experience though). It can be good but you have to have specific people for it, like who can describe things the best.Here's how I'd rank each of them:1. The Devils and The Details2. Champ'd Up3. Talking Points4. Quiplash 35. Blather 'RoundRemember these are MY experiences, don't look at reviews like this one, where it's their opinion, and assume, "Hey I have high hopes for this one then," Because experiences vary.

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is a vibrant collection of party games that is a delightful addition to any social gathering or virtual hangout. Released as part of the well-loved Jackbox Party Pack series, this installment maintains the tradition of delivering unique, entertaining, and easy-to-join multiplayer experiences accessible across various devices. This pack includes five diverse games, each offering its flavour of humour and gameplay mechanics, ensuring that there's something for every type of player.Many consider Quiplash 3 the standout game. It is a sequel to the fan-favorite comedy showdown in which players compete to create the funniest answers to quirky prompts. A new final round adds a fresh twist to the game's dynamics.The Devils and the Details is a chaotic cooperative game in which players take on the roles of a family of devils trying to blend into suburban life. It requires teamwork and communication, and depending on the group's cohesion, it can be a hit or miss.Champ’d Up is a drawing fighting game where players create absurd characters to compete in bizarre contests. It's particularly appealing for its creative freedom and hilarious outcomes.Talking Points is an improvisational speech game that tests players' quick thinking. Given random slides, players must deliver a compelling presentation, which leads to plenty of laughter and memorable moments.Blather 'Round is a guessing game that challenges players to describe a secret prompt using a limited vocabulary. It's both challenging and entertaining, perfect for those who love word games.Overall, The Jackbox Party Pack 7 is a solid addition to the series, offering a mix of creativity, humour, and social interaction. Its strength lies in the variety of games and the ease with which players can join, making it a must-have for parties. However, the enjoyment of some games can depend heavily on the group's dynamics, with certain games requiring more creativity or coordination than others. Regardless, this pack is a testament to Jackbox Games' ability to innovate continuously in the party game genre. It is a recommended purchase for those looking to liven up their gatherings.

_childDocuments_.review: A mixed bag consisting of great ideas and graphic design, and critical oversights that should have been spotted in any kind of beta testing/QA.: best final round format so far, claymation/carnival theming is good and much more fun than the flat abstract backdrops of the previous entries: Very good fodder for aspiring improv comedians and probably will be the most popular at parties, but the scoring system is totally broken by the inclusion of the Engagement Bonus.: Only fun the first few times, the prompts are usually obvious or too hard to guess, and the answers are fed to the presenter through the list of words they're given.: Fun to look at, and an opportunity for the maniacs who bring drawing tablets to the party to destroy the competition. The urge to vote based on the quality of the drawing rather than how well it meets the objective will regularly cause player confusion.: Getting enough people to voluntarily play this game is a logistical issue in itself, and for this reason I've only played it once. It's a ton of fun for people who don't mind the stress of simulating a very chaotic living environment. It's likely very underrated.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best pack in the series. The pack does not contain a single dull game like the previous packs usually do and manages to keep the unique jackbox feel throughout them all. I'm just gonna go through all the games in order of their appearance on the menu, give them a rating, and tell you why they deserve it.Quiplash 3 - 9/10 - Probably the game that the most people was excited for and it certainly met the hype. The new art style is a nice refresher to the classic 2D art style in the two prequels. Tiny additions like being able to choose your own avatar before the start of the game are appreciated and a decent and consistent third round is a nice touch. Overall, with much more creative prompts and a whole heck ton of new ways to make people laugh it gets a solid 9. Why it doesn't deserve a 10 is that the game hasn't went under many changes gameplay wise. It is still the same game as the original essentially with the exception of the third round.The Devils and the Details - 7.5 - The most intense game in jackbox history by far. You essentially complete "household" tasks in order to reach a certain score by midnight in order to move on. Nothing in this nature has ever been done in a jackbox game and its nice to have something this chaotic. Something that jackbox games take pride in my opioion is their easy to learn nature. This game is far from easy to learn, it basically spits a bunch of information at you and says good luck. People who have little experience gaming, will have no clue what they are doing and even someone like me who is an experienced gamer, found it difficult to get the hang of it. It took my friends and I three attempts to get past the first day which is supposed to be the easiest, and YES you have to complete an entire week to win (each day being 5-7 minutes long). Once you get the hang of it, it is pretty fun.Champ'd Up - 7/10 - If you were to incorporate Quiplash, TeeKO, Bracketeering, and a football game, this is what you would get. The game is you draw a champion that goes along with the title of the belt and then you make a challenger to a champion that someone else drew, then you vote, lame. It would've been the perfect game to add some form of combat into it but I guess democracy is the fan favorite. There just isn't really anything unique about the game. You just vote for whatever drawing fits with the theme better or whatever one is the most funny, just like most of the drawing games they've made.Talking Points - 10/10 - Instantly a classic. One of the few games that make you want to keep playing for more than one or two rounds. You start out just like Patently stupid filling in the blanks to certain prompts and other people choosing between 3 of them in which to present to the game. After that people will present their topic except they have no clue what their presentation slides would look like. Each presenter will be assigned an assistant whose goal is to help the presenter by setting up their slides by choosing a certain picture or text. Having the assistant the ability to chose a picture of avocado toast to a god-like dear when you're talking about divorce struggles is just wicked funny. Rating's actually mean something too as if the presenter does good, the audience will, hopefully, rate it higher, giving the presenter more points. Although the creating an award at the end is nice, it would be better if the award names were premade.Blather 'Round - 8/10 - Sweet and simple yet somewhat chaotic. It is a fun guessing game that anyone can pick up and enjoy. Everyone picks a thing, ranging in difficulty, for the other player to try and guess. When it is a person's turn to describe what their thing is, they will have to use premade phrases and words to help the guessers guess it. The describer can also use words that the guessers have guessed in order to better describe their thing. I for one love a intense guessing game and this is a nice touch to the jackbox universe, it just isn't anything super special.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best overall pack, all games are solid, with great variation!Talking points feels like a matured version of Patently Stupid, and Champ'd Up feels like TKO got an upgrade too. Quiplash 3 doesn't bring much new to the table, but there are some nice incremental upgrades like emojis can now be used in answers.Devil in the details is INCREDIBLY fun, the best co-op game they've put out by a mile, the only one I've actually played more than once, Bomb Squad from party pack 2 and Zeeple Dome don't even come close!Blather Round is only max 6 players but it is an excellent balance of co-op and competition and puzzle solving, whilst keeping it vague enough to involve everyone from smart-asses to slow people like me!Overall all the games feel snappier, cleaner and much more well polished, with huge amounts of replay-ability. Previously the go-to Jackbox to recommend was Party Pack 3, this one now easily takes the crown!

_childDocuments_.review: Actually writing a serious review for this game (even though definitely no one will read it) because idk I just feel the need to.Overall, I honestly feel like this is the best Jackbox Party Pack, at least judging from the ones that I've played. None of the games in the pack are a miss; some are better than others, but I still have a ton of fun with all of them.Quiplash 3: Obviously it's just another Quiplash but the "thriplash" questions are a really nice addition that I enjoy, and I really like the new claymation look. I'm personally a big fan of Quiplash, so this game was the main reason I bought the pack, and it turns out that all the games on it are super fun :)The Devils and the Details: This game is REALLY fun with a lot of people; it's very chaotic but in a good way. Reminds me a little bit of Among Us, but less aggressive. A very fun and unique game.Champ'd Up: This game is kind of like a weirder version of Tee-KO (which I enjoy a lot), but it is also really fun and never fails to give my friends and I some good laughs.Talking Points: I honestly believe that this is the best game in the pack by far. The presentation aspect makes it feel very similar to Patently Stupid, but the premise of the game is completely fresh and I've never played anything like it. SUPER fun and makes me laugh hysterically.Blather 'Round: This game is very underrated, in my opinion. It's definitely less of a funny game, and can actually be a bit difficult at times. It's like a mix of trivia and charades. Despite it not being as wacky/quirky as the other games, I still really enjoy playing it (also it has a kind of 80s aesthetic which I vibe with SO hard).To summarize, every game in this pack is super fun in different ways, and I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys any of the past Jackbox games, and to people who have never played Jackbox and are looking for some fun party games to play with family or with friends online. :)

_childDocuments_.review: pretty solid jackbox all-around. there's a couple stinkers but overall worth the pricetag, though it wouldn't hurt to just wait for it to go on sale or get a cheaper previous jackbox either.quiplash 3 is definitely the star of the show, and is a monumental upgrade over 2 simply due to improving greatly on the absolute headache that was quiplash 2's last lash. it's quiplash, a third time, and the third round is just "answer the same question 3 times" which is a great set-up for a "normal-normal-unexpected" answer and just generally a good formula. only complaint is that if you're playing with an odd number of players someone has to contend with shmitty's often very unfunny answers, which is just kinda lame.devils and the details is very chaotic and messy. only played once but it feels like playing mario party on crack with imposter syndrome and bad impulse control so I'm not too crazy about it. having to play little instruction based minigames and cooperate/sabotage is an interesting concept but it's no bomb corp.champ'd up is one of those slow-burn games that gets better as the rounds go on, calling back to jokes made several rounds/games ago can make for hilarious comeback moments and is just fun overall. one of the games that draws the most on... well, drawing, and creativity and is just a great recipe for stupid in-jokes and off-kilter match-ups. despite my glowing praise I have to say that the first few rounds can be a little more slow and plain, but it's a good starter to break the ice in that case too.talking points is bad for introverts and those bad at public speaking. or maybe because of that it's good for them? in any case it's best to play this down a few drinks and act like you're the one member of the group project who didn't do any work and now you have to handle the presentation as a result. great for chatty groups but the voting/hype system is a little bit pointless as it's always maxed out anyway.blather round is great for in-jokes as well, and just overall a fun way to play what is essentially digital charades except with pre-made word-cards instead of actions. can be a little frustrating if your group chemistry is a little off or new so don't play this unless you're playing with some friends you know at least decently well.like I said, overall a great pack. tl;dr very good and creatively-inclined games but a couple are a little too chaotic or reliant on good group chemistry to work as party ice breakers. if you want something better to get to know people, I recommend packs 3-5.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished playing this game and let me start by saying, fantastic game. Now you might be thinking that means I've had a great evening, and it would be a fair assumption, but come and sit round the camp fire and listen to my tale.Sunday will always have a funny feeling to it - Work is looming and the weekend is over and it's easy to forget about the adventures that have been had. Opening Jackbox TV, in a room of people I would have called friends had you asked me 2 hours ago, was a welcome distraction. It brought some hope to my day. Maybe, just maybe all was not lost. Oh what a fool I was. Little did I know I was about to embark on a path of destruction and betrayal.However brilliant this game is, it has a real way of exposing the snakes and the phonies among us. One game of Quiplash 3 and I was already horrified by what I saw. As I watched my genius, beautifully crafted answers get outvoted for moronic gibberish such as the 'The Flying Constable' I could feel the tears forming in my eyes. I powered through the emotions and held it together like a champion. It was especially difficult as I was also carrying the conversation with these dullards so it was essentially a double whammy.Next we had a game of Devil's and the details. Wow - Just wow. As I selflessly rang to cancel dinner plans, fixed the car and ordered birthday cakes. These cretins poured themselves glasses of wine and aimed for their solo win. Now I'm not naive, I understand there is a lot of darkness in this world. I just wasn't aware how close to home it really was. Finally, because the oafs were not satisfied with just ruining my night a little bit, we jumped into a game of Talking points. Player 1 headed to the podium and the silence was deafening. We were playing a game all about speech and not a word was spoken. Easy win you might be thinking, but to my disgust the positive votes were flying in. Upvote after upvote for the mute speech. I know you must be hoping I am joking, but alas I am not. Cruel is the only way I can describe my fate right now on this poisoned evening.After this appalling display, it fell upon my shoulders to save the evening. I delivered an impassioned, emotional speech. A passer by shouted up to my window that he felt as if it was almost an out of body experience. Thank you Steve. I put myself in the firing line and guess what they did? They fired. The cowards ran for the hills when it was their turn.I'm no mind reader but I know you're all thinking, 'How amazing must you be to put up with all of this?' and yes I am probably a hero but I'm not here for credit or praise. This is a tale of caution and woe. Play this game, but be careful who you play with,Highly recommend.
