_childDocuments_.review: Quiplash 3 is more of the silly say-anything fill-in-the-blank favorite, with the "Thriplash" at the end replacing the previous system of everyone receiving the same prompt. I have a blast every time I play this.The Devils and the Details is a cooperative game where you are attempting to complete tasks while speaking over eachother to make sure enough gets done to hit a point total in the end. I did not like this game as much as some of the other co-op Jackbox games like Bomb Corp.Champed Up is similar to Tee KO, but I don't find it as fun as the latter.Talking Points is a great game if your friend group loves improv. You are given a topic to present on by your peers and another person controls what pictures are placed on your slides. It has tons of silly stock-photo-esque things to choose from.Blather Round is one of the most fun games in the pack, perhaps tied with Quiplash. It's sort of like a game of Password or Pictionary with pop-culture items, but the clue-giver is given a limited pre-determined set of words to get the idea across.All around, this is a fun pack that you are guaranteed to get hours of enjoyment out of.

_childDocuments_.review: Best one in the series so far. Newcomer Blather Round is a lot of fun, and kinda feels like playing 20 Questions, if the questions were terrible and unhelpful. Biggest complaint is the lack of any trivia-esque games like Fibbage or the Murder Trivia series. Not the biggest dealbreaker but it is a little annoying to have to open up a separate game for anything in that genre.Overall, really good option if you've gotten any mileage at all out of the older games.

_childDocuments_.review: Like every other Jackbox pack I've played, this one is packed with fun, and I haven't even played all the games yet! Blather 'Round is my group's current favorite. _childDocuments_.review: Jackbox Party Pack 7 is perhaps one of my favorite Jackbox games to date due to one game included, Talking Points. Short review, this offers a lot of variety though it may be some people's favorite Party Pack. Quick review of each game:Talking Points: This is THE GAME of this release. This game will either slay your guests or kill the mood. Basically it's improv power points but believe me when I say it's more fun than it sounds. While Quiplash may bring reliable chuckles with witty answers, if your friends are on point it's like short bursts of stand up comedy. With my D&D group we were in stitches during the entire thing. It can be awkward when you decide to play with your in-laws on a Zoom call and their neighbor you haven't met jumped in to play though. Party matters.Quiplash 3: Quiplash, you know it by now. I think I may prefer Quiplash 2 to be honest, but Quiplash is a reliable staple of any party night.The Devil and the Details: This is your cooperative/competitive game. Kinda like Warioware but you need to talk with people at times so it leads to a cacophony of orders and requests. It's a good type of chaos though.Champ'd Up: Drawing game, didn't get to this one. Will update if I end up playing it.Blather' Round: Gonna be my chap of the pack. It's a guessing game where you're given something to describe with limited ways to describe it. Players then type in their answers. If you want trivia and puzzles sure, but honestly I started putting in joke answers just so the game's Speak & Spell to read it out loud to make people laugh.

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox has a lot of great games throughout the many versions, and I believe that this one has the most good games. Let's just say I was wrong about that.The Party Pack 7 games are great. Along with the aforementioned Quiplash, games like Talking Points and Champ'd Up are so much fun playing with your friends, making strange speeches and drawing weird imagery. And while I personally am not a big fan of The Devils and the Details or Blather 'Round, I still enjoy playing them every once in a while. This game is of course meant to be played in person, but playing it over an app like Discord still works great. The art and graphics are much better than previous games as everything looks polished and well made, which is one of the best upgrades from previous titles.The only things I would do to improve this game would be to add Mad Verse City to this game, probably my favorite Jackbox game ever, but that will likely never happen. Overall, this game is really fun for parties and rainy afternoons alike, creating some of the funniest moments that video games can make.

_childDocuments_.review: What's better than a Jackbox game? Five of them!In this unique collection of online party games, players can compete against each other like never before. _childDocuments_.review: Jackbox delivers again on its seventh party pack. If the purpose of the games included is to create unique, hilarious scenarios, it succeeds. Through smart use of the smartphone, this product "shatters" the ice by helping each player feel like an important part of the group activity (the game).My group liked Quiplash and Champ'd Up the most, but I think the others still add value to the bundle. Each of the party games are innovative in their own ways. For example, Talking Points has a really interesting points system and The Devils and the Details does a great job of creating hilarious teamwork scenarios. Each game is different from the others, which is a good thing because their different play styles suit varying personalities and social scenarios. - Using Zoom's screen share feature is an easy way to set up online multiplayer. Line up participants' video feeds on the top edge of the screen, and modify the volume until they say it's at a good level. Then, you're ready to go. My group's favorite. Players submit answers to prompts which are put up against another answer. The rest of the players give points to the answer they find the best. EMOJIS WORK!Requires effort. Players work together in a family to complete tasks like clean the kitchen or drive to the orthodontist. Co-operative tasks require communication, and having to talk over other players creates chaos. For example, a task undertaken by two family members is to drive to the hardware store. One player holds the map but not the wheel, and the other player holds the wheel but can't see the map.Only game that involves drawing. In the first round you're given a championship title like "worst roommate". Players draw and name a figure that fits this description. In the second round you are shown a player's drawing from round 1 but not the name of the title. The figures clash in the third round and players decide which drawing should win the title.Players first think up ridiculous speech titles. Then, players take turns giving speeches that are controlled by their "assistant", another player. The assistant chooses which images go up on the board from a few options given to them. This game has a very innovative voting system.My group's least favorite. Unfortunately, compared to the high energy, creative game play of the other inclusions Blather 'Round felt lackluster. A player gets a person, place, object, or idea and has to put together sentences with vocabulary provided by the game. As other players guess, they have the opportunity to use guesses given in their sentences. Most of the fun in this came from typing weird stuff and having the computer read it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Beginning with its first release all the way back in 2014, Jackbox Games ditched the quirky gameshow aesthetic of You Don’t Know Jack and leaned into a more varied batch of party games for groups to enjoy with The Jackbox Party Pack.  The yearly drop of odd drawing challenges, snappy social endeavors, and occasional spatterings of Cookie Masterson have been solid for the most part, but Party Pack 6 was a series low that concerned me that Jackbox Games may have finally been running out of gas after being so consistent for 6 years.  But I’ll go ahead and break the ice here: I’m sorry for doubting you Jackbox Games.  I love 7.  Give me more of this every year.  Now let me explain:A familiar face starts us off.  The blueprint remains the same as players will answer two questions with either the most relevant or funniest remark they can think of and will face off against another player with the other contestants and audience voting on the best answer between two players.  A “threes”-based final round remains the only real change, but Quiplash has been consistent since its debut in 2015.  I will Quiplash is the lowest in the pack, but know this is a pretty high bar once we get to the others.Players take on the roles of a devilish family looking to meld into the daily routines of human life, while also trying to be the “bestest devil” by completing the most mundane tasks in a white picket fence suburbia game show.  Players will have to work together to complete challenge tasks (main tasks to help coordinate big events like getting ready for Prom or making a Folk-Rock family band) to finish the week’s checklist, but smaller tasks (like doing taxes, feeding the murderous cat played by the audience, or making breakfast) will help increase individual score as well as fill the Family Meter for the day.  Selfish tasks can net players more points at the expense of not helping the family, but too much selfishness can run a family emergency that hurts everyone.This game is a logistical nightmare as most tasks require a helping hand that players will need to communicate with each other to complete, but a majority of the time other players will be trying to do the same thing while the odd man out may be out being selfish which people can intervene if they aren’t already preoccupied.  With so much talking over one another and shenanigans happening off-center while also making sure you’re the best family you can be if only for a split second to check the list is chaos at its finest.  You’ll be mentally exhausted keeping up with everything, but the outcome of winning feels fantastic.  Devils and the Details usually feels good for one round before moving on for a breather, but it’s a dang hoot.Your obligatory drawing game is actually a banger this year.  I’m notoriously bad at Jackbox’s drawing games, so they don’t usually peak my interest because I don’t have the capabilities to even remotely play them well, even if the joke is to have terrible pictures.  But Champ’d Up gives each player a “champion” of something: has-beens, maxin' and relaxin', Florida.  Once your champion is made you’ll be given another player's champion, but not told what the drawing is the champion of.  Here you’ll create your “underdog” to hopefully sway the audience when the two drawings go against each other in penciled combat.Winning rounds in my groups has all revolved on the punchline instead of the consistency, and the extracurricular arguments and comments absolutely sell the feel of an underground fist fight between 2D amalgamations.  Add even more shenanigans with the later round Tag Teams and Champ’d Up stands tall as Jackbox’s best drawing game, and that was an opinion of multiple people I’ve played with, not just my janky-drawing self.A mental nightmare for introverts, but an absolute goldmine for the word-vomiters.  Talking Points is structured as a PowerPoint presentation for your friends and your only knowledge going in is the opening slide.  Players create three random, weird-as-can-be-thought ad-libs for others to choose for their talking point.  You have control of how fast your slides go, but a randomly assigned partner has the task of picking your transition slides as well as your picture slides.  You as the speaker need to keep your audience engaged as they see each slide for the first time, just like yourself.  The more engagement, the longer the talk, the better score, and your assistant receives an extra half of your total as a thank you bonus for not throwing you to the wolves.Trying to talk your way through situations can lead to some absolutely gut busters, especially watching someone explain how a clown with a balloon in front of an abandoned gas station coincides with how you escaped from a prison of flesh (a real task I had!).  The replayability of this game is near limitless and even people straight bombing has produced some of the best scores.  Talking Points is definitely my Game of the Pack here and one I’m always down for.Stir together a combo of Charades and Taboo with an unnecessarily funny text-to-speech module and you’ve got a recipe of success.  Players pick a word or phrase and instead of explaining it with your voice, you must use a bevy of descriptions to explain the word or phrase without actually saying it.Blather is the easiest to pick up and play and I feel this game will have the most longevity of the Pack as the game feels better with a smaller audience.  Having played this with a full 6 and a smaller 4, I like the smaller intimate parties as your choices play more to the audience and answers don’t get slapped correct immediately nearly as much.  There’s something enjoyable about racking your brain and really chewing on clues to eventually get the correct answer that’s worth the other times you feel like an idiot.  This game is easy to pop on for 30 minutes and enjoy it, much like Earwax does in Party Pack 2 or Guesspionage from Party Pack 3.I could not be happier seeing Jackbox Games back in prime fighting form with a masterfully composed set of games to enjoy with your friends, and I have renewed confidence in what future tidbits the team can make going forward.  Here’s to next year!

_childDocuments_.review: Worth getting but I do feel that this pack works way better in person than online (Obviously difficult though in these COVID times). Talking Points is one of my favourite Jackbox Games from all packs while Quiplash has some improvements that keep it fun and entertaining. Champ'd Up is great fun if you can draw quickly, very similar to the brilliant Tee K.O but not with shirts. The Devils and the Details doesn't work as well online but could be fun and challenging in person, and finally Blather Round I personally found mediocre but can't say I have played enough of yet to give a definitive answer to. Overall, not bad but thank god for the US centric filter, makes it so much better for people outside of the US (like me).
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Have only played Quiplash 3 and Champ'd Up so far, which are probably the standout games anyway, but if you're a fan of Jackbox games, these are worth picking up the pack for. Champed Up is probably the best drawing game in any of the party packs: quick, easy, fun, and not extremely reliant on the prompts. Quiplash 3 features a US-centric content filter, introduced in the Party Pack 6, which makes this the best Quiplash for an international public. Being able to pick your own avatar is also a welcome addition.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a decent batch of games.Quiplash 3: By far the best Quiplash. Final round is also the very best in the trilogy.The Devils and the Details: Chaotic fun. Somewhat difficult over voice chat, but that's part of the fun. Best played on touch devices, though.Champ’d Up: The star of the show. Second round is definitely where this game shines: swapping out drawings for the best laughs is a must.Talking Points: Quite terrible. Powerpoint presentations with holes in them is not really interesting.Blather 'Round: Fun if everyone understands the references. Not as fun when people keep guessing random stuff because they have no idea where they're heading. Definitely easier on repeated playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox Games again made a really well made party game. The games that Party Pack 7 brings to are just absolutely flawless. The soundtrack is also just really well composed. The only thing I just wasn't fan of was Blather Round. Personally it just felt too boring to play and wasn't to comedic.But either way, Party Pack 7 is still a good game for 2020.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Jackbox's so far! I've had great fun playing Jackbox games with my housemates in the evenings, especially Quiplash and Faking It from Party Pack 3. Pack 7 has very easily topped these games in terms of popularity! Devils and the Details is a great game with lovely animations which helps make the game more interactive with your phone; the only criticism would be that it means you're all staring at your phones instead of interacting with one another but it keeps everyone focused at least! My housemates were originally apprehensive towards the speech presentation game but it was just too funny! I was surprised at how extroverted they became as they got into the spirit of things! It kept everyone on their toes and had the entire room in hysterics!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Talking points was fantastic, but very group dependant. Champed up was very funny especially when people deliberately go for very stupid combatants. Blather Round was a surprising stand out, being a very funny but also very challenging charades like game. The Devils and the Details fell a bit flat but might have been better with a larger group. Quiplash is just Quiplash with minor variations, that is to say it's still very good but not necessarily worth it over any other version you can get your hands on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: It's another hit from Jackbox Games. Devil and the Details is the only one that can't really be done remotely as it requires immediate breakout groups. Otherwise, Blather Round is a great take on taboo, Champ'd Up does a great job revamping the drawing system, and Talking Points makes speeches actually kinda fun. Quiplash is also as good as the previous versions, just no real notable changes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Gloriously fun to play, though it obviously requires friends.  Personally, being devoid of anything but dry humor, I struggle to compete in the various games in the Jackbox series that want you to make people laugh, but it's great to see others' senses of humor on display.  The trivia games are great fun.This is one of my favorite additions to the series so far, but one of the games...It's something to do with a household of demons or something like that?  I feel like that's one of the weakest individual games Jackbox's come out with.  Overall still a fantastic party game though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Best Party Pack since Party Pack 3.I love Jackbox games, and I own them all, but honestly, I felt that they had a dip in quality after Jackbox Party Pack 4. I feel like this revived the series. every game on here is extremely fun, rather than just having one or two good games.Since there's a bunch of games in this one, I'll go game by gameQuiplash 3: I mean it's quiplash. What's not to like about this game? The formula of ask a question, funny answer party games will always be fun, regardless of how innovative the game is, and while it may not be the most innovative game, it's certainly fun.9/10The Devil's in the Details: This one is a really fun game to play locally, which is a bit unfortunate given that the world is exploding right now, but if you can get a group together, it's a really fun task based game where you help each other out in this Co-op competitive game. Yelling at your family members and telling them to stop being selfish, then immediately doing a selfish thing is very fun. That being said, a lot of the tasks are a bit simple and the gameplay is a bit repetitive over time.8/10Champ'd Up: This is the kingpin of this pack. This is just better T-KO. All of the negative qualities of T-KO (Your good designs meaning nothing if they go up first, The length of time T-KO takes, the difficulty of complete open-ended creativity, random ways the tie-breakers were broken) were solved and became strengths. You don't have to beat every other player, but you just have to beat another player, and the "underdog" who doesn't know what the competition is, wins in the case of a tie. The game is shortened because you don't have tons of time to design a character, but you still have a good amount of time. There's also not dialogue in between every choice made, you just make the character and name it. In addition, one person gets the category the fighter is fighting in, and then the other person just gets the competition, and not the category. This doesn't give any advantage to one player, and makes it so it's not just open ended, try to be funny.TL;DR - This is one of the best Jackbox games they've made by improving upon one of the other best Jackbox games.10/10Talking Points - Ever been in a class where someone else made the entire presentation, and you were assigned to present it? Well this game somehow made that awkward and difficult situation into a hilarious game. Honestly, the most fun role to play in this is the assistant, just controlling what the next slides will say, and just compounding on the comedy the speaker is making.9/10Blather 'Round - This is the hardest game Jackbox has ever made. Trying to describe something with the extremely limited choices you have makes for basically a word version of charades, that works. It's vv difficult, but vv fun. It's hard to describe it without playing it, which I definitely recommend.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: If you have never played a Jackbox Pack, this is not the one to start with.  It's fantastic, don't get me wrong, but start with #5 if you are building up a collection.  #7 is a fantastic evolution of a number of game concepts that this developer has worked with in the past, but you only realize it when you have the earlier context.Standout Winner:  Blather 'Round.  Fantastic entry in their trivia game series.Tough Sell:  Talking Points.  Not everyone is ready to be giving a TED TalkBest Done After Quarantine:  Devils and the Details.  It can be difficult to sort voices over headsets.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, great party game.All of the Jackbox Party Packs and individual games are really fun to play with friends and family, whether that be in-person or over discord screen sharing. If you are thinking of getting a fun party game to just fool around on and have a good time, I highly recommend this Party Pack and many of the others. If it helps, looking up a YouTube video of some people playing the game and having fun on it can surely help you pick out the Pack right for you.Quiplash is by far Jackbox Games greatest achievement and is one of the funniest party modes I have ever played.10/10, great job Jackbox!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing set of innovations for Jackbox!Several of the games adds customization for yourself, such as changing your character in quiplash, or your pointer in Talking Points.Quiplash 3 is one AMAZING build-up.  Not only is it more of the same amazing game, but it allows you to create your own set of prompts to publish, and discover.  Furthermore, the old concept of "Last Lash" is abandoned (thankfully) and replaced with thriplash... which is far better and more fun than "Last Lash"  Also, the character counter is a welcome addition.The Devil and the Details is also a really good game! An among us-esque minigame simulator that throws you into the chaos of working together with friends, and sabotaging the family.  It really is quite somethingChamp'd up is also kinda neat! Not for the theming, but for the drawing technologies added upon compared to the other games.  The undo button, the marker that doesnt overwrite the pencil, genius.  I would love to see this template reused in any future drawing games, or even retroactively added to some of the other games in other packs like drawful.Talking Points is pure GENIUS.  I only wished it was longer, but I still enjoy this a lot.  The idea of spouting some random junk improv is totally genius.  Improv acting classes everywhere have just gone out of businessBlather 'Round........ pass.  It's not fun.  There's no creativity at all, or any chaos, nothing fun.  It's like trivia, but more ambiguous, and it has you more angry at the game than yourself for not getting a question right.  Not cool man.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: All five games are great, we all think. The only drawback is the tendency for Blather 'Round to suddenly quit in the middle of a game. We haven't been able to play a complete game of Blather in some weeks now. OTOH we are normally playing on Saturday evenings, when the load on the Jackbox servers is presumably very high.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: I know that Jackbox Packs can be hit or miss, but I think this is the best one they made. Quiplash is still as fun as always, and it feels more refreshing with the new Final Round and artstyle. The Devils and the Details might be my new favorite Jackbox game. It's a Co-Op/Vs. type game that involves you doing simple tasks to basically survive human life, and the themeing and chaos makes this amazing. Champ'd Up is a really good drawing/voting game, kinda simular to Tee K.O, but the wildness of it makes it a great game, and a good replayable one too! Talking Points gave me the most laughs I've had in a while. Giving speeches with no prep time is super oddly enjoyable, and the shock factor ties it all together nicely. Blather 'Round falls kinda short compared to the other 4, but it's still a fun, kinda relaxing experence where answers fly and descriptions are vague. Overall, this might seem a bit high for most, but this is a 9.2/10 game for me. If the pacing for some of these games were upped a bit, and Blather 'Round was a bit more enjoyable, then it would be almost a perfect 10. If you need to relax from COVID, or just wanna have a good time, you can't go wrong at all with the Jackbox Party Pack 7. Also as a side note for the entire series I love that these games go on sale a bit, and once you own a Jackbox game, the rest are ~20% off! Sweet!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really find anything bad to say about this pack. This is the first pack where every single game has been good or great.Quiplash is as good as ever, and though it doesn't feel all too different from previous outings, it still remains rock solid.Talking points is a laugh riot as we attempted to improv some sort of speech or pitch to the goofy stock image style slides our friends presented us with.Champ'd up is one of the best, (and quickest) drawing games they've created yet.Devils and the Details is a great co-op addition to the pack (a rare thing) that has us shouting at the trouble-makers while laughing at the ludicrous prompts.My favorite game is blather round. Trying to get across a point using limited references really scratches and itch I didn't know needed scratching.If you have friends, buy this game. If you don't have friends, make some so that you can enjoy this game, and then buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the parade! Here's the festivities:Quiplash 3: Has a claymation style and a new final round where you have to guess 3 blank answers to a question. More of the same as previous Lashes.Blather 'Round: Players have to guess what your'e describing to them but you do a terrible job having them figure it out.Talking Points: How to make a non-coherent TED Talk with "help" from your assistant. This one is a personal favorite!Champ'd Up: Draw your best fighter....literally.Still need to play the Devil's In The Details. Will update when I get to it.Overall: A decent collection for this year. Try out some of the other packs and see what you like!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Each game has it's own charm and works well with 3+ players with only Blather Round being 2+ players.Talking points was the only have my group of friends had trouble getting into, but we still had a few laughs. If you have a talkative group who likes improv then you'll enjoy this one.Quiplash is what you expect but with some amazing claymation visuals and fun music. The ability to customize the promots makes it even more perfect for inside jokes to be incorporated into the gameplay.Blather Round is great. I've played this with 2 people and a full room and had so much fun with it every single time. The only complaint would be I wish there were options to add more than 2 rounds when there are fewer people.I've always had a fun time with drawing games in all Jackbox games and Champ'd Up is no different. Even the non-artistic people in my group were cracking up seeing their drawings go head to head against other players drawings.The Devil's in the Details is fun and engaging, but does take a while to get into it and used to the gameplay. It's definitely worth playing at least once.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I just bought it this last month and enjoy each one of the games! All the new games in this pack are interesting and engaging with people. My favorite ones to play are devil in the details and talking points. The most boring one to me is the drawing fighting game, I find it too similar to others with no big change. It’s fun nonetheless. Talking points is like having to make a ted talk topic and then trying to give a speech to the crowd for points. It’s very funny and engaging with Everyone. I highly recommend this pack. It’s just as good if not better than party pack 6.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the highest-quality package of all of the Party Packs since the 4th one.  All of the games provided stand out in their own unique and fun ways:-Quiplash 3 is the usual Quiplash experience, which is always a good time.  Player-made prompts are pretty fun too!  The only thing is that having a single "final-round" game, Thrip-lash, is kinda strange.  Having all of the round types from Quiplash 2 would be nice.-Devil in the Details is really unique for a Jackbox game, but it's super fun and really well executed.  It's a really fun balance of having to talk over your friends to achieve all of the group's goals, while also staying back long enough to earn enough points for yourself to win the overall game.-Champ'd Up is the "art" game of the pack, but the premise is probably my favorite of all of those so far.  It's a simple premise that provides an incredible range of creativity and choice for each player, which some of the art games in the past don't always achieve.  The production values go above and beyond here as well, and they make drawing much more intens than it should be.-Talking Points is a ton of fun, encouraging snap-judgements in order to make your presentation shine.  I've had a ton of fun with this one, especially when me and the person running my slides can find some great synergy together.  I'd almost like to say this has helped me with giving presentations in college, but I also remember screaming about spaghetti at one point so maybe not?-Blather 'Round is a really clever spin on games like Catchphrase.  It's pretty simple, but the little additions like using player guesses for reference add a ton to the experience.Overall this pack is a ton of fun, and far and away the best value of any pack so far.  If you can only buy one Party Pack, make it this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great set. The rules of play for Champed Up make it a stand out, with lots of hilarious moments. That said, the videos are skipping a lot for me and the load times seem long. Especially when trying to stream it for others, which has never been a problem with these. That made Devils and the Details especially rough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Without question one of the most well rounded Jackbox Party Packs. The only slight criticism I have (and is totally not the fault of the developers) is that a full game of Devil in the Details can get quite hectic with everyone yelling and talking over each other on Discord.Small criticism aside, Jackbox Party Pack 7 is a solid addition to the Jackbox line. Bravo. Can't wait to see what's in store for Jackbox 8.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and amazing game after the 6th. My favorites are Talking Points and Quip 3 and boy is it fantastic. I yet again tell my friends to play this game every weekend, and even tho sometimes they don't, I enjoy watching Youtubers and Twitch Streamers enjoying it as much as I do. I'm really digging the unique style for each game and that each game has an updated version of a pre-existing game in an earlier Jackbox. I hope the company had as much fun making this game, and I can't wait for the 8th Jackbox in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Overview:Quiplash 3: It's Qiuplash. It's the bread and butter of Jackbox that everybody loves. Honestly, I can't imagine them finding a way to f*** it up.Champed Up: T.K.O if you were drawing for yourself. Very fun, and the finisher animations can be hilarious with the right drawing.Talking Points: Remember when you had to bulls*** your way through presentations in high school? Well, put that bullsh**ing to the test. Probably the best game in the pack to play with friends.Devils in the Details: Each time my friends and I played this we had no idea what to do. Really frustrating game to play, especially since it requires everyone working together.Blather Round: 20 questions, except more confusing and restrictive. Probably the worst game in the pack.All in all, this pack is a good addition to the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Really impressive that they haven't fixed anything that annoys me about the 6 previous games like how you can't remove people from lobbies without making a new lobby or how answers arbitrarily have to be short and all caps or how you can only play with like 6 or 8 players for no reasonBut they do have some really fun games in this pack. Absolutely obsessed with Blather Round. Does suck that it randomly crashed midgame and we lost all that progress. Didn't give a crash report or anything. BallerStill a fun game and I recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best of the jackbox options. This still has the the normal competitive options but the addition of a primarily co-op added some variety i didn't even know i would l wanted. Would highly recommend for fun with friends and family. Amazing game for playing online with you with friends and family with only one person having to own it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the best work from Jackbox. Quiplash 3 has a new final game that is much more satisfying than the previous versions. Also, Blather 'Round and Champ'd Up are refreshing versions of the trivia and draw game varieties we come to love from jackbox. That being said, every new party has a dud and for me, that dud is The Devils and the Details. It's simply too long and too convoluted to make for an enjoyable Jackbox game. Also, I've forgotten one of the most innovative game in this new pack: Talking Points. Lovers of Patently Stupid will be at home in this presentation-style improv game where the points don't seem to matter and the main goal is truly to just have fun with it. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent addition to the Jackbox lineup. You've got Quiplash which is always fun, Champ'd Up which is a hilarious drawing game that is bound to get lots of entertainment, even if none of your friends can draw well. Blather 'Round is probably what I end up playing the most, as you can play it at 2 players and it is quite fun with just that amount of players. Talking Points also ends up being pretty fun, even though it can get quite random with the prompts and images. The least favourite of the pack, at least for my play group, is The Devils and the Details, as the tasks can feel kind of random and we didn't really feel the want to keep playing. As a random note, the music in Champ'd Up is very hype, I would jam to it 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Another good game of Jackbox. Quiplash 3 is pretty much same as quiplash 2, Blather Round is fun taboo like game where you have to have others guess a word and you can only use vague descriptors to get the word across, Champ'd up is a fun drawing game similar to TKO where drawings will square off against each other to compete for what best represents a prompt.Talking points is a really fun game if you don't mind standing up in front of others giving a presentation with text and images that are decided by another player on the fly. It has become my favorite game of the bunchThe Devils in the Details is the only game I'm not really a fan of. It requires players to work together to perform simple tasks on their phone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: This one is one of my favorite packs, maybe even the best one. The games:- Quiplash 3: Still my overall favorite game, easy to pick up with lots of comedic potential. The new third round is interesting, but not neccessarily an improvement - but a refreshing alternative. Making your own themed matches or play the ones from other people online is also very interesting. 5/5- The Devils and the Details: By far the most boring game of the pack, if not of the entire series. The tasks are boring, the itneractions are meaningless, the goal of the game is also whatever. Maybe you like it as a team-building excercise, but it really stinks otherwise. 0/5- Champ’d Up: At least on par with my favorite drawing game T-K.O., if not better due to newer functions. The audience has meaningful interactions and the quips help a lot to avoid a spontaneous lack of ideas. 5/5- Talking Points: Basically powerpoint karaoke, somewhat similar to Patently Stupid, but different enough. Requires a little more time and attention by the players, but can reward them with a lot of fun. Points are quite arbitrary here, but whatev. 4/5- Blather 'Round: An interesting take on word guessing games like charades or Taboo. Easier to pick up than the other games in the pack aside of Quiplash and the pre-selectable sentences and voiced guesses by the players generate enough engagement by all sides for a few amusing rounds 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Having been playing these games weekly with friends since the start of this pandemic, pack 7 has probably ended up being our collective favourite. Not too sure we're a fan of Devil, but the rest of the games are great. Special shout to Champ'd Up, which is fun, fresh, snappy and has such a good soundtrack that it's hard to not let the credits song play through at the end of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite possibly the first Jackbox where every single game is absolutely fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: This has to be the best Jackbox yet. There wasn't a single mini-game on here that I wouldn't try again. Please see below for my take on each mini-game.Quiplash 3: Standard Jackbox game, if you liked the other quiplashes, you'll like this.The Devils and the Details: My least favorite game in the pack. You have to collaborate with your friends to complete tasks, and work to accomplish a main goal, such as building a tree house. Tasks are given in the form of prompts that require multiple players to read things from their phone, and also single player tasks that you use gestures on your phone to accomplish. Players could also do tasks that were worth more points, but would sabotage progress. Overall, it never really felt like any single person was winning in this game, and if you tried to win by doing the higher point sabotage tasks, you'd still lose because the main task wouldn't get completed. Replay value seems good, as there is a decent selection of main tasks you can choose to have your party play. This was a decently fun game, and other groups may get more enjoyment from it than we did. Not one I'd play every time, but certainly not one I'd try once never play again.Champ’d Up: The group I play with usually HATES the drawing games, but we all enjoyed Champ’d Up very much. The premise is, each person gets a different prompt for a champion that they have to draw. Let's say you get "Champion of the USA"; you'd draw something that corresponds to that prompt. Next, on your phone you see a champion someone drew, and you have to draw a champion based on what you think their prompt was. After everyone is done drawing, the champions fight and you vote on who best fits the prompt (or however the people you play with like to vote). After that round is a couple more drawing rounds, and then a tag team round where you select from your fighters to fit a random prompt. The concept of the game felt very unique and fresh, and having the prompts really helped everyone's creativity to come up with unique champs.Talking Points: My favorite game out of the pack. It starts out by everyone getting a complete the sentence prompt, and then everyone gets assigned a completed prompt that they have to do a presentation on. The kicker is: someone else chooses the pictures that show up during your presentation. We had a lot of laughs about what pictures were chosen during each slideshow, and it was hilarious watching everyone come up with ridiculous ways to relate the pictures to their topic. I'm not sure how large the variety of pictures is, so that could affect the replayability of this game, much like it did with the later rounds of "Survive the Internet" from Jackbox 4.Blather 'Round: A guessing game, kind of like charades, where you pick a word that players have to guess. After you select your main word, you then have to complete sentences (usually resulting in broken caveman english) by selecting 1 or 2 words from a list that shows up on your phone. Players keep typing their guess, and hopefully things get narrowed down enough by your hints that somebody guesses the correct word. This game wasn't as comedic as other Jackbox mini-games, but still created the right amount of chaos that you expect and love about the Jackbox Party Packs

_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a quick review for all the games here:Quiplash 3: It's Quiplash. Of course it's great. The Thrip Lash that makes you give three answers per prompt is a cool twist and has lead to some fun moments in my streams.Devils and the Details: Depending on who you play with this is either fun or insufferable. My recommendation is to play this with people you know instead of randos in your stream chat that way you can communicate effectively.Champ'd Up: The drawing game of the pack. If you played Bracketeering in PP4, it's that but with pictures. Talking Points: As soon as this was revealed I knew this would be the hidden gem of the pack. You and a randomly selected assistant have to improv an entire TED talk and if it wasn't for Quiplash, it would be the best game in this pack. We have yet to have a game that didn't make us laugh. Hoepfully Jackbox gives us a sequel to this.Blather 'Round: The weakest game in the pack in my opinion but it's still fun. My biggest problem is that there's nothing stopping the presenter from simply giving the answer so there's a bit of an honor system that has to be had with this.TLDRQuiplash 3 and Talking Points tie for best gameChamp'd Up is alrightDevils and the Details is love it or hate itBlather 'Round is weaksauce

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my favorite Party Pack for playing with friends. Quiplash 3, while the final round is a little worse, is the best visual in the series. Devil in the Details gets more fun as you play it which came as a shock to me because I'm not the biggest fan of some of the previous collaborative games from other Party Packs. Champ'd Up is TKO 2.0. If you are a fan of the drawing games this definitely goes up there as one of the best. Talking points is by far my favorite game in this Pack. Especially with friends. I love having to improv a speech not knowing what will show up. It's a mini game straight out of "Impractical Jokers". Blather Round is one of those short but sweet games and is perfect for just a casual round. I don't think there is a single minigame that I really hate in this pack. If you primarily play this game with friends, this is the perfect Pack for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one.While I have loved almost every party pack I think this one is pretty weak. As much as I like quiplash and drawing games, they've grown old because they aren't changing enough about them to make them interesting. Also the final round of both of these games are not good at all, I dread the triple lash and after drawing for a round or 2 before, I definitely don't need a 3rd round where you just swap out people to keep "battling."Talking points is by far the best game in the pack and it's hilarious and super fun so I recommend everyone play that one as much as you can.Devils and the Details is confusing. It's a cooperative game but also a competitive game but it doesn't feel like there's winners and losers? I'm not really sure how to explain it but it just isn't satisfying, the games fun while you're playing it but we only played it a few times and were done with it.Blather round is also pretty fun, I could see us playing that for a while as well as talking points.All in all the price is right and at least 2 of the games have insane replayability so although this pack was disappointing, I think it's worth the purchase, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Party Pack 7 is Jackbox's best. While it doesn't include any trivia titles, every game is unique and well thought out with very high production values. Whether you're new to Jackbox or been a fan for many years, • : More Quiplash but with a third round that is .• : A chaotic team game where players work together (or devilishly alone) to complete dozens of mini-games before the timer runs out. • :  Players draw and name characters to compete with others to see which best matches their prompt (e.g. "Forever alone", "West-Coast lifestyle", etc).• : Players give ad-lib presentations around player generated topics, with supporting players providing on-the-fly visuals. It's an absolute riot of a time, and • : A word-guessing game where the active player tries to get others to guess his/her topic using a very limited set of predetermined words.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Party Packs 3 and 5 and this one is no doubt my favorite. There isn't a single game I don't enjoy, so here's a quick review of each:Quiplash 3: I mean, it's the 3rd one. It's the same as the others. It's kinda like cards against humanity as in "whoever answers the funniest thing wins", except you can answer whatever you want. Not a huge fan of the new final round, though, I think Quiplash 2 was a bit better because of that, but still really fun. My friends and I like to start with this one.The Devils in the Details: Ok, this one is heavy. Think Among Us, as everyone is working together completing tasks (which have you swiping, tapping, and solving puzzles) until they fill a bar. Some of these tasks actually require cooperation. Instead of an impostor each one is simply competing for the highest score, and there are selfish tasks which award lots of points but no benefit, and may in fact hurt everyone if they do too many. You can stop others from doing them, though. This one is fun out of context lol, and gets hilarious when there's a lot of people trying to communicate with each other at once.Champed Up: Probably my favorite. You get to draw the champion of a funny prompt the game gives you. Then another friend sees your champion and has to draw an opponent without knowing what the prompt was. And then people vote for the better one. It gets better in the last round when the prompt changes, allowing you to swap out for a champion that fits better.Talking Points: This one is not for everyone but I really enjoy it. You have to give a Power Point presentation but you have an assistant selecting random pics. You have to keep talking like you totally know what's going on, so it's great if you know how to improvise. Of course, assistans should make sure images can make at least a bit of sense when selecting them. Oh, and the theme of your presentation is chosen based on what the players write. Ngl, this one could actually help develop real life skills.Blather Round: Tbh I thought this one was pretty dull until I got to play it. Imagine Pictionary combined with that guessing game from Inglorious Basterds. You choose a place, character, story or ... thing and people have to guess. You have a limited pool of words you can use as prompts, so it's really funny seeing people get closer and closer as you give them more hints.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Jackbox Games I think this might be the best pack they've released so far:Every game is great.Quiplash 3 is not only just more Quiplash but it's quite a big improvement compared to the 2nd one thanks to the new final round which I feel is much, much better than the final round of Quiplash 2 (Which was very hit or miss, and it missed often)The Devils and the Details is maybe the weakest game of the pack and yet it's still very, very fun. The idea behind the game is quite clever and the final rounds can get pretty exciting. It's by far the most "complicated" game of the pack so you'll want to explain the rules to your friends before jumping in game (I think the tutorial is a bit lackluster)Champd Up is a very creative drawing game. It's a ton of fun and the possibility of using old champions in future runs if you click Play Again is super cool.Talking Points is, at least for my group, by far the funniest game of the pack. We think it's probably one of the best games Jackbox has ever made. With the right people it's just hilarious, the speaker + assistant system works absolutely perfectly, the points system is fun and keeps the audience engaged, the comments and awards are a super fun way to add even more twists to an already fantastic game. The art direction for Talking Points is also really strong, it's just a pleasure to look at.Blather Round requires more thinking than the usual Jackbox Games but it's a very good compromise between a purely knowledge-based game (like Trivia Murder Party or You Don't Know Jack) and a more chill "for fun" game where you just mess around with your friends. The only thing the game suffers from is being too American-based in some words and answers but that's always been a problem of pretty much most Jackbox Games.While the lack of a Social Deduction game saddens me a bit (I think Push the Button is one of the best JB6 games) I still think that JB7 is by far the best pack released so far.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Best pack yet! All 5 games are super fun and super different from one another. Not one game is like bad, at most mediocre but still fun! The mix of the different games is also very cool.The Devil in The Details: Super fun to play. It's mostly coop with some competitive parts but you kinda wanna win together. It's a little hard on voice chat but I think if everyone is in the same room it would be an absolute party hit.Champ'd Up: basically Tee K.O. but with character design. The graphics and music help a lot. Me and my friends are artists so this is just silly fun for us.Talking Points: My personal favorite. It's basically you talking using a powerpoint presentation you didn't make. Which is just chaos and fun all around.Blather Round: An interesting word game. Think of it as reverse taboo. This game makes you realize how hard it is to describe something as general as possible. Best part is that you can use someone's guess as part of the prompt to help the guessers guess the right answer.Quiplash 3: Quiplash 2 was already a staple, but Quiplash 3 is better because of one thing: The Thrip Lash.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best party pack that Jackbox has released. So if you're short on cash and can only pick up one party pack, this is the one for you. My opinions on the games are down below. Btw, sub to randomgamer800 you won't regret it.Champ'd Up- This was okay. It didn't really blew me away but it was not terrible. People who are skilled at drawing will have tons of fun with this. If you're a terrible drawer, you might not really like this game as this game mostly requires somewhat decent drawing skills. The naming of the mascot does help to a small extent to skew the game in favour to those who can't drawBlather Round- Probably 2nd best game of the pack. It's basically charades but you can only use preselected words. Tip: sometimes their easy indication is not really easy. It depend on what your audience is. Gameplay was fun be it I was guessing or giving. Tough game but very fun.Quiplash 3- It's just quiplash. If it ain't broke, don't fix it.Devils and the Details- It's basically a less stressful version of bomb corp or keep talking or nobody explodes but with a fun catch. Honestly, give this game a go, it will really test the communication and teamwork skill of your group. Talking Points-Best game ever, it's just gold. It's so creative and that's why I like it a lot. Mic is highly recommended for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Talking Points alone is worth the price of admission. It's an absolutely brilliant improv game and it leads to some downright gut-busting situations. Play it and see how coherent of a presentation you can give without knowing what's on the next slide!Champed Up and Quiplash 3 are the next best games. Champed Up is basically an Original Character Do Not Steal creation competition. Make an OC that's the living embodiment of the prompt's topic, make a challenger to another OC (except you're not given their prompt,) and watch 'em duel for popularity. The results can get pretty wild. As for Quiplash 3? ...It's Quiplash. Can't really go wrong with Quiplash.Blather Round's one of the harder games in the pack but it's all in good fun. Seeing people struggle to describe things with a ridiculously limited vocabulary is amusing.I'd say Devils and the Details is the weakest game in the pack. If a tug of war between group cooperation and selfish scheming is what you're feeling up to, give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly? They really did an astounding job with this pack. With Quiplash getting custom prompts, it makes the experience even more funny and enjoyable. Champ'd up is AMAZING and probably even better than Tee K.O.! Blather Round's pretty enjoyable, but The Devils and Details is the BEST game out of all the packs. That one is super chaotic and fun! Definitely recommend this title to anyone who is wondering which Jackbox title to buy. This one pretty much takes the cake.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game I played the 5th and 6th Jackbox and both of those were very fun and I expected this game to be just as good as the other entries. Once again Jackbox did very well I only had two games that were a bit lackluster in my opinion.QUIPLASH 3Awesome game me and my friends played this one the most. It is a simple game but that is what makes it so great. Some of the prompts weren't the greatest but the other prompts we had were the best. My friends found this game to be extremely funny.DEVILS AND THE DETAILSThis game was probably one of the longest games out of the 5 but it wasn't bad. I think the enjoyment of this game depends on how good your teammates are at teamwork. This game was good but I didn't find it fun for me but my other friends had fun playing this game. (My friends are also bad at teamwork on Among Us)CHAMP'D UPMy personal favorite is this one. Me and my friends played this as our second game and this game was extremely stupid fun. The has you draw characters for a prompt and the other players vote on. When we played for some reason we kept on putting Jeff Bezos against Yugoslavia... I don't remember why.TALKING POINTSWhen I first started playing I thought this game was going to be the worst. Turns out this game is one of my favorites. To sum up this game its kind of a google slides presentation but you don't control what images are on it so you have to connect the image to what your trying to say. For me and my friends the first round was mindless chaos but we got significantly better with time. BLATHER ROUNDThis game is probably my least favorite of all of them. When me and my friends played it we had little idea what was going on. The word prompts that we had to put did nothing to help people guess the word we had. We eventually started describing our word vocally because the text wasn't working. I don't know if we just didn't understand it but we played several games trying to figure it out but with no avail.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, THANK YOU for the native linux support. My System 76 Oryx Pro linux gaming laptop running PoP_OS! thanks you! Second of all, this game is great, just like all the other jackbox party packs. I own all 7, and I think this one just might be my favorite so far. It includes my all time favorite jackbox game quiplash in its 3rd iteration. My family and I always die laughing, and it has become a family tradition. Thanksgiving, Christmas, and other holidays wouldn't be the same at my house without quiplash. The other games are great too, with the new speech game "talking points" being another family hit. Just remember that there are "family friendly" options in the settings.  Even if you don't have a big family around, Jackbox games can be played over a stream for big laughs! If you like party games, this is the ultimate one. If you like jackbox games and don't know which one to get, make it this one! My only (minor) complaint is that some friends and family members wait until the last second with their prompts, and the jackbox service has a bit of minor lag. If the timer says "5 seconds left" you probably realistically have 3 seconds left unless you are running a super new, super nice laptop or android phone with extremely fast wi-fi. Otherwise, play it safe, answer a few seconds early.Best Regards, -PR0XIDIAN

_childDocuments_.review: All of the games in this pack have resulted in the most fun I've had on a game night. Quiplash 3 is a fast paced head to head competition of wit and comedy. The Devils and the Details is a remarkable semi-cooperative experience where you complete tasks by performing quick mini-games. Champed Up is a high energy drawing game that uses creativity, wit, and a little bit of deduction. Also Champed Up has my second favorite Jackbox soundtrack, just barely beaten by Monster Seeking Monster. Talking Points is a massively chaotic improv game. Lastly Blather Round is a calm-ish word association game with pop-culture prompts. This is the first game I've ever pre-ordered, and I have no regrets whatsoever. If you liked any of the previous Party Packs, I can practically guarantee that you will enjoy this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Party Pack 7

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the strongest overall entry into the Jackbox Party Pack series yet. There's a nice balance between creative and thinking games, hectic and chill games, as well as family friendly options for every entry in this pack. Its weakest game is probably The Devils and the Details due to questionable longevity I'll have to see, but still a fun and different entry, there are no noticeably weak games in this pack.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite honestly the best of all the jackbox games, none of the games are lackluster and all of them lead to incredibly funny group dynamics, whereas in other jackbox games there's one or two games you never touch like split the room or bracketeering; this one has none of those and all are a good laugh for different groups and sizes. Champ'd up is like the upgraded TeeKO, Quiplash is great fun and the final round is much more enjoyable, Devils and the Details replaces push the button as the way you get to ♥♥♥♥ with your friends and talking points and blather round are great cooperative games in which you get to chill and come up with the most inane sentences and cluesI love all the jackbox games but this one most of all

_childDocuments_.review: Jackbox 7 is what I would call the single best Jackbox Party Pack released to date. This one is so absurdly fun to play with friends and strangersDevils and the Details is a chaotic stressful mess that shouldn't be fun at all. I mean, who wants to play a game that is about doing chores? Well somehow they made it work. Devils and the Details makes for a loud, chaotic time and is in my opinion the best way to start a gathering with friends.Champ'd Up is an absurdly hilarious game where you create wacky champions to even wackier prompts. You could be told to make a champion for anything from something normal, like "Champion of the Graveyard" to something that literally nobody in their right mind would suggest you do, like "Champion of Orlando". Plus this game's music SLAPS SO HARD.Quiplash 3 is more or less the same as the previous two quiplashes. Only this time you can create your own custom stories, and use custom stories created by the Jackbox team. Also I love the claymation visuals this version takes on.Talking Points is absolutely my favorite game in this pack. There is absolutely NO WAY that a game about public speaking should be as fun as it is. But my god this game is so much fun. Get together with a group of friends who are good at improv and just see how insane the speeches can get. Trust me, this one is insane.Blather Round is the only "bad" game in this pack, and I use bad loosely. On it's own, its not very good. The sentences are too vague and without large teams of people working super closely together it is nearly impossible to get the answers. However, I've still found enjoyment out of this one. Just not as much as the other games in this pack.Overall, I would rate the games in this pack as follows (from favorite to least favorite):- Talking Points- Champ'd Up- Devils and the Details- Quiplash 3- Blather Round

_childDocuments_.review: TDATD - seems like a game better played in person when this is all over. It was just too hectic for my google hangouts session. Champ'd up - Love TKO. Also love this one. Bugged still AFAIK. Keeps freezing on second round when someone doesn't submit because I think the drawings need like another 30 seconds because you have to ALSO come up with a good name. Once they fix the bug itll be one of my most played.Talking point - Have to have a certain type of group. Its pretty much just doing improv like Whos Line is it anyways? or Impractical Jokers(sort of). Have to actually do a presentation not just read the slides. The whole fun is the speakers reaction to the totally unrelated slides. Have to have people willing to actually act. Really fun though.Blather Round - Like reverse 20 questions. Its not a "funny" game but its pretty fun. Quiplash 3 - The normal round prompts are fine and seem like they have more pop culture references now. Im not sure what other people are talking about with this quiplash's last round. It way better than any other last round. For example my last one was "How would you describe yourself in three words?" I answered "Huge".... "Massive".... "Heart". Those popping in slowly in that order was really funny. Its all in the slow reveal. Best quiplash so far IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: Long-time follower of the JackBox Games and I've thoroughly enjoyed each installment. Some more than others, but this one was a slam dunk. This pack brings some of the best features and qualities of previous titles and refines them down to very engaging and well put-together party pack.It's personally my favorite with the level of engagement the games brings to our group, and the replayability for the games included is incredible. _childDocuments_.review: Quiplash 3 is more Quiplash, which I've never liked as much as their other games. This doesn't really add anything new and wasn't very impressive.Devils in the Details is a fake sitcom where everyone has to complete a bunch of tasks fit for their role in the family in order to, say, build a treehouse. It's stupid fun, and the theming helps it a lot.Champ'd Up is Tee-Ko but you're drawing fighters who will be Champion of a Thing. Someone then has to draw a challenger that can beat them, but they don't know what the Thing is. Round 2 adds a second prompt that no one knows until it's revealed and lets you tag in any of your fighters to represent it. One of the best games in Jackbox. Talking Points has you giving a talk based on someone else's title and your assistant's slides, and you're then scored on a debate-style engagement graph. Fun, but might be a hard sell over Patently StupidBlather Round is about guessing a noun from very limited sentences the player is allowed to construct. As guesses come in, the host player can pick ones that are close and do a hot/cold thing to build of off those. Fun, but full of weird bugs right now. It'd be my favorite Jackbox by a mile if Quiplash 3 had been something more interesting, but even as it is I think it's enough to edge out being the best pack. _childDocuments_.review: Jackbox 7. When I first saw the 5 games introduced for it, I was kinda concerned. After all, a drawing battle game, and the chores simulator looked as if they would drag the game down. However, upon playing it, I found that these fears were unfounded, and rather it was just my personal preference of party games.  The list that follows will be my personal opinion regarding the games, ranked in order from my most favorite to least favorite. The games were all tested in a discord call.Talking Points: Upon seeing this trailer, this was the game I wanted to try the most. It's basically like the invention game from Pack 5, combined with the image round from survive the internet. This game requires you to be able to improv so hard, but if you are able to pull it off, you can have people rolling on the ground laughing. The unpredictability behind this game is truly outstanding, as you never know what images or lines you are going to get, which will probably make you collapse from laughter. I believe this game will provide a good time for almost everybody.Blather 'Round: This is a game that I honestly forgot about as soon as it was released. It was just not super interesting looking to me, and I forgot about it almost immediately. Boy what a fool I was. This game is not necessarily a funny game, unless people's guesses become very outlandish. This game essentially has you trying to describe a person,  story, or object using descriptors that are generally vague, but can add onto one another to make it more obvious. This game is an absolute blast. It's absolute bliss trying and failing to figure out the words, because it's so much fun to build off of pre-existing clues. It may be hard if a player does not know much, if any pop culture, but even then, they'll probably have a good time failing.Quiplash 3: It's just quiplash, which should be expected from quiplash 3. The final round gimmick is fun, as you now have to input three answers that doesn't have prompt restrictions, and it's an actual 1v1 duel, rather than the battle royale-esque style of the other two. The ability to make your own packs return, and it even has a featured packs section, which can potentially extend the amount of fun you can have on this game, as you can actively search for new questions, should the vanilla ones get stale. All in all, a great update to a great party game.Champ'd Up: I should clarify that I am absolutely garbage at drawing, so I have a bit of a negative bias against this game. However, the concept behind the battling drawings was executed perfectly. It's kind of like Tee KO and Bracketeering combined. It's a fun game, that wasn't necessarily what I am good at. The use of deception in this game is pretty fun, as it can lead to a person entirely misinterpreting a drawing, and creating something funny, yet completely unrelated. Compared to other drawing games, this one sits directly under Patently Stupid, Drawful, Tee KO, and Bidiots, yet is still much better than Civic Doodle.The Devils and the Details: I didn't go into this one with much hope, as it looked to be overly confusing. It was much more fun than I had initially thought it would be, but because I play entirely on discord, it was nearly impossible to actually communicate on the team-based chores. You are a group of devils who needs to score points to clear a daily quota. You can choose to slack, and get double points, however, this will cause ruin. I believe that this game is very fun, but is 100% probably much better to play in an actual party, rather than over discord. Because the voice quality of discord becomes garbage when multiple people talk, it will become physically impossible to communicate.Overall, I think that this is one of the best party packs that you can buy. Even though I didn't really like Champ'd Up and Devils and Details, I realize that I'm probably in the minority, and understand why those games are fun to other people. Rating this pack alongside the other packs, I would rank them as follows.1<2<5<6<3<4<7

_childDocuments_.review: Party Pack 7 is far and away my favorite Jackbox compilation.  I've spent most of the last two evenings streaming it for a group of friends and acquaintances online, and there hasn't been a single clunker game yet.: good new accessibility options, like options for subtitles for everything or gentler background animations; the lobby screens are also much quieter now and don't have repetitive host barks, which makes waiting around for people to join up less annoying; the separate game moderator role will be nice for letting hosts of public streams play without getting distracted: prompts are better on average than the ones in QL 2 or XL; the safety quips/Schmitty quips aren't automatic gimmes for the other player; Thriplash (a three-line response revealed one line at a time) is finally a satisfying-feeling round 3, and the claymation theme is wonderfully presented: manages to be chaotic without getting too overwhelming or frustrating, even in online voice chat; the minigames are more amusing than we expected and really get across the theme of suburban alienation: a free-form drawing game like Tee K.O., but with less downtime and no possibility of never getting your submissions picked or getting knocked out in the first round and never getting to see your creations again; being able to build a bench of characters over multiple games with the same players creates a lot of hilarious upsets in the tag-team round 2: frankly, we didn't expect anything out of this game and were prepared to write it off as the dud of the pack, but we've spent the most time by far playing it and loving it.  There is something extremely compelling about successfully communicating an obscure idea through vague pre-selected word lists; one player says he now understands why people in the '50s loved Charades so much.  Also, the host is infectiously chipper and the soundtrack and graphic design are strangely relaxing: a nice balance of guided and freeform improv; splitting the speaking and writing roles between two players takes the pressure off both, and even the most reluctant players in my group eventually got into the groove of the game.  The format is really good for setting up instant running jokes and callbacks from other players' presentations, and even the awards ceremony at the end provides the opportunity for one last joke or one-up

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have an immense amount of personal experience with the Jackbox games, but I've watched them plenty, so I know the games, and I think it's fairly safe to say that this is one the the best, if not the best, Jackbox games yet. An overview...Quiplash 3: It's Quiplash, which has always been a staple, but the claymation art style is super-cool.Devils and the Details: I haven't personally played this one with friends yet, but it seems chaotic as all hell (for the better). It lacks the ability to express oneself creatively, as many of the best Jackbox games do, but for a "game-type" selection, it's very well put together, and the task-oriented nature of it kind of reminds me of Among Us?Champ'd Up: A spiritual successor to Tee KO that might be even better. Your enjoyment of this game really comes down to how good your friends are at drawing and how likely they are to draw male genitalia, but the base concept is phenomenal, even though some of the categories can be a bit hard to work with,Talking Points: Easily the most spontaneous of any Jackbox game, the bullsh*t slideshow concept has never been better. Honestly, if you or any of your friends are half-decent at improv, this game is a masterpiece, and even if they're not, watching them try to stumble over completely nonsense pictures and prompts is comedic in itself.Blather 'Round: A relatively clean pop quiz guessing game with a cool style that works well, but isn't nearly as exciting as some of the others on this list.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh god wear to begin, other than this might be the best pack Jackbox has. Of course the entire pack isn't perfect, different groups will like different games, but all the games in this pack are solid at very least. _childDocuments_.review: This is the first time that a party pack was just five straight-up bangers of games. It's excellent.Quiplash 3 is the standard Quiplash... you really, really cannot go wrong with Quiplash. The Thrip-lash in round 3 is a lot better than getting the same comic lashes over and over in Quiplash 2, so that's a plus.Devils in the Details has drawn comparisons to WarioWare from most of the groups I've played it with. It's certainly unique... incomparable to other preexisting Jackbox Games, at the very least. It's hectic and fun; expect a lot of talking over one another. Champ'd Up is, for me, Tee KO but better. Because there's no successive gauntlet, your drawings don't end up getting stale; having your big hit round-one drawing come back just once in the tag teams gives a lot more impact than seeing the same shirt five rounds in a row. Also, playing with 'same players' lets you swap in drawings from the previous round, which is a really sick touch. My only complaint is the latency issues; every time I've played Champ'd Up, at least one player's device struggled to load the voting in a timely manner. I'm sure it'll be patched sooner than later, however.Talking Points is the pinnacle of this pack, and it is a high-soaring one at that. Think of it like Patently Stupid, but with less work on the individual. Patently Stupid requires you to draw, write a title, pick out a slogan, and only then after seven minutes of work do you finally get to present your invention. In Talking Points, you simply provide three titles to the room, choose one of the three you're given, and you're off to the races. If your favorite part of Patently Stupid was presenting your invention, this'll come naturally; it'll also be hilarious.Blather Round is simple; it's like written Charades. You have to describe a topic [which can be anything from something as simple as Minions to something as nonspecific as Creme Brulee] to the room through using text prompts. These prompts are designed to be as vague as possible; I've seen things as pop-culture reliant as Rick and Morty be described as "a show about a not good evil humor guy" and "wow, familial much?" If you have the right group, this one can be an absolute banger of a game.I reiterate the point I made after my first session of Jackbox 7; This is the first party pack where, with every group I've played with, every single game is a hit.

name: Rain on Your Parade
detailed_description: Rain on Your Parade is a comedy game where you play as a mean cloud determined to ruin everybody's day. Play across a wide range of levels while unlocking new abilities and mechanics that get progressively more ridiculous. It's a mix of puzzle and adventure, a unique blend between Untitled Goose Game, Donut County and Katamari! Travel across the world, inventing new ways of causing chaos and mayhem. Turn the perfectly dry and sunny wedding day into a wet one, unleash thunder and lightning upon the cities, bring pandemonium to supermarket shoppers, destroy farmer’s crops, sneak around military bases and rain down meteors on dinosaurs! Yes, not even the dinosaurs are safe! As you progress in the game you will unlock new and more comical methods of causing bedlam. Use thunder and lightning to scare people out of hiding and set things alight, tornadoes to suck up everything that gets in its path, rain explosive material that you can blow up and even entire meteors and much more. Ruin peoples day with rain, thunder, lightning, tornadoes and many more abilities. Travel the world in over 50 levels causing disorder and havoc to weddings, cities, farms, military bases, parking lots and much more. Give the mischievous cloud your personal touches. Draw a unique face and choose the hat it wears. An upbeat and silly soundtrack that encapsulates the nature of the game. If you're a fan of Untitled Goose Game or Donut County , this will be right up your alley!

_childDocuments_.review: It's goofy, it's charming, and it doesn't overstay its welcome.
