_childDocuments_.review: This is a super cute and amusing game! Based on what I've seen so far, the total play time is approximately 5-6 hours.:- Cute graphics.- Lots of amusing pop culture references.- Easy to play, while still providing a challenge in some areas.- Various ways of customizing your character, and adding more amusement to the game.:- The game seems to be geared towards using a Controller, and I wish it was easier to use with a keyboard. It needs keyboard customization, at the very least. For the most part, there are on screen instructions telling you what keys to use to do things, especially in the Game Menus.There is also one major con I have to talk about, especially if you are prone to motion sickness, as I am. There is a side area that is 100% optional, and the play style is completely different. In the interest of avoiding spoilers, I won't give too much detail, but it's played in 1st person perspective, as a throw back to an old 90s game. I appreciate the pop culture reference and creativity, but it left me with intense motion sickness and an awful headache. (Especially frustrating as I was playing it live on Twitch, and ended up closing my stream early because it made me feel sick.)If you are prone to motion sickness, and you want to avoid it, just don't interact with the "Arcade Machine" that shows up in your home area.Edit: The developers contacted me in response to this review, and have changed the WASD controls so that you can strafe, instead of rotating the camera. You can still rotate with the arrow keys, as well. I haven't done a full test, and using a combo of both WASD and the Arrow Keys can be a little awkward, but it helps. And I especially appreciate the developers willingness to hear the feedback and make changes!!

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, my favourite genre. Cloud gaming.What a beautiful day, sun shines, birds fly, grass grows and brother, I soak people. I’m a force of nature!Yes it looks goofy, but I like goofy.It's a great game with a very simple purpose that it executes very well. It's a blast to play and just as fun to watch being played as well since it's such a simple concept. It just gets more and more enjoyable as you go further into the game. It's just so clever and fun. They do so much more with the concept than I expected. My wife, my wife’s boyfriend, daughter and even myself had a blast with it.It’ll always have a special place for me now because it was the first game my daughter played with me. She was only 2 but she could recognise when she had to press the 'green button' to make it rain if it was over the right targets (I was moving the stick of course). If the devs see this review, thanks!It’s not overly challenging in any way but it’s just some good chill fun. The humour and references are also great throughout. The Dunder Mifflin levels were my personal highlights. There's a mix of "oh I get it" referential humor & actual set up pay off jokes, which is nice. It's a little short, but it also has replayability in the form of a new game + mode with additional objectives for each of the levels.  For me, it's great for a giggle, good humored and varied 'puzzles' that are easy enough for the young gamer, with lots of nods and references that you wouldn't expect (like the office, or scary hospital levels, etc). It has that nice 'I'm having fun and will do just one more level before logging off' gameplay.It's a good time and definitely something you should check out if you’re remotely interested. I'd recommend this game when you don't want to think and want to unwind and have a few laughs. For being so simple I enjoyed this more in the 10 hours I played it than some of the AAA games this year, so take that as you may.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Rain on Your Parade is one of those games that catch your eye as soon as you encounter it. I don’t think there are many, if any, games that feature a cloud as a protagonist. It manages to be more than just a unique visual experience though. The game takes some relatively simple upfront mechanics and expands upon them in creative ways to make a fun, but fairly short, light puzzle experience. Abbreviated Review: The entire story of Rain on Your Parade is initiated as a bedtime story from a grandfather to his grandson. It’s very “Princess Bride-like” and has a few silly moments, but is mostly just a way to set up the experience. The isometric view and tilt-shifted camera focus create a perspective that everything is just the toys from that kid’s room. The people are all made of yarn and the cloud you control is a cardboard cutout suspended from strings. It makes things seem much more “cute,” which is probably a good thing since you’re destroying the environments with natural disasters at every turn.The visual aspects of the game are family-friendly, but it doesn’t keep the violence of cloud-related shenanigans looking pretty decent in most cases. Nothing that will blow anyone away – especially in some of the forest areas – but with plenty of fun physics aspects, it ends up being an entertaining style. They even manage to change up the typically bright styling from time to time with things like a black and white level and even a totally unexpected first-person shooter level.Early on, Rain on Your Parade seems like it might be a little limited in design. There’s a good bit of “get everyone soaked” that is reused in a few different ways. However, it expands significantly beyond the first third of the game. As you start to unlock more powers like lightning, snow, and a physics-flinging tornado, the gameplay shifts to more problem solving with some basic puzzles. Then, out of nowhere, it will throw entirely different mechanics at you.For instance, there might be a one-off level where you’ll be using the tornado skill to fling balls down a lane for a somewhat nuanced bowling game. Another has you defending an area for as long as you can from invaders using all of your skills to knock down their umbrellas and put out the torches they use to melt your slippery snow patches. I was especially entertained by a time where I used my tornado to drag around a ‘black hole’ that grew as it sucked in bigger objects. This essentially made what felt like Katamari Damacy – one of my favorite games.While I wouldn’t call Rain on Your Parade “hard” by any means, it was great to see the variety of challenges that it presented across the 50 levels. Even though some of those experiments ended up kind of disappointing. In particular, the stealth levels. I’ve always had a vendetta against non-stealth games trying to implement stealth mechanics because they always feel subpar. Stealth requires precision and lots of information being passed to the player and the handful of levels here don’t have that at all.Overall, Rain on Your Parade does a lot of things right. It’s very functional and easy to pick up while offering a fairly broad selection of things to do across its relatively short run time. It helps that the game has a “new game+” mode that allows you to do old levels again with additional challenges unique to each one. Aside from those stealth portions, they’re all quite fun as well.The one area that feels occasionally worse than it could be is the sound department. Some of the voices are a bit awkward and, given how limited they are, could have benefited from any decent voice actor. Also, the music that exists in the game is fine, but it gets a little repetitive. Outside of these minor issues though, Rain on Your Parade is a great indie game that shines with its originality even through the clouds that you’ve brought to the party.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Very cute game with an interesting premise. Unfortunately, it isn't quite worth the $14.99USD they're asking. I'd be a "maybe" at $10, and a "yes" at $5. Also, the first half of the game is boring and only gets good in the second half.The game is clearly a labour of love, and there's a lot of charm in the design and aesthetic. But I felt like some of the writing was trying too hard to be funny. It would have benefited from being toned down and a bit more subtle. The references in the game illustrates the difference between "too obvious" vs "perfect subtlety". The reference to Frogger is "too obvious" with the frog hammering it in your head. He not only mentions that he had to cross streets while cars ran him over, which is fine. But then he goes on to say he used to be the star in this popular videogame back in the day. In contrast, the "make the office worker spill his pot of chilli" objective would have been perfect subtlety. But then it went into "too obvious" territory when they named the level "The Office".For both jokes and references, it's okay for the audience to miss the joke or miss the reference. People who miss things won't realize they've missed anything. So they have no negative emotions associated with the experience. But it's "not okay" to squeeze out every last drop from a joke/reference. When you do that, the audience will initially "get it", but then get bored with it. They'll remember the overall experience as being a negative.The early game also drags on a bit too long. The first three levels just have you rain on people to annoy them, and already at that point I was wondering "is this it? Is the whole game just going to be this?" By the late game, things pick up though, with new mechanics being introduced at a brisk pace. This keep the gameplay feeling fresh.Based on the dialogue from the 50th level, you can imagine what happened here. The devs were tasked with making 50 levels, and so they set out to make 50 levels involving raining on people. After making levels based around the exact same mechanic, they quickly realized that this leads to a very boring game. Then they made the Counter Strike level and realized that the key would be to vary up the mechanics somehow. They started brainstorming, and came up with the thunder and snow abilities. They made a few more levels around that but ran into a rut there too. They started thinking more broadly, and figured tornados might also be associated with clouds. This mechanic was a bit more flexible, and they managed to get some more levels out of that. Finally, they hit the 50 level milestone (or perhaps they hit the 49th level milestone and decided to end it with a meta-level -- it's unclear how literally we should take the dialogue from the 50th level). They then rushed the game out the door.I don't know if the above story is true, but it certain fits with the way that the game felt very same-ish up until they suddenly realize they can make the cloud do something other than rain.Again, I'm not sure how seriously we can take the dialog from the 50th level. But it feels like the game would have improved if they took a break from the game for a week or two. Then, after their minds were fresh, they should have played through the game from start to finish, with a critical eye for what levels to cut. That final curation step was what was sorely missing from an otherwise charming game.

_childDocuments_.review: "Rain on Your Parade" is a whimsical and charming game that invites players to wreak havoc as a mischievous cloud on a mission to rain on everyone's parade. While the game boasts an abundance of creativity and interactivity, some mechanics veer into gimmicky territory, like the "doom section," which might dampen the experience for some players.One of the game's standout features is its interactivity. From soaking unsuspecting pedestrians to dousing fires and ruining picnics, the possibilities for mayhem are endless. The ability to pair different abilities adds another layer of fun, allowing players to combine rain with other elements to create chaotic combinations.However, the game occasionally falters with gimmicky mechanics, such as the "doom section," which feels forced and disrupts the flow of gameplay. These segments may detract from the overall enjoyment, especially for players seeking a more seamless experience.Despite these minor drawbacks, "Rain on Your Parade" shines with its imaginative premise and engaging gameplay. Whether you're causing havoc in bustling cities or wreaking havoc in serene countryside settings, there's plenty of fun to be had as you unleash your inner storm cloud.In conclusion, "Rain on Your Parade" offers a delightful storm of creativity and interactivity, albeit with a few bumpy clouds along the way. If you can overlook the occasional gimmicky mechanic, you're in for a rainy day of chaotic fun.

_childDocuments_.review: 10h 6/10 1,5 Yes, you can find a nice written guide  and a video guide . Some tips might not be working anymore since the developer fixed the bugs with achievements. No No No Yes No No No difficulty option NoIn this very enjoyable game, you play as a cloud, which goes out on its way to ruin people's day. you'll start the game with only the rain ability, later in your adventure, you'll unlock thunder, snow, and a tornado ability to ruin people's lives in even more ways. The game is very funny and has a lot of references to other games and other popular things. I had a blast playing through the game. Some of the achievements were kind of bugged during the first days of the release. You could get the achievements where you have to beat a specific level within time and without getting hit in a very easy way, but that wasn't the way the developer intended those achievements. They have been fixed and that increases the difficulty quite a bit. For the achievements, you can first just play through the game and you only have to complete the main objectives. You'll unlock most of the achievements in new game+, which isn't the right name for this mode since you don't have to start over from scratch. You keep your progress but the levels got extra challenges, and some of those will unlock an achievement. A few of those achievements can be really challenging. For the achievement "Infiltrator Master" I needed loads and loads of tries before I was able to get it. Another challenging one is "Gravity Gun" but that one isn't so hard as "infiltrator Master". For those two I've made a youtube video on how to unlock them for those that struggle with them as well. You can find them in the guide section on steam. Overall a very enjoyable game and doable achievements. I most like how original this game felt and the humor in it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cute, simple, and somewhat challenging but not too challenging of a puzzle game, this is probably for you. I always compare the gameplay to the price I ended up paying for it. I’d say it’s accurately priced for $10-15. When I got home from work, I was totally exhausted and ready to fall asleep. I picked this up for a few minutes and still didn’t put it down until I played a few levels. All the levels seem to have about a 5-10 minute play time, so it won’t tie you up too long unless you have to replay a level. I like that it’s objective based and not really time based. So you can just shut your brain off while you figure out how to complete each goal. Overall, I’m excited to continue playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: Rain on Your Parade is a really chaotic puzzle game in the vein of Untitled Goose Game or Katamari, and it's a good one. The main objectives in each level are all really straightforward; good for breezing through if you're looking for some chill fun. What's really great about the game though are some of the secret objectives, and the post game extra objectives. Almost all of the extra objectives have some neat puzzle with a creative solution where figuring them out feels like a real light bulb moment. This game is adorable, it's fun, and it's no pressure at all. Totally worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: This game fits the definition of 'cozy chill chaos'. You play as a chaotic rain cloud, destined to rain on people, and maybe even other liquids. Tasked with various challenges, you use your power of weather to cause chaos wherever you go. This game is filled with references and memes to current game culture, and definitely a game you can relax to, as it's not too taxing on the brain with some fun achievements you can get along the way. I recommend it if you're looking for something chill to play but are a chaos gremlin where a game gives you full permission to Rain On Your Parade!
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: - Cute art style. The characters are reminiscent of Paper Mario- The music is fine, but forgettable- The story is very bare-bones, but it isn't really the focus of the game anyway- Very casual vibes. Easy to pick up and put down thanks to the puzzle game adjacent level style- The game has a good sense of humor and doesn't take itself too seriously. There's fun references (some overt and some more subtle) to other games throughout- I wouldn't really call this a puzzle game. You just hover around and complete objectives, some of which are pretty amusing- The quality of the levels is highly variable. They run the gamut from easy to hard and boring to fun. For the most part, they're pretty middling- There's an NG+, but I mostly just went after the achievements. I might get the DLC at a later point, though, if it gets cheap enough- The game ran like a charm on the Steam Deck- It's a decent little game, but it feels too short for the price. You could complete the main story in 2-3 hours, and there's another few hours to be had in picking up the NG+ achievements, but it's not a whole lot of bang for your buck- . It's an okay game. I'll recommend it since it's Steam Deck verified, but wait for a sale if this looks appealing to you

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game for playing with kids - my 5 year old loves it.Its a cute little-big planet like graphics game. There are lots of games/levels that feel sandbox like and it has some fun puzzle scenarios - reminds me a lot of DONUT COUNTRYGiving it a 8/10I feel that the music was a bit generic and there is sometimes a fair bit of dialogue that likely whomever is playing does not care about - the argument that might be made that "kids are meant to follow the story" but the problem is - there is a fair bit of humor that will be lost on kids at that age..so it will just seem like non-sense sometimes.Second downside is you really want to play it with a controller to enjoy it - I feel that more of a simple mouse interface might have been more enjoyable.Of course its a fairly short title but totally worth the price and your kids might just want to goof around in it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been gaming for 37 years, it's always very refreshing to come across something that isn't so copy paste. Having been a developer (and still doing so), an artist, worked in an office, been bullied, have been using the term hoomans and have moved to the mythical Seattle myself -- I almost swear the developers have been stalking me.I bought the game shortly before the end of my work day and started to play it thinking, okay -- I'll tinker with it and go eat. Yeah, didn't make it out to eat before I made it to the "You Beat the Game Edition".The game has been wonderfully done and does so many variations on play style it never got boring. The artwork is pretty neat and all the various tasks you can do in the levels or out on the world map. You might even say that the game has 51 levels because of the things you can do out on the world map. I won't lie, I thought it was short and I wanted more, but I am far from disappointed from my experience.A couple things to note though, while they do recommend a controller, I did things on the keyboard just fine -- I even painted a poop emoji that looks halfway decent.I don't want to go back to retail eitherAnd sorry Dane, I couldn't help myself. That joke was amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: 11/10 Ruined kid's birthday party WITH FIRE, marched zombies across a city, and pet a dogIf that's not enough to make you buy it, then FINE, let me give "rEaL" reasons.This is a really unique and cute game unlike any other that I've really played. Each level, you play as a cloud with a variety of cloud powers to solve puzzles, do weird tasks, or cause mayhem. Some levels are super intricate, following a "story" (Like the definitely "not" Legend of Zelda level), and can take quite a bit. Others are much quicker, or just for fun, like painting or raining down hands to pet a dog. (No seriously, there is a point where you rain hands to pet a dog. It's amazing.)It's also LOADED with references to other popular media, there's a whole level centered around The Office, a Legend of Zelda adventure, Louise's hat from Bob's Burgers, a Wolfenstein/Doom style arcade level, and I'm pretty sure the level "Quiet Little Mountain Town" is a reference to South Park. There's tons more that probably went over my head, but either way, they were all super fun to experience!As a side note before I forget, the game recommends you use a controller to play, and while I didn't try it with a keyboard, it does feel very natural with a controller!I happened upon a demo for this game out of boredom, and I'm so glad I did. I've only played for five hours, but it feels like I've gotten so much more out of it, and there's NG+ objectives now! So that's pretty dope. There's really only a few things I would change if I could, and that's if I'm being a picky Karen:-Add player "profiles", I want to share with my siblings, and we could always library share, but it'd still be a nice feature. :) (Okay, maybe this comes from a place of "I drew a phallic symbol on my cloud's face and I don't want to explain it to my little sister")-Maybe an easier difficulty for youngins? I'm thinking of my little sister, who would probably LOVE this game. But some levels are challenging (Which is a good thing, I appreciated the challenge!), and seeing as how the playful silliness of this could attract a younger audience, maybe adding in an easier difficulty would make it better for them. -When you start NG+, it'd be nice to see all the hidden objectives as well! Or maybe hints to get the hidden decor items in the level selection map. Maybe this happens after you finish NG+, but I don't see why it would, but if it did, I'll come edit this out. I just reached NG+ myself, which is awesome btw!Anyway, all in all, it's a super fun game. I'd definitely recommend it to anyone looking for just silly fun. You get to play as an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cloud that goes around terrorizing people and causing mass destruction, what more could you ask for? :)

_childDocuments_.review: Sick of the rain ruining your perfect day? Embrace the rain. Become the rain.If you want to see gameplay and watch my first impressions as they happened, click on my video. Rain on Your Parade launches you into the troposphere with the powers of the cloud. No, not remote data storage. An actual cloud. Your obvious power is to rain down on the unsuspecting people below, but you can also absorb liquid vapor, and temperature and other forces will grant you additional powers.... but that's taking this game too seriously. Rain on Your Parade is all about relaxing with a fun romp across more levels than you'd expect. Choose your cloud's color, draw its face, and add a hat or accessory. Or don't. It's cool. No pressure.The world map has a lot going on too, foreshadowing the game's variety. One particular easter egg on the world map had me in stitches with laughter. If you enjoy a novel experience or are looking for a game to unwind with, consider Rain on Your Parade.

_childDocuments_.review: So cute cozy game all that, can be funny and fun to play at times.It is a game for kids, I don't think adult people who played games for most of their lives would get much out of this game.What I found unacceptable are quality of life features or lack of them to be precise. The camera angle is fixed so you can't see the corners or sometimes you can't see where the thing you are trying to avoid is coming from, humans will get stuck in some corners and you will not be able to see them. There is a large life bar in the right side of the screen and that makes the camera problem even bigger. There are no accessibility options or any basic PC options. To restart the level you have to select end level and then press retry after you got booed for pressing 2 buttons too many, what is wrong with pressing R to restart I really don't get it. There is however a report a bug option every time you select a menu so I have a bug to report - this is a console game that has no accessibility options, no basic PC options and awful fixed camera.The game is ok like I said but get this in a bundle (like I did) or on a deep sale because it is really not worth the full price.EDIT : You can't rebind your keys....well surprise surprise.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh how a lovely day can be ruined by something as simple, and essential as water.  And oh how sweet it is to be a cloud with no silver linings, only liquid daggers raining down on the citizens of Seattle.The question is, should YOU play Rain on Your Parade?  I recommend it. From the differing levels and well-executed references, to the charming creatures, to the sometimes meta but always clever cosmetics, Cloudy’s world is filled to the brim and flowing over with charming features and moments that will keep you laughing for hours.Check out my 7 minute review here:

_childDocuments_.review: From: Imalwaystired.blogThere will only be a handful of people that will believe this (and ultimately say this), thank God for Twitter. I believe Twitter is a decent enough institution to allow indie developers to be able to advertise their game in a decent manner. This is how I came across Last Man Sitting and this week's game...I just wanted to play a simple, easy game this week.This week I evaporate and take the form of a cloud and ruin so many people's days while low key saving the world from a LYRICAL GENIUS. This week I played Rain on Your Parade.Rain on Your Parade is a comedic adventure game brought to you by Unbound Creations. The game released on April 15th, is available on Xbox, PC and the Switch and retails for $15.Cloudy only exists because of a bedtime story. The story starts out one with adventure and what it means to be nice, then it becomes a haphazard tale of a cloud trying to save the world from a cloud hating scientist. Dr. Dryspell is the ultimate evil and he will not quit until Cloudy is no more.Cloudy can utilize rain, lightning and snow throughout the entirety of the game. Levels instruct you to rain on people or to stop fire from spreading, use lightning to usher people out from underneath their safe havens and snow to trip up those not paying attention.There are objectives that need to be met and then you move on to the next level. Most of the time the objectives are incredibly easy to achieve and require basically zero thought. For example, there is a level that is literally a rip off of a Counter Strike map and the only objective is to stop the enemy from disarming the bomb.  I played a series of levels based solely off of The Office, I went on a quest that was almost a total rip off of a Zelda game, I played Counter Strike, partook in a few movie inspired levels, ETC.Aside from your basic levels, there are leaderboard levels that you can rack up a bunch of points to be at the top (not me though baby, I'm trash).The game announces somewhere around the middle that you can't really hurt these people because A. they are made of yarn and B. it would shoot the rating up and that was never going to be an option, so what I am trying to say is that the game looks good when it wants to but on closer inspection, it looks like poop. Humans have dots for eyes and mouths (?). Humans are only discernible because there is really nothing else on screen at the same time. Music is good enough that I remember some melodies even though I haven't played the game in a few days.You can openly customize the face of our favorite cloud. I designed mine to look tired because I am, in fact, always tired. Upon completing levels, customization rewards are given out.Rain on your parade is a game by a group of people that wants its players to just have fun, that is very clear but it does get boring at points. Challenge is non-existent, but that is not necessarily a bad thing (it is just for me). It is a really accessible game; perfect for all ages. My wife played it and had a blast, even though she only played a few levels. The humor is really good and it strikes some nerves that some people may not appreciate.Rain on your Parade is a fun game made by fun and creative people and it really shows.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's cut to the chase: Is the game worth $14.99 usd? No. Not without some local co-op at the very least...I would also suggest the developer mind the fire-making mechanics; I found myself having to re-saturate areas that were connected and should've lit. Having to back-track breaks from the immersion of this otherwise mesmerizing game. The camera perspective takes some getting used to and there's no option to adjust it. However, there's no denying the aesthetic and even comedic value of the game. I'll be requesting a refund and will wait until these things are fixed, as I enjoy the experience of the game, but I can't recommend it at $14.99. Not without a multiplayer option and some bug fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: Rain on Your Parade is a charming and creative title that pleasantly surprised me, especially given my typical disinterest in parody or physics-based games. The game thrives on its lighthearted humor, which is accessible to players of all ages, and its inventive level design.With 50 levels to explore, the variety is one of the game’s strongest suits. Each level introduces a fresh gameplay twist or challenge, ensuring the experience rarely feels repetitive. Of course, not all levels are equally enjoyable, but with such a wide selection, there’s enough to keep most players entertained. The humor and whimsical tone provide an added layer of enjoyment that complements the gameplay nicely.For those curious about the game, Rain on Your Parade is a safe bet for a fun and engaging experience. It may not revolutionize the genre, but it’s an admirable effort that showcases the developers’ creativity and sense of humor. I’m eager to see what they come up with next, as this game sets a solid foundation for their future projects.

_childDocuments_.review: A very silly and funny physics based weather simulator.  Full of warmth, humour and mischief, the charming hand-made cartoony art style, hijinks and randomness of the levels makes for a fun time, even if the game is simple and very easy.  Although a simple concept, there’s enough variety in the game mechanics and the references to other video games and witty characters make it quite entertaining.  Great music, good graphics and of fair length with additional challenges to complete after the main game, but it would have been nice to be able to see all of the bonus objectives and collectibles post-campaign and had a few more parody levels.

_childDocuments_.review: If there's one type of game I absolutely adore, its a genre I call "Making Chaos". Games like Katamari Damacy and Donut County.Rain on your parade definitely is great to cause chaos, and the further you get in the game, the more ways there are to make chaos. There are 4 weather effects you can do: Rain, which gets people wet, nothing too exciting there; Lightning, which zaps people, sets stuff on fire, you know, the usual; Snow, which makes some really fun chaos adding slipperyness to cauase people to fall over, cars to skid out of control and a bunch of fun chaos; and finally the Tornado which is just insane, in almost katamari like fashion sucking up everything in reach, except the moment you stop tornadoing everything goes flying. Absolutely bonkers.The game gets even better with new game + adding additional challenges to each level allowing you to take your tornadoes and snow and whatnot back to the earlier levels and cause more chaos.There are a bunch of pop culture references, and some of the levels are homages to completely different game styles like Zelda, Metal Gear Solid, and Gradius. Bizzarrely there's even COMMENTARY you can enable in new game plus which lets the team talk about the different levels and thought they put into the game.10/10 experience IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. Each level is unique, although most are a bit simple. This game is perfect for when you want something chill and colorful just to relax and have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. I played the demo of this game when they released it during the indie thing on steam earlier this year. I loved it, immediately put it on my wishlist, and got it this Christmas. This is my review.This game is without a doubt in my mind, one of the best indie games I've ever played. It is lighthearted fun mixed with absolute chaos. That is the only way I can describe it. The amount of fun I had playing this game cannot be beat.Now onto some basics:Is this game long? No. I beat the entire thing under 5 hours. Granted, I laughed the entire way through.Is it replayable? Absolutely, and it has game+, which makes it more challenging for those who like a challenge. They are also releasing DLC as well as free updates here and there.The artstyle is so unique and cute, with little hand drawn pictures animated on top of cardboard textures, with little strings attached to your cloud, yarn people (which also got turn into a joke as to why its okay that you're striking people down with lighting, turning them into snowmen, whipping them up in a tornado, etc;), it is the absolute cutest. All in all, I loved every second of playing this game, which is why I'm recommending it, muchless taking the time to review it. The amount of easter eggs, references, memes, as well as shade thrown to the gaming industry (I'm looking at you, microtransactions), added to the experience of how fun this game truly is.I literally just cannot get over how fun this game was. Honestly. I cannot. I am going to keep playing, but I really just wanted to review it as soon as I reached the ending. The final level of this game, too? Absolute chef's kiss. That's all I'm saying. Other's might not like it, but I absolutely loved it. Also, you can quite literally customize your cloud in this game with the amount of freedom I haven't seen in a long time. You can draw to have any face you want. Want to have private parts as a face? Go for it! Want to have no face at all? That's good too! Wanna have Cloud hair on your Cloud with a rich anime face? That's great too! You do you boo! You draw it, you got it. That's CRAZY! Final verdict: Absolute 10/10. Thank you for making this game, and thank you to whoever fully reads my review.Please give this game the love it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: So having finished the main game, I still have lots of secrets to find in New Game + (which, I'm quite surprised there's New Game + for this game!) but am well-played enough to say that this is a fun, charming, humble and hilarious little game, and I definitely recommend it. It did take me about 2 and a half hours playtime to finish the story, so in terms of length it's hard to say the price tag is worth it, but much like Journey it's much more a matter of quality here. All the little details, the quality of writing and the variety in the game definitely makes it worth it. It's also very clear the creators had massive fun and a huge amount of creative exploration while making this. It's never too hard, but never boring because of the powers you get and the way different levels mix things up. The art styles really adorable, and the inclusion of some chill gal-less levels and customisation really set a nice mood. If you like puzzles over combat and want a game more about making you feel good and giving you a chuckle, I really recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

I was praying they wouldn't have too many time based missions or other variables that would lose focus on the fun and relaxation part. Good news- very relaxing and fun game. _childDocuments_.review: this game is ADORABLE! every last bit of it is dripping with self-aware flavor. the storyline is cute and each of the 50* levels gives a unique experience from plain raining on people stealth to tower defense to impeccably done references. bought it at full price and i'm very happy with my purchase 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

One minute you're raining on a wedding, then before you know it you're .  Hats off to the devs on that.  It was fun from start to finish and never got stale.  9/10

"Rain on Your Parade" is the rainbow in the indie sky, and let me tell you, this game is off the charts! 🌈🌧️This game hits my funny bone just right! 😂 Who hasn't dreamt of being a cloud and ruining the day of unsuspecting humans? 🌧️ Whether it's crashing weddings or raining out a soccer game, the missions are diverse and ingeniously designed. 🎊⚽I've played it through once and I swear, I can't wait to 100% this game! 🏆🎮 And if there's a sequel or an expansion in the works out there, just take my money, please! 💸💸The visuals are an ode to all the cardboard lovers out there! 📦 It's like living inside a child's drawing—full of color, fun, and imagination! 🌈🖍️"Rain on Your Parade" is a downpour of good vibes, a cloudburst of creativity, and a tidal wave of fun! 🌧️🎉 If there has ever been the ultimate "schadenfreude simulator," it's this one right here! 😈☔Rating: 5/5 Stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ – An Indie Masterpiece that Shouldn't Be Missing from Any Collection! 🏆🎮Yours,Sonsch | Rainmaker and Indie Enthusiast 🌧️🎮💕

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully wholesome and charming game, with gameplay varying from fun for kids to New Game+ that'll challenge adults, and full of references that my generation will enjoy. Definitely good for if you want something to relax, have a good laugh and not worry about pressure to win.I give it a rating of "Ambient Music Video That Gently Lulls You To Sleep" Out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: Rain on Your Parade is little bit of everything and it rarely overstays its welcome. You play as a cloud and it starts simple. You simply rain on people. Eventually you'll get more loosely cloud related powers so you can cause even more mayhem. Yes, there's even a tornado power, though that's the last one to unlock, so be patient. With the new powers, earlier levels might be lot easier. But don't worry, there's new game plus mode that gives you additional objectives. At that point you can also play the levels in any order you want, so you can just have fun.While lot of it is pure mayhem, there's puzzle elements in several levels, especially with some of the optional objectives. Don't worry about causing mayhem as people are made out of yarn (there's also few other excuses in the game, but I won't spoil them here). There's lot of variation within the 50 levels, so there's no time to get bored.In overall, difficultly varies during the levels quite lot. Easiest ones are for example one where the objective is pet the dog and harder ones are usually Dr. Dryspell ones where you get shot at. The first person shooter is maybe the hardest one so far as it's quite long and you have to start from the beginning if you die. That one is totally optional though.If you're unsure if you will like the game, try the demo. Demo content is pretty much in sync with the full game (which has downside that you have to play the same levels again in the full game). If you're a completionist, there will lot of content even after you have finished the game.  If you're player that likes to rush through everything in order to see the end credits, it might be good to wait for a sale. For everybody else, it's totally worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: Cloudy the Cloud is my new soulmate. What starts off as a gentle game where you just kindly patter a few tiny drops of water onto people's head, soon it is bursting with chaos and clever quips!Like I said during my playthrough: This game is my spirit animal. I love the witty little nudges at everything and the throwbacks to old games and memes. Go get it today, you won't regret it! P.S. Can we get more levels? This game needs MORE!!!! MORE I SAY!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: ... can we all hold a moment of silence for Dr. Dryspells' wife? Rain on your Parade is a brilliant puzzle mayhem game that will bombard you with puns on every occasion. It has 50 creative levels that will keep you entertained for hours with great replay value. Even your grumpiest friend will laugh himself off a chair when he gets to unleash a tornado of pigeons on an unsuspecting crowd.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fun and charming! I was instantly sold on the premise and loved it as soon as I started playing. While most of the levels (that I've played so far) boil down to "rain on all the humans," it throws in some levels with different objectives that help to spice it up and keep it interesting. The writing is cute and has great humor as well! Solid game all around, I wish I had a cloud friend that could rain on my enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: A cute puzzle game with a lot of humor and easter eggs. I enjoyed playing it and I'm not done yet, but half way through. It's a good mix of puzzles, bosses, minigames, you can create your own cloud. It's definetly not a game if you are looking for deep story or challenging gameplay, but it has some leaderboards if you like to beat records, the puzzles are getting harder, the jokes are on point. It has different types of modes and some secrets in your cloud house to, can only recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: I love games like Untitled Goose Game and Katamari where you can mess around in large sandbox areas to fun music with silly objectives. This game scratched the exact itch I was having and I'm honestly shocked at the price after how many levels the game offers (along with a NG+ if that's your thing). The game played pretty well save for a few bugs, but overall the customization, extra modes, and humor made this game a joy and I'm sure I'll come back for it again someday now that I've finished it. It was surprisingly difficult in some sections to get all of the challenges, but other than a few turret battles, I never found myself getting frustrated. Overall, 10/10. Highly recommend and totally worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quirky and fun and there are always new situations, new references, and funny events that get me laughing. It's highly entertaining. 10/10 do recommend. My only negative is that it's quite short for the price. I can probably get about a half day's play out of it if I go through the game without taking my sweet time.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game and the dev's sense of humor. The metal gear solid level and a few other magical points took me back to my childhood. Was great to just have a fun game, instead of something so competitive. Reminded me of my fun on Goat Simulator and a few other games that are actual games at their core.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a sheer delight. It takes a goofy premise and runs with it, and the result is a rollicking fun time the whole way. The conceit is a grandfather telling their grandchild a bedtime story about a cloud. You play as Cloudy the cloud, having all kinds of adventures and getting up to all kinds of mischief. The game is not shy about mixing things up with game modes using the powers you unlock, either! I've raised a horde of zombies and ravaged a city, played a JRPG, and gone bowling. It's chock full of references to other games, too, from Metal Gear Solid to Kamari Daimacy to Doom. This is a game that retains all the humor and charm of a bunch of kids playing make-believe, and I love it.It also backs up this humor with some actually decent puzzles. Nothing I've encountered has been  difficult, but I've certainly been challenged to perform my objectives with what I have. As you progress you'll unlock various weather-based powers (in addition to your starting rain) which can interact with things in interesting ways. I don't know how long the game is, but I haven't finished yet after 3 hours and hope it continues for a few more. All in all I can heartily recommend this gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast! This was a light and fun game, and had a variety of objectives and game-play styles. It didn't even take me 30 minutes of playing to recommend it to a few friends for silly adventures. This isn't very complex, but delightful in the easy controls. There's even new game + additional goals, which adds some replay to this, and is super quick to pick up again if you come back for the new material later. Absolutely worth it for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: The story starts as a fairytale. A father tells his son the bedtime storyabout a little cloud that spoiled the party for anyone. Literally, as we see soon. We are thown in the first level and wet all humans to complete it. And that’s not it: Every level is designed different and often, more than one challenge needs to be completed. We water the field crop, we extinguish fire and sometimes we are a well-behaved cloud and pour some hot coffee. Over people, cups, and the floor. The additional tasks unlock cosmetic items like hats, if completed. Further into the game our possibilities to disturb the peace in towns, woods and villages become more diverse. The gameplay is constantly changing between Puzzler, Platformer and back to Flying Simulator due to the variable tasks. The ultimate goal is cloudys personal paradise where she can rain at will. The single levels all base on different ideas. Some are shorter, some require a whole story that needs to be followed. Short films, quests, boss battles make the little cloud fly, thunder and rain. Sometimes you need to avoid laser guns, sometimes just pet a dog. The creativity we are encountering is never boring. The scenarios are brought to us by cute side characters. And every level has little easter eggs, the most obvious is a human with a I❤️Cloud-sign. Every text is stuffed with references and some self-mockery. At the end of each level, we get stars that are shown in the overlay, or points that rank on a highscore. And if we failed or just want more, we can re-enter the level. The humor is a central part of the puzzler. Developer Unbound Creations never failed to make us smile. We are heading to numerous missions that make us grin with schadenfreude. They are all embedded in the telling of our father who pushes the plot further. For example, he installs a villain that is laughing diabolically and rhyming terribly. His levels are more of a challenge towards the end, because enemies need to be taken out strategically without cloud being spotted or caught. The level of difficulty is increasing but remains moderate. We needed to repeat some levels, because we didn’t read the task properly, and the little icons were not very helpful.We never lose track during chaotic situations thanks to an inclined top-down perspective and clear visuals. Sometimes, we experienced frame-rate drops, but the overall performance was stable. The soundtrack is really peppy, the sound effects are on point and we enjoyed our 5 hour long trip with cloudy & friends. Full recommendation to all lovers of mischievous games with colorful visuals and a bit of puzzling. See more Indiegames in my curator group:
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, calming, and unique game. Didn't think being a cloud ruining everyone's day would be so much fun.Edit: Just finished the game and I really enjoyed it! Would definitely recommend. I understand it took a long time to make the game, but overall this was a pretty short playthrough. It's about 4 hours long (with losing some levels/replaying a few). After completing the story, you can replay it again with added objectives or adding the sun for a challenge, just in case anyone wanted to know.
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: I love LOVE games that have rain in them and what better way than to play as a cloud full of it~ Such a cute game! I love the bits of humor scattered around the levels so far. You can tell a lot of passion and love went into this as there's some creativity scattered around so your not just raining water on people, plus I love the references to other classic games! I couldn't help but find myself smiling every now and then, ruining other people's day with my happy cloud :D
_childDocuments_.name: Rain on Your Parade

_childDocuments_.review: Travel the world as a cute cardboard cloud and ruin everybody's day! Unlock new methods of mischief across 50 levels, each with unique setting and objectives. Make new friends and help them too - it's an adorable schadenfreude game. Travel across the world, inventing new ways of causing chaos and mayhem. Turn the perfectly dry and sunny wedding day into a wet one, unleash thunder and lightning upon the cities, bring pandemonium to supermarket shoppers, destroy farmer’s crops, sneak around military bases and rain down meteors on dinosaurs! Yes, not even the dinosaurs are safe! As you progress in the game you will unlock new and more comical methods of causing bedlam. Use thunder and lightning to scare people out of hiding and set things alight, tornados to suck up everything that gets in its path, rain explosive material that you can blow up and even entire meteors and much more.

name: Spirit of the North
detailed_description: SPIRIT OF THE NORTH 2 IS COMING! About the Game [url] Spirit of the North is a single-player 3rd-person adventure game inspired by the breathtaking and mysterious landscapes of Iceland. The story takes root from various pieces of Nordic folklore. Play as an ordinary red fox whose story becomes entwined with the guardian of the Northern Lights, a magical spirit fox. As you journey over the mountains and under red-stained skies, you’ll discover more about your companion and land left in ruin. Uniquely designed to purposefully have no dialog or narration. Players must breathe in their surroundings to solve various puzzles and speculate the meaning of a lost ancient civilization. 'touching & memorable' - GamingBolt '[...] a journey well worth taking' - TechRaptor Key Features: - Make your way across stunning landscapes, on an emotionally stirring journey. - Solve environmental puzzles to change the world around you, using ancient powers bestowed upon you by the guardian of the Northern Lights. - Follow the mysterious Spirit Fox across a land left in ruin as you discover more about a lost civilization. - Moving orchestral soundtrack featuring 14 original compositions.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't say enough about this game! The game's story is told in such a simple, beautiful, heartfelt way that the lack of any reading or dialogue intensifies. The graphics are truly stunning and the controls (I used a controller) are very easy.I would recommend this game a million times over to anyone who enjoys figuring out puzzles (that aren't so hard you're hitting your head against a wall) uncovering hidden lore and to anyone who wants a change from the usual 2 legged characters!The only negative I have about this game is that I didn't want it to end!Anyways! I'm off to look into the mythology behind this game and get some therapy for becoming far FAR to emotionally invested in a little ball of light than any sane person should!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very beautiful. I will say these aren't the types of games I usually play however it was nice to play it with the different fox species as well. Overall the game was nice, but for me personally who prefers some action it was a little boring at the same time. But I recommend it because of the lovely visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A different type of game. There are no bosses, items, maps, health, etc. Just a nice little adventure wherein you control a fox, and are guided through a barren world that was clearly inhabited at some point. The music is somber and calm, the gameplay is open ended and free, and the controls are very bad at times (lol).This is definitely a "hang out" game, and considering the price I would recommend it. Also, the credits alert you to the fact that this was the first game by the creators, and they did an admirable job!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game! For the frenchies out there who play on keyboard, you have to switch your keyboard to english to play. The controls work fine after that. You won't find the most complicated puzzles to solve but it is a truly relaxing game who will take you on a trip. And for someone who traveled to Iceland before, i immediately felt the ambiance coming back. 6h well spent !
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I was enthralled with the absolutely breathtaking visuals in this game. Running around as a fox exploring and solving puzzles. Achievement hunting was a bit challenging, but not terrible. Without spoiling anything, I love all the interactions with the spirit fox, and how you really can look through the eyes of a fox in terms of how you play. I was always looking for vantage points, and climbing anything I could. The excited fox yips and running around with what's essentially a giant stick in your mouth is comical. The lore was interesting, and very close to nature. I did almost as much hopping in this game as running. Cannot wait for the second game to come out, really looking forward to a closer look at the lore and the universe that you're presented with in the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game. It's a beautiful game with lovely music and visuals. I love the fox. But, unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game. There are too many bugs and crashes. I finally, after a really long time and finally having to look up a tutorial, finished a hard part in chapter 3, and I finally got through it but the game crashed before it saved so I had to redo it. Finally got through that, but in an early part of chapter 4 there's a bug that won't let me progress. I was willing to keep playing despite how often the game crashed, but I literally can't progress now. The cut scene happens where a door should open, but the door doesn't open. A beautiful game, I just wish it had been executed better. Really disappointed I can't continue playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It is beautiful, peaceful and a tiny bit of a mind-teaser, but nothing too stressful. A great game to relax and enjoy the scenery. At each level when you freed the spirits, you are unlocking skins and can't enjoy new fur colors. Also while playing a fox(which is absolutely adorable), you don't have to deal with dialogues. A real breather compared to other games.100% enjoying it so far. (reached chapter 4)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very beautiful, the graphics were very pleasing to the eye and the soundtrack made this play-through feel dreamy. Not a single word was spoken in this game, yet the story was very intriguing and continued to draw me in through to the end. I never imagined myself growing attached to a computer generated fox but here we are, overall this game was very nice to play and i'd definitely recommend to anyone looking for a cosy game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The game in all is really cute and fun, I remember getting it because all the people I knew were saying it was awesome.I don't fully agree, I would've loved, maybe, some subtitles for our main character (the fox), its thoughts basically, I get that the game is about an animal, but most things made very little sense to me.I was probably just looking too much into it-Other than that, the game is really fun, and different from most games I have played.The main idea of being able to warp into a 'ghostly' fox is fairly fascinating to me.The abilities of our main character is also pretty neat.I recommend the game for a quick, but relaxing (usually XD) playthrough, fun and easy!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really nice, fairly linear but there is space to explore. My biggest annoyance with the game is twice I've been locked from progressing. On both occasions a set of doors are locked and you need to power up a stone to open them but because the stone had already been powered up earlier then you are effectively locked in. The only way to progress is to restart the entire chapter from the beginning. It needs to be fixed such that if the doors are locked then the stone is powered down so as players don't get stuck
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I would not recommend this game. Gameplay is very straightforward - you pick up power from blue flowers that are scattered around and put the power into something, which allows you to progress a little further. My biggest gripe with the gameplay is simply that the game is constantly stopping the action for brief moments. Every time you interact with the flowers, you've got to wait a couple seconds. When you deposit the power into an object, the game takes control away and shows you what was affected. I found it to be maddening because this is essentially the only gameplay mechanic in the game.In terms of story, this game seems to have taken the "show, don't tell" idea. However, the actual storytelling feels half baked. In the beginning of the game, the fox goes from fine to on death's door in like two seconds flat and you're left to figure out that there's an aura of some kind that is dangerous. The rest of the story is similar, where I end up saying "well I guess I kinda understand what's going on" but I would have liked this part of the game to be more fleshed out.Technically and visually, the game is mediocre. It's a fairly generic UE4 game and I'm sure that a number of the game's assets are taken from the asset store. This isn't a problem in and of itself, but it means that there's not really a coherent art style going on. The game seems to max out at 60 FPS - will not go higher. The menus are some of the worst I've seen - in order to select a 4k resolution in the settings menu it made me go through all of the lower resolutions and it changed to that resolution each time. So I ended up swapping through like 30 resolutions to get to the one I wanted.If you can get this for a deep, deep discount or in a bundle it's not the worst way to spend a few hours. But I wouldn't recommend it for anywhere close to full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the few life-changing experiences I've had. A stunning environment, a beautiful score, a compelling story told purely through the landscapes and the path you trek. I've replayed it multiple times. And with Spirit of the North 2 coming out soon, and the game being on sale, there's never been a better time to experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game with a beautiful story—one that I almost wish I could forget just so that I could experience it again. The art and design are breathtaking without requiring intense resource usage or top-of-the-line hardware. The gameplay is straightforward, the puzzles are moderately challenging, and the story flows so smoothly that it is difficult to tell precisely when it stole your heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a nice story, the puzzles are pretty easy.I like the whole idea of the game and its simple mechanics.However, there are some mistakes in the gameplay. Basically, you can easily break the flow of the game by playing it in just a little different way than it is expected — for example by doing things in unexpected order or by trying to enter to places where you shouldn't be yet. Speaking of which the colliders doesn't work well at all. Sometimes you can simply get stucked in a rock or you can walk through a wall.The graphics might feels kinda old in some parts. Epecially in the first chapter. On the other hand, some parts it has a great atmosphere, I love the visual of chapter 7.Overall, the game is nice, really chill and for whatever reason I felt a sense of nostalgia when I played it. It is worth the money and I recommend it to everyone who is looking for something relaxing to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is filled to the brim with vivid colors and a lush landscape. I felt connected to the Fox the entire time and yet, while there is not a single piece of dialogue in the game, the amazing soundtrack helped tell the story. The puzzles were not too difficult, managing to not stick around each area for too long except for a small amount of collectibles along the way. The platforming felt fun and intuitive (most of the time) except for a few small instances where if you're too close to an object while jumping, you'll sometimes bounce back and have to get back to where you were; not sure if it's a slight oversight or a camera issue, but did not burden my experience. If you enjoy similar games, such as flower, Abzû, The Unfinished Swan, Brothers, Journey, or RiME, then Spirit of the North will be right for you and you can finish the story within a few hours.Rating: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, real talk. It's fun, this is definitely true, but it is so FRUSTRATING at the same time. I am not one for jump puzzles because the jump mechanic is different in every game for sensitivity. This game has a lot of jump puzzles. Another thing that's pretty frustrating is the game doesn't actually tell you what the goal is? I learned through watching walkthroughs that the point is to set shaman spirits free and to eradicate darkness. Cool. But it'd be nice if that was actually told to you in game? I missed a lot of shaman spirits thanks to that. I would have liked this game more if it wasn't as frustrating as it is, both with gameplay and goals. It's fine if you like puzzles and you're all about that 100% completion, but I was really hoping for a relaxing game where I could wag my fox tail and explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful game with a fantastic soundtrack and breathtaking scenery. It took me roughly 6hrs to complete the game and that was going around checking out everything and looking for Shamans. Even though its not as long as I'd hope, I thoroughly enjoyed it and would play again gladly. I recommend the game while its on sale !
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Some inklings of a good game here and there, but the execution falls a bit flat.All puzzles involve barking at a flower to charge yourself with spirit energy - but if you move after barking it doesn't work and then you have to move away and come back to try again. Then you find the thing you need to use the spirit energy on. Repeat until the doorway to the next area opens. In between these puzzles there are a lot of overly long stretches of... nothing. Just holding forward as mostly unremarkable scenery passes by.The controls and camera are also especially wonky, which makes platforming more annoying than challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best game experiences I've ever had. The gameplay, the ambience (!), the overall feeling. Everything about this game is just wonderful!Though it is clearly dedicated to those who seek the experience, not the challenge. This is at least the impression I got. The experience of the game comes from exploring, solving riddles and letting the atmosphere of the game itself flow through you. And I seriously mean that. The surroundings you can explore within the game are just breathtaking. Which is ironic since normally you'd take many deep breaths in those surroundings because you can physically see how fresh the air must be there. You can also make the game to a challenge by hunting collectibles and archivements as major priority. But I really do not recommend that because you then tend to lose track of the wholesomeness of the game. At one point I was tempted to just hunt down all the collectibles as fast as I could, searched every corner and half an hour later I realized that I completely forgot to also savor the moment and atmosphere that I was in. I regretted this so much that I restarted the chapter I was playing. And it was worth it. Because this game is about the experience. You can seek challenge elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

I will say some of the "puzzles" are a bit confusing due to the fact that you are given so much freedom and limited direction, but overall so far I'm really enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I went in thinking I'd like this but, honestly, the game just failed to hook me. It looks reasonably good and the storytelling - as much of it as I saw until the first puzzle of chapter 3 - was nice, but gameplay felt rather weak; the traversing felt not only a bit too slow especially in the snow but also rather confusing as to where I was supposed to go since the spirit disappeared out of sight rather often for me. Maybe the game would have picked up if I kept going but after half an hour I was just bored, so I figured it was for the best to cut my losses and refund. Too bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Same as every other negative review: I wanted to like this game. It's got a cute fox, beautiful landscapes to explore, magnificent music.. it could almost be a kind of Zelda game with puzzles. Unfortunately it feels unpolished and janky with platforming/edges. In the huge maps, specifically Chapter 7 it is so easy to get lost, there is no direction, I almost couldn't finish it. A lot of running around in empty spaces looking for what the hell you're supposed to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a game quite akin to something like Dear Esther or Journey or What Remains of Edith Finch – this is to say your time with the game will largely be made up of you walking. A lot. However, where Spirit of the North differs from the aforementioned “walking sims” is that you’re not playing as a human, but rather a fox. (Well, a fox imbued with magical properties and powers, but a fox nonetheless.) And you’re not walking, but running. It’s an interesting enough setup, although the game itself is rather sparse on variety once things get going.Much of the game will have you running around and exploring its many beautiful settings: some are craggy cliffs overlooking majestic blue pools; others are dilapidated ruins bathed in a monstrous red glow; some are snowy caves hiding mystic secrets. Yet all are equally gorgeous to run through and explore to your heart’s content. Spirit of the North is fairly minimal in almost every aspect, but the game’s graphics, art direction, and overall presentation are anything but. This is one of those “screenshot everything” games, where just about any frame could become a desktop wallpaper, and it’s clear the developers put a great deal of time and effort into the game’s breathtaking visuals.If you’re in the mood for a short but sentimental jaunt through some gorgeous Scandinavian scenery with a twist of magical mysticism, take a run at Spirit of the North.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it was a very pleasant day of running around as a fox.+ Fox.+ Tail wag button.+ Beautiful scenery. + Neat puzzles. Nothing incredibly complicated, and feels nice to solve.+ The spirit tries to guide you to the correct path occasionally, looks pretty.+ Story is mostly environmental, nothing to read, just a couple picture murals.+ Sliding down icy slopes is fun.+ No fall damage. Pretty sure nothing except scripted events will hurt you. - Sometimes you slide off the edges.- Sometimes you do not slide off the edges when you should. Had to restart chapter parts on three separate occasions, due to parkouring the fox where it really should not have been yet and locking the puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: I *really* wanted to like this game. It's beautiful, the story is interesting, and you get to play as an animal. It reminded me a lot of Okami in a lot of ways, which is my favourite game ever made, so great! Unfortunately, there are some *glaring* issues that I simply cannot get over, and believe me I have tried, because like I said, I really wanted to like this game.The issues in question are 1: the game is nowhere *near* clear enough where the ♥♥♥♥ you're supposed to go. The only times the Sprite actually guides you are when it's blatantly obvious where you need to be going, but in sections where it's not clear, it does nothing; not even a hint of an indication where you're supposed to go or what you're supposed to do next.And 2: This game controls like utter *garbage*, I swear QWOP controls better than this game does in spots because the fox is so *unbelievably* floaty. I lost count the amount of times I had to repeat entire sections because the fox either jumped too far, not far enough, slipped off an edge for no reason, hit an invisible wall, or turned/jumped in the complete opposite direction it was told turn/jump in.None of this is helped by the fact the game operates on an auto-save function, and the checkpoints are not exactly close together.This is *really* unfortunate, because it is a stunning and compelling game otherwise, but the focus in a game like this should be on the story and the breathtaking visuals, and I am simply unable to enjoy those things because the gameplay is so God-awful.If anyone is looking for a game that has similar vibes but actually indicates where you're supposed to go and *doesn't* control like you're trying to play using only your ass, then might I suggest Okami?
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a short well now since I finished this game and completed all the achievements, but it still lives rent free in my head. This game is my favourite example of something that both looks and feels like a 'cosy' game, but handles so much more than that. It's challenging in all the right ways without being frustrating while also being calming - a game you can let yourself get absorbed into for hours at a time and just... be a fox. There's something really charming about games where you play as an animal, and this one does it well. Combined with the lack of dialogue and yet a story still told so well. This is up really high on my list of 'niche' game faves! Very much looking forward to the second one! ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this game was a struggle to play. I enjoyed the concept, and I'm really excited to see what they do with the second game but the mechanics for this one are a struggle. The fox bugs in random places, the auto-save doesn't work very well, either. I had to re-do a bunch of puzzles between gaming sessions. I usually like to complete my games with 100% of the achievements, but since this one is so annoying with the mechanics, I decided to leave it unfinish. Again, the concept is great but the execution could've been better and I hope they fix a bit of those issues for the second game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Were the controls a bit janky at times? Yes. Was the camera also a bit janky at times? Also yes. Would some form of map have been helpful? Also also yes. Did any of that detract from my enjoyment of the game? Definitely not! What a gorgeous journey, coupled with a gorgeous soundtrack and gorgeous graphics! Definitely worth a playthrough if you're in the mood for a pretty relaxing game with puzzle elements. Will definitely play the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: In all, I loved my experience being a fox. A lot. Puzzle games are a favourite of mine, and I can say with honesty that I only felt the urge to look up a let's play once in the whole experience, and it was because of my own stubbornness in trying to make a jump that was not intended. Usually, there are a couple times where I look up how to finish a task that I just can't figure out. But not this game. I didn't look it up in the end. There comes a feeling of satisfaction from succeeding that this game utilises expertly.It's a little beta-y in that sometimes I jump into a wall or through a rock, or I can't make a jump unless I land in the exact place that was intended. But that really doesn't matter in the large scheme of things. It is different to my usual games, in that it has no text or dialogue, whatsoever. Sure, there are pictographs, but no words. It really, really made a difference to my gameplay style. For one, I did a LOT more exploring, taking in the scenery with some deliberate elongated pauses to enjoy the atmosphere and view (never know when you'll miss that all-important stick!). For another, I think text might actually have detracted from the atmosphere and story. Also: the music. Fits perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a relaxing game at the least. The soft music that is played, makes it even more chill to play.The reason you'd play, this game is maybe not per se for the story (which to be honestly I didn't get completely so I had to research a lil'bit) or the puzzles (who're easy), but because you play as a fox. Which was the selling point for me hahahaa.Though it's all cute and fun with it's ambient music, it got dragged out a little bit at the end. I'm talking about chapter 7 with the endless walking. This is obviously a walking game, but meanwhile you search for staffs and monks (I think) while solving small puzzles. In chapter 7 you get to enjoy a very very very veeeery long walk, which was kinda tiresome. What would have been nice to see more in the game would be other animals.  It would have been lovely to be able to interact with other animals, but one can not complain.I would recommend playing this game to get out of everything, but not if you're looking for an adventure packed with interaction. This game is simply not that. Fun and relaxing, but a little bit lonesome.
