_childDocuments_.review: This game is way too clunky with unintuitive puzzles, terrible parkour, and random elements for me to be bothered with it more than an hour or so at a time, hence this review. I really want to like this game, the graphics are absolutely gorgeous, the fox is adorable, and I don't mind the lack of an obvious story as I feel exploring the world is the focal point, but the puzzles...I want to be clear that the core concept of the puzzles is fine. Use your powers on this or that thing to open up areas and solve puzzles to progress. Except it felt as if the creators thought up cool abilities first and puzzles second, most of them feeling thrown into the world in areas that usually don't seem that important. There are clever ones here and there, but they will mostly suck up your time because the items needed blend so well into the environment. As for the clever uses, such as , they're pretty good on the surface. Except, are never properly introduced and you'll find yourself looking for the usual pillars only to realize that yet another item has been thrown into the mix without much thought or explanation. For hours you will find yourself running in circles of mostly stone filled environments with the spirit rarely helping you and, even when it does, in ways that are so cryptic they just leave you scratching your head. I've had it lead me to areas or more of puzzles I was supposed to work up to, making me waste several minutes there only to realize the next solution was actually elsewhere. Like great, I think I could summarize the end goal was to make this glowing thing glow more, as is literally the game loop. At least start me off somewhere more relevant to beginning the process instead? The spirit is completely useless and just bogs down the gameplay in my opinion, there should have been a command to ask it for help when you were stuck, it would have made a lot of the puzzles go so much smoother and be worth giving more of a go. As is, as a character it feels nonexistent and very bland, giving us nothing of the cute, possible friendship between it and the living fox hinted at in the first chapter.I also think its worth mentioning some of these puzzles require you to jump around the environment in ways that feel unnatural and that I myself as a player would have never guessed unless I looked it up. . It doesn't help that several surfaces have an invisible wall almost that will smack you off and make it seem impossible to land on unless you do it in a specific or terribly janky way (such as jumping off of the air, and no, this is not one of your abilities). Several times I had to back up because if you're too close to a ledge the fox will freak out and end up turning you away from it (aka the invisible wall thing). So many times I was completely knocked off surfaces and had to climb up all over again because my character was behaving strangely. Chapter four really highlights all my issues with the game and, being only halfway done that just doesn't bode well enough for me to be that dedicated to finish it or continue quite frankly.The lack of story, or an obvious story at least, ends up being glaringly obvious because as one's frustration builds they realize they are doing this all for essentially..nothing. Its not like you get new story beats every time you complete an area, or learn anymore about the cute spirit fox, you just get thrown into another one with more puzzles you have to dredge through again. Can be nice to have something to do with your hands for a while and running around is a good excuse to see all the cool environments and graphics, but ultimately I think the creators needed to take a step back to imbue this project with more purpose. Not to mention much more clever introductions to the potentially good puzzle mechanics. There are so many throw away mechanics it makes it impossible to predict what it wants you to do next.Chapter four part four introduces so many things without explanation it about gave me a headache. Not only are there  These combined caused me to run around the area aimlessly until I  It took everything bad with previous sections and made it so much worse.So, while this is an extremely promising start for indie developers, and I would recommend keeping an eye on the creators for future projects, I can't recommend this game specifically. It is far too frustrating to be worth it, and there are better puzzle and exploration games out there that won't make you want to pull your hair out.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Lovely music. The controls can be a little wonky at times, but overall a decent game. Chapter 7 is a mind numbing, patience crushing spirit hunt that would have been much easier if the game had a simple counter to let you know how many spirits you had or had left. _childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally like puzzle games, but Spirit of the North is one of my all-time favourites. The atmosphere of the game is incredible - it's visually stunning, the soundtrack fits perfectly and I really enjoyed the subtle but complex storytelling. It definitely suits the simpler gameplay, which I found relaxing but still interesting enough to keep me invested. It's definitely one of those games where you need to stop and look at stuff, both to uncover hidden clues and to appreciate how pretty everything is! Plus, foxes are cute :)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: this game is very cute. the music is good and the animations are lovely. but that's about where it stops being enjoyable. the controls are wonky and the swimming is the slowest, most infuriating part. every time you mis-angle yourself even slightly, you fall into water and you have to move painstakingly slow to get back to where you were before. it's also incredibly easy to get lost and have no idea where you're supposed to go. spirit of the north boils down to: collect flowers. use flowers. collect some more flowers. after raging at it for seven hours i honestly don't think i'd recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Got this as part of a bundle with Bramble: The Mountain King, which was an excellent game by the way, this not so much. I did enjoy looking at the environment, very pretty and peaceful, mostly. Unfortunately this game slowly chipped away at a positive review, even now it's borderline. First off the flower mechanic is annoying, I should be able to run through them to recharge instead of having to stop bark, wait for the spirit, then make sure I walk through. It just completely slows down the pace of the game, which is essentially a running simulator. They also managed to make going in a straight line confusing. There was many times where it was very unclear how to move forward, to the point where I had to check a walk-through. Also, unless I am missing something it seems like it only saves at the beginning of the chapter, since whenever I try to quit it says 'all progress this chapter will be lost'. Some people complained about the controls, and they could be a little better, especially while in air, but I thought they were fine for the most part.Lastly the world doesn't feel cohesive, as there many symbols and imagery everywhere that you can interact with but it feels unimportant and symbols don't make sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The world, the music, the mood and atmosphere. This is a beautiful game. The puzzles are not hard by any means, but one did throw me off as its trigger point was further back than I realised. It manages to tell a story without any words or character facial expressions. That said I want to learn more about it all and I'm looking forwards to what the follow up will bring to us. I streamed this and was quite surprised I was making decent progress without it feeling too quick.

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect game to chill on lazy evenings. Despite encountering invisible walls it tempts with beautiful views and the illusion of freedom. New mechanics appear at the point, although they do not go beyond the genre classics. A very pleasant solution is the introduction of segmentation, which allows you to go back to a stage and complete the tasks missing from the achievement. A short interactive story. _childDocuments_.review: Very pretty but incredibly frustrating game. I made it to chapter three where you have to jump platforms until reaching a column with red inscriptions and a statue of a fox. Then made the long jump to the platform that is supposed to take you to a plateau on the left. The fox didn't want to jump this part. Every time I ended up on the ledge underneath and in the water. _childDocuments_.review: I am currently on my third play through of this beautiful game. The soundtrack, setting and visuals are brilliant. This game has turned into my chill game to relax and as a fox fan, borking and bouncing about is pretty fun.I do recommend this game. It is short but still has a lot of content and some interesting little puzzles. My only negative on Spirit of the North is the controls are clunky and you get stuck on invisible walls a bit. The platforming can be a little annoying with the clunkiness. However, this doesn't take anything away from the beauty of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: So, sometimes you'll get lost. There's no map, no objective markers, nothing that really tells you where you need to go or what you need to do. It's a little rough around the edges, some elements of the background lore don't quite make sense and there's a lot of things that go unexplained. Trying to find all of the collectables is like finding several needles in a whole barn full of hay - oh, and the fox barks like dog, but...Who cares?Spirit of the North is such a lovingly crafted game. It's clear that so much time and effort has gone into creating the world we explore. The soundtrack is so beautiful, I've got several songs from it on my favourites playlist on Spotify. As long as you don't mind; getting lost, having to look up Youtube videos, sometimes getting stuck, or playing a game that could do with a little polish, then you'll enjoy it. Obviously, if you prefer a fast-paced PvP, Spirit of the North isn't going to be for you. The only thing I have to compare it to is Stray because the concept (wandering around as an animal) is similar and Stray wasn't very long either, although that's pretty much where the similarities end. However, if you enjoy casual exploration, playing fetch, puzzle solving and Foxin' around, then although it's short, this could be the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: IMO, 4/5.TL;DR:Graphics, 4/5 Good; could be better.Gameplay/Story: 3.5/5. A few times I found myself wondering where to go or what to do and you will find yourself relying on your eyes and retracing your steps a lot. At least, I did. The story itself is slow to unfold but the game overall is pretty relaxing.Controls: Easy but sometimes laggy, Jumping is picky in tight spots.In Depth:Graphic are good but could be better. Seams are obvious in many places and some textures are low quality for the meshes they're stretching over. Overall good though. Controls are straightforward but there's some lag in the response for the controls (On my machine, using controller could be the issue. Controller is easier on my wrists.). The jumping can be... finicky in tight places. The story is mostly told by sheer observation, no subtitles, no narration. Most of your conclusions about the storyline are drawn from murals in game. A few times I found myself wandering around and wondering what I was supposed to do especially when I got to chapter 7 as there's an achievement you can obtain but finding all 28 required spirits is darn near impossible with no way to track them unless you just explore every nook and cranny. (Yeah, it's only for an achievment though.) I found myself backtracking a lot but the game is overall very pretty and the music is relaxing, if a bit repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is not a game that will appeal to everyone. As a part puzzle game, platformer, and walking simulator, there is little high-octane gameplay. Those that wish for an exciting game might therefore find themselves bored. If I could describe this game in one word, it would be atmospheric. Walking the beautiful natural landscape of mythicised Iceland is in my opinion where this game is at its best. Frequently, I found myself pausing to take in the view - a rare event in modern gaming where everything needs to be immediate action. The soundtrack of this game is nothing short of superb. Other than an occasional jarring music track change when entering a new zone, the music was faultless. When the game was dramatic, there was powerful dramatic music. When the game was ethereal, so was the music. Alongside brilliant music, the graphics were also fantastic. There was some jank in cutscenes and when traversing jumping sections but nevertheless this is a good-looking game.Gameplay is where this game is less strong. There are some puzzles, but they are typically rather easy. Also relatively easy was the jumping sections. Whilst reviews indicate that some struggled with this, if you come from a civilisation that has discovered fire and no longer treats illness with bloodletting, you will be fine. As you play you will learn a few abilities. They are cool if not that original and allows for some fun jumping puzzles. Some exploration is allowed- incentive provided by the achievements of activating 8 different ancient murals and finding all 28 Shaman Spirits- but the linear nature of all but one chapter makes any exploration limited. It also lacks replayability although you can select a particular completed chapter to play from the main menu if you have a section, you really enjoyed.Whilst there is a story, it is barely explained. You can somewhat piece it together through context clues and ancient inscriptions, but it is not at all a focus of the game. This did not bother me but if you want a good story, you will be disappointed.Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone that wishes to have a slower experience that encourages you to pause and take in the surroundings. Enjoyment comes from being immersed in the beautifully crafted environment whilst listening to the amazing soundtrack. By no means is this a perfect game and it will frustrate you at times but, much like the local crackhoe down the street, for a small price you will have a pleasurable, immersive, and relatively bug free 4-5 hour experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended. The pacing of the "story" is atrociously slow and dragged out, there's very little gameplay beyond navigating the obtusely cumbersome controls and solving a very similar iteration of the same puzzle over and over again, and you're only able to save once you complete each chapter, forcing you to commit yourself to 20-30 mins of gameplay at a time, by which point you might have fallen asleep anyway.As someone who is a huge fan of both exploration games set in nature and the fantasy genre, this completely unrestrained and over the top blend of Arctic scenery and fictional lore tied up in a walking sim should theoretically appeal to me, but it's done in such a mind-bogglingly uninteresting way that I almost think it should be studied. Not recommended, even on sale. 2/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game (not 100% completion).  Very beautiful and atmospheric, with creative story-telling.  The soundtrack complements the visuals wonderfully, making this a more laid-back, contemplative experience.  There are minor platforming and puzzle challenges to vary up game play.  You even gain new abilities that open up and change how you can approach things.  The levels are well-designed, and the fact you can easily climb rocky/uneven terrain encourages players to explore. However, the encouragement of exploration does make this game's use of invisible walls feel a bit jarring at times.  There will be times when it seems like there is no good reason why you can't continue going in a certain direction.  All-in-all though, this is a minor nit-pick.Also, it should be noted that how much you get from the game (especially in the way of story) will largely be dependent on how you play.  If you approach this with a straight-forward "Get from 'Point A' to 'Point B'" mindset, there is a very good chance that you'll miss a good chunk of the story, as it is not force-fed to you.  However, if you come into this game ready and willing to take your time exploring and look at the clues given, it will greatly enhance your experience.For myself, I can quite confidently (and strongly) recommend SotN.  However, I can concede that if you're not already a fan of games of this style, one should at least prepare themselves for a unique and beautiful experience.  The ending alone makes it all worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful beautiful game. At first I didn't know what to expect from the game, but I very quickly got attached to my little fox character, and the rest is history.This game is stunning all the way around. Amazing soundtrack, beautiful landscape design, simple yet intriguing story line, and control mechanics that are very easy and simple to understand. I bought this game on sale at half price, and even though it is a short game, it was worth every penny and then some.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, and went straight up near the top of my favorites list. But it's not for everyone.This game is a puzzle game, with extremely beautiful landscapes, and you play as a fox. Finding the "collectibles" (it's not really collecting, but it functions the same) rewards you with different coat colors, and at higher levels, they come with new light patterns and more. (Which means getting the achievements is actually worth more than just completion.)The beginning of the game is more walking simulator than puzzle. If you are too tense, this game will either relax or frustrate you horribly. Patience is key. But the landscapes are beautiful. And the places in which the game forces you to a crawl (you are injured/sick), it's a way to force you to think on the story elements.The game encourages you to explore and really look around at your environment, rewarding you with collectibles (and nice views).But the game has no dialogue, and aside from your companion spirit sometimes pointing in the general direction of your next task, you don't get any direction at all. There is no dialogue, and no text. Some people, like me, will love this lack of direction. Some will hate that, and get frustrated.Most of the time, when you get a new spirit ability, the game will introduce you slowly to more complicated ways to use it. Though there is one spot in particular where it almost immediately requires you to creatively combine powers with little to no indication that things work that way. (This only happened once for me.)While others have described the controls as "clunky", I don't think they are. The fox you play as feels very realistic, and while he? does not have the instant response that most action games favor, I never had trouble controlling him. Only in fringe cases did I have any difficulty - when I was far from the normal area intended to be used, and I managed to fall in a bit of terrain that was both slippery (because I wasn't supposed to be there) and also blocked off by geometry. Or I got on top of an object with weird geometry and the hitbox wasn't sure which angle to use. (Still way, way less buggy than Skyrim. I'm surprised how few I've come across seeing as this was developed by three people.)Replayability, once you get all the "collectibles", is unfortunately low. It is still a wonderful walking simulator, and the fox's idle animations are absolutely adorable. But that is the case with all puzzle games like this - once you know how to solve the puzzles, they don't challenge you anymore.If I were to give a suggestion to the devs, I'd say let the player with a completed save file go through all the chapters again with all the powers they get at the end. Let them change between spirit fox and normal fox, and let them loose on the beautiful landscapes as a reward for completing the game.As a whole, I'd give this game a 9.5/10 - almost perfect, and a great way to relax when everything else seems hectic.

_childDocuments_.review: if this game is in your backlog, leave it there, if you didn't buy it yet, don't even do itit's a cute looking game with good music, but that's it. Game-loop is outright boring, with "puzzles" as dull as they get, the controls feel clunky and you have to do some platforming throughout the game. The chapters are like 30 minutes tops in length and I remember that I couldn't stand playing for more than a chapter per session.The sounds, besides the music, are poor to say the least, and the graphics, even being the best part of the game, aren't that special. The game looks like an asset dump.The story is a no for me as well. I love indie games in general, and I tend to like the stories, but this one is as plain as one can be. That isn't that bad considering this game stars a "regular" fox, but I feel some may say that this aspect is the best of the game. That's the most subjective aspect here, but for me it's a meh at best.I hate not being favourable with my review here, but I have literally nothing good to say about this game. Even for free I wouldn't recommend for you to spend your time with this.

_childDocuments_.review: The environments are gorgeous, the fox and it's animations look good, and the atmosphere in the game is amazing throughout the whole thing. I find myself coming back to it every now and then just to run around and chill in the open fields. The game does have a good amount of issues though, most of them minor enough that they can be easily overlooked if you go in not expecting a perfect game. If you like Journey-like games, this might be for you. Some levels can be a bit hard to navigate and one near the end is basically just a large forest that you have to wander through near-aimlessly until you eventually find where you're supposed to be. The puzzles aren't really that interesting, and can mostly be boiled down to two types: carry object from point A to B (most of these being optional unless you're going for achievements) and interact with specific points in an area to activate a way forward. It can get quite repetitive by the end. The game also has quite a few bugs, most of them very minor things related to movement and the different abilities the fox gets along it's journey. There was one big one that nearly soft-locked my entire playthrough though: the little blue spirit that always follows the player around sometimes moves to certain spots on its own to show you things to interact with, well, my spirit companion decided to just... stay at one of these locations, and would not move no matter what I tried to do, and I couldn't progress the level because I needed it to follow me for a puzzle. This happened at least twice in my playthrough, both times I had to restart from the very start of the level/chapter because just going back to the previous checkpoint wasn't enough and would only cause it to happen again.

_childDocuments_.review: Got a chance to play Spirit of the North that focuses on a fox that a player controls, as well as a spirit female fox that guides the player through beautiful landscapes of a mysterious world with gorgeous graphics and vistas. The story or more rather the premise of the game reminded me a bit of the game Submerged which I played and reviewed a couple of months back. The story takes place in a mysterious world that has been ravaged by some sort of a cataclysm wiping out its population, as we travel through the world we discover more details about this world and the said cataclysm, and try to help the world heal from the aftermath of it. Almost all of the story of the game is revealed through stone murals, some of which are presented to the player as a part of the story, and some that are hidden throughout the world/chapters.The game play itself is pretty basic, you travel through the linear world (divided into different chapters), learn more about the world, and gain more powers as you progress further through the game. The game doesn't have any enemies or combat so it could be described as one of those "chill" games that focus more on story, explorations, and puzzles. The puzzles themselves aren't very challenging though, I may have had one or two instances in the game where I was stumped where to go or what to do but in general the game in terms of puzzles was pretty much a breeze.Throughout the game you control the fox and you have actions to wiggle your tail, or bark to which your spirit fox companion will bark back which was very cute. Throughout the game I found myself a little bit attached to the fox as I was following along to his story with growing interest.Performance wise, the game performs mostly OK on Steam Deck, although this is an indie game I would say that this game devours the Steam Deck battery to roughly the same extent as Doom (2016) which I found surprising. This essentially means that on full battery you'll be able to squeeze out about 1 hour to 1 hour and a half of game play before you would need to recharge. The biggest performance issue in the game happened to me when I was playing through the 2nd and 3rd chapter of the game, during those 2 chapters I already had clocked in 3 hours of game play and by that time the game/Steam Deck crashed on me about 4 times while playing through those chapters which roughly equates to 1 crash per hour.Strangely enough, once I made it past chapter 3, I haven't experienced any further crashes for any further chapters till the end of the game so if you are playing on Steam Deck or a laptop and you're experiencing crashes, try making it past chapter 3 and the issue for some reason should hopefully resolve itself. Another downside of the game is the lack of manually saving your game. Fortunately, the game does provide checkpoints throughout the chapter that auto save your game and you can pretty much pick up from that point if you quit your game however for some chapters, the distance between one checkpoint and another can be quite far and if you quit the game without reaching that checkpoint, you'll be reverted back to the previous checkpoint after starting the game again.Overall I enjoyed the Spirit of the North and will definitely give the sequel a try. The game offers a splendid and vibrant environments, and a unique (although a bit vague) storytelling. The performance of the game does suffer a bit at the start when playing the game on Steam Deck, and the game would definitely benefit from having an option to manually save your game. If you're looking for a nice relaxing game to take a break from the regular action games then you can't go wrong with this choice.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Journey and want similar game - this is it. But i would rate Journey noticeably higher overhaul even without considering nice co-op feature.Spirit of the North looks great, especially in a greener part - views in chapter 5 are very pleasing! But chapter 6 feels a tiny bit too dark sometimes, otherwise - great in both design and tech. Water is beautiful, grass is juicy and fluffy, terrain is detailed, nice lighting... Performance is good too, but 60 fps lock was a bit disappointing, plus fur is... Strange sometimes, but considering small team and budget - really great work! Sound is pretty mid, i would say a bit lower then mid considering release year - music feels a bit repeatable during the game, also sound of the game is ABSOLUTELY flat. Only some effects have their place in game's sound stage, but still strictly right or left. You don't feel like you are in the world of the game. It is fun, considering how much effort was spend to make visual, and how lazy and flat sound is. Music itself is fine, it works, but still mix is claustrophobic, not spacious at all, I had dissonance on open 5th chapter landscape with such spaciously tight sound design and music.Gameplay is similar to the Journey - simple, not annoying, without any depth whatsoever. It's just here for you to experience the atmosphere, but I must point out that in the Spirit of the North gameplay itself does not tell the story as good as in Journey. I played Journey first and expected to see more sense in gameplay there, than there was. I played on Xbox controller - controls are good, I haven't had any frustration because of it.As for the story and narrative... Well, it's there) Honestly I expected more from the narrative design, you want some interesting ways to tell the story from games like this, but it seems devs prioritized visuals and overhaul atmosphere above all.In the end this game IS as simple as it looks, but is it bad? Not at all, cute fluffy fox, nice decorations, atmosphere, nothing really bothers you during the game (except Kindred Spirits achievement). It is not a masterpiece of game narrative, it is not a deep  and diverse platformer, it is just a foxy with glowy patterns doing things in a beautiful world for around 6-8 hours (for 100% achievements).Solid 7/10

_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: is quite a mysterious and exciting 3D puzzle/platform adventure filled with wonderful sights and awesome sounds. Take on the role of the protagonist red fox as it disturbs the slumbering spirit of the Northern Lights and forever changes its destiny. It's an experience as a full package that you cannot fully appreciate until you have tried it yourself. The store page describes a game that's inspired by the Icelandic landscape. I fully believe it. The game is split into 8 different chapters, with Chapters 1 and 8 acting as bookends offering a nice introduction and a satisfying conclusion. Chapters 2 is fairly linear and straight forward. After that, the chapters are rather lengthy, each with multiple check-pointed sections with the game automatically saving as you reach these checkpoints. New platforming mechanics and puzzles are introduced throughout the game, and while it is rather casual in the beginning, there are some timed platforming gates that you will encounter about halfway through.Overall the game took me about 10 hours to complete, because I was enjoying my experience wandering the landscape and listening to the absolutely fantastic soundtrack, while searching every nook and cranny for the optional collectibles. I really did try and I thought I did a very thorough job, but much of the secrets still eluded me. One of the optional side-quests is to find shaman staves scattered around to bring to the fallen shaman remains, presumably to allow their spirits to rest in peace. A few of these are required for progression, but most of them are completely optional. I only pieced together about 20 out of 28 of these. Some of them are really hidden very well. There are other optional objectives as well, I will let you discover those on your own.So that speaks to the open expanse of the game. Every chapter is essentially a contained world, often you can reaccess previous sections after going through the checkpoints, but occasionally those sections are completely closed off. You will have to use the chapter selection option from the main menu if you want to reaccess at this point. A couple of the areas starting in Chapter 3 hint at the open-exploration optional aspect of the game instead of following the prescribed paths, but the smaller puzzles in that chapter make it so that it's not so obvious. Chapters 4-7 are where the majority of the game are located.A few of the puzzles stumped me a while, but nothing too complex looking at them in retrospect. The times I got stuck were mainly because of a lack of consideration of whatever new mechanic was just introduced. I am completely fine with environmental puzzles that are not too difficult, because, I have been stuck on similar games before and ultimately had to go looking at a guide because I simply could not progress. This game, I made it on my own.Caveat to people looking to have a completely casual and exploration experience just to take in the sights and sounds, you can do that only for a short while. If you want nothing to do with solving environment puzzles, you will not be able to progress beyond Chapter 3. If you are completely unable to do some platforming, you will also be stuck at this point. The platforming is fairly straight forward until Chapters 5-6 I would say, when you will be faced with some additional timed gates. These are not many, and they not too difficult, but they are definitely there, and you need to be aware of them.Overall, the experience was phenomenal. The controls felt kind of funny in a few small situations, but overall the response is fine and does not detract from the experience. The music will seem a bit overplayed if you stay in an area too long. But every section of every chapter will trigger a new musical loop, so I thoroughly enjoyed listening to the soundtrack perhaps a dozen times as I played through the game. The open-expanse and exploration is mostly optional, so you have the ability to narrow your focus on just completing the story should that be your wish.The game plays as a 3rd person 3D adventure platformer with some fairly simple environment puzzles that features a wide-expanse to explore at many junctures.The controller worked fine for the whole game. I had a couple of times when I paused the game to go do something else and when I came back the controller lost its response and I had to reset the game. Sometimes I could just move the mouse and I would see the options on-screen change, and that would revert to normal, but sometimes I couldn't do that either.Beautifully made landscapes and ruins, the artwork is quite good. There are very few animations as the environment is mostly static, but the interactions between the protagnist fox and the environment are definitely visible. Sometimes they seem silly, such as the fox making huge indentations in the snow just by stepping on it. Overall the environment in this game is quite a spectacle to behold.Despite the graphics looking beautiful, I had almost quit in Chapter 4 because of an overwhelming red glaze over the whole screen/environment for a large chunk of the game. I wish the red haze/fog would be lifted from the game. It's fine having a red sky and red rain, but that haze almost made me lose it. That section made my eyes bleed.I was mesmerized by the music for pretty much the entire game, it really made the experience full in my opinion. Is it the best music? No. There's been a lot of games with excellent soundtracks, and I would say this is well above average.I put in my warnings above, the game is not just a simple casual walking adventure in 3D in third person. The environmental puzzles are fairly straight forward. The platforming + timed gates are probably where some people will get stuck.The game is priced at £15.49/ €16.79/ $19.99 with a 15% discount at launch. I think this is totally fair.I recorded the first few minutes of myself playing without any commentary, you can see it first-hand here. The developers also have streamed it a bit and probably will be doing more as well. My video is here: is an experience worth having. I had fun enjoying the sights and sounds, and the overall experience was very enjoyable. The end screen gives you an option to quit or to stay there after the credits rolled. I stayed a couple of extra minutes enjoying myself and relishing in finishing the game. I will let you experience it for yourself without saying more about it. The game length is just about right for what I would want.I enjoyed solving the puzzles, even though a few of them stumped me a bit at first. The puzzles do encourage you to think outside the box at times. Despite their simple nature, I enjoyed the mechanics that went into these puzzles. The controls are just a little funky in a few situations, but nothing to make a serious complaint about. My biggest complaint is about the red haze in a particular section of the game that I could have done without.I will probably wait for a guide and go look to find all of the missing collectibles that I missed. I tried really hard to explore but still missed a bunch. I do like that these motivated me to traverse all the of terrain as much as possible and to look at the various environmental designs from all angles.What an experience indeed. Another indie gem. Definitely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: What will the world look like when human rule ends? Will the whole planet be relieved, will the deforested areas be reforested, will the greenery eat the concrete, will wild animals populate the streets? We don't know the answers to these questions, but thanks to games like Spirit of the North, we can soak up the beautifully peaceful atmosphere of the future Earth.Spirit of the North won't tell you what happened on Earth. You are a completely ordinary fox wandering around an Iceland-inspired landscape, and you are accompanied by another fox, this time an astral one. There is no story, no narrative, just your perceptions.You ride through the snow-covered landscape, drive in streams, crawl through caves and climb rocks. The point is to absorb the atmosphere and come up with your own theories about the world that surrounds you. Those who expect more than a felt experience, some platforming and puzzles, probably won't get it.As a result, Spirit of the North has flat game mechanics and sometimes too irritating controls... it drags the game down, and not even pleasant music, nice visuals and an emotional story can pull it out. However, if you have a weakness for foxes and are looking for this type of game, I can recommend the game despite its shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautiful game. Very peaceful and quiet, and the majority of my enjoyment was simply wandering around the environments and taking in everything. The story, despite being devoid of any dialogue, was quietly intriguing. I also appreciated the emotional moments, which were gentle and comfortable. I didn't get hit too hard in the feels until the ending, which I thought was perfect and poignant. There were only a couple puzzles in here that I got stuck on, but thankfully I managed to figure them out without ever needing a walk-through. People seem to take issue with the fact that the puzzles were on the simpler side. Honestly, I much preferred the easier type of puzzles the game had, since it doesn't impact forward momentum or let frustration get in the way of absorbing the immaculate vibes of the story and scenic vistas. If I wanted to think deeply and technically, I'd sink my teeth into a fully fledged puzzle game. My only small complaint with the puzzles was the length of time some of the animations went on, specifically when opening something or activating a stone. There's a section near the end where you use different stones to move a pillar of rock up and down, and you'll have to watch each one for quite a few seconds longer than it should take while you figure it out. It's a very minor grievance, but I thought I'd mention it.The controls were mostly fine, a little sticky. Not many of the jumps required pinpoint precision or were punishing for missing them, so perfect movement isn't really necessary. I did find myself wishing there wasn't quite so many sections involving water traversal, mostly because you move so slowly in them. There's also a cute but quickly tiresome "shake off" animation almost any time you leave the water, which I had to start jumping to avoid. It does encourage you to be more efficient in avoiding water though, which is a perhaps unintentional dimension of depth to the game-play that worked for me. Other than that, I liked the few different movement options you get throughout the game, which I won't spoil, but it was genuinely exciting each time I got one.I've seen another common complaint in these reviews, which is that the map sections are too big and there's too much space between puzzles. I could definitely see that if you're playing to be 100% mentally engaged in puzzle solving at all times, but for me, it was perfect. I was actually hoping many times throughout the game that there would be larger areas I could run around in and take in the sights without needing to actually do anything, so I was super happy with chapter 7. There aren't many games that I feel that way about. I usually crave intense game-play stimulation at all times, but it's hard to feel bored sprinting through ancient ruins with a spirit fox companion, watching the red haze trail blaze its way across the darkening skies of Iceland at twilight.Finally, I have to mention the fantastic music. I don't really have any kind of in-depth commentary on it, just that the tracks are beautiful and I immediately added the entire soundtrack to my YouTube music playlist. They fit the tone perfectly and I hope even when I listen to it years down the line it'll transport me back into memories of playing this game.I wasn't intending to write a very long review, just a couple sentences at most, but I guess I was feeling a little stronger about the game than I realized. I picked this up at a discount and even though it's a pretty short game, I would go back and buy it at full price if I could. As it is, I'll just have to do that with the sequel instead, which I will absolutely be playing as soon as it comes out.Thanks to everyone who worked on this for such a great experience, and I'm looking forward to the next one!

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings with SoT. This is a game similar to Journey, Flowers, Abzu or Gris, but featuring a fox in the mountains.  I can see pros and consPROS:- The game is really beautiful and the soundtrack is amazing. - Length-wise it is ok, around 5-8 h depending on your exploration. There are 8 chapters, and some collectibles that acounts for some replays after you complete the game. - the fox learns some abilities that unlocks new mechanics and puzzles, making it fresh and interesting to play. - A few fox skins can be unlocked if you discover enough secrets, a good touchCONS - the pace is too slow at times, the areas are so vast and open, with empty fields and no too much to see or interact with on the background that it takes you forever to reach the next area. - Although each chapter is different from the previous ones, the areas within each chapter, and tasks/puzzles to move forward, are quite repetitive, ultimately making it boring. - There's no story to follow or characters to interact with. - Although the OST is good, after a while you realize it is just only a few short tracks playing all the time over and over, making it repetitive if you play for some hours because it does not change between chapters or areas, from the very beginning until the end.- The most irritating part was the controls, especially in areas requiring jumping or platforming. It is bad implemented, with invisible walls, bad movements, weird turns... you will have to repeat many sections just because the controls are horrendous. - Finally, not sure this is a problem only faced by me, but it had some performance issues, with staggering, frame rate drops and tearing. Overall, it is not a bad game, and if you like similar titles with beautiful aesthetics, OST, slow pace and just relaxing gameplay you will enjoy it. However, if you expect some interesting challenges or puzzles, a faster pace, or do not like platforming, this is not for you, especially considering the bad controls. I personally prefer other similar games like Gris.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary of my review in a few words; It's good. I like it more than a lot. Thank you devs, I love you. My review in more than too many words;I recently was shown this game by a friend on a whim, and since my favourite animal is the fox, I was very interested from the very beginning. I paid for this game with zero hesitation, only watching the first trailer, looking at some screenshots while it downloaded, and I was eager to see what this game was about. I was very happily surprised by the experience that was waiting for me.-The Gameplay-During the gameplay, I was beginning to hesitate, as the physics are quite floaty and jerky, and it was apparent right away... However, for the team of only a few developers who developed this game, I got past it very quickly; I know that developing 3D games can be difficult, and for this, I respect all of the effort that goes into this game, not only for things that were polished, but the things that were also not polished. The controls are fluid enough, however, could use more polish along the long run; it can be frustrating if you're not the patient type, the fox will run out of energy very often, forcing you to walk a bit, and there's a lot of geometry you can get caught on if you're not careful. There also appear to be a number of locations where you would imagine you could enter or crawl through, but are simply blocked off by invisible walls. This can break immersion, but for me, I enjoyed it for the most part.The puzzles in this game are not heavy on emphasizing what you're 'meant' to do, but I found myself learning the solution eventually. I rarely overthought what I was supposed to be doing, but I did get lost quite often, in a good way. That said, however, there are numerous points in the game where I unintentionally sequence-broke the progression by getting to places I shouldn't have been able to sooner, simply by doing simple maneuvers or jumps. I even soft-locked myself by entering a location prior to obtaining the ability to enter it, simply by traversing the mountain above it.-The Art Direction-I, as an artist myself, absolutely love the artistic direction, the pseudo-painting art style, and the constant ribbon of malice hovering over the wonderful landscape is truly a sight to behold; it becomes immediately aware to the player that the colour red is symbolic, and paired with the white landscape for the beginning area, fading out to much darker colours as the game progresses, it truly impresses me to see, having never seen this game previously. -The Sound & Music-The sound design in this game isn't anything to write home about, but the various fox noises are probably not what the general public would consider to be 'fox noises'; however, I personally, was not offended by it. It works for what it does.The music in this game is genuinely beautiful, but the score can get repetitive, as it repeats itself numerous times, especially if you're someone who takes their time wandering through the vast levels as I do. I loved what I heard, but it does appear that the soundtrack repeats itself constantly. Muting the game's music is an option, so if it begins to bother you, get some music and just relax to it while playing the game.-The Story-The story for this game, while at first seems half-hearted and dull, soon grew on me the more I played the game; I suggest not spoiling yourself with this game's story, and while it's not exactly the most twist-of-fate story ever written, it beautifully pairs together with what the game is; for a story about a fox and a spirit, I think it performs wonderfully, and the underlining theme between the player and their companion makes the end of the game a genuinely heartwarming experience. I fell in love with this story, and it completely bypassed my expectations by a lot. I'm very happy to have played this game for the story.-My Verdict & Recommendation-If you're someone who enjoys lush environments, beautifully-rendered lighting and graphics, a light yet emotional story, a beautiful art direction, and an adorable protagonist, I would suggest buying this game; if you can look past certain problems this game has, and if you simply want a relaxing, lightly-engaging experience, I think you'll genuinely enjoy this. I certainly did.-Final Thoughts, A Letter to the Devs-Devs of Spirit of the North,Thank you all so much for working so hard and so passionately on this game; it's very apparent from the get-go that there was a massive attention to detail, and from being comprised of only a few developers, I have a very large amount of respect for what you do. Thank you for bringing this wonderful story and genuine piece of art to players' hands. Your work has touched me on a level that I will hold onto for a very long time. Truly, thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: The PC version is not recommanable.GAMEPLAY: The controls are at best annoying - if your game contains jumping puzzles and small spaces you HAVE to have good controls. You also get stuck on invisible walls and corners where it should be smooth sailing all throughout the game (my friends played it on switch and it's not an issue there). PC port is unplayable.STORY: The idea and message are great, but I wouldn't call it a "plot" as you can sum up everything that happens (besides running, puzzles and fetchlike quests) in one sentence, so don't expect much.LENGHT: If not rushed the game takes about 2 - 3 hours.LOOKS: All the above is a shame as the game looks brilliant. Especially with the music the athmosphere could be great, if I wouldn't be frustrated with the controls every 5 minutes. I'm actually sad to write this beauty a bad review, but not fixing these issues AND charging this amount for a game of this lenght with such problems is simply impertinent. (The reason I got so many hours is achievementhunting and leving the game on while doing other things. Actual playtime maybe 4 hours tops.)

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a linear, slow paced game that revolves around solving platforming puzzles to navigate the world and rid it of the dark energy.Be warned, this game is very slow paced, there is no dialogue at all and zero combat of any kind. There are times where you will be confused about what to do next, it takes a little bit of thinking but its pretty straight forward after the first hour.The game is very short, consisting of 8 Chapters totalling around 5-6 hours of playtime. _childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on to recommend or not. It is a beautiful game and it has smooth play through most of the time (only getting stuck on invisible walls occasionally). However it can be frustrating at times as there is little to no guidance on what you are meant to be doing at any given moment. Which I can respect, but it often left me running around in circles for 10-20 minutes trying to figure out how to move on. After about an hour an a half game play, the puzzles became a little repetitive and not as fun to complete. My last critique is that the "sprint" button on my Xbox360 controller was the left bumper and to move slow was the left trigger. I feel like these should have been switched, since after 3 hours of playing my left pointer finger hurts so much from having to hold down the right bumper and pressing it repeatedly trying to convince my fox that it, can in fact, run.Other-wise it is a really neat game and concept and I loved the first half of my play through running around as the fox and all the small details built into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually the game is stunning, it's immediately clear that someone put a lot of time and love into designing the scenery of these worlds (the living and the spirit versions). The sounds are well placed (except the bark, see below) and the soundtrack fits everything nicely. Controls are hit and miss, mostly fine except for fine controls or low-speed moves. Overall this was a little rough around the edges but remained a good game. It's very short depending on if you go for completion in finding all of the fallen Shaman, I personally didn't bother as those puzzles were frustrating given the rough controls.There are some very minor things that I feel could be updated/changed to make the experience better for players, reducing frustrations or fixing things that make no sense. The most noticeable one is faster animations when spirit charging (or whatever it's called) using those blue flower things, it's so tedious for something you repeat so many times. Same with picking up and dropping the Shaman staff, the animation is way too slow, the main reason I passed up those puzzles where I could. As others have mentioned here, the fox barks like a domesticated dog which throws the immersion out the window (didn't Ylvis do an entire song about this?). Lastly it would be great to see UltraWide supported, especially for this type of game. I know many games with pre-rendered cutscenes can have issues with this, but most UltraWide users would probably accept the potential issues for the added range.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. Breathtaking. Be ready for an emotional rollercoaster. Have tissues ready. You will really feel for the fox. But it's such a good game and story.Spirit of the North plays a bit like the game Journey, but without the online random companions. You're a little fox, in the arctic tundra of Iceland. You travel across the landscape and ruins with a little spirit fox buddy at your side. You'll experience the story and mythology not through words or narration, but by visual clues and amazing music.Playable in one sitting. You'll probably get through in about 6 hours, give or take.  I spent just barely 7 hours to complete, since I was slowly taking my time and found most of hidden stuff in my first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North's description reminded me of Lost Embers which I enjoyed thoroughly. I was excited to play it and experience the game play and story. However, the controls are very ridged and clunky, not fluid at all. Spirit of the North tries to have light platforming, but because of the lacking controls any slight mistake and you fall off and have to try again. You cannot turn mid jump, so if you miscalculate there is no rectifying your mistake, you just have to try again which is a slow process to get back to where you were. There is a good amount of water in the beginning you have to swim through and each time you get out of the water onto land the fox stops to shake the water off. EVERY. TIME. You cannot skip this. You can jump to cancel, but that takes about the same amount of time and you still can't move until either animation is finished. Also there is only one swimming speed: slow. So when you eventually miss that jump and fall into the water it's a slow paddle back to where you were to try again.Plus finding a staff to give to a corpse to set it's soul free/give it peace is tied into being important to the story (as seen in the trailer and game images). The game gives you an image count of how many corpses you've encountered and how many you've missed. As someone who loves to collect things in games, this really tripped me up. They hide them, which can be fun, of course! But it being an important task to the story is very frustrating when after you finish an area, go to the next, and the game tells you you've missed someone in the previous area with no way of going back... that sucks. Yes, there are collectibles that can be added to the game for extra fun and you don't have to find ALL of them to find enjoyment in the game, but this is advertised as important AND there is so little to do (at least in the beginning) that bringing the staff to the corpse is a big deal. It just hurt when I would be carrying a staff for so long, not find a corpse for it to be set free, and I find another staff. It feels like I failed that corpse's soul and failed the chance to complete the game properly because there are a lot of areas where there is no back tracking to find the corpses you've missed. How can Spirit of the North advertise this as a core game play aspect, yet hide them like they are simply just easter eggs?Over the course of the 1 hour I ended up playing this game I only grew more and more frustrated with the clunky controls, slow movement in the game despite the Sprint feature, and the lack of back tracking to find the corpses I missed. I paid $6.52 for this game during the Summer Sale and I still don't think that's worth it for a game this frustrating and unpolished, let alone $20. It really bums me out because I read many reviews on how great this game's story is. Even the beginning gives you amazing story set up without any dialog, but sadly I cannot recommend this game at any price.TLDR: Spirit of the North's game play is so clunky, unpolished, and frustrating that it's not worth $6.52, let alone $20, despite how good other people say the story is.

_childDocuments_.review: You're a fox traveling around Iceland-like terrain helping ancient shamans find peace. The story is unique and the puzzles are challenging, but not too much so. It's almost impossible to navigate where you're supposed to go in some chapters without a tutorial, but that really only happens in some areas. There are chapter-specific YouTube tutorials to get around that if you are frustratingly stuck. I am satisfied with photo mode and could save some really great screen captures. The graphics are a little blockish and the jumping mechanics could be wonky sometimes, however that shouldn't deter you from not playing. The story is worth it, and I will take a small indie game with a few minor frustrations over a conglomerate with micro-transactions any day. I know the developers can fix all of those little mishaps in Spirit of the North 2, which is set to release in 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: Very pretty little game! The puzzles are easy enough to solve without a walkthrough but not too easy to the point where it feels pointless. The fox is adorable, even though occasionally the lil guy controls like a rear-wheel sports car on ice. The music loops can get annoying but are fine if you turn the music volume down. LOVE the shaman side missions! love them! love to make FRIENDS. :D the enemy/danger was EXTREMELY cool, absolutely adored the design, and the ending was so cute i cried. Would recommend buying and playing this for sure.EDIT: If you still need convincing: Designated bark button, designated wag tail button. enough said.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. The music is amazing, and I absolutely adored the scenic views at all times. Iceland is a beautiful place!I could go on for hours about the things I loved, so I'll just cut this short by listing the two things I feel like could be better;- The music, while incredible and very moving, was rather intense sometimes. I don't mean this as in it was too loud, but rather, sometimes I felt as though a boss fight was just around the corner even though it's a very calm and peaceful game.- I felt that the finding of the shaman bodies was very difficult sometimes - this might just be personal opinion and could've been much easier for others, but oftentimes I gave a staff to a body and was genuinely surprised to see the little pop-up show me that I had missed a body somewhere. In particular in chapter 3 there was an area where you had to jump down a hole carefully to reach a body in a crevice, I didn't realize that and just jumped down to go to the next chapter, and then I couldn't go back up to get it. But this is something easily solved with another playthrough, I suppose.Other than those two, I loved this game! Every bit of it! The story was incredible and was fed to the player in bits and pieces, and I loved every new piece of information I got. Running around, swishing my tail, and barking with reckless abandon was also a lot of fun - even if it accomplished nothing story-wise lol. Thank you for the fun, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:- Checkpoint save system has much to be desired- Short length- character movement isn't always smooth when trying to climb- Game leaves you wanting more to do- You can't jump through your screen to live in the beauty of the gamePros:- Gorgeous atmosphere, leaves you wanting to visit Iceland and Europe- Solid soundtrack- No dialogue and no pressure- good/fun puzzles- little to no bug/glitch problems- plot is what you make of it Is it perfect? No. Is it awesome for what it is? YES! Worth getting on sale, but I am left wanting to support the developers for this glorious piece of playable art. Would love to see a sequel or some DLC's. Or another game like this, but longer and more to do. But as a chill non combat game for all ages, Spirit of the North is a no regrets purchase for me. For those looking to escape for a while, I highly recommend picking this one up. It is also available for Switch and PS4/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It is a game that is alot like Lost Ember. In this case you play as a little red fox living in an iceland landscape with many caverns, ruins, geysers, and mountains. The story is based on visual interpretation as there is no dialogue in the game. Straight forward the story is about a fox meeting a spirit vixen and goes on a journey against the red blight. The rest should be easy to figure out as the sight of death and the carvings show a world devoid of life that should be restored. The biggest psychological question is why would the red fox go through with this journey? I have a few theories to answer that. But it's not important.Gameplay wise, it's all an exploration and puzzle game where you overcome obstacles to move another step forward in your journey. There is no combat, no enemies, no major environmental hazards, and you don't have to worry about the idea of dying - which to me makes the story feel a little bland. The controls are manageable. Overall a kid could play this game and not worry about anything.

_childDocuments_.review: While it has it's little quirks and sometimes janky controls, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. The world itself is fantastic. I enjoyed every moment of this game, even the sad ones.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game if you want to and enjoy being frustrated and angry! It has the makings of being a fantastic relaxing fun game but it's not! There is NO direction or guidance given. Normally I don't use walkthroughs but I used one from Chapter 2 on, giving up never to return during Ch#4. My biggest gripe which is a deal breaker for me is there is no manual save, if you leave the game you are stuck having to replay the entire chapter again. If you're lucky there is a chapter part 2 offered to restart at, so you're not totally screwed back at the beginning of the last Chapter you played.  I'm very glad I only paid $1.99 on sale and DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME UNTIL Manual Save is added. _childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere and story is really good and I wish I could enjoy it more, but I find the navigation and some of the progression through levels very frustrating. It can be hard to move accurately where I want to go which exacerbates some very short timing windows and tricky paths from one area to another. I spent a lot of time falling off ledges into the start of a level and walking all the way back because there's no other way up, and as some others have said there's no manual save so you have to do that in the big picture as well by starting over entire chapters if you want to go back to something. Often there is only one way through or out of a place, like if you fall into water a lot of times you have to swim to one or two specific places to climb back out. (I would also like to mention it's very hard to spot most of the monks and the way forward isn't clear in a lot of places, but I'm not complaining. It's just difficult.)I'm in the minority here and you'll probably like it, but personally I can't play this to the end. The frustration trying to get through one of the later levels is just something I don't want to spend my downtime on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is obviously trying to emulate Journey. Same art style on the story boards, same quest to reach a mountain top and the same puzzle mechanics. I wanted to like it. I loved Journey. However, this game is just tedious. The pacing is ridiculously slow in many places. Also, there is no real story telling going on to explain why you, a random, lone fox and apparently only living creature on the planet, are interacting with a spirit and traveling through blighted ruins to a mountain top. To save a civilization on the brink of collapse? No. To rescue fellow critters? No. You really have no incentive to do anything this game leads you to do. Lastly, having the same song playing non-stop throughout most of the game was extremely annoying. Journey did it right and made sure the music emphasized the gameplay. So, while I can appreciate the attempt to make a Journey-like experience, this attempt was poorly executed in almost every sense and has no replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Just gonna say - this game punches well above its weight in terms of visual/presentation. Everything fits together well, and is used to convey a very compelling non-verbal story.The puzzle elements are relatively light - with some platforming sprinkled throughout to give it some flavor. There are moments where it does feel a *bit* like a walking-simulator; but it by no means had me bored. The tonal shifts between chapters creates enough of an emotional journey that the somewhat mediocre 'game-y' elements are more than excused for.There were some minor glitches I encountered (some collectable staves got duplicated, and some decorative chimes got borked by the physics engine), but nothing too bad - I've seen much worse in AAA games.The only glitch that actually bothered me was still quite minor [though *super* minor spoiler warning]: In a later-game scene, the protagonist walks super slowly (as was the clear intent); but the footstep sound-effect was playing at normal speed - giving 2 'steps' for every step the character actually took. It was pretty distracting in a rather emotionally significant scene.In summery, I think this game is fantastic - but I acknowledge it's not a perfect game (none such games even exist). I'd love to see more from Infused Studio (ie. Tayler & Jacob). It's truly impressive what they have been able to put together here.Overall: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a breathtakingly beautiful game that is sure to touch your heart. From the moment you start playing, you're transported to a mystical world filled with wonder and magic.The game follows the journey of a fox as it navigates its way through a gorgeous Nordic landscape. The fox is guided by a spirit that appears as a glowing orb, and together they uncover the secrets of the land and its history.But Spirit of the North is more than just a pretty game. It's a game that has a message - a message about the importance of nature and our connection to it. As you play, you'll encounter scenes that are both beautiful and heartbreaking, and you'll come to understand the impact that humans can have on the natural world.The music is another standout feature of the game. The haunting melodies perfectly complement the stunning visuals and add an extra layer of emotion to the experience. And the gameplay is simple but satisfying - you'll solve puzzles, explore the world, and interact with other animals in a way that feels natural and organic.Overall, Spirit of the North is a game that will stay with you long after you've finished playing. It's a game that reminds us of the beauty and fragility of the natural world, and of the importance of our connection to it. It's a game that is as touching as it is visually stunning, and it's a must-play for anyone who appreciates the power of video games as an art form.

_childDocuments_.review: Game: Let's start with the positive: Spirit of the North is a game that I'd say is somewhat similar to the game Journey. You start off far away from your distant, visible goal and your objective is to reach it. Along the way you'll occasionally bump into some big-picture beautiful vistas and short parts that are pretty decent, almost good.. and the fox is cute.Unfortunately that's about it. The rest of the game feels like an unpolished game with very rough edges.A lot of the game mechanics aren't that fun, like having to go find some spirit flower every 30 seconds to power your abilities.It's easy to get somewhat lost or confused on what to do next.Trying to get an overlook to figure out where to go or what to do doesn't always work. You often just see the environment around you without any clear direction beckoning you to explore further.In other games you'd expect something to draw your attention, or be upfront that there probably isn't anything interesting to find in that corner over there.Some places look important but isn't, while some places look bland and unimportant but might just have a useful item leaning against a rock of the same color as the item, camouflaging it. Probably the opposite of how you want it to be. There's a lot of potential confused running around wondering if you're doing what the game wants you to do correctly.Some puzzles I solved without even realizing it, and I then wondered if I missed some clue, or if that really was the intended way to solve it. "Do I move on, or do I go back and see if I accidentally ran past some hint? Am I overthinking it, or is there a much simpler solution?"Don't get me wrong. I enjoy a game that doesn't hold your hand, but there's some middle-ground where the levels are designed in a way that naturally flows well, and draws your attention to the important things. A puzzle isn't smart or good because you ran past an important piece two times because it doesn't look important and just blend into the rest of the environment.It's not always clear if there's an invisible wall blocking you from nailing that jump, or if you're supposed to take another path to get up there. It might look like you can jump up somewhere, of fit between some obstacle, but the game doesn't communicate that it isn't the correct solution well enough.On top of it all, the controls are somewhat jerky. Controlling the fox isn't always reliable, and you might get stuck on elevated edges. A game that involves so much walking/running and jumping could use a smoother movement system.There are some jarring loading screen transitions and camera movements that make the game feel like it could use a lot of polish.Summary:There's a game with potential in there with nice vistas and a moving story, but it is just overshadowed by frustrating level and puzzle design, confusing game flow and somewhat rough controls & graphics that could've used just a little more work.I'd say only buy this game if you really think the theme has great appeal to you.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like foxes, spirits, and getting frustrated and angry this game is for you.Overall a fantastic game with excellent graphics and very realistic fox behaviour.  Takes a while to work out where to go and what you have to do as there is no dialogue.  However, there is a major fundamental flaw which is simply unforgivable.  The controls are without a doubt THE WORST I have ever experienced in a game, to the point of making it almost unplayable.  90% of the time jumping doesn't work, which is essential for the platforming parts later on, and look sensitivity is a joke with even the slightest nudge of your mouse getting your view totally lost, even on lowest settings.  I spent well over half an hour just trying to jump between 3 platforms.  Until these issues are fixed, which is long overdue, I would not recommend spending money on it.  It could be such an amazing game if not for these major issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate dumping on indie games, particularly when they are not bad games, but I'm also sick to death of indie developers forcing me to use a particular control system because YOU CANNOT REBIND THE KEYS.The game is supposed to be in the same vein as Abzu (another game that doesn't allow key rebinding) in that it's not too taxing, lets you run around a beautiful landscape with relaxing music on. I generally enjoy the games like these; they're a nice break from the Doom Eternals of the world.Unfortunately I found the control system unwieldy; the fox simply wouldn't go where I wanted it to. I wasn't enjoying it and it wasn't a relaxing, pleasant experience at all.Moreover I encountered bugs. At one point I couldn't get past a marker no matter what I did. So I checked a walk-through (which you should never have to do for a game like this) and found they did the exact same thing as me. Restarted the game, did what I did before and it worked this time. That's happened twice so far.Anyway, it's been uninstalled now. It's not a bad game, but it was a disappointing experience personally.Positives: Pretty graphics, pleasant soundtrack, you play a fox (which is always a good thing) and my cat seemed to enjoy watching me play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start this review off by saying that this game is amazing. It has a lot of beautiful environments and a lot of well thought out puzzles and levels. Although the game could use some improvement of the movement it greatly overwheighs it in the level design and the looks. When the great and at times emotional story was over for me i have found myself wanting to play more. The game has simple characters that do not speak and yet it is able to make a amazing story out of them and i don't find myself falling asleep in hours of dialogue. Along with the gameplay and at times difficult movement the game has great soundtracks for the levels that i think fit the atmosphere very well. I highly recommend this amazing game to anyone who enjoys puzzle games and story along with beautiful environments. In conclusion i would like to thank the developers for this amazing and beautiful game and i suggest the person who reads this to buy it and play it all the way through as the journey is worth your time and money. _childDocuments_.review: It's fairly simplistic but that isn't a detractor. As a casual game it was very welcome and even the platforming puzzles weren't frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Good, simple game to sit back to, relax and enjoy- Beautiful, large environments that gives you space and freedom to run around- Great relaxing soundtrack that fits well with the theme. As a piano music listener I enjoyed it very much! The occasional eerie music in darker environments is a nice change too- The puzzles are basic, easy but still enjoyable- The fox model is so cute, and I appreciate the options of using different skins- I enjoyed the lights and glows, it gives the game a nice little touchCons:-  The story is told through drawings on walls, which appears probably around a total of 15 times. Some of the drawings repeat themselves, and most of the time are not very clear. So if you are in for the lore, don't expect much. You get the basic idea of it, but you won't get much more detail than that. SPOILER: You don't really get an explanation as to why there is corruption, just that it appeared, killed people, and you have to get rid of it. - Very clunky, buggy and primitive jump mechanic, it seems like that part of the game was the least worked on by the developers- Although the environments are beautiful and large, most of it is just empty - This is not a game that focuses heavily on game play and puzzles, so if you are looking for that you will be disappointed. It is mostly a walking and jumping simulator, but it can be enjoyed by people who just want to relax- This game could benefit from better sound FX. More sounds could be added to certain actions you do (like picking up the staff, dropping the staff, etc), more variety of sounds depending on what kind of ground you're walking on, etc. Details like that could help give the game a more polished feel.- There are two parts of the game where you are forced to walk slowly which is a drag but not too badAlthough this game still needs some work, I definitely recommend it if you are looking to sit back, decompress and enjoy the environment, without too many expectations from it. If you love the environment, you will appreciate the beautiful, ethereal forest at the end!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short. This is no dialogue, or combat, but there are puzzles. It's also charming, and atmospheric, and I was genuinely invested in the fox you play as. I played through once, and missed awakening a few of the spirits, then went back and played it through in its entirety again to get them all, and even though I replayed it the very day after I played it through the first time, it had not become tedious and had not lost its emotional impact.10/10. I would definitely recommend Spirit of the North. It's a refreshing change of pace.

_childDocuments_.review: 2024 ReviewSo update~!!I'm leaving my previous review here because a lot of it still holds true, but I'm excited and happy to admit that the issues I had during my last attempted playthroughs are no longer hindering the gameplay~! I did a stream of this game recently and not only were the running and jumping mechanics smooth, but the problems with Chapter 2 that I had before have ceased to deter me! <3Now there are still glitches in some ways - like a monk was able to receive two staves for some reason and I accidentally clipped under the water and had to restart a chapter at some point, but I mean, it happens. xD The game is passable, the storytelling is beautiful, and I am BEYOND excited for the release of the second game!!-------------2021 ReviewThis game is beautiful. The only reason at all that I give this game a thumbs down is the chaotic controls. Besides not being able to map controls to our preferred settings and not being able to turn off the rumble feature, I'm having a very frustrating time with controlling the character at all. _childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely gorgeous! From the detailing on the fox, to the absolutely breathtaking scenery, you can really see and feel the heart and soul of everyone on the project. The areas of the semi-open world offer so much to explore, and the incredible graphics of all the various areas will keep you in awe the whole way through.It's not just pretty though, it also plays phenomenally. I found the controls very comfortable, very responsive. And not just comfortable, but lovingly detailed as well. The fact that they incorporated a button for wagging the tail as a mechanic in the game shows an incredible level of thought and dedication. (As well as just being plain adorable.)It's a cute little adventure game that's easy to just boot up and play for a little bit to pass the time, but just as easy to get lost and enthralled in if you so choose. I definitely recommend it if you're open to just a relaxing little game; 10/10 in my book. And lastly; Thank you Infuse Studio for making such a fun, adorable game. The messages at the end of the credits only spoke to the heart put into this game, and I'm so glad you got to share it with us.
