_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game! I heard that just 3 guys made it, 2 developers and 1 soundtrack guy. That's amazing! Considering that, this is a 5 star game. There could be improvements, but the same could be said for most games though. First off, the music, is mesmerizing. My hubby would constantly comment "hows your whimsical/magical game going over there?" Because the music is just like, movie worthy. It's beautiful orchestra music that just takes any location you're in to a whole new level. The game itself is sort of an open world but still a bit linear of a path or direction that you're supposed to go. There are varying puzzles, though a lot of the puzzles follow the same concept which can get a little dull. The scenery and surroundings are so beautiful, combined with the music, really makes up for that though. The game has zero dialogue as far as I remember. There is barking foxes and squeaks from your companion, and that's it. But that's almost what I love about this game, it really puts you in the place of a fox in a sort of ancient post-apocalyptic world, completely alone, finding nothing but remains of hoomans everywhere, and eventually a tiny little glowing spirit ball. I felt alone, unsure, I didn't know what to do. But I figured it out.  A lot of times, it's easier to figure out than you think, you just need to take a beat and think about it. A lot of times, the answer would be something I immediately dismissed in my head thinking "that can't be the answer" or "that can't be where it is..." But it usually was! I really enjoyed helping bring the ghosts their staffs. It works as a sort of collectors item for the fox. Sometimes they grant you help with something. Mostly towards the end of the game. It will show you when they do, there's a camera pan.And then you have the ending... My goodness, for a game with zero words, it had me on the verge of tears. I won't spoil it but ugh, so beautiful what this fox does in the end. I wish they sort of explained it juuuuust a tiny bit more, because as you will see, you won't completely understand all the details of what this fox does exactly and what the consequences are of that choice. And one last issue I have with the game like others have said is the controls! I wish they would at least give a short explanation of each power when you obtain, but like I said, it really does fall in line with how it would be from the foxes perspective. But the jumping button is my least favorite. A lot of times I have to line up my fox right before I make a jump, and IDK how many times I fell off of a cliff when I shouldn't have but man, I got used to it and overlooked it for the games other positive aspects. Like I said, you'll see! But I can't recommend this game enough. It's a gorgeous game, it took me to another place, and I loved that place in a bittersweet way. Great game, 8/10 from me. Definitely worth the price for the amazing work a few guys put into this work of art.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello weary traveller!Seems like you are at the crossroads again, contemplating whether to buy this game or not. The game is a visual spectacle alright, but it has it's flaws here and there. It can use a little bit of polishing in animations and visual glitches. Since it is an Indie, don't expect too much. Sit back and enjoy the puzzles. They are not that difficult. The music is top notch and the landscapes are absolutely gorgeous! The game's not perfect. But is it beautiful? By the Nine Divines, it is! It is a sweet little game if you want to escape your wanderings for 4-5 hours. 12/10 would pet the good fox!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, hear me out. Being that there was a notable little tid-bit saying about Nordic folklore and Icelandic landscape there was and is a lot of potential for this to be like a  Nordic Okami game. Their plan or not it seems... flat. Now, as far as the apparent direction of the game it seems very clear the team behind it either didn't have the team roster to pull out all the stops they wanted or that this is a slower more casual pace they wanted to go initially. But! With games like Hollow Knight, Ori And the Blind Forest, Slime Rancher, The Last Guardian, The Unfinished Swan, Journey, Abzu, Vane, and other artistic vision / cutesy gameplay titles, this game could have definitely been more involved based on what it's clearly trying to tell as an otherwise flattened story. First I want to say that this game is far from trash, but it is likewise not close to "Overwhelmingly Positive" either.Firstly Animation and Music are pretty good. The Style seems "upstart studio" but not awful, but not great. Still, I like it tbh. Now, RULES OF PLAY. These frustrate me in this game being that there are a more than a few times I went to do things having prior been taught by the game then going to use that method to be told "no, this instead". I was notably confused like "am i nuts or does this not work now?" Which, no, I'm not crazy it just sometimes says do this thing different this time. Which I can't scream about this to hard because of that whole era of games that left you to learn it yourself. So. Ehh.PACING & LEVEL DESIGN This game just decides to go 0 to snail and stay there. There were and are a few places they could have cranked the jams so to speak to really drive the feeling of a level. For example the part where you rise and lower the water levels. Building a the level out where diving and swimming faster, needing to breathe and creating more urgency and strategy on the front of how to use spirit and problem solving skills would have sold that stage. The Option of faster swimming and actually being able to fully stop in the water would have also been nice. Oh, and running in "ankle" deep water please? Simply out of that fact a real fox can swim slower/faster, stop in the water/ dive and need to breathe under the water, and run through puddles. Another area is likewise the Plains in level 4 or 5 where you learn to use those rifts to be pushed forwared in short bursts. Instead it would have driven the freeing and foxy speed home to make them stackable boosts. Through each ring you run faster, and Faster, and FASTER, bolting and weaving bursting and jumping until you reach the ramp and WHOOSH you're at full speed and you're rushed over the clearing into the water to hydroplane onto the land right before breaking water to continue then with steady speed up the hill over the clearing and into the next stage triumphant. Pacing like that is in Abzu and Journey and creates memorable lasting experiences fondly remembered. This doesn't do that. But the Trailer did.Animation and Sound Design.Minor Fixes in the catagory, The barking well... have you heard foxes before, I have a vixen that raised pup down the road from my house and uh... well... no? You kinda got it wrong. But mixing the right sounds with the right poses and animations can make things more dynamic and memorable and more fun to perform. Example instead of just a bark and a tail wag to activate stone. how about a stance that's like I mean bizznass and then throwing the head back accompanied with that foxish howl a fox can do and a cool little burst of blue spirit energy and the stone activating all cool and celtic like. with a nice little sound effect like the magic is taking more hold to the runestone. Okami did this every time you summoned the moon is had a sound like mist rushing in to peer back and reveal the moon with the neat little sound after. Or when again, in Okami, you cleanse an area you do a kick-butt howl that liberates the area and kicks off a cutscene. Or how when you run in that game you switch through three speeds and the sound and animation work together to deliver how fast you're really running across any level.This game isn't bad, It's just lacking small to heavy (depending on how you review) amounts of polish that could take it from what it is to something better. And even still, the studio may be trying to go for a completely different feel. And If by any chance they see this and have a bigger team by then/now and they make changes like these we'll all see what this was going to be. But with how I feel (with bias clouding review here) I felt the game wasn't entirely complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this is totally fine to good, except for two things.  The walking, and the stuff you walk on.  Which makes it a mostly ok game, that doesn't really stack up to others in the genre.  If you just want to relax and take in the scenery and music, this is a pretty chill title that is probably worth it.  If you want a tightly calibrated platformer/walking simulator with a tangible world to be in, this may disappoint.This game comes up really short on the two things you need in a walking sim/puzzle platformer.  The terrain doesn't match the bounds/physical geometry.  So, what you end up with is invisible walls and platforms you're constantly bumping up against, which can make you have to start over on some jump pattern or other nonsense.  Second is the motion.  It isn't fluid and your avatar makes these wide unwieldy turns that make precise control next to impossible.  Jumps feel delayed and never get the immersion or experience that you're in this world.  You just have a CGI'd fox that doesn't even stand on the ground but floats an inch above it on 2 feet.These two things together make for an ultimately poor experience in a game that really would need both to shine.  Graphics are mostly ok, there are some holes and missing polygons where can peer into the void of the unrendered, and they happen more than they should.  But, overall this is a pleasure to look at.  Puzzles aren't too challenging or needlessly complex, but still feel meaningful to progress.Finally, while this game looks good, it isn't amazing and looks on par for a game that might have come out a few years ago.  That said, this is one of the few titles that really cooks my graphics card for some reason, so ymmv.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I do wish Steam at least had a “neutral” option, because this option doesnt best express my opinion from a simple glance. I dont tend to give reviews, but i love games with animals and I feel maybe my review will give insight to others who enjoy these kinds of games- i dont hate this game at all but i want to see more animal games and i want to see them come up with quality and unique ideas instead of repeating trends and not polishing many aspects that should be focused on.if youre itching for a new animal based game after playing all there is, then definitely give this game a shot, it wont hurt and i dont think the price is that bad. the game is not awful, and i liked parts of it. but i have also played loads of similar games that did what this game attempted, far better that this. the game play is simple, its mostly wandering around solving simple puzzles with a few abilities. obviously many walk sim/puzzle games lack more features and its not really a problem... but i do feel the game direction is some area was a bit messy in that i saw no reason for certain aspects to be there other than to have a little fun moment (ex. the ice slides). this game has different “goals” you can achieve... theres simple puzzles and then theres ancient humans you can find using a staff, along with some carvings on stone you can uncover. Now, the puzzles are a major part of the progression, but the humans and carvings are optional it seems. and i will be honest, i see no reason in finding them (and i know they give skins, but that is just a simple extra addition to me tbh)... they really dont anything to the story or game. the stone carvings kind of hint history, but barely any at all and feels just as pointless to hunt down. controls are a bit wonky- the animation in conjunction with it are not very smooth sometimes and the way your character snaps to almost any surface makes some movement a bit odd and the camera will jump up and down as you go over these small bumps in the land.. jumping can also be hard to handle in tight spaces or with speed and the geysers were definite odd to handle. Towards the end of the game i found the gameplay kind of tedious (chapter 7 mostly). lots of running huge distances simply to bark at something and follow another path...not super engaging. the puzzle a just very simple and repeat over and over. the solutions are super easy to figure out. The game is quite pretty, i most love the landscapes. this is probably the most positive aspect of the game, but i do feel some areas are just a bit too short and some are way too long/spread out. aside, it is still fun to run through. the effects and all look lovely. it is not the highest quality graphics either but i dont personally care, as i imagine many others dont. but looks dont save every other part of this game. i beleive this is important enough to have its own category.first things first, theres a lot of back/forth about the barking. lets get the facts straight- if you know anything about foxes, you’d know that while they  bark...they also make other noises that are waaay more common than that barking. yips and whimpers and growls. it sounds unnatural to hear the same bark every time and that is what gets me about the dev(s) claiming foxes bark so this is okay... if you pick an animal for your game the least you could actually do it know what it sounds like and add variety to make it natural. there are probably loads of free stock sounds of foxes that would fit more than that. the devs can claim foxes bark but if they looked a little more theyd know full well they bark in specific scenarios and not All The Time.in general the music is nice, but i cant be mistaken that im hearing like the same tracks? do they just sounds similar? it got repetitive. i think there was a mistake in trying to use the music to cover up environmental sounds, its quite empty when youre playing. Spoilers ahead.Alright so, i have the most to say about this end. the game is “speechless” and i know in general that may turn people off, thats fine, its not for everyone. i have played numerous speechless games that i LOVE...so i have to say- the speechless story in this game really fell flat in many areas... theres a lot of ways to do it well and i dont think it was done that well here.right off the bat, the introduction really did not catch me, the “first chapter” was kinda bland and really didn’t imply a single thing to me about what was happening... you are a fox on their own, and come across a spirit fox. You follow it through the world to solve some problem with a weird red disease infecting the land. a simple story is fine, but it lack so SO much character. and there is no lore to additionally back up an already simple concept. i understand some people may have a soft spot for the animal focused story and i wont say i didnt enjoy it to some extent. but i am kind of surprised by the praise it is getting! the fox is barely even a ‘character’ in this story, as in... they dont really have a personality and nor does the spirit. you follow through the world learning almost nothing about it aside from the important points which occur at the end mostly--  the ending is what gets me most, because you expect things to be tied up but honestly it did not bring much closure or sense to the actions you made or what was happening. they didnt explain much of any "why" to your fox being  etc. It all felt like there wasnt anything back up the concepts, thats also why the lack of 'lore' is important to note. It brought zero depth to the story. but i digress- the point is, is that this game really lacks in its story telling. i have played good speechless games. this game couldve used body language and animation to tell about the characters, more visual world building to imply lore and history, flashbacks to tell more history, etc.  i have played many “animal walking sim with puzzles” games and i have liked a lot of them. Spirit of the North lacked in many areas and failed to be a completely enjoyable experience for me. Game play was fine but sometimes wonky, audio was alright, story lacks in many ways and the visuals are probably the best part.... i am giving this game a negative review because i dont see why it is so positive, and it plays off many recent things found in many other animal walking sims- which i really have issue with. theres a bit of a trend these past few years with making ‘unique’ walking sims, by adding an animal into the mix. i think it seems different and people are just hopping on it because there is a lot of interest for more animal based games. and i want that! but i want things that are unqiue, try new things, and dont copy/fall into trends. Spirit of the North falls into many basic trending ideas (animal player, abandoned civilization story, sentient object guides you, attempts a touching story, etc)That is my honest view on the game. As i said if you played all other animal games out there, like i have, then play it if you really want. but i dont think this game is anything that special in comparison to others.would reccomend these games too: Shelter 1, Shelter 2, Paws, Fe, AER Memories of Old, Gris, The First Tree, Lost Ember, Abzu, Journey, Eastshade.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North has some of the best graphics I've ever seen in an indie title, has neat little touches and details to the fox's animations which were cute to watch, has interesting gimmicks, and DID I MENTION YOU CAN PLAY AS A FOX...so why am I giving this a thumbs down? Well, the gameplay leaves a lot to be desired, and I hate to say that most of the game I found quite boring since I really wanted to enjoy this one. There's a severe lack of direction at certain portions of the adventure due to the massive open fields your fox often runs though. What the adventure does contain though is almost constantly doing the same monotonous things over and over again to the same few music tracks. There are interesting gimmicks presented, however most of the time they hardly get time to shine. While the first 2/3's of the game are quite boring and even feel rushed at times, the final 2-3 chapters were enjoyable, unique, and showcased what the rest of the game could have been like. The game is beautiful, and the fox is charming, but I sadly can't recommend this one.Pros:- Insanely good graphics for an indie title- Fun and cute little animations- Interesting mechanics- Beautiful musicCons:- Boring gameplay- Lack of direction- Short for the money- While the music is beautiful, there aren't many songs present

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. There is no narrative storytelling, but the environment tells the story instead. The world itself is gorgeous. The gameplay mostly consists of solving small puzzles while moving along in the world. There is also some occasional platforming. _childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me so much of The First Tree, just without the voiced narration. The First Tree was a very inspirational game for me. And I can say this one is closely comparable to it, except it has a big step-up graphics-wise. It spoke to me sentimentally because of the Northern Lights and how I have a soft spot for it. And also just because of how beautiful the world is, along with the magical soundtrack which was remarkable. The only problem with the game was that some things felt unpolished and finicky, but that didn't ruin the game experience. I had a great time playing it, and I would recommend the experience 🦊
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Well I poked my nose into invisible walls that wouldn't even let me fall off the edge nor get close enough to it to look at the landscapes. Then I got to hold forward while character was limping very slowly while lore tablets were lighting up. Then I got to fall through the water, and since there is *no water under the water*, the poor fox got to be stuck there forever, since I quit.Walking simulators are just not my thing. I played barely an hour, sure. But that was more than enough time to get the impression of controls and how much freedom I'd have in the levels.-The music is pretty.-The fox is pretty, and the fur looks nice on it. The animations (except the bark, which looks weird) are neat, but not quite fluid. Sometimes turning is just a sudden snap to a new direction.BUT ALSO-The jumping is clunky and you won't enjoy your time with it, that much is evident from the first half hour. It doesn't feel wrong, but jumps are very obviously only meant for certain spots, and you don't have much any freedom with it. There is a path you have to jump up right after you leave the cave in chapter 2. Fail the first jump and attempt to jump up to where you fell from. You won't be able to, since you'll slide right off even if it looks jumpable.-You'll be immediately faced with an invisible wall if you decide to walk back in the very beginning. No dead end or a slide to prevent you from going too far back, just an invisible wall. Same with trying to approach any ledges in my experience, you're just stopped preemptively and it leaves a sour taste in your mouth.-If you want to follow the path in chapter 1 along with your ghost friend like I did - think again. It moves very slowly, and there's not much reason for it. There are no sights to admire for more than a couple seconds, no nooks nor crannies to explore. The locations in that chapter are empty and anything that looks like a fork forms back into a single main path maybe 10 meters ahead. After you inevitably outrun the ghost it'll appear later in the level though. I wish the whimsical reviews about "playing with the guardian spirit" were true, but as it is the beginning of the game is just you following a very slow NPC with no sense of excitement nor challenge through a corridor set up with pretty lights. Perhaps that could be considered "playing" in a retirement home, but a video game with the looks and music such as this one could've made it much better.I was expecting Ori, but what I got out of this was disappointment, to be honest. There is never a reason to skimp out on gameplay. Yeah-yeah, start of the game and all that, but it was such a poor first impression that any excitement I had about playing it was murdered in chapter 2. I was hoping first levels would pull me in and make me want to play the game more so I can explore and enjoy its movement systems, but instead I got thrown into a slow-walk segment within the first half an hour.Also the loading screens are abrupt. No fade out or anything, just a sudden jump to logo.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game, with a very meaningful story that is very well conveyed without the need of a narration or spoken language. _childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

Following an attempt to destruct some of the plague which caused the Guardian to disappear in the first place, the ancient floor falls appart and while the spirit keeps guiding you, you eventually fall for your last sleep.Having been alone for so long, the Spirit isn't ready to let his first friend since forever to die, giving you a part of its ability and while It still follows you as a Whisp, you are now given the task to eradicate the plague so you can join back the sky and wake up the long lost Northern Lights.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: One of the most visually beautiful games I've ever seen. The music is gorgeous throughout, though it does repeat endlessly and can get a little annoying if you're playing for a long session. The fox is adorable and lifelike and so cute and enjoyable to play! Cons: The movement mechanics can be fiddly and frustrating, particularly turns and jumps. So many of the jumps have to be timed SO precisely, and I had to attempt them over and over and over. The puzzles were either simple and easy, or completely impossible to figure out without resorting to help from Google. Having to stop and go look up how to get past certain puzzles quickly became annoying. The final Chapter of the game gives you zero hints or directions, you're just left in a massive, wide-open spirit/Heaven type of landscape. It's gorgeous, but trying to find the last few puzzles/clues was just too bothersome and I didn't have the patience to trigger the official ending. Overall, it was still worth playing just for the breathtaking beauty of the Icelandic landscapes, the lovely music, and the charming little fox.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing game - Great soundtrack. - Great story - Peaceful - breathtaking landscapes - Simple story-line but like I said, relaxing, casual plat-former... You will find yourself in vast areas wandering around at times trying to figure out the next area to go.  I think the story was well driven by the gameplay, finding myself wanting to find out what the chapter held for me.  I found this game while searching for similar games to Stray, as in you are a fox in the old, mystical lands of Iceland in this game.  Again, I think the key word is a bit of patience with this game.  The music seemed to help when running around in circles and realizing turning to your spirit self to walk on water or go through a river bend was the solution the whole time an hour later...  I enjoyed the game and the emotional, pleasing ending - hope you enjoy as well

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game. Gorgeous graphics, serene music. An absolute steal for the price. The puzzles get increasingly challenging, which is good. Except when you're stuck in the middle of a chapter and you can't save. Auto save only happens at the end of a chapter, so if you don't complete the chapter and have to sign off for any reason, you will have to redo the whole chapter from the beginning. I'd like to see a touch more guidance in some places. Lots of the game has contextual clues to help you figure out generally where you're supposed to be headed. But there are times where you're in a huge, wide space, and you just have to wander around until you find something. There are also parts where you finish a puzzle, and then you're supposed to back-track. But you could waste a lot of time trying to move "forward" before you figure that out.

_childDocuments_.review: There's just something about this game...The premise is relatively simple, starting you off with little knowledge but giving you gentle nudges along the path. As you play and explore, you pick up more and more of the story. The game play becomes more complex as the story progresses, adding new moves that you will need to learn and master to gain the full experience. That's what this really is; It's less of a game and more of an experience with a few puzzles thrown in that will leave you learning more as you figure them out. If you like games that are more exploration and something to experience, then this might fit the bill. In that, it's similar to the way that Journey or RiME play out. The soundtrack adds well to the experience, evoking moods that easily match what you see playing out on screen.It's not perfect, however. There are spots where the game could use some refinement. Some of the puzzles offer few to no hints on how or what to do to progress, and these spots can be infuriating at times. It'll take patience and exploring to find what you've missed, or where you can climb even though it doesn't look like you can. That's another point of issue: Movement. The environment is somewhat inconsistent on what you can and cannot do, and the hit boxes and usable surfaces are a little haphazard. One moment you can be standing on air and the next, you can't climb up an incline much like those you have before. Other times, you MUST climb an incline that looks like you shouldn't be able to climb it based on previous experience. In that, you'll need to take your time to explore and find out what is and isn't permissible. Overall, I'd say it's well worth playing. At the time of writing this review, I've played 10 hours here on Steam and at least the same on PS4, all for the purpose of enjoying and exploring the environment. After all, there's something about this game that keeps drawing me back to the experience again and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty interesting game. Its pretty light on the puzzles and easy to get through, with most of the entertainment coming from the exploration and landscapes visited along the way. There's a collectible to find which justifies the exploration, but after you do that (and collect what other achievements you're after), there's probably not much point into picking up the game.With exploration hunting, I clocked in at around 10 hours of play. Just charging through probably gives you about 3-4 hours of play time, maybe 5 considering the puzzles. So keep that in mind while deciding if the game is worth it for you. It was an enjoyable enough experience for myself from a sale.

Great for when you want to take a break from FPS, RPGs, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was a nice experience. The story was nicely told with carved ancient murals. BUT I would recommend buying the game only when it is on sale.From Chapter 4 it was getting boring. Repeating puzzles only in a different way or slightly more difficult. The constant charging on the flower was just annoying at some point. Running back and forth lengthens the game unnecessarily.The control when it comes to jumping is very imprecise.The fox suddenly jumps in the wrong direction or is stuck in the walls or even stands in the air instead of on the platform. Sometimes, especially towards the end, it got frustrating for me. It ruined the mood. The atmosphere was best at the beginning and at the end. A little bit more could have happened during the long trip, for example, smaller cutscenes between the foxes or memories when the world was still in order etc. So the middle of the game was just repetitive for me. Maybe that was the intention, but for me it was too long.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give this game a negative review. The art direction is superb and the music is wonderful. The game manages to pull you into a soothing atmosphere and you have moments where you truly get surprised at the beauty it can show you. I love hiking and some of the environnments brought me the same feelings of peace and awe I have when I'm surrounded by nature. But all of these massive positives get overshadowed by the clunkyness and the gameplay. The puzzle aspect could be great, I actually love puzzle games (even though thinking hurts), but this game tends to mix puzzle and open world elements in one, making you search for the puzzle more than you puzzle. The maps are too big (which is why I feel like it tried to have open world elements to it), it leads more to confusion and frustration than fun. The environnements also tend to repeat each other and blend into one which doesn't help the confusion. My least favorite part was the awkward platforming, it really ends up frustrating you more than it does calm you. The game seriously needs polishing. It's such a shame really! Especially for such a beautiful game. Sometimes I even thought that making it a walking simulator with a bigger focus on its story (which is a bit vague and open to interpretation) could have been a better direction for the game and give more space for the beautiful art and experiences the game can offer. Last thing I want to add is that there were moments in this game that blatantly felt too long, painfully long. This is mainly due to the maps being too big and some of the puzzles not being intuitive enough. I understand you need some level of thinking to solve puzzles, but some of them really had the solution hidden away from you within repeating map decor which is just... painfully frustrating. It's not a fun feeling to waste your time trying to search for a solution that doesn't make much sense. I heard they are releasing a sequel for this game, I am interested to see if the negative aspects have been worked on and fixed/improved. I still think this game is worth experiencing because it truly is beautiful. But I have a hard time recommending it unless you're willing to sit throught its flaws. The beauty and art does help forget about the game's shortcomings, which is a massive positive and a massive testament to the art direction being phenomenal.I truly wish only the best for the developpers and artists behind this project. I understand making a game is difficult and involves so so much. Although I give this game a negative review, I truly appreciate the experience it brought me.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: My wife saw this title during the last Steam Winter Sale, and the pretty environments with a cute fox was all she needed to want to play. I watched her for most of the game, and really that's most of what this game is. With no exposition and no real cutscenes the story is a bit vague, and most of the world is a gigantic empty mass with puzzles scattered inbetween. For what it is, this works well enough -- Spirit of the North is essentially a walking simulator, and the environments are spectacularly done with a solid soundtrack to make exploring enjoyable and atmospheric.Where the game ultimately falls short is that there is actually very little game. The platforming elements are clunky, both in controls and in collision boxes in-game, and the huge expanse of the world often provides minimal guidance on where to actually go. Sometimes things which seem optional become mandatory, and others the required path is a tiny little jaunt off a gargantuan field or hillside that takes about 5 minutes to walk around. The puzzles are relatively simple, but this game is also difficult to do in one sitting so it's easy to forget some very subtle things that the game briefly shows you once and then expects you to remember hours later.While it's clearly a labor of love from the developers, I don't think the game is worth the full price tag. We came in at about 9 hours of game time to complete, maybe a bit less, and the level of polish and the underlying content on this title is not such that I think it warrants a $20 purchase. However, I think this is a great title to pick up on sale, especially for kids or for anyone just wanting a casual experience. I think we picked it up for $8-10 or something in that range, which I think is fair.Certainly an impressive amount of work for two guys doing it on their own, and the underlying flaws are understandable in this context.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a spirit fox simulator in which you do whatever spirit foxes typically do. As a spirit, you are sort of wise, but you are also a fox, so you will spend an indefinite amount of time barking at pieces of stone while trying to figure what to do. To put it in another way, Spirit of the North is like one of those rare poems by amateur poets that do not turn out like complete garbage. You can clearly tell that the guy does not use metrics very well, and a number of things are quite commonplace, but all in all he has written a pretty little thing.To put it in another way yet, Spirit of the North is a puzzle adventure game by a small indie company that specializes in 3D models. I mention the specialization of the company because the 3D art of the game is very well made (a few parts are downright beautiful and inspired), while neither the control system nor the interaction between the character model and the environment are particularly polished. Usually it goes smooth, but some jumps for example can get a bit awkward.Some people have defined this game as a walking simulator, but that may be a relevant description for the initial part of the game at best. The game soon asks you to solve simple puzzles of the type, "find key, open door." Of course, the key is spirit foxness and the door... Well, the door often is an actual (stone) door.Unfortunately, in my opinion, the game works better when the puzzle component is at minimum and the exploration component is at maximum (my favorite chapters probably are the 1st and the 7th). This is both because of the awkward controls and because a fox works better as a fox than as Lara Croft.Puzzles are actually well designed. The game does not like to give you hints on how to procede, and yet you manage to find everything at the very moment you thought you were lost. Puzzles are in fact relatively simple, I was never stuck for longer than... five minutes, I guess, but not so simple that some people will not get stuck. In the middle part of the game, however, they become a bit repetitive, tedious, and a bit frustrating because of that.This game is far from polished and certainly not something that everybody would enjoy. However, if roleplaying a fox in the snow is your thing, you may end up seeing the modest beauty of Spirit of the North.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on a big sale 90% off, I think the game is worth the full price, but seeing how often it goes on a sale I say wait for one. This game is good, but it’s not amazing, it doesn’t do anything particularly well, and it is not well polished, but it is a chill game. Spirit of the North is a nice small indie game, that has a lot of potential, that it didn’t fully reach. But it tells a nice story and takes you on a journey; you get to play as a cute fluffy fox :3 I say it’s very mid at 6/10, but a lot of people loves this game and I can absolutely see why. The atmosphere is captivating, and the environment is equally as stunning, and the soundtrack is beautiful. The jumping is sadly junk, and weird hitboxes are everywhere. I got pushed of platforms, or could jump up many times. This breaks the immersion and can lead to very frustrating moment. The level can be disorienting and you can get lost easily. This game needed more polish and it is very clear while playing. The biggest minus is that you  The game doesn’t save at all in chapters; only at the beginning of one. if you experience a game breaking bug, or just don’t have time to finish the chapter too bad you need to start from the beginning. This would have been an absolute deal breaker for me, I wanted to enjoy the game on the big screen with hight settings, and I just don’t have the time to sit for 40 min uninterrupted, the levels can get boring or confusing and I like to take frequent breaks. Luckily, I have a steam deck, where the game looks much blurrier but it runs well; I can just put the deck into a sleep mode and come back later. Not ideal, in chapter saving should be a thing and it makes 0 sense why this wasn’t implemented. It LITTERALYY SAY SAVING when you walk through a checkpoint. Don’t even get me how annoying is it to greet all the spirits in the spirit world. I don’t understand how somebody finished it without a guide. The spirit world as a whole doesn’t work so well and is confusing.  Spirit of the North is not a game for someone who gets frustrated easily. It is a good, small, not well polished indie game, that is worth the try. I enjoyed myself, apart from the frustration. The soundtrack and atmosphere carried the game all the way through and I’m excited for the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: At the fore Spirit of the North tells a simple story. You play as a red fox journeying across a Nordic tundra where your life becomes intimately intertwined with the Northern Lights, as you try to solve the mystery of the red “aurora” in the sky. But it is SO, so much more than that. There are not many titles that come to mind that moved me in such a way that I was brought to tears by the beauty of not just the visuals, but a story woven without a single word spoken. Spirit of the North wastes no time getting you into things right after the opening cutscene. As stated before you play as a red fox roaming the Nordic tundra where there are ominous red “auroras” crisscrossing the skies. This is an open world game and when I say open world I do mean open. I would say most of the time spent in my playthrough was wandering around exploring every little nook and cranny which there are MANY. This game 100% scratches that exploration itch that a lot of us have today not just for achievements, but the pure joy of exploring. Also, again, you play as a fox and who wouldn’t want to do that?As for controls and gameplay it was as expected for a PC release using a controller. My only real request would be the ability to have your fox walk backwards as this would help out immensely for the positioning of some of the puzzles. Spirit of the North can also be played with keyboard & mouse but I found it behaved a lot better for me with a controller. Gameplay again was as expected when you play as a fox,  though I would have loved to see a dig mechanic included as an added aspect to some of the puzzles. Not a bad mark against the game at all, just a suggestion for any game that features a fox as the player character. Beautiful does not even begin to describe the graphics in Spirit of the North. It is quite obvious that a LOT of time was spent making sure the fur physics on the fox were “perfect” and some of the backgrounds to the chapters almost looked photo realistic. I also quite enjoyed the level of detail put into the many ruins you come across/explore as the game progresses. In many cases I felt that I was really running what was left of an ancient culture after some unspeakable disaster.   Avoiding spoilers here, but I also want to highlight how unsettling the corrupted areas of the world look as you work through them which makes it all the more satisfying when you restore them to their original beauty. I will note here that I recommend picking the game up on PC or PlayStation as some of the graphics had to be downscaled for the Switch release and I feel that this game should be played with peak graphics. Trust me, it’s worth it.Now onto my favorite part of Spirit of the North, the soundtrack. I think I made it maybe fifteen minutes into the game before I began to muse on where I could listen to this soundtrack once I had completed the game. At times soft and atmospheric, at others somber and thoughtful I really can’t put into words how much the music really makes this game. One thing I can say though is that the song played during the end sequence is definitely what nudged me over the edge of “teary eyed” into the open weeping of being fundamentally moved. I would also like to note that in a game that contains zero dialogue music needs to take the place of a spoken narrative and the soundtrack of Spirit of the North pulls that off flawlessly. As for re-playability I would say high, very high for Spirit of the North. For the PC release there are achievements but even without those there is still high re-playability. I mentioned before that this is an open world game. Well, I can honestly say I think I spent over three or four hours on my playthrough just exploring or refusing to use the dash button so I could enjoy more of the scenery. Now, you could skip all the scenery and finish it faster but I do not recommend this as taking things slow is one of the things I really enjoyed. There is also an option to repeat chapters if you missed anything or just want to take in more of the landscape, which brings me to my next point on re-playability. Spirit of the North does have a slightly different ending if you find everything. Not multiple endings per say, but different and for the sake of spoilers I will say no more on that.All in all Spirit of the North is definitely a game I can highly recommend picking up along with it’s soundtrack. As puzzle/adventure games go this is one of my favorites I have played to date and I look forward to playing through it again soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is about the journey of a fox that stumbles upon a female spirit that is the guardian of the northern lights. A red plague corrupted the land causing destruction of the Shamans who used to worship this spirit and her own withdrawal. It's up to the player to stop the plague from spreading further and bring the Aurora back.One thing out of the way: The landscapes and areas the game presents to you are gorgeous. The levels are wise and big with collectibles and neat little puzzles. As a reward for the collectibles, you get different fur skins to customize your fox. It's certainly a pretty and relaxing game but I think the platforming could've been handled better as some areas were kind of a pain to deal with. The fox barking like a chihuahua is a bit off-putting and there are some issues with the physics but I don't want to nit-pick too much because for a game that was developed by only two people, it's really well-made.I advice everyone to not focus on the achievements too much as it would only ruin your first playthrough. This game is meant to be played at a slow pace without having to worry about anything so fretting over collectibles just robs from the experience Overall, I'd recommend this game for anyone that is searching for a relaxing experience which is not too challenging nor too sluggish.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North may not be particularly , but wow, does it pack an impact.It feels a bit like Journey, if you've played that. It's the same style of wordless environmental storytelling. It manages to be a lot more emotional than Journey is, though. Part of that is that you're not alone, accompanied by an enigmatic spirit-fox to guide you on your journey to rediscover the past and put a stop to the evil spreading across the land.The soundtrack is amazing, a lot of quiet piano that blends with the environments very well. And speaking of, the environments are wonderful, alternating between wide open fields you can streak around in and old ruined cities full of corruption. Plus some major story curveballs later on – this game may not use words, but it doesn't have to!One other interesting thing is, unlike any other game I've ever seen, there isn't even a hint that you're ever anything other than just an animal. It's a wonderful feeling to step into a game and just not be human for a bit.Overall, this is environmental storytelling at its best. It's an absolutely phenomenal ride, and 100% worth it – at full price, no need to wait for a sale.Oh, and I mean. Look at the controls screen.

_childDocuments_.review: There are several negative reviews about the UI and getting 'stuck'.  I agree that there should be a help button that would make your spirit companion go back through the next step to progress the game.  It does it once (usually) when it's an important step but I've never been able to get it to do it again.  Sometimes it's so important it repeats it.  The game does have some help in this fashion.  There are also online walkthroughs if you are truly stuck.With that in mind, this is a puzzle game.  If you are NOT a fan of puzzle games- this isn't for you!  The UI is limited for a reason, you play a fox so you have very limited interaction abilities.  You can bark, wag, jump, pick things up, 'Super Bark' (for any Bolt fans), run and swim.  That's about it.  The UI doesn't need to be complex for those functions so it's serviceable.If you really suck at easy to medium parkour style games... stay away from this one, it will drive you batty.  If you are a hard core parkour game player... you'll master this in a minute and those portions will be a cake walk... or jump.  You do have to have some minimal parkour skills to solve the puzzles.It's a cute, and relatively easy game through the first 3 chapters.  The first two are on rails, it's hard to mess them up but if you just blast through them you won't be able to reanimate all the Shaman's, which is part of the game and some of the puzzle quests.  If you miss a Shaman (one icon when you revive another will be different from the ones you've saved) you can stop and go replay the chapter with that down Shaman and find them.  In the early game, this is easy, in the latter parts, it's a pain.  You don't need all of them to 'win' but you get an achievement if you do.Lastly, the game is well done, it can be frustrating but any good puzzle game should test your patience.  Where it's challenging is that not everything is obvious as to where things go and what order to do them in.  You either get a feel for the thinking of fox (devs) or you don't.  If not, consult a walkthrough, they are common enough.  It's not worth banging your head on a wall for three hours to solve one of the puzzles.  Sometimes you just need a little boost and this game is capable of it.I got this on sale for $4.  It was a bargain at that price and if you see it inexpensively and are interested in puzzles games, snatch it up... it's worth the price of admission.  It can pull on your heartstrings though so if you are emotionally, uh, sensitive... you might want to avoid it or take breaks from it as needed.P.S. There are a lot of threads in the discussions about Foxes not barking or the reality of one being in Iceland, etc. etc.  If that kind of thing is immersion breaking (I'm not sure how 'immersive' a game about a spirit possessed fox solving puzzles in a frigid wilderness can be) then avoid this game.  I mean really, our foxes here just wanna eat my chickens, not sure about all the other stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely gorgeous!Now hype aside Spirit of the North represents so called "walking simulator" genre where main focus gets the narrative and exploration of the world like in Firewatch or The First Tree. In this case however entirety of the "story" is told through art style, world design and the music, no narrator or buddy to talk to. Nonetheless it worked out perfectly, like I said the game is absolutely beautiful and music doesn't stay far behind adding to the atmosphere.Our protagonist is also a major part of the whole picture as the game is also a pretty good fox simulator. He will bark, wag, squeal, sneeze, shake off after leaving the water, has animatet fur... Our Wisp companion also reacts to our actions and the environment itself bringing our attention to certain details.Gameplay wise there isn't as much to tell. We will get a few powers, solve some puzzles and look around for collectibles which award us with achievements and skins (somehow here it sounds so wrong...) for the fox, some very cool too ^^. Maps are both tight and open also featuring different environments so the visuals stay fresh.Obviously the game isn't perfect. With some maps being very big and collectibles not being as numerous we may end up in long searches for nothing. Some pieces of maps we can go to don't seem like we were supposed to reach but oh well no harm done there ^^". While the Wisp shows us where to go from time to time it's not always the case so getting stuck is possible, this is especially a problem in chapter 7 which is enormous and no clarity on what to do. Having to bark for each recharge of our powers does get tedious. Would be nice if we could swim a bit faster as we can sprint on land...That's about all the complaints I can think of, no bugs or technical difficulties. Although my framerate was unstable it's all on me for pushing high detail and  the end it wasn't a problem and eye candy here is important ^^So here it is: beautiful, emotional, mystical, well made. Still it is a game for specific audience, if you find this kind of gameplay or this genre overall boring then this game won't change your mind. For enthusiasts of it however it is a big treat ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game and let me tell you. It told a story without words. I loved the puzzles and (spoiler) seeing all the souls I saved at the end. I will for sure play through and find the ones I missed. I also really like that as you progress and reach milestones you unlock new fox skins with different light patterns. Overall a really solid, beautiful, and relaxing game with a story that was a pleasure to experience. P.S. Giving aurora walking at the end credits was so fun and a great way to end it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: WOW, another fox game, how original... With that being said, I don't have much to say. It's plain, it's boring, it's repetitive. The world is void of any life or interactability and is therefore not worth exploring (unless you want to collect all the shamans). The story is about as generic as you can imagine.There are abilities you acquire over the course of time, nothing special. However, that's probably the best part of the entire game, as you can dash through the map faster. It sucks how you recharge them, though, it would be better if the bar filled up automatically and you didn't have to search for blue flowers that are usually close by anyway; it just makes the game all that more repetitive.It doesn't help the game is rather short, clocking in at about 5 hours with a bit of exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful and captivating.When I got this, I was so excited and so in love I finished it in the first day. This game deserves more credit and attention than it currently gets. Definitely worth the $20, not to mention how kind the Dev's were. They dealt with me losing a shaman even though I only couldn't find it because it was in a deceiving place. Tay and Jakob, you two are the best devs I've seen yet. Keep on doin your thing, you two are awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: im gonna preface this here, to the team behind SOTN. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart for making this game. this was the most emotional moment in gaming i have ever had, this game was beautiful, well written and everything in between.to anyone who has 3-4 hours to spare please, please buy this game as it was a masterpiece from start to finish. once again, thank you so much to the team for creating this, this is gonna be a game that will forever hold a dear place in my heart. thank you so much.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Tunic does this game better; you play as an animal and have to use context clues to understand what is going on. Though, the story isn't exactly deep or emotional here. The visuals are generic and don't impress me. Weird how the fox model doesn't dynamically adjust its limbs based on the terrain, so it just floats above it if the surface is steep enough. Some of the rocks are hexagonal, which looked strange. Maybe this is implying they are man-sculpted. Sloppy terrain design; numerous floating trees or clipping pieces of terrain. Puzzles are both too easy and unintuitive because things aren't clearly explained. The stone-bearing sigils that you need to progress often blend into the terrain. The platforming is awful and clunky. I'd be more in favor of a cartoony game like this rather than a realistic one. Also, why do we have to make the story about people? And about people that no longer exist, at that. So boring. I hoped it was going to be an animal-focused adventure, with no people, which is an unexploited niche. The ending is alright. The final level is unintuitive. Let's hope that the sequel is better. 4/10 on the enjoyment scale.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This concept was really nice, I enjoyed being a fox and seeing all the pretty sights the game had to offer. That was probably the only thing I liked about this game. Whilst I enjoy a good puzzle, I consider myself to be decent at them, where I can usually do them with no issue. However, this game made me so frustrated with all of their puzzles, it sucked all the fun out of the game for me. Every few feet you take, there's always some kind of puzzle, they expect you to figure out right off the bat on what you're supposed to do, when it doesn't appear that obvious, I wondered around at least 10-15 minutes trying to figure out what I had to do, before I gave up and looked at a video on how to do it. All of the puzzles, I had to use a video to help solve it for me, as I couldn't for the life of me figure it out. Even the person in the videos looked just as confused as I was. Or, if I was close to figuring it out, it ended up being backwards on me, and I had to do it all over again, often times resetting my game to try again. There are spirits you're supposed to release along the way, although, I had no clue where some of them were, even after just wondering around all the time to try to figure out where either I needed to go, or how to do the puzzle. I would look in every nook and crack there was to try to find the spirit to release, but when I go onto the next area, and found another one, it would say I missed it, which I wouldn't have any idea where it would've been! I played through the whole game, as I was hopeful it would've gotten better, but it just got worse, and there were times where I was close to uninstalling it because of the frustration I felt with the puzzles, it destroyed the fun out of this game for me. Good graphics, decent music, but real crappy game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: When I asked for a game to help me during a time of mental volatility, Spirit of the North was one of the games recommended and the one that caught my attention the most. It was also the first game I decided to check out, and my gosh I'm glad I did. The graphics are beautiful (and I didn't even notice any lag), and the story (while one of the more silent & environmental ones I've seen) was gorgeous. The soundtrack complements the game, though there was one point I can recall that the music just abruptly cuts to a new track. The biggest issue I can think of is that the physics is a bit wonky to get used to, but once I did there weren't very many troubles to be had (outside of like one or two pesky jumps); that said, I had less annoyance with it than I did playing MGR's Bladewolf DLC, in terms of platforming anyways.I'd give this game a solid 8/10, it's not perfect but its highs are, indeed, pretty dang high. I will definitely check out the sequel once it releases!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Underdeveloped, works maybe as a showcase for an idea or a concept. Has technical issues, bad autosave system that forces you to restart the whole chapter, losing a lot of progress. Music is repetitive and becomes annoying soon. Spirit of the north is slow paced, which is usually fine by me but in this instance the slowness is artifically generated by making your fox hobble through a tedious maze or swim through a cave system which is just as slow. The controls are clunky as hell and overall the game is not fun to play, perhaps unless you are really into foxes IDK... Returned, awaiting refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Good:Controls are pretty good.Graphics are good.Bad:World design is terrible, very dead and artificial.Story is very bland and the way they tell the main portion of the story in the beginning is painfully slow and annoying.Music is as good as muted, serves no purpose.Running is unlocked in the story, even though you travel alot before unlocking it so you spend a long time jumping to move that little bit faster.The "energy" you use to solve the puzzles can be replenished endlessly at certain points, and they are EVERYWHERE, so the puzzles are not that good.Framerate is not very good especially when moving fast.You move very slow in water this is annoying considering how much water seems to exist in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy little game that was perfect to chill with. I had a cup of tea and 100% the game within two days of gameplay. I purchased this game on a 90% steam sale, so I only paid about $3 for it in total. The most difficult achievements are the kindered spirits and the flying squirrel in my opinion, but there are plenty of guides online . My biggest downside to this game is there is no actual story and narrator, you have to put it all together yourself. Which many people can find off putting, especially for a $20 full price game. I highly suggest buying it on sale to get the best bang for your buck. Sit back, enjoy, and fox your way through puzzles, a beautiful game, and a stunning soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game. Between the soundtrack and the visuals I feel this game is so underrated. Anyone who likes foxes or just animals and nature in general will love this game. I hope there is a sequel or some additional content that can dive into the story and explain it more because it seemed really interesting. 10/10 would definitely play again. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Great game to sit back and unwind (if you're not in a hurry to get all the spirit related achievements). Imo lacks a bit of polish esp. cutscenes and transition between scenes but damn the scenery is beautiful! Must be all those Quixel megascans =). A bit monotonous tho, some mountain flowers wouldn't hurt.  Fox go bork-bork! I wish foxxy was making other noises, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game. I honestly did. The graphics are beautiful, the animations on the fox are great. The music and atmosphere and environmental storytelling is great. But the main gameplay element of the game, jumping puzzles, are just way too janky to be fun. The jump mechanic is infuriating to begin with. You cannot make the smallest of jumps because without a good amount of forward momentum, all your fox does is hop in place. Aiming your jumps is very difficult, so is timing. Be prepared to spend hours trying and retrying the simplest of hops because the game decides you're a pixel short, or your fox decides all it wants to do is somersaults. Also, you can't save except at sparse autosave points, so be prepared to do it all over again when you inevitably rage quit.I got into this game and loved everything about it, but it turns into a rage game so fast I can't enjoy the beauty of it anymore. With a little bit smoother movement mechanics it would be a fantastic game, but unless you're a masochist gamer it just isn't fun past the first two chapters.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game that was easy to follow in the beginning but the controlling mechanics for some of the puzzles leaves you frustrated for the most part. I don't understand what the storyline is about. It is a pretty looking game. It would be easier if the directionals were either for just the mouse only or just the keyboard only. The combination of the two really only works for combat games, not a puzzle game. As are all puzzle games, trying to figure it out is the whole basis. I like a little bit more straight forwardness so that it feels more comfortable to solving the puzzles and not just "are you effing kidding me?" kind of aftertaste. Didn't get very far because the geysers threw me off course when trying to aim for a certain direction. Not bad of a game, though. Could use a little bit more work.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful. Stunning Graphics. Very enjoyable Story.Gameplay reminds me instantly of The Legend of Zelda, which should be in any case a big, big plus. Not overcrowded with Achievments, which seems a nice change these days.Soundtrack can be annoying at start, but gets better later.I also do love Foxes so... 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I usually write joke reviews but this game deserves a sincere one.This game is one of the only ones that actually awestruck me. The idea behind the game is a unique one and is rarely seen done well. The beauty of the game along with the well composed music set the mood for every single chapter. Throughout the game, the different challenges and puzzles will keep you thinking. If you were to 100% the game, it would take around 5-7 hours. It is a pretty short game, but it is worth the money.Although the game lacks consistency in the parkour aspect, the other aspects of the game outweigh it for sure. 9.8/10Would adventure with a spirit fox to the Icelandic mountains again
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a fox and you can bark, that's all that needs to be said.Honestly tho, i wish it had some objectives or gave you clearer directions at times, because i got easily lost in some chapters. That aside, it starts off a bit slow but it's a nice game overall. Very casual and simple, but that's what you need sometimes :)

_childDocuments_.review: From a baseline this game is amazing and adorable. However, one BIG problem I ran into about a quarter way of the game was inaccessibility. It's not possible to change the key-binds for control which, for me, is a big problem as I'm missing fingers on my left hand (where most of the controlling keys are bound) and I'm unable to click all keys needed to make sprint jumps ect.
