_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's time to write a review of this adorable game.I've played for a long time and I never got bored of this game. It's so atmospheric! Beautiful landscapes, relaxing music and intriguing story. Someone can say that plot's very simple, but I disagree. It's really mesmerizing and you immerse yourself in story. Inspiring atmosphere won't leave somebody indifferent! This game will forever remain in my heart and I think that I'll play it many time again and again) Many thanks to developers of this fantastic game. You're the masters of inspiring atmosphere!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The music is amazing. It broke my heart when I finished the full playthrough of the game simply because of the music. And MAYBE some of the action, but let's ignore that, shall we? :) The photo-mode in this game is excellent, no glitches (at least that I know of) and it's perfect for the map of the game. (Spoilers, skip this little end part if you don't wanna know) The Spirit Forest is gorgeous! The butterflies, blue mushrooms, rivers and shading are just mind-blowing. And the performance of each animation and chapter is not buggy WHATSOEVER. So, if you like story games, play this. Or Lost Ember. That game also broke my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Really worth the experience.The scenery is masterfully made and the gameplay is solid.This is a really peaceful game with a little bit of easy puzzle solving, a lot of platforming, and zero combat.It also rewards exploration, there's often something just tucked away off the path that makes looking worth while.There can be some frustration in realizing you've missed something and having to reload the last check point, which can't be done from the in game menu itself, it has to be done by going to the start menu and loading the check point of your choosing.There is also no key rebinding from what I can tell, although it uses WASD and is very standard with its controls I'm not sure if it lends itself to gamers who require this.The story is told through scenery and the markers found along the way, and it is accompanied by very beautiful, soft music.Over all I really love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The cutest most detailed game I've ever seen. You want to be a fox? Solve Puzzles? Play peacefully? these are just some of the perfect aspects of this game. What I love about this game is that the puzzles aren't "brain melting." They are quite simple and easy to complete. If I had more free time I would spend all day just exploring in this game. Foxes are my favourite animal and this game makes me happy every time I play it. The major con I have against this game is that the "Wizard skeletons" are actually really well hidden in some parts. Other than that I love this game and 100% recommend! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Cute exploration adventure game. Took me under 7 hours to complete and get all achievements.It's an intriguing adventure as you explore the ruins of a small civilization and try to root out the sickness that has spread across the land. The world is quite beautiful (it sorta reminds me of Skyrim or something from Star Wars), and the lore is pretty straightforward but interesting nonetheless. There's an overarching mood of somberness but at the same time tranquility and hope, which lends itself well to what is for the most part a walking simulator. There are several relatively basic puzzles (as well as a few more intricate), but I wouldn't call this a puzzle game. For the most part you should be able to just casually follow the story and enjoy the world. You can use a guide to make sure you get all the achievements, but if you explore as much as I do, then they shouldn't be much of a problem.The only negative I have is that the game doesn't seem completely polished. There are places you can get stuck, and some things don't always work quite the way they're supposed to. But it's good for the most part.Overall, I'll rate this 8/10. $20 seems pretty high for only a 6-hour story, but it goes on sale for $4-5 a few times a year, which is worth it in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a very simple walking simulator with levels made out of short puzzles.There are many invisible walls and the collision is messed up making some puzzles feel forced (for example you can't take an alternative route that seems possible) and the collectible puzzles (find the staff and bring it back to the shamans) sometimes become impossible because you left the staff in a place where it falls in the ground making it impossible to reach.Another missed opportunity is that the maps are huge but somewhat empty making it annoying and somewhat boring to complete all the collectibles (thankfully the staff starts to shine the moment you're close to the shaman!)The graphic is the main selling point of this game. It is simply stunning.The game is not replayable since the levels are always the same.Overall it is an ok game that needs some price adjustment (would never pay 16 € for this) but I wouldn't suggest it to any friend considering most people grew up with much harder puzzle/platformer games.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings about this game.I don't regret buying and playing it, but it definitely could have been  . . .  better. It has a great concept, wonderful looks and a good length.Unfortunately, it lacks some sort of guidance, creating boring and - most negatively - frustrating experiences.I love to play as a fox, but the fox character in this game is replaceable. It has no fox-specific characteristics, movement or attributes, that are essential part of the game. It could as well have been a human or any other character you can think of.Overall, this game feels like a missed opportunity for a great game to remember.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sold on this game after the first couple chapters but wanted to give it a chance since it has so many positive reviews. It really starts to pick up in Chapter Three.Spirit of the North was worth playing even though I don't typically like platformers. The visuals are beautifully bright and vibrant, and the soundtrack is calming. I liked that there weren't any enemies and there wasn't much in the way of time pressure so I could just enjoy the game and the scenery. I was looking for a puzzle game and though this didn't have much in the way of puzzles, it was still thoroughly enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: First, it is only partial steam deck usable. I could not get it to work docked and after fiddling about, I could only get it to play in hand held sporadically. Though it shows that I played over 5 hours, most of that time was attempting to make it work. As for the game, it is not really special. The jump command is wonky and the world looks like paid assets. Each area has a staff to find and hand over to a corpse but since everything in a few chapters is Brown, finding the brown stick then the brown corpse was more blindly wandering around until a command was prompted.  The commands to do things were awkward also where you had to sometimes be in a very specific spot to have it usable, The fox's features are not great and though you can earn new looks, they were not really great either. I read reviews where people wept from the story as they played through but maybe that was at the very end, because I didn't really connect with the fox. I connected more with a square in "Thomas was Alone" (BTW  Thomas was Alone is a Fantastic Game!)This is a game that I should love but the pain to get it to work, the bland world, and wonky game play just made it not fun. I tried to push through because I saw it was short and I could not get a refund, but it just is not worth it. The idea is cool so I think that makes me more disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game for everyone. The story is simple and barely present, puzzles and platforming are easy and the game overall lacks any challenge. Gameplay is quite short - finished the game in 5 hours with most of the achievments complete. You will spend most of the time looking for stuff in huge open areas. And it is fine that way. Because it allows you to focus on the gorgeous scenery and nice music. Avoid this game if you are impatient or not in a mood for relaxing chill experience.I've seen few people complaining about controls in reviews, but personaly I have not found any issue using a controller. It is a little bit floaty, but nothing out of ordinary. Found maybe one or two weird jumps but thats it. I would absolutely recommend this to anyone, who just wants to turn off and have a good time for few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: "Spirit of the North" is a chill adventure game with nice visuals and a good instrumental soundtrack that was a fairly quick game without feeling rushed or lacking. I appreciated that there was visual storytelling through wall art or the extras without it being integral that you find every single detail as you play. This, combined with the simple puzzles, makes this game a nice option for a game to play to relax or unwind. Only issue (and it is just me nitpicking) is that the fox barks instead of making typical fox noises. Still cute overall, and I enjoyed all of the little touches with landscape features you would see in Iceland, movements that mimic a fox's natural movements, and the interactions between the spirit and the fox. Looking forward to playing "Spirit of the North 2"!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Most aggravating game I have ever played--polar opposite of what I was looking for from an adventure game. Great story line, beautiful world concept art, But the controls are TOTAL ♥♥♥♥. The fox character cannot be reliably moved and so though you know what to do and where to go you're spending HOURS trying to make simple moves. Horrible, just horrible. Also, so much work went into attention to detail, but with total overkill at the expense of basic game functionality. The fox shakes EVERY TIME it gets out of the water (which you fall into due to lack of control all the time), meanwhile you cannot aim where you're jumping. How did this pass basic game testing / quality assurance?
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY tried with this one. It has the makings of everything I'd enjoy - breathtaking environments, incredible soundtrack, AND I play as a cute little fox? Sign me up!However, not all is what it seems.I've not played this on console, but I hear it runs much smoother than this PC port. This version...is horrendous. The controls are unresponsive and jittery. I felt like I had little control with what direction my little fox friend wanted to go. The platforming on this game is so clunky and there is no fluidity when jumping. The camera also felt stiff, and I feel like it lagged with when I was turning the fox (or vice versa).My biggest gripe, though, is the amount of bugs and glitches in this port. The amount of times I clipped through walls or water is too many to count. I would be forced to reload my most recent checkpoint, which often happened to be at the beginning of the chapter. So I'd sit through the same, slow opening scene to get back to where I was. It ended up leaving a bitter taste in my mouth at how often I had to redo parts, and ultimately I couldn't finish the game. If what people say about the console version is true, I'm more inclined to give this game another go on PS4. However, I would not recommend this PC version.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: the visuals are really really cool to look at, very pretty landscapes and images, although its not perfect, its sometimes hard to control, (i started with mouse and keyboard, but found its much easier with a controller), and the game doesn't do an amazing job with explaining where to go, especially with bringing spirits their staff. but other than that, its a really amazing game, i loved it
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Pro:- really nice scenery- background music is mostly relaxing- great for playing occassionallyCon:- Controls. I often had it, that I wanted to go into one direction and jump, and suddenly the character jumps into another direction.- Collision detection isn't a thing... or it is. My character often was stopped from corners while I couldn't see anything stopping me. On the other hand if you're carrying around a Staff in your maw, the staff will completely ignore the surroundings.- No explanation about the story. After five hours I'm through the game and don't know anything about why the world is empty, why there is a fox spirit or anything. You find some murals, but I couldn't figure out at all whats happening.- Staffs. In the first five chapters you can ignore them. Suddenly in the last three chapters you MUST find them to progress through the level! Of course the game doesn't tell you this.- Mage spirits. You can "revive" them with the Staffs you can find. But they don't say anything, not giving clues about the world.- Rewards. You can unlock other skins, but ONLY by finding enough Staffs and reviving enough Mages with them. I finished the game with 20 of 24 achievements done, and got... NOTHING, because at some point I just didn't care about the staffs anymore. The game doesn't tell you, you need Staffs for unlocking rewards. In the end I had around half of the mages done, didn't got a single skin for it.Summary:The game isn't really rewarding anything. It's nice for playing then and when if you need something more relaxing. Wouldn't recommend getting it for the full price (especially on consoles, as the prices are twice as high there!)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Visually this game is gorgeous. A lot of love went into building the areas you get to explore in this game. It tells a a story and provides puzzles without any words and it is rich with references to Icelandic mythology.The controls however, were a bit fiddly, especially on some of the jumping puzzles. It wasn't dealbreakingly bad though.Also you get to be a fox, a very fluffy one.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: As a lonely fox we travel through a world affected by a disaster and filled only with a remnants of civilization. Our only companion is a spirit fox, guardian of the Northern lights, who is now leading us deep inland, where we will find the source of the cataclysm. Even though there is no imminent danger the journey isn't going to be easy. Luckily our guardian spirit will help us to overcome many obstacles standing in our way. is a fox walking simulator with an occasional platforming. The game is pretty much linear and even though you can "explore" and run freely around, there is still only one route for you to go and only one way to solve the "puzzles". The puzzles consist mostly of you harvesting energy from flowers, reaching some unreachable place and powering up a mural, door or some secret stone to be able to progress further. With new abilities new kinds of puzzles await you, so you can properly enjoy them. ;)Solving the puzzles wasn't difficult, just sometimes hitting the right timing or angle was a challenge. Failing could led to a slight frustration of redoing the cursed section… and it was usually caused by platforming sequences, but I got truly stuck only three times, so it wasn't any horrible experience.On your journey you can find old staves laying forgotten in the ruins, you can then take them to long dead shamans and set their souls free with it (you have to find them first though and some of them are hidden pretty well, but at least as you get closer the staff will light up). You get rewarded for your hard work with skins for your fox! You can then change your appearance to your liking. (The way to change your skin was rather confusing for me - when you save enough shamans flashing "P" appears on the screen. It leads to options and there are hidden rewards,  that's it, I have completely missed that two times. ^^)I really liked the colorful graphics and music, both created a great relaxing mood. The fox is very pretty with cute sounds. I enjoyed how he jumped around or moved in the water. The little details - how he dried off when getting out of water, slow motion - was also rather nice. Game saves only on checkpoints, but you can access that checkpoint anytime from the menu. Like this you can replay only a part of a certain level and don't need to do it whole again. Also you can see where you missed a shaman, which can save you some time.The game isn't of course perfect. When leaving water after a long time he will dry off in a locked sequence when you can't do anything. If you are stuck in the platforming part around water it can be tedious. Not even mentioning that the fox wouldn't be able to take out the staff from rooms or caves the way he does it. ;) The world is bare without much to explore (yeah, I know that it was devastated). But I wasn't disappointed, I have actually enjoyed this calm journey. Story is hidden in the ruins, in the old bones scattered around. Even without words I was filled with emotions. As a side note, I would like to pinpoint another game with a similar setting, . I have really enjoyed it, if you would like you can read more in . The sounds our guardian spirit makes reminded my so much of my Lumini. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Pro:Solid gameplay with great atmosphere. There are cure moments like getting the spirit bark in reply which I did about once every minute... It's fun to explore the levels with the beautiful landscape or scenery.Cons:Not exactly a walking  - or running - simulator, but if you expect a lot of action or intricate puzzle solving, you'll be disappointed.Conclusion:Get the game if you like animals, beautiful landscapes, slow-paced and relaxing gameplay. Don't get it if you're looking for puzzles or action. And if you play it - continue at least through chapter 2, the first chapter is not like the rest of the game.My main issue with the game is that the two weakest levels are the first and the last. And that's a problem. The first level almost caused me to abandon the game and only by reading some more reviews I found out there actually happens something later on. And I don't think I'm the only one. If you check how many players got past the first achievement, it's few, less than 30%. I assume the first level put them off. Which is a shame because it gets much better.And then the last level - some minor spoilers ahead - it felt rushed, like they designed a level and then didn't really think how to best use it. It's suddenly very open-wordly which doesn't work well for this game. I felt a bit lost. And why do you have to run on that path for what felt like 5 mins? It kills the atmosphere. The whole last level took me away from the end of chapter 6 which was powerful. But I forgot all about it because of the tediousness of chapter 7. If they had cut that last level to about 20% of the current size and made it a bit more straightforward it would have been great.And so, while the mediocre first level prevents players from actually playing the game, the mediocre last level makes you forget, to some extent, how great the rest of the game had been.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game; it's gorgeous and has an interesting premise, but overall I feel like the game could have used more polish. The controls don't feel fluid and the fox will often continue moving on his own, with no input from you (which can make the geyser platforming incredibly frustrating). There are invisible walls everywhere, which normally is fine, but they don't play well with the controls. You could hit an invisible wall and then the game immediately makes the fox run off in a different direction (another case of the fox moving on his own), which could end up making you fall off whatever cliff you just spent 10 minutes climbing. And half the time you're wondering if you're actually able to climb up that area or not because the jumping in general just does not work and the invisible walls make it worse.The fox also gets Stuck.On.Everything. He must have a huge hitbox, because I was having to give random rocks and boulders a wide berth cuz otherwise I'd get stuck on them. And when there are multiple parts of the game that are on timers, this becomes very annoying. This also ties in to the wonky jumping that the fox does; is the fox just getting stuck on rocks during the jump and it actually IS somewhere you need to go, or is there an invisible wall there and you should just ignore that area? Naturally, this made exploring a hassle, instead of a joy, like it should have been. Even if you try to jump over every obstacle in your path in order to not lose any speed, the fox still somehow gets tangled on it and everything comes to a standstill. Why can't I jump over a couple of small rocks?? Why does he come to a complete halt and then seems to tip-toe jump over the rock/debris before continuing on?Also, why are the maps so insanely large? You could run an entire map of ARK inside these levels, and yet the story generally has you going in a linear path. If you want to find the 1 collectable the game offers, though, then you need to explore at least a little bit, and the huge maps and control issues ruin the fun of finding these things. I do love the fact that you can unlock different fox skins if you find enough collectables though; it was nice to see some variation.I also would have liked some clearer directions/hints as to what the game wanted you to do. There were times where I completely misunderstood the visual cues and spent waayy too long running around in circles and not making any progress. That may have just been a me thing, though, as I did eventually figure it out on my own, so take that with a grain of salt.There is also very little story involved, and what snippets of story there were, were confusing. I'm still not entirely sure what happened in the game but its open to interpretation, so this really wasn't much of a drawback in the end. But mixed with the other issues the game has, the overall experience just left me feeling underwhelmed.:There's a lot that the game does right (visuals, ambience, music/sound effects, immersion) but I feel that the negatives far outweigh these positives. Might be okay at a sale price. And I can't even call it a chill, relaxing game when you're constantly frustrated at the gameplay and there's very little reward for exploring. Overall, I would have finished the game a lot sooner (and enjoyed it more) if I wasn't constantly getting lost on unnecessarily huge maps, fighting the controls, and getting stuck on rocks and therefore failing timed puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game quite enjoyable and relaxing overall, it was fun running around exploring the place with the game's solid controls.I escaped the map a few times, found a softlock, ran into a missing bit of wall collision.I don't see those as problems though, most of it you can only find if you're specifically trying to do that, if anything it made the game much more interesting for me.Knowing that the game wouldn't have an invisible wall in the vast majority of places made for a fun game of figuring out if I could somehow reach any given spot, and surprisingly often I could, or I could get close to it.The camera mode was excellent as well, and I took many pretty pictures along my map breaking adventures.After finishing my casual playthrough, I went for the 100%, most of which was fun due to know unrestricted the maps felt.The majority of the achievements gave me reasons to explore places I didn't think of visiting the first time through.However, one particular achievement was incredibly tedious.I would consider it a slight spoiler, so read the following at your own discretion:Despite getting frustrated at time with that achievement, the 100% was still a good time.Story wise I have basically nothing to say, the storytelling is mostly environmental.It was quite nice, not the greatest story ever told, but not bad either.I played the game in it's entirety on a Steam Deck, and it performed at a definitely playable level, while still looking good.Definitely would recommend giving this game a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a single-player, adventure, puzzle-platformer walking simulator game. The game doesn't have any text. It is suitable for anyone without any foreign language knowledge (well, other than the main menu).To help you to decide about the game I would like to share what I liked or disliked in the game, then I'll give some subjective ratings about the game contents.-Visuals: The game has a charming graphic. It looks very nice. Character animation, movement, effect it does just incredible.-Great Soundtracks: The game doesn't have narration or text. In this kind of programs emotional sound effects and soundtracks required. Spirit of the North solved this. It explains the story without any word, with great soundtracks, and animation. -Fox skins: If you collect collectibles then you can unlock additional fox skins. Bored about regular fox skin? Open up the menu and change to a snow fox or corrupted black/white fox. Isn't enough for you? The spirit form of your fox changes with the skin you using too. For example, if you playing with a corrupted black fox, then your spirit form will be red instead of the default blue.-Casual puzzles: The game doesn't offer difficult puzzles or cryptic, hard to solve riddles. It stays casual. It might be disliked by some, but this is what the game offers: A casual, relaxing entertainment for anyone between age 4-125.-Fox bark: The protagonist sounds like a dog, and not as a fox. Their barking is similar, but there is still some difference, and it is clear some dog sound was used for the game.-Too short: Not a real dislike, the game offers a good 6-10 hours playtime. I just loved the game, so when I finished it, then I wanted more of it.I really loved the game. I had a constant curiosity about how the story goes on. Spirit of the North price is fair for the content it offers.Story: 8/10Atmosphere: 9/10Visuals: 9/10Gameplay mechanics: 8/10Music/Sound effects: 10/10Voice acting/Narration: 1/10 No voice acting, texts or narration in the game, it gets the lowest rating only because the fox bark sounds like a dog, and not like a fox.Game difficulty: 3/10Perfection time: 6-10h. Chapters are replayable. You can get collectibles anytime. Achievement Guide and full PC walkthrough available. I made one:Follow my curator if you like to see achievement-related information on the store page of the games: completion times, MP-DLC achievement requirements, useful information.

_childDocuments_.review: I would absolutely recommend this game. It's relaxing and casual, with absolutely stunning scenery to get lost in and explore, but in spite of zero text or dialogue through the game has the ability to hit you squarely in the feels. Had I known this, I might have waited longer to play this, but I am also glad I didn't. Cathartic and then some. I'm  steering away from the story, because it's as much or as little as you want to make of it, though you will get more out of it if you don't just rush to solve the puzzles. This game proves though that communication is about more than words. The soundtrack is beautifully composed - I've left it on while I had a nap... It's not a perfect game - in spite of regular save points, exiting the game will sometimes skip you back to the start of a chapter, which can be frustrating depending on the puzzles - likewise if you explore a little too much and get stuck (guilty a couple of times!) your only option is to exit and risk losing progress. This has meant I've left myself on away rather than turning off at times, which isn't always ideal. I really want there to be more, but the game is complete in terms of the story - I'd love to see another game based on a different myth or idea though. And I would play with some tissues to hand - especially if you have a soul at all!! (I spent the end of chapter seven onwards playing whilst ugly crying... >.>)

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North brings the  mythology of ...Players will enjoy breathtaking visuals and its majestic setting in the Nordic countries to the fullest.But with no lines of dialogue or any explanation written directly to the player,  puts the gamer in control of a bubbling fox who has a fateful encounter with a spirit form of the guardian fox of the Northern Lights. From there, it is up to the little red fox to venture through the icy landscapes in search of the purification of his land and, further on, to reach the highest point of the ice mountain.Spirit of the North is a game that bets on telling its Nordic folk story in a very subjective way, so unless your player profile is someone who is obsessed with Finnish mythology and folklore - especially the tale of Tulikettu - don't feel guilty for playing the game for the simple pleasure of knowing its beautiful setting, solving the puzzles around you to advance in the game, as the story was designed for a very small niche of players.Using the body of the red fox and the spirit of the protective entity of the , the player will advance through the beautiful Nordic scenarios, always in an intuitive way, in search of the solution of several puzzles that will make it possible to reach more complex and advanced adventures.Physically, the little fox performs the basic actions of the species such as barking, wagging its tail, sniffing, jumping, running, but things get more interesting when we control the spiritual face of the entity. In this part, some abilities such as the light that radiates from the spirit, essential for progression in the dark caves, or even the ability to overcome physical barriers make the game more challenging in terms of solving puzzles. In addition, as the story progresses, more skills are unlocked, making mastery and understanding of each of them essential for success in the fire-colored fox's quest.The controls have some frustrating glitches as the game progresses. There are many times when the player will feel punished for failures that are clearly caused by unresponsive actions. Therefore, it is important that the player knows that he will be able to repeat movements to exhaustion to master and hit essential commands for solving puzzlesComprised of soothing and relaxing trails,  does not disappoint as it transports the player directly into the icy and lonely climate of the Scandinavian mountains. Conducted primarily by violins and percussion and keyboard instruments, the soundtrack maintains a perfect atmosphere of calm that accurately reflects the best of the landscape and also conveys the necessary comfort for the player to think better and solve each challenge with precision.Bordering on photorealism, I can say that the graphic part of  is the most impressive at first. It's safe to say that the beautiful Nordic landscapes have never been shown in such a realistic way in video games as in this  However, its greatest merit ends up showing its biggest weakness, which is the lack of inspiration in its level design.With vast clean, repetitive scenarios and a high dose of lack of orientation in the scenarios,  uses all its beauty to confuse and disorient the player, who will certainly feel lost for most of the game. your game time. In the end, even though the game has a presentation that is a delight to the eyes, the image that remains of the game is that the set of work serves more to keep the player lost, given the interpretative characteristics of the story, lack of a mini map and beautiful but repetitive settings.On the other hand, the game lacks solid gameplay and the level design leaves something to be desired, making it confusing and repetitive.The high point of the game is in the beauty of the graphics, perfectly married to the soundtrack. A more subjective and relaxing style of play, which becomes even more interesting if the player is willing to research and engage in the Finnish mythology and folklore of .❆ There are no performance issues❆ Beautiful scenery❆ Immersive soundtrack❆ Too much intuitiveness in the story❆ You need to read a book to understand the story❆ Repetition of scenarios❆ Constant player disorientation❆ Repetitive challenges

_childDocuments_.review: is an atmospheric platformer that looks really cool. However, having played through it, it feels less like  and more like a tech demo for the Unreal Engine 4.So, what's the game about? You play as a fox who is fused with a spirit and has to travel across the land to undo some curse. On the way you gain a few abilities and solve a few platforming puzzles.That's it. That's the game.Now the game does have some little lore nuggets sprinkled throughout to keep you guessing as to what happened to the land, but they barely do anything to pique your interest. They're just there to add some variety to the simple landscapes.The problem with  is just that it isn't fun. An atmospheric platformer should amaze you, but it doesn't. The visuals are sometimes cool, but more often than not it just felt like I was walking through a test environment for the Unreal Engine.The jumping mechanics are awful. They feel clunky. I got myself stuck numerous times because the fox couldn't turn properly and keep their momentum in their jump. Also, after every single puzzle the camera zooms to the issue you just solved, taking away control from the player. The first time, this is understandable. If the solution is far away, then sure. But every single time? That just gets tedious.The abilities you do get are very simple. The ability to activate a button, a dash, a dispelling bark and a spirit form. Of these, the spirit form is probably the most engaging, as the others just felt like they should've been part of your basic powers anyhow.Also, the music is really bland. For a game genre where visuals and music usually carry a lot of weight, this one underdelivers on both.Now, maybe this may not be the game for me. Other reviewers have noted that children enjoy playing it. And sure, it's a really simple game. If you want to just solve some simple puzzles with a cute fox, go for it. But there are so many other atmospheric games out there like this one that are much better. Try , try , try . Something similar with better platforming?  is available. Something more surreal? . More story? Introducing . A similar theme as this one?  is a platformer set in the arctic that is incredibly engaging. There are so many games out there that scratch the same itch as this game does and do it better in my opinion.If you want this game, buy it in a sale. It's about five hours long, a few more if you want to 100% it. I'd recommend trying a different one. This one ain't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Parent review: So far I'm happy with this game, it has beautiful visuals and a calming atmosphere. I got this game mostly for my 8 year old son but also for myself because it's up my alley as well. So this game isn't for kids per say, but as a parent with this generation of kids playing very hectic, chaotic clicky games, I was looking for some better options for my kid, to get into adventuring and puzzling and learn PC controls, because lets face it, tablet games are horrible for kids, they simply have no souls. So I'm extremely grateful to have a game like this available, with beautiful landscapes and non-threatening ambiance, my kid really likes it. Played Okami when I was younger and really enjoyed it.  I must say, it's really great to be playing as a fox instead of an armed warrior, like in most games out there, no dialogue also helps us work on other forms of communication.  Thanks to the creators for making this kind of game available, I hope to see more like this from you.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decently enjoyable game. The visuals are the clear standout here, with breathtaking Icelandic landscapes, from volcanic areas to moss-covered mountains and snowy peaks. The fox you play as is very cute and lifelike in both animation and appearance.Unfortunately, there just isn't a lot to do in this game, you're mainly just running from point A to point B, and while the landscapes are huge, they're very empty. Even something as simple as some more collectibles would increase the fun of this game a lot, in my opinion, because currently I enjoy looking at the landscapes, but I never have any reason to explore them much, which is a shame. The gameplay can also be a bit clunky at times, with a lot of invisible walls blocking off areas that don't look like they should be out of bounds, and the turn cycle for the fox is quite wide, making some of the platforming sections a bit frustrating.The music is also one of the weakest aspects, in my opinion. It's not unpleasant to listen to, but it's very generic, and repeats too quickly, so even though it is alright, it ends up being quite grating when you play the game for a while. I ended up turning it off and listening to some Icelandic folk music instead, which honestly fit the game's atmosphere better than the real soundtrack, in my opinion.Overall, it's a decent little game, though. I'd give it a 6/10. If you like games like Shelter, you'll probably enjoy this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very beautiful and relaxing. I got it on sale a few weeks ago and finally got around to playing it this last week. _childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is an open world adventure game where you play as a fox and run through intricate puzzles. The game has seven chapters, each with their own degree of difficulty and puzzles in a massive, open world with different environments.The game has impressive graphics and background music with a lack of glitches. Spirit of the North has unlockable skins for your fox.  For example, you start as an Artic fox and can later play as a red fox or a grey fox, to name a few of the unlockable skins in the game.Spirit of the North is long, but not too long of a game with about 12 hours of gameplay. There are artifacts you can find of an ancient civilization. All the textures are in-depth and in high quality, especially for a game that is only $19.99. Unlike other games, you can’t glitch the game and climb up mountains unrealistically, so you have to follow the paths. For some reason, the fox’s bark sounds more like a dog’s bark, but that is alright. Besides, I don’t see anything wrong with the game, unless you prefer games of other genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a greatly lovable game. I personally love the feel of everything within it, and it's very calming to play but filled with adventure. I also like the fact that you really have to think about what to do or where to do. The point is I love this game with all my heart, and I will finish it multiple times before I move on from it. I thank the developers!(Also, I just had to add that the fox(s) are adorable. So cute I had to name them "Flying Squirrel" ᓚᘏᗢ ♥)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: It's an amazing game. The game looks really good and the music is really beautifull. it's awesome to play as a fox, to jump and run around as one is great. _childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: A nice puzzle and exploration game. The protagonist is a literal fox (or maybe two?). The graphics are charming and the landscapes really feel expansive, even though it's not really an open world game. The storytelling is purely visual but fairly well-executed. Although the game itself is quite short, it's a pretty immersive experience. Downsides: A direct consequence of the visual-only approach to storytelling is that the game doesn't really explain what you're supposed to be doing. This can lead to fumbling around in the first few chapters as you try to figure out exactly where you can explore and what you can interact with, especially as the game uses invisible walls on the borders of the map. There's a chapter select which can be used to go back and do any optional content you've missed, but it does involve playing through the story again without your endgame abilities. Another con is that the controls tend to feel unresponsive, especially the ones related to jumping and some of the spirit abilities. It wasn't unplayable by any means, but the issues slowed down progress and could feel tedious at times. Overall, well worth a try if you like this genre of game. Or if you like foxes. Buying on discount is for the best though.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a glorified walking sim (but with runes, puzzles, and foxes, oh my!) Jokes aside this is a beautiful game, just a few nitpicks. The controls are incredibly wonky (especially if playing on PC) and I really don’t like how you have to save your game on a level by level basis given the complexity of some of the puzzles. Apart from that, I find it pretty relaxing and I love little details like the fox screm, who doesn’t love a good fox screm? Also you can make the fox wag its tail, 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I like the vibes and environment but gameplay is a mess sometimes it is unplayable even. there is no idle animation when you are in water so you have to have a saints patience to catch the geyser properly cuz otherwise you cant control where that thing would throw you.Sound design is another minus for me, all of the sounds felt like they are all over the place I had to play it in silence and why is the fox barking isnt there a song about this already

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute and captivating. I've really enjoyed so much of it - but the game doesn't have many save points so every time the game glitches and I get stuck somewhere that isn't part of the game I have to quit and I've lost chunks of game-play time. _childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know where to start. First I was so amazed by the landscape and the entire setting of the game. I was looking for a game that includes animals in a majestic kind of way to experience a journey or an adventure with them. It reminded me of The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess where you had to find the golden wolf which teached you a new ability, everytime you found him and I thought this game might be similar to that.During the beginning you will see a few cutscenes where you encounter the spirit fox. But I didn't really enjoyed those scenes, the entire gesture and the static movement of the fox was looking kind of weird to me. The next thing is the environment. You will start in an ice landscape but after some time you will get into a lovely green field of basically nothing. It was actually looking dead to me just if the there was something missing or just unfinished. A few parts were stunning but the majority of it was just boring. I do know that it is supposed to look pretty similar to the actual landscape of iceland, but I expected more, maybe some insects, more flowers or whatever. To me it wasn't looking breathtaking or mysterios (except a few spots) at all.While mentioning flowers - there is actually a flower that will give you some kind of spirit energy back after using it during a puzzle or an ability. But this feature was just annoying to me. Luckily those flowers where always placed somewhere around you, so you can get your energy back. But that's the point to me. Your spirit energy shouldn't be a rare or lacking resource if you just get it from a flower. Walking back to one of them to get the energy just made everything uncomfortably long to me. Another thing is about the fox. Walking and jumping were looking really lovely, but getting to a certain point was feeling weird. Turning around and jumping with the fox felt imprecise and kind of slippery. It also happened that I ended up stuck behind statues or walls after jumping around them.Don't get me wrong please and don't forget that this is just my personal experience.This game has so much potential to become breathtaking and amazing and maybe it already feels like that for other people. I was just annoiyed by many little things that you might not experience the same way as I did. I'm still happy that I found and tried this game, but there were just too many things that didn't fit for me and my expectations. I'm sure that there will be people out there who will have a lot of fun with this game and begin to love it's entire setting and grace.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dog barks like a dang chihuahua. That's so utterly off putting, and it's about the worst sample they could have choosen. Other than that, eh. _childDocuments_.review: While I do love the art style, score, and overall vibe of this game it is too flawed to be very enjoyable. Especially for the $20 price. _childDocuments_.review: Played through the entire game in a night and enjoyed almost every minute of it. The game is beautiful and genuinely fun to play. My only complaints are that sometimes the controls were very unforgiving and that made solving puzzles frustrating. The puzzles also didn't get that much more difficult as the game progressed. Those are minor though honestly my main complaint was that the music was lacking. I could have used some more epic swells in music at the big story telling parts, but there was like 3 songs throughout the whole game. All relaxing and nice but It would have had so much more impact if there was something more moving at times. I kind of tuned out the music at times and with no narrative music is a big part of how you convey emotion in your story. Over all, I loved it, and will be playing it again to get all the things I missed.

_childDocuments_.review: „I will lead you on devoured Paths,in the hidden enclosures of your Soul,helping you,finding your Strenght,to geht back your Life Force.“Claudia R. 2014Welcome to the SPIRIT OF THE NORTH.Inspired from the wonderfull Lands of Iceland and its Nordic Folklore, Infuse Studio invites you to the  wonderfull and unforgettable Journey of a Red Fox.It is up to you to lead this little Fox through this wonderfull and mysterious Lands. In the Beginning your Fox stumbles into a Female Ghost Fox, the Guardian of the Northlights, becoming a Fox Form he never would have imagined. Something bad, something Evil is lurking in the Dark, somewhere far in the Land of Souls.And it is up to your little Fox to bring this all to a maybe good End.Leading this little Guy through the graphically, wonderfull Lands will expect solving puzzles from you to make his Progress. This can be by just Jumping to places, but also by using ancient columns or getting through Obstacles. Your Fox cant do it alone. Your Attender is the Female Ghost Fox, following you as a fen fire. You are also able to get ancient Light for your Fox, not only giving him a mysterious Skin but using this Light in special Places.While you Journey this mysterious Lands you will find very old Wallscriptings that will tell you the Story of the Past.  You will also recognize all the Ruins on your way, showing marks of a Civilization. You will also find the Corpses of ancient Monks, maybe the once proud inhabitants of this Ruins. Find their Wands and lay them down there. Set their Souls free und find your way through their Lands.So much to the Story, that isn`t told by a Word, just by pictures and that is something i really like, because of having my own Phantasies about what the Pictures are telling me.If you ever played ABZU or SUBMERGED, you will know what  i mean.The Controlls are well done (for me). First i played with Mouse and Keyboard, but then i used the Controller. Both worked very good, your Fox responded perfectly on the Controlls. SPIRIT OF THE NORTH has large Areas to explore, but your way is mostly prescribed  because of solving Puzzles to open Doors to continue your Progress. This Game also uses Chapters with Checkpoints instead of Saving and you have many points to return, for example when you miss a Monk Corpse.The Fox is really wonderfull animated, the Developer put very much effort in keeping their Creation to life.  Such simple Things like letting your Fox staying to long, he will sit down. The animated Fur that makes you wanting to crawl this sweet fox. The Lightskin, so fantastic animated.  Also a nice point i like, you dont have to fight, just explore and solve the Puzzles to continue. SPIRIT OF THE NORTH invites you to totally dive into this Game and enjoying the Time there, guiding by a really wonderfull Soundtrack..It feels like a wonderful coming together from THE FIRST TREE, ABZU and SUBMERGED.Thanks dear Developer.What do you think, dear Reader?Are you ready to guide a little Fox and his Spirit Friend through their biggest Adventure?Have a nice time and thank you for Reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea this game is going for, but it gets extremely repetitive and annoying after a while. Some of the puzzles are fun, other times they're very annoying. It's not that they get hard, but it's easy to slip up due to the stiff controls. Also, the checkpoint system is pretty damn annoying too, and once I fell through the map, and there was no failsafe to get me back up again, so I just kept falling and had to reset the game, which meant I lost a ton of progress. Sometimes the menus doesn't work either, and once the world wouldn't load. I say steer away from this one. I have no idea how it has so many positive reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through this game for an hour or two, I can say I recommend it but it is definitely not a game for everyone. I played this the first time when I was having a lousy day and wanted something cute and easy to distract me but mostly turn my brain off, and this really did the trick. The beautiful Unreal Engine graphics and relaxing soundtrack are definitely highlights of this cosy game, but let's face it, it's a walking simulator with some reward-less collection and some minor puzzles.This game *may* be for you if: you're like me and you enjoy completing games simply for the joy of completing them, you just want something cute to kill time with while you listen to lectures, work, watch tv, etc.This game *may* not be for you if: you want a rich story-telling experience, you want challenging puzzles, you want to feel rewarded (outside of achievements) for your time and effort.

_childDocuments_.review: this game has beautiful graphics, cute characters, and the concept is really cool. it definitely has the potential to be a good game.but i cant in good conscience say i enjoyed it. the physics are hard to understand, and your fox doesnt seem to know they're on a platform or where it is half the time. and, at least for me, it was difficult to follow the path and comprehend what i was meant to do most of the time. it could very well be a personal gripe, and others may not have struggled with any of this as much as i did, but it made the overall experience very hard to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I found Spirit of the North to be a very enjoyable game.I can sometimes have a hard time with puzzle games, but none of the puzzles in this game left me feeling too frustrated. I could usually solve them within a handful of attempts and I didn't need to look up a guide for any of them.In some areas it was easy to get turned around and become lost, but the areas aren't too large where you can't find where you're going again. I liked that we have the freedom to explore, but I wish you could ask your spirit guide for help when you feel you need it.I also didn't mind the open-ended story. I found it interesting that my interpretation of the story was slightly different than what my husband thought. I was never quite sure what was going to happen next, but I was always pleasantly surprised and enjoyed the new areas we got to explore.It's not going to be everyone's cup of tea, but if you like cozy puzzle games you will probably enjoy this one as well. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is an exploration game, with some puzzles that are not hard, considering you play as a fox infused with a couple of spiritual powers. The fox is the only alive character and there are no dialogues, but the objectives and storyline are easy to understand. The main features of the game are the realistic abandoned places, ruins and natural landscapes you cross accompanied by a beautiful soundtrack. In general, the game reminds me of Shadow of the Colossus, Okami and also the hidden gem that is Eastshade. Perfect for explorers and completionists who enjoy relaxing puzzles and nature themed games.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I fell in love with this game almost immediately when a friend gifted me this. I love being able to explore the beautiful landscape and even use the interesting abilities that get unlocked as you play through it. After beating the game, I had to look something up and then I found out that this game follows the belief that people have in Finland for the Northern Lights. All in all, it's a beautiful game and I would recommend for anyone who love exploration to get this.

_childDocuments_.review: What...an utterly...beautiful experience that was.It's not often a game so simply manages to catch my attention, and draw me in.  This game, in me, reignited an emotion I rarely feel in games today: the love of gaming.  At its core, it is a simple puzzle platformer.  But very quickly you'll see it's much more of an experience, and a beautiful one at that.  The music is somber but touching, while the setpieces are absolutely gorgeous.  I found myself exploring not because of the hidden shamans spirits to save, but because I just loved the environments and wanted to take a look.The story follows that tried and true method of show, don't tell, leaving the player to piece together what is presented.  Nowadays people tend to get caught in the mindset that a narrative needs to be some epic drama with exciting moments and high stakes.  What this game understands, PROVES, is that doesn't always need to be the case.  In fact, some times it's better to take a step back, and let the world breathe a little.  Shadows of the Collosus did this particularly well, and I found myself thinking of that game many times.I really don't have any complaints, other than the desire for more of it.  You can very quickly beat it, let alone 100% it, I'm 5 hours in and am just missing 2 achievements which should be relatively easy to get.  I hope to see more games like this, because this is what gaming should be: a great experience. Play the game, try it out for yourself.  For once, a game that doesn't try to trick you into playing longer than 2 hours so you can't refund it.  It just gives you a great experience from start to finish.  I guarantee you won't want to return it.  Play it.  Enjoy it.  Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for 17 hours, and of that, around 12 to 14 were spent solely on chasing down a lost spirit monk in the second-to-last level in a spirit forest realm. This was not fun. Guides and walkthroughs were of little help because some of the spirit monks WANDER and thus cannot be found in any specific location. For years, off and on, I got on this game again solely to chase down the missing monk and only a couple days ago did I manage to finally encounter him. THIS. IS. A. CHORE.If you like foxes, I would stress to you that you should get this game ONLY when it is at a serious discount. There are some bonuses to this game--cute emotes, a profile background, and a nice badge set which I leveled up to max because after 100%ing this game I deserve it--but I do not think they really justify paying more than maybe around 5 bucks for it. The fox has a few cute animations--shaking off water and limping--but these animations slow down or completely stop you in some areas. You can unlock different skins by getting certain achievements or progress in the game, but...There is no real replayability in this title. Where in other games, abilities you unlock in later levels can be then used in earlier levels to have more fun or access previously inacessible areas, this game does not offer anything of that sort. Worse, once you get used to abilities like sprint/dash, the game feels painfully slow when you go back to earlier levels and are completely unable to use them. This was probably my worst experience with the game apart from the missing monk chase.The story is very vague and nondescript; you have to inference what is happening from crude murals on walls (oh, by the way, those can be a challenge to find and light up too, same with the monks). Basically every seek and find in this game turns it from a relaxing jaunt through the open world (read: boring and lifeless area) to a monotonous nightmare trying to figure out where you are on the map and where you need to go from there.Overall? I cannot recommend this game. If they at least let you return to earlier levels with the abilities you unlock, it could be a maybe. Since they do not, and the achievements are such a pain to get, I'm uninstalling after posting this review.As a final note; I unlocked the flying fox achievement when the game glitched and launched me into the air and out of the map entirely. I could not get back onto the map and had to close and restart the game to get anywhere afterward. I'm keeping the achievement for my trouble, but that is not the intended way you were meant to get that achievement, so yeah--look out for glitches!

Some animations and Invisible Walls can be a little bit frustrating, but I never had any big problems.Honestly, when I first stumbled across this game, I just liked the idea of controlling a fox, but the pure aestethics of the game and the story that you can read into it are simply beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is, in my opinion, a very enjoyable game. It has its ups and downs, but overall it was pretty well done. Now prepare for a long review and an interesting ending (spoiler alert—I gave my interpretation of the storyline!)I bought and played this game on PC, so I can only describe how well the controls work with a keyboard (and I've heard some negative reviews about the game with a controller). But for a keyboard, it's very smooth. The controls are easy to learn: regular movement keys of course; both mouse buttons are used for certain actions within the game, at which point a prompt will appear on the screen to tell you what to use; and a few keys for special abilities. The movement is clean and responsive.Most of the gameplay is pretty simple. You play as a red fox who is aided by a spirit fox, and then journey with your new friend to save a world plagued by a strange scarlet disease. You must find glowing blue flowers to obtain spiritual energy, and use that energy to solve puzzles, open new areas, and unlock special abilities. As you do so, you can occasionally find hidden staffs, which you can pick up and carry, and when you near the staff's owner, the blue gem glows and sparks. You place the staff beside a robed skeleton and its spirit rises to give you a respectful bow before disappearing. Throughout your adventures, you find many of these spirits, and can free them if you choose (it's actually optional—the staffs and their owners are hidden everywhere, and it's kind of an extra side mission to free them).The music is phenomenal. It's beautiful, haunting, melancholic, and sometimes a bit eerie. There are a few times where it's a bit weird though, like you move a few steps in one direction and the music abruptly changes, and then you move back and it changes again. And sometimes it doesn't quite match your environment, or it gets you hyped up for the wrong reason. For example, it can be slow and creepy, and gradually rise and intensify, building suspense, and it finally crescendos when you reach whatever it is you've been walking toward—and there's nothing to justify the terrifying music. Often there's nothing there at all. But aside from that, it's wonderful music. Now for some of the negative bits. A few of the puzzles can be frustrating. Sometimes you've got to get the timing just right, or jump from the exact perfect spot in order to reach your goal. Sometimes you have no idea where to go, because the terrain doesn't always have a clear path. Often the actual path is hidden or obscured, and you have to go searching for it. Sometimes you go the total wrong way and have to find your way back. And don't get me started on the water and swimming mechanics. One, the swimming is incredibly slow. Two, when you come out of the water and onto land, even if it's just a tiny sliver of land, you must wait five or six seconds for your fox to shake the water out of its fur. At first, yeah, that's a cool animation, but when you're trying to make that one jump puzzle and keep falling into the water, it gets annoying. And there's another thing. Towards the final chapters of the game, when previously it was optional, freeing the robed spirits becomes necessary to progress. I didn't exactly mind this, since I'd been trying to free as many as I could anyway, but it would've been nice to give more of a heads-up for those who might not really care.So yeah, there are a few things about the gameplay that I don't exactly like, but boy, the graphics are absolutely gorgeous. The landscape is a beautiful replica of Iceland, with its rocky, icy mountains; dark, mysterious caves; large, grassy plains; flowing rivers and sapphire lakes; and the wind ruffling your fur and swaying the grass wherever you go. As you travel through the world, you come across several crumbling structures, stone houses and towers, even a few of what seem to be villages. These structures are where a lot of the puzzles take place, and where there are many robed spirits to be freed.And now, for the final part. The story. The storyline is, admittedly, a bit hard to follow. There is no dialogue, no narrator, nothing to explain what's really happening. It's kind of up to you to figure it out. There are vague murals, carvings on the runestones, and symbols everywhere, but it's still rather difficult to understand. The easy bit is this: a strange, terrible disease has swept over the land, manifesting as bulbous plant-like things that spew red spores everywhere, leaving a scarlet trail in the sky. You, a red fox, have partnered with a spirit fox (the "Spirit of the North") to try and save the ravaged land. After that, it gets confusing. I have tried my best to interpret from what I gathered from the runestones and murals, and what I didn't know, I filled in myself. So I have built a story that hopefully makes sense for this game:file:///C:/Users/naomi.LAPTOP-0GH7QA42/Downloads/Just%20a%20Fan's%20Version%20of%20the%20SotN%20Storyline.pdfIf that link worked (hopefully it did) and you managed to read the entire storyline, I congratulate you. I also hope that the storyline makes sense to you. Honestly, I just played the whole game and then wrote the entire thing afterwards. I really like how it turned out. Now, I'm not sure how true it is, or how correct the details are, or how much of it is what the developers were going for. But really, I searched for like 20 minutes all over the internet and couldn't find a single thing that truly explained the storyline of this game. So I decided I'd write my own based on the pieces I could fit together, and whatever blanks there were, I'd fill them in myself. And I think it's a pretty good story, even if it isn't exact to the game. If the link didn't work and you couldn't read it, sorry. Maybe you could download the game and play it, and then see what storyline YOU might be able to think up! It's all in the imagination. Try it out!Despite its difficulties and annoyances, this game is pretty great, and I totally recommend it. It's a lot of fun and super relaxing. Thanks a lot for reading this far and I hope you enjoy your day.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually got this game because FOX and AURORA BOREALIS, but mostly fox. I love that you play a very fluffy looking fox there, even if it makes doggy noises. That was a bit weird, but still cute that you could "communicate" with the spirit ball through the barking. It is very pretty. The story being told through wall paintings, rotten buildings, shaman spirits and events isn't entirely original (there are similar enough ones - though totally not the same), but it is nicely told and actually kinda pretty, even if the story is not a "pretty" one per say. Also totally love the blue fox and what happens later.... I could totally do the last part a loooot.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an experience, to say the least. One that I thoroughly enjoyed and absolutely loved. I highly recommend this game for anyone looking to experience a completely visual story with no enemies and a number of puzzles.Depending on how quickly you pick up on the puzzles, and how long it takes you to figure out where to go, Spirit of the North should provide roughly 3-6 hours of content. According to my time played my first playthrough took 5 hours and, sadly, I failed to return 5 staves to the bodies scattered around the maps so I have a bit more to get out of it yet.I honestly believe that this game is well worth the asking price. It was a delight.

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game. It's visually stunning and the music in the game is very relaxing. _childDocuments_.review: The game is a journey and you must get to your destination with the help of a spirit guide. Along the way you will acquire certain skills to aid you. These skills are introduced in stages as you progress and once acquired can be combined to perform tasks to help you solve puzzles. Some of these abilities weren’t explained very well which left me stuck on one puzzle and frustrated on another. Relying on pictures to explain things doesn’t always work!The fox uses jump frequently but if you are too close to an object the fox will have difficulty jumping on to it. Accompanied by the camera moving around unhelpfully, navigating in tight spaces can be difficult. For example, I had completed a puzzle which dropped a pillar of stone for me to walk up and continue. I must have spent fifteen minutes trying to walk on to this when it should have been an easy and simple task. Similar to Lost Ember there is no narrative and the story unfolds through brief cut scenes and ghostly figures. The story was incomprehensible mostly. I had a semblance of what was happening but it didn’t invoke much emotion in me which was disappointing. The puzzles weren’t too difficult to solve. I never had to use a walkthrough to complete the game but I was suitably challenged throughout. Most puzzles can be solved by just exploring the environments to find stone tablets to activate. There are inaccessible areas that you will need to use your special abilities to access and difficulty levels increased as you progressed. Gameplay involves following a spirit guide through the scenic environments of Iceland after a trail of red mist in the sky. Along the way you will find barriers blocking your path in the shape of stone doors, thorns and rocks. You have to find a way to get through these barriers and continue your journey. The main mechanics are as follows:🟢Blooms are luminescent flowers which infuse into your body and allow you to transfer this energy to stone tablets. This is often enough to open locked doors early on in the game. Sometimes there will be more than one tablet to find to unlock a door, and often these tablets are cleverly hidden around the area.The blooms are plentiful early on but become sparse and difficult to locate later on in proceedings. To infuse a bloom, you call the spirit guide by barking, and he arrives and activates the bloom for you. I was a bit confused as to how many different blooms you needed to open doors initially as sometimes it didn’t work. What was happening though was that the guide was activating the blooms but they weren’t infusing in to my body. You have to make sure you walk and wait on the activated flower whilst it infuses into you. Another example of a mechanic not really explained properly. 🟢When stood on these produce jump gates which can project you through the air and cover large distances. They also produce water geysers which can lift you in the air to reach higher parts of the map. 🟡Gives you the ability to run rather than walk. It is the first ability you learn and you acquire this quite early on in the game.🟡Gives you the ability to call over the guide to activate blooms. I found out later that it can also be used to locate your guide if you get lost following him. Only if you are close enough, a bark will zoom in on his location, otherwise you will have to find him. On a couple of occasions, I just started the act again to pick up the trail.🟡You can transfer your essence into the guide and control him. The guide is able to walk on water, and travel through barriers, like thorns. He can basically access areas that the fox cannot. This was the most interesting of the mechanics to use. The spirit form only lasts a certain amount of time. There is no countdown or clock but your essence is returned to the fox after a brief spell in its body.🟡The guide can warp through the air for brief moments making travel much faster. Combined with sprint this can help you jump over larger distances or reach tablets faster to transfer energy.🟡You can use your bloom energy to explode plague tethers that block doors and exits. HOLDING the b button builds up your energy until it explodes destroying the blockage.Along the way you will find staffs which you can give to shamans to awaken their spirits. Mostly these are achievement based but occasionally you will need to find and deliver the staff for him to open a door. Again, I had issues with the staff. It does not float and it does not rise with objects. Twice I had to abandon a delivery as the staff got trapped under water and another time it got trapped as it would not rise with a platform I was on. There are 28 shamans to find and they can be very well hidden. A tough achievement to locate them without a guide. The landscapes of Iceland were impressive and the fox’s movements were imaginative. There were some nice touches with the way the fox behaved, shaking his fur as he got out of water, cuddling up in the snow as he rested, and swimming through the water. It all looked very professional. There is a peaceful orchestral tune being played throughout the game which loops and doesn’t change much. It never seems to get repetitive or boring however and it is a wonderful arrangement to listen to. Curator Info: This game was received for free through curator connect.

_childDocuments_.review: A brief review of Spirit of the North and similar games: Spirit of the North is inspired by the landscapes of Ireland and based on Nordic folklore. It is an adventure game where you play as a red fox who becomes connected and intertwined with the guardian of the Northern Lights, who is represented by a magical female, spirit fox. You journey through the snow and ice and over mountains to learn more about your spirit guide as well as the land that was been left in ruins. Solve puzzles and use your own experiences to theorize about the meaning of a lost ancient civilization. This game was suggested to me by a viewer and I did not expect to fall in love with it as much as I do. It’s absolutely gorgeous and the fox yips resonating through the empty environment really illuminates the feelings of emptiness and loss.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirit of the North

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit of the North is a single-player 3rd-person adventure game inspired by the breathtaking and mysterious landscapes of Iceland with various pieces of Nordic folklore. The game purposefully has no dialog or narrative. Breathe in the surroundings to solve various puzzles and speculate the meaning of a lost ancient civilization.

name: Fight Crab
detailed_description: Crabs Powered by Simulated Physics! Take control of a simulated physics-powered crab and take on various opponents in this 3D action game with one basic rule: 'flip your enemy over to win'. Take advantage of a wide range of equipment to beat your opponent down: claws, swords, guns, armor, jet engines, and more. Stop your opponent's blade with your pincers, run along walls, and generally go full-on crab with all the fighting techniques at your disposal. Get the total battle crab experience with amazing procedural animations and spot-on accurate collision detection - just like you've always wanted to but probably never realized. Featuring 23 types of crab, 48 different weapons, and 11 unique battle stages! 1 vs. 1, 2 vs. 2, online/offline battle modes... This game has it all. Enjoy campaigns and training modes while waiting for your turn in battle! Campaign Mode featuring over 41 battles as well as training, rankings, and more! Go through the entire campaign on your own, or cooperate with friends - you can get the full experience either way! Test your might in the advanced-level Hard Mode and wave-based challenge stages to really hone your battle skills. Link up with VRoid Hub Go into battle sporting your very own original avatar on top of your crab! Original avatars can be seen by other players online, so you can show off your bitchin' avatars to players around the world. In some completely different, super weird world, crabs have mastered human weapons and taken over the land. Now immortal, these crabs cannot be killed by gun nor blade. However, there is one crustacean rule by which all must live: 'He who turns his back to the ground shall know defeat...' That's right - get flipped over on your back in battle, and you have no choice but to submit to your opponent. You must now embark on a journey to become the strongest ever seen, and flip the entire world itself onto its back.
