_childDocuments_.review: I have been a South Park fan for what feels like forever, so don't think of this as a hate to South Park, or to the game, but my personal opinion of the game, as a person with almost 100 hours in FBW and a good 30 in Stick of Truth, I hope I can help shed some light on the differences of this game.Gameplay: 4/10The gameplay is pretty mid if I'm going to be honest, I know it takes time to really let a game grow, but for now, I rate it a 4 just because there isn't any special gameplay. Unlike FBW or SOT, you have no special powers besides the fart escape, health totem, and all the others, which I didn't even switch out the basic powers as every good few minutes I'd have to heal like crazy because it's just boringly difficult to go through your first time, there isn't much tactic in the game. In FBW, you need to learn when to use ur special abilities, who to add in your party and what abilities are best against your enemies, in SNOW DAY, you are button mashing and farting a couple times.Story/Lore: 1/10I'm not gonna lie, after playing FBW, this game felt so EMPTY, like for one..WHERE IS CRAIG X TWEEK?? And also, where is the beauty of the last two games? There's no side missions, no 'open world' map, you can't explore and find fun things, you are bound to 3 or 4 lines of dialog per character, and then the only story you get is in the 5 missions you have for the WHOLE game, it was extremely boring to go through since it just had such a bland story, I really didn't enjoy the fact that there was just nothing to do besides kill a bunch of enemies and listen to Cartman make a joke about you breaking the game again, which can't even happen cause guess what? There isn't more to the game! Worth what you paid: 2/10Unless you're a die hard South Park fan that needs to have every ounce of merch, games, shows, and movies of the game, YOU SHOULDN'T BUY IT. It really is worth half of what the selling price is (at the moment 30), and there isn't barely anything you can do, all you're seeing is a bunch of 3D versions of a small cast of characters, button mashing, and a lack of any relative or interesting story, the only good things you get is a cool dino hat and you get to fart. It really wasn't worth the moneyTime: 0/10SOT felt short, but you did have a vast majority of things to do with a interesting story and fun gameplay, FBW is the Fallout 4 or Fallout New Vegas of all the fallout games, perfect timing, side missions, fun gameplay, you really can't put it down, plus it has really fun dlcs! And WAY more cosmetics then SNOW DAY or SOT, eitherways, you can finish this game in less then 4 hours if you really wanted to. This game felt fast and honestly, I felt like if I just played the Captain Crunch DLC for FBW it would take up the same amount of time as this whole game did. The whole time I played, I told myself; "once I finish these 5 main missions it might open new things! Maybe even side missions!" but all it opens is some Nichole stuff...like, there really isnt much more to doEnemies: 1/10The only one I actually enjoyed going against was the final battle, it was a LITTLE fun, if you're playing with friends then I don't doubt it would be way more chaotic, but for me a singleplayer person, the bots suck crap and died immediately, to the point where I just left them and fought on my own, the enemies are not hard and they are just boring and easy to kill. along with the random BullSh*ts that really aren't that scary, and just another boring addition.Graphics: 3/10 They really could've stuck with the 2D, not saying I hate the 3D but it really didn't need all this extra stuff, if I'm going to be honest, the 3D made it look funky and weird, all of the characters look kinda gross, especially with their dark matter eyes, and it's just not the best looking game, it just doesn't fit a South Park game and I actually was very excited to see how the 3D world would look for the town but..was disappointed to find out that we were only going to see so little. _childDocuments_.review: It's okay. The story and jokes are what shine but in between those parts, ya know the actual gameplay, its very meh.It is kind of like Vermintide, in the sense of the melee combat, go through stages, kill waves of enemies, do an objective, with a taste of slight randomness with the card system of upgrades.My main issue is that there really isn't a lot of feedback on the actions you do. You can attack people, get attacked, and it doesn't really feel like you are making any impact. You have to look out for the damage numbers, healing numbers, health bars etc to see if things are actually working. I have had several times where I try to activate an ability that just didn't go through cause I was finishing a different animation, but I wouldn't really know if the ability happened because, there really is no difference besides specifically looking for the animation to happen.Using an ability for 20 damage feels like it has the same impact as a normal attack that does ~8. The health bar barely goes down, you really have to wail on people a bit so even if you use the ability you don't notice the bar goes down much. Getting low on health, you have to watch your health bar, its hard to tell when you are getting hit yourself.Mostly the gameplay is run around and spam click, and just wait for people to die, use abilities when you can, and then move on. I guess if you are looking for a chill thing to play and not really take seriously to enjoy, its not bad. But you don't have the story to carry the gameplay like the other games did.

_childDocuments_.review: I can agree with majority that the game doesn't have a lot of content, but I don't think it's such a bad game, especially considering the fact that most modern games are $69 and this game costs twice less. But despite lack of content, I still think this is a good game. It has fun and challenging game play (I suggest playing the game on hard), with variety of enemies that forces you to think about how you play and make you create strategies, fun bosses, cool skills and bonuses for them. I really like balancing system that makes you start at your weakest state in beginning of level and build your character up as you progress. I do think the 3D cutscenes are pretty good and keep up with South Park vibe. They are fun to watch and its cool to see familiar characters been 3D. It's boring to play the game alone, but if you have a friend or better a group of friends, I think this is a fun game to play together for few evenings. I wouldn't recommend buying it right now, but I think its a great game to get on sale. I really hope developers won't abandon the game and will release more content. Also the game is pretty much bug free, maybe I haven't played enough but I still haven't encountered a single bug.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty awful. Pros: - The game runs well. I do not meet the recommended specs listed but the game defaulted to ultra and I havent noticed any framerate issues.- The game looks nice. Granted I do not think that it's very graphically intensive (it looks like it could've been a PS3 game if im honest).Cons:- I genuinely don't think the game was bug tested. TWICE I was thrown out of the map by something, getting stuck on the scenery, meaning I could not move and just had to quit the level.- Your AI teammates just plain don't work. For example, at the end of the stan mission, you have to traverse the roof tops to get to him. One of my teammates needed reviving. I walk over to him. I revive him. He gets his 5ish seconds of invincibility before instantly dying again. Great. Now I have to complete the level with 2 teammates if I don't want to quit and start over. At one stage, you get catapulted to the other side of the road to make your way across those buildings. This would be fine (albeit pretty blatantly just a way of dragging out the level longer) if your team actually followed you. One of my teammates was stuck on the other side of the map. At this point I just closed the game.- The gameplay is simply just boring. It's repetitive. I understand the game is a hack and slash. That's fine. But that mixed with the fact that moving feels like you're trudging through mud and the game just doesn't feel satisfying to play honestly just makes it a drag. If a hack and slash game is what you're after, there are definitely better and far cheaper options. - I saw another review calling this a '£30 mobile game' and honestly, I couldn't agree more. This would feel right at home on the app store for £3, on an iPad so a kid could just mindlessly press the screen for a few hours. However, it does not cost £3. It is not on an iPad. It is on steam. It is £25. £40 if you spring for the 'dIgItAl dElUxE EdItIoN'. Side note - the fact that there's DLC day one really just feels scammy. I know over time it has become common practice, but that doesn't make it feel any different. - Finally, there's just a glaring lack of content. 5 levels? This genuinely feels like it could've been thrown together in a few weeks. I actually hope this was just a game that was already made and South Park Studios just bought the rights to make it South Park themed. At least then there could be an excuse as to why its so boring.It's really a shame, I remember seeing the trailer for the game months ago and was actually excited for the game to come out. Hopefully DLC that comes out can actually save the game, because if this is how it sits permanently it's going to be a real stain on the South Park franchise (not like the games pre Stick of Truth weren't already bad enough).I really hope that this game can be redeemed, but I don't hold out a lot of hope..

_childDocuments_.review: Hi. as a big fan of south park (games and tv-show), this DM comes from a place of love. i recently purchased the snow day game and really enjoyed the concept of the story and the fact that its a 3d-game. BUT you guys have left so much behind that could make the game better, and keep players in for a long time, vs a short story. FIrst, we got to talk about PVP. there are so many other game modes that can be made for this kind of fighting game like 4 teams of 4 battling out for time to get most kills. you can do elves vs other team in a CS:GO style where the bomb is a stink bomb, a MOBA-like gamemode, a team deathmatch, special boss raid events vs famous characters from the series like manbearpig etc. rewards can be dark matter and special event costumes, weapon skins etc. when it comes to weapons, you could increase the number of weapon costumization options. the weapons dont need to have more effects of boosts, but like having a dildo as a main weapon or a tampon gun for ranged weapon. this was a cool thing in the other games, and its a bummer that you left it behind. kind of like skins in CS:GO, they look cool, but dont give any effects. being able to costumize your new kid in many ways is also good, but weapons would be my #1 wish. hope you guys take this into consideration, as it would keep the game alive longer, build a community around the game, esp around boss raid events. another thing would be to add more maps with the different game modes. have famous locations from south park feature as a part of the battle arena like the school backyard, inside different famous buildings etc.

_childDocuments_.review: "South Park: Snow Days" is like being invited to the world's most irreverent snowball fight, where the gloves are off, and so is any semblance of political correctness. Imagine every character you love (and love to hate) armed with nothing but their wits and an arsenal of icy projectiles, in a game that's more unpredictable than Mr. Garrison's career choices. The graphics? Let's just say they're as refined as Cartman's dining habits, which is to say, charmingly crude. The gameplay is as smooth as Butters on a good day, which means you're in for a hilariously bumpy ride. Whether you're dodging a barrage of snowballs or the show's trademark satirical barbs, this game guarantees belly laughs and maybe a few frostbitten fingers. In the end, "South Park: Snow Days" is the perfect game for fans who like their winters cold and their humor colder. Remember, it's all fun and games until someone ends up in a "Oh my God, they killed Kenny!" scenario.

_childDocuments_.review: While South Park: Snow Day! retains some of the franchise's signature charm amidst its mediocre graphics and subpar controls, it falls short in many areas.Considering its current price point and lack of substantial content, I cannot in good conscience recommend purchasing it at full retail price. The game begins to hit its stride just as it nears its conclusion. Despite promises of future content updates, fundamental issues persist that cannot be remedied through mere patches. For a game centered on hack-and-slash mechanics, its execution is among the poorest I've encountered in recent memory. The combat mechanics lack weight, with hits feeling unsatisfying due to a lack of sound cues and an inability to chain attacks effectively.Furthermore, the AI teammates, essential for solo play, are virtually useless. They frequently find themselves incapacitated, often positioned far from the player character, and fail to assist in obtaining necessary items to progress. While playing with friends or random players can marginally improve the experience, at best, it feels like polishing a turd.Perhaps, the real ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ card was this game all along.

The fact that I feel like I am 3 hours in and almost done with game leaves a bad taste in my mouth. The combat system is fun for sure but the lack of lock on or attacks that can miss incredibly easily without direct aim make it feel clunky and sometimes unsatisfying. While the story is funny in it's South Park layered comedy, the fact it's so short on launch makes me want 20 dollars back with the promise of more DLC with extra chapters and more weapons/cards. I'll finish the game and see what the DLC is like from my friends or influencers, but I am not sure what to expect coming up next and hope they continue to improve this game for free or as little charge as possible to make it a true addition to the South Park game franchise. Get it if you wanna, but it's ok rn.

_childDocuments_.review: Was worried about the reviews but please dont listen to them if your interested. Being a die hard South Park fan since the beginning I think they did an awesome job and its not as shallow as people are making it seem. To be fair Ive loved every South Park game, including the ones people consider "bad" that could be why Im loving this right now. It honestly gives me vibes from the 1998 South Park 64 doom shooter mixed with 4 player co-op feel of South Park Let's Go Tower Defense Play! but with Rogue-Lite power up unlocks and a Perk System, decent amount of Cosmetic unlocks too. Im also playing the game on Hard which is making it pretty challenging tbh. The card system is pretty cool, closest thing I can compare it too would be the cards in Fallout 76 for your SPECIAL perks but different for every "run". I got downed about 12-15 times before finally dying about halfway into Chapter 1, I really hope it keeps that challenge going forward into the game, it makes the rogue aspect of it a lot more fun. I havent played multiplayer yet which im hoping to in the next few days after I get a bit more into the game. On that note this is the first time Ive seen a "No Spoiler" option for when your matchmaking, which is a great idea.     I really hope they add more content over time and keep going with it, its been awesome seeing the characters in 3D again like the oldschool game, a lot of fun and definitely recommend to South Park fans, worth the price forsure12 - 13 hours later Edit: Gets old quick, had a lot of potential but missed it, still enjoyed the initial playthrough, worth playing for cheap, bummer in the end, couldve did a lot with this one

_childDocuments_.review: While this game isnt really my cup of tea, I still like it so far.Im a much bigger fan of all the checkpoints, offensive humor, and how strategic the other game was but I think this game has some interesting rules. The cards are a fun and unique addition to this game, and having to hit the enemies is a good idea to get players to fight.Okay, now im going to get into my personal experience playing this game.When I first loaded it up the first thing I noticed was how slow and laggy it was! This isnt much of a surprise since my computer definitely isnt made for gaming, and in order to be able to enjoy a game I have to turn the resolution all the way down. This isnt the game's fault, but I thought it was worth mentioning.Once I started the initial cut scene, I realized that the audio and video wasn't playing at the same time! Fortunately, the cut scene only establishes that theres a really bad snowstorm, school is canceled, and Cartman is going out to play. I already knew all of that!The options to customize you character is pretty limited, but im pretty sure you can buy more stuff from Tweek and Craig so its not an issue. The actual game play is interesting. As I mentioned before, I had to turn my resolution all the way down. The thing is, the cards are in 3D which means I cant see them clearly. It takes me FOREVER to read what they say, and it doesnt help that Jimmy is yelling at me to hurry up. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards are also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! I could be almost done with a wave, but then they'll use a card and make all the enemies alive again. Its so annoying!The bots also drive me crazy! If they were real people, I would yell at them so much I would lose my voice. They NEVER do what I want them to, and it would be better to find some friends (I dont want to though because im shy, so bots it is!). Im REALLY bad at these types of games, and it doesnt help that im an angry person in general. I barely got halfway through the first level on medium, so I guess this is my opinion as somebody who isnt great at these kinds of games.Despite all the negative things I said, I still think this game is fun and DEFINITELY will take over 5 hours for me to complete. Its probably not worth $30, but if it gets updated then maybe. If you aren't a South Park fan or not a fan of this genre, wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Negatives:-Game is Incredibly Short, Campaign can be completed in 3-4 Hours.-Wish there was more replay ability to each stage.-There is limited build varity in the game with the current weapons available and most people I played with online seemed to run the same weapons and powers. -Side Characters dont offer much in this game, Randy in particular is just shoehorned in to the story by cutscenes. When he mentioned Scotch has all the TP thought there could be a raid like mission with Randy!Positives:-The Updated Models and Environments to 3D i thought worked well, Didn't take away from characters and lended new depth to the town and sets the scale of the snow storm as entire buildings are snowed in.- The Interactions with the Main Boys had good humour that was expected going into the game. Paladin Butters as the Rules Lawyer for the game was Great and having Henrietta as a card dealer was nice to see the Goths get represented!-Messing with the in game Powers and Weapons there are some unique synergies you dont see to often which I highly recommend if playing with a group. The Gravity Orb and Chees-It powers combined can make a large amount of brainwashed to fight along side you. Or if you like a range build Turrent and Drone make for a fun combo.Alot of Reviews compare this to the Previous games Stick of Truth and Fractured Butt Whole, and it is hard not to seperate this entry from them. Game May have worked better if it didn't continue the new kid story and was released as a South Park Arcade style game which would make sense at the price point of the standard version. Worth buying if your a long term fan of the series or if it is on offer. But other than that can't recommend this one

_childDocuments_.review: "South Park: Snow Day" delivers the excitement of an actual snow day... if you spent it doing chores. In a bewilderingly PG turn, it's as if South Park went on a field trip and left its humor at home. 🌨️Give it a few hours and the main story is complete, this game ends quicker than Cartman's diet plans, lacking the series' punch. It's got cool powers and stuff, if you're into the thrill of finding loose change under the couch.It's as lonely as Butters in the rejection corner. Diving into 3D, THQ Nordic apparently thought, "Hey, let's give them less of what they love!" Stripping away the rich narrative and humor and gameplay, is like going to Casa Bonita and only getting to eat the napkins. 🌮As for the price? Picture Cartman selling "raffaele ronca's cheesecake" memberships—overpromised and underdelivered. Could've used a price chop or, wild idea, content that screams South Park."South Park: Snow Day" feels like getting novelty underwear for Christmas—sure, it covers the essentials, but where's the fun in that? Hopefully, DEVS catches on that we're in it for the cheeky thrills, not just to keep our bits from freezing. 🩲❄️

_childDocuments_.review: The game has too little content and outright feels shallow in depth of the content it does have. Wait till either free-updates (None planned to my knowledge) or a massive sale goes on to even try it. Otherwise, not even for the base price of $30. The deluxe edition/season pass is definitely not worth it, even with stuff planned currently.I got this game in good faith of the two previous games, stick of truth, and fractured but whole. I really enjoyed those two and was curious about this one. I do like the "Rouge-like" Coop Mission based game-play, akin to old gauntlet dark legacy game and other quick level beat em ups.But where this game quickly falls apart, and the worst offender in my opinion is the  3 Melee Weapons, 3 Ranged Weapons, 8 Skills (2 at a time), and roughly 4 Perks per weapon/skill as you upgrade through a run. With Quick Math, you can try every combo within 252 runs. But skills/weapons perks/abilities do not interact with each other, so by run 6 or 8, you can probably already find what works best and stick with that and only that.And the story/length, that is the next major issue. 5 Levels with essentially 3 middle pieces that can inter-change for run differences. Or 4 levels with that ability, and a single area climb for the final level. The levels are beautiful, but the the replay-ability is just- not worth going through a 2nd time, unless you are attempting to 100% the game. I get there is a theme/world design of 'Snow-agedon' but having a legit pallet of only white wears on you fast. There isn't an open world, only a hub and its levels, so you cannot explore south park as a town in 3D, which sucks, but not holding it against the game. I will say it sucks to only see areas and not actually explore them like previous games.Writing. That's the next problem in my book bellow the things said above. There isn't any edge, there isn't any of the iconic south park jabs, there isn't any thing that makes me think of south park writing other than the names of the characters. The closest things we get to south park humor and writing is cartman calling kyle a 'Dru', and Uncle Jimbos Fetch-Quest, but even then it feels like... How can I put it? Scrubbed from anything too offensive and meets the simplest of terms of what a jab is? The writing isn't there for me.I bought the deluxe edition of the game, not gonna return it, but I definite do not recommend it in it's current state. Looking at the Season Pass, I don't have much hope for that either. 1 Named Ranged Weapon, 1 Unnamed Melee Weapon, and some updates to the daggers, along with cosmetics throughout the year (Up to October). In my opinion, this game is going to die out within a or two months if new content isn't added for free, and the wait for the full 'Season Pass' is just- too long for such little content.If you want to buy the game, wait for a sale. I'd say this game is worth $10 dollars in its current state (Base game), and maybe $15 dollars for the whole deluxe edition once everything comes out in october. I was just thoroughly let down by the lack of content and writing. I still truly hope it gets free updates through the year, but that is my only saving grace on changing my recommendation for this game, and even then I have to try out the hypothetical free content anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: For a fan who has played both Stick and Fractured, it is definitely a big change to what I'm used to.I've beaten the main story in normal mode at the time of this review, have 13 achievements, and yes, I have the STD. Socially Transmitted, that is.The game is pretty fun for what it is. I'm biased, partially because I got the game as a belated Birthday Gift, and also because I'm really into the show. I'm going to actually split up this review.- For those who like Stick Of Truth...This game is fine. It's got the characters playing their DND esque characters, but you don't get to play as said characters at any point. In Stick, it wasn't heavily emphasised for the fact you played with the characters, and instead formed itself on the creative way you could change or impact the story by picking elves or humans. It had an alright mode of combat, it wasn't too long (My first playthrough only took me some hours), and the story was somewhat intriguing. It was the first South Park game that really took off with its own story and plans, and has its charms. With that said, what is improved upon in both games is the combat, which unless you really liked how Stick played, that is a HUGE upgrade.- For those who like Fractured Butt WholeThe game is really a big shift from what you're used to if you're going into Snowday. In Fractured, the Customization has a bigger impact on your character, and not just talking about the Skin tone joke that everyone has seen. All clothing have stats, like in Stick, but as well as that, you collect MULTIPLE powers, allowing for your character to have so many outcomes. The story changes based off of your powers, your actions, blah blah... and said story, while its sometimes harder to follow, gives not only your character so much power, but gives us insight to the other characters in ways we didn't see before in just the base game. You see how Tweek and Craig work, you see how Kenny's alter-ego works with the other characters, you see much more with having to decide between which parent you love more. It's a genuinely interesting point, and again, like the original Stick, you get to play alongside the other characters. MORE of the characters too! While in Stick you only get to pick one buddy at a time, in Fractured, you get three at a time that cannot be switched during battle. Interesting.Now how do these two comparisons fall into place for Snowday?Snowday is in 3D obviously. A lot of people have ripped on it, but SouthPark isn't exactly made to be in 3D. With that said, it does well! I personally had a really noticable glitch however visually in every cutscene, PRESUMABLY because of my colour blindness settings. I've never had this problem before, but the colours and the lighting will flicker and change between every shot, and its really distracting.Otherwise, the visual art of the game, while sometimes the lighting can meld together really weird, the game is appealing, and I don't get a majority of the visual complaints besides "its not like Southpark." The opening cutscene in particular was a really nice transition!Audio wise, I found in my playthrough that there were some moments where without subtitles, I would not know what characters were saying, even in cutscenes! The mixing sometimes comes off as odd, where Cartman seems too quiet when yelling at Stan, or where Butters' voice sounds oddly far away, or where Kyle's speech is quiet AND only in the right ear, when that doesn't make sense visually. This again, might just be a problem for me.Playing wise, the game isn't too hard to grasp. I like the controls, minus the [Z] for emoting, but that's literally fine. Plus, you can change your Keybinds. There were a lot of times however where when I was swinging or aiming, or even switching between weapons, that it wouldn't charge up a shot, or charge an attack. This was even if I wasn't playing with other players.Multiplayer; I wish there was a communication feature, not too dissimilar to Splatoon. The reason I bring Splatoon as comparison being, they're compact, and they give you options that are ambiguous to situations at times. A simple "This way!" can mean a lot of things in a competitive shooter, but in a 4 player game, it's pretty obvious. "This way! We need you to move forward!" It'd be a time saver for sure. And yes, while you could say the new kid being the silent type contridicts this; just make it a pop up with a ding sound.Just an idea.Oh and yes, STD achievement comes from Multiplayer.Multiplayer otherwise just sometimes has glitches, or lag, or there's just nobody hosting, but if you host nobody joins. It's a weird cycle I've gone through at times and I can't really find the issue.Finally the Story.Story wise, it didn't make sense to me that the New Kid from the first game, was the same as the second game, and also this third game? I was under the assumption that the New Kid from Stick and Fracture were different new kids? Maybe I missed something while playing Stick and Fracture where they said that? It didn't click with me regardless. The Story with a majority of the characters feels rather brushed over. There were A LOT of Cutscenes in both Stick and Fracture, that would connect your character into the other characters' lives, so you would feel guilt in say, siding with the Elves, or siding with the Humans, or beating your first ever friend up, or having Cartman turn on you, or even just having your buddy die. There was a sense of guilt and consequence. In Snowday, the story is oddly disconnected from you as a player. You complete the quests in any way and the story goes on. There's a lack of any idea that your character connects to the other characters. In scenes after you've beat up the other characters, the only time they ever interact with you is if you fart on them. You can interact with Tweek and Craig, or Tolkien even feels more connected, and they will talk to you.With those at the table, the main four all talk amongst themselves, and in cutscenes, the only time they talk to your character is to tell them to do something. This is after having no time to actually interact with them as characters instead of beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of them in a boss battle.I admittedly play South Park games for the characters. Yet, it oddly enough doesn't feel like these Characters or their growth are even here, when we as the player character just sort of see the cutscenes happen and then go back into slicing and dicing.The game isn't terrible, it's not great either. I'm giving it a good, but I beat its main story and don't really feel anything about it. Not even disappointment just a weird sense of "what did I just play?" The final cutscene is  the most emotion I felt to the characters, but it wasn't really anything interesting for me. The ending cutscene doesn't have our player character at all, doesn't have our main four characters really learn anything besides they were wrong, and also they like the snowdays because it brings them together as friends.This game could have done more if it let us play as the other characters possibly. It could have done more if the levels were more interesting. It could have done more if the story had more than Randy showing up for toilet paper while the kids fight over who has better rules. _childDocuments_.review: Whatever you do, don’t go into South Park: Snow Day! expecting more of the same.   The same here being a sequel both narratively and mechanically to the franchise’s two excellent turn-based RPG adventure entries to come out in the last ten years. Instead, like most childhood snow days, South Park: Snow Day! is a flurry of high-intensity action that leaves you and your friends (if you have any) exhausted yet ends sooner than you wish it did.  Gone are the expansive, detail-stuffed, living episode story campaigns that made The Stick of Truth (2014) and The Fractured but Whole (2017) so fun to explore and unpack, replaced instead by five multiplayer ARPG missions, most of which are really just a series of wave-based arenas broken up by gates that unlock after you kill every. last. everything. Die and it’s back to the beginning, though, as with most modern rougelites, you’ll keep some currencies you can use to improve your individual stats for the next run. Whereas prior South Park entries focused on exploring the iconic titular town and interacting with its many unhinged inhabitants, Snow Day! is unapologetically a straightforward button-masher that’s only on occasion broken up by fairly low-effort fetch quests or environmental hazards you’ll need to blast your way through.  Now, if you’re a long-time fan and feeling a little low after this intro, chin up! There’s still a lot to enjoy about Snow Day, as it’s still very much an entry in the South Park saga. Most of the town’s usual suspects are on display here, and watching Stan, Kyle, Kenny, and Cartman bicker in crisp 3D cutscenes about their respective fantasy kingdoms and their liberal interpretations of Butters’ rulebook is endlessly entertaining. Well, not endless, I suppose, as one consequence of adding a dimension to the animation is subtracting from the story’s total runtime. I zipped through Snow Day’s enjoyable if unremarkable plot in about six hours (not sure why Steam says four), well short of the franchise’s prior story-heavy entries, and much of that time was spent grinding through trash mob after trash mob.   Luckily, the combat system itself is pretty fun. You’ll start each run after selecting from a handful of melee and ranged weapons, picking a couple of utility skills that are tied to your “Pissed Off!” adrenaline meter, and then choosing between several global “♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥” cards, like bubble shields or meteor showers, that can quickly turn the tide of a battle. I spent most of my runs wielding the gap-closing dual daggers, an elemental wand, an AOE healing totem that can help revive downed allies, and this putrid cat urine spray ability that temporarily flips baddies to your team. At the end of each arena, Jimmy will offer you an upgrade card that you can further buff if you slip him a toilet paper bribe, because people’s priorities change during an endless snowstorm, ya know? At the end of each mission—each of which gets you closer to unearthing the mysterious cause of this apocalyptic snowstorm—you’ll face a boss, one of whom is a secret character the publisher explicitly told me not to mention. These boss fights deliver mechanical depth, challenge, humor, and spectacle, and each combines with Snow Day’s above-average soundtrack to make for a memorable end to each mission.  Before wrapping up, I’ve seen some allegations swirling about Steam forums that this game is a microtransaction-riddled hellscape, and I can happily report that that’s not the case. While the multiplayer-oriented Snow Day! is a big shift for South Park Digital Studios, I completed the game without spending a dime, and only once did the game tease some optional DLC my way. As the matchmaking servers were down while recording my pre-release review, I also got through the game just fine on my own, unless you count the auto-fill bots that seamlessly join your empty party at the start of combat encounters.  In the end, Snow Day! fails to live up to the lofty standards set by The Stick of Truth and The Fractured but Whole, but it’s still a fun, funny little time that mostly justifies its $30 price tag. I’m giving Snow Day! an aggregate MEGA score of 3.21/5 (full scoring breakdown, from Plot to Sound, available in video form) and am happy to answer any questions you have about the game or my review.

_childDocuments_.review: If you come into this expecting another Stick of Truth or Fractured But Whole, you will be very disappointed.That being said, I really like whats here, but I also understand the "mixed" rating the game has. Its not trying to be either of those games, its trying to be something different, and I really do appreciate the effort to make something different rather than making the same game for the third time. This is a level-based, action rpg with a focus on combat over story, and it does this pretty well.I feel that this is a great starting point for a much larger game. As it stands, there are 5 chapters in the game, and once that's done, you've experienced all the story this game has to offer, but there is some ounce of replayability within these 5 chapters. Segments are randomly selected from a few options of locations, each with its own enemy placement and variety. The levels are very nice renditions of popular South Park locations, but as this is "Snow Day" everything is covered in snow, which makes the levels blend together in a rather disappointing sort of way, it makes them feel same-y.The story is funny, a continuation of the New Kid's adventures with Stan, Kyle, Cartman, Kenny and Butters. Other popular characters, such as Tolkien, Tweek, Craig, Clyde, and even Henrietta and Nichole make appearances, with some segments of the game revolving around helping some of the adult characters, like Randy, Ned and Jimbo. But THATS IT! There are almost no other characters that are remotely involved in the story, or even make an appearance.I was disappointed by the lack of single-player support. You can play offline with 3 bots, but this makes the game SIGNIFICANTLY harder. They really push for you to play levels with other players, much like a "Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance" experience.I think there's more to come with this game after the dlc for the season pass has released, and I do look forward to that, and the game itself at the base level is only $30, I paid $50 for the digital deluxe edition, which I feel i got my money's worth. I also purchased the $220 Collector's Edition for PS5, and I think the quality of items was really high, but not really worth $220, I feel $150 would be a more appropriate price point for that edition.All in all, I really like this game, its a great experience with friends, and I will continue playing it until I reach 100%, but am definitely going back to playing SoT and FBW for the 10th+ time afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand why the game has gotten mixed reviews, but also am upset that it has. People saw this game and wanted it to be another version of the previous two games which is completely understandable, I would've loved that too, so people keep comparing those two perfect games to this game. Is this as good as them? No not really, but that doesn't mean this is a bad game. Personally the price of the game also does not really match how long the game is, but disregarding the price and not comparing it to the previous games, this game itself is still a very fun game. They took that players wanted a co-op south park game and this is what they thought we wanted, it's not, but it is still a fun game and I'm sure it is fun with friends too. _childDocuments_.review: As a dedicated fan of the South Park game franchise, I was thoroughly disappointed with their latest release, South Park Snow Days. The game developers have failed to understand that game development requires a balance between a captivating story and innovative technology. Instead of creating an interesting story and meaningful gameplay mechanics, the developers chose to make a 3D game out of a 2D artwork, leading to a lackluster game experience.I urge the developers to learn from their mistakes and take note of what makes a great game - the story, the gameplay, and the overall experience. As a fan, I hope that the developers will invest more time and effort into creating a compelling story and engaging gameplay mechanics in future South Park games. As for South Park Snow Days,  I  hope this is  the last game I returning due to its poor storytelling and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so let's start by saying I have been DYING to play these games but never could justify spending the better part of $100.00 or more to get all 3. I picked these up during the recent THQNordic sale. I completed the Stick of Truth in 11 hours (did miss quite a bit achievement wise but whatever), and Fractured But Whole in about 18 hours, not any of the DLC's but I'll come back to that.This is a fun, re-imagined style of the South Park games. It's a lot more hack-n-slash, a little more open-world in the sense that you're not just fighting on a stage every time but actually fighting in a 3D environment you can move through with obstacles, jumps, overwatch areas, chokes, etc. I get what they were trying to do, but they did it so right and so wrong.Firstly, even after just an hour in this game I can tell you it makes a critical error a lot of other games do - forcing you to be the entertainment. Yes of course there is a short story, it is funny, there's a lot of classic characters that make appearances and funny dialogue, but the game is so co-op centered that the combat feels extremely boring and repetitive despite the open movement and 3D environment theme. You just fight waves and waves and waves and oh no, a stronger wave with some special enemies, then you do that 3-5x per chapter then fight a boss. The entire time all you hear is one-liner dialogue being clipped off by combat, generic combat music, and honestly some grossly unbalanced weapon sounds. (The staves are unbearably badly mastered, they're louder than any other thing in the game by like 4-1.)You can beat this game in about 4 hours if you push and there isn't anything really to do after that. Again, the game is banking on you playing with 1-3 friends and frankly, I do not myself, nor do a lot of other people, have 3 friends wanting to play a kitschy, niche comedy game when there are so many other titles at their disposal. Secondly, bugs. Bugs, bugs, bugs. Lots of clipped dialogue, progression loss, awkward movement and combat mechanics.Thirdly, lack of inspiration. Again, I go back to the devs relying on YOU and YOUR FRIENDS to make it fun. There was endless customization in SoT, endless customization in FbW, in this game you can choose 1 of 3 melee weapons which are VERY generic and 1 of 3 ranged weapons which are also incredibly generic. No buddies, no puzzles, no mysteries, no open-world, no choice in what you do next. It's a linear, 5-chapter hack-n-slash abomination that relies on you and your buddies to make it fun, rather than the game itself being fun.As I said previously, I really get what they were trying to do but this just isn't it. I finished the first chapter and said aloud to myself "Well, I guess I'm going back to FbW to play the DLC's after all" because this game just failed to inspire, which sucks because I was excited as hell to play this after logging nearly 32 hours in the last two games over the past week or so. (Yes I have no life on my days off and am a die-hard SP fan, judge me.)All in all it's not terrible, it's just very, very below the bar the last two games set. After SoT I was skeptical about FbW being only able to customize my costume and abilities but not necessarily items and equipment, but this is a far cry from even that. Pick 1 of 3 weapons for melee and ranged. Pick 2 abilities. Go fight endless waves of nonsense and we'll give you 45 seconds of funny dialogue and story after. Repeat 5 times. End of game.Trey and Matt talked about this game praising how you can "make you own kid" and loving the idea of the "blank slate New Kid" who is whoever you are, which was great in the first two games. There is 70% less customization in Snow Day than SoT and FbW so I have no idea what they were talking about. You don't even get gear, or an inventory, or crafting, or on-use items or potions or summons. They stripped away everything great about the first two games to make it 3D and Co-Op. Which again leads me back to, and say it with me - You and your friends are expected to fill the gap of a lackluster story and overall weirdly short game. Classic case of shooting for the stars but forgetting to bring your spacesuit, or oxygen, or the keys to the space ship, per se. Get it while it's on sale and you'll have a few hours of monotonous beat-em-up interspersed with quips and one-liners from your favorite residents but other than that, especially if you like the first two games, prepare to be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the greatest game, but definitely better than a 3/10 (IGN)South Park Snow Day brings a fresh twist to South Park, and while everyone is griping that we aren't getting another Stick of Truth or Fractured but Whole, I was definitely excited to see a different kind of game coming with Snow Day. Yes, the game is short, but its all about replaying the levels on higher difficulties or with different equipment/cards. I have genuinely enjoyed the time I have spent playing the game so far and can see nothing but potential for the future of this game. With some regularly added content, this game could do very well. I really think adding some sort of PVP mode would be the biggest addition to make this game that much better. There could be a capture the flag type game mode, or even a "VIP" style mode where each side has 1 of the 4 South Park kids as their leader to protect while they try and take out the other. I know this would be an extensive add, but with multiplayer co-op already being there, I wouldn't think it would be too much to add something like that, if even for a limited time event.I am excited to see the future of this game and hope there is a lot more to come. With new weapons, cosmetics, story chapters, and game modes this game will become great! All in all, I'd say this game is a solid 6/10 with lots of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game wasn't outright bad, its not anything close to the previous iterations. I wouldn't hold that against this game if it wasn't for the lackluster product its become overall. It just doesn't offer enough to justify it as a good title, but not terrible enough to outright condemn it.The premise of the game is clearly a wave based brawler in 3d. Very action oriented, no more of that turn based stuff from the previous games. Enemy types fairly limited overall, combined with a paltry five missions that you can clear in a single sitting; it almost feels like this game should have been early access. The card system and how it resets every mission at least makes replays possibly more challenging or at the very least slightly different each time. I'd almost compare the level designs and objectives in each mission to be like that of vermintide, but even vermintide isn't this linear. A big plus is coop for me, and I highly recommend going in with others because the bots are just not that good and don't bring as much variation or support to each skirmish.Sadly, I have to give this game a thumbs down as its negatives do outweigh most of its positives for the price tag its sold at. This is a discount buy at best, otherwise just go back to Stick of Truth or Fractured But Whole.

But this wasn't a redemption story. It was a shameless cash grab. And my favorite part of the last two games was completely absent from this installment. This game reminds me of how they'll throw SpongeBob on various games as a rebrand to sell old ideas off the famous characters. No story immersion here to be had, no "bringing players into South Park".. I fell cheated honestly. They could have just made another DLC for TFBW and made millions happy for the same price of 29.99!?!? Instead we got this, the first game on steam (the only) that I've asked a refund for. To each they're own I guess.. But this was my experience and 2 cents.

_childDocuments_.review: Snow Day is much different from the last two games by the South Park team (Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole)If you're a fan of the show you should love it!The title is short, but sweet at 5 levels that are intended to be replayed with new incentives overtime. Took about ~8 hours to play the game for the first time beginning to end and feels like a lost episode of the show.You might prefer Stick of Truth/fracture style overall, but it's fun to see the team mix it up for a unique game Stick of Truth/Fracture But Whole still feel like they hold value with Snow Day, because do miss free roaming the town and going into the characters homes. Some scale is lost by going 3D where maybe a future game could be the perfect mix of the elements. The Snow Day combat is so much better than the turnbased, and overall a game is suppose to fun and Snow Day is just that. The game mixes 2D cutscenes like seeing the show and even in full 3D it still feels in the tone of South Park with a new never before seen vibe (at least since N64!). Just seeing the lights reflect off the snow in 3D is a fun new experience from a cartoon that started with construction paper. Really has the "Hit and Run" feeling when simpsons went 3d, yet it still feels like the show it came from.  Just so much fun! Play it!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game.  Sorta short.  I like how after beating the game that there is a new layer of items to receive and dark matter options to attain. I'm not disappointed, but I did expect a bit more.  I still feel that the pre-release reviews were a little too tough on the devs, but I'm not sure if I want to spend more money on this game with the upcoming DLC's if it is more of the same.  If the DLC's are $5-$7 then that would be acceptable.  Definitely not worth buying the season pass right from the get go.  I am hoping that there are content updates planned to expand upon gameplay, without having to buy a DLC.  This game is MUCH shorter than The Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole.  Would play again with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Trey Parker, Matt Stone, and the Steam Community,This game isn't terrible, but it's not that good either. As a long-time fan who has been watching South Park for 22 years, I was incredibly excited for the past year to dive into a new South Park game. I always love the work they do! However, my excitement quickly turned to disappointment as I found that this game had restrictive exploration, limited scope, short length, lack of humor, lack of difficulty, and lack of engaging content.One of the aspects that disappointed me the most was the game's restrictive exploration. As a devoted South Park fan, I was excited about the prospect of exploring the town's familiar locales and getting into the kind of hilarious mischief the show is famous for. However, my expectations fell short when I realized I was confined to Cartman's backyard with little room for exploration. This lack of freedom to roam around town was a significant letdown for me. I actually found myself looking at distance mountains and buildings from Cartman's Backyard pissed off that I didn't have the option to travel there on my own.On top of the restrictive exploration, the game's overall length and difficulty level were also disappointing. Playing on hard mode, my friends and I managed to complete the game in about two hours. Surprisingly, we only encountered one challenging moment early on, where we died once due to the learning curve. After that initial hurdle, the game felt relatively easy and lacked the sustained challenge we were hoping for. Then, after just 5 chapters, the game was over. This quick completion time, combined with the lack of difficulty, left us feeling like the game was over before it truly began.Despite its shortcomings, I must admit that the powers, weapons, and cards in the game are pretty cool. South Park Snow Day does a decent job of incorporating the show's signature humor and style into its gameplay mechanics. The variety of abilities and items at your disposal adds a layer of strategy and fun to the game. However, the enjoyment I derived from these elements was somewhat overshadowed by the game's limited scope and short length. It's a shame that these cool features weren't fully utilized in a more expansive and engaging gameplay experience.In conclusion, my experience with South Park Snow Day was disappointing. With limited gameplay, lack of humor, restrictive exploration, limited difficulty, lack of engaging content, and short length left me feeling unsatisfied as a fan. I hope that future South Park games will provide a more immersive and enjoyable experience for fans like myself. Hopefully, this was just a rough draft for a potential South Park RPG. If Trey Parker & Matt Stone were to take the foundation of this game and expand upon it, adding more content and depth, it could potentially be a solid experience. Until then, as fellow gamers themselves, I believe Trey Parker and the team can understand why I gave this game a thumbs down. I'll continue to play and will update my review if the DLC's make the game more expansive.Yours truly, Chat GPT

There's only 8 base weapons with 2 alts, so 10 weapons in total & 8 magics. Which at first sound like a lot but quickly just meh. The story is fine enough if not extremely predictable. In short, get this game if you like South Park & you like repetition for no real reward. Otherwise just play Stick of Truth or Fractured but Whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. I think a lot of the reviews are honestly pretty dramatic for the studio trying something different. I also prefer the older style with turn-based, however, I can't fault the studio for trying something new and executing it fairly well.What  deserve to be ripped on is that if you're playing solo, you can't beat the game on the final boss...or at least it was impossible for myself. The AI is  that they all insta-die in the same spot right off the bat, leaving all of [BOSS] to target you, and , with  of AOE dumped in ONE massive area that you  get out of. If you die, there is no loading in at checkpoints, you have to redo the  level. For the other levels it wasn't a big deal because it would rotate (which was pretty fun), but it seems unacceptable for the final level that is entirely story locked. You'll waste 20-30 minutes just to get back to the boss stage again and again, until you realize that it's not doable solo.If you want to combat that you can't do it solo, you have to use matchmaking...AND the matchmaking . You cannot see what lobbies to join, you join randomly into random quest chapters even if you select what chapter. If you're hosting, it takes forever. You're essentially put in waiting hell if you don't have friends who're willing to play with you and have the final chapter unlocked. The only other glaring issue that wasn't too big of a deal was the audio. The levels are a bit all over the place.The game is genuinely fun and rogue-like, the story is solid and short, but obviously with the game style changing it's less in depth and less skits. It's less playtime and in-depth than Stick of Truth, but it's $20 less and re-playable if you're into rogue-likes. I love South Park, but the game was clearly not properly tested before launch and I personally would prefer if they don't do the rogue-like again.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review to correct a few statements i'm seeing across other reviews here. You have not "beaten the game" in 3-5 hours. You might have finished each of the main missions ONCE in that time, but that does not constitute "beating the game". Each mission is different - I've replayed one mission 3 times in a row, after failing the boss fight with some randoms, and had different missions picked every time. For example - the 3rd mission where you have to "pass the trial of strength" - can be multiple different missions: Lighting the Witchfyre Pyres, Stealing from the 6th Graders, Helping Jimbo find items to sell- and even further, the items and locations are different in every run as well. To add on to this, After you beat the 3rd mission, you unlock free DLC via Henrietta which gives you access to unending zombie-survival style missions, AND after you beat the last mission of the campaign, you unlock Nichole, who allows you to take on extra challenges for other rewards, similar to HEAT in Hades. Now for the Cons - Yes, the game is "short" but it's made with replayability in mind. Different card combos let you play in different ways and playing with friends massively increases what is viable versus playing solo where you basically need to run a healing ability and an escape. Having one person with a heal and a turret while a melee person runs the charge and gravity bomb is a blast. pun intended. The options are a bit limited now - there are only 3 main melee weapons and 3 ranged weapons, but i expect more to be added eventually, and the cards you pick still allow you quite a bit of variety to how you play. My single biggest complaint has to be the lack of a communication system of any kind. No voice, no chat - all you have are emotes, so unless you're playing people you already know in discord, it's pretty hard to communicate specific ideas like "I'm running these powerups" or "I need to run to the restroom". etc. All in all - this is not multiplayer Stick of Truth or FBW, it's more of a hack and slash with some roguelike elements, but for the price, i think it's a fine game to pick up to play with a friend or two.EDIT: Well, It seems we've been let down again. The new Snowball weapon is PAID DLC, so even though they're tossing us a few free cosmetic DLCs, the actual gameplay elements (which the game SORELY needs) are locked behind an additional paywall... I had some solid hopes for this game, but it seems to be diving further into being a piece of trash. RIP.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I LOVE south park, but this game ain't worth 30 bucks. The Good: The art is great for a 3D rendition of south park! They keep the cut scenes similar to that of a south park episode, but the game play animation feels more smooth. The Game play overall was fine with the rogue-lite elements of the card system allowing you to choose how to strengthen your abilities. There are cards specifically for each of the different weapons as well as your powers!The Meh/Bad: Story (Meh):The story is neat as it feels like that of a "Special", but it lacks the impact of one. The story was way too short with 5 levels in total with each varying in length from 30-50 minutes depending on how much you rush through. I played through the game on Hard difficulty for all levels, but I only party-wiped once on my play through. There also didn't appear to be that many jokes aside from Butters and Cartman giving you ♥♥♥♥ in the middle of combat. The ending also felt rather unsatisfying as it left me disappointed with a feeling of "That's it? That was the entire game/story?" Abilities (less than Meh):I played through this game solo, so I was given 3 other AI "new kids" to play with, but they are limited to combating and reviving you. You are also able to choose from a list of 8 powers at a limit of to two choices of "powers" that you can select before starting my mission, but the AI do not appear to have any powers equipped whatsoever. Now I don't have an issue with the abilities themselves, what I have an issue with is feeling the need to equip the grouo healing power (I believe is the only healing power that doesn't require cards.). Completing this game by yourself is slightly challenging as you have to rely on your AI teammates to stay alive while also keeping yourself alive, and since they can't use the group healing power, you would likely need it to stay alive. This leaves one spot as a "for fun" power that you can choose from. Now maybe the easier difficulties would've allowed me to not feel the need to bring the healing power, but I do not want to bother replaying the same missions to find out.Replayabiltiy (Bad): There appears to be a lack of any real replay-ability in my opinion. Sure you can buy upgrades, but they keep increasing in price requiring a larger grind. I only needed about 6-9 upgrades to complete the game, so any more would begin to feel like overkill. When you complete the game, you can find another character in the levels to make a pact with and make the levels more challenging.... for cosmetics. I didn't do this as the levels felt meh by themselves, so I don't want to replay them again just to make it slightly harder. There are also only 3 melee weapons and 3 ranged weapons in the base game in which I only touched 1 of each as I thought there would be more story/game to work with.Price (Bad):This game is not worth $30 for a 5 hour experience (4 hours if you don't die!) with alright game play and a unsatisfying story. I also checked the DLC list, which also appears to be just filler content and nothing new to the story. I also thought the Underpants Gnome Cosmetic would be exclusive to pre-orders, but boy was I stupid at thinking such since you can buy this mediocre cosmetic for 3 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not anything crazy and expecting anything besides southpark being southpark is getting your hopes up for a game you're not getting. TLDR; if you expected them to make a 3rd installment of the other 2 games' themes, this isn't for you. If you enjoy southpark and just wanted to have a little fun for a under 60 game, you 110% can get something you'll enjoy from this.This was a pretty decent and fun roguelike with a more centered focus on the overall story. It was short but a nice little break from other games. Hard mode gave me a balanced amount of combat so I'd recommend playing on that for more of a challenging or honestly just better combat to engage with. This is a game to have fun for a few hours, with friends or randoms or bots, and just chill with it. The roguelike elements are actually pretty good for a roguelike. They flow a lot better than a lot of roguelikes tend to struggle with and you genuinely feel upgrades. The skill tree is a bit grindy but functions as actual upgrades for your character. Balancing is maybe a bit off but for the most part, everything seemed like it could be used without putting yourself at a massive determinant for using what you want. Co-op worked really well. I was able to jump into random matches without a hitch and playing with friends didn't take ages to join. They even have settings so you can dodge getting spoilers while matchmaking.The world itself is pretty well done but maybe feels a little too lifeless at times as the city is covered in snow and a lot less south park residents are going outside.Jokes were a little toned down but to be expected. Much much harder for the IP to use as much edgy humor categories as it did in the past with other games. That definitely was noticeable but nothing crazy. The characters acted like kids on a snow day in south park. What you would want.Combat is a little jank at times but there's some real combos out there you can have fun with. Use the flamethrower wand and the black hole balloon. You'll have some funAll in all, this game delivered a fun little 3D experience. 30 bucks is a little steep for the amount of content but where there isn't content to play, a lot of the work obviously went into making sure the game felt like the IP in 3D and making it keep the theme. It's biggest flaw is that game mechanics needed more focus over the look but when we're talking about games that are using a IP, this definitely is not at the bottom. It's a pretty mid in that regard. Content looks like it could be pretty decent for anyone wanting to rotate this game as a little breather from others. We'll have to see what they have planned once we start seeing visuals of that DLC. And it's important to note day 1 DLC did happen and that's always a rough move to make in consumerism. I'm not a fan of this tactic but it wasn't crazy overpriced 20 dollar skins so not really as bad. Just leaves a bad taste in people's mouths.

_childDocuments_.review: (TLDR SUMMARY) This game is a pathetic disappointment which seems slapped together hastily with no care toward the original content or its many fans. The graphics are ugly, the gameplay is shallow, the story is minimal/lacking, and the level design is lazy. This is coming from someone who has perfected Fractured But Whole, and is a huge fan of the show; do not waste your money on this pathetic attempt at a South Park Game. I told myself, if I can't trust the South Park creators to make a fun game, then I can't trust anyone. This was it, I promised myself when I was pre-purchasing this game, that if it sucked I would never pre-purchase any game ever again. And I am so very disappointed. South Park: Snow Day is a third person hack-n-slash game that is largely reminiscent of Vermintide 2 and Left 4 Dead 2 (but not either of the other South Park games). You drop into a level and fight a bunch of no-name enemies. These enemies include 4th graders, 5th graders, and preschoolers; all of whom unfortunately have the voice of a preschooler (the. same. exact. voice). Also unlike Vermintide 2 and Left 4 Dead 2, the weapons and special abilities are all; basic, boring, and lacking in any form of variety. Unlike those games though, which contain many fun levels with interesting and unique playable characters; South Park Snow Day has five completely generic levels that look incredibly similar, with four completely generic playable characters. You are no longer "The New Kid", you are one of thousands of new kids that hang out with Cartman and follow his orders. Every cutscene seems desperate to make you feel unique, "You're the real New Kid" Cartman says repeatedly; only for you to drop into another random game where the main cast call you Player # (1-4) in any cutscene. Cartman constantly complains about you being "OP" and ruining the previous two games for everyone involved, invalidating any success that you might have once had. The kids in South Park have decided to make everything fair with random card draws and balanced mechanics, so you can no longer be the cool New Kid you once were.Speaking of the levels, I now understand why this game is a winter wonderland; the developers couldn't be bothered to actually program South Park in 3D. The game has covered absolutely everything in a mountain of snow, a basic and repetitive texture that in no way resembles South Park. They include a sign or an occasional building from the original town, but none of them can be explored or entered, merely being a part of the background! You are forced onto a linear path during your travels during which you are constantly surrounded by hoards of enemies. There is no time for exploration, there is no time for humor, there is not time for fun. Between button mashing like crazy one or two characters deliver a singular voice line. This game lazily throws South Park tropes in the players face between bland and monotonous gameplay. One of the main cutscenes in the story is Cartman doing his "ha ha ha ha ha ha na na na na na na" laugh, Kyle saying "f*** you Cartman", and then cutting away. The next thing you know everyone is at a table and chatting, and the war you had only just started waging is ALREADY OVER!I am a very easy man to please when it comes to games, so long as the game reaches a certain bar of quality, and posses any of the following qualities: The games need to be fun, or made with love, or contain pleasant art, or have a well-made story. This game does not meet ANY of those standards. I WANTED TO LOVE THIS GAME! I WAITED FOR SO LONG TO ENJOY THIS GAME!The disappointment I feel right now is crushing. I...will never pre-purchase any game ever again. Please do not waste your money. This game is worth $10 at most.It's insulting that the game puts such focus on getting your friends to play with you How is anyone supposed to convince their friends to play with crap with them? Why would they want their friends to waste their money to play these 5 levels with them?

_childDocuments_.review: It's South Park but without all crude humor and ridiculousness that makes South Park...South Park. Yes, there are some funny moments but it's the cleanest South Park among the show and games and I don't understand why. Gameplay wise, it's as basic as can be but fun to play. The card system is different but nothing new or groundbreaking. Back 4 Blood has a similar system if you're familiar with that game but Snow Days is beyond simplistic along with everything else. The cards given to you change based on what weapons and abilities you are currently using. The card will apply some sort of modifier to the weapon or ability. There are plenty of different variations which are nice but it's so limited to what cards you get since you only draw cards 3-5 times in a level. This would have been much nicer if we actually collected the cards and had a type of loud out to stick to based on your preference. There's no RPG element to this game. There's one item (Dark Matter also known as Poo) that is the games level currency. You collect it through each level and then use it to purchase Perks that range from upping your damage, raising health to higher rates of Dark Matter and Toilet Paper drops when playing. Toilet Paper is the other currency that is only used within each level and does not carry over once your run is completed. During the run you will collect and use TP to level up your Cards to raise the modifier on whatever card you choose to level up. These level ups only apply during that one level/mission.The game itself is broken down into 5 levels/runs. Each level has you traversing through a section with an objective while enemies attack you trying to complete objective. Once you complete the objective and clear enemies you'll get a card and then proceed to the next section. Some randomness the game has may have you doing one section on the same level one time and then you go to play the level again and you'll get a section you may not have played through on the last time you played the level which does add some variety but not much as there's only a small set of these sections.Once you beat the game you unlock modifiers to the level which will handicap you which adds some replayability as doing these modified missions will get you extra cosmetics.tl/dr Summary: Could have been a much bigger game with more detailed RPG elements and things to collect/level up over your career and also be consistent with South Park humor and story telling as whole like the previous two games.Pros: -Art looks really great. Seeing the 3D models of all the characters was really cool as well as seeing the town of South Park as a 3D environment.-Weapons, and abilities are limited but fun to use.-Great Co-Op Game-Wasn't $60-Each run is somewhat unique in the encounters. You can play the same level twice and you may not get the same sequences each time which adds some variety and replay-ability but not a lot.-There's is a free DLC add-on for a horde mode with 4 levels but it only lasts 8 waves and takes maybe 20 minutes to do.-Encountered very minimal bugs and performance wise plays really well.Cons:-Costs $30-Will take 3-5 hours to complete if you really chill and take your time. Potentially shorter.-No feedback loop.-Cosmetic Unlockables only-No leveling system-Perk system is basic and grindy for no real reward.-No PvP-No real reason to keep playing it after beating the story other than to grind dark matter for perks but what's the point?Overall: Could have been much more. Needs PvP and double the amount of story missions to make this worth $30. Due to the poor sales performance I really doubt this gets a whole lot of updates but who knows. I'm happy to have played it but had I known what I was getting, I would have waited till it was $15-$20. It's a hard choice on giving it a recommendation or not but at this time, I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this for a total of 39 minutes and in all honesty, after 39 minutes, you'll get the gist of what this game has to offer which is very little in comparison to its predecessors.  I am ALL for a game or genre throwing out what works for the sake of experimentation.  It's experimentation that pushes games to actually innovate on stale formulas. but we have seen what a successful south park game looks like, and we've seen it adapt and evolve. I would hardly call what was built in "The Stick of Truth" and "The Fractured But Whole" stale or old, but I can tell before the first hour is up that this game ain't it.  It barely scratches the roguelite surface, with levels that are too short to see builds evolve or come together and too dull to keep things interesting.  Apparently, at only 5 levels offering a barely acceptable level of variety, the result of the tutorial and first level is just you clumsily trudging from fight to fight through generic biomes and and boring enemy types getting cards that make things slightly more interesting and losing those cards before you get to see your idea of a build come together.  Cards make combat visually appealing but players won't be doing anything differently to make them happen, resulting in a game that mechanically is low effort, forcing the 3D visuals to carry the weight.  But while a lot of the humor and appeal of South Park is when it pushes the envelope, here that bite is pretty much non-existent.  I'm sure there are things to like as players get later into their play sessions, and at $29 its a low ticket to entry for a group of friends, but I find it hard to want to continue playing a game so bland and plain in the face of what South Park, and other developers, have done before at higher costs.  If you're new to South Park games, ignore this one entirely.  If you're a South Park vet, be prepared to be disappointed and confused at how we got here.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial thoughts: This is the most 6-out-of-10 game I have ever played and therefore it gets a recommend, but it's just so limited. It doesn't do anything BAD (well, elf voices are kind of crap) it just doesn't do anything exceptionally well. However, the more I play it the more I kind of like it because the card system is worthwhile and I do like unlocking stuff and having modifiers. They can go a long way in making fights feel different. If nothing else I will forever appreciate the "bulls***" mechanic where you can play specific "bulls*** cards" to give an insane modifier for a few seconds, like invincibility, resurrection, metoer rain, etc. They are appropriately named because we've all played games where something happens and you say "that's such bulls***" so props on that. Otherwise, it's a kind of janky 4 player co op. I feel like initially the enemies do too much damage but maybe it's just the right amount? I've never died, but have come close. Upgrades feel impactful. Running/sliding on ice get tedious quickly but there are upgrades you can buy to lessen that. At first i hated the dagger combat but then realized that if you can get better at timing the dives it can be kind of fun. Ricochet arrows are the way to go. I'm also a little more inclined to be positive about the game because Question, the developer, did a decent enough job here after landing this license and they do not have a ton of games under their belt. Definitely need to see more small developers doing well. They priced it on the cheap, and you can find it even cheaper, so it might ultimately be worth your time. Maybe watch some no-commentary gameplay videos and judge for yourself. Don't believe everything some rando on youtube with a ring light, webcam and bad facial hair or cat ears thinks about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The price tag should clue you in that the game is very light on content (as far as single player is concerned) so far, but what it does have now is worth the $30. The screenshots are doing the game a huge disservice - it's true that the game takes its cue from the intentionally rudimentary visuals of the TV series, and the fact that it's set in snow stages limits the colors you will see at any given time to predominantly white and grey. But if you crank up the quality to Ultra (and the game is optimized enough that you can do it even on a mid-to-low-end card like the RX 6600), it's got a lot of lighting effects that make the game look a lot more vibrant than it should.The combat is tight enough as far as hack and slash combat goes, but the gameplay loop itself feels a little bit underdeveloped - like it was only part of a much larger game. Think of it as very similar in structure to Plants vs. Zombies: Garden Warfare 2's Turf Takeover game mode. Hopefully they polish it a bit more over time.Story is where the game really shines. Sure, the dialogue and themes are overly sanitized compared to what you will see on the show (and this should surprise no one, in our age of censorship), but it still contains Stone and Parker's trade mark wit. Everybody still feels in character (Cartman is still crass and lacks morals, Kyle is still the snappy nemesis, Butters is butters, etc.). Haven't tried multiplayer yet. I have no opinion on it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a recent player to this game the only problem I am experiencing is lack of other players.Despite some people saying this game is short, it is 5 episodes that run atleast an hour+ long each depending on the level. Each level being snow themed but each having their own specific set of difficulty modifiers that are random though different aspects of the game. Every level ending with a different boss and each having their own fighting mechanics. (At the time of this review they have added more levels as well.)This the game is a fun multiplayer game where the announcer will comment on the performance of the team along with a decent variety of ways to fight. Snow day also has an endgame about finishing out the lengthy skill tree by collecting points, you can also collect special cosmetics by continuously increasing the difficulty and increasing the rewards mid gameplay. The game is about taking that 1+ hour and evolving yourself as the level progresses, you can choose your weapons and abilities but the upgrades that follow are randomized.There are no microtransactions.I like this game and appreciate buying it when it went on sale.  Its a tough game solo, so where my shorties @??
