_childDocuments_.review: It took me a few days to be able to write this review and a few days of playing.Snow day is only and only a co-op game. Real players get replaced when not available, so you play in a group of four. That makes it a PVE RPG.  Something fans asked for? I don't know.Now I was looking and searching for the RPG elements, since single player is not available for this game they are limited.  You have the choice though, through gathering DM, dark matter your character gets stronger and you can choose to be a Thief, or a heavy fighter. the Mage character is somehow missing in the perks but I guess you have to choose abilities that match Mages in order to play. Laser Eyes for example..The whole run i was searching in Kupa keep for the weapon and abilities perks i had collected and upgraded.Since I mentioned single player is missing in this game this RPG element is limited.Everything depends on the run you make, say you want to play the first chapter you can upgrade weapon and ability perks with toiletpaper you collected through Jimmy but these upgrades are temporarily.I say this because 'the book of laws' Butter is holding in kupa keep only contains COMMON cards you collected (so no upgrades)  If you people  know different please tell me.So I guess this game is PVE minded and you cant expect much more than a group adventure through 5 missions.Its a good waste of time, the graphics are amazing, the controls are less, fighting wise I dont like how the bow shoots for exampleI hope the south park developpers never stop making games, though it was a bold decision to turn this game around. I hope they come back soon with a sequel to the fractured butthole, a single player game with some nice 3D action, i am sure they can do it!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the skepticism from 2d to 3d change, I was really hoping that this game would at least be fun with the creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone being in control over this game.  Within the 1 hour of playing this game, I wasn't having fun.  It's a boring hack n slash with rogue-like elements thrown into the game.  Mind you, this is coming from a guy who has over 800 hours on Warframe, mindlessly pressing buttons whilst feeling like a braindead old white fart who sits at a casino pressing a button.The game tells you that you can use charge attacks but what's the point when all you do is mindlessly hack and slash like as if it's a dynasty warriors game.  The gameplay feels like PS2/PS3 God of War games, you defeat enemies, acquire currency that you can use to spend on stuff.  The abilities and weapons in this game are also pretty lackluster.  I'm not sure if there are actually more weapons that you can get later in the game but from what I saw, it's lackluster.The soundtrack is not as memorable as the ones from the previous games, the sound effects are also really not satisfying to hear.  They sound so dull and unsatisfying, the previous south park games had really good sound design.  When I strike my daggers into a bunch of elf baddies in this game, it just feels like I'm slapping baddies with a napkin or when I'm using the fart rocket ability, there's no punch.  Sure there is a fart noise but it doesn't sound loud enough and there's no punch to it.  It just feels like the game's audio is glitchy when it's not.  It's just feel so dull and dead.  It's like having the BFG-9000 from DOOM 2016 making the most pathetic silent firing sound effect in video games.The voice acting in this game is really cheesy as well, I'm not talking about the original voice actors for South Park, they do a good job in this game.  The voice actors for the elf enemies sound so cheesy and corny.  It ranges from funny like in a so bad it's good movie to just annoying.  They sound like Ike, I'm not even sure if these elf characters I was fighting were meant to be other forth graders or younger kids.The charm in this game is also lackluster, I remember first time I played Stick of Truth.  First thing I did when I saw Cartman was melee attack and fart him while he complains, berates and cusses at me.  I did this with passerby people as well and the reactions are funny to hear.  That was funny and it never gets old.  For this game, it doesn't feel fun to bully Cartman or anyone, the reactions feel like they don't care.The character customization is a downgrade from the previous entries.  In the previous entries, you can change the color of your clothing, in this game you there is no color changing.  I get that this was probably difficult for the 2d games but this a 3d game, you can make multiple textures or use a color sliding tool.  It really doesn't make sense in my eyes.On the plus side, the game has a tolerable file size which these days with AAA games becoming more and more space hungry.  It's a plus in my books.  I'm able to play the game at maximum framerate with Ultra graphics.  .  I haven't found a laundry list of bugs that break the game.  Which is also a plus in my books.  The animations on the characters when they talk is alright and the models look decent.  But that doesn't mean that this game is fun.  The game uses unreal engine 4 so people can just extract the assets for modding.This game feels like a game I found on Yahoo! Games back in the 2000s that was extracted by the developers and turned into a south park game.  This game is disappointing and I really hope that there is still rolm in tuning up the game and making it better but I doubt that will happen, even if they make the game a lot better the comedy and humor doesn't feel dark.  Other than that, I'd say get this game when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I preordered this game and I go back and forth on if it was worth it. For the story, I enjoy it. It's a short and silly story that follows up an episode we might've forgotten about. It's nothing too special but it's not without its merits. Fighting is decent. It's not too bad, but you can be easily swarmed and weapons are very limited and sometimes don't work at all. Wands don't do much of anything, and smacking only gets you so far when seven archers have you pinned to a wall. Fighting can get annoying if you're surrounded, and the AI players aren't the greatest. The graphics are fine and they translated okay in a 3d space, there's not much to say and personally I don't mind them. They hold up okay and they're not too ugly.The upgrading system is okay, if a little boring and repetitive. My biggest gripe is the walk/run cycle. You walk super slow which is grating for massive maps with multiple fetch-quests. You can run, but your stamina drains fast. The running speed should just be the new walking speed.  I also ran into a glitch where in the middle of a match, my progress wiped. I was disconnected from the game and told to do the tutorial again. I had to cycle the entire tutorial once more. It saved my gold, but my hundreds of dark matter was abruptly gone. I went into matchmaking to finish the last stage of the game then uninstalled it. It wasn't the first glitch I ran into either. I often got force disconnected from public matchmaking, meaning I would need to find a new match and replay the entire round all over again. ESPECIALLY annoying if it was a fetch-quest-heavy one and/or you had good battle chemistry with your teammates.  Do I recommend it? Honestly, for a small time-killer, yeah I do. It has its moments and it's not going to destroy your wallet or ruin your day. But it's for the more dedicated fans that are okay overlooking the flaws for a good time with the cast again. For non-fans, being South Park is the biggest thing holding it up because it wouldn't be able to stand without that fact. Wait for a sale or give it a skip if you're not a big fan. _childDocuments_.review: I’m not going to sit here and tell you that this game is perfect and you should drop everything you’re doing right now and go buy it… because it is not.However, I will say that South Park: Snow Day! is worth a try. If you are willing to look past the few minor bugs and disregard the fact that it’s graphics are different from the show, this game has a very strong back bone and foundation for future updates that have already been confirmed by the developers. I would recommend watching or re-watching some of the newer South Park episodes to understand the jokes in this game though.Now I would like to share my opinion on why this game has the amount of negative reviews that it does. Personally, I think that people are afraid of change. Going from 2 very well made 2D games to a 3D game with only about 5 hours of content is a big pill to swallow and I think they are right to be worried. Although, from what I’ve experienced in the game, I’m hopeful that I can extinguish these worries that you might have if you are still on the fence about purchasing this game.Let’s talk about the bad aspects of the game. Firstly, that it only has about 5 hours of gameplay currently at the time of writing this review. Although this may seem like a little, South Park: Snow Day! has many other ways to squeeze a few more hours out of it. For all my fellow achievement hunters, getting all the achievements is a great way to make the game last longer. There are also different contracts that you unlock when you complete the main story and these can get you some pretty cool cosmetics from the show. There is also a skill tree, and an “endless” mode where you can try to survive for 7 waves of enemies attacking, while you get stronger every wave you complete. I have done many of these ways of getting more fun out of the game and I’m at about 15 ish hours. Another part of this game that isn’t great is the bugs. Although few, some of them are pretty annoying. I would like to note though, during my 15 hours of gameplay, most of these bugs are pretty rare, and you don’t need to worry too much about them.Now, for the good part, let’s talk about what this game -in my opinion- does really well. Firstly, I think that the story is very funny and really well made.  It may not feel like an entire South Park episode because you are teleporting around the map and you may get disoriented, but I feel if you are willing to look past that you can get a ton of enjoyment out of the game. Another benefit of this game is the price. For only about $30 you can’t go wrong. Another part that I enjoyed was the combat. South Park: Snow Day! has a hack-and-slash style of combat and during every mission you get to choose different upgrade cards in order to get stronger and I found this to be a really interesting part of the game. There are many different builds that you can make - making every time you play a new experience! When re-playing different missions, they won’t all be the exact same because there are different modules that can be swapped out, changing the way you experience the mission! I could keep talking about what I love about this game but these are the main points.The final thing that I love about South Park: Snow Day! is the community. I became involved in the South Park community through the official Discord server.  Everyone that I’ve met have been nothing but friendly and enjoyable to play with. I honestly feel I might have met some long term friends that I never would have met without this game. As a final message to the developers, thank you for creating such a great game and here’s to many more!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to point out the store page has a lot of misinformation. They claim this is the first South Park game with multiplayer or Coop, this is false. They also claim this is a RPG, this is also false. They also call this a South Park game: if all it takes to call it a South Park game is putting the main characters on the cover, then we're doomed. Back in the days of N64 there was a Southpark game where it was a shooter, 3D, and it was generally disliked by everybody. A lot of people felt that it did not capture the spirit of South Park at all. This game is somehow worse than that game. Unlike the previous two games which were made by big name studios and starred tie-ins with the show itself, Snow Day is made by a tiny little studio named Question which made "The Blackout Club", a multiplayer-only flop. The story is pretty simple, a snow storm wrecks South Park so the kids go outside and play. Snow Day is yet another attempt by Matt Stone and Trey Parker to sell overpriced DLC while preventing you from exploring South Park as much as possible. On release day you can PRE-ORDER a season pass that promises "one new weapon" and "one new mode", so for $25 you might theoretically get something worth it. I think this kind of shows how Matt and Trey have always been a decade behind the gaming industry; nobody likes these rip-off season passes, and anybody that has learned to read knows it's a rip-off. Speaking of being a decade behind the industry, remember those generic third person shooters where you clear arenas and fight your way  to a boss? You know, those games that were popular like 10 years ago? That's the entire experience. You are The New Kid, who silently fights their way across a bunch of frozen zones loosely inspired by South Park. Objectives are standard uninspired crap like fight badguys, bring things to the place, load a turret, etc. The most basic stuff that you could possibly be doing in a game. Scenes with the actual South Park characters in it are few and far between, they appear for about 25 minutes out of the four hour playtime of the entire game. The enemies are NOT voiced by Matt and Trey, but a group of twelve year olds (I am being very serious, it's the same kids they have do the fourth graders on the show I think) so there's kind of only so much range they can show off. Which brings me to the number one reason why this game does not work: It lacks the South Park charm, it feels like a low budget fan game because there's barely anything that can be identified as "South Park" here. All they did was dress the kids up like wizards and warriors again while making a simple third person shooter around it; happily stealing mechanics from everything they can think of in order to scam some money off some stupid kids. Question is an awful game developer, and I hope Matt/Trey drop them like an empty bag of cocaine.

You get to choose from only three weapons (double daggers, sword and shield or giant ax) and two powers.  Also at the start of each area, there are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards that can add another power, but they don't really change the battles all that much.  Another thing that is wrong with the battles are the enemy dialog.  It's so annoying, overly repetitive, and meaningless.  After completing an area, you get to spend your dark matter that has been collected on a skill tree, but you don't really get enough to make it worth your while.  You are required to grind dark matter to complete the skill tree, but the game is so boring that it's not worth it.All in all, this game fails at every turn.  Save your money or buy Stick of Truth or Fractured but Whole.  They are both leagues better than this pathetic excuse of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game set in the South Park universe, look elsewhere. Apart from the minor backdrop of continuity from TSOT/FBW, this game oozes "game first setting second" vibes.I bought this game a day or two before release, knowing it was not an RPG, but  still at least hoping for an enjoyable setpiece-filled world. Every reference is minor, every detail feels shoed-in. Even with friends, we can't help but want to play something else.What it does well:-The combat & card systems are certainly unique for what amounts to a 3D roguelite.-The artistic style is what you'd expect a 3D South Park game to look like, with some clever mechanics to hide imperfections.-The voice acting is mostly tolerable, with a few serious exceptions. Looking at you, Randy.The cons:-I honestly can't bring myself to go back for a second session. Everything feels hollow, to say the least. Even with Koopa Keep filled with other characters, nothing feels memorably placed.-The level environments are completely forgettable, and rarely feel connected to actual South Park landmarks.-The story is terrible. Yes, it's not supposed to be story-focused, but it's just so... sorry the only way I can describe it is shoed-in. It feels like they had an actual story and cut 80% of it out before release, or it was written to accommodate the base amount of gameplay. This is not what you'd expect from South Park.-There's an annoyingly SMALL amount of customization, cosmetic or otherwise.-The language and behavior of every character is not on-brand with what we know about South Park. It feels more like a THQ brand-pump game than a South Park one.I'll be returning this product. I expected at least something akin to a South Park brawler with meaningful dialogue that I could immerse myself into the world with. Instead I got this "fudging" boring game. (That's not me being polite, that's the non-main characters toning down their language).

_childDocuments_.review: If you're interested in South Park: Snow Day!, please realize it's a completely different game from the last two (Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole). Those are turn based RPGs that play out like an episode while this is a 3D card-based beat 'em up, rogue-like. It's very much designed to be played with other people, but you can still do single player with the help of AI party members.The game is fairly short and can be frustrating at times, but for $30 (release price) I'm not upset with it. It has some occasional glitches / bugs but overall I'm not having a bad time with it. I found myself getting frustrated but always returning to it later on. It still has that trademark South Park humor and the story is amusing (though again, short). I've seen people complain about the graphics but honestly I enjoy the look. I do prefer the style of the previous games but for a 3D South Park game, I feel like they nailed it artistically.A bit of a ramble but just to quickly sum it up, to me it was worth $30. $60 or $70? Absolutely not, but brand new at $30 I felt like I knew what I was getting myself into.

_childDocuments_.review: I just bought the game. I'm a big fan of south park because of the acid comedy and the non-care for the politically correct. I love The Stick Of Truth and The Fractured But Hole (I played both games in Nintendo Switch) and I was excited for this new game. _childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a hack-and-slash combat game, not an RPG. The Stick of Truth was one of the best games ever. But this is nothing like it and is not fun to play -- there's basically no "South Park" content, just a basic combat game. It feels like Matt and Trey weren't even involved. There are basically no jokes, there's very little story, and the combat isn't fun. I'm a huge South Park fan but I'm not going to be able to finish this; it's just not enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: As a big South Park fan, it hurts to say that this game just isn't it.It is a huge step down from the previous two games.The game feels like a cheap mobile game, while there's nothing wrong with mobile games... this one costs 30 euros.The combat in this game feels very clunky and cheap, and the locations in this game all feel the same.While they said this game should make you feel like you are in an episode of South Park, it does not. It feels like a cheap hack-and-slash game with a South Park skin.If you are playing alone, you get three little morons assisting you in battle. Their AI is not that great.The last two really felt like big South Park movies where they went all out with the jokes; in this one, it just feels like they are playing it a little bit safe.It might be fun with friends, but that does not make this a 30 euro game.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Gamers need to relax and just enjoy games. This is a brand new take for the future of south park. This product reminds me of fat princess fist full of cakes. A budget title that can be replayed over and over. I am just hoping they decide to add more content to this game. There is 5 levels with a story that is funny. It has a good premise that carries over from the last two games about making sure people will stop breaking the rules. They wanted to make a game that they could update more frequently. If they put something in the show they can put it in the game. This games future is dependent on south park team following through with what they said they wanted to do. You support games ideas and their future. I would like more of an action south park game in the future. Turn based is fun, but it's been done before twice. So they wanted to make something fresh. Gamers hate change which is crazy to me. They don't like experimental titles that lower the price while doing something different. People will be upset you can beat this in 5 hours. There is a lot to explore during the missions. I feel we need more titles like this that really allow devs to make something new. If you are here just for the story wait for a sale. This is a quality game. I will probably grind this for another 10 to 20 hours easily. I will get my moneys worth and if you are south park fan it's a must have. If you aren't I wouldn't recommend it. I don't see what this game offers that other games don't and there is nothing wrong with that. It's 30 dollars for a reason. Just enjoy your south park and don't let the reviews deflect your from your enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: What sucks the most is that the previous two South Park games were so great. _childDocuments_.review: I've played every south park game so far and unfortunately this one falls incredibly from the high bar. _childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: As much as i love South Park... this just aint it. There is way too much getting stun locked until you down, forcing you to reset the entire thing from the beginning (and these are some really long missions) so if you die during the boss fight, prepare to spend another 45ish minutes to get back to it. (The Stan boss fight is pretty much why I stopped and decided to vent for a minute)Gameplay wise, it's just a button masher... I like button mashers sometimes. The AI is completely useless. So that adds an extra unnecessary level of "FUN" if you could call it that.It's all linear gameplay for the most part. Stark's Pond let's you choose which way you wanna go, but that's about it (from what I've seen so far anyway.) No more all of South Park to explore. No more side quests, no more finding easter eggs while walking around. I hated the first trailer and seeing it was a 3D game instead of the 2.5 from the previous two, but I figured i'd just muscle through it because of South Park but... 3D just is not what South Park was intended to look like. It isn't ugly by any means, but this is SOUTH PARK. It will always look better with the Construction Paper cutouts cussing at you.And probably most egregious of all... it's just not that funny. By this point in Stick of Truth and Fractured but Whole, I had to pause the game so I could finish laughing multiple times before continuing. This time game, well it got a few chuckles out of me, but nothing gut bustingly funny anymore.6/10 (so far) if you like South Park, get it. If not, find something else to play.Edit: Spelling and added the bit about the friendly AI

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable dungeon crawler with rogue-like elements and a mix and match class system. It's limiting with only five maps and only three melee and tree ranged weapons, but the card system keeps a fresh rogue-like feel to each run. Plus South Park humor and essentially a whole sequel episode to (an although dated at this point) episode from the show. At $30 with additional DLC at release, it's not the best, but it's pretty fun, and you can trust me because I'm a Yelp reviewer.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing South Park game. Is it clunky at times yes but if you are a die-hard South Park fan you will have a blast playing it. Especially with friends. The game follows the shows/games timelines which is great.Do take in consideration how short the game actually is though. I have 5h so far but that is because I was exploring every single little corner as it amazes me I can be in my favorite fictional place in 3D. I do believe that if you rush it you might be able to complete it in 2 to 3 hours.Performance is great. Graphics are great. Movement is a bit clunky at times. Soundtrack is good. Story is great. If you are a fan and have money to spare buy it NOW! If you aren't that interested in South Park maybe wait for a sale.UPDATE: Chapters will have some different objectives if you replay the game. However the game is quite short unfortunately. It took me under 11 hours to get all achievements and unlock nearly everything. There is also a harder wave/kill all enemies mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Yea its lacking in content but its also not $60 and if you like South Park you're probably gonna buy it anyway. It's a fun with friends rogue-like set in a cool environment.The upgrade path is fun but gets grindy after upgrade 18. But to be fair you don't need to be maxed out to feel powerful. It's all about using the perks to your advantage and getting ULTRA-LEGENDARY cards. Similar to Descent in The Division 2, the damage perks are nice but if you lean towards economy instead more TP will serve you better in the end.Gameplay is a bit clunky and can be frustrating at times. It reminds me a lot of Gunfire Reborn which is probably a better game albeit not about South Park. The last level music is hella annoying and I ended up muting it completely. Needs some more tactile feedback in the combat system when you're hitting enemies.Personally I love the genre and subject matter of this game. With a few more levels. game modes, cards, and a ton of more shop options this game would have been WELL worth the price of admission. As it stands, if you're on the fence, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not worth it's asking price of 30 euros, maybe 4.99 euros at the current state of the game and the season pack is just a big ♥♥♥♥ you to the players.+ Some fun cinematic moments+ The arena mode is decently good+ Soundtrack is decent+ Levels seems to have randomized section- Price is just awful, they should be ashamed for it- No class system so every player is just the same guy with one or two differences- Small weapon and power pool- You can't customize your character as much as in the previous games- The cosmetic options don’t have much to offer- Can’t have more than one facial feature. I'm glad that they tried new things with the mechanics and the design but this shouldn't come at the expense at the replayability and overall soul of the game.To be frank, overall I'm becoming more and more disillusioned by modern gaming, particularly when it comes to existing series or IPs. _childDocuments_.review: Game is nothing compared to the previous two games, Stick of truth, and Fractured but whole. Only 4h in playtime and i have beat the game on hard on my first run through. Only 5 missions, a total of 3 melee weapons and 3 ranged weapons. No armor, no different tier weapons to find or upgrade too. The only upgrade system they have implemented is the same you would find in a rouge like game. The one being a false sense of achievement. For the Black matter a lot of the upgrades seem like they could be there from the start because it is all player stat based. increase speed by 30%, increase damage by 10% ect. not really upgrades, just nerfes your paying to have undone. With the in game cards that get reset after each run, They are fun and unique, but with the limited amount of weapons to choose from, they become repetitive fast, making you tend to stick to the same builds that work. There are no collectables in the game to try and hunt down unlike the first two. The maps look so amazing and were fun to explore, only to be left disappointed when there was a invisible wall blocking the path or a roll of toilet paper waiting for me. There just wasnt any pay off for looking around. The comedy was alright for the first mission then slowly became non southpark type humor. Its hard to describe, buts like watching a pg-13 southpark that has a lot of mature jokes replaced with well nothing, no boundries were being pushed, it was such a safe game, it didnt feel like it was made by the southpark team at all. If you are a big fan of south park and really want to play this game, please for the love of god wait till its on sale.Multiplayer :  I dont understand this new trend of multiplayer having literally 0 communication system. Why have voice chat to talk to your teamates, when you can have a silly emote of a thumbs up or down. Want to tell your teamates to hurry up? cant. Want to let them know they missed a chest / upgrade? cant. This game is the perfect multiplayer game if you want to sit in isolation and not talk to your teammates what so ever. Not even a in game chat system. Just emotes. This is the standard now a days for a *multiplayer* release. but why?One of my biggest enjoyments with Stick of Truth is getting to actually be in the world of southpark, seeing familiar places from the show, and easter eggs sprinkled throught. Its all just snow here. Sure you can see City Wok and 2 other places from a certian angle on a level if you look at the background. But it just feels like you arent really in southpark too much

_childDocuments_.review: You the reader should only continue with your purchase if you are a decently big fan or more of South Park, or at least a somewhat of a fan of South Park, and you have a friend that is at least an average fan of the show. You also need friends. I've never played the game alone, but I can't imagine it's all that fun.The gameplay for South Park Snow Day is alright. It meets the requirement for what kind of game it, but if doesn't feel like they innovated past the bare minimum. There's only three weapons in melee, and three in range. The 3 melee basically do the same thing in terms of damage, however they do do somewhat different things, like the shield, if you couldn't tell, blocks stuff. The Range weapons are better in my opinion, whilst we all know weapons do damage no matter what, the range weapons at least feel like they do different things, whereas the melee weapons, even though one weapon looks like a heavy weapon, doesn't feel like you're doing anything different to the knives.There are five levels in the game, each taking about 20-40 minutes depending on the difficulty. The levels are actually quite good. each one isn't the same as a previous one, and they all end with a boss fight. the boss fights are pretty good as well, all unique. There are different enemies in each level, at least in terms of the harder ones. Your typical goon will always show up in a later level, as well as every enemy, but each level introduces a new enemy, and can piss you off according to what you're personally good at dealing with in video games.The story is alright. It doesn't make you feel like you're hanging with the gang, or in a south park episode, which is one of the best things about the previous two games. This game just makes you play with the gang, and play the part of new kid, rather than making you believe that you are in fact, the new kid. It's a snow day, a particularly deadly one, and all the kids decided that then was the best time to go out and play. Part of me wishes they did something new in terms of the aesthetics  the story surrounds (Stick of truth was fantasy, fractured but whole was super heroes), instead, they went with the fantasy one again. With what we got though, it's not world ending. The first two levels don't really do much with the story, it's more of an intro to their game they're playing, and the third and fourth have little story involved. It's simple, it's not complicated, but with how the gameplay is, I wish they would at least have put a little more into the story. Doesn't entirely matter though.Despite what may look like a negative review, I think it's still a decently good time with a friend. after all, that's the whole point of this game really. It's not amazing, nor is it good. It's not bad, it's just ok. only ok, not 'pretty ok', not 'just ok', just 'ok', which is why I'm not not recommending it, I'm just recommending it to specific people. Again, people with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I read the reviews on the store page and thought this was a case of Steam-dwelling neckbeards over-analyzing it to death. Like they were expecting this to play like Middle Earth: Shadow of War, and it didn't. I thought the reviews were expecting jokes of fish stick proportions, and got slightly less.Then, I got my unemployed friend, who had just sold 500 bucks worth of Counter Strike skins on the steam marketplace like an idiot, to buy it for me and himself so we could try it out for ourselves. After all, I have never once in my life been disappointed by a South Park product.My god does this suck. It sucks harder than your mama. Did you think that 'your mama' joke sucked? That 'your mama' joke was funnier than anything you'll encounter in this game. It's not that the jokes weren't great, nor were they bad. There just weren't any.It's like they spent 95% of the allocated budget on acquiring the rights to the South Park intellectual property, 4.5% on a teambuilding day, and then had about $78 left to make the actual game.The game itself, mechanically, is worse than what you can get some Indian on Fiverr to make you for less than the cost of a Big Mac. The writing feels like they had it done by some students. From an elementary school.I remember playing a PSP game roughly 13 years ago that had better combat and graphics than this abomination. That game not only had the groundbreaking light attack, but also a heavy attack!Are we making AA games with ChatGPT now? You really expect me to let you keep my unemployed friend's $30 for this garbage? Whoever green lighted this ass burger for release possesses Druish levels of greed. Watching your own parents die is funnier than this game. Chewing gum provokes more emotion and excitement than this does. The sole of my shoe is more interesting than this game.I'm very sad that the South Park team (or most likely Paramount) sold the rights to the South Park characters for use in a video game and then entirely stopped caring about what was going to be done with the franchise. Which is undeniably what happened here.If you wish to still enjoy the rest of South Park's other content, do not play this.

_childDocuments_.review: I am having a blast with this game. It's essentially a South Park themed arpg/roguelike, where you can choose from 6 different weapons, and temporarily power them up with tons of different cards throughout each run. There are also permanent upgrades from currency collected. There are 5 levels available to do standard runs on, as well as 4 separate smaller arena areas with a "horde mode" type game. There is also an option for difficulty modifiers and more cosmetic unlocks after beating all levels for the first time. Going through each of the standard levels there is a story that I found very enjoyable as a huge fan of the show. In my opinion, combat and movement feels good - a bit floaty at times, but everything works as intended, and many of the skills become super fun to use after a few upgrades. There are also surprises in terms of what the weapons can morph into - for example on the wand you can actually get chain lightning, even though the base wand attack is a flamethrower. Was also very happy to see every level absolutely packed to the brim with secrets, from hidden resource chests to special card upgrades, exploring is rewarded. As a huge fan of roguelike games and South Park, I will definitely be playing a lot more of this.

_childDocuments_.review: IGN gave this game a 3. That makes this game sound like an unplayable mess. That kind of score gets you dirt hyped down to expect this to be a wake up and cry nightmare of an experience. What we have here is a 6 out of 10, but that's only really at best. The combat here is alright. Hits connect with enemies and they take damage. Doesn't feel as crunchy or as impactful as most other beat-em up systems, but it gets the job done. Upgrades and powers are fun to use if you don't mind pummeling hoards of very similar enemies in very similar looking arenas (with some recognizable differences in design, but not much. They're all still snowy wastelands. It's on theme, but you do want more variety and enrichment in your enclosure.).Don't come into this expecting a plot like the epic story of the two previous RPGs. Those are more comparable to the movie or the specials in scope. This is more like a regular episode of the show in scope. Maybe not quite as crass or full throttle as their usual material, but they're still a pinch of poop jokes in this. It does leave you wanting more, but looking at what the season pass offers it doesn't look like muuuch more is coming juuust yet.My advice, get a friend or two to play the campaign with, and Danse with Ravenous Shadows with random matchmaking. There's still something worthwhile in here if you're looking for a mindless brawler to pass a weekend with. And if you're writing fan fiction for your New Kid oc you based on the Stick of Truth and Fractured But Whole, there's a nugget of inspiration in here for you chew on. Also yes, there's a dedicated toot button, but I'm not gonna tell you what it is.

I hope content updates make the price tag worth it but until then, it's a no.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I really like this game. It gives an interesting feeling of nostalgia mixed with cool modern roguelike elements. Of course there really needs to be more weapon and spell variety. The environments are really pretty, although it's a shame we can't freely explore the town. I'm excited to see the future updates for this game. After seeing the reviews I had the bar set so low for this game, and while I wasn't blown away, I was surprised with how much fun I was having. There needs to be some work as the gameplay is a little janky and it's a bit light on the content but I really hope they continue developing this and adding stuff. Even in its current state I'd still recommend if you like south park and roguelike/hack and slash games
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: $30 does not justify 5-6 hours of content, there are plenty of games for $30 that will provide you 2-10x the amount of hours of gameplay. Had to refund this because I was disappointed after buying and seeing there were small chapters after playing through chapter one. It's a fun game though and I would buy it on a big sale.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game for a long time just to be totally dissapointed. I hope they make the next one like the first 2 games that played like a southpark episode. This game is to short too buggy and no fun at all its basically just fighting people nonstop and picking things up to take from a to b. For real not even worth 10 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: SOUTH PARK: SNOW DAY!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is like you're in the actual show, even the 3D brings it all to life even more and they did a damn good job in showing it. Combat is well implemented and it has a roguelike element that'll keep you on your toes each time you play. When you fail a quest, you will be able to replay it. However, what most people fail to mention is you will receive different scenarios. There's not many, but it does add some uniqueness to watching the different scenes come to life.It took me and my friend 7 hours, and that's from actually playing the game. There's also a free DLC you can download and you can unlock more fun through a wave system game mode.EDIT: Changing my review since nothing really has been done to the game since I played it when it came out.Saying all of that, the game doesn't have replayability and they're making it worse by adding DLCs. The game needs a bit more content in it too, something we can grind for. I defended them at first, but they made it clear they don't care about the game, only to milk it for money and take advantage of the "South Park" name. The DLCs shouldn't be DLCs but free in-game updates since it's cosmetic items for the most part. Honestly, don't bother -- even on sale.

name: Gunfire Reborn
detailed_description: About This Game: Gunfire Reborn is an adventure level-based game featuring FPS, roguelite, and RPG elements. Players can control unique heroes—each with different abilities—as they adventure through procedurally-generated levels and pick up randomly-dropped weapons. You can play Gunfire Reborn alone or cooperatively with up to three other players (4-player co-op). Every level is random; each new restart is a brand-new experience. You will meet different heroes and experience new weapons, items, checkpoints, and unique combat rhythms throughout the game. Game Features: FPS+Roguelite+RPG combined gameplay, construct diverse Build through death cycle for different experience Elaborate, yet randomized stage experience Over 100 different items and various weapons Many heroes and multiple game plus with different game mechanism Unique art style Co-op level-based adventure

_childDocuments_.review: Game itself is an amazing concept and it has TOO much potential. There are some issues here and there but not game breaking bugs (except for one time where the screen was flickering and I had to close the game and run it again) it IS a little in the risky buy side as it's in the early access and feels kind of unstable. _childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I have never enjoyed a roguelike game this much. I'm having a lot of fun and it's extremely addicting especially playing with friends. Crisp combat, pretty strong weapon balance, lots of weapon variety. No desync/disconnects, even running at 80ms ping with the host. Graphics are well optimized. Definitely worth picking up.I'm hoping to see more content in the future as I've beaten all of the content with all the heroes in under 30 hours. I've pretty much unlocked everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty fun roguelite FPS with some RPG elements. The devs update the game every week and add new content. You pick a character which has a skill tree and go through levels in the game, picking up weapons with random stats (maximum of 2 weapons), upgrading weapons, and upgrading skills. There are also jump/dodge puzzles in the game to slow things down from all the shooting. When it comes to the RPG elements, there's a lot of build diversity and each playthrough seems different due to the roguelite aspect. The game is a bit buggy (welcome to early access), so expect weird things to happen, but also expect the developer to eventually fix it (they do look at bug reports). Anyone looking to play this should avoid extremely high ping sessions and ensure that either you or your buddies have a stable connection ("get off McDonald's wifi and get real internet").
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: VERY fun rogue lite FPS that seems simple at first but is deceptively deep. The systems at work mesh together almost flawlessly and make every perk selected or every weapon exchanged a hard thought out decision with lots of trade offs and side grades to consider. For the price, it's more than extremely worth the buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good game, especially knowing it's only early access.There's a lot to improve on, but it seems like the devs are pretty hard-working looking at how communicative they are with the players.Here are some pros and cons, and after that I'll add some things that I think the devs should consider adding.Pros:+ Gun play is awesome - The gameplay is smooth, addictive and simple.+ It has a lot of charm - The artstyle combined with the cutesy characters and enemies make this game pretty charming and pleasing. The maps look cool too.+ The weapons - They are mostly exciting, fun to use, look cool and feel good.+ Characters - Working to unlock new characters (and unlocking them) is a lot of fun, knowing that the progress you make doesn't go for granted, the characters themselves are all unique and fun even though I feel like some are just better than others.Cons:- Upgrades are not very exciting most of the times.- Checkpoints - You can only quit the game once you eliminate the boss of a level for the game to save your progress.Here are some things that I would add/change:* Obviously anything in the cons section.* Make it so you can quit after passing through each door.* I haven't beaten the game yet or earned everything - but I heard that some people have and now don't have a lot to play for, so maybe having a non-micro transaction battle pass or way of earning cosmetics for the characters, weapons and maybe even enemies would be a cool way to keep the player engaged more.I will probably update this as time goes by but these are my opinions for now, comments are allowed if you want to ask anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Decent looter-shooter with a rougelite flair. Better with friends but still entertaining on its own. There doesn't seem to be as much content yet as I would have expected since its now out of early access but its still a solid game with good mechanics. Decent variety of characters, weapons, bosses, environments, etc. Hopefully this game sees continued development but its pretty good as is. recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Great FPS roguelite, it's incredibly fun to play with friends.I like to think of this game as a more casual version of Risk of Rain 2:- I don't have to rush my friends- You can read what power-ups do before you pick them up- If you end up not wanting the power ups, you can drop it- All loot is instanced, no competing or asking for itemsIf you love multiplayer roguelites, definitely give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: this is some good sh*tComing back to add on, the f*cking value you get for the price point is absurd. There's a great amount of content and TONS of replayability thanks to all the different builds you can try out with 4 different characters. Each character feels unique and fun to play. They all have an ability that recharges over time, and a secondary that has an ammo capacity. They also have different stats such as different health pools and either having a rechargeable shield, or armour that can be gained back in various ways. Along with that each hero has 3 different skill trees that you get to upgrade throughout your run which can upgrade the way they use specific guns, and modify their two abilities. The game feels pretty solid, enemies have pretty large hit boxes for the most part so you don't need spectacular aim to enjoy this title. You start off with a base gun that you carry with you at all times that doesn't feel too underwhelming, and you're able to carry an additional 2 weapons with you. You're able to dash quickly and jump to avoid being hit, while the game tries to emulate doom in this respect its definitely a lot slower and can feel a bit sluggish. As you play you'll find numerous guns that are all surprisingly unique. Some guns even have an alternative fire that let you do something different, for example one guns alt fire creates a sphere which increases the damage of projectiles you shoot through it. As you find guns you'll quickly notice that they have inscriptions attached to them. These, just like scrolls, have various rarities that increase in power and can also have some very interesting and even game changing effects.This game seems to draw a ton of inspiration from the Borderlands series, as there are different elemental effects that have status effects attached to them, along with being more effective against the different types of health pools that you will encounter. These elements can be randomly assigned to your weapons, or you can find talent upgrades that adds or changes the element of your ability. The elements are;Corrosion: Strong against armour, applies decay which slowsFire: Strong against health, applies burning which deals weapon damage over timeLightning: Strong against shields, applies shock which deals small AoE damage and increases subsequent damage takenThese elements are also able to combine with each other to produce various effects like explosions adding to the carnage.Aside from your characters skill trees, you may find various scrolls throughout your run that will add some interesting effects to your character, some being a simple revive, while others can be a passive effect that alternates between offensive and defensive stats. The scrolls are divided into different rarities so while some may seem mundane, others can be really game breaking.This game has a progression system outside of your runs which have massive benefits to your future runs, as well as each character having a single column of upgrades specific to them. These upgrades are essential to really getting to the fun parts of the game, as some of the upgrades unlock finding guns with the rarer inscriptions I mentioned earlier, and increasing the likelihood of finding higher rarities. Though it can seem at times that this is a bit of a grind mechanic as the earlier upgrades are pretty necessary as they increase your total health, ammo capacity, and ability capacity, thankfully these are the earliest upgrades you get and can max them out very quickly.This game has online co-op of up to 4 players, and you can even go into match making to play with randoms if you don't have anyone to play with. I would say this game is best enjoyed solo or with a couple friends though, as playing with randoms over the internet can still feel pretty lonely as there's no communication system.This game isn't very visually appealing. The character and enemy designs are interesting, but are very low poly and that can be a major turnoff for some people. The movement can feel a bit sluggish, even with the ability to dash around. The UI is pretty horrendous too, something I hope will be fixed when the game is fully released. This game is still early access, while bugs seem to be rare Borrowing from Borderland's philosophy of elements and innumerable amount of gun mods this game is a fun action packed adventure rogue-lite spin on the loot shooter genre, at the extremely low price point I'd say this game is worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool idea for a game, i love it and i hate it. On one hand, its a very mechanically clean, well optimized fps roguelite with a satisfying variety of skills and weapon types to use; tons of potential there already. On the other hand, i cant stand to play it for more than 1 or 2 runs at a time before i remember why i stopped playing it last time. I've played the game 80 hrs, made it to 'reincarnation' and experienced the full range of content to the final boss at least 5 times, there's a part of me that really wants to love the game, but..The enemy AI is the most annoying of any game I've ever picked up in my life. Absolutely EXCESSIVE movement and head bobbing, ranged enemies just hiding behind walls and firing their projectiles into the walls. The ONLY thing some of these enemies care about is being a difficult target for you. That seems to be the developers' intention when programming the AI. Enemies will defy all logic and common sense just to zigzag and bob their head around or do everything they can to break line of sight with you at all times, even if it means they can't attack you either.Again, the game is so cool, fresh, polished, optimized, and fun otherwise but I'm not kidding when I say the way some of the enemies behave is just so outright *annoying* that I find myself getting pissed off on successful runs just because it wears my patience so thin. I'll probably try playing again once a year or so in hopes that they dial back the head bobbing, zig zagging, and LoS breaking of the enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Think procedurally-generated, roguelike Borderlands, but with extra emphasis on broken builds. I love exploring new ways of pushing the limits of the game while also taking on harder and harder challenges. Have I spent several hours farming one guy in the game so that I could rack up 4000 HP, allowing for my weak play skills to beat some of the game's hardest challenges? You bet I have! With a wide array of characters to choose from, family friendly themes and frequent updates, I love playing this game alone or with friends and I'm excited to see where the devs take this game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Well this came outta nowhere as a pleasant surprise for me! After being heavily pressured into getting this by a certain friend of mine I had very little to no expectations of what was coming my way - the game looked a lil' off-putting and generic from screens and all the furry animals weren't really helping me get convinced. As I started playing through , i found the gameplay fun, mildly satisfying and enjoyable but nothing that blew me away. Compounded by the fact that there seemed to be  whatsoever in the levels , I was not particularly convinced or thrilled to continue. Over the next hours and days however, I found myself returning...and returning...coming back for more runs. Each time getting a little further. Each time matching up with different players. Each time unlocking more things for myself. Each time expanding my array of  as they call it in game. It's truly hooking me in thus far and I've really come to appreciate what it offers! It's simplistic art style is endearing and pops just enough. The overall gameplay across the different, well designed characters feel balanced and fair, although of course you can have runs where you feel like a puny pathetic peasant and others where you're GODLY from the get go. I definitely see some Borderlands flair and inspiration across the maps , gun designs and enemies too which  bodes well with me. Overall, it's a great game for those looking for an exhilarating rogue-lite FPS experience just disappointed that some aspects such as the bloody MUSIC was looked past , hopefully there's an opportunity to add it in the future. Oh and the final phase of the Polar Monarch right now is pretty balls - ya' gotta have PURE, unfiltered high-tier DPS to manage it in time or well it's all for nothing, too bad folks. _childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I like and enjoy the randomization on abilities and map for each play through - making it a different experience.  The pacing is good - the way the game breaks up each section helps you see your progress with each world. Fun with a group of friends and fun solo.  I found myself looking at the achievements list at one point and sayin, to my husband's chagrin, "Hmm... If I die by a trap twice I can unlock that?  Let's do it!" haha!  I also enjoy the weapons you can unlock throughout the game based on types of kills or types of feats you accomplish overtime, again that makes you feel rewarded.  Experimenting with the new guns was also fun for me as well.I was disappointed at first that I couldn't select a different class when you first start to play the game. Mainly because I was playing with a group of four and we were all the same.  However, it didn't take us long to unlock the others and it did feel rewarding to get them over time.  Still I would like to recommend that they have at least another character to play that you can get pretty quickly early on to help with anyone grouping up with others.  Having the mix of abilities is fun and adds another strategic value to each play-through.If you like FPS and roguelite games, I would recommend to give this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game since it first came to Steam. One of my favorite roguelites over the past few years! Development has been steady and the game has improved so much since I first played it. Its first DLC was a day one purchase for me with zero regrets. Tons of fun to be had, especially with friends.My ONLY real desire for this game is some sort of shorter run type. The game is so fun, but being forced to commit to a large block of time to complete runs can be hard sometimes. Especially getting the stars to align with friend availability. I would play much more if I didn't need to set aside a two hour block for it. (Maybe I'm just slow)Highly recommend this game, though. It's been installed in my library for a loooong time and will remain so for a long time yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: If anyone is still on the fence, I would say buy it now before the price increase for 1.0. The game is absolutely worth it and the devs keep it up to date pretty often.1.0 UPDATE:I'd say this game is still worth it with the content they added. It will give you and friends many hours of playtime and fun if you enjoy co-op shooters with a rougelike twist.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite roguelites of the last few years. The game has quite a bit of replay value, thanks to large amount of ascensions(passive abilities) you can choose between for you character. The ascensions are given randomly, and this can sometimes make the game quite a bit more challenging if you don't get what you need to make your build work. You might find this frustrating if you don't like a game with a good deal of random elements to it.There is also a large amount of weapons to choose from that have random stats. The weapons are very diverse, with some having unique abilities attached to their alt fire.I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys roguelite shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: With this game now at 1.0, I feel I can finally give this game the verdict it deserves: it's a damn good rougelike. Taking elements and inspiration from Borderlands and similar games, and infusing that with the gameplay of a rougelike, is a match made in heaven. Gunfire takes these elements of looting & shooting, infuses them into a nice selection of characters with their own skills, and ends up with a very complex and rewarding experience. The game's progression was one of my biggest gripes in early access, due to how slow it was, alongside a significant hump early on. This has now been rectified, and the progression feels much better and smoother.However, while I do enjoy this game, I cannot call it perfect, because it definitely has its hiccups. Gunfire is much more punishing to play solo as opposed to co-op, since you can only revive yourself once per run. In addition, the game's original language is Chinese, which leads to some occasional inconsistent translation for English and other language players. Overall though, Gunfire Reborn a very enjoyable rougelike experience for fans of the genre, and would even be a great introduction to the genre for fans of Borderlands and similar games.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Imo there's nothing that makes this better or even on par with Risk of Rain 2. What jumped out to me in the time I played is that the movement feels sluggish, the weapons are boring, the enemies are forgettable and The game itself gets stake REALLY quickly. Items don't change up the gameplay that much and your build is strictly dictated by whether you can match your weapon attributes and your buffs (because if you don't you're underpowered).
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun and simple work in progress RNG dungeon runner.You get 3 stages, 3 sets of weapons to find, light, heavy and special and 3 characters to play with unique special powers.The cat is a debuff stacker, the bird kicks things and the dog solves problems by applying more gun.There are very few technical bugs. Mostly animation glitches and some wall clipping.However the heavy class of weapons generally outclass their light/special counterparts by a huge margin.Also some of the assets appear to be ripped straight from Overwatch but hey, i still see doom 1993 assets in modern games and Overwatch used to be a popular title.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: It's essentially rougelite Borderlands. Each character has a unique skill, grenade and a combat preference that gets upgraded as you see fit through each run, so some runs because of rng you might be using a character based on his grenade tree, or abusing his skill or maybe parts of both, etc. It gives good flexibility to make even the same "build path" feel different since you won't always get the same skill ups every run. Overall a genuinely fun game, even better with friends (pubs aren't bad either). You can honestly get 50+ solid hours out of this game by the time you can unlock most things, so for the price it's actually more than fair.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth every penny of its cost. It is a quick smooth gaming experience if you are looking for a shooter to play with friends or alone. You can play with newer folks on normal or do some pushing in Reincarnation with seasoned friends. This has been in the rotation for my friends for a while now. Developers have been involved from Day 1 and this is a great game to pick up and play through the new updates when they come out.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a great game for some multiplayer fun.The comparison to a mixture of Borderlands and Risk of Rain 2 has already been made, and it describes the basics very well. If you like roguelike shooters and want to have fun with a few friends (up to 4 players) this game is for you.Bugs: So far i haven't encountered any noticeable bugs, it's polished and runs smoothly. Multiplayer seems fine, too, i haven't had any problems.Content: Unlocking all the Heroes, Talents, Weapons and Scrolls is fun, but i wish there were a few more levels and bosses! But that's not a major complaint considering the price and high quality of everything that's already there.Long term replayability: To be determined, but i guess it's decent if you play with friends. An Addon or two would be great!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Negatives:- The graphics are the bare minimum, they are solely functional, and not all that pretty to look at. Though this makes the game run very well on older computers.- The music has nothing special or noteworthy about it. It's like french fries without salt.- You tend to get burst down in half a second from full health in the later areas if you position yourself wrong.- The characters are often less versatile in efficient gun choices than in other games.- Gunplay is kind of outdated.- No sliding, running, crouching or climbing. You can dodge though.- The boss in the forth area is a run ender if you are not completely broken in the survivability or damage department.- You are required to look everywhere at a bunch of walls to find all challenge events and orange chests if you want to have a decent chance at beating the 4th area and unlock your full potential so the real fun can start. This makes runs very long.- Runs tend to be around and sometimes slightly more than 60 minutes if you try to become as powerful as possible and get through the 4th area, but you can save at campfires at least.- Queue times in matchmaking are long (~6? min waiting for 2 player co-op) and the netcode is not that great. You can not expect to find 4 player lobbies, and 3 player lobbies are very rare. - Multiplayer does not enhance the experience as much as in some other games.- You start with only one character choice, and will have to grind a bit to get the other characters. - Available weapons is very limited in the beginning.- RNG can screw you over a bit.Positives:+ Great variety in guns, which are often very different from each other. They are also very plentiful.+ Each run is very different, even if you run the same character, with the same guns and the same build.+ You will become a monstrous amalgamation of chaos later on in runs if you collect all the scrolls you can get your hands on.+ The skills are very well designed compared to many other games and are often very synergistic. You will not find boring passive skills like +30% health or -15% damage taken without a fun spin on them.+ Good variety in characters and their skills.+ Interesting enemies and bosses with varied abilities.+ Fun parkour challenges and mini bosses.+ Very well optimized, and almost no bugs whatoever.+ Is what would happen if you put guns in a xianxia. Those guns... They are not normal. + Good game overall despite it's shortcomings. Very fun for a run or two on occasion. It's a nice experience watching your character grow unpredictably into an absolute beast over the 4 acts.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Magic animals commit statue/lizard/tall man/fat man/demon/penguin/misc genocide. Use the justice, its a baby vomit lizard that you slap to reload. Kill sandworm from dune, or the dad from Berenstain Bears after one too many hard ciders. Befriend a panda and become a high speed death turtle. Good game if you like shooting and being fast. Kinda grindy sometimes but feels good to get good and beat high difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR : feels like a full non-early-access game with plenty to do and high polish (except the translation is a bit wonky), a great roguelite where you often feel you got stuff that shouldn't be this overpowered, but its challenging enough to still kill you, especially on elite difficulty-This does not feel like a game thats just come into early access at all. even with the only 3 levels, its still so fleshed out and polished that you could be mistaken for a released game. Running through the 3 5-stage levels also feels like an appropriate length for a roguelite. we'll just needs some more for variation.this is basically deadcells progression with immortal redneck gameplay, and theres so many cool items that every run has something and when you get your favorite guns perks and skills and get some "shops" that let you upgrade some modifiers on your guns to your liking, man you feel like a god.the gameplay is absolutely fantastic, really hits the nail on its head, gunplay feels fast and solid, and you really feel the gun upgrades and perks work when you get them. the graphics are low poly style, and it works well and the guns look and feel great and wildly varied in design and purpose.combine that with plenty of permanent character upgrades and new weapons to unlock, and 4 player coop, and an elite difficulty that you get after completion, which adds traps and harder enemies throughout the game, and its early access and already this polished and full of content, this is going to be a great game once it sees its full release. But already 100% worth its money and fun to play
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves the borderlands game play loop in theory but hates it in practice I feel like this game was made for me. A run wont last longer than 30 minutes I can just pause whenever I need and there is so much variety in every run. Its been my go to game every night since it was in early access and its remained that way since. I've played it both solo and with friends its a blast either way. Making an extremely powerful build is stupid easy so even I can feel great while playing but there is definitely a high skill ceiling there for anyone who wants that. Art style is really pretty and I love all the various enemy designs even after seeing them all I like looking in the bestiary once in awhile just to check out the designs. Overall I highly recommend for anyone that even seems slightly interested because it definitely delivered me more than I could have hoped for this title and maybe it will for you as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game that you can play alone or with friends. If you are looking for a borderlands type of game with roguelike elements, then this is it. This game has many familiar weapons along side of some unique ones with pretty cool combos and builds. You can tell that the developers has put a lot of love and attention to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of this game is very simple: you start, you shoot, and try to survive till the very end with the weapons and scrolls provided. This might not sound like there is much in the game, but is more than what people realize until they start getting into it more frequently. It is captivating and very addictive as you progress more with the characters. _childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game as it has been described as being similar to Dead Cells, Borderlands, and Risk of Rain. I have played a lot of all three of those games. This game is like none of those games. I imagine people draw these comparisons due to the fact that weapons drop out dead enemies randomly, there are skills to acquire, and because you can get resources from the environment. So why isn't it like any of those games?This game is lacking in polish first of all. The argument that it is in early access could be made, but this level of polish is fundamental. Enemies don't make sounds when approaching you, feedback on being hit is non existent, enemies and their head hitboxes are comically large, shooting feels wavy and airy even on low sensitivity, enemies are so so easy while bosses have mechanics that make them unfun, feeling like a "hard" enemy that is designed to keep you playing the same part over and over just to unlock more for your character (which would be fun, if this game was fun). This game has some interesting ideas, but the execution feels like it is trying to take from a lot of things without bringing anything incredible to the table. This game takes from all of the previously mentioned games without improving on that formula. It's actually just a worse way to try and play these games, which is why I feel it is similar to none of these. I could see maybe playing with some friends, but honestly, there are a lot better games I could be playing with my friends. I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is a promising co-op rogue-like FPS that has the gun play of an old school shooter like Serious Sam, with the character and perk systems to that of Borderlands, and the aesthetic of a cell shaded League of Legends roster. While it's all of those things in one well knitted heavily Asian themed ball, it's also decidedly rogue-like to a possibly unfair level of design. I don't mean this in a "git good" kind of way. The game will choose your fate based on the drops you get and it's up to you to run with the flow of it. It's still very beatable and enjoyable but compared to other rogue-likes on the market, this one gives you far less player choice due to its requirement of in game loot drops (and many other RNG favored systems) without there being set in stone places where players can visit to make adjustments. There are stores that randomly appear in game, but one is for upgrading weapons (something that is usually unfavorable in the early game depending on the uniqueness of the weapon's inscriptions) and the peddler generally doesn't sell strong weapons worth the cost. The guns are all fantastic (and generally varied). You can get amazing perks that have extreme ranges in differences they make to the game, and you can find very strange and unique scrolls (there are a ton that are unlockable in game). The upgrade tree feels rewarding rather than unimportant, tedious, or grind heavy. This game has a lot going for it and I hope the Devs keep to their roadmap.My biggest problem is with the game’s consistency: It can just be very tough to cater the run to a desired build or play style when luck is not on your side. Suggestions for further development---A crouch button. I'm trying to teabag my friends.---Level secrets. There are no secrets in this game at all. Yes, there are the slightly hidden gold chests and the vaults, but those are hardly hidden. There should be more secrets that require skillful platforming or a difficult side level boss battle to complete both of which are guaranteed to spawn once per each area. This rewards investigation and player knowledge. ---A guaranteed scroll shop once per area/theme. You should be able to sell, buy, or trade scrolls here. There are currently very few scroll options that are player chosen. ---More visualized weapon synergies based off of elements.---A frost/water element. ---Map hazards or more things I can shoot specific to the map. The maps feel a bit repetitive after a while. Random chances for traps to be placed on the map (that hurt both players and enemies) would shake this up.-More rewards for playing a certain style or way (take no damage on a whole floor, beat a boss in less than a minute, etc.). The game already has a good bit of this, but it's mainly focused around kill counts.---Run options that can be customized in the main menu. These could be "hell" runs where the game is made faster and more difficult with better drops. This could be a whole system like Hades did with their "Heat" option. This works well with my previous point for unlockables.---Better challenges, which can be selected or purchased through a vendor, that can offer guaranteed rare rewards per a room.---An option to make the whole floor non-divided. The door separation idea has been shown to work very well in other similar games (Enter the Gungeon, Binding of Isaac, Hades, etc.). The thing is that those other mentioned games have multiple select-able directions players can take for pathing and advancing through the level. This isn't true in this game at all; the maps are generally linear. The way it is currently is fine, though it would be interesting to see how the gameplay adjusts to a non-stop flow of enemies coming from the next normally blocked off region.-This would also help with pathing: doors that aren't the correct direction should have a different visual design that isn't a floating sigil. It's very easy to mistake an exit for a vault in the desert area. It can just be generally non-obvious where the next area is, although the floating indicator is helpful.All in all, it's a lot of fun with friends and is very fluid as far as movement and gun-play goes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little FPS rogue-like. There is permanent progression (which is quite solid), pretty diverse weapons, and quite good gameplay. Pros - Fast gameplay, snappy action- Seems very well optimized, or at least compatible with lower end machines. Never seen it drop below 140 FPS on a mid-high end PC.- Multiplayer!- Loads of ammo and nades so you never really run out, making the gun-and-run style flow seamlessly- Most of the upgrades feel super powerful, but the game is scaled accordingly well - you get both a challenge, and that feeling of "being overpowered"- Permanent progression/character upgrading feels pretty good and has a noticeable difference- The elemental system feels pretty good though some of the descriptors are a little unclearNeutral- Tile-based levels can feel repetitive, but also means you know the layouts after a few runs- Some abilities/talents definitely feel much stronger than others, which makes the weaker ones unappealing- Most of the weapons are okay to decent, while some are overpowered af and others are absolute garbage. - Some enemies feel kinda same-y (especially in the first zone)- Visual direction may not be appealing to everyone- Some weapons and animations are clearly ripped off from Overwatch lolCons- Still EA so limited content overall (2 character choices, fairly small artifact/"scroll" pool)- Some weapons are definitely overtuned, which means a lot of runs might end up feeling similar (Kunai/crit/poison build)- Some hitboxes feel very very off or misaligned- Perma progression can feel super slow after level 40 or so due to upgrades costing ridiculous amounts of currency- Some visual jittering due to limited animation frames; more noticeable at 144 hzRecommended if you're looking for a light looter-shooter or a rogue light FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of grimdark games or shooters in general, but the cartoon art style keeps Gunfire Reborn lighter, and it is lots of fun with plenty of challenge.  It's a roguelike, so when your run is over, that's it... you start over next time at the beginning.  The fun and replayability come from building your character out each time.  You are dealt "cards" throughout your run in the form of ascensions and scrolls that power up your character, and must choose the ones that will work best with what you have going on this time to be successful.  It plays a little different each time, because your different cards cause you to lean into different playstyles or synergies depending on what you have.Highly recommended for those of us who find building out and improving to be one of the most fun parts of any game.
