_childDocuments_.review: At first glance it doesn't really look like much, or at least that's what I thought when I got it in around 2020. So I might be a little biased as I've seen this game grow into what it is today.This game is an absolute hidden-ish gem in my opinion.Gunfire Reborn is a quick and fun FPS rogue-lite with a rather simplistic, but very colorful and cute art style and some surprisingly fluent movement control.The basic premise is you shooting your way through three (and an optional fourth) areas while the enemies scale in number, power and strength as you progress through the area's stages. with a big boss fight at the end. You equip your character as you go through the stages, be it by the enemies dropping weapons/scrolls, buying them from the merchant that shows up at random each stage or though the stage's vault portals. In a typical rogue-like fashion, if you die or quit, the run is over and you have to start again from the beginning.I don't know if I'd consider the game as hard as some reviews suggest, but if you're starting out expect the game to be a bit rough with you. But there's a nice, satisfying feeling when you get past the newbie's curve balls the game throws at you if you stick with it.Some enemies and bosses do feel unfair at first, but once you learn how to deal with them, this will start to feel less like an issue.The sense of progression comes partially from the upgrades you can buy at the end of each run, weapon and scroll unlocks, and by you learning the ins and outs of the game yourself.One of the few things I'm a bit torn about the game is generally the lack of damage feedback you get, so you sometimes, in the midst of all the chaos, may not notice you're taking damage from an unseen source and that can lead to some frustrating deaths. (Recieving bleeding damage comes to mind as an example).And if you're someone that likes to play through matchmaking, it can feel a bit desolate; specially at lower difficulties.I feel this game's Multi-player mode is best played with a group of friends. But it's also a very solid Single-player experience. Other than that, It's a rather polished experience, except for the occasional translation mishaps or new content bugs (which do get fixed quickly if reported through the in-game feedback tool, the developers are very attentive to it).The game isn't too demanding, hardware-wise; though it can get a bit CPU-heavy on the later stages at higher difficulties. Any modest GPU from 2012-onward can easily breeze through it at max details, at least according to my own tests, and some friends' hardware setups. It's also a game that demands nothing from you, no limited-time events, no seasons, or anything live-service that is so popular nowadays. You play and quit whenever you want, and you won't miss a thing, content-wise.I recommend it! Specially if you have a bunch of friends willing to play with you.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I'm playing the game wrong, but this feels like there is one way to do things; and that's it. Ranged. Several of the characters literally say in their description, "MASTER OF SWORDSMANSHIP!!! DASH IN!! SLICE AND DICE BABEH!!!" But I've tried countless number of runs with the aim of going close-quarters, and even with very tanky builds, I just cannot do it!! Not to mention there are three bosses that you can't actually hit with melee, kind'a rendering it entirely bloody useless!Now that isn't the only reason I'm giving it a negative. I realise the harder difficulties are just that: Difficult. But so often on Nightmare I'll be on an insanely strong run, but regardless, if you get hit: You die. Or at least very close to.. That's part of the game play, sure! But as a result, it feels like unless you get tanky, OOORRRR unless you get good movement, you really are at a disadvantage - And not a small one either..Now again, I realise that's part of the game play, but for me this is just a negative because it doesn't really allow you to play how you want too. I feel like there are few optimal builds even for just the second difficulty; not to mention that some play-styles literally don't work in certain circumstances, which is odd IMO (especially considering the character description says it is aimed at being played that way, but the game punishes you for doing so.... I mean really that's just dumb).There are of course positives (the other reviews speak enough of those) such as the game play in general is fast paced, it is fun for the most part, the animations are nice and smooth with enough visual aids to know how to react at almost any given moment (though on the occasion you will die to... something... from 100% HP and be left entirely clueless) and of course there is a vast variety of guns to try out and they all are relatively, in theory, viable (although again, as above, it feels as though some are entirely broken comparably to others).There is a lot of hours of fun here - And if you enjoy pushing the meta to it's limit, then knock yourself out. But if, like me, you enjoy trying random play styles, or mixing it up with that crappy weapon just trying to see how far you can go with it - Prepare to be a little disappointed in that the answer is often "Not very..." _childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, and you should play it. Think of it like someone took Borderlands 2, The Binding of Issac, and Risk of Rain 2, put them in a blender, and set it to 'puree'.While the comparisons to the Borderlands games are abundant (Characters with vastly different active skills and play strats; the damage types of Fire/Electric/Corrosion; shields and health; guns with a template and varying abilities, some minor, some game-changing), there is enough where you can separate it as its own thing. While there are ascension (skill) trees that can change how a character is played, there are scrolls that can be collected by any character that have similar effects. Many of these types of scrolls and ascensions can stack in ways you can have stupidly overpowered builds, or at least make it that your not-so-overpowered build has a hole patched. The weapons also have a unique identity; each one can vastly change how you choose to attack an enemy. And the inscriptions (stats) they have can mean they just deal more crit damage or have bigger magazines, to spreading elemental effects or getting extra damage on kill for a few seconds, to summoning elemental balls, or even completely change the unique ability on a gun even further.The game has a pretty cute aesthetic too. The furry main characters are pretty cool (no I'm not bais, I really like their designs). The enemies and locations are pretty cool too, and apparently, all represent a section of Asia, which is really interesting. You will learn to hate things like the Nihilation Monks or the Arsonists, especially their elite versions. And much like Borderlands, hit their Red Health Bars with Fire, Blue Shields with Electricity, and Yellow Armor with Corrosion. They function like they do in Borderlands (more damage against the type it is weak to, less damage to others), but they also can combine into fusion effects to added weirdness (charming an enemy to be an extra target, another heavy and stackable DoT effect, or just exploding and damaging all people near them). The main elements also have their own effects like Burning (DoT), extra damage (Shock), or a slow (decay). And there are scrolls, ascensions, and inscriptions that can take advantage of that too.Finally, they keep adding things like new game modes (a survival mode) or harder difficulties (not just a vertical difficulty tweek, but ones where you can get combos of scrolls to add new effects or give ENEMIES scroll effects too). Even with the DLC adding new characters and weapons, with more in the works, there are a LOT more ways to play. They also add free updates, and have a roadmap in game of what they plan to add. The developers are engaged, and it is great to see.And when played with friends, you can consolidate your scrolls and abilities together to ensure that you all can have super insane builds. Make a tank to take the focus, a sniper to destroy things far from battle, an alchemist to inflict status effects upon status effects, whatever works.The only downsides the game has is when first starting out (the talent trees take time to unlock, and on your own it is a slow process), and it has the same issue of 'Stop and Start' game play issues that Borderlands has (you go through a room, clear it out, then have to spend time looking over to see if you missed anything, and with partners, swap scrolls and weapons.) At least it fixes something like making your items instanced to you until you ping it, so no one can just up and steal that legendary that dropped for you, unless it doesn't fit you. The story is also non-existent (like it is there but doesn't really have much of an effect on things), and it has a considerable amount of 'Engrish' in it. To be fair, though, I like that last bit. 'Challenge Succeed' sounds so awesome when clearing a room. At least the descriptions of scrolls will tell you exactly what they do, so you know exactly how they will react to other effects you do have.TLDR: Buy this game, buy it with friends, destroy all in front of you, then go back to the inn and do it again!

_childDocuments_.review: What is a good way to describe it? Furry doom mixed with whatever Rougelike you can think of. and before the term "furry" drives you away, let the gameplay speak for itself. smooth controls and chaotic yet calm encounters, depending on your play style, want to sit back with a sniper and pick enemies off before they can fight back, go ahead. Jump into the frey with a sword and brawl anything that dare glance at you funny, no problem. The best part is it does have that balance between Skill and RNG some games are a test of skill as the Upgrades recieved aren't quite what you were after, but still viable. Some are what I call "Canonical Doomguy" runs, where builds went so in you're favor you wade through enemies like fire through gas doused paper. but here's where the balance comes into play, even on "Doomguy" runs, It will easily bring your run crashing down as the enemies scale rather smoothly, not too powerful, but noticeably tougher. best I can say is "The game makes you overpowered, because the enemies will be just as so." keeping you on your toes even at the best of points. Lastly, the game rewards risky moves, taking a fall to grow further than before, like "oh no, I got a curse that reduces my ammo, but got a scroll to negate 3 instances of damage every 30 seconds" or "I take more trap damage, but my lucky shot went through the roof." yeah you have a downside, but what you get usually outweighs the bad.Edit: Game is still being updated as of making this and has only gotten better

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my low playtime, I have a good 30 hours or more over on the Game Pass port. More on that in a moment.Gunfire Reborn is what happens when you take the absurd guns and character classes of something like Borderlands (there is a gun that literally gets thrown like a grenade for a reload, and one of the characters is straight up a Gunzerker), and then take the "roguelike but with steady progression and unlocks" formula made famous by a lot of games of the genre, such as Enter the Gungeon. Throw it into a 1-to-4 player FPS where the game scales based on the total members of your party, and a rather simple but very effective skill, and you get a game that's easy to pick up, hard to master, and oh so satisfying to find synergies in.Unfortunately, that's only on the PC release. The Game Pass version isn't directly ported by the devs. It's instead handled by 505 Games. Usually they're good at what they do, but they fumbled hard with Gunfire Reborn. Whereas the PC release just got a major update with new content, and has a DLC already, with another DLC slated for spring, the Game Pass port is more or less a buggy beta release. Many guns are missing, the two DLC characters aren't purchaseable, and the recent arena mode update for PC was not present. Heck, a good chunk of the game wasn't even fully localized. Looking at you, Cursed Red Chests. As of the writing of this review, some of these bugs, and the localization, have been fixed, but there's no excuse for a lack of content.There is also a mobile phone port, which to my knowledge IS supported directly by the devs. To my knowledge they're only a minor update or two behind, but otherwise it's equivalent to the PC release if your phone can run it.Running it isn't difficult, but what may catch some low-end PC users is the particle effects. Late in runs, they can really swarm the field, especially in multiplayer. That said, the netcode is fairly reliable (on PC). And it's really easy to queue up with random folks or to join your friends.Overall, Gunfire Reborn is a very solid game with a formula that works. It sticks to it and yet gives the game a wonderful personality. The various level aesthetics are all unique despite there only being 4 ish total states, and with a nice roster of characters with different playstyles, there's something for everyone. You can go it alone or cause mayhem with friends. The cel-shaded characters pop, and each are very identifiable.If you love roguelike shooters and love guns that become chainsaws when reloading, love elemental shotguns, and love Chinese history and mythology, then you will love Gunfire Reborn. Just.. please avoid playing on Xbox Game Pass.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I am usually not much for writing reviews, especially long ones, so take it as a compliment that I decided to write one for this game, especially after seeing how the devs are very attentive to community feedback.This game is really good, let's just get that out of the way. I think it is excellent at filling a design space that was surprisingly lacking ( that of first person roguelite/like games). And I usually don't even like FPSs ( and I am very very bad at them) but I still like this game A LOT.Where I am at the game right now: After playing the game for a few days, and having beat the game in the standard difficulty, I have spent my latest 8 hours or so of gameplay  grinding to unlock all the items and level up my account before tackling on the harder difficulties. What I like:- Gunplay feels really good, responsive, and intuitive. I mentioned that I am bad at shooter games and have played very few in my life, and yet I am easily able to hit enemy weakspots and snipe them from a distance with little effort, which I believe is a statement of how good the game feels, not my personal skill.- The game aesthetics are refreshing to see. The big inspiration on Chinese themes and visuals are uncommon in the genre, and the creative use of mythological creatures for enemy design is clever and fun.- Enemy design overall is fun, and varied. Enemies come in various shapes, sizes and movesets, and most of them are very fun to fight, even the harder ones specifically designed to be more 'frustrating'. The enemy AI is also surprisingly good where it didn't HAVE to be. Yes, it is still a bit buggy sometimes but the enemies move in interesting ways, take cover from you, dodge roll from your shots, in a way that feels organic.- And finally, just a very good overall foundation for a game that is still in early access, and that with extended dedication by the team behind it could turn out to be something iconic.What I think could be improved:- As I mentioned I haven't tackled on the harder difficulties past Elite yet so perhaps this is something that is already more present in those, but I think the game could use a bit more work on stage variety at the moment. It is already starting to feel a bit repetitive to me as both enemy placement and level design repeats VERY often ( although since the game is so fun you really don't feel it as much). Perhaps just having more permutations on which enemies show up and where would already help this, but some more levels would  obviously help a lot.- Although gun variety is already very good and will certainly improve with more updates, I feel that guns may be a bit imbalanced? I am not sure if it's just my personal preference but there are guns that clearly feel much more powerful than others, and I am not too sure if this is an intentional design decision.- Character ascencions are interesting and exciting, and allow for many different builds. Occult scrolls, on the other hand, don't feel as exciting to me. They are certainly powerful and very important for your build, but many of them feel a bit more 'passive'. I would like to see more scrolls that change the way you play the game.- Characters are amazing and super fun, but they are also clearly designed to be 'specialized'in certain things. This is not a bad design decision, as all characters feel powerful in their own way. But personally I would also like more characters like the first two that have a bit more build variety than the others. The later two characters, the tiger and the bunny, feel almost completely railroaded into using snipers and SMGs respectively.- I am usually not that much of a fan of Roguelites because I dislike the overall grindy character progression, and in my opinion this game is  guilty of that. I don't mind the unlock requirements for guns and scrolls ( although a couple of them ARE a bit ridiculous, looking at you Demonlore..) but the account leveling system is straight up a huge grind. I have already played for more than 20 hours and there are still a lot of talents left to get, and it is starting to feel like a chore because there are some very key features ( such as selling guns and scrolls) locked behind the later parts of this leveling system.- The visual and sound design in this game is super good, I especially love the menu design as well as the music before a game starts. However, there are a couple things that are a bit awkward and could use some work. Examples:   1. It is a bit hard to see which gun you have on which button just by the HUD.  2. I would appreciate the inclusion of character names in English as well (not just in their bio)  3. Sometimes it is a bit hard to tell where the damage is coming from, most shooters try to make that a bit more clear  4. Character design is great, but at the risk of being flamed to oblivion by angry 'gamers', I was a bit disappointed with the design of the latest character, Tao, which is the only female character. When I saw her 2D art on the loading screen and game news I was super excited to unlock her, but her in-game model is weirdly  sexualized in a pretty childish manner, and her damage sounds are anime girl moans. I am by no means a puritan but the other characters are so cool and interesting that she sticks out like a sore thumb.Conclusion:Well those are my overall opinions on the game at the moment, I will probably edit this review to include my updated views after playing on the harder difficulties but overall I think this game is really great, and with the right care by the team behind it will turn out to be something really special.

_childDocuments_.review: browsing through the reviews, it's a wonder how nobody has brought up this game's terrible boss designs.you've probably read through a number of reviews so i'll keep my contribution brief, i'll stick to things i haven't seen anyone mention yetbosses can and will hard counter you, and there isn't much you can do about it.-bosses that spam AOE's faster than your dodge cooldown-bosses that demand either extreme close range or extreme long range, sometimes in the same fight-bosses that demand you immediately understand their mechanics or get punished with your hp bar, sometimes fatally. enjoy dying confused to a boss before you read their patternsbosses will use very powerful attacks with little to no telegraphing, with spasmatic animation when it is telegraphedthis isn't to say bosses are hard or even complex. i haven't seen one use more than 4 different attacks, they don't really respond to your positioning unless you're in their butthole, and their gimmicks are glaringly obvious and force you to take a linear approach.this is probably the main reason people are saying that off-meta builds aren't viable. the best way to beat the game is to out-dps any boss that your build otherwise can't handle. it's stacking crits (called lucky shots) and damage in any way possible and pummeling into their weak spots. you can completely own zone anything even if you don't get perfect rolls for your build as long as you stick to the damage stacking modeli think the worst part is that these issues don't become obvious until you've beaten the game once and unlock the next difficulty options, i imagine people would be at that point invested in going further into the roguelite loop, only to come out disappointed. i was at one point having fun in the higher difficulty because i was moving around much more and felt forced to respect enemies as their damage and hp increased (aside from boss fights, which just felt weaker in comparison). this died in a lightbulb moment in my latest run when i realized that i wasn't actually respecting enemies, what i was doing was trying to cut down the cognitive load of having 10-15 different enemies on screen at once with different patterns and movesets by trying to quickly kill as many at once before i could meaningfully react defensively to whatever remained. i didn't care which ones i killed, my positioning, which were most dangerous and why, i wanted the visual noise to stop. unpleasant memories of late stage overwatch came flooding back before writing whatever disparate thoughts i had on this game to share, before uninstalling it for good.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels about time to recommend this now that it has hit version 1.0.Gunfire Reborn is a roguelite that mixes FPS and RPG elements. Each hero has unique abilities, passives, and roles. You can play solo or with up to three others (4 players max) and the experience feels better with others in my opinion. Each run is procedurally-generated and you will learn patterns overtime. A typical run will see you collecting goblets to fill out your skill trees, scrolls to power up various aspects of gameplay, and improving your weapons. What does the game have at time of writing this?6 Heroes (each with an "ultimate" ability, a secondary ability, five passives, and three skill trees for eighteen skills)148 Scrolls of various rarities (normal, rare, legendary, and cursed)48 Weapons (including rifles, shotguns, and swords to name a few)69 Enemies (including sixteen elite variants and seven bosses)4 Acts/Areas (with two to four subsections to complete each)2 Modes (adventure and daily challenge)4 Difficulties (one of which scales when beating it)...and potentially more to come!The developers have been very active since release with adding more into the game, balancing everything related to heroes/skills/scrolls/weapons, bug fixing, and overall listening to the community. The first year has been quite the adventure and am looking forward to what they do next and onward.

_childDocuments_.review: You start in stage one. Every stage has several areas/rooms you have to clear to get to the next stage. Every stage has   different looking areas and unique enemies. By killing enemies you receive souls, coins and sometimes weapons and   scrolls(powerups/perks) as a drop. The difficulty and your strength rises with every area and stage you clear. At the last   area of the stage you will need to fight a boss. Currently there are 2 bosses for every stage and you will need to fight one   of them who gets selectet by random. With the coins you collect during your run you can upgrade your weapons or   by all sorts of items(not permanent upgrades). The souls you can spend to upgrade your talents in your skilltree(more   weapondamage, enhancements for heros and more).  Some weapons and scrolls perform better on specific hero. Some scrolls work great together and others match together   horribly. It is needed to match the scrolls to your hero and his/her skills to get sronger and not weaker. This really adds to   the replayability of the game. I should probably also mention that you unlock scrolls and weapons by killing an specific   enemies. Weapons on the other hand cuuuum with different enhancements, when dropped, which become stronger in   later stages.  The Multiplayer is fun but sometimes a bit laggy. Its also not rare to have a high ping. Althogh my PC isn't the best and is   over the minimum requirement for the game I have bad Fps drops when a lot of enemies and/or players are on the screen.  They are all possible to get some more challenging than others. I enjoyed getting them all.I recommend the game to every roguelike fan and to everyone who wants to play an amazing roguelike game.You can spend easiely over 120h in this game and you will not get bored. For 10€ this game is just amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an FPS Rouge-like, which means, it's brutally satisfying to play. However, I do believe this game has greater potential than it currently has. The runs that you will be playing will be relatively the same, as this game focuses more on linear progression in a run, rather than it all being up to chance (generally, there are a lot of RNG factors that can be completely random, independent from your current stage). For example, on stage 1 you might get the Tiger Cannon with 2 attributes, those being of the basic type, like 20% more damage, or 50% more magazine size. Later on, you might get a Fire Dragon with 6(!) random attributes, those being of a high rarity(!!). While I think this is good, and removes a high percentage of RNG, I consider that introducing more randomness in the player's progression would definitely improve the replayability, creating those memorable games where you had a massive power spike in the early stages and cruised through the rest of the stages. However, this lack of chance in terms of what loot you get, is good for keeping the game interesting, as if you don't get lucky in other roguelikes, your run is generally over and you start anew. Here, if you die it is generally because you messed up and took a wrong turn while fighting the enemies. I give this game an 8.5/10. This game is excellent for the price or even higher. P.S. If you have friends that own it, give it a try with them. After all, it's a co-op roguelike, what else would you want?

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about Gunfire Reborn:Overall, the game is pretty enjoyable. The gameplay is fun and everything about it *feels* great. The gunplay is satisfying, critical hits feel crisp, movement is incredibly smooth, and the rogue-like elements are intuitive. You can have a great time playing this game solo or with friends (assuming you and your friends all have above-average internet connection... more on this later).But..- After about 30 minutes to an hour of playing you'll have already seen everything the game has to offer. You will continue to unlock new characters/weapons/abilities/bosses, sure, but they really don't affect the game that much, nor do they revitalize it with anything truly new, unique, or interesting.- The talent tree has permanent upgrades you can unlock between runs, and it is SUPER helpful. In fact, probably a bit TOO helpful. You'll often find yourself unable to progress any further in the game until you grind for the currency needed to get X upgrade on the tree. This also makes playing with significantly higher or lower level friends pretty disheartening, as one of you will be relatively invulnerable and dealing 90% of the damage while the others waddle along with minimal upgrades.- (Opinion) Each of the six characters feel very restrictive in their playstyles, and if one of them doesn't fit you perfectly well, the game may be significantly less fun for you... I've been unable to find a character I really enjoy/that fits my playstyle, so this feels very... "meh" to me.- Lots of little issues here and there that can disrupt the immersion and become a frequent annoyance.- Multiplayer uses a peer to peer connection system, which is perfectly fine in-and-of-itself. However, should your friend's wifi flicker out for a fraction of a second, you'll find yourself unable to reload, swap weapons, use abilities, or do practically anything else. You'll also notice that the enemies become invulnerable, freeze up for a moment, and then teleport, killing you instantly. It's not so much the lag that is an issue here, but the fact that all elements of the game are ran on the host's end. You have absolutely no control over anything as a connected client, should you be faced with internet issues, making multiplayer feel rather clunky.- Multiplayer (part 2). Should you decide to play with anyone with significantly more or less skill than you, it's likely that one of you will be dead for a VERY large portion of the run. Every time someone goes down they get a "down penalty," which decreases the amount of time they have to be revived. This means that, eventually, revives just won't be possible to pull off, leading to lots of spectating. One of your friends can still bring you back into the game later, should they be lucky enough to find a certain NPC (the peddler). You'll also revive if your friend beats the next boss, but keep in mind that this usually takes a while, since any survivors will be facing multiplayer-scaled-enemies with less teammates. -----TL;DRGunfire Reborn is fun for a little bit, but it has too many issues and not enough content (even for a roguelike) for me to recommend it or say it's worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: *DISCLAIMER FOR ANYONE NON-SURE IF WANNA BUY*Although the game is currently in Early Access, it's fairly solid. Being by a HK/Chinese-based studio and featuring some questionable grammar and syntax in the store page, your first reaction might be that it looks like the many shovelware/asset flip type garbage games that are unfortunately cluttering the Steam store; not in this case!Gunfire Reborn, to describe it better than the Steam Store page, is a rogue-like (or maybe rogue-lite; i honestly am not sure what the distinction is between those two terms) first person shooter, with semi-randomized guns a la Borderlands, that can be played solo or cooperatively (online), and some light RPG elements. You play as one of either two characters (only one of which is unlocked at first), running through rooms and fighting enemies until you reach a boss fight for the level; I would compare it to Risk of Rain 2, The Binding of Isaac, or probably its closest relative would be Immortal Redneck. Upon death, you can invest currency gathered during the run, called "soul essence", into levels in a skill tree, and you can't carry it over to the next run (at least, at first), so you're encouraged to invest as much as possible into whatever skills you can to improve your chances on the next run.The combat gameplay is surprisingly solid for an Early Access game; there's great variety in weapons, and most if not all the guns I've tried have been fun to use and felt precise and fairly balanced. There are some status effect type things that can stack to broken levels pretty easily, but the game seems to be a "give high damage, take high damage" type affair, at least at the time of writing.As I mentioned earlier, this game is still in Early Access, so you can expect a little glitchiness here and there, but it seems to mostly come in the form of visual disparities, like your co-op partner's gun looking different to you than to them, or certain effects not properly displaying to the other player. In about 30 hours of play, neither myself nor my friend I've been co-oping with have noticed much in the way of game-breaking bugs. However, the developers are actively soliciting feedback, so in the event that you do encounter any, you can send a report in-game very easily.Because English is not the developers' native language, you may notice some funky looking grammar or word choice, and if I'm being honest, some of the names of scroll effects or guns read like they're items on a Chinese restaurant's menu, or like they weren't properly translated because maybe the original word doesn't have a good equivalent in English. Here's hoping that these little issues can be corrected before the game truly launches, but for now I'm giving it an 8 on the basis of fun, addictive co-op gameplay and the fact that it's only a $10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: As always, I have to lament the simplicity of steam's review system. If I were to rate this game on a 10 scale, it'd be a 6 or maybe a 5. I think this game is very overrated, and despite my semi-positive experience with it, I am putting in a negative review to point out how many issues this game still has to work through. It still feels very much like an early access title, since content wise it is lacking a lot, and the design seems beyond jumbled.The game isn't really unique in its design, and unfortunately it doesn't really do anything very well, at least not enough to carry the game.The gunplay is also very unsatisfying, with a lot of the weapons being ones I don't even touch because they're beyond useless for most characters. I wish there was some more impactful feedback from crits and weapons like the shotguns/snipers. With the character I play the most, I tend to use machineguns, and they're like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ water hoses.For me, the best part of roguelites, is that they offer interesting progression through unlocks. Well, after 8 hours of playing the game, I'd already beaten the first two difficulties and unlocked every character bar one (since the same currency to unlock that character is also one tied to the progression, which is a system I really dislike). The unlocks of new weapons or perks then became a trickle, which immediately killed most of my desire to continue playing, but I've still managed to put in about a total of 14 hours, though a lot of those last few hours have been boring and irritating.The different characters on offer should be what drives the variety of gameplay, but at least three of them are reskinned copies of each other it feels like, and I've ended up mostly sticking to the lightning bear and sword bunny, since their design seems to actually have some thought in it, instead of being "unique special" + grenade, like the rest (aside from the aegis dude which i've yet to unlock). I was especially disappointed with the bird and dog characters, since they seemed like they should be fun, and I get the feeling that a lot of people especially aren't a fan of the bird, seeing as a pretty simple achievement for him is one of the least unlocked in the game.The game has a serious lack of variety, especially considering the fact that you always see the same route: clausterphobic temple > desert ruins > weird japan-folklore-inspired area with no direction > literally antartica. That's it, those are all the areas in the game, and you'll get the see the first one the most, obviously, and none of it is interesting enough to sustain the game on the 20th playthrough, when you've already exhausted every possible layout. A lot of roguelites are very good at diversifying their levels, but Gunfire Reborn isn't one of them.Later difficulties also become especially RNG dependent due to the nature of the first level, as it is very hard to put a lot of distance between yourself and the enemies, nor is it easy to find cover to avoid hits that will do 40% of your health in damage and are spammed everywhere. This issue is less a problem on later levels, but most of your runs on nightmare+ are instantly ended if you get bodyblocked in a corner by 4 enemies and one of them has a grenade or a sword. So, the first level definitely needs an update. It is the first level in the game and the one you see the most, but also the one least outfitted with interesting variety or fun enemies.I think this game especially suffers in the design area, since a lot of things are just plain bad design, such as the first level or the enemies that inhabit it. Another area that lacks proper design is item/perk readability. A lot of perks will ♥♥♥♥ up your run (thankfully all except the cursed ones can be removed manually) if you pick up something detrimental during combat. A lot of roguelites with item pickups tend to go for very obvious designs so you know what is what, but in Gunfire Reborn the perks are all just the same scroll, with a colour variety for rarity. Also, golden (legendary) scrolls aren't always something you want to pick up, and the result of this terrible way of handling readability, means you'll always have to wait until after finishing an area before you go through each item and checks what it has to offer, which hampers gameplay a lot by forcing you to slow down. This is less an issue with weapons, since they are clearly distinct, but, with all the different perks, you still end up needing to read through each item and what inscriptions it has.For the asking price, this is an alright game, but I think a lot of people will encounter the same annoyances as I have after playing the game for a while.One last note I wanted to add is that, given that the daily challenges are supposed to be something that diversifies gameplay, it is quite ironic to see all achievements tied to it are some of the least unlocked in the game. The daily challenges are by far the worst designed part of the game though, so it makes sense most people don't even have "beat a daily challenge" as an achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: A fresh newcomer dev team giving us a familiar yet solid take on the rouge-lite genre, Gunfire Reborn takes aim with solid art direction with fast paced challenging gameplay. It holds its own with the now thriving market of many like it but how far ahead is this now fully released early access title? -/TOMBS, SPEARS, UFOS O MY!\-The team who put this game together offered players with a clear take on an already established gameplay style. You begin each run with barebones weapons, skills and scrolls. Each aspect is nothing fully new to any seasoned vet in the field but the pure untapped mish mash of options lets your furry character ascend to godhood in so many odd and wacky ways. Why for me Gunfire holds itself so high in my head were the nice touches given to everything. The art has this low poly yet surprisingly detailed clean feel. Enemies for their respective zones have varying looks, attacks and a slew of oddly charming designs. Yes Gunfire added UFO’s in here too and it all feels like it belongs. The zones themselves which you will be getting very acquainted with over many runs each have a nice contrast with one another. The beginning being a standard tomb with plain walls, basic torches and some fire traps along the way. The desert really helps the player get some fresh air with more open arenas to fight in. My favorite zone being the third, having the rainy fish village crawling with octo gunners, catfish soldiers and a giant frog warship. Gunfire Reborn is a treat to look at with just how well the art keeps the light hearted tone alive and well. -/The Animal Pubcrawl\- Gunfire Reborn has you picking from a wonderfully distinct cast of would be heroes. The main gimmick lies not within their animalistic features but skills only they can have. Bunny samurai with magical swords she can summon at will, fast swiping bird leaping into battle or a dog who brings on double the pain with twice the firepower. I found myself entrenched deep within the belly of gameplay options given when I find myself drinking a goblet to enhance a skill or modify another part of the kit to really find interesting and sometimes oddball ways of dealing out damage. Ao Bai, the resident dual wielding dog of death, can go with a fun full auto build. Maybe that won't suit you, if you get lucky explosive rockets filling the screen with that satisfying ding will suit better. Not only does the game allow you to pick and upgrade the character mid run but an outer, less deep shell of the talent system too. After each run successful or not you may be collecting little bits of magic called soul essence. With this after each run you can spend it on basic things such as skill cooldowns, ammo supplies or more heavy gameplay changes such as etching weapons or scrapping old items for a bit of extra cash. I do wish the game offered more in the talent tree as grinding it out feels almost tiring and kind of empty with the progression. Talents are not the only thing you are unlocking though, what kind of game would be titled “Gunfire” without its title stars? -/Gunplay Reiterated\- Gunfire Reborn has some of the most insane, wild and downright fun weapons I have ever used in a modern game in some time. To the basic fast firing minigun to a literal dragon wrapped on your wrist ready to spew fire at a moment's notice. You can even get a nice touch of melle oriented toys to swing around if you wish to. I only found a few weapons not to my own liking but with how many there are everyone should java a must pick with just the sheer variety on site. But just having a weapon is the beginning for you and whoever tags along, inscriptions are yet another side to this coin. They can make you blast our faster amounts of bullets, slimb numbers with crits or just decide you get to fire two shots at once on most weapons, double firing rocket launchers. It is easy to see the clear comparisons to the larger than life Gearbox owned franchise with the guns yet Gunfire doesn’t try too hard in just duplicating the winning formula. Every gun still plays as it should without a huge reliance on bloated stats needing to drop with increasingly rare crits or magazines. You can just pick up a weapon and have it function as it would be with a nice dash of magical properties that help it do more of what it does. -/A friend in need\-Gunfire Reborn has a lot to offer in the Coop space that has been lacking in recent years. Quick fast paced gameplay for up to 4 players. Average times of 45 minute games and a very forgiving selection of difficulties as well. You are not even required to play with 4 people to get the most of Gunfire, the game just gets even more crazy with each player added. The downside of a game such as this is how punishing death can be still. Dying in coop can mean you could be waiting with nothing to do for some time. Reviving players is only possible with the randomly spawning shop keeper or after a boss is killed. Meaning those who got unlucky can be left unenthused to continue or bored watching slightly janky third person models run around. If you are unable to find friends you can also try out your hand at matchmade games. There is a barebones experience with this, text chat along with voice chat helps with communication. The biggest problem takes place on the menu with how some game mode and difficulty have wait times up to 10 minutes or beyond. But if you are used to longer queue times this should not be an issue. -/Final points\-Gunfire Reborn has so much potential in becoming the next big fast paced coop shooter people are looking for. Following some of the stronger gameplay trends in the modern age and refining them to suit its vision. Strong art direction helps establish this vision more, giving off enough delight for the eyes and ears. With some minor gameplay hiccups involving odd third person animations, off putting death penalties and a progression system left a bit too bare. I still can’t find an excuse not to pick up a quick run and smile along as I toss a grenade at my enemies so that my handheld mortar can finish the job. I will see myself playing this game for some time hoping for even more to come with such a promising development team.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine, if you will...A rogue-like. Imagine in that rogue-like, you are first-person. Now.. combine the aspects of loot from Risk of Rain 2, with a RPG-aspect of improving talents.. and now, continue to think.. each time you run-through, you gain a scaling buff that persists through that entire run that keeps getting stronger the longer you play.Now you're in the game, shooting things and fighting enemies with unique abilities. And you find a swirling purple rune on a wall--then you enter it, and find yourself suddenly facing a mini-boss and get your shoopo kicked in. You get sent to a main menu, and get to put points into talents and dive back in.. the enemies are the same, but the map is not. And you just keep finding better and better guns--and then.. you find Hell. A shotgun that rapid-fire shoots and even if you're reloading mid-combat, you slot it once and then begin firing at a full clip once more.That is this game.It is fun, action-packed, fast-paced and frustrating at times but for something in early access? It is surprisingly well-polished and EXTREMELY difficult. AS the boss fights themselves are extremely tough. They have tons of health, deal tons of damage, and have phases where their mechanics keep getting more and more difficult and complicated. Unlike other rogue-likes, where the enemies just get scaled health, damage and armor? Each zone after the first one? Has enemies who are hella tougher by default, regardless of how much time you've spent in the game.I highly recommend this game for everyone who enjoys a looter-shooter rogue-like.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is the lovechild of Risk of Rain 2 and Borderlands infused with a heavy dose of stylization that can only be described as Okami but Chinese with a heavy dose of chibi.Gunplay is pretty standard, most weapons are projectiles but a good chunk of them have projectile speed fast enough to feel reasonably close to hitscan at close range, and as a result only really deterring the freshest of newcomers from taking longer shots, not to mention the weapons that are -actually- hitscan. The sound and visual design is what really helps sell this here, as the variance in weapons is closer to the first Borderlands, which felt like it was full of guns that happened to be slightly magic, than it does to the rest of the series which could fire pretty much anything out of a barrel for the sake of a joke or a shock to the player. This gives the game a more gritty dungeon crawler feel while still being darkly cute in its more blatant aesthetic.Enemy variance is a little less interesting than you might think, you'll be dealing with melee guys, relatively low hp crawlers, grenade guys, tall skinny snipers, and heavies with either shields or close range high damage weaponry. The affix system ripped straight from Diablo III helps quite a bit here, as do some minor changes in how you have to interact with the enemies depending on how far into your run you are; the crawlers in area 2 are a lot larger and more powerful, but their size means their additional HP is basically worthless. The heavies from area 1 to area 2 become absolutely devastating, as they go from being large horse statues that mostly serve to annoy you in the middle of a fight to being large scary Roadhog lookalikes with flamethrowers that will nuke an unsuspecting player in the midst of a sniper duel.Level design isn't necessarily exceptional but there's enough verticality and variance to room shape where I don't mind that I'm fighting in the same rooms a lot of the time. It helps that many rooms/chunks are locked to specific areas, which gives me hope for more rooms added down the line as more weapons are added and need to be accounted for. My only real complaint here is that the challenge rooms are very samey, especially the platforming sections. Platforming sections which require perfect dash and jump placement/timing, otherwise you have to start entirely over again, which turns to frustration quickly on even the shortest sections. We need more variance here, and we need some of these sections to have added hazards and more forgiving platform spacing. Less boulder rooms as they aren't difficult, they're only boring.Weapon inscriptions, much like red text in Borderlands or any text in Diablo, add small bonuses to your weapon that can change  how you play and how viable your weapon is. This is great until you realize that you can only upgrade your weapon's damage, you can't change, buy, or affix further inscriptions. This can make finding your favorite gun early in a run  disappointing and depressing rather than exciting like it would be in a game like Synthetik: Legion Rising.Overall, combat feels really good and even though I only bought this 2 or 3 days ago it's quickly become one of my favorite roguelites/roguelikes of all time. I hope that the characters get added with more interesting abilities and that maybe you get more options to what your dash ability can be as you level up. I hope that more guns that resemble Borderlands 1 get added, kinda like the Star Devourer or Concealed Ammo or Piercing Flame. The dev team would do well to skew damage scaling away from straight number-walling like Risk of Rain 2 as there is no organic leveling system, and skew it more towards interesting stacking with damage over time elemental effects like Borderlands or even Immortal Redneck, a game which clearly shares a lot in common with Gunfire Reborn.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an FPS roguelite where you can play as various characters with as goal to survive the Tomb, Desert and the Fjords and defeat the end boss, Yoruhime-Maru. Just like many roguelites, every run in Gunfire Reborn is different. Each time you play, different guns, ascensions and scrolls present themselves. Scrolls have varying abilities that can aid a build or work together well with a specific weapon or ability. Many of them can be found but they can also be bought at the Peddler or traded for via treasure chests.You don’t have control over what ascensions (character upgrades during a run) you find, but each time you find a goblet containing one, you get a choice in 3, of which most you can upgrade two more times after taking. There are a lot of unique guns to choose from (currently 40 different base guns), with a lot of them having a unique function or ability. On top of that, they can all have different statistics and properties to them, such as increased projectiles, magazine or reload speed, a different element or a gun-specific upgrade. This variation allows a lot of guns to be used in many different ways and for many different builds.You can also upgrade your guns at the Craftsman. He can make your weapon stronger and also reforge any possible Gemini inscriptions. The latter are an inscription that if both your guns have it, they become active and work on both your guns, such as a shared amount of crit damage, or shared magazine, shared damage type (element fusion), etc.There’s currently 3 different characters, all with unique abilities, ascension paths and playstyles:* Crown Prince who can shoot an orb that locks enemies in place and has weakening smoke grenades* Ao Bai who can dual-wield guns that combines and amplifies their strength and has explosive grenades * Qing Yan who is a martial arts character that attacks by using leaps to land on enemies and then cleave them with his wingsThere are currently 3 zones: Longling Tomb, Anxi-Desert and Duo-Fjords. Each have unique enemies, elite minibosses and a final boss. They also contain vaults, which are a single area that contain a reward, but to obtain it you first have to survive a challenge, such as a trap parkour or fighting off more enemies.You can play with up to four players in a single game. Playing with more players makes the enemies stronger but it also allows you to trade scrolls and weapons with your teammates so that everyone can more easily go for the build they are trying to get.In a nutshell, this game is Borderlands mixed with Binding of Isaac in Sea of Thieves graphics. It has great replay value because of the different inscriptions guns can spawn with, as well as the different scrolls and ascensions you get each time.This game is in early access and while it is a fully-fledged game, it is still worked on when it comes to squashing bugs and adding more content. The devs (only 3!) have shown incredibly potential for this game to become even better and are working hard to add more and more to it. It’s very addicting and can make you really forget the time. And all that for the ridiculously low price of only 10 bucks, outside of sales. Better get this awesome game before it may have a price increase in the future, because for the amount of content you get, this is a true bargain.Also, consider joining the Discord:  where you can find players and chat about the game, as well as suggest and discuss new features.

_childDocuments_.review: You know you can just like call me, right? You don't need to go to the effort of making a Borderlands Roguelite with Co-Op Multiplayer. You don't have to work this hard to impress me. I love you just the way you are.Jokes aside, Gunfire Reborn immediately drew my attention for being the exact genre jumble to be a perfect master key for my interests. And now that it's got a full release, I feel like it would be a good time to throw my hat into the ring to tell you just how much it's improved.What I like:-Lordy lou, the weapon variety. Other games, you get the usual smattering of weapons. In Gunfire Reborn? Pistols, Submachine Guns, Assault Rifles, Bows, Throwing Knives, Fire-Breathing Lizards, Iron Man Gauntlets, Swords, A shotgun that is alive that you reload by feeding fish, A frozen Javelin that returns to you after you throw it- I could be here all day.-The gunplay also feels really good, generally. Some of the weapons are a little underwhelming, but generally fights feel very good to be engaged in.-Movement feels very fluid. Everyone has an air dash for free, which is really necessary if you want to be able to consistently dodge. Some of the more powerful weapons will slow you down, and you have to decide if it's worth leaving yourself open to have access to such high damage. It makes you think fast.-It feels very hard to have a "bad" gunfire run. Most of the weapons are strong enough on their own or most skill builds have enough synergy that generally speaking it's difficult to have a run that feels genuinely weak on most characters.What needs work:-Some of the later characters have the "Darkest Dungeon Mod" problem of being way to reliant on their own mechanics and tied up in synergy so much that they barely have a use. I don't want to reduce the cooldown on my terrafarter to give me nine stacks of bungomart which leads me to deal more damage with corrosive weapons if I'm standing upside down and reciting the torah. Just give me 40% more headshot damage and call it a day. Worst offenders of this are Qian Sui and Lei Lou, who feel like there is (1) viable build for, and that build barely involves guns.-The Translation is kind of spotty. It's improved a lot since the beta, but a lot of the phrasing is still kinda weird. A lot of the times the word "a" is replaced with "the" which makes the game sound needlessly formal.-A lot of the upgrades, like a lot of the characters, are needlessly specific. It kind of makes you build something really weird and lopsided just to try and use the buffs you have.-Enemies kind of all have giant heads that are easy to hit, and it sort of feels like damage on anything but the head does next to nothing. I get that it's the style and all but it'd be cool to move some of the headshot damage to bodyshots.All that said, I think Gunfire is a very good game. Highly replayable, very arcade-y, and has kind of taken the place of other games like Killing Floor 2 in my mind as braindead dude-shooters. It's a whole lot of fun, and I really wish that I wasn't getting into it when I have so many term projects due. But that's a whole other thing.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT Nov. 24th 2022:Gunfire Reborn launched in early access on May 22nd, 2020 and went "full release" on Nov. 17th, 2021. All of my previous review still applies, and the game HAS indeed gotten better with time. New characters and new gamemodes followed the full release with new weapons, scrolls, and modifiers to add flavor. The developers have done a good job of keeping their momentum going after a strong start. My only gripe is that they are heavyhanded with nerfs to scrolls and abilities that didn't need changing. Every couple patches something will get changed and you will be scratching your head wondering "why?". I can't answer that question either. The point of the game is to have an awesome power fantasy when you get the right combos of upgrades and items. If that goes away, the game won't be fun. Don't be so quick to nerf things is all I ask. I've heard this game get called "Furry Doom" and "Furry Borderlands" by friends. Those titles are meant to be endearing. And they end up accurately describing Gunfire Reborn. The game's cast of animal hero classes, creature enemies, and polygonal artstyle adds charm to an FPS industry dominated by realistic graphics and "gritty" settings. The game is a roguelike yet plays closer to Doom or Borderlands in the minute to minute gameplay. The upgrade tree allows you to grow stronger with every run, yet the bosses and enemies never feel like pushovers. Gunfire is still in early access and every update improves the game's weapon pool, enemy scaling and has even seen new classes added. Their roadmap looks solid and I expect Gunfire Reborn to only improve with time. If you like roguelikes, FPSes and co-op, you won't be disappointed for $12 USD

_childDocuments_.review: (60 Hours in at time of review)This is an addictive roguelike that I can best describe as a co-op roguelite abilities and gunplay similar to Overwatch, and an artstyle vaguely similar to borderlands. It can be played solo or with friends, but I vastly prefer it in co-op. All of the characters have interesting builds you can do with them, although I prefer turtle boi and the tiger. The mechanics are easy for anyone who has played an FPS or roguelite to pickup. It's an extremely satisfying game, and I don't have many complaints thus far.My complaints (as of V1.0)-* There is no option to see the current damage % or lucky shot % you are doing at any moment. You can manually add all your scrolls and ascensions together but that is tedious* The re-rolling gemini mechanic really sucks.  300 for copper per reroll is just way too much considering the odds for getting both weapons to have a matching gemini.Things I think they should add going forward-* Branching paths in terms of levels. Right now it's a linear 3 (or 4) level game. I feel like adding on more levels as options would give each run some more variety.* More heroes. This one is obvious, but it'd be nice to have a few different options for heros.* Unlockable cosmetics for existing heros. I'd prefer if these could be bought with essense or unlocked via certain achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting roguelike FPS that I highly recommend. The game at is core is very simple.  It makes you run through 3 themed levels with various stages that get shorter per level.  The enemies getting harder as your progress through the levels.  What makes it very fun is the various randomisation that makes it truly roguelike:-The plentiful weapons and their modifiers aka inscriptions-The passive you can find via scrolls-The end stage bonuses (ascensions)-The maps themselves also randomise-The end level bosses are all randomised with 2 variations at the end of the level (except the 3rd stage, 2nd boss WIP)This makes the game almost truly live up the phrase "no 2 runs are ever the same.What makes this game amazing though is truly figuring out the synergy between the weapons and scrolls that you have making some fun Godlike builds in one run.Please note: In the beginning you are extremely under developed for the normal. Until you buy some nodes on the skill tree, you are going not going to get very far on normal.  But when you put in the time you will get stronger overtime where normal is no longer a challenge and you can comfortably move onto higher difficulty.  Do note that at nightmare, your winning becomes a game of chance where it only becomes doable with a good build.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I should mention that I never was a fan of the roguelike/roguelite genre. Quite frankly, I’m not a fan of random elements in the games, with the exception of randomly generated maps and encounters. I genuinely hate when the combat and progression are tied too much to pure luck to make strategizing and thinking ahead almost impossible. But with all that in mind, I’m pleased to say that I really like Gunfire Reborn.7.5/10, will keep it updated as the game develops.Gunfire Reborn kind of came out of nowhere. Some barely known studio, coming out with what is apparently their first title… I have to say, it’s actually rather impressive. It’s also pleasing to see that they haven’t abandoned their project and continue to improve it at a steady pace. For the time being, it doesn’t have much content, but it has a pretty nice gameplay formula and a solid foundation for improvement. If things go smoothly and we’ll be getting new playable characters, new weapons and scrolls, new locations and enemies and most importantly - more context to what’s going on, as well as proper endgame, then this game has some bright future in front of it. Fingers crossed and best of luck to the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like; tower of guns, mother gunship, enter the gungeon, risk of rain 2, neon abyss, synthetik, paladins, or spell break you might like this game. A nice mix of cute characters, cool guns, and great replay-ability.  --The Crown Prince (Starting Character): His smoke bomb is a bit underwhelming but his E ability is amazing. He is a great middle of the road starter character with a lot of potential for great team comps.  --Ao Bai (Goodest Boi): His grenade like The Crown Prince's isn't great, however having the dual wield abilities has an crazy dps and status effect potential. (Laser Gloves + Lightning gloves = almost guaranteed confusion and dual infinite range lazer god) I understand having 2 swords would be OP but it would also be fun and challenging.  --Gian Sui (Oogway/TMNT): Legit OP. Having kills right after shield end refills shield and punches refill it while its up and reflect damage while its up and having up to 46 punches and shield charge upgrades make you invincible for an entire fight. Then pair with an upgraded sword and the scroll where if you kill within 7m you gain 1 hp even when not shielded you'll be a force controlling the battlefield.  --Tao (Space Jam Samurai): My personal favorite to play as. Having the abilities where Fatal Bloom, and gun shots spawn the Swords out swords and increases to their stacks and damage the dps potential scales up pretty fast.  --Lei Luo (Tai Lung/Raikou): His lightning abilities make his status effect synergies a powerful asset. If you have The Gemini stat for weapons sharing status, one corrosive, one fire you can fatal current into lightning bolt and stack all the status effects and melt faces.  --Qing Yan (Hawlucha/Jiandiao/Harvey): Bird Man Cometh. Another great character for the every kill in 7m gains you 1 health scroll. Swords, Shotguns, and dynamic entry is a good combo. His higher starting stats are good because his need to be in the face of the enemy makes his runs quite hard in the later waves/difficulties. Its still gratifying to hit that high jump kick crit. Razor wings damage leaves something to be desired but a nice kick in the face always raises my spirits ----Non character things: -I like the art style and how even with the enemy and level design change so drastically and still manage to fit the theme.-The living guns (lizard/dragon) are both funny and useful for the rolls they fill. -The bosses transforming after beating the, so many times/higher difficulty adds both difficulty and replay-ability, it's nice to not have to fight the same boss after the same levels every time.-I use Rogue-like/Rogue-lite games as time killers but even after a short amount of time this has become one of my favorite of the genre.-Great as time killer, fps warm up, or a fun with friends fps game for when you don't want to play a genre that isn't a battle royale, a 5v5 comp, or cod/halo mp-THE BEST PART OF THE ENTIRE MP EXPERIENCE IS THAT EVERY ONE GETS THEIR OWN LOOT AND IF ONE PERSON GETS A DROP EVERYONE GETS A DROP AND THEIR IS NO LOOT GOBLINNING. I CANT STRESS ENOUGH HOW IMPORTANT THIS IS TO BOTH MORALE AND FUN OF THIS GENRE.----Cons: -Even though the bosses can change running through the levels in the same order every time can get a little monotonous, but that is how games of this genre have always been. -Some Characters don't seem to scale into the later floors as well as others making a team comp hard when a lot of people want to play as the same characters. (Though i'd rather have the worse characters buffed then the good ones nerfed) ------RATING : 10/11 Would play again, my new favorite rogue-lite/rogue-like 10/11 because nothing is perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool gameAfter 100 hours I have now decided to write my probably first review here on Steam.About the game:This game is a shooter that has been very satisfying to me over the days I've been playing it. It is one of the few shooter games that I have actively played and enjoyed (I'm more of an RPG guy).You have a certain game system that is repetitive.You always come to some kind of oasis where you can go to the first area. There you kill monsters to get copper coins, soul essences and sometimes scrolls. From time to time there are also hiding places, which you can open with a shot. There you have certain challenges, which you have to overcome to get to a box, which can contain either three, or one magic scroll. (Tip: When you are at the stones in the first area, there are two chests. When you find the first one, look for a flamethrower. There near it is the second one). Also, in some areas you will find chests, which you can open and choose something, but you don't have to. This can be for example money for life <-> life for money, a cursed scroll for a magic scroll (Only select if you have Evil-Banishing-Talisman in your possession!). You have to overcome 4 levels to get to the boss. This one is very hard at first and almost impossible to do, unless you are familiar with such games and damn good at it. Once you have mastered a level, you have a crate available which holds a skill point for that round. You can always choose between three.When you die, you have the possibility to revive with soul essences (which I would NOT recommend at the beginning). But more about that later.After that you enter the second area and the process starts all over again. There are other monsters, other challenges and other bosses. The second area is a desert and the third is a, I would almost say beach/water area.Once you've done that in normal mode, you unlock elite mode, where the monsters have more life and some attributes. For example, they are resistant to an element, or are more agile, have more tankyniss or are more robust.If you die before that, you can distribute your soul essences at a talent tree. At the beginning they cost quite little, but with time they become more and more expensive. Weapons/ScrollsYou have a certain number of weapons and scrolls at the beginning, which you can choose when you complete a challenge or defeat a boss. Scrolls can be of the rarity "normal" "rare" and "legendary". By completing challenges, which are automatically integrated into the game, you unlock more and more weapons and scrolls and thus have more and more choice. As you play longer, you become more familiar with them and realize which weapons are good and which are not so good. (Snipers are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ OP in this game) ... and the Weapon Collision. Online Co-op ModeYou can enter the online mode at lvl 10 by clicking "matching" in your lobby and then clicking start.In the online mode you can start your adventure with other players. Search times always vary by time and by game mode. On nightmare you have to wait longer than on normal as example. You can be lucky enough to get into a lobby that carrien you, so you can get a high number of soul essences and you can learn a little about gaming. It's great fun when you don't have dumbed down players on your team that die permanently. :DCharacters:Each character has his own abilities that make him. In addition to that, they have their own little talent tree, which is specially designed for them.In the beginning you play with a cat, which can throw smoke bombs and drop an energy ball.At lvl 25 you unlock a dog, which can carry normal grenades and as its special ability both weapons at the same time for a short time. (This does not include snipers or bows).At lvl 40(?) you unlock a bird, which is very strong as a tank and frontliner. He has the ability to jump on his opponents with his leg and beat them up with his wings.On lvl 55 you unlock a tiger, which is the child among the snipers, but also quite complicated in terms of skill distribution, if you have never played him. Once you understand the character though, you can make up to 200k+ dmg per shot with certain scrolls and passives. (I can send you a guide on this if you're interested).It's a really well done early-access game and I'm excited to see what expansions are to come!

_childDocuments_.review: Interested in Gunfire Reborn? Well let me just ask you something. Have you played any of the Borderlands games and enjoyed them? If you're answer was yes then my next question is why haven't you bought this game already?!Rogue-lite is one of my favourite genres and Gunfire really scratches that itch that keeps me coming back for more. It perfects the formula for the FPS rogue-lite in the simplest way possible. It may not be as complex as other games like it, but it doesn't need to be. It's just fun to play, end of story. The enjoyment of the game skyrockets when playing with some friends. Each friend can choose from a nice roster of characters who each have their own special play-styles and abilities. Some characters don't even need the main aspect of the game, which is guns, to absolutely destroy the enemies. So if you get tired of pumping lead into enemies, then you can get your hands dirty with the right character builds. The game also features a nice selection of guns which can suit each play-style. Each gun can also get some juicy inscriptions that drastically increases their damage. Alongside the guns are occult scrolls that can be a big boost in power or a curse upon a run. This is where most of your synergies comes from and can be thought of something like items from another one of my favourite games, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth. After completing a level or defeating a mini-boss, a player is rewarded with a golden goblet. This is where the biggest deciding factor comes in for how you want to play a run. The skills you choose for your character dictates what ability you will focus on. For example, when using the crown prince, you can either choose to only use his smoke grenades to evaporate the enemies or you can go all in on his freeze orb to stun lock them forever. This is what gives the game its replayability. Its not just the scrolls or weapons that you can get each run, but also the character that you use and the skills you receive from each golden goblet.At the end of each run you get to use a currency called soul essence to permanently upgrade aspects of the game that will make the next attempt easier. So there is almost always a sense of progression even if you fail a run. Even if you complete every upgrade possible, you can still use soul essence on harder difficulties like reincarnation to make runs easier. Soul essence's soul purpose is to make the game easier as you also use it for a single revive when downed. There is a good reason why you would want to make the game easier with soul essence, because enemies will dominate you in mere seconds. Make no mistake, this game is challenging. You might fail a lot in your first couple of attempts because you have no upgrades to help you. The more you play, the easier it gets because of your experience and the upgrades you get for your characters. Speaking of difficulty, the enemies and bosses. There are a lot of enemies and unique designs for each stage. Something as innocent looking as a paper lantern will strike fear into you when confronted by a group of them in-game. The bosses are all well designed and a good challenge to end of each stage (if you don't one-shot them of course). I would love to see more bosses added to each stage to really keep runs interesting. To summarise the game I would say it is the most fun that you can have while playing as a dog with two fire-breathing dragons as weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game. It's a roguelike that borrows all the best parts of borderlands and there are a variety of characters that all feel very different and all are very fun to play! As I've gotten better at the game I have been playing the higher difficulties, but sometimes it just feels way too cheap. Some areas are way too big to solo and projectiles can be hard to see and dodge effectively. Apparently they have a hit rate, but regardless, It doesn't feel fun to turn a corner and get hit by a crossbow bolt that instadowns. That being said, the scaling on higher difficulties in multiplayer is also insane. On a solo run, the Golem will have 400-600k hp. Whenever I play with friends, the Golem has upwards of 1 million Hp, for example. Despite these things, the game is extremely fun. It can feel awesome when you get a crazy build going on and you're just running through all the rooms like it's nothing. I also like the randomness of builds and it makes it feel different every run, even if you play the same character over and over. I would recommend picking this game up at full price, but to hold out on DLCs till they're on sale. The base game characters are all very strong on their own.

_childDocuments_.review: For what little there is, this game is great.  It already has a healthy mix of characters, scrolls that augment your play style as you collect them, a clean art direction, and solid movement.  For this being a Rogue-lite FPS, it shines for what there is.  There are currently three characters and each one has its own little gimmick to how they play, but it's still completely viable to just decide to run up to an enemy with a fully auto-shotgun and blast stuff in the face.Movement I want to draw attention to.  In an FPS game, good movement feedback is a cornerstone and messing that up can cause everything else to not matter.  That's not the case here.  It feels good to just run around, jump, dash, and dodge into or out of danger.  As a note, depending on the gun your currently carrying, move speed is effected.  The old "Run with a knife like Counter-Strike" philosophy works here.  Thankfully, you're given a emergency backup weapon in your third slot you can't drop called the Foundry and you will always move at max speed when its drawn.  Remember that for the platforming challenges."Platforming in an FPS game!?"  Don't worry.  The platforms you need to land on are (almost always) fairly big and square shaped.  It's actually really hard to miss your jumps and these challenges only exist in side rooms you explore for additional loot.  Also, no enemies spawn in these platforming rooms.  (Except for one, but it's literally a single enemy and he's in your way as you progress, so no fear.)The roadmap is up and we are expecting several new stages, bosses, and even more characters, bringing the total up to around 6-7 characters.  That's impressive!  Also the game has already sold over 1M copies, which is a huge amount of money for such a small company that is very responsive to customer feedback and bug reports.  Support the devs.  This thing is good and I hope to see it grow to fruition.

_childDocuments_.review: A great roguelite that has a lot of variance on runs by using character-specific abilities as well as a lot of cool modifiers for weapons, movement, defenses and said abilities. There are some incremental upgrade that are character-wide, but these will barely do a difference compared to how crazy some of those perks/modifiers you can find during a run will do.Best of all is that if you're playing multiplayer, you can trade these scrolls with your coop members to maximize your build even further into stupid numbers territory. A lot of replay value and the guns do feel good if you make a build to make them shine, otherwise they'll be an accessory to very powerful abilities.I really recommend this game, even if you'll see the same maps over and over, you won't tackle them the exact same way in between every runs, which drives away the repetition and boredom factors. And if you get bored - try another character, or focus another aspect of your characters. The game is forgiving, but sometimes you'll get a bad run, and that's fair enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't even surpassed the second "area" but I can still confidently say that this is one of, if not the best fps games I've played.  Highlights:+ The game mechanics feel remarkably fresh.  It is the "Slay the Spire" of FPS rogue likes because it is the first FPS    rogue like that completely nails the best of both genres, much like STS did for its genres respectively.  You probably    haven't played a game quite like Gunfire Reborn!+ When you are on one of those overpowered runs that feel like you entered cheat codes, you're having a blast.  When    the RNG gods frown on you and you're somewhat lacking in power, you're having a blast.  I honestly don't know if its    possible to rage quit this game because if you die, its usually your fault. + It will probably run well on your low end PC.  I am constantly looking for games that my computer can handle, and this    one runs between 100 and 120 fps on my Dell XPS 15 9500.  + Movement, skills, and gunplay feel incredibly smooth.Needs Improvement (This is mostly for the developers to see, please don't let these discourage you from purchasing this amazing game!): + The soundtrack is forgettable.  I would love to see the devs implement a new soundtrack that is as catchy as the    gameplay is because this game truly deserves that.  When I think of standout soundtracks, I think of games like Skyrim,    Loop Hero, and the Super Smash Bros Ultimate menu screen.  Those sounds are forever stuck between my ears.     Definitely don't think Gunfire Reborn needs a vibe like the games listed above, but my point remains:    I need to remember the music of Gunfire Reborn years after I've played it for it to truly be a 10/10 game.  As of right now,    I do not remember the music even minutes after exiting to desktop.Yep, that's it!  That's the only major critique I have for Gunfire Reborn.  Happy gamin' everyone.
