_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is another rouge-like shooter that has done a fantastic job of making the game as addictive as possible.For most games, how I define the greatness for the most part is based on how re-playable the experience can be. And Gunfire knocks it right out of the park with that one.Although Gunfire is still in Early Access with many changes and additions planned to make their way in, it already is super solid for how it is currently. It's enough for me to say that if it didn't have (EA) attached to it at the moment, I would definitely believe that it was a ready game.Gunfire Reborn is just like Risk of Rain and Binding of Isaac and all other rogue likes in which when you die you start fresh, but it does a good job by still making you feel like you're progressing even though it's a restart for every session.The game implements a very thorough Talent tree in which the profits you make in your runs can be easily converted to the skills you wish to enhance, to better off your upcoming runs in the future. With this, each skill you upgrade is also represented as your player level. The more skills you unlock, the higher level your account becomes. And when it doesn't come to replay ability, Leveling system is immediately the right hand man for what gets me hooked on a game.The weapons in Gunfire are pretty self explanatory, they're guns. But for those who wish to use other means of attacking they put that into account too and also added cool gadgets and gizmos to use instead. Such as, a laser glove, a fire dragon, a whole lizard, and even primary skills that each unique character has catered to them.Thankfully if one character doesn't suit your taste with their play style, they also have 2 additional ones currently that spice things up a little.The list of characters and their specialties:The Crown Prince (Cat): Elemental damage, Smoke Bomb usage/buffs, Energy Orb Primary skill.Ao Bai (Dog): Gun improvements, overall sustainability perks, grenade buffs, Akimbo Gun Primary SkillQing Yan (Bird): Overall sustainability perks, winged attacks, Claw Leap Primary skill.Although there may seem very few in character numbers, their uniqueness makes the game play experience completely different from each other.The game also uses a very subtle elemental system of three elements: Corrosion, Fire, and Lightning. With these three elements, based on who you're fighting they may have an element that consists of their being. By figuring out which element counters which, you can choose the appropriate weapon to gain bonus damage on said enemy. As well as dealing less damage if the enemy element is countering your current weapon.A complete run of a Gunfire session takes about an average of forty minutes minimum, and up to an hour or longer afterwards. Don't expect to win a session on your first try, but with the help of unlocking items and learning each enemy's combat styles, you'll be soaring through the rooms in no time.I've had my eye on this game for quite some time and finally got the urge to complete the purchase and i'm shocked as to how much time it has already sucked from my day to day life. The matches are played so differently every time that once i'm finished I hop right back in and see what new situations I am put against to squeeze my way out of this time.If you are a fan of Risk of Rain and Binding of Isaac's play style, as well as most rouge genre games, Gunfire Reborn is surely up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun in co-op. Each weapon is handcrafted – most of them have unique mechanics and slick animations. You can create builds out of weapons/scrolls/ascensions found along the way, and it feels rewarding to see them work together in synergy. The characters are smol and cute, each having their own set of abilities and progression.There's a good variety of enemies; most elite enemies and boss fights are fun. The vault levels with parkour/traps are also nice. RNG can be slightly irritating at times, but the game allows you to rely on your skills alone until you obtain better loot. You can also ask other players to trade weapons/scrolls – a scroll that's near-useless for their build might make a difference in your paws!If you play a lot, the environments may start to feel a bit repetitive, but their design is really nice, and you may find yourself focusing more on the fun gunplay and unique rewards, than being troubled by repetition.Works well on Linux (via Proton)

_childDocuments_.review: i echo the words of most others: Replayability of Risk of Rain 2, mechanics of Borderlands, and gameplay of Doom. that isnt an exaggeration. Rogue-lite aspects are finding weapons (which are all creative as hell. for example, wrist mounted tiny dragon that acts like a flamethrower,) upgrades to your core abilities and elemental damage at the end of every arena, and scrolls that buff you and occasionally have downsides. Its a rogue-LITE because there is permanent progression in the from of talents. Stuff like ammo capacity, health/shields, and some special ones like getting a free weapon at the start of each run or the ability to shoot purple walls to unlock secret dungeons.The Borderlands in it comes with the elemental damage mechanic, general gunplay, weapon stats, and the enemy health. There are multiple elements that work with one another for beeg damage (for example, corrosive damage + fire damage = explosion.) all weapons drop with random stats and modifiers, and once you buy the upgrade for it, intrinsic perks (for example, pistols can drop with a 25% chance to instakill on headshot.) Each enemy is unique, and have the health pool of an enemy from BL (hard to explain, but thats what it feels like.) There are bosses at the end of each level which require 4 stages to get through, and in all of its glowy fashion, they die in a lootsplosion.The Doom comes from the arena to arena combat, with a heavy emphasis on staying mobile and dodging whenever you can. A bit unforgiving at times, but wheres the fun in easiness?TLDR; this game is the bastard child of some of the genre respective greats of our time and is incredible. plus, early access, meaning more content!

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I suggested waiting to buy this game. After taking a break from this I came back to play it after the devs had released a few updates.While I still don't think this game is complete, I can say that you will still get your money's worth.The Good:Guns: Guns still feel amazing to use. In fact they actually feel better since I first played. They're satisfying and always fun to experiment with.Combat: There's always a lot going on. You really need to be aware of your surroundings and kill quickly. Previously I had an issue with needing to hide too much. While that still happens on occasion you'll be engaged in high pace action most of the time.Bosses: Bosses don't seem to have changed much since I first played, but I was already fond of them as they were. Intense battles against unique and interesting enemies. What's not to love?Characters: Something I didn't touch on before were the characters. With the addition of a third character I feel the need to talk about them. Each character is unique and plays a different way. They won't all stick with every person, but I'm sure you'll find at least one you like. While I would like to see more in the future I can easily live with the 3 the devs gave us.Loot: Finding loot is always exciting. Whether it be a gun, a scroll or another upgrade point. The best part is that when playing in co-op, loot is client side. That means no loot ninjas, but you have the option to drop loot for teammates if you desire. So it's safe to say the loot system is very player friendly.Perks: One of my biggest issues was that there didn't feel like there was enough control over what perks you got with each character during a run. This hasn't changed, but they did change the perks themselves to be better. Now it doesn't feel like you're getting screwed over when you don't get what you wanted.The Bad:Content: Pretty much my biggest issue right now is that there isn't enough content. You have 3 areas and each area has 1 boss at the end. You may get some secret areas with mini boss like enemies, but I don't really count those being they're always random. Being this is in early access I'm assuming this will change with time. I'd love to see more areas and if possible maybe some branching paths to keep runs unique.Overall this game is a lot of fun and I now feel like I can say it's worth buying. It may not be done, but with how much progress the devs have made since my initial review of this game I have high hopes for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definetly fun and if it had less positive buzz around it I would give a thumbs up, but it has disappointed me in a single crucial way (and a few other smaller ones) that forced me to downshift my excitement quite a bit so I just want to warn you on this issue. For the record, I played solo.Despite all its strengths - mainly the fun gunplay and core gameplay loop - the enemy design, especially the boss design, suffers from extreme swingyness. What I mean is that on all my runs so far, I will feel godlike invincible and have a lot of fun with a build that seems like it's going in a good direction, then all of a sudden just get instantly killed. This happened once or twice with a wave of smaller enemies where a lot of damage quickly piled up, but it's usually manageable. Their attacks are for the most part well telegraphed and while they can catch you off-guard and deal a lot of damage quickly, so far I've usually been able to take cover and turn the fight around. Not so for elites and bosses (except the first who is an absolute pushover). These mothertruckers will 100 to 0 you instantly with some of the worst telegraphed attacks I've ever seen in an FPS. AoEs that spawn behind you, projectiles where it's not clear whether you're supposed to dodge or shoot them, or just a laser that oneshots you if you stand in the wrong direction. Fun stuff.I don't think I'm terrible at the game. I make mistakes, sure, I'm still learning, but in my 5-6 runs so far I've never died on the first stage and in the last 3 always got to the 3rd stage. It feels all the more defeating when my amazing run suddenly comes to a halt. Doubly so because the new weapons and items you unlock via in-game achievements drop *instantly*, which is a really cool system except that it means your first few runs will be supercharged with additional item drops that then get wasted because of attacks or mechanics you couldn't possibly anticipate. The worst offender was probably when an elite in the third stage spawned a variant of a familiar enemy that - unlike the regular version - explodes on death, killing me instantly in what I thought would be the run to get me to stage four.I don't know if that's what's actually going on, but it seems like bosses are designed in a way that brute-forces the usual roguelite-flow, where you're not expected to win on your first few runs and are instead supposed to get more experience and in-game upgrades first to gradually progress each time. Which isn't very rewarding when it feels like a binary learning experience of "now that I have died once to this and know what it does, it will be 90% less deadly next time". Either that or it's designed primarily with multiplayer in mind, neither of which make the problem better.Maybe I'm doing something wrong, but I usually don't have the option for a more defensive build either, at least not with the standard starting character. Perhaps he's particularly squishy, which would then also be a terrible idea not to start off with a well-rounded character that gives you several options of building him. Come to think of it, build variety in terms of level-up abilities is pretty minimal. I can either upgrade grenades, my other activated ability, or elemental damage and...that's it. Nothing really exciting, just percentages and a few passive abilities. And the same ones each run. Similar thing goes for the items and weapons, but at least there you're continually unlocking new ones, so it should get better with time.Overall it's fun and I see the potential to love it later, but it has a TERRIBLE starting experience which seems like it could be roughly adressed pretty easily by tweaking a few numbers. As it stands, every death is not a motivation to try again and improve, but feels like a cheap trap that makes me want to close the game.

Dispatch beasts from ancient Chinese mythology (and, on occasion, completely normal fiddler crabs) with electric submachine guns, wood-furnitured gatling guns, rapid-fire mechanical crossbows, sci-fi death rays, auto shotties with drum magazines, and semi-auto sniper rifles. _childDocuments_.review: This game is way too fun for the price. Here's a breakdown of what it plays like:It's a simple FPS rogue-lite; you progress through 3 different zones, each zone broken down into several levels, and the last level is a boss fight. If you die, you get to spend some points to improve yourself before trying again. If you win, you get to spend more points. Currently, you can play as one of two characters, each with a distinctly different playstyle. It can be played in coop, and it's very synergetic and fun (more on that below).Each level has potential of having optional side areas that can be a simple fight, a mini-boss encounter, an obstacle course, or a platforming puzzle. These are always worth doing, as they will give you extra loot. There's also an NPC traders and crafters where you can buy and improve equipment.You fight using weapons, skills, and grenades. All attacks can be enhanced with elemental damage - elemental damage can also proc, and combining procs will result in satisfying effects. Progression during a run consists of scrolls, and ascensions. You start each run without any of either.- Scrolls are found around the level in a variety of ways - killing certain enemies, looting certain chests, buying them from npc peddlers, etc. The effects can be positive (+40% run speed after dash), sacrificial (double shield, but health is capped at 1), or cursed (-50% accuracy). Most of the positive and sacrificial scrolls can be dropped, while cursed scrolls can't, but you will never "accidentally" get a cursed scroll - you get it through conscious decisions. - Ascensions are improvements to your skills, grenades, or elemental damage. They are earned at the end of each level, or very rarely during an optional side area called a vault. You choose one of 3 upgrades picked at random from the character's pool of 18 upgrades, and each upgrade is tiered.With all of the above mechanics combined, you can make some very interesting builds, such as:- heavy elemental damage- infinite-ammo bullet hose, - long-range sniper- close-range tank- high-crit damage dealer- etcHowever, given the RNG nature of rogue-lite games, you're forced to experiment with new builds in each run, which can yield some very surprising results.Coop is very satisfying. The enemies are tougher, and more abundant. Loot is instanced, so you won't fight with your partner over weapons and scrolls. Also, each person's instance has randomized loot, so if an enemy drops a weapon, one person might see an smg, while the other might see a rocket launcher (same goes with scrolls), so it's possible to help each other work on certain builds by communicating.Overall, the only thing i find lacking is content - I want more of this game. However, the amount that I got from the current price tag ($12 CAD) is already amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game at a great price.  As you rack up kills on different enemies you automatically unlock new weapons and scrolls/artifacts, ensuring the game stays fresh with variety.  When you die you can invest in a variety of talents, like more ammo/grenades, free advanced gun when starting, extra health/shield, increase chance of specialized weapon signature, etc.  Making the game quite addictive wanting to keep improving those stats and getting further along in the adventure with more advanced and varied weaponry.On the downside, where I think the low price offsets any temporary negatives (game is in EA), the shooting doesn't feel as good as many other shooters.  Some of the controls and key mappings seem a bit rough (at least for k/m, I'm not going to play a shooter with a controller) but on the plus side they are remappable which I recommend you consider doing.  Also multiplayer matches, at least late at night, can be difficult to find, especially if impatient.  I've only played solo so far and don't feel you have to play multiplayer to enjoy the game.  There are several enemy types and once you beat a boss the next zone is completely different looking.  The bosses are a real challenge, something to work those talents toward.  Game does a great job of keeping things interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is sort of like Risk of Rain 2, but full of anthropomorphic furry characters with a variety of fun skills and abilities and played from a first-person perspective.The low poly cel-shaded art style is cutesy and easy on the eyes for extended play. Enemy variety is decent, but not so bloated as to become impossible to follow what is happening at any given moment. Generally, they follow fundamental design choices like so:Bulkier enemies that will try to stomp or charge you will always be large and obvious, whereas long-range options and 'marksmen' sort of opponents will be slender, but excessively tall in comparison to the player in an attempt to signify their purpose and help them stand out from the background. These consistent values, strictly adhered to, in visual language help to elevate the typical cover-dodging firefight game that Gunfire could've been into something greater.While the game, and some aspects in it, can be a little janky, it has only improved over the course of its lifespan; it also performs very well on even some lower end machines.The guns, which is an inadequate word to describe some of the game's weapons (kunai, some kind of bone cannon, just an actual lizard you slap to reload), are varied and fun to use but may take some getting used to. Some are clear favourites for me, namely Hexagon and especially the Wheel Saw; DLC is a factor in the guns that may drop (Hexagon is limited to owners of the Visitors of the Spirit Realm DLC, for example).Physically standing behind cover and peeping enemies is a valid strategy, also including the use of a dash as a roguelike staple feels good despite the game being first-person, and the game firmly encourages and allows players to take it at their own pace outside of immediate danger.Despite my time with the game being primarily singleplayer, I have found the co-op multiplayer runs well and is just as fun. I particularly enjoy the Sun Wukong style character introduced in one of the game's DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down one of the greatest Rogue-lites I've ever played, the game has no right to be this good considering how low quality it looks in terms of graphics, SFX and animations, but that is honestly to it's benefit because this game can literally be run on a potato and on sale you can get the game and all the additional characters for a lot less than what a sub par AAA or even AA Multiplayer game will cost ya (tho this game can also be played in Single Player just fine...)So the game is basically a chinese Furry FPS Borderlands Roguelite with 12 playable characters (6 unlockable with game progress, 6 that are DLC only). The reason I compare it to Borderlands is because it uses the exact same elemental system (Burning, Corrosive, Shock) and the playable hero characters all have a Primary (ultimate) ability with a Cooldown, and a Secondary ability, usually requiring resource management along with your primary, secondary and starting gun (which has infinite ammo and scales along with the area).The whole point is to make it through a gauntlet of arenas filled with traps and enemies that are specifically themed around each stage (there being 5 total with about 5 or so rooms each including bonus rooms called Vaults and a final boss room). As you beat each Stage, you will unlock Ascensions which basically power up your character further and allow you to build around a specific play style that the tree supports. once you get through all 5 Stages and defeat the bosses in each, the run ends and you can begin another run again, which, depending on the difficulty, can take an average of an hour and a half to beat... There is a permanent Talent tree which you can eventually unlock in it's entirety, along with an individual hero tree for each character consisting of about 5 passives, and even after you've unlocked everything (which doesn't take anywhere near as long as it used to compared to when the game was first in Early Access...), you will still have plenty of things to use your soul essence on, as this game has a tremendous amount of replay value, whether you play Solo or with a few other friends...The only major criticism I have to give is honestly that the netcode could be better... if you're playing with people who are on the other side of the planet, and the ping is above 150 ms, you're gonna really feel it bad... You'll experience blank shots, rewinding, teleporting and even just randomly dying... but outside of that, this game is phenomenal and I honestly cannot recommend it enough! I rate it a solid 9/10 +Addicting AF gameplay loop (seriously, this game is crack... don't play it late at night or you may end up finding it is suddenly 6AM and you got work in a few hours)+Many weapons, to choose from and many characters to play as, all with their respective strengths, weaknesses and specialized play styles+Fairly easy to pick up and play+Affordable price (DLC included, especially on a sale)+Great replayability, including more game modes with additional options as you unlock harder difficulties+Cute Characters+Can run easily on most lower end PCs (even works really well on a Steam Deck)+is still being updated with content as of this review-Bad Netcode-Graphics don't look the best, SFX and animation are quite wonky and cheap looking-Some may find it repetitive and dull early on-Average game length requires commitment (tho you can save and quit at the beginning of each stage in case you gotta take a break, tho this is for SP only)

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is a roguelite first person shooter that borrows the best elements of borderlands (various unique weapons, action + skill tree mechanics, elemental affinities minus the infamous Slag) while completely forgoing the grind and instead lets you in on the action immediately. No quests, no map travel, and no inventory hassle; it's all grab, go, and shoot. You can also play with up to three friends/randoms or just play solo.The mechanics are tight and the gunplay is satisfying. Most of the weapons are uniquely fun and the current selection of characters are great to play, each offering multiple different playstyles depending on build. This is also the only roguelite in recent years that have me still hooked and playing long after a first win.Perhaps my only gripe is the balancing.The first 2 bosses are great, albeit on the easy side, with clear tells and enough leeway to dodge/react while on the other hand, the 3rd boss has instakills that gives you a much smaller time to react all the while throwing mechanics at you at a pace that felt disproportionate to the overall experience. Having finished a couple of runs in elite and trying for nightmare clear, not all weapons/ascensions are viable and some are just straight up bad, at least in my experience playing only on solo. Though I do think this is just the side effect of ARPGs/looter shooters with multiple difficulties in general.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good and worth the price. A roguelite arena shooter with scaling co-op, you basically go from one arena filled with enemies to the next, picking up magical scrolls and chalices to perfect your build and working on crafting the ultimate weapon. There are six playable characters, each with a unique playstyle distinct from the others, so there should be something for everyone to enjoy, as well as a lot of replayability. The combat is very Doom-esque - frantic and fast, not moving could mean the end of your run very suddenly - and there are 11 difficulty levels to scale with your ascension of the skill tree and climbing skill with the game, with the later difficulties adding new mechanics that spice up the gameplay a lot, making the higher difficulties quite a bit more fun once you get there. There are lots of weapons, scrolls, and achievements to unlock, as well as the six characters and a pretty good-sized skill tree, so you'll be busy with this one for a while. Art style is very nice as well, reminds me of Borderlands, and the characters make funny sounds. The developers have been putting out consistent updates for about a year already, adding new content and quickly fixing bugs and balancing the game. Overall, I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone who likes roguelites and first-person arena shooters, or anyone who is looking for a fun co-op game to play with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what I wish Borderlands was - it's like all the best parts of Borderlands' gunplay and character building, but without the grind and the artificial difficulty walls. I played co-op with a friend abroad, and even at about 160+ ping, I was sniping enemies and didn't feel like there was any noticeable lag at all. It is p2p though, so it'll be dependent on both people having decent internet connections.

_childDocuments_.review: It's straight up just far too easy to die. Guns that require close range to be effective are rendered moot by high damaging enemies. Even with a ton of upgrades, you can have an enemy spawn in front of you and two shot you before you can react.And the reward for successive runs is to do the exact same thing again. Dungeon variety is very limited, with runs feeling the same every single time. There's not enough difference between runs, with the random upgrades not really affecting your playstyle much at all. Rather, they seem to only enhance your abilities slightly without changing how you play that run, which is wholly determined by your guns. As for gun choice, see above.I haven't found anybody doing multiplayer matchmaking, so solo seems to be the only way to play without friends also buying the game. Therefore, you end up getting one self revive, and then it's over if you make a small mistake again.The guns all actually feel great, but the fact that you die so quickly with few healing options makes choice feel fairly limited.

_childDocuments_.review: As I write this, Gunfire Reborn is in early access. Don’t let that fool you. This is fully playable game that is receiving routine updates to add more content.I’m a casual gamer who enjoys playing games with my two daughters on our LAN and when I can arrange time, with my friends online. I wouldn’t call myself anything more than an average skilled player. If you are similar, then normal difficulty will at first be a challenge. The bosses will seem undefeatable. They aren’t. Keep learning, leveling, and fighting. The win is worth it. If you’re a veteran player of rougelike or FPS games, normal may just be a walkthrough for you. Never fear though. There are also elite and nightmare difficulties that can be unlocked by beating the previous difficulty. You’ll begin the game as a “mysterious visitor from the Spirit Realm” who also happens to be a cat that looks a lot like Puss in Boots. The mystery cat has no name, but is known as the Crown Prince. Why are you here? Crown Prince of what? Cat from the Spirit Realm? And most important, why are you raiding this ancient Chinese tomb? None of that is important right now. Just load your trusty Foundry revolver and get in there. The skill system is set up so that you earn soul essence throughout each game. You can use the earned soul essence once per game to revive yourself or, after your demise, to build skills/perks on a fairly standard skill tree system. As you improve your tree, the game becomes easier to play and you will get better and better at blasting your way through levels. I recommend that you accept the defeat and simply upgrade your skills. After all, you can just play again and you’ll have more perks when doing it. Along with the perks, as you gain soul essence, you’ll also unlock new playable characters. Currently there are four additional unlocks as I write this, a dual wielding dog adventurer Ao Bai, a martial artist bird Qing Yan, a lightning and thunder controlling tiger Lei Luo, and the most recent addition a sword master rabbit Tao. Each has different abilities and each requires a slightly different play style. And most important, each is a whole lot of fun to learn and play.You’ll also gain coins while “exploring.” You can use these with a randomly placed peddler and craftsmen at various points in the game. Why are these two standing in a combat zone selling goods and services? Why are the bad guys not hurting them? They’re clearly selling to both sides, right? An adventurer does have to get his or her magic buns and weapons upgrades somewhere though and coins don’t save between games, so take advantage of the deals they offer.Maps are generated with each new game. You’ll see the same rooms and areas frequently, just connected differently and with item locations moved around. With all the assorted enemies trying to stop you from claiming your rightful chest of loot you really will not have time to take in the view or get those Insta pics anyway. Focus on the targets and move.Controls are cake to learn, straightforward WASD game with a few extra buttons for options. Music is fitting and sound effects are good with some being a little amusing (in a good way). Graphics are excellent in my opinion. I’ve played this single player and with two and three players. All playthroughs have been equally enjoyable with only a single game crash so far (ok, the first time I met the second boss, Ichthyosaurus, and he roasted me in seconds wasn’t so enjoyable, but I’m over that now).Add all of the above up and you have hours and hours of play possibility with the potential for far more from a development team that is delivering on every promise so far. I am looking forward to seeing what the team builds into the next update. But none of that is important right now. Just click the Add to Cart button and get playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an absolute gem. I'm partial to rogue-likes/lites, and this game has that "something special" that just begs you to do one more run.The gameplay is what really sets it apart from other rogue-lite FPS games like Ziggurat and Immortal Redneck. It plays smooth and the elemental effects will be familiar to Borderlands players, but there lies a deeper element of status effects by combining elements that you have to find out about yourself. The weapons, while seeming like there aren't enough to allow true variety, actually have a huge distribution of effectiveness based on their "inscriptions" - stat bonuses and effects that are randomized on the item card when it's generated.Man, I could go on and on about how great this game is, and I haven't even touched on things like your Ascension buffs or Talents yet. At $11.99 USD FULL PRICE, this game is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is tons of fun. But it's got a fatal flaw that the devs completely ignore.It's a 2+ hour long game where anyone who disconnects/game-crashes/etc has no ability to reconnect, and the player slot cannot be filled. There is a short (60sec IIRC) lag grace period before a player is removed from the game, which is a very poor attempt to address the issue, since it only works for short lag spikes (and even then it is iffy if it works)In my experience most multiplayer games have had this happen to at least one player. Usually it cripples the run, and definitely kills the fun when you lose a friend.Search the forums, you'll see it frequently requested and never addressed. Some of the community even tries to pretend it will be bad for the game somehow if this is fixed. I won't recommend the game unless it's added. If it were here, the game is extremely fun, and an easy recommend for co-op fun, but it's just an exercise in "how can technical issues ruin a night".

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is a very satisfying looter-shooter roguelike with great multiplayer and smooth gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Man. I really wanted to enjoy this game more than I did. I played it almost religiously, as I often do with new rogue-likes, but this one has yet to pull me back. Especially because I feel like it's now just been done better with roboquest. Both games have: - 3D platforming, but Roboquest has more stages and more environments - Cool guns a la Borderlands, but Roboquest has more variety and (almost) all of them feel satisfying and fun to use (except for you, throwing grenade) - Both have character/class systems: and Roboquest, while having less than GR, still ends up feeling better and cooler to use - Both have a perk system, where you can define a build over the course of a run, but Roboquest lets you have more determinism in which perks you actually get by means of the class system. - Bosses that use both bullethell and run and gun elements, but Roboquest has more of them. Frankly, its kind of shocking that a game that just came out already does what this game does but like, 3x better. This one has just sadly fallen really behind in the grand scheme of things, which is disappointing. I really wanted to like this, but if you are liking what you see here, I recommend looking at Roboquest as well, same price tag, and I'd argue you'll get more playtime out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am torn on this game.  I see a lot of potential for fun, but it feels... mediocre.  Unfortunately,  my multiplayer experience hasn't been the best, and I believe that is where the crux is.  If you are playing with a group of friends or other players around your player/character level, this could be a blast.  Solo play is... meh.  It gets old fast.Gunfire Reborn is going to have a hard time keeping and attracting new players if the multiplayer experience is sullied by impatient players and vast differences in skill levels.  I believe this is why the game play could feel rushed to new players.  Which is odd because your characters movement speed feels sluggish.  Another issue i have is that by the time you get to the point in the game to where your character feels powerful, the game is over.After 5 hours of play I'd have to give Gunfire Reborn a 5/10.  Get it on sale with friends.  There are much better games of this type available.

What's terrible about this game: - Fixating too much on a single build can be punishing at higher difficulty  - Undertaking too much on the successful formula - Game mechanics doesn't really test your reflexes - Negative inscriptions on weapons sometimes can be annoyingGunfire Reborn is a First Person Shooter Rougelite genre, it's not a looter shooter! This game is definitely not for everyone, a lot will like it including me, some will hate it, that being said, it's a great FPS Rougelite. Hopefully they will add more content in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Update Nov 20th, 2021While it's nice to see the game come out of early access and have added additional content such as characters and weapons, my initial gripes are still present a year after the fact. Side-areas are still predictable (with generally one or two Elites variations showing up) as well as being cheap shotted by snipers and bosses regardless of skills or most scrolls in the game. This issue is ESPECIALLY prevalent in the Daily Runs. Since they hiked the price to $20, you're better off putting your money elsewhere.Written as of Sep 8th, 2020Game has potential, however a lot of gameplay feels padded against the player because there's not enough content or randomness in place. Main issue is that there's no real sense of progression with characters. At Level 36, my character feels as brittle as it does at Level 1 and that's with filling out skill points in health and damage trees. By the time you get to the second world, (assuming you can get past the first boss by out-cheap-shotting him) you need to have a lot of damage under your belt which just isn't there unless you get incredibly lucky or synergistic scrolls to show up on your run. Not to mention, main and side rooms get awfully repetitive due to the lack of variance in environments. After about 30 minutes, you'll get the jist of what side rooms have to offer. Again, I wanna like the game but unless there's an overhaul to some core mechanics and randomness, save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: is another title to the ever expanding list of early access roguelites, but it changes enough to be given a shot. It has its own unique charms and features while staying true to the genre, and at an $11.99 price point is honestly a steal! Like most roguelites, the story is more of an afterthought in Gunfire Reborn. While it may not have exciting narratives with fancy character development, it does provide a unique premise with a setting that is often underutilized. The setting is heavily inspired by ancient chinese lore, which provides a sense of mystery and sacredness to all aspects of the game. With typical things you would associate with that setting, such as pandas, tombs, kegs, monks, etc. While it may not be the most unique setting for games as a whole, it is refreshing to experience it with a different light in the roguelite genre.Now we get to the fun part, the gunplay in Gunfire Reborn is top notch for an FPS roguelite. Combat in this game revolves around balancing your movement around the stage with the help of your dash ability, all while firing your three weapon slots, throwing grenades, and using your abilities. It is certainly not a shooter where you are meant to take your time with calculated shots, and more in the run around like sonic with a bazooka realm of gunplay. It really is a fast paced shooter that constantly ramps up the difficulty until you reach your limit.With 39 weapons to choose from, ranging from a default pistol to fire breathing lizards and poison tipped kunai blades there is something for everyone. You get your default pistol permanently, and can pick from any weapon for your last two slots. And then add on 100 different occult scrolls, that can drastically change your build, while also upgrading your characters abilities there is a lot of variety in potential builds. If there is to be one department Gunfire Reborn delivers it has to be the sheer amount of tools at your disposal.A common trend in most roguelites now-a-days is to add a form of progression outside of actually being in a run, and it’s present in Gunfire Reborn. During your run you get a form of currency called soul essence, which is earned at a very slow rate. Then in return you can use these soul essences to upgrade different aspects of your character from health, shields, ammo count, drop modifiers, and much more. This adds a whole new level to the game, as instead of taking it one run at a time it turns into gearing and leveling your character for complete destruction. I will warn you that at the end of a run all your currency earned must be spent to upgrade right away, so if you get 35 soul essence and your health upgrade costs 30 that extra 5 will be lost as it's unable to be spent. This encourages a slow evolution of power until you eventually become an unstoppable force. And each different character has a separate talent tree, so be prepared for lots and lots of runs.The visuals in Gunfire Reborn are not mind blowing by any means, but it does have this indie charm that is so hard to hate. Everything from the characters, the NPCs, guns, even the menu is all heavily stylized. It may not be the most polished game, but it certainly has a case for being one of the most charming games. The art style is simple and easy to follow, but still gives off an incredible atmosphere. The game gives off vibes of coziness and simplicity, and just adds to the addicting nature based on the ease it gives on your eyes.Again the sound design follows the same path its visuals take, simple and satisfying. There might not be 1:1 M16 sound bytes, but instead each gun offers a unique and pleasant pop. Each kill has an audible sound played, which makes chaining large rooms even more pleasing. The abilities have the expected mystical tones when casting, and the creeks and moans of the tomb tie it all together. The OST while not a masterpiece by any means, is adequate to the overall tone of the game. There isn’t much variety in the different songs, so be prepared to listen to the same song on repeat. Gunfire Reborn is not just another roguelite doomed for early access eternity. It is a refreshing take on the genre that offers enough unique differences to be worth a look. With a focus on combat and build variety with a nice progression system, Gunfire Reborn is looking to occupy a lot of your future free time. With a price tag of $11.99 Gunfire Reborn is a hard deal to pass for anyone a fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A fantastic rouge-lite shooter with borderlands like gameplay. Extremely fun with friends or solo. Many of the issues it has can be excused for a game that's only been in early access for a little over 6 months. Support great early access games like this. If you like first person shooters and/or great rouge-lites buy this. PROS:Extremely well optimized with lots of options for graphical settings. I personally use a crappy 7 year old laptop and it runs easily over 60 fps at almost all times.Great servers and easy match making. Great options for controls, with almost all elements re-bindable or with secondary options.Tight and fun gameplay, takes the best elements of borderlands and turns that into a great rouge-lite.You always feel like you're making progress. Every run earns you upgrade points and you never feel like you wasted your time, which is a feeling I often have with other rouge-likes/lites.Each character feels different and upgrades feel great and impactful. Bosses are fun, and with one exception, feel polished and fair. The scroll system greatly impacts how you play and is extremely fun, making each run different. Weapons are fun and creative, from lizards who shoot grenades out their mouths to demonic shotguns you feed ammo. Clear explanations for how to unlock new scrolls and weapons, with most unlocking by just enjoying the game. A full weapon, scroll, enemy, and boss recorder/viewer in the main menu.Each run has it stats and items recorded for you to look back on, which includes the loadouts of each member of your party.An option mid-game to look at the stats and loadouts of you and your party, which includes overall damage done (which I always find fun to learn).The option to drop or share any items you find for your party members to use instead.A great well thought out "hard mode" that unlocks after beating the final boss. This adds both traps and special enemies, making it feel fresh and exciting. CONS:The amount of time it takes to unlock new characters is far too long imho. You unlock the dog at 30 and the bird at 40, which can be a grind to get to and then feels way too quick. I understand there are only 3 characters but they can be better spaced out. Character balance is a little off, with the bird especially feeling overpowered with the right build compared to the dog. Some weapons feel vastly inferior to others which, while this may be intentional, makes some runs much less fun solely based on RNG. I often don't have this issue when it comes to upgrades and scrolls.Some scrolls don't seem to function as well as others, with some element buffing scrolls seeming more like debuffs. Chests that allow you to "upgrade" random features/bonuses on your weapon are very unclear and confusing. I often don't know if the weapon gets actually upgraded or i just rerolled it and got worse bonuses. I often ignore this option for that exact reason.Vaults ("optional" challenge rooms that appear randomly in levels) vary massively in difficulty. Some are a cakewalk while others have mini-bosses that are harder than the actual bosses, especially during the first stage/level. While some may disagree, I don't like getting curbed stomped either from traps or very strong enemies when I haven't even had a chance to get any decent upgrades or weapons. The golem boss is far less polished and fun than the other bosses, especially with his placement as a possible first boss you can fight. After beating the first boss 5 times it seems to have a 50% chance to have you face the golem instead. This boss can easily be a run killer and I dread fighting him each time. After you get better upgrades he's much more manageable, but damn is he not very fun. At the time of writing this review he is the most recent boss added and obviously less polished. I hope/expect that the devs will improve him.Sometimes reviving allies feels finicky. Could use more accessibility and sound options. WISHES: More characters, at least 4 options would open up party options significantly. More weapons that add more options, shotguns especially.More bosses, levels, and enemy types. While only 3 stages and 4 bosses works out fine, especially with the addition of elite mode, I simply want more. Customization options, even if that just means changing colors for each character/hero. Conclusion: Its great, with many of the pros outweighing the cons. I simply want more from the developers and can't wait to see what they add in the future. I feel like I already got my moneys worth though, it is totally worth the price. This is the best early access game I've personally played.

_childDocuments_.review: Game in Early Access at time of purchase.I paid ten quid for this game, and have gotten 55 hours at time of writing. After Gearbox mugged me off for £60 by removing a setting from BL3 8 MONTHS after the games release, rendering it unplayable to me, I was recommended this game from someone on the GBX forum. I have several EA games from Humble monthly, but have never knowingly purchased one. Considering the price (£10) when I got it, and after watching a few gameplay videos, I decided to give it a try. A Wise decision.Pros:3 Characters (so far) - With skill trees / Special abilities3 Levels (so far) - Broken into several (4-5ish) mini-maps.Several 'Vaults' within each Level.Main Bosses - Sub Bosses - Unique BossesMany different enemies.Shedload of weapons with unique abilities.Another shedload of Scrolls.Great gameplay (if maybe a little basic), with lots of variety.Each run is different. Graphics fine.Sound fine.Controls fine(ish)Re-playability - Through the roof.Dev's constantly updating (and while not all updates / buffs / nerfs etc will please everyone, that's the EA purpose. Cons.Key mapping needs a serious look at, especially for left handers.Some additional sound sliders required for certain sounds. A couple of bugs (only two in 55 hours), that I have noticed.That's about is for the cons. As a newcomer to this game type, I was initially a little frustrated at the beginning of playing this. I was not aware of the mechanics of a 'Rogue-lite' game. And progress initially seemed slow an arduous. Thankfully, the issue was BNIF (Big Nut In Front) ie, me!And the main advice give on various forums, really is the only sound advice... Keep Playing. Build Your Souls. Level the character.Do not expect to steamroller the first level immediately. Accept that failure is inevitable.So that's my review. For an Early Access game. This thing is top-notch. The devs are active and responsive. The game runs smooth, gun-play is great.It is very More-ish!Updated to July 2022.Plenty of additions. New Maps, Characters, weapons and scrolls. More everything. Truly a labour of love for the developers.Pick this up.ETA --I also bought the DLC without even looking at it. And have not played it yet. The dedication this Dev has shown from the beginning, with Fixes, Content Updates, has elicited a trust I rarely give out.Look at my playtime compared to BL3. Of course they are not really comparable.But I know I got more fun from Gunfire Reborn.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Surprisingly Addictive and Fun Co-op FPS Rogue-Lite!Review:Gunfire Reborn is a fast-paced, first-person, co-op rogue-lite shooter developed by Duoyi (Hong Kong) Interactive Entertainment Limited. It features a unique art style, fast-paced action, and procedurally generated levels that provide endless replayability. Despite its relatively unknown status, Gunfire Reborn is a hidden gem that offers a surprisingly addictive and fun gameplay experience for both solo and co-op players.Gameplay: 8/10Gunfire Reborn's gameplay revolves around completing various levels, defeating challenging bosses, and acquiring new weapons and upgrades along the way. The game's rogue-lite elements mean that each run is different, with procedurally generated levels, random weapon drops, and unique character abilities that keep the gameplay fresh and engaging. The fast-paced gunplay and cooperative gameplay make Gunfire Reborn an enjoyable experience that is easy to pick up but hard to master.Graphics: 7/10Gunfire Reborn features a distinctive, cel-shaded art style that is both eye-catching and appealing. The game's characters and environments are well-designed, with bright colors and fluid animations that enhance the game's fast-paced action.Sound: 7/10Gunfire Reborn's sound design is solid, with fitting sound effects for weapons and enemies, and a decent soundtrack that complements the game's action. While not groundbreaking, the game's audio effectively supports the gameplay experience.Performance: 9/10Gunfire Reborn's performance is generally smooth, with the game running well on most hardware configurations. The game's controls are responsive and intuitive, and the gameplay mechanics are well-implemented, allowing for a seamless and enjoyable experience.Community: 7/10Gunfire Reborn's community is small but passionate, with players sharing tips, strategies, and custom content, such as mods and custom levels. The game's co-op multiplayer mode offers a fun and engaging experience, with players able to team up with friends or other players online to tackle the game's challenges together.Overall: 8/10Gunfire Reborn is a surprisingly addictive and fun co-op FPS rogue-lite that offers a unique and enjoyable experience for fans of the genre. Its fast-paced action, rogue-lite elements, and cooperative gameplay make it a must-play for fans of shooters and rogue-lite games. Whether you're looking for a challenging solo experience or a fun co-op adventure, Gunfire Reborn delivers a thrilling and enjoyable journey that is sure to keep you coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun coop roguelite with simple but nicely stylized graphics. Definitely benefits greatly from coop but it's still alright, if much more difficult, solo. Each character starts with 2 unique active abilities and can unlock 5 unique passives with soul essence, the persistent currency earned by playing the game. The game has a wide array of weapons with semi-random passive attributes that alter the weapon's properties. These attributes change damage types, weapon stats, can apply various effects on-hit or on-kill, and more to add interesting variety when picking what weapons to use for your build. Due to the random nature of power ups in each run, relying on a specific build is unlikely and you'll often have to make the best of what you're given. This can lead to wildly different power levels between runs but this is mitigated somewhat by a large talent tree that is universal to all characters to permanently boost your stats as you play.The actual gameplay is a fairly fast paced, first person shooter, room to room dungeon crawl with a boss at the end of each level. Upgrades and weapons are found fairly regularly as you move from room to room via universal buffs in the form of scrolls or character specific buffs in the form of goblets. Some characters are better than others for solo play depending on their abilities and in general the game feels skewed towards coop. Luckily there is a matchmaking system for people who want to use it, I've never actually used it so all I can say is that it exists. The visuals are simple and blocky but I like the art style. All in all I would definitely recommend it for roguelite fans who have a friend or two to play it with and only recommend it to solo players if you just REALLY like first person shooters or roguelites.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal, especially only being early access as of now.I'll be talking about 3 categories:-Graphics-Gameplay-Bugs/glitches~~~Graphics:I love the graphics implemented in this game. They feel so simple, yet smooth and refreshing. The overall aesthetic of all the areas is visually appealing and definitely worth praise. It's also extremely easy to distinguish different sections of the map.8/10~~~Gameplay:Addicting. Just completely addicting. This game is balanced just right, posing a challenge yet still rewarding you for advances. You die, upgrade, and go through the map once more. The satisfaction of beating each boss is the best part. Headshots in this game are especially great. They do tons of damage, but still not enough to simply one shot a character. The weapons feel slick and easy to use, some being more difficult than others. I believe the scrolls could be a bit more balanced. Some just feel too good, while others feel completely useless. An example of this is the scroll that allows you to heal 1 hp / item/copper picked up. I personally think this should be nerfed or touched upon a bit.9/10~~~Bugs/Glitches:Not many noteworthy ones. However, during co-op, my friends and I have experienced some very noticeable lag. The game may freeze suddenly, with everything just sitting in place. Other occasions weapon shots don't register. I haven't encountered any solo (yet), thankfully. For early access, this game has much less bugs than other well known and polished games.~~~Overall:8.5/10This game is definitely worth the buy! It's a rewarding and enjoyable experience. Time flies by when playing it. If you want a fun fps rogue game, this is 100% worth the $12 it current costs.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly fun game to play alone or with friends. It's reminiscent of Borderlands (500-700 hours across those games; I recommend them, too), but has an enjoyable arcade feel and unique character building structures. There are various characters to unlock and play through the adventure with at your leisure. These characters have specific abilities unique to themselves, implied playstyles (though not mandatory) that are great for diversifying your play sessions with your buddies. Though this is not a "main-game" type of title, it's replayability and revisitation factors hold up pretty well between friends. The only con that I can think of for this title is that there's not much content beyond what I'd estimate to be 40 hours worth of time (ie. no new unlockables as of yet, and the "Adventure Mode" is fairly short once you've built up the universal talent tree enough to help you get through the different modes with ease). It's a great videogame, but I hope that we get more content down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly nothing but pure fun. Almost all the weapons feel extremely satisfying to use, the heroes each feel unique and are an absolute joy to master and train with, and it's really hard to ever get tired of playing this. The community around this game is very helpful and active, and so are the devs. The devs care a lot about the game and they really listen to feedback a consistently. The progression in Gunfire is really however you want it to be. I know people who have finished the game in the span of a couple of weeks, and some who have taken months while playing almost every day. Either way, you'll still always come back to this game no matter what. Each hero has a specific set of skills and their own skill tree that you can mess with every game so no run is ever the same. Guns feel distinct and some feel like they even have their own personalities, their designs and abilities are just great. When it comes to the actual combat, I have honestly never seen more fluid movement or combat in any other game, it feels ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing playing this game. The scroll system in Gunfire Reborn is also a big part of it. Each scroll applies certain effects that make every run feel like a fresh new adventure and it is insanely fun to combine your scrolls with your set of weapons, skill tree, and ascensions to make the perfect build. Gunfire Reborn, to me, is just a perfect game in almost every way. I instantly fell in love the second I started playing. I cannot recommend it enough, solid 9.7/10. An absolute must-play no matter what kind of gamer you are, you have to try this game at least once.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn combines the rogue-lite run progression of Risk of Rain with the first-person shooting and extensive loot of Borderlands, creating a fast-paced FPS rogue-lite experience. Developed by Duoyi Interactive Entertainment, this indie gem offers a refreshing take on the genre, providing players with a thrilling and challenging experience. Players can control unique heroes with different abilities to experience diverse builds and fight against various creatures, bosses and challenging environments.  It involves battling through randomly generated levels, and with each run, players gain experience and can upgrade their abilities. The RPG elements come into play in character development and the ability to upgrade weapons. This combination creates a dynamic and challenging environment. The game offers a variety of heroes, each with unique abilities, allowing for a diverse range of build gameplay. The game has a roster of 10 diverse heroes, each bringing their own flavour. Base stats, talents, and skills differ, making each hero unique in the game's strategic puzzle. This diversity allows for a wide range of playstyles, with certain heroes synergising better with specific weapons and occult scrolls.As players progress through the game, they can unlock new abilities and upgrade their existing ones, allowing for a relatively high degree of customisation. This system encourages experimentation and strategic thinking, as players must decide how to best allocate their resources to suit their playstyle. You face a tradeoff of saving your coins to upgrade your weapons later for an easier late-game versus spending your coins now to have a better chance at surviving the early game but risk having no coins to upgrade.Unlocking these heroes is a journey in itself. Some require reaching a certain talent level, others demand payment in Soul Essence, and a few are hidden behind the gates of DLC. The game features procedurally generated levels, ensuring a unique experience each time you play. However, it gets annoying as you encounter the same tileset every run in different orders.The game's arsenal is a treasure trove of ~58 distinct weapons, each with its own rhythm and style. The weapons are diverse and well-balanced, ensuring no weapon feels overpowered. From the rapid-fire rate of some to the devastating critical hit damage of others, each weapon is a unique instrument in the battle symphony. Some even possess exclusive effects, adding a layer of strategy to the combat. Precision is the key to this dance, with accurate shots rewarded with greater damage and additional effects – as like any FPSEven though this game has a matchmaking system, it is unfortunately not well-executed. Players can only match with others at the same difficulty, a counterintuitive setup, as most of the player base is at a higher difficulty level. These higher levels are only accessible after completing the preceding ones. This presents a substantial problem for new players, who are less likely to find a multiplayer game due to the limited pool of players at the introductory levels.Furthermore, playing with randoms often leads to an imbalanced gaming experience. If one player surges ahead of the others, the rest of the team becomes mere cannon fodder. This scenario can detract from the game's enjoyment, turning a potential cooperative experience into a frustrating exercise in futility. Gunfire Reborn is a well-rounded game that offers a unique blend of FPS and roguelike gameplay. Its engaging gameplay, dynamic music, distinctive art style, and diverse weapons and enemies make it a standout title. Despite some issues with its multiplayer system, the overall experience is highly rewarding. Whether you're a seasoned gamer or a newcomer to the genre, Gunfire Reborn offers a unique and engaging gaming experience worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn has been one of my friends' and I's go to games for the past few months. There's hardly any story to speak of, just run and gun action. There's a solid variety of weapons and skills and the character selection at this point is pretty solid. That said, every character is clearly made to specialize with a certain gameplay style and all of your weapons and skill points are randomized for every run. This can be a bit frustrating when all you get are weapons and skills that simply don't work for your character (or are just severely underpowered for your run) but when things work out, they work incredibly well.Enemies often come in overwhelming numbers, which feels fantastic when you get through a swarm that you didn't expect to beat. There are some platforming elements in the game, which can often fall short. Some characters are naturally faster than others, allowing them to jump farther. Some characters simply aren't capable of making certain jumps unless you have the right abilities (which, again, are randomized). There's one in particular near the end that is absolutely abysmal and I tend to skip it every time.This is definitely a game designed to be played with friends. Running this solo is not only unnecessarily difficult (there's some enemies that hit so hard they'll take you down in a couple of shots) but can get a bit boring. The game also encourages creating a synergy of skills which is almost impossible when playing solo.They've recently added a Reincarnation mode, which is similar to Torment in Diablo 3. Every time you beat a Reincarnation level, you get the next one with better loot and more soul essence (in game currency used to purchase abilities that carry over between runs). This adds a huge amount of replayability to the game and I have yet to find the cap to Reincarnation levels.I'd recommend this to anyone looking for a game to play with friends where you're not worried about story or finding something new. It's a great little grindfest that gets new content with some regularity.I'll continue to update this review as the game receives more content and comes out of Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, characters are rewarding to play with in their own ways, weapons all have their own twists that makes them truly unique to use. The style is really nice as well.It's a shame that the player-monster balance has been completely thrown out the window with powercreeping for the players only. If the new almighty talents added on top of the old ones a few months ago weren't enough to make the game a complete cakewalk, the new difficulty added on top of Nightmare (the old final difficulty) to even things out gives out special buffs that are so powerful, it loops back as being even easier than Nightmare. Thus, this game becomes nothing more than a number optimizing sim; where progressing until the end is almost guaranteed, and the only thing left for you is to see how much you'll be able to crank up your damage numbers.This seems to be how the developers want their game though, since they've made that intense, one sided powercreep during early access, AND never bothered to tweak how a specific weapon can permanently deal ELEVEN times more damage with any of the plethora of scrolls and affixes that recovers ammo to the clip since the beginning. I don't expect this to change with the full release, or any subsequent content update.You might get a kick out of this for a few dozen hours while progressing, but at the end of the road you'll be left with just another game whose main attraction is to optimize numbers through gameplay devoid of any challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun first person shooter roguelike with randomized loot, progression across runs.Let's get the most important point out of the way. Combat just feels good. This is super important, because this is how you'll be spending 90% of your time in the game. There's a distinctive sound when you get a critical hit (not too difficult since enemies have large heads and weak points), and another distinctve "ping!" sound when you get a kill. For some reason, this really freaking works for me. I love shooting enemies and hearing "ping! ping! ping!" I also just love seeing huge damage numbers (critical hits and lucky shots). The animations are fluid, enemy attacks are clearly telegraphed. Weapon variety is high, though not infinitely high as say Borderlands. There are a large number of base weapons, and then can each roll with various modifiers, which keeps things interesting.The different characters do play quite differently, and don't neatly fit into the archetypes of "dps, healer, tank, support". Each is perfectly capable of solo'ing, but would have different strengths and weaknesses in a group.The amount of grinding required to unlock stuff is a bit steep initially, because you're not able to carry your permanent progression currency across runs (until you unlock that ability). I have put in 28 hours and just unlocked the fourth character. I think it would have been cooler if you got a new character every 2.5 hours or so (or just make them all unlocked from the start). The other characters are not necessarily OP compared to the starting character, just different playstyles. The game is actually not too difficult, so people who are relative noobs to FPSs should still be able to jump in and have fun. The real difficulty only occurs when you are swarmed and have no crowd control. You can pretty easily defeat bosses without taking any damage once you memorize their attack patterns.Overall, it's a great game! Looking forward to unlocking the rest of the weapons and then doing dailies, etc. UPDATE: just beat the final boss for the first time and thus unlocked Elite (hard) mode, which is a bit more challenging. Phenomenal game. There's still a lot for me to unlock, and they're going to add more biomes and characters before launch!Would love to see a "New Game+" mode just to see how bananas I could make a single character. Would love to see more boss variety. Elites should be more common in normal areas too. My Favorite Character is Lei Luo because I love using snipers, especially on bosses. The other characters are fun too and offer completely different play styles. Looking forward to the next content update! What are you waiting for? Buy this alreadyUpdate as of 100 hours in: it's still good! The two new characters are interesting. The last biome is pretty cool, but is pretty much a stomp since you have four previous biomes of items helping you by that point.

_childDocuments_.review: I considered writing this review a day ago.  I had two hours of gametime and now at the time of writing this I have 3.  I can tell you that I was going to recommend this game even in its current state.  I started out the game feeling like it was slow.  The character seemed slow to get around even though the first stage maps are small to begin with.  Enemies are varied and can surprise you but after a few rounds you learn the attacks and the timings.  You will die very quickly and easily in the beginning.  And I didn’t quite understand in the beginning that this game has serious ramp.  It goes like this:You start out with 0 talent.  Literally and metaphorically.  You don’t know the moves of enemies to dodge them and you have no literal in game talent to earn new perks.  As you play and lose you will earn “talent” which is used to unlock perks which begin the “ramping” process.  You see at first you will feel like a piece of s*** dying easily and not finding great weapons.  I thought that this was the game.Its not.  You see eventually you’ll gain the ability to unlock better weapon drops, more variation, better affects and so on.  And all the while you’re getting better drops more often for guns, you’re now also getting more scrolls.  Scrolls are the wonderful mutators in this game akin to RoRs items.  They change your abilities and give you enhanced powers.  For example, I love the advanced jogger pants because it makes so that I can dodge with a 2 second cool down.  Partner that with the scroll that makes it so that 35% of the time your abilities don’t trigger a cooldown at all, and you suddenly have a good chance of double or triple dashing on the regular.Now suddenly a stage that took 30 minutes and a guaranteed death at boss is completed in less than half that time and the boss is a cakewalk.  And it’s so satisfying.  Unfortunately, this game is somewhat brutal in a sense that as soon as you reach a new stage that is completely fresh  you are guaranteed to die from an unknown threat announcing itself.  I generally don’t buy early access games anymore unless they are very far along in development.  So this one was sort of a gamble for me because it seems very new.  For $12 USD however this is a really hard game to not recommend.  Hell even if they were charging $20 I’d still be recommending it.Bottom line is: Repetitive learn/adapt gameplay, combined with borderlands guns, and risk of rain items makes for an extremely fun game.  Add some coop seasoning and interesting and distinct art visuals for flavor and this is just a really great deal and a great game.  I look forward to seeing its development.

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing just how far this FPS+Roguelite+RPG has come since it's early access release. Now, just recently making it's 1.0 debut this a great example of what a communicative and hardworking team can do with an idea that they love. I believe that at it's current price Gunfire Reborn is an excellent purchase, and if you get it during a sale then you're even luckier. To put it simply I find that Gunfire Reborn plays very smoothly. It makes it easy to sit down, relax, and play a run or two. And for those that are interested I would say that a run typically takes about 30 minutes to an hour, depending on things like the difficulty level, which there are many, and your skills in the game. I would say that Borderlands inspired is a safe way to describe the overall feel of the FPS gameplay and loot systems in the game. That being said, when compared I think that Gunfire Reborn has even more ways to customize your play experiences with character builds, scrolls (buffs), and weapon modifications, that I actually find it to be the better version for me. I just hope that if you read this far and it looks and sounds interesting to you too then you give it a shot. I don't think you'll be disappointed if you do. *Lastly the Gunfire Reborn team is pushing for the "Better With Friends" (2021) award so please vote if you agree with that sentiment, I have played many hours myself in their Co-op modes to prove that it can certainly be true. For me though this is my "Sit Back And Relax" award for many of the reasons I mentioned above. If for you it's "Game Of The Year", "Labor Of Love", or Best Game You Suck At", then I'll just say I understand, it was a tough call lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like the idea of hunting down synergies in a Borderlands-like game, but hate filtering through literal hundreds of guns? Do you like rolling for guns in Destiny 2? Do you wish either of these games had a faster, more roguelike-esque gameplay loop?Yeah, this game does that. It starts slow, especially because you have to unlock the ability to open secret rooms--but as you continue playing, you'll eventually unlock perks like getting a free gun at the start of the game, or the ability to add a new perk to your guns, which make it easier to get a run going. There's unfortunately a point at which some builds start falling off in power, but that only happens well after you've beaten the main game loop the first time.

Can be somewhat frustrating if you're having bad runs back to back; performance issues with your PC can also make the game more taxing as the game is still running when your screen is visually locked in place via lag. _childDocuments_.review: if they add any more paid dlcs to this game i am immediately changing this review to negative because that would mean the price of the game with dlcs would likely double at the least. the dlcs add some good extra gameplay and characters, but adding more with achievements is pesky.gunfire has some similar competitors to it with a roguelite aspect, being that all the room layouts are pre-determined, but you won't come across them in the same order twice in two full separate runs. similar to some source games, there is no sprinting, but a dash is implemented instead. it's a skillful mechanic that can be used to dodge if timed right, but it's not something i use the most often for that purpose. it has three elemental effects and dozens of weapons to choose from, although many are unbalanced when they're first released. still, though, the devs of this game prioritize keeping the game smooth and bug-free as much as possible, and regularly add patches. the team cares about their game very much, more than many developers you see out there in the indie field, surprisingly enough.what's kept me from going head-over-heels into recommending this game is something the game mentions that's stuck to me since i first started playing: the builds. it mentions even in a loading screen tip how there is no worst weapon or worst scroll, or something along the lines of that. however, there are weapons that are just godawful compared to their elemental counterparts, and i've only found myself using them if i end up getting a series of elemental scrolls for a certain element. otherwise, there's always one of the three similar variants of a weapon which does the best, instead of them all being rather equal. still, the weapons are plentiful, so it's not that big of an issue. the bosses, however...that's a different story. a couple are not even bosses and more just bullet-hell enemies/precise-timing events, like the hydra or ichthyosaur offspring.  the new alternate final boss is sort of on the "meh" because it just keeps healing. i guess it's a clever alternative to overpowered builds and putting their skills to the test behind that, but fighting a boss for several minutes because it keeps regenerating most of its health back is just annoying. if you play on a lower difficulty(which there's a lot of difficulties you can choose from, since you can increase the difficulty each time you beat the highest unlocked difficulty up to reincarnation 9, currently) i doubt it would be as much of an issue, but it's still noticeable nonetheless.those are really the only grievances with the game i have, even though there's some clear inspiration of some weapons and effects that the game took from other roguelites or rpgs. to simplify, the dev team is active and very passionate about their game even from the start, and balance as much as they can. the dlcs add some characters that are broken in some ways, i suppose, especially nona, since her iron wing can still revive her which in the early days of her release led to me singlehandedly completing high difficulties because iron wing would just revive me whenever i went down. if you want to experience the most broken runs, i'd advise doing so whenever they release a new character or weapon, since they usually can be used for crazy builds upon initial release. there's still weapons and bosses that are the equivalent to "the bloat" in the binding of isaac that people intentionally avoid or despise because they're much worse than their counterparts, but i guess that's inevitable to some extent when you have multiple bosses per region of the game

_childDocuments_.review: The game has grown to be very disrespectful of your time and choices. Many of the choices you make in Reincarnation, the primary difficulties played, make you feel like you lose out on something else when you make that choice instead of making you feel like you gained something. The boss vaults feel disproportionately difficult compared to actual bosses, much of the game feels like a bullet sponge fest later, and you are often left with choosing quality of life buffs instead of fun options because the game locks quality of life options behind Spiritual Blessings. Your strength feels always either too little or too much, with no way to mitigate that due to the abundance of a lot of meh options or option that have downsides that are too great. (I'm looking at you Deflection Shield). The over-abundance of Enhanced Scrolls has also become a great detriment because you are now either forced to take enhanced scroll boosting options at the very start, and lose out entirely on fun or build defining Spiritual blessings, or not take those options and have no way of getting any enhanced scrolls outside of the 3 or 4 that you might get, let alone those enhanced scrolls actually being useful or fun. Too many options in this game right now that feel BAD when you have it instead of being something workable or neutral. All in all, the game definitely feels like it's gotten worse with each update instead of better. I do not regret the 400+ hours I have spent and I enjoyed them greatly, but I definitely cannot recommend this game any more.Update 12/1/22: Went back since the Spiritual Assault update added 2 more achievements for me to get. The new mode is definitely very fun, but has severe balance issues that make it feel like the options for viable setups is even smaller than the normal mode in Reincarnation. Overall, my sentiments from my initial review still stand. Also if anyone has ideas for making tiger work in the new mode please let me know lol It's a nightmare trying to get the clear on him.
