_childDocuments_.review: Good Gameplay. Thoroughly enjoyed this game. I like Rogue-lite/likes and this one didn't disappoint. It is mostly because when you have a good gun, the gunplay is great. My gripes with this game are the gun variety (don't like 90% of the guns)., your inability to get the gun you want during a run, and the random upgrade via chest.  The gun thing is pretty simple, there are only a gun or two that work with whatever build you are trying to get during a run, the odds of you getting that gun, with the correct amount of attachments and leveled up decently is nearly impossible. So you WILL be using weapons you don't like. Annoying. But would just be better if there were more options along the way. Just too many guns, and most are garbage for your current build. (PS, they added guns with updates, which just makes it even harder to get the gun you want). Bad design there.  Your character has upgrades which you get drip fed after completing stages, however, these are completely random. At times you can get 3 options that are all for something you aren't using, and that is annoying. Again, wish I had just a little more control, 4 options would be better, or making them optional buys may be better, IDK, but it is very annoying when you need to upgrade a specific skill but never can because it just doesn't ever show up.  I understand these are kind of mechanics in the rogue-like/lite genre, but I think they could be better here. All in all though, I do like playing the game, it is still challenging after unlocking mostly everything (but that is highly dependent on your luck during run, just wish it was a little less based on luck and a little more on the skill side). Definitely worth a buy if you like reactive shooters

_childDocuments_.review: A rouge like fps with Borderlands like elemental mechanics and gameplay. It's really fun and surprisingly challenging. There is also 3 different characters with their 2 unique abilities to play with. There's a skill tree for each character and every power up you pick through out the game changes your stats and gameplay drastically and most of the time they are power ups with no down sides. It has similar boss fights to Borderlands but it executes every aspect of it much better even when compared to borderlands 3. Every new stage also has very cool and unique themes.This game has a lot of potential to be very popular and even in its early stages of development, its decently polished, offers various good content and is a steal for how little it costs.

_childDocuments_.review: I had originally not recommend this game and I'll leave my original review below. The funny thing is, I still stand by everything I said in my initial review and yet here I am still playing the game 83 hours later. Although I wish there was some more variety in the levels themselves and I find the game a little grindy, it's just so fun that I keep finding myself coming back to it over and over again. I often want to play a solid, clean FPS that isn't bogged down by a lot of cut scenes or story and this is the best one out there.Original Review:I've gone back and forth on whether or not I would recommend this game. At the end of the day, there are three main issues for me. One, the procedurally generated dungeons have very little variety. I know the game is in early access, and I'm sure this will get better with time, but there is very little difference from run to run. The game starts to feel monotonous very quickly. Two, the progression is extremely slow. Most of the upgrades are very expensive and only go 5 points at a time. After playing for 20 hours, my stats are still not much higher than when I started. Third, the power-ups, or occult scrolls, feel unbalanced or unexciting. Here is an example of unbalanced upgrades. For the first 15 hours I played, every time I got the ability to have three dashes (instead of one), I would beat the first boss. Every time I did not get that ability, I would die at the first boss. All in all, there's a lot to like here, but I ultimately find it too repetitive and too much of a grind to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Firstly, I must declare that I am incredibly biased in my assessments due to how much I enjoy playing FPS Rogue-likes/lites, but this is also a plus given how many I have tried up until I came across this beauty. I found out about Gunfire Reborn when it was recommended to me on Steam at around May 2021, before Tao got released. I instantly fell in love with the character and weapon designs presented in the trailers and quickly bought it to give it a try. I can say that I wasn't disappointed and that the purchase was completely worth it. As a solo casual player I had tons of fun upgrading the extensive Skill Tree slowly but surely, getting further and further into the game every attempt. Learning enemy patterns was tough at first, given the amount of damage they deal to you, but the sense of progress made it all a lot more fun.A couple of weeks later I got a friend to buy the game as well, and this opened a whole new part of the game for me. Playing with friends is EXTREMELY fun. Teaching someone and learning new things together makes the gameplay way more enjoyable than just rolling through it solo. Every run, you get to share upgrades and try to make each other's build the best it can be. The element of teamwork is well implemented here, with plenty of ways to assist each other. So, as a casual game for you to play with your friends, this is a great option.Now, in regards to the more in depth side of the game; balancing is kinda wack. Not that this is not a good thing, it's just something to keep in mind if you want to get good. The fact you can just learn three or four combos that absolutely demolish the later stages of the game might be a turn off for someone that wants equally good and varied strategies, but I honestly don't care. I just avoid OP combos when I feel like it and take them when I want to break the game in half. For some people it's a good thing that you can be an invincible God of destruction in almost any run if you play a certain way and pick specific upgrades.This week I finally decided to go for all achievements and ended up finishing some of the more grindy ones with friends and steamrolling through some of the more specific ones. This was probably the most fun I had with the game and I'm glad I was able to use everything I learned to help me get the harder achievements.For those who think the game might get repetitive after a couple of runs, it really doesn't. Unless you just care about winning in the fastest way possible every time, there is a huge amount of content to explore and master. Each character is unique and can be the basis of amazing builds, even if not optimal. Learning by yourself is totally doable and you can always resort to helpful guides to learn more in-depth mechanics (like how Lucky Shots work).So, to conclude my review, I must say that this is a good game. A great game even if you plan on playing with friends. The movement and balancing might not be perfect, but I still prefer this over other games of the same genre due to its personality. It oozes with charm and I absolutely love it.Graphics: 9.5/10Gameplay: 9/10Enjoyment: 9.5/10Soundtrack: 8/10Recommend? Yes, definitely. This review was made right after achieving 100% achievements. (102/102)

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended, while generally not a roguelike fan I consider this one very good. The obvious and easy comparison is to Borderlands, and I think they've done a very good job adapting some of the ideas from the game to a roguelike formula.Each character has 2 skills, each with a designated skill tree. Most of them are interesting, especially the more recent ones, and depending on the character they can be independently useful or have amazing synergy with each other.Skill tree passives are called "Ascensions" and are given at set intervals in progression and will contain 3 randomly selected ones, of which you get to pick 1. Most of them are good enough that you will infrequently feel like you've been completely robbed.The generic passives are called "Occult Scrolls" and are similarly found at set intervals in progression, sometimes in sets of 3 and sometimes only 1, can be bought from the peddler, and also drop from elite and boss enemies. Again, much like ascensions, they are balanced well enough that you almost never feel like you've just gotten shafted. Unlike ascensions you get more of these per run, and the pool is just comfortable enough that you can count on finding some of the common and rare ones you're looking for every time.The weapon design is varied and has a few standout interesting ones. The balance for weapons is much worse than the other two character building components, but not so much so that you'll ever be stuck with a "bad" base weapon. You'll find one of the ones you like with good rolls every run. Rolls are (almost) all good and are usually your standard number-go-up fare, with some weapons having their own unique ones that might buff its unique function.Enemy design is good, nothing has hitscan attacks so you never feel like damage is COMPLETELY unavoidable. Bosses die way too quickly. Don't have a lot to say here.Current issues: The latter half of the game is almost always too easy, difficulty drops off very sharply after acts 1 and 2. The new "Bizarre Dream" feature is great, makes runs more interesting and in some ways more consistent, but some of them are way too strong compared to their drawbacks and make the game much easier. Spiritual Link has no drawbacks and is insanely strong, but does make the game more interesting and should probably just be a base feature. The drawback of Lone Wolf is completely offset by how strong some of the Spiritual Blessings are, but the feature itself is fine. Independent Fortunes gives too many scrolls and most of the drawbacks are ignorable. The others are fine how they are, and are all pretty cool. The status effect "Miasma" is inflicted by using the two status effects best suited for shields/armor, but if the enemy has all of their health converted to either of those then it becomes completely useless and only does 1 damage. The "point blank" challenge event should be tuned down or removed.Things I would like to see: extra ascension and weapon rerolls, you can only reroll either under very specific circumstances, even 1 free one per run would be a welcome addition.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend but BEG for some balancing. There is ZERO reason to buff my orb as cat. You get rather directed in play style in that sense. Other than that, there is too much loot/buffs. If you averaged 30 scrolls a run, it would take 5 hours to see every scroll IF YOU DIDN'T PULL THE SAME ONE TWICE! Meaning you could go all day without seeing all of the scrolls. Same with hero buffs. The dev needs to add more levels before adding any more scrolls.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: First day I played must've been glitched. Since then I've had no issue finding multiplayer matches. Usually within 2 minutes you'll have a full squad to run with. Tons of replay value, lots of fun. Hopefully they add more content though because within the first 4 hours I beat normal mode and honestly hard doesn't feel that much more difficult. Once you learn most enemies/move sets/map layouts it gets MUCH easier (as do most rogue likes) but this game I don't think has enough content yet when compared to the big boys in the same field. They do have the FPS thing going for them at least so it helps.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I'm addicted, thank you. Insane game that I can finally settle on for a pretty long time :)However, in my opinion there should be improvement on the hit accuracy overall especially on bow because sometimes I see my arrow went through the enemy and didn't get a hit, and notice a really weird hard lag spike at Yoruhime-Maru when the ship does the sideway cannon barrage caused me to get oneshot and my dash didn't work at charged even I'm at 200+ FPS. _childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast! Fast paced action, roguelike progression, and continuing updates means this game has high replayability. People have been describing it as a combination of other popular games like Borderlands and Risk of Rain 2. I think that's a fair judgement as the weapons and loot system in Gunfire Reborn are a mash-up from those 2 games.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game with lots of weapons, items, power-ups, and playable characters. The FPS elements of the game work well, and the shooting and dodging feels very satisfying. This is a game that makes you feel powerful, you can blast through hordes of enemies extremely quickly, but the enemies can also kill you just as quickly sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Very predator behavior. They make the very first boss very difficult to where you either have to keep playing and dying to the exact same dungeon/boss over and over again til you have enough to skill up your skill tree a bunch or you'll pay up and buy a hero to get skills and buffs locked behind a paywall. This was appealing to my son so we all bought it to try together and alone or together we couldn't come close to beating the boss with only having one, sometimes two dashes. Then his shield regens and he spawns a bunch of adds which is fine but if he hits you and you don't dodge it perfectly? Dead. Two hits sometimes one good one and you are dead. This is not noob friendly or fun, its down right predatory. They knew what they were doing when purposefully making the first boss like that. Definitely refunding.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting something unpolished seeing as it is an early access game, and i was pleasantly surprised. The game feels finished, the gunplay is responsive, each character feels different and interesting. Multiple playstyles possible for each character and all of them seem viable if you've gotten enough power ups for them.Elevator pitch: think Hades roguelike features with borderlands-esque weapons and classes.The only downside i can think is coop. This game doesnt have servers, coop is hosted by someone and everyone else will have both: their and the hosts latency fluctuations, spikes and such. Even playing with people in my hometown i sometimes felt like missing shots i shouldn't be missing and getting hit by things i shouldn't be getting hit by. And even with this caveat the game is still a lot of fun with friends (just don't let that 1 notorious friend with bad internet host the games).
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that this is the most fun multiplayer shooter I've played in I dont know how long. So why the thumb down review then? Well I took a break from the game for about a year after I had unlocked every character and maxed out their skill progression but decided to come back to it now that I've noticed new expansions for sale. Unfortunately on reinstall I've discovered something has happen to my save as I installed to the same location as before but after having done so I'm back to level one. I've jumped through the standard hoops of checking file integrity and the like and I'm still out of luck, Countless hours of game play lost.After poking around some I found a discord channel where the developer had in the past directed people to get help for problems like this. Unfortunately it was awash in unanswered requests for help for the exact same problem I'm having.So I here I am leaving a negative review for a game that I love because it's more or less dead to me at this point given that I have zero interest in starting completely over from scratch. Maybe the developer keeps a closer eye on its reviews then it does on its own support server on discord and I'll hear back from them and get some support by doing this. If not then I guess I wont be buying any expansions.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game to play with friends or pass time alone. I find myself losing hours when I start even with intentions to only play a short time. Repetitive and mindless action with a big skill tree for each character. I honestly just play as the first character you get because I didn't unlock another one until I had put so much work into the first. Maybe make it a bit faster to unlock characters so it doesn't feel like taking a big loss starting at square one so much. Deterred me from even trying the others. One issue is the walls extend beyond the actual walls themselves. Bullets often get stopped by an invisible edge when trying to fire from cover. Overall a pretty sweet game though and would def love to see some cool DLC. 8/10. Side note. I honestly can't remember how much I paid for it so I cant say whether its worth the money or not, but it definitely is if it's sub $25.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I have played this game quite regularly since it's come out and I still love doing runs  to try out new builds and different weapons. The updates and bug fixes come out often enough to keep you busy and fix issues within the game. I have yet to play a round of Gunfire that has been exactly the same and I love this about the variety that the game offers.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: It's Borderland meets Hades. If you like any of those, you would probably like this one too. Tons of content, nice gunplay, each run feels a bit different.The game looked quite bad on screenshots, but in dynamics it's much better.The biggest downside is the gun balance - a lot of weapons are weak, and some are completely useless. Hope devs would continue balancing the game and adding a new content.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This was on my wishlist for a long time after watching a pretty entertaining twitch stream featuring the game. I kept putting it off for some reason. I knew that it'd be fun but I just always put it to the side. Finally I pulled the trigger during the sale, and a normally well priced game became an even better deal around the 10 dollar mark. It is by far well worth your money. The game feels fun. It's mainly fighting your way through a variety of settings, encountering quite a few types of enemies, always looking for the sweet loot, and quickly comparing tons of different weaponry that drop. There are heroes, talents, unlocks, challenges, build types, etc; all the things you've come to know and love in roguelites, etc. The gameplay loop is well balanced and much time can pass quite easily which is a testament to creating a good sense of difficulty and scaling. It is quite hard and often I've died suddenly but usually based off a poor decision. This feeling of uncertainty even as you become powerful keeps the game engaging and alive. It good ways it reminds me of Borderlands 2, Hades, and Risk of Rain 2 while still doing it's own thing. Colorful worlds, fun heroes, cool weapons, pretty responsive gun play, big RPG style numbers flying up on the screen...I've enjoyed it for a few hours now by myself and had a ton of fun fighting along side my brother, so the co-op is great too. Pretty stable game, no bugs yet or anything weird. Mind you, I've only played a few hours but I really do see myself putting on music or whatever and really enjoying the gameplay loop and building up the heroes. If you've had this on your radar or are just looking for a simply fun shooter to play alone or with friends it's just a great, great deal. The content seems to be coming along too.EDIT: 1.0 is finally here and it's great! A new stage, new guns, a new character, new scrolls! More mechanics to test out and combinations to experience! Yet another reason to grab this game!EDIT #2: DLCs are great as well. Lots more guns and a few more characters to master! I feel like even though there may be 'the best meta' etc to do a run, there are many many paths to a good build via so many scrolls and weapons! Still highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 38 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 11 now. My son got this game from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. _childDocuments_.review: overall game it is pretty good. different characters with different abilities, tons of different options to make yourself powerful and enemies are challenging enough you don't get bored. one of the biggest dislike of the game is cross play. takes forever to even find one teammate, finding 3 is annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Game balance needs work. The first boss have several moves that can take down your entire shield at full, or kill you in one hit if your shield is down. Problem is, your dash refreshes every 3 seconds. So either you try to abuse the AI but trying to run around a pillar so the boss' moves would get block by the pillar, or... you can use one dash, and then die in next move. Also the boss charges his shield back up after every 10000 dmg you do to him... just... why? It just pads out the fight longer and isn't fun or engaging in anyway. If the devs can't even make a good first boss, that's not a good sign. The gun play feels good, but the power ups are hit or miss. It tries to copy borderlands but it's not as well thought out. Like in borderlands you can go down but then you can get second wind if you kill some mobs. But in this game, if you go down, you have one chance to spend some energy, and that's it. Not to mention your power doesn't work on the boss as well. I've gotten the special ability to do a 4 sec hold, but on the boss it barely last a sec, What's the point of upgrading your powers if they're not going to work on a boss? This is not an ARPG where your status effect depends on the class of the enemy... Because in ARPGs, you have multiple skills to use, and so even you can't CC the boss, you'd still have at least one movement skill, not to much you can drink potions. I like that this game tries to do something different by mixing vermintide with borderlands, but it feels like cargo cult science and the devs doesn't know why certain mechanics are the way they designed to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire reborn is an early access could use some polish (certain UI elements go off screen, you shouldn’t be warned before leaving the perk shop if your not going to loose any souls, moving around when knocked feels odd, etc), and more content (guns, scrolls, room designs, etc), and some of the text is feels like it was written by someone who doesn’t speak English very well, but overall is still very fun.The gun play is solid, and while there aren’t too many guns, each one does feel unique. Outside of a few enemies (most notable minibosses) TTK feels good.It would be really nice to see host migration implemented so if the host disconnects, someone else becomes host and everyone else can keep playing.Overall things like these are excepted in an early access game and don’t prevent you from having a good time. If you like FPS and rouguelite games, this game is great
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games to play daily. The game is simple yet very in depth. It can start slow with unlocking heroes and weapons, but getting through the grind gets you to feeling like a god with how powerful you can get in each run. (My) Average run is about just an hour, so its a nice short but not-too-short experience. Weapon selection is wide and varied with both familiar and unique uses. Highly recommend you give this game a try, its a really fun time

_childDocuments_.review: Very passionate, witty developer with a knack for realising what he's good at and consistently outputting more and more of that. And unlike buckets and buckets of skittles, you never find yourself saying "well, that's too much of the same stuff". You'd think after the fifth installation of the (mostly) same characters, the (mostly) same enemy types, the (mostly) same elemental-based RPG system, it'd get old. It really doesn't.I enjoyed EBF1 and 2 as turn-based RPG games originally on Newgrounds. It was a cool duo of flash games to play when you're bored. When EBF3 came out, and I realised I had a world map to explore, characters to level up and gear to get instead of an already-maxed-out RPG fight-engine experience, I became hooked. But I never enjoyed playing those games on browsers....So the decision to boot the games over to Steam was phenomenal. I don't know what's wrong with me, but booting games up on Steam and earning Steam achievements is my motivation to play a lot of my games.Matt Roszak has branded his own image, based on typical JRPG tropes and characteristics. You can see a lot of the characters in this game in other genres if you go play his flash games, including a bullet-hell game and a QTE game.Enough of the context. Here's the summary:It's a turn based fantasy adventure, as you'd expect. You may think "wow, that's totally original, never seen that one before" and I'd be on your side. But the charm and care, the humour and references combine into an homage that singles itself as something new, something familiar and something reliable.It plays out like a normal JRPG. You fight monsters (not randomly, thank Godcat), you level up - you get stronger. You venture weird and wonderful realms, you slave away for NPCs who stand in one spot and command you to get stuff.If you're a fan of JRPGs and turn-based combat, you may look at the art-style and go "wow, this looks so trash" and as a result denote it as drab, boring, or potentially easy. But there's a lot of depth in this game. And each instalment adds in new mechanics that change up the game DRASTICALLY. In EBF3, it was pretty basic, but the whole appeal was (aside from being able to use Lance) acting like a standard RPG as I mentioned before. EBF4 added in a prime new character, a deeper story, the backup system, end-end-game content and NG+, more status effects and elements, and this one adds in summons, weather which affects statuses between turns, and removes a chore: mana, instead implementing more cooldowns for more moves, which previously, the 'good' moves would just give a negative debuff to the user.You'll warm up to it, even if from the get-go it looks lacklustre. I personally enjoy the art style and the humour, and there's a huge difficulty curve on bosses if you play on epic.One thing I didn't like about this game were amount of shared skills there were, it's a cool feature but it was annoying to be able to dedicate a true 'healer'. The equips, especially the flairs in this game are amazing, though, so it offsets nicely. I wish you didn't have to use captured monsters as materials for upgrading, and I wish you couldn't catch bosses. It made me painstakingly have to re-fight each boss on both Zero and Epic, for the capture and achievement respectively, and it burns my completionist complex where I've been collecting one of each monster, just to have that monster now be a gap in my Bestiary in terms of capture, then I have to go back and catch an extra.The haste mechanic is nice, but it feels like the Viking Monolith ends up being an end-all solution to summoning. I'd rarely.. just rarely... find myself using any 50 SP+ Summons because I may not have SP for Viking Monolith, or I need SP for Stumpy Gloop or Slime Bunny.I think the summon system needs work, a good idea would you'd be able to have two non-backup monster slots and you could summon specific monsters to help fight in some way.A solid experience. I'm 50 hours in, and I still need to do the  on Epic. I've gotten close... but I wish there were more strategies to those fights other than set guides I've seen online. It feels like on Epic the fights just overwhelm you with constant nukes and AoE, and you can't cover all the elements through resistances.The 'equip' function during battle would come in handy here if it didn't consume a turn. I get it'd be really unbalanced to be able to change equipment on a whim - maybe you can only change one equip per turn, and any more than that consumes your turn? According to the devlog Matt wanted to take this feature out completely but it was contested highly, I'm not sure why though.Overall, a charming, funny, solid experience. It's not game of the year, and it's not the best story-wise, but it doesn't try to be. It offers a nice amount of content, surprising depth, and differs enough from other instalments to warrant its pricetag.I'd recommend it to anyone who has time to spend on turn-based RPGs, and I love the developer to bits, so please check out Kupo Games and Matt's humble beginnings.Looking forward to future releases.

_childDocuments_.review: - Super fun rogue-like- Cute furry characters to choose from, all with their own unique skills and abilities- Buuunch of weapons, scrolls, and ascensions to choose from.- Constant updates and support from the devs (with free content too now and then + DLC)- Infinite replayability, and always fun to come back to- Even BETTER with friends, up to 4 player co-opSeriously, whats not to like about it?
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly good and deserves your patronage.  A wide variety of characters with fun abilities, with low performance requirements, a charming style, and a "roguelike" where you won't die strictly because of RNG.  I would like to emphasize the last point, that I don't mind dying in this game because I don't feel like I'm getting screwed over by RNG, that by the time you're past the first zone you've likely got a reasonable build no matter how you decide to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Game got me through some really tough times so I'm pretty biased. Characters play different, the guns are a plenty and the damage be insane when you learn the game. The characters are cute, the artwork is wicked, the gunplay is simple yet massively fun. If you have friends to play it with, just makes it better.Small side note: if you play with friends, get the one with the best internet to host the lobby
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to recommend this game, but I can't with the game breaking bugs that keep occurring. The game will sometimes rubberband you, even in single player, which can cause you to die. Sometimes the game will lock up right before an explosion hits preventing you from dodging it and thus killing you. I'm guessing the particle effects and sound effects are loaded on demand and are not preloaded, which means they can cause this lock up while loading the assets. And sometimes I will dodge out of an explosion area and somehow still get hit by it. I've had Nihilation Monks spawn under ground beneath me and it doesn't show the damage area, so I don't know what is hitting me or from where. The hitboxes for enemy weakpoints seem really off. Sometimes it's super easy to hit them and sometimes no matter how hard you try, it won't count shots against them.I also don't know what kind of "end game" they have planned. Like will there be some form of infinite progression? Longer term unlocks?The game has potential and I enjoy it up until I hit the bugs and then I stop playing it. Hope to see it improve.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun overall but the controller support sucks. Aim assist can't be turned off even though there is an option for it. The frame rate is a whole issue by its self. The higher your frame rate the more sensitive the controller settings are. For example: let's say that you capped your game at 60fps and had your sensitivity set to 30. If you then changed your game to uncap frames, the sensitivity, all though it says 30, will act like you've set it to 230. I enjoy the game but until the aim assist issue is fixed I wont be too inclined to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rogue-like for those who enjoy loot-based FPS and want to jump straight into the action. It will be unforgiving, but it is never impossible. I found that whenever it felt like a challenge was too difficult, stepping back to relearn weapons, class abilities, and builds brought me back into completing challenges consistently. If you find that some enemies and bosses defeat you quickly and your patience is wearing thin, take a break, watch a video tutorial, and give it another try. As long as you're having fun, there's no shame to be had in getting some help.If I could only request one thing from the developers, it would be a new game mode featuring procedural maps!
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun. I read the reviews and went in with an open mind of giving it a solid chance. You start out not knowing anything about how the guns and scrolls work. Once you figure out your builds based on the weapons and hero you select, it gets much, much better. Just know that sometimes its better to give up on a run and upgrade than to revive and try to keep going. Also, multiplayer is fun, doesn't start until you're level 10 but you're probably better off playing with friends than with randoms because most of the time they expect you to know exactly what is going on and will run off without you. If you like rougue-lites and looters, this game is definitely worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: A fun roguelite shooter. Like most Roguelites, there a bit of a lull in replayability until you can start moving through the reincarnation difficulties but overall I really enjoyed this game. Much better to play with friends since once you get into the high levels you can get one shot easily and blow your whole run there.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. It's easy enough for casual players to get into, while still having plenty opportunity for progression and difficulty for anyone who wants to keep playing. The gunplay mechanics are satisfying, the weapon variety is interesting, and the roguelite mechanics are strategic. It's definitely worth trying out, especially to support the developers who consistently come out with content updates for their game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gunfire Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: Gunfire Reborn is an adventure level-based game featured with FPS, Roguelite and RPG. Players can control heros with various abilities to experience diverse Build gameplay, use randomly dropped weapons to explore random levels. This game can be played by single player, or Co-op up to four.

name: Immortal Legacy: The Jade Cipher
detailed_description: About the story: In order to explore the mystery of his past, TYRE, the former special forces soldier with a special constitution, came to Yingzhou Isle which was located in the legendary Dragon Triangle area. After being attacked by mysterious creatures, the plane that TYRE took crashed and he lost contact with his companions. He found a lot of traces of human activity on the island that had been believed inaccessible. While exploring the terrible secrets behind anomalies despite unpredictable threats, he gradually unfolds the mysterious origins of an ancient Chinese legend. A breathtaking adventure begins here. Game features: · Splendid but the uncanny game scene When staying in the weird climate and treacherous terrain of Yingzhou Isle, one must be cautious to make every step, because danger may hide in the corner of beautiful scenery - cliff and perilous peak above the sea of clouds, ancient and spectacular ruins, enclosed and sinuous underground mazes ...  · Full of thrilling battles You can use a variety of close-range and long-range firearms and do everything you can to survive the swarm of mercenaries, supernatural creatures, and ancient guardians. To be a precision archer, a bomb madman, or a lonely swordsman? Survive to see the truth. · Dangerous adventure You'll meet a group of unique and charismatic characters, crack the deadly traps along the way and piece together the disturbing truth of the story with rich details. Courage and wisdom can only solve difficult problems, however, the bond between people can heal hearts. About the game: 'Immortal Legacy: The Jade Cipher' VR version was released in overseas regions on April 17, 2019 and then launched in Europe, North America, Japan, and Asia in succession. With the innovative full free move, excellent atmosphere rendering and rich interactive elements, the game was highly praised by numerous VR players and was nominated as “Best Action and Adventure Game” at the TIGA Games Industry Award 2019. Today, the non-VR version of the game has launched on Steam, with brand new ways of performance and upgraded atmosphere, it is ready for you to pick up the gamepads, feel the perfect touch of weapon guns, experience the mysterious legends that you feel familiar with and explore the mystery of Yingzhou Isle. _childDocuments_.review: Immortal Legacy: The Jade Cipher is like walking into your local Gamestop and seeing that single copy of an odd/new release on the console games shelf for 19.99.  When you check out the box it is bizarre and strange so you immediately purchase it because you've got to check out such an oddity and it turns out to be a nice little gem.  I enjoyed my 3+ hours of playtime with such a bizarre title.   The only thing I still cannot wrap my head around is how colorful and attention to detail they provided to the main npcs but yet the environment/baddies are all bland in color and detail (except for the Dragons and final boss). _childDocuments_.review: ...Well it’s… um… it was an… an experience?I’m happily confused, is that a proper description?The last couple of years have certainly introduced a slew of new and inspiring aesthetics from foreign markets, that we know for sure. Some have even grown from the heavy influence of popular games from the west. Now, most of these are battle-royales and uninspired mobile crap young kids use to vacate their parents bank accounts but every once in awhile we get a game like Immortal Legacy. Made with total and UTMOST sincerity and baffling design decisions, taking bits and bobs from many games over the last 8 years to create a bizarre amalgamation of scenarios in an attempt to make it big in the videogame industry.Something Immortal Legacy failed at, tremendously. But it made a fan out of me!The game begins in the backseat of a futuristic aircraft heading to a mysterious island, the main character, only dubbed TYRE, mulls over his tragic and equally mysterious and promptly forgotten-and never-addressed-again past before the metal coffin he was riding in is severed in two and plunges him straight into the world of action set-pieces and MacGuffin hunting!At least for the first half. It’s 2013’s Tomb Raider just without the disturbing amount of Lara Croft abuse porn!Yeah, this game is a master-class of picking up concepts and then throwing them away. Right off the bat we are rescued by a streamer-waifu who then gets kidnapped and we don’t see her much until the very last cutscene of the end of the game, which is the defining trait of everything following it. Our Waifu-Bait running into the fray of very rapey mercenaries and not acknowledging it? You got it! A climbing mechanic that is most certainly a leftover from the PS4 VR port? Absolutely! Sudden body-horror and survival horror elements ripped straight out of Resident Evil 7? Oh it’s the entire second half of the game!I’d hate it if it wasn’t just so charming and sincere!The shooting is A-okay, the weapon juggling is pretty liberal and the combat is by-the-numbers, the boss-fights suck yet the actual budget of the modeling is AAA despite having the length and tone of a mid-00’s eurojank shooter. This is Chinese-Jank, and I LOVE it!I haven’t felt this charmed by a mediocre game in awhile so I’m gonna stop with the hints of whats to come. It’s not a good port by any means and the astoundingly lackluster options and lack of key-bind changing is gonna be a major turn-off but it’s nothing too extreme. But I can’t help but recommend this game when it goes on sale!It’s no surprise that Immortal Legacy failed yet I wish it didn’t! With the burgeoning Chinese videogame market, I hope we get more experiences like this over mobile games and crappy battle-royales! Give her a go! You’ll be confused as all hell!
_childDocuments_.name: Immortal Legacy: The Jade Cipher

_childDocuments_.review: As i can't compare this version to the vr game, i have to admit, that this game is from the controls very complicated and inappropriate for an action title. The graphics based on the unity engine look really good and run smoothly. But unfortunately the menu lacks the personal adjustments, except for the display resolution, high and low as well as depth of field on/off, everything else adjusts the game automatically. The settings in the menu also are awkward, you can only choose a setting by pressing "wasd" and confirm with ENTER. The action feels tormented slowly, as our main character moves too slowly and can't even jump, the weapon selection is a disaster (Q or E must be held down while moving the mouse inside the inventory on the corresponding weapon - but even this works very slowly!) So i didn't have much fun with this game. Notice, dear Development: A few improvements with a patch could work wondering here.

_childDocuments_.review: The search for immortality is just one reason that brings you to Yingzhou Island, located deep in the Dragon’s Triangle. Playing as ex-special forces soldier Tyre, you’re also here to discover the truth behind your mother’s mysterious death. Finding out how that event and her enigmatic past are tied to the secrets that lie at the heart of the island will see you battle through not only a mercenary army sent in to excavate it, but the horrors they’ve unwittingly set free.

name: Coromon
detailed_description: The sun begins to dawn on Velua, a new day for the world and a new day for you, a freshly minted Battle Researcher of the global research society known as Lux Solis. It’s your first day and everything goes smoothly until a mysterious force attacks your latest workplace. Build up a squad of Coromon, track down the invaders, and grapple with a rising threat that endangers everyone on Velua! True to our commitment to let you play how you want, the latest update brings color customization for Coromon, fruit-to-cake conversion using the brand new Lux Kitchen, and new Cake recipes to make! Coromon is all about taming the eponymous wildlife and challenging the rest of the world: other wildlife, trainers, or titanic bosses! Build a team from more than 100 charming creatures, defined by their elements, traits, and skills. Catch, train then set them loose on your rivals! Master a stamina-based battle system where every action costs energy, so choose skills and attacks carefully. Deal damage, sap enemy stamina with status effects, or nullify them through dozens of conditions to emerge victorious. Challenge friends online and see whose Coromon squads are the best of the best. The first day at Lux Solis is just the first step in a much greater adventure. Soon you’ll be thrust into a story grand in scope and great of importance, as a mysterious, alien threat emerges. It’s up to you to help Lux Solis put a stop to their dastardly designs. Pursue the antagonists’ trail across six major zones and cities, with dozens of interconnecting routes to explore. Each one brimming with quests, secrets, and items to find. Explore the furthest reaches of Velua, from frozen glacial caverns to the depths of blistering deserts. Play a key role throughout a fully-fledged classic JRPG narrative, complete with plot twists, turns, and revelations that not all is as it seems... Coromon empowers you to create an experience just the way you want. Difficulty is more than just stat changes. Each option changes the fundamental mechanics, making the game as challenging as you want. Want a stress-free, chill playthrough? Immerse yourself in the story on the easiest setting without hassle, or focus on tactics, number-crunching, and resource management. Want a more high-stakes challenge? Use the built-in Randomizer and Nuzlocke modes to put fan favorite twists on the creature catching experience. Create the trainer you want, using hundreds of customizable elements like hair, fashion, and more. Customize the look of your Coromon! Prefer a Potent’s color to a Perfect’s? Just set the right element. We're honored to be able to provide Coromon to you, a game we've poured our heart into. Coromon is our tribute to the classics of this RPG sub-genre. While staying loyal to the core gameplay, we wanted to add new features but also keep the iconic retro look, with a modernized pixel art style. Thank you for checking out Coromon. We hope you will enjoy the game as much as we enjoyed creating it!

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically Pokemon but better than anything that Gamefreak has been putting out in the recent years.Maybe it's because i'm a Gen 1/Gen 2 boomer, but Coromon really managed to scratch the itch in a way that reminded me of the days i spent on my Gameboy Color as a kid.I have yet to finish the game, but 100% recommend it. The price is more than reasonable, and it's very well polished. Difficulty isn't too high either, but challenging enough that the player will need to properly build their team pretty early on in the game (else some fights can turn out to be quite hard), which i think is a good balance.Overall a good 8/10 monster-taming game, you won't regret it if you like the genre !
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: I have not donated anything to Coromon and I am one of the best Coromon players.I recommend it to other gamers since the visuals are great. The Pokémon, or "coromon," you will encounter and capture each have their own distinct appearance. The animations for each ability are fantastic. Because the finale is so brief, the narrative line may not be all that excellent. There is nothing you can do after the game except capture the perfect or "shiny" coromon and PVP against other players. The coromon potency, or "shiny" system, is one of the greatest because the greater the potency of the coromon, the better the stats. In contrast to Pokemon, even if you receive a shiny, your stats may still be subpar. This is not a pay to win game since you must work for practically everything in this game, such as gold for better quality spinners, potent scents, and perfect coromon. There are no quick cuts for the three factors I stated previously. There is no monetization, but you may make a donation and receive rewards that will help you in the game. However, the advantages will not lead players to become overpowered because all of the rewards obtained by contributing money to Coromon may also be obtained by putting in a lot of time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun and addictive game, reminds me of a game you'd play on a Gameboy, for hours trying to beat. (They kept the save button feature, maybe not the best carry over feature) It does offer autosave but it saves every 20 mins...so make sure to save. Aside from that the story line is not like the game you're thinking of, the idea of catching the coromon is the same, with 3 spins to capture the coromon. However the coromon do not have much of any resemblance to the game you're thinking about right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game that improves on an already proven successful formula and genre!I have been playing since the demo released and watching the growth and development of the game has been absolutely inspiring. The devs are fantastic, have taken all critiques and feedback into consideration and continued to improve the game alongside the community until it's launch. If you enjoy monster taming? I highly suggest giving Coromon a chance. The quality of art and sound is top tier, the level of care and attention to detail in the mechanics and general quality of life is refreshing and the devs have succeeded in making a game that is not only charming but feels good to play. Thanks again team!*EDIT*It's since come to my attention that a few people have had issue with the smaller move/creature pool and increased puzzle elements and I felt I should add my take.It's impossible for a new indie game to come out of the gates competing with something like Pokemon with 20 years of creatures, moves and additions. That's just a fact that needs to be accepted.Also regarding the puzzles? I enjoyed them! It felt more refreshing to me to have some different gameplay aspects instead of the traditional pokemon formula of endless trainers and battles which...really gets repetitive and boring after a while and makes a short route feel like hours of work. In comparison Coromon by breaking up the pacing with puzzles and variety has felt a much more refreshing experience! I barely even noticed the hours I've racked up.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad Pokemon clone tbh but it's not better in any shape or form either. Most of the evolutions are rather uninspired (much like Gen 1 Pokemon with 3 level evolutions), most moves I've gotten were just borderline pointless while others oneshot next to everything. The move pool the Mons learn goes counter to their type and supposed use (stats / skills). The RNG mechanic for potential in Mons is just as awful as the crappy IV Pokemon had. The encounter rate was mind-numbing, it's crazy. Walk two steps, fight, walk another step, fight.I lost interest after some 8 hours I guess and the first Titan defeated. If you're really into Pokemon but played them all to death (especially the really good mods the scene offers) then this might do it for you. But I just don't see anything setting this game apart or making it especially worth your time. It's also just very grindy with no exp share and just a few 25% or 50% exp held items. The difficulty customization people often point to is a neat idea but I personally just prefer a set challenge and not some stupid amount of settings ranging from brain-dead easy to pointless drag.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game but HATE the platformer puzzles. Waaaay to difficult for casual play. On steam deck it plays great. Not a battery killer. Offline is a plus. The puzzles infuriate me because of the controller lag from hell. I'd like yo get through the story but GD!If I had known atform style puzzles qere i  the game, I would not have purchased.The skill system character trees are awesome. No breeding but still fun. Story is better than Pokemon. Building mons is way more up front with lesser grind.For me though, I do not believe I will finish the game because of the mandatory infuriating puzzles that lock me in until finished.

_childDocuments_.review: It plays like Pokemon, feels like Pokemon and grindy like Pokemon, but with several interesting gimmicks that differentiate it from Pokemon, so that Nintendo won’t go Death Note on them.  So far I enjoy the game and I can adjust the difficulty anytime I want and I think most of the Coroman I’ve encountered was cool.  Love the sprite work and overall art style being simple and easy one the eyes instead of the need to make it photo-realistic.  There a puzzles and dungeons that require some thinking, so that's great and it also helps that the music isn’t terrible either.  If someone out there has a Pokemon itch that needs to scratch, I recommend buying this game to relief that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat the game. If you like old school pokemon games, you will probably love this game. At it's core this is a pokemon game, but when it comes to technicalities it's quite different. I also loved the references and subtle humour in disguise. I'm really hoping there will be a sequel. I also experienced a couple of bugs regarding steam achievements but the game itself had no flaws i can think of. Very well balanced and lots of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot to offer - but is marred by a memory leak. After 30 minutes or so, FPS will drop. Until they address this, the work around of relaunching every 30 minutes is all you can do. Supposedly the team is working on a mobile launch, fixes are not likely until that is released.The Good: the game is fun. battles are rewarding. Coromon are well designed and even though some far outperform - there is a focus on quality over quantity. There are no Coromon that are absolutely worthless. Game progression is fun, plenty of customization for your character if you care about that. The potential system is neat, adds different color variations. PvP is fun, there is a meta. Fast travel opens up fairly early. Story is good/great if you care about that.The Bad: previously mentioned memory leak, mobile release holding back updates, the potential system makes catching anything that isn't at least "potent" feel bad/pointless, grinding for "Perfect" encounters is a pain.The meh: Some people may be frustrated that their favorite monster is outclassed by another in the meta. The leveling system is fine/source of interesting items/ money. Music/graphics may not be your jam (but then you wouldn't be look at this game if that was the case)

It enjoys it's story and puzzles, has a LOT of pop culture and other references.It's Skill point system makes battles a little more tactical, stat changes matter a LOT in this. Coromon has a built in Nuzlocke difficulty, built in randomizers and a fully customizable game settings. The potential mechanic is fantastic, higher potential means stronger Coromon.You won't be dissapointed.Hopefully there'll be DLC or more to play in the future. Another region would be great!

_childDocuments_.review: Great pokemon like game. Yes, it has fewer monsters than pokemon but i think the quality of life choices they made in the design are great. Like being able to change traits, easy leveling to avoid too much grinding, etc.  Love that shinies are potent or perfect mons. And not just a product of chance that makes no difference. I like the pokemon x golden sun mechanics. Looks great, sounds great, lots of fun. Hope there's a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically just Pokemon Soul Silver but with better graphics, animations, and better quality of life features. Not perfect, right now I'd give it a 7/10But keep in mind this game just came out recently at the time of this review, and this team seem passionate about making an awesome monster catching/fighting game. They will keep it updated, and maybe even add dlc.So don't let some minor negative things or annoyances (like not being able to move the order of your coromon's attacks, like you could in pokemon) bother you too much because remember that they can and probably will update this regularly. Get enough people to buy it and they said they'll add multiplayer very shortly after release.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: As of patch 1.0.19, a lot of the gripes people had with this game have been improved. It does seem that the devs are working hard. I'm changing this to a positive review to show my support and appreciation, but there are still things reducing my motivation to play.Original review:I don't know if I can honestly recommend a game that I don't have any desire to finish...It's not a bad game. As a love letter to Pokemon, it's of great quality. However, it feels like the devs focused way more on the story and assets than they did on the actual experience of playing the game. Between the baffling lack of quality-of-life improvements and a terribly bland experience, this game does little to improve on the Pokemon formula.I want to love this game, and I hope that I will some day, but until the experience itself is made more enjoyable (or at least until the devs start communicating more with the community), it's going to stay on the shelf with a negative review.If you're looking for a high quality not-Pokemon game, it's worth your time. But I think I would personally rather play Pokemon fangames like Glazed and Infinity.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a game that seems to be clearly inspired by the old-style Pokemon games. However, I found that it added a lot of its own twists to the concept, along with an entire set of original creatures to collect, and a plot that I found to be both intriguing and entertaining to follow. I really enjoyed the 34 hours I spent running around in this world, and training my team, and I think most fans of Pokemon games will find a certain nostalgia and a lot of fun in playing Coromon!There are a lot of things I love about this game. First of all, many of the Coromon designs are so wonderful; Bittybolt was by far my favorite, though I was a huge fan of many of them, enough that I struggled with who to keep on my team of 6!Secondly, the environments and interaction mechanics were I think on the whole well thought-out, and the world was on the whole enjoyable to explore, finding little crevices and finding hidden items.Thirdly, the customization options I found to be great! Starting with your character customization, including hair color, accessories, etc., but extending to gameplay. At the very start you are able to choose what settings you want to play with, essentially customizing the game to be as easy or as challenging as you care to make it. There is even a randomization section, where you can customize what Coromon appear, how they evolve, and other elements. I really appreciate the inclusion, and would consider using some of these elements in future playthroughs!There was one major issue that I had that I thought worth mentioning as well. I noticed that when I started my play-through on a Mac, I wasn't receiving achievements, and it seems that a recent update caused a bug that caused the game to stop launching on my Mac. Fortunately I was able to pick up the save file on a different computer, but it seems like the experience on Macs is still being fine-tuned; I saw mentions that the launch issues were being patched, in the discussions on Steam, but if you are using a Mac maybe check out to be sure it will work okay for you! Also be aware if you are an achievement hunter that a lot of the achievements may be quite difficult to get, so be prepared to invest some time!Other than that, this game was honestly like a little burst of nostalgia, mixed with the excitement of exploring new things, and as a huge Pokemon fan I really enjoyed it! If it looks like something that's up your alley definitely check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a monster-tamer game heavily inspired by the Pokémon games. Here you’ll catch and raise monsters that will help you in battle throughout a classic RPG story. If Coromon is clearly a work of passion and really tries to improve the formula, it falls a bit short and delivers a very average experience that is at times frustrating and tedious. It is however a game that any fan of the genre should try. If not ground-breaking it is at least a nice experience with stunning visuals and cute monsters. Coromon labels itself as a modern take on the classic monster-taming genre. Is the 2022 title that much of a twist ? let’s find out.  The strength of Coromon probably resides in its amazing pixel art. The game is aesthetically very pleasing, from it’s very simple yet colourful view from above when you move around the map to the very detailed background whenever you enter a fight. The game is full of colours and is downright inspiring itself of all the popular video games aesthetics. But what makes the pixel art that great is that it’s combined to really good animations and makes the whole feels very articulate and organic. This is especially true in regard to the monsters’ animations and their move. However, some of those animations can be a bit long and it can be very frustrating not to be able to skip them in battle. Another weird animation choice was the usage of emojis to convey emotions during dialogues. I can understand the limitations of 2D games, but they were often not working with some serious parts of the story. If the pixel art of the game is quite remarkable, the music on the other hand is a bit “classic” and nothing seems particularly ground-breaking. _childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews very often so this'll probably be all over the place. Had a lot of fun with this. I liked being able to basically make any team that I wanted and cruise on through. The story is passable but I didn't buy the game for the story. Bought it for the beautiful sprite work and gosh is it a sight to behold. The animated sprites are absolutely gorgeous to look at. The music is okay, inoffensive at best, at least to me. The variety of mons was nice. I found myself catching many things I wasn't initially interested in just to see what they would evolve into which is how I found one of my favorite lines; Moffel. Didn't care for that little guy but once he evolved into Digmow, it was over. Dugterra is also fantastic. Another monster that was worth the wait and trouble, Mino. Completely useless to me when it was a little thing but when it evolved, was a mainstay. Completely decimated just about everything, especially with the ability to raise it's attack and speed after every monster defeated. Criminal. Love that guy. Small but I enjoyed that you could change the spinner it was caught in. I liked having my fire types in fire spinners, etc. Another thing is being able to raise the potential of a monster to basically make them shiny, higher stats and all. Can only do it once per monster but it's pretty cool all things considered. Only found the scripted perfect ones out in the wild but was still pretty cool to have my normal little ones turned into potent just with luck. Also there's exp share items which is GREAT when you want to add a new addition to your team that is not on the same level. Or one that hasn't evolved yet and is becoming obsolete (Looking at you Mino).Battles were fun albeit easy(except for one, my favorite actually). Boss battles were more on the tedious side but not too hard. I think they would be the only real complaint I do have for this game. The final boss was especially annoying in this regard. Ginger my Toravolt absolutely carried me through that battle. Speaking of my favorite battle actually takes place towards the end of the game. You go back to the main campus and are forced to fight The game has a few difficulty options, even allowing to play as a nuzlock which is pretty cool in itself. I may return to play it on a higher difficulty but I enjoyed just how casual it is. I've never really been good at min/maxing out at team. I just like to hit a button and watch the health bar drop to zero. This gave me that.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a game I can't help but enthusiastically want to throw at everyone I can. As someone whose happiest, most memorable experiences with a certain other franchise (the name of which we shall leave out of this review, but you know it) were during its third, fourth, and fifth iterations, this is a game that hits all of those sweet spots that other imitations and even that series itself have failed to deliver on.Exploring a new world, finding new and interesting creatures at every turn, with gameplay that's quick and snappy and just the way I like it in a game like this. It's something I've been craving from a game for years and years that I thought I wouldn't be able to experience again without picking up old games in that other franchise.If you, like me, have been hankering for a monster collecting game that scratches that itch that the "real" ones just haven't been able to, you might find exactly what you've been hoping for in Coromon. This is a game made with a lot of love, FOR people who have a lot of love for monster collecting games, and every new turn has been a blast. Between just the demo and only an hour or so of the full game alone, I've been having more fun with this game than other games like it have provided in a long time, and I can't wait to dive back in and experience more of it. Heck, I'll probably come back to update this and make a more detailed review once I'm done with the game proper-- and when it's not launch day and I'm not in a hurry to get back to playing!Not so long story short, I emphatically recommend this game. I can't say it's for everyone, necessarily, but if you're looking for a game about exploring and catching and taming monsters, Coromon should be at the top of your list - yes, even above that other one.Also I really really want a big, squishy Sheartooth plushie. TRAGsoft and Freedom Games, please make it happen, yeah?-----------------Playing the game some more, having already posted this, I want to make note of some things that I think folks might appreciate knowing about in particular:- The sound design of the game is a treat. The sound effects of all the moves have impact to them and add a lot to the battles, and the soundtrack is just awesome- you get new tracks where you might not expect, and they're all great.- Arenas are all unique based on where you are, and it gives battles a real visual flair here that helps you feel more "in" the world during combat.

For some people that's worth it, but for me, this game was boring and went nowhere fast.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Does what Gamefreak don‘t, 'nuf said. Possibly the best Pokemon clone I've ever had the pleasure of playing up to now, while still bringing enough fresh design elements to the table to firmly stand on its own. Without further ado: if you consider yourself a Pokemon fan from the first hour even slightly, this is a must. You will most likely kick yourself in the arse later on for not buying this game, seriously. Don't get turned off by the overall youthful look and presentation. I feel like this game tries way less to have kids and teenagers be its main target group than Pokemon. It feels more fleshed out and isn't afraid of relying on the player using his brains, which is great.I want to give a big shout out to the BGM designer(s) also. The soundtrack is often reminiscent of Final Fantasy games (8 and 9 in particular) and I'm awestruck how well crafted those songs are, considering their shortness. I don't know why the devs didn't invest more in the soundtrack people, it would most certainly have paid off. As it stands now, it sometimes feels as though the composer(s) felt like they had to wrap things up, because the devs gave them a loop time of 60sec max to work with, which is a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: "What if Nintendo made a pokemon game where they implemented frequently  requested features from the community?"I was expecting a scuffed pokemon experience but what I got was a better pokemon experience than Nintendo has ever given us. This is very much gen 3/4 pokemon taken to a modern stage.The developers are clearly passionate about Coromon, there's no mistaking they wanted to make the best monster collector game they could make. Proven by even post-release updates that keeps improving the game.The game supports PvP, has only 1 version so all Coromons are obtainable for you, and it has its own spin on mechanics and storyline (no gyms, boss battles).Also supports multiple modes we had to mod pokemon games for. Such as Nuzlocke and Randomizer features. AND you can change the rules for your game at any point by going back to the computer where you set your rules.And personally I really like the mono-type on mons. In Pokémon past gen1 it felt like the further we went the more obligatory it was for all mons to be two types (even adding types to previous mono-type pokemons in later gens).Coromon is an excellent high quality game for 1/4th the price of a pokemon game but x4 the quality.

All of the elements that made Pokemon fun are here, with perhaps some different "spices" here and there that does make Coromon it's own thing. I'd give it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is the Dark Souls of Pokemon games.Difficulty modes? Built in randomizer? Custom stats? Attractive visuals? It's like an alternate timeline where Pokemon spent the past 25 years improving their video games.It really makes me happy to see a new generation of game developers whose entire motivation boils down to "you ruined my favorite game, so I'm going to make my own version."I really love this game. I think it's just about the best Pokemon clone (which I absolutely do not mean as a derogatory description, there is nothing wrong with more pokemon games and Coromon wears its pokemon inspiration on its sleeve) that I've played. It’s been a long time since a game made me giddy the same way I was when I got Red version on the Gameboy but Coromon got me.  The last Pokémon games felt like a step back.  This game feels like the earlier gen games but with huge QoL updates.The Coromon roster is so good! Definitely felt like quality over quantity. So much variety in designs and I never felt like I found a Coromon that was just straight up outclassed by another one. Even in single player, creating a team is so strategic and rewarding because every Coromon has a role on a team. Balance is nearly perfect. Trainer battles remained challenging throughout the game. Even with some light XP grinding I never felt overleveled for an area. Bosses were REALLY fun, too. Challenging and formidable. Even had to retry a couple times for the 2nd boss. Strategy is also much more important than Coromon levels, which feels really rewarding.Writing is cute and fun. Very charming. The stakes of the story were compelling, which is refreshing in this genre. The art and animations are equally amazing. Not just the talent but the nostalgic feelings they evoke. This really felt like an upscaled GBA game, and the Coromon have insane personality in their movements and body language, and everything is designed very clearly. It is a delight to look at.I feel like the one thing Coromon does a lot better than recent Pokémon games is have distinct environments and towns. The level design is consistently engaging, which is really impressive for this genre. The puzzles are compelling without being frustrating and every "dungeon" feels distinct. It's refreshing and a nice change from the Pokémon games while still retaining the essence of it. There's a lot of customization to make your play through fit your style or more challenging (there's even an in-game nuzlocke set of rules).Honestly I had a blast and can only encourage anyone that’s a fan of these types of games to try it out. For the price it’s absolutely worth it. It's one of very, very few pokemon-likes that actually captures the sense of adventure and discovery of early pokemon games and even improves on it, rather than just blindly copying them and hoping for the best.And now that the new update is out (including a new ending storyline) I’m actually excited to get off work and play some more. I’ve been so burnt out on gaming in general but this I’m loving.So happy to see Pokemon fans have grown up now to create more games for this genre. What a time to be alive!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a pokemon-esque creature catching, turn-based RPG. Overall, I would reccommend this game whole-heartedly. It has some minor flaws, but is a really fun and challenging experience. Graphics: Coromon is done in a beautiful pixel artstyle. All the creature sprites are well done and the world/background art looks great as well. If you miss how some of the older GBA/DS Pokemon games looked, you will love the look of this game.Creatures: Overall, I think the vast majority of the creatures have great designs and are animated well. Some of their names are mediocre, but still a good roster for a creature catching game. The only major complaint I have is that there is not a lot of creatures in the game. I really hope this game gets a larger rooster though updates or dlc, cause why not have more of a good thing? Other than that, I feel some tweaks to a few creature's movesets would be nice. A few coromon I have encountered have had such poor movepools that it makes it a struggle to use them despite their stats being great. Other than that, I'm quite satisfied with the creatures in this game. The Devs clearly a quality focused approached Difficulty: One thing many will notice is that Coromon has very customizable difficulty. The game can be as hard or easy as you want it to be. Even playing on normal difficulty can be challenging at times, so this game does not struggle with being too easy like some recent pokemon games.Length: This game seems to be a good length for its price. As of writing this I am 23 hours in and about halfish way through. Although keep in mind that I'm the completionist type who likes to explore and do side-content, so that increases my playtime. Summary: Coromon is beautiful pokemon-esque game with a small but high-quality rooster that has done a great job at keeping my attention and hitting that GBA/DS era nostalgia. If you like this type of game, I highly recommend giving it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable monster collector that's similar enough to Pokemon for people to pick up and understand, but with enough differences to stand out and be its own thing. Would have liked duel-types for type variation, but overall I'm really enjoying it.Edit after finishing and patch updates:The last few areas really lean hard into ice physics and block pushing puzzles, which slowed the pace to a crawl and made things super frustrating. Also, the patch introduced a new plot that retroactively affected my save file, introducing a load of high-stakes stuff that I had no context for. It's not quite enough for me to change my recommendation, but it means I'm less likely to suggest it to friends, and I don't know if I'll continue the post-game adventure or start a new save.Also, the new crystal currancy and the daily missions were really unnecessary.

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice to finally have a good Pokemon game again. This is without question trying to emulate older Pokemon games with some tweaks here and there, a few highlights for me:Built in difficulty system which includes Nuzlocke option. Should be noted I've only played on what the game calls "insane" difficulty which is the Nuzlocke mode, so many game features are disabled for me.No HMs, instead you, the player, slowly gain upgrades and abilities which serve the purpose of HMs, thereby allowing you to use whatever Coromon you want.SP system, similar to Temtem here except it doesn't allow the AI to kill itself with poor SP management. If you don't know, instead of individual moves having a limit on use, the Coromon has a SP guage which must be spent to use moves. You can rest instead of attacking to recharge it, and various moves can reduce, replenish or increase the cost of SP adding a new layer to strategy.Modified shiny system. There are two colour variations beyond the standard and they represent the Coromon's potential. With the colour variations only happening for Coromon with very high or Perfect potential.Otherwise this really feels like Gen 3-5 pokemon, but I can enforce Nuzlocke rules, which for me at least was a game winner right there.A final note for the Nuzlockers out there, the game makes one excellent change to Nuzlocking, it limits your catches by giving you an item which summons a Coromon from the area you are in when used. You can be anywhere and it will summon from every encounter table on the current map. This means you can spend some time training and learning the local Coromon before you decide to get your encounter, allowing you to prepare a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Mmm, this is good. The newer Pokémon games have lost a lot of their charm imo and this game manages to reclaim a lot of that original magic whilst having its own style that elevates it beyond being just a Pokémon clone. There's some nice QOL that the newer Pokémon games could learn from and some really fun ideas, like the coupons for the shop to encourage you to make one big purchase of supplies and the teleporter to instantly fast travel to places you've already been. The game is a bit more challenging than regular Pokémon too, so those supplies are going to be necessary. No breezing through without any heals here. But what really nails it for me is the choice of monsters. I actually found it hard to choose who to put in my party cos all the options are good. There's no obvious trash mons that you're never gonna touch (looking at you, Dunsparce). I feel like I could make multiple viable parties out of the ones I've caught so far and it's really hard to choose who to drop when you want to bring in a new mon to try out. There's also a smattering of puns and references which always appeal to me too, giving this more humour than the competition. I can't wait to get deeper in. It's definitely worth a look.
