_childDocuments_.review: I'll edit this review as I play.Looks great, plays great, not fan of the palette but it's clear this has been made by absolute fans of Pokémon strategy, and I could feel early on that combats might eventually become quite interesting.However, a couple negatives :- Keyboard controls are awkward at first, but the WASD layout is all right, allowing to play with one hand. Still, for such game, the absence of customizable layout is weird.- Menu navigation could be better.Most notably when you wanna switch mons, the game pops another window showing the full party, while it's already on displayed in the pause menu.Pressing down at the bottom of a list (and contrary) won't bring back to the first option, so when you want to save, you gotta scroll through everything.In menus like appearance editor, when you hold right from the rightmost option of a window, you get moved to the next window rather than on the lower left of the same window.This sounds like nothing, but these added together make menu feel more awkward than they could be.- Goal-oriented aspect early on.Some mechanics feel like urging me to complete something rather than just doing whatever I want. I'm mainly talking about the loads of milestones and rare Potent mons that I met early on, making me go "Gotta do this now, catch that now, do these quests, check my rewards, etc".Pokémon is a lot chiller on this aspect, with its very broad main goals : progress to the next area, capture all pokémon. Since these come naturally and there's no time constraint, Pokémon allows to do whatever you like without any pressure, and you only take on quests if you want to.I can choose to ignore Coromon's milestones and Potential, but these still put pressure on me for doing things rather than enjoying myself.Being able to choose the "EVs" is very interesting competitively, but I obviously invested everything into ATK from start to help oneshotting stuff.The SP regen after a fight is a real bummer. In Pokémon, even with a oneshot attack, you can only wonder whether you'll get out of a cave before running out of PP/items.In Thunderous Cave, I had mons with 6 to 10 levels above the wildlife, EV-maxed in attack, so regardless how long I'd spend there, I'd mostly oneshot anything, replenish more SP than I spent and get xp on top of that.There're enemies that deal status on contact, excepted the game also gave me an item to counter that very early.Rather early, there are tools to precisely lower enemy hp.Cubzero (ice starter) learns Splash at level 20, which is basically a budget False Swipe, very good to precisely lower enemy hp.In the worst case, the battlepass thing gives Kiwano Rock on tier 8 that reflects 15% dmg, which is also a potent capture tool.It's nice to get those early, but I might've prefered to get these later on, making me really crave for tools to accurately weaken foes, which would be really satisfying once I get them.Shop coupons are a fun addition, but pressured me into playing as greedy as possible to get absurd discounts. Since coupons are ultimately money pouches, I think capping the limit of refunds wouldn't be a bad idea.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Pokemon-clone. Perfect balance of story/gameplay/puzzles. Unfortunately, ends rather abruptly with no real post-game.5/5 Mechanics. It is a little *too* easy to overlevel and breeze through the first half of the game though.5/5 Sprites and animations (seriously, they're very impressive).4/5 Level design. Each area felt unique and had just enough exploration to not feel like a hallway simulator. Would have liked to see a few more places to go back to and use abilities you gain later.4/5 Music. Some real bangers and it never drones on. I had some old school Rare vibes in a few areas that really made it lively.*Special shout-out to the bosses. _childDocuments_.review: Coromon is very obviously a Pokemon clone, and in some regards (for e.g. soundtrack, world size, no. of monsters, etc.), a clearly lower budget clone. However, the game is very, very charming (something newer Pokemon games have stopped being), and it is super successful in satisfying that Pokemon itch. The starters are cute, and most Coromon evolve into pretty cool looking monsters.The game introduces its own unique mechanics into the familiar turn based system, all of which work together well, but with some experience it's easy to see the way to easily exploit mechanics. The game also attempts to place more meaning on the 'shiny' mechanic, but honestly you can ignore it for the most part in a casual run through. The game also allows the player to customise the difficulty in a number of ways to have a really catered playthrough, which is really cool of the devs.The best parts of the game for me would be the 'dungeons' that culminate in 'boss-fights', analogous to the 'gym' and 'gym-leader' setup in Pokemon. In this game though, the dungeons can be pretty serious sometimes, and combined with the simultaneous exploration and puzzle-solving, it really did make me nostalgic for the first Pokemon games I played. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Its fine so far. Very obviously inspired by pokemon, has many of the same beats (especially in the beginning). The story however, is terrible. Instead of letting you explore the world and competing in some kind of battle system...it is a story with multiple dimensions, macguffin stones, and other junk. The XP boosters make it way too easy, if you just take a couple minutes to do some training, also incentivizes you to just use one coromon to do all the work, while the others just sit back and gain XP...pretty cheap.  The worst part is how slow it plays. You HAVE to sit through all the cut scenes, and dialogue. There isn't a fast skip option (i haven't checked the settings, but it should be standard).  There is no summary on the moves you are using so you have to memorize what each does, which is just annoying.  I just wish it was a bit more open, with more things to explore that don't have anything to do with the main story.  It's just very straightforward, go there, do the thing, go to the next thing, and do the thing....it literally won't let you proceed to areas with high level enemies....it has someone stop you or a barrier in the way that can only be taken down by the thing you need to get next...and I know pokemon had some of that, but it felt more expansive than this ever will.  I still find that most of the moves are useless, some don't even seem to be necessary...ever....just worthless all around. Like a move that charges up your next move for double damage....however, it costs 3 SP, and using my fire skill costs 4...so I'll save 1 SP, and open myself up to being hit...if I don't kill the enemy with the first hit. There is no real way to know how much damage you will do...because no stats are available in match...strange choice.  IDK, its fine, don't spend much and don't expect alot.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a monster taming game, it means that the whole purpose of the game is to catch monsters and make them battle each other against other tamers, while progressing in a story. The gameplay feels really close to Pokemon while bringing new mechanics, like the modules that you can get for your gauntlet. There are 114 Coromons to catch, that and their shiny forms. Let's talk about the shiny system, there are 3 versions of a Coromon, standard, potent and perfect. You get the idea, the more potent a coromon is or close to it's perfect form, the stronger it becomes. The game also makes the hunt for shinys really fun and easier than in Pokemon, which is a good thing. I'd say that one downside is that the story is brought rapidly to conclusion, but it makes up for it in replayability.With all that said, I can definitly recommend the game in it's current state. Bugs are rare or literally inexistant and each Coromon is unique in it's own way. I haven't really touched PvP, but I assume that a 3v3 match system is really inovative.

_childDocuments_.review: A time waster. The game is full of padding and obstacles designed to slow you and your progress down. Any time I start to enjoy the game I get hit by another annoyance. I am the 1 percent of players that has the level 99 Coromon. The only ppl who beat this game were streamers. Just look at the global acheivements. I think I have 8-10 gold acheivements. Only 57 percent of ppl have collected the starter Coromon. Only 37 percent have Evolved a coromon. The percentages keep dwindling below 25 from here on out. Its really sad.The game is boring until you reach the forest with the mushrooms that you pick up. They're Coromon finally drop decent experience points that make grinding and team building finally feel worth it.  This game has Layering issues with its plants, mushrooms, fire, desert, and perfumes. Even some of the ice tiles do not line up correctly or match adjacent tiles. if your a gamer You might not notice. But anyone that develops game can see it.The desert part looks nice but slows the game to a crawl. There is not enough Coromon to keep the desert interesting. It is really noticeable in the pyramid area. The digging portion of the game is just bad padding. The spooky area has some visual cool stuff but drags game play to a crawl. The puzzle is annoying filler. The Purgil afterlife section is boring and pointless. Some of the Coromon are beautifully animated and look well though out but others are mid or just lacking all around. Some have still frame animations but it just barely moves left to right like a wave. Its an odd contrast. This game doesn't have as much content as pokemon and it feels like a project cut short. Theres about 100 cormon and 20 recolor/variants. Then theres 120  special recolors and 120 Perfect Coromon. There are better fan games and even better monster designs on Deviant art. This game is 50 percent a waste, 30 percent meh and 20 percent good. This game did everything possible to not get sued by game freak. But it barely devolops its own identity. This game feels like boot leg Fire Red.Catching Coromon is a chore. It is so easy to kill low levels. Even if you have 2 cormon fight each other with similar levels. Its like bashings rocks together. You use Slam to deal 20ish damage. Then your opponent charges up and deal double damage. Then triple damage. Just use a cormon that has the opposite element of what you want to catch. Other wise use the heart stone. I really don't want to eat fruits or cakes every 2 minutes when a Coromon has a status affect. Like I just ignore them. I have never had a Coromon fall asleep, Nor have I been able to put one to sleep. There is a sleep spinner So I assume that sleeping Coromon are in the game but maybe they forgot about that mechanic. Coromon only get drowsy. The purchasable skins look like dumb color washes. Like Blue swurmy, Pink Swurmy. 90 percent are trash. Can we stop daily logins and weekly logins. It sucks and its dumb. I want to play a game cuz its fun and rewarding. Not because I will miss out on content if I don't religously play every in my library. The bad out way what little good this game has. Look I caught a shiny, to bad its not a Perfect Coromon. I have only caught 1 (Perfect) cormon so far. So good luck wasting your youth trying to catch them all. I really wish that someone would make Monster rancher 4 but better.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for those classic monster collector and trainer vibes, this might be just what you're looking for. It is for me.The mechanics are familiar yet different enough to where it has it's own feel to it. The typings aren't too hard to figure out after battling with them. I like how some typings are specific to moves and not the Coromon themselves, such as cutting, heavy, magic, and so on. They don't use power points specific to the moves, but the Coromon's overall stamina where different moves require more and you can spend a turn to rest and regain stamina.The Coromon themselves have great design. I love the potency mechanic of the game. Instead of shinies, there's 3 tiers on a 1-21 number scale. 1-16 I believe are normal, giving normal coloration and stats based on the rank, 17-20 are potent with a new coloration and stats based, and 21 is perfect with a unique coloration and best stats. It does make it to where I prefer partying only potent or higher Coromon, but for a singleplayer runthrough it shouldn't really matter.The character customization is definitely better than the older Pokemon, but it could still use a little more. It took a little getting used to not being a silent protagonist, but it's not a big deal. Once I accepted that I respond to people with text I began to really pay more attention to the world and story, which so far is really unique and fun to what most monster trainer games have.It has difficulty settings from everything to healing after each fight to once a Coromon faints, it's released. Things like shop discounts for supplies are options too so you can make the game as relaxed or as challenging as you like. I went for the default experience to get a feel for what they want the average player to experience, which is a nice middle ground. I'll have Coromon faint and sweep depending on the matchups, and I like that they'll throw some tough fights at you now and then.All in all, I recommend giving it a try if you're a fan of the genre. Not all Coromon are out, some evolution trees aren't complete so you can't finish evolving everything you catch, but I can't wait to see when they have their dex finished. 4/5, but could easily be a 5/5 once all the planned features and Coromon are completed.#TeamBabyShark

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)After 623 hours, I can confidently say Coromon has so much to offer that it’s hard to put down. With a deep turn-based combat system, unique creature designs, and a story that’s both nostalgic and refreshing, Coromon is a gem for any monster-catching fan. Here’s why I’ve spent so many hours in this world:Coromon is a true treat for fans of strategy and classic RPGs. Every encounter requires thought, as you’re not just mindlessly grinding; each battle is a test of skill and tactics. With unique skill trees, abilities, and elemental interactions, the game keeps you on your toes. This depth makes battles feel rewarding, and even after hundreds of hours, there's always room to experiment with new strategies.Highlights:Skill Customization: The ability to build your Coromon with unique skills and traits adds incredible depth.Challenging Encounters: Every battle requires strategy, from elemental advantages to tactical move timing.The creature designs in Coromon are a perfect blend of nostalgia and originality. Each Coromon feels unique, with well-designed evolutions and backstories that make them more than just stats on a screen. There’s a wide variety, ensuring that finding, catching, and training them never feels stale. Some have become true “companions” on my journey, and the thrill of encountering new ones remains strong, even after so many hours.Highlights:Distinct Designs: Coromon has its own unique aesthetic, with designs that stand out.Varied Evolutions: Evolving your Coromon is both satisfying and full of surprises.The world of Coromon is vibrant and filled with character, from lush forests to mysterious caves. The story is an engaging blend of adventure, mystery, and humor, with unexpected twists that keep you invested. It feels familiar, but there’s a layer of modern storytelling that makes it feel fresh and immersive. Plus, exploring every corner to find hidden Coromon and rare items is a joy in itself.Highlights:Rich Environments: Each area is carefully crafted and full of surprises.Engaging Plot: The story strikes a great balance of humor and mystery, with plenty of lore.Once you complete the main story, Coromon offers plenty of endgame content, from battles and tournaments to finding rare and legendary creatures. The game’s constant updates keep the experience fresh and add extra challenges, making the journey truly endless. There’s always something new to do or discover, which is a massive bonus for completionists and dedicated trainers alike.Highlights:Continuous Updates: Keeps the game interesting with new features and events.Challenging Endgame: Offers depth for long-time players looking for new experiences.Coromon perfectly balances classic monster-taming with new mechanics that add depth, strategy, and replayability. After 623 hours, I can say it’s a game worth every second. The attention to detail, engaging battles, and unique creatures make it stand out, and it’s clear the developers have crafted it with love. If you’re looking for a game that blends nostalgia with fresh, strategic gameplay, Coromon is a fantastic choice.

_childDocuments_.review: After a few play sessions i have to say i like this game.  You can really tell it's had a lot of love put into it by the devs.  they set out to make something familiar, but also a bit prettier, and they absolutely succeeded.  They didn't try to re-invent the wheel, which i think turned a few players off to the game.  But they never implied that was their intention....  this is a nostalgia trip with some nice upgrades.Like a lot of players i absolutely love the option to change some very frustrating settings and make the game a bit easier and less of a grind.  Would have killed for this in pokemon emerald lol...  You can set it up so your team members heal each time they level up, lessening about a thousand trips to the healing center per play through.  you can even allow players to steal other trainers team members right in the middle of a battle.  I may try this on my 2nd play through, but haven't done it yet : )It's still a grind in a lot of ways, like pokemon, tons of repetition, and if you're not into that, you may not like it.  Again, they didn't really add anything groundbreaking to the genre.  They just cleaned it up and presented it with a better paint job.  I have no problems with this, in fact it's exactly what i was hoping for, but others may have had other ideas of what this game would be.  I'd give it an 8 out of 10, good game, worth the price in my opinion, but if you're wavering, just wait for a sale, it will go down eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon peaked my interest when searching for a Pokemon-like game that wasn't Pokemon. I wanted to find a game that had the same appeal and charm as the Gameboy Advance/early DS era of Pokemon, combined with building a team of 6 creatures to battle with in turn based combat, and thankfully, this game is just about everything I had hoped for. Coromon takes the tried and true formula of "creature collector" games and tweaks it just enough for it to feel like a fresh new adventure. From new creatures and methods of capturing them via "spinners," to boss battles that are in place of gym leaders from Pokemon, to the unique biomes and characters around this new world to discover; Coromon takes nearly everything enjoyable about this genre of games and elevates them enough to make it just as entertaining as many AAA titles.One of the biggest plus' this game has is the ability to customize your experience however you like. There are a multitude of ways to play, such as making the game incredibly hard and tedious for yourself, or making it easy enough to feel like you're just going through the motions to get to the story. In addition to the four difficulties to choose from, you can also change things to give yourself a more grueling challenge, such as randomizing items, evolutions, trainer Coromon, etc., or giving yourself a Nuzlocke-esque challenge by disabling running from battles, limiting items you can use in battle, or different variations of restrictions on catching Coromon in your playthough. The customization in this game is far and away some of the best in the genre for tailoring your experience exactly how you would like to play.Another impressive feature is the creature designs and traits. There are a multitude of fantastic looking Coromon, all with unique combinations of attacks to use and animation similar to that of Pokemon Black/White. All Coromon have 3 levels of strength called "Potential" that will determine how strong they get upon leveling up. Any Coromon 1-16 is Standard, 17-20 is Potent and 21 is Perfect. There are only specific ways to encounter Perfect Coromon, which provides an extra challenge not only for finding them but also for capturing them as they have a lesser capture rate. The reward is definitely worth the effort, as Perfect Cormon add extra bonus stats for every level up, making them significantly stronger than Standard Coromon of the same level.All is not perfect with Coromon, however, as I did think the story lacked a bit of refining. There easily could have been more expansion on certain elements that would have made the story feel fully fleshed out. The ending of said story also felt too abrupt, not offering much to chew on after the final climax, and the post game content isn't much to ride home for. You do get some new challenges, but any hope of rematching the Titans, getting more insight on the aliens, or seeing how things have changed after the finale are all but missing from the game.Coromon is a fun alternative for those looking for a creature collecting game that brings the same feel as the older games in the Pokemon franchise and need a bit more to chew on in the genre. The terrific sprites and art style paired with an interesting premise and unique world to explore make this a game worth playing. Replayability can be hit or miss, as there are a vast array of customization options to feel like a new playthrough is enough to differentiate from a normal playthrough. However, once you have gotten to the end of the story, you may be feeling left a bit unsatisfied by a lackluster conclusion after your epic journey. I believe if a DLC were to come out to expand on those elements, it could greatly improve the experience, and give players a more satisfying conclusion.As the game is by itself right now, I would give this a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it called Coromon because the magazine that frequently leaks Pokémon news is called CoroCoro?Pretty damn good Pokémon clone, all things considered. Hell, it does a lot of things better than Pokémon. It's well-balanced, the potential system is so much more fun than shiny hunting, the spritework and animations are phenomenal, repels are timer-based instead of step-based, you can change moves around on the fly, devolve your Coromon, change their color palettes, increase the battle speed, increase the overworld speed, change the type of spinner your Coromon was caught in, *DEEP BREATH* there are no HMs, no catchable legendaries, no intrusive gimmicks, and the story is...okay, well, it isn't that different from any other Pokémon game.It doesn't need a phenomenal story, but the writing did take a noticeable "meme-y" dip in quality once you hit the desert town, but it thankfully picks back up afterwards. At least there weren't gyms in this one.I vastly preferred the big boss fights you had at the end of each area, those were far more challenging. Actually, this whole game was more challenging than any Pokémon game I've ever played (if we're not counting Johto's insane level curves).As far as negatives go, I missed Grass Types more than I expected I would. Those usually have a lot of fun designs and that was just absent from Coromon. There's no dual-typing, which means most designs don't stray too far from their gimmick. And while there are quite a few solid designs in the game, I noticed there were a surprising amount of...slime-inspired Coromon? Every type except Normal and Ice has at least one, with a couple having two. I mean, none of them are BAD, but I just found it a little weird that there were so many lmaoAnyway this game is pretty fun. If the Pokémon formula has gotten stale but you are still itching to play a monster tamer, give Coromon a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: A lighthearted Pokemon clone with a splash of Golden Sun. The gameplay is fundamentally Pokemon with a few tweaks and QoLs and a fun shiny/IV system. The monster designs lean toward the "cool" side rather than cute, with earthier, dark color palettes. There are a bunch of novel moves and abilities, but the elemental type system is unfortunately a bit more simplified than Pokemon's 18 type system however. Also the monster count is about 110, which might leave collectors hungry for more.The plot/writing is whimsical and adventurous, it is structured like a traditional jrpg where you travel the world and help various people with their problems while collecting what you need. The spritework is gorgeous and detailed and definitely the strongest aspect of the game. Despite the strong art, I think the attack sound effects are a bit weak.Difficulty is well balanced, a tad harder than a basic Pokemon campaign on normal mode. But there are lots of custom difficulties modifiers and options to crank up the difficulty as you please. Very well polished, meaty JRPG with a fair bit of replay value. Postgame is currently lacking but apparently free DLC is on the way. Great fun for monster collectors and team builders.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little Pokemon alternative with some extra sprinkles thrown in.Unfortunately, it suffers from a lot of the same problems as others in the genre, such as all of the moment to moment interactions being much too slow with no real way to speed them up (Menu navigation is a pain), and the game being monstrously too easy if you just stick to using one creature.The whole "Oh no, this super powered monster is going to beat the crap out of us!" followed immediately by defeating said monster in one or two attacks while taking negligible damage got old literal decades ago, as did spamming one of two high damage moves depending on the typing of your enemy - Granted, this is more a problem of the genre than of this game specifically.The ability to alter the difficulty in such a specific way is nice, but making it harder doesn't change how the aforementioned strategy plays out, in fact it only really makes it even more optimal, thus urging you to do it.Better written than any Pokemon game I can think of, though that isn't a high bar - Your mileage may vary when it comes to the ambient writing, depending on your tolerance for every single pun ever being made.The RNG is bananas, especially in the early game where variably multi-hitting, non-100% accuracy attacks are rampant (Like a move that hits 1 to 3 times and has 90% accuracy) and you run into a local weather effect that just gives you a random chance to miss on your turn.It looks pretty good, and the Coromon sprites are nicely animated with some sub-pixel shading stuff going on, it's a shame that there are only 114 of them to collect - Probably a lot for a small team, especially with them being all new designs, but still a fair fewer than the 151 of the first generation of Pokemon.Only 7 types too, with no dualtypes (Technically 13 types, but 6 of them are for attacks only.)Without making enough changes to keep anything fresh or avoid the problems of older Pokemon games, this title really can't afford to be offering up a worse experience than said games, which it seems to be doing.If you're curious about the genre but can't afford to get any of those new Pokemon games, or find some way to play any of the first 5 gens, then I guess you'll find some enjoyment out of this.If you're a fan or veteran of Pokemon then just... Play Emerald Randomisers or Kaizo Romhacks or something, lol.Seriously, the only thing I can really recommend about Coromon is its soundtrack, so go give that a listen.

_childDocuments_.review: So first I will state the obvious, yes, this is a lot like Pokemon. You run around catch creatures and make them battle. It's a system that works and that's why Gamefreak have done the same formula for 26 years. Coromon has put a breath of fresh air back into the genre. You start the game out with taking a new job as a battle researcher at this company and you're going through taking on research tasks and gathering information of more of the coromon. That's as much of the story I can go into without giving away the major plot points because this game while the story isn't revolutionary is better than "hey go out there and become the strongest trainer of the region". The puzzles in the game are not overly complex but not easy either. they take a decent amount of thought and make you feel smart when you complete them. Instead if gym leaders you will face off against a titan that you're trying to get their essence of. With this though is where I believe the game gets ridiculous. During normal progression once you get to the titan it's about 5 levels higher than your strongest coromon. For example the first titan was at level 25 and my strongest going into it the first time was about 19 with the lower ones being 15. So in order to beat it i had to do a pretty lengthy grinding session to do so, even getting my whole team to 21-23 i still struggled to defeat it. SO prepare for some lengthy grinding sessions before each boss. This game does play a lot like old school Pokemon with the more difficult puzzles, and of course the random encounters. THis is a feature some people will hate to see come in but as for me I absolutely loved it. It's like opening a present each time, you never know what you're going to get. This game also features two categories of Coromon that are more powerful than the normal Coromon with a palette swap. You can come across a potent or a perfect and these work a lot like how shinies in Pokemon. A potent has a 1 in 34 chance of appearing and a perfect is a 1 in 3000+ chance. I really enjoy this system and it makes them more rare but not so rare that they feel unobtainable. Overall I would reccomend this game to any turn based RPG fan and Pokemon fan if you're wanting a newer game that plays more like the older versions.

_childDocuments_.review: Given that this game covers a genre that I would very much love to see more games take a jab at, it's only natural that I'd give some thoughts on it. I'm giving it a thumbs up since I do not regret playing this game, but there are definitely features that was either underwhelming or just plain bad. And naturally, I will compare it to the Pokémon games since it quite obviously borrows a lot from that franchise in terms of gameplay. - The sprite quality is immaculate.- Lots of QoL additions that Pokémon games could take notes of.- Music feels very fitting and enjoyable.- Looks like all Coromon are fairly viable, obviously some more than others but if you do like a design visually then there are ways to make it work in your team.- Exploration is rewarded with plenty of chests and hidden items around all areas.- Very cooperative when it comes to what attacks you can have on your Coromons. Flash skills can be used endlessly, and previously learned moves can be re-activated on the fly.- The potency system allows you to allocate stat points to the stat you want, and it's easy to reset that investment.- While the sprites are great, the designs are overall rather underwhelming. Many species already get the point across from the base stage and then proceeds to just get bigger or more mature, while others can be described as "animal with its element added on top". It all works out in the end, but it was rare that the next evolution stage built further upon the concept or introduced something new.- Potency being linked to alternative color palettes. The potency system itself is fine. In Pokémon, I never bothered to look up what IVs my mons have, and I never hunted for shinys either. But with this system, it's like the game plants the idea in your head that any regularly colored Coromon isn't as strong as it could be, and if you do encounter one you already have in your team, you feel incentivized to replace it. Felt like a needless connection to what'd otherwise be a voluntary undertaking.- There are 13 types in the game, but only 6 of them exists as defensive types, or types the Coromon themselves will have. It's an interesting idea, but I'd rather have seen more of them as Coromon types to introduce more variety in designs and team setups. On a brighter note, the game can help you by displaying the type matchups so that you don't feel you need it all memorized.- The SP system, or Coromon's version of Pokémon's PP system. I understand the intent, where more powerful moves will consume more SP, thus adding a layer of strategy to not recklessly spend your energy. However, what actually happens is that regardless of what you do, you will feel punished. If you use moves with less SP cost you may take more damage, or drag out an encounter. If you end up spending your SP and is forced to skip a turn, you'll take damage or give the opponent a free turn too. I played with the option to refill all SP upon level up, and I still found this feature to be annoying at best. It could've been an easy fix if Coromon not on-field regenerated SP each turn to encourage switches, because as it is right now, it doesn't really add strategy, it just adds pressure.- You will often see yellow emojis during conversations. I suppose they're intended to ensure the player understands the current mood, but to me they were about as needed as sitcom laugh tracks. Sadly, no way to disable them in the settings.- While most interactions with NPCs have a comedic undertone, the main story is actually trying to be quite serious, only to not have an appropriately intense climax and you instead end up feeling that the game wants to wrap things up quickly. I personally also found the The game could've been more, but it also fulfilled my expectations and then some, so if I'd have to give it a score, it'd be around 6/10. It's a complete game, and for a monster catching game without Gamefreak's budget, it made a good job of rekindling the sensation of what the Pokémon games used to be.

_childDocuments_.review: As of the time of writing this review I have played approximately 6 hours of this game and I feel like I can already give a decent review.Whilst fundamentally I would recommend this game as it gives a pretty decent GBA era Pokemon experience, it is worth knowing that I personally feel there are some core issues in the game that could be worked upon to increase the fluidity of gameplay and increase general playability.One of the first issues I noticed was that grinding was a hassle. So far every time I go into an area to grind if my Coromon arent decently ahead in levels to the wild Coromon then it can be a struggle to keep the Coromon alive that you want to grind levels with and this leads into one of my next issues. The damage values for general moves feel a tad overtuned, in the early game (or at least the first 4-5 areas, Im currently at Donar Island) the health values that most Standard and even Potent Coromon have means that in a wild area they are knocked out in potentially 2-3 hits and with the Health Cakes S costing 200-250 and the Health Cakes M costing 700 gold, being able to heal outside of a town healer is expensive to keep up considering it could take up to 3-4 wild fights just to afford 1 Health Cake.The game also seems to completely collapse if its tried to stream through Discord which is a complaint most of the other reviews have noted.In conclusion the art style is nice, sprite designs are awesome although more active animations would be a nice touch the game suffers from some balancing and streamline issues, with apparently an unsatisfying story end and mostly frustrating grinding experience. I would still recommend this game but if I were you Id get it on sale unless some of the issues are sorted.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a shameless ripoff of pokemon.  However, It stands out quite well in that it has tons of new creature, hehe, comforts.  It still adheres to the original formula of what works without any of the silliness that pokemon is adopting these days in order to force novelty into a worn-out franchise.I think it's better than pokemon in most ways. It doesn't shove stupid things in your face you have no interest in (boring waste of time beauty contests, required online feature showcases, megadigiterrastrialvolutions, dumb side quests).  It's just plain pokemon, like pokemon should still be, but with loads of improvements like an achievement system with levels, rewards, and more rewards for accepting rewards.  I also like how it handles HMs.  Your character has the skills rather than the pokemon so they're available all the time.  The sprite work is excellent, and the shiny/nature/IV system is refined into a single scoring system coromon calls potential.  Potential ranges randomly from 0-21 for each monster. Higher is better in EVERY WAY, appearances and extra stats that you can allocate any way you want.  Appearance changes to color pallet occur with higher potential (shiny), but if you like another color scheme you can change it to anything lower than the pokemon's current potential. All of this is how pokemon should have done it!  The music is cute and appropriate.  The graphics overall are pretty great for what this game is.  The boss fights are excellent compared to anything pokemon has attempted outside of Legends.  It is hard to make these games challenging without being insanely grindey or just straight up breaking the game's own rules, but this game strikes a nice balance there as well.  The bosses are difficult, and aside from how many rounds it takes to defeat them, levels don't matter as much as the rhythm of the fight.  Each one has a gimmick like being able to 1-shot you if you don't do something, damaging your entire team after reaching 1/2 health, or being invulnerable to damage if not exploiting its weakness.  That being said, I also never lost a fight the whole game.  I didn't grind outside of screwing around trying to get the area achievements and find all the rare Mons, so it's not a very difficult game.  Thankfully, there's an app for that!  The game has incredibly granular difficulty settings allowing you to play however you want.  On top of that, you unlock further customizations via item rewards, shop purchases, and achievements.  In these games, time invested is almost always the way to get stronger, so if there are parts you don't enjoy repeating over and over again, or you just want certain areas to go by faster, you can toggle the settings in ways to speed up those undesired aspects.  Like if you don't enjoy farming money, you can 1/2 the price of shop wares for example with an item you find.  I guess if you are just really bad at these types of games somehow, you can just make the whole thing a cakewalk if you want to.There are puzzles and they are some of the puzzles I have ever played.  I did not forget a word in that sentence,  The puzzles are really obvious and dumb except for when they aren't and take way too long to figure out.  Yeah, this is definitely the game's weak point.  Pokemon puzzles are also pretty terrible, so I feel like this is more of a hail-to-its-inspiration rather than a serious fault.I like that NPCs are aware of how dumb the world of pokemon is, kind of like cassette beasts.  I like that the people talk more like people than weebs.  But I don't like that this game is pretty low on content.  It's not short or anything.  It takes a long time to complete but when you're done, you don't really feel like you've done a whole lot.  Having big N's budget really helps out with that problem in pokemon games, but I'd rather play this any day.  Quality over quantity!If you think Pokemon has been terrible starting directly after Alpha-Omega remake generation, this game is for you.  It keeps all the best parts of those games without introducing all the awful ideas that followed.  I won't even say this is a game for purists.  There are loads of objective improvements that pokemon implemented in later generations.  It's a game for people who liked pokemon when it didn't suck and want a better experience, new story line, and new monsters to chase.  It's not perfect, but it's the best pokemon-clone out there.  It feels quality, and the music doesn't make you want to stab yourself in the ears like cassette beasts does.Update: there is a new included DLC that implements a shop system of purchasing special editions of certain coromon, character cosmetics, and high-tier items otherwise limited in quantity in the game (master balls, rare candies, shiny attracting spray).  I don't think the shop addition makes the game any better, but it is an option which I like!  I just like choices.  Nintendo has been our-way or the highway since forever and this game gives you choices all over the place of how to play.  Really great job with this game.  I hope there will be another!

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 Right of the bat the Coromon sprite art is real nice and is a highlight. Progress is mostly linear through the world areas and is well suited to the game. However, "the grind" is not well balanced for a timely PvE experience; perhaps for something with MMO like PvP it would be more inline. The game features a double rarity system - Base encounter chance in wild + potential rank from 1 to 21. The odds of getting a very high potential specific 'Mon are pretty low even with item boosts.Additionally, there is excessive use of hidden items throughout without any on screen ques. This results in interacting with every tile to ensure to don't miss something until late game. Moreover, this really slow down the pacing of the action and gets compounded mid-game with a second hidden item type that requires a specific item to search for it. Lastly, the tactical depth is pretty minimal. The game doesn't do a lot to deviate from the Pokemon red/blue combat formula.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have many hours in the game, so I'm not sure how valid my opinion/review is at the moment, but I will say with utmost certainty, I absolutely LOVE this game so far.To me, this is the Stardew Valley of Pokemon. Ever since I saw its first reveal about it coming to the Switch, I was immediately hooked. As someone who has been disappointed by each newer Pokemon game, I wanted a game that brought me back to my childhood; why I loved the series in the first place.Playing Coromon, I feel like a kid again! The animations and art are absolutely spectacular, the different Coromon designs and types have been incredibly interesting to experience firsthand, and the amount of player customization and optimization is outstanding! From the very start, you get the character creator, which is already more vast compared to the actual Pokemon titles. And the game customization options are absolutely fabulous. Not only are there different preset difficulty settings, but there's also custom ones you can make, making Nuzlocke experiences even more viable, as well as fun gimmicks like being able to capture trainer Coromon, if you want to have that setting on.The one con so far that I've experienced is that there are a few stuttering frame issues. Not sure if that's on my hardware, or the game itself, but that is something I have noticed.I know the Switch port got delayed, which is saddening, but I totally understand it. Even though I bought it on Steam, I will be buying on Switch when it's available. I want to see this game thrive and flourish!Thank you developers for this amazing experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Frustrating, shallow, and uninspired mini-games and puzzles hold back an otherwise incredible creature battler RPG.Coromon is a science fantasy creature collector role playing game. The player takes on the role of a newly-hired researcher with the goal of learning more about Coromon, a group of over 100 unique species of fantastical creatures. Finding themselves thrust into a globetrotting adventure, players can expect to collect a variety of creatures, customize their skills and party for strategic battle, and explore a variety of aesthetic environments... when they're not being forced to participate in horrendous mini-games or inane puzzles.To start on a positive note, Coromon's creature collection and battle mechanics are among the best in the genre. There are a large variety of creatures to customize one's party with, and each creature family feels unique with their own distinct strengths and weaknesses. Creatures can memorize four skills to use in battle from lists of skills unique to each creature (adding more skills to their lists as they level up or use certain items) alongside a special passive or active trait. When considering skill and trait loadouts, there are thousands of combinations to choose from when customizing Coromon, creating deep, tactical depth. Battle mechanics are intuitive, though the in-game guides are also great at explaining mechanics in detail if the player doesn't completely grasp them at first. Also noteworthy is how reasonable it is to "retrain" aspects of your Coromon that are normally notoriously difficult in other creature collection games.The art and music for Coromon is nothing short of exceptional. The game is illustrated with beautiful pixel art in every corner of the world of Velua, with animations that breathe life and personality into every creature and battle skill. The variety of tracks in Coromon is a pleasant surprise, with memorable musical themes throughout the experience. Composed by Davi Vasc, the combination of synthetic strings, brass, and even electric guitar alongside bright piano melodies creates a soundtrack that perfectly services the different moments of the game and becomes instantly nostalgic.Unfortunately, this is where the positives for Coromon end. Though I typically restrain myself from using the first-person perspective and histrionic language in my reviews, I cannot understate how utterly detestable the narrative experience in Coromon is. While the writing of the narrative delivered via dialogue and worldbuilding is serviceable, the player character's participation in the game world's events manifests in unpolished out-of-genre gameplay, the inclusion of which feels utterly inane. For example, one chapter of the game's narrative involves infiltrating a palace in a desert country, and requires the player character to traverse a heavily-guarded barracks building without being spotted by enemy NPCs. Upon being noticed, a Coromon battle is not triggered - instead, the player gets a game over screen and must restart the segment from the last checkpoint they reached. This shallow "stealth" gameplay (and I am really reaching to use that term here) has no place in a creature battler RPG like Coromon. Though it may have been designed as a way to add variety to the game's narrative, it only served to make me miserable and desperately wish to get back to the main gameplay of Coromon. This is only one example of such an unenjoyable diversion, others include a more frustrating variation of the board game Mastermind and a series of mind-numbingly dull fetch quests in a snowy village, which felt like artifical time wasters as opposed to fun gameplay, and these side errands must be completed in order to progress through the game.While I loved the aspects of Coromon that were related to the core promise of the game - creature collection and tactical battles - the amount of other nonsense in the game is so vast and frustrating that I was unable to complete the game. While I do not regret my purchase, and I believe that Coromon has made important strides for the future of the creature collector genre with its innovative mechanics, I cannot in good conscience recommend anyone to actually play this game, as I don't think they'd be having fun half the time.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the game today and I really enjoyed it!○ Introduction :• Coromon has a lot in common with Pokémon games but has some original concepts, which makes it a new experience. Skills have icons and no longer show as a name only. Really refreshing!• The soundtrack is... hmm... not bad, I'd say? Let's say decent. It fits for a game like Coromon. _childDocuments_.review: Coromon is hands down one of the best Monster Taming games out there, in my mind far exceeding the recent additions to the Pokémon franchise as it takes the genre back to it's roots, and innovates on it in ways Pokémon has refused to do for many years now.The tameable Coromon are all beautifully illustrated in hand animated pixel art - accentuating their personalities and unique designs. Whether you like your creatures to be 2D or 3D is a personal preference, but I do believe it suites the nostalgia associated with the genre of Monster Taming games.Unlike the Pokémon games of today, Coromon allows the player to tailor their difficulty settings to suite their play style, making Coromon less of a "grind one starter and spam the hyperbeam" experience - and more of an actual strategy game that challenges the player to allocate stat points and abilities wisely - especially when using the included nuzlocke mode.By far my favourite addition in Coromon is the expansion on Shiny Hunting, now allowing players to encounter 'Potent' as well as 'Perfect' Coromon, adding a much needed in-between that keeps players excited for wild encounters - rather than them turning into a repetitive annoyance.Coromon also includes tons of quality of life features, one of my favourites being stat-point reallocation - allowing to build  your team more strategically. TRAGsoft has done an amazing job with this game - especially for whatever budget / time constraints I'm sure they must've had whilst developing Coromon.I sincerely hope this game garners enough attention and attains a passionate fanbase for years to come, as I'd love for the developers to have all the freedom in the world, devoid of budget / time constraints to turn this gem of a game into a series better and more renowned than the predecessor that inspired it!

The Deck battery drains faster playing this 2D game than it does playing games like GTA V or Cyberpunk.  There are posts going back 7 months or more pointing out this issue, and the Devs have replicated the issue, but still no fix.2. The second issue applies to everyone regardless of whether or not you're using a Steam Deck.  The selection of Coromon is very limited.  As other reviews pointed out, there are only around 100 Coromon total, most being a part of another's evolution line, leading to only about 40 total evolution lines to explore.All that said, this game is crazy fun when it's working properly. The art style and animations look better, and more uniform, than any other Pokè-Like game I've seen.  Although the selection of Coromon is very limited, the ones that are available are fun and creative.  I will say that I wish less of the available evolution lines were bugs, and more variety of animals were used as inspiration.

_childDocuments_.review: Last edit 5/12 3 PM ESTI have completed the demo and transferred to the full game. I will say so far that if you are coming over from Pokemon, there are similarities that will make you feel right at home, but just enough different things to make the experience feel fresh. I did not stick with Temtem because of its always-online nature and from how vastly different it was - with Coromon I feel right at home with the mechanics. I firmly believe that if you are a veteran Pokemon fan looking for a game to scratch that monster-catcher itch, while also providing a decent challenge, Coromon is a very good game that fulfills all of this.The many QoL changes made here also greatly enhance the experience, much of it returning from Pokemon fan projects (which is far from a bad thing):Battles are challenging, which is a refreshing change of pace compared to what we have recently gotten in Pokemon. You are forced to switch between different Coromon throughout each battle to tend to different elements/types. The Titan boss battles are bulky and difficult, necessitating a properly trained team most of the time. At the same time, there are options in the game's settings menu and at a terminal at the start of the game to make the game easier or more difficult depending on what you want - a more casual, easier playthrough more akin to Pokemon's X and Y, or a challenge run with nuzlocke rules? All there, all built in.This game also has a much simpler type tree and does not have any dual-type Coromon. This is not a bad thing necessarily - if anything, this makes it easier for newcomers to get a mental grasp on and memorize.This game looks really nice. I love the battle backgrounds, I love the Coromon sprites (and the designs for them are also quite good as well), I love the overworlds and how varied and interesting they are. It definitely looks like the mobile game that it was intended to be, but you wouldn't be able to tell that just at a glance. The spritework is  - major props to the team that made them....Do I really need to elaborate?Oh yeah, it's on Spotify, too, so feel free to make your own judgement. (Spoilers, obviously!) NOTE: The launcher has been disabled. This section reflects the game's initial version when it first came out and when this review was initially posted.This was a MASSIVE disappointment for me personally. DO  PUT A LAUNCHER AFTER I PRESS THE PLAY BUTTON. LAUNCH THE GAME!The full version adds a launcher before the game actually starts, advertising other Freedom Games titles. I absolutely  think this is necessary; if I want to look at your games, there is a "check out the Freedom Games franchise on Steam" button on the store page that I will click if I care enough.The launcher itself has also caused problems with people not being able to start the game, and it additionally impacts Steam Deck verification. You gain NOTHING from adding a launcher - so don't do it! When I hit the play button, the GAME should load. Do not put ANYTHING else before the actual game unless you absolutely  to!The more I play the game, the more I notice that this is very clearly a mobile game first, and is not necessarily made for PC. This comes with benefits - being able to navigate with a mouse as well as with a keyboard or controller is a welcome addition - but that also means it is not optimized very well performance-wise. Which leads into the next and probably biggest criticism I have with this game...Crashes and graphical glitches everywhere! For a lower-end game like this I am a little bit concerned as to how many issues I have seen. The Discord overlay does not work and causes consistent crashes, and you have to disable a Discord setting to be able to stream the game. There are also various different problems going around with some graphics cards. I have not personally run into any of them myself, but they are definitely not good, and are very common. I would definitely wait a little bit to see if they are ironed out further.Some story elements drag for some time longer than they probably should, and some puzzles I find myself even questioning if they are puzzles at all.  While it is clear that the developers are attempting to try new ideas with the genre and they are fixing a lot of these issues with patches, a lot of this leaves me scratching my head and wondering how it got past the conceptual phase, let alone testing.Despite the flaws with the story and performance gripes, I very much recommend this game. It's a very solid monster catcher, and if you are coming from Pokemon, you will most likely have a good time with it. Coromon is not afraid to try new things, but at its core it is very familiar.If my verdict changes as I continue to play through the game, I will update this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is everything a fan of creature catchers could want from a pokemon clone and more. Not only does the game double down on the positive aspects of pokemon games by making a lot of less significant aspects of the game significantly more streamlined, but it adds a great deal of its own creative features that make for the most fun I've had with this kind of game since Black & White. The best of these new features is easily the shiny system in which shiny Coromon are not only cosmetically pleasing and distinct from their basic counterparts, but ideal stat wise as well. Everything else from berry growing and harvesting to building a team and experimenting with moves is very fluent and fun too. While the player is more than able to take their time progressing through the story, there's also plenty of ways to speed things up and rush the story. There's also quite a bit of end-game content that's not nearly as grindy or monotonous as a pokemon game. Likewise, there's plenty of side quests and non-story content the player may wish to return to once the main quest line is over. There is quite a lot of emphasis on puzzles throughout the goofy but likewise grim story, taking the player through a simple setting with a surprisingly solid foundation for this game to take place and progress. The puzzles were probably my least favorite aspect simply because the restart mechanism in the event of failing a puzzle isn't particularly appealing. Another unfortunate aspect about the game is that despite an adequate range of Coromon numbering just upwards of 100 and the game's own verbal emphasis on a wide variety of strategies to be used, certain Coromon were completely underwhelming compared to others in terms of both raw competence in battles and application of certain strategies, making certain strategies like accuracy manipulation easier and more optimal than say defensive or status strategies. While battles may not have as much variety as some would like though, the options menu is actually incredible in this game. There's a lot of customization options for battles, general gameplay, audio, graphics, etc. There's even a built-in randomizer and nuzlocke mode, which individual customizations for separate settings that gives Coromon a lot of replayability on top of end-game content. Overall this is a great creature catcher/pokemon clone, which definitely has a lot of care and polish put into it.

You can feel the deep love the devs have for this genre and everything that makes it great! The pixel art is incredible, every environment is soaking in character and the sprite-work for the coromon and their skills is outstanding. The designs are one of my favourite parts of this game, every coromon was unique and visually interesting. The music was outstanding, when that electric guitar hits in the menu theme... damn. The devs have been super receptive and friendly, they have been really awesome and responsive to feedback.But by far the biggest surprise for me was the story. There are emotional beats that actually landed for me and the end hit me a lot harder than I was expecting!I didn't get too far into the competitive aspects of this game so I don't feel comfortable commenting on that part of the game, there is an active discord community for those who want that experience. _childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a classic monster taming experience that will remind you of older Pokemon games but have all the bells and whistles and quality of life improvements of modern monster tamer games then Coromon is for you. Even on normal difficulty, Coromon is pretty challenging and there are many ways to increase difficulty as well as add randomizer elements, do nuzlockes, and more with a wide variety of customizable settings. Coromon are relatively balanced stat-wise and every Coromon feels like it has potential to be overpowered in the right team and with the right set up. However, I will point out that some movepools and traits are simply superior to others and some types are severely underrepresented in the moves department unfortunately. The story isn't great but it's pretty interesting and there's promise of future updates to alleviate the rather abrupt ending.Titan battles and puzzles can be annoying in some ways for some but for the most part I found them enjoyable.The game is simple to pick up and learn. And I am still thoroughly enjoying it. The potential system is an excellent replacement for the shiny system most games employ and perfect hunting never feels hopeless not that you even need perfect forms for PVP now anyway. The thing that really makes this game an absolute gem tho is really the incredible devs. Devs listen to fans, quickly resolve issues, and clearly love and slave over their game. It's so refreshing I can't even begin to describe it. I'm not used to being spoiled by devs as a longtime Pokemon fan so it's just a breath of fresh air. I would highly recommend this game. I loved it when I started and still love it just as much or more now.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very good imo, it's challenging but not too challenging (You can change the difficulty at any point). I did get stuck once for like 30 mins because this boss was a royal pain, but when I beat them it felt so satisfying, I honestly wasn't even mad. I'd rather a game beat me up a good number of times, than I breeze through the game like water through water.There are a lot of quality of life stuff like being about to check a Coromon's stats when leveling up or there potential goes up. And regarding potential as a mechanic I really love it. When a Coromon's potential goes up you allocate point to any individual stat of your choosing. They also use stamina as energy to be able to use moves, which is one of the best additions in my opinion.The Coromon are very well done, as well as their animations. There are also a lot of useful moves, even the early game move don't feel that bad. The puzzles in the game are very clever and interesting, they have that nice level of difficulty that doesn't make me hate puzzles, and it's pretty forgiving when you fail.There are likely stuff I forgot to mention, maybe like one or 2 negative stuff, but I honestly can't remember. My memory isn't the best, my bad. Edit: Had to add this one, the music is very very good. I'm literally about to buy the soundtrack right now to support the Devs. Didn't expect it to be this good, but it's a welcomed surprise.This is a very strong monster taming game title for the genre, Coromon definitely has a good head on it's shoulders. I was truly surprised how well made this game was, and I play on Linux too. This game actually has heart, charm, and they listen to feedback and suggestions. Very big kudos to the Dev team and everyone else involved, I truly truly pray that they can make many more games and bring some major competition to the genre. _childDocuments_.review: Ok so this is a weird review for me because I am super mixed on this game. Please don't misunderstand this game isn't bad at all but its a lot deeper than pokemon was. In pokemon the game didn't ask much of you other than to kind of build a semi OK team but other than that it was pretty easy. In coromon however that is not the case at all. I've spent a couple of hours alone looking at just stats of the coromon and planning out their level ups and stat increases. I found that if you really don't know what you are doing and don't plan well this game can quickly become a living hell. so there is a lot of trainer battles and at first they aren't so bad but later on they get more challenging. I found myself running back to heal my guys more often then I would have liked. This is what I mean by the game can become a living hell,  if you don't plan stuff out and raise the correct stats when needed you can quickly find one of your coromon because shear trash like I did and I regretted treating it like pokemon. I had to go back and train a whole new guy to replace my now trash one and that worked way better. I am not saying this is a bad thing, not at all honestly but if you don't know about it you can waste a lot of your time like I did.  Please keep this next part in mind that this game is a grind. I am not super far into the game and there has already been three moments were I thought about shutting the game off because I just wanted to progress and the game just had more stuff in the way than it really needed. Another HUGE issue I can see is this game as mandatory puzzles that must be solved in order to progress in the game. These puzzles are not however super hard but they aren't easy either and you will most likely spent 20 to 40 mins messing with them. The puzzles are really annoying because the game already has alot of grinding and then you need to stop and complete a puzzle.The different types are interesting to say the least but I will say I thought It was weird that your starters are a ice, fire and water. Unlike pokemon were one of the types is rare and worth taking that simply isnt the case here, you can pretty much find a fire type in the grass right outside the starting area and a ice type like 30 mins to an hour into the game. I personally would have like to see more of a impact on that first choice you made. I ended up taking the fire one because I thought I wasn't going to find alot of fire types early. If I was to go back I would honestly go water because that seemed like something I needed and was missing but other than that I really didn't feel like my first choice mattered too much.The game looks really good and there really isn't any crashing or glitches at all and all the models look really good, I have personally fallen in love with a couple of them because they are such good models.In summary, good game but you need to put more thought into your team than pokemon and this game is very grindy with puzzles that you must complete. I think its honestly worth grabbing and worth your time, you just need to be aware that your going to have to think and be smart about what you do. Its not like pokemon were after you spent like 30 mins getting your guys to 15 the game plays itself, no, not here. The other trainers will go toe to toe with you if you aren't constantly raising your levels. Now that I know what I am doing I will most likely restart my play through so its alot smoother. Anyways I hope this helped some people out.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is like a 6/10 at best. it has some good ideas in terms of some gameplay elements and creature designs, but the lack of dual typings makes most creatures feel really same-y. there are also some puzzle and filler sections that are way too long. it honestly feels a lot closer to nexomon than pokemon if youve ever played that, but the music and art is really good.overall its a decent creature collector that drags itself a bit too long and in my opinion lacks depth. idk how competitive is bc i havent tried it yet, but since shinies determine stats in this game i heard most ppl complain about it being a grind, though i cant say much myself.edit: addressing the comments to go more in detail, i feel like every creature being monotype automatically makes gameplay and monster variety a lot more shallow. i think the typing system hurts me more because some types being move only is a great idea, however i think thematically most of them dont make sense to be move only such as air and foul. secondly, since there are so few types (7 monster types + 6 move only types), i feel like the game could benefit more from dual typings in order to make it more varied.in terms of game pacing, i feel like most of the decisions they made ultimately just make the game more tedious. a good example is the potential machine, it is a good idea on paper, however in execution its not very good. the machine only works once for each monster, so youre forced to reload saves in order to get better potential rates, plus the machine only completes after taking 1000 steps, so grinding for a potentially good monster is just a walking simulator. some of the puzzles and stealth/obstacle sections also drag on a little too long as said before.i did not try pvp purely bc of the fact that i of course had to try and essentially farm shinies in order to get the best potential monsters to win. i also was at a point in the game where i didnt feel like i could complete yet, and not everyone will be as committed or available to grind for pvp.all in all i do not like the game bc it is just fundamentally at fault for me, however if you do not mind these problems then it is a pretty decent game with great polish. i do not foresee myself continuing to play unless they add more types/implement dual typing, which i dont think is happening anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: So incredibly fun! I feel like I'm playing Pokemon for the first time again since 1996. I haven't enjoyed the Pokemon series since 3rd gen, so this is such a breath of fresh air. I'm 14 hours in, and only on my 3rd titan. It's definitely worth the money~My favorite thing is that the grind doesn't seem bad at all because you're always on the hunt for potent and perfect Coromon. My whole team is potent, and while I haven't found a perfect yet my brother has, so I know it's possible lol.The moves are fun and I love that many of them are specific to each Coromon. The designs are also original and fun (though sometimes the designs confuse me as to what the type is). I'm in love with Dugterra and Grimmask! There's of course some balancing issues to be worked on, but I know the team is good for it. I can't recommend this game enough, and look forward to tournaments!

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of really good aspects of this game for a Pokemon like, and I really wanted to like it and even beat it, but the flaws started to get to me too much.The GoodGreat Designs for the most part. (Subjective, but I like the shark.)Music sounds great, lovely tunes to chill to.Quality of life items such as the Fruit Fetcher, the Remote Coromon Storage, Infinite Repel.The BadThe Puzzles are much to left be desired :c They often get in the way of the fun, or are just tedious. Some require you to have precise stealth, or others require pattern recognition without very good foretelling. The Boss Fights are... 50/50. Their designs feel off to me personally, which is subjective. They did provide a challenge, but if you don't succeed the first time you will have to go through an entire un-skipable cutscene every single attempt. If you fail on the puzzles, it will not just reset you at the beginning of the dungeon, but give you a game over, for example I got hit by a blow dart, instead of taking damage or get pushed back. I had to press "Try Again", they aren't hard, just tedious and bogs down the fun.The story is okay? I can't really comment as it was just, an alright experience. Nothing I hated but nothing that special, and I don't really blame the writers for that. The Npcs you interact with are a bit corny, and that's fine. But none of them have a really different personality outside of "Quirky, Excited, Scientist" they shuffle from these three personality traits a lot. Pokemon does the same for a lot of them, so not gonna take points.Overall? 6/10 I think it's definitely worth picking up for $5 if you can, just to give it your own try and experience, but overall I think it could of used some more time in the oven in certain aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid creature-catcher, as far as these things go. _childDocuments_.review: A very competent take on the Creature Collecting genre.My favorite change compared to pokemon is the combined shiny and IV system. There's a Potential range from 1 to 21 that affects how fast a monster gains Potential levels, a level separate from normal ones. The different appearance comes into play here too. Standard appearances is in the 1 to 16 range, Potent 17 to 20 and Perfect is at 21. What makes this system even better is they added the option to change the appearance of a monster to any appearance you've obtained before, so you can use your favorite color scheme.Besides that monsters have a pool of moves you can select 4 from at will outside of combat and you can teach them others from what are essentially TMs and are unlimited in use. Also the monster designs are some of the nicest I've seen in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is such a breath of fresh air from the stale monster tamer giant that is Pokemon, and the monster taming genre in general. TRAGsoft did a phenomenal job with this game, from the challenging puzzles, to having a hand in how to raise your mons, to the palatable storyline. Not to mention the soundtrack, map design, character design, pixel art and mon design, there were all top tier and the reason why I love indie games so much. There's so much passion poured into the game.Although the game adopts many of the systems from Pokemon, it didn't feel like a copy of their stuff; just familiar systems but built with ease-of-access in mind and most importantly, making it fun. Some of the puzzles were actually trickier than I expected (even had to look up the answer to a few!) and I appreciated that because the game isn't just a steamroll. It's interactive and present, the point video-games are supposed to be. Also the biggest thing I'm a fan of, I can actually catch ALL coromons! Seriously, who markets the phrase 'gotta catch em all' and not let us catch them all in a single game? Been grinding my gears for decades. Finally, many of the end-stage Coromon evolution designs look so absolutely fantastic! This motivated me to discover all the coromons in the game. So thank you TRAGsoft, for doing this right.The only thing at this point in time I wish I had more of was end-game content. Can't wait to see what updates are next!

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Best "Poke-clone" out there. Amazing QOL. Great cast. Get itFirst off, this game isn't perfect. But what is here is so fantastic, I can't recommend it enough. I think all games in this genre(I suppose it's called creature collector?) are going to be compared to Pokemon, which is unavoidable, seeing as how Pokemon basically invented and dominated the genre for 20 years. A tremendous amount of franchise fatigue has turned me off of these games, but on a whim, I decided to power through and give Coromon a chance. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ what a decision that turned out to be. edit: Before the Coromon themselves, I'll mention the type chart. Only 6 types, all of which are familiar, however there are 7 additional types that are only found on moves. Magic, Foul, and Heavy are three of them, which aren't in Pokemon, so you'll have to go through the tedious process of using them in various battles to learn what they're effective on and resisted by. Except you don't. You're given a type chart immediately, and also very early on you get books on Coromon basics, moves, field conditions and status effects, to name a few. This is a MASSIVE point in Coromon's favor, providing the player with all the vital information they need on types, moves, etc. This takes out an excessive amount of grind and tedious experimental learning.  It really shows consideration of the players experience by the devs, and I for one appreciate it greatly. First thing I'll mention are the Coromon themselves. Most of them are fantastic in design, with beautifully animated sprites, reminiscent of gen 5. Only 2 come to mind when I think of the ones I really didn't like, but that's still a higher percentage of great mons than any generation of Pokemon. That's all subjective anyway, so how about their viability. While I haven't been able to try them all yet, each and every one seems to be well thought out in how it fits in with the rest of the cast in terms of stats, moves and play style. There aren't any ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Coromon that are only there to make others better by comparison. Even the early game Coromon manage to carve out a niche for themselves that allows them to retain viability throughout the game. It's amazing. The story is nothing spectacular, but it isn't terrible. I really don't have much to say on it. I'll leave that up to you to decide, but I suppose the main point is battling the 6 titans. They sort of act as boss battles in lieu of gym leaders. They're actually really fun to find and battle. I'll leave it at that to avoid spoilers or any unnecessary details.  How about the world.. It's... pretty good. Tons of unique and diverse environments and biomes to go through. The Coromon themselves are mostly found in the environment of their type i.e. sand types in the desert, fire types in a volcano, etc. For the most part this is true, but there are a decent enough distribution throughout the early game to get a diverse enough team to have multiple types, each with coverage moves, for any challenge you may face. Again, well thought out on the part of the devs. Fantastic. The puzzles are.. well that depends on you. I like them. They're larger, longer, and more frequent than any Pokemon game. Whether this is a pro or con is entirely personal preference. I like them. They aren't difficult, but they are long at times, and start to drag just a bit before the end of the cave/dungeon/whatever. I saw a few reviews that mentioned how much of a pain in the ass they are, and how they derail and butcher the pacing of the game. I disagree, but I understand the sentiment. It's really just up to you. By puzzles, btw, think of strength puzzles, ice floors in caves, and ♥♥♥♥ like that in Pokemon games. Press a button to open a door, press another to open another door but i closes the previous door, etc. So what's the difficulty like? Is it as hard as B2W2 and USUM, or piss easy like modern games? Well that also is up to you. There's a plethora of difficulty modifiers that allow you to really customize your experience. Every element of the ultra hardcore nuzlocke is individually toggle-able. Everything from only one mon per route, to fainting=death, no fast travel, held item limits, and more. You can really make this a hellscape of torture and suffering in every way, punishing yourself for any and every mistake, regardless of size. Or you could play it like a Pokemon game, and just mash A through the entire game and never really try.There's more, especially quality of life additions, to mention, but you're probably sure at this point whether or not you want the game. I can't recommend it enough, and strongly urge you to get this if you're just burnt out on Pokemon games being the same dull, bland and plain experience over and over. I mean really, the trailer is accurate. It's a great game, in many many ways, and deserves a try.
