_childDocuments_.review: As an OG Pokemon fan, this game is very refreshing, it's alot like Pokemon, but I don't have to pirate anything to play it on pc, and  I can just play this on my phone (I mainly play on phone).  But along with it being very similar to Pokemon, it has some key features that make it it's own game.  The 2 tier shiny system is pretty damn neat and has me captivated to at least get all of the 1st tier of shinies.  Also, personally, this The Best Pokemon-Like game I've played and seen, I've seen a few others, like Cassette Beasts, and then a newer one that is supposedly like Digimon, but those are both kinda cringe in my opinion.  The story is a little corny, but it's nothing I can't tolerate. The sprites, monsters and scenery are top-notch! They did a GREAT JOB! Dailies feel pretty damn great for unlocking new skins, just an extra something something to do for cool stuff. Things that I'll just say I'm not sure of, because I don't necessarily dis-like them alot, they just make me feel unsure whether I like them or not: 1 v 3 wild battles damn, son,  can feel annoying waiting those extra turns, but again, I do still get some enjoyment out of it.  Rare Monsters, nothing I have came across seemed to be rare, some are just take slightly more time to come across than others. No one of a kind type deals, which maybe they were avoiding to keep it different than PKMN.  Ok one bad thing, PC storage seems to messy and un-organized for me, unfortunately, I have thought of what I don't like about it, it just feels bad. Also no trading Mons is kinda strange, but not the end of the world.  But overall, this game really slaps Devs, GOOD JOB!! I Really hope you make a sequel!! One more thing I forgot to mention is that part of the reason this is so refreshing is all of the Mons are NEW!! Feels so good, unlike playing Pokemon and seeing some same-old guys.

_childDocuments_.review: Heads up regarding grind/difficulty issues : the game has the most flexible difficulty options I've ever seen and there's nothing wrong with tweaking certain features towards casual especially if your leisure time is limited.Pixel artists and fans can't pass this title up. Monsters have silky animations at herculean resolutions/frame counts and all with fantastically rendered lighting and textures. The environment work is also brilliant and complemented by an excellent soundtrack and level design. Overall, they simply did not need to go this hard artistically, but they invested so heavily in the visual presentation that I doubt we'll EVER see an entry in this genre/style that will even attempt to outdo it. My single reservation is on behalf of Pokemon fans who are looking for cute characters above all.  We get a good share of cute little guys, but overall there aren't as many you can form an emotional bond with.  That's just what you get when your focus is on how the characters work as part of a game as opposed to a merchandising empire.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon improves on the Pokemon formula in terms of the small details. I will mention several items and aspects from Pokemon Red/Gold since Coromon is inspired by the popular franchise. Music for each town/area livens up the mood. Ghost town is spooky and battles against bosses are exciting.- Berries - Can grow specific fruits in pots and pick them when ready.- Escape rope in caves/Fly- Lux Recall that lets you transport to any town- Bike- Run and can change setting to turn on at all times- Shiny- Potent is the equivalent. Potent scent to use and this increases chance of Potent Coromon appearance- HM moves- Gauntlets with push rock, burn, etc that lets you use special moves outside of battle without the need to teach Coromon a weak attack- 4 moves allowed in Pokemon only- Can enable or change 1 or all 4 moves before a battle- Stats - Can choose which Stats like Attack or defense to increase when leveling- Buying items - Can use coupons to decrease cost of buying items- Difficulty - Several modes and harder modes for players that want a tougher experienceMain aspects missing are gym battles, no rival, no Elite 4, and no breeding. Some minor weaknesses are below.- Puzzles that are somewhat tedious and involve collecting items, timing a jump, and stealth.- The need to level up Coromon to defeat last boss. It is level 70 and yours are around mid 50s or low 60s by that point of the game.- Few achievements require multiple playthroughs.- Antagonist do not present a challenge. They throw some Coromon battles at you, but it does not add to the story.This game is enjoyable for Pokemon fans, contains atmospheric soundtrack, and is a worthy successor to Pokemon. The developers continue to make updates and show a devotion to improving the game.If you want to learn about the future of Coromon, check out the interview.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good poké-like with a twist.Moves are learned and retained and you pick a choice of four at any one time. You can also teach your mon a selection of other moves from TM like manuals which can vastly improve their usability as often you'll be adding something.Stat changing moves and buff/debuff moves can be powerful but like Pokémon you're usually better just aiming for type weaknesses. Strength vs Special attacks are varied also and all mons have their own strengths and weaknesses in battle.The game is well balanced and I rarely felt overpowered except perhaps one dungeon around the middle of the game where I fell into a perfect strategy against all the mons in the area.There are a few flaws: the story is fine but nothing special, the battles can be slow sometimes and you can teleport around freely for most of the game so there's no threat or need to use items when you can just backtrack. There's no post-game as yet but allegedly there are some free updates planned so watch this space.Over-all definitely worth the price if you like monster trainer games and especially if you miss the gameboy/DS days.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of monster catching games, you might enjoy Coromon. It is "good enough", but some aspects bothered me enough to make this a negative review. Overall I think it treads a bit too close to the game series it obviously takes inspiration from. Compared to the games that inspired it, there are much fewer elemental types and the overall battle complexity is much less as a result. Elemental types aren't sprinkled out over the course of the game but rather concentrated in specific areas. You'll get nearly all Electric type Coromon in the first major dungeon for example. There are a couple of exceptions, but I often found myself wanting more variety in my team that I couldn't get until a later dungeon let me catch several of a new element type. The encounter rate is frustratingly high, often just 2 or 3 steps between battles.The milestones system is a ton of manual work, tons of clicking and need to remember to check it periodically. I'm not fond of being made to feel I need to min-max my stats with potential, traits, and stat adjusting. The dice rolls are extremely unfair. I've seen enemies get 5 critical hits in a row, and enemy multi-hit attacks seem to always land 2-3 times. Conversely, I miss a lot and my multi-hit attacks consistently only hit one time. Boss battles are full of frustrating, cheesy mechanics. Give me puzzles or give me random battles, but NEVER both at the same time. An intrusive battle breaks the flow of my concentration on the puzzle. I can't believe this mistake is still being made.  I have a strong dislike of puzzles that require precision timing. I was thinking about leaving a positive review, but I changed my mind once I encountered a mandatory minigame requiring a bunch of precision reflexes. Its alright, it just irritated me with a bunch of little things.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: *Review contains spoilers*I want to like it,  but I can't.I'm a huge Pokemon fan, and I also love Nexomon. So this game sounded fantastic to me, and I enjoyed what I'd played of the demo two or so years ago. So this was a day-one buy.It started off a lot of fun. The monster designs are great, the battle mechanics are enjoyable, and I enjoy hunting for potent and perfect coromon. I even like the cute little emoji reactions. They add a lot of charm and character. However, there are two huge points of the game that just ruin it for me.First, the puzzles. There are just too many. One of them falls over an area I'd like to explore, but the idea is to rush across the desert from tent to tent before the hot sand burns through your shoes. Adding puzzles is fair enough, but they don't even add a challenge. They are just frustrating. If you fail, you go back to another checkpoint. You don't lose anything other than your time. There's nothing to spur you on to try and do them perfectly, since there's no in-game drawback. This is especially frustrating for someone with dyspraxia like me. My disability doesn't cost me much in games, I play Monster Hunter and enjoy it. But with the puzzles in Coromon, one small miss-click or finger spasm and I've failed, then I'm graced with the 'try again?' screen and it's back to the previous checkpoint. There is no way to bypass them.Secondly, the titans. This is where the grind comes in. I don't mind games with a bit of a grind, but each boss is a wall. If you aren't prepared, you are going to have a hard time. The first boss is level 25. Beat him with a team of level 25s, and every wild Coromon in the zone after it will be ten levels or more below you. So if you want a new team member, you will need to get it up to level 35 for the next titan, which is soon might I add.If you like games with a grind and puzzles, then you'll like this game. But it just wasn't for me. I thought I just needed a break after getting to the town (and the stealth puzzle...) after the second titan. But I have no desire to pick it up again. Unfortunately, I wont be jumping on any sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest. Having played through the entirety of this game,  You're better off getting Cassette Beasts. If you only want to play the pvp, again, just wait for the cassette beasts pvp update.Not even for the PVE experience is this game worth its price point. Never have I seen a game start so strongly and trail off so heavily. I've played for 59 hours in total and I am hoping I can bargain with Steam for a refund.The writing goes from a story worth the absolute barrage of text and lore they throw at you, to a memey "and then and then and then" format that just ends in you skipping all the text and checking the quest log for what you're meant to do. The "30 hours of story" they promise comes in the form of random difficulty spikes (which aren't that hard to begin with, (You'll probably want to play the game on hard, but you also wont, You'll hear why soon) and then little mandatory minigames/puzzles that do nothing but take up time. Remember the fun "slide around the ice til you reach the goal" portions of Pokemon? Yeah well there's a whole 2 dungeons out of the 5-6 in the game dedicated to that! And even a whole town! Whoaaa 30 hours of story! And just before these sections is a whole dungeon with arrow traps and a wall maze/ puzzle with about 4 battles in it. Remember battles? The whole reason you're playing a monster tamer to begin with? Yeah those pesky things are sprinkled into this puzzle game for you to the point where by the time you finally see another trainer you forgot you just added a new mon to your team. And then you wipe the trainer in 3 turns and that's you last battle for 15 minutes. The second dungeon that leads to the first boss fight is peppered with battles. And since you're so new, it feels challenging and amazing. Once you beat this boss you feel accomplished and proud of your skills as a trainer. Cherish this. This is the last time this format is used, and therefore, the last time you feel this way. Everything, and I mean everything from here to the final boss is memey and disappointing. Even the final boss is less of an epic crescendo and more of a "Oh. I thought I was fighting her, but I guess I'm fighting the big bad instead." and then you wipe it first try because of how incredibly easy the game is. After you defeat it, you never hear from the main cronies who have been harassing you all game. You don't even battle them once. It's like if Team Rocket just pulled up in every town, went "Nyeh you're gonna lose" and the game ended without even a "damn, you beat our boss, you got hands." Nope. Just credits. I finished the story in *maybe* 15 hours total, and that's generous. My runtime was spent primarily shiny hunting and getting ready for pvp. (Btw, the shiny system is tied to the IV system. A "perfect" shiny ,21 potential, has 126 points to distribute. Potent (16-20) has less, and so on and so on so you can see why a pvp focused player like myself would WANT to spend time catching mons.) Well, after sinking 20-30 hours into creating what I thought was a great team, I found out was time well wasted, because you can just hop into pvp and create whatever mon you want with perfect stats anyways. No point in spending gold giving it the perfect trait, hunting the perfect item, seeking out the TMS to give it the perfect moveset, dumping hours into finding the perfect potential 21 mon. Nope. Go catch one, hop into pvp, add it to your "team" and you can change every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ detail besides it's color.Now all of this, and honestly, ALLLL of this, I could ignore if the main game mechanic wasn't so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. Remember PP? From Pokemon and most other monster tamers where you can use a move a certain amount of times? They replaced that with SP, which is like a stamina bar for your mons. Hoollyyyy Sh*t, it is so fun being down to your last mon in pvp or pve, getting ready to use the move that will net you the victory, pressing X where the "Fight" button once was and immediately, without notice, skipping your turn to "rest" and gain half your SP back. So great.This game is, by no stretch of the imagination, hard. So you'll probably think "I'll just play on hard"Sure, have fun, if you like mandatory Nuzlocke... They could have literally just scaled every mon you fight up but 4-5 levels or something. Or allow the Ai to actually play the game and not spam "Increase my defense" when you're hitting it with Special attacks.... But nope. Hard is just Nuzlocke. Which is so easy to cheese because the AI is terrible.The literal only time I died and had to go revive all my mons is a 1v1 that happens in the last quarter of the game where a guy approaches you wearing an ice pokemon hat, says his favorite pokemon is an ice pokemon, his name is that ice pokemon's name, says "lets 1v1, only our favorites" and throws out a water pokemon, knowing you prob chose fire to counter ice... (remember that memey writing I mentioned?)People will swear by this game, but if it's so great why is no one playing it anymore? If you've been paying attention, you'll see I spent 15 hours on story, 20 - 30 on team building, so where's the last 5 - 15 hours?Sitting the pvp lobby.... There's no one on the game. The new Ranked season started, I won ONE game and I was top of the leaderboard for like 2 days. The only way to find any players besides the 1 or 2 you might find in queue is through the Discord. The Discord community is GREAT btw. (Not sarcasm. Honestly the only upside of this horrendous game) Very helpful, very awesome people. They helped me tweak my pvp team and everything, but it was pointless in the end because ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the pvp sucks. Especially with the SP system, it makes it tedious and irritating. I'm happy to put this game in my rearview and I only hope Steam lets me get my money back.EDIt: They did not give me the refund.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a decent alternative to pokemon, but it does have some issues.- The rain effect during battles needs to be toned down, i get a headache every time i see it.- When going through the tower to get to Voltgar i got stuck for 10 minutes because the path i needed to use was obscured by the bottom wall.- You can't use the Potential Reader on wild coromon.- The fight with Voltgar is needs balancing, i shouldn't be struggling with a boss when my coromon is 10 levels above the boss. As if the devs felt they needed to meet a quota of at least one gay relationship in their game and for some reason decided to go with the Nikola Tesla and Thomas Edison reference characters which i feel nullifies any sort of pro-gay representation as those two in real life were enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: the coromon designs and sprite animations are very well done. unfortunately, thats just about the only good thing i can say about this game as a creature capture.i got the impression that this game tries to be Pokemon But Tougher, but i feel like it failed to address the parts of pokemon that are already slow in the first place and now made even more unbearable with coromon's big jumps in enemy levels, long routes/caves, and lack of money grinding options. making your way back and forth to the trainer hub gets really boring, really fast- especially when i have to grind for around 5 levels every time i get to a new area. the potency system doesnt help, if you have a team of normals just by luck, you will need to spend even more of your game time grinding. the story is also baffling in terms of writing, execution, and the fact that its very clearly unfinished at the end. the theme of technology is not well executed, npc dialogues are often internet jokes and dont add much to the world, and the villain team is completely disconnected from the world of coromon. i also feel like the writing in several areas like the desert and mining town also falls into overused and outdated tropes. i know creature capture games arent known for their quality narratives, but i feel like i need to mention it in this case, seeing as the devs advertised coromon as having a compelling story all this, combined with smaller issues like the attack animations taking so long, and using the gauntlet feeling so repetitive, makes the entire experience of coromon feel like a huge slog with little narrative or gameplay reward

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a game with beautiful pixel art and delightful music, and is definitely a neat spin on the monster catching/collecting/battling genre. I'm several hours in and have had a hard time putting it down. The monster designs are cute, and there are some unique takes that I think have great execution (there is a phoenix Coromon that turns back into an egg when it faints!). That said, this game is very much a grindfest. If you plan on getting into competitive PvP in this game, you will need to steel yourself for hours of RNG-filled wild encounters and soft resetting, as only the rarest of colors have the highest stats you will need to optimize your builds. It's like if Shiny Pokémon were the only Pokémon viable competitively, so anyone wanting to get into competitive battling would have to become a shiny hunter. Additionally, Traits, Coromon's answer to passive abilities, can only be changed by spending the game's currency and walking 1000 ingame steps. In a game where monsters can have up to 4 possible traits, it can take quite a while to get the right traits on your otherwise perfect monster.If you are a casual player, however, you should have no problem enjoying Coromon without feeling the need to optimize your team to perfection. A good strategy is usually enough to pull out of battles victorious, and it's always satisfying when you win a difficult fight.EDIT: Played further into the game and stumbled upon the most infuriating "puzzle" yet: a jump rope minigame and, of all things, Flappy Bird, both of which are REQUIRED for story progression. Both of these are things I actively avoid in games because frankly, I don't like them and I don't have the reflexes to be good at them. I find it somewhat unreasonable to, halfway through the game, require the player to play a game of highly specialized skill completely unrelated to what is otherwise a turn-based monster collecting game. I'm honestly kind of turned off from playing further just because of these being necessary for story progression.EDIT 2: With the recent 1.0.18 patch, the requirements for this segment of the game have been changed, making the jump rope minigame a bit easier to complete and changing the Flappy Bird clone to a more fun and engaging minigame. They also changed some mechanics that allow for players to more easily get Potent and Perfect Coromon, which does relieve some of the pressure of grinding and soft resetting. I think these are great improvements and I'm glad the devs have listened to fan feedback.7/10. WIth some quality of life improvements, this could be a truly great game, but I think the large amounts of RNG needed for optimization hold Coromon back from being as fun and engaging as it could be. Several puzzles being inaccessible for some people due to requiring fast reflexes or a good memory that doesn't get distracted can also prevent some people from getting through parts of the game without assistance. That said, the game itself is still beautiful, has a brilliant soundtrack, and has some unique battle mechanics, making it a charming and fun addition to the monster collector genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game after about 20 hours without playing the demo before (which let you keep your save)Overall thoughts:Solid creature collector game, stays true to the core of pokemon like creature collector games while also adding in its own spice that helps the game feel fresh. Sprites are pretty good, not the greatest ever some are generic but overall does the job for me. The names however are pretty bad but I really don't care about that so to each their own. The puzzles are good but very long and drawn out (you do a puzzle room and you feel like you're done only to enter another room and its the same puzzle again).The variety of monsters is super lacking, overall the variety is fine but when you're in a zone you only see monsters from that zone and 95% of trainers have a team of monsters from that zone so you rarely see monsters from the previous zone which gets boring and makes you just use 1 monster that will counter that zone. Speaking of counters the types in the game also are just weird. not bad, but weird. You have your general types but there's no grass type? the types are also singular and cant have dual type yet certain coromon can learn moves of all different types (started with fire starter and beat the game with him having 1 fire move 1 rock move 1 poison move and 1 foul move). It makes things weird because they are implied dual types ie. flying coromon which isn't its own type but they can learn flying moves, or bugs that learn poison moves but are normal type or electric type? Just makes things really hard to predict around and hard to build a "dream comp" because even though its fire type it might know water moves!The module system is nice but also pretty useless i don't think i used the stink module once cause it only makes 1 area of grass repel monsters? like what. Mostly just use the push module the rest are only used when the game wants you to. Literally learn the rock break module to use it 1 time for the story and that's it. Overall the animations are really good I was pleasantly surprised but they get pretty annoying because they are very long and theres no battle speed options so battle can be SLOW and i mean SLOW.Also this game is a grindfest make sure you got your hp cakes or be ready to do a lot of running back and forth you will fight battle after battle with no breaks in between. and the battles are tough sometimes, especially since you cant buy repels you have to make it with some weird recipe it just means sitting in A LOT of fights you wish you weren't in and towards the end of the game you will fail to run away more than you will succeed. The game is very good overall, it was good enough for me to sit through 20 hours and beat the game however with all the things mentioned above I found myself rushing to beat the game and not exploring much anymore because the battles and puzzles become tedious very fast. 6.5/10

It can be quite challenging and the experience can be quite customizable, which I really appreciate. This game plays very similarly to Pokemon, and a great alternative to it. I think a lot of complaints come from people very familiar to modern pokemon games where their hands are always held or fan-made rom hacks where they can use an emulator to use save states and speed up gameplay. I think options are always great, and in the future, a speed up option would be good for these players. Personally, I think the animations do a good job at playing quickly and respecting your time just fine. It can be challenging at times - unlike modern pokemon games - and I really like that.If you are even remotely interested in Pokemon or the monster taming genre of gaming, it's an easy pick up. Very active/responsive developers that clearly care for the game, and this game has a lot of polish and charm. I enjoy it a lot so far.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for April 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before May 7th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.It’s PokemonCoromon has such an obvious influence it even ends in Mon.  But at the same time, it also does things everyone wants to see.  This has a customizable difficulty with interesting choices like limited heals at the doctors, limits to monsters you can catch, and more.  Every character also gets a trait when it’s caught and those traits can make two similar creatures vastly different.  There’s also the ability to customize the stats of your creature and so much more.  Compared to the main genre which feels like it’s stagnating at times, Coromon feels like the breath of fresh area the fans of the genre are begging for. But at the same time, it’s Pokemon with most of the same negatives.  You’ve seen much of this idea before, and while there are tons of fresh moments, the majority of the game is leveling up monsters, fighting x number of bosses, this time you fight Titans or something, and while there are new abilities, you will feel like you’ve done this before.  Also, there are only 124 monsters here, and while there’s more content in other areas, having fewer characters than the first Pokemon game is a weird choice.  I know, this probably has more animations or art requirements, but It still feels odd. Pick this up if you like Pokemon.  This is a pure Pokemon style game, but it’s also so well done and does enough new that fans who may have been burnt out on the main series will probably find something fresh here.  At the same time, it’s not going to change most players' minds if they aren’t already fans of Pokemon. _childDocuments_.review: A very endearing little game! If you like pokemon, you'll like this. The graphics hold a note of familiarity, and the gameplay/ fight mechanics are also similar in style. Different to pokemon is the multitude of little add-ins that improve the basic idea of the game. For example, as well as having money and your (knock-off) pokemon to play with and find, you can grow little berries that you can give to your coromon or use to make potions; solve unique puzzles within the game (not too complex, but make life interesting); and even dig for gems to sell or give to your coromon. There are also lots of hidden things you can find just by looking in every setting. I thought each town was really well thought-out, and I thoroughly enjoyed trying not just to get rare coromon but also the slightly different spin it has on the monster collecting style that pokemon is famed for. The music is reminiscent in genre to pokemon, but the game is definitely individual enough to be given credit as its own thing. Have already spent a lot of hours (and have a lot to get through) just by passing the time doing these little things that improve the experience. Highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Good but not Great:This is a good monster collecting game, and one of the top ones that can satisfy your need for more additions in this genre. At this price, it is a steal deal. Pixel art is great and the Coromon all look very well designed. I think this is the first game in this genre where I haven't disliked a single monster. The puzzles are amazing, and all the biomes feel natural and fun to explore. The shinnies are phenomenal! It has some very fun game modes and settings too. Totally worth spending time on, and probably the best implementation of any game in this genre.But that doesn't mean it can't be better. First let's talk about the world. It is okay but I felt that the world grew tinier and tinier the more i progressed into the story. The first two location(cities/towns) were well populated but after this, you are basically going into a new location and expecting to talk to 5 strangers and walk into 2 houses. It felt rushed to me. Each new location gave less than what the previous one had and honestly it just never got me immersed into the game. The biomes were made well but none of them felt connected. As a player I always felt teleported to a new one.Next, let's talk about the plot. It is not great, and it feels forced into the story as though the team never had planned any and just added an antagonist force and blended it with the plot. Aliens? C'mon, anything is better than that.Next, we should talk about quests. They were good and well fun to complete but often times I hated the rewards. Clothing and certain battle items were loved but berries and cakes and spinners? No. Even the Milestone rewards and Gold Chests in the over-world began to fall back as I progressed more. Nothing felt worth it. Even skill flashes which were a dope addition, never felt useful. Most ones you could get sucked and even after reaching the frost biome, there is like 2/25 skill flash that I actually found useful. More of them need to be distributed throughout the game.Finally, the Coromon and their skill distribution. There are some coromon who only learn moves of the type they are and then there are some with decent coverage. Why not give all coromon some coverage? That part is missing to me and that too felt rushed. Like the devs game attention to some and just left the others as is. If skill flashes are poorly distributed through the main game, at least the coromon should learn more by themselves. These may all seem like nitpicks but as a casual player, I enjoy such additions very much. So much so that, without these additions, both me and my friend who got the game had to quit playing around the "Ice Mountain" biome because we were simply bored. If some of these don't matter to you, then Coromon might be the best monster taming game you might have played in a while. And it is still, as is, very much worth every dollar. I hope some of these nitpicks can be heard in future instalments in the series as I am very much interested in seeing more from this studio! Good luck!

_childDocuments_.review: Edited after after 20hrs. Going to keep it short. The game has nice pixel art, with decent music, but it lacks charm. However the one thing that kept playing in my mind as I was playing this was...."Makes me want to play Nexomon" So I am not recommending this. For a few reasons. 1) the font kills my eyes. Pixel art games are fine, pixel font? Why? 2) There is just better out there. This does not reinvent the wheel, nor does it even attempt to. I think they played this very safe and as a result, the game feels paint-by-numbers level of bland. 3) and lastly, this one a me thing....but I hate puzzles. Why in the world would I, someone sent by the company to either protect a titan or save a fellow researcher then be accosted by someone else working for said company, and blocked by an inane "figure out the code as I F with you" puzzle? If the bad guys set up a trap I have to finagle my way around or through, fine. If a colleague is the one hindering my progress...hell with that. _childDocuments_.review: Coromon manages to take the worst elements of Pokemon and cut the best parts of Pokemon.- Dual typing is gone, replaced with attack-only types that should have fun interactions, but in reality add less depth than if they were simply put in as full types with creatures able to have 2 type tags. It doesn't even add much to combat because you can have a fully party of every main type to cover any weakness and get the Same Type Attack Bonus which massively increases damage over simply getting a good matchup with an attack type move.- Pop Culture Referential Humor. I think this is fine in moderation, that being said, Coromon uses it to an extreme degree to the point the world doesn't feel believable or stand-alone.- The main character isn't silent, which isn't a bad thing necessarily, but the main character here is so generic and lifeless, that I found their dialogue to be a waste of time and hated them.- Character customization options are poor. Because the game chose a chibi / Maple Story artstyle where the character is represented with about 60-80% being just the head, most your body options don't have enough detail to really notice fine changes and I couldn't really tell them apart and the facial options not strong either. I ended up just making the ugliest thing known to man so I couldn't misplace my character as a result because I never found anything I liked.- They decided to faithfully re-create the part of the Pokemon experience everyone hates: The tutorial. Where you can't do anything but talk to NPCs for a good half hour and slowly get shown mechanics that are inherent to the Monster Catching/Taming genre.- Personal preference: I found the Coromon "cries" to be poorly balanced audibly (some really loud and some really quiet) and I released one of the starting Coromon immediately because I found the cry to be that irritating to listen to.- Note about difficulty modes: Most of these modes are restrictions that are made from self-imposed "Nuzlockes" in Pokemon games, however, I think that development time could've been spent better polishing the game's fundamentals or from what I've heard its ending sequence, since at the end of the day, it took a lot of time to make these systems when a player could've gotten the same result without them, and on top of that, I'm sure the hardcore audience will still do self-imposed challenges on top of these ones anyway at some point.Silver lining: They did replace Pokemon's EV system with something you can control very easily which is great. However, relegating the IV system to "shiny" varients I wasn't a fan of personally because it made any regular colored Coromon not worth even considering picking up since those varients are much more common here than in Pokemon.

_childDocuments_.review: I have many hours in the demo version of this game.Coromon is a visually gorgeous and mechanically deep Pokemon clone that outshines the blueprint in many ways. The systems added are simple yet add depth; the story and world are brimming with character, unlike recent Pokemon games; and the graphics, music, and design are all incredible. Seriously, $18 on sale for this game almost makes me feel guilty. Often times, when reviews state "you can tell a lot of love was put into this", it's code word for "this game has heart but isn't actually that good." Coromon has a lot of love put into it, lots of heart, and is very good.I do have a few complaints that do not affect my recommendation, but I'd like to see potentially changed in the future:- Battle animations. They are notably long. I really, REALLY wish there was a speed up button or animation length option in this game.- The font is incredibly straining on the eyes. I think there should be a proper Serif font option--I know it would conflict with the game's aesthetic, but for accessibility purposes, some people (me included) have difficulties reading the pixelated text.- The amount of Coromon is small, with only 114 currently. To be fair, all 114 Coromon are interesting, unlike Pokemon, so the 114 is used better here than 114 in Pokemon would. But still, you can't help but feel like there's potential for more. - Limited post-game content. However, the bulk of this game is already large, and there's as many hours as you want in doing tasks like completing the Pokedex equivalent with variations, battling others, etc. And so YMMV for this aspect. I haven't run into any bugs/crashes in the full release yet. If you like Pokemon--ESPECIALLY if you like the older Pokemon games--this is a no-brainer. I've played many -mon clones on Steam and this one is by far the best. I dearly hope the devs continue to support this game for a long time, as I truly believe that it has the potential to become huge.

_childDocuments_.review: I really did want to like this game. I'm a huge fan of monster collector games (pokemon, monster sanctuary, digimon cyber sleuthes, etc), but this one just lost the spark for me. There are plenty of features that are great. Customizing your mons is accessible, farming isn't too difficult, there are some quality of life features that make it pretty easy to play. However, it lacks anything that makes me want to keep playing the game. In order to keep me playing, a monster collector game needs to have an interesting story, battle system, world, or catalog of creatures. The story so far (I've only just beaten the ground boss), is pretty tepid. I imagine this is meant to be a children's game and the story reflects that. That's fine, but then I would want a battle system that has a decent amount of variability. Maybe an intricate skill system that would allow a variety of builds for my crew? The system in Coromon is a similar rock-paper-scissors to pokemon, but with less variability. Do you have a move that the opponent is weak to? If yes, awesome; if not, sorry try again. Okay, well then is there at least a world that is interesting to explore? This is probably the strongest facet of Coromon for me. Unfortunately, the areas still don't have enough visual pizzazz to keep me interested. As a pixel graphic game, this is somewhat understandable, but Monster Sanctuary is another pixelated monster collector that does this beautifully. The biggest difference here, I think, is the interactions with the environment. Coromon's world has only a few methods of interacting with it and those are pretty monotonous in each area. And finally we get to the catalog of creatures, which is the biggest disappointment for me. Coromon follows the pokemon formula for this: you have several distinct evolution lines that use level to trigger the change. This is a great system that I usually enjoy. Seeing what my small mons grow into is one of the greatest sources of excitement for me in this style of game. Unfortunately, the evolutions lack impact in this game. Let's compare a starter in this game to gen 1 pokemon. In this game, my icy bear turns into a slightly larger icy bear; meanwhile, in pokemon red, my fluffy-tailed turtle turns into a bigger turtle with SHELL-MOUNTED CANNONS. Once I realized that I didn't care what my mons turned into, I couldn't really get myself to continue playing this game.If any of these facets had been compelling, I think I would have actually enjoyed this game. However, I don't think I can recommend this game to a fan of monster collector games.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty happy to see an indie studio do a monster collection game.Unfortunately, rather than a unique take on the monster collection game, this is a direct clone of pokemon. And I hate to say it, but if you haven't played gold version of pokemon from 20 years back, you may want to do that instead . . . This game doesn't do things differently at all.  So I am not that  excited to play this game. Additionally, this game feels like it was made so that the "nuzlocke" challenge is more integrated.Meaning, during my adventuring, I had to go back and heal so many times, just so I don't use up my precious items and gold. Even pokemon didn't feel like a slog in that way. There are other poor desgins that make the adventure feel like a grind. As another review pointed out, the movesets are incredible bland.  It loses a lot of the strategic layers that pokemon does have.The game has about 110 monster varitieties - with around 5 actual monster types. . . so even less than the first pokemon game.  . . just something to think about. It becomes apparent what is wrong with the game once you put a couple of hours into it. In terms of what you can do overworld and in battle, it is just extremely limited.  If you haven't played monster sanctuary yet, I recommend that instead. But Coromon just isn't different enough or good enough. It isn't bad for the price point I guess . . .

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically Pokémon if the series managed to evolve beyond one time gimmicks and the heartless milking of a big franchise name.It plays well, it has a nice pixel-artstyle, cool monster designs, great music and a lot of cool gameplay ideas (for example the monsters don't forget attacks, you activate 4 for combat). The game is also more engaging as it's a lot more challenging than Pokémon. Status ailments and stat debuffs are actually really useful and the general balance of types seems to be a lot better. There are also different difficulty levels and even optional Nuzlocke functions (but don't bother using those on your first playthrough or you're going to have a bad time). Also you're not forced to play a ten year old child traveling the world.This game is dirt cheap in relation to the content and quality you get.Tl;dr: If you like Pokémon for the gameplay and not just for the nostalgia of your long lost childhood happiness, then get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice monster-tamer game. It does an admirable job emulating old-style pokemon mechanics and game-play. I had a good time playing it.It's like pokemon. Turn-based battles, with type advantages, items, and so on. Some puzzles and platforming occur throughout the game. It seemed like fun to me. Perhaps at a couple points the 'mon encounters happen too frequently. I suspect the real issue is that not enough XP is given per win. The final 3 locations in the story required me to stop and grind my coromon levels up significantly. The grinding isn't that fun because it's just repetitive. I passed the time by listening to podcasts/videos. I used a few XP chips at the end to speed it up. I probably should have used them more frequently to cut this grinding down. I liked the story, but it's nothing too fancy. On par with pokemon. You get to save the world. Nice pixel graphics. The art-style is good. I think the individual coromon are creatively designed and unique.  Seems fine to me. Nothing super unique. The game uses a "potential" system to measure the quality of the coromon. In other words, you can catch a "normal", "potent", or "perfect" coromon. I eventually got my team to switch to potent coromon but it took more time to find them. I don't know if it's needed. I only came across a few perfect coromon, so there's a lot of luck there, and I can't imagine spending enough time to complete the coromon database for this game (catching normal, potent, and perfect versions of EACH).

_childDocuments_.review: A great game to scratch that Pokemon itch. There's something for all Pokemon fans.You've got:- difficulty customization, including easy mode, Nuzlocke options, randomization, and smarter AI for your comfort or to challenge yourself- multiple color palettes per Coromon for the shiny hunters- access to your Coromon storage anywhere- the ability to reset potential skill points -- potential skills accumulate faster for potent and perfect Coromon- the ability reroll a Coromon's ability (with some RNG)- the ability to permanently increase potential values -- this means nearly-max potential Coromon can be perfected- customization of Spinners (pokeballs)- cooking with berries to create healing/buffing items- auto-fruit collector for all those cakes you're gonna make- access to more than one Platinum Spinner (Master Ball)- Battle Tower post-game content (new as of 1.21; haven't played it yet)There's a spectrum of cute-ugly-weird-bulky Coromon available to you. You have Bittybolts (inspired from a beta Pokemon design) and then you have Krybeests... and whatever the hell Grimmask is (I love it). If you don't like a Coromon's perfect or potent color palette, you can opt to change its skin to normal or a custom one from the Style Shop at. You can evolve/devolve Coromon at will, if you meet level requirements. There's Skill Flashes (TMs) and no move is ever fully deleted. You have access to all skills, but only 4 can be active at a time. I loved figuring out strategies to make my teams of Coromon feel powerful.There's puzzles that are a clear love letter to early gen Pokemon games: conveyor belt floors, ice sliding caves, navigating in the darkness. There's also unforgiving stealth parts that require quick reflexes and timing. Some people will hate that more than me. The main downside is the dated humor/meme references. The serious scene in Alavi (last in-game town you reach) had tonal whiplash that felt bad, but in a funny way. What offsets that for me is the refreshing diversity casually present in the game (male Nurses, a disabled professor, gay scientists).The story pre-1.21 was disappointing and anticlimactic. Post-1.21, the story is still  decent, but there's added detail and depth to the world that's 100% an improvement from its previous iteration. You learn a bit more about the antagonists, their goals, and Crimsonite. There's more focus on the environmentalist/eco-friendly theme, which I appreciated. Side characters who've been around since the start of the story get to appear and do stuff instead of feeling forgotten. IMO I would like to learn more about the Wubbonians and lean more sci-fi, but hey, they hint at a sequel... The devs put a lot of love in this game. The customization options have gradually been added to the game since its release. Two more evolution lines were also added with 1.21, which, while not a lot, added some more diversity to my second playthrough. I appreciate that the devs don't want to waste my time by making much of the stat management convenient. The sound design is solid and the soundtrack reminds me of the Hoenn OST.Overall/TLDR; definitely recommend for any Pokemon fans who like charming and detailed pixel art, completing a collection of all monsters, Nuzlocke fanatics, grinding for levels and shiny hunting, or for people who want a harder Pokemon game.

However, the gameplay is feasibly even more brainless than in Pokemon (other than the nice SP system) due to limited movesets/types and traversing the world is a tiring chore.If there were an option to make the entire game run at 2-3x speed (as with emulating Pokemon), this would probably feel significantly less bad to play. _childDocuments_.review: In spite of being in the same game genre as its infamous competitor, to call Coromon just a "Pokemon-clone" is to do it a disservice, because it really tries to improve on a lot of quality of life that Pokemon has not implemented into any of its games yetThe improvements start at the very beginning of your adventure, where you can basically assemble your own ruleset for your playthrough. You can play in a very "classic" way, make certain aspects easier or harder (f.e. you can set if you need an extra item to revive a member of your team, or just a normal healing cake, this game's version of potions), as well as set options for a Randomizer mode or a "permadeath" mode, so you can keep the game fresh with new challenges and quirks even on multiple playthroughs.Another aspect that pleasantly surprised me is how much the game allows for flexible build crafting within your team. The moves known by your Coromon can be switched on and off anytime outside of combat. Similarly they can learn extra moves for so called "skill flashes" by just owning the Flashdrive and turning on the skill, making the skill flashes effectively infinitely reusable.Additionally you have a lot of freedom in how to further train your coromon and specialize their stats in certain ways. Similar to Pokemon's IV and EV system, Coromon spawn with a certain "Potential" betweeen 1 and 21. In addition to their regular level they gain "Effort XP". The higher the potency the more Effort XP they accrue whenever they defeat an opponent. with every Effort Level they gain, you get the opportunity to distribute 3 additional stat points to directly increase Offense, Defense or Health stats.In addition to gaining more stats this way, thereby growing stronger faster, Coromon above a certain potency value also have a different appearance, similar to a "Shiny" pokemon. But even further than that a Coromon with a potency of 21 is considered "Perfect" and has YET ANOTHER different color pallette, and it's really fun to go on the hunt for these rare versions, both for the prestige and in oder to bolster your team's power.The game also has NPCs who provide services to manipulate these values, like resetting your Effort distribution, so you can "respec" if you made a mistake, as well as means to increase potency or change a coromon's passive ability, of which they have 1 out of a selection of up to 5, depending on their species, so there's a huge variety of them.As for the story: You are tasked with collecting the Essences of the 6 "Titans", legendary Coromon who keep the main elements of the World Velua in balance. For that you have to face each one of them in combat, while some mysterious group of Aliens is working against you, for reasons of their own, but I won't go into more detail to not spoil too much.However it has to be said that the ending of it all is rather abrupt. There are even certain names and even what looks like an entire Zone of the game hinting at a continuation that never manifests. And so the whole thing ends on a rather unsatisfying cliffhanger.Adding to that there's not really any PvE post-game like a Duel-Tower or a Battle Zone (or at least the game does not point you to it) it seems the only thing you can do it play the PvP ladder. So that was a bit of a letdown.In terms of balance the type chart feels ok, with certain coromon types standing out as particularly capable offensively or defensively, so f.e. you can startegically switch in a defensive type if you don't know what you'll be up against, and you have a good chance of resisting whatever your opponent may throw at you. However different to Pokemon half of the types only appear on skills, and never on Coromon themselves. This leads to a weird imbalance, because many of the strongest attacks have an attack only type but they can never get the damage bonus from matching the type of the Coromon using it, as well as one type in particular having no offensive weakness, meaning it cannot be resisted.Additionally the Titans use mechanics in their encounters that can feel pretty cheap to the player, sometimes even unfair. Also they are overleveled compared to the story progression, so if you level your team to par, you will be overlevelled for the area that follows it. That's a weird design decision, beause you cannot capture these titans like you could legendary pokemon, so this could just be done by cranking up their base stats, while leaving their Level in line with the progression.Last but not least: This game is incredibly well optimized for mobile play, with several means of control from mouse and keyboard, over controler/steam deck handheld to even touchscreen support already properly implemented and a UI to support every control scheme very well.All that being said: Coromon still a very good game, especially for me who has been left a bit disappointed by Nintendo's recent output in this genre. With the options to run a proper Nuzlocke, or Randomizer challenge run without the need to mod the game is something that will probably have me come back to this game at a later point. Who knows: maybe there will be some DLC to continue the story as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is arguably one of the best Pokemon-like creature-collector games out there, although it achieves this by copying the vast majority of its mechanics and play-style wholesale from our beloved franchise.It's almost a playable version of "can I copy your homework?" "yeah, just change it up enough", although in my opinion, some of the changes aren't for the better.(My review hit the character limit - oof - I'll try and shorten it from the 3-mile essay it was)Firstly, the graphical style, artwork and general feel of the game is great. It has gorgeous graphics reminiscent of titles like Stardew Valley or Graveyard Keeper and manages to somehow make even the 'mons fit into that artstyle.The 'mons themselves are also all unique and none of them made me think "wow, what a ripoff!". They also have good-looking attack animations.The overworld map is also very pretty in my opinion, with very distinct areas that fit in with where they are and how you get there. There's everything from a rural farming town, to a creepy town next to a swamp and even a gorgeous desert town (and more I have yet to discover).The soundtrack is another plus-point as each soundtrack is fitting for the areas it's used in, with each town feeling unique; Bonus points for the 'mons cries being their actual names as well, which is something I always wanted from Pokemon (to use the anime cries).I also like how here, instead of needing to get lucky with IVs and natures and shininess, then grind out EVs, here it's all in the "potential value", which you mostly tell when you enter into battle, as the game will tell you whether a 'mon is standard, potent or perfect. There are also ways to increase odds of potent and perfect pokemon as well.Now, that doesn't mean it's all good, as I think there are several big negatives with this game.Firstly, the dungeons that lead to the bosses are too long and tedious, while the puzzles that fill those dungeons are ridiculously over-used and makes the dungeons feel like a complete slog. Having to return to a checkpoint 20 times because you hit a ghost or a dart-trap was more than frustrating. Even the sliding tiles and door lever puzzles from the first boss were way overused.Secondly, this game is a bit of a grind-fest. Wild 'mons don't seem to give barely any exp and so the only way to level-up decently is to defeat every trainer on a given map-tile. On Normal-difficulty, battles are set-style too, so have fun trying to swap-out-train lower-level 'mons. With this, you'll also be constantly back-tracking to the nearest healing centre.Even with grinding a decent amount, some trainers and the bosses will out-level you and, in the case of the bosses, have 5-10x more HP than your main, if not your whole team combined.Then there's the style-shop. Simply-put, the skins are extremely cool, but screw having daily and weekly tasks in a 99% single-player game, especially when it'll take you 1 week+ to buy a single 900 currency skin; You'll need to play this game daily, completing every task and maybe in 6 months you'll be able to get every skin from the shop. Although you'll be long-done with the game before you probably even get a single high-end skin.That currency should have been the milestone reward and the skins should have been cheaper overall.This isn't a live-service or mobile-game, so don't put junk like that here.As for the story, it's there. For me, it's neither a negative nor a positive. It's reminiscent of Pokemon with how you'll be the saviour of the world and fight against the "evil team"; Again, it's there, it's fine and serves its purpose.Overall, part of me wants to put this game as not recommended, however, it's fun. It's mostly fun because it takes so much of its mechanics and gameplay from Pokemon and even bad Pokemon games are fun.Although, this game wasn't sloppily put together unlike recent Pokemon, as it runs well with no notable bugs, glitches or crashes, nor was it developed by a multi-billion$ mega-corp. Oh, and it's not being sold at £55+ either, with a separate version with 3 'mons difference for another £55+.So, for those reasons I'm saying that I recommend this game and will say that any Pokemon (or creature-collector) fan should pick this up; You'll get your money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a solid monster collection game. As someone who hasn't liked any Pokemon games since Pearl, I thoroughly enjoyed myself here.The most prominent thing to point out is how beautiful the sprite art is for the Coromon. The monster designs are  I can't think of any on the top of my head that I straight up disliked, and that is one of the best aspects you could hope for in a game about collecting creatures. Also, there is a system in the game that makes "shiny" hunting more tolerable for casuals. Every Coromon can be Normal, Potent, or Perfect. Each with their own color variant. Even though perfects are still tedious to get, Potent Coromon were similarly satisfying to find.The combat is good. One huge thing this game does, that I think every indie monster collecting game needs to do, is let you quickly see type match-ups mid battle. Compared to Temtem where I  can't remember most of the match-ups. Along with this, things like stamina and status effects being able to wear off on their own over time helped a lot in terms of keeping the pace steady.Now for all of you hardcore fans of the genre, you'll be happy to know this game has its own in game difficulty settings, including both nuzlocke and randomizer options! As for the "default" settings, I genuinely got wiped a handful of times. Some trainers would keep me on my toes, and many of the boss fights were pretty brutal. The only thing I can't comment on is PvP, as I haven't really delved into that.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah Coromon, what a complete and utter failure (tldr at end):One of the better things from the demo that they dropped the ball with in release was the story and how it was surprisingly open for a linear game. Taking part in a pretty expansive region, you're tasked with defeating massive boss monsters called "Titans" to save the world or something. What made the story so good in the demo were the abundance of side-quests that allowed you to do things at your own pace and offered really good rewards. Instead, the number of them you get in the post-demo areas is single digits and all of the characters you meet seem "area focused". "Oh look, a guy from the desert region, I'm never going to see him again in the next place." In addition with the game being nowhere close to finished, the story seemingly just stops in disappointing fashion with some promise of future DLC.So you beat the game after about 20 hours, time to delve into that juicy post-game content right? Wrong. Despite being out of early access and thus considered a complete game, the post-game is so barren and dearth-ey that it's almost an embarassment. Aside from attempting to catch every possible form of the rather small mon-dex, there are a total of two repeatable trainers who use the same team in every battle. That's it. It's a massive disappointment seeing a game in 2022 have less playability than ones released in the 90s.Probably the biggest nail in the coffin is the sheer amount of bugs this game had at launch and still currently has. A bunch of moves (ghost ones especially) don't work properly, for a bit you could get softlocked in a couple of the regions, and the game has a tendency to crash especially during trainer battles. It's probably the biggest letdown of all, as for a non-early access game you expect at least a bit of polish.Ultimately it's hard to give this game anything close to a positive review when it fails on so many different levels. As an pokemon spin-off it has less content than any of the main series games including the original ones. As a non-early access game it has a sheer number of bugs and filler that makes it feel like a 6hr game with about 20hrs of pointless diversions. Considering how good the demo was and what they did between that and the release, Coromon may go down as one of the biggest steam disappointments/"what-ifs" of all time, matching the likes of PUBG.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for 7 hours and like other reviewers have said it's basically a pokemon clone, but it's done really well so far.  I started out trying to play with some elevated difficulty settings such as losing your coromon when they faint.  I found that due to the inherent increased difficulty, length of various hostile areas, and cost of restorative items, that the paranoia of losing my crew had me returning to town so many times that it became not very fun and progress came to a crawl.  I turned off that feature and I'm still finding it to be challenging but happy to know that I won't lose team members due to RNG.  There's also an ability that lets enemies hit and faint your coromon who aren't even on the battlefield! That would be a horrible way to lose your best coromon who is low HP on the sidelines.  It's good to know that if the game does become too easy that there are options for increasing the difficulty.  Or that if I wanted to do another playthrough I can completely randomize the coromon you encounter in different areas and also in trainer battles.   There's a LOT of settings you can tweak for a best-fit experience.One of my biggest complaints is also one that's been mentioned before, some of the status effects and other actions that involve multiple text boxes seem to pop up and go away very slowly and become a bit tedious.  It would be nice to have ways of speeding up these more mundane aspects of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very close to being good, but I feel like it just isn't there yet. The game feels unfinished in some aspects: the plot (which is advertised as one of the main selling points) kind of just ends with no real resolution, and there are allusions to "another adventure" as postgame content, but none of that seems to be in the game.The mechanics sometimes feel very restrictive. The roster of Coromon seems small to me. There are 106 Coromon (plus 8 Dark Magic Coromon that are just other Coromon but recolored and with a new type), but only 42 evolution families — this makes it seem like there are far fewer Coromon than there actually are, especially when later areas seem to just reuse Coromon from the beginning of the game. The final area of the game, the Ruins of Ixqun, still features Humbee and Golbeak, the final evolutions of some of the first Coromon you see in the game. The Pokemon equivalent would be seeing Raticate and Pigeot in Victory Road. There are no Dual Type Coromon, which makes battles significantly more linear than in a game like Pokemon. Another thing that contributes to battles being more linear is the fact that there are only 7 Types of Coromon (and an additional six types of moves). It's trivial to assemble a team with absolutely no weaknesses since there just aren't that many variables.My only other complaint would have to be in regards to the Potent/Perfect System. Potent/Perfect Coromon are this game's equivalent to Shiny Pokemon, however, Potent/Perfect Coromon get more additional skill points that you can invest in stats. While this sounds neat at first, since all your "Shiny" Coromon will be competitively viable, unlike in Pokemon, where you can get a shiny that's competitively worthless, practically forcing Competitive PVP players into shiny hunting is awful. I have a team of Six Perfect Coromon (Glamoth, Volcadon, Humbee, Eclyptor. Krybeast, and Cyberite). Perfect Eclyptor is given to you for free, but for the other five Coromon, in order to make them perfect, I had to find a Coromon with a Potential value of 19 or higher (21/3194 chance, even with a Potent Scent it only becomes roughly a 63/3194 chance), and then go to the Potentiflator in order to increase the potential of the Coromon. If the Coromon is a 21 (1/3194 chance, 3/3194 chance with a Potent Scent), it does not need to be Potentiflated. If the Coromon is a 20 (4/3194 chance, 12/3194 chance with a Potent Scent), it is guaranteed to become perfect when Potentiflated. However, if you found the far more common 19 Potential Coromon (16/3194 chance, 48/3194 with a Potent Scent), you only have a 60/3194 chance of it becoming perfect, forcing you to save and soft reset for the perfect. I normally wouldn't mind this — there should be some level of work to getting a perfect Coromon, in my opinion — however, you're forced to save and reset BEFORE handing the Coromon over, so unless you get lucky, you're forced to walk a thousand steps inbetween each reset for the Potentiflator to work. You're resetting for a 1.879% chance, so you'll often have to do somewhere in the neighborhood of 30-40 Resets before getting the Perfect off of a 19 Potential Coromon. It seems completely unnecessary to force players to walk the thousand steps thirty to forty times when the only reason this device exists is to reset before using it, hoping to get a perfect Coromon.If the game updates with reasonable postgame content, and maybe story rewrites (the Devs have said that they're reworking the ending), then this game would be a recommend. However, as it stands, I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best 2D Pokemon like game you find here. It has many Quality of life improvements, even own nuzlocke and randomizer modes. All the monster look neat and it is really easy to build a team you like, yet challenging to min/max the full potential. Also handles the concept of IV and EVs really accessible with the "potential" system. You can set effort values by yourself, which acts like a second level bar and IVs are a simple set number you can even check at the start of a match. You can consider a perfect potential of 21 even a shiny Coromon. Every Coromon got 2 alternative colors depending of the potential and perfect is very rare without helping items.In regards of online functions: You can PvP friends, but searching randoms takes a while. Trading is not possible, but you can find every coromon sooner or later regardless and a battle tower kind of deal unlocks after the credits, but only avaiable for singleplayer.There is also a progression pass and dailies, which are never mendatory to do. The rewards are gems, which you can spend on some special skins for your monster. I took the shark starter and grinded 400 gems in one week to make him fat, it is hillarious and gave me a reason to play.The only thing I think is lackluster is the story. While I like the approach it feels near the end, that it want to get into a big climax, but the end is just feels like "You win :) Credit time"Edit: There is another thing that really made the game less good near the end, but it is a spoiler for until you reach the second last temple All in all a recommendation if you want to play pokemon on PC, are a fan of the genre or want a game to grind stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: There are some ways that this is an improvement over Pokemon. The first thing that comes to mind are difficulty options and additional settings such as being able to pick a monster when the battle starts. There are also attacking types that a monster cannot have. But there are way too many flaws.Additional difficulty optionsAttack only typesOption to enable and disable which 4 moves are available at a time (instead of a move re-learner)Attacks use SP which is shared between all moves and can be recovered by resting for a turn (prevents sweeping)Some attacks are more balanced and weather is more balanced except hailYou can change the color of your fidget spinners for your monstersIV equivalent is better but still heavily flawedShiny monsters are based on their single IV value (there are also two different forms)EVs can be placed into specific stats you wantNot quite enough monster selection (106 without duplicates that have the type mentioned later, 114 total)Few viable attack optionsType chart does not make senseNot enough typesTypes are not balancedSome types are much better than othersTypes are only super-effective against 1 other type except waterThe type used by the villain is extremely overpowered and frustrating to play against (resists everything but itself)You can't capture the overpowered type till the end of the game (2 minutes before the game randomly ends)You are forced to capture new monsters at random pointsStory is bad, somehow much worse than most of the Pocket Monster gamesHeld items are generally useless except a fewAbilities rarely effected anythingPixel art needs more pixels (mostly only an issue for characters and monsters, scenery looks great)Game is not difficult but frustrating at timesSome moves have slightly less than 100% accuracy for maximum frustrationWhy does hail randomly freeze a non ice monster with a super low chance?Most of the puzzles are annoying but solvable by a 4 year oldYou will find more yourself that I am unable to think of at the momentA synopsis of the story would be: Child stops aliens with fidget spinners fired from an arm mounted bey-blade launcher. I would rate this game a 3/10. If you enjoy Pocket Monsters a lot and don't mind the lack of pixels, you may enjoy this game quite a bit, but probably would rather play your Pocket Monster game instead. You may come across some bugs but nothing completely game breaking. I am not sure what end game content there is supposed to be besides online battles and completing every random fetch side quest in the game. If Game Freak added the good things about this game to Pocket Monsters that would be great.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag. It has lots of good and bad sides to it. On first look it seems like a pokemon copy and not much more. The story has a similar feeling. There are everywhere scientists that are researching the Coromon, something that you also have often in pokemon games. You have the same kind of puzzles as in a pokemon game. With blocks to move, doors to open in the right order etc. Most of the puzzles are well made. But still they feel so similar to Pokemon puzzles. The monsters have their own attacks. But many have very similar feel and effects to Pokemon moves. Like at the beginning I catched an cow like Monster hat has a tail attack which hits the enemy 1 to 3 times. And therefore has a random damage output. Pokemon has an claw attack with the same mechanik. I know that its difficult to come up with completly new ideas. And Pokemon uses many mechanics, puzzles, story tropes etc. that where invented by different RPG games. What bothers me about this game is more the presentation like the overall art style and the mechanics look so extremly similar to Pokemon. In my opinion they should have tried more to make this game unique and not like a copy. Then it would stand out more. I give this a remonandation. But be aware that its: 1) extremly difficult 2) has a slow start 3) feels very similar to Pokemon. At the beginning you will habe to grind a lot and can die easily if you are not careful. If you dont like grinding and want same easy game where you can completly turn your brain off and overpower everything fast, better stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is an exceptional addition to the world of monster-taming RPGs, offering a refreshing blend of nostalgia and innovation. Drawing inspiration from beloved classics like Pokémon while infusing its own unique charm and mechanics, Coromon provides an immersive gaming experience that captivates both newcomers and longtime fans of the genre.One of the game's standout features is its captivating storyline, which unfolds in a beautifully crafted world filled with rich lore and intriguing characters. Players embark on an epic journey to become Coromon Masters, unraveling mysteries, and forging bonds with a diverse cast of creatures along the way.The gameplay mechanics of Coromon are meticulously designed, offering a perfect balance of strategy and accessibility. The turn-based battles are engaging and dynamic, requiring players to carefully consider their tactics and team compositions to overcome challenging opponents. The game also introduces innovative features such as the Coromon Fusion system, which adds an exciting layer of depth and customization to creature management.Visually, Coromon is a feast for the eyes, boasting stunning pixel art graphics that evoke a sense of nostalgia while still feeling fresh and modern. Each Coromon is beautifully designed, with distinctive personalities and abilities that make them a joy to collect and train.In addition to its compelling single-player campaign, Coromon offers robust multiplayer features, allowing players to battle and trade with friends from around the world. This adds a social dimension to the game, fostering a vibrant community of players who can collaborate and compete in exciting ways.Overall, Coromon is a must-play title for fans of the monster-taming genre, offering a captivating blend of engaging gameplay, rich storytelling, and charming visuals. With its perfect balance of nostalgia and innovation, Coromon stands as a testament to the enduring appeal of creature-collecting adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly every gripe I had for this game was fixed in a couple of updates. A lot of the game's randomness can now be toggled, and you can tune a lot of settings to play the game how you'd like. The music in the game is pretty good overall, and the sprite-work especially looks good. The monster designs are a nice change of pace, too. Many of them look menacing and badass rather than cute. I have two major problems with this game: For one, there are still frame-drop issues. Regardless of your computer specs, the game will lag (even on Steamdeck). Secondly, there is no post-game content. To me, this was extremely disappointing, since I was excited to use my team and potentially raise more Coromon for new challenges. Unfortunately, there isn't anything left to do after you beat the main story. Overall, this is a solid monster tamer game. Check it out if you want a nice alternative to Pokemon.

_childDocuments_.review: This game rocks.  In fact, I'm surprised it isn't more popular, though I suppose the fanbase may grow steadily as the game gets potential updates in the future.  As it stands May 2022, the game's story is complete, but there isn't much postgame outside of competition, which is good, but not great for people who prefer offline activities, such as myself. The story of the game is pretty meh.  But, so are the stories in Pokemon games, which is what I'm playing Coromon for.  I actually think the pretty meh story delivers exactly the kind of feeling of when I was playing the first few Pokemon games for the first time.  This very much feels like a classic Pokemon game to play, all the way down to the music and overall cheery vibe.  The visual style reminds me a bit of Stardew Valley and The Escapists, but has this extra beautiful color palette that my eyeballs really found to be a treat.The monster designs in this game are DELIGHTFUL!  Seeing each 'mon for the first time was very exiting for me, as my favorite part of these kinds of games is the unique designs I get to see featured.  It was a pleasure building up my squad along my adventure.  The balance of the game (I played on normal difficulty) is very good for people used to the JRPG turn-based formula but want a little bit more of a challenge.  The level curve felt mostly consistent and in general, felt pretty balanced.  I had difficulty with a few battles in the game and felt engaged for each battle.The potential feature is also AWESOME!  As a shiny hunter, this game majorly rewards staying out and hunting for the best version of a Coromon you can possibly catch, and having more than one color variant makes team building feel extra special.  I liked the way the entire game felt to play and experience, it's really something any Pokemon fan should play, it evoked this deep feeling of joy and nostalgia as playing Pokemon as a kid did.  It's an awesome effort from fans of these types of games and it shows, in my opinion.  Don't miss out on this sweet game!!

_childDocuments_.review: Personnally i would not reccomend this game, the creature design is really solid, and i like the idea of the different forms being better rather than a complicated breeding system but there are some serious flaws.Type ChartThe tyoe chart makes no logical sense, and there are some types that only apply to moves... Why? Fossil Fighters only needed 5 types to be good, Coromon has types like Foul, Cut and Heavy, why? Why does Cut beat Electric? Who knows. There didnt need to be as many types as there are, and their advantages dont exactly make sense.The puzzles.I havent even made it to the first titan yet. the Thunderous cave is stupidly long and i wandered though it 3 times because i didnt catch the story wanted me to go out of the cave to another location to move foreward.And i wanted  to stick it out, but then i lost to the fuse puzzle and i decided to quit. It would be difficult for the games first "challenging puzzle" if there were no changes, but you added a timer and all this other crap that just makes it feel unfun and frusterating.PotentialMy final gripe. I had a coromon with a potential of 20, and i had seen that there was a facility that allows you to increase potential if you pay 2500 of the ingame currency. For those who dont know, a perfect coromon has a potential of 21 and is considered perfect, so i spent the money to upgrade it, and nothing happened when i got it back, the game didnt explain that you cant upgrade a coromon to be perfect, its just stuck at 20. These are the 3 strikes. Im out, great concept but it drags on in places for no reason. Gets boring and needlessy difficult.
