_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are nice. The music is probably one of the best parts of the game. Nice monster designs (not the best in my eyes, but pretty good). Unfortunately, these positives are drowned out by a myriad of problems, which I imagine aren't an issue if you're aiming to playing competitive or nuzlocke modes. I haven't finished the game, and I don't think I will. Below is why.It's generally boring and a slog, with a lot of grind, too frequent wild encounters with a lack of variation in species in an area, weird balance issues, and uninteresting story and rough dialogue, and areas that long overstay their welcome (not helped by the lack of healing points and the annoying stamina system, mostly because it doesn't replenish between battles). A pet peeve of mine in monster taming games is that accuracy is a stat that should not exist in turn based games (fight me). If you do have accuracy to deal with, damaging moves that reduce the target's accuracy should definitely not exist. Items are too expensive. Berries and cakes are weirdly implemented: there are cakes and berries that do the same thing like healing statuses, but berries can only be used if your mon uses it in battle when held (seems like a dumb restriction to me). Berries grow too slowly. Annoyingly grindy dailies for cosmetics currency which would only feel right in a mobile games. Cosmetics are too expensive. What puzzles exist are uninteresting. It also has a constant stutter that happens a couple times a second all the time (I found this pretty annoying when running around).I don't feel like I'm having fun with this game. It's a pretty game, and the devs should be proud of that, but it ultimately doesn't do anything better than Pokemon does. There are a number of mechanics which are just an annoyance, or are mechanics taken from pokemon but changed to become (more) annoying. The first sentence of the this page says "Coromon is a modern take on the classic monster-taming genre", yet the only "modern" thing about it seems to be the inclusion of dailies and grindy cosmetics. I find myself disappointed in what Coromon is. If I wanted more pokemon, I think I'd rather play pokemon ROM hacks over Coromon. You'll get a similar (arguably better) experience in many aspects.  In some ways, I think Monster Sanctuary has spoilt me a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option, because this game is fun, and there is a lot you can get out of it. HOWEVER, there are a lot of problems with this game. A lot of the problems are small nitpicks, that normally I would brush off, but a lot of small things add up to a big thing. For example, it is easiest to play this game with a mouse and keyboard, and it seems to be designed around that. However, there is no sprite for your mouse, it's just the same pointer that your mouse is outside of the game. That's really minor right? No way something like that ruins a game for you. Except you notice so many small things, that it just makes you want to play one of the games this one is ripping off. This game does not have the luxury of having a unique concept. You see these small annoying things, like how insanely long berries take to grow, like genuinely hours pass and they're still not ready, and it just makes you want to play a game with the same gameplay and mechanics and without those problems.This game, at its core, just made me want to replay monster sanctuary and pokemon diamond. Because at the end of the day, those games are exactly like this one, just without all the small annoying things.There's a lot of cool stuff in this game, like the difficulty system is just the rules for a nuzlocke, which is awesome! But there's a lot to hate too, like the lackluster story, the insanely low chance of getting useful "coromon" (It's a 1/3194 chance to get one that gains stats at a good pace), the genuinely cringey dialogue (the "humor" is EVERYWHERE, and it's half god awful puns, and the other half is reference humor, like oh my god, they made a character that looks like ash named ashton, isn't that funny??? They literally make a pickle rick joke in the game too. It's just "look, you recognize that right? We made a character that looks like indiana jones, that's funny right?)This game has a genuinely interesting mechanic for how moves are used (your coromon don't have uses for specific moves, they have basically mana and moves have different costs), but other than that, this game is just worse than its competitors. Play it if you've already 100%-ed monster sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that makes me wish Steam had a rating I could give this game between "good" or "bad".I've played quite a few monster catching RPGs and Pokemon-likes over the years, and Coromon is just... kind of there. It's very aggressively similar to Pokemon, from the base mechanics, to TMs, catching, trainer positions, even down to the scale of stats and numbers. It makes it very difficult for the game to establish any identity for itself. There's just nothing really unique or interesting about it in the time I played. While there's a few creatures I kind of liked, most of the designs are  a bit bland.There's a number of relatively unique ideas, such as types that no creatures can have, but deal more damage to specific other types, but making a dedicated "stab" type that works well on electric creatures doesn't add very much over, say, some moves just having an "anti-elec" property. Mechanics like Stamina penalize the player and only the player far more than PP ever could, and just leave me asking myself "Why did they make the choice to add this? Just because other people did?"I'd like to play more of this game to see if my worries about things like this are unfounded, but... There's just nothing here to pull me back in. So much of the appeal of this sub-genre is in seeing something in front of you that makes you think "Woah! I want one of those!" or "I wonder what I'm gonna see in the next area?", catching you off guard with fun surprises as you comb through each area and try to collect one of everything. And, to their credit, some of that the game does very well, with hidden items galore, and side quests aplenty. But, at the end of the day, I just wasn't having fun.

_childDocuments_.review: When I planned to write this review it was going to be a cautious thumbs up, but unfortunately I just... can't. The main flaw to the game is that they stay squarely under their obvious influence's thumb, but tried to cater to "hardcore" fans of it: The obsessive shiny hunters, the online super-competitive folk, and those who wanted more challenge (Nuzlocke, etc.)And in so doing, they never figured out a target audience to aim for and failed to capture one.Storyline: It's... there. It's a thing. It points distantly to some deep concepts, but never explores any of them. The whole story line is like a summer puddle, it looks enticing from afar but by the time you get to it, it's dried up because it was so shallow. The ending in particular feels exceptionally unearned and incomplete.Graphics: The GBA-style art looks mostly great. The Coromon sprites are MOSTLY great. There's a few weird bits. My biggest gripe is that the battle screen has zero concept of perception, which makes the back of your own 'mon feel tiny in front of the enemy.Sound: The game was at its best when it wasn't trying to go "Lets get something super close to Pokemon." Lots of sounds and jingles are such close copies you almost have to admire the dev's boldness. But the few times they went with something completely different they got something great, the theme used in a single building in a single town in particular is a major earworm.Gameplay: Ugh. Here's the biggest breakdown for me. The game is a slog to play, and not a rewarding one. Extreme grinding in one area to get to par, then everything is the same level range as you progress until you reach the next where you rinse and repeat. The major spikes already make for an obnoxious level grind, but the rest of the game design makes it even worse. Every area overstays its welcome with a massive, sprawling layout that takes a great amount of time (and, often, an aggressively high encounter rate). There's treasures to find tucked around, but they're often unrewarding. Combat is tedium, with one-hit wins being unlikely even with a team 10+ levels ahead of your opponents. Most of the RNG and movesets are built around slowing every single combat encounter even further. Status ailments feel overpowered... but are poor choices to use against NPCs/wild encounters, they're meant to slow the player down even further.Similarly, puzzles frequently appear and are at first novel and interesting (though many are cribbed directly from Pokemon), except the developer tends to throw longer variations of the same puzzle at you over and over until you're sick to death of them. The stealth sections were particularly grueling and far, far, far too long.All in all, this is a game that not just has no respect for a player's time, but is outright hostile to it. It will waste your time constantly in so many ways, not with fun but with things like running in literal circles while you wait for the 9th Trait change to see if you finally get the trait you want or a seven-round battle of 3-on-1 against wild enemies you've fought a dozen times already."Does this mechanic add fun for our players?" was a question the developers clearly never asked themselves.The game was a slog, and one that never felt very rewarding.  And because of that, despite all that they do right, I can't give it a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the "Very Positive" Rating fool you: This game has no original ideas or "its own spin" in any way; This is a 1:1 copy of Pokemon EXCEPT WORSE. Instead this game only copies the combat and basic ideas of Pokemon, but executes on them way worse, without adding anything of its own. Coromon is "Pokemon but Worse" and I do not see any reason to recommend something that is significantly worse than what it copies.  This is not a question of "but Coromon is an indie game", because the *general ideas* of this game are nonexistant. Even if you have less ressources than a AAA company, the least you can ask for is for indie developers to have unique ideas, but Coromon lacks that entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this was an enjoyable little game.  It obviously wears its Pokemon inspiration proudly, and ultimately I think it does what Pokemon does well.  Raising a team of monsters that grows with you throughout the journey.  That's the core appeal of this genre to me, and Coromon handles it satisfyingly.The sprite work is top notch, and the monster designs are creative and cool.  There were few that I disliked.  Building and raising a team of Coromon is a joy.  Towards the end, it can start to feel like you're seeing a lot of the same monsters over and over, though.  Just a few more monsters would have been welcome, but the ones we have are all pretty fantastic.The world is creative.  Each town has a unique flair, not just visually, but also in the attitudes of the people living there.  The highlight for me was this desert town with a corrupt town guard that charges toll just for entry.  The dungeons were cool too.  Gone are the straight hallways of Pokemon.  There were a lot of puzzles here, none of which were so difficult as to be frustrating, but just enough to keep the player engaged.The comparisons to Pokemon aren't always positive, though.  The type system is mostly lifted from Pokemon, but here it's simplified, almost to the point of being dumbed down.  There are fewer types overall and no combined types.  Coromon don't learn many moves outside their own type either, which can make combat feel a little basic.Where Coromon is at its weakest is in its narrative.  The story passes by with very little sense of tension and almost no emotional weight.  By the end, it almost felt like the story was building up to something, and then it just ends.  I remember saying "that's it?" when the story reached its end.So, overall, if you're looking for a profound narrative or a complex gameplay experience, look elsewhere.  But, if you're looking for a simple monster collector with a non-complex storyline, then you'll get what you paid for with this.  Overall, I enjoyed my time with Coromon, but your results may vary depending on what you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Story required reflex games ruin this game. Some achievements seem to be broken. If all you want is a creature collection game that isn't Pokemon, choose something else. This game tries to go in too many different directions, and feels like it never settled on a destination. -----I feel like this game could have been good. Some parts of it are done quite well, others not so much. I understand that a lot of the extra elements that are within the game are there to differentiate it from the game its based on, to make it different enough not to get sued out of oblivion. I went into this game with that understanding, but was still let down. The elements that shine in this game are what are good in Pokemon, the rest? They all feel like they were put in to make it 'different' enough, and the game-play suffers for it.To start things off, the reflex games. These games are one of the main reasons for my bad review. I wouldn't review it poorly if the reflex mini games (which do not respond properly on keyboard and mouse, requiring extra button clicks or taps in order to get the character moving in the first place and thus add to the difficulty in a way that does not feel intentional.} It feels like loose controls, like the developers ran out of time, or they didn't care enough to fine tune things enough to make the mini games really playable for everyone. Secondly they're tied to story progression. That's right, a reflex game can soft lock you out of the second half of this game if you cannot do it. To top all of that off? There are achievements that are tied to reflex mini games, and the scores required are ridiculous. Suggested ways to beat them? Keep trying until you get it. I'm not particularly good at reflex games in the first place, and probably wouldn't have purchased this game if I had realized how much weight they had in it. I play games to have a good time, not have another job. If that were not enough to give a bad review, some of the achievements seem to be bugged, my character's research level is currently 53, and the achievement for reaching research level 50 has yet to unlock. I'm not sure if the achievement is tied to advancing further in the story, it wouldn't make much sense for it to work that way, but its either bugged or tied to something that isn't readily apparent. The Coromon art is good, the battling feels natural, but considering that battling is only half the game here, it isn't enough to make the game enjoyable. Especially when they throw quests at you like "beat a Coromon 3x your level, with no help from the rest of your team, no held items, and no items can be used during the battle." It feels like a waste of time and effort, for something that likely won't enhance the game much if at all. The "Potential" mechanic feels good, and I generally like it, especially with ways to improve your odds of encountering Coromon with Potential, but again, the creature collection part of the game just doesn't make up for the other deficiencies. The game-play generally feels boring, with a lot of backtracking and grinding, which makes me want to play it less than I do other games that have a more engaging story. The story itself is part of the problem here, not enough information is given to the player at any given time. You're basically told "hey go grab these essences" without any explanation as to why they actually need them, or how this helps with the apparent alien invasion. It doesn't feel like there's a reason for me to hurry and save the world, it doesn't feel like there's any pressure at all to actually work towards finishing the story.The game feels overworked, and like the developers never played it to completion.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that i have been looking for a oldschool Pokemon like game for years. I've gone through many browser pokemon games and actual published games over the years and this is probably the most polished unique monster taming game in the market.This game has nice familiar mechanics but with much more streamlined and smooth game play. One such example would be HM/module function which is no longer intrusive to your skill builds or having an HM slave. The type system is quite basic and easy to grasp with comparably small number of coromons (114) which is a small quib of mine. Hoping the roster is expanded with more versatility. Overall well designed mechanics.The story is good with a light hearted tone as it doesn't take itself too seriously. The world opens up as the story progresses which allows players to play though level appropriate areas without stumbling onto overlevelled opponents. There are enough surprises and secrets that may trip you up every now and then. We go through a lot of terrains with their own unique traversing puzzles. The puzzles in the overworld provide a good challenge with normal-medium difficulty in general. The game doesn't have an underwater section which will hopefully be added in the future.The overworld has good pixel art that suit the terrain and style of the different areas. The coromon sprites are well designed for most part and very few are in the lazy/bad design catagory. Battle backgrounds are nicely designed for different areas. Everything is great for most part, although some skill animations could use an upgrade.The music is soothing and fresh while having that nostalgic vibe at the same time. Skill sounds are crisp and suit them very well. Not much to say, its great.Fun and well thought out gameplay with many quality of life improvements over other games. Great visuals and audio with good character designs. Nostalgic and fun for older players of this genre and fun and innovative for the young audience. I am a casual player for most part and had quite a lot of fun in my 30+ hours of gameplay and considering that content updates are expected in the future i will say its well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I can't sing its praises enough. Not only are the models great, but the Potential mechanic is so clever! It actually rewards you for finding the different color variations. Instead of just a cosmetic change, which the creature is usually weaker compared to regular colored versions; the different color Coromon level up and get potential points faster or slower depending on what color you got. However, one thing i would add if i had the chance would be the ability to use the Potential Scanner gadget during battle. That way you aren't wasting spinners in quests like in the sidequest you need to get two potential 14 or higher buzzlet for a researcher. To end on a high note, something else this game does very well is money and resource management. Both healing items and spinners are quite pricey for the rate of currency acquirement. Thus it makes the player really think about how much of something to buy; and also makes the player do whatever they can to make the most out of the spinners and healing items in battles. In other words, it subtly teaches critical thinking on several levels.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a wonderful creature collector! What stood out to me right away is the options for difficulty. Basically every rule or option you can dream up. Change shop prices and level up mechanics? Catch other trainers’ Coromon? Randomize basically anything? Build-your-own Nuzlocke with any rule I’ve ever seen and more? It’s wonderfully customizeable to our desires. Even settings to reduce RNG!After that you appreciate the wonderful quality of life features. Don’t like the evolution? De-evolve, and we’ll level up your ABILITY to keep it on pace! Change your ability to one of 4-5 options for a tiny fee, and improve your potency (because screw EVs, put the extra points where you want). Change your scores around, change the spinner (pokeball) they’re in, every town gives you more and more!The story is also nice and fun. More involved than many pokemon games but less than many RPGs. I’ve never had an issue with the standard “you’re 11 and everyone expects YOU to save the world” thing, but the fact that you’re an adult who’s doing this as part of a job actually adds quite a bit. Suddenly it makes sense when some random person you’ve never met is calling you to fix a problem, the department head gave them your number. Oh yeah of course you’re trusted, you're from THE TITAN TASKFORCE, they don’t know you’re new. When I went into an area halfway through and I had a TEAM there it made me happy. Sure they were performing all the standard “puzzle hints, item giving, or fighting you” NPC tasks, but it felt better. And the Titans got to be actual threats with like 8 moves and absurd HP, actual bosses!Now there is one major issue I have. I HATE that there's a huge store but it's locked behind daily rewards and IRL waiting and online PvP. Timegating is just annoying when you have to do your gaming in a few chunks per week. and for skins, yes you can just do daily challenge rewards, but it takes weeks for enough for 1 skin. Keep that garbage out of my single player games! This isn’t a mobile game trying to squeeze me for microtransactions, there’s not even gameplay DLC, so why are you gatekeeping things behind days logging in? really left a sour taste in my mouth at the start, though I grew to ignore it.That said, I do love this game, big recommend if you want a great pixel based pokemon esque game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, as a monster catching game, I think this game is solid. The story is kind of okay, the usual "band of baddies trying to destroy the world" or something, but where it falls short is the characters and motivation. As of the time of writing this review, i have collected 4/6 essences, the equivalent of beating gyms in a pokemon game, and still have no idea what the baddies are trying to do, and the only character that really is relevant is the professor, who calls you now and then, otherwise, each area has its own characters, who once you leave an area, are no longer relevant. As far as the actual gameplay goes, I think it's great. When catching coromon, the only real thing that matters is something called potential, which is basically like an IV value. EV's aren't a thing, because you basically assign EV points when the EV bar levels up, and their abilities can be changed for a small fee, and natures arent a thing. So, theres only 1 layer of RNG to fight when trying to catch the "perfect" coromon (and the game gives you means to boost the potential of wild encounters), and there is a way to raise the potential of a coromon by atleast 1 for a small fee, so with the max being 21, a potential 20 coromon is basically a potential 21. Lastly, the moves are interesting. Theres 7 types coromon can be (no dual types), but theres more types that can only be tied to skills, like cutting, or foul. This means they cant get a STAB, but make you feel less bad for running non STAB moves. The music is fantastic, the coromon designs are very very well done (im a fan of older, less anthropomorphic designs), the different areas are colorful and memorable, and the pacing/challenge is (in my opinion, as an above casual but below hard core player) is good. I regularly have to be mindful of hp, type matchups, and over all stamina of my team. Ive yet to be whiped out, but I regularly have my coromon faint. Even the wild encounters can hit pretty hard. And dont get started on the bosses, theyll have HUNDREDS of Hp along with unique mechanics. Makes having stall/defensive coromon really useful. Overall, i'd give the game so far maybe a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a reasonable side-grade to a traditional pokemon game. If you wish they were still making them like Black and White, this game is a good fit for you.This game's main problem is that it's an upgrade on the traditional pokemon formula across the board without any introspection into whether or not that formula is any good. For example, the accuracy stat in pokemon is criminally underutilized. It's bad design to have a whole stat that the player can barely interact with. Coromon fixes this by giving the player efficient tools to debuff accuracy. Unfortunately, having an accuracy stat in the first place is also terrible design. In the original, the two mistakes cancelled out. Here, the improved design actually ends up making the end product worse.Another good example is the SP system. In the original Pokemon, you have Power Points which limit the number of times you can use a move. This system exists because it's entirely possible to get into an infinitely repeating game state. Power Points force a conclusion, because eventually someone will run out and Struggle their pokemon to death. Coromon mistakes Power Points for a badly put together resource management system, and replaces it with a much better designed resource management system of SP. Again, this improvement makes the game worse: SP no longer fulfills the function of forcing an end - anyone can recover half their SP by skipping a turn - and adds an extra layer of annoyance to grinding levels.I think the weakest point of the game is the type system. There's an obsession with "balancing" types in pokemon-likes, and that's a fundamental mistake. I'm more than 10 hours in and 90+% of the interactions in the game are type neutral. It's really weird to have a bird and a bug fighting each other and have no type interaction at all. Or to have Ice be neutral against Sand.The strongest point of the game is the monster design. The creatures have a distinct style and they look great. As I acquired more of them, I was really torn about which 6 to use. They all have interesting traits that suggest different builds I'd like to try with each. I wish there were more diversity in wild Coromons, but I really appreciate that there aren't any throw away designs. Ultimately, the monster design is what these games live or dies on, so this game is a winner for me. It's also hard to make a game that departs significantly from Pokemon's mechanics without alienating big chunks of the fan base, so I give them a break on the mechanics I found annoying.ETA: The ending of this game rules, so that adds a lot to it as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those gems that have the possibility to win several awards!It has one of the most detailed area designs i have ever seen in a Monster-Capture game (Temtem take notes!).I have played over 12 hours now, grinded, farmed and puzzled my way through a beautiful world, filled with so much love that you just know that the devs ADORED Golden Sun and Pokemon!Apart from the scenery, the quality of life changes that i was wishing for for years in Pokemon got implimented into Coromon brilliantly:"Why would a teenager go on such a weird dangerous journey every time?"- Dont need to be a teenager! Be a full grown bearded guy who still lives with his mom and found his dream job after a while! A job that lets him conduct actual research missions instead of filling a "Pokedex" that has already been filled in several previous games. Bookcases actually mention a book about all Coromon exists, but the Protagonist "WANTS to find out about all of them himself"."Why is it so many underdeveloped villages who just seem to have no relation with each other?"- Not in Coromon! You even get Story missions that help improve the life in those villages for the better. Truth be told the game takes place in the year 2120, but that makes sense with the technology present. I could go on and on about the game for hours, its just such a gem to me... but for those willing to give it a try without spoilering to much I shall list the Pros and Cons in short.+ 114 Coromon+ GREAT combat scenery+ Amazing battle animations+ Coromon specific Attacks that make sense+ You can decide how to level up a Coromons Stats+ Implimented Nuzlocke Mode (Iron Man Mode) and Easy Mode+ BEAUTIFUL Scenery!+ Hidden Objects EVERYWHERE (Click everything! All hail us Lootgoblins!)+ The gauntlet powers are fun!+ The teleport system is very QoL+ Great Humor! Makes me wanna read everything!+ NPCs feel "real"+ The Protagonist talks!- I dont like the repetitive music! Especially during cutscenes it doesnt fit. It doesnt feel right when you are in a house in a relaxing city, but get a very dramatic and action rich cutscene, but the music keeps being relaxing. Biggest Con for me. (Id rather play music from youtube and mute the ingame music)- Sound effects for menue and level up/exp are very uncomfortable imo. Very high pitched retro sounds that just "hurt" and are louder than other sound effects- A few bugs that end in a black texture for combat scenery and teleport menue (Can be fixed by restarting the game sometimes)- No "real" adjustable window size. Only set options that are either to small or to big- Pixelated Text-Font hurts my exes when playing fullscreen or 3x window. Wish there was an option to change the font to normal- weird "difficulty curve": A lvl 28 can sometimes twoshot a lvl 60 or even oneshot. On the other hand if you decide to not go full dmg, it feels hard to kill 28 with a lvl 45 ... Strange stuff, but maybe i build wrong ^^'- german translation sometimes ruins jokes or doesnt make sense for unique item namesThats it. Overall i do give this game a 10/10 given the fact that i bought Pokemon Shining Diamond 5 days ago, but didnt play it even once after getting Coromon on sale xDGet it! A new era of Monster Capture begins!

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've really enjoyed the game, and love the amount of difficulty customization included. Coromon designs are pretty good, and I appreciate the fact that once you unlock a move, you can reassign it at any time.My only real complaint so far is the grinding in the game. For a game with so much customization, it baffles me that there isn't a way to speed up exp gain. When I was a kid I didn't mind the huge grinds, but these days I might only have an hour or two each day to play, and it's just not fun having to spend all my daily game time grinding instead of seeing new content.I know the modern pokemon exp share is typically disliked due to how easily you can over level, but it's so much more convenient for people with limited play time. Would be nice if they could add an option in the difficulty settings to make the lazy orb a party wide item. Even better would be if you could set a level cap on the lazy orb, so that it only gives exp to pokemon below a level you set when activating it. That way people that want party wide exp can have it, and those that don't want it can still have their held item lazy orb and everyone's happy.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall,It has an interesting difficulty selection as it can be standardized as well as customized. Monster design is unique and well done in my opinion with good flavor and useful options for a growing team, an extremely pleasant implementation of TM system without the need to actually handicap your team, innovative merge of Shiny and innate potential mechanics. Very good customization system for player character as well as re-rolls for monster stats, passive abilities, monster spinner with different colors, even a +1 to innate points if by some chance you were unlucky to receive a Potent Shiny instead of the Perfect Variant that everyone seeks (These can be found in each major town - recovery area - top floor)The grind is unnoticeable, going as far to say it was self imposed on my part wanting to get more potent variants and experiment with team composition. (It has exp share items, lvl boost items / skills for wild encounters, even a 1h long exp buff for extra measure)The game does its best to help out whenever possible but can be a nuisance sometimes as the main quest objective tends to backtrack and get you lost, but other than that no real issues. The game crashed on me once, never experienced it for a 2nd time up to this point, i can safely say it has a good autosave/save system and didn't loose much progression. _childDocuments_.review: It's without a doubt that, in recent years, the once iconic and highly-respected mainstream series of Pokémon has gradually gotten worse over time as it's gameplay has been simplified in ways that appeals to a more broader audience without offering much for it's more seasoned and mature gamers, coupled with the sharp increase in a lack of quality assurance and the masses of bugs and glitches that have turned the series from a pioneer in the video game industry into just another 'has-been' title that's mainly played by casual gamers or those who primarily play what's 'popular' to play as it were.Given the desire to go back to Pokémon's roots then, it's no surprise that we eventually came to a point where a serious effort was made into actually replicating those fond experiences that Pokémon used to bring back when it was strictly a 2D game from it's origins on the ancient Game Boy all the way to a not-so-old Nintendo DS, hence the eventual release of what I would consider to be quite the ingenious inspiration in the form of Coromon, a game that was in the works since as far back as 2014 having taken approximately 8 years to fully release.Since no doubt immediate parallels will be drawn between this indie and the big franchise it is taking obvious inspiration from, before delving into the gameplay itself (since some of it's gameplay mechanics will be very similar to Pokémon whilst others are surprisingly different) it is best to showcase first what this game does similarly to it's famous counterpart followed by what it does differently to detach itself from Pokémon to form it's own unique identity.Starting off with the similarities, obviously monster collection is still a big part of this game as, alongside the natural aim of being the most powerful of them all for some players, the main focus of this game as a 'Duelist Researcher' is to capture and discover all 122 species of Coromon as well as face off against an evil force that gradually becomes more significant to the core story as the game progresses.Adding onto that is the important of type match-ups against various Coromon you fight in the game, as ignoring this in favour of using those you like and any moves that are 'cool' to use will likely result in some serious struggling in certain parts of the game depending on which Coromon you mainly use, hence the focus of diversifying your team as it's a key theme to the overall plot of the game alongside other expected aspects of the Pokémon games. (A 'hub' to heal your Coromon as well as to engage in online battles, stores to sell you various useful items, talking to NPCs for general chit-chat alongside the occasional useful items given away, either for free or when you complete a favour they ask for you to do etc)Now for what Coromon does differently, one of the things that stood out to me immediately was that, although Coromon has fewer types than in it's aforementioned counterpart with Coromon only having 7 types as opposed to even the 1st generation of Pokémon having a considerably larger pool of 15, this game diversifies the usual type gameplay by adding a further 6 that are exclusively tied to moves that Coromon can use, with each of the 7 types of Coromon (noting that each Coromon will only have a primary element as opposed to Pokémon's main and secondary types) having their own strengths and weaknesses against the 13 different types of moves which results in a strange alteration in type-match ups that is surprisingly welcoming for both simplifying the process for casual gamers whilst also introducing a new way of keeping track of types for more experienced players when keeping in mind the extra types for attacking moves.Another key difference is how the story plays out where the main narrative is concerned, seeing how each Pokemon game has largely followed the same plot of becoming the 'best trainer' of said region by means of defeating each of the 8 gym leaders in a set order followed by facing off against the Elite Four before a final face-off against the leading champion to end the game on, as Coromon does not have any 'gym leaders' of the sorts to fight against, rather this game's primary goal is to reunite each of the six Titans in an attempt to fend off this game's evil foes who, to keep it light on spoilers, are bringing forth a new 'element' of sorts that seeks to dominate all the others and become the only essence on the planet Valua.This funnily enough ties into the game in it's gameplay so to speak, which is a good point to touch upon as, although if you know Pokémon well enough this section may come off as redundant, Coromon's main gameplay cycle revolves around using the monsters you have captured and raised to fight off other wild or trained Coromon, either to battle them for XP/gold or to catch them with this game's version of those Pokéballs, that being 'spinners' that vary in quality and effectiveness depending on the situation at hand, as each level gained will increase a Coromon's stats as well as potentially evolving it into a stronger form with bigger boosts to said stats.Much of this and more is what made Pokémon an incredibly fun RPG for many players, both new to the genre and veterans, to come back to time and time again to enjoy for wildly different reasons but all, more or less, enjoying the simple to learn but VERY hard to master gameplay that was as deep and difficult as you wanted it to be.Such is what Coromon truly leans into as, rather than have the one set difficulty like most Pokémon games save for Black & White 2, Coromon truly allows it's players to customize just HOW hard the game can be as it can be as simple as having every battle heal any damaged Coromon to full and shops being at half-price on it's easiest difficulty to  the complete opposite whereby any Coromon that faint are permanently lost to the wild and are only able to catch ONE Coromon per area among other strict rules, all of that and more to offer something for every kind of player here!Speaking of which, another popular feature seen in Pokémon games is the incredibly rare 'shiny' versions that many a dedicated Pokémon player will spend MANY hours finding for just a chance of finding one, as Coromon brings about this feature in a somewhat unique way, having not just uncommon 'potent' versions at around a 1 in 35 chance or so of appearing but also the true bona fide 'Perfect' Coromon that have even more visually distinct colours than their Potent counterparts, approximately a 1 in 3,500 chance of appearing.Something to note though is how this ties into Coromon's other levelling system of 'Potential', a somewhat slower meter that, once filled, will allow the player to allocate 3 points at a time to any of their Coromon's specific stats, with those with a higher potential ('Potent' Coromon having at least a level of 17 Potent whilst 'Perfect' ones have the maximum of 21 Potent) having a higher statbase than their weaker counterparts which, although not quite enough to make a huge difference, still does have an impact where competitive gameplay is concerned, so no doubt it has it's drawbacks too where this game's online battles are concerned!And indeed, with how multiplayer has progressed over the decades, Coromon does come equipped with it's own online system that allows you to engage with other players to fight them with your own carefully-built team, albeit I had some difficulty with finding people to fight against at the time of this review, suggesting that the online scene isn't as active these days sadly.In conclusion, Coromon is a Pokémon-inspired game that pays homage to it's main source of influence in the best ways possible by taking what works so well and carefully putting it's own spin and alterations to keep the gameplay fresh so engaging for both newer and more experienced players and I would wholeheartedly recommend this to anyone who is looking for a new Pokémon-inspired game that lives up to it's name!

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Pokemon for PC, only much, MUCH better, Here is why you should go with this version over the tried and true classic: 1: The obvious plus side is it is on PC, which means a decent screen size, which is great for those of us older folk and just those with less than stellar vision or who just get migraines trying to make out images on a 3 inch screen any real length of time. 2: A much smarter story line. The story line is much more intelligent and well thought out. Coromon also has some tongue-in-cheek humor moments that is while still family friendly is aimed at a slightly older crowd. 3: you don't permanently loos skills. You can choose between battles which skills you want your Coromon to have, so unlike Pokemon when you gain more than 4 skills you have to start choosing which to kiss goodbye to forever (or pay an large amount or use a rare/hard to find item to regain a skill if you decide it was the better choice) , in Coromon you never lose those skills and can interchange as needed when not in a battle. 4: Customizable characters. Finally! You have the ability to change up your appearance, from skin color to outfit to glasses to the hat you are wearing. none of the 1 of two options nonsense here. You can finally have a character that doesn't embarrass you with how they are dressed wandering around.Also for the female model, none of that feet splayed far apart while keeping the knees together nonsense pose either. you stand and walk like a normal human.  Hurrah for equality that Pokemon is still struggling to understand in the year 2024. Now to be fully honest: Normally I don't care -scantily clad maiden warriors are a dime a dozen after all in many games- but with Pokemon it is so glaringly obviously meant to make them look incompetent and less than intelligent, it is aggravating not to mention that it is also pointed at young female gamers, many of which are struggling with their body image and sense of worth enough already. So, I am calling Pokemon out for it, yes. 5: finally one that may just be my own taste but I like the music in Coromon better. While the battle music is fairly similar, the background music to me is far less grating on the nerves when you have to listen to it for any real length of time. true you can always mute the music, but having something that doesn't drive you to do that in the first place is always a plus in my book. Summary: In short, this is Pokemon with all the major requests the fan base has made of the years and never got, and all those complaints never addressed finally someone listened to and resolved. I will take this game over Pokemon or Palworld any day.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi, I'm a casual monster taming gamer!Coromon is incredible! The sprite work is so pretty and animations are so smooth! The lovely environments and illustrated battle settings are so wonderful! I'm so impressed with the attention to detail all-around! Really great art direction in my opinion!Coromon offers character customization and cosmetics throughout your journey! So if you're big on customization (like I am), you'll really love that!Coromon also features 114 monsters to collect, including two additional 'shiny' variants of said Coromon called Potent and Perfect Coromon. Potent being the 'Uncommon' shiny and Perfect being the rare shiny. I really liked this because it really motivates the idea of collecting monsters in a fun way that offers more shiny variants, especially for more casual players who don't enjoy long grinding for the rare shinies. I really like how engaging the story in Coromon is with the player. Instead of your player being mute, your character actually converses with the Story NPCs, making it feel way more natural and fun. I really enjoyed this as it felt more like I was there VS playing a character. I really love the emotes that appear when conversing (that they also use for battle moves)! It makes it much more interesting to engage with NPCs both in story and in side quests. Side Quests are also awesome to see in a monster collecting game. I love it so much as I enjoy completing side quests before continuing story and the side quests just add onto that so well. It's not overwhelming either, it's just the right amount of quests to complete alongside story progression. I don't want to give too much away, as Coromon has and is so much more than what I expressed here. If you love monster collecting games, you will absolutely fall in love with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really solid creature collector game, similar to Pokemon. None of the Coromon feel particularly weak. There are some nice QoL changes like how you can level up Coromon that aren't in battles to allow you to grind one quickly. You can try new moves you unlock and quickly switch it out if you don't like it. Sometimes you'll fight multiple Coromon but the game will scale them down several levels so they don't feel overpowered. There's a lot of small but welcome changes from what you'd be used to in Pokemon.A big difference within the story is that instead of collecting badges by defeating gym leaders, you fight legendary Coromon. These are Coromon you cannot catch. They have about 10x the health similar leveled Coromon have but their attacks will be just the same. Most of them have some kind of gimmick as well that typically triggers when you get them to half HP to throw you off. If you have trouble, just abuse items on the stronger Coromon against that type legendary or grind. Don't worry, there's also XP boosters to grind faster.The world has some beautiful pixel art. A lot of the Coromon have some cool designs and the attack animations on the stronger attacks are really fun to watch too. If you're looking for a Pokemon-like game but don't have a Nintendo system, this is definitely for you. Even if you have a Nintendo system, I still think this is worth your time. It took me about 25 hours to complete it. I enjoyed it all the way through, definitely recommend it if you want to play something like Pokemon.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't have anything bad to say about Coromon, it's a decent game in itself and if you like monster collector games you will (most likely) like Coromon. The Story is pretty standard- not that that is a bad thing, especially if you just want a game to settle down with and enjoy a smooth ride- the monster designs are all very smoothly animated and incredibly charming in their own rights, the boss fights are VERY fun and appropriately stressful if you're on level. The new system of being able to change your monster's "skins" on the potency system based on which ones you've collected so far is ingenious and I have nothing but praise for the idea. The game is pretty customizable both in character/monster appearances and team- there isn't really any WRONG ways to play the game. I'm always a fan of combat systems that break the mold of Pokelites, and Coromon's stamina system is appropriately punchy and easy to both pick up and enjoy. The OST is, while not bad, fairly lackluster. I don't remember any of the tracks after playing them nor did I find the majority of them to be particularly impactful. The Sound Design is... fine, but similarly nothing stands out. It's a good, decent game that is very worth the price you pay for it. Theft Mode is my favorite additional game mode of all time and it's what elevated this game to one of my favorites in the niche. There is nothing funnier than catching someone's monster and then releasing it in front of them.All in All, 8/10, Good game. Solid Game. A little forgettable among the heavy hitters in the genre coming out- said as someone who really likes this game. If you like monster tamers you WILL (probably) like Coromon.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend Coromon to a Pokemon fan that is looking for a more in-depth Pokemon?  No.  But is Coromon an adequate clone?  Yes.  Coromon is basically the original Pokemon from Pokemon Red and Blue, with some improvements.  The basics of gameplay remain the same, certain Coromon types have advantages and weaknesses against other types; while Coromon has simplified the Pokemon types and added some new ones, if you're familiar with Pokemon types, you're largely familiar with Coromon types.  Beyond that, Coromon adds a "Stamina Point" system, basically powerful attacks eat up Stamina Points at a higher rate, and you can inflict status effects that will damage stamina points, such hazy or poison; this replaces the limited uses of the Pokemon system.  Al of the advancements in Cormon are solid changes, but none of them fix the central problem, nor the central lack of my interest, in Pokemon/Coromon combat. That said, there are some very helpful diffuculty settings in Coromon.  If you want to make things easier for your kids, you can.  If you want to make it so you can catch other trainer's Coromon, you can!  My biggest complaint is that none of this livens up the central combat sytem, nor the central premise of the game, namely collecting all of the Coromon.  So...here's my recommendation, if you want a game that is truly trying to do something new with the genre, try Cassette Beasts; it's a way more adult, way more interesting monster collection game.  If you just want Pokemon on PC, or Pokemon with a slightly different coat of paint, then Coromon is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is a hard Pokemon fan I cannot recommend Coromon enough. I had this game wishlisted for a while, unsure if it was right for me and I bought it up a whim and a sale. I've had so much fun and realized I wish things in this game were PART of Pokemon!! You can cancel evolutions and get bonus' to the mons traits! There are Commons, Potents, and Perfect Coromon - a shiny system that not only has two variants but also actually has effects to the stats! There is even a Potency Increase machine that allows you to basically semi-shiny your Mons if they're high enough on that stat! You can change moves WHENEVER YOU WANT. They still allow for HM like things with Skill Flashes, but if you scroll to the bottom of your Coromons available moves it just shows you all the kind that are available! The game comes with essentially Nuzlocke difficulty settings and customizable difficulty that can be altered as people need! On top of all those pro's it's witty, it has side missions, the 'potency hunting' feels rewarding even as a grind, I  recognize the story where I'm used to the latest stories of Pokemon dragging and being somewhat slag. Overall I have the highest praise for this game. I'm currently 22 hours in and I'm just about to reach the second 'boss', I've been streaming this game and enjoying it a ton. Even for full price I'd recommend this game, but I suppose that depends on your money situation so look forward to a minor sale if you're on the fence! If you like Pokemon this game does no wrongs in standards and comparison. _childDocuments_.review: A pretty decent pokemon-like, with a lot of grinding and long puzzles. Sometimes, I'd wish there was way less texts, and I just end up skipping them.My main issue with the game is that it relies heavily on a hidden stat: potential. It affects how many points you'll be able to invest in a creature, alongside his normal leveling curve. It changes everything. And guess what? Your starter can be perfect, or garbage.They also give you tools to read potential just before the first boss, and a way to read it in battle way later. So, you just end up roaming in loops, hoping to catch shinies, so that you can stop investing XP in your starter with a potential of 5. And if you're daltonian, have bad memory, or use night mode, well, good luck. Because some of the shinies have very little variation, ie. a normal variant is #ee33ac and its powerful version is #ff33ac. At least, there's a small tooltip that appears in combat, but it's missable.So... Yeah, it's pretty hardcore. There's a lot of grinding, and you basically spend the first 20 hours of the game fighting with a couple of shinies, or whatever you can find. You can really get to level 45-50 when farming on levels 21-29, XP is easy to get. Bosses are a bit of a challenge, but one-shotting everything with your 1 or 2 shinies is the META. And it's not very compelling.Dungeons are a bit too spread out, and too crowded with fighters. When exploring, you just want to avoid them and rush to the next coromon center.

_childDocuments_.review: Another day, another Pokémon carbon-copy... but hey, it only makes sense when Nintendo refuses to let their favorite cash-cow out of sight. The demand for a PC-version is there, and SOMEBODY'S gonna fill it! So with that in mind, how does this one stack up? It's not the worst one I've played, honestly, and it captures the aesthetic of the older Pokémon-games well, along with providing a slightly more mature, if also rather nonsensical, story. So far so good.Thing is, this game has the same problem that a lot of these attempts to duplicate the Pokémon formula do - it's SHALLOW. Wherever the gameplay of Pokémon hasn't been copied directly, it's been simplified, dumbed down or otherwise made less interesting. Fewer types, fewer interactions, no type immunities, no dual-types, status-moves don't take types into consideration (sand-type takes less damage from electricity but can still be paralyzed just fine), no breeding or egg-moves, no natures...Now, credit where credit is due. They've added a neat system of 'Potential', which gives each critter two potential level of 'shininess' that doesn't just provide a palette-swap but also makes them stronger. Depending on the Potential of the 'mon, it'll gain extra stat-points as it levels up - with high-potential critters getting them faster and thus winding up with more of them by the time they hit the level-cap. These points can then be distributed as you please... which the perceptive might notice is just a simplified, more openly-displayed version of Pokémon's IV/EV system.Honestly, I was very close to giving this one a thumbs-up - yes, everything's been dumbed down compared to the real Pokémon-games, removing the underlying level of complexity that made those games a treat for adults as well as children, but that seems to happen with EVERY BLOODY GAME of this kind, so hey. However, a bigger flaw became apparent as I kept playing, and then confirmed by skimming the wiki: There is no end-game to speak of. Most of the available 'Coromon' reach their final evolution in their late 30's, early 40's at most - with the few that take longer being rather unimpressive and not worth the hassle. There are no Dragonite/Tyranitar/Salamence type 'Pseudo-Legendaries' that stand out noticeably over the rest of the cast in terms of strength, just like there are no actual Legendaries, no Mythicals... by the time you've finished the first dungeon, you'll have a team of level 30-something creatures who've reached their last evolution, and there's basically no reason to ever trade them in for anything else - especially since you can freely swap between every ability they've learned AND your entire stock of TM's whenever you like. Combined with the fact that the game only has 106 catchable 'mons, and it kind of feels like playing a Gen1 Pokémon-game where the last third of the Pokédex has been amputated. You even get to meet some awesome 'Legendary' types - the Titans - but they're purely boss-fights, and cannot be caught or obtained by any means.EDIT: Turns out, right at the end of the game, you DO get a chance to catch something the game CALLS 'Legendary Rarity' Coromon... but they're nothing more than slightly souped-up palette-swaps of mons you've been able to catch since the very start, so my point stands.So, yeah - can't recommend. It's got its moments, certainly, and for a Pokémon rip-off it's decent value for the money... but if you've ever played the real thing, you'll be hard pressed not to notice how many ways it comes up short.

_childDocuments_.review: Gamefreak, take notes! THIS is how you make a monster collector game! Coromon is undoubtedly one of the best games I have ever played, easily overshadowing all recent Pokemon games. It brings back the nostalgic feeling of when I first played Pokemon almost two decades ago, while also bringing actual challenge back to the genre. Coromon is one of many Pokemon clones that I have tried, but this one really gets almost everything right. I'm going to highlight some of the pros and cons I thought about while playing, as well as give a few suggestions for improvements in either an update or a (hopeful) sequel. Pros:- Incredibly customizable. From battles to catching to item management and more, you can really customize just about anything you want in this game, allowing you to make it as friendly or challenging as you like. I personally played through the game on the normal settings, not changing anything, to see how balanced the game felt as intended by the devs, and I have to say I think they did a pretty good job. Fights were tough, but not impossible. Strategy is very important, and while I did grind a tiny bit for levels, it was only to equalize my party to the enemies, and I never came close to feeling overpowered. - Tons of Quality of Life improvements. I say improvements as a comparison to Pokemon. There are SO many helpful QoL changes from Pokemon here that for some reason a multi-billion dollar company cannot be bothered to implement, but this game pretty much has everything you could ever want in it as far as ease of access and accessibility goes. Don't like your Coromon's trait? Change it! Don't love your current moves? Switch them around! Your Coromon died but got enough xp to evolve? It will evolve anyways! This game seriously does just about everything right. I cannot even begin to list everything here.- Reasonably interesting storyline. The story in this game certainly won't win any awards for incredible writing or plot twists, but it definitely did an effective job at keeping me engaged and interested. Certainly more interesting than the stories of 90% of other games I play. - Bopping Music. The music bops. - Not just a clone. I mentioned this is a Pokemon clone, and while yes, it is, it's also very much more. From the different Coromon types and matchups, to completely original designs and ideas, to a new Stamina system in battles, Coromon definitely differentiates itself from the competition. What I really liked was the balance it found between Pokemon-clone and unique game. It felt familiar enough to hop right in and play it similar to how I would a Pokemon game, but different enough that it was fun to learn the new mechanics and adjust my usual strategies accordingly.- Plenty of cool Coromon to catch! There are over 100 Coromon, each interesting and unique, and many with special traits or skills unique to them as well. I absolutely intend to play the game several more times, using different Coromon and strategies.- Some good puzzles and non-battle gameplay. There are some fun puzzles throughout the game like switches for doors, moving around walls, switching up cart paths, etc. that are not too tasking on the brain but still require a bit of thought and can be satisfying to solve.Cons:- My only major con for this game is the "mini-games" it forces upon you. Not to be confused with the puzzles, these reflex-based, timing-based abominations are incredibly aggravating. Specifically the spirit one. Unlike the puzzles, they do not require any complex thinking to figure out, and simply require you to act fast, which is not particularly easy due to the one other con I will mention, poor controls. These mini-games end up feeling incredibly tedious as you attempt them over and over again just so that you can continue with the actual game. There should REALLY be an option to skip them. With how customizable everything else in the game is, I'm almost surprised there isn't. - Not the greatest controls. This isn't a huge deal. Outside of the abysmal mini-games mentioned above, the awkward controls aren't really a big hindrance or issue, but they could definitely be improved. I think the game would play much better on a controller. That being said, they could be much worse, and being able to use either keyboard, mouse, or both is a nice touch.- Sudden ending. The story was cool but ended kind of abruptly. I would have liked a little more wrap-up on what exactly happened after you beat the final boss.Suggestions:- Show stat increase value on level up. I love that the game always shows you the stat improvements whenever a Coromon levels up, but it only shows the original value and the new value, not the actual number it's being increased by. This is obviously an incredibly small issue, but it would be nice to just see the numbers at a glance instead of having to go through each stat doing quick math to see what the value change is.- Unique Final boss music. The music in this game rocks, so I was pretty disappointed there was no unique final boss theme.- Balance the Dark Magic Coromon a bit if possible. I'm no expert on game balance, but the Dark Magic Coromon being resistant to literally everything is pretty annoying. Kind of defeats the purpose of type matchups and requires you to just try and brute force your way through. Maybe make them resistant to what they would normally be neutral to, and neutral to what they would normally be weak to?- Healing around events. Something Pokemon did that I liked was to heal your squad up before a big fight, or at least give you a chance to heal yourself before starting a fight. Some of the events in this game come out of nowhere and through you into battle and your squad might be already mostly dead and in no condition for a boss fight. Giving the player a chance to heal before starting these fights would be pretty nice I think.Verdict: 9/10 - An absolute blast of a game, only marred by its unskippable reflex-based mini-games. Why spend $60 on a company that doesn't care about its playerbase when you could pay 1/3 of that for an amazing game like this?

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★☆For anyone who enjoyed the classic Pokémon games, Coromon delivers an enhanced and improved experience. The mechanics are familiar yet refined, bringing in new features while staying true to the old-school formula. It’s the perfect game for relaxing on the couch with a Steam Deck! ★★☆☆☆The storyline is decent but lacks a strong conclusion. It’s long enough to keep you playing but doesn’t stand out or feel particularly fulfilling in the end. ★★★☆☆The visuals are lovely, capturing the nostalgic pixel art style. While some monster designs could use a bit more flair, the skins are a nice touch and add variety. However, it lacks the kick of something fresh and innovative. ★★★☆☆The weather effects and environment-based puzzles bring a fun, nostalgic feel. The shiny system, though a classic feature from Pokémon, has a new twist here that makes it interesting. However, it’s still missing a fully immersive experience. ★★★★☆Playing on the Steam Deck while relaxing on the couch, especially during downtime, was a blast. Multiplayer battles with friends added a lot of fun, and farming skins, shinies, and milestones kept me engaged. Overall, a great experience for the 40 hours invested.Coromon is a fun, nostalgic trip for fans of classic monster-taming games, with some well-thought-out improvements. While it doesn’t revolutionize the genre, it offers a solid experience perfect for handheld play and casual enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon is a Monster Taming RPG with great design, lots of love put into it, and adorable creatures to capture. The game manages to make you feel like you are an 8-year-old rediscovering this on your Gameboy for the first time and before you ask, it is not a bootleg pokémon.Coromon is a refreshing take on the monster taming genre with the help of an easy system, adorable creatures to discover, excellent battles, and old-school 2D sprites that are making me feel nostalgic for when these games first appeared.First things first, there is finally a story to follow in such a game! While the bar really isn’t high and the story is quite hit or miss, this just proves anyone can actually input a storyline no matter how basic to these games.You are a young researcher for Lux Solis, an organization dedicated to the study of Coromons. Very quickly, your hero abilities kick in and despite being completely inexperienced you are tasked with quite literally a titanic task and set out to explore the Velua region.Gameplay-wise, Coromon offers a lot of replayability with various levels of difficulty that you can fully customize as you wish including some permadeath features. These customization named Nuzlocke allow the Coromon experience to be an on-demand thing adapted and customized by the player. On top of that, online PvP battles are available including a ranked mode, which can honestly be really fun.  You will get to catch Coromons with a fidget spinner and get to level them up through battles, in the wild, or against other tamers. Each Coromon comes in various forms, standard, potent and perfect, each affecting the stats and potential of the creature. The most perfectionist of us will know exactly what to do with that information should they want the best possible team.Sadly, while you can breeze through dungeons quite easily, you will encounter some boss fights that will be quite challenging and will require you to do some grinding due to them being absolutely overpowered. Graphically speaking, the design is simple and yet really well done. The use of 2D sprites in such a modern context is aesthetically pleasing and at no point did I feel like it took away from the game. As mentioned earlier, it is a good mix of modernism added into a game that will not fail at making you nostalgic.Furthermore, the level design is really good. The zones are extremely fun to explore, and quite different from one another. The puzzles and side quests offered are at times interesting, but can also quickly turn into a chore should you be lost in a dark cavern with an absurdly high amount of encounters. Coromon introduces some variety with environments that have an impact on how you navigate the map, like a desert burning your feet unless you find shade in time for instance. These mechanics, while unique to Coromon are sadly at times quite painful and add really little to the game.Finally, let’s address the  in the room, Coromon doesn’t hide from taking huge inspiration from Pokémon you can find a lot of references to it throughout your adventure. Though, Coromon stands out in the fact that it is a project made by fans for the fans, it is definitely a labor of love, made by developers that are proactive and taking the pulse of their community (a quick look at their Discord will show you that it is the case). It is definitely neither a bootleg of Pokémon or a cashgrab. If you are interested in the monster tamer genre, Coromon brings an interesting and refreshing take on it while making it feel both different and familiar enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing - great artstyle, great evolution lines, good QoL changes that current pokemon still hasn't learned to implement - puzzles are fun and actually make you use your brain (I know, such a difficult concept for some of you).  The level up mechanic in Coromon where you can put stats where you want is a great change - no longer are you only limited to getting an increase in specific stats when you level up.   When you unlock "potential" you can put points wherever you want.  Want a special attacker that decimates everything it touches but as a result is a glass cannon?  Want to dump all the points into sp def and def to make a tank?  Go ahead, you are not limited - obviously some Coromon will do better than others, but the idea is you are not limited, you can do whatever you want, including respec your coromon if you don't like what you've done so far. I have seen people complaining and saying they are not going to buy because there is no speed up mechanic.  I say to you, good riddance.  We don't need people who just speed their way through the entire game to get their quick dopamine release then post on the forum or a review about how bad the game is because they fast forwarded their way through the entire game.  If you like Pokemon but dislike what it has become over the last 10 years, you will love Coromon.

_childDocuments_.review: TL; DR: A really, really fun monster taming JRPG. A familiar experience to classic pokemon with it's own flare that changes how you look at battles.The good: .The art in this game is amazing. The overworld looks clean and simple while still being vibrant. The coromon sprites are amazing with great designs (props to them for listening to the feedback of megalobyte during the demo days). .The battles are really fun. While it uses an SP/MP system like other monster taming jrpgs, it's far more plentiful about how much it gives you when recovering. This gives the battles a fun structure where a coromon can continually be in battle and still do something meaningful while at the same time still ebig somewhat restricted..The bosses offer a nice challenge, for the most part you can expect to have a decent chunk of your team be knocked out(even if they are easy enough to beat on your first time around). They also have fun abilities that help to seperate them all and prevent them from just being big creature with big stats.The bad: .Technical issues. While I believe it is fully fixed now, release day was full of clashes. This seems to have sorted itself out after that day as it has never crashed again for me after that day and there was a patch later that has fixed it. One continual issue i've had is that the game is that sometimes it would turn black and it would then come back just fine but now it continually switched between me using the gamepad and keyboard. .Movepools. While coromon have stats that match their designs great, the same can't be said for some of the movepools. Sometimes there will be mixed attackers that will only ever get good support in one of their attacks. Somethimes there will be pychical/special attackers that have movepools completely focused on the other type of attack..While a much smaller issue, the main vilains of this game rarely appear, making it feel like they're almost non existant during the story. And the mixed:.The potential system. It's a fantastic way to have your own version of shinies while changing the effectivness of each coromon in a similar way to EVs but it's not casual friendly. You can make it through the game just fine without any perfects but even if you're just going for potent team members they can take an annoying amount of time to hunt, often stopping the game in it's tracks ust to find one.Bonus stuff I can't really comment on:.Online, it's really nice for them to go out of their way to include an online mode, I've never used it though so I can't actually comment on how good it is sadly.

If you're fed up with the current direction of pokemon and just want more of the same old with new mechanics this game is definitely for you.I started playing as of patch 1.0.0.0 and this feels like a complete game. The main story took around 27 hours, some of that time was spent hunting for specific coromon and filling the database. I've not touched online play so I can't comment on balance and fun to be had there.I'm looking forward to any future updates this game makes.

_childDocuments_.review: As a game clearly inspired by Pokemon, I'll start off with the positive differences.The SP system can be tedious at times, but the variety from being affected by certain attacks and statuses, as well as overcharging, keeps the battles entertaining.Your party earns experience even after fainting. Such a small change from Pokemon, but I would say it's objectively better than having to lose out on experience, especially since it saves me from an annoyance Pokemon has stuck with for decades.The Potential system is just so much easier than the cluster of IVs and EVs Pokemon have. Having a second experience bar to allocate points, or save them for later and use them at ANY time, is convenient."Shinies" being objectively better than other Coromon. With Pokemon, the alternate color palettes are completely useless, other than bragging rights. With Coromon, I was always excited when I encountered a generally more pleasing color palette and the "Potent" popped up, acting as a double incentive to add it to my party.The animated sprites. Pokemon Black/White had so much charm, and the animations were so impressive that they completely overshadow the 3D models used in current Pokemon games. After seeing the trailer for Coromon, I was immediately swayed by the animated sprites into purchasing it. Newer Pokemon games lack the ability to charm me, but most individual Coromon sprites are simply fun to look at, and make the adventure more enjoyable.The individual route music, while not particularly memorable, is pleasant enough.The different battle music is all catchy, with a unique matching feeling for when you're in a cave or against a Titan.The negative aspects of this game are also intertwined with some of the positive aspects.The way it's designed.Certain story events introduce unique Coromon, but you are not allowed to catch them. There is NO reason given. When trying to use an item to catch the Coromon, the game will simply state "You aren't allowed to do that here." After the first Titan fight, you immediately encounter a different type of Coromon which somehow resists every type. If you try to catch it, you will again be given the message "You aren't allowed to do that here." This ingrained the idea in my mind "I'm not allowed to catch these, so I shouldn't even try", but they did receive an entry in the Dex, so it can be reasonably assumed the player should treat them as unique boss fights to overcome rather than add them to your party. Much later on in the game, you encounter more of the mystery type, but for some reason you are now allowed to catch them. There is no reason given. It is simply poorly designed.To completely bar you from even attempting to catch is, at first, just a disappointment. The Titans are understandably stronger than any single party member you could add to your team, but having to use your entire team's strengths with statuses, debuffs, and a bit of luck end up making the Titan battles surprisingly enjoyable.The Dex entries have a pathetically small amount of information about the Coromon. Considering the main character is specifically part of an organization of SCIENTISTS, it was almost offensive to read an entry on something I had newly encountered but the only information available was "the two dog heads fight over who the goodest boy is."By far, the biggest disappointment is the writing. Everything is so generic, based on a generic fantasy plot. I was initially intrigued at the change of the main character having a prominent speaking role, in addition to being part of an actual scientific organization, could have potentially lead to interesting plot developments. That intrigue was replaced with annoyance as I realized the main character has no personality whatsoever apart from being a goody two-shoes hero. The most personality encountered is inspecting different items and having a random pun ready. Instead of having character personalities be shown through dialogue, they are instead shown through emojis. Emojis pop up over a character's head after they say something. This makes sense for Coromon, since they can't talk, but it seems like more of a crutch when it's used alongside human dialogue.The main antagonist group sometimes speaks in backwards sentences. When you read them backwards, they are generic bad guy phrases. I don't know why; a potentially interesting alien invasion coupled with having to slow down to read normal sentences does not make them compelling whatsoever and only serves as a nuisance when forced to turn what should be a normal sentence into a chore.The story ends on such a flat note. A simple boss battle that tries to seem more important than it actually is. It does make a decent attempt by having all the previous boss fights contribute and giving small, but important, buffs throughout. Unfortunately, I never felt as though they mattered. The final boss doesn't do anything drastically different from previous ones. There isn't even a different soundtrack for it. Afterwards, the main character is sleeping in bed and visited by an NPC that goes "wow wasn't that a fun adventure? wait til next time, we're going to SPACE!" It felt like slap in the face after such a lackluster ending.Overall, I enjoyed Coromon. But I cannot recommend it. The main reason I purchased Coromon is because I had lost interest in Pokemon over the years, but the animated sprites of Coromon were so charming and reminded me of Black/White, games that had an actual interesting plot which is nowhere to be found in Coromon. I would only recommend this to people like me who are bored with the lifeless 3D models Pokemon use nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Launch-day hotfixes seem to have fixed every technical problem I've come across - had one crash before the hotfix, but the game's autosave function put me right back where I was anyway. Also, I've heard people talk about a launcher, but I haven't seen it. Seems like if there was a secondary launcher it was patched out almost instantly.Getting past the technical, yes, it is very similar to Pokemon, but there are some vital differences. The most important, in my opinion, is potency. Shiny-hunting in Pokemon is a headache, but Coromon's equivalent to "shinies" (Potent and Perfect Coromon) are much more rewarding to go after. There are basically two XP tracks, one that gives your Coromon an across-the-board boost when it levels up and one that lets you distribute points to make more deliberate builds. Potent and Perfect Coromon advance along the second track more quickly, making them easier to customize and more powerful on the whole.There are other differences from Pokemon, too. There are fewer types, and you can view type advantages during fights, making the actual combat a bit less daunting while putting more focus on party composition. It makes it both more accessible and more rewarding to put together a team that really works.Coromon is also hard. Not Shin Megami Tensei hard or anything, but I lose party members pretty consistently in trainer battles. If you're a nuzlocke enthusiast, you'll have a field day with this one, especially since it actually includes a nuzlocke mode. I've never done a nuzlocke run myself, but I know they're very popular with creature collector fans, so it's a nice gesture to include a mode that enforces nuzlocke rules.Overall, Coromon is a refinement of the creature collector. It's not "just" Pokemon, but it's also not entirely different. It's complex but also approachable, blending the best of Pokemon with new, clever elements that set it apart and make it its own beast entirely. Can't wait to see competitive play, nuzlockes, speedruns, etc.
