_childDocuments_.review: 60.4h (78/80 achievements, finished the game) No. Yes (~64 achievement). Yes (~1 achievement). is a monster-taming game, similar to . It offers 124 monsters to collect, separated into 8 types.- Fast-paced gameplay- Customizable difficulty- Easier rate to catch "shiny" monsters- Grindy endgame content- Slow saving timeIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 was displayed in top-down, pixelated visuals. Despite having simple-looking characters, the monsters look more varied, ranging from cute to cool. Combat is also displayed from a different angle than  games, giving a unique take on the visuals.The story is straightforward. It tries to follow the same route as  games where there is an antagonist group that is trying to do bad things, except that rather than focusing the story on you becoming a Pokémon master, 's story revolves around stopping the group from doing anything worse. The dialogues are lengthy, but you won't miss anything if you don't follow them.  is played just like : you choose a starter monster and use it to go on your journey. The difference is that you'll get a second monster after you choose your starter, and instead of gyms, you'll have Titans. There are 7 Titans based on each type that are spread around the world. Going to each location will be done on foot, triggering battles whenever you step on grasses outdoors or anywhere you walk indoors. Trainers will also be placed around the areas to test your strength and give you exp.Despite the similarities, some things make  different. The potential system is one example. Each monster has a potential value, separating them into normal, potent, and perfect. Monsters with higher potential will benefit from extra stat points and be distinguishable from their different color. It's similar to shiny, except that it will also have a stat boost. Finding potent monsters is easy. I found 10+ potent monsters in the wild without even doing anything. You also can increase the rate by using other items, which also work for perfects. This makes it easier to hunt for them, and the game really accommodates this by providing a different encyclopedia entry for normal, potent, and perfect monsters.Puzzles are also in the game. It is available in most areas, which are mostly related to the story. I didn't have any difficulties in finishing them, although it served as a good breather from the monster hunting. However, some of these require you to walk slowly, which can give you issues if you speed up the game speed too much.What I liked about this game is that you can speed up almost everything. You can speed up the text, battle animations, and even the game speed. The game is quite slow at 1x speed so this is a blessing. Again,  uses the same combat system as , albeit with different typings. Each monster is categorized into one of the eight available types, although other types that are exclusive to skills exist. To be honest, I had a hard time remembering the weaknesses and resistance, especially the non-standard ones since I couldn't map them in my head.You can only choose up to 4 skills to bring to battle, but you can change which skill to use whenever you are not in battle. This is very useful whenever you want to set up a strategy, especially for monsters that have a lot of typing coverage. Playing the game at a low level will also require more strategy on your end, which will make you swap the skills based on the enemy that you are about to face. The game itself is easy to beat if you are over-leveled, though, and you might be doing that without realizing it if you explore each area thoroughly.Aside from catching all normal, potent, and perfect monsters, there is a single content that will open after you beat the game: Battle Dome. It's like Battle Frontier where you have to beat an endless amount of enemies. To be honest, I hate these kinds of modes. However, I still found the content to be easy, provided that you have a team with decent type coverage. It'll get boring if you try to get everything that the place has to offer though since you need to repeat the whole thing several times in each difficulty - my mind went numb from doing it.I finished the game in 30.3h. I then tried to catch every monster for an achievement, which got me into ~40h mark. The rest of my playtime was spent in the Battle Dome to get all 3 stars from getting enough winning streaks from all modes.The game offers 4 preset difficulties with a customized one. I finished the game in the hardest difficulty and didn't find it too difficult as long as you are over-leveled, which I did without realizing it. The only issue I had is the hardest difficulty that is similar to , meaning that 1) you can only catch the first monster that you find and 2) your monster will leave the party if it faints. Both that and all other content (including Battle Dome) can be mitigated by save scumming. Despite having a lot of similarities with ,  still manages to stand up as its own game. I liked how you can speed up everything, and how each area is not too long to clear - it just makes it so addicting. I couldn't stop from exploring new areas and kept on wanting more. Moreover, the game seems to encourage you to catch them all by introducing items that can increase its encounters and different encyclopedia entries for normal, potent, and perfect monsters. The end game might be a grind and there might be not much room for competitive players, but it's still there if you want it. If you like monster-taming games, you can't go wrong with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was my first experience with a monster taming game that isn't Pokemon, and it was just alright. For context, my favorite Pokemon game generation was 4. I think overall, there are some good mechanical and QOL improvements made here over Pokemon, but nothing groundbreaking and I found nothing that would make me want to replay this game over and over like I did Platinum & SoulSilver (and Red & Emerald, for that matter). I liked the puzzles (they are mostly movement puzzles/mazes). I liked that you can change traits (inherent abilities) and upgrade Potential (stat ceiling). I liked that HM equivalents are used by the player character, not locked to monsters and taking up a move spot. The environments were relatively varied and interesting. I liked the music overall (the synth-laden battle theme is a standout). The plot is original, although this does not necessarily mean it was a great story (basically it's a cautionary tale about the environment, but includes aliens and it's *their* environment that's been destroyed). Lastly, I liked that there was a reason to try to catch better versions of the same monsters beyond a cosmetic difference. On to dislikes: the names/appearances of monsters in this genre of games are very important IMO and even Pokemon does not nail this (especially after Gen. 4, thus my earlier comment). This game suffers from uninspired monster names (Mudma, Squidma, Arcta, Skuldra) and the corny name issue Pokemon exhibits throughout its history (Cubzero, Bittybolt, Acie/Deecie, Chonktoad). I didn't like how there were only 7 types (Fire, Ice, Water, Electric, Normal, Ghost and SAND) and no dual monsters were dual type. I especially didn't like that there are several more TYPES of moves that are not represented in monster typing (Poison, Foul, Heavy, Magic, Air, and CUT) when several of those could have easily been represented and many monsters were begging to have that typing but didn't. Overall, the type interactions made sense but were oversimplified due to the limited monster types. Water type is overvalued (especially in the early game), as it is the only type to be 2x effective against 2 actual monster types and 0.5 affected by those types (Fire and SAND). I'm stylizing SAND and CUT in caps because they deserve to be highlighted for being so dumb (how much of a leap would it have been to make it Earth type?). Ice type somehow resists the most types, so it wants to be defensive, but most ice types don't seem tailored to this role. You can't feed a monster a berry outside of battle. You can bake that berry into a cake and feed that cake to a monster, but this is not advertised or made clear at any point. You have to read a book in-game or stumble upon the "oven" you carry with you to find this out, but also why force the player to do this extra step? Frivolity. The player character is a "battle researcher", but it's never explained why this is a job in this universe, or what the ordinary battle researcher does (aside from stand in various fields and caves throughout the game to generate XP and money for you, the player character). You are, of course, the chosen one, so your role/goals are special and only you can save the world, but if the world didn't need saving, it kind of seems like your job would be to make animals fight each other basically so you can watch them do so. This makes for an even flimsier and less defensible idea than that in Pokemon, where battle is basically a sport. Finally, the most objectionable 3 aspects of the game are the move similarity (to Pokemon moves), the catering to "hardcore" players, and the low monster species count. I can count on 1 hand the moves in this game that are not a 1-to-1 copy of a move in Pokemon (to the point of copying damage and accuracy values). I was immediately turned off by this because if I wanted to play Pokemon, I'd play Pokemon. I want to see some originality in the fights, not just set entry hazard, increase stats, use high damage move, repeat. This was done, I believe, in service of the second issue - catering to "hardcore" players. This is immediately apparent when the game asks you "do you want to play this in Nuzlock mode?" right at the beginning. There are also sorts of unnecessary difficulty modifiers and ways to mix up the vanilla experience, and it seems resources were put towards these zany tryhard game mode modifiers instead of the base game, to its detriment. Release these later, or as mods for those who want this. Lastly, there are technically 114 monsters, but 8 of those are "evil" versions of others, so there are functionally 106 unique monsters designed for this game. That makes for an average of 15 monsters per type, which isn't so bad until you consider that almost every evolutionary line consists of 3 monsters. So there are basically 5 monsters per type, and if I had known that from the outside, I probably wouldn't have purchased this game. The aesthetics were there, and some improvements were made upon the familiar formula, but I think it is an overly simplistic, dev wish fulfillment rip-off of the games that defined many childhoods.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good pokemon-adjacent game.Some nice quality of life features: HM move-equivalents are attached to the trainer, not the monsters (so you always have access, no need for HM slaves). You get the ability to teleport between towns quite early on. There are fruits you can grow in various locations on the map, but there's a drone that will both retrieve and re-plant them for you. You can access coromon storage from anywhere after you get a certain item. Relatively cheap to change the Trait of a coromon to any other Trait its species could have. The Exp Share type item(s) are acquired pretty early, and they don't reduce the experience gained by the coromon that actually battled. Some interesting wrinkles on the formula: all coromon are single-type, and some types *only* exist as moves, with no coromon of that type. Titans, the gym leader-equivalent, are (mostly) a single super-massive opponent rather than a team (combined with the fact that they're all single-type, the main effect is that it's a little easier to plan for each).The IV-equivalent, Potential, is easily visible (especially after you get a certain item relatively early game). Rather than IVs going directly to stats, it's a second experience bar. Every time it fills you get 3 points you get to distribute however you want, which is nice (and there's a way to reassign them for a cost). Shinies are based on Potential - higher potential forms have different colors. There's a Daily Achievements feature that's trying to encourage you to log in every day, which I find a little annoying for this kind of game, but honestly you can ignore it entirely and your progress in the game will still be perfectly fine.Competitive has some nice balancing features: level and Potential are set the same for all coromon in PvP, low-accuracy moves are all set to 100% accuracy with an adjustment to their power based on their original accuracy, moves with a % chance of inflicting a status effect instead become "every other" or "every third" or so on depending on the original %. I'm not super into PvP but what little I've played with it, I've liked so far.Overall it's good! Honestly you probably knew if you wanted this or not based on my very first sentence up there, but I hope this helps.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a really hard time to decide whether to recommend this game or not. Ultimately I had fun playing the game, and with over 100 hours of gameplay, it'd be a shame if I hadn't.The problem I have with this game, is that it really fails to stand out and be its own thing. It's clear the game is trying to be similar to pokemon and that's fine. But the developers should really have spent some time to come up with some more unique aspects that it's doing better than pokemon.The combat mechanics are pretty much the exact same as pokemon - rock-paper-scissor turnbased. The graphics look nice, but the design of the monsters leave a lot to be desired. The storyline is child-friendly and nothing to write home about.There are some more things I feel the game should have dropped and went in its own direction instead of just doing a more boring version of what pokemon is doing:- Instead of pokeballs you have spinners. they are exactly like pokeballs but their design is, well meh- You get to chose between 3 coromon at the start, each one of their own type and probably the worst one that comes to mind:- Throughout the game you learn to remove obstacles, surf on water and other things, but instead of it being your monsters that learn those abilities, it's some kind of sci-fi hoverboard that teach you to cool technology like surfing or fishing. I mean sure, that's different from pokemon, but instead of it being your monsters that interact with your environment, it's now some sci-fi aspect that is completely disconnecting your monsters from the game when it doesn't come down to fighting, making your coromon feel like little more than trained warriors.Do you think you'll feel a close connection to the first coromon you caught? Well, too bad cause it probably wasn't a perfect coromon. If you want the BEST team, you need to scratch all your weak coromon and spend hours grinding for the perfect coromon that has cool colors.TL;DRUltimately I had fun playing nostalgic game, but I find it hard to imagine why I would ever recommend this game over what it's trying to mimic. I haven't touched a pokemon for 10 years, but if someone told me they really wanted to play a child-friendly game where they catch and train monsters, I would still tell them that the older and bigger franchise has coromon beaten.

_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve played a Pokemon game before, you’ll be more than a little familiar with how Coromon works. After getting your starter Coromon from the lab, you’ll take them out to fight others in turn-based combat and level them up. Then you can use Spinners (which are totally different to Poke Balls I promise) to catch more Coromon, and raise your own adorable army. This game is a mustHas good graphics fps, combats, soundtracks and achievements aswell !
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: [EDIT] I decided to change the rating to positve, given that my opinion was more of a neutral one, and also due to the fact that the game is still being improved with new patches coming on monthly basis. Initial opinion follows:The first impression was very positive: nice looking graphic, great music, and some basic ideas taken from *MON series. Unfortunately the further you are in, the more of a slog the game becomes. Exploration becoms boring as most of the things you find are cakes (no fun equipment for our pupils similar to *MON series). Story is lacking any meaning or memorable characters that would get you hooked in. Dungeons are tedious and unnecessarily long - which I think even developers noticed by introducing checkpoint system. My last big complaint would be menus - UI in general - and controls. The menus are clunky, for example accessing Save option from the menu requires 6 button presses. I prefer to play games on a gamepad but the game was definetly designed for touchscreen in mind, as some of the tooltips are not accessible through gamepad controls but are accessible instead if you click them with a mouse (therefore simulating a touch event), not mentioning that big Cross button that can close the menu in the upper corner.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended for you to buy if you like pokemon games. Furthermore, the gameplay is fun, really good story with a little bit jokes there and there, battle system is not hard to understand, and lots of cutie coromon!It's really hard to find a perfect coromon, especially because of really low percentages to find them. Meanwhile, the potent/shiny is not hard to find, you just use a few item and eventually you'll find them.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Saves are uploaded to the cloud on the developer's side. Transferred over to another PC just fine.Literally just pokemon on PC but with various QOL additions and some slightly deeper RPG elements. If you like that, go ahead and grab it. If you don't and wanted something different out of an RPG that isn't just Pokemon again, well look elsewhere. You've got a lot of detailed pixel art and a ton of poke- I mean coromon to mess around with. There's genuine effort here and it wears its inspiration on its sleeve. Whether or not that's a good idea to just copy a game formula that itself has copied itself for almost 30 years, well that's another debate. At least it's not locked to a Nintendo platform or an emulator to play it. You can play it right here on Steam or even mobile. Mobile version I believe has microtransactions, so far I haven't seen any for the Steam version.Otherwise I'm curious how they'll handle cross play (if they do) between the PC and mobile versions in addition to future content. TemTem is advertised a pokemon MMO on Steam but this is more of a single player experience so I wonder if this is going to be a one and done kind of thing or if there will be expansions/dlc to keep players coming back. I haven't had any launcher issues that were purported by other players, in-fact I don't think my saves are going to any sort of cloud despite showing icons for it every time I save. No Steam cloud either and I can't seem to find my save folder to back it up. A bit frustrating for a game that might have hundreds of hours of progress put into a single save file... One crash so far, game has an autosave so thank god for that but you should save whenever you can.We have a curator page if you're interested in checking out more titles:Thanks for reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty well into the game now and have been loving it. I'm a long time Pokemon fan (gen wunner) who has become a bit disenchanted with the current crop of games, but this game scratches that itch!I love the difficulty options and built-in Nuzlocke options, so you can really tune your play-through regardless of your experience level. The "dungeons" and Titan fights also have a really great feel difficulty-wise. Difficulty is something Pokemon tends to fail at, so it's nice to have a monster taming game that feels challenging enough to make the whole experience worthwhile.I love the Potency system! Great job taking the obnoxious EV/IV system from Pokemon and turning it into something I actually enjoy engaging with. I also like that the "shininess" of a Mon is tied to it. I've played competitively with Pokemon, but still felt that the whole system of tuning and re-stating was a convoluted mess. The soft-reset and hard-reset options are great!I have a few gripes though that I hope the Devs may take a pass at when they can. I really like to sort my Mon's skills manually, so the fact I can't do that seems like a really odd decision or oversight. Even R/B/Y let you do that.Another issue is that the Coromon PC is pretty bare bones and it would be nice to see that get some of the features in the newer Pokemon games (box organization, move, tag/marking). Overall though, I'm very pleased and look forward to more updates and hopefully expansions. I'd also love to see some of the "Skill only" types become fully fledged types. It seems like it's hinted at in game, so that is nice at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review: Coromon. It plays like your classic pokemon game which is good for players that are looking for something like. The monsters and pixel art are really good. The side-quests adds a bit of activity and life and that's nice.There's a lot of convenient features such as being able to change a Coromon's trait, the moves they learn are permanent so you just need to pick and choose the 4 you want to use. Change your characters appearance or your coromon's spinners and so on.Now for the bad. The story/game is very short and roster is even smaller than pokemon's base game with some duplicate mons in the form of the dark magic typing that can't even be used competitively. So if you take those out you are at about 106 mons and you'll encounter the entire evolutionary line without even needing to evolve to discover them through your gameplay which kills the magic of discovering coromon through evolution alone.End game is also non-existent. The ending of coromon feels like a rush job and tells that the game was released in a incomplete state.Another issue I have is having a coromons stats gated through their shiny forms which still feels very grindy for me despite the conveniences that were put in place. But if you don't mind these issues then go ahead and buy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

_childDocuments_.review:
Coromon is a modern monster taming game with retro pixelart. Coromon brings an immersive storyline, strategic turn-based combat and challenging puzzles to a classic genre.

Use powerful moves to take down your opponent's Squad. Use your skills to poison, stun or damage your opponent with an arsenal of available skills.

In the region of Velua where Humans and Coromon live in harmony, a shady organization is on the verge of releasing a dark power upon the world. Will they succeed in their evil plans, or can they still be stopped?

Step into the role of a young hero joining the technologically advanced organisation of Lux Solis. Gather your favorite Coromon to create a powerful squad. Together with your Coromon, you'll have to train, fight and puzzle your way through an adventure-filled world!
_childDocuments_.name: Coromon

name: Tentacular
detailed_description: Wishlist Tentacular! Discuss secrets, solutions or give feedback.. We’re always looking for players who want to playtest new features. About the Game Ten out of Tentacles! INKredible physics allowing you to fulfill your squid dreams. Inhabit the giant body of a mighty-yet-mild tentacle monster raised by the quirky townsfolk of La Kalma, a remote island colony packed with puzzles. Kraken your brain with 60+ mind bending puzzles Tentacular is a heart-warming physics-based puzzler bursting with inventive, immersive gameplay and lots of humor to boot. Solve puzzles using playful tools to build strange contraptions and spectacular structures, or wreak havoc with your lumbering bulk! Enjoy a lengthy VR story experience with a playtime of over 10 hours Experience a sweet and funny adventure about figuring out where you came from, and where you belong. INKubate incredible towns with the brand new Island Builder Expansion Build your ultimate island in the brand new Island Builder Expansion – free for all Tentacular owners!

short_description: Tentacular is a VR game about a gigantic but good-hearted tentacled beast trying to figure out its place in the world.

_childDocuments_.review: Played only for an hour so far, but I want to appreciate that someone's making a puzzle game in VR with actual story, world, and continuity and not just a tech demo or a bunch of random levels.Otherwise the game is kinda like Stolen Pets, but with physics. The tentacle controls work well (reminds me of Gorn) and there's a good feeling of weight and physical feedback. The style and story are very endearing. If you liked either Gorn or the Stolen pets, you'll probably like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by Tentacular's wacky looks, beneath its age-friendly exterior lies a crafty puzzle game with a great sense of humor that requires you as a player to work with the limitations of your massive Kaiju body, but that doesn't mean you won't can amuse enormously with the long tent cells and the powerful suction cups.Watch my first gameplay here: Tentacular is set around La Kalma, an island where when you turn 16 you have to find a job to make a contribution.Now it must be a coincidence that you have the misfortune of just turning 16 in the game, so your birthday is celebrated with a job referral, but this doesn't always go as smoothly as you are not a human being like the inhabitants of the ground.Tentacular can best be described as a physics puzzle game, as the discovery of these crystals prompts the local professor to invent MAGNETS, objects that can be used to fully connect objects and Poe. revolutionize construction. Sometimes that means building different structures with them to specifications and making sure they last long enough to take a picture, but sometimes it's just stacking building materials properly and relying on balance. Or sometimes it just hurls rockets into the air through rings, trying to land the passengers being ejected in a particular spot.The controls in Tentacular are pretty simple, with basic VR triggers for gripping things and joysticks for moving and turning. However, unlike other VR games, you don't have hands to grab things, but rather two huge tentacles that you swing around, so bad luck to be exact. And with the grip here you can't just curl up the tip of a tentacle or something like that, but instead control the suction cups on the tentacle, and where on the tentacle you pick up an object with those cups makes a world of difference. Moving a large concrete block with the tip will be extremely difficult, but easier with the center. Not to mention that it can also affect factors like your throw.Suppose you don't want to obey you can also incorporate a destructive play style and throw objects at wherever you want and deal damage, you can grab cars and throw on buildings, take people and throw them into the water, or just use your other tentacel as use a baseball bat, but in any case, all these skills are useful and necessary while performing your job functions and other objectives.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it! Pretty good VR game. They do a lot of things right that make it a good VR experience. It should serve as an example to other VR devs. Every menu is a physical object and it all feels very polished and fluid. Plus it's just a lot of fun. There's a sandbox mode to let you smash, build and play to your heart's content. Good stress relief. It's very gratifying to chuck a character that's annoying you. I got 14 hours out of the game in my first run and I have plenty of reason's to go back. I do tend to "stop and smell the roses" to get my money's worth. I did all the sidequests in my first go. It just might be a little cutesy for some and the graphics cartoony, but I like that kind of thing. Not to ruin it but the ending is actually pretty epic and "spectacular." Got a bit teary-eyed it was so beautiful.Bit of a warning: this is a physics-based game and it can be frustrating at times because it can go wonky. The most difficult parts are side missions that you can skip. So, you can get through the story part of it without too much difficulty. I did spend over an hour on one particular mission because the physics kept going haywire.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a pretty fun experience overall. If it's on sale, it's a steal. That's my TL:DR. Now for a bit more.THE PROSThe idea is solid and executed well in my opinion. You're a giant octopus monster with two large tentacles for your main way of interacting with everything. Along these two tentacles, it allows for different levels of strength and control over objects. At the tip, it's weaker, more floaty but you can really fling objects far since your arm is whip-like. At the base, you have the most strength and it's the closest you'll get to holding something directly in control of your hand. This makes for controls that at times are fun but also frustrating due to the precision required in some sections of the game, both main story and side content.The game looks great with a low-poly, cartoon style to all aspects of it. Definitely not an eyesore and since it's simple, the game runs flawlessly! There's even a fun little easter egg hidden all over the game that makes me hungry because I love JIF peanut butter. The story is a tad simple but hey, it works fine and every now and then, I'll get a chuckle out of the dialogue. THE CONSI really only have two large cons for this game. One is the amount of repetitive rambling from the characters while you're doing missions. They'll keep repeating the same phrase over and over, having large text bubbles that can get in the way while you're trying to work so you're practically forced to throw them somewhere else while you're clearing the level.The other con is the amount of precision that is sometimes required in the game. Granted, that is the main challenge but when you have physics that are also wobbly, it can be annoying. The most precision required is limited to side stories so it's not that huge of a deal but man it's frustrating at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: A nice and cosy VR hidden gem. The puzzles are very casual and laid-back but aren't scared to challenge you at times, the physics of the giant tentacles are an absolute joy to screw around with and the inclusion of a sandbox mode is nice to see and pretty fun to play around with on it's own. The art style, while quite basic, is really cute and definitely has it's own charm. It's not the longest experience; most native VR experiences aren't, but this is a pretty dang solid one.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game for the physics , story, cuteness, sandbox, humor, creativity.... it goes on and on. I would like motors, springs, gears etc for the sandbox and the ability to remove the tentacles and just use your vr hands for detailed builds in the playground.  Is that an option devs?  Cheers and great work
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Very good VR puzzle game, love it!Tentacular has so much cool ideas and a great premise of having two wobbly tentacles to solve all the hilarious puzzle objectives. I had hours of fun and the price is totally worth it.Sometimes it can be a bit frustrating or seem to be unfair, but overall the and graphics are really cute, the music is awesome and the tasks are always fun - especially those where you can make up your way of building solutions with magnets and all sorts of objects you have all around you.Played with Valve Index and RTX 3080, no issues at all on PC or Headset/Controller level.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Played on a Valve  HMD/ControllersWhat did I just play? :O What actually just happened?!Hey internet user, are you tired of looking at that other tentacle stuff and want to control them yourself while being bossed around by people from the Wii universe? Well you have come to the right place XDSo this game popped up in the curator program, and without looking at anything I hit accept and jumped straight in. What a weird experience I just had! Pretty surreal, honestly. Its a remarkably charming and adorable game, thats well put together. You play a creature with tentacles, (was not explicitly said what I am, so Im leaving it at 'creature') and begin your journey on your 16th birthday at such time that you need to get a job and help out your community. Which basically gives the developers an excuse to get you to do all manner of tasks! The game has a good level of polish and feels thoughtfully made - how ever obscure. Suitable for all ages.Its designed to be played in a fixed area and actually (properly) supports seated. Some simple enough options, volume mixer sliders, height adjustment, dialog speed, and some basic graphic settings.Using max settings with a 3090/12900K, even with SS tested at 300% the game ran smoothly. At 150% SS the game typically used less than 30% GPU. In other words, anything that is marked as 'VR ready' should be able to run this game. One small note, it was using more than 6GB of VRAM, so if you have less than that you will probably have to turn down settings/SS.Surprisingly fun game, good quality, wholesome. Fairly priced. ^^d
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: I do recommend Tentacular, it's a very cute narrative-driven physics puzzler for VR. Beware though, there is a lot of text box reading involved in this game as there are no VOs, all the characters speak gibberish. Despite that I enjoyed the narrative even though it's obviously a simple story geared for families. Elon Musk just happens to be the butt of several of the puns.In between the story, there are several puzzles to solve. The good news is that there is a lot of variety in the physics puzzle and I would consider them to be casual-style puzzles. There really isn't anything too mentally challenging although I was stumped on a few of them for longer than I want to admit. You have all kinds of objects / tools / magnets to play with that have different effects. I did find some of the puzzles frustrating just because they weren't difficult, but the process of solving them was frustrating. Obviously, you have giant tentacles instead of hands so some of the challenge is in that very fact.Game is running on the Unity Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting a steady 90 fps. I did not experience any serious issues or bugs. You do have full locomotion and snap turning available, however it is within a very limited area (because you a God's eye view of the action and the world looks like a small diorama). There aren't very many graphics options available, only anti-aliasing and shadow quality.Overall, I do highly recommend this game. I had fun. It took me approximately 8 hours to complete the main campaign, but there are side missions afterwards that extend the gameplay, as well as an open sandbox experience. I think this game is perfect for families. It is very polished and if you're thinking this is a quest port, well, honestly it looks great in PCVR and it's a full game, not just a demo.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden VR gem. Devolver Digital has made some hilarious games in the past and it's interesting to see a weird game from them, a VR game on top of that.Playing as some sort of a lost Kraken, you befriend a small village of people and help them sort out their problems while trying to sort out who you are. They essentially teach you the basics and then let you go from there to solve each situation you're called into in a create way. Some players might find certain missions fun or frustrating, depending on how you want to play. I only ran into a few of these missions and it was mostly because I accidentally bumped something or was overthinking the solution. Most players will likely get frustrated with the magnets and how they attach permanently to literally anything they touch unless you destroy them.There's also a sandbox mode which I think is a really neat idea for more creative players.The visual presentation of this game is really well done for VR, the world is very small but keeps everything within reach without being overcrowding. Controls are simple but your ability to control is clumsy at best, on purpose. Also, those ending credits were a sharp idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game here, not finished it yet but having a great time with it. There loads of inventive ideas and cool puzzles, and the plenty of challenge with all the little side missions. should be very re-playable too with its extra sand boxy stuff away from the main story and the fact you can beat missions in a variety of ways. should probably also mention i liked the art style and the humour in the game.  easy recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game. Great style, interaction. design, puzzles. Its a puzzle game with character, and I would liken it to Job Simulator in many ways. If you like Job Sim I think you will like this title. Good story, cute characters, and thought the wobbly arms can be frustrating at times, its fun and meant to be that way, otherwise it would be too easy. Perhaps a wobbly factor setting could help reduce the frustration.I really like this title and think it a bargain for the price, especially when you compare it to other similar titles.I hope to see more innovation like this in the VR world.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Tentacular is a brilliantly designed game perfect for VR.  The experience unfolds as you travel from island to island, each presented as a charming 3D diorama that reminded me of the level design in The Curious Tale of the Stolen Pets.  Each scene has just enough detail to bring it to life along with an eclectic cast of characters to interact with.Tentacular is a charming interactive experience with a cute story and engaging physics-based gameplay that’s fun for the entire family.  The game is admittedly a bit linear and unless you are really having fun with the Playground area this is a one and done once you have finished the 5-7 hour story.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Tentacular is a great VR puzzle game. There is no super complex stuff here but whats on offer works exceptionally well. The puzzles are not so much hard but an excuse to just have fun messing around but they don't feel too basic or underwhelming. Its a really well polished little experience with a lot of effort put in to the writing and sandboxy elements, and the developer really focused on little interactivity features with the world that make this game fun and enjoyable to play. Its definitely a worthwhile VR game at full price, but if you're still a bit unsure definitely consider picking this one up on sale for an afternoon or two of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Congratulations to the developers, in addition to their creativity, they did a great job in the development, because I had no problems at all throughout the game.The game it's so much fun and some interactions are actually quite funny. I was laughing at the characters' reactions after I threw them away, hahahahI highly recommend this game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: This game started off really fun. It felt like a bit of puzzle game but with physics and tentacles, I really enjoyed how goofy yet fun it was.But then the bad annoying and straight up frustrating missions started. All about building up stuff where things have to stay in exact positions. Now, this wouldn't be the end of the world if you had hands, however, you have tentacles. This not only means that you can never be precise, but it also means that when you try to be precise, your tentacles will glitch out and break everything you tried to make.Some might argue that using tentacles to build stuff is fun, I disagree. I came here because I wanted a fun puzzle game with stupid physics, instead what I got were some puzzles and then just this awful building stuff with no way to skip it (as explained in the edit, there is actually a way to skip levels, apologies).I think this game starts off being really interesting, but quickly starts to rely on building and stacking as well as its magnets, leaving the game to be less of the type of puzzle game I expected it to be. I was hoping for interesting puzzles and having the tentacles be utilized in interesting ways, rather than just be like annoying extended arms that just make building and stacking so much more frustrating than it has to be.If you like that kind of stuff, feel free to get it, but I personally would not recommended it.Edit: the devs actually responded to the review which was unexpected but appreciated. Apparently there is a way to skip levels by using a cheat code, I know the game said this but I thought they were just poking fun at the player, which was my misunderstanding.I will continue playing the game and if the game stops giving just balancing puzzles, I will update this review in order to reflect my changed opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and cute. Very enjoyable campaign. The gameplay mechanics are... well, if they aren't unique to this game, they're certainly not overused in VR. It's almost an octodad or QWOP-like, in that your interface with the world isn't rigid. It's more fluid (or perhaps... gooey) and organic, which is part of the challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable, quirky and honestly quite funny.  I love the visual style, the town and various locations are like looking at one of those wonderful model train displays (except i don't get screamed at for touching it). The wee cars zooming around (then exploding after a hurl them), the way the townspeople parachute back if you launch them into space. fantastic.Runs well, simple to pick up but requires a bit of finesse. I can see how the movement of the tentacles could frustrate some people but its a "work with what you got" situation which i think keeps immersion up adds to the silliness of it all. Its all physics puzzles, nothing ground breaking but damn fun and thematically fitting.Honestly id be happy with just a larger town/island with more interactive buildings and people/props to just look at and mess with, again sofa king adorable. This perspective of being large is just so fitting for VR. Highly recommend,
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Eh. It's okay, the story made very little sense and the magnet puzzles were more annoying than fun. A couple things I did like however was being able to pick up the little characters and literally throw them as hard as possible to hear them go "Wee" and then see them parachute back down to their original spot, also the idea of whacking someone with your tentacle to talk to them/skip their dialogue was pretty funny.6/10 Overall
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: This game has taken first prize for my all-time favorite story VR game. For good reason. It feels like Giant Cop, but EVERYTHING was just perfect to me. The story gave me many laughs, the challenges were as much fun as they were challenging, graphics looked amazing with no issues, and had a satisfying ending. Best of all, it is my 5yr olds favorite VR game as well. He LOVES the world they built (and destroying it). Once I unlocked boosters/rockets and all the vehicles, I couldn't get him to stop playing. It really is an amazing game that was made with love. If you are on the fence about buying, DON'T BE, it is more than worth it. Can't wait to see more from the dev!
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's here. A VR title where you play as a tentacled kaiju going out into the world. Not to destroy things though. You're there to help the citizens of La Kalma which you are actually one of. Setting out into the working world at the ripe age of 16. You need to contribute, ya know.Tentacular seems (I only have 2.5 hours on the game so not sure if there's more here or not) to be a physics based puzzle game where you use your huge tentacles to move, throw, suction, slingshot, beat puzzles into submission. One puzzle has you trying to get an object, a large boat, up into the air and all you have to use are large steel i-beams and M.A.G.N.E.T.S. Yes, they are magnets. Very powerful magnets. It's up to your creativity to do it. After I figured out that there was no hand holding on how to do it, I managed to create a very wobbly solution. Shout-out to the stream chat for the suggestions!I had a lot of fun picking up up everything including the townfolk. A cool little detail is that if you try to throw them into the water, they have a life raft pop up around them. No drowning of these folks. You can chuck them pretty far out though. Just saying. There is also an area where you can do custom building on your own private island. I suspect I won't go there much as I've never taken to that style of gaming. I'm looking forward to getting more hours in of this VR gem. It's a nice break from the rhythm games I normally play in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I didn't know what to expect when I first heard about Tentacular. Is it a fully sandbox game where you always hover at the edge of town and mess with the townfolk? Yes. Is it a traffic management game? Yes. Is it a contruction game? Yes. Is it a narrative puzzle game? Yes. It is all of these and more with well thought out puzzles and missions that carry a brilliant story about you, the squid who was once seen as a monster, but given a chance to work alongside the town with larger than life projects that reveal some out of this world truths.What's most impressive however is the physics and attention to detail with the suction on your tentacles. I generally don't enjoy throwing things in VR because there is a lot that goes wrong with timing of releasing the trigger or grip buttons or motion tracking as you throw. In Tentacular however, it was the smoothest and most accurate throwing experience I've ever had in VR and this surprised me because of the floppy tentacles that extend beyond your hand. Not only that, but you really feel the sense of weight of an object depending on how you hold it. If it's a large ship or a block of cement and you hold it at the tip of your tentacle, it'll stretch and be difficult to move. Hold it with the whole tentacle and move it with ease. I thoroughly enjoyed the ability to move, rotate and place the miniature items as well because it really showed how delicate and accurate the suction mechanic can be. Loved it!Although I like sandbox games, I generally don't spend as much time creating things as I say I would, however, with Tentacular, I keep thinking of different things throughout the day that I'd like to try and build with the new parts I obtained throughout the story.Played using Oculus Quest 2 through Virtual Desktop.Definitely recommend picking this one up!
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

_childDocuments_.review:
Ever felt like a squid out of water?

Tentacular plunges you into the ocean-dwelling hulk of a gigantic, kind-hearted tentacled beast trying to figure out its place in the world.

Raised among humans on the bustling and eccentric island of La Kalma, the time has finally come to unravel the secrets of your mysterious origin while working as the world's strongest handyman. Help your human friends to research a strange and an incredibly powerful energy source through a colossal collection of action-based activities and constructions puzzles, using your titanic tentacles to aid your quest for answers and unlock elements for your very own playground in the creative sandbox mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Tentacular

name: Cartel Tycoon
detailed_description: DLC San Rafaela coming soon! About the Game Set in the fictionalized '80s Latin America, Cartel Tycoon tells the story of a time when the cocaine took over first the US, and then the whole world. Ridiculously rich drug kingpins rule over glorious empires, creating thousands of jobs. But a maelstrom of violence threatens this criminal underworld from within. Build an empire of drug production and smuggling chains while managing rogue lieutenants, state authorities, and public opinion. Rival gangs, the DEA, army and even the CIA all threaten your growing business. Death is inevitable, but not the end. When you die (it never really ends well for drug lords), crown your successor, and build your empire from the ruins all over again. In Cartel Tycoon, failure is inevitable and violence begets more violence — but for the cunning kingpin, unimaginable profits await. Play a variety of modes Story mode for those looking to dive into tens of hours of rich narrative within the game's world. Hardcore permadeath Survival mode for those looking for a challenge. And a highly customizable Sandbox mode for those looking to play by their own rules! Key features Grow your empire. Develop your humble farming operation into a massive logistical system comprising plantations, laboratories, aerodromes, and more. Reign your way. Tycoon action on an epic scale with dozens of upgrade paths and endless strategic combinations. Death is inevitable. When your capo falls, promote one of your unique lieutenants to take control and continue growing your cartel. Everything - and everyone - has a price. Launder your hard-earned cash to develop your empire, maintain your lieutenants' allegiance, and bribe corrupt politicians. Defend what's yours. Evade the authorities and square off against rival cartels on the path to profit. Endless replayability. Explore a dynamic narrative system with dozens of unique characters combined with limitless sandbox gameplay. Play a variety of modes. Story mode for those looking to dive into tens of hours of rich narrative within the game's world. Hardcore permadeath Survival mode for those looking for a challenge. And a highly customizable Sandbox mode for those looking to play by their own rules! Featuring an original soundtrack that captures the era with psychedelic and Latin American influences.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game on and off a few times in the lead up to 1.0, and to be honest, it's always ended letting me down. The most fun I've had is just jamming along in Sandbox to the (genuinely EXCELLENT soundtrack,) building up my empire and expanding at my own pace. The problem is that the game forces you to play the story mode should you wish to unlock more than a tiny handful of options for your playthrough.Here's some additional problems I have:1. Failure is often creeping and unknowable. It's perfectly possible to lose a game because you expanded an hour and a half ago and didn't realise you'd set a series of dominoes in motion that would slowly drain your entire balance dry. This is neither fun nor engaging.2. The way the story saves is utterly obnoxious. For an early example, I was replaying the initial storyline, where you have to pay off a character with legal money. I stockpile over the right amount of legal money, and then without realising, a day before the due date, I drop a few hundred dollars below the list, thus failing the quest. Can I go back? No, because the game has now quicksaved the split second the 'you failed' dialogue began, quicksaved after my Capo changed, and then quicksaved a third time when the next quest started, thus, locking me into this situation unless I reloaded a save from two hours ago. True genius.3. The way logistics works can be infuriatingly terrible. I've had trucks dump 15K directly into a laundering facility that is  with no way for me to re-assign it without the trucks immediately funnelling the money straight back into that same laundering building. I've given feedback previously on the Discord and through the official channel, and it's pretty obvious that some of my major irritations (especially the story mode/sandbox mode one) are intentional design choices that I can't avoid if I want to play this game. Which, unfortunately means I probably won't be playing this game that much going forward, despite being a fan of city builders and the aesthetics and sandbox gameplay of this one being damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm with the others who have put more than 10 hours in the game. It starts out great, it's fresh and new. And even as someone who LOVES time management games, this becomes micromanaging hell that you can't seem to get out of. It's just a frustrating cycle at this point. I'll certainly check back often since I really do like the game in general. But frustration does not equal challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Devs need to put more focus on this being a criminal organization that you're running with lots of moving parts instead of a generalized logistical manager with loads of caps and regulations.Cartel Tycoons creators need to take a step back and remember its title is CARTEL Tycoon. As of right now i'm pretty sure they think they're making a Package Delivery Tycoon.1. Gang structure is really bad RL Cartels have excess amounts of soldiers, cars, and money. Cartel Tycoon doesn't reflect that excess in anyway. For the gang they've gone with a system of "Lieutenants" only, soldiers/muscle are not really represented in anyway there are no cliques or anything to command or direct you're simply dealing with a character and some characters don't even have the ability to fight in combat!? Where's the character's bodyguards where is the hired muscle? None of that is represented in your organization at all its a VERY shallow system. You should be able to hire Lt's then buy muscle on top of that and that could increase the fighting power of the Lt but instead its all preset RPG "special character" style layout with predetermined combat powers. Same for building they give the owner a combat bonus when a fight breaks out but it would have been better if I could buy muscle and implant them in said building for a stronger base combat stat eliminating the need for my Lt's to run around taking care of every conflict and allowing me to prioritize the defense of critical buildings to my organization.Instead they give just Lt control and generally Lt's have useless abilities that your never gonna be able to optimize thanks to how the entire system is formatted especially having to keep an Lt stationary in a city because if you don't you lose the city. So every city you control your sacrificing a Lt just to make it not get lost and there is nothing useful or productive your Lt can do inside of the city making them completely useless filler. On top of that killing a Lt completely divides your Cartel unless its done in secrecy which like 5% of the Lt's have this ability. This is suppose to be cartel life people don't get eliminated and everybody looks at each and goes this boss sucks i'm done,  everybody says "its just business" and moves on but not in "Package Delivery Tycoon" everyone is going on strike and is going to fall out of line over one elimination. And now with the new "Balancing" patch certain Lt's have Terror requirements which doesn't make any sense at all. What Lt refuses to be part of an organization because they don't have enough heat on them??? The whole point of most organizations is to fly under the radar and avoid heat!2. AGAIN RL cartels have EXCESS amounts of soldiers, cars, and money. Your struggling to make money almost the entire time until the end game of a map. When the reality is you should have excessive amounts of dirty money pouring in even from the beginning with the biggest problem being limited amounts of businesses to wash it clean.Cars and trucks are always limited sometimes to a point that make no sense and completely stops you from making money. You start a whole delivery company and it will get 1 delivery truck? Seriously? Trucks and cars for your buildings should be able to be bought separately and without little to no limits on how many you can buy. Its as if there some government regulated limit on how many cars or trucks a building can have MAKES NO SENSE. And sure you can upgrade your buildings and get more trucks/cars but again this technology on the research tree isn't available until almost the complete end game of the map!Which leads me to profit margins that could be much higher from the start and on top of that the supply and demand system for pricing goods is god awful and changes way too fast for something that your producing infinite amounts of. Plus the price is dictated by your output supply instead of destination demand which is represented by a slow baseline increase which doesn't make sense cause it never really changes so the the market will never have a demand increase or have a demand higher than what I'm supplying it slowly dwindles down to bare minimum everytime. Furthermore I feel like if you were making more money overall through better margins and whatnot you would go through the research tree faster thus giving your access to more reasonable buildings earlier in the map but again the base profits/cars/trucks of the level 1 buildings are terrible.3. (Lastly and most importantly IMO), there's no real underground factors in the game yet.Hopefully this will change since the game is still in development and there are prisons and guerrilla camps and other buildings that simply say "Coming Soon" and have been for quite some time sure would like to see what the plan is with that?But as of this moment the bribery/corruption aspect of this game is again VERY shallow. Where is the police chief that i can bribe so i can permanently freeze my terror star so the police won't raid my building as long as I can afford to pay him my buildings should stay raid free! Or the judge to stop the warrants for my raids? Or the politician that backs off the DEA? Your connections are a whole lot of nothing... They've got it where you work your way up on the "Terror" bar which is a whole other set of nonsense that's very poorly implemented especially after this "balance" update. To which the police begin to randomly block roads and federales raid your buildings at random. You can bribe the blockades but it has to be with "clean" money which doesn't make any sense to me seeing as its a bribe but with the federales you just have to suck it up and try to use your political connections or fight back when they raid you which if you win they will go him with their tail between there legs for a while. But even your connections in the city again is very limited choices being reduce terror or unseize buildings. And sometimes its cheaper just to pay the fines to reopen than unseize through your connection. But again your not really pulling strings in your connection that puts you in a position of power or advantage just always the ability to salvage something that's already occurred to you. No judges in the pocket no police chiefs or anything of that nature, again SHALLOW. This is a big reason why Cartel Tycoon doesn't feel like "CARTEL" TycoonI will commend the devs on there constant updating but again they are going on about balancing and making money getting more easy and things when your not letting the cartel be a cartel you're regulating a black market your not focusing on the criminal aspect of everything but instead the mechanics of a system that isn't matching the genre of the game. I will update this as time goes on but right now I can't recommend this in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: FIRST IMPRESSIONS After about two hours of gameplay, specifically the campaign, I'm enjoying it.  As far as a criminal enterprise simulator goes, this is fun.  There's a slight slope of a learning curve to certain mechanics that you might miss if you don't read the instructions, which appear in an open book icon at the top left of your screen. The campaign doesn't exactly take you through these mechanics.    OVERVIEW The game seems to focus mainly around building your criminal organization mainly through establishing a thriving economic network: build businesses, make money, expand your territorial control for more business opportunities.  The bread and butter of your criminal empire are plantations where you grow your drug crops and interconnect them with distribution areas (airfields, seaports, etc.) for dirty money that you'll need to launder through legitimate businesses that you can also establish for legal money.  You'll also be able to hire lieutenants to assist your captain or captains (?), each with their own abilities.  Increase their experience to be able to access more of their abilities.  CONS I wish you could delete roads or maybe I'm missing the option to delete them.  It wasn't until after I built my first few farms and connected them to a warehouse that I realized that there should be a specific way that farms and warehouses should be oriented in order to maximize the effectiveness of their transportation system.  Without being able to delete these roads, they end up cluttering the landscape and make it difficult to place future structures or even tidy up messy placement.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary - July 2022: This is probably one of my favourite games at the moment. It has so many strengths which lend to replay-ability. The fact that the dev team have worked so hard on it shows that there is real passion around making a good game. This excites me a lot and I'm really excited to see what DLC and other stuff come out in the future.  I definitely recommend this game to anyone who loves the RTS genre. It has a unique take on RTS that allows you to play it without fear of a significant overlap with other games you might enjoy.EDIT 2: It's the end of July 2022. a LOT has changed since my last review. I feel like i'm parroting myself.  The improvements and changes are moving at an amazing pace. The dev team is so interactive and working so closely and openly with the community, taking feedback, fixing issues, etc. I am SO excited for v1 release.  I have raised a bunch of bugs and feedback around improvements. So far it looks like everything I would like to see to fix/improve the game is being released in v1.0EDIT: it's the end of November, 2021. A LOT has changed since my review & I can say with absolute certainty: This game has improved amazingly well.  The dev engagement via discord for bugs and feedback have helped shape this in to an exceptionally fun game.  I just keep wanting to play it, but at the same time I want to give it another miss for a few months to see what else they do to make it even better.  A lot of the issues & balancing that I was having probs with have gone away. July 2021 - I really like the concept of this game. There are *SO* many issues &  balancing that need addressing, BUT it is alpha and that's as it should be.  If they can fix the majority of the balancing issues & bugs by the time this goes Beta, it'll be a really, really good game. For now, I don't think I can play it much more. The complexity curve goes up very quickly the bigger you get, to a point where I legitimately can't play anymore. I had to reduce a lot of the settings to make it easier and even then by the time I'd captured my third city, it'd gotten to a point where the balance was too skewed to one side and I couldn't continue. I did enjoy the game and I am really looking forward to coming back to it in 6 months to see the progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun and worth your money.  The game is a little light on the management side of things, and there's not a lot to do once you've conquered the whole map except to deal with annoying events.  The money laundering aspect needs a serious buff, I think.  You can basically max out the entire map's laundering capacity with a couple of reasonably small production chains; if you have visions of filling the map to capacity with meth labs, that won't be necessary.  I had hoped that I could launder dirty money by producing food and other legal exports on a large scale, but then I discovered that exporting spice via the land border can lead to an event that makes exporting spice generate terror for some reason, and I just gave up.This limitation to laundering money creates a number of significant problems.  First, it means that in mid-game, I no longer care about the police/roadblock/dea.  Because I have more dirty money than I know what to do with (even with the best laundering buildings in the game) it doesn't really matter if a production chain goes down.   Second, the game just turns into an annoying grind while I wait for my minions' power to get to the point where I can go on the offensive.  I don't have jobs for them since they can't export, and so I'm just left to micro their loyalty and deal with them creating terror.  Third, production chains get backed up and you get a notification for EVERY building that is overflowing with any item (which in turn means that I just ignore any notifications because there are too many).    As for exporting itself, I don't see any value in the seaport or land trade since I have to keep track of what items are generating terror.  This is just pointless micro when I'm trying to min/max a production chain.  Having to keep lieutenants there is also more micro that I don't think is really worth it, since I'll probably end up generating terror.  More control over what is exported and when would be helpful.  For instance, if I have 100 of an item in the port and that item is now generating terror, I can't stop the export except to find an idle lieutenant who can deliver and give him an order to remove the item.  This is just annoying.  Optimization doesn't seem great.  Again, with a few small chains the graphics were getting pretty choppy.  Micro with lieutenants is pretty tedious and uninteresting, as is monitoring and making deals with cities.  There needs to be a better warning system for when my loyalty is too low.  I can't tell you how many times I lost early on because I didn't know my loyalty was critically close to zero.  A better system for determining what is generating terror would also be helpful.All in all, a good game worth the price I paid of $30.  Probably not enough logistics management, and a bit too much micro, but overall pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon is a fun take on the tycoon genre. The game mechanics, game play, graphics, and economy are what you would expect to have in a tycoon, though are not very deep. That does not mean the game is bad or feels incomplete, it is just not as deep and complicated as other games in the same genre. This allowed me to be able to jump into the game when I wanted to enjoy playing, without feeling like I would have to relearn the economics if I had not played for a few weeks. The average mechanics and game play are forgiven by the fun 'cartel' theme and polished graphics. While the theme drew me to the game, the small, but enjoyable stories they are creating kept me playing. I have worked through both stories so far and am looking forward to the next big updates. The developers are actively working on the game and have kept a few unused buildings in the game to show what the future may bring. Pros: Fun theme, nice polished graphics, the 'tycoon mechanics' needed to make the game enjoyable are present.Cons: Those looking for a deep and complicated tycoon, may feel the game is shallow.

I love the challenge it poses to try and build an empire while staving off all the aspects set to destroy it.  It would be nice if the terror/stars/Police were not so hard coded to really send your cartel into destruction.  For an EA, it's in great shape, very playable and has a lot of different ways to try and beat the system, but does really become labor some later in the game trying to micro manage all the aspects with limited personnel for the amount of coverage needed.  Really can use some streamlined and cohesive building management screens as well as a functional employee management screen, allowing you to change multiple peoples ranks and or pay at the same time from the same screen.Also, need to add hotkeys for menus and management screens, all the clicking gets tedious after awhile.Improvements I hope They Make:1.  Let my cartel fight back against the DEA, Army, Police,  the way cartels really do, let me bribe and buy every politician, judge, police chief..everyone in the area to protect me, run interference, block raids, all the good stuff that comes  with buying crooked people, if they can't be bought, let me blow them up in car bombs like real cartels do.2.  If my Capo is caught, why is death the only option, don't i get a trial, can't my friends  from suggestion #1 above, can't all my bought people help me get a "fair" trail at the local courthouse?  And if the trial isn't going my way, let me have my cartel start firebombing some stuff to ensure my freedom..or just let them break me out of prison.3.  Let me do what all cartel leaders do...let me bribe one or more of the incorruptible US politicians, CIA or the DEA, let me buy protection from them, allow me to corrupt the CIA into smuggling my drugs for me.  I have millions upon millions of drug dollars, let me buy something more useful than more drugs.4.  Make the Terror level and the stars realistic to some degree.  Right now they are just punitive.  I should be able to bribe people to cancel all DEA investigations and remove stars, i should be able to work quietly controlling my empire right under the DEA's nose because I bribed everyone i could and have the full protection of my local mayor and police chief.If you get a 1 year reign as Drug overlord, that's lucky....why do you want me to have such a short run at the top, Pablo Escobar had 15 years at the top.

_childDocuments_.review: Have this game since 10th of November. Many things have changed over these months.This game has a nice concept, it is pleasant and allows you to put your plans in action in many ways.The real problem with this game is the fact that you have to micro-manage almost every money-laundry action.They have introduced residences that help with that in a way, but most of the times you have to move the money on your own because the capacity of the residence is max. Furthermore unless you only trade smuggle opium, all the other drugs bring you a lot of dirty money that cannot be converted into clean, even by using all the available choises a city has to offer. So, you end up with tons of dirty money that you have to stash in your city, by micro-managing only! (remember the residences's capacity is always maxed). Its getting really annoying having to deal with this every 2 mins, making it really hard to expand or follow story.Now the lieutenants have different traits, most of the times usefull, but the way the game obliges you to place at least one of them in a Captured cities, Ports, Airports, or Checkpoints makes them useless. If u do not place one of these guys in any of these stations, you lose it. Trying to expand is really hard because you have to recruit lieutenants that have attack points so you can win the fights but you have to recruit and some other weaker ones so you can place them to the Captured cities, Ports, Airports, or Checkpoints. The games allows you to have 15 lieutenants maxed with 1 of them being the Captain. Each one of em demands a payment either in dirty or clean money. Sometimes paying them in dirty money proves to be hard cause they have to have access to it from the building they are stationed.Moreover, over the time they demand a promotion and if you are not planning to give em one, you can raise their salary. But if they arent promoted, i noticed that they lose their morale faster and demand bigger payments in small times from the previous one.Overall, its a really good game with rough edges. If they manage to fix these problems and automate the laundry transactions in a better way and fix the requirements for Captured cities, Ports, Airports, or Checkpointsfor it is going to be more pleasant to play. Remember it is still Early Access. Sorry for the long Review, hope i helped!Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting take on the strategy and management sim category, but I think the developers missed the mark on several aspects of gameplay. Great concept that has potential, but not a buy decision for now. - The "Residences" essentially function as cash distribution points in order to keep your businesses afloat, however, the actual task of moving funds between sell points and those cash distribution points is cumbersome. Where-as you likely only have one sell point to move your products early on, distributing that income out across all the distribution points evenly is impossible, and unless you are ordering over-priced lieutenants to manage all of you cash movements, you are essentially sunk from the beginning. - The research system is well enough, but the massive amounts of "Clean/Legal Money" it costs is ridiculous. Add-in paying lieutenants in clean money (Because you can never get "Dirty Cash" where you need it, and you can barely generate enough to actually utilize the system. - The commodity prices in relation to building upkeep can slowly generate profits, but again, the distribution and resource management system is overly complex with for no apparent reason, and has you micro-managing to a degree that even I don't enjoy. Even if you manage to be profitable, expansion comes at the price of trying to fund a new residence, multiple lieutenants to transport cash, and the inevitable cartel wars that leads into my next point. - Their Heat/Notoriety system is ridiculous, it only ever increases unless you have a mayor reduce it, but again, generating clean money to then pour into the city in order to generate citizen appeal so that you can leverage the mayor barely works. I think it's a great concept, and despite its issues, the game is a fun. However, there needs to be a lot of work done before it reaches a true playable state.
