_childDocuments_.review: Got this game while in early beta and absolutely love it. The devs have kept updating, balancing, and fixing bug issues throughout the duration of the beta, and have kept doing so through the full release of the game. I have seen some negative reviews from some of the newer players who have decided to give this game a try and maybe this post will help get them/you a foot in the door and off to the right start.TIPS: (Recommend playing the campaign before trying any other modes)1. The pause button (spacebar) and fast forward buttons (1,2,3 numerical keys) are gonna be your best friend. pausing the game as soon as you begin either a new story, sandbox, or survival mode is a must to get your bearings and to plan out where you will be building your facilities. Since you can still interact with the map and most features while the game itself is paused, this allows you to get most of your building placed before any events may pop up.2. When you first enter the game and then pause the game, THE FIRST THING YOU SHOULD DO is select your neighbor’s territory specifically the RED territory is what you want to focus on as that will be where enemy gangs will launch attacks from. In those red territory(s) you need to click on the city for each of the red regions and “talk” with the leaders in those cities (the GOAL is to INCREASE LOYALTY) as the higher the loyalty; decreases the chance to be attacked by those rival organizations. Doing this first will completely remove the possibility of being attacked early/ or potentially at all in the game. There is a cooldown to when you can talk with them again.*Note: You will begin dialogue with each of the leaders and be given options to choose from in response to their questions and statements and your choices WILL ALTER your loyalty with them EITHER POSITIVELY OR NEGATIVELY. (Low loyalty = gang attacks, High loyalty = no gang attacks). It is up to you the player to find what dialogue combinations work and what doesn’t work as there are to many of them for me to explain.*THIS IS IN REGARDS TO AMADO STARTING REGION*3. After finish talking with the mentioned leaders, what you want to do is while the game is still paused click on the hammer icon “Buildings” and select farms and build 3-4 in the highlighted green area for increased productivity Make sure that you leave enough space to build a warehouse that can cover your farms or else you will need to manually transfer goods from farms to your storage/warehouse.4. While the game is still paused select the research button (The light bulb) in the very bottom right hand corner select the river pier 1 and research all 3 (minus the tank icon) options each one cost only $800 but will drastically increase your cash flow in the short run as you will be able to hold more resources at piers, sell more resources at piers, and have the ability to send lieutenants to accompany shipments increasing volume.5. After selecting the research mentioned above, click on the river pier, and upgrade it in order to start using it as a distribution point. Once its operational you can either use a transport company or lieutenant to move goods to the river pier (This will begin generating you dirty cash). Also make sure your residence once you select it has a route to the pier (Click the plus button at the bottom of the residence and select the pier, as this will have your residence consistently gathering the cash from the pier.)NOTE: when selecting the pier there will be a cargo tab, everything is initially selected to be sold. You may want to deselect (grey out) everything except for the goods you want to sell or else the AI will automatically begin selling goods you may want to be saving for packaging at your workshop.6. Once all the above is done you should select your city (Amado) and click the plus buttons to build a taxi company as that will begin generating passive clean money. You can use either dirty money(tan) or clean money (blue) to build. I recommend dirty money as you have stable source coming in from the pier.__________________________________________________________________________Additionally stay away from lieutenants with high terror levels at the beginning of the game or you will run into issues with them going out of control and becoming volatile as some may have already experienced.*These high terror lieutenants can be managed in 2 ways effectively from personal experience *1. Only higher them Under 2 circumstances in EARLY GAME:     A. Early game and you are under attack from rival gangs and need the extra combat          power to defend your buildings(If you followed the above suggestions in dealing          with red territories this will be a mute point.)     B. You plan on attacking an enemy territory such as the yellow territories which are           not ruled by enemy gangs and then plan on assassinating that lieutenant after           accomplishing your goal, thus removing the possibility of them going out of           control (you can also increase their pay to increase loyalty but with lieutenants           like *TONY* unless the world is burning he will never be happy).2. Save them for late game:*You can manage high terror lieutenants in the late game where you have large sums of dirty and clean cash by consistently running festivals at certain laundering facilities which increases your regions overall loyalty level. *IF YOU MAX REGION LOYALTY THROUGH FESTIVALS AND THE LIKE YOU WILL GAIN A PASSIVE BUFF* This buff will passively increase all of your lieutenants loyalty over time.*BY MAXING "REGION LOYALTY" and keeping it maxed out*It becomes impossible for lieutenants to become volatile regardless of their desired terror levels. But again this is only possible if you HAVE A CONSISTENT FLOW OF CASH to keep festivals going.THE ABOVE SHOULD HELP YOU WITH THE BEGINNINGS OF THE GAME BUT DOES NOT INCLUDE THE LITTLE TRICKS YOU WILL DEVELOP AS YOU PLAY. HOPE THIS IS HELPFUL.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun to set up little production lines for various drugs. Challenge in export without garnering too much attention. Needs some hot keys but otherwise easy to use and understand. Graphics are nice and pretty. Some balancing issues (briefly touched on below). Needs scenarios not on the main island. Diplomacy is key, and buying from villages/gangs. Recommended, but enjoy it as needing work. I found though late game was a downhill spiral as everyone just wanted to go volatile regardless of how much money i pumped into them on a regular. Production chain and logistics was a little too simplified or unobtainable. You'll play with opioids for too long. Need some early game diversity. Research takes 5eva, go straight to canniboids and then coke. Ampths were so out of the research tree I didn't need to even run a criminal empire when i got them. Don't attack unless you're ready to pay for eased tensions. Can the depreciation of goods be a little less steep; it'd be cool if a 'legit' business was actually viable too? Some issues....Impossible to stop warehouses from getting completely full on a regular. Became too tedious to worry about and I just had to constantly pay to bring the terror down instead of managing the empire. Interesting mechanic but late game its a notification nightmare. Oh, the entire production line is full again... maybe don't drop off that much then!!! Shutting down production buildings doesn't fix this issue either. Transport buildings are very limited. Possibly intentionally, but this prevents spreading facilities around the map which might have provided a bit more industry. Otherwise production is a very localised matter. Transport and Warehouse builds need to be able to be configured while building. They grab goods I didn't want them to have before I could do anything about it. Then I have to either tediously make a lieutenant move the goods to where they should be (and likely loose it in full buildings), or just leave it and have random stuff everywhere. Worse when they are higher tier. Construction also needs to show a boundary line to help line up additional builds and provide space for roads. Liked the way roads are built; nice, simple, clean. Seaports shutdown some 'container' resources commonly, so get the harder stuff out by plane, and bulk out by pier. No warning either (or hidden in a flood of other warnings!), you'll just look and it'll be confiscating vegetables. I just had coffee and vege containers and switched whenever it happened, but frustrating. Money logistics is a little impossible too. Need some better ways to automate that around the map. Perhaps allow residence to chain to other residence to keep a balance between them? Can't get Lieutenants to do it cause the capacity of the residence is too small and the lieutenants will just leave the excess on the sidewalk. I had a port sitting on a constant $900k and I had to waste a connection on residence all around the empire to distribute it. Hotels in every city might help. Why cache it when it'll be full again and I can't launder the buried money ?Lieutenants need to stop requesting stupid things at a penalty of loyalty too. There is only so much space on this island for another airport. Ended up ignoring it or burning down an existing airport just to put the new one in. Can't I just send them to the Salsa club to build up some loyalty ? Late game trick might be to just not answer the phone.. but thats a bit close to 'stop playing to keep playing'. Combat is unbalanced. Either the gangs will wipe out something you need constantly, or their constant undefeatable raids will frustrate you to end the game early. Solution, just diplomacy the hell out of the gang leaders. Buy whatever they are selling... throw it in the bin if you need or direct it straight to a port. Talk the talk. Forget fighting, once you have enough power to face them you don't need to face them cause they are already diplomacy'd down or you've quit. Combat would also be cool if you could build something like a compound, which prevented intruders from going past the gates without a fight/warrant. This would prevent the guess work and rapid slamming of spacebar when the sirens or gunshots go off - followed by a rapid re-deployment of any lieutenant close enough. Otherwise they just hit where-ever they want, while you have to pay a trespass penalty. Needs more active defensive combat, as well as aggressive steps to lower enemy gang strength. They seriously had 34 strength most of the time while I had 17. Edit: why not make production take much longer? It'd be more valuable but a bigger gamble. Much more risk to protect ?

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon is a business management game about plants!I'm kidding, it is more than this.Cartel Tycoon is a standard survival strategy business management simulator. What is different in this game is that it is inspired by the 1980s/1990s drug trade in Latin America. Growing, producing and smuggling drugs then money laundering and dealing with other cartels is one thing ... however, since when a significant proportion of video games do not involve doing extremely illegal things?!Unlike other similar games, try to step away from the game while it is running and you will come back to a deficit, full warehouses, buildings and seized by the police. _childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon is a game that seems to be designed to cater to a niche audience. If you're someone who's a fan of the cartel genre, then you might find this game to be right up your alley. However, if you're someone who's just looking for a fun and engaging experience, then this game might not be the best fit for you.One of the biggest issues with Cartel Tycoon is how quickly it gets boring. The game starts off with a lot of mechanics to learn, which can be overwhelming for new players. But once you get the hang of things, you'll quickly realize that the game doesn't offer much in terms of variety. You'll find yourself doing the same thing over and over again, with little to no change in gameplay.Additionally, the game suffers from a lack of balance. Certain mechanics are overpowered, while others are virtually useless. This can make the game feel unbalanced and frustrating at times.Overall, while Cartel Tycoon has potential, it falls short of delivering a fun and engaging experience. The overwhelming amount of mechanics, lack of variety, and unbalanced gameplay make it hard to recommend to anyone who's not a die-hard fan of the genre. If you're looking for a more enjoyable and polished experience, there are better games out there that are worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: The game offers a fun experience and represents an innovation in the world of management games. However, the challenge it presents can be considered quite demanding, although it may be somewhat unbalanced.At the beginning of the game, you are faced with the challenge of managing the needs of the characters with limited financial resources, which can be quite challenging. However, as you progress and obtain higher-level products, you may experience a reversal of the situation, with a surplus of money and the difficulty of deciding how to best use it. This aspect of the game can be compared to the situation of the famous Pablo Escobar, who eventually had so much money that he didn't know where to put it.Despite these challenges, I believe they are an integral part of the gaming experience and contribute to making it interesting. Furthermore, the game has the potential to become even better with developer support through the addition of new content and improvements. Ultimately, it's a management game that deserves attention, especially considering its affordable price.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon is a fantastic management simulation game that challenges players to oversee multiple supply chains and distribution networks. One of the game’s unique features is the management of two currencies: dirty money and clean money. The constant bottleneck in laundering dirty money into clean money adds a layer of complexity, as accumulating dirty money can either be wasted or attract the attention of authorities, creating a production ceiling that players must navigate.Unlike many games that reward unchecked expansion, Cartel Tycoon offers a more realistic approach, especially for a drug/criminal enterprise. Over-expanding your production while neglecting your distribution networks or laundering systems can lead to significant penalties.I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys managing supply chains and networks. Cartel Tycoon is a fun and challenging management sim that will keep you engaged and on your toes.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to those negative comments. This game is already much more finished than most other launched games of this genre. So I would suggest when you feel frustrated first time going into the story mode(which has a tutorial embedded into the story), you can hop on to the official Discord or just try to think for a minute or a two before leaving a negative review.The major complaints now are:you cannot cancel orders, the money laundering opportunities is way less than what you can possibly earn, yet the money you can possibly earn is way less than what you are able to build -- but to encounter these softcaps you need to first not fail, as this game is a bit more difficult than Frostpunk in normal difficulty (in story mode, the sandbox mode is much easier as you have the fund to unlock plantation) Which is, again, another reason why I do not understand where so many negative comments come from -- this game is so polished that you guys fail to recognize this is only its first few days into EA, rather than a finished game? Do you guys remember it took the Prison Architect dev 4 years (alpha+beta) to let players choose how many prisoners they wish to take in?You can definitely buy and enjoy the game now if you like the more difficult difficulty of the following games:Banished, RimWorld, Tropico series, Prison Architect, End zone, Transport Fever, Railway Empire/LOGistICAL, Foundation/Ostriv/Anno, Overcrowed/Mini Metro, Surviving Mars, Oxygen not Included, Ceaser/etcAs this game is all about setting up a smooth production chain, do not overproduce and over-expand, and manage limited resources, with depth in optimization (easy math, but very versatile) and layout planning(location, roads, supply chain inter-connections).

_childDocuments_.review: First 10-15 hours are great, but once you start getting into the mid-late its just a micromanagement hell. You figure out or or two productions which are the most profitable and stick with it forever, so not really needed to upgrade the techs to others late game.Your gang system (henchmen, whatever they are called) become disloyal and leave if they don't get a raise, which sounds expected, but giving them the bare minimum increase every month or so works much better than 10x that amount right up front, where they would earn much more.. So just another tedious thing to constantly check on unnecessarily, when the last time when the last raise was before it becomes an issue.Anyway, game felt great and cool concept in beginning but quickly falls apart once you get into the mid to late game with so much tedious micromanagement that it becomes a choir, stripping away all the initial enjoyment you felt. Its not a skill issue as you would have with something in other factory-style management games like Factorio, its just the way the game was designed and no way around it as it lacks any real depth.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the concept of this game, but there are a lot of "features" that make it unenjoyable for me. Although I recognize this is still an alpha, I suspect to final game will still inherently carry the excessive hand-holding and flipping of switches on/off.1) The only way to manually save your progress (disabling auto-save) is to exit the game?2) Dirty money doesn't balance quickly enough between Stash houses and Money laundering buildings. For example, my Hotel will be overflowing with cash ($65k+). Further collection attempts from smuggling operations result in tens of thousands of dollars in losses while my terror rating explodes and my Casino across the street sits virtually empty (ie $3k / $45k capacity). There's no "smartness" to collection. It should function more like this:Deposit Cash in Hotel? No, Full.Deposit Cash in Casino? No. Full.Deposit Cash in Residence (if connected) Yes.Top off production/warehouse operations within vicinity? Yes.Hemorrhaging cash with literally dozens of other places to stash it is stupid.Edit: Today something broke with the Journalist where I'm holding over $200k in dirty money and can't 'see it' or access it in any of my buildings. Hours into a game and it's ruined. GG.3) I want my Lieutenants to get paid with dirty money and to go get it themselves wherever closest--rather than stealing goods that are valued 2x-5x more than their normal pay. NOBODY steals from Papi Capo and lives!4) Production Buildings turn off automatically when funds run low, but don't turn back on when replenished. This is annoying.5) Police raids on smuggling ports are fine, but more automation is needed here. Give users a policy feature to control the behavior of what happens during these events. Toggling switches all game long is tedious and annoying. Let users automatically shut down and resume operations during these events. Overall, this game has a lot of potential and could become great with just a bit more automation. For me, I don't particularly enjoy all the hand-holding and turning buttons on and off. I do enjoy the elements of entrepreneurship and free enterprise. But the game is incredibly punishing if you make the wrong move. And rather than find a means to recover from your mistake, you're often sent down a cascading landslide of bull$%^&. Manually saving your game helps alleviate some of these unfortunate mistakes so that you can make more informed decisions, however it forces you to exit the game to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: Any long strategy game should have a save feature - it sucks making it 8 hours through the campaign to only get shafted by a series of random events and have no save to go back to. Strategy games that have mandatory iron-man mode always on use it as a crutch for not having enough content. Give me the option to turn it on and off.Even worse than not having saves is that you will run into scripted events in which you are often not given enough information to make informed decisions (you will not know the actual requirements for succeeding until after you select a choice), its game over. For example, you are told at a point in the campaign that you either need to pay someone off or kill them. If you choose to pay them off, you are given an absurdly high dollar amount with a time limit. Ops, sorry for not letting you know how much and that it's timed before you clicked it! In my next runs, now I know I need to save money in preparation of this event. That is crappy game design.The difficulty level is unreal, and it is also almost impossible to come back once you fall behind even a bit. I'm a legendary/ironman xcom2 player. I enjoy a good challenge. This game is not a challenge. To do well in the normal campaign, you will need foresight into what works and what doesn't, with no room for mistakes... which means you will likely have to play the first 50% of the campaign multiple times to really get the jest of it. I might still try and power through the campaign, not because I like it at this point, but because I put in too many hours to not finish it. From a game mechanics perspective, many systems are pretty wonky. There is no way to split orders, or have certain amounts of money go to certain places. You can't control stockpiles. Resource management is essentially non-existent. Finally, the two most annoying part of the game: 1) The constant popups of your underlings asking for raises and promotions. Its just not fun to navigate. I have too many other things going on to deal with their whining.  2) The ridiculously over-tuned police constantly locking down your stuff.I WANT to like this game. The setting is great, and I love that we finally got a mafia/cartel game that focuses on the business rather than guns blazing. However, the developers have a lot of work to do it get it up to scratch.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game very much, however there are some very annoying features that give my carpal tunnel a run for my dirty money, and I don't even say that about playing a game like CSGO.There is too much micro-management especially when you reach the end-game where you expand more and more. Your lieutenants start off basic and then they end up like children that has to be told what to do constantly when your empire reaches its peak. I'll give you an example, I have a ton of dirty money that needs to be laundered across several houses, hotels and whatever property. They have to be sent to the bank and the taxi company to fund it with cash. The problem is you can't keep them there for too long cause if there's too much dirty money it attracts the attention of the police. Imagine doing that for 10 different lieutenants and 20 different properties while your storages are full, police are raiding you constantly and you have to micro manage that stuff too.It becomes less of a game later on where you can kick back and pretend to be a drug lord to a chore where even your capo is an errand boy that has to give your lieutenants a helping hand smuggling and doing whatever, because again, they have to be told what to do constantly like they're children who never learn how to do their jobs.Another example is when you go to war, a lot of your production gets shut down. Think of having multiple cities you are running and having to re-open over 100 production sites ONE. BY. ONE. click by click because there's no way to queue this somehow.Those are a few examples. You still have to feed the general of some barracks, some prison warden a constant supply of whatever they want in order for them to keep working for you as you are constantly micro managing the other stuff I've just mentioned. Go tell your Lieutenant to do that while you are bleeding out of money to play the game with, cause they weren't ordered to deliver the dirty money for laundering AGAIN.It wasn't obvious to me for the first 2 hours of the game, but now that I'm past that I regret that I can't ask for a refund. I wish this game would work on these issues but it seems to be a common complaint that hasn't been addressed since release so I'm not feeling optimistic. Please correct me if I'm wrong and it has been worked on since release but it needs more improvements in my eyes if I were to change the feedback of my review.Overall, I love the game's artwork, music and its feel. It is definitely the best cartel tycoon simulator I know as of this review since this is the most in depth one I know, however, I don't wanna play this anymore because I can't actually just enjoy the game, personally, if I'm constantly micromanaging everything and telling veterans in the business what to do because they still don't know how to tie their shoelace by now. _childDocuments_.review: It took me a few starts until I could figure out many of the core mechanics, but I think I now have a reasonably solid grasp of the game. Overall,  has bags of potential, and with the suitable polish, could be the crime strategy game fans of the genre have awaited, particularly in the wake of flops like .Pros+ Appealing design. Other reviews have claimed the game evokes , and they're not wrong. The map is vibrant and appropriate to its setting.+ The core mechanics surrounding the production and smuggling of goods and the generation of legal money are pretty satisfying. + Cartel members have their strengths and weaknesses and can all serve a particular use within your empire.+ There is bags of potential for modding in this game.Cons- It is not always entirely obvious why a building is not working, why illegal money is not being laundered etc.- The Loyalty v. Terror balance is a bit off at the moment, in my opinion. It is easy to accumulate Terror but can be prohibitively expensive to diminish it. Whilst there's nothing wrong with this principle, it does lead to large stretches of playtime where you are not doing very much other than waiting (for money to accumulate, for loyalty to grow etc.)- Enemy gangs and law enforcement are pretty bland at the moment. They should have more flavour.- Combat is very simplistic; what "score" your cartel members have vs the enemy's strength. Something like temporary bonuses to sue in individual fights could help spice combat up a bit without radically changing the system. For example, a one-time use bomb for attacks on enemy gang holdings increases your attack score.I will write a full review when I have played more hours. On the whole, though, if you are a fan of tycoon games or crime simulators, this is worth checking out. There are still plenty of kinks to be ironed out, but  has the makings of an excellent game when it is the finished article.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I bought the game on sale for 10€. For that price, it's really good. Probably one of the best 10€ games you can get. But if someone pays more... oh boy.The game is ANNOYING. I mean it exactly as I say it. The story mode is a "Free Play" with a tutorial upfront. I eventually started clicking away the dialogues because the German translation is really poor and, as a stylistic choice (fitting the setting), it's interspersed with some Spanish talk. Since I don't speak Spanish, it's just incomprehensible gibberish to me (which is not translated into English or German, so you don't know what was said). This wouldn't be a problem if the texts weren't so endlessly elaborate. Every text bubble, every dialogue, everything in the game is like a small book (like this review :P).In essence, it doesn't matter because every quest in the game boils down to "bring X goods to location Y." It gets tedious after 5 minutes. The difficulty level is, de facto, non-existent. The game practically bombards you with money, and it never stops. After 60 minutes, all my underground bunkers, villas, airports, and ship harbors are bursting with money, so I went through phases of just demolishing all buildings and letting the game run in the background at full speed to launder black money into legal money. The game has absolutely zero balancing.Annoying point number 1: The enemy AI is just there to annoy you. The cops are just there to annoy you, always in pairs. That means if you mess with a hostile gang, you can bet money that in the background, the cops will disable your operations, even if you have 0 attention. And if, like me, you have no buildings left because you're waiting for black money, then it becomes apparent how poorly scripted it is. Because the cops still come even when you're practically doing nothing. If they don't have production facilities to raid, they'll take something else that belongs to you. Whether it makes sense or not doesn't matter. The main thing is they always come when you have trouble with a hostile gang.Annoying point number 2: When you demolish buildings, a piece of road always remains. You then have to painstakingly demolish it separately. With 200 buildings, you have 200 small pieces of road hanging at the entrance road. Have fun!Annoying point number 3: The granularity of this game is so annoying. You build a new warehouse, and it automatically connects to everything within reach. You then have to manually disable it in every supplier. If, like me, you build super compact, the list can be 60 points long. And this "generate extra work" aspect really permeates every aspect of the game. Whether it's a quest where you have to manually bring counted goods somewhere or buy TVs and game consoles manually in a bar menu, of which you can only buy very few at a time because... well, there's no reason except deliberately making it annoying.Annoying point number 4: As mentioned in point one, the AI is only there to annoy you. In plain language, it means they neither build production buildings nor do anything else. Enemy gangs occasionally send a troop by, that's it. And you don't even have to react because they just go bang bang a bit and then leave again. Just like that. But what's even more annoying is that the cops only annoy the player. As mentioned, they always come when dealing with gangs and occasionally without any understandable reason. But only to the player. The enemy AI never has to deal with the cops. Coupled with the fact that they always come together with the enemy, it creates the impression that there is no difference between gangster and police.In terms of content, the game only consists of putting farms side by side. You then choose which drug to produce there and may need another one to four buildings to refine the drug. All of this is then provided with the two always identical logistics buildings (logistics office and warehouse), and that's it. No matter which drug you produce, the process is always the same. But why even change the drug? There's no reason. Regardless of the drug you choose, the profit margins are so absurdly large that there's no reason to optimize anything. After a few minutes of playing, you have so much money that you have to start burying it (literally), or the buildings will overflow.Have you noticed that many people write something like "I only sold avocados" or "I became the vegetable cartel"? It sounds humorous but is simply a valid game strategy to avoid the mountain of annoying details in the game. You just produce fruit and sell it. Money is not an issue in the game anyway, but in the case of vegetables, you don't have to wash them beforehand. And since salaries or ongoing costs are practically imperceptible, it's just the much better way to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: For the person reading this hoping it's the cartel management game they've always dreamed would be released... here it is baby.Nothing quite as satisfying as watching a convoy of trucks carrying 100 kilos of cocaine stuffed inside a chicken drive right past the Federales convoy on their way to t1tty f*** your cocoa farms.Or burning down a warehouse stacked to the ceiling with cash rather than letting the DEA seize it.So much potential for this game. I played the demo months ago and literally called out sick the day it dropped.That being said she needs work. A lot of work. Why in the name of god can a semi truck only hold $5k? The bottlenecks in this game are unbelievable. At the peak of my cartel I was laundering about $100k/day and that wasn't enough to keep up with the amount of meth and cocaine I was slinging.My factories were running around the clock pumping out more meth than my little smugglers could handle. At one time the DEA seized a port with over $250k in cash and close to a metric ton of narcotics, and I wasn't even mad because I'd been trying to move the money for weeks. Logistics need to be overhauled so we can launder and stash money more effectively. Also, please give us the ability to hire sicarios when we need them. No reason my multi million dollar organization should be low on man power. I've got an 80 year old woman helping me capture enemy landing strips because she's good with a machete apparently. Hired guns should be easy, I should be able to hire a few lieutenants and their crews without effecting my cartel's roster.Muscle should be kept separate from administrative, or make it easier to organize within the cartel itself. Another thing. For the love of God please work on the stash houses or "residences" and make them fill your laundering facilities capacity, not just drop off a few grand. I had 4 stash houses placed outside my most active port and they would continuously reach capacity and attract attention while my banks and casinos literally minutes away are sitting at half full.Besides that, freaking amazing game. I've been wanting a good cartel sim since I was like 8 years old and first tried cocaine. Keep up the good work, and once all the little things are worked out give us more involved smuggling, like different routes and territories. I want to fight over control of different export territories. More in depth gang wars would be fun too, it's very easy to avoid attention if you're careful, but forcing us into bloody conflicts with other gangs would be very fun. I want to kidnap lieutenants, do drive by's on their territory, TP their grandma's house, black mail their politicians, all that.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute waste of potential, this game is.  It instantly reminds me of and makes me feel the pain, which was Evil Genius 2.  If you love to play a game with a half-hearted build/logistics model, dumb-as-rocks AI, and useless events/goals ... this is your game.  This is Evil Genius 2: Narcos Edition (not to be confused with the original classic "Evil Genius")  It is extremely shallow and barely rises above a mobile game.  The AI is non-existent and poses zero threat.  You can literally not attack once, and the AI will zerg you, woefully outmatched if you lean heavily into an assault-focused lieutenants, until it/all gangs commit suicide (they lose 1 power per loss -- zero = death/gang removal).Teching, focusing past the base opium drug to higher tier meth and coke ... pointless.  Spamming opium plantations, without a further need of refinement/tech, will keep you overloaded on dirty cash, which bottlenecks at the very few buildings you can build to clean money (banks and casinos -- the only two worth building)  you will have millions in dirty money, and slower than a snail, clean the money in mere thousands.Please don't get me started on the "logistics."  Non-existent.The artwork, graphics, music are amazing.  However, this game also has the audacity to give you a disclaimer referencing the 1980's trug trade, circa Pablo Escobar.  What a bait n' switch.  It's not deep enough for actual, intelligent gameplay and rated Peggy 13, at best.

_childDocuments_.review: After a good 30 hours or so in this game, I have some issuesFirst of all, had a blast for about the first 15. Once I realized this my immersion in the game dropped tremendously. You can capture their export routes, you can capture their farms and production, but they will still remain as strong as they were before. Not seeing any other trucks/vehicles in the map should have hinted at this but I guess I was too involved with my own stuff to care.The diplomatic approach seems severely broken. I could sweet talk all the gang leaders and have them at zealous level but they still would not join. There should be options to force gangs into cooperating. I don't want to send all my people to kill every single opposing gang just so they stop attacking me.Lastly, without customizing sandbox options, Lieutenants will continuously ask and ask for more money while their loyalty falls. This led to extremely highly paid people that offered nothing in return. You can't fire anyone, only murder them, which makes everyone else's loyalty drop leading to a never ending cycle of pay raises.TLDR:Have option to stop gang attacks or make them less frequent.Simulate other gang economies (you're the only one building, exporting, producing).Add diplomatic options to force gangs to join or cooperate. The dialogue system becomes tiring and seems too random.Stop endless pay raising and loyalty drop among your people.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on Cartel Tycoon. I think there is a good game in here somewhere, but currently there are too many nuisances for it to be enjoyable.The short overview of the game, you are the Capo of a Drug Cartel. You build production and delivery chains to smuggle drugs, which give you dirty money. You then ferry said dirty money to cities, where it is laundered into legal money. You research new industries and upgrades to make everything bigger or better, and have lieutnants and your own character who can drive around the map to either help your production/delivery, or fight enemy gangs and occasionally the cops.Currently, there are these major issues that break the game for me. And this is after giving the game a lot of time to try to convince me otherwise:- Lieutnants will give you random quests. Failing, or even declining to do them, results in a loyalty loss, that must be compensated with a payraise. These missions are random. Lieutnants can suggest something you were going to do anyway, or a mission that is effectively just free benefits... or they suggest completely inane, stupid stuff that makes absolutely no sense. Why would I build a new Aerodrome? No, better question, where would you want me to build it? We have one region and there is literally no place where it will fit.The dumb part is that they are never related to anything you are doing, or your current situation. And they can literally come one after the other. "Give us all a medium payraise!" demands a random new lieutnant, even though everybody is at high loyalty. Which means either just accepting that you will suddenly spend a massive amount of extra cash on upkeep, or take the loyalty hit. It's stupid.- The logistics and production amounts are incredibly annoying to balance. This goes for both the laundering of cash and the export of drugs. The game encourages a "More, bigger, faster" approach to empire expansion, especially with research. But you will rapidly run into constant issues of full storage. How many farms do I need to supply a drying rack, without having my transport company or warehouse overloaded? How many Opium farms can I afford in relation to my export? Normally this should be an engaging question. Instead it basically amounts to "Produce until full, turn production chain off, wait until everything is sold. repeat". If you try for diversity instead of specialization, you will REALLY resent this later in the game.Same goes for laundering. There is just no engaging way to try for a blanced input to output ratio, other than just turning everything off and on again occasionally.- The game does not encourage production diversity enough. Opium and dried cannabis are all you will need, ever. If you research upgrades to your smuggling points, you can export so much of the stuff that you never even need to take a look at anything else. The basic River pier / Aerodrome can eventually ship such an absurd amount of stuff, that sinking prices don't matter. And that's before I mention that certain lieutnants have an abilty that lets you sell the produce at markups. I was rich beyond anything I could ever spend without needing to touch cocaine or meth. Which is a shame.- Lieutnant management is tedious. They want a promotion or raise regularly, and the only way to do this is to just open their individual profile and raise it manually. The limited cartell slots also mean that eventually certain Lieutnants escalate their pay to dizzying heights, at which point the best thing to do is have them shot or sent to prison. You will never really get attached to any of them, and it's a shame that the only interactions you ever have with them are almost all negative (I.e. having to raise their pay constantly, them giving dumb missions etc.). The Lieutnants that want a certain terror level above 0 are especially crap, since there is no reason to play that way. The fact that they lose loyalty if you don't play suboptimally makes them annoying, and not worth bothering with.All in all, a lot of this is really fixable. And if you are happy with excessive micromanagement, the game can be fun. But for me, it heavily depends on what the future of the game looks like.

You'll still be f***ed up by government when your products are marked as "suspicious" for no reason and you won't have spare cash to restructure your bisunesess.Late game is also disappointing: now new mechanics, just game freezes and scaling up your production to further scale up freezes and get more pointless money which you already have more than enough in mid game.To conclude, I wouldn't say that the game is worthless, it just has nothing to offer except an interesing setting. Otherwise, there are plenty of other supply chain simulators with much longer, more complex and interesting gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Not terrible, but not good enough right now. It's a bit slow initially, needing a lot of repeated manual actions until you accumulate enough money to research buildings that help run things smoothly, like residences, better roads, bigger trucks, etc. This is made worse because the controls are clunky too. For example, you cannot cancel a character's action in the middle, and some actions are repeated automatically. Say you ordered a character to deliver money somewhere, he did, and then you realize he picked up another load to the same place, which you don't want. You click "stop delivering" because you want him to stay guarding the city, but he keeps going, completing the delivery and then just sitting at the destination instead of returning to the city he is supposed to be watching. A city not watched by a character eventually gets attacked and you lose it AND get a lot of terror, which starts various agencies investigating you, a status you can only get rid of by your capo's death. By the way, there's no intermediate saving, only "save and exit". All this trouble because the controls are not great. The concept is unique and there are some interesting mechanics that aren't in other games, like overflowing building capacity bringing heat on you and a heavy incentive to operate without attracting attention which is then very difficult to get rid of. Maybe it will be good some day.

_childDocuments_.review: I give it a 2 out of 10, and here's why. It really boils down to two reasons.The biggest reason is that it requires unsustainable micromanagement, beyond what you are capable of doing in the game. Your men (the trucks going to and from farms, warehouses, transport companies, etc.) are always either doing too little of something, or too much of something. You are always producing too much product, or not enough. You always have too much dirty money, or too little. And somehow you never have enough warehouses. Even with an independent transport company dedicated to each one. Doesn't work, I tried. And all of these issues will end up piling up on top of each other, resulting in an almost unsolvable mess. I've tried many different strategies to remedy this, and nothing really ever seems to work. I can't even imagine the logistics of producing something more than weed, given the logistics hell of just getting illegal goods to ship properly inside legal goods. Which is too bad, because there's quite a few illegal products to produce. But in the 10 hours I've put in, I have yet to even touch those products because of how much of a pain handling beginner products is.The second reason is that the power of your lieutenants is so low, they are basically worthless in a fight with another cartel. The enemy cartel will always roll in with 20 or so strength, and with 7+ lieutenants, I'm lucky if I can break 15 power. I guess you're just...meant to lose every time. Which really doesn't make sense. Oh and while you're busy losing, that raises terror, which sends the cops in. And guess what, they almost always overpower you too. And don't even get me started on the horrible balancing act of sacrificing all your respect to lower terror...So ultimately, this game gets a 2 out of 10 for very poor scaling and just...terrible to handle micromanagement. Which is too bad, because I really wanted to like this game. And before you think, "oh well he's just bad at playing sim building games," NO that is not the case. That is my bread and butter. I've been playing macro and micromanage sims for over 15 years, and this one is the first that I have had to put down due to piss poor design. The devs could probably fix the scaling of enemies in a future update, but unfortunately I doubt the management could ever get fixed without a complete overhaul.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon has been a lot of fun thus far. It's a Management Simulation game with a story-line (even though I fail regularly at trying to pronounce Spanish words! Eek!) and I couldn't be more thrilled with it.  You start out accepting a job from a mysterious figure who gives you a residence and has you selling "flowers" (opium!) as well as setting up a money-laundering ring. The tutorial is easy to understand without being cumbersome or frustrating to get through, so you feel like you're playing as you're learning instead of waiting to pass a checkpoint. The dialogue is interesting and extremely well written. Plus, the game is absolutely gorgeous! If you're fond of management simulators I would absolutely recommend checking this one out! There looks to be a lot of different zones to explore so I'm enthusiastically looking forward to continuing playing! Thank you so much to Tinybuild and Moon Moose for offering me a key to this wonderful game! This review is an initial reaction from my first bout of game play, so if I have anything to add later, I'll just edit this review. Be well! Enjoy, and keep your enemies at bay <3Edit: I've sunk quite a bit of time into this game this week, failing and restarting.  It is a very hard game to master, but once you do, it's actually really easy to increase your money gain to a point where you cannot launder it fast enough. The trick to the game seems to be to never allow your threat to hit the second star, which is fairly easy to manage if you bide your time and pay off the reporter fast enough (I took to hording money in the actually city so paying her off was a lost faster) Overall, a very fun game once you figure out a way to manage the frustrations (the attention of the police, the second star, makes the game damn near impossible. Let alone when you've got the military blowing up your crops!) The game could definitely use some balancing, but overall, still a very fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: There is some potential here, honestly there is, but the game is pretty frustrating as a "workflow simulator.  This has significant issues with balancing and a poor tutorial that does not teach you how to manage making money correctly in the game. You are frequently attacked by overpowered rival gangs that you have no hope of fighting back. There is no way to permanently reduce your terror stars, creating a game system that is designed for the player to lose. Buildings and lieutenants have prohibitively expensive upkeep costs and lieutenants do not do enough to support gameplay as you often need to simply park them in bases to prevent losing control. Everything is wildly expensive but it takes a stupidly long time to actually launder money with your limited amount of trucks, even with lieutenants who have truck buffs. However, there is no way to know this by playing for less than two hours because the gameplay loop takes so long to understand whether you are doing well or not. The focus of this game is more tycoon/tropico like and less fighting. Taking sites over is just a simple numbers game at the moment. Have one more offence point and you win a fight in the end. Violence begets you a terror rating, get to high and your operations will get seized/closed. So getting 2 aggressive is not a viable option.The tutorial needs some work as many comment it doesnt bring the basics needed to succeed and i agree. Loading my save a few hours or a day later and my issue was fixed or changed.It took me at least 10 hours to get a grasp on things and after that you could clearly see the possibilities for this game. Just go slow, adding 3 dopium farms might sound good but when you can't sell em or repackage em quick enough your full warehouses attract attention and the law will come pay you a visit.You really gotta micro manage your warehouses and transport companies a bit but after that i was making money by the boat loads. (Small Tip: Struggling with the logistics ? Just make small virtual islands for yourself with one type of product chain and dont let them interact with another production 'island' unless you start to get your head around the way warehouses and transport companies works.)One of the cooler things is that you can 'buy' the peoples respect with heavy bonuses by building churches and such. This game has so many cool and new ideas (not all perfect tbh) in my book that it certainly deserves a look when you love the early tropico or similar games.I would like to mention that the soundtrack is a masterpiece , it perfectly fits with the game and has a very relaxing vibe to it.Things i would like to see:Fights just needs more to it then a simple numbers game. Pay off cops, federales to come fight for me or send em after rival gangs.Possibility for blockades so you can stop advancing police or rival gangsNo terror for legal goodsMore things to do with your underlings: Train, fire them, have the possibility to don't die or be arrested, more options in generalBridges or transport boats for logistics.Laundering operations draw attention when the money is full (should be when its over full capacity)The possibility to cancel a move or other order in transit.When underlings are on transport and the site gets attacked they shouldnt die or get arrested as they aint there.A possibility to upgrade all buildings from a type on the map or per province at once. (Later game this get tedious)Why can i build only one building at a time. I' am a business man and time is money.Possibility to 'starve' a rival gang (when taking away everything they own, the strenght should go down sporadicly).There is only one thing i realy don't like and that is the fact that gangs get power when you take over a city. _childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of drug dealer simulator I was really excited to play this game because I got it in a bundle with said game. I was hoping it would be that game but on a larger scale. While this was the case once I finished my first play-through I felt mixed. First I went through 3-4 different games before getting my winning run. It was a fun journey of learning how to use each built and mechanic in this game in order to make tons of money. The learning curve was large but it felt decently manageable. That was until I got to the mid game. Early game is fun. You either are focusing on building up your opium or weed farms along with packaging them with everyday items in order to maximize profit. However once you move onto territory expansion and anything above weed the game kinda starts to fall apart. Territory expansion is done by doing favors for the mayor of a city followed by then taking it over. Some favors are fine like cleaning up gangs and illegal buildings but some require and member in the cartel to have a certain ability which makes the game frustrating. Because they will sometimes request a character to kidnap someone or kill your own members. The main issue I have is that there is no hostile take over mechanic. Which I would love cause I spent about 1-2 hours leveling up a guy just to get one skill only to find out that I can't promote him because the hierarchy is too limited. You can only have 14 members in your gang but the problem is that 5 are only useful for deliveries, 4 are have one sort of good skill, and the other 5 are best used in micro managing. I get why the tree is so small but it makes the game feel too slow and puts you into holes where you have your whole gang set up but because no one can kidnap you have to remake the gang. Now granted there is a starter character with those skills but I don't want to pick a Capo based off the convince of the game I never played before. It show be based of what I think would be interesting for the gameplay style I want. But at least there's a building who give people who can do that without taking up a slot. But remember that's very important for the next thing that makes the game fall apart. Every drug above weed. The first two drugs aren't that bad they are cheap to sell cheap to make. But that's not going fast enough I need some coke. Coke started off fine but the value of it is so high that when you start getting boxes filled with the stuff you get tons of dirty money. Too much. Laundering is not fun in this game. The best building is the bank which does and average of 3,000$ a day and each city can only have one with early game opium and weed it's not that bad heck even if you send it out in packages it still covers it but everything above that makes so much money the bank can't launder it quick enough. After a week of coke production I maxed out my bank. So I built a casino which does I think 300-500 less. Filled it up. At that point your only choice is the cache which has money go rotten if in the cache for too long. It feels like a tycoon game that punishes making money. But you can micromanage but the reason I bought this game was to make a big auto Cartel. Final point I have is gang leaders. There are two ways to deal with them kill them or hire them. Do not hire them. It is way easier to kill leaders than hire because hire requires full respect from them which you get a small amount of every 15-30 minutes which is too long. Overall it had a fun start but sorta got confusing and stressful near the end. I do not intend on playing this game again for a little while because the amount of prep I didn't know but expected to have was too much and slowed the game down. It is not worth the 30$ price but it is worth the on sale price of 10-12$. I don't have any plans to buy the dlcs

_childDocuments_.review: Aug 3, 2022 EDIT: This game is getting way too many downvotes from clueless people. I see people complaining about certain things but they just simply don't understand how to play the game, so they think the game isn't working right. There are several QOL issues in the game, but many things aren't broken so much as unclear -- everything in easily manageable as long as you know what you are doing. There is negligible tedium.This game has a number of very well-thought-out touches that impress me and catch me off-guard. For example, I found the terror system too forgiving. I wanted it to punish me more. Well, the sandbox mode lets you adjust all sorts of things like that. I set terror to 250% normal, and wow, it's pretty close to the experience I wanted!Then I started feeling like it was too easy to smuggle things hidden in vegetables. After a few months of this in-game, I was so impressed to find that the authorities had started suspecting my vegetable shipments! Especially with 250% terror, this was strongly encouraging me to change up my operation and use something other than vegetables to hide things. Not only that, a few months later after I had pissed everyone off up to the CIA, they started outright confiscating any vegetable shipments I tried to send through a particular smuggling point. So cool! I was very happy to be placed under this kind of pressure.So many little touches like this really make this satisfying to play. ***The Story Mode is buggy, confusing, and terrible. You will be subjected to all manner of nonsensical twists - for example, you'll read a confusing story about your lieutenant shooting the mayor because he's aligned with the Guerrilla faction. It doesn't say which lieutenant it is. Then your leader executes the lieutenant. Once gameplay resumes, you are given the mission of executing ANY lieutenant. The reason? Because they're aligned with the Guerrillas. So you're given the story before the event happens, which is confusing. Then you're told to kill literally anyone, just because. And then whoever you kill, it's justified, because they were aligned with the Guerrillas. Huh?Anyway, the Survival Mode is great. This game needs a strong UI and QOL pass on certain things, e.g. you should be able to set sell priorities at your smuggling points and you should be able to set the storage of your laundering sites below max if you don't want them hog all your liquidity (i.e. you need some funds outside of the laundering circuit to fund upkeep and construction).Overall, a great game and deserving of a high rating. I trust they will polish in time, and I'd love a DLC or anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game so far is a very enjoyable management sim game. It's very relaxing and steady until the federales raid your farm and everything crumbles in front of you. The roads can be a bit finnicky.The UI, which is hugely important for this type of game, is mostly very good, though there is some info that would be nice to have, like daily financial info, rather than weekly and monthly, and maybe a screen that shows where all the storage is. These things could possible already be in the game and I just missed them, it took me over 3 in game hours to see where all Lieutenants are listed.The narrative in the story mode was surprisingly compelling to me. Might not win an oscar, but it is definitely a good driving force for the tutorial and quests.I've played 5 hours as of now, and I still feel like I have plenty of game left. And it seems like it would be a good replayable game as well.Definitely worth picking up if anything I mention interests you. If the devs add more to the game in the future, then that would make it an even better game to pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played cartel tycoon since the beginning. The game is in a much better state than it was on release and therefore I am very proud and grateful, as the game definitely has something to it. I find true enjoyment in the challenge that the game provides with certain mode and starting point combinations. When the numbers just keep creeping higher and higher and you've nailed the entire production to launder ration without anything overflowing, it is truly satisfying.My strategy before the fight and stash update mainly focused on getting my lieutenants as powerful as possible as early as possible and going to war on absolutely everyone, relentlessly fighting to erase all enemy gangs. With the addition of weapons and lieutenant stamina, taking a city by force has become much less attractive. My strategy totally changed. I only use weapons and lieutenants for defence and possibly for taking a building or two with valuable resources in it, otherwise it is much simpler to just burn the enemy buildings. I now make friends with rival gang leaders and then recruit them. I finished survival mode without any real trouble without having a single war. I find this ironic, as the fight and stash update was aimed at improving combat, it achieved the exact opposite. Attacking rival cities with the intent to eliminate the gang is a very bad decision. 30+ Power difference, 80+ weapons and still my lieutenants run out of stamina before the end of the war.... Seems stupid. All in all I am happy with the fight and stash update, as it opened a completely different strategy. I now see enemy gang leaders as recruit-able lieutenants and use this as a strategic element to gain an advantage or a needed lieutenant ability. I enjoy Cartel Tycoon immensely and I will continue to do so, as I wish to 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR : Great Graphic, Great Music, Terrible Balance.the game is what you expect.. a great drug lord management sim, with great graphics, nice GUI and nice music.but that is where my praise ends.At the current state of the game, i couldn't recommend the game yet.the game is ridiculously hard. definitely not for casuals.Levelling up your liuetenant raises their salary to a significant amount.plus, there are finite number of people you can hirebut you still need people to guard your aerodrome/seaport as well as cities you own.there are 3 levels of drug (opium, cannabis and cocaine) you can sell, but to sell the 2nd and 3rd level of drug you will need significant amount of money to research the buildings needed to grow and process those drugs.In addition, the penalty of getting your heat is very highDEA keep preventing you to export your goodsPolice will seize your building if you store too much productand to reduce the heat is very costly.you need to a lot of money to reduce it.So what will happen in most games is that you need to really build your empire slowlyotherwise you'll end up unable to pay your lieutenantsor getting raided/investigated by policeor both.Oh in addition, you don't wan't to get you Capo @ your main character killed.the game does continue as such that one of your successor became the next Capobut the penalty is too greatyour buildings get seizedyou lost your friendship with cities you already ownedyou might as well restart your game.In short, you better watch how the developers play the game to get the optimal build orderor your drug empire will crumble.Oh, and did I tell you that there is no manual save?There is no manual save.The game auto saves on exit.if you f'd up, then you might as well restart your game.It feels like They Are Billions all over again.So, that is what i feel about the game at the moment.note that the game is still in early access, and the developers may not yet get the balance right yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those cases where I wish Steam had a NEUTRAL rating. I neither hate nor am fond of this game. I've played business sims for years now. I'm a master exploiter. Once I learn how a game works I can take it to the extreme, such as the great fun I used to have in the original Sim City of increasing the taxes to a ridiculous rate to get sick amounts of money, and then dropping it to get everyone to come back. As such, Cartel Tycoon is another game like that. If you've played them, you get it, and there's absolutely nothing new here. The only difference is that you've got a filthier theme and it's well-researched. 1980s narco trade in South America? Cool. But mechanically speaking if you're used to business sims you'll fly through it and I noticed a few bugs. In particular, transportation of goods is at times ineffective and outright broken. Playing through some earlier parts of the tutorial, in fact, revealed this strange issue where properly set up resources and pathways still yielded none of the requested results in spite of following things to a T. Those are easy fixes, however, the main issue is, if you're into these kinds of games, is it worth it? Honestly for a little, maybe, but since it's built on practically every tycoon game before it the kinds of people who'd even want to check it out will likely be disappointed in the long run. Thus, again, I wish I could give a NEUTRAL rating to this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review after Goals & Gains update: Still can't recommend this game. The new update improves things a little, however the biggest problem is still there - this is a logistics management game that doesn't let you manage your logistics. Compare it to something like Anno, where you have control over your entire production chain - how much to produce, where and how much to store, trade volume etc. In Cartel Tycoon you make the supply chain and then let it run itself for a while, until one of your storage units fills up, gets seized by the police which causes a disruption for a while. Then you wait or pay them off and rinse and repeat again.Now, I'm not against the police mechanic. You need something in the game to create difficulty for the player. But sacrificing a lot of the management aspects of a strategy game just for this one mechanic seems kind of a lazy solution to me. I really want to like this game, it has a lot of good ideas and nice art design, but I just can't recommend it at full price. Maybe at half the price it's worth a try for a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: [Based on Early Access]So I caved and got a game in its Alpha stage since it seemed that good development was put in from the get go. _childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon – The fix you have been looking for, or a bad trip?Cartel Tycoon sees you play the part of an up and coming Capo in a fictional South American Isle. Your goal, as the name suggests, is to build a thriving cartel while avoiding all the pitfalls that come along with the territory. The game begins with your character, low on funds and down on his luck, answering an ad for a business partner in a newspaper classified ad. A conversation follows that sees you partner with a mysterious individual in the flower selling business. How are your opium poppy growing skills?As with many tycoon/city builder type games, you begin with some start up capital which you need to invest. Buy some poppy farms and warehouses to store your product, set up local businesses to launder your ill gotten gains and bribe local officials for a smoother ride. Hire some lieutenants to protect your assets, deliver your shipments and help you expand your empire. All of the tropes that you would expect in this setting are present, and for better or worse there are no surprises in terms of the cast of characters and the plot. The graphics of the game are simple but good and I really enjoyed the hand drawn art style of the cut scenes, I just wish there were more of them. Most of the dialogue and story progression is in the form of text boxed telephone conversations, which after the introductory artwork was a bit disappointing.  In the game’s story mode you are led through some simple beginning missions to learn the various mechanics of the game and build the narrative and it was here that the game fell a bit short for me. The pacing of the early missions seemed a little slow and I felt like I spent too much time waiting for things to happen and accumulating resources/money. Whilst that is inevitable for this kind of game I wanted a faster pace in the beginning to hold my interest and get the hooks in and it just wasn’t there.It is worth noting that this game is in early access and is very polished given that fact. If you are a fan of the tycoon style games and like the idea of your own drug empire with none of the risk, then this is a very solid foundation to build from and is likely only to improve from here. That being said, if you are looking for something new and innovative perhaps this isn’t the game for you, at least right now. The storyline and mechanics bring nothing new to the table and whilst both work well and are entertaining enough, nothing stands out. There are quite a few features and mechanics that are in the roadmap for future updates and hopefully these will bring the variety and depth that this game needs to take it to the next level.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me be clear up front: if you can't tolerate Early Access titles that have a lot of problems, don't bother picking this up yet. The "rough edges" on this thing are like sandpaper. I'm not going to go through an exhaustive list of every awkward UI element or frustrating oversight in the game's mechanics, but buyer beware: there are many, and they need to be fixed.That being said, I had a ton of fun playing this and I'll certainly be back for more. This game is more than just another tycoon/management game with a pallet swap and a new aesthetic, this thing turns many of your tycoon-citybuilder-management-sim-whatever expectations on their heads to give you a genuinely new experience.For starters, unlike most tycoon games, where the key to success is maximizing the production of every building and pushing as much product out as possible while stocking all of your storage facilities to max, you can't do that here. You'll lose, and fast. Overproducing not only causes resources to be wasted, it attracts the attention of law enforcement. Any building that stocks an illegal substance to its max value has a risk of being raided, and your distribution points (seaports, airports, and border checkpoints) have limits on how much product you can safely move through them. You need to carefully  production, pushing it as high as you can [/i]safely[/i] get it, while making sure your warehouses never accumulate a surplus. Sometimes you may even need to burn a building down and run, so the less you have in there, the better. The key is to build light and safe, instead of big, and that's an interesting difference from most games in this genre.Secondly, you cannot (and  not) over-expand. To gain territory, you have to fight rival gangs for it, and this will quickly get the attention of higher tiers of law enforcement (think: GTA). To get around this, you have to think about what you can get with the least amount of work and what you can do with it; consider the tradeoffs of bribing officials to use a city without taking control of it, or hide contraband inside legal goods to pass them through rival territory unnoticed.And finally, the dirty-money/clean-money dynamic is pretty cool. You can pay for anything with either  money (in the bank, works electronically, and doesn't require an infrastructure to use) or  money, which you hide on your private property and, because it is cash-only, has to be physically moved from location to location by gang members. Dirty money is easy to get (you get it from all drug sales), but cant be moved through rival gang territory or through government checkpoints without paying a portion in bribes.To get clean money, you have to launder your dirty money, either by funneling it into service industries (taxicabs, churches, amusement parks) to create legal cover for its existence, or by calling in favors from politicians and paying them under the table at a premium. You can then use the clean cash to pay for legal services or support buildings without plugging them into your network. But you can avoid doing this if you are able to establish efficient delivery lanes from your sell-points to the locations where you want to pay your employees in cash, but remember that storing too much means it could get lost or trigger a police raid.Everything in this game is a balancing act, and that's what sets it apart from other tycoon games. The trademark of a lazy management game is the ability of the player to simply make more of everything and brute force their way through the story. Here, subtlety is a large part of the strategy and it gives the game that extra edge that it needs to really shine.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a year since someone cared about this game. There is much focus on automating actions, yet automated actions rarely end up in an automated supply chain. For instance: imagine the game told you that these farms, over here, produced X product per time period, and these factories consumed X product per time period, and these outputs consumed X product per hour. It would be really easy to figure out what to do in this game. Imagine you are a game dev. Imagine that you realize that you can't really find a mechanic to keep people interested, because once they know it takes 8 product per hour, reaching this delivery mechanism, to turn a meaningless infinite profit for whatever time period, they lose interest. Nothing about this game will ever maintain interest, beyond "Can I max out the skills?" or "How much many can I actually make before the counter overflows?" Nothing really matters, and that's why this game doesn't matter...

_childDocuments_.review: This is an early access version of a game called Cartel Tycoon. The name basically already explains what it's all about. It's basically a new city builder/strategy game with a rather "illegal" setting as you're the Boss of a cartel and with diplomatic and violent ideas you're basically trying to grow your organization. Keep in mind that Cartel Tycoon is currently in Early Access and available in the Steam store and available with its own unique TinyBuild launcher. The game was developed by Moon Moose and published by Release Date: 18th March 2021 (Early Access).Last known update: 10th April 2021.As mentioned RTS games aren't really my cup of coffee which means that I usually try to avoid them. But with this game, I had a sudden urge to play it, probably because I watched the entire Narcos series in one day and wanted to see how good of a drug lord I would be if I decided to lead a cartel. Jokes aside, this game looks and plays very nicely despite it still being in Early Access. It offers cutscenes with a protagonist and a pretty lengthy campaign as far as I could tell. Let's take a better look!Compared to the previous build of the game that I reviewed some months ago the developers did a fantastic job at making the tutorial a lot more helpful. Now you get a dedicated taskbar and a guide that explains everything in detail. Another addition was the fact that now you can hire lieutenants that can actually help out in various activities such as transporting goods, perhaps have a 20% income boost for a limited time or be able to make a robbery. All of these additions really made the game a lot more understandable and do-able.The map is divided into many cities and each city does have a Mayor/ Leader. Your main goal is to earn their respect by doing various tasks that will be presented on your lower left side of your screen. Lastly, I should note that violence isn't really the main theme of the game. It does not glorify the violent aspect of that lifestyle. Obviously, you do have some options. You can send a specialized member of your cartel to burn some buildings from the other cartels, you can even command another one of your members to assassinate an enemy. These are the main options when it comes to violence. The developers added gang wars that would activate once you have left one of your cities or buildings for a long time. You can capture it back if you got enough firepower which is why you should invest in some powerful lieutenants. One last occasion of violence occurs when you're out of legal money which means that you cannot pay anything. The result comes with the game over screen where the game explains that you tried to flee the country but got shot close to the border. The statistical aspects of the game are definitely the strong point of the game. I really loved the multiple options when it comes to illegal money laundry. There are quite a lot of buildings that do get the job done, going from placebo Taxi offices to Jewelry stores or even Circuses.  To go from raw product to legal cash is a long journey. First up you have to grow raw product on a farm (Opium), then a warehouse takes the Opium and stores it. If a lab is within reach the warehouse will then bring the Opium to the Airfield or Seaport. You can then theoretically ship it via plane or ship but the D.E.A might be sniffing around and investigate which will force you to stop using these buildings for some days. So then you have to hide the product somewhere between vegetables, coffee, or spices which I do consider a very deep and interesting aspect of the game. Basically hiding a small number of drugs in a box with coffee and smart things like that. These act as storage multipliers with a specific amount of available units respectively. After finishing a tour the drug money will be stored at the airport, harbor, or border post. After accomplishing all of that you can start with the entire "money-laundry" labour. Then it is yours to do with as you please. Keep in mind that in each area you do get highlighted efficiency areas and combined with the efficiency ratings from the buildings you can achieve a pretty tactical system of production. Once again the addition of gang wars and robberies will benefit the player a lot but what I really liked was the fact that you can speak to the lawyer of the city and ask for some help which can be about D.E.A confiscations, Loyalty, or even ask for a sum of money if you’re in deep trouble. SPOILERS AHEAD!You are a man called Cesar Garcetti and you have ended up in a city. You wander around and decide to call for a job. A mysterious voice starts speaking. After some jokes and business discussion, the mysterious man hands you the keys to start working with some plantations. After you have proven yourself worthy the mysterious man visits you. His name is Miguel Angel Gacha and he is basically one of your friends and the man that gave you a future as well as being your mentor. The game does not offer much of a traditional story but more so it tells a story with small discussion while talking about various events.These are the only things that occur. Everything else just feels like a sandbox RTS game and I am totally fine with that. Your goal is basically to become the strongest cartel in the country, simple as that.Keep in mind that the developers added some pretty nice cutscenes. I have to say that they really fletched out the story a lot more.The Visuals aren't anything new. It looks like a traditional RTS/City building game. On the contrary, it does look like a nice and tropical Latin country. The tutorial got much more user-friendly compared to the previous version I reviewed some months ago. The story feels a lot more imaginable than before where the entire storyline was structured around speech bubbles and text. Overall I can only give this game a very good rating, especially for Narcos and City Builder fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not normally do reviews, but I felt this particular game deserves one. I have been playing this game for a while now to include repeated hours from the demo that came out for free, lol.
