Example, I never really relied on residences because the function to provide dirty money to every facility within range was not working properly, now it is. Also residences now seem to know when to stop collecting dirty money once its storage is full, that was quite annoying especially if it caused attracting the attention of law enforcement every single time. There are a few things I would like to see and hope that they can consider it. First off I like that you cannot just simply afk and make tons of money, I was angry at first cause it seemed like it was cool I can go to bed and wake up in the morning to find i have millions of dirty money and a few hundred thousand clean money. Nope, game pauses cause some cartel member wants a raise or promotion so that scratched that. While the game is called Cartel Tycoon, I still do not get the feeling I am in a cartel or at least running one. We have a nice Cartel family tree so to speak, but it's quite limited. As you progress and eventually have a money making system in place, you really do not need members who have money making skills, what you really need is members in your cartel with more combat or attack points. I have been trying to figure out how to keep myself from getting any terror stars, but every time I've attacked a city controlled by a rival gang it takes so long to take over that I always seem to get that first star. I have tried every trick i can think of, I've even hired several members just to have that extra fire power. You would think odds of 26 cartel vs 6 enemy gang would mean I should win relatively quickly, however that was not the case. Every city, and transportation point needs to have an officer stationed there or else it generates a meter indicating a rival gang member will attack it. This makes good sense, but again we are limited to members of our cartel. I do not feel at this time we have enough to cover the map, and as I already set as an example with combat, try taking over the map with less attack power because you need to keep people in place. I hope they will implement the ability to recruit not just officers, but perhaps troops or guards for each area. I know this is just a game, but when I see shows like Narcos on Netflix lol, those guys had some serious hired man power. Each lab, building, and residences all had guards. This would help alleviate the need to leave officers behind, and also add more reason to make all that dirty money and clean money. I wanted to hire guards.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has issues in it's current state. It's tutorial is good at teaching you the basics of the game. The concept of the game is amazing, and it's gameplay has a great amount of promise. But the problem is, the tutorial is only good at teaching you the basics of the game. The concept is amazing, and the gamplay has promise. Let me explain.The tutorial gives you a good platform at the beginning, but you hit a brick wall around the 1.5 hour mark when stuff starts going wrong (I'll get to that later), and the tutorial has already passed. You see that your farms aren't doing anything, suddenly everything is falling apart because you built another building, and the logistics system just can't handle it. You don't know what to do other than demolish the building, and take a loss. It's frustratingly annoying and just doesn't work.The gameplay needs to be worked out. There are major balancing issues and issues relating to logistics that need to be worked out before this is a 25$ game. The once you get to the Police stage in the terror counter, you have entered a whole new world of hurt. If you don't want your stuff seized for 20 days you better hope you have a lot of people with a lot of power. The CIA holds true to what it's known for in blowing up everything it doesn't like, except instead of blowing up communism, it's blowing up your drug empire. Logistics in the story mode makes me want to pull my hair out. Luckily I won't need to due to my hair falling out naturally due to stress after trying to manage the logistical system. You'll suddenly find that your buildings no longer work for some reason you don't know about. You can't fix it. You can only hope that it stops before your people get disloyal and the DEA, Police, and Federales shut down all your stuff. I can't recommend buying it now, but if the developers continue to work on the game and implement community feedback, this is a game that would definitely be worth spending money on. Thank you for coming to my ted talk.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVE the music in this game!!- have it running to listen to the music while I write this review.I'm not really sure where to start other than it needs a lot of polish. I will just start by saying the price is a bit higher than it should be for what it is currently offering, but that's how EA works. You may want to wait on a sale to purchase, unless you are like me and buy in because you like the idea and want to help support a company develop a new game. That said, I will just kind of touch on a few things I found annoying and limited my play time. I am not saying these things should change for sure, just saying these things made the game less enjoyable for me, and they may have reasons I didn't pick up on for being the way they are...-Paying employee- I like the choice of dirty or clean money, and especially product in a pinch, but I feel like they want money far to often. Since you probably need them moving something around, or at a place that doesn't have dirty money sitting around, they likely need to use clean money to be able to get paid while doing tasks. I like the system overall but it was to demanding to pay 8 employees or so anything other than clean money, unless they were sitting in town basically.-Building in towns- I feel like there probably should be more than 1 of each type per city, and more buildings per city. Some small balance there, to make it more enjoyable and feel more custom, and less limited. Just some tweaks to make it a bit more involved or something.-Micro managing of deliveries, especially money- This happened to me early, that I was not able to have enough people carrying enough money from my seaport to the town. Especially then from that town to the next one over, both of which have airports. (that cannot move money) That seems like a good option in my opinion, that if you have a port in each region, you should be able to move money easily between them. Or just let people carry more? Not sure how to tweak this without running into the next issue.-Money Management- I liked the problem of needing to launder the money. I just didn't feel like it was moving around as much as I would like, say, to fund the development of another region. It just takes far to long for employees to move money 8 or 12 thousand dollars at a time. Possibly the solution I present above for the previous problem solves this? Overall it feels like this game is promising, but has a lot of overall balance work needed. Which from the frequent update pace it looks like they are working hard on. Hopefully they have a good community and keep getting the feedback they need to find that balance of new/familiar and fun/challenging/rewarding. Overall happy with the purchase if nothing else for the music!! Hats off to the composers, the yes recommendation is for them.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon offers an engaging gameplay experience, particularly in Sandbox mode, but it falls short in a few key areas. While the game itself is enjoyable, the story mode fails to capture the same level of interest. Having played through the tutorial and a portion of the story mode, I found it lackluster and not compelling enough to continue.Sandbox mode is where the game shines, providing the freedom to build and manage without the constraints of a storyline. However, a significant drawback is that not all features are unlocked from the start. In particular, the restriction on Cartel leaders and emblems is frustrating. For a mode meant to offer unrestricted play, having these elements locked behind progress feels counterintuitive.While I understand the intention of encouraging players to achieve milestones, this design choice detracts from the Sandbox experience. It reminds me of back in the early days of PlayStation Network on PS3, where the focus on grinding for achievements often overshadowed the enjoyment of the game itself. Despite these issues, I still HIGHLY recommend Cartel Tycoon, but it's important to be aware of these limitations.

_childDocuments_.review: ProsThe production of both legal and illegal goods is handled pretty well and having to manage your heat levels adds an extra challenge that other more traditional management sims do not.  The handling of clean and dirty money is also a new element to be mindful of and admittedly, took a bit of time to understand completely.  ConsYour lietenants constantly need to be paid more, which can be difficult when you can lose large parts of your business empire due to losing your boss to death/prison.  You also risk losing your smuggling sites and cities to enemy gangs with no way to guard against them at checkpoints.  Between the limited amount of hired hands you can retain at one time and the ever-increasing expense of their wages, your empire will be prevented from growing beyond a set size.  Compounding this issue is that your pool of hireable talent has no method to reject candidates you don't want.  While you can find people who will work for free or very cheap, you are often limited to choosing between 3 people who start out wanting higher wages.  Managing heat and threat levels needs a tweak imo as at current, once you attain a threat level like DEA or Police investigation, there is no method to permanently remove them except one which is both destructive to your empire in terms of lost businesses and zones and loss of personnel.  There is a mayoral favor you can do, but while it costs a lot, only results in a temporary reprieve of one threat.  Money laundering businesses need to have a setting to restart once they have been replenished with dirty money.  Recommendation to buy if you enjoy management sims and want something a little different from the usual business types, with the caveat that it is still in early access and could benefit from some QoL improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: This game and I have been on one hell of a journey. I played it for my channel and was completely lost at first. I'm not the best at following directions, but this game really felt like it left so much out of the tutorial that I had trouble grasping how everything worked. It took a few restarts before I started to understand the respect and law enforcement systems and how to balance everything. I tend to hurry through tutorials to "get to the real game" but here the tutorial is NOT meant to be finished, it's meant to become the basis for your future operation so take it VERY slow and hold off on completing objectives like a jackrabbit. Once you actually have a handle on how the game works, it's awesome. The learning curve though is STEEP. Maybe this is an ADHD brain issue and an issue with my play style being very brutish, but this isn't about going in fast and hard. Slow and steady wins this race. This game may not be for everyone, but it's become one of those I can't stop playing. There's a lot coming in the future as you can see from the developer's website, but even in it's current state it scratches the itch in my brain just enough to keep me coming back. I'm motivated by the money, but find myself constantly battling over the balance of dirty to legal - something that I actually like but may frustrate others. It's not an easy game to play and it's not quite as accessible as other games with the "tycoon" label, but this is a drug operation, son. Did you think things were gonna be easy? Overall I highly recommend this if you like complex games where you may have to restart multiple times. This is about getting it right and sometimes playing the hand you've been dealt ISN'T the right way to handle things. I suspect there will be many people who don't recommend this game because the learning curve at present (4/4/21) is VERY steep for some.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like the game more than I do, there is potential here but the game is marred by balance problems and strange design choices that just leave the game feeling too frustrating and chaotic to be enjoyable for extended periods of time.The game play feels far less like slowly building and expanding your empire, and more more like a messy juggling act where every step forward throws another ball in the mix and if you drop 1 ball everything comes crashing down instantly.Between mini quests, gang attacks, federal raids, stock control etc there is far too much micro to get anything useful done. There's always some more pop ups or events coming to ruin your day, or you know just prod you a bit while you're busy trying to do other things.If you try to do pretty much anything meaningful, the terror will rise to the point the feds will sporadically shut down your assets meaning you have to go through things 1by1 to shut them down so you don't create MORE terror from having full warehouses then switch them back on again when things calm down.The more you build and expand the more this happens meaning it's far easier and more manageable to have 1 small but efficient and high tech production line. Having multiple lines and export points etc very quickly becomes unmanageable due to the sheer amount of manual inputs and micro managing required for each one.So with this in mind you spend a couple of hours managing and researching this, set it up and... then what? You've got more money than you need, everything you need researched and things aren't rapidly collapsing on top of you due to your very small size. So why scale up? It only brings more problems and issues that usually mean you make less money, lose gang members, raise terror and have police on your back etc. It's way more efficient, safer, easier and usually more profitable to stay small. Even if you did choose to grow, there's nothing to spend the extra money on.There is 0 point to expansion and way to much micro management to make expansion fun on it's own. The game is essentially won or lost in the first few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆Cartel Tycoon, an indie strategy game that puts players in the shoes of a drug cartel leader, presents an intriguing concept with the potential for an engaging and immersive experience. While the game has its strengths, it falls short in certain areas, leaving room for improvement.One of the standout features of Cartel Tycoon is its unique setting and theme. The game dives into the dark and dangerous world of drug cartels, offering a different perspective and a departure from typical strategy game themes. Managing resources, expanding territory, and making strategic decisions to maintain control of the drug trade provide a sense of intrigue and challenge.The game's visual style and atmosphere contribute to its immersion. The hand-drawn graphics and vibrant colors create a distinctive aesthetic that captures the essence of the game's setting. The soundtrack adds to the overall ambiance, enhancing the sense of being a powerful cartel leader.Cartel Tycoon's gameplay mechanics provide a decent level of depth and strategy. Balancing production, distribution, and security while navigating the challenges of rival cartels and law enforcement can be engaging. The progression system, with its unlocks and upgrades, offers a sense of growth and advancement as players build their criminal empire.However, Cartel Tycoon is not without its flaws. The game's tutorial and learning curve can be overwhelming for newcomers to the genre or those unfamiliar with similar management-style games. The lack of clarity in explaining mechanics and objectives can lead to confusion and frustration early on.Furthermore, Cartel Tycoon suffers from repetitive gameplay and a lack of variety. Once players grasp the core mechanics, the gameplay loop becomes predictable and monotonous. The lack of diversity in mission types, events, and challenges hampers long-term engagement and can result in a feeling of stagnation.The AI in Cartel Tycoon is also lacking in depth and intelligence. The rival cartels and law enforcement agencies often exhibit predictable behavior, making encounters and interactions less dynamic and strategic than they could be. Additionally, the pathfinding and AI behavior for workers and vehicles can be inconsistent and frustrating, affecting the overall flow and efficiency of gameplay.In summary, Cartel Tycoon offers an intriguing concept and visual style that immerses players in the world of drug cartels. The gameplay mechanics and progression system provide moments of strategic satisfaction. However, the game's steep learning curve, repetitive gameplay, lack of variety, and AI shortcomings detract from its potential. With improvements in tutorials, gameplay diversity, AI behavior, and overall polish, Cartel Tycoon could become a more engaging and immersive experience. As it stands, the game appeals primarily to players with a specific interest in the theme and genre, but may leave others seeking a deeper and more varied gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all - after playing for several hours I can say that game is already fun in the state it is even though it still has quite a lot of rough edges this early into early access.   The theme is intriguing and is beautifully reinforced by visual style, music and gameplay mechanics. The main gameplay loop of juggling trying ot get enough profits/launder enough money while still trying to lay low to not attract too much attention of the law is quite engaging. Playing cat and mouse with the law is fun and already allows for some deep strategizing and I think it can be expanded a lot upon to make a system really deep and interesting. The difficulty can be quite ruthless - your cartel getting just a little bit too much infamy can snowball really quick to armies blocading cities and rival gangs attacking you left and right all culminating in assassination of your cartel leader. This is not a game over here though - new leader can be chosen and empire rebuilt anew. It is painful anyway! This is rather unusual for a tycoon game in my experience but it keeps you on your toes and plays nicely into the whole theme of dangerous and ugly cartel buisness.Now regarding the current problems of the game.  My main complaint is that after several hours I did manage to figure out that the 'slow and steady' approach is really efficient here. Just waiting and reducing terror to zero after a while allows to proceed with expansion harmlessly for quite some time. Just repeat when terror grows close to a dangerous level again. The main problem here is that the game does punish you for being too confident so player naturaly starts gravitating to very passive playstyle. And with nothing pushing player into action the game loses much of the thrill of cartel-law cat and mouse game - which is the most fun part.  The other problem I want to highlight is apparent uselessness of leutenant. Or rather as the game progresses and your territory grows their only use becomes to sit on the points of interests like ports (which get attacked and captured if no leutenants are present) only asking for money from time to time and being generally annoying. It feels to me they can be so much more than a rather forced limiter on your drug empire growth.  Other reviewers highlighted incomplete tutorials and overall vagueness of the game regarding your goals or means - this is true even though I did enjoy to a degree puzzling out the way everything works myself. I just hope this will get resolved over early access period.  There are also some usual early access issues like placeholder or nonsense dialog here and there disabled objects and so on - these I hope will also get resolved.In conclusion: despite some problems the game is fun and has a lot of potential to get much better.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a bit of a mixed bag at the moment. It's definitely enjoyable setting up a successful production and smuggling operation but it's probably a bit too easy at the moment.Yes, when you have earned the attention of the various law enforcement departments then you are in for a rough ride, but once you know that, it's relatively easy to keep your terror rating low and never get to that point.Rival cartels and gangs are currently fairly passive (sandbox); they don't seem to expand their operations and very rarely launch any attacks or attempts to take your territory. It's pretty much entirely in your hands when you decide to steamroll everyone and own every region.The other funny thing is what to do with all your money. At one point i had millions of dollars, nothing to spend it on and was struggling to find places to store it.I know the developers have a fair bit of content coming, so I'm sure the challenge side will be addressed. Would also be good to have more options to spend money on, like weapons for your lieutenants or a luxury mansion we can waste money on.Summary:The game is good fun and worth buying, but be prepared for a limited challenge at the moment.

It forces you to expand as quick as possible instead of taking your time building up your empire first before expanding, which if not done properly, screws you over and its just better to restart. Secondly, about half the random events just seem stupid. Example, having the DEA send an audit to one of your LT's seems reasonable. But having a prison on a part of the continent you haven/t even looked at somehow obtain a random LT thats sitting in your residence with the only options other than death arent open cause you havent taken over a prison 3 islands over before the first year is done seems a tad bit extreme. There definitely needs to be a second opinion on the logic of events. Otherwise, game is extremely fun to have on a second monitor while watching a show or movie. _childDocuments_.review: For 10$, it is definitely worth the play, but the sim-city setup is very straight-ward once you figured it out, so the games will trend towards being very boring after the initial 5 hours. Besides that, the AI is rather dumb, especially when it comes to your structures. For example, your warehouse will take all resources and redistribute them even when the secondary modification structure is next to the production structure. (Thank god it delivers automatically within range of ports). It made transport companies somewhat irrelevant unless you are trucking things across regions (which you will not do given how inefficient it is). This means you need multiple warehouses to have the "truck power" to keep things running uninterpreted if you have just 4-6 30% primary structures. There are also other dumb algorithms that they didn't optimized enough, such as dirty money distribution. You will get a concentration of dirty money in a single low "wash" building while the rest higher capacities one starve b/c of initial build order. Enemy AI is essentially retarded, since they will raid your stuff and leave their city undefended, which allows the player to clear out all enemy once you can mass hire ppl or have started with a gang of ppl.Overall I'd say it is about a 5/10 or 6/10, but for 10$ on sale, it is ok-value.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hope that Moon Moose follows up with a sequel to Cartel Tycoon.  There's a lot the game gets right.  The art is excellent, the various capos and gang members are fun and the cartel hierarchy is an interesting concept.However the core gameplay loop just isn't very fun.  The game is a resource management/supply chain management simulator at its heart and while these type of games are literally about moving A and B to C so you can make D and combine that with E and so on - this aspect of Cartel Tycoon is just more tedious than anything and never really works smoothly.It quickly devolves into a mess of inscrutable connections between farms, warehouses, "transport companies", etc and you essentially can never have a "perfect" balance of these things.  Which would be fine, that could be part of the game, but the way things end up breaking seems arbitrary.   For instance, the trucks that pick up and deliver items from your warehouses and onto the next step in the supply chain have to literally go pick up, bring back to the warehouse, then leave again to deliver items to the next building.  And you're watching this going.... OK can we just deliver to the next building directly?   OR why not have trucks picking up and trucks delivering at the same time?Even better - If warehouses could facilitate direct deliveries along the supply chain, and only actively store items when a backlog occurred, I think the game would feel a lot more fluid.As it stands you spend an inordinate amount of time trying to optimize things before basically giving up.The various story campaigns of the game also feel very samey.  You're on the same map (one additional was added with the DLC) and the game essentially cheats to provide a challenge - the police, etc, will spawn out of nowhere even when they shouldn't based on the current "terror level".Also the various dialogues you need to slog through just end up becoming a chore.   Every conversation with another character is this long winded affair that is maybe fun the first time - but these conversations repeat, often.I think the devs maybe focused so much on the "flavor" of the game, the themes etc, that they neglected that games actually need a fun gameplay loop at their heart.  Cartel Tycoon is *almost* there.

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems to be focused on logistics, unfortunately the logistics aspect of the game is one of the worst.  You often find yourself building many warehouses (tasked with collecting items from grows and placing them in a central location and/or delivering them to a production workshop).  However, there is no way to determine which warehouse delivers to what workshop as long as the workshops are in the sphere of influence of the warehouse.  This is fine in the early game but as the game progresses, you need more granular control to determine which warehouse is delivering to specific workshops and which warehouse is collecting items from specific workshops.  So mid-late game you end up having to hire and utilize your lieutenants for remedial jobs.Residences are supposed to help with collecting dirty money from the various seaports, airports, etc into a central location but the dirty money needs to be distributed to various places which have been selected to run off of dirty (rather than legit) money.  But the residences only collect the money from an extremely limited number of export points (because there just isn't a place for many additional export points, nor a need) so the residences are mostly useless since they do not distribute the dirty money.  So again, you're relegated to using high paid LT's to do remedial tasks.The whole logistics aspect of the game is rudimentary and without much intelligence or control making the mid-late game far more complicated than it needs to be.  If the game is focusing heavily on logistics then the entire logistics gameplay needs a serious look and quite possibly an overhaul.At this time, this is merely a fun distraction for about an hour but quickly becomes a frustrating game of destroying and constructing buildings a few millimeters away to attempt to manipulate the rudimentary logistics intelligence.

You'd think that a tycoon game designed around setting up supply lines would have even a modicum of AI when it comes to transporting goods but I swear they are purposefully programmed to be as terrible as possible. All your dirty money gets crammed into the one building to launder it, despite there being 3 available to use, requiring you to micromanaging delivering the money elsewhere. Need two of an item to be delivered to a building to combine into a new item? Watch as all your trucks only deliver a single item there, while all the buildings within range producing the other max out their storage and cause your terror level to rise. Seriously, I watched for 5 minutes as my trucks kept cramming a single item item my workshops, maxing out that storage, the other one completely empty, while all the buildings around them maxed out their storage of the other required item and stopped producing. Either the devs were too stupid to fix these issues, they did not care, or they purposefully did it to artificially jack up the difficulty. Either way, it's pathetic and this game sucks.

The premise is cool. The mechanics are good (though flawed).I can put up with production lines that back up no matter how much I try to make them perfect. I can put up with the fact that, for a reason I can't fathom, T2 raw materials keep ending up in the transport depot when there is still plenty of room in the target production structure to store them. I can tolerate the glitchy tool tips - the ones that show your building as without a road connection when it clearly has one or shows them your casino as out of money when you just dumped 20K into it. I can accept the under explained mechanics; managing your lieutenants' allegiance isn't a hassle once you figure it out, but it's not clear at all what makes them tick.I can accept all of that (and have, clearly - just look at my hours). What I can't accept is getting to the end of a very long quest chain and having poor writing, scripting, and coding waste my valuable time and leave me frustrated and annoyed. This is the opposite feeling I'm supposed to have when playing a game.The quest required me to defeat the national army in an engagement with assistance from a faction and a specific lieutenant. Rather than making the event scripted, however - which would mean that it happens as soon as I have the allegiance of the faction and the lieutenant available - the game decides that I have to "activate" the army on the terror scale. So in order to get the army's attention, I have to piss them off by terrorizing the citizenry. It doesn't "tell" me this, mind you - it took a little while before I realized that I hadn't missed some cue or something that would activate the next quest phase.Ok, fine. Laborious, but fine. But here's the thing - when the army gets "activated," they go wherever they want to go. They can go into an enemy gang's territory, which is no bueno because I can't fight a gang and the army. They could go on one end of the map or the other. And they come out in a flurry of government activity - you'll be looking around trying to figure out - are those cop cars, DEA cars, or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ army hummers coming my way?So here I am chasing the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ army across the map. I've gathered all my lieutenants and I'm literally reactivating the star over and over again to try and get the army to go somewhere where I can 1.) fight it and 2.) get to it in time before it leaves. After the third try, I realized that this is stupid. This entire issue could've been avoided by making the event scripted.I still don't know if I'll even bother trying to play it again. It is possible that I've misunderstood the quest - but as I don't think I'm a stupid person (har har), I'll assume that I haven't and that if I have, it's because the game has been unclear, which is a problem all its own.Lots to love here, but I'm not going to reward what I consider to be poor design with a positive review. If you are reading this and you are asking, "Well, is it fun?" Yes, it is fun. You will get your time out of it, even if you buy it for full price.But I'm not going to recommend a game whose mechanics are wasting my time - whether by poor design or negligence or both.

_childDocuments_.review: The most vital part of your empire, transportation of cash and product, or in other words the very life blood of your organization, has a complete mind of its own and you'll find yourself more at odds with the pathing system and resource management than you will any actual physical or political threat the game can give you.I only have 12 hours on record and I've already lost count of the number of times I've placed roads my trucks seem to never use or connected buildings to pathways and main roads that still give me a big red warning of being "not connected to roads".. a warning that never seems to mean much considered the trucks ignore it anyway.The game was designed with complex resource management in mind, which would be fine normally speaking, but the game never can seem to decide between giving you the overwhelming task of handling everything or automating most of it itself, so instead it runs on this strange, unwieldy hybrid system that allows you to build roads and tell which buildings you want your transport trucks to service, but never which trucks, where, in what order, or what products you want them to take to each location... the game decides to do all that for you, and its never very good at it. In fact, I would even say its absymal at judging what resources I want where.For example, to sell certain products through certain ports you need to disguise the product with a workshop, a building unit that will take two resources and turn it into one that can be smuggled through a port for lots of cash. My workshop was next to mainly vegetable farms and a warehouse full of them, and across the way in another territory I had a larger plantation with an attached warehouse overfilled with 200/200 flowers. My workshop has stalled production because it lacks the flowers to make the disguised product, so you'd think the logical conclusion to be drawn by my transport company once I connected it from the warehouse with flowers to the warehouse with veggies would be to bring the flowers from the other territory close to the warehouse attached to my workshop so production can resume...... that is not at all what happened. Instead, I watched for 20 minutes at max game speed while each of the trucks from my transport company mindlessly hauled vegetables from the warehouse next to my workshop to the warehouse already full of flowers, and not a single time did any of the trucks bring back the flowers I needed to continue production. A warehouse full of product just sitting there, now being buried by carrots and cabbages while the staggering upkeep costs on all my buildings and management chipped away and away at my clean money until I was bankrupt and facing mutiny.That lack of control, specificity, and good pathing logic is a wall that keeps popping up and interfering with the enjoyment I'd otherwise be feeling playing this game, and unfortunately, until they fix these issues dramatically or the game goes on sale, I cannot fully reccomend playing it unless you don't mind dealing with the frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10The game has been dumped on quite a bit, but when something positive is said about it, it's always true. The game has multiple systems that all work well, and when you progress in it, it feels really rewarding. Progress is a big part of the game, it has a gigantic research tree, a big map to take over, and there's always multiple ways to progress. 6/10The game has four campaigns to play, one of them being the tutorial, which is one of the only things I do not like about this game. The tutorial is buggy and limited, and just a big mess, but i'll get to that later. The early campaigns that you play feel like you have to rush through all of the quests, and just leave a mess of unorganized and ugly systems behind you when you finish the campaign. The later campaigns are especially long, and do not feel like the earlier ones. The good thing about the campaigns is the length, each one becomes longer and longer, and overall you're going to be spending forty, or even more, hours on the campaigns. Each one becomes harder too, the fourth and last campaign even being listed as impossible. 8/10Tycoon games often manage to become idle games about halfway in, Cartel Tycoon does not. It feel involved, since if you even leave the game on for half an hour, you'll come back to burnt down buildings, full warehouses, no money and a load save button that is looking as clickable as ever. One of the systems that really immerses you is the loyalty/terror system, it is a sort of reputation and moral part of the game. You get loyalty from citizens that live in regions that you are in control of, you can build casinos in their cities for them, you can donate money to them, and make their life better overall. This will be met with rewards. The terror system is more punishable, if your terror keeps going up, by gang wars, failing to smuggle illegal goods etc. You will get attention from the police. At the start, local police arrest your buildings that are full of illegal goods, and eventually it goes up to the police blowing up your territory. If your loyalty goes down to zero, you get killed, if your terror goes to the max, you get killed. And another member that you hired in your cartel will become the capo. I expected the terror system to also have benefits too. For example, you are feared, not loved, and you are notorious. And you will need a lot of power to keep up with the attacks, but only bad things come from terror, which wasn't too much of a deal breaker though. The game has a lot of good gameplay mechanics, but I can't list them all here. 7/10The developers of this game are always responsive to suggestions and reviews that they find, the community page on steam is overflowing with developer responses. But they don't respond to a lot of the big problems. The community of this game wanted Cartel Tycoon to feel like you're really making progress, you're building an empire and you're getting rich. They wanted to spend a day in the office of their gigantic mansion, then go out to the pool and swim in a pool of cocaine. But the developers wanted it to be more of a survival game, running from the police, managing your money, seeing what the market is used etc. The voice acting in the game is very good, though it is not present in most of the conversations outside of the campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game in early access. I am assessing it as I played it. Currently the unique buildings around the map: Mayan/Aztec village, Guerilla fighters, Prison, Airport, Army Base and any others aren't implemented. Also the meat building and lumber mill aren't in. I also haven't played the survival mode or the hard? story mode, but I don't think these would solve my issues only exacerbate them.In my opinion, this game suffers from too much micromanagement, not enough ways to move resources, capos are boring, not enough ways to dump dirty money (w/o a lot of micromanagement) and that with industry in just 2 or 3 regions you don't need to expand anymore.Sorry this is gonna be rambly.1) Not enough ways to move resources.This is a game about moving drugs and dirty money around to get clean money. Yet because to pay for upkeep with dirty money you have to either use one of your limited and expensive residence buildings, or micromanage a capo to keep money stocked up, you end up building small production plants around the residences. These plants are then placed based on where the efficiency of the base resources is best. Here's the issue, often the resources you want to combine don't have 100% efficiency spots next to each other, and you CAN'T SHIP RESOURCES BETWEEN WAREHOUSES. This means that if you have a coffee plantation at 100% efficiency, it probably isn't next to, or even close to, your production plant for meth or cocaine so you have to choose to sacrifice the efficiency of one of the goods and massively expand its footprint, which likely means there will be buildings outside the residences' range, which means you can't build the interesting production chains the game wants you to believe you can make. This is especially bad when you consider the toll road export spots have an interval of like 4 hours, and the highest throughput of goods. So if you thought "Ah Ill build my facilities to fill up that toll road and make big bucks" you can't because you won't be able to cram enough facilities in range to both grow drugs and package them in clean products to ship out without having the entire thing be dragged down by warehouse trucks shipping product out of town when they should be moving internal to the production chain and vice versa.Ideally I think you should be able to have warehouses ship to other warehouses, so I can build my coffee farm in one zone and ship it to the meth labs / workshops in another zone without the trucks abandon the production chain so by the time the ones shipping the product get back there is product ready to get shipped again.2) Not enough ways to dump dirty moneyBecause residences are so constrained its difficult to make sure that each one maintains a stable supply of money without the production chain breaking down because the trucks are driving all the way across the map to a port or toll road to collect money, and then all the way to a city to dump it in buildings which leaves little time for maintaining the local production chain. And yet, its still very easy to earn 500k a month in dirty money with just one seaport. problem is, its virtually impossible to clean all that money without having capos constantly shipping it out to whatever city you put the hotel in or constantly doing the "Favor" micro for the lend money (ugh).Also the clean money is just boring, raise the loyalty of the people, what does this do? nothing. just lets you reset your terror level. wooooo... oh wait you can use it instead of dirty money to pay people and buildings, oh it just teleports to them, in a game about logistics... woooo... Let me do something cool with the clean money, make it the end game condition or something in story mode, cause right now you conquer the whole map and nothing happens.3) The ****ing CaposI like the idea of the capos, its cool to give your organization some depth and internal politic-ing. Problem is they do nothing on their own unless they hit the "rebel" zone, do one tiny annoying thing and then go back to being satisfied or whatever. Why? This is probably the defining part of this game as a city builder / management game right now aside from the theme and yet its squandered with crappy micro heavy pawns with crappy skill sets that constantly demand more pay(without notifying the player when it enters the rebellious zone) despite just sitting on a port or city not even using their skills / perks. There's like 10 different versions of "X farm is a little bit better, but its going to mess up your whole production chain causing an imbalance that'll get the DEA / Police / whatever to come shut the building down" there's only like 2 guys in the whole game that have bonuses that are good for having them sit in a port / toll road / city, and yet that's what you end up doing with *literally all of your capos* as you expand across the map. The "arrange a deal" skill is super micro-y and has annoying animations that are slow to load and can't be skipped like with the mayors. The kidnapping and robbery missions are only useful early game to get cash but they'll push your terror too high unless you micro it like crazy so its not worth it. The assassinate skill is cool for internal politics, its a shame there aren't any other than "i want a different capo to be the head guy now" and after mentioning all of those that leaves the capos with what? being mules for dirty money? how does that make sense in the setting? It also seems like theres a fixed set of capos that appear in order? maybe this changes based on the starting guy / starting location? but i couldn't be bothered to find out. Conquering the map was dull enough as is.Its not a major bullet point but also:The villages feel super micro-y and not worth it so i never touched them, maybe add them to the story / tutorial to show their value? The Depot needs an explanation as well. The aerodrome upgrades don't say if they increase shipment size so I never bought them because just having more storage space isn't useful for them. I wish there was more to do with the mayors. It takes way to many clicks to interact with the mayors (part of the micro issue)Positive things to end on:Theme is great, its a shame the mechanics let it down.Story mode was cool, shame it just ends once you hit the mid game.Idk what the unique buildings are gonna do, but hopefully then build on the above and aren't just more micro like the capos are right now.The game is fairly pretty with a good art direction.Hopefully further content expands on the good bits and changes or improves my gripe areas, cause right now i can't recommend this.Edit: I forgot to mention that the music is okay but its sooooooo repetitive that it grates my ears after like 15 minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I've only played a couple of hours, I see a lot of positives with the game.  First off the game is optimized and runs well on a pc with a GTX 1080ti and a Ryzen 7 2700.  Even though that my hardware is now a few years old, I didn't have to turn down any of the settings and maintained consistently high performance during my time playing so far.When first starting the game, the storyline introduces you character and his role for the game.  Without giving any spoilers, the storyline was easy to navigate and not too long while giving you a sense of immersion within the game.  From the start the tutorial missions guide you through building your first farms as well as introduce you to the management system for resources very well.  I was very happy going in blind to be able to learn the controls and plot out routes for my lieutenants without needing to use a guide to get started which is very refreshing.  As you progress through the tutorial missions, you are eventually turned loose to figure more things out on your own and I have to say the developers did a great job with making the interface intuitive and the systems make sense.  I won't lie there is quite a bit of micromanaging within the game, but that is part of the experience that I enjoyed most.Overall I would recommend checking out the game and I will continue to play more of the game as I haven't even scratched the surface.  It feels like there will be plenty of content to keep you engaged for hours upon hours and even though my first playthrough ended in me getting arrested, I immediately wanted to play again and fix the mistakes I made, which again is all apart of learning the game.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Alright I played the game a bit more. I do not have a lot of time recently. But the game is fun. I was hoping for something a little different it does not make it a bad game. Just not my style I guess. But their have been updates, bugs have been fixed. Honestly the game is fun. The gang update is really fun. I'm changing to recommend because like I said, the game is fun. Just missing too many marks to be the kind of game I was hoping for. I wish there was a half and half recommendation. One of the biggest down sides of the game, the fact you are the boss, you are in control. Yet you are doing all the work,  you are fighting, you are transporting. The boss is the boss for a reason. The boss does most if not all the behind the scenes works. rarely showing up to kick some ass. But when he does show up he is one scary mf. As the "Capo" I don't seem frighting, The AI does not look at my character as frighting. In fact the mayors laugh in the players face. If that happened irl, the mayor would not being his family again and he knows this. Another downside is the lack of alliances to other gangs, "Deals" Like hey you keep to your territory we keep to ours, and no issues arise. Or the fact the CIA, FBI, DEA have no interaction with other gangs. I know this being addressed, but until we see it I can't believe it. We can also look at warehouses, so your telling me, in the middle of nowhere is a warehouse gets too full, (Remember in the middle of nowhere) The cops automatically get on to us. I don't think so, that does not even make sense. Maybe if we had an underground lab cooking blue crystal and that started piling up, then yeah maybe. But we don't. That needs to be addressed. Assassinations, they are great, and fun. But after every assassination terror does not need to rise. You know how many cartel members are assassinated daily. NO because 80% are not found until years later decomposed in a barrel at the bottom of a lake. Like this is another feature that makes no sense. The fact your cartel members don't talk is weird. Unless I have not seen it. It's rare but cartel members do talk, and when they do we should see more police presence. Until we get rid of a rat problem. I can say 100% if this is in the game or because I have not noticed it. And if it isn't wth, that would make an amazing feature, Someone talks you cap em. Some enemy gangs are a bit too powerful, I'm not asking for an easy win game I do love challenge. But I do not love multiple gangs coming up after me with 25 power, and I'm sitting here with 15. Now it happens yes, But over and over and over again. It ruined the game for me, I actually put it down for bit. I want to go back to the police situation again, I honestly think the police system over all just needs to be "lowered" a bit. The constant wave of police after police. Like it's not my fault the AI is taking to long to deliver products, Or taking to long to harvest. Why should we have to pay for a poorly designed aspect of the game. The DLC: The new DLC it looks great, Looks like fun from the trailer. Do you honestly think right now is the best time to push a dlc for the game. I feel like the community has given the developers plenty of information to work off of, plenty of aspects to fix. I feel like some of these issues should be addressed before you start looking like another game company "Cough cough Paradox cough" And throwing out DLC to hide some poorly written aspects of a game.Like I said: I have only played about 5 hours, I am going to put more hours into the game. But It needs to be worked on. From the videos and live streams, and personal experience this is what the review is based on. I know people look at a 4.9 hour review and go "Well he didn't even play the game", But actually you should look at it as "Oh he played the game for 5 hours and ran into this many issues, that's kind of a turn away". I love the game, I love the idea behind the game, And honestly with these minor updates I would change my review instantly. I'm looking forward to a brighter future. If all goes well, "We're gonna make a lot of money together"

_childDocuments_.review: The logistics of this game are challenging at first, but if you go through the story mode, read the tool tips on the side with more in depth explanations of how to use different aspects of the game such as delivering drugs to warehouses, combining drugs with legal supplies, how to make more in depth drugs than just opium etc... It starts to make sense.Yes it autosaves anytime you quit, thus further challenging you to stick it out. Over my 26 hours, I've reset this game countless times and my girlfriend even asked how many times I reset. I had lost count, but that's how I enjoy games, I love making mistakes, going (Oh, THAT'S how that is supposed to be used) and then trying over. And I completely restart because I want to see how good I can get.Over the course of doing this, I eventually got to the point where I was making way too much dirty money and couldn't hold it in my hotel, residences, or at the Seaport/Checkpoint. I literally didn't have enough buildings to clean all of my money, and started looking at how I could optimize the cities so I could have more residences and less hotels/research centers near where I was exporting so I could continually keep up with cleaning all my dirty money. I ended up finding out you can directly store money in cities, something I didn't even realize you could do.I think this game is unique, a lot of fun (personally) and challenges you to make mistakes, learn and keep going. If you're looking for a straightforward play through and something that will hold your hand, this isn't really it. The devs do guide you in the right direction but also leave a lot to learn. Be patient and try not to get frustrated.The only thing that's frustrating to me is once you do you get these concepts and learn, the game quickly becomes pretty easy, redundant and boring, but this can be chalked up to it still being in EA, I can't wait for further updates to release more playable characters in story mode, the ability to use the prison and international airport. But until then this game does provide a good amount of content that is enjoyable. I'd recommend a sale if possible, but still a great game nonetheless

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the time played.  I experienced a bug where the game continues to "run" after I save and exit.  Had to have steam end the game.The game doesn't tell you basic information.  Why are deliveries down? Why is the airport not selling the vegetables?  Time to investigate! Why is my transport company not moving coffee to the workshop?  No idea!  It is connected to both. Transport company is set to only move coffee.  Why let me connect to them if it does not work?  Why does the transport company have so few trucks?  Even if you start the game with a million dollars you still only get the one truck per company. This is a game about logistics!The quests your goons give you are annoying.  They constantly want you to build stuff whether you need it or not--whether you can afford it or not. Not accepting the quest reduces their loyalty. Lose/Lose.  Just leave me alone and let me build.While taking over a vegetable farm got a quest to not take over buildings for 30 days.  I said sure, that is fine.  This is the last farm.  Accepted quest and immediately failed because the attack was in progress.  Why was that one counted? Why give me that quest while an attack is in progress?The laundry buildings suck up your dirty money.  I basically have to pay for my operations in legal money because otherwise my economy gets shutdown because of the laundry operation.  Why doesn't it pay my workers first before cleaning the money?  Also, you have to deliver dirty money to build which is an annoying step to take when constructing using dirty money.The police will absolutely seize a farm shortly after you pay 4000 to free it up again. Due to how easy it is to have logistics issues the police end up visiting quite often due to your stuff piling up.   The game starts with several buildings laying around to use.  Saves money right?  It is a trap.  Your terror will build up and your stuff gets seized. Just build things and ignore the free buildings.I want to like this game but it has too many little issues like that which makes it frustrating to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid game that takes about 15 hours of gametime before you finally "Get it"I saw complaints from other people about "desired terror levels being unrealistic" for lieutenants.To address that the Los Zetas cartel in mexico famously had members disguise theirselves as soldiers and stopped multiple buses (I believe it was 107 people) and had the people kill eachother and the winners were forcibly recruited. They do this to scare both the government and rival cartels but jimmy fat-ass is typing about cartels in his RGB room in his upper middle class home in San Diego. - Also it's an easy mechanic to avoid by simply recruiting cartel members without a desired terror level but whatever.Others i've seen are lack of difference of play I agree with this, there is no reason it should be difficult for the devs to add procedural generation to the map and more variety in gang leaders, i've only noticed like 7 different ones in my entire playtime in this game and their dialogue is static, in other words if you know the dialogue tree and how it will affect relationships you can easily cheese a good relationship with the rival cartels no matter the difficulty, this needs to be randomly generated for a fresh experience every playthrough.Other than that the only reason I can think of the common gamer wouldn't want this solid game is because it's a tycoon, tycoons are confusing when you're first learning the logistics and the economy, I rarely play video games but this stole my life and I highly recommend it if you're into the genre.Here's one thing that isn't advertised that I love: You don't have to manufacture your own drugs, you can simply run drugs across the border for the rival cartels through deals and pay them off after you profit, much like how the mexicans are to the columbians.Zero crashes, I can't recall any minor bugs but i'm sure they're there

_childDocuments_.review: If you find my review helpful please don't forget to click that thumbs up, so others can see it as well.Cartel Tycoon has some unique mechanics that are different from other games in the genre. The story and interactions feel like a perfect fit for the games style. I often found myself with a smile on my face from the dialog. I do want to warn everyone that there is lots of micromanaging that happens after the first 20 minutes or so. Once a task it set it repeats, but some task in the game are annoying and end up stopping if someone happens. Then even if the problem is resolved it doesn't start back up unless you tell it to. I do hope they add further automation and allow you to set a lieutenant to auto resume the previous task. While it's fun doing the lieutenant shuffle at first, it gets old real fast. There are a lot of territory battles going on and when you pull someone off to fight for you, they lose their original task. So you have to remember what they were doing and from what location.  Now with all that said this game is a charmer, and it is still in early access. I like what I've seen going from the demo to the early access gameplay. Lots of great improvements and changes that put the game in the right direction. If you don't mind supporting an early access title, and running a drug cartel sounds fun, then look no further the shipment has arrived. Here is my first look video.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a son together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 6th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you for all your help

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, don't mind the playtime. I am one of the early supporters of the game and have some 280 hours on my profile for the "Earliest Uncut" version of the game. I provided extensive feedback for the game and used to be one of the community playtesters for early builds in the past. By concept, Cartel Tycoon is a great game. The recipe for this addictive drug is "Tropico meets Frostpunk meets Narcos series". Visuals, narrative, characters, music - all that is done well and does a lot for the immersion in the setting. As for the gameplay itself, with my in-depth knowledge of the game and its mechanics I unfortunately can't recommend it for purchase in its current state. There is a number of issues I feel you should be aware of before making a purchase:1) This game will not provide you an all-powerful Escobar experience. It's not about building a large criminal empire and earn millions daily. The screenshots you might see with the map covered in buildings are actually not representative of what happens in the game itself. Your operation will be fairly small, laundering capacity will be a huge bottleneck, and while the map is pretty large you won't need or want more than a couple of production chains. This is because all cities on the map combined are not enough to launder the cash a single Workshop III producing coke will provide. The message of the game instead is "crime doesn't pay" and "it's bad to be a narco". The odds are stacked against you. Once you attracted attention of law enforcement, it will only go downhill. So, in effect, this is an "Escobar on the run" simulator. 2) The tutorial for the game is pretty basic and ends abruptly, leaving out quite some intricate details and mechanics you will need to succeed. As such, the game is not too newcomer-friendly at this point. Expect several restarts before you get hang of things - fortunately, a Discord community is there to help you out with a dedicated player tips channel set up and stuff.3) There are tons of micromanagement - in a game with a huge map you will find yourself needing to constantly babysit individual farms or seaports. This adds to what I said about your empire ending up to be fairly small and contained. 4) Lieutenants are one of the issues right now - they are mostly useless, their salaries are constantly increasing to the point you'll spend the majority of your income on their upkeep of all things. And now with how you need to house every city and every smuggling point with a lieutenant, a novice narco can easily lose the game because of how crippling to the economy their salaries are.5) There is no late game, or end game, or a way to "win" for that matter. The game is not balanced towards cocaine / any large operation. There is nothing to spend your money besides the upgrades which only serve to earn more money. There is no "goal" to work towards outside of story mode, which is frankly just a glorified tutorial at the moment. 6) There is little control over logistics and laundering, and while automated it is flawed and will earn you terror not for your mistakes but for things outside of your influence. 7) The game is still pretty raw/unpolished, with typos, leftover dialogue from the previous versions that makes no sense anymore, and similar shenanigans. 8) There is quite a lot of content missing at the moment, preventing you from getting an intended experience of the game. Lumber mills, food factories, prison, military base, airport - all that is "coming soon" stuff.In conclusion, my personal belief is it was still too early to push this game into Early Access. I'd suggest you wait for the full release this Autumn for the best experience.TL;DR Great concept, but lots of gameplay flaws. Wishlist and wait for 1.0August / From Russia With Love Update:Long story short - most of the points I brought up half a year ago still stand. Tutorial - still imperfect, not obvious to the newcomers and even has bugs. Expansion - still punished by various systems. Late game - still not a thing. Micromanagement - still horrible. New content - still nonexistant for the most part. Lieutenants - still a crippling issue. Polish - still close to none. Roadmap - once more the devs fail to deliver on planned Roadmap features on time (must be 3rd or 4th time already) - the tasks they've set before themselves, no less.There were some positive changes over time, no denying that. Logistics got considerably better and you can now get your boss a fancy helicopter. Oh, and they also got a community manager to interact with the players. But for every positive change they also added something bad or controversial, or broke something that used to work fine. Latest "Market" feature is a good example - the game now severely punishes you from even the slightest specialization, instantly downing the prices on everything it thinks you're selling too much. At the same time, many things with the game that were a problem and were reported months and months ago are still an issue.To sum this up, Cartel Tycoon heavily suffers from weak game design, poor leadership and bad development planning. These are the factors that keep it from becoming a great game, and I dare say will keep it so going forward. So wait for the reviews on what 1.0 is like before commiting to a purchase.July 2022 / 1.0 Update:A year ago I said this game was nowhere near being ready for Early Access. And now I say it's nowhere near to being a 1.0 release. There is a number of issues which have been known for months, but nothing has been done to address them. There is a number of additions to the game that were on the Roadmap for a long time, but many were once again scrapped or postponed. While the end product is serviceable, it's plagued with quite a few bad game design decisions, a solution to which has never been worked out. Let me just give you some examples:- lieutenants loyalty, it constantly drops with the only solution being you having to increase their pay indefinitely, and when that starts to massively outweigh their usefulness - kill them and get new ones;- long-range logistics and smart distribution of money not being a thing, preventing you creating large production chains that would span the whole map, and forcing you into several small operations instead;- a "market" feature was added aka the more you sell - the more the price drops. Not only is that unrealistic, since given the theme of the game "this product creates demand for itself" but is also overtuned. Like build a couple farms of opium and you are already overflowing the market. Super unrealistic.I could go on, but you get the idea. Players asked them to make people's loyalty useful - and they added bonuses that proc at certain loyalty threshold. But, the devs, being themselves, "balanced" that with loyalty draining all the time and people killing capo when it reaches zero. All those design decisions combined lead to a gameplay loop where you are forced to expand, taking progressively more and more bad decisions, until you're dead.Also, today I was banned from their Steam forums after commenting on a thread about Moon Moose's origins as a russian studio. I pointed out most or all of the devs are based in russia, and there you go. The thread is gone as well, in the effort to cover it up. They also tolerate a lot of pro-russian propaganda on their forums like "you shouldn't blame ordinary citizens for the war in Ukraine" and whatever. As a Ukrainian, I find it disgusting. TL;DR A passable game with nice music and art style but with an identity crisis, frustrating and underwhelming gameplay and the development which was a dumpster fire due to incompetent devs and low budget; and it's also made by russian studio, if you care about that, which you probably should. Just get it on a sale, if you have to.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially found the game intriguing after watching the trailer and a few let's play videos. The concept of managing my own drug cartel with micromanagement and police interference seemed appealing. However, as I delved deeper into the game, my enthusiasm turned into disappointment. Contrary to my expectations, the game felt more like a survival challenge than a tycoon or cartel management simulation. The game play revolves around building something up only to see it inevitably torn down without much player agency. Even with careful planning and preventative measures, losses seemed unavoidable. In my first play through, I encountered a frustrating situation where a rival cartel threatened to take over my operation. Despite pausing the game to strategize, I found myself severely outnumbered, unable to defend my empire effectively. Even recruiting lieutenants for additional manpower proved insufficient, and my empire collapsed without much chance to retaliate. The most disheartening aspect was discovering that the rival cartels lack true AI. Instead, they follow a scripted pattern of sending waves of attacks, lacking any dynamic behaviour or strategic decision-making. This repetitive and tedious game play quickly became boring. A major factor contributing to my decision for a refund was the flawed Lieutenant (LT) system. Attempting to raise a lieutenant's salary backfired when I realised I couldn't lower it afterwards. This led to all lieutenants having the same high salary, draining my resources and causing my demise. Additionally, the limited functionality of lieutenants, mainly as soldiers, felt restrictive and unfulfilling. The assassination ability, meant I thought I could deal with rival gangs, turned out to be ineffective as it could only be used on my own lieutenants. and why would I do that when I've already sunk so much money into them unwillingly? This lack of strategic options and meaningful decisions made the game feel like an endless cycle of misery. Overall, the game's deceptive appearance and lack of depth in AI and game play mechanics left me thoroughly disappointed, prompting my request for a refund despite surpassing the two-hour playtime limit.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon is a decent underworld resource management simulator.Here is what I feel the game does well:- The overall structure of the game is good. You build resource buildings that can produce the basic product for narcotics sales, you build different processing plants to turn those products into better products, and you have to build your distribution system. There's a variety of ways to move your product so you have plenty of choices and ways to get around the law.- The Lieutenant system is good with its ranking system. When you start getting people in those upper-echelons you have to be very particular about who you promote. With limited spots at the top, you may find trying to keep someone's loyalty in the long-run a challenge.Here is what I think the game does okay:- The financial system of "dirty money" and "clean money" is a little "meh" for me. Since you have to have storage for "dirty money" it's kind of a limited resource, while "clean money" is infinite. The game says you should try to avoid spending "clean money", but I found it was the other way around. "Clean money" was much easier to use.- The "battles" in the system are adequate, but kind of bland. You send a character who has a higher power score than the place you want to take over and the bar slowly moves. If you send more people there... it didn't feel like it made much of a difference. I saw little difference, for example, of the bar moving in my direction if the power was 4 vs 3 or 6 vs 3... Maybe the differential has to be much more to make a difference, but I feel if you have twice the power, it should be over pretty quickly. Also the longer the battles go, the more heat you generate so having a way to finish battles quickly is kind of a necessity.Here is what I think the game can improve on:- Logistics is my #1 complaint. A lot of how the materials move around doesn't make sense to me and there's not a lot of customization for priority of resources. For example, if you have a warehouse, a transport company, and a workshop that all can hold your opium crops, there's nowhere (at least that I've seen) where you can prioritize where items can go. Items all go to the warehouse first, and then are distributed to other places as the game sees fit. When I have a task to smuggle opium at a seaport, and you have to do that by hiding them in legitimate goods, but most of my opium is going to the transport company to be sold at the pier (something I don't want to completely turn off since it's a fairly quick source of "dirty money"), it's kind of frustrating. It's also not a small imbalance, either. I see trucks with 12 opium go to the transport company and then a truck with 2 go to the workshop, There's no way to balance it out, or have more go to your workshop, even if for a limited time. The only thing I can really do is turn off the ability of a building to receive a certain type of cargo.- The Heat bar is something that can be improved. The mechanics are okay, where if you attract too much negative attention, various law enforcement groups will start to pursue you and try to disrupt your activities. The biggest things that I don't like about it are the random events that pop up that can influence the bar (the journalist one is a particularly cumbersome) and how few events really make an impact. It kind of just builds and you either have to sit and do nothing but what you normally do, or hope you get a chance to lower that bar. I can understand that making it too easy to lower the Heat can make it too easy, but making it very difficult prevents aggressive expansion. It feels like it's there to just drag out the game.Since it's still in Early Access, there's certainly a lot more work to do on the game. The revamped Tech Tree was really nice and if other mechanics get as much of an overhaul as the tech did, then I think this will definitely be an outstanding game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Really solid Early Access gameloop, very promising future, supply chain builder with really well delivered Cartel theme.Having got hooked to the demo these guys released a few months back I had been patiently watching the 18th of March approach with interest. Cartel Tycoon is a supply chain builder with a really well delivered Cartel theme. It's Early Access currently and it shows with various 'coming soon' features dotted around the game, but I'm still enjoying the current game loop enough to have got 14 hours of gameplay with no sign of stopping soon. I think there are clearly a few balancing issues to be addressed that potentially sabotage the late game but I haven't hit that yet and am still enjoying growing my Cartel operation. I am very excited for the future of this game, even now with its' bones bare it's fun and addictive.I love the thematic features such as dirt/laundered money. That combined with the various other mechanics such as bribery really capture the feeling of being a Cartel boss. I thoroughly enjoyed realising I was making more money than I could launder, to the point that it was becoming a hazard and a burden (gave me Breaking Bad vibes). I was desperately trying to spend and distribute all my dirty stacks as quickly as possible. While simultaneously planning expansion into new territory to help me increase my laundering throughput. I've seen people criticising the game for bottlenecks in export and laundering but to be honest I really think this too fits the theme, it feels like the game is not about building the perfect engine and letting it run. But instead about having to constantly problem solve and be creative to overcome all nature of wrenches thrown into the works, again really playing into the theme of Cartels who have to operate in a constant state of flux due to Law Enforcement and other outside influences. Bottom line is I really felt like a criminal businessman and I loved that.

_childDocuments_.review: Cartel Tycoon is that rarest of games; something that, on the surface, appears simple and cartoonish but which, underneath, lurks a serious and hardcore strategic experience.Sure, there are gang wars and bribery and smuggling ... but Cartel Tycoon is pretty much a business simulator with those sexy elements on top. Build infrastructure, watch your finances, secure you marketplace and watch as the money rolls in. With most business sims there are complications. Just like here. Only here the complications involve rivals trying to murder you, the people falling out of love with you and trying to murder you, your own workers falling out with you and trying to murder you ... you get the gist, right? A lot of murder happens, whether you want it to or not or provoke it or not.And then there are the authorities. Who for some reason don't like all that murder and mayhem. If you think keeping a lid on that stuff is easy, guess again. Even if you're attacked and merely defend your turf, the "terror level" rises with every shoot-out and assasination attempt. And watch the people you hire and their distinct personalities. If they don't feel that there's enough action in the business they will, quite literally, go out and create their own mayhem.So a business sim, yes, but in what other business sim does one of your loyal staff go on a kidnapping and robbery spree, bringing the heat down on your company and forcing you to send another worker to burn them alive? Welcome to Cartel Tycoon.Honestly, this game is all kinds of brilliant, all kinds of crazy. I've tried running a legitimate business, importing and exporting goods and crops ... you still have to maintain a gang of hardened criminals unless you want to get picked apart. You still have to bribe customs agents, cops and local politicians. There is a depth and complexity to this game which has to be experienced to be believed.Honestly, I cannot recommend it highly enough ... and this guy is still in Release 1.0 ... and will just keep on getting better and better and deeper and deeper. I've not even scratched the surface. I have 80 hours in this game and only very recently did I start producing cocaine and then methamphetamine. My first 60 plus hours were built on marijuana and opium ... this guy has it all.
