_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a game that could be described as a mix of a metroidvania and a 3D Zelda, and is probably the closest thing to the question "how would Hollow Knight play in 3D" - which is a compliment.I'll start by listing all the positives:- Movement and traversal is fun. That's one of the most important things to get right in a platformer, and Blue Fire does that well. Movement is fast, precise, and you've got quite a few movement upgrades to find. By the end, you're zipping around the map at high speed, which feels great.- The level design is overall very solid and satisfying. Each area, while not being very original (forest area, lava area, poison area, lots of ruins...) has its own look and atmosphere, which is helped by the OST which is quite decent.- Performance. While the art style looks good, it didn't captivate me. But it also has the advantage of making the game rather performance friendly (more than 100 fps the whole time at 1080p with a GTX1070). - The game doesn't have too much filler. I finished it with most of the side content on normal difficulty under ten hours. The platforming challenges were overall enjoyable to play through, but I wish some of their concepts could have been used fully in the main game too.However, the game also has in my opinion some things that hold it back:- The game feels as though it was meant to be longer, but had to be cut down in order for it to become the finished product. Which would be fine if it wasn't so noticeable, when the story setup kind of changes midway through. Spoilers: - The combat isn't very enjoyable, and feels a bit messy. There's a few good ideas, like a dodge that can give you airtime to handle flying enemies, but a lot of times combat will just revolve around parrying enemies to hit them back. Hits don't feel very satisfying either. Combat was more of an obstacle to get to the next platforming section. The few bosses however sometimes managed to switch things up a bit.- There are a lot of optional platforming sections, which you can play through to increase your total health amount. While a lot of them are reasonable, there's one in particular that's accessible early in the lava section. This ended up being the hardest part of the entire game for me, and I don't really understand why that particular challenge is here early on given how hard it is compared to all others.- Two optional quests (and one of the two in particular, you'll know which one) feel like they should have alternative paths to complete them, because they're really not happy endings. And while the tone of most of the game is quirky and fun, these two feel kinda out of place in a way. But that could be just me.- The lore and characters are kind of there, but don't matter too much. A bit more personality would probably have been welcome. One of the areas you find has a lot of characters, and they usually have some funny personalities which I would have liked to see more of throughout. (Special mention to one character who shows up to explain some lore and just leaves, despite supposedly being a capable warrior that could help you).Overall, if you dig these kind of games, and are fine with the few drawbacks I mentioned, then I would recommend picking the game up - around 20€ seems like a fair price. I'd be really interested if the developers added more actual content to the game or an expansion to it, because the core platforming is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a 3D-platformer. The concept behind Blue Fire is similar to Hollow Knight. However, Blue Fire is nowhere as good as Hollow Knight. It falls short of Hollow Knight in terms of world-building, combat, art, boss design and level design. You are a failed experiment meant to save the world. The objective of the game is to clear the corruption and save the world. Gameplay-wise, a controller is a must. Most of the game involves complicated jumping puzzle and memorising the map. Combat takes a backseat.The game is very painful in the beginning. You start with no double jump and no wall-running, so the start will entail numerous deaths by falling into the darkness. I wanted to toss the game away at this point of time. Luckily, if you rush through the initial stage and get double jump and wall-running, the game becomes playable.Combat. It starts out easy then increases to Dark Soul and Darksiders level difficulties, with enemies taking half your life-points with a single hit. 2 hits and death. You will then want to learn how to parry and kill. Parrying is hard to do for a novice. You will have to kill a Fireball Wurm with a Parry.Jumping. It is one of the weaknesses in this game. 3D jumping puzzles are horrendously difficult because the jump direction involves the view angle. When you get double and triple jump + double dash, you will go, "Phew, finally!"Conclusion, Blue Fire is fine to play. I believe the game may have over-advertised the content. If you look at the art and the floating castle in the sky, you would think there were more monsters and you get to explore a massive castle. However, that's not the case. You have around 10 zones with obtuse jumping puzzles and a few more boss levels. The game is a pass but it's not the same quality as Hollow Knight ie It's not polished. I believe it copies from Zelda, Hollow Knight, Dark Souls.1. Has a worldNot a proper one but some effort was put in1. Targeting IssuesUnsure if it's on purpose or just badly coded to target boxes.2. Too much of a CloneYou can see the clone effects of Hollow Knight. Even the voice overs are similar.3. Content Isn't 20-hourI guess the problem is that games like Hollow Knight set a very high bar for similar games. 4. EnemiesA melee humanoid, slime and floating lasers? That's it? Like 3 distinct iterations?1. Make Combat FunDon't target boxes and NPCs2. Don't air dash to the head of the warrior by default. Very confusing. Yes, you can "needle" the enemy but is it necessary?

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely great action adventure game that did scracth that pre-BOTW Zelda itch!• Gameplay •Take Zelda, Mario-like obstacle courses, add a hub-world akin to Banjo-Kazooie's, add some dashing and wallruninng for some precision-platforming and you've got Blue Fire! Aside from the main quest there are some sidequests to do, some collectables to get and a variety of themed areas to explore.This game did really feel like the classic Zelda formula to me, which is something I miss since the new BOTW format.• Graphics •Very stylized and colorful, not dissimilar to Wind Waker's art direction, just a bit darker. The graphics aren't extremely impressive by any means, but work well for this game and the color palettes in some environments are very nice indeed.• Soundtrack •To be honest, I didn''t really notice the soundtrack. This means it doesn't stand out, but also doesn't stand out in a negative way. It fit the game well, but just isn't very important to the experience.• Story •Defintely Blue Fire's weak spot. There is a story, and while some of the sidequests can have pretty cute short stories, the main plot is pretty standard and bland. It's basically the usual "sealed evilness has awakened and you need to stop it" situation. It works, it drives the game, but it's certainly not why you should play it.• Performance & Bugs •I have experienced some weird glitches that needed rebooting the game, and I have heard from some people it's possible to get game-breaking bugs as well... Overall I didn't have much issues though. Performance was great, I played the game on Steam Deck. Only Deck-specific issue seems that cloud saves don't work.• Fun Factor •A lot of fun! The tight controls, varied environments and upgradable abilities made this game great to play. Some sections are EXTREMELY hard and did frustrate me somewhat, but I'm absolutely looking forward to a sequel!!

_childDocuments_.review: Just about done with the game and I wanted to post my thoughts on it. Overall I'd give it a 9/10. It has a lot of great Zelda aspects to it like the dungeons, side quests and fighting style. There's shrines in this game that are a lot like the BoTW shrines as well. It also looks a lot like Wind Waker which is cool. The charms you can collect remind me a lot of Hollow Knight. The two main characters kind of look a like as well. Also there are some tough jumping puzzles that remind me a lot of Path of Pain. It isn't really a souls game but it does have the feature where you have to get your souls when you die (it's just money in this game though). Bosses in this game are fun but not super challenging (yet at least).  Honestly some of the regular enemies are tougher than the bosses.  The game does crash from time to time but it just came out so I'm sure it'll get fixed soon.  Most of mine were when an enemy would kill me, it would crash. Or right after I'd save at a shrine. _childDocuments_.review: Zelda Wind Waker Design with Souls-Like Precision PlatformingIf you're like me and love platformers then this is right up your alley. I did not expect a couple of challenge rooms in that it was gonna have me doing strafe-jumps. So in that regard, you know the kind of challenge you're gonna be getting right out the gate.This game I feel like would have been more well-known and loved if it weren't for the time of release. A lot of platformer fans skipped this one because Little Nightmares 2 came out a week later and Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury a day after.Pros• Controls/combat are smooth and responsive• Collectibles aren't too frustrating to acquire and are rewarding. I like a lot of the skins offered• Graphics are nice to look at• Challenge rooms are fun and some are quite tough• Each area is unique in the sense of it's not the same dullness you can sometimes see in games these days and utilize your power-ups well with traversal• This is mainly a 'me' thing, but I found fun in finding cheese spots to cut corners and collect things that otherwise forces you to acquire them later in the game. I actually managed to get some earlier on just by abusing platforming mechanics, wall running and the like. Felt rewarding for the time I put in.Cons• If you don't like platformers then stay away. My wife doesn't like jumping puzzle games/platformers and mentioned during my game play that she wouldn't be able to play this and probably would have quit an hour in• The music is 'meh'. I don't know if it was just my volume because I played with the default, but there wasn't much and the music was not memorable for me after completing the game• Sometimes the targeting for ranged weapons is finicky/janky. Only happened a few times, but when it does you'll likely have a "Bruh" moment like I did.• Not much replayability. Once you complete this game there isn't much reason to boot it up again unless you want 100% which is collecting things, so onto the next one is likely what most players will do once you get credits.Overall 9/10 and I recommend. Had a lot of fun with it and I wish it was more popular and well known.

_childDocuments_.review: I've read a bunch of times in reviews and the Discussions page of the game that others don't like that the game doesn't give you clear directions- I suppose if you want the solution always given to you, that argument is understandable, but I really enjoyed having the complete freedom to explore all the areas of the game at my own pace, with backtracking old areas almost always leading to some new discovery, some new reward. The next point has also been said a lot of times, but as a big fan of all three I can definitely confirm that the game is a mix of Zelda, Hollow Knight and Dark Souls. Blue Fire has the Puzzle aspects and the same graphics as Zelda, the difficulty of both Hollow Knight and Dark Souls, a similar setting, character design and soundtrack as in Hollow Knight, and a similar way of telling lore and of leaving the player clueless as in Dark Souls. Having struggled a lot with enjoying Dark Souls myself, I can totally understand players who pick up Blue Fire and, after an hour of playing, get too frustrated and quit. It takes some getting into the game.Other players have called the gameplay wonky for different reasons. I agree that the camera perspective can, at times, be confusing and infuriating, but in the entire time that I played the game it never hindered me from having fun. I've also seen complaints about the jump'n'run mechanics, to this end I have no understanding, I don't know how anyone can not understand the simple mechanics of the game. At the beginning, you jump and you dash. There's nothing complicated about it. With time, you learn to double, triple jump, double dash, wall jump and wall glide, and more, these can be slightly trickier to get the hang out of, but certainly not complicated.There's a lot of other topics worth mentioning, but no one has probably read to this point anyways, so I will leave it at that. For about 20 to 30 hours of intense jump'n'run, puzzle and fighting fun, plus a recently released free expansion (included in the mentioned hours) which was super fun, Blue Fire gets a clear recommendation from me!

_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me in a very good way. In the beginning combat felt a bit wonky and wall jumping was very frustrating due to how the camera is set up. However, as the game advances, between understanding its quirks and unlocking movement abilities, it feels very rewarding and I was, in the best of ways, hoping the game was longer. The best part about the game is the platforming for sure. There are special platforming challenges called Voids that are very fun to go through. Near the end, with most of the movement abilities the player feels like he's basically flying through the map, which is a good thing because in Blue Fire there's a large amount of backtracking to previous areas and unlocking new ones to explore.The combat was only so-so for me. I feel like enemies sometimes signaled wrong, and the dash, while being very good for platforming, makes you move a bit too far during combat. There's also a parry ability that feels pretty good to use. Overall I felt combat felt more like button-mashing than anything else.Lore-wise it's fine, the characters are sweet and the whole mythology felt a bit vague, there's a lot of ideas that could be developed further in a sequel. I hope the devs do consider making a sequel. Feels like not many platformers of this caliber are being made nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the fact this game has as few reviews as it does is criminal. Blue Fire is a very fun 3D platformer with all sorts of collectibles to find. The fact that you use emotes to find some of these secrets gives them pleasantly surprising utility. The bosses in the main story are super easy for the most part, but the final boss of the Void of Sorrows DLC is...whew. Speaking of Voids, man are these isolated platforming challenges fun!! The DLC adds some...absolutely difficult ones and the option to go into em without some of the more platforming-friendly abilities like getting a third jump or second dash really adds to the exponential precision-induced suffering quotient. The story is there but mostly bare bones with not many lore scraps to find either which is a bit of a shame, maybe they'll flesh out more in paid DLC down the line. In short, get this if you like 3D platformers, and while it's on sale for $10 it's a steal. They're going to add another free DLC that's basically a 3D platformer Mario Maker so if you're like me and want to play whatever sorts of cruel constructs that other players might have in their minds, possibly involving electric shock and buzzsaws of death, then that's something you can look forward to. Exploration in this game in general is also really fun, there's always something new to discover if you just look around and I think that's pretty special. All in all not just 3D Hollow Knight quit sleeping on this game people WAKE UP AND EMBRACE THE CULT OF QUACK! PS. Quack.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a 3D action platformer, where you play as a classic Nameless-Chosen-Warrior to fight the Evil Shadow and save the corrupted lands. If that is not edgy enough, our protagonist is a dual wielding sword, wearing a hoodie and a mask! With glowing eyes! (Honestly, that is my reason I got this game). As mysterious as he is, we delve deep into the floating castle, to unsolved the mystery behind the chaos inside the castle. As I stated above, there’s not much going on with our protagonist, except his fashion choice. With that, we awake in a castle, already corrupted with darkness. Then we proceed to meet NPCs, that told us, that we are the only hope to save the world. That’s it. There’s not much lore either, except from what the NPC told us. And I don’t feel any kind of urgency to save the world ASAP, because the NPC is living their life peacefully doing their business. It’s an action platformer game. But honestly, it’s more like 90% platforming, and 10% action. Don’t expect much from the dual blade that we had, because we can only do a simple 3 attack combo. There is only 1 (ONE) blade related skill. And even that, it more useful for platforming (it said so in the loading screen tips, and all the enhancement of that said skill is to increase length or heights of the movement). For that reason, the game is more enjoyable when you get all the traversal skills like double jump and wall run etc, because the map itself is precise platforming (even in the city, you need to parkour your way from house to house). The game is pretty generous with the in-game currency. You need to break objects to get money, and defeat enemies to get souls. Both are for upgrades and buying stuff. Not much grinding is needed. To increase the health bar, we need to do platforming challenges called the voids, which I think, this is . Because there are more of this challenge than the bosses and type of enemies combined. It’s very clear that the Dev put more effort into the platforming challenge than the combat mechanic. There is an accessory system called Spirits that we can equipped to enhance our abilities. But then again, more than half of them are for the convenience for platforming, like increasing dash length and remove fall damage, etc. On the brighter side, there are some NPCs with their problems we can help to give a bit variety in the game. The focus here is our character, which we can change our hoodie into something our liking through the game. Other than that, all of them are mediocre to meh. Almost all the NPCs are designed like blobs with a bit of a cosmetic slap on them. That also applies to the enemy’s design, which most of them is just a slight difference and change of color. That also applies to the world design too, which all of them are really bland, and oversaturated with a single color. This is that type of game, where our character is mute, and all the other characters just make grunt noise whenever they talk. The music overall is pretty chill, and the boss’s music fight is quite good. Not bad, nothing memorable either. Final ScoreThis game barely passes my bar, because I gotta admit, the platforming challenges really deliver, and the cool looking protagonist. I dropped this game when I first played it (ver 1.XX something) because it was so unbearable and boring. Years passed, I powered through the game and it became more  bearable. This game has more potential to be more Action-Platformer game, rather than Platformer-Action game.

_childDocuments_.review: Get it on discountThe start of the game is kinda painful with a near complete lack of mobility, a symptom of being a metroidvania, in the beginning you only have a dash which stops you dead for a moment at the end. There is absolutely no momentum in the movement so when you stop an input you just stop on the spot which doesn't feel very good to me, though by the end of the game you have access to enough options that it makes it pretty easy to get anywhere you want.The combat is kinda dull, your only options are ground attack, air attack, and block (as well as a simple spell you get a little into the game as a ranged option that I basically never used) which would be fine if implemented better, the enemies are not very interesting and alot of them just feel the same, their attacks aren't really telegraphed in anyway so the only way to use the parry is to try to predict when and which of their attacks they'll use, there are alot of flying enemies and most of them fire something at you and it just seemed best to ignore them so they added nothing to the experience, there is also little incentive to bother fighting enemies as they only drop an item used to upgrade your mana which is maxed out pretty easily, so once you get that there isn't much point to combat at all as it's not very interesting and you get nothing out of it.The game also has a currency you can collect to purchase things from various merchants available in the game, it initially limits you to 3000 ore (the currency of the game) and any amount collected exceeding your limit is just erased from existence, you can purchase a few wallet upgrades from the different merchants (for ~80% of your current wallet limit). By the end of the game getting ore is dull due to it only being available as items in chests you which you can sell to merchants (those plus the ore I collected naturally throughout my playthrough only allowed me yo buy ~70% of the useful things that were for sale) as well as pickups randomly around the game world and from destructible items that drop a small amount of ore both of which respawn when you reload an area, towards the ending the quickest way to get money was constantly reloading the same area with a bunch of pickups and it's kinda tedious. If you are going to have a currency system in the game you need to make getting the money either a natural process of playing or interesting to gather (e.g. have rewards from side missions total enough to buy everything, have enemies drop money or sellable items) which this game fails at completely, by the time I had to farm money to buy everything I had basically everything I cared to so the only incentive was purely completionist in nature and getting the money was incredibly boring. I'm not a fan of limited wallets as they only really drag out games and never really add anything good to the experience.There was also absolutely no indication for where to go nor was it very intuitive so you will at some point likely spend some time randomly wandering around the areas of the game wondering where you missed a path or item required to progress, this would be fine if the game world was more interesting to explore but the game world is fairly boring most of the time, there is no map whatsoever and there is a fast travel system you eventually gain access to but there aren't many places to travel to and you can only travel from one of the shine thingies that you can travel to which makes exploration and any backtracking fairly tedious, loading times between zones is also fairly slow.The previous part was written after completing the main game (9.6hrs) as it quit out to the menu after beating the final boss and there was no indication of any more content being available after that, but there is a free DLC (tho it's not a seperate download) section available after completing the main game, it consists of mostly more void challenges that I forgot to mention in the previous review as they were fairly unremarkable, it wasn't too bad, slightly better than the ones in the main game but still not that great. My major issue with the DLC is they often have you climbing up and the deathplane is only at the bottom so if you don't die on an obstacle then you can be falling for a while before you reset to a spawn.

_childDocuments_.review: Some aspects of it are fun, but I don't feel the need to finish the game, due to the nature of 2 quests that just feel uninspired and already bore me thinking about them.Some leveldesigns were questionable, and downright confusing or unintuitive. _childDocuments_.review: The battle of Greatness vs Mediocrity:This is a game that shows that struggle in every singe of its aspects:- Platforming sections, especially the Voids, are amazing and movements are very slick and responsive.BUT- Fighting is not only simple but, actually cheap and repetitive, borderline boring.- Game's aesthetic is very beautiful and has a special charm to it.BUT- Story is weak and characters while charming never really "click" or create a connection to the player.- Exploration is great at first, you wonder if you have the skill to try and make it to a certain chest or objective and can have a lot of fun.BUT- The plethora of movement options/spirits make exploration too easy after a while and take all the challenge away. Becomes completely trivial.All in all, game is worth giving a go if you want to try a 3D metroidvania that tries to mesh elements from Legend of Zelda, Souls or even Super Meat Boy, from where it clearly takes inspiration, never actually getting to the excellence levels of those it tries to emulate.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like to thrown 'hidden gem' around often, but I do think this game certainly is that for me. I had never heard about this game until watching an Iron Pineapple video in which it was featured. However, unlike many of the other games he's covered, this was stood out to me and, having played it, for good reason.The visuals of this game are lovely. I never thought something felt out of place, though I did feel that some areas could have used even just a bit more to broaden the appeal or make it stand out a bit more. The music was quite good! It's definitely welcome while running around and trying to find what to do next.The game does lean towards the easier side of the spectrum, which is perfectly fine for me as it's enjoyable to play casually. However, some of the trials you do for more health can be sudden spikes of difficulty which sometimes feel jarring compared to what the game throws at you overall.Lastly, my biggest complaint, which is more a nitpick, is just I wish there was a bit more polish. For example. I found healing to not trigger sometimes when things got frantic in the end and I was moving around more. Usually just slowing down for a moment would let it work, but it was a bit frustrating as, sometimes, the healing would work if I was walking around. Again, nothing that would lower my opinion, but just things I wish were a bit more polished up.Blue Fire is quite a lovely addition to one's library. The experience justifies, and more, the price you'd spend. Or if you catch it on sale, I would highly recommend! Either way, you'd be missing out if you didn't at least give a gander to this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. It has a "metroidvania" and "Zelda" style and feel to it with smooth controls and simple but fun game play. Level progression can sometimes be confusing and frustrating as A LOT of exploration is required and missing the slightest hint can have you looking around for what to do for awhile. When you do finally work out where to go or what to do it can be rewarding but having a way to direct to "where next" would have improved the game play.Mechanics are great, there is a progression through the mechanics that eventually lead to making your time traversing the world much better and easier through a variety of unlocks. Both the mechanic unlocks and zone unlocks gives you a satisfied feeling of progression.The enemies in the game are all kind of the same but just different looking mobs with slightly different mechanics. There are boss fights as well which were quite easy but I still enjoyed fighting all the same.Overall my experience with this game was a positive one and I'd recommend it. I'm not much of a platformer and some of the void platforming challenges were quite difficult but fun once you get the hang of it and rewarding when you complete them.

_childDocuments_.review: After trying to play this game twice 1 year apart from each other I can't recommend this game. I didn't complete the game but stopped at 60% as the gameplay was getting too repetitive and in particular, collecting something like 15 orbs just to progress with the storyline is beyond crazy. I think it's something you expect doing if you wanna complete a game with all the achievements, but that's my personal opinion.The game doesn't have a map. You often find yourself backtracking just to find the right path.The story wasn't that engaging either.What I liked about this game though, was the graphics, the setting and the platforming part, expecially the Void one (small platforming levels scattered around the world).Overall I don't think it's an enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since a game has been able to capture my full attention like bluefire has, It's not a perfect game, there are many janky bits where you can tell the devs missed during their final polish, but the mess adds to the fun.The only negative point I have about this game is regarding the DLC, I'm genuinely certain that most of the final void levels were not play tested properly, the switch levels primarily where platforms change on and off constantly, pretty often I would run into a set up that was just completely impossible because the timing was out of sync.It became frustrating instead of fun, which is fine for me since I'm willing to throw myself at a problem until I break it, but others might get discouraged and give up.Overall I'd give this an 8/10, absolutely worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid plattformer, albeit not without issues. If you like 3D plattformers and don't mind the game feeling a bit floaty: This is a game for you. If you need snappy, solid plattforming with good feedback: This isn't it. I also do not recommend going for the DLC. Play the story. Enjoy the 100%. It's about 11h for that. The DLC (Basically just more, harder Void challenges) just magnifies the issues with the plattforming. Playing through the story can feel a bit frustrating in the beginning until you explore and gather Spirits, the add-ons of this game. These added abilities (i.e. triple jump, double dashing, etc.) allow for ok movement that let you even break some Void (Plattforming) challenges (by skipping certain parts). The game can be a lot of fun at that point.However, the abilities will not fix how floaty and light the character feels, especially in the air. Or the killplanes/deathzones. Those are incredibly wonky at times, sometimes killing you even though you clearly aren't touching them. Especially if they are moving. Screw the moving killplanes. If surviving a jump is 50/50, even though you do it the same, is not fun nor well designed/implemented.Add on that the emptiness of the Voids, it can be very hard to judge where the hell you are and where you will land. Especially on the moving props, which are luckily mostly in the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: This game emulates Super Mario Sunshine, Wind Waker, Dark Souls & Crash Bandicoot REALLY well, with a handful of nods to A Hat in Time and Hollow Knight thrown in for good measure.  It doesn't feel like it's doing anything outside the box here.  It's got a mix of everything that makes those games great - punishing failures, expansive worlds, minimalist handholding and crazy movement tech.It works, and it's frustrating, but it works well.  The music's nice and atmospheric.  The difficulty doesn't make it unplayable, but it does feel like it lies a bit to make you feel comfortable before breaking you over its knee.  There's no map system (that I know of at the time of writing this), so you're stuck relying on your memory as to what routes exist to where.It does lack a bit of polish in some elements:- The camera clips out of bounds in some areas.- Ultrawide resolutions have some elements expanding off the screen (I play on 2560x1080).- The controls for gamepad aren't rebindable.- The sound balance seems very loud by default (there's sliders for these).After completing the game, I can no longer recommend that you play it - the game crashed during the credits sequence, and afterward, several of Windows' built-in features like Event Viewer and other programs that rely on the same .NET Framework stopped working as well.  Blue Fire itself crashed on loading afterward, too; I'm now staring System Restore in the face while it does it's thing.After System Restore fixed the problem that plagued my entire PC, I then had to go back and finish off the final boss one more time.  No crashes, of course, but by then I was already far too frustrated with this game beyond the terrible endgame boss design and the level design ramping up in difficulty beyond that which was advertised towards the end.No game should say 'Ok, you 100%'d the game, time to break your computer'.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat game. No clue why people are comparing this to Darksouls. It's not hard at all. Visually and gameplay wise, it seems more inspired by Hollow Knight and Zelda. The platforming is about the hardest thing in this game, but the abilities you unlock trivialize them. The platforming and movement feels solid. I actually like that the dash can be controlled for precise movement. Combat is dull though. I never used the shield, and only remembered I had a magic blast toward the end, which I still didn't use. I didn't use any of the combat spirits until the last boss either. Bosses were pretty mediocre, and didn't incorporate the use of the abilities you get from their dungeon. I only died to the last boss once, and that's because the heal button seems finicky unless you're standing completely still.My main complaint would be that the movement abilities (and some of the basic moves like sword spin) didn't seem to be properly tested. I was able to get into areas I wasn't actually supposed to because of this, and almost soft locked myself at one point. They're ridiculously powerful, allowing you to bypass entire platforming sections without even touching the ground once. The wall running is also not that great, but not frustrating outside of a few void puzzles (which I ended up just abusing the jump powers to get past). My second complaint would be that this game doesn't really tell you where to go. I was able to figure it out once I memorized locations, however I noticed a lot of people seemed to be wandering into places they weren't supposed to yet and ended up getting killed. Maybe that's why some people think it's hard, they were just going the wrong way.Two small complaints are the use of B as accept, interact, and shield. I was able to get used to it for interacting, but in shops I ended up buying things I didn't want. The second complaint is the doors that lead to gates. Just lock the whole door instead of having me go through a loading screen twice. Some of the environments were visually lackluster, and the world's design makes zero sense. The first village is designed like everyone living there has all your abilities to jump around, yet the second isn't. Sometimes a doorway can take you from a frozen cave, to a temple, to a lava cave in mere seconds. Overall it was pretty neat. I was able to 100% it in 10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue fire is a diamond in the rough, there's no denying the bugs can take away from the experience, specially in a game that requires patience already, i had no major issue with the bugs except with the fire boss, i had to kill myself after beating him cause the game would crash if i went through the portal and the start menu was unresponsive. Other than the crashes the more frustrating part of the game were the damage chains when you get hit multiple times and it feels a bit unfair, this happens with the queen of darkness which i found ok cause its the final boss but it can also happen occasionally when you are traveling through smaller platforms, this is frustrating and can get worse if you end up falling off the platform, i like the lack of immunity frames but it does feel a bit unfair at some points.  That being said, the good outweighs the bad in this game. The controls are precise and you never feel like its unfair when you mess up the platforming(unless you wandered away to the areas you cannot yet progress through), the character is very responsive and the fact that the player controls the length of the dash and the duration of the jump give the player as much control as one could wish for in a 3d platformer. It has a beautiful world and it's VERY fun to explore; the game can get pretty hard but there's way to power yourself up as well, its not impossibly hard, but it is harder than your average game and you will need patience if you want to do everything(namely the voids which to me were the best part of the game but i'm aware they can feel tedious or too punishing for some people).If you wanna know how celeste would feel in a nintendo 64 style platformer this is your game, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I see people referring to this game as a cross between Hollow Knight and Zelda, and while that's fair, I have to say that playing it gave me feelings of Super Mario Galaxy - the movement controls are excellent.  As a 3D platformer, this is an extremely fantastic game.  The world does feel a bit small yet empty, though that is mostly mitigated by the time you get to the first town.  I do have a few grips:-Primarily that the game is too short.  I still got a good 11 hours out of it and just started the DLC, so saying it's "too short" is really a matter of wanting more.-The combat needed a little more polish.  This is a tad nitpicky, as the combat isn't BAD by any means, it just felt like it was missing something - it's about one step above a hack and slash.  This is most evident when facing the bosses, as they all felt a little underwhelming, but there also isn't much variety in the enemies - of which there are 4 types in the entire game (5 if I'm being generous), which I could categorize as leeches, fighters (possibly splitting off another category from this one called 'sewer monsters'), 'Floating Heads', and Shooting Heads.  Some shoot ice, or fire, or lasers, but that's basically it.  I guess technically there are giant worm monsters in one area too, but they pretty much just attack from a distance and hide if you get too close.-On occasion (three separate times I can recall off the top of my head) the camera just kind of...doesn't really do you any favors.  It happened to me consistently in one specific spot of the last Void challenge, which...made things more annoying than they needed to be.-The endgame feels rushed - there's arguably two to four "dungeons" in the game.  The first two are clear cut, with ability items and bosses at the end, then you might count the Steam House and maybe even the tower in the Abandoned Path (personally, I'd say the former is and the latter isn't).  But there's six bosses - the first two, the Shadow Lords, and the final boss.  It works out this way because two of the three Shadow Lords (depending on if the Steam House is a dungeon, otherwise it would be all three) are behind other barriers besides dungeons.  That said, it still feels much better done than "that area" in the first Dark Souls game - not really an 'incomplete' sort of rush.  It's still very serviceable.-Related to the above, a lot of abilities are obtained AFTER this endgame section begins, which just feels like a missed opportunity to expand the world a little bit more after you get some upgrades.  Again, this would be better if the game was a little longer, and the world a little bigger.These are relatively minor gripes.  I still enjoyed the game very much.  It's got good graphics that honestly remind me of OG Wind Waker, the movement is tight and controlled in a way that...I don't know I've EVER seen in a 3D indie title.  Play it for yourself, the game's a solid 8/10, and I look forward to seeing what this developer does next.EDIT:  Regarding my criticisms of the boss fights, I'm going to make a VERY big exception to the DLC boss.  Although it follows much of the same patterns as the other bosses, they are more fleshed out and a lot more fun and challenging.  Easily the best fight of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't sure what to expect going into this game but for me was overall easy and straight-forward most of the times. Time played and took was for 100% (though notes at 99%?).I think the largest issues I had at first was the direction or 'Where do I go next'? Once I got half way to the game (Graveyard), I was confused on really where to go next but didn't realize what I was looking for was just a door away but didn't hint at it. Backtracking was also alittle pain at times which cause the initial confusion from above but as time went on it became rather easy.Platforming was rough at the start and increased at time went on. Once you are near the mid of the game, and if you completed some of the side quests or bundle of spirits the platforming becomes rather easy and bosses became a breeze to defeat. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, great game, you should buy it, but it could use a "director's cut"I've played the entire base game of Blue Fire and seriously enjoyed myself. The platforming is tight and responsive, and many of the game's areas force you to be creative in your navigation. The early game is strong, with lots of rewarding exploration, and while your move set is limited at the outset, you'll quickly learn to be creative, and the two temples you come across are definite highlights, with lots of rewarding puzzles.Unfortunately, as you reach the back half of the game the quality starts to fall off. There are no more temples before the bosses, instead it feels more like a boss rush. Nothing ever approaches the density and inexorability of Stoneheart City. It's still enjoyable, but it seems the devs were running out of time and/or money as they got to the second half, and the experience suffers accordingly. This game is prime material for a director's cut that would polish what's there, and flesh out the second half.Overall I would still strongly recommend you play Blue Fire, just be aware that it will fall off in the last half to third or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: I often make reviews before completing the game, but this time I was determined to beat the game first and it wasn't hard to keep myself playing. Thanks to my friend for buying me this for my birthday. It's not the longest game as you can see from my hours, but each hour was packed with good challenges and entertainment. It's not the most challenging platformer but it doesn't need to be and as someone who doesn't play platformers much because I suck, I really appreciate that. Still, there's some really tough challenges especially in the Void runs I very nearly gave up on many times but thankfully those are optional. The sound design/quality is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, it's like my subwoofer has never been properly utilized until I first booted the game. The level design is fantastic, the graphics are cute but also keep me immersed in the world, I love everything except maybe the combat. It feels a little lacking at times, most noticeably during boss battles. Still, mechanically there's no issues. I ran into one bug in Stoneheart City where I was dashing around in the air and fell down towards a corner directly ahead when facing the shrine which caused me to fall for eternity below the map but aside from that I've had no issues.The story is nothing to write home about but I'd rather have that simple and proven structure than something trying to be more complex and clever than it knows how, something I've seen in too many games these days.There's a lot of clear inspirations taking place in this game and it takes from them in all the right ways and places. Dark Souls, Zelda, Assassin's Creed(?), Hollow Knight, likely some others I didn't notice. The blend felt very natural and right.As I said the game isn't super long, but it doesn't have to be. It reminds me of the days of Ocarina of Time where I could beat it in a full work day. I also said I don't normally play or like platformers very much, but this one is different. What we have here is a gem, and I don't use that term lightly. Props to the team, I hope this game blows up, it deserves it.brightshadow (top neg review currently) raises some very valid concerns I hadn't thought much about, except for that last part about the final boss. I figured it out pretty fast, they aren't THAT hard. I was hoping for a good challenge at the end and we got one, but it's not ridiculously challenging. If you've beaten a 3 star Void run you can beat the final boss first or second try.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game and it had an intense zelda vibe. So basically expecting a zelda game i kind of got a little frustrated. The characters and story is simplistic, the items i got are neat but don't change the puzzles or combat.And the most annoying thing was a missing sense of direction and a map. Everything felt like i cheated my way forward and was never really sure where to go.But after that, i dropped those expectations. Not having a map rewards exploration and there is a lot to explore. Instead of puzzles there is platforming and especially later with the use of spirits this can get a lot of fun.And bosses get more challenging. Not a perfect game, not for everyone. _childDocuments_.review: Fun little indie game. It's a similar game to Hollow Knight, but in 3D, with the cell shaded style of Wind Waker and far more about the platforming. The story is alright but a bit paper thin. I suspect there is more lore to read on than there is in the game. If there is, it really should've been in the game. What the game does well (for a budget indie game) is the gameplay. It's not perfect and there are plenty of things I would improve; lots of rough edges and a couple of conflicting design decisions.The combat is serviceable, if not a little rough around the edges when combined with the movement and camera. There are boss fights; most of the early ones are pretty easy. The later ones I've done so far are more difficult but nothing you can't do in a few attempts. The platforming is a lot of fun, but also a little rough around the edges. Some parts of the game, namely the void challenges (optional platforming challenges of varying difficulty) require precision timing and movement, but the game goes out of its way to make it difficult due to the rough camera and how jumping off walls is inconsistent. So far, I've done every challenge so far bar 1 5 star (max difficulty) challenge which required way too much precision for what the game allowed. The camera and lock-on is not that good. By default, the camera has this smoothing behaviour which is really off-putting and has caused a number of deaths. This can be disabled but you lose some of benefits of having a smooth camera. The lock on frequently decides to have a tantrum and face the camera away from the thing it's locking onto, most of the time in the opposite direction. This often means missing some visual queues and where attacks are coming from, which can mean loosing a bit of health, losing progress in a platforming section or death.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite good and is generally fun to play and most definitely fulfills the promise of a cross between classic zelda and hollow knight but i do have quite a few nitpicks about it as a whole, first off the lore is given in the third area, second the damage is relatively clustered, ore without selling (only available in stoneheart) is incredibly slow and grindy with enemies dropping balls that are important for mana and if not you need to manually go to the inn or arcane tunnel void statue and break a ton of stuff for ore, third the parry window is tight and doesn't deal much damage and even when you do land it; it isn't usually the best option as most encounters are ganks or enemies with AOE attacks that impede approach. I found the most viable option to be jump away dash, slash two-five times then jump slash again DI away repeat, fourth the queen of darkness boss fight is very hard to understand at the first phase and without proper spirits is hard to air stall long enough to outlast the orb, fifth spirits are relatively left field and incredibly unbalanced like triple jump, double dash, phantom platforms, and double heal which allows you to cheese most overworld obstacles, six this isn't a nitpick more a general grievance but the last five voids are just super meatboy-path of pain-celeste masochism fests, seventh despite being told of 6 gods we only ever get to see 3 of them and the others merely in a retrospective cutscene and items, eighth the general progression after reaching rusty village is vague at best and troubling at worse with multiple backtracking quests just to finish the game, ninth the overworld wall slide is very constricting which is fine but makes early game walljumping janky and annoying, tenth emotion statues are a neat addition but there's no multiplayer to show them off yet the platforms have no checkmarking and the rewards are completion fluff, eleventh the nomad literally rips you off, twelfth the ore total leave tons of ore to be needed in order to get all the items, finally thirteenth (and this is important) the namesake blue fire is very hard to acquire with six of the ten being mid to late game two are just randomly sold by the innkeeper's daughter in stoneheart. Overall 8/10 would play again (except those last voids)Edit: Void of sorrows:Wow, this was a truly amazing dlc; It too a substantial amount of time to complete and the voids were simply gut wrenching and painful yet oh so rewarding. The new npc was a underwhelming to say the least and the Von boss fight had questionable lore and was much easier than I personally expected given what it takes to initiate it. However on the topic of difficulty the void were notably unbalanced but were all fun with a little bit of jank hitboxes on things like the moving death platforms or those invisible platform switches, on some voids it takes like 10 minutes while on others it takes a marathon. On the outfit side and weapon side it wasn't much but what was there wasn't bad. Overall 9/10 very good and worthwhile especially for a free dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: The thing i can say about this game is its good... until it isn't.The controls are almost on point, but there is no control for speed. you push forward on the stick, you go at full speed, theres no way to walk. the enemies are well designed and varied, but their hitboxes are weird, and its sometimes hard to see when they are about to attack. the save points make sense, but there aren't enough of them. the jumping puzzles are really interesting but frustrating.the good stuff tho - this is someone who said "i like zelda windwaker, i'm going to make windwaker" and damn if they didn't nail the artstyle and level design. the music is absolutely wonderful, and the storyline has been interesting. the being for me is don't really like the whole fetching your body mechanic unless its really REALLY well done (see hollow knight). instead of pushing you to get better and learn from your mistakes, this just feels punishing and a way to extend play time. why are there no saves when you get to a new area? if you die on one ledge, why does it respawn you all the way back to the one you left from? all of this adds up to a frustrating sense of "i really should love this game, its got everything i want, but it just doesn't work." bad games i can handle. good games are good. but when a good game is bad, its a travesty.if someone came up to me and said "man i loved zelda windwaker, but it was way too easy" i'd say "my friend have i got a game for you!"This is not a conversation i've ever had. i want to like this, i really do - but i can't. you can see where things aren't working, and you can see WHY they don't work, but you can't do anything about it... and that is INCREDIBLY frustrating.this game just isn't for me, but I truly hope that it is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue fire is an absolutely adorable game. It, to me, is very akin to Hollow knight and Darksouls but in a very cute 3d style. The world itself is well made, with great care to how it flows in it’s own story and within itself. The world is built in very cute little side quests and npcs, that each breath life into the world without making it up front and center. It’s subtle world building that makes the world feel more complete.The “armor” was very fun to see, nicely designed and extremely cute, giving a good contrast t o the dark desolate land we are saving. It was nice that it wasn’t stated as some of the really nice looking “armors” were early on.The powers, or spirits, you pick up along the way added a very nice bonus to however you play, especially the dash ability. Plus the flavor text, and how you obtained a couple, are really cute and funny. It showed a good bit of care given to every aspect even in just some flavor text to a power.The section akin to the silent realm from Zelda, at first glance did make me groan, but as played it. Was nice. You are not on any timer, it’s the same map just tinted blue, and nothing is chasing you. The ambient music and visuals were very relaxing, it was more just explore the map again and look in the paths you didn’t take. No stress, no mess. I felt it is what the zelda silent realm SHOULD have been like as these still offered a nice challenge that didn’t feel like inflated challenge.The bosses of this game were easily my favorite part. Looking for their tells, getting into a pattern, and t he visuals. Everything about the bosses worked to build one another up in a very good synergy. Plus the music for the bosses had me getting hyped up for the fight, even dancing a little. Speaking of the Music, the OST for the entire game is perfect. Each area is paired beautifully with a theme that is a nice ambient touch and perfectly fits the area it’s apart of. I find myself just listening to the music because even outside the game it holds it’s own. At the end of this game, I found myself speechless. I loved the final fight,m and I loved that after you complete the game it  then offers you another challenge. Beat the game on an even harder difficulty than hard, and perma death. I very much approved that after you beat the game. They offer you more, test your skills. You know the fights, now can you do it without dying?I feel, challenges such as those are best after you have completed the game once in games such as these, it is fair since you know the fights and will know what to expect so a death to something new doesn’t rob you of progress since it is perma death.Lastly the voids. These little off the path realms challenge you to parkour your way to an end and are absolutely a blast. Even some of the harder ones are fun. I did find myself getting frustrated at one, but that just pushed me to beat it even more and once did, felt so satisfying. These are also totally optional, they offer upgrades. Health and with the orbs you get in them, spirit slot increases. So you can add even more challenges to yourself by not entering them.From the parkour, the combat, the visuals and audio ambience, all in all, a great game that is absolutely adorable!

_childDocuments_.review: I learned about this game when Iron Pineapple covered it in his Steam Dumpster Diving series. He described it as a mix of Hollow Knight and A Hat in Time, and I immediately fell in love with its premise. I'm a big fan of both of those games, so this was right up my alley.Thing is, while both Hollow Knight and A Hat in Time are awesome, I feel like they are polar opposites in a way. Hollow Knight goes for a sorrowful, dark atmosphere and a satisfyingly hard difficulty. A Hat in Time, in turn, goes for an upbeat, happy feel and a relaxingly easy difficulty. So, how did Blue Fire combine the two? Well, in several ways. More on that later.I do enjoy this game, but I think I ought to point out its flaws right from the start, so you don't get the wrong impression. First of all, platforming can be very finicky at times, with stuff like wall runs and ledge grabs occasionally not connecting, way too many situations where max jumps are necessary, and the difficulty curve is not so much a curve as it is a wall, preceded by a long flat-ish line. Also, the combat is pretty simplistic, and the boss fights are disappointingly easy, oftentimes even easier than A Hat in Time's.Now for the stuff I like. Firstly, I really love the atmosphere in this game. It primarily goes for a Hollow Knight-esque post-apocalyptic darkness, but I think it leans into the cuteness more than Hollow Knight did. The main character is adorable, and you can make him perform all kinds of endearing emote animations, including a nice homage to Hat Kid's world famous smug dance. The NPCs tend to have really cool designs, and some of them are outright precious in personality as well. The devs really split the difference between their two main inspirations when it comes to world design and overall feel, in my opinion.Second, the platforming, despite its finickiness, is quite enjoyable. The "void" levels are pure platforming challenges that are mostly really fun and satisfying. They're like the Time Rifts in A Hat in Time, in a way. It also helps that the game world is full of little secrets in every nook and cranny, and you have to platform in creative ways to get to some of them.The game world is gradually unlocked in Metroidvania fashion, with new moves allowing you to get to previously inaccessible places, much like Hollow Knight. The platforming itself, however, feels more A Hat in Time-like, with the "combo jumping" over long gaps, wall running, and all that. Where in A Hat in Time, you'd jump, then double jump, then dive, then cancel your dive, in Blue Fire, you jump, then double jump, then dash, then spin attack, not necessarily in this order.The few dungeons the game has are really nice too. Shorter than the average Zelda dungeon, but still full of fun bits of platforming and puzzles, plus a ton of optional items to grab if you're observant enough. I only wish the dungeon bosses weren't almost all extremely easy, which kinda soured my mood after running through the cool stuff hoping to get to a formidable challenge in the end.The story is a sad tale of a dying world. Again, similar to Hollow Knight, but leaning a wee bit more into the cuteness. It is not world shattering, but it's nice enough, and certain side quests did make me feel really sad. It's a bit like Dark Souls or Hollow Knight in the sense that very little is straight up told to you, and there are several pieces you need to put together yourself.Overall, I feel like this game is worth it for the cute-dark atmosphere, the fun (albeit janky) platforming, the enjoyable exploration, and the really nice story. I just wish the combat was better and the bosses were harder.EDIT: Hard mode is just bad. Removing checkpoints from the voids is not a good way to increase difficulty, it only makes the game frustrating without actually increasing the challenge level. If you play this, play only normal mode, even if the combat is kinda trivial.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating this now that I've played and finished the free DLC expansion. The 9-10 hours it took to play through the main story were solid. Clean visuals and stylistic charm combined with intuitive controls makes for an enjoyable experience. The game typically does a good job shifting between the more open/sandbox experience and the linear 'void' sections (think Mario Sunshine's 'secret' levels or A Hat in Time's Time Rifts). Overall, it feels very good to control and move around with the main character, especially as your toolkit expands through game progression. My only real complaint is that the combat felt like an afterthought and unfortunately one-dimensional. You can essentially just steamroll through the common enemies by mashing or doing aerial attack strings, and (at least in the normal difficulty settings) there are enough health drops and upgrades that you're very rarely in any actual danger of losing all your health.That is, until you beat the base game and get into the DLC, and man is it brutal in the best way possible. Enemies are powered up to the point where you want to use your parrying and z-targeting as intended. It also comes with a new set of extreme-difficulty voids to play around in. they require precision platforming and for you to basically use every tool you have. Luckily there are still checkpoints so you don't have to beat the levels in one go and spirits make them a bit easier, but they're very satisfying to complete nonetheless. Also, without any big spoilers: I was a little disappointed in how the base game's final boss was handled and how abrupt it felt, but the expansion's ending blew my expectations out of the water. I can't speak for how it played at launch before the balance changes and bug fixes, but if you enjoy 3D platformers at all this game is absolutely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: [Update: Please note that this review is about the game in the state of the Sword of Steel version. After I published it, a free DLC with additional gameplay (new region, more void levels, a new boss) was added, named the Void of Sorrows. And recently also even another update came out, called the Balance of Justice Update, which obviously features quite some changes and improvements, among those another difficulty as well as new names for them. So take my review with a bit of caution, can’t say anything about all those changes, and I’m not sure if I’m going to replay the game. But for what it’s worth, even if only for historical reasons, here goes the original review, hope it still helps a bit:]You can definitely see that this game is heavily inspired by the Hollow Knight/Dark Souls trope (the general atmosphere, environment, characters and some mechanics), but it’s less fight-heavy and hard in that regard, and also with a bunch of Zelda references strewn within. So far nothing new you might think. But what really makes it fresh in my opinion, is that this time those well-known elements are being realized as a kind of challenging 3D-platformer, with everything you can think of, wallrun, double dash, triple jump and whatnot. Music is awesome (best news, it’s even included for free, fantastic chorals I absolutely adored). So as a package, the game really does a lot of things well. Nevertheless you should be sure what to expect when playing this game, or else you might get easily frustrated as a casual player. But let me elaborate.The game features two difficulty modes, Newcomer and Recommended. Actually I played both modes in 2 save files simultaneously for about 2/3 of the game to compare them, and I have to state, Newcomer actually isn’t really that much easier per se. Prices are lower (though money never is a problem up from the point you get the double gold spirit orb), fights get a bit more forgiving (especially against those annoying flying enemies that can instakill you otherwise with their ice attack), but all jumps and dungeons are still the same, and don’t underestimate it, they can get pretty demanding. Most noteworthy difference probably is that in Newcomer (due to a patch) checkpoints were added to the void levels, and those are kind of essential. Normally void levels (which are half-optional but give you additional hearts as a reward) are really hard, because if you fail one of the many difficult jumps during the rather long path you have to start from the beginning, which makes those (especially the higher levels) really tedious and annoying. So what Newcomer does, it makes those levels doable and less stressful, even if only 1 or 2 checkpoints are added at most times (with the exception of the last 5-star void level which got none), and as a result, in Newcomer the game is easier to 100% achievement-wise. What I’m trying to say, that’s actually the reason why I, at some point, only continued and finished my Newcomer run. But nevertheless, even the Recommended run is manageable, got a good friend who did it without serious problems, so it just might depend on how encouraged you are. ;) Anyway, my feeling was that Newcomer makes the game more Zelda-like with a certain exploration feeling, while Recommended is more careful progression oriented, sometimes grindy and meant for precision/hardcore platformer gamer-types (especially in the later void levels). And it’s probably worth mentioning that some very important upgrades are hidden in some cryptic side quests or off the track, so be prepared to look up the one or other guide. But apart from that, and even if the game admittedly got a lot of design flaws mentioned here and there (like the non-relevance of gems and many items, souls dropping in the water when dying, the pressure-sensitive dash, some void level time cycles, certain camera angles, feeling of depth etc.), it’s still very fascinating and kind of addicting. I absolutely enjoyed playing it below the line, so all in all, a definite thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game draws inspiration from games I love like Dark Souls, Zelda, a Hat in Time, and most importantly Hollow Knight.  However, there are some pretty heavy flaws that really make the game annoying.  First the pros:-The game runs pretty well.-The art style looks cool.-The music and atmosphere is on point.Now the nitpicks:-Shielding is kinda useless, dodging is almost always better.-You can't shield in the air where you will spend a fair amount of combat.-Story didn't really grab me for my time playing.Now the cons:-Platforming doesn't feel good, you don't refresh double jump or air dash off of a wall jump which just feels really wrong.  -You don't have that much aerial drift, and if you release the dodge button part way through, you are brought to a near full stop which can be helpful at times, but usually just feels bad.  -No map feature.  The world itself isn't too bad to navigate, but this is an exploration game with Metroidvaina style progression.  This means you can encounter areas which you cannot access right away with your items, and it would be REALLY nice to be able to mark these spots on a map to remember to come back to later when you get more progression items.  Finally, the fatal flaw:Like I mentioned, this game seems to heavily draw inspiration from Hollow Knight.  However, this is a 3D game and Hollow Knight is a 2D game.  This is a VERY important distinction because in a 2D game its very easy to tell your characters exact position in the world at all times.  In a 3D game you can only tell your characters exact position in 2 out of the 3 dimensions at any given time.  This makes precision platforming a LOT more demanding.  This issue is highlighted in this games homage to Hollow Knight's white palace/path of pain.  Precision platforming just doesn't work as well in a 3D environment, and this is before you factor in the annoyances with this game's controls.  Not only that, but if you are stuck on this platforming section and you have to leave your PC to do something, you CANNOT close the game.  If you quit the game and try to come back later, your character will respawn back at the last bonfire (or whatever its called) that you last rested at.  This means all of the progress you already made is lost and you will have to do it again.  That is my primary issue with the game.  The developers just did not put enough thought into how this style of game translates into 3D.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must-have for any platforming enthusiast. The controls on jumps and dashes are precise, and the levels push your ability to utilize precision to the utmost. However, there is also an element of creativity, where you can select certain bonuses that enhance your basic movement, in addition to story-earned upgrades. Given the challenge of movement in the beginning, this lends a sense of immense satisfaction as you enhance your capabilities and can reach previously unreachable spots. That said, there's intense satisfaction in reaching certain hidden objectives early, in finding your way into areas that you're not supposed to be in yet, and testing yourself against late-game challenges a bit early. You can also nerf yourself to try and see the minimum requirements for getting past certain challenges.Let me give you an example (slight spoilers on what abilities are unlocked): there are levels called "Voids" that are basically a jumping puzzle that you can retry infinite times. These have a varying degree of difficulty, from 1-5 stars. Early on you learn that 2 and up can be quite the challenge. I found one that was 4 stars, in an area I snuck into, that should've been locked because of my current jump length. I tried it, and though it was GRUELINGLY difficult, after about 50+ tries I got to the final jump of the void, only to find out that I literally could not make that one jump. I looked up a guide and saw someone using double-jump for it, and I thought that's what I needed! But the next (official) level unlocked a wall-jump. This, on the surface, was still NOT a double-jump, an ability that makes timing and precision a lot easier, and would've clearly unlocked the final jump. However, I noticed wall-jump had a mechanic where you could gain a little bit of height if you jumped away and dashed back. With this alone I was able to clear the final jump! INCREDIBLY SATISFYING. I was able to clear a level early, just by leveraging the mechanics!Other people will point out this game's shortcomings, but honestly the satisfaction of being in a difficult-but-fair platforming paradise makes this game absolutely stand out as a gem. If you love platforming mastery from classic games like the Prince of Persia series, recent games like Celeste, or even just difficulty like in Souls-like games, this one is worth exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly do not understand the positive reviews for this game. There is, almost, the promise of a good game here, but this simply isn't it.I have seen a number of people compare it as a 3D Zelda but that's also wrong. It is a platformer through and through, closer to Mario than Zelda. However, the platforming is bad, the camera is zoomed in way too far and is your enemy, and the "combat" of the game exists only to make the platforming worse, as far as I can tell. You get as upgrades most of the platforming moves you'd expect, although you only start with a dash. You add wall running and double jump and a little more but those are your core moves. Wall running in particular is poorly implemented, as it's incredibly inconsistent: Sometimes when trying to jump for height, you will just get glued onto the wall after half the jump for no reason. Other times, you jump directly at the wall and you just don't stick at all. Sometimes the wall jumping (back and forth in narrow gaps) just leaps you to the side as well as up and away which means you might have to burn your dash or double jump to correct for it, neither of which you get back until feet on the ground.The shoddy, erratic, loose platforming is compounded by the random difficulty (some stuff feels fine and is incredibly easy, other stuff in same room is nearly pixel perfect and requires you KNOWING exactly what to do first), terrible camera, and terrible checkpoints. You will frequently redo 90% of a room over and over because something screwed up at the end, or you had to make a blind jump because of the camera, or or or or, there are just so many reasons why the game will make you fail something and redo an entire area. Even the TOWN requires finicky platforming where if you fall anywhere you get warped back to the save point. Checkpoints as a whole just may as well not exist, they are arbitrarily placed and rarely good enough to feel meaningful. Get a game over? Now you have to run back from one of the (rare) save statues back to where you were, including boss fights. This can even mean just 2 minutes of running through easy simple corridors with no hazards, it's utterly pointless and a waste of time.But the camera. The camera is the single worst thing about the game. The "challenging" (I use that word loosely because if the camera and controls were better, it would be a lot easier) platforming sections you will use your camera control MORE than your movement control because you have to constantly re-orient the camera, often after every single jump. When talking about timed areas or moving platforms you often don't have time to fix the camera so you are half-blind. Which means you fail, and then you know where to jump, so you do the first part again and then make it the second time, only to fail later because again: timed and can't see.The combat in the game seems like it was forced in to make it more than a bad platformer. You upgrade your max health by completing the Void platforming levels, which seem optional at first but they aren't because pretty quickly you run into enemies that do 4, 5, 6 hearts of damage per attack and can chain attacks. Also, most enemy attacks cannot be interrupted, and have little to no warning, and leave no window for retaliation. You have a parry move, but it uses your mana, which you only recharge by using your limited healing (think flasks from Souls games), and the parry windows are so small it's honestly not worth it. Basically, you should just avoid all fights besides boss fights, or enemies you HAVE to kill because they are flying and will knock you out of the air when trying to navigate a room, which there is no small amount of. To kill those, you either use your mana bar to very slowly whittle them down (literally 10-15 seconds of standing there charging, releasing, charging, releasing till they are dead) or lock on and hope the game chooses to let your air attacks connect with them to keep you in the air, otherwise you fall and they get free attacks on you. Oh, but don't get too close, because then you take damage and fall and they get a free attack on you. But this is all done in the air while locked on so you have very little read or control on everything.The Void challenges have no checkpoints at all on the normal difficulty, supposedly they do on easier one, but checkpoints aren't a "difficulty" thing, they're a tedium thing, so that's another design miss. It's incredible how much time this game wants you to waste - every single element just ends up feeling like it's padding. The chests which are scattered all over and can require some incredibly difficult platforming often only have gems which you can sell for money that you don't need because money is everywhere. In a Zelda game these would be actual upgrades but here there are almost none worth doing.There are a bunch of other annoying things that really add up to "not fun" as well. There are a lot of people you can buy stuff from, or want money to give you something - but you can't sell to them, which means you have to go SOMEWHERE ELSE, sell you gems, and come back, and you are limited by your wallet size because Zelda did it, I assume. Bosses have pretty typical attack cycles but instead of just being difficult to weave in attacks during them, you straight up cannot hurt them EXCEPT for when the game says you can. Which means 5+ cycles minimum to get through a boss, once you know the cycles, but usually 10+ because of janky targeting or some other thing. There is no way around this. Bosses are essentially auto-scrollers, and it's really boring, especially for the later bosses where you might actually die and have to redo it (after walking the 2 minutes back through an empty corridor to their room, of course, because that's also lots of fun)I've tried to push on and give the game a fair shot but it's just a bad game. I truly don't understand how anyone who has played a good 3D platformer or even a Zelda game could enjoy this. You COULD make a decent game out of this with a bunch more work: completely overhaul or remove the combat (add actual windows to attacks, reduce number of flying enemies designed to stop platforming, add abilities beyond "attack" or "bad fireball"). Zoom the camera out by a factor of 3 or 4 so you can actually see what you're doing when platforming. Tighten up the platforming interactions and controls. Add actual checkpoints to areas so you aren't wasting time constantly. Make chests / secrets have some value or worth. Add a map, even a simple map.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it, I'm usually not into platforming, as I don't like to be challenged with my poor reflexes, but this game is nice, sometimes challenging (especially some voids), but it's just what it takes to have me retry until I get it without getting on my nerves, and that's quite a performance nowadays. _childDocuments_.review: A pretty frustrating experience.If you really like plattformers (like me) this could be a game you would have some fun with. It tries to be too much, it's not Zelda, it's not Hollow Knight and it's not a Souls game. It takes inspiration from all, but don't do any of it well. _childDocuments_.review: The appearance of Zelda the WindwakerCombat and death penalties similar to Dark SoulsHardcore platforming that puts you right back in the action after you failThis game is so so fun. I love it. I'm glad i found it. So why am i not recommending it? Because there is no map. Never before have i seen a game so utterly crippled by so little for me. I cannot hope to beat this game without a map. A 3D, hardcore, action, platformer with backtracking needs a map. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for August 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before September 7th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.I heard a lot of buzz about this game, and I get why.  This is a Dark Souls-esque game, with a great visual style placed on it and a bit more story.  Players are in control of an experiment and must travel through the land, fighting evil monsters, tackling large challenges, and trying to find their way.But this is also very Dark Souls-esque in its difficulty.  I found myself having a few early issues while I got a handle on the combat.  There’s a good parry system, a very fluid battle system, and what appears to be great hit detection.  The downside is that Blue Fire is pretty challenging, which also is probably a positive to most fans of this genre. There are some special platforming sections in the game to get health upgrades, and there’s a decent amount of distance between checkpoints.  However with at least 11 hours according to How Long to Beat, this will be a meaty adventure, and the experience so far is good.  And while I think it is a little hard, there is an easier difficulty as well which I haven’t tried, but kind of invalidates all the difficulty criticism. Pick this up if you like Dark Souls.  Check this out if you like the graphics, this is solid and I’m only surprised it’s this far down the list.  It doesn’t have the most publicity, but it’s worth checking out.   If you dislike Dark Souls, you probably will also dislike this. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:
