_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like the game because I like Indie Games and Hollow Knight. TL;DR: Beautiful graphics, nice NPC's, barely any action, combat is non-fluent and movement system just never feels nice. Also some bugs here and there.The game looks beautiful. And usually when you start a review like that you know a game is bad. Which is the case.  I really like the character designs, the NPC's and the environment, I really do. I love that the game has an implemented camera mode which allow good angles. But I rarely can rarely enjoy the world out of many reasons. One is the enemies, they are just placed so horrifically. They are stationary air targets in your way, just for the sake of it. They are not there to enrich to world, they are just there to stop you from moving, nothing more. The combat seemed very appealing to me, but honestly, you rarely get to it and if you do, it is just 1-2 enemies in their own little corners. Then there is a lock system, which seems alright, but reeeally gets clunky once you fight aerial. First, you can only dash and double jump once in air, only once. No reset for hitting those enemies in air like in Hollow Knight (they did it right) which make you fall down in a stupid way, especially if the enemy moves backwards and you try to catch up only for being punished with fall damage. Now let us get to the movement system. It really could be easily fixed with one patch or a mod but let me get into it. The camera, generally, has a hard time following you around, it is rather slow and often gives you unfavorable angles. It first feels alright but as soon as you get to spots where the platforms are far and you need to dash, it gets frustrating.. Many times, you will fall down not because the platforming is hard, but because it is just so damn inconsistent. You wanna grab on edges? Too bad, because you reaaaallyy have to touch that 1 pixel of the edge to grab on to it. Then comes the wallrunning. I really don't know how you can mess up wallrunning, seriously. Why does it feel bad to wall run? Because first of all, there is no dash and jump reset. That means if you dash to a wall and jump of it, you cannot dash again. Which make you then again rely on grabbing edges. Which feels so inconsistent with the already slow camera. Which is even much much worse when you fight and dodge enemy shots, you really just cannot get a proper feel to the gameplay. Then, you cannot jump upwards repeately on one wall to reach an edge because, just because. To top it all of, water insta kills/resets your character and damages you AND there is fall damage. A platformer with fall damage which discourages early, fast-paced jumping. What kind of platformer has fall damage? Please. There are also the void challanges (a bunch of parkour) which really is just never fun to play and all you stress yourself for is just for some extra hp.There are also some bugs which disable levers/switches or put keys for doors behind that locked door...some people could not 100% the game because of that even.I really wanted to love the game but no matter how much I forced myself to bite through, it is just never more fun then a few minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good.Fun platforming, pretty boring combat.Slightly janky, but not to any problematic degree.Exploration is fun.On normal the game gets pretty easy near the end and later platforming challenges are easily broken with the better movement abilities.My only real complaint is the backtracking I had to do like 3 or 4 seperate times as I unlocked all of the things to actually use most of the stuff you find going through the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished and unpolished is what I feel describes this game best, just opening the game on PC the menu already tilts me, like come on why can I not click on sections of your menu with my mouse. Why am I forced to use WASD + space like a caveman, even worse in game you are forced to use control + alt to switch between pages, like wtf is this.Before I write 20 paragraphs about all the things that suck I’ll just bullet point them:What I mentioned aboveLack of ingame map (or way to unlock one)Very easy to get to places you aren't supposed to be yet (and then be confused as to what your supposed to do to progress)The art is kind of dull and feels lifeless/lacks characterTiming of block/parry feels offThe good:It runs smoothly, the movement is at times funI ended up playing till the first dungeon boss fight (after being lost for a while)Killed the boss and it was so uneventful I felt like I killed a regular elite enemy that would be found in another game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty much two games stapled together. The main game is a beautiful platforming-lite adventure with some optional movement additions, with only two forced upgrades: wall-riding, and the eventual double-jump. You start with a single jump and a dash/air dash, and with this you can brute force a lot of puzzles that seem to need the full double jump.  And then there's the precision-heavy "bonus" void challenges. They're not necessary but they give you extra health. Except the "increased jump height" spirit. Several platforming challenges are based around the default jump height and are impossible with the higher jump. In addition to completing the challenge, there's 30 collectables per challenge, get 60 and you get an extra spirit slot to give you even better movement bonuses. My favorite example is there's a really tall area, if you schmove your way to the top of it with only the double jump, it gives you a triple jump plus there's some bells you can hit for fun.It's a game of two systems, combat and platforming, and while you need to be okay at both, you only need to be good at one.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet game. It's the dark souls of the 3d platformers. With a stamina and magica bar, weapons and interconnected areas, the world feels massive and intimidating. Each upgrade you get feels important and changes the way you move through the world. Although the controls dosen't feel polished at first, you can see how this was a passion project for a group of people, and did a really good job at creating this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, the best way I could describe the game feel is "hollowknight lite" with 3d platforming.There is the classic progression of abilities you might be familiar with, you start with just jump and attack, but slowly you gain things like dash, wallrun, double jump, sprint, ranged attack, and spin attack for that extra power and height. You also have "spirits", which work like a simpler version of HK's charms, every one is a single slot, but unlocking slots is part of progress, some are combat QoL, but the real juicy ones are for mobility, increase dash range, have 2 dash charges, increased spin attack height, faster movement overall, extending every platform by letting you walk several steps after the cliff. The combination of all movement abilities makes you feel like a movement god, and I very much appreciate it.Combat is rather barebones in comparison, you have ranged and parry using the same mana resource (also upgradable), ground combo and aerial combo (naturally weapon can be upgraded too). The mob encounters are kind of mundane, and you'll probably parry every once in a while for a dopamine hit, but that's about it. Where it shines is bosses, cause there movement starts playing a bigger role, you've got all kinds of AoE and projectiles you've gotta watch out for.The devs noticed which parts they were good at, so the free DLC (accessible in first Fire Keep area, cause it was not obvious to me at all) focuses on that. The short platforming challenges called "voids" were sprinkled throughout the game and allowed you to increase your health, instead in the dlc they added more of them, and way more challenging ones, closer to what white palace in HK would be. In the end you get a new special boss, in a pretty bad plot twist, but oh well, playing through it was definitely worth my time.Visually the game is pretty distinct, I might not be a fan of some textures and models repeating, and some areas being insanely more barren than the starting locations, but the artstyle carries it hard on its back. The architecture, varied biomes, stylized vfx are all mixed into something that never tired me through the 20 hours.Similarly the music, while somewhat minimal, adds to the charm and mood of the game. I might listen to main theme and "abandoned path" sometime outside of the game, but it's not absolute top shelf material.Story is filled with exposition, and while fairy tale background and lore is decent in many aspects, it didn't pull out anything unexpected. The one time it tried in the dlc, it failed miserably. I don't want to bully it too hard, cause it does have some good in it, and there is potential in writers of the studio.Overall, I think it's worth it, it has some jank, but also a lot to enjoy. It goes for pretty cheap sometimes, and if the sales and recommendations (especially including feedback for the dlc) are high enough, they might drop even more content for it, and I'd be down to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Why do I need to put a thumb up or down for a review? Whatever. Every game is a thumbs up because I could be doing something worse.  After completing the game: There are a lot of upgrades in the later half of the game that help with only having a single jump and dash. The effort can be a bit too much in the early with only the dash and jump. Flying platforms that have you waiting to jump on like a bus route are painful. Why?Playing the waiting game isn't fun.Dashing is bad is platformers. Why?Too difficult to predict and to correct after mistaking the distance. Respawning can be awful. Why? Falling can take five seconds to try again and adds up to being an annoying amount of time.Missing a map isn't a good time. Why? Easy to not know what to do next. This is bad because taking the time to explore freely wants you to put in the same amount of effort it would take to complete the main tasks. Side task are as hard as the main task making me want to just get back to the story. Had to used a walkthrough to figure out the next thing to do. The level environments can look similar and some jumps can be different to the point where I needed to check how to do it right. Having tons of health is great. The combat isn't deep and feels like a nice minigame.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a good game. It can be called a soul like, however, I do not agree with this. Out of everything, the most vibe that this game creates is A Hat in Time. A wide range of mechanics obtained during the game campaign allows you to get into the most unforeseen places already in the first phase of the game, only to understand that developers have foreseen this. But also you can get items and abilities in ways that were clearly not intended, which makes flexible platforming even more enjoyable. Platforming in this game is very interesting and never feels unfair. Blue Fire is like a Super Meat Boy but in 3D, easier, and with a bit of slasher. Sometimes it feels boring and generic, but the game is worth the money. So, give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delightful mashup of some of the greatest games which have come before. Also, the player character is just so cute.If you have played games like The Legend Of Zelda Wind Waker, Breath Of The Wild, Dark Souls, Super Mario Galaxy and A Hat In Time, you will surely see the inspirations that went into this love letter of an action adventure-platformer. The degree to which the developers remixed the elements from great games of the past goes beyond transformative and lands squarely in the realm of masterfully crafted.I was immediately enamored by Blue Fire's incredible soundtrack. Every track has been a stunning piece which properly captures the atmosphere of the various areas of the game. Atmosphere, painted with a Wind Waker inspired art style, is where this game's soul really shines through. Nailing a feeling and experience I find hard to put into words.Combat encounters are manageable, sometimes challenging, if a bit simple. Meanwhile the brunt of platforming is taken to The Void, detached little challenges that test your jumping and dashing talents. The gameplay is at its best when these two halves are blended into the larger experience. Making way for fun dungeons rife with secrets and treasures.Although at the time of writing this I only have a little over 3 hours of game time. I can sincerely see myself taking the time to 100% this game. Do NOT sleep on Blue Fire.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is one of the best 3d platformers you can get, especially for it's price... But it's not great. The genre has seen some pretty serious stagnation.Blue Fire has combat that is very shallow, and it's movement system is very boring. After slogging through the very slow paced early game, you eventually get access to a range of abilities that is pretty basic.Three jumps, two dashes, a wallrun, and (most interestingly) boots that let you walk off of platforms for a few seconds. The issue with the entire game is that the platforming built off of this relatively basic movement is pretty restricted. The level design just isn't that great as a result. It's all super linear, instead of the open ended platforming across rooftops that makes other basic 3d platformers fun.The most interesting thing you'll see on the platforming side is some basic floating blocks that you'll be chaining wallruns and double jumps off of.For the combat, you'll see a few basic enemy types that aren't utilized in interesting ways. Run away from the different flavors of explody boys, and dash around the bullets of the turrets. Boss fights usually involve dodging some basic hazards in between hits.Still, the exploration is actually pretty fun, even with the basic movement set. Oh yeah, and the sound design is weirdly pretty good for a game that looks like this. The sound effects were great, and the music was really well put together.I feel the foundation of this game is very bland, but at I got it at $6 on sale... For all of it's simplicity, it's still a pretty competent game. It'd be hard not to recommend it at that price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: So far... What do you have here is essentially a metroidvania game that's in 3D.I'll go ahead and confess that I play games with the goal of 100%ing them so usually I'm biased towards to overall game pacing and difficulty, Blue Fire felt like two faces of a coin together in that sense, which I think is a good trait for a video game.Here's your jumpy cute chibi cartoony looking character with simplistic environment, you are given a small region that later interconnects with it's individual parts, just like Dark Souls games, while the game has a strong Dark Souls feel, it's solely for it's atmosphere rather than it's gameplay, so don't go expecting a souls-like in Blue Fire. As for it's gameplay:There is combat and there is platforming, the platforming is about most of the part of the whole game, while you still have regular and "epic" fights here and there and obviously you have grand boss battles that are more than well-done enough for a game that wasn't meant to be focused on it's fighting. Gear progression is linear, there are no stat distribution, you equip whatever has more numbers on them, progress is very convenient, simple, aka streamlined. You travel the region and talk with different NPC, get goofy lore bits off of them, obtain key items that unlocks the passage of another area, pretty much in the usual metroidvania sense. Although the story is nothing impressive, I'd easily say the game has a story for the sake of having a story, by no means it's bad, it's just there so that you have a surface level story that goes along with the game's atmosphere.There's also a side content which was almost flawless as a supplement for me that complimented the nature of the game quite well; you have access points spread out in the regions, upon interacting with them you are sent on a different small dimension where you have nothing but platforming, while most of them felt like a walk in the park, there were 2 levels of it that had me restarting a few times until I could beat them. These side content are not really mandatory to progress in the game, you could simply ignore them, but completing them with success grants you increase on your maximum health points and completing every one of those finally awards you the best looking outfit in the game (solely cosmetic), but take my review with a grain of salt because everyone's pacing with platformers may differ greatly and I can see these mini-levels being too notoriously frustrating for some people.All in all, the game is well polished, has an okay-good sounding music and audio, a little short lifespan (excluding the DLC) and most importantly, very accurate response on both movement and jumps (which I believe is the crucial in the making of a platformer game)
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is A Hat in Time meets Zelda. Visually it's Hollow Knight meets Wind Waker.It kinda feels like it might have needed more development time or a bigger budget, which is why i really want this game to get a sequel, but it was overall a fun experience and definitely worth picking up, especially when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall pretty solid. IT STARTS SLOW though, it seemed like the game really started only after I got to the first city. I would say it's a mix between Zelda and Hollow Knight. It's not difficult, but still fun. The most challenging parts are the platformer challenges, even gave me some A Hat in Time feelings. The game doesn't have a map, as most reviews already said, but I didn't think it was that much of a problem. The story is completely thrown in your face, so if you don't want to search for answers this game is perfect for you. Took me 14 hours to complete the game a 100% (wasn't in a hurry at all). I got the game in Humble Choice, but I would definitely recommend it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: While my review says 6hrs my save file is around 11. This game is short, not counting the voids and hunting for all the upgrades/spirits beating the game took just under 10hrs. Its also kindaeasy, only two bosses gave me trouble and one was the final boss. This game has very obvious inspirations in Hollow knight and the Legend of zelda series. Mix this in with hat in time movement and youve got one hell of a platformer. Despite the length and difficulty this game is really fun. The combat and movement is satisfying and fluid and you can skip parts of areas, dungeons and voids by using the right movement items, spirit upgrades and a bit of imagination. I skipped two small parts of the second dungeon and parts of most voids on my last runthroughs of them.Overall 10/10 game, especially if you like platformers. Instant favourite for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the negative reviews dissuade you. Blue Fire is good. Really damn good I'd say. It has some jank and some issues but I still think it's worth playing through, especially at a sale. Also play on a controller if you can, I think it makes things a lot easier.If you like 3D platformers and Zelda-like adventures, then Blue Fire's gonna hook you up real good. You're gonna be dashing throughout the world, picking up items, equipment, cosmetics and that key that's gonna unlock the next area along the way. The boss temple design is straight up classic Zelda. Now the puzzles and the combat aren't anything to write home about. They're serviceable. IMO, the platforming takes center stage. After you start getting special items and building out your moveset, the sky's the limit. By the end, I was combo-ing 3 high jumps, two dashes and still being able to wall climb on top of that. However, it is a bit of a shame the environments are mostly linear or after one exploration don't offer a ton more to find. But the voids, basically Super Mario Sunshine-esque platforming challenges, make up for that imo. That being said, there comes the jank. Wall jumping can be a bit finnicky and you'll occasionally jump in a different direction than you intended. The lock-on camera for enemies in the air is a bit janky too. Personally I also thought the parry system was a little inconsistent but ymmv. I'm sure there's more I'm forgetting but just know that there's some jank here.That all being said, I'd still put Blue Fire at an 8.5/10 or so. You can finish it in ~10 hours and there's even an additional DLC that takes about 2-3 hrs on top of that. the gameplay is solid if janky, the story....exists, its really nothing crazy. But it's fun and the music especially is excellent. I also personally like the aesthetics and art design but you may not. Again, pick it up on a sale and have a fun time
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: After finishing the game I can wholeheartedly say this is a great little game. Looks like it took me about 12 hours to finish the final boss, and my total completion rating is 90%. There were a couple voids I just knew wouldn't be worth the sweat and had no issues finishing the game without the few extra hearts and spirit slots. I would say the middle hours, say hours 4-7 are the most challenging. After approx. hour 7 is when I had unlocked ALL the mobility moves and it was *incredibly* rewarding. Essentially a whole new game experience when you're able to fly through the air with no sweaty hands. Also the super cute tunics were rewarding to hunt down, my friend's favorite is the Infinity Robe and mine is the Shadow Cloak :) **I'm about 5 hours in and really enjoying this game. I don't remember if I purchased it on sale but I would say for the full 20 bucks its worth it. The platforming challenges are tight, progressive in difficulty, and fun to master as you start to feel like youre flying through the air. The combat is pretty easy for me once I got the main mechanics down. The atmosphere and music really make this game for me. Even as I fail at a jumping puzzle and have to redo it 7 times, the music is really enjoyable. For those complaining about junky controls - PLAY THIS WITH A CONTROLLER! I can't imagine playing a platformer with a keyboard and mouse. Ori and the blind forest, Hollow knight, Blue Fire, these games are WAY more enjoyable with a controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... I thought I'd like this game more than I did.   I wish there was a "Meh" option because this is not a bad game.  That is not to say I am a game developer and could do better on my own or as part of a team.  I always feel bad bombing decent enough attempts at exciting game building because I know this is their livelihood, and I know I'd suck at making anything as good or better.  That being said...The GOOD:The graphics and overall aesthetic.  They are definitely up to par in terms of fidelity, artistic qualities, and original design.  I love the way the main character looks and animates.  The overall visual polish is great too!The game play.  The character controls well with tight jumps and fun enough swordplay.The cutesiness.  For some reason I have not progressed far enough to identify, you pay for emotes with in-game currency.  They are fun but so far have served no additional purposes.  I just assume they're trying to cash in on the fortnight momentum.The BAD:The combat.  I can't say it'd be a better game without it like some have commented, but it certainly isn't fleshed out or well-realized.  The level design.  I will not be continuing to play it for this reason.  It is easy to sequence-break and get trapped forcing you to reload.  In 2 hours, this happened to me three times.  Progress in this game must be deliberate.  In a game where exploration is emphasized, why would you not conduct more thorough player-testing?  Some of the dungeons are long, frustrating, and without checkpoints too.I will not be requesting a refund because I like supporting smaller devs.  If you're hard-up for cash and feel that buying video games is still a sensible expenditure given your current financial situation, maybe pass on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: updated pre-patch review below, read the whole thing. TL;DR, a fun, if brief, Metroidvania with cool movement tech and fun platforming.I love the concept of this game, and it's *almost* well-realized. The thing that keeps me from recommending it is that I've run into a consistent crash in what I assume is the early-mid-game, seemingly triggered by attempting to leave a certain area after entering it. If it were merely a gripe I had with the design of the game I would not feel the need to write this. But as it is, I have to recommend against buying it until bugs like the crash issue I'm seeing are fixed.===After a patch to fix the persistent crashing, the game is - obviously - much more playable and stable. I'm glad the devs released it so I could see the game through. I had no further crash issues and only minor non-critical bugs post-patch. I notice that a couple of Steam Achievements have not popped for me which I have definitely gotten in-game. Oh well...Overall, the biggest remaining problem I found with the game is that there wasn't enough of it. It feels like far more than a demo, but is not quite paced like a full game. I went in expecting a somewhat short experience, but still found myself wanting a couple more full "dungeons" - which became a forgotten concept past around the halfway point, in favor of further progression happening during general map traversal. The surprisingly robust amount of collectibles and expansions feels "condensed" into too small a game world. I would say the game could have been half again as long or even double, and "felt" about right for length. Obviously this is easier said than done for a small dev team! The combat especially suffers from underdevelopment, although a couple of the bosses are still challenging and rewarding to face down. I think it was intentionally kept simple, which is totally fine - but I would've loved to see more than three or four basic enemy "templates" which all have the same basic tactical approach of "hit, dash away from during their attack, hit again."The movement and platforming is consistently a lot better than the combat, and I really appreciated how sidequests and optional exploration unlocked options to expand the player's mobility instead of gating those options entirely behind the main quest progression. Probably my favorite thing about Blue Fire is that there are many platforming challenges and obstacle courses where there isn't only ONE right way to get past. Also, there are a couple of neat tricks and movement techs that I suspect speedrunners will enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: (Got through Humble Bundle)(Plays great on Steam Deck)(9.5/10)If you're a fan of platforming games and are looking for a challenging adventure, then this game might be perfect for you. It combines elements from two popular games, Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Dark Souls, and adds a unique platforming twist to it.The game features challenging voids that provide a refreshing break from the normal pace of the game, and the rewards for completing them are satisfying. The graphics are impressive and fit perfectly with the game's style.Combat can be tricky to get used to, but once you've mastered it, you'll feel like a powerful warrior. Although the game isn't extremely difficult, there are some areas where you might need to consult Google for help.The game features a linear dungeon crawling style that requires you to utilize every part of the map. The developers have clearly put a lot of passion and effort into this game, and you'll be rewarded for exploring areas that you might not have thought possible.Overall, this is a great game that will keep you engaged for hours. The game offers plenty of challenges and rewards, and it took me about 19.1 hours to achieve 100% completion. I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys platformers and dungeon crawlers.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is fun with a a pretty good level of challenge and I'm glad I played it. The stylised graphics are nice to look at, the music is pleasant and helps build a nice atmosphere, and while the story is simple, the NPCs are very charming and fun to interact with.That said, I had heard going in that it was a Metroidvania with Zelda-like dungeons, and I think that that's a little bit misleading. There are only 3 dungeons, two of which are very simple and don't test your spatial awareness all too much. As for the Metroidvania aspect, you stop getting major progression upgrades about halfway through the game, and if you think of Metroidvania maps as a type of puzzle, then the game doesn't have a lot of "noise" in the puzzle design sense - there's almost always only one way to go; even when the game splits off into three objectives about halfway through, there's pretty much nothing blocking any of them for very long that would force you to explore and find new abilities. I won't begrudge the game for its short length since this *is* an indie game, but I do think there could've been a bit more done to make the map a bit more complex in that way, which would've helped. Essentially, almost every side path at any given point either dead-ends immediately or leads to something completely optional. That said, this structure is not inherently bad, it just wasn't what I was expecting, so if you go into it without those expectations then it's fine, I just think the tag may set some people up for a bit of disappointment in that regard.Combat is fairly simple but wailing on enemies feels fun enough and there's some depth with the ability to shield, parry, and shoot an instant fireball which gives you options. The first couple of bosses were pretty underwhelming but the later-game bosses are all multi-phase endeavours that require you to make use of your full platforming capabilities to dodge their attacks. They're very fun and pretty intense. Unfortunately the DLC boss was held back a bit by a lot of little gripes that added up and made it more frustrating than fun for me personally.I don't have much to say about the platforming challenges that hasn't already been said elsewhere, but I like them. They were mostly fun and fair, though sometimes the depth perception can be a little wonky (especially when trying to hit the blue diamonds) and I've had the game eat my double jump quite a few times, especially against the DLC boss. I haven't tried the no-checkpoint difficulty because I feel like I wouldn't enjoy it, but as far as I'm aware it is an option if you're very good at platforming and want a greater challenge.This game is an extremely strong first showing from this studio and I can't believe I hadn't heard of it until recently. I look forward to seeing more from them, especially if they do more games similar to Blue Fire.

_childDocuments_.review: So what happens when you mix Mario, Zelda and hollow knight into one 3d game, a pretty alright experience. Blue fire was a pretty ok game, it definitely had its moments, yet also felt drawn out and empty. One major thing that made hollow knight so good was that its world felt lived in, whereas blue fires feels empty, and I don’t think that’s intentional. The game is not all bad, it’s pretty challenging, especially the voids, and it controls well enough, but I found my experience bogged down by uninteresting characters an forgettable locals. Not to mention the game constantly crashed which in some cases required a new playthrough, completely breaking the game, and even not letting me beat it, as it always crashes right before the game ends. As an indie game effort, it’s pretty good, but in find it difficult to recommend to most people.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of the review I'm about to write because I feel like this game hits a lot of marks for me, but in other regards it comes so short it hurts.(Quick edit: I did complete the game 100% before writing the review)I'd describe this game as "It's really good, but..." As in, I LIKE what the game offers, but there's something about it that frustrates me.For example, the platforming is fun and brutal, BUT sometimes it's not clear how you're supposed to get somewhere and it's not clear what walls you can run on or what platforms you can stand on. The combat is really fast and flashy, BUT enemy hitboxes (especially melee enemies) don't make any sense, and there isn't enough enemy variety to make me use most of my kit. The level design is pretty good and allows for exploration in places I'm not explicitly told to go, BUT a lot of the way the game progresses you is by showing you a random cutscene that only then tells you you should go interact with these things you've been finding.I could go on about more things that are good, but fall short, but that's not a fun review to read or even a very helpful one, so I'll sing the games praises that it does deserve.The overall atmosphere and aesthetic was rad. I super enjoyed the goofy characters as well as some of the more serious ones. You definitely don't get too attached to any of them seeing as you never interact with them more than a couple times, but none of the dialogue was offensive, and some of it gave me a good chuckle. The music is fine enough. It's mostly there to create atmosphere, but I'm a huge fan of dark souls, so it did what it needed to do for me. The areas all had nice colors and were decorated enough that it wasn't super confusing where I was.Ultimately, I did enjoy the game, but it's hard for me to recommend something like this. Platformer games and Souls-like games are up my alley, and I have a lot of patience for them, but I really had to force myself to finish Blue Fire.  While I did have a mostly positive experience with the game, I don't think I can recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Tries to be one part platformer and one part Souls-like but didn't manage to create satisfying gameplay of either of these genres for me.Primarily, this game is a platformer and it controls well with a fun dash move and an eventually learned double jump that helps stabilize your character + give you more opportunities to do long ranged and tricky maneuvers. But the game rarely offers interesting platforming sequences and is full of slow, tedious platforms that mosey their way over death pits where you don't have many ways of showing off your skills, and what's worse is the game loves dotting platforming obstacles with unnecessary floating enemies that add discordant shockwave attacks nudging you into its awkward combat which mostly involves dashing into something's face, getting in 1-2 attacks, and dashing away, and HOPING you don't fall into any one of the millions of death pits enemies are contractually obligated to float over (This also applies to half the bosses in the game for some reason too, and it never stops feeling clunky to me even though I didn't find the combat to be difficult.)I think the game doesn't do a great job monopolizing on its own ideas or bringing things to a greater potential. A good example of this is in an early dungeon, you activate these slow moving statues to get them to stand on buttons needed to progress. This is an idea taken right out of Zelda: Wind Waker (where the game mirrors a lot of its visual design from) but the problem is this mechanic never gets any interesting use. The button that needs to be pressed by the statue is always only a few feet away and there's just... no obstacle? No puzzle? I don't understand the reason for even including this in the game, it never gets more complicated, and no I'm not boiling it down or oversimplifying it, they really are: Move statue 5 feet to the left. That's it. And I feel lots of obstacles in this game feel like this: A concept that's not utilized well at all almost as if you're completing the opening chamber from Portal over and over again where the game is just explaining the concept of putting blocks on buttons to you.But on the reverse end, the only real hint of challenge the game offers comes from mostly optional obstacle course rooms entered via shrines littered around the world. These can be a nice change of pace simply due to being focused platforming sections (which the rest of the game is ironically lacking in) but they're either far too easy or brutally punishing in a very un-fun way (and there's no in between) And by punishing, I mean in that way of making things fake-hard where no individual obstacle is a challenge but you have to do 10 or so simple/medium obstacles in a row and if you mess up even one, you go all the way to the start again. It's lazy and frustrating and a shame that this is the only time the game even attempts being challenging. And what's worse is the first platforming shrine you encounter HAS checkpoint platforms in it, but they never use these again for reasons I simply don't know. it's as if they forgot they even existed when this could've made later "difficult" shrines actually fair and perhaps even fun. Oriane's Saw was the most notable offender to me.Blue Fire has a major padding issue in its second half. The game attempts to double up on itself where the final chapters of content almost all require you to do a tremendous amount of backtracking throughout effectively the entire game. One chapter you're tasked with finding four gate entrances that stem from old content areas that you likely came across before, but couldn't interact with because you didn't have a late game MacGuffin. And another chapter has you return to almost every major area in the game and collect scattered orbs that simply make you replay the level cause they're not placed in interesting or hidden locations for the most part, they're almost all on the main pathways that you already traversed the first time you entered the area. Imagine if the second half of a Mario game had you return to World 1-1 and simply play the level again but you HAD to collect all the coins, and then multiply this for about half the rest of the game. It's just not fun. I wouldn't be complaining about this if it was something you could've done the first time you entered any of these zones, in fact, that would've added some zest to the kind of bland straightforward sections and possibly even give the game a less linear nature, which could improve its overall flow and replayability.And when you complete these backtracking chapters, the game launches into its final boss. This surprised me since the game is mostly a platformer, I was hoping for a large difficult finale feeling platforming dungeon before the climactic boss fight and felt pretty disappointed since I felt like I hardly did anything new in the last couple hours of gameplay and the game was becoming a bit of a boss rush in its final hours, sadly highlighting its wonky combat even more.The final boss IS fantastic though. The visuals, music, and attack designs are astonishing and the game ends on a high note for sure. I'm glad this boss didn't float over a death pit the whole time lol. I wish the rest of the combat could've been this fun and well-designed... I'd unfortunately go as far as saying it was the only boss fight I enjoyed.Blue Fire's visuals are sensational and I think this is where most of this game's praise is garnered from. The main character is cute and cool with tons of instantly lovable cosmetics and emotes to collect and all the environments could've been lifted directly from Wind Waker with a colder tone. I was immediately impressed from the title screen alone. Unfortunately the gameplay constantly feels like it's in an unfinished Alpha stage, as if they planned out the game but didn't really finish it or polish it up.And despite how long this review already is, I'm glossing over several things throughout the game I also felt were not well-handled, such as its broken (and kind of pointless feeling) economy, long distance between and awkward placement of NPCs you can sell items to, dialogue boxes that have its text blend into the brighter parts of the environments, an abundance of boring fetch/backtracking sidequests, annoying level traversal before you get double jump, an underwhelming plot with a rather abrupt ending, an inability to warp between zones until the late game furthering the padding problem, ALL the weapons in the game are identical in gameplay making me wonder why you don't just get permanent damage increases instead...With better level, obstacle, and world design, this game could've been pretty great, but as it stands, almost every element of the game beyond its visuals and the feel of controlling the main character are lacking in quality.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does everything wrong starting from right around the time it's too late for a refund. Level design that makes depth perception impossible. A hub designed like a platform challenge that you're expected to play through dozens of times just to talk to vital NPCs. A vital NPC who was put earlier than the hub despite only selling things you can't afford before reaching the hub. A wall run/jump mechanic that functions horribly & is only partially explained.Parts where you fall for a ridiculous amount of time after a mistake before the game finally respawns you. A timed section with confusing level design centered around wall running right after you get wall running. Constant rewatching pointless unskippable scenes. The hub is literally a maze. No indication what you can & can't wall run on.The pipe platforms are programmed the same way as pipes in other games where you're not supposed to stand on pipes, which is that you slide off for no reason unless you stand in just the right spot. Constant forced backtracking in a giant labyrinth world with no map & no waypoints. Y goes back for no reason. B confirms for no reason.It's impossible to die unless you stubbornly try an idea that isn't working dozens of times because your health bar is absurd. You can beat the first boss by just running into it & attack it repeatedly while tanking every hit & you'll still finish with a lot of HP left.There's a high platform with a chest on it in the hub. It looks like you can wall jump to it but the game just doesn't let you so trying causes you to fall & get trapped in an invisible box on top of a giant lump of poison.The game is full of giant lumps of poison that hurt if you touch them but instead of being carefully placed like hazards normally would be to make a game fair & fun, they're placed like scenery. In other words, wherever looks good. I fell in water at one point & got hurt twice. Once by the water & once by a random little chunk of poison in the water.The game tells you it autosaves but it doesn't tell you manual saves are the only saves that matter because autosaves save so close to nothing I'm not even sure what they save. An autosave always puts you back at the last place where you manually saved even if it was multiple areas ago.There are giant spike pillars & touching any part of the pillars hurts you even though the spike is small & is only on top. There's no fast travel, no teleporters, & nothing else like that so saving time is simply not allowed.One of earliest massive glaring signs of lazy design was when I entered the hub for the first time & met a merchant selling clothing dyes & I wanted to save before buying one but the save point was across a huge gap & it didn't look like I'd be able to come back any time soon if I jump down to it so I just carefully chose a dye, put it on, & found it was a drastically different color than the picture showed it to be. One of the dyes is labelled "light grey" but the picture is blue. Not even light blue. Just blue. How does something like that happen?This game is mostly filler. Filler consisting of the same rooms with nothing new to do in them on your way back to whatever merchant you're revisiting.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a 7/10 game. Nothing special, but nothing horribly bad either. The game is a 3d-platformer with Zelda-like dungeons and exploration. By the end of the game you have a wide variety of "Spirits" to equip that improves your arsenal of platforming tools that improve further upon the game's already great sense of freedom and flow. Even better, you will definitely have to take full advantage of these in the end-game voids/rifts. With a few exceptions, I found the Voids to be pretty well balanced difficulty wise and I enjoyed that they forced me to use all my tools at my disposal. The story and combat is pretty meh, but that's nothing new for a 3d platformer.As for complaints about maps and not knowing where to go, I personally dont get it. I feel like the areas are very well defined and connect in ways that are made obvious. I never found I had to do too much backtracking anyways, but on that note I explore everything that I can before moving onto the next area. I think what would really help is simply being able to see the name of an area before moving into it, rather than after moving into it. In the end, if you want a basic 3d platformer with a fast and flowing toolset, then I'd suggest picking this up!

_childDocuments_.review: Very nostalgic and has some neat ideas along with charming visuals. But there are a lot of buts. But the critical path is always murky. But the map design is repetitive. But combat is extremely limited and level appropriate enemies are guaranteed to combo you to death.This has gone form "pretty difficult" to unplayable at this point. I am nearing the end of the game, and the constant hazard laden platforming over instant death pools of lava and poison has ceased to be fun. Both the combat and the platforming ask you to be creative and crafty, but "don't get hit" is the only advice the official strategy has and there are very few tools at your disposal.Maybe there will be a patch where they add the rest of the controls, or get rid of the disappearing fire worms that will kill you from the next state.

_childDocuments_.review: So, for starters, I think that if you like puzzle platformers with a mix of metroidvania, you should get this game. It grabbed my attention for the whole way through, and I enjoyed most, if not all of the gameplay. Some of the mechanics felt really nice, and once everything was combined towards the end it felt great just to move around.The only things I really have qualms with is that some of the platforming doesn't really mix well with the camera control and movement controls at times, and that the game also cheated me out of 100% achievement completion (this is minor though). Sometimes the camera will just mess you up and you'll have to restart an entire section, and other times it's hard to judge how far away something is unless you control the camera well enough yourself.On the note of the achievement completion, two achievement triggers didn't fire even though I did what they say, and have completed the game as proof of it. The two achievements are essentially story tied since you have to do them to progress. Just hurts that I don't have 100% now because of it.P.S.Game also has a lot of crashing going on at the moment, and there are a few bugs like getting stuck in a wall at certain locations, but this ultimately doesn't take away from the quality of the game. _childDocuments_.review: 8/10Bought this game while looking for games similar to hollow knight, started it up and found what i was looking for. Platforming majority with some combat elements and general NPC questlines here and there. Good; i do so like how this game rewards exploration, the more hidden a powerup the more unballanced it is, and so it should be, i climbed halfway up a cathedral wall and did something i thought was impossible and was rewarded with a triple jump, so it should go like that. I also love how it encourages you to go back to previous areas and find new rewards while not feeling tedious. Also how you can change currency to a special item that has no use besides selling it for currency, it helps to have a system similar to this in games like this as it pretty much allows for banking. Another thing is that if you put in the effort the bottom can seem to drop out of the difficulty somewhat so if your struggling with an optional area early on then just come back when you can quadrupal jump and can run faster than the land speed record. Another thing is the quite large amount of NPCs that add to make the world feel alive and work as either vendors or questline givers, or sometimes just exposition buckets which can be good in moderation which this game has.Bad; The combat feels slightly clunky and more like turn based combat, go in and hit then back out and bait an attack then rinse and repeat. The regular walking also feels slightly slippery and the jumping can't seem to decide whether to be floaty or drop like a brick. Also the way forward can seem a bit vauge at times but its never more of a quick fix to solve it, by just going back and re-treading your steps. The soundtrack isnt all bad but theres just not much too it, its there and it does sound things, thats it. So in conclusion if you want a great platformer that rewards exploration but the combat is more just there then this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've entirely completed this game with the exception of one void that I couldn't beat. Now that I'm putting this down, I have a lot to say about this game.tl;dr:Blue Fire has the potential to be one of the best games I've found on steam but inhibits that potential with bizarre game design and poor game direction. However, I will still recommend this to anyone.The strongest thing that this game has going for it is how it feels and looks.  There was passion in the art here. It was very obvious a lot of hard work went into making the aesthetics of Blue Fire look phenomenal and successfully did so. There was so much detail in every raindrop and the synergy it had with the surrounding environments and textures was perfect. Another, strength is the platforming and the control mechanisms that make it work.I'm not going to consider this a spoiler because of it being introduced almost immediately when you start the game but the voids are what I looked forward to during my playtime. Gauntlets and platforming challenges scattered throughout the levels create such a strong contrast between these mini-levels and the actual environments that are necessary towards progression. They're hard, they're original and they will challenge your patience. Controlling my character and getting to know it's limits was hard to get used to and was the cause of some frustration at the start. I learned that any mistake I made was entirely my fault. I've read a lot of reviews criticizing the platforming mechanics and although they're different and sensitive, its something to master. I feel like it was designed that way as well. Looking at a platform  the size of a penny across a huge gap then being able to maneuver your way to it, landing directly in the middle, just as you planned it. There isn't much room for mistakes and forces you to learn and perfect every stroke.The story felt like watching a folk singer at a small town bar it was so boring and unoriginal. It was predictable. It was dull. The dialogue had me spamming A through every encounter because I knew there wasn't a single word that would've been remotely interesting. Listening to the quest-essential blabber of NPC's would've made you thought this was created by beta phase AI. Everything about the lore and the story fell by the wayside in my mind, making my experience feel heartless.Another glaring issue was the progression design and its back tracking. I mean like, yeah, hollow knight is a clear inspiration that successfully bounces off of while still being somewhat original. But the metroidvania style backtracking made no sense and led to nothing but disappointment. You'll go through six really small biomes/levels. Then you'll look at your journal and think to yourself "Oh, I'm only 22% completed wowee!" Then you'll get a quest to go collect 20 orbs back in the beginning three levels, bored to death and hoping it opens up some exciting new biome or quest. And then it opens an exciting new door, dripping with potential, relieving your anxiety that there isn't anything new to explore. The door opens, it's a boss fight. You exit the arena and receive another quest involving backtracking through the same ♥♥♥♥ for some meaningless and boring reason.This game disappoints. A small yet hard to ignore flaw is it's heavy reliance on cosmetic cloaks and emotes. It's a single player game and you'll spend two hours collecting a random object for an npc and your only reward is a pink cloak. Emotes serve the purpose of uncovering hidden chest. But after just finishing the game with every quest completed, I look at my inventory with all the random loot I got from emoting and they are literally useless. Can't sell them. No more quests to serve possible purpose. I have three dead rats and a bowl of rice just for my viewing enjoyment I guess.HOWEVER.I've spent twenty-three hours playing this game, thinking about how something so structurally beautiful and satisfying can no longer be squandered by the annoying and seemingly lazy poor choices. My answer?An update.A huge update.An update that will turn this game around, onto the road leading to be one of the greats."But ewan, you just made me decide not to buy this with everything you wrote above!"Well, continue reading chap.This game deserves downloads. This game deserves players and most of it all, it deserves appreciation. But not right now.What this game doesn't deserve is to be seen as a failure and cast away to the pit of failed passion projects. I really hope the devs read these reviews because all this needs is an update. A fix. In my perfect world, an massive overhaul of the bland and disappointing aspects will come to make this game the beautiful ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece I know it can be.Enough of my tangent, this game is fun. And if I were you, buy it. Play through the entirety of it. Gain a great knowledge of how the devs excelled at such a project and where they failed miserably.Because one day,one daythere will be an update.And all this ♥♥♥♥ will be fixed. Opening up the door for a new contender for the spot of favourite game of 2021.Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a platformer RPG drawing inspiration from games like Legend Of Zelda and Mario. The core gameplay is not bad, but the game is ruined by the absurdly masochistic precision platforming required to traverse some parts of the game. Nowhere is this more evidenced than Voids. Voids are extremely difficult gauntlets requiring millisecond precision timing and absolutely no mistakes. To give you an example of the problem, imagine trying to land on a small cube approx 1m in diameter, 10 meters away. First you have to jump, the height of your jump is determined by how long you hold the button, requiring precise timing of release. At the apex of your jump you have to double jump, again with the same mechanic of holding down the button longer. Now, you have to dash, holding down the button longer makes you dash further. The key here is the dash takes about 500-600 milliseconds to complete, it's very fast and long reaching, making it easy to overshoot your target. In many cases if you didn't let go of the jump button at exactly the apex of both jumps you will not be high enough to land on your target when you dash. Remember we are talking about a small 1m cube-platform here. Oh! and once you land the cube collapses under you after 1 second, so you can't stand still!Now imagine this if you will. You must wall jump (and you slide down as you do) along a large corridor of rapidly moving sawblades, with spikes on the floor and ceiling. Then, two more corridors with even more sawblades and spikes. Hyperventilating yet? Onwards to approx 10 x 1m collapsing cubes with swinging sawblades between them for even more spice! Oh, and then another 3 corridors (with no safe place to stand between) of alternating densly packed sawblades, and lets add swinging sawblades between each row so you have to time it perfectly and can't stand (cling?) still. Sounds bad right? Well there are no checkpoints and if you touch a single trap you have to start over again from the very beginning! Did I mention you randomly detach from walls, sometimes wall jump at odd angles, struggle to percieve depth as you rush through, and the camera likes to bug out thus glitching your perspective and viewing distance during this whole ordeal?!?!Imagine if every single piece of heart in the Legend Of Zelda series required you to go through this in order to obtain it? That's Blue fire!The overworld doesn't escape these idiosyncrasies either, with many parts of the map requiring high levels of precision/timing with few checkpoints. Unlike LOZ, when you fall in a pit you don't reappear on the last piece of solid ground you stood on, only some platforms count as checkpoints and they are often far apart. Also most of the map has a pit of some sort.Combat feels a bit clunky and underwhelming, sometimes your attacks don't go off when you click, and many enemies have attacks with instant hitboxes, yet that are super easy to predict once you learn the pattern you can force the ai into.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the devs first game and it shows, it has some good stuff (platforming, environments) some meh stuff (combat, story) and some bad stuff (writing). There's better games to spend the same amount of money on but if it's on sale I recommend it.The bosses are enjoyable from the third one onwards but pose little challenge in normal mode, overall the game is easy on this difficulty, I've only died once in the free DLC. Didn't bother with hard mode because it seems to only 1) increase enemy damage but I did not care for the combat 2) reduce the number of checkpoints (supposedly during platform challenges, I did not verify this but why would you ever have this as an option is beyond me, just extra frustration for the player).Some rambling:The spirit mechanic seems to be inspired by Hollow Knight charms, however it's not well balanced, some of them are super good while others useless, and they all have the same equipment cost. It's interesting that about half of them upgrade your movement capabilities, some of them are super broken to the point of making most platforming challenges (Voids) in the game trivial.I've actually replayed all main story Voids without any movement spirits and found them all reasonably doable and mostly fun.The DLC Voids however are quite hard without any spirits (believe me, I've tried) and balance wise they feel all over the place. Here I eventually gave up and easily completed them with all movement buffs activated. There's probably an optimal spirit combination one can choose for each Void to make the DLC challenging and fun instead of challenging and rage-inducing, but it's the devs job to make sure the player has just enough tools to overcome a challenge in a satisfying way, not the player's. Overall the spirits that buff your movement feel like the devs weren't confident of their own platforming difficulty, which again, first game, perfectly understandable.Closing statement: the game has a secret  so it's a 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game after the first major update since launch (in August 2021). Many bugs people complained about seem to have been patched, because I didn’t experience any game-breaking bug.There are 2 difficulty levels: newcomer (easy) and recommended (normal). I played on “recommended”.:• Visually stunning• Music is great• Freedom to explore, and interesting and diverse areas• No map, which makes it feel really rewarding once you figure out how to get to where you want to go. The world isn’t that huge to require a map, and I think it would be way less immersive if there was a map.• No waypoint markers, which also makes everything more immersive, rewarding, and makes the screen less cluttered. There aren’t many main quests and side quests, so it’s not that hard to keep in mind what your objectives are while exploring.• Steam achievements are, essentially, completing all the quests. I like how straight-forward it is. There’s nothing absurd like “Complete the game in 2 hours without dying” or hidden achievements you would never find out without looking up on the Internet.:• Enemies get too powerful too fast. It’s scary at first, because out of nothing you walk into enemies that can kill you with 2 or 3 hits. But once you get used to how they behave, it’s not that hard to deal with them.• Special rooms in which your platforming skills are put to the test. Some of them are REALLY hard, and there are only checkpoints in the newcomer mode. And the camera angles sometimes get annoying… However, it feels very rewarding once you beat them, and the rewards you get really help you become stronger.• Lack of enemy diversity. Throughout the game you face very similar enemies, it’s like they’re the same, but just wearing a different costume. It felt boring at first, but later I realized that it didn’t matter to me, because on this type of game the combat is not really what I care about, so having a lot of enemies behaving in a similar way ended up making things easier.• The bosses are kind of boring. It’s hard to understand the pattern of some bosses, and in some cases it’s hard to use the function to lock the camera on them. I just ended up smashing buttons. I was able to kill most of them on the first try (even the final one), though, and it never took me more than two tries to kill any of them. So, in the end, since I’m much more into exploring than into combat, it didn’t matter that much.:• There’s some dialogue with bosses in a language invented for the game, which is kind of impossible to decode, so I hated going through dialogue that I could not understand.

_childDocuments_.review: If Super Mario 64, Hollow Knight, and Demon Souls had a child (somehow), it would be Blue Fire. If you're a fan of any of the aforementioned titles, this is worth a play through. I myself have spent 21 hours and have gotten a 100% playthrough, and those hours were enjoyable.Art: 8/10• The art was unique and stayed fresh throughout the game. We've seen art and style like this before but not too often.Sound: 9/10• The music for the game was well done. It help push the story through when needed and it was nice collecting items while it was in the background. Soothing~Story: 5/10• The story was short, the side stories were the other 1/2 of the game. The side stories didn't help drive the main narrative through to the end, so the main story was lacking background or involvement. Beating the game, you do feel "meh" for the ending given.Characters: 6/10• The main character has some good swag, just not enough story for them to develop any relationship with. What's a hero without a story?Enjoyment: 7/10• The game is enjoyable for a precision platformer. A nice fresh mechanic to platformers while maintaining nostalgia. It was pleasant!Conclusion: 7/10• Good Action Hack-Slash Precision Platformer

_childDocuments_.review: this is a fantastic game. i love seeing indie developers make 3D platformers (my fav genre!). i was pleasantly surprised by the fluidity of movement & how expansive the world is in this game. it takes atmospheric inspiration from dark souls, hollow knight, and LOZ: Ocarina of Time & gameplay inspiration from Super Mario Sunshine & A Hat in Time to make something truly special and unique. sometimes the controls don't seem to work when they should (especially with wall jumping), but nothing that seriously hampers my enjoyment.i just wish there was a map!!!!!!! there are so many secrets and lil areas in this game & it can be incredibly difficult to remember where you have and haven't been. you might be able to remember while playing, but if you step away from this game for even a little bit and try to come back to it, you'll probably be incredibly lost. pretty much every 3D platformer has some kind of map or at least a clearly marked/laid out central hub to guide players through levels, so i'm not sure why the developers just...didn't include one in this game. but i digress

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly inspired by games like Hollow Knight and classic Zelda games, I was convinced I was going to enjoy myself. _childDocuments_.review: Ok, before i start this, i just wanted to put this disclaimer here: i am definitely biased towards this game due to the length of time I've been following it. however, i will do my best to keep my biases out of this, just know that they do exist. just wanted to give that heads up. anyways, blue fire time.there is so much i love about this game. the visuals are great, the soundtrack is awesome and stands up regardless of repetition, its nice and difficult, its one of those games that just oozes charm. however, the crowning jewel of it has to be the gameplay, especially the movement. it is quite frankly phenomenal. it handles EXACTLY as it feels like it should, and feels so good to play! as such, its actually a really good speed game (both i and my hours of play time on record can testify to this fact).unfortunately, it does fall short at a few places, specifically with the low amount of dungeons, and the story. first, the dungeon point. unfortunately, for budget and time reasons, the devs had to scrap a notable amount of content, leaving some things feeling kinda unfinished. HOWEVER! things might not stay that way for long. you see, the devs are actually hard at work on making dlc for the game, and from what they've hinted, they'll be reintroducing cut content back into the game! (oh and also there is a decent chance that a void editor will be added). to be honest, those are pretty much my only complaints.so, to summarize, the game is really good, especially with the gameplay, and the story falls kinda flat but is otherwise enjoyable. this is my first time doing a review, so i probably forgot to mention some stuff, but yeah. i highly recommend getting this, it is definitely worth itp.s. don't ask about the ducks, that's an inside joke from the discord (btw if you like the game, feel free to join the discord. everyone is super nice. also we have ducks as priorly mentioned)

_childDocuments_.review: This game desperately wants to be a 3D Hollow Knight. Unfortunately, the only aspect which stands up to the inspiration is the art style.The combat is completely bland. Enemies are few and far-between, and your options are laughably limited. The core 3-swing combo is detrimental to use, as most enemies will attack and hit you after you're locked into the third swing but before they get hit by it. There is a block and a ranged attack, however the former is infinitely clunkier to use than just dashing away from an enemy and then dashing back, the latter is laughably underpowered and borderline useless, and both share a limited resource in mana, which is never really explained. I 100% completed the game, never used the fireball and rarely used the shield, and still have no idea what gets you your mana back. The platforming is most of what this game is, either tranversal within the game world, or completing the linear 'Void' sub-areas for HP upgrades. In fact, the 'Spirits' (literally just Hollow Knight's 'Charms') overwhelmingly affect your movement over combat, and I never found myself using any of them that didn't boost my movement in some manner. The Void stages remind me of the secret stages in Super Mario Sunshine, only you keep your entire kit within them. They are rated in difficulty, which you can see before entering, and there are only 2 significantly difficult ones (each of which took me 30-45 minutes alone). That said, the game does handle failure and checkpoints quite well. The Void subareas don't punish you for failure beyond returning you to a checkpoint when you fall (unlike my main gripe with Hollow Knight, where failing a platforming section too many times sent you all the way back to a spawn point with a death), but they do suffer from a LOT of wasted time. Many of them are very vertical, and the only 'death plane' is at the very bottom, so if you're on the final checkpoint, and fall, you have to fall for a good 5-10 seconds before getting to try again. This adds up VERY quickly on the harder Voids, where you also have cycles and moving platforms to wait on, dragging each attempt at a section out a frustrating amount.Additionally, Blue Fire suffers from the classic 3D platforming problem of a terrible camera. While I never encountered any times where the camera moved itself into a poor position, I would often be trying to tackle a platforming section, get past something like a swinging sawblade, and then have the same sawblade cut off the camera while I was trying to do the next bit. Or just being forced to platform in odd ways while also having to pilot the camera to see what I'm doing, while adjusting my angle on the left stick to continue moving the direction I want as the camera spins. And don't get me started on the total lack of depth perception. I cannot count the amount of times I was hit by a trap or attack that I would have swore was relatively either in front or behind me. Many long sections of swinging traps in some voids are completely devoid of any ground or other possible indicator of where exactly the hazards are, beside that they're swinging by in some general area.The atmosphere, at least, is pretty good. The art is gorgeous, and the music fits the setting alright. It's not a soundtrack I'd return to, and I never found myself just looking around enjoying the scenery, but it works. The story (and the writing as a whole) leaves quite a bit to be desired. In fact, a good bit of the main storyline does feel directly ripped from Hollow Knight (defeat 3 big bosses to open door to final boss, the main character being a smol construct of the evil force and the good force, etc). The parts that don't are okay, but are often just presented via blocks of exposition.The biggest disappointment, in my opinion, was the dungeons. They were actually pretty good! Legend of Zelda format, with single use keys and a 'key item' that granted a new ability partway through. The problem is that there really aren't any. There's the first 'tutorial' dungeon, then you are immediately sent to the second with hints about there being 5, one for each god that needs saving. Then, after the second, that particular plotline is thrown away entirely, and it shifts to the Hollow Knight-esque 'explore to find the 3 bosses to open the door to the final boss'. There's another 'dungeon' later on, with one of these macguffin bosses at the end of it, but it's significantly worse than the others, and mostly just consists of a few linear platforming challenges, then leaving to go get the key for the boss from a random cutscene.I 100% completed the game in under 9 hours, with no guides at all. If you really like 3D platformers, and also enjoyed Hollow Knight, you might get your money worth if you buy Blue Fire on sale, but ultimately, I don't think I can recommend it at full price. If you are interested in Blue Fire, and  played Hollow Knight, go play Hollow Knight first, then come back if you're REALLY jonesing for a mediocre 3D platformer inspired by it.

_childDocuments_.review: I finshed the main story and all expect 2 or 3 of the basic (none-DLC) voids. You can probably finish the game in 10h or so, if you tried. Side stories and such add quite a bit more hours. That said, the game doesn't really tell you very clearly where to go. There was one point where wandered around for 1-2 hours because I did not understand where to go. Without googling I would not have found it. The story is fine. It's nothing special but it's not bad. The secrets, hidden quests and so on, also the side quests, are actually really nice and fun. The combat is very meh. You don't have a lot of options. You usually just use dash and smash things with your sword. You have a limited amount of mana for ranged attack which can help but also does terrible damage.Early enemies are kinda easy. Later ones are a bit tedious. Firing laser at you every second and if you have no mana for the ranged attack it's very tricky to take some enemies out. There is also a wurm that hides when you get near him. And he snipes you across the map. You have to perfectly parry his attack to kill him. Nothing tells you that and it can be very, very frustrating if you do not know that.Overall though, the game feels like it's 80% finished. A lot of mechanics are there, but just don't feel very fluent. Your standard 3 attack pattern does a medium dash at the end. You probably will dash off a platform at some point. Doesn't happen very often, but it's just annoying. The wall grab/jump is miserable. Sometimes you grab a wall when you don't want to, stoping your jump when you needed to get height and killing you. Other times wall grabs will not register when you are trying to wall jump. It's dumb.Voids. Voids are a really cool idea. And they are just.... not as fun as they should be. A lot of crystals or platforms are quite small. And since they are floating somewhere in the air it's rather hard to judge distances. In additional, you have to look at so many different things from so many different angles. It's very easy to miss something, die and then have to start over again. It would be way more enjoyable if you could actually move as you wanted in the harder ones. However, often it feels like the camera or game itself screws you over. I don't regret buying the game. If I new beforehand how the gameplay would feel though, I wouldn't have bought it. If you are calm and patient and don't mind games where you sometimes get screwed by the game. I think this is a great to pick up. If you want a game that plays smooth and where you can only blame yourself when you die, then it's probably not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gemThis game starts out a bit like Dark Souls - no context, same slow, dead, gothic vibes, no tutorial save for a few ground messages about basic controls, and a slowly revealed history told by barely coherent NPCs showing up in the weirdest places, with a single central town (well, no spoilers). What I was not prepared for this game to be is living up the high standards set by Hollow Knight: this game a very serious platformer, where you start out with a basic jump, but eventually you'll get more movement options that I really don't want to spoil away here, allowing you access to previously unaccessable areas of the world map that you may have passed a couple times since. Which is important, because the world is smartly interconnected, and there is no world map, local map, quest marker for anything, to guide you: you are completely on your own, and I loved this because I was forced to remember everything, and I highly recommend you to go in blindly and use no wikipedia or youtube guide (I did not one switch where I needed 4 and missed only 1, than had to facepalm how could I forget that long poisonous hall I never went through despite having the abilities to do so for a long time at that point). Combat will forever remain simple, bosses are kind of easy, but it's not really the point, the point is always exploration, platforming, remembering where you may have came across cute, weird, and generally goodhearted NPCs you can interact with. Also you can find emotes that you may think is not a huge deal in a singleplayer game, but doing the right emote at the right place (little marker on the floor depicting the emote) will get you a new equipment, so you can find really fancy new character skins and stronger swords (there is only one weapon with increasingly stronger attack damage but trust me, it's that kind of game where this is enough).What the game truly excels at is platforming. Movement and controls are incredibly fluid and comfortable, the map design is awesome and keeps expanding the already known locations with new layers as you grow, camera is smartly used (there are looking glasses sometimes offering you alternative angles if you are not that much into finding a new platform that is usually hidden by a wall you could jump over, just did not think so if you should). Also there are Voids, which are essentially standalone challenge maps, which if you successfully finish will increase your maximum HP and you'll need that for the final boss. Also you get a neat skin if you finish them all. This is one of the very, very few games where I did everything to the point of 100%-ing it out with all Achievements, and while 12 hours playtime doesn't seem like much, it very much is. The game doesn't feel short at all, nor too long, it ends where it should, although the ending is a bit abrupt (you defeat the final boss, and the credits IMMEDIATELY roll, no ending cutscene or anything, or showing the fate of the world, the people you met, or you, it's just... over in 1 second). But!You loved this game, and you want more of it: here comes the Void Maker, a free upgrade to the game where everyone gets a map maker to create their own insane platforming challenge maps, and share it with overs. And suddenly this game is Trackmania, and oh boy the content just never ends. Highly recommended at roughly 50% off if you are from a poorer region like me (or as part of any bundle, you may even have it from a Humble Choice / Bundle and not be aware of it), and recommended if the full price is your hourly wage.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for 2,6 hours now, and did 10 %. It seems like a shorter game, but hey, it's not as expensive too. So it's a good deal!This game feels like a wild mix of Legend of Zelda: Windwaker, Mario 64 and Dark Souls.Here is why:- Fighting, the health and inventory system and generel the controls are very inspired bei Legend of Zelda. You have little hearts as life points and you have a similar fighting and lock on system.- The void levels feels like the vertical towerish levels from Mario 64.- Your progression through the world is linear with some hubs and short cuts. Together with the you "you die you start at the safepoint. And if you die again you loose your money." system is clearly inspired by Dark Souls.So far I really like this game. The emote system, you learn emotes to interact with objects and npcs, is creativ and the mix of these games works for me very well. Together with the 100% accurate movement, every fail is really your fault, its very motivating.Only critisism I have is that there could be more ambient music. There are only a few zones with ambient music. And these are superb. That's why I really want more of it.
