_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is really likeable, you can see that devs put in effort and soul, but the game is really lacking in gameplay design.Graphics/visual style and music are on point.In almost every other aspect there are always some major oversights:Platforming:Overall, controls are good and there are some good platforming sections in overworld. The entire thing reminds me most of A Hat in Time - similar speed, inertia, movement physics - but Blue Fire is a bit more advanced. Now the problems. First off, a game does a very poor job of telling you where you can go and which spot is out of reach yet. You might struggle with a ledge that seems just a tiny bit out of reach or even on the opposite - sequence break another spot. The platforming challenges called voids are big (bigger than should be allowed sometimes) gauntlets that return you to the beginning if you fail. And they really ARE long. Combined with awful depth perception inside them and the fact that you cannot see your shadow on some platforms makes them painfully frustrating. They might quickly turn from a side attraction to the worst part of the game. And this game reeeaaaly likes to put those voids everywhere, while not letting you play them from at least a checkpoint. Fall damage. In a 3D platformer. Granted, you can negate it with any of your moves, but why is this a concern in the first place?Environment blurs and stretches while dashing/falling. Mmm, headache fuel.Combat:Actually, this one is awful in its entirety. It feels like they were making a decent platformer and then forced *this* in. The only good enemy type to fight against is a typical sword-slashing knight. That’s it. Good relative to the rest. All your foes do little to none attack indication or wind-up, those that do are incredibly slow.There are small critters that attack you immediately after you step close to them, some of which can get you stunlocked. Then we have pulse-emitters just to annoy you during platforming. Then the exploding blobs which blow up with no proper visual cue of radius or timing. Then the laser blobs - go from boring to stupidly overpowered with each new iteration.Bosses - can't say much about them or if  they’re really bad or good. Just mediocre. They can be a challenge but are at the same time a chore.Level design:Overworld is mostly fine with some nicely placed secrets, decorations change frequently, layouts rarely repeat.Additionally, some areas have some old Zelda-like dungeons. They’re zelda dungeons, that’s all I can say. Maybe you hate this design, maybe you like it. On the other hand, in many locations you won’t feel any verticality at all. The environments might seem small, but they are a bit labyrinthian, while you have no map, good luck.There is a problem with knowing where you can or can’t go I mentioned in platforming. The game forces you to visit an NPC to ‘pop souls’, in other words sell stuff for currency. And currency is another story here.Checkpoints are extremely rare and make you pay for them.Overworld is divided into rooms which load after you go in. And sometimes there is an obstacle on the other side. Now go back and wait for it to load again.This is hard to explain, but there is almost nothing to help you quickly get back to action after you fall into a pit/liquid. Most rooms have spots that bring you back on every entrance. No more, no less. And times when the game has the decency to face you in the right direction might compete in rarity with checkpoints. Inventory and journal:You can get different looking robes. Cool.Journal though is filled with redundant information about completed quests and empty spots for quests you haven’t yet found. They made the emotion list dynamic, what’s the problem here?Limited wallet. Did we travel back in time somehow? An awful fragment of the past, at least devs back then did it to restrict story progress. Here, as far as I know, it's just an annoyance. A big stain of ♥♥♥♥.Spirits - an analogue of Hollow Knight charm system. They contrast with the game’s style greatly. They’re more like some scribbles. Maybe their effects  are better? No.I’ll summarize here - if you have a high pain tolerance and a lot of patience - try it. It’s good at first, maybe you’ll get into it and forgive the game’s flaws. It has blatant disregard for your time and almost never exercises good design practises, but at the same time it has a charming feel to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is we have Ocarina of time at home.Its a good game, I had 2 game stopping crashes/bugs on my whole 12 hour run.Exploration wise it doesnt mask its inspiration in zelda, but the jumping and dashing elevate it to a new level, with the right combination of spirits (buffs that you collect that alter certain of your properties) you can attain a range of movement that feels downright broken and trivializes even the hardest voids.You can be an OP double dashing, tripple jumping, platform summoning, blade dash jumping monster but you have to earn it.For sure it was worth my time and money, despite it having issues that show the size of its developer the game has love and care put into it that rises above its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: The word I'm looking for is frustrating. Well actually the words I'm looking for would make steam draw a little row of hearts, so let's just stick with frustrating.the movement feels slippery, the combat is insultingly easy, everything is poorly explained (I was taught how to emote but not how to parry) and the level design is so bad that there has to be a cutscene at the start of some rooms to tell you where the points of interest are. That just feels lazy imo.The thing that made me call it was early on where a section of platforming has you running around on some pipes above an acid pit. Pretty standard fair for this particular genre, but the edges of the pipe were fully rounded so going even a hair over the edge meant you would just slip off into the pit.I'm sure my opinion on this game isn't helped by the fact I just finished Pseudoregalia (a far superior platformer) but I don't think my conclusion would have been much better under normal circumstances. For sure a lot of my complaints could be fixed by the sacred art of git gud, but alas gitting gud can't fix the boring art style and the bland sound design.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It seemed to have so many elements that I like to see in games. But unfortunately every element in this game falls short, leaving any part of the game lackluster at best. One of my biggest gripes is just how stiff and kinda lifeless the animation for everything in the game feels. That combined with decent, at best, sound design leaves combat and platforming kind of unsatisfying. This game is meant to be about the combat and platforming but when both of those elements fall short and aren't challenging, rewarding, or fluid then I think there is a problem. Anytime that platforming was a challenge it was more frustrating than anything else. And subpar platforming combined with no map, exploration also suffers. It's fun to use the movement that you get in the game but the world never really pulled me in. Things felt like they were there because they had to be for the sake of the game instead of having an interesting world to explore. The plot felt really unnatural at points, too. Things would just happen. There is a character in the game that is just a plot device, they show up just to shove exposition in your face, give you some big plot item to progress which made things feel disjointed and forced. So it would quite literally feel like the game just said "Oh hey, you got this far, well let me just unlock that part of the game for you now." Now despite my complaints I don't think this game is bad. This game has some good ideas, but I feel it doesn't execute them well enough and it all just falls short. It all just feels unpolished and unfinished which is what is stopping me from saying this is a good game. Overall, I really wanted to like this game but unfinished and unsatisfying mechanics with very stiff animation keep it from being something I can strongly recommend. 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like boring mashy combat and terrible platforming? Then this game is for you. It looks great. It sounds great. But actually playing the game? It's some of the most obnoxious platforming I've ever had the displeasure of experiencing. When you're not fighting with the camera to figure out where you need to go, because you probably won't see it, there's always something that's just out of your range trying to mess with your progress on top of the poor visibility. The combat is about as complicated as the "combos" in Sonic 06. I.E. there's one button and you press it 3-4 times and there's your combo. It's kinda boring and very dangerous at times. Hero Kid here like to dash forward about 4 feet when you hit the attack button and that's not too bad except when you're standing on a platform that's 6 feet wide. You'll find yourself throwing Mask Kid off platforms unintentionally all the time in most of the areas in this game. This is made even more annoying by the fact that the ground doesn't exist. It's just not there. Almost every area in the game has water/pits/goo/whatever all of the place and you've gotta play hopscotch to get anywhere and if you fall in, you take a little bit of damage and go back to a spot that's always farther away than you want it to be so you can do it all over again. Now I realize that may not sound too terrible but consider this. You've got a 20 foot gap to span with your jump and dash. That jump and dash will take you 20 feet and 2 inches. So if you're not nearly Mega Man pixel jumping some of these situations you're gonna have problems. Oh and before I forget, save points? I think I've seen maybe 2 in the game and the most recent one is an area back from where I'm sitting. So when I end up getting a game over because a little dude knocks me off a tower because I can't get the camera where I need it to attack the guy, I don't start the area I'm in over... I have to go back to a previous area with those 20 foot jumps to get back to the second area with the 20 foot jumps and the 6 foot platforms, just to get back to the structure I've gotta jump up and around and inside and out just to get to the top and get knocked off by an enemy I can't see or target. Again. And again. And again. This game started out feeling pretty good. Kind of a Zelda clone with some Souls influences in it but that quickly went away and the whole thing turned into those obstacle courses from Mario Sunshine, but with hidden enemies just waiting to do their AOE burst attack (which they all pretty much seem to have) and knock you back down the well you just spent 7 minutes trying to find a way out of. And if you're lucky, you'll only hit what little ground there is and take some fall damage and not end up in the drink and have to go back to the beginning of the room... or the one before that... or the one before that. I had hoped this game would be fun. It was picked for me to play by a patron of my YouTube channel and the first night we streamed it, it was pretty good. Night 3 out of 4 here and I cannot wait for next Monday to get over with so I can uninstall this very pretty to look at, and very nice to listen to garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire isn't a bad game but I just never had fun with it. It looks fine, controls fine, has okay combat, and I like what it's going for with a mix of Hollow Knight and Zelda. But it also has none of the charm of either of those games and is just a meandering, dull experience. I don't think levels were procedurally generated but the overall world structure is so sloppy and bizarre that it sometimes feels that way. It's never fun to explore, checkpoints are few and far between, and signposting is nonexistant. And why are key NPCs that you're expected to return to buried in the middle of dungeons where otherwise you have no reason? Blue Fire is also home to maybe the worst "town" I've ever seen in a game. I can't even describe what it was going for.Again, there's nothing mechanically really wrong with this game but it's just not worth the time to play. The story is especially bland as it's the same generic fantasy tripe you've heard a hundred times. What if there were gods but one god was bad but then also there were knights and one knight was bad and you're the only one that can save this world for reasons that aren't explained even a bit. Also for some reason there's a character that's more capable than you that's always behind doors you unlock waiting for you who only exists to lore dump and then leave instead of actually helping for...reasons. Ugh.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game with a nice artstyle, very nice movement, a rather loose "story" and terrible combat.I really enojoyed the movement and the world just perfectly complemented it. It starts out quite snappy with a basic jump and can be upgraded to a tripple jump with a double dash and a spin attack for even more haight. All of that works and feels quite polished.It feels very good to breeze trough areas you had previously a hard time getting around in.There isn't much Story to speak of, which is good for me since i don't care for most of them in this type of game.That "I don't know where or who i am, all i know is that i must kill!"-meme sums this story up pretty good.All the upgrades you find are usefull in one way or another depending on your playstyle, but none of them will change your playstyle drastically. The Weapons where quite dissapointing, none of them had any special ability or something like that... straight up just change the look and damage. And the worst part was that i had to buy the strongest weapon, i got it quite early as well, so it was just very disheartening to see every other weapon i actually found out in the wild or got as a quest reward to be worse.But now we're coming to my biggest gripe with this game, the combat. I'm an avid Souls and Zelda player which attracted me to this game in the first place. Still i had a very hard time getting used to the combat, and i yet have to get properly used to the "rythm".The main problem lies in the fact that besides the spin attack the combat never evolves beyond the standard 3-Hit combo you have from the very beginning. The fact that i have no invincibility frames when dodging and enemies don't get staggered (except for flying enemies) change how you have to react to them. While this doesn't need to be a bad thing it sadly work against this game. Most problematic is the whole enemie concept. Most enemies have only 1 attack, maybe 2 for sword wielding foes, they will relentlessly spam those attacks as soon as you're in range. Sneaking up on them is impossible.So unless you can totally overwhelm them or you perfectly parry all attacks you'll be stuck doing hit and run attacks until said enemie is dead, since most enemies do AOE attacks.But once again, in the right setting this could be a good thing.Sadly enemies barely telegraph their attacks and their tempo and "rythm" just makes it hard to even want to fight them. It's really hard to explain.My lock on breaking constantly event thou the enemie is still visible and the dash not always going where i expect it to go makes it hard to fight flying enemies until you get more jumps and the upgrade for more melee range. While i could keep pocking holes into this combat system (like how you have to charge your spinn attack and as long as you hold that charge you can't do a normal attack anymore, and you loose that charge once you use a ladder or get hit by something) i can gladly say that enemies are rather sparse, at first i tought this was a negative point, but once i realised how bad the combat is, it was quite the blessing.This still doesn't help that the bosses where the worst i have seen in a loooong time. Their boring designs and rather unfair and unfun movesets (the rythm problem is most apparent here) their only saving grace is their minimal HP, so they atleast dont last long.The only boss i somewhat enjoyed was the "fish" in the water temple. He was the only enemie with a semblance of a good moveset and was actually fun to fight. In the end i would say that If this game had a bigger focus on combat and less on the platforming i couldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: My top indie game of the past year.Blue Fire is a wonderful little mix of every Zelda game with a touch of Souls for flavor. The game's visual design is reminiscent of Wind Waker, down to the individual dead rats and gems. The main currency is gained by breaking jars and pots and other world items of the sort, while others are gained through completing challenges and defeating enemies. The game has 2 types of powerups; permanent abilities gained through story progression, and spirits which have their own special slots and can be swapped at save points.The story is vague and your goals are usually spelled out, it's a very direct game. There is no missable content, then entirety of the game can be completed without worry of skipping anything, all game features are available without need of Internet access.The game offered both Normal and Hard difficulty modes upon first starting, Expert mode became available after completing my Normal mode playthrough. Expert mode is permadeath, so you'd better be prepared for this one!The majority of the trials (pocket dimension challenges similar in style to BOTW shrines) were pretty easy to do, but a couple got downright mean. They were optional, so no harm done there.Here are my times for total completion:Normal base game, around 8 hours.Normal DLC, around 1.5 hours.Hard base game, in progress.Hard DLC, TBD.Expert base game, heck naw.Expert DLC, also heck naw.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be straight with saying that I'm on the fence about giving this a negative review. I might come back and review this after fully finishing the game.I'll also say that unlike others, I've not experienced any crashes yet so I can't comment on how bad that is, though I expect there will be followup patches to correct those issues anyway.My biggest problem though is the insane amount of platforming. I stayed spoiler-free going into this and simply knew that it had elements of The Legend of Zelda, Hollow Knight, and Dark Souls. This sounded like the perfect set of games to mix together and indeed, in the very beginning of the game there are plenty of hints that this is the experience you're in for.However, as you start getting into the story, the combat doesn't ramp up but instead the platforming does. And by platforming, I mean that if you miss a jump then you usually fall into a bottomless pit (or the equivalent of that) and lose significant amounts of life. And of course, the only way to increase your health pool is to complete shrines which are essentially ramped-up platforming stages.You know this game is for you if you say yes to all of the following:- Do you enjoy punishing platforming to navigate between main areas? - Is the idea of reaching a new town boring to you, specifically because towns are usually safe spaces free from getting hurt?-  Do you instead wish you could be forced to engage in platforming exercises to navigate said towns, knowing that if you miss a jump then you'll be granted the gift of having to do all that sweet, sweet platforming all over again in order to meet whichever NPC you were originally looking for?- Do you enjoy the idea of entering platforming sub-stages while ALREADY in a main dungeon (which, of course, is driven solely by platforming)?- Do you basically wish someone took the saying "When all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail" and applied it to a video game, with the hammer being "platforming"?I mean, to be honest, the game isn't bad. It's just that I wish they turned down the platforming dial a bit and instead focused a bit more on other core gaming mechanics (e.g. combat) to deliver a more balanced experience. I'll also add a side note and say that items are a bit too expensive in the game. Expect to spend a fair amount of time hitting barrels to collect souls so you can buy stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the 8 hours I spent on it, however if you're a fan of its (very obvious) influences and artstyle, you might still enjoy it a lot. While it periodically provides some decent platforming bits during the Void sections, Blue Fire's barebones story, clunky combat and, often times, confusing level layout leave a lot to be desired. There are occasional moments of brilliance here (Stoneheart City is a BEAUTIFUL place, especially to just mess around jumping and dashing), but they are very few and far between.Much of the combat in the game is super super basic, being able to cheese most (if not all) enemies by dashing on top of them and repeatedly slashing them, and I fail to see the reasoning behind adding so many weapons when all they do is add just a little bit more damage, when they could have instead made it so different weapons had different effects (such as some ice blades making enemies slower on hit, for example). Many of the sidequest are simply going from point A to point B to point C, and the lack of a map really shows here, as many many times I was left running around aimlessly (especially at the start) not knowing where to go at any moment. This unfortunately lead to me sequence breaking the game many many times using collision in the scenery and getting around nooks and crannys in walls, reaching ledges I shouldn't be able to or making my way to places I really should not be at. My biggest example of this was quite early in the game, entering Temple of Gardens from Stoneheart City I obviously could not cross the ledge to progress, but since the game's forte is in its platforming, I assumed that I was supposed to make my way around it, across the walls and drop down to an area below, which left me walking around aimlessly for a good while before I realised I was not supposed to be there.However, as you play through it you can FEEL the potential this game had, and I believe that with just some polishing up here and there, the devs have an excellent, excellent 3D platformer and metroidvania fusion on their hands by their next title.

_childDocuments_.review: "Blue Fire" is a captivating entry into the metroidvania genre, often recommended as a "3D Hollow Knight." While this comparison holds true in terms of concept, it falls short in execution when compared to the richly detailed world of Hollow Knight.The combat in "Blue Fire" is undeniably fun, albeit a bit easy (especially for seasoned Metroidvania players). There are three difficulty options, and I picked "normal," which felt too easy. The platforming segments (which are all optional and each provide a maximum HP upgrade) are enjoyable as well, with most being very easy, though some present a real challenge.One of the most intriguing aspects of "Blue Fire" is its nostalgic charm. Many areas in the game evoke a sense of familiarity, such as the Lava area, which reminded me of Skyward Sword. However, the environments, while familiar, are ultimately forgettable. None of them stand out as particularly new or unique, as they fall into familiar tropes like sewers, castles, lava areas, and temples. That said, the graveyard area stood out with its artistic charm and is the best area for me in terms of visual appeal.Unfortunately, the lore and story of "Blue Fire" are not particularly engaging. I can't recall the names of any characters, as none made a significant impact or stuck in my mind. The merchants didn't offer items or services memorable enough to commit their locations or inventories to memory. Additionally, the protagonist doesn't seem to interact meaningfully with the narrative, and I was left unsure of his connection to the story—perhaps I missed something.Despite its shortcomings, "Blue Fire" stands out as a solid indie game. Its unique take on the metroidvania style in a 3D environment offers a refreshing experience that fans of the genre will appreciate. If you're looking for an entertaining and well-performing game, "Blue Fire" is definitely worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game and it is very close to day 1 release but man it needs more polish and level design changes. So you expect a reward for using the environment to access a hard area but instead you find it just soft locks you. Everything in the game you can buy gets insanely expensive (especially the save points right after buying an expensive elevator) unless you grind currency in the game which is a waste of time. So many issues right now but there is a lot of potential there. Platforming feels nice and the exploration is fun (could use more rewards or direction early game) and combat is fun but simple. If they can fix some of these core issues I'll change my  recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like the idea of a hack-and-slash 3D platformer zelda-like, buy this game, on sale or not. It's good fun. Use a controller.This game is great. I 100%'d it twice pre-DLC, did it  for the DLC, and I'm still considering reinstalling it for another round. Buy it, full price or on sale. The movement is hugely customizable if you get the optional upgrades and satisfying even with just the stuff you get on the main path. You'll be able to do some really wacky movement options and skips when you're at HALF the maximum potential.Besides the fact that there are so many movement options to help you dodge and position, don't expect the world from the combat - it's perfectly fine and serviceable, but it's not where the game shines. _childDocuments_.review: Pros: Fun simplistic combat and exploration. You can build your skills/powers, and as you do so, you inevitably enable yourself to explore further. I like the art style. The difficulty took about 20 minutes to get used to, but once i got the swing of it, it's been smooth sailing from that point onward. As may others have said, it does feel like Hollow Knight meets Zelda in many ways, unfortunately that brings me to the cons. Cons: The story, to me, isn't gripping. I'm 8 hours in and i've already forgotten what the purpose of this adventure was. Its not to say it's poorly written, it just hasn't kept my attention. I know to explore, and when i find enemies, i destroy them. That's enough for me, but it may not be enough for everyone. There's no map. This is not TERRIBLE, but it adds an element of difficulty and frustration that didn't need to be there. All doors look the same, so you do need to commit the routes to memory when back tracking. On a positive side of not having a map, It did cause me to go back to explore prior locations later in the game, and it led to me finding new and helpful items. I would absolutely recommend someone who enjoys games like Hollow Knight, Ori and the Will of the Wisp, and Zelda.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like the Legend of Zelda, and 3d platformers like a Hat in Time or any 3d mario game, than you'll love this. The only gripe I have for the game is it can be easy to get lost but this minor downside is nothing compared to how amazing this game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me a lot of how Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time with the play style and feel. I really enjoyed this game and beat it in it's entirety within 14 hours. Some of the story doesn't direct you in the needed direction so may take some figuring out to proceed. Only ran into a couple crashes/issues.First issue was in the Fire Keep near the first void. I got stuck between the wood frame and the wall while trying to dash to scale it for the spirit.Second issues was while collecting soul fragments in for the final lord while in the Firefall River. While collecting the last soul fragment while the air tunnel pushes you up caused my character to fly during the cut scene so the 3/4 didn't appear and instead the game locked up.Third issue was after playing the game for a good bit of time where I beat the final boss then loaded the save game. I tabbed out of the game to compare what I unlocked with what's on the web for if I missed a spirit. The game crashed with an unreal engine log.I most enjoyed the user interface as it indicates all your quests with completion to help keep track of your progress. Boss fights were still challenging and the voids give you a break from the combat in a relaxed manner. I wish the game had more content to it but feels like it is still growing/developing.With the defeat of the queen it would be nice to collect the soul fragments of the former five gods for restoring them to their temples. I think that would be a nice aspect to bring life back to the land/castle. Maybe even reward the warrior/hero with new blades by each of the gods as you restore them mainly for aesthetic. Then give the option to fight the former boss in a special shadow realm to revisit the battle scene for the fun of it by talking to the (shrunken) god of that temple.

_childDocuments_.review: You're basically in for 3D Hollow Knight with some discreet zelda-esque dungeons (puzzles swapped for platforming challenges), and that is a good thing! Though landing out of a dash in 3D will never be as simple/intuitive as in 2D, the controls are tight, the platforming challenge's are solid (but nothing exceptionally unique), and the performance is *spectacular*. Combat's a bit bland, but it's also pretty quick so not too big a mark against.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game "100%"(not a few cosmetics you have to grind barrels for).  As a game designer I have a lot I could say about this game, but I'll keep it simple. It has amazing potential and could be great if it just cooked in the oven a bit longer. Other than the movement, the game feels like it is in BETA. I wouldn't pay A$30 for it. I think if one of the Zelda, Hat in Time or Dark Souls influences were removed, the game could thrive! (Dark Souls I think)PROS;- Movement feels amazing and works really well- Very satisfying to play- Looks and sounds awesome- Decent amount of game and challenge- Later boss battles are fun- Great level design for the platformingCONS;- Lots of crashing and a few major bugs which ruin the experience a bit.- It tries to wear too many hats and suffers in it's major areas because of it.- Combat isn't satisfying and almost felt annoying/pointless- Some of the platforming level design can be buggy and and stretched to the characters limits- Checkpoints in frustrating positions, creating lots of wasted time to get around simple areasAll in all the game is good and I love the concept, but with other games like Hades that have came out recently, it doesn't even compare for the price. If there was less attention to the 'Cool Factor' and less in the kitchen sink, it would be amazing!7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, one of the best games I've played in a long time. Dark souls meets Zelda with metriodvania aspects. The game is not as unforgiving as Dark souls but still has that challenging combat. Having the movement mechanics from metroidvania style games like double jump, dash, and wall jumps in a 3D space is brilliant, fun, and really brings the parkour of the game to a new level. Even when I was struggling to do some of the more challenging parkour failing again and again I was still having fun. I always felt like I was in control, every death felt fair. Every time I died I knew what I did wrong, not once did I feel like I got screwed over by the game. There are very few games I 100%, but I enjoyed every second of it. 10/10 A must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Played through everything 100% while streaming to my girlfriend and I enjoyed it! I got it on my Switch a while back but I wanted to switch over to PC because some of the challenging platforming was a bit trickier on the lower resolution of the Switch. (also I wanted to get all the achievements on steam)This game centers a lot around platforming and movement mechanics. It's quite challenging so it may not be for everyone, but luckily the hardest platforming in the game is optional content.The game is structured somewhere between a Soulslike, a Metroidvania, or a Zelda game, and plays like a hack-n-slash/3D platformer. There's also cool little challenge stages called Voids that remind me of A Hat in Time. These voids reward you with HP and in my opinion are way more fun than grinding shrines in the open world Zelda titles. I've completed every void and they definitely can be a bit challenging, but none are too bad.The boss fights were pretty fun, however some of them felt like I just had to take damage in the process of beating them, which hurts the completionist in me because sometimes I like to hitless the bosses in the games I play. In the case of this game I decided I'm good with just beating them and progressing but there was definitely room for some polish for the bosses/combat.As you'd expect with this kind of game there's a story with an obscure world/lore that's enough for you to understand how to progress at face value, but you can look deeper into if you really want to, similar to a Souls game or Hollow Knight. The ending was a bit brief though, I would have enjoyed a longer end sequence to tie everything together after beating the game!I could go beyond drawing comparisons to other games but I feel like players would benefit not knowing too much information going in, just enjoy the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 3d platformer that takes elements from Legend of Zelda and Dark Souls. Now imagine that it takes the jump and plattforming aspect of dark souls instead of LOZ. The jumping feels wrong. The Dash is controlled by how long you hold the button which is interesting considering the duration is between 0.1s and 0.3s, leading to you over/undershooting a lot. Combined with the camera which is completely player controlled, this leads to moments where you put the camera in top down only to jump against the wall because it was too high to grab.Oh speaking of grabbing, the game allows you to grab ledges to climb up, except when it doesn't and you fall to your death/the last point the game deems checkpoint worthy. Sometimes this is the very start of the level.Considering how frustrating the jumping is and how poorly the checkpoints are set you can only imagine how fun it is when combined with timed levers, you know the ones that already sucked in a good game like LOZ.I fought my way to the first dungeon to get my first progress item which gave me the ability to wall jump and run (with a limited stamina bar). But wall jumping does not automatically jump straight away from the wall, instead it uses the stick to determine if you want to jump 37° away into the next abyss (to not respawn on the last solid ground/before the ledge but a ladder you have to climb before you can try again). Oh and sometimes the wall grabbing works and other times you just fall along the wall (or the grabbing works but not high enough leading you to jumping too low to grab a ledge).Ok i though i will endure, but guess what, you know the time gated levers i mentioned earlier ? Combine them with this wall grab mechanic and absolute unintuitive level design and i decided i don't want to waste any more time, although i usally like LOZ-inspired games.I won't mention the combat which is barebones at best: you have a attack a parry where the timing is weird and the dash and most of the time attack attack dash is enough.The game needs some improvements before i would call it playable:-better checkpoints for jump and run areas (don't spawn me back at the very beginning because i couldn't grab the ledge caused by the camera) -stop with the timed levers, nobody likes them-maybe don't let items drop into the water, you know the water where you will get to the last respawn if you touch it.-improve the plattforming and rework some areas that are poorly builtSo all in all i would not recommend the game although there are some (although not original) features. If you are masochistic and want a plattformer that feels more like a tech demo, be my guest.

_childDocuments_.review: The best aspects of the core gameplay, puzzle solving mechanics, and music are PAINFULLY similar to elements of the games that influence this one. _childDocuments_.review: This was a very pleasant game to play. I loved immersing myself in the world, it was pretty, charming and felt good. Exploring was simple and satisfying and the progression while not complex felt really nice. It's simplistic but it knows that and just gives a chill time. It's a chill atmosphere and it completely charmed me from the moment I saw it. A very good game to relax and go through and I can see myself going back to it. The movement and abilities are fun, the rewards you get feel great, the art style and atmosphere is an experience in of itself.That being said it of course isn't perfect and by that I mean... theres a handful of things that really REALLY had me questioning it. The combat I can get over, it's simple but felt kind of inconvenient to deal with things and I really feel like it needed more fleshing out. In this case more enemy types and things to encourage your use of abilities rather than being model swaps of things that are annoying to fight. There wasn't much variety which is unfortunate because theres a ton of unique events that don't introduce new kinds of fights or challenges and some of the bosses make me think this could have been made a tad bit more interesting. This mixed with fact that combat is a bit clunky and impressive at times and it kinda sits weird with me.Another huge thing is it's direction, that is to say theres barely any. The thing is common sense can kinda get your through, the world itself isn't all too complex but the seeming lack of effort to give you any idea of where you're exploring through was a little infuriating. Important areas are mostly unlabeled or conspicuous, or sometimes you'll need to get to somewhere but what that thing is is completely unknown, and remembering stuff can be a pain because for some reason theres no mini map or any kind of marker or way points. I have no idea why, you'd think this would be very important but they straight up have no kind of map to understand the world better. It makes it infuriating to find where to go at times.And one last thing that was annoying where the bugs. Sometimes soft locking or almost soft locking but not only did it exasperate this games lack of direction by sometimes confusing me but it was just really damn annoying to traverse sometimes when the game just wouldn't respond properly. Crashed once or twice and while it's not a deal breaker MOST OF THE TIME, it is very much there as a problem. And not just that but sequence breaking was stupid easy. There's so many things you can just use to get places where you shouldn't that even a toddler can figure out to the point where I'm genuinely unsure if it's intentional or not and only confused me even more trying to figure out where to go.I would also mention that a lot of the platforming sections are a little dumb. Mainly the voids, some of those did not feel designed with the movement in mind, and by that I mean like the camera being an extra obstacle and there feels like theres a little too much of it but other than some frustrating voids I can live with it.I know I just spent the majority of this reviewing complaining about stuff, but I do genuinely think this game is a good time. I saw it, was immediately charmed and beat it in a few days and I'm very glad I did, this was a gaming experience worth having, I feel a bit of soul cleansing from it. Just be prepared to occasionally have to wade your way through a few issues every once in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played more than a couple of hours of this game so this review is my initial opinion. And that opinion is...Mixed but hopeful.First off, I grew up playing games like sonic 3 and Mario 64, I love a good platformer and one of my favourite games of recent history is "A Hat In Time". So when i saw another platformer with a tiny protagonist and high focus on mobility I was all in.Since this is a long review, here is the short version. For the most part, I have enjoyed the game with 2 notable exceptions which I will get to in a moment. First the good stuff: The animation, the aesthetic and the awsomeness of carrying two swords that are bigger then you are. The bad? Dialog and the 2 most dreaded words in the industry ... game...crashes ...Animation: a lot of games by indie developers all use free models they got from blender or unity and they are never that good. They are fine for place markers so you can work on scripting scenes, interactions and planning levels but when the time comes for you to pay for that super cool looking avatar or the well rendered furniture to make you game worth something, so many indie developers, who just want their game on the market by this point, don't seem to put the effort in. Not Blue Fire though. The theming and style of everything, the enemies, the hero even the rubble, it all matches and as someone who tried to design a game as a hobby i can tell you that is really bloody hard! There are no obvious graphical problems where characters glitched through walls or suddenly t posed for no reason (*cough* cyberpunk *cough*) and it all just blended together to make the game look and feel like a solid, polished cohesive unit.Aesthetic:  I loved the slightly creepy nature of the game i have seen so far. An abandoned castle? hell yes! creepy scince experiments? Hell Yes! An intrusive dark material that seems bent on consuming and destroying everything? HELL YES! Cartoon style? YES YES GOOD GOD GET OUT OF MY HEAD YES! The game has gone out of its way to make you feel there are hidden secrets for you to discover, in the first few minutes i passed dozens of locked doors an a was forced to jump over a pile of corpses that looked suspiciously like the protagonist.... That being said the option of a map would be useful, making the levels a creepy maze like castle makes for good game play at first but after you spend 5 minutes climbing over obstacles only to find you have been going in the wrong direction for 4 of them it does get a little grating. "Yes this is a lovely corridor with a giant pit in it, I can really appreciate the pit since i fell into it a dozen times while trying to find where I am going!!"....What was i saying? oh yes! I liked the styling of this game.Awesomeness of carrying 2 swords bigger then you are: well....That's just self explanatory.So... the negatives.... remember those? well here they are: Dialog and the dreaded Game crashes!Dialog: There is plenty of text and story line lying around in this game, at one point i came across a dried up fountain and it started talking to me! And while in real life I wouldn't expect gripping dialog from an inanimate object, if i was in a video game world I would expect that, if a developer was going to make a fountain talk, he would at least go out of his way to make it make sense!Seriously! some of the dialog feels like it has been translated from Chinese to English by someone who learned the language by watching Game of Thrones at 5x speed!  "Fierce warrior of the shadows, upon the dawn of shadows my brothers have fallen, I too fought the shadows. Through the tunnels, beneath the city filed with shadows..." I could go on. Either that fountain had just had a stroke or it stopped talking just before telling me to "insert slot b into tab n for joyful happiness!"  There is no audio in this game so patching dialog wouldn't be hard on a future update and I would suggest that some rewriting of the script may be needed because the level of repetitiveness of a few words broke the immersiveness and when a few words repeated over and over ruin an otherwise great game, it's a terrible waste.I mentioned a patch because oh god does it need one because...Game Crashes: I played for 2 hours and the game crashed 5 times! Luckily it is pretty good at saving progress so I only lost a couple of minutes each time but every time I moved from one area to another, there was a better than even chance the game would crash and kick me to my desktop! So....Conclusion:Would I recommend this game? YesWas this game well done? YesWere the controls a little finicky? Yes but not to the extent i would call it a negative pointDoes the game still need an update: Unfortunately yes.If you liked A hat in time, you will like this too. It's not perfect, as i said, the difference between the story hinted at by the world and what i have found is a big problem and the game does have some performance issues but I would and have recommended this game and at the end of the day, that says it all.The Orange Knight

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on 100% completion and 8.9 hours of gameplay. Would I recommend this game? Yes, this is a nice little game, and I really like its aesthetic. It has a cute vibe, but there’s also a level of grittiness that really helps build that atmosphere. Everything in the game works well together, from the sound design and music to the art style, which is really nice. While it’s a platformer with some bits that can be a bit challenging, overall, the game is very forgiving and quite easy.At the beginning of the game, the first few hours can feel a bit slow and confusing, but once you get more comfortable with the controls and have gained a few upgrades, the pace picks up depending on your playstyle. As for the gameplay, the main aspect is platforming, and to be honest, apart from a few of the void challenges, most of it was quite easy. The tricky bits were mostly about getting used to the mechanics. For instance, with the dash, it was just about understanding the distance it can cover, and the camera can sometimes be a bit annoying during platforming, making you do something you didn’t intend to.The game doesn’t do much hand-holding, so you may get a little lost at times, and in this aspect, it reminded me of how Dark Souls progresses. However, there aren’t many areas, and they are fairly linear and easy to learn, which actually works in favour of the game’s vibe. While there is combat, there honestly isn’t a lot of it. Enemies are either in small groups or pretty much alone, so combat is super easy. The boss fights are similar—nothing too difficult and very easy to understand. The only mechanic I didn’t fully grasp was the final boss fight, where it shoots out a big ball shield over the arena in phase one, but it was still easy enough to beat without fully understanding it, which should give you an idea of the game’s difficulty level.Overall, this is a nice little game that provides a mostly easy platforming experience with a few small challenges here and there. I would recommend waiting for a good sale, as I feel the base price is on the upper end of being considered reasonable for the content you get.All the achievements in this game are really easy, and you’ll get them all by simply playing through the game and completing all the quests—both the main and side quests. I had no issues unlocking any achievements.It might help to check a guide if you have trouble locating something needed for a quest, as you might get lost occasionally. But for the most part, you won’t need one, as you’ll naturally find everything you need while exploring and playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It has a certain charm like Hollow Knight, but my my, it has a lot of flaws. It has bad platforming, awful attempts to make wall-running puzzles that are downright frustrating. The warp / checkpoint system requires you to collect an absurd amount of Ore in order to unlock new checkpoints and the only store so far you can sell gems and other items for Ore, are located in the main city. That's right, if you find a new vendor somewhere else in the world, you can't even sell your items. So if you don't have enough Ore on you, too bad. You just have to make do with what you have, and if that means you can't get any checkpoints, too bad. This is quite frustrating when you have made it really far, only to die and be sent back to the main city for example, given that it's your last unlocked checkpoint. The combat is... sighThe combat is alright for what it is, but the game doesn't give you a lot of ways to avoid incoming attacks. You can, if you time it, dash out of the way. But later on when you have fast shooting laser enemies, it's seems like a much better option to use your shield.Except this "shield" gives you an absurd amount of knockback, more often than not, sending you off the edge into your death. What is the point of the shield? It consumes mana AND it knocks you off the platforms? Who thought this was a good idea? Oh and there are only 2 "Dungeons" for you to complete, then it turns more into "Go here and there, kill these bosses" that are ridicilously overtuned and the way to said bosses is, sorry for my language, flat out cancerous. I really want to leave a positive for Blue Fire cause it IS a charming game. But it has too many downsides for me to recommend this to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is Hollow Knight meets Wind Waker meets Hat In Time, but only half as much polish and a fifth of the content of any of those three. The first two dungeons are perhaps the best zelda dungeons I've ever seen outside the zelda series. Unfortunately they're literally the entire game. After a series of nearly linear hallways, you go through two dungeons and then the game hands you three hour long fetch quests requiring you to just barely retrace your steps through rooms you've already been to and then the game just ends. There is a core platformer here that is really, really good, but unfortunately the combat and bosses form the vast majority of the content and the combat is sub par at best. There are a long string of side quests that are simply not worth your time, given that they only hand out cosmetic rewards, and most of the level design outside of the two feature length temples is substandard to broken, featuring gimmicky jumps, downright abysmal camera angles, and more than a metric ton of softlock locations that you can simply fall into from a higher location and be utterly incable of escaping.The Game flat out promised me that there would be 5 Temples in it, numerous times, from numerous NPCs as you play through the game. To find out that there's only 2 (and a half) is a gigantic slap in the face. The three final bosses of the three final fetch quests aren't even New. they're reskinned versions of each other because the devs ran out of either time, money, or care.If You're starving for a new Ocarina-Like, Blue Fire provides. But I recommend it with two caveats. First is get it on sale, its only about 9 hours long but only about two to three of those hours is any good, and second is that you can go ahead and quit the game after beating the Water Temple / Uthas Temple, because every point after that is unfinished, threadbare, and quite simply not worth your time. It just drags on and on until the game ends.

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole, it's a good game. In my opinion, too much backtracking and the general game flow is a bit weak at times. I couldn't finish the void because I didn't have the wall jump ability. I left the void and couldn't get anywhere - soft locked.The combat system is good. Animations are smooth. Performance is superb.There is a volume slider for music, but not for sound FX and ambient sounds - why? I never play at 100% volume and like to be able to understand people in Discord.The overall art style is simple but nice to look at. Nice toon shading for characters and creatures and overall good selection of low poly environment assets. Post Processing is also alright. The controls are intuitive and fun.You can see the big inspiration from Zelda. For the price, I can somewhat recommend the game.  However, I probably won't finish it.Since I support indie studios and the game itself makes a decent impression, I give it 5 stars. With a big studio, there would definitely be a deduction in the overall rating.

_childDocuments_.review: I sometimes wish that only certain games tried to be less pain in the ass. Blue Fire is one of them. The premise of the game is so good, and the game itself is actually polished enough to make you want to play it more however, once you get going and progress through your adventure it becomes more and more pain in the ass where it should be the exact opposite. To define Blue Fire: it's a bit of everything. Action-platformer, somewhat action-adventure, perhaps even a Metroidvania. Not in the sense that you actually utilize your tools and skills etc. to progress with the game as you backtrack but it has interconnected maps mostly and there is a hub world that connects the most. And, although it's not a strong Metroidvania some skills you pick later on inevitably help you progress later in the game. If you see souls-like in the tags don't mind it. It is true that there are very few fountains -similar to bonfires- you get to save your game and similar to DS1 being able to fast travel via them unlocks much later on. You lose your currency (which is 'ores') upon death and you need to get back to them to retrieve what is lost. None of those are problematic though. The game is mostly easy, combat is one of the strongest drawbacks of the game as it lacks polish imo. You can parry, you can dash but neither of these feels satisfying and the whole combat system itself does not feel rewarding. Platforming is tough and sometimes it lacks depth if not polish but when you get certain skills (such as double jumping) it becomes easier and much more forgivable. While I was truly ready to forgive platforming, the combat usually made me angry and dissatisfied. Even when I was ready to forgive it then there is the problem of backtracking. The game has quite a significant amount of side quests most of which require you to find specific items. Then there are voids that are needed to complete (you can think of them as trials/dungeons with rewards, especially similar to the ones in Fenyx Immortal Rising) to get a health upgrade. They are doable but completing things is not the challenge in this game, it is rather finding them. Finding all the voids, the necessary things for side quests, and especially souls (which are literally glowing orbs placed throughout four of the maps which you need to backtrack and explore the maps once again in order to capture all those souls in a vessel) that are required for unlocking one of the bosses. (btw, although I have not slain three remaining bosses the ones I completed was very simple in terms of gameplay. Same thing goes on with the regular enemies. The combat is usually very simple, I don't think it has enough depth in terms of animations & pattern variation and it leaves you asking for more, but you rarely get any better than what's already available in the few first hours of the game.)The game locks the main boss behind three story bosses. One of them, un♥♥♥♥ingfortunately, is locked behind the main quest which begs you to backtrack 4 maps that you've been to before and explore them once again to capture souls. That is idiotic. I don't want to be mean here but why would you ever need to do that? There is no map and I never thought I'd need it until that point. When you introduce a new hub area with a bunch of new sidequests and then another main quest that wants you to capture some ♥♥♥♥ throughout all the maps then you need to have a map. I don't remember any ♥♥♥♥. I don't want to remember any ♥♥♥♥. After 7 hours it's just more chore. Yeah, there are guides. And even with those chore stuff, the game is still arguably short. But, it's not fun. I don't get why you pretend to be a NES64 game when you easily can have a minimap for each section (at the very least), there are no technical limitations or boundaries anymore. It's obviously a design choice that I cannot understand, I just don't. The game is very forgiving and tries not to be hard at all. You just need some specific items in order to progress and while you do it you get more skills & health upgrades to help with your progress. It's an old zelda-esque game. Why would not a developer want their game more accessible, especially to casual fans?Anyway, to slay a boss you need to slay 3 bosses, and to do that you need to do some uninspiring stuff. There's that. I eventually gave up. If you are more patient than me and don't mind unnecessary stuff -which I think put in the game to make it longer in the first place- give it a go. It has sweet aesthetics and tracks. The level design and platforming are bearable, it's just the game refuses to lend a hand to the player. If only it was more akin to Zelda BOTW (where we could actually have access to all the bosses but also needed to complete other things in order to get stronger, all these with a minimap of course) it would have been something beautiful. I see this as a missed opportunity. If there would ever be a sequel, I really wish the devs make the best out of it by overcoming their shortcomings. ps: I also admit that the review is inevitably biased as whatever I think the game lacked of and whatever I wanted devs to add in are all in accord to my taste in gaming. Some people do not mind exploring a map for hours, some people do not mind getting locked of something and do more, explore more, grind more in order to access and complete it. They feel more rewarded and satisfied. Some people do not mind anything at all, they just flow through the game and do whatever they are asked. I am not one of those guys. At least, I was not that time around. As a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who sinked 20 hours into Balan Wonderworld (which at times had much worse platforming compared to this and as a whole was much worse a gaming experience), I do endure when it's plausible. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not making a fancy review so much as a rant/rave. ♥♥♥♥ it.+No open world. +No procedural generation. +No rogue elements. +Not an RPG. +No radio towers to reveal maps. +No crafting. +No "you can beat the game whenever you want".+No slow, boring gliding. +No arduous stamina based climbing.Just a good old fashioned, no bs, classic action adventure in a sea of open world crafting sandbox nonsense. Takes itself serious, feels great, makes you actually engage with all parts of the game. But it still lets you have fun and gives you a real sense of progression. Recall things you might have missed. Backtrack to old areas with new abilities to find new exciting things in an interconnected world. It doesn't give you everything at the start and tell you to get lost. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I thought it looked like a cool Zelda x Hollow Knight mix, and after playing it for ten hours, that's EXACTLY what it is. The movement is crisp and clean, the controls are easy to pick up and challenging to master. Even though Blue Fire (very obviously) takes inspiration from several places, it is ALWAYS its own game. As of right now, the game sometimes crashes while transitioning to a new area, but the auto-saves are generous, so you never lose too much. One thing in particular that I love about this game is that the developers give the player 100% agency. Plot progression is locked behind dungeon keys and such, but other than that, you can explore the entire world in your own way. I accidentally sequence broke near constantly because I was searching every nook and cranny, abusing every jump, dash, ability, trick, or exploit to search high and low for collectables and spirits. I got the whirlwind hook before the first temple because I managed to use the dash and the fireball creatively to hover stall over a gap. The devs built this game with freedom in mind, and it really shows. PROS:+ Ultra-tight controls make platforming incredibly rewarding.+ Lots of abilities to unlock and abuse+ Fam, the entire game is absolutely stunning. I've set three different screenshots as my wallpaper.+ THE SCORE THOUGH+ All of the characters are charming and adorable and several will likely make you cry.+ Perfect Zelda/Hollow Knight/Dark Souls blend that makes it impossible to put down.+ ELEVATORSCONS:- Game sometimes crashes when changing areas. This will probably be fixed very soon. - It could still use a bit of polish. Lots of terrain models clip into each other, a few enemies have unclear/unfair hitboxes, and there are a handful of minor bugs.Overall, Blue Fire gets a 9.5/10. I cannot recommend this enough, and I haven't even finished it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is almost perfect, but it also just has too many flaws for its own goodbefore i go further, i want to say that i do highly recommend this game and wish to support the developer, what they've made is something truly special, and despite being derivative of other things, (namely hollow knight, dark souls, a hat in time and a bit of wind waker) it truly does feel unique and special, the contrasting elements of those games do blend well and it has enough of its own flare to make it stand out. legit, play this game.now then, that out of the way, this game is...well its hard to put itas i said above, its a mix between various games, and it doesnt try to mask it, and honestly thats fine. for one thing, its easy to know if you'll like this game, just from if you like any of the games its inspired by, and it never goes too far with its inspiration, i cant exactly call it a rip-off of dark souls, hollow knight, a hat in time or wind waker when it also has its own identity.it helps that it also controls really well, and the more you play the game, the better movement you get. you start with just a single jump and a short dash. you have 2 upgrade (spirit) slots, 3 points of health, and a little bit of mana. simple and gets the job done. you can also attack enemies with your swords in a simple 1-2-3 hit combo, and do a little emote. but as you trek along for your quest to kill the queen, you'll earn more abilities and spirits. until you feel like your average method of traversal is just exploiting the game. first you get an air slash that can gain you extra air, then an upgrade to gain more air if you do that after a dash, then a wall run (which also lets you wall jump), then a double jump, then a triple jump, then a dash-extender which MASSIVELY extends the length of your dash, then a jump height increase, then you get yet another upgrade for your air slash that increases the air gained, then you get the ability to run, and probably other stuff im missing, the movement is the best part about this game and (aside from the wall run/jump) it all feels super good and responsive. some of these are spirits for the spirit slots, but you can have all the movement related ones equipped by the end. doing void challenges and grabbing orbs in there allows you to spend the orbs for more spirit slots (max of 10), and just finishing the void challenges nets you a free heart. you're gonna need em.the void challenges are both one of the game's highlights and one of its flaws. they're these somewhat short areas based on pure platforming. think mario sunshine fludd-less levels, but if fludd is never taken from you, and by that i mean you retain all your upgrades thank god. that doesnt make them easier, and in fact, id say they're harder. much harder. they tell you the difficulty before you enter them, thank god. 1 star means easy, 5 stars means hard. but you'll quickly notice that most of them are 4-5 stars. i'd recommend saving those till you have absolutely everything in the game. some require late-game abilities without telling you. you can cheese it at times, i did several without even knowing i needed a double jump for it. once you understand the movement, you feel like you understand it better than the game understands it. anyway, once you get to the 5 star voids, thats when hell begins. having to wait for slow platforms, doing 180 leaps of faith jumps because you cant move the camera and jump at the same time, instakill spikes everywhere that send you all the way to the start, all while trying to get every single orb. the timing and pattern memorization can be insane, theres several levels that seem like they came right out of super meat boy, even down to the difficulty, but where SMB has very tight wall wall jumping with a very clear path.... this game doesnt. the wall running is the most jank part of the movement and sometimes when youre doing these voids, there will be so much ♥♥♥♥ in front of you that you cant tell when you should go. i could forgive it all however, if the voids didnt blind me. see, the voids are just pure white, and then theres also bloom on top of that, and all the platforms are a light grey. so i hope you like blinding white, because you cant even turn the brightness down. thankfully there aren't too many void challenges, but you will encounter them regularly as you're traversing the many levels. speaking of the levels, they kinda.... arent goodi mean they can be, but they also feel kind of half baked. im not quite sure how to put it. its fine at first, but the moment you take the elevator to the sewers, the game takes a hard dip for a while. for the next hour or 2, you feel like you're going the right way by way of the wrong platforms, thinking "this has to be the wrong way, no sane designer would do things like THIS". that thought continues as you head outside to the stoneheart city and this is when you realize the rest of the game was designed around later game movement. the part that tipped me off is when i went to the shrine in the middle of the city, saved and jumped down to a ladder just past the shrine, easy to reach, it seemed like the right way, like the game was guiding me to this direction. save point in center, new path beyond that with a giant door. but no you cant go there till later, and beyond that door is a locked gate. this is when you have to go back to the shrine and realize... you cant make the jump... you have to die (or save, quit, continue) to get back. the game feels like you should have a double jump or even a wall run by this point, but no, you dont get much movement till around 40% of the game is done, and then the game just kind of gives you one ability after another. hell i got the triple jump before the double jump, and at that point the game just starts feeling a lot better and a lot easier. it is kinda nice getting the double jump after so many other upgrades, so by the time you get it, you feel like you can effectively use it in tandem with your other tek. i know i may have contradicted myself here by saying the double jump should have been gotten earlier then praising how late you get it, but i do feel like the movement should be more evenly spread out, like maybe before entering the sewers you get the air slash. that gets you a little extra air so its like a double jump, but its one you need to charge and it only charges on the ground so you cant abuse it. though it does have one major flaw. to charge it, you first need to attack. attacks move you forward. that is a death sentence in some voids with the tiny platforms. its less of a problem by the time you get the double jump, so maybe its my fault for doing voids as soon as i see them, but i still feel like it should be improved. _childDocuments_.review: I cannot say that I am a huge fan of 3D platformers, but I am a huge fan of souls-likes. And Blue Fire makes me think that indie soulslikes should be 2D.First off, I wanna say few words about platforming. I found the camera to be so terrible that it alone makes me wanna stop playing. In this game you need precise movement very often, and seeing where your character will actually go after jumping (especially off the wall) is borderline impossible in some cases.Dark Souls comes to my mind here because camera was terrible in that game too; but at least you did not need to do wall jumps and precise dashes there...Second, atmosphere. I personally did not like the semi-cartoon-ish artstyle here, but that would be ok if there was a compelling story / lore to compensate. But this game also tries to be sort of comedic and 4th wall breaking at times, which just does not fit.As for combat, the fighting itself is ok IMO, but the terrible camera hurts it thrice:1. dashing jumping mid-combat is just not good, because it is hard to predict where your character will land2. lock-on helps a bit, but in here it does not work right IMO. It is very hard to explain though3. finally, it is just overall very easy (I beat the first boss, and I did not die to enemies a single time during my playtime)I feel bad criticizing this game so much, as I can see that devs tried hard with it, and I really hope other people will like it more than I did

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a decent game. I'll put down some pointers and you can decide if it sounds like a purchase:1. The music and visuals are, often, surprisingly fantastic. But once in a while they're grating on the eyes and ears. 2. The combat is good! You can dash around and regain your jump on aerial combos. But on the ground, your third hit combo makes you dash directly into the enemy you're hitting, very weird design. 3. Collectables are fun to attain... but most have literally no purpose, so you can sell them in a shop for money you won't ever need.4. The saving grace of this game, for me, were the Voids. You enter into these scattered challenges and test your limits of movement and platforming. Upon completion they increase your health, which feels very rewarding. Absolutely perfect design on those. The DLC portion includes Voids as their main focus, which was incredible!! 5. This game is like a mashup of Wind Waker and I, Ninja with some brooding lore. In my opinion, the devs tried to include a lot of fun elements, without fully mastering any of them. Still, it's a fun experience that you might enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This game RUUUUUUUULES!!!!!EDIT: now that I have beaten the game (just got through with the final boss, nothing after and not every quest), I will write an actual review of what I thought:THIS GAME RUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUULES!!!!!!!!!!!!!Blue Fire is a great example of a 3D platformer that really understands movement in ways that put it up there with classics of its genre. if you are even a small fan of games about jumping and moving around, I recommend you buy this as soon as you can, for you will not regret it. The level design in Blue Fire is so well done that everything you can and can't do is very clear. There are many ways of getting to where you want and need to go, and those ways will come to you very naturally just out of how the play feel works. This game understands platforming.I must also give praise to how the act of collecting things and the sword combat are also a good mix with the movement and level design. Everything in this game surrounds movement, from jumping from one place to the other, to defeating a powerful god (?)I will say though, I personally did feel a lot of other aspects of the game were really not as strong, thus making some of the game feel... weak? That feels mean to say, but it is how I felt playing. The story, premise, world building, characters, etc. all made me feel... like I didn't have much good reason to care, aside from a few exceptions (who doesn't find the elevator guy at least amusing?). Though none of this felt much intrusive.The real problem of this is the bosses, which do get a little bit in the way of my fun. I admit that they are all just as much platforming-oriented as the levels themselves, but their huge heath bars and telegraphed attacks don't do a super good job at making you feel like you're in a fight, and I wish the more difficult jumps and all were more integrated into the fights. Fortunately, none of the boss fights ever get super in the way of playing this good game.What I liked the most were definitely the optional "void" platforming challenges. Those tests of button-pressing skill are my favorite parts of any game with confidence in its movement mechanics, and the confidence in Blue Fire's is extremely deserved. I beat all the void challenges before the final boss, finding the portal to each one very naturally when exploring; none of the things I really wanted to find in the world map were ever difficult to find, and I love that about this game.I hold much excitement in my heart to see what else this game and this team have in store for me, because Blue Fire is genuinely some of the most fun I've had with the jumps and the wall runs of video games in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: ✅ Fluid and Responsive Controls✅ No insulting quest markers/design.✅ Optimised Performance✅ Beautiful World and Fun characters✅ Engaging, Fun and Fair Design Language.✅ One of the most fun and versatile move-sets (Start to End)❌ Only uses Xbox controller prompts (DualSense Works but the buttons are shown as Xbox)❌ Locked to 1080p (Render resolution can be increased or reduced)The game controls are amazingly responsive and fluid, Please don't let the rage reviews slander this game's utter masterclass of moveset design.If you want to bash the game for "lack of controls" or "bad level design" you're probably very new to platforms and posting negative reviews will do no good but deter someone who is a fan of hard-very hard difficult platforming games.Blue Fire is a indie gem in a sea of indie games that deserves way more attention that what they actually get. Blue Fire takes many aspects platforming fans love and turns it into a segmented platforming playground, Backtracking may seem annoying at first however everything being completely interconnected Its never too much of a trip to get to a quest. This game doesn't hold your hand and its honestly refreshing being allowed to use my brain, The developers must of been a fan of many platformers as there is lots of design language and love to older games that really shows the confidence the developers have in their players.Blue Fire will eventually lead the player into a powered-up state that will often seem "overpowered" and it feels great after the initial beginning move-set being a lot more simple let flexible. However as faster and further you can jump the game very much so remains a consistent difficulty through the combat and level design all the way through as you'd discover new paths you may of not of noticed through acquisition of new powers. The game is far closer to Metroid than Dark Souls however you can use checkpoints to save, tp (late game) and re-assign your abilities. Everything feels earned in this game which really makes it feel like you earned the power you get down the line. I really enjoyed Blue Fire and while I'm far from done with the game, I really do hope the negative reviews slow down the allow this game to grow and perhaps breed some sequels or updates. The game is deeply under-rated if you see it on sale its an absolute no-brainer and even not on sale the game is super cheap for what it is. I really hope the best for all the people leaving negative reviews because the game very far from bad how some people twist it. The tone on most vary from having issues with their controllers or just not having the necessary skill to perform certain maneuvers. Huge shame most of the negative reviews complain about issues that either don't exist or are just blatantly wrong. You are the sort of people 🤡 that are driving an industry towards the simplest and easiest games which shackles creativity, along with any sort of skill development more difficult games provide.Please refer to the definition of "Game" for more information.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire looks like a very promising hybrid between 3D Zelda and Hollow Knight, but sadly the game has too many flaws for me to enjoy:- The combat is very underwhelming. Mindless button mashing is often more effective than timing or tactics.- The game only has a handful of save points. Quitting or dying means you have to replay a significant portion of the game.- The platforming can be very frustrating, especially when you have to jump to platforms you can't see (arounds corners, behind a wall etc).- There's NO map. If you find a new key or ability, you'll have to search every area again for a locked door or a new path you can access, which is very annoying without a map.- Shopkeepers are spread throughout the game world, and are hard to find without a map. Warping is only possible in the second half of the game, and only between the sparse save points.- There's way too much needless backtracking. For example, to access some of the later bosses in the game, you need to find new paths or dozens of hidden orbs in sections that you've already played. The latter actually made me quit the game: to reach some of the orbs, you need abilities that are well hidden in other area's. This game requires you to search the entire game world over and over again, without a map and with only a few save/warp points. With over 500 games in my backlog, this felt like a huge waste of time to me. Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much worth my $20. I would describe Blue Fire as a blend of Hollow Knight, LOZ Windwaker, and the BloodSouls series.
