_childDocuments_.review: its pretty good! It's like a weird hybrid of Legend of Zelda and hollow knight. The marketing made it seem like a Dark Souls platformer which in some spots it is but for the most part it's actually a really great adventure game.The bosses weren't too difficult and nothing really to write home about except for the last one which was actually pretty fun! the combat is fine for a platformer game not overly complicated.the challenge stages that you do for heart containers are Dope and a great change up from adventureingthey are really well done and i have no complaintsthe character moves really fluently which i like he can jump like four times!the sound design and music are great!i would say my favorite place is the tower in the abandoned path it's really fun to traverse.now for some criticisms..... the first two bosses of the game were lame As It Gets! we are talking literally almost no effort you can tell most of the boss budget went to the last four bosses. the shield is so worthless that i actually forgot about it during gameplay and apparently you can parry things but the enemies in this game are so easily conquered i don't see a point literally almost every enemy can be thwarted by jumping and hitting them on top of the head repeatedly by doing this technique you can actually avoid all of their attacks... but i really don't mind that because more complicated Fighting would have ruined this game.the main character is like way too edgy looking for this game...he looks like the emo kid that no one takes seriously and everything about his looks contradicts The Game and how he plays in the game because in the game i actually like him and he's kind of adorable with all the little outfits you can get for him....if there were different masks that you could get that possibly could fix it!And the ending was lame as hell and i felt amazingly unfulfilled After playing such a great game!but in the end i can't recommend this enough it's a really fun timeit's very nostalgic for me to play it! _childDocuments_.review: This was a good compact souls-like platformer. Overall not too challenging, though the Voids can get difficult. There is some lack of direction and is best played in quick succession in order to remember everything. I also had difficulty with depth perception at times with the platforming challenges, but I guess that's part of the fun! Overall enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Every review of Blue Fire begins with a comparison to give a general idea for the feel of game, Zelda comes up alot alongside Dark Souls (but what isn't compared to Dark Souls these days?). However I'd compare it mostly to Hollow Knight if only in terms of general vibe.Its not Hollow Knight though, obviously its 3D, but its more that every element of the game comes across as lesser. The world is smaller and less interesting, the controls more limited, the platforming slightly floaty, the enemies less varied. Its by no means a bad game but its put itself into a position where its compared to some of the best games out there and thats a problem.So ignore the comparisons if you go in expecting a Zelda x Dark Souls or a 3D Hollow knight you'll be disappointed, instead know that you'll be getting a competent action platformer somewhat flawed but good enough that the majority of players will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: While the story isn't particularly mindblowing or interesting, the side quests and dialogue of characters is well made. The biggest draw in this game for me is the execution of the platforming and the feel of free form to it - the game may feel slow at first, but the more you explore, and the more moves you unlock, the traversal becomes extremely fun. The customization and unlocks really feel worth the explaration on a similar level to how Hollow Knight's upgrades felt.The challenge platformer levels feels challenging and the amount of solutions and skips you can incorporate in them based on the skills you have picked, can make it a different experience each time.Now on the other side, the things that don't work well in this game is combat... While the enemy attacks are well telegraphed anything aside from the bosses feel clunky to fight - the hitboxes on some enemies and especially flying enemies are the bane of enjoyment in this game. Parry will be your best friend for the most part.The last thing that I feel iffy about this game is the camera work, because of how small the character is and how high he jumps, the camera tends to drift a lot in different directions and it's definetly not helping during some advanced air movement that you need to pull off in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Blue Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire does well in several areas, such as level design, platforming challenges, soundtrack, movement, controls, and visual design. However, there are a lot of confusing design choices that I think keep it mediocre:- The money system becomes irrelevant because every level has large collectible packets of money that respawn every time you reload the level. - You are quickly introduced to temples of the gods reminiscent of Legend of Zelda, and each gives you a movement ability - but the game suddenly abandons this concept after throwing two at you in quick succession.- The difficult platforming segments required to increase your max health are very fun, up until the game throws a series of upgrades at you that you can equip to completely break these platforming segments by giving you additional jumps and dashes.- You can guarantee you'll revisit each area up to three times, as the game waits until the very end to let you activate certain objectives you've passed by several times already. - The game advises you to try mixing up your combo, but there's nothing to mix it up with - you have one attack combo and one ranged ability that you can't really weave into the combo.- Finally, the story is completely dry - every piece of lore you receive sounds the same (X number of gods, Y number of champions, etc), the ending is totally unfulfilling, and the plot never advances past "You are a special boy, go beat the big bad and save the world".Overall - not a bad game, but I think your time would be better spent playing or replaying the games that inspired it, like Wind Waker, Hollow Knight, and Hat in Time.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that's actually fun to traverse, has (most of the time) rewarding sidequests, and is just.... good.For people wondering what it's like because the trailers lead you down one path, and the souls-like tag leads you down another, but imagine if Breath of the Wild compacted all of its content into the first zone, but instead of puzzle/combat shrines, you get platforming shrines called voids, and you also get absurd mobility and the hollow knight charm system... that's Blue Fire.My only real complaint is that hitting air enemies is kind of annoying because of how floaty air movement can feel sometimes, but like... _childDocuments_.review: The videos I saw looked fun, but if you're interested in a platformer with tight, consistent controls, this aint it. Between the weird fish eye lense feeling and the variable dash AND jump length, it feels like trying to park a boat sometimes. Basic platforming sections feel irritating, and combat is just as.... unwieldy? When you swing your sword, you move toward the target, and for a really long time surrounding the action you can't use your shield, so it definitely doesn't reward the fast paced style of play of many other slasher games.I haven't played a lot of this game, sure, but I was looking forward to it being fun and I find myself anxious to put it down after less than an hour. So no, I don't have the full story on how things progress or if they get better, but I'm a customer like some others might be considering, and this is a real, valid experience I had before putting the game down. If I'm bored one day and this gets reinstalled, I'll update this review to reflect my further findings. Until then, it's a pass from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this to be a decent enjoyable game. Before I played this game I was expecting it to be a sort of 3D Hollow Knight, mainly based on the similar aesthetic. While it does borrow some ideas from Soulslikes, the gameplay is quite a bit more similar to Zelda with a heavy emphasis on 3D platforming.The platforming in the game is pretty good. You start off with a basic jump and air dash movement but can unlock items that grant you wall running and double jump for example, that improve your movement and allows you to explore previously unreachable areas. What I liked about this game is that it reminded me of 90's 3D platformers in the way that you could sometimes cheese your way to reach some platforms and areas you shouldn't be able to reach till later. Basically that freedom to utilise the movement in creative ways. The best example of this is with the Void levels which are optional platforming challenge levels scattered throughout the game. While there is a "correct" way to do them you can also cheese your way through some of the more difficult parts by clever use of the movement abilities. The early void levels are trivially easy but I did quite enjoy some of the more challenging ones you can find later in the game.I quite enjoyed the design of the different areas in the game as they're all designed around getting you to use the full range of your movement particularly if you want to dig out some hidden chests and items. It's worth taking time to explore and trying to get to the more out of reach areas to see what you can find.This games biggest weakness is the combat. Although this game takes a few ideas from Soulslikes, it is definitely not reflected in the combat. It is quite simplistic and offers little challenge. You can gain additional health slots and health recovery slots quite easily, to the point where even the late game bosses are trivial. The only boss that gave me difficulty was the final boss, and that was more down to not understanding the mechanics of the fight initially rather than the difficulty. So overall while I found it to be a pretty good game, Id recommend it more as a decent 3D platformer . If you want a more challenging game with excellent combat and boss fights you won't find it here.

_childDocuments_.review: Having 130%ed the game, I'd say it's safe to say this is a masterpiece and a personal favorite. It's not that often you see this good of a progression system and such good movement, all from a platformer that also has some of the best OSTs I've heard in a game.  However, the game suffered from some stutters, sometimes leaving me with up to "20fps" according to the counter, which would go back to normal, only for them to drop again. It's surely a "my PC problem", but it's still worth pointing out, since it ruined a big part of the experience for me. Also the camera could be unfair on some challenges, which I'm not a fan of, giving you unfair deaths (it's very rare though). Overall, very good game, definetely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start the review proper, I find the comparisons to Zelda and Hollow knight somewhat misplaced, but not in a negative way.But first, what is Blue Fire in the first place if it's not that? Blue Fire is a swift action-platformer with a high emphasis on mobility. Most of your challenges are not related to fighting enemies, more on that later, but navigating the platforms and navigation puzzles the game throws at you. The biggest source of these challenges are the 'Voids', semi-optional challenges based around pure platforming you can complete for extra maximum health. Rather than killing you, falling off the platforms or touching a hazard will just reset you to the last checkpoint with no damage taken, so you usually can't get a game over in one of these locations either, allowing you to try as often and as long as you like.Now feels like a good time why I don't think the comparisons to Zelda and Hollow Knight aren't entirely fair to the game. Zelda is a game about finding many tools and using the right tool for the right job, and Hollow Knight is a vast Metroidvania with a huge amount of exploration. In Blue Fire, what you unlock are for the most part mobility tools. After unlocks you have access to a dash, double jump, wall running and a whirlwind attack that acts as a tertiary jump you only get access to by deliberately charging it up beforehand. In addition to that the game is also very linear with very little backtracking, weapons you find only increase your numerical damage without offering new utility and the things you need to do for progression when backtracking are very signposted. The aforementioned whirlwind attack is actually one of the most fun tools in the game. You're supposed to obtain it after unlocking the double jump, but with some clever wallrunning you can actually use it much earlier, acting as a means to navigate platforms in a much more creative and fun way and accessing locations that are supposed to be out of reach at that time.In truth, the way the game builds itself around mobility and platforming reminds me a lot more of a faster-paced A Hat in Time with advanced airdashing and some speedrunners are probably having a field day with that fact. Unfortunately, like A Hat in Time, combat is very lackluster and bland, but AHiT deliberately avoided combat where appropriate and built its bosses primarily around platforming. Blue Fire feels very confident and its combat, and unfortunately there just isn't enough meant on those bones to really dig into for that. Bosses are extremely formulaic and all feel more or less the same to fight. You have a parry mechanic (using a shield that drains a separate resource you fill by dealing damage), but it feels greatly underutilized. There is one enemy in that game that you defeat by parrying their projectile, which will send it back at the attacker, but this mechanic isn't used by any other boss or ranged enemy so it feels like a real missed opportunity.Having gotten all that negativity out of the way, the platforming in this game is excellent. The developers have hidden all kinds of silly knick-knacks in strange out-of-reach places in the main game and the Voids are really fun to learn and navigate. If you aren't particular interested about the combat part of most 3D platformers I definitely recommend sticking to the regular difficulty, all the increases do is make enemies deal more damage and add some extra tedium by removing some checkpoints. It's nothing that adds to the challenge in a interesting or organic way and the game shines by the far the brightest during its platforming challenges, of particular note the optional free DLC content that unlocks automatically after beating the final boss, giving you access to 16 new challenging Voids.But if you can stomach a serviceable if rather mediocre combat system you are rewarded with an extremely fun 3D platformer that will not disappoint on its movement mechanics.If I had to give the game a numeric score, I'd probably give it an 8 or 8.5. A well-crafted world for platforming with extremely fun movement, held back by largely uninteresting combat and monotonous enemy design.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Nice souls-like world and cute artstyle-Action combat and parry system are decent overallCons:-Camera can't be pulled back and is very wonky while platforming, which also throws off depth perception when its needed-No checkpoints during the platforming challenges making for some classic-levels of difficulty that can be off-putting to some and not even worth trying after many attempts-Difficulty cannot be changed once selected-Lacks a much needed map for a metroidvania that has many tucked in paths that have to be explored, some of the required backtracking can be unnecessarily tedious without it.-Lacks warp points for the above reasonsThe game just became unfun to play after a few hours. The gameplay and level design feel like a mashup between Souls, Zelda and Mario games without much cohesive synergy that makes it stale and somewhat boring to play after a while. Its a cheap pickup when its on sale, however I would not recommend this game at full price and would have refunded if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: The first half is great but it runs out of steam super quickly. Only 2 dungeons in and the game is completely out of interesting content. No new abilities, only 2 new areas, nearly-identical NPC's, and 3 underwhelming boss fights + the final boss as well. Imagine a metroidvania where you have every ability only halfway through, and how dull that would be. This game does exactly that lol.For the second half of the game you end up backtracking through very long-winded sections to get to 2 different sets of interactive objects, which you have almost-certainly already found your first time through them. Only now you can finally interact with them because of totally pointless mechanical gatekeeping. One set of these interactables is just 4 orb things that make a bunch of collectibles appear, that you have to then go grab. (Like those bits in Skyward Sword except even more tedious cause there's no gameplay twist). And the other set is 4 switches hidden behind load zones with absolutely 0 indication that that's where they are. (Tons of load zones throughout the game will also just have locked gates behind them. Why not just have the gate block off the load zone itself???? It's such a waste of time.) Both of these sets allow you to access a very basic boss fight. Then there's a 3rd one that is accessed after getting through the 2 new areas, but I would assume it's just as underwhelming as the others. I cannot be bothered to finish this game, it is just too tedious.As good as those dungeons in the first half of the game are, the bosses in both of them are nearly identical. They only have 1 attack, and it's the same one between them. Combat is definitely not a strong point for this game, but with the boring boss fights, and super unreliable air combat, it ends up being a detriment to the gameplay rather than something simple enough to be inoffensive.Anyway, the pacing overall in the first half is great. New characters to meet, with cool stuff to buy from them, a bunch of sidequests that you'll pick up, and the Zelda-like structure with the dungeons and gaining new abilities is super well done. The second half of the game however, you will have nothing left to spend your currency on, besides like 1 special case where you get an overpriced item that lets you run a bit faster. Every NPC is just the same model with like 1 different piece of clothing on it, and the final 2 areas you gain access to feel way too sprawling and spread out, with much sloppier platforming compared to everything encountered prior. The game suddenly feels so much more empty and I would theorize that basically what happened is that this latter part of the game is simply unfinished. Cobbled together a lot more sparingly than the first half of the game was. It's genuinely baffling how lifeless everything suddenly feels once you reach that point. Almost like playing an unfinished beta or something.I cannot in good faith recommend this game just for it's better first half. You'll only get like 3 hours of fun stuff, followed by 5 of endless tedium and mundanity. It's just simply not worth it. The potential is absolutely here for something incredible, but it completely flops on execution. Like, REALLY flops.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, the art style is simple but pretty overall the core gameplay is pretty smooth. That being said, the game has some glaring issues, primarily centered around there being no map, no clear objectives, and overall just no feeling of progression IMO. In order to feel excited to come back to a game after I've put it down there needs to be some feeling of accomplishment and wanted to explore just a little bit more/ get a little further etc, but this game really doesn't have any of that for me, every time I open it it takes several minutes just to orient myself to remember where I am and what I was trying to do last, and like I said there's no map whatsoever, so once I do figure out where I'm supposed to be going I have no clue how do know if I'm actually going in the right direction or just aimlessly backtracking.Like I said though, core gameplay wise, mainly the platforming, is good. The combat is pretty bland, borderline bad to be honest, but this isn't an action game so its forgivable. _childDocuments_.review: Slight warning i dont think this is a game for everyone, you have to already like 3d platformers and be used to not having a mini map. (Played on steel update)This game does a lot of interesting things, but falls flat by the finishline.  I would like to see what this studios next game is now that they found some success and can finish their vision.Good:-Platforming feels pretty good for an indie 3d platformer, completed all the voids which are probably the best part of the game and only found 2 to be blatently unfun(even then was able to skip about 75% of lucas climb with some tricks). Bringing us to our 2nd point.- there are no real invisible walls, and most terrain, even sloped is pathable.  If you see a place you can likely get to it with some tricks.- Endgame movement feels really clean and almost busted with how fast you get around.The mediocre-Lore/story; kind of interesting that everything takes place in an enormous castle reminded me of metroid fusion, there are some weird boss dialogues that are in a language you dont get to understand which feels bad since i dont want to look at a wiki to know the story. - No map.  While some compare this game to darksouls it feels more like OoT with mario controls, this means that a map would be extremely helpful in some of the dungeons- Only 2 real dungeons in the first half of the game, this is where the game feels unfinished, i expect that the 3 shadow lords were going to have dungeons that got scrapped due to time or budget (this feels especially obvious in Beiras shrine).  In addition to this your character pretty much has all their abilities by hour 3-4 which seems like their could have been more things to add to a zelda style experience- This game wants to be dark souls but doesnt really commit meaing you lose money if you die and you have an estus equivalent but not the actual difficulty or bosses that the "genre" is known for.  Personally these felt extremely underbaked with the estus never improving in potency and improving in quantity 3 times in bursts rather than spacing your 8 upgrades throughout the game- the voids are both your health and utility upgrades, i didnt mind this since i liked platforming, but if you didnt or werent good at it the game probably will deadlock for you- Combat, this was OK for me playing on recommended difficulty.  I thought the game was probably too easy due to the shield being able to instantly block all damage the second you see the enemies movement.  Like other people said most of the enemies look like reskins even if they have a few different moves.  Honestly it would have been better to have less guy in armor foes and add in some beasts or larger monsters to reinforce the sense of scaleTHE BAD- The bosses, which in normal zelda esque games are a fun puzzle are excruciatingly boring, while they have some cool designs and lore the 3 lords of shadow are essentially just strafe til the invuln phase breaks then dash in for a combo or two.  The final boss was decent but unchallenging due to the fact that you can just plummet off the arena to avoid damage.-The spirit vessal, this is pretty blatant and boring padding.  You are forced to revist old areas and collect 60 glowy orbs to progress with the storyline.  If youre going to make a collectathon section use the areas that are fun to move around in(the voids) instead of a filter over an area that has already been explored, or at the very least let us use all our cool movement options and make it a timetrial where you know where the next orb will be and go fast.-Tunics/swords: Again this feels really unfinished, i can almost see that they wanted a majoras mask thing where different tunics could give you different abilities, for example at one point you can buy a disguise of an enemy guard but nowhere do you need to disguise yourself.  The swords as well feel like they may have had extra mechanics but are just very slight damage increases and extremely minor cosmetic changes.  You may as well have just had a unique resource like in hollowknight you could turn in for damage increases while progressing through the game.-Money/ore/shade orbs:  Why is the optimal way to get stronger to run in and out of the town gathering large ore orbs from reloading the area. Why even have a mana system if the only offensive tool is terrible and why make enemies worthless for progression in anything that isnt mana.  At the very least there should have been a way to trade shadeorbs in for ore, not that you ever really run out of money since in the very first town you can double your ore drops.In conclusion this game shows a lot of promise but really could have used a cleanup pass on development.  Still if you like platforming in an oversized world I would still recommend this.Probably a buy it on sale game and run through it in a weekend never looking back

_childDocuments_.review: Love the art style, the music, even 70% of the movement ideas. But the character is so floaty, using an Xbox Controller for reference. There is a camera setting rotation speed but nothing for movement sensitivity. And on a scale of 1-10 it's somewhere around 18-19. Every little flick shoves you about 3ft in a direction you don't want to be. There's no movement deadzone, there is camera deadzone, and even with camera sensitivity cranked to max, the camera is still pretty slow to adjust. Normally there is some room for error to overcome some of this. But there isn't here, and I want to like this game.There are challenges you can find that so far give me only more hearts. And one of those, I can speed to the last 2 "souls" then all of a sudden I can't make a jump 3 ft in front of my character, almost like gravity got cranked up or the "grab ledge" mechanic suddenly switched off. Character just falls. Period. After about 12 attempts on one basic jump, mind you there are a few pinpoint dash jumps you have to hit to get there in the first place, it's rather annoying. I'm not done with the game but it quickly went from, "Wow, this is an awesome title!" to "Wow, they really failed on the precise movement huh?"At this point I can not recommend this title to anyone.Update: Essentially tripled my time. Got to the first "temple", think the game mentioned 4 total. 30% of players have the achievement for getting to the first temple. And I feel like it's because of the "sewer" before it. It's an absolute pixel perfect jumping nightmare. The check pointing in this is so weird. Fall on one side of the room (Even if it's towards the exit) and boom. Back to the starting platform 25 jumps away. Fall on the other side? Pop back up on a ledge 15 jumps from the exit. And when I said pixel perfect, I meant it. There's a narrow band, just as wide as your characters feet to walk on on each pipe. Even if they are narrow or wide pipes. Too much one way or the other, down and back to 15/25 jumps away. As stated before, the game expects you to be precise but gives you the handling skills of someone floating in space using a fire extinguisher to move. The floatiness of the controls is insanely high. And the sad thing is, I want to see more. The combat, the evironment, the music, sound effects, art style. It's all on point. And it's brought down by the movement.

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts out slow but after 5 hours I've unlocked warp and am on the hunt for the remaining 3 temples, 3 mini bosses, and a corrupted queen.It's a connected world like OG Dark Souls, but the game is closer to Prince of Persia: Warrior Within/Reboot. There are basic combat encounters on tricky platforms or in tight corridors, usually one enemy at a time or one strong with one to two weaker enemies.The hardest parts of the game relate to platforming and momentum. You little dude is a bit too floaty, and casts a small shadow which makes launching into jumps a bit of an art. The moves themselves are great, with the usual stuff from platformers complemented by a few neat touches; wall running is free from sticky routes which means you can (while wall running) run along at full speed, come to a halt and slide down, or change direction and go back the way you came; jumping off a wall can be followed by a dash toward it which allows you to climb a little.If there is a complicated sequence of moves you can imagine, I've found it in this game. It's generally difficult in a way most traversal focused adventures won't attempt. For instance, a nice secret I found early on had me dash into a series of vertical wall jumps with another dash at the top to reach a fairly narrow ledge.As for story, it's probably what you want from an action adventure, and where the Zelda and Dark Souls influences are felt most. The world is on the brink, and you could in theory sort it out for everyone by killing off a whole bunch of bosses. Naturally, you're the chosen one, wear a light tunic, and are about 40% the height and 20% the weight of every NPC you meet. You travel the world, saving the gods from corruption overrunning their temples, and dealing with characters from various factions of unclear allegiances. So, not exactly A* work, but like the combat, the story and world building gets the job done allowing the true strength, the traversal, to take centre stage.In other words, it's good.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun like gas station nachos or like a hot dog at a sport event. It isn't the highest quality game but its very satisfying. I am playing through the game right now I am guessing closer to the half way mark based on the reviews and video ive seen of the game. I just can't recommend this one. I find myself constantly enjoying the game and then the janky platforming and controls shakes me back out of it. The platforming which is honestly the largest chunk of what make up the game is fun but the controls don't work as they should because this game requires some pretty quick thinking and fast reflexes and moments and the controls can't keep up. example. wall running/jumping works like this. you run at a wall jumping at it your character grabs and slides either forward or backward if you stay still you might think your character would slide directly down NOPE, you slide either forward or backward, and when you jump away from the wall instead of jumping diagnol toward the direction you jump you jump directly away from the wall... The biggest pull of this game is pin point platforming goodness and it delivers sometimes but with the janky controls it just sours my experience with every moment that I should think "yeah I messed up" clearly is more of a design flaw by the devs. The game makes a lot of strange choices and could really use some quality of life improvements with controls and menus but the over all experience is solid. I got the game on a pretty good sale meaning I didn't pay anywhere near full price... I am glad I didn't I'd of wanted a refund quickly... but since I didn't pay full price I don't mind just enjoying what I payed for finishing it and moving on. The reviews ive seen have been gearing toward the positive and I can see why. But if you were expecting a platforming adventure with tight controls and tight combat its not here. the combat is bouncy and floaty and the platforming is janky. But if you come in lowering your expectations and want a fun little game to just turn your brain off to play it. if not find something else.One last little shout out the music here is amazing like seriously Ive turned most of the sound effects off and just left the music running on high with my speakers, its beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: While the below points are all still true, it has now been 2 months and this game still can't run on my PC. The fire boss fight still causes an unreal engine crash every time in different spots each time. I have messaged the developers, created support threads on steam and sent in many, many support tickets. They are unable to fix it. There is no excuse at this point unfortunately, not even for a small indie developer. I'm sorry. I can't recommend supporting this game, although I can't deny it's an incredible one. My PC has an RTX 2060 Super, a Ryzen 5 3600 CPU and 16 GB of RAM. That is to say, it's fairly powerful. I experienced about three dozen unprompted crashes to the desktop throughout my 15 hours with Blue Fire, ending in a particularly egregious one. During the fight with the boss of the Fire Temple, ten times in a row, Blue Fire crashed with no warning, leaving me with a message that Unreal Engine 4 had stopped working for an unknown reason. I uninstalled and reinstalled the game, verified the system files, updated my drivers, and continued to experience the same CTD. The boss fight is bugged, and I am unable to continue or finish Blue Fire as it currently stands. I sincerely hope this is addressed in a patch soon, as this game is too good to miss out on. But in a soulslike game where every bit of lost progress is a brutal step backward, issues like this are impossible to look past.Overall, I am extremely impressed with Blue Fire; it walks the line between Zelda, Dark Souls, and Hollow Knight so finely that it truly finds its own identity. If not for the consistent crashes, I'd recommend this game to absolutely anyone who enjoys any of the aforementioned titles in a heartbeat. As it is, I'd advise readers to wait for a patch. Blue Fire is unbelievably fun, engaging, gorgeous and just the right level of difficulty. Your hands will turn blood-red and sweat will drip from your brow as you try to stay alive for just a second longer. With the success of the immersive sim open-world style of Breath of the Wild, fans of the traditional 3D Legend of Zelda games are unlikely to see another one in the next decade. Blue Fire feels to me like a genuine new Zelda title, and that's perhaps the best praise I could ever give it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this, but it feels unfinished. First off, what I liked:+ The movement is generally quite fun and you get to perform some impressive maneuvers near the end.+ The Void sections, which are focused platforming rooms disconnected from the general game world, are really great+ The game is not afraid of asking the player to use the whole moveset in challenging ways+ The artstyle is pretty good and the game seems impressively well-optimisedNow for the unfortunate properties:- The world design is lacking, which is a critical point in an action-adventure game. The game has a strikingly unique setting on paper with the whole game taking place inside a giant floating castle. But you only get to even see the outside world and part of the exterior in like two small rooms. The places inside the castle feel disjointed and not very evocative of the larger setting (volcanic caves?), which is a huge dissapointment and missed opportunity. Seeing how cool the castle design is in the menu screen made me want to go there. The individual areas also don't have a very good sense of place, which isn't helped by the game not having a map at all, making the world layout difficult to imagine as a whole. Furthermore, they're more or less laid out in a straight line with two large interconnecting rooms that don't feel very organic.- There are parts in the game world where the platforming gets frustrating and punishing (the graveyard tower is a good example), which could easily have been mitigated if the overworld made use of the shortcut system that is already implemented very well in the voids. Often, it is not very clear where you will respawn after falling, and sometimes it is right next to an ememy that will repeatedly blast you over the edge again.- The story seems as promising as the setting at first. You are seemingly an experiment made of equal goodness and corruption to be able to withstand the evil, and you see many earlier attempts at making you disposed in huge piles, bluntly explained as "corpses". Then the game never elaborates at all. You also get the story of a god betraying their pantheon seemingly as a setup for the main villain, thus leading to the corruption, but that is also just forgotten. There is barely any cutscenes or narration after the (pretty terrible) final boss. You just see it die, there is a vague explosion and the credits roll.- There are points where the game world does not seem fit for the movement at all. Some platforms were more tiny than the movement feels precise enough to deal with. And while wall running is fun, the same mechanic is used for Mario 64-style vertical wall jumping without distinction, which doesn't work at all.- The music gets kind of annoying and forgetable, as is the npc's going for a kind of Zelda-quirky that it does not nail at all, but that's a matter of taste. There is a great game in here, the parts where I had fun were excellent after all. But sadly, for me the sum ended up being less than the parts. I hope the developers learn from their experiences, because I am very sold on a great adventure-platforming game in a unique setting with this kind of movement.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is aspiring to be a Legend of ZeldaxHollow Knight game and does a decently good job of mimicking a lot of those elements, but overall it doesn't feel cohesive.  It looks very nice, but is lacking greatly in many aspects in terms of game design.  Here are my (many) issues, which evenutally led to me quitting the game, in no particular order:- The movement doesn't feel right, you have a decently high top speed when running and you essentially hit that speed instantly when starting to move, this leads to minor movements for platforming being very difficult.- The world feels empty, there aren't many details in each of the areas and a lot of places are just mostly open space- In order to move out of the first major area, i had to collect 2400 of the currency in the game, which was very annoying because i was picking up currency every chance I saw, and I still had to go back through the level grinding for the last 600 or so. In my opinion, early game should NEVER be gated by currency pickup.- It doesn't make any sense (and can be very frustrating) when entire towns are platforming challenges.  - You drop your soul EXACTLY where you die, with the exception of boss rooms, so if you die by falling off a platform into water far below your platform, when you respawn you have to take intentional damage to jump to retrieve it rather and void out, rather than it appearing on the nearest solid ground.- The wall run ability doesn't work on all walls (which isn't explained, it makes no sense and it really feels like there is no rhyme or reason to which walls you can run on and which you can't). Your stamina use during a wall climb is also different between the overworld and in void challenges, which doesn't make sense.- Combat early game is pretty trivial, flying enemies can be killed with 2 or three energy blasts from a distance (you can shoot around 8 before running out of mana, and there really aren't many flying enemies)  and most ground enemies can't hit you if you are above them, so you can just spam aerial attacks and never have to worry about getting hit- This is a small, but incredibly frustrating issue: barriers that are immediately on the other side of a loading zone.  there are a decent number of places that you clearly come back to later with a key or something, but you have to go through a loading zone to find out.  I don't want to sit through a loading screen to take 2 steps to find out i just have to turn around and go through the loading zone again- Some of the void challenges suffer from global cycles mixing with variable timed platforming.  The point of a global cycle with platforms and things is for a player to be able to sit back, figure out the pattern, and execute the movements they need to get through the challenge. There were some challenges that I faced where a platform starts moving through an area with global cycles when you step on it. This is not an issue on its own, but when you can't see the parts of the global cycle until after you get on the platform and move partially through the area, the point of global cycles is immediately negated and it makes the platforming basically impossible unless you get lucky and happened to start the process at the right time by accident.- The bosses i did end up fighting didn't pose any challenge at all, and seemed pointless overall.  The only reason i had to take 2 tries to fight the second boss was because he glitched and wouldn't pop out of the ground once i killed all the enemies he spawned in the second phase, so i had to kill myself to reset the fight.  They don't utilize any of the skills you pick up in their dungeons so they feel like just variations of the same fight... run up and hit the boss, run away to not get hit back, there is no variety.- This is just being nit-picky but was incredibly frustrating for me when platforming: the dash has a variable length depending on how long you hold the button, which feels really awkward.  holding a button to jump higher makes sense, but with a dash ability, it just doesn't feel right.- NPC's are REALLY boring, none of them feel unique and i found myself just skipping talking to people if they didn't sell me anything, I quickly stopped caring about the plot because everyone just said the same things over and over again, with no new information- I also don't understand why interact and shield have to be bound to the same button, i found myself on many occasions shielding briefly instead of grabbing a ladder, talking to a person, opening a chest, etc.There are a few other issue that i didn't mention because at this point I am already beating a dead horse. Honestly i don't even think all of these things would need to be addressed for me to want to pick it up again, the big issue is that all of these problems compound onto each other at the same time and annoyed me to the point that i didn't want to pick it up anymore. If even a few of these things were fixed, i would be willing to try it again, but until then I don't really think it is worth my time.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is a 3D adventure platformer first and foremost.Pro: - Looks cool and atmospheric- Music is okay- Sound effects and special effects are alright- Exploration is rewarding- Freeform puzzle solving, platforming sections in open areas are funCon:- No map or quest markers in large 3 dimensional areas with multiple exits and hidden sections. If you're playing this blind, you'll waste lots of time running around searching for the right exit or items that you need to progress.- It's a platformer with the 3D camera of Dark Souls, meaning you are effectively blind in narrow corridors where there are obstacles everywhere- Combat is pretty much irrelevant. Enemies are pushovers, movesets are heavily limitedConclusion:If you don't like platformers, you won't like Blue Fire. If you do like platformers, Blue Fire is going to make you feel like 3D platformers were a mistake. Having to deal with the camera getting stuck and randomly turning or not turning on its own is miserable, especially since the more difficult the platforming sections require precision jumping in narrow spaces. On top of that, you don't even know where to go half the time, so it all feels like you're just wasting your time.It starts out fun with platforming in open spaces and few enemies, but after about three hours in, things turn sour.

Cons:However, this game isn't perfect, the combat is Simple, jumping in the air and mashing attack is all you need, the enemies come in 3 varieties, Floaty, Humanoid, and little critter. The bosses come in one variety and the final boss feels cheap making you jump off the platform in order to damage her.  there is a lot of money available in the game but not a lot to spend it on, i found myself with tons of valuable items I COULD sell for money but never needing to, I think this could have been mitigated with some late game shop that sells very expensive things. There is no map. Why is there no map? I found myself lost constantly and feels like a third of my playthrough was spent wandering around trying to find that thing i know i saw somewhere around here. Glitchy, although not game breakingly so I did have issues with the wall climb not registering correctly making the voids more difficult than they otherwise would be, also certain spirit abilities not registering like the walk on air after a ledge I found would work 70% of the time and othertime just.. Not leaving me plummeting. Overall 8/10, it's a lot of fun and even though the combat is boring the platforming is a lot of fun and really rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed all content in the game and I can safely say it was one of my favorite experiences of the year. If you like 3D platformers at all and dont mind a slight challenge this game is for you. I was blow away by the quality and quantity of the content for the price. I saw in another review that someone compared this game to Dark Souls. This is completely inaccurate. For one thing combat is not this games focus. Moreover It shares practically nothing in common with the game play of souls other than an interconnected world which is also a key trait in many other games and most obviously The Zelda Series which is really what this game is structured most like. This games elevator pitch is really "what if Zelda was the 3D platformer?" It has a connected world and several dungeons that are built upon the lock and key game design of Oot era Dungeons. Wherin you often unlock a traversal tool to help complete the dungeon and then open the world to reach the next challenge. The twist is the main challenge of all the overworld and dungeons is platforming. I would describe the tool kit to be Mega Man Zeros abilities but in 3D. The Dash mechanic works very similarly to Mega Man X  where you utilize the dash to boost forward momentum to gain more control and reach farther areas. This game offers many places to use its ever expanding platformer tool kit in optional shrine like platforming gauntlets. They are heavily incentivized as the offer health upgrades. The exploration of the game is extremely open ended and fulfilling, exploring often leads to even better platforming tools to find even more secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does some great unique things within the 3d platforming genre. You start with a very limited moveset and then gain platforming abilities through exploration. They function almost like gear in an rpg where you have a set number of slots (you gain more as the game goes on) and create a build of whichever platforming abilities you desire such as a triple jump or double dash. You truly feel more powerful as you progress. The game has zelda-like dungeons almost solely based around platforming which for someone who loves 3d platformers like myself, I enjoyed thoroughly. It's fun moving through rooms, getting keys, etc. all by completing platforming challenges and puzzles. My biggest issue was the game definitely could benefit from a map that helps you understand what or where your next objective is as there were a couple of times I was not sure exactly where I was meant to go. All in all though, a fantastic game with great ideas. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR:- Great graphics, nice atmosphere- Awesome OST, really great integration in game- Lovely exploration, you're free to go where you want and come back later- Combat system feels unbalanced and most of the times not interesting.- Quests are a bit repetitive and the story lacks depth.The game is really interesting and takes influences in many well-known games, blending them all together in a creative and interesting way.- The main quest/secondary quests resembles a lot BotW, in both its mechanics and its content. It is still interesting but lacks depth in my opinion. Activities often consist of exploring the world until your retrieve x item y times or find some people, but it encourages the player to explore the world in its entirety, so it's not a huge con.- The character looks a lot like Hollow Knight, and the clothes have a BotW feeling. The art style is very consistent and pleasing to the eye, without being realistic. It gives a really nice atmosphere.- Speaking of atmosphere, the OST is incredible. Music can be stressful in delicate situations, different environmental elements blend in perfectly with the BGM of each location. However, it sometimes lack smooth transitions when switching places, but not always perceptible so it doesn't make the OST any less wonderful.- The combat system is the definite flaw of the game. You gradually unlock new moves, but you can easily play without them. Most mobs are no-brainers, and difficulty isn't linear among bosses. First ones are really easy while the last ones feel too powerful. - I loved exploring the world. There are many places you can't reach at first, then come back with new power-ups and finally reach it. There are different places that I loved visiting again, discovering all that I missed at first. Really interesting design, great use of height and easy yet interesting gameplay.Some timed doors felt a bit unforgiving, but not too hard.- Game is really great to play even with a keyboard. Great job on that!

_childDocuments_.review: Some thought Hollow Knight was overrated, but the extent of praise for this game is absurd in a way. Blue Fire is a Hollow Knight-Zelda hybrid project. However, it is much smaller in scope in terms of mainline content (reminds me of BOTW's rather small mainline content compared to all the exploration layers, except without the super vast exploration-based content). Story wise, I wish this game was more like Hollow Knight, because then I wouldn't have to listen to a generic story with a generic lead, and just experience the story through the gameplay on my own terms. Controls are pretty solid, but the camera is super annoying in some 5-star void challenges. The void challenges aren't really that hard, but some voids are annoying (unless you discover some some clever shortcuts to speed your progression). In a way, voids have more enjoyable gameplay since you have a more reasonable amount of wall slide/jump stamina to work with for platforming, though void design is bare bones. I sort of like the charge up lock on dash trick, but I kind of wish this wasn't mentioned in a lever pulling tutorial and left for the player to discover (optional secret skill vs. mandatory action once or twice). The Inventory is just as annoying to navigate through as BOTW if not worse. Cut scenes feel so dragged on. Bear in mind, I assumed that heal items were hard to come by, so I eventually forgot about them until the second last boss. The early game is okay, but the dungeons are kind of boring, while the bosses are a little cheap in terms of how easily they hit you, despite them being easy for the most part. Some areas are super tedious in the early game and proved to continue being slightly annoying to traverse in late game, mainly Stoneheart. The torch lighting quest is kind of cool because it encourages the player to inadvertently encounter the other major boss quest lines while pursuing one of them. I have no problem with Steam House, it's just okay. However, the Soul Fragment quest is pointless filler that just copies a feature in Hollow Knight in a more annoying way, particularly in Forgotten Path (nice that it leads you to a useful soul that was hidden in early game though). Really, this game was trying to be 3D Hollow Knight, with its soul system being a more accessible charm system (that part is nice). But it takes the worst aspects of BOTW, like cookie cutter bosses and some side quests that nobody wants to really try to figure out (I have no desire for 100%). The late game bosses are all easy to learn, but they are super cheap. Some are cheaper than others (blue>red>green [there are not many other ways to describe these ones really]). This boss combat feels somewhat broken, and surprisingly, the final boss feels the least cheap, even though I had to use 5 heals on my play through. There is no excuse for having so many heals that are easily replaceable. If the combat was tight, you would not need to rely on the mobile game/Minecraft Dungeons trope of easy heals. One thing that I will say is that the three-dimensional perspective can really make precise combat more annoying in general, and that's more of a limitation for 3D platforming than anything else. Music is good but it didn't really resonate with me all that much. Visuals are nice, but some areas look way too homogeneous and that is probably partly why I find them annoying to navigate. I didn't come across any glitches, I just felt that the combat was iffy in general. Figuring out where to go and finding the voids was fine (felt vaguely like Super Mario 64's Castle), I may have forgotten about the elevator to Firefall river when I stopped playing for a few days after the cut scene that showed that opened path. I didn't really like how gates just decided to open after I went somewhere important and returned, it just doesn't make much sense from a world building perspective. I don't think the game really needed a map, though I found myself doing laps around towns to find one forgettable NPC in a forgettable house.Overall, it is nice to see developers that honour successful modern adventure titles like Hollow Knight, Zelda 64 titles, and even BOTW. Nevertheless, this truly feels like a fusion fan game more than a standalone indie title. It's a solid project, and I don't necessarily "not recommend it", I just don't think it holds up compared to the work its derived from in terms of tight gameplay. Keep up the solid game development, I feel like there will be a project that better resonates with me from your team soon. Wishing all the best!

_childDocuments_.review: is a 3D action-platformer. While failing to translate 's seamless platforming experience to the third dimension,  still manages to offer a fun indie experience borne from its mix of platforming, combat, exploration, and questing. Not exactly a novel experience so much as a blend of some leading series from different genres, this one should satisfy some tempered expectations of those series' fans looking for a new spin on action-platforming gameplay.You play as a nameless soul, tasked with cleansing corrupt forces from a giant floating castle. Using your twin swords and your platforming skills, traverse over a half-dozen open areas with your ever-increasing arsenal of movement abilities to defeat evil enemies, wicked bosses, and the malevolent force causing the carnage. In the meantime, tackle plenty of sidequests, gather loot from exploring levels, and show off your pure platforming skills in the game's many otherworldly Void challenge levels. wears its inspirations on its sleeve: it is a 3D  in its aesthetics, overworld, platforming, and premise, the save and healing system of  with some  combat, dungeons, and missions interwoven alongside 's platforming challenge levels. While this game offers an ambitious experience trying to integrate all these different sources, it falls short of meeting the quality of any of them. That's not to say this game is a failure; it's fun in its own right, but just not exactly in the same league as any of these series.Let's start with the platforming. " in 3D" sounds like an easy win on paper, but it is far tougher to execute. First of all, 3D environments simply pose more of a challenge when trying to implement tight controls for overcoming obstacles or hiding small, secret areas - meaning 's world offers roughly a tenth of the depth or reward for exploration that 's does. Second, a 2D game can simply show the player all that needs to be seen from the display of a single screen. 's greatest challenge doesn't come from an enemy or an obstacle: it's the camera. Adjusting the camera to actually see where you're aiming during the toughest platforming challenges is a massive annoyance that unintentionally compounds difficulty. Depth perception, as a result, is often an optional thing in this game - meaning many jumps turn into leaps of faith. Not exactly an airtight platforming experience.The  inspiration takes shape in parts of this game's combat, dungeons, and quests. Combat almost feels identical to the swordplay of  at times - though  offers a few more customization options, the core combat ability stays locked to a variety of sword maneuvers and a weak projectile weapon. This game also has two dungeons that feel distinctly , albeit shorter and simpler ones. And if you're a fan of those quests from  that involve collecting orbs across a map you've already explored, you're in luck!The -style checkpoint and heal systems stand out a bit less than the other points of inspiration largely because, unlike ,  is an easy game. This reviewer completed it nearly 100% without dying once. The game throws HP upgrades at you as part of its platforming level gimmick, and this game's version of Estus Flasks are plentiful in random drops. So long as a player takes a pretty completionist approach to the side content, they will remain well above the game's difficulty curve - which does mean  could serve as a nice introduction to the - type of ultrahard games.In spite of the critical tenor of the preceding review,  is still a good game at its core. Over the roughly 10 hour playtime, players will scratch the itch for platforming through different worlds, beating enemies, and powering up. While in some ways the faults of the platforming system prove that it may be better to stick to 2D when crafting -esque platforming challenges, I can't necessarily fault the devs for trying (nor for failing to meet the impossibly high standard set by Team Cherry). Including the OST free with purchase is a nice touch. Check this one out especially if it's on sale.  gets a B-.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Fire is difficult to describe. Its a game that ticked many boxes for what i was looking for though i barely new it at the time. In a typical Metroidvania style you upgrade your characters movement through the map and can go zoom zoom the further you play. Combat lacks finesse, but the twilight princess vibes and superbly executed jump and platforming parts buffer anything that might be lackluster about blue fire. If you are looking for a platforming oriented metroidvania with zelda vibes - we got temples, bosses, chests with upgrades, vendors, we got sockatable boons, discoverable weapons, Robes that act as skins and even quests requierements and even some neat NPC dialogues (dont expect much story or depth here!) - go for it. As i played it over the course of ~10 days with not much time at my hands i had the need to look some stuff up because i forgot where the routes were that i couldnt access with my current abilitys. The game has no hint system what so ever, which is refreshing in the current hand-holding tutorialesq gaming environment.You will experience backtracking but its zoomy, you are fast and fly through the map where in the beginning everything was seemingly a slog you did not know about. The overworld is distinguished enough that you will remember most rooms and areas you have been in before.You will 100% be entertained for the 7-9 hours you will get out of this!

The level design, lore, enemy variety, and everything else are the bare minimum. After 5 hours of playtime, I had 0 deaths, 1 softlock, and 3 crashes. So, it's an uninspired experience that crashes every couple hours, and I returned it. I feel the tiniest bit more cynical.Don't bother with this one: just replay Hollow Knight or Super Mario 64, and you'll have a better time.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game, and it's dlc for around 20 hours and finished everything 100%, i think it has enough pro and cons to balance out and this should really be a mixed review, but as far as my experience goes i'll lean towards the negative, and here's why:The game lacks a clear direction, and i think it's one of its biggest sins.It starts off as a similar game to Dark Souls with a cutesy look and some platforming elements, you can in fact see the fire shrines, the cryptic storytelling, the "estus flasks" and the initial aestethic all point towards it. After the first hour or so it moves to a Wind Waker style game, introducing dungeon, that unfortunately lacks some level design polish, between the time it takes to complete the two dungeons there is NO fire shrine for around 2 hours, that's why i found they forgot about the direction at one point.After the second dungeon there's another change and you are basically sent to clean up the previous levels to fetch lots of items in the old environments so we can face the other bosses, that imho should have been in their own dungeon, and we shift towards a more platforming style. At this point you'll be around halfway through the game but probably you will notice that fighting enemy is useless since you should have maxed out the mana, only thing the exp is used for, and also because it's so easy you'll rarely be up for a challenge and very rarely use your flasks to heal, not that the combat is the strong point of this game as you only have a combo of three and that's it.Then there are the voids, this game platform style challenges, i think except for two they are all balanced correctly, maybe steering towards easy once you upgraded your platforming skills but nothing too bad.After the fetch quest is done you face the final boss and the game ends.The dlc is free and accessible after the final boss and is basically comprised of only void challenges plus a new boss, the problem i have with this ones is that the vast majority of the 15-20 included are trial and error of the worst kind. So i really can't recommend it playing unless you like this kind of genre.Traversing the game world is mostly fun and the platform part works really well so the fact they transformed it into a trial and error doesn't sit well with the part of the game that was working the most.All in all i can see the love the authors put into it but this game is ultimately plagued by a general incoherence of design that doesn't let a player enjoy it completely.

_childDocuments_.review: But, nevertheless, it's an AWESOME game, a true GEM of it's genre and I enjoyed it that far. Lots to explore, the lore is short but explained. These interactions are simplified, but adorable nonetheless. And returning to old locations after learning new moves and/or emotes, to unlock even more mystery.If you don't mind jumping parcouring, this is a great game to dive into. The Void Parcouring by completion, you earn an extra heart. By killing entities, you obtain dark shards to upgrade your mana, because it will come in handy when the time is nigh. Level design only gets better the deeper you go into the game, which is a great plus. Ussually it's the way around, where a developer looses interest and wraps things up. I do not have those vibes with this GEM.From all the Soullike games I played, this game comes pretty close and adds it's own specialty: Jumping Parcouring.But I stay with my own commitment: I do not like jumping parcouring, in fact I hate it. It's just that I am at the moment charmed with Soullike games and try to collect them all and ofcoarse play them as good as I can.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. If you liked playing Zelda or MegamanX or Metroid or Mario (3D games), you will feel at home with Blue Fire. The atmosphere and ambience of the world of Penumbra is very intriguing, making you always want to learn more.The beginning of the game is a bit hard and a bit frustrating while you learn to control your character, but as you progress you will feel you are the hero yourself.The platforming is excellent, the character progression is great, side story npcs are funny and interesting. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game pretty highly. The combat is fun, the platforming is fluid, and the overall challenge is just about right. If you want to know if you should or should not buy this game, the answer is you should. You can stop reading here.If you want to know my full opinion: This game is good, but flawed. This game has had corners cut, and the edges are still very sharp. The game is absolutely rife with allusions to content that it simply doesn't have. There's a ton of secret chests that are hard to find, but most of them are full of unique garbage items that are never used for anything. Tons of NPCs will highlight text in red to indicate it's important, but it references things that will never happen or characters that don't exist. The game showers you with valuable gems to sell for funds, but everything can be bought with the money you find by just walking around. Finally, and this is a fairly minor spoiler, the game has no after-care at all. You beat the final boss and BAM! Credits. I'm not asking for a full post-game scenario, but some indication of what just happened and what it meant would be nice.It's a little tough to levy complaints like that against this game. I know for a fact that the developers put their hearts and souls into it, and it really does show. The game exudes a scrappy, inexperienced charm that I can't resist. I liked it enough that I went through the effort of finding nearly everything it had to offer. I'm still missing .25% away from full 130% though, and I fear it will stay that way forever because there's just not enough of a community to make exhaustive checklists and guides for it.

name: Ever Forward
detailed_description: Ever Forward is an adventure puzzle game — it is the story of Maya. Maya is lost in a strange world somewhere between reality and imagination. She is alone to confront her despair on her journey of discovery, where she must unlock her memories and confront her fears to unravel the secrets of the world. Players will need to use their observational skills and intelligence to solve multiple puzzles to piece together the mystery of Maya's past and what dark secrets she has buried. Key Features Puzzles For more than three years, our designers racked their brains, designing puzzles with the 'puzzle gamer' in mind. Players will feel deeply challenged and motivated to solve each puzzle, and some puzzles have multiple ways of being completed to fit different kinds of thinkers and logical processes. The Art A color pallet of soothing pastels and futuristic tones designed to simulate the absurd nature of the dream world. Adventure Players can collect fragments of memories in the world to unlock new areas and new puzzles. Mechanics Mechanics range from simple movement and jump to teleportation and gravity control; the player must use stealth and observational skills to navigate each puzzle. 永进 Ever Forward

_childDocuments_.review: Ever Forward is beautiful puzzle game with an emotional story.  Depending on the way your brain is wired, it will either be pretty easy for you or quite hard.  It was the latter for me, but I got there......finally!The bones of the story is that the mother is a very busy scientist and has little time for her 12 yr old daughter.  Government officials have stated that it is too unsafe to go outside, so you're stuck home all the time. [A reason was never given for this]You start designing your own security bot, but your mother isn't interested in that either.   The story is enacted by short cut scenes between each puzzle and are well done.Graphics are lovely.  The natural world is full of gentle pastel colours whilst the imaginary world of Maya is very futuristic and dark in design.  The soundtrack is full of mellow synthesizer sounds and the sound effects of the security bots are great!Game play involves getting a box to a red column of light.  You need stealth to get past the security bots and have to work out how to distract them in multiple ways.  As the game progresses, you are able to teleport and use gravity for your purposes.To solve the puzzles requires logic reasoning, dexterity and speed to get to something before it moves.  In some cases, it requires precise throwing of the box, which can be rage inducing near a bot!  Be prepared to die multiple times.Gravity was introduced towards the end of the game and I found it incredibly frustrating to use.  You have to wait for the right strength of wind to move and if you do it wrong multiple times, it gets old very quickly.  The timed aspect of it makes it difficult for slowpokes like me!The Gravity aspect was my only criticism with the lack of English subtitles for the final scene with her mother.  I didn't know what was said in Chinese.  The end of the story did leave me scratching my head, so it is really left up to your own interpretation.  Spoiler alert:  Puzzle lovers will definitely enjoy this.  Buy on sale.  8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ever Forward has a surreal aesthetic to it with an intriguing story arc.  The mellow synth soundtrack and wonderful use of color palettes made this puzzle platformer easy on the eyes and ears.  Unfortunately, that's where I stop giving glowing praise for this game.  The puzzle mechanic developed within this title is rather frustrating most of the time.  You're required to carry blocks to specific end points while traversing various platforms and avoid sentry turrets.  It's a scenario that is repeated to a fault.  Some solutions felt clever, while others tipped towards vague and tedious.  I really wanted to enjoy this more than I did, as I consider myself to be a puzzle enthusiast.  I'm sure there will be plenty who will find everything in this title to be just fine, and I get it.  I, on the other hand, grew quite tired and agitated when it was all said and done.  It's, by all means, very playable.  It just didn't win me over when it came to the actual design of the puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this lovely game, Ever Forward.1.Visually, I was met with a vibrant and appealing world design. The main character is cute, although I would recommend the devs used a more realistic voice actor for the child. Her excited and general tone always sounded forced, which is unappealing.2. The story, although I'll admit I have mixed feelings about much it actually will hit home with most people, was interesting enough to allow you to make up your own mind about what was going on. The cut scenes are short and sweet, and even though there isn't much story, I feel it's one of those 'you fill in the blanks' kind of deals.3. Game play. The characters movements are fluid, and feel natural. Not being able to run when danger is close, while at first felt frustrating, added a real sense of suspense. So I gotta say that this was a nice touch.4. Some mechanics were not obvious right away, but after a bit of trial and error (and melting my brain) I was able to figure out what to do. There isn't any real hand holding going on in this game, so that adds to the challenge. There is a hint system that does help.5. The puzzles were good, but not great. Yes, there were some difficult ones in there, and yes they also melted my brain a few times and caused me to walk away and rethink. That's absolutely fine. My only real issue is that I feel there are times when a solution doesn't really present itself too well, perhaps that is my own fault though. One particular puzzle felt like it needed more of a cheesy workaround rather than solving it the intended way. I guess I will have to see how others solved it and rethink my approach.Conclusion: Overall, Ever Forward was enjoyable and frustrating all at the same time, which is what I would expect from a puzzle game. If you felt it was too easy, call Mensa and book yourself in. If you felt it was too hard, then breathe, walk away, and take a break. Come back with a fresh mind and try again.Tip: The environment and the way it's designed can hold the clue to solving a puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to iterate that while I recommend this game, it's purely to give some support for the developers since the game has a great foundation. I personally had some issues with the game.These issues have nothing to do with how hard the puzzles were, as I've finished the game in 2.1 hours. The main points I want to touch up on are the Story, Puzzle Design/Mechanics, and Game Length.Before I touch upon these things, I do want to say that the game is beautiful. I love the art style.--- 1 - Story --- The story was all-in-all good. It had some ups and downs as well as a climax.  One of the problems that I saw in the story was that there were gaps in the story as not everything is explained very well. I was often led to guess what is occurring and most of my questions were never answered later down the line.  The other problem is that the story itself is fairly generic. This is my own interpretation from what I've seen and heard playing it, so if the developers would like to point out if I'm wrong then I would be grateful. --- 2 - Puzzle Design/Mechanics --- Puzzles generally consist of getting a cube to the end by getting through obstacles and robots with vision cones. Sometimes there are more robots, cubes, or obstacles. Sometimes there are no robots or obstacles. New mechanics are shown to the player over time in order to keep the puzzles from getting stale. Most of mechanics shown to the player can be influenced by the player. This is important in a puzzle game since players shouldn't need to rely on something out of their control to complete it. Puzzles should be completed with their own ideas and knowledge rather than uncontrollable timed mechanics. I will note that this does not mean timed mechanics can't be used in puzzle games, but they need to be done right in order to ensure that it's more than just waiting for the light to turn green at an intersection (metaphorically speaking). The following bit will touch upon the mechanic that I did not find good.  The puzzles in this game had great foundations, and I definitely believe more can be done with the ideas that the developers came up with.--- 3 - Length --- This is a short and sweet section.This game is short. I can understand the reasons why it is short, but for a 15$ game it is short at 2-3 hours. Looking at the other reviews I can take that the average completion time is at about 3 hours, if not a little bit higher. There are only about  puzzles and the story itself is also fairly short.I personally wish more was done with the game, but it was a good step in the right direction and wish good luck to the developers in their future endeavors.

_childDocuments_.review: Maya is a little girl who lives alone on a peaceful island far, far out at sea. The waves are calm, stone pillars loom out in the distance like faraway guardians, and a huge tree stands tall and strong with its roots entangling the earth. Maya isn’t completely alone though, Hestia is Maya’s floating companion cube, a quiet friend who is with her always. One day, out on the beach, something strange appears – a familiar building manifests and a puzzle appears, leading to a memory Maya has forgotten. Seek out all of the memory shards to find the truth about the island, and the secret hidden in Maya.  2-3+ hours to complete, Ever Forward is an adventure puzzle game that is short and sweet. Beautiful graphics, a great soundtrack, fun puzzles and an interesting storyline. The Island is explorable and has secrets and animals you can pet, and the puzzle domains are interesting enough and can be challenging. If a puzzle is too hard, the key for many lies in the layout and the environment. A mix between fantasy and sci-fi, Ever Forward was super fun to play and I’m glad I took a chance on it!

_childDocuments_.review: Before I purchased this game, I was a virgin with no friends and no chest hair to speak of whatsoever; I considered my mere existence to be a dismal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the already tattered tapestry of human history, but all of that changed when I found Ever Forward.I was dubious at first, I don’t generally consider myself a puzzle gamer, it was actually the title and description that struck a chord with me; I thought maybe if I could help a cartoon child move forward in her life, perhaps I could do the same for myself, still being a mental child trapped within a weak and twig-like body myself.So I clenched in my hand a 15 dollar check I had received for filling out hundreds of hours of online surveys, money that I had originally planned to use to pay for food or possibly save up to get the termites and cockroaches out of my 5 square foot apartment; I clenched that check, my heart racing, and smashed that purchase button with the strength of a thousand suns, and boy did my investment pay off.Upon completing my first playthrough, I instantly became a slayer, a chiseled beast of muscle and hair. My gluteus maximus has grown 7cm in muscle mass diameter since purchasing this game as I clenched my butthole and whole ass every time I was nearly detected by a sentry bot, which is basically every six seconds of gameplay. My experience with Ever Forward was basically a slow motion earthquake on my computer chair, rocking with the motion of the ocean as I continued to solve puzzle after arduous puzzle.My first playthrough complete, I turned off my computer for the first time in what felt like millennia and dragged my now gigantic ass all over town to various local swimming pools where I would cruise, successfully, I might add, for hot moms; these hot moms were powerless to resist my newfound confidence and Adonis-like badonkadonk bod. They gravitated towards me like a riptide inside a black hole.I’ll keep this review PG-13 for all you hot moms with hot kids out there who might be reading, but I would be remiss to mince my words, so I’ll say this: I have been ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ constantly since I finished the game to the point where I’ve been worried about my heart exploding on multiple occasions. I am getting my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ right now as I write this review.Anyway, let’s talk about the game itself.The puzzles are hard as ♥♥♥♥. Based on the achievement list, only 5 percent of people make it past the fourth puzzle, so if you want to kick this game’s ass, you better cancel your 2 o’clock meeting with Lauren from accounting, order in a wheelbarrow full of strap-ons off Amazon and arm yourself to fight back against the rigorous ass blasting that this game will assuredly deliver to you otherwise.Your goal in Ever Forward instantly becomes obvious: you’re on an island that is otherwise pretty chill,  but some weird alien ♥♥♥♥ is invading your island so you need to go and shove boxes up their many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and send their ♥♥♥♥♥ asses back to the shadow realm. It’s about real estate, they’re driving your property values down. That might be some kind of allegorical allusion to society or the world we live in or some ♥♥♥♥, but I prefer not to think too deeply about these kinds of things.
