_childDocuments_.review: I really don't want to leave a negative review....I love Warhammer and I love Streum studio's game(I bought this at full price and I own every games from this studio) but this is just not the game so called "Doom meets 40K"...just...No.Where do I start this?First of all, the weapon.All the weapons are just not really fun to use. They are mostly hitscan weapon with only three types of projectile weapons. And all of them are pretty inaccurate even when fully upgraded. Unlike the weapons in Doom, in which you have to switch weapons for different kind of enemies, in Hired Gun, all you have to do is just spray your enemy to death. And the default rifle are actually good at it, so there's no point using other hitscan weapons...It just no real tactics at all.Second, the odd gameplay choice.This is the biggest gripe for me sadly.  Like why can't the player switch the default revolver with other weapons? The combat flow are ruined when you want to switch to your second powerful weapons but instead you switch to your stupid revolver and died.And whats the deal with the healing mechanism? You only heal when you're hit by the enemy? Why's that? Why not do this like Doom? Just drop health packs when the enemy dies! Or like the game Spacemarine, when you can replenish health by executing the stunned enemy! It's true that you can heal yourself by killing the enemy in this game but when most of the enemy can teleport and jump aroud like circus monkeys and the MORE distant between you and your enemy the LESS health you replenish, all it left is FUSTRATION. And the combat flow suffers from that a lot.(Like the only goal in this game is chasing moving health packs all the time.)Also, the melee kill mechanism are just stupid. You can press E to instant kill any enemy without a shield. WTF. It's super silly with all the jack looking melee enemies rush to your postion, standing there just to wait for you to press E on them in line.(You are invincible when melee animation.)Also, some player's abillity are just grabage. Like the knife mode, it's useless when you can still take damge form the enemies.(Why not make it like a super health boost/ temporary infinite ammo/or a stealth mode so you can kill them in a cool way? If I can kill my enemy with a heavy bolter, why use a knife and goose chase the enemy around???)And why all the levels are built on an instant death pit? I CAN even fall to my death in the Hub World!!!! LMAO. The level design are a visual mess and I almost not using the wall run ability cause the level sturcture are so twisted and peppered with obstacles that you don't even sure you can run on it or not, and there's no benefit for doing that, since you can just grapple hook to any places you want.Lastly, the animation.It's so bad that it almost make me laugh. Everything feels janky and rough. The melee animation are a mess and they clip through walls and ground a lot. It takes too long and you will see enemies runing around shooting at you in the background or they just surround you and stand there waiting for their turn to die (if they are melee type enemies). And the cutsenece angles are so messed up like I though my game are going to bugged out.To sum it up, just go play Doom, It's a whole better game. This games does not worth the discount price let alone the full price.(Also, dear developers, It's OK if you don't have the money to do the facial animation, but please make the voice acting sound fun!They all sound bored to their bones! And don't try to use those wierd camera angles to cover it up. It just make things even more confusing.)

_childDocuments_.review: S'alright. If you really want more detail...It's a resoundingly 'okay' game. Isn't going to win any awards, but it'll give you some hours of fun if you like fast paced FPS stuff. The Good: Shootin' stuff is fun. The actual straight up gunplay is a bit floaty, but it's easy to overlook with the mobility of your character (after the first two missions) and the extra non-gun based abilities you unlock. There's enough options in how to approach combat that it's hard to get too bored, even with the small enemy variety. The 40k theme is spot-on. Locations are...well, as varied as they can be considering the narrow setting of the game, and I was surprised how much they managed as far as differentiating each zone as they did. They really got creative with some level locations. The Bad: The protag is a tunnel visioning, overly aggressive moron who is literally only good at killing things. I'd have rather had a silent protag than have to listen to this complete and utter moron react to -anything-. The voice acting for the female protag is...I can't tell if it's a bad performance, or just really poor voice direction. Jericho is the only member of the cast that I didn't wince at once, and his performance may just be that he can work well despite poor direction. Who knows?'Cutscene' animations are...bad. Stiff, awkward, you can tell they covered as many characters mouths as possible so they didn't have to animate them. The animation budget was absolutely barebones. It feels like they really had plans for more third person stuff, considering that you can customize your own appearance to a half decent degree, but it ends up pointless since you only see 'you' in loading screens and the menu really. Also the less said about the UI and weapon/gear management the better. It's really really bad. You get used to it eventually, but there's no excuse for things to be as awkward and unintuitive as they are.The story overall is really whatever. It's small scale, but you're stuck as the least interesting character in the entire thing, who is pretty much jerked around and told what to do/manipulated into what to do by everyone else. As I said, the protag is a complete moron. So. Yeah. I've played worse 40k games, and I have only played a handful of better 40k games. I don't regret the time I spent with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is surrounded by beautiful 40k environments and visuals. There won't be a thing you see that's not 40k-touched. That being said it's specifically "hive city underworld" 40k. The game makes an ample explanation of the immediate setting, that you're in the underbelly of a hive city. And that's all you really need to know. There's cybernetics, gangs, guns, and enemies using those guns to kill you.It's also nice because not only are the lore details and scenery well done, they come together to make a great 40k (or rather 40k-adjacent since it's more Necromunda) shooter. I was worried since the same developer/publisher put out Space Hulk: Deathwing and while it had some beautiful environments and details, the game was brought down by mediocre audio/dialogue, mundane story, and unenjoyable gameplay.The last good 40k shooter, although third person, was Space Marine. Necromunda Hired Gun is a welcome addition to this small category.I'll preface this with there's plenty that feels like the developers spent time playtesting and smoothing out to make sure things feel right and play well. But there's still many other glaring things that stand out that seem like maybe they had to deprioritize it in the face of other issues that they wanted to fix before release.Off the top of my head it's mostly that the dog just appears when you summon it, like right out of thin air. Compare it to games like AC Odyssey and KC Deliverance where your horse appears off screen/camera, and actually trying to spot it spawning in is difficult. And honestly I forget the dog exists really, I think a good solution would be occasionally hearing it bark in the environment, like in the pipes or something, and when you summon the dog it runs or jumps out of somewhere near.Another thing is that the majority of characters are wearing some form of facial covering. I imagine this makes sense since the underneath of a towering hive city is probably mostly noxious gasses but it's also noticeable that those  facial coverings don't really have good, if any, lipsyncing with the dialogue. So it seems like they decided to shelve that for later to focus on other priorities too in development (which makes sense and is a bit respectably clever as a programmer myself).It's an enjoyable game and an enjoyable 40k shooter. If you're a fan of 40k, you'll likely enjoy it despite the caveats. If you're a newcomer to 40k, you'll probably still enjoy it for its gunplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a janky mess. Get it for cheap.Aesthetics are nice and its decent game for a warhammer 40k fan, but many of the game mechanics leave it lacking. It's a game centered around loot, but player can't manage their inventory apart from mission launch and end screens or even see the stats of the items unless selling them. Game difficulty is a mess and it is hard game even on easy difficulty with endlessly respawning enemies with hitscan weapons. You can only have 3 medkits to restore your health per a really long level, which gets compensated with Bloodborne-style lifeleech that is active few seconds after youre being hit and Doom-style executions that also restore health. This works well on easy difficulty but is cumbersome mechanic at hardest difficulty thanks to endless enemy spawns, especially on bounty missions. AI is dead, they just charge at you but compensate that with numbers and godly aim from long distance.Worst thing is crashes and bugs. Game has crashed 10+ times for me within first 5 hours, after that I stopped counting. There are also game stopping bugs like clitching inside wall that makes you lose all your progress in a mission. There is no manual save.Get this for cheap if you are warhammer-game nerd, avoid otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Bugs and performance issues aside the core loop is solid and some of the level design is really top notch in evoking the imagery of an industrial underworld. There is some good level design and the levels themselves have a few routes you can take for the most part with your chosen skills,weapons and upgrades allowing you to tailor it to your preferred playstyle. The weapons feel chunky and impactful and the abilities allow you to integrate wall running, grapnel hooking and slow mo... etcThe biggest drawback however is that about halfway through the game stops offering you new things to play with. You stop unlocking guns and the enemy types just repeat. I would really like to see this expanded with dlc adding the final three gangs and some of the old necromunda enemies such as sump crocs, ripperjacks, spiders and the enforcers to name a few. The story is also pretty non-existant but I don't think that ever really mattered, just a few lines of dialogue to justify the set pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: As a 40K and Necromunda fan, I really wanted to like this.The backdrops are lovely, and the item gathering and customization systems are decent. I could probably tolerate the clunky UI, lackluster plot, budget voice acting (1 voice actor per gang), and filler grinding if the base gameplay was good.Unfortunately, for the base gameplay they couldn't decide whether they wanted to focus on FPS, RPG-style activated skills, or parkour-y stunts. They just didn't have the resources to do this combination well, so it resulted in a combination of boring activated skills, lackluster FPS, and wallrunning and sliding that are incentivized but just not that useful or exciting. The AI can spot you at great distance, shoot you with surprising accuracy, and deploy vast numbers of fast-moving enemies.I wish they had just opted for a more basic cover-based FPS, or a 3rd-person action RPG, or something else that they might have had the resources to do decently.At least there's an easy mode so I can get power through the campaign, and see what other lovely scenery they've put together.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM meets Warhammer.  + Takedowns+ Artstyle+ Gameplay+ Story  - Menus- Inventory - Way too much unnecessary stuff  Gameplay is very Quake/Doom like (Double jump, air-dash…) Takedowns are probably the most enjoyable part of the whole game. Characters look very good, unfortunately, there are no customization options only the outfit colors can be changed. Side missions are very generic and repetitive. Way too much stuff going on in this game, grappling wallrunning air dodge… the movement is all you can imagine but does not feel very smooth. Wallrunning in particular was pretty bad in my opinion, the levels are just not made for it, and when you manage to find a straight wall that you can wallrun, there are no enemies around most of the time. Inventory was bad, it took me a while to get used to it. It felt a lot more like a 2010 game. Instead of perfecting a few things, this game tried to fit as many things in it as possible.  5 - 10 hours   Easy  Worth a try  The mastiff becoming a cyber-dog with the upgrades progression was very cool to see, I would like the see same thing on the main character but I understand the difficulties with that.“Side missions” I am not sure what happened there, and why are there so many.All of them are just quick repetitive missions with a simple goal so that you can get some easy money I guess, I did not really feel the need to play them while doing the main missions. Weapons and abilities, another less is more case… You can equip up to 6 different weapons and use X abilities, I would either limit the amount of the weapons since I rarely used more than 3 anyway or at least the abilities. To be honest, I never used most of them just because the button was on the other end of the keyboard + there not being any tutorial for the abilities and pretty much getting all of them at once made it impossible to remember anything. Weapon damage is also all over the place, for some reason the most powerful weapon when it comes to damage is a short variant of a double barrel shotgun, while heavy guns feel completely useless, especially on a higher difficulty. Overall the game felt very  average. Price seems to be raised just because they slapped the Warhammer 40K tag on it. To be honest, I had no idea it is Warhammer 40K related in any way, I did find out after I beat the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't lie to you - Necromunda: Hired Gun is a janky game. It's got not-so-infrequent bugs, a story that would be run-of-the-mill if it weren't so confusingly told, a muddled interface, and very little variety in its gameplay. I'm recommending it regardless, because of four elements that outshine the total lack of polish. First, the moment-to-moment gunplay is simply FUN. It's fast-paced and frantic, enemies explode in gratifying ways, guns have a satisfactory kick, your various bionic powers are fun to play with, there's just enough variety in hostiles to keep things interesting, and every weapon feels suitably different, even before you start customising them. I played through a number of the secondary missions for cash, and though they're repetitive, I still enjoyed scraping through each one. It's seldom a chore.Second, the visual and sound design is spot-on. The game brings the grimy depths of Necromunda to life in all their horrible diversity. Each level looks substantially different, each character you spend more than a minute interacting with is extremely striking and memorable, and there are dozens of little details that will stick with you and inform the way you imagine this setting even long after you've finished with the game. As a series of places and people to stare at and listen to, this game is a triumph.Third, the aforementioned customisability. I have a real soft spot for games that allow you to futz around in meaningful ways with your weaponry and abilities, and Necromunda: Hired Gun certainly does that. More pressingly, for me, it actually reflects that on the models; the fact that the guns you mod look substantially different depending on your upgrades, and even show whatever trinkets you've hung on them dangling from the barrel in-game, is a huge plus... if a little traumatic when it comes to your mastiff's cybernetics.Fourth, the mastiff. You can, indeed, pet the dog.If you love grim dark sci-fi and fast-paced gunplay, this is definitely worth your time... though perhaps not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: What a weird surprise this game was, never expected for this to drop and be so good. It is mix of a fast pace frantic shooter and what vaguely feels like a board games idea of a weapon system. Instead of just having loot like you would in something like Borderlands or Shadow Warrior 2, you are finding set guns and +1 and +2 versions of them. The ones you get in the beginning are just as good as the ones you find later, only leveled out by the +1 and +2 versions of them. The only downside is, you can't buy the +2 versions of the weapons, so you have to rely on luck that you will pull one from a loot crate. Otherwise, I found the upgrade system really fun and it allowed me to get insanely powerful in the late game. Instead of just bumping your stats, it encourages the in-your-face gameplay that this game really excels at. I would recommend this to any fans of shooters or 40k.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: The game is decent and does well in capturing the sense of scale and atmosphere of Necromunda and the gameplay is generally fun but it's not for everyone. There's a few echoes of EYE, one of the first Streum game in the gameplay, some will like this others not so much. As the gameplay is fast paced, more down to fast reactions movement including making use of the grappling hook for verticality. Those who wanted a more tactical slower paced shooter will likely not get one with it.While I'm ok with it that, two things I don't like are that you can't save progress during a mission (and they are quite long) only between missions. And you can't organize your inventory whenever you want, not even in the home base/operations hub. Instead you can only arrange your inventory just prior to launching to a new mission, which is not good. I also have issue with elements of the controls, such as crouch and slide being bound to the same key, i like to use a side mouse button on my 5 button mouse for dodge/slides but having to crouch with that mouse button, it doesnt feel right. I ended up using shift key for crouch and dodge, which is not ideal but works better.So there are problems,but  to me the pros outweight the cons and I have generally enjoyed fighting my way through the hive city so as a 40k fan I give it a thumb up despite of the problems. Those who are less forgiving, may not get on with it so much, but overall there is fun to be had in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game basically exists for fans of Necromunda. If you're already a fan of the universe and setting, then you're bound to enjoy this game. If not, it's likely a solid pass, unless you want a lesser Doom clone.The highly mobile and Doom style combat is fun and adrenaline-inducing. Gun play and customization is solid and feels great. Story seems decent so far (I'm only a few main missions in), but by no means is it the real focus of the game. It's really all about the combat. Enemy spawning seems odd at times and the knife takedowns are a little janky, but shooting at stuff feels great, even when it's a lore-appropriate bullet sponge like an Ogryn or Ambot. I've been a huge fan of Necromunda for over a decade, and this game allows me to explore the Underhive like I've always wanted. I get to run around in my Escher gear, using Escher weapons and cause chaos for anyone who isn't me. Having a hub to hang out in between missions and pet my doggo is icing on the cake!Overall, give Hired gun a go if you like Necromunda or 40k as a franchise. I grabbed it during this year's summer sale for cheap along with some skins. I felt it was worth it at a reduced price to be sure, but maybe not so much at full price. If you're looking for a more polished game with similar style of gameplay, just get Doom Eternal instead.Hope to see you in the Underhive, sump-scum!

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is an explosive FPS that does a few crucial things fantastically to a point where a lot of other less stellar aspects just don't end up mattering. Firstly it has a large number of giant, incredibly detailed and gorgeous WH 40K environments that are just a joy to fight in. You have a double jump and a grapple hook to help vertical travel so these levels can just be massive which works with the setting. Secondly the weapons are absolutely glorious with each looking, sounding and feeling unique and just ripping through enemies each harder than the last one. The visuals from the look of the weapons to their effects and enemies response to them(usually blowing up in many ways but also just getting hit) are exactly what I like.So yeah between having a blast just using these weapons and moving through gorgeous environments for most of the game the bad parts just aren't anywhere near bad enough for them to slow my roll at all. The animations are iffy and cutscenes are clearly really cheaply done. The side missions are fine for money but are not good extra content. The game crashed on me a bunch of times but only during loads where I didn't actually lose any progress. The Voiceacting is actually decent but the story is very filler. So nothing gamebreaking but janky in places. Overall Hired Guns core is simply so good I had a hell of a time regardless. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a mixed option, I'll give this a mixed one. It's not that bad and provides some fun, but has flaws.Not worth at full price, buy it at a discount. If you didn't like the new DooMs then you will not like this game 100%.What is this game? Basically it's DooM 2016/Eternal on a budget with a few additions set in W40k hive decorations. And when playing you are just forced to compare them.The good and the average:-The visuals are ok, the OST is mostly ok, worse than Mick Gordons ofc, the sound design is ok. But for example there isn't any ambient music in lots of places or sound wise the place feels empty. The combat sounds and voice design also could have been better.- Aesthetically it provides some of W40k underhive vibe and has some good visual design decisions.- The gameplay has some additional elements in a form of augmentation powers which help and provide gameplay variation both in movement and killing abilities, making it a bit like Titanfall. In general elements it’s DooM on a budget.- You may rerun any mission and there are side missions which are a part of a level with a certain simple objective: like attack the objectives, capture points or defend the area, etc.- The enemies, the level design and gameplay loop are generally worse. Lots of times enemies spawn from all directions and you are just forced to jump dodge around the place without any tactic, except a lot of attacks are instahits so you will lose hp no matter what. The pathing of enemies isn't that great and their general behavior and variations mostly feel generic. The level design and enemies spawn encounters are much worse “synchronized” in terms of combat feeling. But yet still there are fun fights to be had.The bad:- The pacing on some levels is bad, they may drag too much or throw too many enemies at you in one place, sometimes unneeded endless hordes, or too little. But some leves are fun and most of the levels have interesting encounters.- The guns don't feel impactful or really different when firing and in terms of their effects on enemies.- The itemisation system is not needed and is bad.- The side missions are generic and lazy, the faction standing system is useless.

_childDocuments_.review: W O W this is bad. I really thought that the reviews were exaggerating, but as it would turn out, they really undersold just how janky this entire game is. This game fails on absolutely every junction, save for maybe the graphics. Gameplay, animations, plot, voice acting, dialogue; all of it is just some of the most discombobulated dross I've seen in a game this price. It is all bad, and not the "Bad, but charming" kind of way that you get from a small indie studio doing their best, but lacking skill. This is like if you hired a whole bunch of talent, but none of them had ever made a shooter before, so no one had any idea what to do. They just started slapping ideas together that they knew people liked, and hoped that would be enough.The guns, arguably the most important part of a shooter, all feel absolutely dreadful. The revolvers feel way too underwhelming; the assault rifles even more so. It's like you've been given a BB gun against a juggernaut. Everything just feels like you're playing some F2P mobile game because, instead of just making a regular game, they decided to make a looter shooter where loot is about as sparse as the fun. This next thing doesn't make much sense if you don't play a lot of shooters, but this game simply feels terrible during fights. The bullets never go where they're supposed to, the weapons feel like they have some weird delay that makes them close to hit-scan, but aren't, and the sensitivity just never feels like you can get it quite right. Even when it doesn't feel too slow or too fast, it seems like your aim never actually goes where it should. Even when you aim at someone's head with a scoped revolver, the bullet just doesn't land. Enemies feel like a blob rather than anything humanoid, and the white outline solidifies that, so there's a huge disconnect between headshots and body shots. The looting is clearly just there to try and keep people playing. Half of my short time spent playing was exploring the nooks and crannies of the first two levels, and the amount of empty space is absurd. Within one massive, open, optional tucked away area, there was a single loot box. The rest of the area had no enemies, no ground loot, and no crates. The first two levels are nothing BUT that; empty space and linear combat. For what reason did they add loot if they weren't going to reward the player for exploration? They even have an "Exploration stat" for crying out loud, but exploring is the biggest waste of time possible. Worse is when you realize that if you don't waste your time on every level looking for that one loot box per empty square mile, you'll be under geared and chewed up like a toy for missing out on what little loot you can get. The animations...oh god, the animations. I really found myself laughing at how bad the animations in Turbo Overkill were, especially considering they were fine using it in their main trailer...but that game is made by one guy. This was made by a team, and the animations are hardly any better. It's not just the occasional poor animation, but ALL of them. Movement, idling, conversation; it's all an absolute joke. This game's graphics mesh so poorly with everything else you see because you're constantly being shown competent graphics that try to pull you into this grungy world, but are then affronted by animations worse than what an art student would make for their 1st year project. The voice acting is some B movie quality stuff at best; the dialogue, even worse. Nothing screams ineptitude like your character shouting "He's not my fwend!" 7 times in about 2 minutes. Very funny, didn't wear off the first time at all. You also have the "I should have worked alone" trash, which is honestly fine if the game is self aware and has that charm of something made well aware of what it is.This game is not that. It has absolutely no idea what it is, and that's the motif of this entire trash fire. Is it an arena shooter? Is it a cover shooter? Is it a looter shooter? No, it's all of the above. This is the magnum opus of Jack of All Trades, master of none. This does a whole bunch of stuff, but it does absolutely nothing well. Above all else, it's just not fun. Your money would be better spent on just about anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: The game fascinates with its atmosphere. The grim and detailed world of Necromunda draws you into its dark, gritty environment. Each level is meticulously designed, creating a sense of immersion in this dangerous and brutal world.The gameplay is a highlight for fans of fast-paced shooters. The speed and intensity of the combat keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. I particularly enjoyed the variety of weapons and abilities available for use in battles. The cyber-mastiff is a fantastic addition, not only aiding in combat but also adding a unique twist to the gameplay.The graphics are impressive as well. Stunning effects, sharp textures, and the overall art style make every battle visually striking. Despite some minor technical issues, the visual presentation is strong and engaging.However, not everything is perfect. While the combat and environments are excellent, there can be a lack of variety in the missions. Some tasks feel repetitive, which slightly diminishes the overall experience. Additionally, there are occasional bugs that can be a bit annoying but don't significantly detract from the enjoyment of the game.In the end, Necromunda: Hired Gun is a thrilling and atmospheric shooter that's well worth playing for fans of the genre. My score of 8 out of 10 reflects the high quality of the game and the enjoyment it provides, despite a few minor flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna address something really fast ahead of everything else and that is the performance. Contrary to what some people claim, this game runs absolutely fine sans some short load stutters that I think might be caused by the fact that I'm playing it from a crappy old HDD from like five years ago. Medium settings, 1080p, stable 60-70 FPS on a 1050ti with ryzen 3100 and 16gb of RAM. Compared to Deathwing's launch, this is leaps and bounds ahead so if you can run Deathwing you can run this, no questions asked.Overall, it's a B-production sort of a game. It's not particularly well polished(though given who Streum On are, this is extremely polished in comparison) but at its core it's a great game. Gameplay. Not sure where those comparisons to Doom of all things come from, it plays nothing like that, more of a Titanfall-ish experience. I guess finishers confuse people. Gun customization is an unusual surprise, but a welcome one; nothing says "successful bounty hunter" as a royal purple autogun swinging from your hip after all. Grapple hook is more of a Just Cause style ordeal, getting you to a location instantly, so don't expect fancy swings from it. Weapons feel as solid as they come though I would kinda prefer heavy stubber to sound meatier. Dog can be petted and upgraded, but your personal good boy's AI is a bit on the janky side. Still really good at showing scavs what's what. Overall equipment system is alright but there's a suspicious lack of extra armor types which would be neat to see addressed, seeing only underarmors is kinda weird.Story? An excuse to get you to unlock more levels. It's inconsequential. Slightly brought down by bad audio mixing but it really is just a vessel for move violence and nothing else. You can try following it but that's entirely at your own cost. Side missions are gonna be very familiar if you've played EYE, they just drop you into a location and let you go at it. In short, no points deducted since it doesn't get in the way, just don't expect a thrilling intrigue or something.Visually it's not exactly a AAA production ordeal, you can spot some dodgy textures, but overall it's an absolute treat. Great design, nothing less I expected from Streum On frankly. They just get how 40k should look like. Helped by lighting, though some of it is kinda too bright in places but it usually makes sense when it happens. Some more stalwart people might object to bolters having picatinny rails but that's on GW introducing them like several redactions ago and devs just going with the flow. Ogrins have slightly odd animations but nothing offensive.Overall I can recommend Hired Gun with very little hesitation. It might need some patching to smooth out minor wrinkles but it's a pretty decent game. It doesn't reach for the stars but it doesn't really need to.Maybe wait for a sale if $40 is too much for you and other reviews seem confusingly negative(as some of them are full of bollocks as mentioned in the preamble) and you're just not really feeling like risking a simple, B level production game at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun one but with a number of problems that keep it from every truly being great. I understand why there is no sideways thumb button. A "Meh" recommendation. The idea is the reviewer should, at the end of the experience, be able to say for certain if someone should, or should not play the game based on all the criteria they have reviewed the product upon. After all, no one would want someones expert advice on something to be a shrug of the shoulders. That being said, if there was ever a game I would apply the "meh" option of recommending, this would be one of them. Let's get started. TL:DR at the bottom.The Game Loop - Necromunda is a game that plays like most action games of the era. There's upgrading your character, upgrading your companion, upgrading your guns, all while not being at a Borderlands style of loot grab. More of a Ghost Recon style of weapon upgrading. Different barrels, scopes, stocks, ammo make for a slightly beefier gun, or faster but less powerful variant. All of these systems play as well and as worn as you might expect. Increase bullet time, increase armor, increase refresh rate on pet. All of it tied up and packaged in that nice and complex technobabble that is Warhammer. You didn't "upgrade" your armor. You ripped out your chest and replaced it with a titanium plate. You didn't enhance your eyes with laser surgery, you popped that sucker out and replaced it with machinery. It all works and fits well. The Story-The story is next, and this is one of those sideways thumb kind of moments. The story gets the job done, but it never wows. Granted, I don't think story was ever a key part in the development mindset. It's a story of betrayal and vengeance and that is enough to propel one forward. What doesn't mesh well is that while the story is linear to the point of nausea, the characters all seem like they have something more to tell. Not the main characters either. The Bar Tender, for example, is one of a few people I found myself more curious about that didn't get expanded.             -as an important sidenote. I, myself, don't know much of Warhammer, but I do really enjoy the design of the whole thing. I won't ever pretend to know anything about the lore beyond "It's all gone to hell in the 40th century." From what I found out on reading, however, is the main quest giver is an actual prominent character in the WH40K universe. So, wasting his potential does seem like a sin against this story telling. The Gameplay-Gameplay. This is where it gets strange. The weapons and tools for the job (your dog, grenades, healing items) are all top notch. The Dog upgrades from a flesh and blood mastiff to a nightmare hound from the mechanical hells. The guns are chunky, clunky, and complex. Animations on them are great. Sound effects are mostly spot on, with most guns sounding great with only a few underwhelming offerings. Money is plentiful just by doing side missions and keep you swimming in upgrades. But then there's the other side of gameplay.A hit scan system that just sees your enemies hit you from whatever distance they feel like, and damage that sees your health fall from whatever full is for you, right down to that last ten percent. The "resistant to damage when near death" perk becomes an absolute necessity because of how this works. The incentive; "rip and tear until it is done". They were entirely too inspired by Doom here, and instead of a game featuring gunfights, you have a scramble to damage your enemies to regain health, smashing your melee button to get into a instakill animation to stop from taking damage. The instakills want to look really cool too (and sometimes do) but other times it seems way too quick on the animation, or jumbled during the animation, and you can't tell what's going on anymore besides "The enemy is being removed and you are being rewarded with a bullet shield for the animation and health." This becomes tedious instead of awesome. It becomes necessary to melee to survive, and when enemies pop spawn ceaselessly around you (Literally, they will NOT stop coming and they spawn pretty close to you. Not in front of you, but just around the corner), melee lock ups become the only way to survive the day.Wall Running. I love it. I hate it. For the most part, you don't even need it. It looks cool when you do it, until it looks awful when you do it. The truth is, it auto-runs on the wall if you press jump a second time near a wall. If you're not expecting it to mag-lock to the wall and start running, you'll find yourself running off the edge of the map and into lava. Other times, you're Keanu Reevesing your way across the hotel lobby in the matrix and feeling bad ass while doing so. It's another love/hate relationship here. For the most part it works, right up until it doesn't.The Verdict-With a minor playtime of about 7 to 10 hours for the campaign (I take my time and look around a lot. Faster runs may be 5 to 7.) and an unending number of objective based side missions (Hold area, Hunt enemy, Eradicate Enemy, Free Prisoners, Collect the Stuff) There's a little bit to keep you going back or just gathering up more money for the upgrades. Problem is, there's nothing off to the side beyond that. No upgrades for your home base area, no cosmetic collection items besides skins for guns, hell you can't even have a drink at the bar (dunno why, but that bugged me). No people beyond quest giving every says or interacts like they are there. No lore items to store in your collection library (not in a significant way anyway). There's just an overall lack of polish and consideration to things that would have made this more long term. The combat is fast paced, with glaring oversights to how the enemy hits you, how hard and fast they hit you, and how you heal it. The story goes just far enough to tell you what to do, and never far enough to feel fleshed out and well done. In the end, this game is fun. At full price, It's hard to recommend, but I did enjoy it for what it was. On a decent sale, this game becomes much more attractive to pick up. Fun and frustrating, ups and downs, highs and lows, this game is great when it's all working right and a slog when it isn't. If you're a forgiving player, you'll enjoy it well enough. If you're easily frustrated or demand a tighter product for your money, look elsewhere.The Good-Weapons and Companion Cyber Mutt are great.The graphic design is absolutely stunning. True WH40K design as most of their games are.Sound design is extremely well done in most areas.The Bad-Combat becomes laughably bad at times when overwhelmed with pop spawn hit scan enemies.Life Bar is there for show. In reality, you only get the bottom 20% of your health most of time.Kill To Heal is done to death here, and overdone on the melee lock up to the point of ridiculousness.The Ugly-The story never tries to be any more than it has to be. Nor do it's players on the stage (NPCs)The Wall Running. It's both awesome and abusive in nature. Love it and hate it.No extras. Side missions are only for money, never for another tale to tell.If you want a number attached to this, It balances on 7/10, tipping toward 6. I enjoy it for what it is, but boy do I wish there was more to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the main campaign + some side mission grinding for upgrades in just under 10 hours.  Thoughts:The decision to make this a pseudo looter shooter is a bizarre one.  I do not believe this game needed those elements.  They basically added grinding, which I'm not sure anyone really wants.  You also run out of new guns to unlock around half way through the campaign, which was a bit of a disappointment.  I was enjoying trying new guns out, but for the last half of the game I stuck more or less to the first highest quality gun I found entirely.The upgrades are about half useless as far as I can tell.  For whatever reason, you can only bind one key to use special abilities you unlock (and it replaces your ability to quickly use a healthpack).  Otherwise you're accessing these abilities from a power wheel when you click the middle mouse button, but the game isn't paused during this so I mostly only used one power constantly.I liked having the dog available as often as possible because he lets you see enemies through walls.  However, this would be less necessary if the levels were less weird and you didn't need that sort of thing to help you find your way through the game.  Also, in combat, the dog could sometimes get in the way of you quickly eliminating enemies which grew tiresome.I did a lot of complaining here, but I actually had a lot of fun with this game in spite of all of it.  The combat is fast and frantic which feels weird in comparison to the cover shooters we've mostly had for the last million years.   Weapon customization (excluding needing to find +3 versions of the weapons) was neat, I particularly enjoyed my bolter and my double barreled shotgun.  Also, it'd be great if the Doom Eternal guys could learn a lesson from these guys on ammo, because Necromunda basically doesn't care which gun you use, and it's wonderful to have ammo shared across the different weapons.TLDR:  Neat little game, kinda janky.  Not a 60$ game and it shows, but fun for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game has a fantastic atmosphere and excellent dialogue, it contains too many issues with this game to be an enjoyable experience. I have had issues including but not limited to having the game launch on the incorrect monitor with no way to fix it, sudden spikes in performance having my fps top at 130 and randomly tank to 20, and unreasonable amounts of motion through the use of head bobbing and screen shake, even inside the menus, with no way to turn it off.The gunplay has a good look to it, but it feels very untested. The creators seem to attempt to replicate DOOM's style, which makes it feel more like an unrefined "shoot everything" style of game, with no real reason to change your weapon at all.Overall, this game looks great in concept and environment, but there's a lot that needs to be tuned and fixed before I'll throw $55 AUD at it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Warhammer and Necromunda fan I am surely biased - positively biased - towards this game.It looks nice, the designers created not only picturesque and variable environment, but the humor and small hints of dialogues, propaganda posters and other minor details indicate true love and dedication for this game. It catches the spirit of the Grim Darkness.If you're a fan of aforementioned setting - this game is a go at least to see the visualization.As a game, it is still raw and unfinished. I waited for half a year as fixes were released, and at least skipped the phase of non-working ladders. As a dedicated fan, I can forgive crashes, stucking in textures, ridiculously drafted-state cutscenes etc.Game design is where things start going downhill. Shooting feels unpolished. Guns look great, they technically shoot and feel different. Bolter, an iconic Warhammer weapon, feels like a full-auto slow firing machine of obliteration - which is good. Bolt pistol on every single shot feels the same - but shoots as fast as you click. Which kinda destroys the impact and immersion into the gunplay for obvious balancing reasons.The game balance is even more lacking. Grind walls are not trouble per se, though the game might provide hints of player level for plot missions.The worst part are boss fights. Not only they are grind-walled to your surprise, they are broken by nature. Infinite enemies spawning, paired with one-shot boss weapons - this is not a test of skill like Souls-like, there is no skill to develop. This is test of patience, grinding and breaking the game even further finding blind spots in Boss AI.I really wanted to love this game. Tactical Necromunda (Underhive Wars) lack AI, lacks endgame content and many things, but it is at least playable. Sorry Hired Gun, for me you are a Fired Gun.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I review this I just want to state, that the warhammer community have a serious issue with being willing to accept total crap as a "good" product and it reflects poorly on the universe when games like necromunda unhive war, and Warhammer underworlds are considered to be decent games. They're not, both are incomplete trash that are kind of insulting when you see a khorne blood warrior with no idle animations listfuly swat at a ork, like a blind kitten. I'm saying this because i care about the franchise and the majority of what we get is mobile dreck, with non of the passion or energy the world deserves. Which bring us to Hired gun, Streum On Stuido are one of the better developers of war hammer games. Yes most of what i've played from them are Euro-jank but that's to be expected from a smaller studio making a high budget game. But they at least care enough to put the effort in to properly represent the universe. The game it'self is a momentum shooter similar to the new dooms, with a kind of janky spell system which they really should have defaulted to tab for, but regardless they significantly improve the game play. The game itself is beautiful, a little let down by GW insisting on developers using their product line in the world, but that's a GW issue. This is not going to be a "Main game" for you, over all this is a one time play through which is pretty but kind of forgetable, and secondary missions are basically some brink level go back and kill some guys kind of thing.My real complaints are that stealth is straight up impossible despite being implied to be a part of the game, implying the existence of items by having "light under suit". making a distinction like this kind of promises a medium or heavy suit that's not in the game, and the returning infinite enemy spawns from 'Death Wing' Over all, i'd say 6/10 it's a good game, way above average for a Warhammer game. The important thing is they basically murdered 'underhive war' as a necromunda game, that ♥♥♥♥ let me down so much. Underworlds did too but, I mean i knew that was gonna be crap when they did the first dev interveiw.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks great but just isn't fun enough for me to continue playing. Gameplay tries to emulate the high speed combat of Doom Eternal but fails to learn several important lessons from it, most notably that you need to make a game like that very readable at a glance. Enemies are nigh indistinguishable because they're all the same kind of humanoid person with shabby armour and they're tiny at a distance. You start firing and sometimes they have shields, sometimes they don't, sometimes the shields go down fast, sometimes they feel like minibosses. There's big hulking guys of varying toughness occasionally.This game feels like it needed another 12+ months of iteration time to find the fun and revise some core design issues. It doesn't feel like it knows what it wants to be. On the one hand it's Doomish but it has ADS, and it discourages being out in the open moving fast because you'll get melted by all enemies with hitscan weapons at once. It's a looter shooter RPGish game but there's no damage numbers or health bars to tell how tough enemies are or which weapons are effective. It's the worst of both worlds.

Go there, talk to this person, then this person, then go to the bar and talk to this person, then pick a mission- A few bugs kept making me restart the game, cause some grapple-hook movements place you inside a wall and you can't get out. - A few times the game crashed on me with no apparent reason. One time was between missions, on time was in the middle of a mission.- I had to complete almost half the game to start understanding how equipment management works in this game and after getting most of the expensive tools and gadgets I honestly can't say which one does more damage. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Level aesthetics;- Interesting Campaign;- Nice Arsenal of 40k weapons.Cons:- Poor Side missions design;- Enjoyable but shallow combat;- Atrocious interface;- A bit short for the price tag- no significant updates since release.To expand on the above: the levels are beautifully lore-friendly and can be breathtaking, as expected from the team that delivered Space Hulk Deathwing. That being said, while it improves on the formula substantially, the game seems to dsuffer from similar shortcomings.The main Campaign is really nice and enjoyable, and will have you explore a multitude of different environments that will please greatly any 40k fan. The story is decently interesting, with good voice-acting that will almost make you ignore the janky animations of the characters. Your Arsenal of weapons is varied and offers a good choice on how to blast your enemies away. Some very iconic weapons like the Boltgun or Plasma Gun are enjoyable to wield, and the Character skill tree gives you some very nice (if a bit OP) powers to choose from.--Now, aside from that, the side content is really disappointing. The first time you'll select one of the side bounties (to play as, you know, a Bounty Hunter) you'll be brought back to one of the levels you already cleared, but confined to a small portion of it, where the AI just spawn seemingly randomly around you, even in areas you just cleared.This combines with the poor combat mechanics: the game tries to give you a lot of movement freedom à la Doom, mixed with Titanfall (wallruns, grappling hooks, etc...), but the enemies don't really play into that style. They will shower you with bullets from everywhere (remember the spawning frenzy?), and it is really hard to take cover, forcing you in a hit and run playstyle.The health mechanics are a bit weird too, with you having a Shield and a Health bar, but your shield does not refill on its own, but rather needs pick-ups, effectively becoming just another health bar. You can theoretically replenish your HP by damaging enemies right after taking damage yourself, but because of the aforementioned gameplay mechanics, it is almost never enough.Thankfully, most of the game can be cheesed through by exploiting the Takedown mechanics: an enemy can be instantly executed from any angle, provided their shield is down and that you are close enough - even the 'big' enemies such as Ambots and Ogryns. And soon enough you'll even unlock a power that lets you execute a shielded enemy and strip them of their protection. Of course you're invincible during the takedown animations (which are a bit sketchy but varied), meaning you can just leap (with your grappling gun) from one foe to the other, just chain executing them till they stop spawning.__TLDR: the gazme is beautiful and sports an enjoyable Campaign, especially for 40k fans. However, the combat gameplay and the side content can be a bit disappointing, so I'd recommend waiting for a sale to try the main story out.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative reviews seem to have been under the assumption that this was going to be a triple-A release with the kind of gravitas that comes with that. Hired Gun is a wonderful double-A-ish title that brings some careful polish in some departments and loveable eurojank in others. It's not so odd as to be impossible to pick up on its own merits, but if you enjoyed some of the stranger traits of E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy then you're in for a very familiar, pleasant sort of experience. The mobility is crisp, guns feel good, and the weapon diversity is far from lacking. Weapon customization is excellent, and the palette of player characters you're offered has something for everyone on it. Bugs are minimal, mostly cosmetic at worst. Performance has some potential issues at the highest end, but the game maintains its visual charm even at reduced settings. The cybernetic system doesn't demonize you for augmenting yourself or your mastiff, and in fact it's only upsides to do so. The story isn't some record-setting narrative experience, but it's strong enough to stand on its own and the side missions are nice little compliments to help you earn currency or find rarer weapons. It feels like the game has an underlayer of mechanics that I don't yet totally understand, but I've enjoyed all my time playing it and I'm looking forward to giving the game a shot on a higher difficulty after this clear

_childDocuments_.review: I bet it smells like rotten eggs.Necromunda: Hired Gun is a first person shooter set in the Warhammer 40,000 Universe. You play as the Hired Gun, a mercenary/bounty hunter on the tail of the Silver Talon, a wanted gang leader with a massive bounty. Being a wanted gang leader on Necromunda must be like being the biggest zit on a teenager's face. After his team of other mercenaries are killed, the Hired Gun teams up with discount Felix Jaeger and a Hive scavenger I like to call “Potato” and sets out on an adventure to get revenge on the ghost that killed his team as well as collect on the bounty of the Silver Talon. I'm not entirely sure where the game takes place on Necromunda, but I'm about 99% sure its Hive Primus, the Palatine Hive of the planet where most of the important things happen. If you're unfamiliar, a hive city in the 40,000 universe is like a Mega city from Judge Dredd, but built up instead of outwards. Usually they're pretty crummy, but the Necromunda Hive cities are infamous for being the champions in the “♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥” category. Cities like this exist to build -something- for the Imperium of Man at large, weapons, armor, vehicles, food sometimes, building material, this hive in particular manufactures Lasguns en masse. Particularly the Nihilis pattern, which is a pretty garbage lasgun, also known as the “Cancer Lasgun”Because it gives you cancer. Hired Gun's story is kind of hard to talk about. Basically things just kind of happen, people tell the hired gun where he (or she) needs to go, and then he goes there. Sometimes he finds what he's looking for, sometimes he doesn't, repeat for about 9 missions before something ACTUALLY happens. There's an overarching plot about your implants in the game, but its only brought up every now and then, for the most part you're just wasting dudes until you reach the end. You can put him in as many  games as you want, I'm still not reading the Kal Jerico books. Your enemies come in several varieties, almost entirely from the gangs you see in the actual Necromunda tabletop game. House Orlock, basically the mooks Necromunda. They produce the majority of Iron on Necromunda and hold a monopoly on Ashe Waste convoys. They also make the booze. House Goliath are roid raging super gorilla's that were originally made by the Nobles of Necromunda as a slave race. Big strong boys with big strong guns and clubs. House Escher are the girls that have a monopoly on cooties and giving kissies. Also drugs, they produce a lot of drugs. Some sort of defect makes their men come out all weird looking. So you can guess how they keep their numbers up. Uh. Cawdor and Delaque, aren't in the games. Van Saar and the Palatine Enforcers  are only mentioned, and the Squats are MIA. And you can bet your ass Klovis is MIA. There's also a re-use enemy from the other 40k game from this developer for, like, one mission. But that's a spoiler. The game's difficulty is kind of like a seesaw. I played this game on hard and there didn't seem to be rhythm or reason for the difficulty spikes. Sometimes I got wasted on B-grade missions and then sauntered through S-rank missions like a saucy minx. Outside of the main quest, which can take you anywhere from 5 to 9 hours to beat depending on the difficulty and how serious you take it, you can also do side missions for extra money. They just reuse the main story maps and reuse a small number of objectives. But they only kind of exist so you can afford more of your implants earlier.Gameplay is where the game shines. The guns are nice and crunchy to use and fire, and whatever you hit is going to turn into a fine, tasty red paste real quick. The game accounts for a large number of weapons from the 40k universe. The Autogun is one of the earliest weapon and works as you would think, as a regular assault rifle from other games with a bit extra kick.The Bolter in Necromunda is particularly nice, working as you would think a bolter would and absolutely mulching whatever you're firing at. A good time to talk about the gore in the game, with limbs being blasted off, heads going flying away,and guts flinging from corpses as the top half explodes until constant “I don't want you to exist anymore” fire. Blood even drips from the ceiling when you're done, its a nice touch, that's usually only something I see in DOOM Wads or other gory classic shooters.Outside of that, you also have a host of abilities. The Hired Gun can heighten their reflexes and basically just make everything sloooow You have an auto aim ability that just blasts heads off, you can blast people with your bionic arm, launch towards them, or go on a knife-stabbing spree. The Underhive of Necromunda looks exactly like you think it would. A hive city in general is hard to fathom, and I can't even wrap my head around something like Hive Primus on Necromunda. There are entire parts of the city that are lost to the Houses, and these gangs fight in wars that make World War 2 look reasonable in comparison. Necromunda: Hired gun is in general a good time, if not a bit stupid. There are parts of the game that, looking back, I'm not entirely sure how I got through. They can throw dozens of dudes at you at once and they come in multiple flavors, some enemies even taking a few solid seconds of shooting to take down. You do have a lot of options, and even a grappling hook as well as wall running, strafe dashing, and sliding to keep your distance, but man, it can be rough.Get it on sale if you can, or don't, I'm not a cop. The gunplay can be a lot of fun, and its nice to see a completely different world than the rest of Warhammer 40,000. No pun intended.Okay,  pun a bit intended. Necromunda: Hired Gun gets 6 hard to follow execution moves out of 10. 1 in every 5,000 North Atlantic Lobsters are born bright blue.Special thanks to Outic for gifting me this game. He is now the Underlord of Hive Primus and I can no longer contain his girth.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, I had a ton of fun with this game. It has it's problems but it was way better than I was expecting. Would def buy if you're looking for a game similar to DOOM to waste some time on.Story:The story leaves a bit to be desired. But I really wasn't expecting all that much from a game based around chasing bounties. Basically the entire questline is based around hunting down someone for a massive payout. There's a couple of twists here and there, but story def isn't a main selling point of this game.Gameplay:I honestly enjoyed this game more than DOOM: Eternal when it game to the gameplay. Ammo isn't anywhere near as scarce so I got to actually enjoy the weapons I like more. Combat is fast paced, it lets you grapple hook, double jump, wall run, dodge and move at fast asf speeds (There's a bunch of other abilities as well that you can unlock as you play). The combat areas are all pretty big and let you take advantage of the movement pretty well. Enemies didn't feel super obnoxious and sqongey (At least on normal). Also you get a doggo that rips people apart that'll appear after you play with a squeaky toy, so that's a plus.Visuals/Music:I'm not all that fussed normally when it comes to graphics so I thought the game looked pretty noice. Everything ran smoothly on ultra which is actually pretty rare for me (usually I have to bump things down to medium to get stable frames). The scale and style on things were pretty awesome. I'm not massively into Warhammer, but I've heard it's probably one of the best representations of the scale of things out there.I enjoyed the music. There's some cyberpunk/wild west themes going on with heavy metal jamming while you're in combat sometimes. Nothing too outstanding but it was good.Customisation:The game lets you choose your own character model at the start of the game. Most of them look pretty cool, but the female voice felt pretty eh. On top of that you can choose a few colour schemes for your character and doggo that you can swap out between missions. Weapons have a whole attachment system alongside some skins (You can also rename your weapon if you grow attached to it). I've heard some Warhammer fans don't like it, but I honestly wish Darktide had a similar system.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, the reviews here have a power to exonerate an otherwise poorly critically performing game. Seeing that square on Metacritic turn yellow is sure to give me pause when deciding on what to play next, but Steam's "Very Positive" usually sets me back on the right track. But only 70%?! I mean, what the hell, guys? Any lower than that and I'd have to call in the Chirurgeon to give your bionics a look-see, what with that giant stick up your rear starting to qualify as one dangerous cybernetic implant.Set in the gruesome and vibrant steampunk world of Warhammer 40k's Necromunda,  is a ridiculously fun time. Streum On Studio seems adamant to get the fun parts of its cult classic  into a more palatable form and in front of a mainstream audience, and I think they did a solid job of hitting that mark. Having another shooter focused on movement, creative ability usage, and designing the perfect arsenal out of almost two dozen weapons that you can kit out with different mags, scopes and barrels, is as refreshing as it is exciting, and something we could definitely use more of. Like, seriously. Doing a retro shooter with the Space Marines front and centre is the safest bet you could make, second only to another strategy game.  might not look like the most innovative or daring title out there, but it sticks out compared to the developer's previous output, which found itself a niche of its own, as well as the wider scene of Warhammer 40,000 games, by not conforming entirely to the standards of a mid-to-high budget release, and bringing and retaining its own brand of weird and jank.That being said, it seems some sacrifices had to be made to fit something like this into a game that looks closer to a modern release rather than a Source mod, as everything in , except for the core experience, doesn't feel all that meaningful. Sure, all the ways to kill a cyberpunk is the most important piece of the puzzle and, at the end of the day, what you should be here for, but with the story, the characters, the weapon progression, the side bounties, the hub world (uh-huh, keep going, almost there), and certain gameplay mechanics all just sort of "being there" instead of properly fitting in, the picture ends up a little fuzzy. Unfocused. Lacking direction. I was left with more cash than I'd ever need, way before the conclusion of the campaign. Having made the promised reward from the bounty hunt at the centre of the game's plot many times over through the side missions, it was hard to stay invested in what was happening, made all the more difficult by the constant confusion and barebones understanding as to who all these factions are and how in Throne's name they relate to one another—aside from everyone wanting the biggest slice of the same pie. But the prospect of 'em getting deliciously vaporised or dismembered in one of many spectacular ways, sparks and blood flying all around? That kept me going.Well, I guess now would be a good time to say that I haven't actually played ...yet.

_childDocuments_.review: When I see "Streum On Studio," I am always reminded of their first game, E.Y.E.: Divine Cybermancy. That game is janky as hell but was a really fun experience. So when they released Deathwing, my friend and I were hyped because it looked so cool. It turns out that while it's janky, some fun can still be had. Then they released Necromunda, which should have the simplest gameplay of all those games (run-and-gun boomer shooter), but somehow they managed to make it the JANKIEST.Ok, good parts first. If there is something that is consistent with these guys (aside from jank), it’s that their art department always knocks it out of the park. The backgrounds, character design, weapons, and the trains (OMG the train) are just beautifully well done and scrappy, exactly how a Hive City should look. Every level looks great, and there's a good variety of places to explore. If you're a fan of Warhammer 40K, this aspect will not disappoint. I also appreciate that the developers chose Hive City as the setting; it brings to life a location that is seldom explored in Warhammer 40K. Hopefully, the next 40K games will also explore other places, not just the usual cities and battlefields.The sound is passable, the voice acting is good (can have a lot more of variation, though), and the story can be summed up as "I don't care."Movement feels snappy, and you can perform a lot of acrobatics (double jump, wall run, sliding, etc.), which all feel very responsive. Shooting the guns feels satisfying, with a sizable choice of armaments, so the game has a solid foundation. I don’t really have any issues with the shooting mechanics, except for what accompanies them, more on that later.With all of that out of the way, let’s talk about why this game has an identity crisis. The overall shooting and movement suggest that it's a fast-paced boomer shooter, but then the weapons have "types" like in a looter shooter. I'm talking about something similar to Borderlands, where an assault rifle can have effects (burning, toxic, etc.) and rarity that affects its damage and buffs. This, in turn, results in a variety of enemies that have "weaknesses" to certain types of weapons. Some enemies, despite having the same model, feel bullet-spongey because you need to use the "right" type of weapon. This adds a layer of complexity to the fast-paced shooting that doesn’t match the pacing they’re going for. There are also other problems, such as it being hard to differentiate enemies when everything looks so green and brown, the limited variety of enemies, shield guys still shooting even after you yank their shields off, and your dog and their dog, etc. They should have just committed to one type of shooter instead of creating this jumbled mess.On top of all this is the jankiness of the game, which ranges from minorly annoying to "how do they even ♥♥♥♥ this up". My favorite part is the process of removing a weapon from your inventory slot without selling it. It's freaking easy! Let me list the steps for you:    Find the weapon vendor because, for some reason, there's no inventory function.    On the vendor menu, click the list of the weapon type you want to remove.    Buy the cheapest weapon of that type.    Place that weapon in the slot of the weapon you want to unequip to exchange it.    Now sell the cheapest weapon so your inventory slot is empty.    Done! Very easy; 10/10, please reevaluate your life.There's still a lot more I could list, but the experience feels like you're driving a car with the driver's seat not on the left or right, but in the center. Yes, you can still drive it. Yes, you'll get used to it. But yes, it sure is painful as heck.So, do I recommend this game? Actually... yes, because despite all the pain, it is a somewhat fun game, and there aren’t many Warhammer 40K games available right now. But again, please only buy if:    It's on sale (I got it for around ~$6).    You are highly tolerant of jank.    You have a semblance of interest in Warhammer 40K.    You've exhausted your options for shooters and want to try something different.Whew, that's a lot of jank that I wrote!----List of Janks that I found- The "Press Enter" on the Title Menu is unclickable- Animation is overall stiff, on gameplay and on cutscene- Audio mixing on a lot of cutscene feels weird, especially the explosion sound (most of it sounds like a wet fart even though the explosion is in front of the charater)- When you are trying to talk to NPC, you'll need to wait for them to return to default state before the talk prompt is shown- Dialogue choice can only be chosen by hovering the mouse, you cannot use arrow button- Side missions does not have BGM Music- Side missions has infinitely spawning enemies because no reason- When you die, you actually have 3 loading screen. One when you Inject the Med-skull (forget the name) you got a mini loading terminal animation, and then you get the loading where you and your dog are walking, then the loading where it loads the level (This actually grates the hell out of me)- Might as well rename the dog as Janktiff with all that bug and janks on that poor canine. Even the act of calling the dog is jank as hell

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is an FPS by Streum-On who have also made E.Y.E. - Divine Cybermancy and Space Hulk - Deathwing. As opposed to the more free-form E.Y.E. and the constricted, slow Deathwing, this one is fully focussed on mobility and ease of gameplay. This is quite obvious in terms of the many movement abilities and mechanics and how important they are. Skills are more powerful and easier to use than in E.Y.E. and they are less in number. The game is very clearly built around all of these mechanics just as much as around the weapons.Bad:- Some Takedown animations take too long and are not satisfying.- Physical shields are often difficult to deal with efficiently and impede the flow.- Some weapons balance issues.- Aiming-down-sights of limited use (combat usually too fast and at close range)- Lacking atmosphere in terms of soundscape and soundtrack.- Depending on environments enemies can be hard to spot sometimes.- Confused design vision for inventory (too few status item slots, too few for spare weapons etc.)- Loot system mostly amounts to stat bonuses.- Character system grants all meaningful options very quickly and only allows for limited upgrading.- Menu interaction can be confusing at first.- Goliath bossfight designed badly.- Story presentation and plot progression are weak.- Map and objective for Bounties can only be picked from a partial and randomly selected list.- Mission summary screen does not provide any information on kills.- AI behaviour can at best be called straightforward.- Incessant AI spawning can be a problem in some spots.- No maps without constant respawning (E.Y.E. had them)Good:- Inventory interaction and customization flow very well once familiar.- Movement mechanics make game fast and satisfying and the attached evasion mechanics help with higher difficulties.- The grappling hook has a lot of range and grapples onto almost anything.- Skills are easy to use and impactful.- Hidden chests are often placed in creative ways, encourage exploration (and use of movement mechanics) and help break up the pace. - Campaign maps are often very impressive and encourage use of the movement mechanics.- Massive amount of aesthetical details on the maps.- Soundwise the game may often lack atmosphere, but the aesthetics partially make up for it.- Relatively varied map and mission design.- Bounties give uncomplicated, easy access to more gameplay. - Unique gang aesthetics and equipment.- Detailed and varied character models.- Very deep weapons customization that also makes a very big difference visually and sometimes also soundwise. - Guns sound beefy with proper feedback and gore.- Good, fitting soundtrack for the fast, gorey combat.- The Mastiff and Enemies know how to get around the environments.Overall it is a clear, easy recommendation. In spite of some problems Hired Gun is simply is too good when it comes to mobility and gunplay as well as aesthetics.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I really gave this game a chance but in the end it just ended up being Doom Eternal but inferior in every way.  - Gameplay is made incredibly difficult by the general jank/poor design. Large amounts of respawning hitscan enemies completely undermine the rapid mobility system and I quickly found myself hiding in corners and small rooms waiting for them to come to me. Even then, this didn't stop them from spawning directly behind me and hosing me down before I had time to react.- The inventory management system is needlessly confusing. It felt like the developers were trying to reinvent the wheel with this one. What you don't put in a loadout slot at the end of the mission is automatically sold.- The side missions boil down to just you killing or capturing targets in re used portions of the campaign levels. I wouldn't generally mind this much but the portions of levels used are very linear and do not lend themselves well to the gameplay at all. I found myself often rushing through narrow tunnels and passages, ignoring the rapidly respawning enemies so I could get to the objective without wasting my precious stimms and medkits.- The story or what little there was is mostly there to explain why you're hopping from level to level gunning down baddies. I can't speak for it as a whole as I didn't finish the game. - The best aspect of this game was simply its artistic and world design. The environments and characters are well detailed and very evocative of the 40k setting. For the most part all the enjoyment I derived from the game was from soaking in the details of the world.In the end Hired Gun was a let down that I had high hopes for despite Warhammer's bad track record with video games. It has some redeeming qualities but ultimately as a video game it was largely unenjoyable .
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This is like a crustier version of Doom Eternal with some looter shooter mechanics. It definitely feels like it lacks a bit of polish here and there, but it does a good job at being your average stress relief shooter, with overall decent movement mechanics. Scopes kinda feel like arse tho, but it's not like if you're going to use them a lot in this game.If you want a smart shooter game where you have to be tactical and stuff, I'd advise against buying it. But if you just want a cool fast paced run and gun shooter, give it a go.

_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game just doesn't feel finished to me. The fighting is fun the weapons are great. The story is meh and I wished it was more flushed out . Levels just end sometimes you would think there would be a huge cinematic cut scene of explosions or of a huge train shifting into gear but no it just cuts you back to the lobby area. There were multiple instances of being stuck  in the level itself most of the time it is from the grappling gun catching something and you are somehow clipped out of the level itself. After this happens you either have to be lucky to find your way back into the level or you have to exit the game. All the characters seem to have something covering their mouths as a way to not have to sync their lip movements. I feel like this game could have been so much more and wanted it to be much more but it just didn't make it. It feels like the production was rushed and they just needed to finish the game so they took a lot of shortcuts and provided this as the final product.
