_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this.To me it feels like a more fun Doom.While the textures and polish aren't quite at Doom level these are the things it does better:   - World Design: A really well realised depiction of the 40k universe.   - Gameplay: In Hired Gun you move faster and have a more interesting  move set with more options.   - RPG Elements: Choosing your body augmentations is fun and interesting, including for your dog!   - Gun Customisation: This is really fun you can choose any weapon and customise it for your situation.   - Interesting and Diverse Enemies: Pretty sure I have scratched the surface but so far very varies and cool looking      enemies. There are a couple of stutters when the levels load and the game has crashed a couple of times, but this is no worse than and AAA game,If you like the recent doom games or shadow warrior give this a go.I like it
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Does this game want to be Doom (2016)-meets-Warhammer 40k? Yes. Is this game a tad on the janky side? Also yes. Is this game FUN? Oh heck yes.After finishing the game do I feel the same way? Yes, but...If you're a Warhammer 40k/Necromunda fan you'll have a decent time with the setting, however I can't imagine anyone else giving the game much of a second thought. The game unashamedly wears its influences on its sleeve but sadly reveals all it has to offer far too early. There's an interesting story in there somewhere, but you're only ever catching a snippet of it. Some sort of collectable log system could have filled in the gaps & expanded the exploration aspect of the game a bit more than simply treasure chest hunting. As it stands you're basically an unnamed side character in a Kal Jerico short story.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I did not have an ounce of fun playing this. The game is beautiful, and it is cool to see 40K environments rendered in such detail, but this game feels like a total conversion mod rather than an actual game. By which I mean everything feels incomplete, janky, and unpolished. Level design feels random, and does not mesh well with the mechanics, enemies feel like dumb walking turrets or bullet sponges that react little to getting shot, the animations are either stiff or spastic, the sound design is utterly flat making everything sound like it is coming through a cheap mono speaker, and the gunplay while fast, lacks any impact that would make it fun or exciting. At its best, this game is mediocre, at its worst it feels like an overly ambitious first crack at making a game passion project of a single first time dev, style affair that would normally be free as shareware. I love the 40K setting, but I'm getting sick and tired of seeing it getting handed to these bargain bin developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I hope that Steam will implement 'middle' option in the reviews some day, but this one will be positive.Yeah, the game is jankfest, clearly made with fairly stock UE4 on a very tight schedule and a modest budget. It won't grab awards or high praise even from WH40k fans. The gameplay systems are a mishmash of several better games (loot from Destiny, DOOM-esque pacing, some RPG-elements akin of Deus Ex, Titanfall 2-style platforming). It kinda works, but the jank is severe at times.But some parts do click perfectly, especially the atmosphere. And when they do, Necromunda is the best WH40k experience since Space Marine. Game is clearly made with love, care, and yes, with a lot talent. Many downsides are due to the small size of a team, budget constraints and clearly very limited play testing.But you just can't go wronk with 40K as a setting. Huge-ass train, grimdark everywhere, constant lore pieces hidden in some neat little details, terrific art and the sheer feel of Necromunda... It's very true to the setting and I salute the devs for that (though some stock fonts are clearly ass, sorry).The gameplay is fun too for the most part. It's repetative, mindless, but fun.My take? It's... Well, okay. Good enough FPS to spend an few evenings. Huge plus that this game is not overstaying it's welcome. 8-9 hours of more or less linear SP campaign plus some boring side missions. Necromunda is also balanced in terms of difficulty. Almost no cheapshots and arenas are wide, without idiotic choke points and stupid boxes to stuck on.Devs are clearly aware about the slew of problems and in a process of fixing the most glaring issues (especially idiotic audio mixing), so I'll hold off my judgement on some problems for now. And I hope that Focus will give the sequel more time and money, because the potential is clearly there. Just not yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a ton of fun. High speed violence, extensive cybernetics, lots of fun guns, customization, pretty sold level design and fun side quests. The story is a little thin but it's so fun running and gunning like a bionic badass that it's easy to overlook. The setting of Necromunda is well realized and invoked both the style and the tone of the setting very well. Definitely worth a purchase.

_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game has 13 main story missions and endless side missions. Up until the 12th mission, I would have recommended this game easily. It is flawed but super fun. However, the last mission was a mess of bugs for me and I almost couldn't finish it.The combat in this game is super fun and fluid. At first, I found it too challenging even on normal but without too much grinding, I was able to start upgrading myself and my dog, and get better weapons, and it began to feel a lot more fun. I started doing side missions to have fun and not only because I needed money to get upgrades. That being said, some mechanics are never explained like elemental damage, as well as many stats and upgrades being poorly explained.I have never played a Warhammer game and the story made no sense. A bunch of factions and events come at you too fast to keep up. The cutscenes explained very little. In addition, inventory management is a confusing travesty designed by someone who had a few too many energy drinks before passing into a sugar-induced coma, leaving an unfinished mess.Two biggest complaints:Firstly, the game uses stims (a health item) to allow you to come back from the dead, and you can't carry more than three, forcing you to restart a level or go back to base, get upgrades and try again (sort of like old school games which had limits of 3 lives before needing to start over). Falling into a void due to a bad jump or missed grapple counts as one of those deaths. I like the idea of making reloads cost the player as a level of added difficulty. The problem is that the game also wants you to explore but some level design elements are inconsistent. You can wall run on THIS wall but not that IDENTICAL wall right after it. Also, you take no fall damage and levels are very vertical, resulting in massive jumps being common. You see a platform below and think you can jump to it, but turns out its actually just scenic background, causing you to fall to your death. This means that you have to either limit exploration or be prepared to restart to a previous checkpoint because there was a ledge you can't grapple to beside looking like every other ledge you can. Punishing repeated deaths is only fair if your level design is consistent and coherent.Secondly, the final mission bugged out. During a big battle - right before the final boss fight - my controls stopped working, killing me and forcing me back to base. I eventually figured out that the default keybinds had deleted themselves, so nothing worked. After fixing that problem and getting back into the fight, my HUD suddenly disappeared during the same big fight which means that I couldn't tell if I needed to restore my health, which of my abilities were still on cooldown, if my dog was ready to get back into the fight, if I was running out of ammo and needed to switch to a different weapon etc. It then suddenly came back during the final boss fight.Overall, this game is a bit of mess. The combat is fun so I recommend it for that alone, but be wary of some jank and bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this moment, almost a week after release, I don't believe it's a game that's worth its full price point.It gets several things right like the scale, the ambiance and the feel of its universe as well as a robust movement system and gun handling.But that's about it, and it also gets some things really, really wrong. In fact if it weren't for those particularly bad parts I would've given it a thumbs up and a warning for jank.UI: it's visually fine, but otherwise it's a complete mess, one that even an intern UX designer could improve. The whole loot system is utter and complete garbage, as is the inventory and really anything outside of the main menu. You cannot open your inventory in missions or outside of very specific points, you cannot change your starter pistol (only improve it a bit apparently), stockpile equipment, equip a weapon you picked up during a mission unless you did so while it was still on the ground, and the list goes on. Seriously it's a great example of "how not to do loot".Level and Mission Design: while the scale is really cool and some environments slap, the levels are generally pretty meh in terms of design with main paths stupidly hidden and a whole lot of jumping around, backtracking and ♥♥♥♥ through empty levels to find a path. Enemies spawn in your face and it's hard to say where they came from or where they're gonna come from. Some enemy squad comp are just spam and plainly not properly tested for fun.Side missions are some of the least well presented content I've ever seen in a game of this scale. You click on a (bad) menu, pick your loadout in another (bad) menu, then get a loading screen and drop in a part of a main mission level, just cut off for size. Then enemies pop from here and there (mostly infinite spawns) and grind you down until you find whatever basic objective you gotta do (= press E or shoot stuff). Then boom, you instantly stop and get another loading screen, you're done, bye bye. It's so unexpectedly barebones and poor...Anyway I won't ramble any longer but besides bugs and a pretty bad AI, it's those 2 elements, UI and LD that really prevent me from recommending this unless you're dying to explore Necromunda. This game needs love, lots of it and not just to debug it, but also to improve the shreds of content on the sides of the main story.

_childDocuments_.review: runs fine on a 2080ti, no major FPS drops outside some loading hitches between elevators in some certain levels. good movement system combined with responsive gunplay and a small skill tree to progress your character. voice acting is atrocious and the story is about as vague as you'd expect from the EYE team. outside of the occasional janky execution, no major bugs have been experienced in 2.5hrs of gameplay. week-long sale on launch day is a very nice gesture.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a neutral rating then I would. It is not deserving of a thumbs up, nor is it deserving of a thumbs down. Pretend I am holding my hand horizontally and wobbling it a bit whilst making an "eeeeeeh" noise.It is not a bad game per se, it is just a bit "meh" when looked at overall. Visually it can be very appealing at times. There are plenty of screenshot worthy moments. Environments can be very atmospheric and make you feel like you are trudging through a hive city. Environments are StreumOn's strong point (much the same with space hulk deathwing). The gunplay and weapon +traversal systems are serviceable, but nothing to write home about. Your cyber mastiff is nice to have (mainly to pet and throw meat at in the quest hub), but you could easily clear all the content without needing to use it at all, except where the plot requires it.The main issues can be summarised as follows:*Lack of polish / many bugs / unfinished feeling / general Jank. If you have played space hulk deathwing (including enhanced edition), it is on a similar level. Broadly functional but plenty of tooth grindingly frustrating bugs and technical issues pop up frequently.*Voice acting. Genuinely terrible for the most part. Immersion breaking and, at times, so bad as to make me want to headbutt the wall and scream obscenities. It sounds like they rounded up some random d***heads from the nearest bus stop and paid them in cheap beer to rattle off some dialogue.*amount / variety / pacing of content. You have a very finite number of story missions, some of which are actually a lot of fun. Outside of these you will spend your time in a very small quest / trader hub where you can upgrade your weapons, mastiff and your augments / cybernetics. You can accept non plot missions from a bounty board of sorts, but these fall into about 4 different types and take place in a handful of environments which you will return to many times (so you can level your way past the deliberate and arbitrary progress walls they have put in to try and stretch out the small amount of story content). This all grows old rather fast.The comparisons that have been made comparing it to some sort of off-brand, bargain bin doom eternal clone with a 40k skin slapped on are not inaccurate. I bought it on sale for under £20 and played 19 hours before i had enough (all story content cleared, all upgrades purchased, and as many side quests as I could stomach), so I guess that is not the worst value for money. Had I paid full price for this then I would be really quite unhappy with the end result. If you love 40k and you can get it for under £20 then it may keep you moderately entertained for a while, otherwise you may want to skip it. Clearly the devs have a lot of love for the 40k universe and have tried to be faithful to it, but it just misses the mark in various ways IMHO.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Hired Gun is an old-school shooter with an amazing setup but it falls flat on execution.First things first, the environment is amazing. Setpieces, backgrounds, locations and details are through the roof. Some of the best 40K stuff I've seen in a shooter (though there weren't that many to be fair) in a long time. On par with Spacehulk but being located under a hive city it gives a really new and amazing perspective.Story-wise however game just doesn't come through. Description pompously promises that you can be a proper bountyhunter picking contracts and executing targets yourself and all that...But you end up being just a killing machine. No killing "characters", just hoards of similar-looking goons to get to a tougher goon who is supposedly a boss of some value.No one asks this game to be Hitman but still.Repetitive gameplay. Many arks left unanswered. Campaign that starts with you going for the highest bounty, despite making few times the reward money in the process, and ends without answering any questions.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Bolter Muder Simulator!give it some time and wait till its a lot cheaper sadly its very short and feels unpolished, storytelling is bad, ran into some bugs but they are working on those i guess.theres a lot of room to improve, could be a great game in a year or so, dont bother playing just yet (or paying full price)
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: From what I know about warhammer games, this is probably one of the best ones, and if you're a big fan, get this game, it's worth it.If you're just looking for a shooter to play though, stay away until a barrage of good patches or a good sale.The game has many positives, the overall visual design is amazing, and you can feel good intentions behind almost every gameplay aspect.But, it's jarring to play, for many reasons.I won't go into much detail, but the biggest issue in my opinion (aside from lackluster performance) is that everything feels disjointed. The combat is supposed to be a flow of movement, shooting and melee executions that seamleassly transition into each other, but they don't. Movement is a clunky version of what titanfall 2 has to offer, with all the right moves available, but they do not flow together well. Shooting feels just plain bad. A bit too inaccurate for one, and it's awkward to handle during movement. The animations not only bug out a lot, but they are very clearly a seperate entity from the rest of combat.If you're not a big warhammer fan, there are too many better alternative for fast paced action shooters to justify spending money on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: The cut scenes take control of the character to the point that you can't look around at this incredible atmosphere. It really takes you out of the experience and it feels like someone is putting your head in a vice. Only letting you look at what is to be looked at. If it broke into 3rd person it wouldn't be so bad, but in first person it feels like it is taking my agency away.Minor gameplay things, very hectic. Always having the enemy flanking you and always outnumbered. The character practically has plot armor. It's not hard, just suspension of disbelief wares a little thin. It hasn't been established that this is a Doom guy or a Master Chief, it is just some guy sent do do an improbable task.Co-op would have been appreciated and would bring some believably to rampaging through a hellscape unscathed.I am aware of the 40k and some of it's lore, first game that I have played. It feels like the I have been dropped into this world, no lube. The character you play is aware of the narrative, but outside of the narrator and npcs giving exposition dumps I am not feeling it. To much telling and not much showing. I would have like to see a functioning forge world looks like to contrast where I am and why the character needs to bring the Emperors justice (or whatever) to this place.From what I understand from Warhammer 40k is that this is an uncaring & unkind universe where the weak are weeded out and only the strong survive unless you live on a paradise world and even then. The player should have a character die because he was overwhelmed. Pick the next person to go through the meat grinder where you left off. Let me feel the dread of this awful place full of death and chaos. Give me consequences for being weak, this guy isn't a space marine. It's just a guy with robot arms and a dog, just like everyone else in this campaign.So much potential and is beautiful, but the feeling isn't there. I can see what it is going for, but I can't seem to connect with the world or its characters. I want to like it, I just don't as it is. I think it needed some more time in the oven to get me invested.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's astonishingly bad.It runs terribly while not stressing the hardware. Not only is the framerate half of what you'd expect, the game keeps stuttering all the time.The animations are terrible.The AI is awful.Voice lines repeat, sometimes 3+ times in a row, a few dozen times in a fight.There's way too much screen shake, it's hard to see anything when jumping (and it's supposed to be a movement shooter).There's a pointless looter shooter element, and other bloat that interrupts actual gameplay.The visibility is god awful - enemies blend into the background completely.This isn't just average or mediocre. This is unacceptably terrible.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like a cool game, but most of my experience has been frustrating. I'm happy to elaborate at some later point if needed, but basically my big frustration is with the enemies. I played a couple of campaign levels and those were mostly fine, but then the game told me I should rack up some money by playing side missions. I've made about 20 or so attempts at these "Status B" missions or whatever they're called, and I have seriously only been successful on them like twice. They're horribly balanced, and this mostly has to do with one enemy type. You can run along quite happily blasting at the normal grunts, but as soon as you run into an energy-shielded guy, you're toast. They'll soak up a full magazine of hits and then one-shot you with some kind of energy orb. I'm playing on the third difficulty and, yes, it warns you that enemies will soak a little more damage. But come on! This is ridiculous.  I'm quite comfortable playing recent shooters like Doom and Doom Eternal on Ultra Violence and Nightmare, so I really don't feel like it's my lack of aim or reflexes or whatever. The game keeps giving you this stupid tooltip that tells you not to "be shy" and to run up to enemies and kill them to get health back. But how am I supposed to do that when they're soaking up full magazines of ammo from my fully kitted-out guns? Guess what? You can't get your health back if dudes be absorbing all of your fire. And half of the time you're fighting them in these big open rooms where you've got guys spraying ammo at you from all over the place.It would be one thing if there was some kind of obvious countermeasure, like a shield-busting plasma or electric weapon type given to you around the same time these enemies started showing up. That's something that Doom: Eternal (the game that this game is clearly taking cues from) does. But that hasn't happened. You just keep running into these guys and getting absolutely wiped out.  There's a little electric punchy fist you can use to eliminate the shields, but that takes like half a minute to recharge and by then you've already run into two or three more shielded enemies.  It just feels like I'm missing something, but at this point I don't feel like it's my fault. I'm not a stupid guy. I checked for alternate ammo types. I tried a handful of different weapons. I upgraded some of my base abilities. I tried sniping guys from a distance. I tried running in up close. I tried wall running and being ultra mobile. None of that stuff gave me a big enough edge against getting swarmed and clobbered by these shielded enemy types in some big open room (the two I played were an ash pit and the top of a huge train). If you wonder if I'm any good at FPS then look at my achievements. I'm not the best ever, but I know my way around an SSG. If I'm not upgraded enough to be playing these side missions or if I should play the campaign first to unlock more stuff, then tell me to do that instead of acting like I should be able to conquer the energy shield bro missions.That's my main gripe, and if it weren't for that I'd be playing right now instead of typing this stupid review. But if you're still reading then you must care about the details, so here are a few more gripes:-The takedown system is garbage. The on-screen prompt isn't clear, it has very little range, and you can't really tell which enemies you'll be able to do it to. -On the same note, enemies look very "samey" despite having radically different capabilities. To go back to the Doom thing, it's not hard to tell a weak zombie soldier from a more powerful revenant. In this game it's much harder to tell who is a level 1 crook and who is a level 99 boss. Certain enemy types are distinct, but I'm talking about the difference between a gun grunt who will go down in one blast and a shielded, roided out dude who's going to one-shot you with a plasma orb.-Enemies don't make obvious footsteps or sounds to let you know they're coming up behind you. This is often enough for you to get killed without knowing what happened-When you use the grapple to pull away an enemy's metal (not energy) shield, you have a super high chance to instead pull yourself into a non-shield enemy standing nearby, thereby putting yourself in a spicy dicey little situation that you didn't want-It's really easy to accidentally dismiss in-game information or tutorials because they pop up while you're doing things-Abilities are too slow to recharge, and don't have obvious audio cues. Seriously, go back to what Doom Eternal did - give us a little gas can noise for the chainsaw or whatever-Your character's health ONLY recharges by collecting pickups. Some base-level health or shield regeneration would do a lot to help you catch your breath. Instead, it's super easy to get cornered and then you know you're toast as soon as you come back out.-Multiple times I died on top of health or shield pickups with my screen literally showing me that I had shields left as I diedSo overall I'm feeling let down. Part of that is because of the immense positives: The graphics look cool. The guns are fun to shoot. The world seems engaging and the environments are awesome. Before I ran into the shield bros, I was having a great time. But dude, the gameplay needs some retuning or some re-explanation or *something*, because it's just not fun to get cornered and wiped out on what should be nifty little side missions. I wanted to like this a lot more, but my first few hours have been ROUGH. Maybe I'll come back once my patience meter has recharged.Side note: I genuinely tried to google how to deal with these shield guys and didn't see anything helpful. If you have the secret sauce for dealing with those guys, then hit me with it. Maybe I'm supposed to just play the main story more, but the game said I should play some side missions and so I didn't want to move on without giving them a fair shot. That's what led me to my frustrations.

_childDocuments_.review: Action is good, almost like doom in a lot of respects. The voice acting is a little over the top, quests, dialogue and investment into what is going on is low. You can basically kill tons of stuff with any weapon. You get very unexcited about drops pretty quickly. The vendor never sells anything good, always +0 & +1. So after upgrading all your mods there is nothing to sink all the extra credits you have. Lastly and most importantly the inventory system is literally the worst I have ever seen in any game. You cant open inventory in a mission, and you can only modify weapon load outs at predetermined locations.  You have to buy weapon mods for each new weapon, you can't take them off of the last gun.It seems that the developers have no intention of fixing the problems and complaints since I am playing almost 2 years after release, and the complaints haven't changed. Doesn't appear than there are any future plans for the game, and the DLC's are only cosmetic. The action and game play is good enough to excuse getting for 5-10$. I got my copy with humble bundle choice so around the 5-10$ mark. Took about 34 hrs total to beat and get 100% of the achievements. Once you get to that point you can move on with your life.

_childDocuments_.review: Objective rating for pure gameplay, plot, and FPS mechanics: 8/10Subjective rating for dumb oldschool FPS + WH40k fans: 10/10In brief, this game slaps. There's a campaign with mostly well scripted events, interesting objectives, vibrant locations, secret areas, and diverse enemies. Then there's a mission board in the hub where you can take quick bounty missions to grind for gear and credits. They're pretty homogeneous and reuse the same maps for the type of missions, but you unlock the S tier missions pretty quick and get big credit bonuses when you need em.Pros:- Pretty game, runs pretty well at 90% resolution with my upper medium rig- Guns are great representations of all classic WH40k and handle really well.- Weapon customization has a lot of options to fit your playstyle. Stripped down Fallout 4- Lore is lore. It's great and immersive and you really feel like you're in a hivecity- You jump, double jump, dash in air, wallrun, walljump, and just fly around shootin', melee takedownin' hoes- Xray vision, melee 'berzerk' mode, shock, electroblast, crush, autoaim, slow-mo, etc- Dog- Dog Augs- Pet dog- Progression through game feels fluid and hasn't gotten stale (at 8 hours)- Loot is plentiful and has a vast variety of statsUgly:- EDIT: Default pistol is now able to be swapped out! Great work! - Gun customization has some issues. Each gun is the same base gun (there is a large variety tho!) with different mods on it. However, if you get two of the same kind of guns and unequip a mod (say a long barrel), it doesn't keep the mod, so you have to re-buy that same mod for a different gun. Trinkets and damage mods are able to be swapped between guns, but it would be nice to strip guns for parts.- Inventory UI needs an overhaul. No shift/alt/etc click equip, no hovering over equipped gear for stats, no stat comparison unless you begin to equip an item and you have to specifically click on the slot to equip it. Small quality of life issues but take a look at WH40k Inquisitor in comparison.- Dog is busted. Terrible AI, dies pretty quick, only useful for summoning to see enemies outlined through walls. Which is super cool!! But that's sort of similar to the augur vision ability. Some better dog AI would definitely be cool. Personally, I'm not a fan of having companions in FPS games so it doesn't bother me at all, but if you compare it to other titles with friendly friends at your side, it does fall short.- EDIT: They fixed this glitch very quickly!  Great work devs. - Inventory is a bit limited. Would like to see some more slots for certain gear and weapons. Game autosells loot you don't pick up after a mission, which is kinda rad, but the low slots for certain items means you can't hold onto a variety of gear and have to make the decision immediately whether you want to use X or Y. For an FPS that kinda saves you a headache but I'm a Lootaholic so I like to have a bit more options.Game rocks. Go buy it. It's worth. A little rough around the edges, but it's a solid dumb shooter and a GREAT WH40k lore game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've cut off somebody else's thumbs and grafted them to this stick, which I've attached to a lever.  I can just pull this handle here, and... THUMBS UP!  and keep on typing.  That's a high tech solution, I tell you what.So you could be playing this game instead of reading it, so let me give you a quick paragraph to send you on your way:  Doom and Metro 2033 drank too much and fell into Sunset Overdrive's closet.  Nine months later, they named the baby "Hired Gun".You run around at high speed like a cracked-out lunatic, jumping off walls and firing wildly at dudes while people talk in outrageous cockney accents.  I guess there's a plot?  There's people who have a chronic lead shortage and it's your mission to remedy that imbalance.  You can get healed by being aggressive, so it's to your advantage to go utterly crackhappy on fools.  You don't need to skulk about or take cover or whatever, you jump off walls and generously share lead, that's what you do.The game just looks gorgeous, frankly.  Mmm.  It's rusty and claustrophobic and weirdly industrial and looks pretty much like the seedy underbelly of the basement of a giant, planet-spanning city should.  It oozes character, and I'm enthralled.  You're even encouraged to explore as they hide various goodies hither and yon, and with all your movement skills the game is as vertical as it is horizontal.But in the interests of being honest, the melee animations are kind of a mixed bag.  A few look off.  A lot are really bewildering.  I mean, yes, you're frantically trying to kill somebody who isn't cooperating, but it's really hard to parse the action.  I'll be the first to admit that hasty melee ambushes are going to feel very confused and off-center, but it's a bit personally bewildering and I don't like it.  A few others have complained of bugs, but I have not had that experience, it's been remarkably polished for me (melee animations aside).But in the end, I'm glad I bought this game, and I'm likely to stream or record it when I go back to it.  I'm quite stoked and I wish I had less work to deal with so I could play this longer.  If you liked E.Y.E. Divine Cybermancy, this isn't it.  But you know how atmospheric that game was, so you don't have to take my word for it:  this is too.  Two (of somebody else's) thumbs up.  On a lever.

_childDocuments_.review: There's just no doubt in my mind anymore. Games Workshop don't like video games and don't like people playing video games. As in all of the Warhammer and Warhammer 40k franchise games since the early 2000s, the only people who seem to be even remotely interested in providing some sort of quality are the artists. I'm going to start by saying I don't know nor do I care if the developers had little time, lots of crunches, impossible demands. It's not my problem and should never be my problem. You should get this game if:- You like infinite enemies spawning immediately on top of you, behind you, in front of you, all within 3 feet of you. - You like game breaking bugs on every level, including the main hub. - You like auto aim grapnel (which you cannot change) which prevents you from using it for its intended purpose to reach tricky platforms. - You like wasting your money. So I'll start by saying there was a lot of potential in this game, but it was completely squandered to the point where I cannot imagine myself completing it in its current state. Let's start with the main draw to this game - progression. This game has no progression. There will be no point in this game where all the money you spend on your bionics, dog, weapons and items will seem worth it. Why? Because the Mastiff's only use is to see enemies highlighted, its attack is ridiculous, takes too long and more often than not, enemies ignore it completely. The bionics? They give you new abilities, that barely work, even upgraded, are too short, and cooldown for too long (even with the fastest cooldowns) all this while you are under constant attack. The game tells you to complete side missions if the main missions are too hard, but the side missions are MUCH harder than the main missions for the simple reasons that enemies spawn infinitely in them. You think you cleared a room only for enemies to respawn in it the second you set foot outside, shoot you from behind as you're stuck in a corridor under fire from the next room and kill you. In one of the FIRST SIDE MISSIONS I've killed over 100 enemies before I could even get half of my objectives. The items they dropped were mostly ammo, sometimes grenades, rarely refractors. So I didn't even get anything out of it and my kill style was C, even though I utilized takedowns, wall runs, grapnels and slides constantly. Guess when you kill 100 enemies you just can't look cool enough to pull it off. Any enemy in the game has better shields than you. No matter how much you upgrade your refractor, the lowest scumbag in the weakest gang will always have a stronger refractor than yours and no matter how much you upgrade it, a single shotgun blast from the weakest enemy will always take it down. I'm good at shooter games, been playing them since the 90s, almost always on the hardest difficulty. Completed both the new dooms on ultra nightmare even. So that's about progression. Enemies are boring. They just are. Other than the occasional special enemy all enemies in the game in all factions are exactly the same. (At least from what I got to so far, so take this with a grain of salt). The combat is far too quick guns do too much damage (both yours and the enemies') and since sniping isn't an option in this game (due to enemies spawning on top of you no matter where you are with the exception of extreme platforms occasionally) doing so usually gets you killed. The enemy AI is garbage, they run at you and shoot and sometimes throw grenades. No group tactics, no utilizing strengths of individual enemies such as shield units to go ahead while others form lines of fire, no using the environment. Why even bother? The original FEAR had much better AI and that's over a decade old already. Takedowns take too long (even though the animations are very quick they're just way too long forming sometimes 3-5 actions in one animation) which allows enemies to instantly get to you and blast you as soon as you come out of it (because giving you invincibility for long enough after you come out so you can get out of the gangrape didn't occur to the devs) so using them often to get kill style is a pain in the ass. Your mastiff's AI is so bad that he won't attack an enemy right in front of him because he's standing on an elevation of one inch. Most of the time, it doesn't even do anything, just standing wherever you leave it and barking, often causing me to get confused when I think other mastiffs attack me. This game should have been about the environments, and in the levels it is, except there's no interactivity, no time to absorb the atmosphere and the levels are extremely contained into arenas and corridors with little to no actual exploration (no looking up and seeing a chest on a ledge is not exploration). They present you with this insanely interesting world and then just give you the middle finger by making your hub about as big as Commander Shephard's bedroom on the Normandy. The tutorials and informations are basic and don't cover half of the aspects you'd want them to. Now let's discuss bugs.This game had no QA and if you tell me otherwise I'll call you a liar. Nothing is polished. The bullets don't even align with their visual effects. Enemies will run into a wall for an hour because they can't path their way around a door. Stims will respawn you over a pit causing you to fall out of the game and be forced to quit. Grapnel hook sometimes auto aims at nothing even when you're aiming right at a platform (especially if that platform requires you to jump off of a railing into a death pit so you can get a shot at it, which makes some levels piss me off.) My only question is why do game devs don't have pride in their work anymore, what drives someone to release a game that could be the hit of 2021 as the ♥♥♥♥ of 2021? Force your executives to play the games through on hard difficulty so they actually have to experience the game. Feels like there was little to no passion put into this game gameplay wise and it's a damn shame. I hope future updates will fix this into something better. ♥♥♥♥ Games Workshop. ♥♥♥♥ their money laundering figurine scheme. ♥♥♥♥ their inability to understand that good video games can make them a lot of money and the Warhammer and Warhammer 40k franchises are the kind that BEG for a good video game. And ♥♥♥♥ whoever released this game without QAing it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's buggy in places. The story is confusing. The dialogue is bad. But you won't care about any of that, because it's immersive and it's fun. The environments are huge and beautifully rendered; I've never seen ANY game capture the grim, industrial-gothic darkness of Warhammer 40k as well as this. The levels are varied, taking you to a variety of Underhive locations that really establish the world through visual storytelling. There are tons of hidden details that establish the feel of the setting, and it's really cool to stumble across each of them. Character designs are equally fantastic, both enemies and NPCs in the hub zone, and add to the amazing visual worldbuilding. Gameplay is straightforward but fun. Warhammer 40k games have often focused on having players be the big, slow, tough Space Marines, but Hired Gun is all about mobility and frantic action. It definitely owes a debt to the new Doom games, but in a good way. This soundtrack is also a BOP, helping set the tone of the world. It's different from what we've heard in 40k games before, but in a way that really fits the different setting and protagonist. I really hope the game gets enough support to expand with DLC so that we can see new enemies and new environments, two places that this team REALLY seems to shine.

!Gunplay is satisfying, great punchy sounds for the guns and nice gore effects with dismemberments.The environments are well designed, it's faithful to the dark and gritty 40k universe.At first sight you know these devs put their hearts and souls into all these assets, environments and 3D models just like they did with Deathwing.Level design is pretty good, lot of verticality within the levels and with all the abilities honestly it's a blast to play.Just like with Doom Eternal, in this game the arenas are your playground, there's a lot of freedom offered to the players to create their own would have prefered if it was possible to bind dashing and wallrunning to separate keys.Having different actions bound to the same keys well I would say that's not the smartest idea but that's still playable.If you like fast paced fps then you will like this game, even more if your a 40k fan.Just don't expect something as intense or polished like Doom Eternal and you will have a good time playing it.I see a lot of negative reviews and honestly I think these people don't really know what they are talking about.While not perfect Necromunda: Hired Gun is far from being a bad game, it's also not budget to create their games.Performance are rock solid everything on ultra DX12 it runs butterly smooth on my aging rig.So I don't know maybe some people are actually playing on trash potatoes pc _childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is a fast paced solo shooter that has amazing stage design, fluid movement and fun combat and is a great homage to the 40K (Necromunda) setting, though is a little rough around the edges and could have used some more polish to really make it shine. If you like fast paced combat, execution finishers or the 40K setting I recommend picking it up if you can get it on sale.As a fan of the 40K setting (and the Kal Jericho books), the story fits right in with that series. Set on the hive world of Necromunda (a massive city where billions live, separated into different strata layers) you play as a bounty hunter, taking on missions to earn your keep and survive. After accepting a bounty on the Silver Talon, the mission goes awry almost immediately and ends up with your team dead, you nearly being terminated and only surviving because of Kal’s timely intervention. Working with Kal and rebuilt with a range of new cybernetic limbs and parts, you hunt down leads on where the Silver Talon has fled to, while you are hunted by those who want both Kal and what’s been installed inside your head. I thought the story was good, and seemed like a good epilogue to the book series.Movement and combat are the focus of the game, as you slide, grapple and wall-run around the spectacular environments, killing as you go. Staying still will get you killed fairly quickly, continuously moving is what the game is all about, and the game fully supports you in this as you can wallrun and kill with abandon. You have a grapple to get to out of reach areas quickly, can slide fairly long distances at speed, or can sneak (but this would be the most under unitised ability in the game). The environments are well designed for this, offering multiple approaches with loot chests hidden in difficult places that encourage exploration. Combat is ultra fast paced and the game does a great job of making it interesting by having a fairly decent amount of enemies to fight, and plenty of weapon options, and “powers” to use. The game has light RPG elements, as you purchase upgrades to both yourself and your dog, which can do standard things like giving you more HP, shields, or energy, or unlocking other powers and better rewards. In a somewhat nod and wink to the table top games close combat is completely overpowered and with plenty glory kill animations, HP recovery and a fairly generous invulnerability windows that can mean when upgraded you can conga line from one enemy to the next with pure impunity. Some of the other powers just disintegrate enemies. You can call your dog, who will happily maul everything in the game (including the genestealers!) and acts as a great distraction magnet.There are a large selection of weapons from the 40K setting, and they perform as their background suggests they should. Bolters make enemies explode when shot and sound great, lasgun’s can take limbs off when overcharged, stubbers actually feel powerful and shotguns do stupid amounts of damage. Grav guns fire black holes, and plasma guns obliterate enemies. The smaller guns (like pistols) are actually useful, and each weapon can be significantly modified (it’s not just boosting stats). You can take 6 into a mission (from 4 categories), but actually keep a selection of around 20 or so you can choose from.You fight enemies from a few of the major gangs found in Necromunda, (Goliaths who generally favour the big guns and close combat, the female only Eschers and the tech heavy Orlocks). Each have multiple different types of troops, with their psykers (magic casters) being different, and Ogryns having both ranged and melee versions. There are Ambots, which act like giant robotic weapon platforms, and a genestealer cult to take on. While the enemy AI isn’t anything to gush about- most enemies rush towards you in an effort to blown apart or group together making group kills easier, the genestealers are stupidly fast, strike from weird places and they absolutely destroy you in combat before you know what has hit you. There are plenty of boss battles throughout the game, and these are surprisingly difficult. The bosses are absolutely bullet sponges, and are constantly receiving reinforcements and force you to use the terrain and all your powers.All that said, there are some issues which reduced the fun. I had significant crashes to desktop until I re-installed the unreal engine redistributable that comes packaged with the game. If playing with a keyboard and mouse forget trying to use keys for any shortcuts, and use the mouse wheel instead to select your powers. The game doesn’t point out that its nearly pauses when you do this, so it’s much quicker when trying to use powers. I found in some instances when wall running the guns refuse to fire when aiming down past a certain angle.The stages are wonderfully designed and really capture the of the setting. From fighting through derelict cities, wastes, sewers, a power station, spaceships, a moving train, chapels and foundries it is quite unique and a lot of care seems to have been put into how the environment looks. That said, this game pushed my old 1080 to the max, and I had quite visible screen tearing issues when playing at ultra settings. Dropping the visual quality down to high resolved this. The game won’t win any awards for character models, but there’s enough variety to keep things interesting (and to be honest you are usually moving too fast to really pay attention). The animations and vocals from the doc don’t seem to be in sync, with the animations playing once, before the vocals kick in and the options menu appears.The games soundtrack features plenty of heavy metal, which amps up in combat before quieting back down in between firefights. This suits the fast paced gun battles. A stand out mission for atmospheric music would be where you encounter the Genestealer cult. As soon as you enter the area the music changes, and it actually makes it feel quite eerie as you are looking at what appears to be a massacre. You get the nod that something coming up (with tons of ammo laying around), and then nothing, and then when you think you are safe you start screaming as you are attacked from random places. The vocals were a bit of a letdown with each gang seeming to only have 1 voice actor and repeating the same lines for every enemy, though the NPC’s, Kal and the hired gun were serviceable.Easy to get 100% achievements, with only a few requiring some work to be put into them.For more reviews please visit

_childDocuments_.review: Plenty of features you would expect from a looter shooter are not present:- adjusting your loadout during a mission- inspecting your inventory, like, at all- having a key that swaps between two weapons (traditionally mapped to Q)- bosses and mob types that require vastly different tactics and weaponsThe game quickly devolves into a sloppy, hectic mess. Bullet-sponge enemies, mobs spawning behind you, dark silhouettes on dark backgrounds, annoying screen effects, whatever your shooter heart despises.In the end, I found myself mowing down enemies willy-nilly, not even caring what they are or what they can do. Every once in a while you must use one of two skills that destroy magic armor (good luck if they're on cooldown), and for enemies that have shields, you use the grappling hook. Beware: If your back is not making constant love to a wall, enemies *will* spawn behind you. If you run out into the open to engage enemies head-on, you *will* get shot at from various angles by enemies from miles away. You can regain health by killing them, but unless you significantly upgrade that particular skill, you'll survive barely, paycheck to paycheck. Enemies hit like a truck, and they all have assault rifles, so there's no dynamically dodging projectiles, just frantic dodging to up the imaginary "dodge percentage" and get hit less.The game lifts about half of its ideas from Doom 2016 and Eternal wholecloth, in both function and design. Unfortunately, the devs aren't quite capable of reproducing all of them flawlessly, and many they straight-up misunderstand. Here's one for you: What was so great about the glory kills in Doom? They're quick. Well, down here in Necromunda, they take, literally, up to 5 seconds, and even then, most of the time I can't tell what in the Emperor's name even happened.Did I mention that you're actually controlling a third-person character in first-person? You know what I'm talking about. That awkward feeling that something's off, the slight delay before every move, the camera jolting back and forth after every input.Graphics are stuck in 2013, but the art direction is so stellar that you won't care. Voice acting is good, audio mixing has some issues at times. Music is pretty forgettable, but far from bad.I'm truly sorry to say that it's just not fun enough to keep playing. I love the 40k IP, I love shooters, and all I see with this game is squandered potential. You might get a kick out of it, but don't expect a smooth gameplay loop. This one's jank all the way through.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent old school feeling fps at least compared to most fps games that come out these days. Pretty fun game you can double jump and grapple hook and you can upgrade your character with different abilities and things which is pretty cool. You can also find a lot of new weapons and items around the levels which you can equip and modify and stuff. You can also buy weapons if you need to. The main story is quite short unfortunately if you are half decent at fps games you can probably get through it in 6-8 hours depending on the difficulty setting. The game does have a lot of side missions though which you can do to earn more money to purchase things which is neat. You can also replay previous weapons to find hidden chests to get some better loot if you want so there's a little bit of replay value there. You even get a pet dog that you can upgrade and its pretty useful when there's a lot of enemies after you. The graphics are quite good and I like the aesthetic they are trying to go for although sometimes it is a bit difficult to see things. The game runs okay, could be better, I did have to lock the framerate to 80 to get more stable framerates and there are still some framedrops here and there which is a shame. The game in general does feel very unpolished, like there are quite a few bugs like one bad one I encountered was when looking through ironsights the crosshair was super off center which was pretty bad and there was another bug where an elevator stopped working for whatever reason but aside from that I didn't have too many problems. I didn't really like the female voice actor for the main character but otherwise the voice acting was pretty decent. Cutscenes were a bit scuffed though, definitely could have used a bit of work. Overall its an interesting fps, could have used a bit more polish but mechanically it works pretty well, would have preferred a longer campaign but other than that its not too bad. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this game has been out for over a year and there's still basic, glaring programmatic issues like being unable to set the resolution of the game. WTF. *Ahem* sorry for the trash review. I should say a bit more. Admittedly I only really had time to give this game an initial impression, I got it on the humble bundle. I remember being very tempted to buy it on release but it was such a crowded window that I didn't and kind of forgot about it. After my first hour, I have never been so thankful I didn't buy a game.This is a game where 90% of the work put into it went into figuring out how to make the game look good while only using 2 colors. This is one of the most shallow gameplay experiences I've had playing a shooter probably since the original Homefront on the Xbox 360. A game where the mechanics are few, and the reasons to use them are fewer. Gameplay reduces down to holding the left-mouse button while looking at a doorway with mindless flesh-bags funneling endlessly through it. I feel like going into detail about things like the numb-skulled AI or floatiness of the shooting mechanics would actually deceive you into thinking that the gameplay has any amount of work or thought put into it. This is a warhammer 40k walking sim  but with the inconvenience of enemies and lame-duck RPG mechanics. I railed on SpaceHulk Deathwing for having terrible design, but that was at least a game that tried to design something cool.For all of the tags this game has thrown on it, it's is one of the blandest games I have ever played and probably the most disappointing Warhammer 40k title to date, unless you want to see a detailed hiveworld rendered in 3D so badly you are willing to suffer for the pleasure.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen so many reviews that have given this game a "mediocre rating" though I couldn't disagree any further. Necromunda is a straight up technical mess. First off, the wall running mechanics are incredibly unrefined. You know there's problem with the game's physic engine when you can wall run backwards. _childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is a fast-paced FPS, taking place in the Necromunda planet, within the Warhammer 40K universe. It's a bit rough around the edges, but all in all, it's a pretty fun and old school game.Despite being a pretty straightforward game (there's no open world, no infiltration, you're just supposed to run and jump around with all guns blazing), it lets you handle situations in a whole lot of different ways. There's a good amount of guns and powers, you can wall run, use a grappling hook, double jump, or jump-dodge-jump again, use a bullet time, an aim bot, etc.Once you start getting good at it, it's pretty satisfying to run around at a crazy speed, dodge a million bullets, blow up half a dozen guys in an instant, will doing some pretty neat parkour.But, let it be known that the game is still slightly bugged. While strafing and jumping around like a moron, I found myself stuck in a rock or in a wall more than once. Some jumping mobs end up falling off the map (which can prevent you from getting any further when it's a boss). Other than that, my main beef was the execution animations: they are, truth be told, quite bad, and would have looked bad back in 2010. And I wish the dog/mastif was more important. It was heavily advertised as a selling point of the game, and it ends up as a slightly disappointing companion you can summon every few minutes.Lastly, I'm not really familiar with Necromunda, and the game won't help you get acquainted with this sub-universe. The plot makes no sense and the game makes no effort to explain its setting to the player.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm putting this review as a "Yes", but it's mostly because Steam doesn't have a "Neutral" option and I'm a positive type of guy. But really it's a "maybe".To be simple, it's a StreumOn game, through and through. Which means a lot of good stuff in some aspects, and a lot of jank and lack of polish in some others. If you've ever played E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy, you know exactly what I'm talking about there.I'll fully admit I wasn't entirely convinced in my first 2 to 3 hours of playtime, it may also not help that I'm not the biggest War40k connaisseur. But the more I play, and the more I'm starting to get upgrades and getting the hang of them, the more fun I'm having with.Let's start with the jank.There are some mechanics that are... uniquely implemented and kind of poorly explained, notably the inventory and loot system. Basically, despite some looter shooter aspects, you're not allowed to keep more than a handful of guns in each category, and if you find a weapon in-mission, you're allowed to equip ONE, without knowing its stats. Whetever you keep it or not is decided at the very end of the mission - take what you want, sell the rest. See that small grid on the right of the loot screen? Yeah, that's your entire inventory. It's not THAT bad, but it does take some getting used to and you need to be aware of that.There are also some faux-RPG elements, like armor, items and archeotechs... But basically, there's only one type of armor that I've seen so far, one type of lucky charm, and the equippable items all have basically the same function, buff one of your stats up. It's weirdly "elaborate" for what little there is in terms of variety on that front.And then, gameplay wise, some animations are janky as all hell, most notably the Takedown ones. It serves at a simili-Glory Kill system à la DooM 2016/Eternal, but with some misunderstanding of what makes them work in that game. Here it's slower and jankier, and you can basically walk up to a dude a shank a ♥♥♥♥♥ whenever you want, unless it has a refractor shield. And you'll be bound to do that a lot, considering it's one of your primo ways to regen health.The plot... exists. It's serviceable. The voice acting is also serviceable, but there was an issue with the audio mixing. It may be fixed now.You can do some basic mercenary missions in the same maps than the main campaign, with an objective. It's basically there if you need money or just want more combat, but the spawn rate of enemies can get completely out of hand.And the Mastiff mechanic is also a tad buggy at the moment. Sometimes it works fine, sometimes your dog just won't do ♥♥♥♥.On a more personal note, there's no animation cancel for the guns. You know in some games, when you can switch to another weapon as the new mag is loaded? Yeah, that doesn't exist here. You either wait for the entire animation, or cancel it entirely, even as visually the new magazine is loaded in. It still trips me up more than I'd like.There's also a distinct lack of melee weapons and combat, you have one Augmetic that makes you go super fast with a massive knife. It's powerful and quite useful because of other mechanics, but... that's it. In an universe where chainswords are a thing, tis a bit of a bummer (well, okay, to be fair, a Hired Gun may not have easy access to that kind of tech).On the other hand tho...The game is fun.The combat is actually quite good, in good part to the weapon's feedback. Every gun feels powerful, sounds powerful, and will leave some nasty marks on the basic goons you'll face all the time. One shot to the head with a Stub gun will be enough to make the head go somewhere else. A sawed-off shotty point-blank shot? The entire body will be purée'd. It's satisfying.The mobility is pushed quite far, you can wallrun, wall jump, dash, slide, double jump - and you're even rewarded with a dodge bonus for doing so. It's not Titanfall level, but it's not that far.You have a lot of Augmetics, all with powerful effects like slow down time for anyone but you, pull out a big knife and run around like a madman, have a temporary aimbot... And all of those are on separate cooldowns. Yes, it gets as ridiculous and awesome as it sounds.As for the weapons and visuals... It's 40k through and through. The scale is absolutely massive, and the universe has a lot of details put into it. I was a bit giddy when I got my hands on a Bolter or a Stub Cannon - talk about a Bigger Iron !And even the Mastiff gets some love from me as well despite its janky state... At some point, I just see him maul a random hiveganger, I'm finishing mine, and I just see him bring me the leg of the poor sod he killed. What a good boy !So yeah. The more I play it, the more the game is winning me over, despite its flaws.Just know what you're getting yourself into, and you should have a good time once you can get past the jank.Either that, or wait for patches.

_childDocuments_.review: No, sorry, another swing and a miss by the same ship of fools who created Space Hulk: Deathwing. It just doesn't work well enough to be fully satisfying especially when rightfully compared to DOOM: Eternal, which may have been a bit over the top but at least worked. Execution animations get old after just a few of them and the animations themselves don't seem that well executed. It's frustratingly difficult (not to mention grind-heavy) to the point of being nearly unplayable as a single player game on anything above Easy mode, the side missions are much harder than the actual campaign missions you're trying to grind up currency for the upgrades to attempt, and most environments in the game look even worse than Space Hulk: Deathwing. It's just a very low-grade experience in every category identifiable, and all it does is bring to mind better, but still not perfect games like Destiny 2 and DOOM: Eternal. If you've already played either/both, you may be better off just passing this one by until it's at least half price. It is fast-paced and violent, as advertised, but neither thing really qualifies it in any way as a good game.Forget about the dog; it's an advertising gimmick. Basically a navigational tool (to light up enemies and objectives) and fully upgraded he's still less useful than a weak Palico in Monster Hunter. Not very useful in any situation with more than one weak enemy engaged.

_childDocuments_.review: If Doom is the daddy, then Necromunda: Hired Gun is the teenager...not quite a child or baby, not quite an adult.The Warhammer 40k universe/setting is amazing & depicted beautifully..if you're a true Warhammer 40k fan, then you will enjoy it for that alone.If you're a seasoned Doom fan, you will notice the cracks in the AI and few janky things here & there.However all in all, it's a fun run'n'gun experience..and it's frickin hard too!I don't touch easy or normal difficulties..jumped straight into Hard and it's been both ok & absolutely brutal at times.Got some nice abilities, weapons, the mastiff is cool, and upgrades are nice..some weapons are absolutely crazy and that's part of the reason why I would 100% recommend this game.It doesn't have the polish like Doom 2016 or Doom Eternal, but it certainly feeds that craving.Love it!

_childDocuments_.review: In it's current state, the game is OK for an indie game. I enjoy the W40K universe and there's a lot of that to see here, but being in the universe is no fun in this game. The game wants to be a doom-esque shooter with rapid pacing and flying about, but the environments are often too large and under utilised or populate. This is compounded by the poor AI (both spawning and in action).  Additionally, you'll have long walks through vast areas of nothing to fight a group of maybe 2-5 goons, keep walking then wait for the AI to spawn. Several times, I cleared a room  and had to wait for the final AI to spawn in - often I'd have to use the dog to see where they were on the map. The Kill the officer missions are awful - you'll clear the map and see the badies slowly spawn in behind you.

_childDocuments_.review: This would be a really good boomer shooter if it had been completed. There's at least 3 plot threads that just peter out with no conclusion, you have the entire arsenal before you're halfway through the game and there's even a heavy weapon slot that just isn't used. This looks and feels like act 1 got nearly complete and then the budget was cut. The gunplay is basic but solid and more or less satisfying, but it needed *more*. The whole thing needs *more*; more story development, more options for upgrading your bionics and your dog, more missions, just *more*. It's sad to see that not even the modding community wants to make that happen. Here's hoping Boltgun is better.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the game so far, i finished the first two levels and two side missions. So obviously I'm not that far yet, but I can already tell I'm going to enjoy the game, especially for the price I paid. I had eight dollars credit with Humble Bundle and the game is 27 dollars currently if you have Humble Choice in the Humble Store. Even though I paid around 20 after tax, I still think for 27 it would be worth it. It's kind of like a poor man's Doom. So don't expect a polished game as it's far from it. But I find it to be very fun so far. I love searching all the nooks and crannies for the chests and grabbing all the loot I can to upgrade my character as well as the dog which I totally dig. I also love how you can modify every part of each gun among other things. Again, the game is far from perfect but if you like first person shooters at a budget, then I think this game is worth the price I paid, but for forty dollars plus tax which is how much the game will be sold for on Steam after June 10th, I think the game may fall short of expectations at that point for some people who are picky.I'll update my review in the near future after I spend more time with the game but as it stands, I still recommend this game at the sale price I got it for. It's janky but it's been really fun for me as I mentioned earlier. I bought the game not expecting much, but the games already exceeded my expectations and then some. The world design is great, the customization is awesome, i love the guns as I think they pack quite a punch, the melee is fun to watch as there's a wide variety of takedowns to perform, the powerups and upgrades are fantastic as well. I like being being able upgrade the dog as well as I'm an animal lover so it's a big plus in my book. At the end of the day the games mindless fun that provides a great deal of entertainment if you like shooters, even if it is a poor man's doom, that's not a bad thing in my opinion, especially if you grab the game on sale as I have.

_childDocuments_.review: People who expected anything but a typical fun but janky Streum On Studio game are fools and deserve the disappointment.Honestly a very fun game that is eerily similar in parts to Streum On Studio's first (and best) videogame E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy. The game overall just oozes atmosphere and drives home the fact that Streum On are a bunch of Warhammer nerds who deeply care about the franchise. The good:Visual presentation: Absolutely stellar. The whole game is incredible eye candy filled with an insane attention to detail according to the gritty feel of Necromunda, same as it was in their previous title Space Hulk Deathwing. Where as Space Hulk Deathwing had more diverse areas, Necromunda's areas are all in all a mix of rundown industrial wastes. Given that, the team still did amazing job with what they had in terms of terrains.Gameplay/Gunplay: Very fun. Your character is extremely agile and able to traverse all sorts obstacles with a mix of wallrunning, grapling hook, or just his sheer speed. Gunplay, as is the staple of Streum On's games is top notch and tight, all the guns have a very satisfying feeling to them, enhanced by the very visceral gore of dying enemies. The gun selection is very decent for such a title, from Warhammer's regulars like bolters and heavy bolters, to some more gritty options, like the extremely oversized Stub Cannon. Another personally great part of the gun selection is their scale, while the regular revolvers and autoguns are more reasonably scaled, guns like the aforementioned heavy bolters and stub cannons are comically oversized, as it should be in a Warhammer game (this fact leads to hilarious confusions by the members of steam discussions, who are confused that heavy bolter takes up half the screen even with maximum FOV). The gameplay is further enhanced by buyable and upgradable abilities, which while not as wacky as in E.Y.E still have fun stuff like bullet time, autoguided laser projectiles, and a literal aimbot. Sound/Music: Great soundtrack by the composer of E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy Olivier Zuccaro perfectly sets the atmosphere for all the parts of the game, be it a huge battle or exploring a deeper parts of the hiveworld. I am personally not one for listening to soundtracks while playing videogames, however I made an exception for Necromunda, and it did not disappoint. The sound overall is well done, especially when it comes to the weapons (answer for the great question of whether the videogame bolter sounds good is a resounding yes in this case). Length: For a 40$/€ game (29 in my case with launch sale + greenmangaming sale), the 10,5 hours that it took me to get through the main campaign + around 3 optional missions is more than adequate for me.Price: As already stated, thankfully Streum On Studio don't try to act like triple A developers and the price reflects that. From my experience I would say that even the full price of 40$/€ is adequate.The bad, ugly and janky:The gameplay jank: New players who might not be acquainted with Streum On's previous titles, might be put back by certain elements that they like to put into their games. Namely stuff like random critical strikes regardless of headshots, optional missions being just a simple objectives (kill 10 beefy enemies, defend point etc.) on the maps that you have already went through in the campaign, or respawning enemies. I'm thankful to say that respawning enemies happen only in the optional missions and not in the story missions. However the combination of two makes optional objectives not really that engaging, or fun to grind repeatedly. Thankfully the only reason to even play the optional missions is to earn some extra credits for buying upgrades or upgrading weapons, so if you're not into that sort of thing, you can easily skip them, the game should be completable without them. As a last thing I would like to mention the grappling hook. While a nice addition, it works only when it feels like it. When it does feel like working, it will most likely not grapple you to the exact place where you were aiming at. Feels like some kind of countermeasure so that people won't use it where they shouldn't and get out of bounds. Also the weird HP regen system: you get 3 medkits for a mission, and 3 respawns (if you buy them before the missions that is). After that the only way of regenerating health is first getting damaged, and then for a certain amount of time you heal from the damage you inflict (kinda sorta lifeleech). The issue arises when you get as low as 3 HP, where every single hit kills you, and therefore you have no way of getting health back, other than dying and respawning.The difficulty jank: Every enemy you encounter has an aim equivalent to a typical 12 year old Fortnite gamer on 60+ mg of adderall. When they lock onto you, they'll just rip you to shreads with absolute pinpoint accuracy. In several points where you have to fight several enemies at once it gets kind of silly. The only types of attacks you have a chance of dodging are slow moving projectiles like rockets, or hammer dudes jumping on you. The only way to combat these god gamers disguised as hive world inhabitants is to either hope that the weird HP regen is able to keep you alive, or to start glory killing them (and boy.. will we get to the glory kills). The difficulty selection tells you that the higher difficulty will grant you more rewards, but I haven't really noticed a difference (in loot, I have noticed the huge difference in number of loading times I had to sit through after getting my face violated on hard difficulty). Therefore I see no reason to play anything but normal difficulty, or even easy, if for whatever reason you want to just finish the game for the story. But about that one..The story jank: It's pretty meh. You won't get any epic Warhammer sagas here, more of a run of the middle hive war gang war stuff. The animation jank: The biggest glaring visual issue in the game are some of the animations. For enemies it mostly applies for the big guys like Ogryns. Sometimes their animation while running onto you just bugs out and they appear to be angelically floating/almost T-posing towards you. The biggest animation issues come from the glory kills. While glory kills were a nice addition, they are flat out broken, gameplay and animation wise. You can glory kill an enemy from any HP level, the only thing that stops you from doing so is their Refractor Field (aka. armor/shield). When you do so, you are put into a state of complete invincibility. Yes, that means that you can just straight up glory kill whole squads of enemies, even the ones with Refractor Field if you get a certain upgrade, without any repercussions. Animation wise, while there are about 3 different glory kill animations that look decent, most often then not they just don't connect with the enemy, and you end up stabbing the air. Also, when you are in a process of glory killing, any sort of knockback (biggest offenders being hammer dudes) will knock you away insane distances, but only in the glory kill animation, so when you finish the kill, you'll get instantly teleported back to the corpse. Very disorienting.The inventory jank (look, i just like writing the word jank ok): There is no inventory. Yea, I'm not kidding. Yea, I don't get it either. The only pseudo inventory you get is in the hub world, where the only way of even accessing it, is talking to a weapon's merchant. So when you get a new weapon in a missions, you can either bank it to the aetherial inventory (for selling or keeping at the end), or equip it straight up. But for some reason, into missions you can only go with 2 main weapons (bolters, grenade launchers, what have you) and 2 pistols. I really do not understand what they were thinking with this.So all in all, a very fun, but janky (told you) game. Don't let the length of cons dissuade you, I fully recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are only two reasons you’d be reading this. Either you’re my steam friend and this review is up on your activity feed (if so keep scrolling) or you’re a hungry Warhammer 40k FPS fan checking out if this morsel of 40k FPS action is worth your time and money. Either way, I feel bad for you.40K Fans know good 40k FPS experiences are few and far between. Seeing as there are only like five 40k FPS games and some of them are multiplayer focused. Even so, I would only recommend Necromunda Hired Gun to the most diehard 40k fans for its sale price. For the average FPS enjoyer, you’re not going to get a memorable or high-quality experience out of this game. It’s trashy fun, and it has its good aspects, but since I want others to take my recommendations seriously, I do not recommend this game. I wish I could rate a game “neutral.”First, the good.Necromuda hired gun tries. It does. It just doesn’t do a great job. Its level design, environment detail, and environmental story telling are good. A part of what kept me going was seeing where I would go next, and some of the environments I thought were legitimately high quality.  The lower hive of Necromuda is rich in lore and detail, and the developers made the most of it. I think this aspect made me decide to keep playing. I didn’t ask for a refund because I truly enjoyed the opening few missions.The weapon selection and gunplay is good as well. Plasma weapons, lasguns, bolters, etc, feel good and are fun to use in combat. The plasma pistol was especially fun to use and see your enemies get melted to pieces from it.That’s pretty much it for the good stuff. Environments and gunplay are important yes, but don’t outweigh the other considerations. But for a diehard 40k fan, this might be enough for you! And if so, I’d recommend it on sale.Now, the bad. No matter my subjective opinions of the game, an objective fact is that the game crashes a ton. During my playthrough, it crashed at least 5 times. Its frustrating for sure. You lose your progress, lose your immersion, and lose your steam. And its not like this is a long game. If I play a game for 40 hours and it crashed 5 times, that’s one thing, but an 8–10-hour game crashing that much is not a good look.The story is also bad. I mean this is 40k. We’re not expecting 500 IQ story lines with subtle complexities. But the story in Necromunda Hired Gun is told poorly and the game is not even designed to be a story focused experience. In between missions, you get a handful of dialogue lines from NPCs that push the story along, but you always return to the “select missions menu” and can play any mission out of order. Its more of a retro “Mission select” but with story elements. But, they could have done a better job with the story elements, especially having 40k lore handed to you.The combat, to be brutally honest, gets old. Enemy AI is bad. They do not take cover, they do not use tactics, they do not present meaningful gameplay challenges to the player besides having big guns and big health pools. Aside from environmental aspects, much of the combat looks the same from level to level. Spam your movement abilities and use every gun until they are all out of ammunition.Also, some gameplay elements serve to annoy the player and draw out the gameplay time. There are several missions where you must collect little power core things and take them to a power station to get something running. This means wandering around an environment looking for objects. Lame.A part of me feels bad for giving this one a negative review. Its not horrible. I finished it and didn’t regret my purchase or time spent playing. It’s just not good either. 40K fans looking for a high quality “doom-like” shooter might want to try Boltgun, which I would recommend.

I'm playing with a 3070 paired with a 11700k and 32 GBs of ram, yet the game's framerate regularly sees massive frame time spikes and lurches down to the 30's or so regardless of graphics settings.
