_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for July 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before August 2nd, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Necromunda: Hired Gun is based on a Game Workshop game called Necromunda, in the Warhammer 40k universe.  You’re on a mechanized planet, and the locations here do not disappoint, whether it’s the furnace locations during the first level, or an epic train that passes in the second, there’s a huge sense of scale and discovery here, that’s impressive. It’s too bad the rest of the game just doesn’t work as well as the levels and locations.  There’s a particularly bad character model that I’ll try to show here of a big brute, but it was a bad enough model that it made me start realizing it’s more visual trickery and filters that made the other enemies acceptable, at least I think so.  The gunplay in the first hour is average at best, and there are some weird control choices, such as combining the use, melee, and reload all on a single button, which is awkward for the melee takedowns. Then again some moments reminded me of Ghostrunner for the wall-running that’s rather good, and a few moments were visceral like Doom Eternal, but a weaker form of both if I’m honest.Pick this up if you love First Person shooters, I liked the environments here and would love to see more, but this is a Games Workshop game that tends to have a decent amount of Jank.  As always when it comes to these types of games, I recommend people check out Mandelore’s reviews if they want a more in-depth look at the game, which ultimately is positive though it does mention a lack of polish at launch. _childDocuments_.review: I had a fun 12 hours with it. As always, Streumon's visual presentation is fantastic, but expect bugs from anything they make.Their *core* gameplay is incredibly solid. Lifesteal augmetic that only activates when damage is taken forces you to stay fighting in order to keep your health up. You hide in cover only in order to wait for that power to come back, so you can run back in, take damage to activate it and refill your health bar. It's brilliant... I didn't think you could do that to encourage the very DOOM 2016/Eternal-like brawling gameplay, with hitscan enemies. Mixing in powers to quickly destroy the shields of tankier elites makes the combat flow incredibly well.There is a lot of negativity coming up now, but it's mostly talking about wasted potential in a single aspect of the game, rather than real problems the game has. It's a single, super minor issue I take seriously, and it doesn't change that the game is fine (albeit short).Firstly, to finish off the previous train of thought: when your opponent is plinking at you from far away, you use your movement to get to them. Obviously a double jump and grapple is going to be welcome to close the distance (or create distance) quickly, but you're immediately introduced to wallrunning and wall hopping, while 90% of the game is not built with it in mind. There's an entire augmetics tree for improving dodge chance while wallrunning/hopping but there's basically nowhere you can practically do that in the game. But my single most major issue with the game is weapon variety. I've always held the belief that EYE had some of the best guns in gaming, and I've been following Streumon because I believe they can make a roster that can top it. This is not that roster. I'm going to review every weapon in the game, starting with guns that are good, and ending with guns that are bad. This really should just be in the Steam Guides, but I felt it was important to illustrate what's happening here.Pretty standard automatic weapons. Shoots fast, good at close to midrange. Pretty good bread and butter weapons, combine with the slowmo and aimbot powers.For the heavy weapons, don't use the precision mechanics. The heavy bolter's special shield barrel makes it basically unusable outside of aimbot, both because of the accuracy/stability loss and because of visual clutter.For the plasma weapons, don't use the condensed cells. Gaining a bit of extra damage per shot is not worth losing 27 shots per reload. With the exception of the Plasma weapons, which fire projectiles, these are all the exact same weapons, with slight variations in magazine capacity, fire rate, and damage. You're gonna want 2 or 3 of these in your loadout, because none of the other pistols are good, and they're the best, most reliable ways to deal damage, working very well on their own, and making empowering abilities like slowmo and aimbot even more empowering. You mod most of them the exact same way, too - Max out damage and armour penetration first, accuracy and stability next, and every sacrifice to handling is worth it because you never need to aim down sights with these. Streumon included 3 good semi-autos, though!Pinpoint accurate, perfectly stable, and a lot of damage to boot. Pretty good precision weapon. Death machine when combined with the slowmo and aimbot powers. Kills Ogryns in one charged shot to the head!Remember, these things are tiny flashlights to things like  and  This is what they do to It's like a slow, homing missile that only has an explosive payload when it kills something. Hurts to get hit by the projectile. Hurts the victim's friends even more when the projectile explodes. Good for fighting faraway crowds, and sometimes agile enemies. Don't combine with slowmo, the projectiles aren't hitscan, don't inherit the speed you get, and are already very slow.Use the high explosive rounds for a very big area of effect that does good damage. Good for clearing crowds at around midrange, or if you're feeling lucky, use it at close range to activate your lifesteal augmetic.You use the stubber pistol in random execution animations and to open chests. You will always have a base level stubber that can't be replaced because of these. I'm pretty sure the full auto counterparts actually do more damage per shot than these. I wouldn't go out of my way to use these unless, I dunno, I felt like setting up a turbo fire macro. Long Las but bad. Has recoil, low capacity, slow firing, and like 2 points of extra damage over an uncharged las shot. a shotgun modded for full damage can only imagine to perfectly land all pellets on an ambot or ogryn in your face (an unwise position to be in) and still does less damage than a single bolter shot. they murdered my precious depezedore so bad i'm in tearsStreumon are usually pretty good at bringing interesting weapons into their games. I personally believe that EYE has my favourite weapon roster of all time, and despite its flaws, I think Deathwing has a good weapon roster too. It's unfortunate that this game only has, like, three entire  guns, and it's one of the main reasons that I would never say that this game is "EYE 2." It's a shame, because the rest of the guns have potential, if only they were better tuned. And if some of them... didn't exist?And it's not like a lack of variety hurts the flow of the game too much. Your guns are still very powerful, but they're taking a bit of a backseat. You're more focused on movement and using powers strategically this time around, rather than just using 4 different, uniquely powerful guns (though I think both would have been nice haha ;-;).Overall, I think it's a good game. I don't think it's Streumon's best game, but they worked hard on this, and this is clearly what they wanted to end up doing.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in the July Humble Choice bundle, and I am loving it! It's the most fun I've had in a single-player FPS in a long time - it's dark and gritty, difficult in places, and the story is forgettable, but the gunplay and skills are so satisfying to unleash that I don't care why I am murder-machining my way through the game. Plus it's Warhammer, and Warhammer is badass.I think it's the structure of the gameplay that has me enjoying it so much. There are main missions to complete, of course, but after the 2nd one is done side missions open up. These offer ways to earn more money with which to upgrade my skills and abilities, which in turn make completing main missions just that much easier. They're awesome, too, because they're quick and fun, the rewards are good, and they've allowed me to unlock things like greater rewards for completing side missions and improvements to my abilities.And using abilities is very important in this game, because having decent FPS skills alone has not been enough to keep me alive. The improvements in my combat abilities are tangible, too, and it's really nice to go from struggling to take down certain foes (♥♥♥♥ those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with energy shields) to being able to chew through them after disabling their shields with an upgraded Haywire Pulse. Being able to slow down time for longer has likewise proved incredibly helpful.The guns themselves are also satisfying to use, largely due to excellent sound design and damage upgrade variations that offer decent spectacle (fire damage on a fast-firing shotgun looks SO cool!), and Hired Gun encourages using them as much as possible. For example, it takes a leaf from DOOM's book by giving you a skill that lets you heal by shooting enemies in a small time window after taking damage, so you're incentivised to keep moving and shooting as much as possible. Traversal is pretty sweet as well, with wall-running, sliding, double jumps and dodges to make getting around the huge environments a lot of fun.I am also only playing now, with the game patched and stable like it apparently wasn't at launch, so I'm seeing it at its best. After playing for 12 hours or so, I can definitely say that if you've been thinking about getting it but you've been on the fence, you should totally grab it. At the time of writing it's on sale, so it's a great time to dive in.I am only on the 4th story mission as of this review (I've been farming cash for upgrades via the side missions), so maybe it gets worse in the future, but for now I am very happy with my purchase. I'm enjoying myself so much, in fact, that I am considering grabbing other Warhammer titles that I've had my eye on (Underhive Wars in particular), in the hope that they have also been improved by patches in the time since release.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on sale, so take that into consideration: it's worth around $20, $25, no more than that.Necromunda is... OK. The game itself wasn't too buggy once it got started up, but the startup is extremely unstable--for some reason starting up the game would immediately cause my computer to go into a BSOD and the only workaround was to stay tabbed on something else until the opening intro started playing. Visuals are fine. I'm not an aficionado for graphics and I had them set to medium for most of the playthrough, nothing stuck out as particularly ugly or unsightly (at least, unless it was deliberately meant to be as part of the visual style).I'm not too familiar with W40k but I know enough to realise Necromunda diverges from the usual tone of crazy Commissars and Space Marines. I'd say the store pages' art and videos do a great job of exhibiting Necromunda's specific take on the W40k franchise.Voice acting is okay. The female player character voice actress does a better job than the male one, and I think that's because the male player character voice actor was pushing his voice too far out of its natural range to make himself sound gravelly. Nobody's taking home any awards here, but there's no lines that stick out as "I-need-someone-to-go-to-bleak-falls-barrow-to-fetch-something-for-me" or "English voiceover dub" levels of awful. That said, the dialogue ends up feeling a bit shallow since all of the conversations the player interacts with are strictly 1-to-1 conversations between the player and one character at a time.The story is flat. It's mainly a thin framework used to get the player between action segments and the story ends pretty abruptly and unceremoniously.The gameplay itself isn't everyone's cup of tea, but it was a fresh change of pace from what I'm used to. Technically the player can get healing items, but the main way to recover from damage is to get melee kills in this game, so there's a lot of emphasis on close quarters and mobility--the structure of how character progression works reminds me a lot of the Far Cry franchise, but the actual gameplay reminds me more of Warframe: speed, aggression, and special abilities are most important. The game doesn't take the time to tell you this, but it's important to always bring a couple of weapons specifically with high armor penetration+radiation damage. There's an armored enemy called an "ambot" which becomes fairly common in the later sections of the game and they take forever to kill without weapons that are specifically modified with them in mind.Enemy variety is shallow. Said simply, there's several "factions" in the game but they're all essentially reskins. There's one type of big monster enemy (I'm not saying what just for spoilers' sake) that appears for a single mission then never shows up again and never gets mentioned again.The mastiff companion is also quite useful as-advertised, though the mastiff's appearance changes permanently and irreversibly when you have it upgraded, so be aware that upgrading the mastiff's skull past step 2 will turn it into some horrific nightmare-thing, admittedly appropriate for W40k's tone.The best I can say for this game is at least I don't feel ripped off for the $25 price tag. Necromunda is not everyone's cup of tea. Parts of it are clearly underpolished and it's clear that the developers wanted to do more with the game and the setting, but shoved it out the front door before really putting the elbow-grease into finishing it properly.Is the game stressful due to the occasional clunkiness and unstable programming? Yes.Am I going to put 300+ hours into it as tends to be my average for games I really enjoy? No, I'm pretty sure I won't.Was it also memorable, visually interesting, and kinda fun? ...Yeah, despite everything, I guess it was.The gameplay tries to come up with its own thing instead of just copy/pasting the gameplay from somewhere else, and it's at least not a total mess. The best way to avoid disappointment is to avoid expecting too much (and avoid overpaying).

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the campaign after two days of playing (14hrs) and whilst I can't say this is my dream game, I would certainly recommend it to 40k enthusiasts. The recent history of 40k games have been appalling, so in that light this game is a really solid step in the right direction!Game play is fun, very much inspired by Doom's frantic run -wall run- and gun, with less hordes and enemy variety. There are plenty of side missions to stretch out the brief campaign, augmetic and weapon upgrades are handled nicely. But the weapon options feature several classes that soon become obsolete, leaving you with 5 - 6 solid weapons (boltguns are sick in all formats). Yes there are little glitches and the graphics can be a little janky at times, but the environments and character models are all stunningly reproduced. The voice audio also needs drastically raising and general sounds effects could use some tweaks / fixes as others have statedThat said, Devs please make some FLC or DLC to give a bit more replayability! The story wasn't really that enthralling given we didn't get any solid backstory on our protagonist or any emotional connection, so I would just focus on exploring more of necromunda, perhaps even seeing some of the upper hive! Fix the plasma guns and gravguns, I feel they really don't hit nearly as hard as the bolt gun or grenade launcher. Also it really bugged me being forced to carry that level one autogun, please let us trade it for higher level equivelants!I'm really looking forward to a sequel or perhaps another 40k game in a different setting (Armageddon would be pretty sweet). Thanks Devs! <3

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for something close to Doom 2016 without the 'weapon/enemy restrictions' of Doom Eternal, Necromunda: Hired Gun is a good "B Budget" choice. I'll go in greater detail here in just a moment, but for those who want the quick version: The game runs and works really well, especially for a fast paced FPS, but be prepared to forgive the poor animation quality. If you're in it for the gameplay itself, it's a great power-fantasy parkour shooter with enough challenge in it to keep things interesting.Okay, long version. And we'll start with the main negative that you will notice as soon as you hit "Open This Rust-Damn Door!"The Janky AnimationsY-yeah >>; I have no excuses here. They definitely look off and it takes a while to see past them. Takedowns are something you will be doing a lot of if you want to go for 100% Achievements (since they are near crucial  to increase your Style Kill rank at the end of a level). They're choreographed well, and I can see what the animators wanted to do, however they really do lack a lot of impact and rely on 'camera shakes' to fill in the gaps... Which doesn't really work. Granted, these animations do not hinder the gameplay specifically, but you will be disappointed if you expect "Glory Kill" levels of detail and impact here. You're invincible while doing them, and they do give you a little bit of health while getting rid of an enemy (or at the very least their shields).Menus are kind of a mess, but you get used to them. Some things were kinda dumb, like having 3 slots for 'pistols' and three slots for: Basics (assault rifles, shotguns), Heavy (Miniguns), and Specials (Plasmaguns, Grenade Launchers, Sniper Rifles). A little weird, but I found just having the three basic guns were enough for all my needs/encounters. Especially with the amount of powers you get.Finally, A personal one...The Dog AugmentationIf you're a fan of WH40k, you know what you're getting into: Hardcore Cybernetics and Skull Decor. I honestly really liked the add-in of the dog (Mastiff) in the game, let alone using it as a 'power' of sorts. However, you are pushed a little to upgrade it; afterall you want your companion to be useful to you and not just get immediately killed once summoned (not permanently in the slightest, don't worry). Annnnd the way to upgrade it is through Augmentation...You can see where this is going.At first, I started with the Body so I could summon it faster or something, and that altered the looks of the dog itself; as expected. It just got some plates along his back, and I thought "Oh, that's not so bad. Let's try paws next, give it a bit more armor on the legs-" NOPE! If you choose the paw option, you Amputate Your Dog's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Legs, then replace them with bionic ones.I'm not a WH40K fan, but I should have expected this >>; However, I didn't, and there's no way to "go back". So the reason why this is a bit of a 'negative' thing for me is that I'm a bit torn with having my dog being Useful to me while looking... Unpleasant (in a matter of opinion, of course. Especially the damn head "options"). Or, you can have it look good (love that Hellhound skin) and be a rather unreliable 'power'. If they could just allow players to customize the Mastiff's looks (aside from like two main-skin choices that are 60% replaced by any Augmentation upgrade) this entire section could be waved off. But really, it just left me feeling guilty through the rest of the game....Really. That was about it for negatives. The story's kinda meh, might be better if you're a fan of the franchise but it didn't connect with me. However, nothing offensive here, no strong feelings about it one way or another.Positives! This'll be alot longer of a section because it has a lot of good points here:-Gunplay: I played with M&K and after some adjusting I got it to where I felt really comfortable with the aiming. There is a lot of movement in the game, but often enough using movement abilities will increase your aim assist (especially with wallrunning). Weapons themselves felt good, honestly. They had a decent variety and could be customized quite well to your own play style. Don't want to ADS while moving around? Build your weapons with a focus on accuracy. Want to turn your Sawed-Off Shotgun into a 'Sniper Rifle'? Go for it. And this was something I honestly really praise about the game: it didn't really need to balance the weapons too hard because you're the one doing the balancing. One gun can probably get you through a mission, sure, but it probably won't be easy, let alone entertaining. Have fun with what you're getting. If it doesn't play the way you want, spend some coin and get some parts to change it to fit your style/purpose. Say, if an enemy is giving you a hard time, build a gun focused on taking that bugger down. Its really cheap to buy parts (save for ONE part) and everything's unlocked once you have that gun.-Parkour: This was implemented really well in N:HG. In the beginning you have a Dash, Wallrun, and Slide. After the first mission you get Double Jumps, and after the second you get a grapple hook. Doing any of these will give you a passive Dodge bonus on top of actually being hard to hit (as well as the aim assist mentioned earlier). As expected with games like this, you are constantly moving around at relatively high speeds with plenty of places to use these abilities. In theory, it may sound a little off, but in practice I found it was a lot more fun. To the point where N:HG nearly ruins a lot of other games for me after getting so used to the mobility and speed >>; Mix that with...-Powers: This is a Power-Fantasy game, and your character- though a bit squishy, gets an entire arsenal to play with. Apart from your mentioned Mastiff, you can slow down time for better aiming while keeping yourself at the same speed. You have auto-target that can give even the weapons with the most ridiculous spread have pin-point accuracy for a short time. You have teleportation/laser explosion thing(?) as well as a long ranged version that can auto-target up to 6 people within range. They all have decently long cooldowns, but once you get them unlocked you have them all on you at all times. They are made to be used, and they are fun to use, honestly. And that's kind of the point of them: They're Fun.-Level Layout: As mentioned before; this is a Warhammer game. And it's... Let's just say that the theme is quite 'creative' in general. I honestly think the art direction of the levels themselves are quite good, but how the layout makes use of your powers and abilities is quite outstanding. A few places were hard to navigate, but I never really found myself lost or frustrated attempting to get somewhere/figure something out. There's lots of little hidden credits, ammo, and shield refills if you go looking for them, but none of which are really needed. If you are going for a high rank though; you want to search for hidden chests (your Augur Array ability can help you seek these out). Going for the "A+ Student" Achievement will slow the game down quite a bit due to needing to find most of these chests in a level (not all required) but that's about it.Overall, I highly recommend the game if it sounds fun to you. I barely encountered any bugs (grappled myself into a wall once, but that was it. The game has a slight checkpoint system, so I barely lost any time) and if you can get around the stiff animations, you'll have a good time. I'd give it an 8/10. If they could fix up those negative two points I had, I'd probably push it up to a 9. A tad expensive, but I definitely had my fun with it. It's currently this month's Humble Bundle, and N:HG alone would be worth the price there

_childDocuments_.review: Another in the long line of warhammer games that are better then the average warhammer game but subpar when compared to basically anything else. It's like if doom eternal took itself more seriously, but then made the gameplay and music worse. The best thing about it are the visuals and ill admit they are incredible, but that doesnt make up for the short comings.Enemies with absurdly high health totals are essentially a constant issue. The enemies are inhumanly accurate, making fun strategies like wall sliding and dashing behind them essentially worthless. The take down animations are cool for about the first mission, and then you realize just how long you spend stuck in cutscenes of you doing the same "super cool" take downs. The mastif is a fun addition, but sadly they are very buggy and often get stuck on geometry or flat out refuse to attack enemies within sniffing distance. Overall a solidly underwhelming experience that i could not be asked to see to completion. If you want a good 40k game go play mechanicus, if you want a good shooter go play any of the dozens of exceptional ones.

_childDocuments_.review: There are some very cool set pieces in what I played of this game and it's got a great visual style but it's ultimately let down by fairly mediocre gameplay and a customization system that throws you into the deep-end without doing much to keep you from drowning in options.The parkour system is OK but feels clumsy compared to games with similar controls like Titanfall 2. In one instance, I got "stuck" on a pillar where I was just doing a loop, wall running in a big circle trying desperately to find my bearings. In another instance, I wall ran along the side of a platform instead of grabbing it - I ultimately ran off to my death that time and lost some credits as a result. Cool...A couple other issues that ultimately led me to uninstall and write this review:* The B-missions / side missions are just kind of combat arenas made up of parts of existing levels and are filled with pretty annoying enemies. They're shooting you with some pretty high-damage weapons, higher damage than anything I've seen in the campaign. Toward the end, most of the enemies what felt like too many shots to kill and a good half of them came out with body-height shields.* The hissing noise that the chests make is way too close to the hissing sounds in the environmental music, so much so that it impossible for me to tell if I was near a chest or just at a point in the music that *sounded* like a chest. Hidden chests are fun but the audio confusion made me stop searching for them which is a huge bummer in  a game about finding better loot.* Speaking of loot, I had a really hard time parsing the loot in this game. The depth of customization is cool but I didn't feel a meaningful trade-off between certain guns. The AR did a good enough job taking out enemies at mid and close range. I occasionally switched to the SMG but found myself quickly swapping back to the AR once I'd killed whatever was close. The shotguns were incredibly disappointing - the options were either a double-barrel breach-loader OR a pump-action that doesn't feel particularly powerful. The revolvers felt similarly weak for what they are.* You get a dog but it feels super squishy and doesn't seem terribly useful. Your dog's not with you all the time, you have to summon it. Once summoned it runs around for a bit, usually grabs a guy, and then de-spawns for you to summon it again on cooldown.

_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: - Lovingly crafted Necromunda visual- Incredibly detailed maps (ruined by cons)- Weapon variety (ruined by cons)- Weapon customisation could be neat (ruined by cons)- A not mediocre soundtrack- Wants to be Doom so badly, but fails to emulate it effectively- The huge variety of weapons means little as half of them are useless in the mindless close quarter combat, the ♥♥♥♥ am I going to use a max-zoom long-las for?- A very lazy approach to enemy spawning where you craft a map first and then try to jam gameplay in to it afterwards- Enemy AI spot you instantly, charge you, fire constantly and that's it- The health system is a constant tug'o'war of searching the rafters for energy cells and masochistically exchanging fire with enemies for health and hoping you die last- Visual clutter forces the game to need to highlight enemies for you- Physical clutter voids most of your evasion mechanics like wall running, a game where standing still means death should not have so many static wall/floor obstructions- The game feels like it is moving about 25% faster than it should be, just for the sake of frenetic gameplay- Needlessly confusing and janky inventory system, why are you trying to reinvent the wheel so poorly- It's a looter shooter that hates you collecting loot and forces you to ditch it constantly- Your dog is just a gimmicky activated ability that zooms around the arena ridiculously or sits still doing nothing- Bafflingly useless default keyboard scheme with ridiculous positioning- Narrative/NPC interaction is badly executed, confusing and provides no exposition for anyone not already deeply versed in Necromunda lore- Levelling up seems to mean nothing- You can unlock all available powers almost immediately and from then on it is unsatisfying incremental upgrades like "make an ability last 0.1 seconds longer"I want to like this game but it is a real hot mess, frankly, with a whole bunch of on-paper good ideas mashed together very clumsily. There are layers of different games in here that just don't work together very well and are just kind of there, for instance wall running for traversal becomes pointless once you get a grapple almost immediately. Pick one.It's going for "ballet of death" but all it ends up with is "noisy cluster ♥♥♥♥", wasting its potential. It took a very high level look at Doom and copied it across without appreciating any of the nuances that stopped Doom's gameplay from just turning in to a tangled heap of explosions and viscera.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just so glitchy and unpolished that it isnt worth it in its current state, and Im frankly skeptical that will change- texture/decal blinking and glitching- enemies just magically spawning in front of you so you can do a retarded ultrakill conga line- retarded AI that gets stuck- laughably stupid plot (not in a B movie good way, more of an 'oh good can they try to be any edgier')- key response for executions hit or missThis should not have been released in its current state.  Its a mediocre shooter being carried by fans because of the setting.  I expected way better of the folks who gave us E.Y.E. and they let me down here
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: As a living creature, your time is priceless. Don't waste it playing this game. I really wanted to love Hired Gun but I just can't. Pro : art-wise, it's a hit. Looks great. Nails the atmosphere.Cons : nothing else comes together. The quality of this game is even lower (far lower) than E.Y.E, if you can believe it, and E.Y.E was a heap of jank built on a piece of string and a wooden board with two nails stuck in it. Games you can play instead : Dusk, Nightmare Reaper, Amid Evil, Forgive Me Father, Wrath : Aeon of RuinBiggest grievances :- ENEMIES RESPAWN OUT OF THIN AIR RIGHT IN FRONT OF YOUR FACE, OR WORSE, BEHIND YOU, WITH NO SOUND CUE. That is the worst part of this experience. Not only does it shatter the immersion into pieces, it also becomes cheap, irritating, and absurd. You can kill a clump of 5 goons and watch them all repop a literal second later right where you killed them. They don't even produce sound when moving. - The general gameplay balance is a complete joke. It's way too hard, and not in fun ways, with a lot of excessively accurate hitscan arrayed against you, your run speed feels juuuuust a tad too slow, etc. Highest difficulty is just a meme. Melee enemies damage you instantly. Shielded enemies are utterly absurd. - The animations are trash. Nothing feels right. The takedowns are horrendous to look at, with screen shake galore and misplaced objects, eg, stabbing thin air. Feedback when hitting enemies is non-existent. - Many of the visual effects are totally obnoxious. Plasma guns, for example, blind you when you fire them, and you just can't even see what you're shooting at. - Guns feel eh. Not good for an FPS. This is just a complete shame. This game could have been amazing with a few heavy patches. But as it is, it's not worth playing even on sale, because you are a mortal creature with a limited lifespan (if you'll allow me to presume)I had 66 hours on E.Y.E, because it was playable. This isn't playable, this is W40k-skinned ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

And why use A and E  to navigate between MENU tabs??? A and D or Q and E would make sense, whatever this is... does not.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10.This is a game of two halves.The actual mechanics are good. Environments are excellent, the detail is fantastic, guns work as they should for anyone that knows the lore. The upgrade portion is fantastic, gives you a little something to strive for and carry on. Combat is great once you get the hang of it. As long as you don't play the new DOOM games beforehand. They tried to do that and ended up with a watered-down version.It fails on just about everything else, though. The story is very average, a poor effort when such care was put into the detail. The side missions are instantly immersion breaking, pulling down the quality of the main plot. Without these, the story might be more interesting, but such is the feeling  of just grinding for money that the entire game just loses something.While those main missions are relatively interesting, there is nothing to care about, nothing to get you invested in what's happening. The main character is an a**, the side characters aren't really of much interest either.And they could have been.Spoiler Warning.If they had access to the Kal Jerico IP, why in the hell wasn't HE the MC? There is a character that is likeable, interesting and comes with his own universe and cast of characters. I'd have paid double for a Kal Jerico game with this sort of production value, instead we got this mess. Jerico is a bit player and shows none of the roguish charm that so defined the original stories.There were genestealers... once. That could have been a hell of a big-bad, instead we got a generic gang member. Necromunda, in its various incarnations, has included, in no particular order: flame-wielding fanatics, mega-spiders, necromancer psykers, ultra-fascists, Lovecraftian monsters and more. We get none of those, none of the whacky flavour that so defines the 40k universe.We get an antihero hunting for money. Something that's been done a dozen times. Vanilla in a universe of potential flavours.God the sheer waste of this opportunity makes me want to spit. It could have been so magnificent, they clearly had the budget to make something unique, but all we got was the same old shooter with different skin and a couple of gimmicks.Buy if it's on sale. Or if you don't know anything about 40k and haven't played Doom or Doom Eternal.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't say they are breaking the mold with new style and game features, but they do get it right. If you want a mind numbingly quick, reactionary, and on the edge of your seat FPS, look no further. Combine "Doom" gritty atmospheric layout, with very early " James Bond" grappling hook movement, gives you endless ways to drop in, smack into, or down right kick through baddies. Story is just captivating enough to keep coming back to play bounties. If you don't know much about the Warhammer 40K universe, don't be pushed away, the game gives enough back story and things to listen/ read to give you enough of a back ground to understand what is going on. all in all 8/10, id suggest to my friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this with the info, that I am not really knowledgeable about Warhammer at all apart from picking some stuff up from Trailers and other Warhammer video games.That out of the way, I have to say, that I really enjoyed playing this game. It's a game, that takes inspiration from a lot of other games, either intentionally or it is just my brain making these connections. But that doesn't matter as most of the things work. Wallrunning, grappling hooks, mid-air dashing, double jump all together make for a really fast and aggressive game, which is right up my alley. The takedown kills feel a bit like a cheap ripoff from Doom 2016/Eternal and they don't really flow as well as in the previously mentioned games. And yet, the gameplay works really well, especially since the different abilities you can upgrade throughout the story make it even more fun.The story on the other hand is too confusing for most players. I got the rough gist of it and it kept me going, but the real star here is the maps and the environment. Just the crazy scale of the different apparatuses and the bombastic explosions and other happenings make for some really great eye candy. The sidemissions are another story though, as they are simple missions of "collect 5 of these", "kill 10 of these" and other questions similar to that. They also end, once you have done all the changes, and give you no way to search for the treasure chests in the map, so I'd recommend collecting them in the campaign and skip the side missions unless you need the credits.I'd recommend this game to anybody that likes fast paced shooters with some gore and a gritty world. Reminds me a lot of cyberpunk meets mad max.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It seems a slowly refilling bar has been added to limit how often one can melee, this is something of a bandaid for the overarching problem, and I am not sure what they did to fix anything I have gripes with, mostly because the game has become to unstable for me to play for very long due to crashing with update #4.The devs basically took everything they learned from EYE and overlayed Doom 2016 on top of it....just remove the 'doomesk glory kills' for traditional melee. The enemy AI can't attack you while you're trying to 'finish off' an opponent anyway, so there's no point to them other then to look cool or feel bad ass. They only feel in the way of the gameplay if anything, I wasn't a fan when Doom made these unskipable repeating cut-scenes required to play the game at all, I am still not a fan of them now.The weapons are overly flashy making it impossible to tell if what you're shooting at is dead or not, and the hit indicator is not a substitute for being able to see what you're shooting at. More often then not I find myself just picking the smallest magazine size and magdumping everything I fire at. Ammo management becomes a problem for harder difficulties, not because there are more enemies or anything special the devs just got as lazy as every other dev when it comes to shooters and difficulty, they just tilt the health scale, what you used to be able to take is lessened and what the NPCs can eat for ammo is increased, nothing more nothing special. I find myself just tapping the fire button and bull rushing the enemy just to get an auto-stop combat kill for a free health and ammo regen which I find tacky, the only tactics this game has is avoid and burn ammo into the big things anything human just bum-rush/facetank into melee range due to health regenning for doing damage and taking damage, which makes no sense. Secure a small health and ammo refill with an auto-stop combat to watch the same cutscenes over and over again. A mindless chase down what you wanna kill and melee it spree.The game is also riddled with bugs, ADS not going back on while holding it after a reload, 'glory kills' breaking the camera requiring a restart. Holding down fire doesn't work after a reload, invisible walls this clipping that. It feels like this was rushed to release after the AMAZING art team finished everything, leaving the rest of the game from soundscape to how the game runs unpolished.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It just constantly feels like i don't know what i'm supposed to do. Maybe you can chalk it up to i'm bad at all of it, but the upgrade system is persnickety the levels feel like they fly by when i'm not dying because dodging with this movement system is unprecise, things are so jarring that i still don't know whats going on even when all enemies are dead, the list goes on but the main problem i have with the game isn't the story, to sum it up the world and the graphics are really cool but the dead pan characters mixed with gameplay that while thrilling for a little bit ends up feeling like i'm supposed to be playing a hardcore parkour game that they shoved Warhammer and FPS into at the very end otherwise they wouldn't get funding, i'm sorry but i don't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels undercooked and it's such a shame.It's overall a decent experience, but far from being great. Let me explain.Graphically speaking is more than enjoyable. It has a very cool setting with great lighting effects, you can breathe the attention to detail they've put into recreating a WH40K world worth exploring. Also, the OST is pretty good most of the time, and that's where the "great" part ends. Gameplaywise The game works okay-ish, but it has lots and lots of flaws. First of all: there is no inventory management while in-game. You can manage your stuff only in your hub right before missions or going to vendors in the hub area. Second problem: gunplay. Guns feel punchy and powerful, there is enough variety and customization, but at times they would refuse to shoot. It's a weird and uncommon bug, but common enough to be adrressed. Third issue: movement. Movement is fast, jumps and wall runs are satisfying and the grappling hook is a cool idea. Too bad it feels clunky a lot of times. Movement is slippery and imprecise, landing on small platforms can lead to your death and the hook doesn't always work as you'd expect, refusing to get attached to certain surfaces or platforms.I had a lot of fun nonetheless, it's a mediocre experience that could have been great if the devs put a little more time into it worth checking out if on a great sale. It's a solid 6/10 overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It really wants to be Doom in Necromunda. Unfortunately the controls are way too floaty, the shooting way too all over the place, and the melee not nearly as satisfying as Doom. Combine this with progress stalling bugs after years of patches and I did not have fun with this. Get it on sale if you really love the world, but don't expect too much here.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: So disappointing.First off, I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate the nuDoom style that's being mimicked here; glory kills 100% limit the style of game you're allowed to play into run-gun-and-press-button. You can't snipe, you can't stealth, you can't melee. You must keep moving like a hummingbird blasted out of his dumb bird skull on ritalin just to keep health up enough to not get one-shot by some jetpacking moron who tries to cram his entire body up your ass. It's stupid.The entire design philosophy of this game is wrong. It should have been an open-ended bounty hunting experience where you could experiment with equipment builds, like the aforementioned stealth, sniping, melee (which isn't even a thing), etc etc. The levels are huge, pretty, and varied (in 40k context obviously) enough that it's a no-brainer even to a sub-30-IQ idiot like me. But nah. You are required to zoom around and do i-frame glory kills because whoever wrote the master design document played nuDoom and wanted to copy-paste it.Also difficulty balance is whack. Easy is pointless and yet normal is like very hard in other games; as in, in order to survive you've got to take cover, but you're not allowed to because of jetpacking turds or dogs or whatever and there are a limited number of medkits you can bring. So that leaves rolling your face over the keyboard in "le frenetic" fjdiad9sa0hjd9sg.So frustrating, and it's not fun. What feels like half the later levels require running around to collect batteries in order to power up some bigger battery...because yeah, five minutes of searching in a lightspeed zoomer shooter is precisely what makes people enjoy the product. I do enjoy that there are randomly-generated bounty missions and I don't mind recycled tilesets, but the gameplay itself is the issue.It's not worth it even on sale. PS. I also loathe nuDoom for the same reason, but at least the nuDooms are better than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This is possibly the most generous thumbs-up I have ever given because while Necromunda: Hired Gun’s core gameplay is fun, almost everything else surrounding it ranges from mediocre to bad. The poorly implemented looter-shooter mechanics and badly paced story serve only to waste your time, and the game, overall, suffers from a lack of polish.But underneath its many issues lies a fast, frantic, ultra-violent shooter that will (mostly) scratch that DOOM itch. It gives you plenty to work with in both weapons and abilities, and the open-level design lets you put all of it to good use. I think you’ll have fun with it, even if you’re not a Warhammer fan. Also, it has a grapple- sorry, grapnel hook. I can’t complain about that.Recommended, but wait for a deep sale.Watch the full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of DOOM, Titanfall, Wolfenstein or any other high speed FPS you will love this game. If you are a fan of 40K this game actually immerses you in a way no other game has. The graphics are incredible and the environments and set pieces are beautifully GrimDark. My only real complaint is that there's no Photo Mode
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It reminds me of perhaps my favorite game from this developer, EYE, in all the best ways. Plus, it combines 40k into it more than it already was. On top of that, the customization and cybernetics aspect is a great time. Though it does make me wonder how the hell they got a potentia coil (and other "mechanicus-only" implants) in him but- hey- I'm not going to complain. They are fun to play with.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I think it tries to do too many things poorly.The campaign was okay after you get the grappling hook.  Before that was awful, as the wall run barely works.The looter part of looter shooter fell flat; it's really difficult to find chests, and normally they just have garbage in them.What did this game in for me was trying some of the extra levels.  They're recycled, more difficult, and still require the bad wall run stuff.  And just like in the main game, if you fall you just die.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: The base game here is fantastic, there is a lot of passion behind it. The game needs a lot of tuning, polish, and some more explanations. The 40k theme is fantastic here, amazing aesthetic and soundtrack. You can easily waste time just looking around the environments. The ways to move around and blast stuff is very satisfying. A good few different guns and ways to customize them to your liking. Long range, close range, melee, and explosive possibilities.Personally, I had no technical issues. FPS was solid with no dips, and no crashes. I have a very overkill PC though, so check other reviews.I only had a few in game glitches. Stuff like enemies not moving, gun sights being misaligned to where the bullets were going, and one soft lock where I got stuck in a wall after using a stim. Playing most of it through on easy, enemies are a very odd difficulty. Either being easy kills or oddly bullet spongy while looking the same or with very minor differences.A few missions in they introduce elemental damage. I still have no idea what elements do. Stats just say they add damage on guns and loot just says resistances? Fire, Electric, Toxic, Radiation. You and the enemies get them. How each interacts with each other, what the different color enemies mean, all never explained. So have fun figuring it out.Finishers / Executions are very jank. In function and gameplay. It wants to be like Doom. There is no way to tell if enemies are open to be finished so you just have to run up and guess. The animations break and just look very rushed. Side missions end the same instant you finish the objective. So you don't get any time to collect loot on more hectic missions. There's really no endgame or worth while loot to chase, no unique / special weapons or armor. There are drip fed upgrades. But you're only going to keep playing this game if you enjoy the action it provides.Why can't we replace the default pistol? It becomes worthless very quickly and wastes a slot. I get it, you use it in finishers and it's the signature gun, but at least let me swap it out with a higher tier one. And finally, you can rename your guns but not your Dog???
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It’s janky, the dialogue can be hard to hear, and I didn’t really pay attention to the plot.  But the enemies aren't sponges and you can fly all over the place.  It’s beautiful, I love it.  Big dumb fun.High quality AA gaming.  If you liked Elderborn, Deathwing, or Serious Sam, you’ll prolly be into this.  Or if you like futuristic hobo death battles.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm keeping my original review below here, but the conclusion of the game was so disappointing that it tipped it over the edge, so I had to change to a thumbs down. The final boss battles were extremely boring and the conclusion of the story was very, very bad. The voice acting, the boring and static cut scenes, the terrible antagonists, a half baked attempt to do some kind of plot twist.. it was just all so bad, it leaves me with a bad taste in my mouth.This gets a passing grade by the skin of its teeth. It's really a mixed bag; gunplay feels solid, levels are pretty cool, the setting is badass. But holy mother of all deities, this inventory UI is so godawful it makes me want to blow my brains out. Also the loot system is really half-assed. Either stick to a streamlined fixed-guns FPS, or make an actual looter shooter that's fun. This here is just a lazy in-between and I can't imagine a soul on the planet liking this. Also the NPC- and enemy models look so bad, with hideously botched faces as if we're back in 2002. Also, the story is poorly written and most of the voice acting is extremely bad. Enemy AI is also often incredibly dumb. So why the hell do I still give it the thumbs up? Well, like I said, shooting these guns feels really good, and that's a pretty damn important thing for a shooter. (get it when it's really, really cheap)
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: You know when someone says something was "not bad", that's what this game is. But take that in the literal sense, because it wasn't a bad game by any stretch, but it wasn't really that good of a game either. I was going to try and write a full on review for it, but basically if you want to shoot things in a 40k setting, go for it (just probably wait until it's on sale for less than $20aud), other than that, everything else is just really mediocre and the overall "Mixed" rating that it has at this time of writing is about what to expect. We really do need a "Neutral" rating on here because that's about where I sit with this tbh. 6/10, had a bit of fun while playing it and the game's kinda cool and looks pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Take on the role of an anonymous mercenary on the most infamous hive city in the entire  universe: Necromunda. A paper-thin story, delivered via some hilariously bad cutscenes, and poorly balanced combat mar an otherwise fun and frantic shooter that has some of the best level design around.  Unbelievably for a game set in a universe that's filled to bursting with lore, there's almost no storyline here. You're thrown straight into the action with no sense of who you are or even why you're doing anything. The story is delivered rapidly in small chunks like it's being fired at you out of a tennis ball launcher. It wasn't until the third mission before I had any idea what was going on. I wouldn't put too much effort into understanding the story because it's just a paper-thin excuse to rack up a higher body count than polio. You were betrayed on a mission that saw your two squadmates killed and you're now out for vengeance (I think). However, you continue working with the guy who sent you on the mission in the beginning, and then it transpires you barely knew your team members that were killed, so your character's motives are completely ridiculous. Oh, there's a side story about an implant you have been given by the guy who set you up, but it doesn't factor into any of the plot other than a passing mention in some of the cutscenes. Speaking of them, they're some of the worst I've ever seen. Most of them have the camera in the wrong location like they've been shot by a bunch of drunk art school students, none of them advances the story one bit. Also, the less said about the truly awful ending, the better. It's obvious that the game isn't relying on its story to encourage the players, so let's look at the gameplay. The game is heavily modelled after  and other old-school FPS games, only not as well polished. It's all geared towards being as fast and as fun as possible. You can double jump, run along walls, and sling yourself around using a grappling hook. There's not a huge variety of guns and you can only have a loadout with four of them; there's a pistol you can't unequip, another pistol slot, and two main weapon slots. The guns are your standard variety of shotgun, assault rifle, heavy and energy weapons on a triple-tiered rarity scale. They can all be modded to quite a high level which ironically makes the rarity levels redundant. It's possible to mod the starting guns to a point where they'll carry you through the entire game. While combat is the main source of fun in , it's also where the game's flaws come to light. They've gone for a style of combat where the objective is to ping yourself around the area as fast as you can, spraying bullets until everything is dead, but the lack of balancing is criminal. At higher difficulty levels, the enemies barely miss, so you'll be reduced to just picking off as many enemies as you can before charging in, which isn't how the devs want the game to be played. The enemies spawn in behind you relentlessly, meaning you'll spend a lot of the battles constantly getting shot in the back. There's a bizarre takedown mechanic that can be done on virtually any similar-sized enemy without a shield (even some bosses!) regardless of their health level. The takedowns take so long to complete and often don't line up properly, so you'll perform a head-chopping animation to someone's knee, only for their head to pop off like a bottle cap. It's also difficult to see what's going on during them, as the camera bobs around like an earthquake has just hit. There is a melee option but you need to buy the upgrades for it, and it's useless, as you move far too quickly to hit anyone and just get picked off. One of the selling points was the inclusion of a dog sidekick, but this suffers from the same lack of polish as the rest of the combat. You summon the dog using a squeaky toy and "summon" is the right word to use there, as he just pops out of thin air next to you. He'll highlight all the enemies in red and attack them. But he can't follow you if you move to a different level so he's only useful if you call him right in the middle of a firefight where the enemy highlight isn't of any use. I went through the game without upgrading any part of the dog because he was just so useless. It's almost as if the dog was added after the game was completed with no testing to see if he worked or not. That's a really common theme throughout . The game has loads of ideas crammed into it, with seemingly no effort put in to make them complement each other. The movement mechanics are designed to keep the game as fast as possible but the goons' aim renders it suicidal to use them. All the guns have rarity levels but the modding makes them pointless. There's a story but it's so thin and the cutscenes so poor that it's incomprehensible. The dog is included to help in fights but it doesn't do much other than get shot at. This is clearly a game that did not undergo a lot of playtesting. The graphics are where  stands out, namely in the level design. This has got to be the best, most authentic representation of a hive city that I've ever seen. The sense of scale is enormous but it doesn't feel deformed as if the levels are big just for the sake of it. The size of everything feels normal with the transport train level being a particular delight. Streum On Studio aren't very good at gameplay mechanics, but they're immensely talented environmental artists. They've got the dirty, gritty aesthetic absolutely perfect. If you're a  fan the visuals are well worth the price of the game alone. There is a lot to explore with treasure chests hidden in loads of little nooks for you to find bonus high-tier loot. The sound and music design are both terrible. Enemies make no real noise moving, meaning you'll only know one is behind when you get shot in the back. The voices don't sync up to the character movements during the cutscenes. The voice acting itself is also dreadful. All the lines are delivered in a dull, monotone that has zero emotion to it at any stage. It's also mixed terribly so that each line sounds like it's being delivered at gunpoint. There's no effort to get any of the conversations to sound natural and the music is as generic a metal-sounding soundtrack as you're likely to hear. It doesn't stand out and you'll barely even notice it. While this is a game with an awful lot of flaws, it is a title with a lot of potential. Many of the flaws can be ironed out with patches, although they will not be able to fix the horrendous storyline. Even as it is, the game is a fun little blast through some of the most detailed and incredible industrial levels you'll ever see. For  fans, this is one of their most iconic worlds made flesh. It's not a perfect game by any means, and it does need some patching, but it is worth the cash if you're looking for a mindless good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those strange, rare body horror gems that people who love Cruelty Squad or E.Y.E. are gonna love. Action packed and pretty disturbing (the physical dog upgrade mechanics are genius),the story is interesting enough but the character design and the voice acting take it to another level.   The upgrades are overwhelming in a good way,lots of stuff do aquire and tons of guns to mod,each having their own branching system for new gun parts. Level design is stellar and everything is detailed down to the tiniest skull rivet or a bullet dangling from a gun. Great game, Def worth the asking price IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely quite disappointing. Necromunda contains the ingredients for a decent action shooter but falls short and fails, primarily due to the abundant technical problems. During the game, I experienced crashing, the HUD would occasionally disappear, enemies and bosses would get stuck in walls, technical performance was underwhelming, spoken dialogue would sometimes be too quiet and would only be decipherable through subtitles etc. Another issue I have is that the game feels like it is lacking a bit of cohesion within the gameplay elements. There's cool ideas like the Mastiff companion, the looter shooter pickups can be fun, there's executions in the style of the modern Doom games, wall-running in the style of Titanfall 2, grading at the end of each level and more. From my experience though, not all of these ideas properly gel together. Some of them feel like they are not implemented purposefully enough, it's what I would describe as design bloat. There are good parts to the game though. The game's art direction helps sell the strengths of the Warhammer 40K universe. There's also a decent soundtrack in here that would certainly appeal to fans of modern Doom. The core gameplay can also have some moments of fun (but to repeat myself, not all of its' elements feel purposefully implemented).With these comparisons to the modern Doom games, I can't help but mention that I've gained a deeper appreciation for them. There's a level of polish that went into those games that makes them the gold standard for PC ports. With Necromunda Hired Gun, it feels like the developers were not given enough time and resources to give the game the care and love it deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a Streumon Studio game. It's janky, but there's a tremendous amount of love and passion put into this game. Anyone with even a fleeting interest in 40K will find this incredibly cool, and the game plays like a slightly less polished DOOM.Streumon once again owns the genre of designing a cool world and then cramming an obscene amount of gameplay features into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: So when I heard this game being described as "A 40k game with the Doom formula", it immediately had my attention. So is that an accurate descroption?...Well....kinda. Here's the breakdown.It's a VERY satisfying 40k based shooter. The atmosphere and theme is perfect, the weapons feel accurate for the most part (esp the bolters), and it actually gives you a different perspective to the 41s millennium than you may be use to. There are no space marines, chaos cults, or any of the other overarching factions you'd usually associate with 40k. There is a single xenos race that appears, but it's very limited. You play as a lowly bounty hunter in the bowls of a hive planet, and the whole game takes place in that context.Now as for the gameplay. Is the Doom comparison accurate?....Sort of. It very clearly draws some inspiration from Doom. It's a face paced shooter with brutal combat where you kind of have to stay moving all while listening to a fantastic heavy metal soundtrack. Thats about where the similarities end tho. The combat is fast paced, but if you're looking for the same blood pumping, raw carnage that you'd get in say Doom Eternal, you're going to be disappointed. You also have bionic abilities that you can unlock and enhance. Oh, and you have a pupper....a MURDER pupper....and you can cybernetically enhance the cyber pupper, but most importantly....you can PET the pupper.Now on to the flaws, because while the game is definitely fun, it has quite a few of them. Most glaringly is the animation quality. The model animations have a tendency to glitch and be really janky, especially during the take downs/glory kills. I don't think I had a single glory kill behave the way it was supposed to. The gore and death animations are also pretty pathetic, enemies are basically bullet sponges that when you finally land the killing shot, whatever part of their body the shot hits basically pops off like a blood filled water ballon.  Also, it didn't happen often, but the game did crash on me a couple times, thankfully not at critical moments. Having the dog is def cool, but the way it was executed feels like it could have been better. There were also some design decisions I found very questionable, like the fact that you can't swap any of your weapons, gear, or even look at your inventory mid mission. You have to choose your loadout at the start and thats pretty much what you're locked into for the mission. THAT I was particularly annoyed by.Overall, the game does have some very clear flaws. and I do think it falls short when it comes to the DOOM comparison, but as a 40k shooter in a time when the quality of a given 40k game is very much a coin toss, I think it still manages to be very enjoyable, and for a fairly reasonable price (If this were a full $60 release, I'd probably be much harsher on it). Worth a try for any 40k fan, def if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's such a shame I have to leave a negative review, but I just cannot recommend this game to anyone, not even on a discount.Being an enthusiastic noob to the world of Warhammer 40K, I was looking forward to this game and bought it instantly when it came out, hoping that it will pull me in more and give a much better sense of how this world works beneath the shiny armor of the space marines and the holy wars. Just to have a feel of living as an average Joe in one of the most famous hive worlds of the Imperium.Well, it suck, that's how it feels.This game wanted be something similar to Borderlands + Doom Eternal + WH 40K + only god knows what else. Instead it became the worst fps game I ever had the misfortune to play.I tried 3 times. 3 times to like this game. I failed...Or perhaps I succeeded not wasting more time of my one and only life on something that clearly was just cobbled together, with no guidelines, no clear vision., if you ever read this... Next time make sure whoever you give the licences to to create something under your IPs, that they are capable of delivering something good. Because this is just a pile of stinking garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: As a Warhammer 40k fan who also played both DOOM and Titanfall, this game is fantastic. I am a simple man, so the whole run-in-a-room-and-kill-everyone-then-move-on-to-the-next, is not a problem, though if you do not like that kind of game, this might not be for you. The stability is pretty good, only had 2 crashes, though none of them happened during a mission, so i guess i was lucky. The frame rate is good, running 75 fps 95% of the time with all options on high. My rig is a 3070, 16 gig ram, i7-7900k clocked to 4.8 GHz. Though in some of the later missions i noticed drops to around 50 fps but was back up to normal in the next room of the mission.In general the game makes you feel like a total badass, the music is great and the gameplay is fast and a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: In advance, note that I am not an existing 40k fan going into this.  So although my experience was rather "meh", perhaps an existing appreciation for the universe would carry an existing fan through.  I got this in a bundle, so it was roughly just a couple dollars when you break it down.  If I paid full price I would probably regret it.  In 8 hours I've finished the game, and maxed out all my character upgrades.  Loot is mostly meaningless-- I finished whole game with just the first new gun I found plus attachments.  Basically every aspect of the game feels like it's missing a bit of polish-- Loot, movement, shooting, cutscenes, dialog, active abilities, economy, enemies, etc.From what I understand the recreation of the 40k enviroments are pretty good though.  So if you just want to explore those a bit, this may work for that.  That said, if you came here looking for a looter shooter, don't bother-- and if you came here looking simply for a run-and-gun shooter, you are better off sticking with DOOM Eternal.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets one thing right, and while its the most important thing, it is ultimately impossible to overcome just how much they did wrong.First, the good: the game play/gun play is awesome.  The guns feel great, the movement is fast and fluid, it runs great.  The shooting and movement, the two most important things, by far, in a fast paced FPS, and they nailed them.  This is how guns and movement in FPS should feel.  If you've ever been turned off by a game because you felt like the guns seemed so weak and underwhelming, you'll enjoy playing with Necromunda's guns; they thump in the best sort of way.  There's some issues with accuracy when aiming down the sites (the game can be waaaaay off), its really not as large an issue as you'd think, because you hip fire at least 70% of the time, and almost never take anything close to a 'sniper' shot (despite the huge levels).  Everything that goes into the power fantasy of being a bad ass, gun blasting, bounty hunter, double jumping, wall running, and grappling hooking across levels while you never stop firing is there in spades.So why the thumbs down? Almost everything else.  The menus and UI look like they didn't have a UI/UX designer on staff, and just had random developers each make one menu - they're awkward to use, have weird and inconsistent keybindings, and are rife with just basic, fundamental design flaws (ie, don't make things that aren't buttons, look like buttons).  These design issues really start to come up in the levels, which are simultaneously impressively huge and detailed, and also so poorly designed that you're barely able to see anything and waste a ton of time exploring dead ends. Basic design mistake #1: creating areas of the level that have no purpose - they have hidden chest to encourage you to hunt around, but the levels are so huge in scale, you inevitably end up trying to go somewhere you're not suppose to and die. Basic design mistake #2: inconsistent/hard to see colorings to mark in game items.  This is really basic game design - you use consistent and unique coloring to make items and parts of the level (ie, climbable ledges) that the player needs/interacts with easy to see.  They just...don't...and you will have trouble spotting basically anything from a distance, including most bad guys.  The dog will mark enemies for you, and you can get some powers that help, but there is really no good substitute for bright, easy to discern, coloring.There's also some bugs and some of the normal, and some acceptable 'double a jank' with things like animations, but the audio is almost inexcusably broken right now.  Music and guns sound ok, but all of the voices in the game are glitched and play at almost an inaudible volume, including in cut scenes.  I'm assuming they'll fix this shortly (they've already patched/improved it once), so I don't really deduct points for this.Ultimately, the game is a lot of fun, as in the game play and movement.  Everything else just hurts the experience.  If you love the source IP, this is a pretty solid game, because the flaws probably won't bug you much, you're here for the warhammer.  If you loved something like Doom 2016, and you already beat Doom Eternal, then I guess this isn't a terrible option - the gameplay is similar enough that if you enjoyed one, you'll probably enjoy the other.  Most other games still occupying this sort of space are retro style shooters, so it being an underserved niche, if this sort of FPS is your jam, you'll probably enjoy it.  Everyone else though, will be turned off by and unwilling to get past the bugs, jank and awkwardness to enjoy the admittedly fun gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, I do. But I can't recommend it to the general community because of how unstable it is. It crashes A LOT. Frequently, it'll crash in the exit menu, basically robbing you of any reward for the mission you just completed.As for the general gameplay, its fun, but it feels like its trying to be DOOM Eternal without understanding what made that game great, so while its combat is enjoyable, it feels like its missing something. Melee is far from satisfying, as you cant really SEE anything that's happening because the animations go by INCREDIBLY quickly while also somehow taking forever. Like the knife throwing execution. the character is moving insanely quickly, but the entire animation takes a solid like three seconds to completely play out and its not guaranteed you'll even be in the right location for it, so you may just see little bits of your arms flailing and the guy randomly die with no real idea of what just happened. most executions lack any feeling of impact as well. Voice acting and sound mixing also leaves something to be desired, but the sound design itself is amazing. It generally works extremely well for the setting.There are dozens of little issues everywhere that don't break the game, but relegate it to a sort of death by a thousand cuts situation. There are too many small issues to try to overlook them. Which is incredibly disappointing for me because I REALLY wanted to love this game, but in its current state, I just can't.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun plays, and feels, like it wishes it was Doom: Eternal. It 'wants' the highspeed gameplay where you're zooming around the map murdering your way through droves of goons and mooks while having to account for the occasional slightly higher-powered Big-Bad, and then an eventual boss battle, but it all just falls flat at times. As a long-time 40k hobbyist and enthusiest for the setting, there is a small essay worth of things I could touch on. But in the interest of making a coherent review that doesn't feel like literal homework, I'll try to keep it brief to the points that will matter to most people. Necromunda: Hired Gun lacks the flow they're clearly trying to copy from Doom:Eternal with its more high-speed arcadey shooter dynamic. You're given a number of re-tries whenever you die in a single mission (essentially extra lives), you can repeat missions for greater loot, and you have a number of abilities you can unlock and then can be accessed on a timer per ability. While a number of these abilities can be fun (thermal vision to spot hidden foes, a super blade that kills things in one hit for a short time, and of course your dog friendo who essentially helps you fight), most of it just doesn't work well in-game. Yes, this game has pretty visuals. the environments have been nailed, and they did a good job of capturing the aesthetic of the gangers in an underhive. That being said, said-gangers only exist to be canon fodder, so if you're expecting deeper stories or intrigue then you're not really going to be getting any of that. Pretty to look at, hollow on the inside. Power-ups, and abilities, feel gutted. Some of them are 'way' more helpful than others, but most of them are largely useless or will simply get you killed because this game does a horrible job of conveying how much damage you've taken before you simply die. Thankfully you can buy up to 3 extra lives per mission, but you'll burn through them almost instantly since you literally rez in the same spot you died. You know... the place 'every' AI just murdered you a minute ago? And they'll start shooting at you nearly instantly as soon as you get back on your feet. So, I hope you can get away, otherwise you'll just die over and over in the same spot. The HUD and user UI is horrible in-game, and VERY un-intuitive. The weapon layout is confusing, and for whatever reason does't allow you to manually map out your guns for your 1-6 basic & pistol weapon slots. Furthermore, if you find a better gun in a mission, it doesn't logically trade out with the gun you're currently holding, and instead you just drop a random weapon. Which means you could easily drop your BEST weapon for some gun that 'looks' useful, only to find out afterwards you traded for literal horse-crap and make your entire mission go from possible to nearly un-playable. I want the enjoy this game, but its not a good game. Its got too many annoying aspects, straight up bad gameplay, and it quickly starts turning into simply a horde-shooter by level 4. I can't in good faith recommend this game to others. The voice acting was fun. And I liked the design of the characters skeletal-looking bionic limbs. Besides that though....5/10
