_childDocuments_.review: This is not a good game.There are two things it gets right - art direction/graphics and music.Everything else is subpar. From best to worst:The movement is pretty fluid and well done. Grappling hook works well, and on High difficulty, you need to keep moving. However, I found that even on hard difficulty, strafing left and right is enough and there's no need to run up walls and perform tricks to survive - and even with investment into the skills, ADADing and shooting the enemy is better.The difficulty jumps dramatically between Normal and Hard. Normal is too easy, Hard is in many places unfair and boring as some enemies become bullet sponges.The UI is very janky. It's apparent in every step. When you're in your home base, where you can't summon your mastiff nor shoot, there are still constant prompts to press the corresponding buttons, even though they don't work. Dialogue menus can't be cycled through using WASD or arrow keys, you must select the dialogue option with the mouse - and yet there is an option (with a constant reminder) that you can press E to actually select the option you're hovering over instead of just clicking it. Your abilities are selected from a wheel - and you must pull it up every time you want to use an ability. There is no selecting an ability and using a shortcut to reuse it - every time you want to reuse it, pull up the wheel and select it mid-combat.Enemy variety is very lacking. There are apparently multiple gangs, but they generally all look the same and behave the same. More on the AI later. The optional mission board shows very many various gangs, and even cults, but you meet almost none of them, they exist only on that screen. It's cool that you can apparently do missions for the local chaos cult, but this has no impact on anything, as far as I can tell. All enemies can be separated into Ranged, Melee, and Big Boys. 70%/25%/5% of enemies, respectively. It hardly matters what weapon they're shooting or how much shield they have - all of them are generally approached the same way. Bosses are without exception boring human-sized people with guns who generally behave the same as any other enemy, but have 20 times more health. A couple endgame bosses behave slightly differently and have some special moves, but this doesn't change the approach to killing them.Many weapons feel good, but most are objectively best and can't be close to competing with others and vise versa. I'm talking outfitted heavy bolter having time-to-kill on a large enemy being 15 seconds of nonstop shooting, while the big Plasma Rifle (which I can't imagine being useful on regular enemies as it has 4 shots that can't even one hit kill many) taking one and a half minutes.The dog is useless. A fully upgraded dog, which costs nearly as much to upgrade as the PC, will inconvenience a single enemy for a few seconds, maybe kill them if you're lucky. In that time, you'll mow down the rest of the room yourself.The story is boring and uninspired. The main character is well-voiced, but has little personality, motivation, or character development. This is true for almost all the characters. Most of the supporting cast help you for no reason. Every time you come back to the main hub, you walk past the same couple of NPCs saying the same exact thing, conveniently related to whatever mission you just did. You have to listen to them repeat the same bit every time you do any optional mission. Half the missions feel like uninspired filler. MINOR SPOILER: As you've seen in the trailer, there are  Similarly, missions seem random and do not progress your goal. The PC's motivation the entire game is to kill a mysterious Silver Talon to collect on a bounty. The bounty is 250,000 credits. All endgame upgrades cost upward of 100,000 each. You gain probably over a million credits chasing this person. You have no other motivation at any point in the game. It's like if instead of looking for Ciri and saving the world, Geralt's grand quest was to kill a drowner that pays 100 orens instead of 20. Despite this, you go on mission after mission to slaughter hundreds upon hundreds of gang grunts. They tried to do an unimaginative twist at the end, but failed utterly - I didn't think "aha, I suspected this!", I thought "Oh. I don't care and never did." The ending has no implications on the world of WH40k, Necrormunda, or even to the main character. The optional missions are bad and janky. When I was deciding on whether to do one, I was never thinking "Am I ready for this?" or "Should I risk it for some extra cash?", I was thinking "Do I really want to invest the time and effort into killing some random dudes for flimsy non-story reasons in the same map I just finished or can I finally move on to the next story mission? There are only  story missions. Most of them are dumb filler. Some parts of missions are dumb filler, such as "There are no enemies in this large room. Run around and find 6 batteries on random shelves to proceed. Found the batteries? Door still won't open, gotta oil it now. Go find the oil button above the door, then come back to the controls and open it again. No enemies or anything this whole time. The jank is apparent in such things as the mission immediately fading to black when completed. No extraction. Example: the optional mission is to kill 20 special enemies. You're thrown into a big room or a piece of a level with infinitely respawning enemies. Some of them are "special". As soon as the final bullet touches the 20th "special" enemy, everyone stops shooting, you stop moving, screen fades to black and says "mission accomplished" and takes you back into the hub. Janky, weird, boring, unfinished.The AI is absolutely broken. I am hardly exaggerating when I say I killed 50% of this game's enemies by standing across a large room and shooting at them with impunity. Other reviewers mention that the AI is janky, but it isn't just that. It's broken. If you're a certain distance from the enemy, they will not notice you even as you shoot them. They won't react, take cover, try to shoot back. This distance is smaller than many larger rooms and long corridors, and the game even has a sniper rifle and a long scope you can fit to any weapon, which achieves magnification that wouldn't be practical at any range short of the range AI don't react to being shot. If an enemy does notice you, they will almost never try to shoot you from far away - they will run straight at you very slowly to get right up in your face to start shooting - even if we're in a large open room. They will queue up to climb ladders to get to you while you shoot them. They will randomly stop shooting. They will not flank you or use any tactics. They will spawn right on top of you, in front of you, and in closed rooms, CONSTANTLY. This is more apparent since your useless dog lets you see through walls and you SEE them spawn. Many MANY times they spawned within a few feet in front of my face.Psyker enemies teleport right on top of you and are immediately vulnerable to finisher, which renders you immune to damage for the duration. You end up killing entire hordes of them by slowly brutalizing them one by one while being riddled with bullets spending 95% of the time in unkillable animation. Conclusion in comments

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of the strangest games I've ever played. Not game play wise but critically, You can almost physically feel the untouched potential emanating from the screen. It's a constant fistful of getting your impression to change between Positive and Negative, like Necromunda could of been great but instead it's just good in certain aspects.The game feels like if Doom Eternal 3-Pump Chumped Borderlands, and then Necromunda came out because Borderlands was convinced not to abort. Then growing up Necromunda tried really hard to lead a promising life.It almost seems as if Streum dumped about 85% of the funding they had into the Level Design team because the environments in this game have plentiful moments of eye candy. Everything else though was told to take a massive hike. The Animation quality is subpar at best, I think the only real interesting animation work that was done with this game were the first-person executions. Other than those gameplay moments the cutscenes feel like 4 minuted baked SFM shorts, and then there are other moments like the load screen in between levels where your character walking is using some sort of Unity animation pack. But then it gets weird because there will be moments of the character interacting with stuff and the animation looks like a guy literally sold his life span for the quality just out of no where.The Gunplay feels really left out on, as if you don't really feel much incentive or reason to swap between guns best suited for comboing or taking down certain enemies. You kind of just find a good gun and stick to that one gun while occasionally swapping to change it up every now and thenThe movement is okayish, I mean it plays like what they tried pulling from Doom Eternal but they kind of rushed the prospect of adding flav to what Doom Eternal squeezed out onto the plate. And now we have really borked wall-runningThe Voice Acting has it's moments, Not much of it occurs but when it does it's a mixed plate of Talent.The Story is mid, It's not great but its passable to just sort of shrug off and not mind to much. It's plot pacing and writing is (to me) most similar to Shadow Warrior in some manner.In short, Cop the game on sale instead. It has its moments but not well enough for $40.00 USD

_childDocuments_.review: It's SO bad. Even with the technical glitches aside. It has the worst gunplay I've experienced in 10 years. You constantly feel like you're wrestling your guns to aim at enemies, fighting your guns to just aim. Weapons feel like they have no punch, except when fired at you of course. Your shield doesn't regenerate and your health only regenerates a tiny bit for a few seconds after taking damage. The atmosphere and environments are AWESOME, best 40k levels I've seen. But literally everything else is trash. I'm SO disappointed I waited to buy this on sale, I should have never bought it. The gun handling is just terrible, the game shouldn't be hard. But it is SO HARD to hit things, no matter how much I mess with my mouse controls, just aiming at a target is nearly impossible. Doom Eternal, Ion Fury, Half Life 2, Call of Duty, Bioshock, Shadow Warrior, the list goes on, virtually EVERYTHING has a better feel to aiming than this. This feels like Surgeon Simulator or Cooking Simulator but for a shooter, that is the ONLY sense of control I can compare this too.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great concept with a great look and combat style, but its essentially a doom clone that is trying too hard in its execution. Until they make some major quality of life and balancing improvements, it will be utter crap. The enemies at all levels seem to have hit scan weapons and seem to know my location perfectly the moment i become known and fire at me despite being several rooms AND WALLS apart. The AI would just follow me and fire in my general direction, funnily shooting flat walls that were in the way.Enemies also seem to spawn merely out of sight, so hiding in a corner and having an enemy spawn in the dead end directly behind you is common. There seems to be stealth elements available, but the AI doesn't seem to acknowledge their use as they always knew my location the moment someone smelled a fart i passed 30 minutes prior.  is great, but needs major polishing work.

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty darn good.  Its got face paced shooting but you can do just as well moving slowly dropping Underhive scum with well placed headshots before they even know you're there.  There are a variety of weapons for your perusal and you can mod scopes, muzzles, stocks, magazines, ect.  Not Escape From Tarkov crazy but similar to the most recent call of duty. The gunplay is decent and feels similar to Doom but with fewer enemies and higher bullet damage.  A couple of downsides are that the dogs movement is slightly jank and the AI is kinda dumb.  Level design is really where this game shines.  So much dystopian grim dark to explore. They also have done a great job making the maps vertical... and the scale....  The UnderHive of a Hive world is dark, grimy, and dangerous but they still do a great job of bring the true awesome scale of a 40k Hive world to the forefront.  The characters are so-so for me so far.  The voice acting ranges from decent to good.  And the plot... meh.  Its okay.  Not particularly bad. _childDocuments_.review: Necromunda Hired Gun rests its foot on the accelerator of dynamism and violence, yet it has an imprecise aim. Many of its problems derive from strictly technical stumbles, some of which can be solved with special updates (such as bugs or application crashes), while others are innate in its playful DNA, and have to do with feedback from the shots almost totally absent, with an artificial intelligence crude beyond belief, and with a general flatness of the shootings. The always timeless charisma of Warhammer takes care of everything, but with a license of this value available, we are convinced that Streum Studio could have done more to honor the Imperium.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: If you know what you're getting into, I can recommend it easily.This isn't a highly polished game, there's a lot of jank (some interaction lag and 'glory' kills come out too fast and blurry, even with motion blur turned off) but here's the thing...It honestly delivers what it promises.First and foremost, if you're a 40k fan, you're already use to dealing with 40k games ranging across the spectrum of great to absolute smoldering slag.  This is a solid 7/10 but if you're a fan, especially of Necromunda you'll just be happy to finally see this place face to face.  The art department here can't be commended enough and the movement is "almost" as great as Titanfall 2's--it can get a little floaty but hard truth, I'd rather that than having cement shoes on.It's a really weird universe we live in when 40k FPS's are super rare and even more weird that good ones are somehow harder to find.  However, this easily hits "top 5 best Warhammer" video games for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: An inexcusably clunky Inventory system prevents it from ever being anything better than a 7/10 FPS, but if you are looking for an immersive Warhammer 40K shooter, then this is it.  For PC, the possibility of patching, upgrades, and DLC content give it some promise.  But if you're looking for Borderlands 3 in the grimdark of the 41st century, then we're going to have to wait until they hire better writers and gun designers.  Still, I'm enjoying this a lot for a fresh release, and look forward to where the devs will take this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid buy, no doubt. It may be arguable if it is worth the 40 dollar asking price, but I definitely think so. If it goes on sale though, it is a definite must buy for shooter fans.Basically this game seems like the developers looked at the DOOM reboots and said: What if Necromunda Warhammer though?And it definitely delivers that. From the visceral combat to the slapping soundtrack and all the flowing mobility with the double jump, dash, and grappling hook. Its fast paced, fairly challenging on harder difficulties, and totes the graphical style to hold up to the Warhammer name. All the environments feel gritty, grimy, and seem to ooze slime along with detail. Definitely not a perfect game, and it's lacking the spit and polish of the DOOM reboots they are so clearly inspired by, but if you liked Id's new DOOM remakes you will almost definitely love this game.Small warning: The game stutters a lot when you first start playing it, no matter what system you play it on. I have it on Xbox Series X as well as PC (3060/5700xt) and both of them stutter pretty hard for the first 2 minutes of gameplay. But once it gets going, this almost completely stops even after loading into new levels.Campaign is pretty short, but there is some good side content and the missions definitely offer replay value. Update: Came back to revisit after my first playthrough, and had to note the really cool new loading screen at the beginning showcasing your character and your cyberdog. Awesome. Oh did I mention you get a cyberdog that you can customize and outfit to look like a pitbull/death machine? Definitely a highlight of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Being a huge fan of both Warhammer 40,000 and FPS, I'm used to disappointing/limited choices when the two are paired. I've played Deathwing extensively and even played the little known game Fire Warrior which will soon pass 20 years (hard to believe)...neither has impressed me.I must say that disappointment has ENDED with this game. It is fabulously executed and tons of fun.As others have noted and you are probably aware, this game is VERY similar to DOOM in pace and gunplay. Your character runs around like he's on crack and there is no "stealth" or walk button to be found. Frankly, I'm surprised you can even crouch in the game to be honest. There is still plenty of cover to use to kill the pace when needed and give your character a much needed break.There's a perfect variety of weapons, not too much and not too little and the gun effects and sounds are great on a good sound system or pair of headphones with satisfying audio that punches through and really gives that impression of hard hitting ballistics. Tons of upgrade options are available for those interested in doing so.Enemies, while not a group of John Wicks, provide a decent challenge, especially on hard and above. The enemy is cunning and It's very easy to get swarmed or shot in the back if you aren't careful.The upgrade system is robust and intuitive, although the buy/sell mechanism can be clunky at times and confusing for new players.Finally...the visuals are stunning on Ultra. I run a 3060 ti, which is MORE THAN ENOUGH for this game, which can be run on much lesser GPUs. I love the little touches such as the animated candle flames on the pause menu. When you look at touches like this, it makes you appreciate the detail put into the game.If there was one thing that bothered me is that you sometimes forget that this is a Warhammer 40,000 game. This can be either a good or bad thing, depending on your view of the universe or your investment in the Warhammer 40,000 universe. This is more likely due to the limited coverage of Hive worlds, lorewise, rather than fault of the game. Nevertheless, you are often reminded of where you are as many buildings, decor, and entities remind you that you are, indeed in the 40k universe. Even at full price, the game is well worth it.If Darktide is anywhere near as good as this, I'll be more than happy to sign up for that one too!In summary...Combat paceGun mechanics and soundVisuals ChallengeReplayabilityEnemy designLevel of detail/nice touchesSometimes does not feel like a Warhammer 40,000 gameCan be a bit confusing in the beginningMenu navigation can be challengingStore/Upgrade mechanics take a bit of getting used toMany have complained about bugs. I've yet to encounter any...

_childDocuments_.review: A solid thumbs up to this game.Did you want to play Vermintide but without coop, with loot you can get during the mission (and is actually rewarding) and guns? This is it.Detailed gun customization straight from Call of Duty, Loot of different quality, Secret chests that do actually take some time to find, Doom-like controls with double jumps, long jump, hook and wall run, no cooldowns so go crazy.Different passive and active skills to purchase for yourself and your dog.Different items to boost your character on top of it.Huge maps where in most cases enemies already present and not just spawn on you out of thin air.Decent graphics for what it is, runs in 1440p in solid 108-120 fps in Ultra. At the very beginning there was some stutter but it might be caching as it was gone afterwards.Sounds could be better, but good enough. Gore is on point, shooting enemies with a shotgun have a solid thump to it with enemies reduced to gibs.It's a Warhammer 40k FPS and without the usual Space Marines, great.After their struggles with Deathwing they finally got it right. Now all they gotta do is follow the Vermintide steps and expand the game.Not an AAA game by any means and it shouldn't be expected.A surprise to be sure, but a welcome one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with a quick answer to a question. Should you buy this game? It depends. If you just want a short single player shooter with little depth, this is probably worth it. If you want a game you can play for hours upon hours, this game is definitely not for you.On release: This game had some performance issues and bugs that got past quality assurance teams. While this isn't necessarily unexpected at this point, certain bugs made me almost have to restart entire levels simply because mission critical doors wouldn't open. Luckily, I managed to use ANOTHER unintended bug to get around that with a bit of effort. Performance wise, I would say the game is a little too intensive on my hardware (my laptop still runs on a GTX 1060). Aside from that, I didn't really have any other problems with quality of the game.Gameplay: The gameplay feels like a slightly slower paced Doom Eternal. The only real difficult I ever encountered was when I had run out of ammo with no way to get more. The constant need to check for all the loot chests did get kind of irritating after a while. The contract system got repetitive after a while and purestrain genestealers were just not a fun enemy to fight. The story missions are the most fun part about the game, though.Story: I wasn't super invested in the story of the campaign, but to be completely honest, that's not what I was playing this game for. Considering its similarity to Doom's gameplay loop, that's not too surprising either.Dog: I thought the dog was neat, but it was very lackluster in gameplay.Overall Score: 6/10, still better than Twilight.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a diamond buried under a 1000 pounds of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Eventually you have to ask yourself how much ♥♥♥♥ you are willing to dig through in order to get this diamond. For me the answer to that question became clear fairly quick.The gunplay is amazing but the game is PLAGUED with issues that hold it back.  Frequent crashes, horrible input processing for controllers that make the game unplayable, extreme difficulty spikes that limit your ability to enjoy the aforementioned gunplay. The world building and lore are interesting but the implementation is so unpolished that the beauty is lost. On a lesser note, the animation quality is noticeably poor for games of the day. This level of jank is unacceptable in a game released this recently, especially one that has been out for more than a year at this point. Do not buy until the reviews get better, you will regret it. ESPECIALLY DO NOT BUY IF YOU PLAN ON PLAYING WITH CONTROLLER.

_childDocuments_.review: I was gonna compare this to E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy and it turns out this is the same developer. You can feel the same brand of weirdness across the board, from player movement to wacky plot delivery to the various game systems. Fortunately none of it is taken to the same level as E.Y.E hahaThe game is a bit buggy - I had to restart one mission because an event didn't properly trigger, and another because I fell through the world. Combat abilities allow you to approach combat in wildly different ways but it takes a bit of grind to afford unlocks so you can't really try stuff out for fun. A refund/respec option would made the game much better imo.Different enemy types fight in unique ways which is quite fun, unfortunately there's only one set of enemies so it does start to get stale after several missions.Weapons aren't very well balanced, it feels like some are just plain better than others. The loot quality system feels frustrating as a result. Oh and the inventory management system is flat out terrible.I really enjoyed combat as a whole (abilities, enemies, etc). Unfortunately it's delivered in a wrapper that feels more like a janky fan mod than a well crafted product. Tentatively recommended but only if you're super interested and it's on sale or in a bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing many great FPS games like Doom, Bulletstorm, Rage, Borderlands this game felt like a low effort cheap product. It is an unsatisfying experience from start to finish. First, let's talk about good things. Graphics look nice and gunplay is good. Weapons are varied, and it's fun to use them. I'm actually surprised about that. These are the only good things about Necromunda. Rest of the game is pure garbage. Sound mixing is horrible. You can't hear the dialogue most of the time. Well, the dialogue is poorly written, so it is not that important I guess. Weapons take too much space. While reloading some weapons take up %50 of your screen and you can't see the enemies because of it. Grenades are useless and splash damage is ridiculous. I wasn't anywhere near the enemy, but I still got damaged by my own grenade. There are suppressors and stealth mechanics in this game but what is the purpose? This is a fastpaced FPS, why would you include a stealth mechanic. It is pretty useless, after you kill one enemy every enemy on the map knows your exact location and starts to bomb rush you. Your dog companion is a missed opportunity just like everything in this game. Level design is so clustered and complicated that most of the time I couldn't understand where I should go. Because %80 of the levels and textures look the same it is pretty easy to get lost. At least they put waypoint beacons, thanks to these beacons navigation becomes easier. Grappling hook sometimes work and sometimes doesn't. Animations are janky. They are janky as sh*t! Watch a cutscene in the game, and you'll understand what I mean. It seems that developers also knew how sh*tty the animations were so they hid them behind a shaky camera. While you are performing a killing animation camera goes ape shi*t and you can't see jack sh*t. It is really nauseating after 2 or 3 animations. Finally let's talk about the most frustrating thing that nearly made me break my keyboard. Infinitely respawning enemies. This trash mechanic doesn't serve any purpose other than slowing the player and interrupting the gameplay flow. Also enemies spawn behind your back without any warning and because of this garbage mechanic you lose health. In Doom, when a demon is about to spawn you have both audio cues and visual cues. In this f*cking game they just spawn and start shooting at you. One time, I killed an enemy and another one popped right on top of the dead one's corpse. F*ck off dude! If you want to play a cheap Doom clone made by talentless hacks Necrosh*t Hired Jank is your game. Just go watch the launch trailer. Even in launch trailer you can't see more than 5 seconds of uninterrupted gameplay. Because devs knew they were releasing a pile of dogsh*t and they tried to hide it as much as possible. If you haven't played Doom, go and play that. If you have played Doom, play again. This game isn't worth the money and isn't worth the time you spent on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers ahead This game started out as a fun little romp though Necromunda, but it rather quickly slid into a short,depressing slap in the face of 40k fans. Not only is the game barely 8 hours in length for the campaign, but the lack of an ending, nausea inducing melee animations, and lack of overall variety in game play styles leads me to believe that there will be an enhanced edition, or massive amounts of payed dlc.   but the rest of the filling of this game is random side missions that are the same 4 variants : defend the area, rescue target, destroy X amount of Y, or Kill Target, all of which is filling reputation bars for the different factions, that do nothing other then give not faction specific weapons. The story over all is near impossible to follow, with cut scenes jumping from one static model to another, before throwing you into a new kill arena, with several of the bosses just teleportation you into there arenas with no explanation  The wall running mechanic is well done, though the lack of open spaces, save for big killing areas, makes it hard to implement it into the style of play the devs intended. I personally just used DOOM 2016 style of go very fast and double jump.  The Sparse amount of weapons in this game, totaling 14 by my count,  has a fair amount of customization, but is mostly cosmetic, the attachments doing barely any noticeable difference. Along with the player customization is abysmal, only allowing for 5 of the same outfit of different colors .I had fun with this game in the beginning, but only 3 levels in, the fun of blasting another ganger in the face with the Emperors blessed bolter, ran dry. I got this game on sale at  $34 US, and its still not worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky and frustrating.  Avoid.Pros:* The shooting is really fast paced and can be fun.* The visuals are great.  It really feels like you're running around the dirty, disgusting underbelly of a giant hive city.* Your dog companion is pretty cool, but until you level him up quite a bit he'll be spending most of his time on cooldown.* The levels are big and have lots of nooks to explore.Cons:* The UI for menu navigation is a hot mess.  Seriously, I haven't seen a UI this poorly designed in about 20 years.* Leveling up is grindy and repetitive.  You'll spend a LOT of time in the same few levels, fighting the same handful of enemies.* Instant melee takedowns are incredibly overpowered.  There's no buildup or weakening required, just get close to an enemy and slap the interact button.  You're invulnerable during the animation and they restore health. You can clear whole levels just zipping from enemy to enemy doing takedowns.* Wall-running is clunky and works inconsistently.I could go on, but honestly the game just isn't worth the time it would take to write up a longer review.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna lie, I definitely understand the criticism this game has received. And for the most part i think it is valid. It's clunky, voice acting is sometimes poorly mixed and overall pretty bland and bad, the fact that there is a loot system makes weapon modding for the most part obsolete and it is all in all rough around the edges. There is no denying that.However i didnt really mind all of this. I personally believe the game is fun to the extend that i can actually look above all of those things. A lot of people call this game a DooM/Titanfall knockoff. And yes, while there are similarities to those games I think the game does one thing better than the others and that is: It works it's mobility in the vertical rather than the horizontal. It offers so many possibilities in terms of mobility: double jump, dash, grappling hook and wall running. You can essentially fly over the map and it's an absolute blast to play for me. Visually it is amazing. Not in terms of graphics. Those are clearly outdated and you can absolutely see where they had to make budget cuts. But the beauty for me lies in the games visual design. While I am not a Warhammer Nerd/Expert I still do appriciate lots of it's designs and details to look at.. And exploring the more or less open world areas can be really fun and rewarding. In terms of story I cant say much. I believe there is one. And it might be even interesting for people who are very deep into the 40k lore. I do not know. But the bad voice acting and writing makes it absolutely forgetable to me. So I cant really tell.Unfortunately what people dont see is the fact that this is the 3rd project of a small french studio called "Streum On Studio". A studio that I wouldnt even consider AA in terms of size and experience. But they make up for it in passion and love for detail. I see that and I appriciate it a lot. And i think that is some of the reason while I can look past the bad. That and the hands done (even tho rough) fun gameplay.Would I recommend the game for full prize? Oof. I honestly dont know. Dont get me wrong, the game is amazing and I love and recommend you play it. But I feel like some of the criticism is valid. And considering that and the lack of polish I personally believe that 40 bucks is a bit overprized. I'd argue that 25-30 would be a solid deal. Note: The devs seem very active and engaged. They've already released 2 major patches adressing some of the issues. (not all of them obviously)

_childDocuments_.review: Separate reviews for 40k fans and non 40k fans with a conclusion for both:For non Warhammer 40k fans: the game starts off feeling a lot like Metro 2033, as you crawl through one sewer grate over ruined building to the next. Combat starts and the heavy metal starts playing and it begins feeling like Doom, as you deliver one takedown after the other, your guns roaring seemingly nonstop. Your characters grim one liners one after the next makes it feel like a Judge Dredd film. All of these together define Warhammer 40,000.For 40k fans: It was fantastic to see a hive city like Necromunda fleshed out. Distant machinery thundering along with leaky pipes miles above in the dome mimicking an artificial thunderstorm was amazing. The game looks great and is constantly reinforced by the sound and feel of the guns, the visuals of the gangs and the 2nd star character (after your dog) the dome runner Jano, being the most believable 40k character in the game. Well done all around. The story however was more of a confusion then the first 12 of Abaddon's black crusades. I would consider myself well read on things Necromunda, even Kal Jerico, But they definitely reached on this one, it was not a smooth transition from one plot point to the next - by Helmawr I have no idea what they were trying to portray with it.Conclusion:My biggest gripe with this game goes along with Necromunda Underhive Wars. Why the ♥♥♥♥ are we only seeing 3 of the 5 main houses of Necromunda? They're mentioned at least, along with a handful of the other factions. Its like leaving 2 main characters out of a story - you're hurting the setting far more than helping. Necromunda is massive - an abundance of factions and foes that you almost can't keep track of in the beginning makes the setting feel massive. Maybe they'll be added DLC like Underhive Wars, but having only 25% of the setting released initially is beginning to drag.Besides a few bugs, slight clunkiness, parts of the story, and some aspects like your dog feeling pointless - the game was solid. Have a few drinks and in a couple of sittings you'll knock the main story out. This game has serious potential if the developers revisit it after the feedback from the release. Future dlc + a few reworks could leave this as one memorable game, standing tall amongst the giants like Dawn of War Dark Crusade.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting is great. The gameplay is fun. The enemy AI leaves a little to be desired. The game is pretty short, and the "endgame" is basically nonexistent. It feels like a solid framework for a much larger game. I envision something like Destiny 2, but across Necromunda (not sure a single bounty hunter story works across the whole of W40k universe where individuals are insignificant and death comes easily), but to achieve something like that, the skills will need to be reworked, the armor and equipment will need a rework as a single piece for your entire armor set kills the "loot chase" for that slot, the way weapons work currently seems fine, but there is too few quality levels (across all items) and too little difference between quality levels and it kills the desire to hunt for +3s. The inventory system is kind of clunky. The game will need multiplayer, at least cooperative, and this will require a larger "hub area". I also think that since each area is loadable at any time anyways by queuing up a bounty, the bounties should NOT load you in and you should be able to walk out of Martyrs End and navigate through areas to the one the bounty is for. Obviously this would include loading screens, so functionally it would be the same as before for area size and processor load/gpu load, but would give the feel of "travelling" across Necromunda, even if often each loading screen is just found at a train station or tunnel that could technically "go anywhere". This would also allow fast travel and a map that could bring Necromunda to life. I feel like this game has the potential to compete with Destiny 2 for online looter shooter, more so than borderlands or any other offering, but a lot of its subsystems would need reworks... and it would have to happen without damaging the current gameplay or aesthetic. Huge potential, fun game, not enough content. I kinda follow a rule that if I can get 1 hour of fun for each dollar I spent, the game is a good game. I spent 33$ and I am to 27 hours of enjoyment so far as I write this, so its close.... really close, but Ive run out of things to do. Would pay monthly easily for an MMO version of this.

It honestly comes across something from the 2006 - 2012 (think something like BulletStorm, but not nearly as smooth as that). The animation is god awful right now. For example, whenever you summon your dog, it literally just spawns next to you like a code command! You could have done something nice with this, like have him jump into frame from behind your character or something! Another example is the "Brutes" (I think they're called that...), they come across as a Unreal engine plug-in /place holders for Orcs, & they just re-skinned them! The moment they start to attack you or try to move around, it becomes blatantly obvious that this was put in in alpha & hasn't been changed since... Oh & "Take-Downs" look awful too. Think Doom, but with the models & camera going nuts.Again, I had fun with this game, but right now it's not worth the 40$. Maybe 20$ at the moment(Give it a year, I feel like most of this jank will be gone by then...). _childDocuments_.review: After 27 hours and all achievements unlocked, I think I can finally drop a review.Hired Gun is a game with real qualities, and real flaws. I'll list them and try to remain as objective as possible. <The qualities (or "good" points)>- a nervous, efficient, fast and brutal gameplay similar to the new DOOM games- slides, double-jumps, grappling hook and wall running work really well- a good level design and a great art direction that depicts the grim, gothic underhive of Necromunda perfectly- different powers available (bullet time, auto-aim, berzerk...)- good feeling with most weapons- great soundtrack that jumps from atmospheric, quiet tracks to raging industrial metal- it respects the original material ; the fans of 40k would appreciate that- you can pet the dog!<The flaws (or "bad" points)>- almost every technical aspect of the game is flawed ; the game suffers from framerate drops, crashes and the optimisation is just not good. From my experience, those crashes tend to occur mostly during loadings, or in menus. It's definitely frustrating. This is *the* main issue of the game.- the game is short if you don't play around and just focus on the campaign.  A shame because the levels are great, and have a real identity. Sometimes you feel that more would be welcome! I definitely wanted more- plasma weapons do not feel very satisfying to use (but at least they do no explode!)- the dog is a skill, not a constant pet. You have to summon the good boy if you want him to help you in combat- the ending is a bit too quick. The final fight is tense, but the ending itself could have been better, more satisfyingDo I recommend it? Well, you probably noticed the blue thumb, so yes I do. Hired Gun is a cool game, especially if you need a quick shot of a fast paced shooter, that takes place in a rather unique setting. The gameplay works fine, no doubt about it. It's intuitive, it's nervous and overhaul fun to play. Also, Streumon being a very small studio, do not expect a triple A DOOM-like. Better know what you buy. Again, in my opinion, the only real problems (and they are, indeed, problems) are the technical aspect. The devs are actively working on fixing the issues, but the risk of crash is present (never experienced any data corruption tho).If it's too much of an issue for you, then I'd definitely recommend to wait a bit, until patches drop. But at the end, I genuinely believe the game is worth it. It just needs to be polished. I hope this review was informative enough and as objective as possible. Yes the game is flawed, but yes it is also fun to  play. And as 40k/Necromunda fan, I've been quite glad to explore this universe once more.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes It's hard being a 40k fan - time after time disappointment after disappointment (see also - Dawn of war 3, Eternal Crusade, Titanicus dominus, Warhammer gladius)This game is something I WANT to love but there's some really serious flaws that really drag this downI've got to give fair credit - the environment is absolutely amazing, they really nailed the aesthetic side of this game, each and every level is a beautiful work of art but then it's all down hill after thatthe sound design is APPALLING - enemies can literally run up behind you with no noise what so ever and there's huge chunks of effects that should be there but simply aren't (huge boulders landing, completely silent lifts etc etc)  - and while the  metal sound track is good I honestly don't think it belongs in a 40k game - NPC dialogue is deadpan with the same lines often repeated over and over again as the enemies charge at you.the "side" missions are just random objectives on maps you've already completed - and they give you a grappling hook that literally is coded to not work on specific sections to stop you from going places - it's also completely possible to just effortlessly walk out of the map (no bugs, just walk across a bridge, round a corner, and you're out)they give you 5 weapons slots but for some reason they lock two of them into being pistols only (on top of a further 3rd mandatory pistol), greatly hampering what would otherwise be some nice weapon variety and I can't fathom why they would do this. The game also heavily advertises your cyber mastiff companion, who is oddly on a cooldown for some inexplicable reason and more often than not gets stuck in places because you as the player are way more mobile than the dog, so you spend more time without him than with.half of the UI functionality is never explained and the PC control are weirdly janky at best (for instance, having to press ESC. to continue???) This was clearly rushed to get it out the door for the yearly skullthrone sale and I really wish the developers weren't pushed into this, because it's clear that love and care went into this game - it just need another 6 months to a year to clear up the jank - I hope the devs can pull a no man's sky with this one - I would love to give this a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t know much of anything about Warhammer 40K. I know there’s a God Emperor, I know there’s Space Marines, Inquisitors, giants and elves and Nergal and whatever other scattershot knowledge comes from a general proximity to nerd spaces and the occasional digital foray into the universe. What I know very well is E.Y.E.: Divine Cybermancy, one of the wildest, jankiest, most fascinating FPS I’ve ever played on the PC. Combine the developers of E.Y.E. with the wealth of 40K’s unknown wonders and the collision results in Necromunda: Hired Gun.	An FPS carrying on some of E.Y.E.’s traditions with RPG systems in the form of gear and optional augmentations (refitted, I should presume, to the Warhammer setting), Necromunda has less of the slapdash construction of its predecessor and much sturdier bones. For example, I didn’t even need to restart once due to becoming utterly lost and feeling as if I had missed something. From the jump I could click with just about all the gameplay concepts presented to me, probably because they read like a greatest hits of the last five years or so of FPS – you’ve got Titanfall’s wall running and grappling hook, NuDoom’s emphasis on aggressive action and even more aggressive guitar riffs, the speed and brutality of the remade Wolfenstein games. If it sounds derivative well, there’s a reason for that, and I don’t know necessarily that it’s more than the sum of its parts but it doesn’t matter much when the sum works out to fast, efficient movement through enemy-infested arenas navigated with a wealth of skills.	The cleanness comes at the expense of some ambition. The same way this feels like a list of “That’s cool, let’s do that” from recent games, E.Y.E. felt like a list of cool things pulled from all sorts of places beyond games, up to and including most of Warhammer’s setting. Which makes for a good fit here, since 40K is so incredibly packed with character it’s hard for a game that does even a passing decent job of capturing the setting to feel thin on the worldbuilding front.	The sense of incredible scale in 40K is what has always appealed most to me and Necromunda, set on one of the universe’s literally unbelievably overpopulated, overindustrialized, hyperdense Hive Worlds is a perfect showcase of that scale. Statues of saints and heroes fill out cavernous rooms and precipitous drops through lattices of rusted, breaking catwalk. Fire spurts into the sky from smokestacks, steam and vapor fill out the narrow passages between towering pipelines, one entire level takes place on the biggest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ train you can imagine. 	For as brilliant as these are aesthetically they lack a bit in design, usually just corridors linking rooms with the occasional inspired verticality, all the better navigated with the grapnel gun provided rather early on. 	What happens inside those spaces makes up for them being gorgeous boxes and tubes. An early tooltip advised me to observe enemies, because they all behave differently. Knowing that E.Y.E. was a game in which foes hurled themselves at me with reckless abandon, I wondered what the interceding years might have taught Streumon Studio. I guess it taught them to fib on loading screens. 	But that’s okay, because foes hurling themselves at me turns out to make Necromunda the great experience that it is. There’s a plethora of ways to dispatch foes – the shooting, of course, with 40K staples like bolters and plasma guns, but also powers granted by augments like Crush that let you move instantly to melee range with a literal bang, or Blast that...you can guess that one, or Perfect Aim which also I guess you can guess these names aren’t exactly clever. I was a big fan of the Strength Booster that handles like a powerup of old, ditching your gun in favor of knife and boot that will kill in two hits if they don’t kill in one.        There’s also a dog you can call in, a beautiful mastiff who perfectly represents what bits of jank do remain in the formula. I’ve seen a lot of folks call this eurojank, the specific kind of held-together-with-spit-and-rubber-bands feeling of staid classics like S.T.A.L.K.E.R. or Gothic or the entire publishing catalog of Focus Home Interactive (ed: guess who published this game)(Brad: I am ed, I have no ed, these reviews would be better if I did alas I must rely on a Bit). But that, to me, speaks to the sort of 7/10 game that is immensely fascinating despite the fact that the game engine is actually just a prayer, half the systems don’t work exactly or at all until a modder finds a .ini tweak six years after release, the animations seem to have forgotten the existence of kneecaps, and if I pick a female character I will be misgendered the entire game.	See, that mastiff is pretty eurojanky, he comes in at the squeeze of a rubber rat and warps around while barking itinerantly and pinning down single enemies at a time and getting in between your bullets and your enemies too often. But that’s pretty much it. There’s some animation snafus, the bossfights are a twitchy slog of occasional instadeath, there was a time I needed to restart a mission because the game kept respawning me out of bounds, you can sort of break progression by grinding side missions for not-that-long to purchase every augment upgrade very early on… 	That’s not a eurojank list of problems, that’s just a regular one. This is an ordinary 7/10 game, the kind of thing people will refer to as a guilty pleasure and I will hiss a little because there is nothing guilty about the pleasure of Crushing a pack of enemies, double jumping up, backdashing out, Blasting four more, and grapelling away to safety before anyone hits you, all while your dog warps desperately to keep up. 	And like, you try to keep up with the story, probably. I suspect that being a Warhammer 40K fairweather fan was not the impediment here, the story is told mostly through disjointed cutscenes that fade to black back and forth between folks in conversation (usually the player character of choice – mine was a cool Asian lady with an utterly baffling accent – and a boss called something like Spite ♥♥♥♥) and chit chats with a few allies in the hub area. It’s very basic stuff, you’re a Hired Gun, which is what it sounds like, chasing after a high value target. Kal Jerico is here, which probably is enough to make some people go “Oooh!” but I went “Huh” at the funny man with little braided hairs, and there’s a late game reveal I figured meant something to someone but when I googled a character’s name the sole result was “Val Kilmer Deus Ex” which, honestly, sums this game up. The review is over, I could have lead with that and gotten the point across. Go home. And play Necromunda: Hired Gun if you want a good-not-great, head empty sort of shooting experience rounded out by a very weird dog.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: it's a linear shooter where you go through levels and shoot everyone in the face. With titanfall/codbo3 movement. Sure, there is rudimentary upgrade system and some resemblance of loot, but it's so simplistic you could ignore it. You ain't looting stuff, you are selling stuff. It looks and sounds as much 40k as possible, it's tries hard to be immersive and true to the source material. And yeah, it's janky as you would expect, it's a budget title from an indie developer.It's also quite fun when it clicks (it often doesn't tho) and it's true to the bone WH40k experience. And what's most important it's not boring like all previous action games in WH40k were cursed to be. It's the first time you got FUN 40k shooter game, you know.People who expect looter shooter would be disappointed - it's all about the money, not the hardware. The whole system designed this way so inventory management doesn't stop the game to a grinding halt when you are on a level - you can swap gun instantly if you found one, but everything else goes to "I'll sort crap out after the level is finished" blackhole. And you can't even take everything to your base, crap gotta be sold if it doesn't fit you pockets. All guns are identical - there is a tier and a type and that's it. The game basically forces you to sell everything and build your own gun instead. You take on a missions, sell crap, get money, buy stuff you need, rinse, repeat. Levels are quite expansive, beautiful, with great lighting and design and are interesting to explore, there is cutscenes and setpieces. Level designers clearly have a raging boner for 40k style. Performance could be better, I guess. And the game is raw, man. Like unfinished raw. Bugs, glitches and all sort of things happen all the time, but nothing game breaking.The game's a must for 40k fans that eager not only to dive into the world and soak in atmosphere, but alo to play at least something fun. And it's somewhat solid recommendation for anyone else - it's still a fun FPS game if you don't expect it to be something that it isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok when it works. As far as Doom clones go, it follows the formula pretty well and I personally really enjoyed the high amount of customization that you had on your guns. Being able to put a scope on a double-barreled shotgun and reconfigure it to make a slug shooting sniper was really entertaining. Unfortunately, there are just way to many issues that can't be ignored. The game is extremely janky and buggy, and also very unpolished; many have discussed gamebreaking bugs before me, but as far as polish goes the "glory kill" animations are messy, enemies will literally spawn in front of you with NO warning what so ever, and the gun play feels... inconsistent. I could list many more.Add on top of this the questionable writing and story and it just doesn't work. I feel like this game could've been really good if they just took time with it and focused on the polish, bug fixing, and presentation rather than trying to add in as many bells and whistles as possible. The customization options and variety of mechanics are fun, sure, but you can't enjoy them when you can't even consistently play the game!Overall, it was a great recipe but didn't get enough time in the oven. As Gordon Ramsay would say, "IT'S ♥♥♥♥♥♥' RAW!" Do yourself a favor and if you are interested, DO NOT buy at full price. Not worth $40.

_childDocuments_.review: ❤️💔🤍🤍🤍The second you get into the game, you’ll know if the game will be playable for you or not. The Field of View (FOV) can cause a massive fisheye effect, making the world look distorted. Simply increasing the FOV doesn’t help either, it just makes the effect even worse. I’m sensitive to narrow FOV as it can make me feel nauseous, but thankfully the default value was okay for me and my screen. Problems with this game continued as I selected my character at the very beginning of the game. After I clicked a few of the portraits, some bug occurred and the portrait on the right suddenly didn’t match my selection on the left, so I had to restart the game. Not great to encounter bugs within the first minute of the game. Before I get into even more of the problems I encountered, I do want to take a moment to appreciate what I liked. The environmental design is great. There’s some good Warhammer 40K visuals, and the larger-than-life architecture of the hive world is portrayed well. There’s also an excessive amount of gore suitable to the grimdark setting. The character design is great. There’s a lot of combat with House Esher, a gang of punk rock Amazonian women that are both pretty and deadly. I also appreciated that this game leaned more towards a classic design philosophy for House Esher (toned waistlines and thin limbs) as opposed to the figurine redesign in 2017. In terms of gameplay, the shooting felt fine. I ended up getting an upgrade that let me slow down time for everyone except myself, so that made the game feel like  on steroids, which I thought was enjoyable. There were quite a few options to choose from, so I’m sure there’s something interesting for different playstyles. The developers tried to incorporate some  movement and also put in a grappling hook for traversal. It works well enough. There’s no fall damage, which was fun even though it got a bit silly at times. Anyway, back to the problems. After playing a couple of missions, I encountered a bug where my weapon just stopped working. I couldn’t shoot, reload or anything, and had to quit to the menu and load the last checkpoint, which fixed the problem at the cost of losing progress.  In a later mission, I had a boss fight where the boss decided to permanently disappear during the boss fight (did he fall through the floor?) and I ended up fighting infinitely spawning enemies and couldn’t progress without restarting the boss fight from the beginning. At one point the game stopped responding when I opened the upgrade screen, so I had to end the process in Windows Task Manager. The second to final boss in the game bugged out during the fight, and ended up just standing still in the middle of the room. In terms of lore, most dialogue is packed full of references to individuals and groups and it’s easy to feel overwhelmed. The game doesn’t do a good job introducing anything beyond just mentioning them.That is, if you can even figure out how to talk to NPCs to begin with. The game claims you’re supposed to walk up to them and press the interaction-key you’ve assigned, but the game seems very specific about when exactly you can do so. For example, the shopkeeper needs to finish her animation when you walk up to her, before you can enter the shopping screen. There’s this important story NPC you have to talk too as well. Every time the game wanted me to talk to him, nothing happened when I tried interacting with him. I had to jump around like an idiot, wiggle back and forth and then suddenly it randomly worked. No idea what was up with that. The inventory system is a mess. It feels very limiting as you are unable to access your inventory unless you’re on the mission preparation screen. It’s needlessly hard to compare items and the UI doesn’t feel streamlined for what it’s trying to do. I had problems finding information about items. In some menus, I’d hover the mouse over them or click on them, but it wouldn’t do anything while in other menus it worked. It felt inconsistent and the information wasn’t readily available when I needed it.  That said, the loot system wasn’t very imaginative to begin with. There’s nothing that modifies the gameplay, only raw numbers that get higher. You either get more health, more armor, or more crit chance. That kind of stuff. Still, if I’m trying to decide if I should sell or keep loot that I find, and I can’t see what I have equipped, well, the UI just isn’t functional. If you don’t care about the game being more than a little broken, and you’re interested in the visuals, theme, and setting, it’s okay enough to give it a playthrough on Easy as a mindless power fantasy, at least for a little while. That said, I’m not sure there’s anything here for anyone but the most hardcore Warhammer 40K fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is trash of the best sort, I loved my time with it.Okay, it ain't trash, there's some great stuff in here (some of the combat, art design, soundtrack and the like) but it's all bogged down by half-baked systems (loot, character progression, faction system WITH TWENTY-ONE FACTIONS IN A LINEAR SHOOTER), clunky and rough animations, total lack of polish, uneven level design (both graphicaly and gameplay-wise, you get lost way more often than you should), uneven gunplay (while janky it feels good most of the time until you get to guns that block your view while reloading or shooting) and absolutely abysmal mishmash of poorly written dialogue and half-edited cutscenes that try their best at storytelling but fail so completely it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ funny.And bugs, tons of bugs. Clipping animations, glory kills that raise you one meter higher with each frame, broken skills and weapons that DELETE your oponents, ragdolls so bad that, when they get timed with the sound just right, produce true comedy gold of the best type. You get the idea. This ain't Cyberpunk's "so bad it's awful" bugs, it's the "so bad it's amazing" variety.And that's pretty much the game in general. For every dull moment, broken mechanic, absurd cutscene there's either some decent gameplay thrown in, or an amazing set piece (they *do* get Warhammer better than most studios do), a truly shocking look at the lore of the setting, or just some great bugs that make every level a unique experience.I enjoyed my time with Hired Gun immensely, either having fun with the game or having fun at the expense of it - But I had fun nonetheless. There's some real passion and idea thrown in here too, can't deny, including cool Warhammer additions (TITAN-CLASS TRAIN WAS METAL AF, I WANT A MODEL).So, yeah, is it a good game? Hell no. But damn me if it ain't one hell of an enjoyable one.Side note: Checked the credits, apparently the game didn't have any designers apart from the Lead Designer?... I guess it may be some nomenculature quirk, but still, case in point: Necromunda: Hired Gun is what you get when you create a game without designers - A broken mess that should be a case study at universities.Did I mention I loved almost every second spent playing it?Amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this brief: The Campaign is too easy, first. There aren't enough weapons, but the weapons that *do* make it in are pretty solid, aside from the fact that the sights don't line up on anything properly. The movement is supposed to give you an edge. It doesn't really. It just gives you vertigo, and the hostiles still hitscan you like no tomorrow. The voice mixing is awful. The dialogue sounds like it was written in french and then dubbed over using machine translation.The plot is paper thin. This is not a Necromunda game, it's a generic shooter story using Necromunda as flavor. The "twists" are contrived and literally don't matter. Don't expect even Doom Eternal levels of storytelling here, this ♥♥♥♥ is yoshi's island. The environments are beautiful. Get your screenshots in the native 75 FOV (seriously who's idea was this?). _childDocuments_.review: As a 40K fan I was ecstatic when I heard about this game, now after playing it even after 4 patches I still can't recommend it. The gameplay is a weird mix of DOOM and Titfanfall 2 but it fails in both departments. I finished Doom 2016, Doom Eternal and Titanfall 2 on the highest difficulty levels (without permadeath) and I had a ♥♥♥♥ ton of fun! It was difficult sure but fun nontheless! Here? Nope... there's nothing fun about it, no matter the difficulty, because the gameplay is an unsatisfying mess that doesn't even know what in the Emperor's name it wants from you. Once you do one or two missions the feeling will creep up on you; that something is off here, that something is wrong, so very wrong. It's the realization that the game's combat simply does not have an idea of it's own identify. It tries to copy other games but it does a poor job at it and it feels like they added stuff that simply shouldn't be in there because it doesn't fit the gameplay at all. It's just Emperor damn awful.The side missions get repetitive fast because the combat isn't fun, the story is almost non-existent, the combat abilities are just there because they sound fun (they aren't) but honestly I see no use for them besides the one where you slow time. The weapons are really nice but the inventory system is annoying and frustrating.The only good thing about the game is the atmosphere and the locations and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ did they do a really good job in making the maps. I love the maps and how big they are, which makes it even more painful that this game is such a mess. It also doesn't help that I've crashed a few times by now (even after all these patches) and my HUD disappeared at one point. That's really just the final nail in the coffin for me.As a 40K fan I really wanted to like, no, to LOVE this game but even the lack of 40K shooters on the market won't make me accept such a half assed, buggy mess. I'm gonna try and finish this game because I wanna see how this will end and I want to see more of the awesome maps but I wouldn't recommend the game just for that.If the devs are listening and plan on making another 40K game my suggestion is to work on the combat, sometimes less is better if it's more defined and aware of what it wants from the player. But keep the map making and atmosphere because those are the game's strongest points so far.

_childDocuments_.review: A janky, but functional fine and beautiful mess of a game.If you can get past the slight issues regarding some awkward animations and some other finnicky bits like the loot system, the gameplay is amazing. Extremely satisfying gunplay, overall great sound design for the weapons, and I cannot explain how much I love the movement.Many people here are saying to just play Doom. Hnestly, I found that dull even on release. I had to force myself to finish it. It was good, but really didn't meet the praise I was given for it.Necromunda, however, is eurojank in the best way. It's just fun.Am I biased? Yes. I played E.Y.E. a decade ago when it first released. I have a huge tolerance for jank, and Streumon studios has a special place it my heart already. _childDocuments_.review: I'll give it a thumbs up because of its great 40k atmosphere with its gorgeous levels, great art design and decent audio. They were onto something with this. Clearly, the intention was to deliver a Doom (2016) style shooter with looting mechanics. Unfortunately, they've stumbled along the way. As authentic as the maze-like levels feel, they don't play well. The developers have great arena shooter movement and gunplay figured out but the combat revolves a lot around navigating complex levels while enemies that randomly spawn around you. Occasionally, you get some Doom-style open arena battles, and the game feels like a blast during those sequences. However, most of the game isn't nearly as exhilarating, a lot of chaotic hyper-fast movement in tight, intertwined corridors. I count these developers among the most promising in the shooter genre. But they've once again fallen victim to their ambition. Once again, they've tried too many things at once, resulting in a game that really doesn't succeed at anything other than atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... a nice game. But know, what you are signing up for.Well, it's a Streum On Studio game, and bears the marks of their previous games as well (EYE Divine Cybermancy, Space Hulk: Deathwing). By this I mean playing the game feels like it was developed by aliens, who themselves never played a video game, but had others describe the experience to them in great detail.If they want to implement something, they just do it, never mind whether it will work out just fine, or not at all. The result is an odd, occasionally frustrating experience with plenty of curios and glimpses of something awesome.The good:- Game (supposedly) looks absolutely beautiful. (I played low graphics, since my PC can't handle more).- Brutal, high-speed combat with plenty of devastating weapons.- Best WH40K FPS game out there.- Great level design (excecution is another matter).- Great style.- Doggo.The bad:- Total lack of balance: so many 1-hitting enemies, brutally strong shields on officers, and ridiculous health-pool of bosses.- Side mission balancing is ridiculous. Got instantly deleted when I first jumped into a B-level (weakest) side mission, had to learn to play entirely differently.- Even though the game tells that enemies shoot inaccurately while you are performing various parkour stunts, they don't really. Got sniped plenty times mid-air while flying on the grappling hook.- Lack of explanations both mechanics and story-wise. If the player is clueless about WH40K at the start, they will be none the wiser at the end. And I'd recommend to open up controls and read up what actions the character can do from there.- Using abilities feel bad. Clunky access, meele mode is utterly useless. No healing for ability kills. Although some of the abilities can be really satisfying. The game can be completed without using the special abilities, though later levels reqire the player to collect items to open up gates, that are hard to find without abilities.- Poor level execution. No clear indication what can be walked on / grappling hooked / wallrun. And falling to the depths is instant death. This makes platforming and high-speed parkour combat really really frustrating.- Most weapons and weapon mods are totally useless. They don't allow for different playstyles, they are the same as others, just worse.The ridiculous:- The game forces the player to keep the starting pistol always equipped, that is the worst weapon of the entire game.- There are enough slots to have every kind weapon in the inventory, but not actually, because for whatever reason, there is one additional slot for heavy weapons and one less of standard ones. Therefore no, you can't actually own all weapons simultaneously. I guess one of the weapons was misclassified, and no-one bothered fixing it. It's feature now.- The game is almost exclusively CQC focused, and most weapons kick like a mule, yet the customization options are full of high-magnification scopes.- Long, drawn-out execution animations are really immersion and pace-breaking.- It takes some time to get used to the immersion breaking grappling hook. It trags the player through walls, ceilings, any sorts of obstacle, like there is nothing in the way.And so on. I'm sure I left something out, but it's plenty as it is.I would not recommed purchasing at full price, but at 50% off, it's a nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun tells a middling story within the walls of Warhammer 40k's infamous hive world.Performance is...a lot like the story. Middling. On a five year old system (i7-6700k, 16gb, MSI 1080) at 1440p I was able to keep a pretty steady 60 frames on Ultra but there are some definite stuttering issues when first loading into maps and before and after cutscenes.The gameplay is, in simplest terms, an arena shooter. For mobility you've got a dash, that can be performed on the ground and in the air, a double jump, wall running, and, after a few missions into the story, a grappling hook. It's all done well enough, there isn't anything spectacular about the motion but the combat is fast and frantic if you engage the enemies. Sitting back and picking them off, in most cases, turns into an infinite loop as most enemies seem to respawn until you pass a certain invisible checkpoint.The weapons are fun but some 40k staples are lacking in the sound department and general feel of the weapon. I expected a bit more percussion and THUD from the bolters while the plasma and lasguns feel okay, again middling.If you aren't a big fan of 40k I would say you can skip it but for someone like myself, that slaves over plastic crack, it's a lot of fun to see things like corpse-starch farms complete with massive, twirling grinders and the other nooks and crannies of Necromunda's hives and domes.

_childDocuments_.review: Can be fun but the jank is real with this one. 10/10 for atmosphere and aesthetics, 4/10 for the story, 7/10 for the gameplay.To break it down, the atmosphere is 100% on-point for Necromunda and 40K in general. Corpse-starch factory with cathedral architecture? A train the size of a modestly-sized suburb? Can't see jack for lack of light? You got it all. The story is... there, for what it's worth. Unsatisfying is the word I'd use to describe it. You can have a story about a bounty hunter and not have everyone a cardboard cutout. To avoid what limited spoilers there are: there's no clear goals for anyone except your character (a fat payday). It's not so much mysterious or incomprehensible as just missing basic elements. They try to wrap things up with a monologue near the end that makes vague allusions but it doesn't pique any further interest. You can't really care about the human equivalent of a bag of potatoes.The gameplay itself is functional and I didn't encounter any particular bugs (so that was a plus) but my main complaints are with it feeling mainly underdeveloped. The mobility system was quite excellent with a grapple and wallrunning, allowing for smooth transition in gunplay. They did remember to add limited auto-aim during wallrunning so it's actually functional in combat. That part feels good, but the rest not so much.Gun customization is limited and there is no good explanation for the different elemental damage types. Why should you care between toxic, radiation, fire, or just basic damage? Was there a bonus damage thing for certain enemy types? All you see is your gun damage numbers go up. There's also zero augment customization, not sure why they list that as a selling point. You just buy them and they're yours forever.Why do I have four slots for armor? I'm only ever going to wear one at a time and there's no benefit to changing between them.Why is my dog appearing out of thin air with no clear cause? They could have added a simple teleportarium effect or had it climb out from behind a corner or something. It's also odd that there's a cooldown timer for the dog. Does he have to go and hide in a corner to lick himself clean every minute or so? That's a dangerous proposition, what with the jaw enhancements.Enemies do hit hard so it is decently difficult. They try to keep you in the fray with a limited period of health regen if you deal damage right after taking some or just letting you auto-kill any normal-sized human with an interact prompt, which also gives health back. The only thing limiting you from meleeing everyone into the floor is a knife cooldown. Knife cooldown - that's another weird thing. That could have been balanced some other way, like witth Doom (2016) where you had to damage them enough before getting your takedown goodie bag.I don't regret getting N:HG (which is why this is positive) but it's not worth full price. As of writing it's half off and I'd say that's fair for what you get. With a decent rework this could be an excellent game but as-is it's a decent one with good atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: A very hard recommendation to give. Honestly most people will be put off with the janky, buggy, rough and terrible sounding game on offer here. The story is a little all over the place with a disappointing ending and side missions exist purely for money making and nothing else. The bugs weren't major but frequent (some of which I was genuinely impressed how they messed it up), fps drops (just little ones) were just as frequent and many moments of AA jank rear their ugly head, sometimes funny and sometimes frustrating, The voice acting is alright. Just alright. When you can hear it over the terrible mixing (devs are trying to fix so that's a plus). The characters don't have enough about them to make you care and the bounty hunter I picked sounded straight from an English Soap Opera (not a compliment). Now, if you are still with me and wondering how I still recommend this thing after that list? It's fun. Super fun. It's a mid tier, b tier, AA shooter with obvious influences from DOOM 2016 and eternal. It's fun to use these ridiculous OTT guns that pop enemies heads off. It's fun to use bionics to turn a couple of enemies into literal puddles of gore. It's fun to wall run and grapple to get cool cinematic kills and search for treasures. It genuinely got me interested in warhammer 40k due to the amazing guns, cool looking characters, interesting sounding factions, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genestealers that spooked the frick outta me and the simply amazing world design.Hired Gun clearly isn't the best looking game ever but people with a lot of love made environments that make you forget that and think it's beautiful... in it's own warhammer 40k way.If you cannot put up with the issues that I front loaded this review with then please dont bother. If it doesn't bother you, you are a 40k fan and/or just wanna shoot some stuff in an enjoyable gory fashion then go for it. I'm glad I did play it and got 100% achievements in my playthrough too.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend that very specific people purchase this game, because it's exactly the game Streumon has wanted to make. If you have a casual interest in Warhammer 40k and want to see a Hive World from the inside or get a way-too-close look at a tech priest, get this game. If you want a well put together shooter with a lot of guns, freedom of movement, and upgrade mechanics, there are already a ton out there that are more polished than this.Necromunda: Hired Gun is not an exceptionally well-made game. The animation is pretty spotty at times, the voice acting is alright, the music is good enough, the plot exists, and the gunplay is fine. It has its share of bugs at the moment (a few days after release,) but I personally haven't run into anything too weird.Edit: After the first patch (when the game version stopped showing .58 and started showing 1.5 on the main menu, not sure if that was just me or everyone,) a lot of the takedown animations look much better and the game seems to run more smoothly.HOWEVER!The sound design is solid, the visuals nail Warhammer 40k, and you can pet the dog. My computer was a pretty good gaming rig six years ago, and it's handling the game on High without issue. If you played Streumon's EYE: Divine Cybermancy years ago and thought "this is just a janky knockoff of Warhammer 40k's universe," this game is just EYE with the Warhammer 40k license and some of the wrinkles smoothed out.I've enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I got this game from the Humble Choice, I gotta admit that I considered buying it even before... and now I'm glad I didn't.So in the very beginning I gotta say that I'm not into the Warhammer universe, even though I played some of the RTS games released in the early 2000s and I really enjoyed them. Necromunda looked like a solid FPS inspired by the newest entries in the Doom franchise, but it turned out to be a mediocre shooter, that tries to be something it's not.So due to the heavily industrial setting it reminded me of Quake, but then it really tries to mimic Doom 2016 and fails miserably at the most important thing making Doom a masterpiece - the gunplay. Even though the weapons' sounds are pretty good, they somehow lack the kick and excellent feeling present in the ID Software's production. Necromunda then adds some RPG elements and treasure hunting to the mix, to reward the player, but in all honesty, with miserable gunplay I could barely feel any difference after upgrading my guns and some of the skills were more of a hindrance than help.Also even though the graphics aren't any great it seems to drop to some pretty low framerate on many configurations. In the very beginning I tought it was a problem with my notebook, as it's got a pretty old by now GTX1660Ti Max-Q, but then I read some comments and it seems that even on some crazy configs it tends to drop frames, so the optimisation is another downside of Necromunda.With the technical problems, a mediocre gameplay and pretty marginal plot added to the slaughter simulator, Necromunda is pretty hard to recommend for the full price therefore I give it a negative rating.
