_childDocuments_.review: Nice little FPS game set in Warhammer universe. Art style, atmosphere and world are great, graphics are also nice and for UE4 game it's pretty optimised and with AA set on high, it was mostly fluid 60fps. Since it is AA game, it sadly doesn't have polish of AAA game and it's not as thought out and bugs drag it all down, making it more like mid-budget Doom Eternal game with how combat tries to be fast paced and fluid, rewarding more agressive gameplay.If you have nothing against lower budget spectrum of games, like Necrovision, you will have good time. In no way it's Doom competitor, but it is ok game for what it is. Grab it on deep sale or in a bundle.Good:- shooting is fun- parkour works ok, but feels rather situational- guns sound good- abilities are useful and easy to use- dog is also pretty useful and helps you find enemies (you also have ability for that, but dog is more useful)- another showcase of how awesome and brutally awesome Warhammer 40K is- Mick Gordon/Andrew Hulshult-spired OST, it is ok for combat noise, but it's not something you will go back toBad:- plot, like in most of those games, is incredibly basic and it's better to pretend it doesn't exist with how cliched it is and how mediocre ending is (although it is nice there is some kind of sequel bait, because I would like second game with more polish)- graphical glitches and bugs, like enemies getting stuck, gun not shooting even when you have ammo or gun not reloading when you have gun- animations can be terrible, like in one mission where you exclusively find "creatures" - they feel unfinished and like some of the frames of animation are missing, because they don't go to you, they are getting pulled towards you like you are some kind of magnet. It feels awkward and they cheapshot you, because that animation skip results in attack- balance feels off. While on normal it's managable and ok, any higher difficulty feels rather cheap, with enemies doing insane amounts of damage (although, just like in many other games, when you get some power ups, game gets easier)- bosses are terrible, have insane amount of health and can take long time to kill, last few bosses have the same exact pattern of crouching in the corner and shooting you, throwing grenade, walking and then crouching, shooting etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I've got not much play time but I've desperately tried to like this game as I'm a big fan of 40k. I even put the game down for over 2 months to see if the dev's would fix some of the issues I have but booting it up again I can see nothing is fixed. This game is awful. At not point should you purchase this game for anything over $20 USD and I still would say that's a hard sell. My biggest complaints with this game are:- Awful animations- Questionable gunplay- downright poorly designed inventory systems- boring plot- BUGS SO MANY BUGS- Poorly designed movement system- Bad user settingsAnimations:Animations in this game are at the level of flash animations from back yonder. During cutscenes characters CANNOT stand still. EVER. They're always moving their arms in jerky movements or during some uncanny valley type of animation. Movements of NPC's during these scenes feel more like animatronics then anything remotely appealing. What makes it stranger is that the animations during combat from NPC's are fine? They're totally acceptable and good. The level I expect from a AA game but then whenever they're not shooting or whacking you with an awesome thunder hammer they revert back to this janky hard to watch style. Gunplay:Most of the guns feel awesome to shoot. Bolters shoot big heavy rounds that make satisfying noises, miniguns sound like miniguns and feel weighty and etc. But the impact of all these weapons? Extremely lacklustre. Now this might overlap a bit with bugs or even go into graphics territory but it is incredibly difficult to determine if an enemy has a shield or not or if you even hit them when they don't have any visible animation to show impact, 0 zero is auditory due to the cacophony of gun fights and no blood is visible because everyone you're fighting is also shooting the lightshoweffects 3000 blaster they picked up from Imperium Walmart just around the pipe bend before coming to kick your guts in. It makes weapons like the plasma gun feel incredibly weak and awful as there is no way to tell if you hit your target and how hard you hit them. That's why guns like the bolter and the gravity gun feel ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. You hit someone once or twice with those? They're dead. And when they die you see an explosion of gore, you hear a scream and you even get a little hitmarker to show u hit them. The lasgun and longlas are also extremely unattractive options to use also due to their need to scope in for extended periods of time to get that gold 1 tap, in a game with a high speed movement system and swarms of enemies to rival a bloody zombie survival shooter. In other words, most of the guns are great but not all guns got the same amount of love for sure.Inventory system:Its bad. You get loot from either killing enemies or finding chests. When you find a new gun it doesnt display anything apart from the name of it, the slot it takes and the keybind to pick it up. But when u pick it up it replaces one of your weapons. SO you have NO IDEA if its BETTER OR NOT. Effectively making loot useless till after a mission (not the end of the world). But, then you have a very limited inventory to manage your loot. You get 4 slots for armour items, 4 for boost object things (they give some buffs), 4 for 2 other things then like 4-6 for your weapon categories? For example; there are 4-5 different heavy weapons. This means you can have all of them and room for a spare but then each weapon might get buffs or attachments that make it better at different things. So the tiny inventory really hurts as a result. And no its not a realism thing because they cant carry that much. Your character can carry tonnes but an extra weapon slot or 2 is too much? And anything that can't fit in your inventory doesn't go to your bank or some other larger inventory, oh no. It gets sold! And whats money for! More guns and upgrades! But there's no inventory upgrade! The inventory system doesn't at all feel tested. The Plot:The plot is boring, I'm not gonna spoil it in case this doesn't convince u this game is bad but the plot is so mind numbing that I put on anything else on youtube to supplement it. It's a poorly veiled excuse to kill bad guys and that's not awful in its self if the gun play was more interesting (see above for why that doesn't save it)Bugs:Bugs plague this game. Bugs that make the game painful and annoying will continue to plague you from your first mission to your last. Whether it's enemies spawning in walls and being able to shoot at you but not vice versa, to plasma gunners of a specific faction being invisible due to a shader error that you can't solve and the dev's still haven't. If you're going to play this game expect a absurd amount of bugs, even for a AA game. They're charging $55 AUD for what acts like a $15-20 AUD game they can't excuse this amount of bugs.Movement system:It is, without a doubt in my mind, tacked on. This movement system is not awful. I think its quite good not Titanfall 2 level but good. The issue comes from how it literally makes 0 difference to the game. The only time you are required to use the movement system (outside of traversing the level in mandatory sections) is when you get swarmed by 3 enemies that cannot be killed in one hit from your gun, so you have to jump up to avoid the pummelling. That's all. The grappling hook is neat and also useful for getting out of trouble but you're more often to use it accidentally thinking the shift key is the dash while in mid air key, then to actually traverse with it. Also who the ♥♥♥♥ puts Ctrl as the dash key? And then makes the rebinding for it also linked to the rebind for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slide? (this is explaining the awful user settings part now) It feels like 0 thought was put into that decision. I did lie a moment before accidentally. There is one weapon strat where the movement system is useful, although still not necessary, and that is thanks to executions. Executions allow you to instantly key any normal sized enemy that doesn't have a shield if you are close enough by simply tapping E. Not only does this make you invincible but it also replenishes portions of your health for each kill you make doing this. This strat completely blows all others out of the park making you unkillable blood leeching demon and rewards you for minimal effort most of the time. Oh and did I forget to mention? The worst animations play during these executions! You'll find your pov warping as you do an extremely flashy but dissatisfying melee kill on an enemy that feels like you just punched a wet pillow.Finally just to finish this rambling up a bit:- I have a high end computer (r3700x and 3070) yet my game looks like complete ♥♥♥♥ imo. I've seen the screenshots and people say it looks beautiful (HELL I've seen gorgeous videos of it on the tube) but for somereason at max settings it looks incredibly dulled and covered in low poly dust. The end result is it looking like PUBG on the lowest settings... that bad.- the set pieces are AMAZING. There are numerous missions where the set of the mission is fantastic and just makes me even more upset when the mission itself is incredibly dull and/or my graphics look so bad it turns this into a playdough art piece. - People seem to be spouting that this game brought an end to the long list of awful 40k games. I'm glad you're enjoying this game but I for the same reasons I wouldn't say a far cry game is a necessarily good game I wouldn't say this one is either even tho I enjoy far cry. This game has such a low level of polish that the price tag feels absurd. Go play Deathwing if you want a 40k shooter thats better than this (but still really not great) or wait for Dark Tide which APPEARS to have more invested developers. - This game reeks GW price gouging- the cyber dog is pointless, its literally just a marketing ploy I'm sorry but they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the dog up tooHope this is helpful. This game was incredibly disappointing, I'm sad its this

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a middle option between like and dislike because I enjoy the game in a "dumb, turn off my brain, oh hey look 40k" kind of way. if you're into 40k and you want a single player FPS in the setting you'll probably like it. it's a perfectly adequate game on its own, but if you're not a 40k fan the game isn't going to do much for youThe story is bare bones and the gameplay is repetitive. there is only one type of level and that level is finish the level as fast as possible as you run through walls of lead and lasers. the levels look like they want to be explored but the game punishes you for exploring because exploring takes time. the level layouts look like they want to allow for multiple playstyles, but because every level is just a "get swarmed" level there's no playstyle beyond full blast pure aggro. _childDocuments_.review: Having played the first few hours of Necromunda: Hired Gun, I can or at least I believe I can present to you all an honest opinion. First, this game is in some ways (gameplay in this instance) similar to DOOM 2016/Eternal. The gunplay and combat requires you to be always on the move, engaging enemies quickly before moving to the next area in succession. Enemy executions like with DOOM are fast, visceral and easily accomplished when in close proximity to enemies. Fortunately, like the aforementioned DOOM franchise, executions provide temporary invincibility during the animations so that at least gives you a few brief moments of respite before going back into the faster paced combat.  Overall gameplay is fast, frantic and enjoyable for any fps player. Now, here comes the opinion of a long time Warhammer fan. This game is honest to god beautiful to look at, it perfectly captures the sheer oppressive atmosphere of a setting this most often relegated to descriptions in the lore. Honestly, this game does that sense urban blight, gothic monstrosity and industrialised hell justice. The term 'feels lived in' is somewhat overdone, but this case the world feels 'over' lived in. There are bones and other remains of the many countless denizens of the Underhive scattered throughout the various environments, areas built upon older structures that are in turn built upon by others. The various areas you traverse are characters themselves, telling of the monumental human suffering and privation that has now become so common throughout the 41st Millennium. The devs have done the 40k/Necromunda setting justice. I look forward to playing through the rest.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's fast, shooty fun set in an impressively well voice acted, aesthetically pleasing world.They got the Warhammer feel right; bleak, hopeless, but still colourful. I've read lots of 40K; including most of the Necromunda books, and this feels like it's set in the same place; good work!The sound design is good, the guns feel like they have impact and the pace of the combat keeps your heart rate up (fast movement, fast kills and fast death; don't stop running and you're in with a chance).And the voice acting! I was pleased to find that all the characters I've encountered so far from the ambient passers by to the main characters, including your own (playing the male, haven't heard the female protagonists voice yet) have excellent voice acting! It makes the setting quite immersive (for a Warhammer fan).Really fun game once you learn how to play it; I recommend it as a fun shooter with an interesting story.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying this game, i am a lifelong Warhammer fan but i have never been into Necromunda games. _childDocuments_.review: I usually wait till I finish a game but wanna get this out before the sale ends for any potential buyers, I was skeptical about this game due to some of the reviews but Im glad I bought it. I think a lot of the negative reviews are mostly players who payed full price and maybe feel it wasnt worth that cost, but on sale for 14$ I think I got a steal of a deal. It reminds me a lot of doom 2016 which I loved. The set pieces are gorgeous, the level design is great, the animations are ok, decent enemy intelligence, the gun play and combat is fun, a lot of player customization both in style and loadouts, some areas which you can be sneaky assassin, and lots of abilities. Im not a huge warhammer fan so Im not sure how accurate it is to lore, and Im listening to the story which has me interested but havent gotten far yet so I cant attest to either of those, but its a game Ill definitely finish and maybe return to every once and a while just for the rust punk aesthetics and fun gameplay. It does have some annoyances, such as looking for mission items, a out of place loot system and some pretty bullet spongey enemies but the game doesnt overstay its welcome and can be finished in about 8-10 hours. Its rough around the edges but underneath that its a gem if you can look past its flaws. I also highly suggest the N7e enhanced graphics HD preset mod at nexus mods which is really easy to install and helps saturate the faded default colors.

_childDocuments_.review: Hired Gun is very reminiscent of Streum's other 40k offering, Deathwing. It does a very good job of capturing the look and feel of the Warhammer 40k setting with its vast maps full of towering gothic structures and industrial grime. The problem, like with Deathwing, is that it drops the ball with everything else. First off, the basic gameplay just isn't very fun. The shooting feels like something out of a recent fallout game, with spongy enemies and guns that make a lot of noise but generally feel like they have very little weight or impact to them. The bullet sponge enemies are a doubly strange design choice considering you can also one-shot most of them by walking up and initiating a very janky melee QTE. It's the worst of both worlds and it sucks. Another odd thing about the game is that it clearly expects you to do a lot of grinding like you're playing borderlands or something. The are a bunch of repeatable side missions you can do to farm currency and build up reputation with different factions, but it's all pointless since there are only about a dozen guns with three tiers of quality, all of which you'll just pick up in the main campaign anyway if you do even a moderate amount of exploration. The faction reputation thing is also strange in that there are no unique rewards for maxing them out, just a bunch of random loot indistinguishable from what you get after a standard mission. It feels like something left over from an earlier, more expansive build of the game that they just left in despite not having the time/money to flesh it out. On a more positive note, the game does have really stellar voice acting, but it's in service to a plot so forgettable that I can barely remember anything about it despite having just completed the game. I really wish these guys the best since they obviously have a lot of creative talent (they also made E.Y.E.) but they need to stick to big ideas/art/aesthetics and hire someone with the appropriate skillset to handle the actual gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute banger of a game that I feel too many people are sleeping on due to the devs' past work being janky at best in the case of E.Y.E and downright bad in the case of Deathwing. Necromunda knocks it out of the park as far as I'm concerned and it achieves everything it sets out to do beautifully.The gunplay is fantastic and I was hard-pressed to find a single weapon that did not feel great to shoot ganger scum with save for a couple. Every trigger pull is responsive and flashy and oozes particles are gore, sound design is top notch.This game's frantic, almost spastic pace combined with it's ruthless difficulty will force you to play by it's rules or die repeatedly. It makes Doom Eternal look like Halo when it comes to the pace and speed of combat. Wallrunning, grappling, sliding and weapon swapping at here in droves and even with the occasional "slow time" when you open your power wheel to fire off one of the half dozen awesome augmetic abilities the combat is fierce and fun from start to finish. Game has a pretty bangin' soundtrack as well, generic heavy metal but it fits the theme.I was skeptical about your robo-dog companion and how a four legged critter would fare against the sheer verticality of Necromunda's maps but the devs remembered they were making a video game and not a walking sim about fungus zombies and emotions and made the canine leap incredible distances and even through floors and walls to rip some thugs throat out. The game is campy and does not take itself too seriously if fun is to be had.All of these abilities and movement and carnage is further improved by a very light looter-shooter addition that never felt overwhelming or tedious. About halfway through the game you've most likely got a few "favorite" guns and can spend a little cash to kit them out to your preference and imo that was perfect. This isnt Borderlands and the minimal stats you must keep track of in game are minor flavor that shouldn't distract you from the game's core elements: combat, environments and enemies.Speaking of levels, these environments are some of the most INCREDIBLE set pieces I've seen in a game. 40k is about mammoth buildings upon gargantuan structures and the devs delivered in droves. Nearly every single level is an enormous semi-open map thats dripping with detail and size, seriously these guys know how to design a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool level, even their older work with E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy was phenomenal.All in all Necromunda is one of the handful of 40k games that, in my opinion, breaks the curse of the franchise and stands out as not only an excellent gem of a 40k game but just a solid and fun 9/10 AA game if I'm being honest. The ONLY thing I can criticize about this game is the story which is a bit thin and not really too high-stakes. You will become somewhat attached to two or three characters but beyond that it takes a backseat to the incredible shooting and awesome maps. Another criticism would be the later levels, despite their beauty, were rather confusing to traverse and made it difficult to find hidden chests or determine where to go to advance but not impossibly so.All in all, go buy the rust-damn game.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Hired Gun is fun and dynamic but suffers from under-explaining its own design philosophy and mechanics. For those expecting deep build-crafting or gun customization, that's not what the game incentivizes. Buy one level in each skill ASAP, bind the skill wheel to something convenient, and you're gonna have a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Plagued with bad balancing and poor deisgn choices.One minutes you'll be rolling over sparsely populated braindead ennemies, then you'll suddenly be swarmed by infinitely spawning waves at such a rate that you'll never even have time to fullfill your objective. Add the most boring type of bulletsponge boss-type ennemy into the mix for an infuriating experience that often feels like you can only burteforce your way on by constantly dying and buying medkits and on the fly...
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game expecting nothing, and I now consider this game to be on par with dawn of war and space marine for the top 40k games. Hired gun makes every weapon fun ( I will say I spent most of my playthrough with the grav gun and grenade launcher because they feel amazing to use.) The game it's self is short but leaves room for updates and possible DLC. My biggest gripe with the game has nothing to do with thee main game itself, (it's just a minor nitpick) but the side "bounty" mission, which are randomly generated on previously played maps. I filled the reputation with the helot chaos cult and the corpse grinder cult, and did not gain any cosmetic changes ( I do not mean a new outfit, but a small change to the character model) to my character. Unlike if you fill out the reputation with the inquisition, which does add a cosmetic change to the character. Other then that I have no major problems with the game, the fact I can even gain reputation with my favorite factions from the tabletop is an amazing feature which I hope is expanded in the future. If you find that Hired Gun is on sale I can not recommend this game more then I already have. This game was an amazing love letter to Necromunda and 40k and it shows. (plus it's amazing game period)
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty good Doom 2016-esque shooter. there is some jankyness when it comes to the totally not-glory kills, but other wise it is a solid shooter with light rpg elements and is honesty far better then i expected, considering WH40k's track record for games. i hope the future of WH40k build upon this
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Jankiest shooter I've played all year.Stiff and stuttery animations, over-cluttered visuals to the point you NEED hud-overlay enemy outlines to be able to see the enemies, story is 'there', dialogue is good on mute, tiered loot (+1% whatever buff), amateurish level design.If you want a good shooter, play Doom.If you want a good 40k themed shooter, play Darktide.Recommended for 5€4/10
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Did not expect to enjoy the game as much as I have so far.Gameplay is a ton of fun, very fast, agile and frantic. Difficulty is challenging but fair.Graphics are great, I'm a fan of the over-use of volumetric lighting. It looks like a mid-2000's era game but drenched in lighting. Artistically, some of the coolest environments I've seen in a game in a long time.Music is fitting and pretty good, sound design is great.Runs great on bottlenecked systems, well optimized with DLSS and works with ultrawide.Story is not that great but it's not a dealbreaker for me.I find most warhammer games pretty meh but this one is honestly worth playing. I've always been interested in budget/AA(?) games and this is not only a good budget game, but a good game.Picked up on a sale for $25 and so far it's worth it to me.Edit: Beat the game and the ending isn't that great however I dont really care as the game itself was fun enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game with fantastic world building. The attention to every little detail in necromunda really blew me away, I didn't expect a doom-style shooter but it was enjoyable nonetheless.Only criticism I have is with regards to the female voice actress for the player character - as I didn't think the voice fit many, if not any, of the characters you have available to play as.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It is good.The fact that this game is compared to DOOM says a lot.But, no, it is not DOOM, it is definitely not as refined, although the devs obviously picked some gameplay ideas out of it like the need to keep fighting to stay alive, glory kills (which are unfortunately a bit too long, too janky, and too shaky cammy to be truly enjoyable), grappling hook and double jump + dash...But it is a power fantasy alright, maybe a bit more so than DOOM because the latter wants to be a puzzle and forces you to play a certain way whereas Hired Gun is pure mindless massacre no matter what you equip or shoot with. You put out your trusty overmodified bolter and never let go of the trigger as you run through all those herectic corpses.It is dumb fun, and it just works. It runs 90fps without noticeable framedrops on my GTX1070 i5 6600k at a bit downscaled 3440*1440 as it renders a detailed set of the Warhammer 40k universe.This is a simple game which reminds me of the good old days of gaming. There is no stealth bs, no grind necessary, no rpg elements to indulge with, no min-maxing, no meta build, no microtransactions, no forced gimmicks.You have a gun, you shoot, you proceed, you unlock more guns as you go, you shoot some more, the story doesn't try to sell you anything, doesn't lecture you on anything, you find secrets, you become so strong that previous bosses are now mob enemies, you keep on shooting, and that's Hired Gun in a nutshell.Keep in mind that this is not a big production so keep some expectations in check. For example, the voice-acting is akin to the kind we had back then on games like Halo 1, Jedi Knight, Star Trek Elite force... the bit cheesy almost always off and out of tempo, be it for story related NPCs in cutscenes or enemies who die like "Oooh... Oh no my head exploded.... Aahhh".As not perfect as it is a good, functionnal unlike most big late releases, Hired Gun's only requirement for its enjoyement is for you to put you brain aside as you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the Doom that tried, but failed.Firstly, the gameplay itself is lacking in balance and innovation. The mechanics feel unpolished and underdeveloped, failing to capture the frenetic, heart-pumping action that made Doom such a hit. The controls can be clunky, making it difficult to execute the moves you need to survive in the game.Moreover, the enemy design and encounters are disappointing. The foes you face are poorly designed, lacking in imagination and creativity. The battles themselves can be frustrating, with enemies that seem to come out of nowhere, making it difficult to plan your strategy and react in time. This can lead to a sense of unfairness and frustration for players.The loot system is another area where this game falls short. It's poorly implemented, with items that seem to be scattered randomly throughout the levels. This makes it difficult to find what you need when you need it, and often feels like an afterthought rather than an integral part of the game.Not worth it's full price, barely worth with 50% discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I will review this game as a positive, with some caveats. If I could vote "neutral" I would. It's barely positive.First and foremost, don't buy it at full price, for the love of god. It's not worth it. I got it for something like 7 dollars off ♥♥♥, and if I'd paid the full $55 AUD for this, I would definitely have reviewed negative. I don't think it's worth that much for the amount of content.So about the game, it's definitely a Streumon game, for better or worse. If you have played Space Hulk: Deathwing, or even E.Y.E. Divine Cybermancy you will feel distinct similarities. Among which, kind of mediocre gunplay, and waves and waves of respawning enemies. It had a couple of buggy moments, but wasn't too bad. The worst was when a Goliath boss jumped and landed through the floor and disappeared, disallowing me from progressing. The whole thing has kind of a low budget feel. It's not terrible, but it could have been a lot richer and greater than it was.Instead of word diarrhoea for more paragraphs, let me break it down into a simple pros vs cons list:PROS:*The environment art is phenomenal. It's really great actually, and really sets the scene and the scale of Necromunda. The lowermost depths of this disgusting Hive City are realised in a faithfully unbelievable way. This is the main PRO here, to be brutally honest.*The guns are conceptually cool. I like being able to have a boltgun or a plasmagun. *I liked the voice acting for the main characters; the bounty hunter, Kal Jerico, Jado.*A couple of missions were quite fun*I really love Warhammer 40,000CONS:*Not enough gun progression. I'm hardly a looter shooter enjoyer, but I found that my guns kind of peaked like halfway through the game, where I had +2 to most weapons I was using, and the +2 long las I was using kind of stayed faithful beyond the period of novelty it provided. I was hoping for a +3 or something but it never arrived.*Not enough factions. There are so many factions in Necromunda, and the game only shows you something like 5 of them, and after a while I got tired of shooting the same Goliaths and Eschers and whatnot. I really hoped to see some Van Saar or Delaques, or Redemptionists or something.*The campaign was quite short. Like 10 hours give or take. For a $50 game I would expect at least 3 times that.*The dog WAS kind of useless after all. I found him kinda handy in the beginning but later on he would just get annihilated in big groups of enemies, and couldn't really do that much to help even if he didn't.*This kind of ties in with earlier CONS but I felt like I'd more or less seen everything the game had to offer (except levels), far earlier than I was done with it. *More ♥♥♥♥ I can't think of anymore, and I'm tired of writing this by now.The main takeaway is that basically, it's kind of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game, but if you like Warhammer 40k like me, you should probably get it (ON SALE), and think of it as a tour of the Necromunda underhive, and just enjoy the art. Like I said, the environments are really cool. Whoever worked on those is holding the rest of this game on their shoulders like Atlas. If this game had been done with a bigger budget, so it could have a better campaign and more depth, it would have been amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, serviceable, worth buying and playing, but don't expect wonders. It's like Budget Doom Eternal a Necromunda setting. Doom set the bar super high tho, so "budget doom" is still good.Gameplay is heavily inspired on Doom reboot and Doom Eternal, with constant movement being the norm rather than finding defensive positions, game also pushes you to be agresive to heal instead of avoiding damage through positioning. Doesn't feel as good as Doom Eternal, but it's still fun. Big drawback is enemy AI. It's bad, which means difficulty comes from overwhelming numbers (of enemies, damage, shields, hp, etc.) and needing certain counters for certain enemies. Fun but gets old.RPG elements are mediocre and easily forgotten. Gun customization is good tho, and it's quite fun to build your guns to your particular taste for your particular strategy. The dog is... optional. Like you can include it in your game or not and it doesn't make that big of a difference.Graphics and sound are good, but unremarkable. Sometimes it's hard to see what's going on, but that's location-specific. Music is good, but not remarkably so. Voice acting is adequate, but not impressive. The story is there I guess.The game is fun. It won't be your favorite, but it's money well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: A run 'n gun FPS set in the dark future of Warhammer 40,000 etc. The vibe and aesthetics are pretty good. The gameplay is like a janky Doom 2016 with less interesting fights and enemies, and introduces some RPG-like loot and leveling mechanics which never feel like the add to the gameplay in any way. It feels like it's on the verge of being good but never gets there.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: OKAYFirst 8.0/10The things that were...bad1. The skin textures were like play-doh and it was somewhat distracting2.  The gameplay flow is essentially that you move to a area and then spend a lot of time bunny hoping/dodging/using powers to avoid depleting your HP pool - you recover HP in 3 ways. FA kits, Doing damage shortly after taking damage, or ressing with a Stimm. The game puts you again a massive amount of foes and often its only a matter of time before your floating around 20 HP and dodging like mad.3. Sometimes the firefights are a bit hard to track...like your blind because of all the lights and smoke and I found this to be the trickiest part of many of the boss battles.4. Overall the main story is about 8-10 hours depending on your level of skill/comfort.5. Some area's are essentially made not traversal even though they should be - like your grapple will not work to latch to area's they don't want you going - luckily that is pretty often not a issue.6. Some of the bigger mobs offset their limited mobility by the devs giving them the ability to burrow/teleport so that they cannot be sniped by a player who is taking advantage of being more mobile then them.The things that were good1. You have a lot of freedom to move and travel - Double jumps/Slides/Grapplegun - in fact you will need to get comfortable with those mechanics as they give you passive "immunity" frames in the form of a %chance to not be hit while doing them - attacks just don't register on you. Same goes for mobs doing combat rolls FYI.2. Guns last a long time - if you find a gun you like you can keep using it - I used a gun from the first mission until I finished the game. You can tweak your weapons to make them better once you find your guns of choice. I was a bit disappointed there were not more gun types - but I suspect they were out of theme (no meltaguns or Las guns except for the Long Las....no needler rifle either!)3. You got a dog you can tweak out - this feature takes some getting used to but in invaluable as your dog can be a good distraction and also detect/give you info about enemy positions and even perform takedowns.4. Aggressive gameplay is rewarded with recovery thansk to a auto-sanguine implant and I recommend upgrading it.5. You can upgrade your baseline stats with gear AND cash by amping up your bionics.6. There is a awesome soundtrack of industrial/metal music (I actually turned DOWN sound effects and music UP which is rare for me...some of the guns are VERY loud)7.Your given a few character options which effects some dialogues and your overall appearance (not that you often see yourself)8. The Story was REALLY well done and fit into the WH40K setting perfectly with a painstaking attention to small details.9. There are side missions you can do for the factions to earn extra money + loot to help you over tough spots by gearing up.10. Later in the game there is a mob that will creep you out - it was very well done....I won't spoil that suprise..Overall if you liked freeform parkour movement like Mirrors Edge/Ghost Runner/Titan Fall 2 your going to be very comfortable in the fire-fights. That said there is a comfy shooter in here. I think just as a shooter it would be a solid 5 - as there is nothing new here; but the combination of parkour mechanics and player progression really pushes this game ahead and with a good storyline and VA work as a cherry on top. If you amped up the textures and added a bit more variety to the upgrades/weapons and made the storyline a bit longer - I could see a 9-10 out of this game to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is an acceptable shooter, and I would say one of the better Warhammer games I have played recently, but that's not saying much given the quality of most Warhammer titles.  I do not have a lot to say about Necromunda really, its a passable game that I enjoyed playing. I would only recommend it if you get it under 20 dollars, I would have a much more negative opinion had I paid full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun rarely transcends what is a boring generic shooter with a fast pace and a nice setting. The story is forgettable and scattershot. Combat fares better, with decent mobility and a capable arsenal. The level design has some large interior spaces, although within them are idiotic enemies that are difficult to locate. Enemies spawn from everywhere and it all makes for some rather clunky action. Although the numerous bionic powers are helpful, they do not elevate the combat. Hired Gun needed to use its setting better and fine-tune its mechanics because even when ignoring its many shortcomings, it does not have enough quality gameplay to earn a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously suffering from the lack of focus.Everything is half-cooked or someone else did it a lot better a long time ago (Bulletstorm, Doom, Metro, Borderlands, Rage)For an action game combat is incredibly boring and the main challenge is actually spotting the enemies.Zero quality of life features (pause, save, buttons serving the same purpose across different menus).Looks like it had a potential to be really good if done in a serious way (metro-style) with tactical and stealth focused combat or in full bullet hell funny style (like, say, Bullestorm or Shadow Warrior).Right now it looks like a marketing team forced  everything that even remotely worked in any successful game of the last 25 years to make the product appealing to everyone.This game is like a balding man in mid-life crisis, sporting leather vests and a motorcycle trying to be "cool".
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Got it for 3 dollars on sale and I'm still disappointed in it. Its just not fun, at all. The 40K themes feel tacked on at best and non-present at worst, the combat flow and gameplay is ripped from DOOM yet somehow downgraded to an absurd level, the sidequests are impossibly hard compared to the main story quests that are piss easy, every level feels and looks exactly the same, the only thing to fight are some indistinct models that feel like gangers from a half-baked Fallout 4 DLC. No Genestealers, no Chaos, no Imperial Guard, nothing you'd expect to see in what is apparently the "BIGGEST Hive City in the Imperium".There are some cute little posters and environmental details, but they feel out of place because nothing involved in the actual gameplay has anything to do with 40K. Like, if this was just a generic post-apocalypse mercenary game, it would be the exact same. Nothing involving 40K matters to this game, its plot, or its themes.I could go on and on about all my nitpicks, but it isn't worth it.Just buy DOOM Eternal. The gameplay is just a flat BETTER version of this, and the art design isn't fighting with the setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired gun----------------------------A fast paced fps set in the warhammer 40k universe.taking place in one of the most famous underhive cities.Necromunda.The game has a "ok" story but the lore and some nice fan service moments when it comes to warhammer 40k. The soundtrack is great the gunplay is fantastic. Its a solid fps game that will give fans of the franchise tons of fun.Sadly there are some issues. Janky animations, Audio bugs and stuttering.Out of those three, audio is the biggest issue. And I hope they fix it.the game is fun. Its awesome to go in guns blazing killing the rival gangs in the world of necromunda.You are a hired gun, you take on bounties and you pet your dog.Have fun !
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a masochistic mess where "side missions" just spit bullet sponge enemies against you constantly, them shooting plasma while you have stubbers and shotguns that take several shots to the face to finish off NPCs. What is the developer's way to counter that? Why of course - parkour. You are supposed to jump from the walls when enemies lose track of you and it somehow improves your aim. I'm not kidding, doing parkour improves your aim. I thought I was a bounty hunter, not an Eldar Harlequin using the Dance of Death.At least Doom Eternal actually gives you *working* weapons and stuff/ This is garbage. I went through few campaign missions (the train one was cool, some very very well done level design, incredible), and now I can't finish side missions as I constantly get overwhelmed by shielded enemies with automatic plasma weapons while I have a shotgun, heavy stubber, an autogun and five grenades. Weapons feel abysmal, weak and ineffective, take too long to reload (your enemies never have to reload anything). You are no Space Marine. Maybe I am supposed to buy some augments, but how I'm going to grind for that as side missions just overwhelm me? Add to it bugs (the tutorial had a bugged door that required me to redo it), parkour (why?) and your dog, a useless gimmick that takes too much time (again) to use and slowly does something (or not) and then of course is on cooldown.The story I've seen so far doesn't have me thrilled too much either. Doom Eternal was fun, this isn't. Even being an avid Warhammer 40k fan that I am, it quickly stops being fun. The train level was good so far. The rest was nothing outstanding. I don't know if I will ever get back to this game, as frankly working on programming complex forms is less frustrating than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: From te beginning I had a feeling that this game is like something I played before... hell it is like many games I have played before, but then around half way it came to me. If you played Soldier of Fortune back in the day, this is it, with a serios face lift both in gameplay and asthetics. Of course the Warhammer 40K world makes it feel different enough but it doesn't change the fact that it is a mindless run and gun adventure. There are 3 things I can write up as an absolute positive: -The gameplay is dumb fun with ridiculous vertical and horizontal movements while spraying lead (and plasma) to everywhere. -The other is the map designs. There are no two completely similar map and the elements they used are astonishingly grandiose. Giant statues, sunken building, mountain high piles of corpses. Everything feels like a race of giants lived here and their world was burried under centuries of filth and rust.-The third is the weapon modifications. You can shape a whole platera of death dealers to your own image which is very nice. Too bad that around half way of the game, you will have a favorite set of weapons and the rest of the game, the loot won't give you any joy. But the interface of the game is anything but user friendly, even in the hub between missions setting up your character is a pain in the butt. Would have been so hard to put in an inventory, really?Other than that the story is in complete shambles, it doesn't make any sense and doesn't do anything to make itself feel like your own. The ending is just as much of a dissapointment as the whole campaign. If they would have spent as much time at the writing table as they did with the level designs, this would have been a 10 out of 10 epic legend.Why am I still recomending the game? I don't know. It made me come back between sessions, but no further than the end of the campaign. Buy it only if it is basically given for free. Anything more than that would be a waste of money.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Has some nice visuals, captures the grim dark feel nicely, the upgrade systems are nice, but even though it has a lot going for i, it still seems to miss the mark on the game play aspect which is a real shame as i was looking forward to this, the voice acting is very weak and the game feels sparse and empty, the Cyber mastiff is nothing more than a novel gimmick more than a tactical game play choice, I feel there is a solid foundation here that could be built on to be a great game, but after only 2 missions in it already became tedious and uninteresting to me, it didn't engage me with story or action sadly.  Hopefully with some updates and fleshing out of content it might get better, but as it stands i can't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: So I picked this game up specifically because of the "mixed reviews". It looked good, and I was wondering why it wasn't at least "mostly good".Come to it, it is actually pretty good!The story isn't groundbreaking. You are a bounty hunter, and you are hunting a bounty. No spoilers there. But the execution is competent. You never feel like you are some cosmic space hero, or suffer from main character syndrome. You are a scummy little bounty hunter, and you are here to collect, and shoot anyone who gets in your way. The mechanical game play is solid. Feels like Warframe and DOOM had a baby and left it in the under-hive. With its focus on speed and hp regen tied to damage output its easy to forget you're not the tankiest MF around. A Space Marine you ain't, and die you will if you try to wade in. The dog is the most unique part. Cool down cyber hound you can modify and sick on enemies or use to escape. YES! The fact that the different tiers of upgrade actually show on the model both in and out of mission were a big win for me. My good-est boy "Commissar Chompers" kept me in line and in the fight. The powers. Honestly I didn't use anything but Loot site until like chapter 8. Honestly its on me for dismissing them as not great because I didn't take the time to play with them, and was just running and gunning. They do however make for some much more powerful game play. They could have used a better tutorial but you don't get any until after that stage. There is an arena ware you could have been told to go after getting the upgrades, and that would have done the game a solid.The progressions is kinda cool, but fell flat with no real reason to push the secondary bounties after you finish your upgrades. The rewards were meh, and by the time you are clearing S ranks, you pretty much won't need anything but the cash reward if you still havn't finished with the Doc. Ware the game shines like the freekin Astronomicon itself is in its level design and set dressings! By the Emperor did this game nail the look and feel! I've played a few 40k games in my time and only the Inquisitor (Martyr in my case) come close to capturing the aesthetic. The metal is bloody  and rusted, the gore is gory, the grim is dark, and the scale is just right to make you feel the weight of the hiveworld above you crushing down on the tiny little human you are. And when it goes creepy, its just enough. Chefs kiss to the level designers. The game does have its flaws. It differently feels like there was meant to be a stealth mechanic that was scrapped. The inclusion of silencers as an option with targeting lights "giving away your position" felt really unnecessary with enemies able to detect you from a pixel in view across the map. The voice actors who were in it gave it their all. But they were in short supply. Really only like 3 actual dialog characters, 3 shop characters, and then anyone not a boss only gets like 2 precious voice lines to repeat, so "Don't make me waste em!" All in all the game was fun. and hit that sweet aesthetic sweet spot I'm always looking for from 40k.Its not super long so give it a play though and just let yourself have fun as a the grimy little gutter skulk with a laz pistol and a cyber dog you know you wanna be!
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with fun mechanics. Mild crashing issues with making a large amount of cybernetic upgrades at once, but otherwise functions well.The side missions vary greatly in difficulty. (I can do S-rank kill the leader but can't do B-rank control the zone missions) but they are still great for money and loot.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: For non 40k fans:Its a slightly janky but fun movement shooter in an interesting setting, with great visuals, atmosphere and soundtrack. Gameplay is pretty fun but the story is mostly forgettable.If wallrunning was like in titanfall and animations were good it could almost pass as a triple-A title. For 40k fans:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHH OH GOD IM COOOOOMIIIING AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game, while flawed, is still a whole helluva lot of fun. You can see, from this version, that with some more development time, and a little bit more polish, that this game has what it takes to really be an excellent addition to the Warhammer 40k universe.  The issues I have with this game are also, for the most part, minor, while the things I love about it, I love a lot, which is why I recommend it. The flaws: The menus. The menus are awful, confusing, hard to navigate, and overall not very user friendly, things like being unable to switch your guns from your preset loadout in a looter-shooter, or being totally locked out of replacing your main pistol, despite being able to get clear and obvious upgrades from said pistol that are just overall better, that you cannot really use because why would you have two pistols equipped when you could have a pistol, a sawed-off shotgun, and an smg, all equipped at the same time? I know I don't want that, I just want to be able to replace the pistol I already have! Next; the animations, you can tell that, despite its flashy graphics, this is, indeed, an indie game, the animations all work, and they're all mostly readable, there's no confusion, but they do look rough, so this is a thing that really just needs more time to flesh it out and make it shine. And lastly: The combat. It's fun, but, it feels a little, ehhh, lackluster. In a fight, I'm pretty much able to walk through the whole squad of enemies and tap E on them, to go into a takedown animation, that makes you invincible, and heals you. I am playing on the 2nd hardest difficulty, as well, so, kinda disappointing that at any time I can switch to "ez mode" where I just bull rush the closest dude, chop his head off, and then do that ad infinitum. I think the staleness of this option is also enhanced by the lackluster animations, because they only look alright, and don't really play up the flashiness that I expect, due to their lack of polish, tho again, since this is an indie game, that just means it needs more time to be worked on, and I doubt it's the fault of the developers.The features: HIGH paced, GRATUITOUS action, almost at the level of the most recent Doom games, nonstop shooting, killing, looting, the guns feel pretty damn good (at least, my favorite shotgun sure does!), the voice acting does convey some really strong emotion, the graphics are killer, and totally fit the idea of necromunda perfectly, and the story, at least so far, has me interested, though how that will continue on, we will see. This section may seem short, especially compared to my lengthy dive into the flaws, but I think that's OK, because  honestly, regardless, and in spite of, the flaws I found with the game, I still think the game is incredibly fun, and overall, amazingly well done for an indie group, and I can't wait to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read this, I *would* recommend this game for people who are big fans of the 40k universe and are just looking for a time sink simply due to the fact that the systems seem mostly accurate.  However to anyone that is slightly less of a fan, or who has never heard of the universe, I would not suggest purchasing the game, and I suspect the latter group is the majority.I wish there were an in between option, but given that there is not, I have given this a non recommendation. This game is something for the killteam players, or anyone that knows more than the idea that there's a hive world in the 40k universe known as Necromunda.That out of the way, the pros:+nice environments, really gets you into the idea of being in the underhive+the customization for weapons is nice+there's an option for an 'old school' difficulty+the game clearly had a lot of soul put into it and I'm sure with continued work it will feel great to play, I hope this will be the casecons-the whole thing feels like a game from a decade ago with new graphics slapped on-the animations are pre 2007 level, go play crysis or gears of war if you don't believe me, I mean just play bulletstorm and you'll get a better experience on that front-the game is very unpolished-grappling hook seems to only hook onto specific areas, and even then sometimes it gets you stuck in geometry-enemies are way way too repetitive, after the 2nd mission I'd already seen pretty much everything, and I was more or less fighting pluralities of the same few enemies over and over, even if there was a little model difference it would be nice-despite being main selling points, there are very few places you can actually wallrun effectively or use your dog, the only time you use the dog is when the mission is essentially already over and the last few enemies broke their ai and can't find you, so you need to bring him out to spot them-the 'glory kills' as you would recognize them from doom, are very janky and unpolished, it feels like the devs were trying to show off their animations rather than keep the fluidity of combat going-for some reason the interaction menus with the barkeep and the questgiver are really janky, you need to twitch around with wasd a lot to get into the right spot where interacting with them will worksubjective cons:-the enemies keep respawning forever, which you can use to farm, but it's really annoying and just depletes the sense of achievement during a mission-the mouse controls feel a bit off, I tried tweaking them as well as I could but they still felt off, as if maybe mouse acceleration was permanently on or something-dodging and crouching should be separate, so that dodging forward is an option at the very least, without it being a slow animation that I have to be careful about activating lest I die in the middle of combat, I'd suggest just removing crouch but it's clear that crouching is integral to a lot of the game accessibility

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun, for all of its faults, offers an experience compelling enough that fast-paced shooter fans will still find enjoyment. There isn't a lot unique about it, but its use of all the aspects that make games like it great works in its favor. There's even a solid audio and visual suite, making its atmosphere one that enhances its world, rather than complementing it. That doesn't fully excuse the abysmal story though, which barely scratches the surface of its source material and leaves you empty by the end credits. Despite this, if you're looking for a fast-paced Warhammer shooter, and are okay with it being rough around the edges, Necromunda: Hired Gun should still offer an enjoyable experience.If you'd like to see the rest of this review and more like it, check out . _childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Necromunda, a planet-sized microcosm of scheming, crime and villainy set within Warhammer 40k universe. Mirroring its galaxy-spanning counterpart, Necromunda is a place of constant turmoil where innumerable gangs struggle for power and riches. One may begin to wonder - how come that Hive Primus, seat of Imperial government, seconds as the greatest centre of illegal activity on the planet? Out of sight, out of mind as they say. Nobles and honest citizens inhabit the highest parts of kilometre-high city-spires, enjoying luxuries such as sunlight, imported food or running water. However, long past the point that sun rays could ever hope to reach there are still kilometres of inhabited industrial patchwork before the bottom. Proper Necromunda begins in so-called underhive, a place where word ‘civilian’ is a figure of speech and gangs run majority of the industry on behest of the noble houses beyond. Long enough the imperial taxes are paid above, the below at large will be left to its own devices. Robust introduction notwithstanding, Necromunda is essentially a separate, roguish setting within WH40k universe and truly a selling point of this high-paced FPS. At least for those familiar with WH40k. As for everyone else, reckon you are here for the “hired gun” part. Waiting ahead is a single-player campaign starring 13 missions of substantial size and length, coupled with side-missions for a quick buck and as much replayability as one desires. Under the circumstances, a hired gun is perhaps the most mundane occupation imaginable within the underhive. What gives the protagonist an edge over the competition, is an extensive set of bionic augmentations. More metal than flesh, you can double-jump, wall run, dash mid-air, use grappling hook and we haven’t even got the upgrades yet. To name a few, they involve shooting lightning out of your arm, bullet time and temporary auto-aim. Ludicrous mobility is extremely useful in Hired Gun’s unusual environment. Most of the areas in the game are surprisingly open, especially vertically, often containing multiple floors of half-derelict urban nightmare to explore; all filled with additional supplies, enemies and an occasional loot chest.Hired gun’s protagonist may very well be a living weapon in their own right, that said, the sizeable arsenal at the player’s disposal is nothing to frown upon. Conventional assortment of shotguns, machineguns and pistols is matched by a choice of futuristic energy-based weapons. Chief among them being the grav gun – firing a homing green bolt that creates a miniature explosion around the killed target. Primary source of the new toys is secret chests hidden within every map. While finding some of them is challenging, the player’s augmented eyes can reveal the treasure’s location through the walls. To keep things varied, every weapon can be customised to better match your playstyle. On that note, a significant amount of scopes and silencers dedicated towards long-range, stealthy engagements which seem for the most part redundant. Given that protagonist’s modus operandi favours blowing a hole in the wall over finding the door, any attempts at stealth would be downright counterproductive. As soon as the mission ends, somewhat abysmal inventory menu appears, allowing the player to decide which equipment they want to keep. You are likely to spent quite a while after the first mission, trying to make some sense of it. All unwanted items are automatically sold, providing the player with credits, spent mostly towards upgrading the bionics of protagonist and his trusty dog companion. Deserving a separate mention is the cyber-mastiff, somewhat oddly summoned via dedicated skill. The hound will fearlessly draw the enemy fire and tear out the throats of the weaker opponents, only to vanish into the grand beyond, until called upon again.Ordinarily, it would stand to reason to cover the enemy variety now. Sadly, it truly takes hours spent in-game to start noticing how much of it there technically is in Hired Gun. Most of the time so much is happening on the screen that if not for the outlines on the enemy silhouettes, one could overlook an enemy standing wide-open 5 meters ahead, let alone identify them. Pragmatic approach divides the unfortunate cannon fodder in the player’s way into gunners, psykers, melee and heavy units. Take note that there are over 10 different types of “gunners”, which frankly doesn’t amount to much. It is one of the game’s aspects which seem to suffer from its neck-breaking pace. Another being Hired Gun’s soundtrack, introducing heavy riffs to spice up the thickest fighting. Regrettably, most of the fights end so abruptly that it rarely has a chance to properly kick into gear. On the sound design note, everyone in Necromunda have a thick british accent, and frankly it fits perfectly into roguish feel of the game.However distinct in terms of setting, when it comes to Hired Gun’s gameplay, at least a broad comparison with the latest DOOM is inevitable. The game at large feels as if the developers at Streum On Studio tried to reinvent the invasion of hell in their own image, while also replacing most of fine-tuning with cocaine. On one hand, the results are mostly fun and adrenaline-inducing, on the other, it would explain why the game breaks so much. To begin with, this title’s movement allows for a much greater freedom than the developers intended. Thinking I might be onto a secret I managed to get out of bounds within the first 5 minutes of play. It didn’t occur a lot, however once you get stuck, the only way out is to load the latest checkpoint. A far greater issue is how unstable the game is overall. Hired Gun crashes a lot, and despite my hardware otherwise running the game smoothly on the highest settings, during my 32 hours of play it crashed around 20 times.Moreover, there are certain design issues too. Hired Gun is only enjoyable on “hard” difficulty setting. It makes the game a true challenge and, more importantly, the increase of the enemy damage successfully makes up for AI shortcomings. When played on normal, only the fiercest barrage can hope to put the protagonist down, as the powerful self-healing abilities remove any necessity to stay ahead of the opposition. The moment a single opponent can put you down with 3 shots, the game suddenly requires a much more thought-out approach. A minor, although frustrating example is the rating given to the player after each mission, specifically the “kill style”. Over the regular course of play rating of “B” is the highest you can hope for, as said statistic takes into account not the kill variety, but headshots and melee assassinations only. Having a break-neck speed FPS favour methodical head-hunt puts the merit of the entire rating system into question.Ultimately, Necromunda: Hired Gun wholeheartedly shares the fate the most of its Warhammer-licensed brethren – it is unremarkable for the wider audiences, yet appealing to the fans of the setting. Whatever potential the action-packed demeanour of Hired Gun may had, it is butchered by its technical difficulties. That said, when it works as intended, this game is a really good time and should satisfy any FPS enthusiast who doesn’t shy away from B-grade titles. Should you happen to enjoy both shooters and WH40k, this one is worth playing for the portrayal of the underhive alone, a decent game it comes with, is a bonus.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty janky version of a 90's run and gun shooter with a loot system and hub/lobby welded onto its side. Missing some game play settings that would help it like ADS sensitivity. Low FOV. Resolution is buggy and can only be changed in windowed mode for some reason. Odd lobby mission selection game play instead of a more fluid approach. Story is meh. Lots of sound issues or missing sound.Loot system is very poor, inventory system is missing. Mods can not be swapped between guns and are not terribly interesting, so no point in stripping guns down. The guns i used were okay standard weapons that can be found in every game, didn't get anything interesting  like las, plasma or bolters before the return window. Loot is gained from random treasure chests you have to hunt  down by sound queues which means you have to turn off music or you wont hear them. You cannot equip your loot after you pick it up, you have to hold e if you want to use it in that mission. The weapon modding is not "Endless weapon and augment customisation", its very bog standard.

_childDocuments_.review: The gunplay feels really fun, but the story is bad ( not really interesting, over way too quick, ending right where it seemed like it might finally get interesting and it is also  completely linear and basically boils down to "go there to get more information that i totally dont already have and just refuse to tell you")The animations are often janky and i've had plenty of times where i used the grapple mechanic only to end up stuck inside of geometry or outside of the map entirely (inside geometry was mostly fixable by grappling again, but outside of the map was usually not).The difficulty hardly seemed to matter when it came to loot quality and quantity, meaning the only thing you'd do by increasing it is fight harder hitting enemies that still fall like flies with any decent weapon (my favorite of which i litteraly bought in the first shop as a +1 and later upgraded to a +2, never saw a +3). I started the game by running through the first map a few times trying to achieve high rating  and ended up with a lot of +2 items that i was basically using until the end of the game, because they were just better than anything i dropped, even though for most of the game i cleared the campaign maps looking for chests and then went back in a 2nd time to actively grab all of them (with a guide if need be, though that was only really neccesary in a few of the early levels where i didnt have my wallhacks upgraded so they'd help me find treasures).The bounties differ vastly in reward, with the bounties with a lot of prize money usually also getting you the most cash from loot, while low bounty missions were just a waste of time for the most part. (Campaign is always low bounty, but that is to be expected). The biggest flaw about the bounty system is the faction reputation that you can increase to get a +3 item, but for me the items i got were always way worse than the ones i got from mission even if the mission items were only +1 versions.Most abilities felt severely unbalanced: Strength augment was really strong damage wise but it would leave you very vulnerable, while crush and blast dealt massive burst damage on low cd and had basically no drawback (these two abilities were strong enough to take out most campaign bosses with a little help from the shockwave to get rid of shields)The Mastif, your pet dog was completely useless, even fully upgraded, only really serving to mark enemies for you, which you could also just do with an ability, that also had the added benefit of guiding you to treasure chests (though if you used anything but iron sights it would render your scope practically unusable, but you could turn it off at will).If you were hoping for a decent looter-shooter then you will be disappointed, but the gunplay feels good enough that i'd say at 50% off this might still be a decent pickup if you like the WH40K universe, primarily the Hive World setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Worth it while on sale.Play on normal. Some enemies are already bullet sponges, playing higher is torture, taking 10+ mags dumped just to kill. Keep your money up with side missions between main missions, this will keep your cybernetics up to date which will keep you at a better level to face off against new enemies. Someone complained about shielded enemies recently, but there is literally an ability that breaks shields instantly. The game isn't that long, and I probably won't play it again, 15-20 hours are probably what you should expect at a slow pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very fun game, but as it is right now, it is too broken to recommend unless you really like the 40k setting and don't mind pushing through some bugs and janky gameplay. It seems like it was rushed to release in time for the SKULLS event, which left a lot of the game feeling unfinished and full of glitches. There's several times in the story where the cutscenes jump around and feel super disjointed. I can think of at least one time where there's 4 characters in the cutscene and it ends super disjointed and all of the sudden your character is fighting the bad guy with no explanation for what's going on. if that wasn't bad enough, the fight feels bad to play since there's fire everywhere and the villain is teleporting around an arena you can barely see in. It's a super cool idea for a fight, but it feels like the developer was coming on a deadline and threw several things at the wall and didn't check to see how anything worked when it stuck. Also noteworthy, the fight broke the game. The game didn't crash, but the player character and the villain both got stuck in place and wouldn't move, no abilities/weapons worked. The music played and I had to restart the mission.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't the most polished, but for its prize and unique setting and gameplay loop I'd say it's quite worth it.There's a couple of accessibility issues to make the game enjoyable but after binding some keys it becomes a lot better.I have a mouse with 2 side buttons which help the keybind issue A LOT, I'd say completely mandatory for how fast the game wants to be.The weapon wheel doesn't have a slowing time effect like DOOM so it's completely useless, so I recommend binding the buttons 1-5 for weapons you like, then have  bound close to WASD so you can always take down an elite shield in 2 buttons with a Pulse into an Execute, then have Grappling Hook and Ability selection on the side buttons.That way you can have the god awful default bindings made for a controller dealt with to enjoy the fast paced action the game is, due to its jank it can be EXTREMELY hard even on normal with sub-optimal setups, but because learning how to play around it's rough edges and finding the best weapons for you I pushed the difficulty up to Oldschool just because it feels like the game was intended to beat your ass like a true Grimdark experience.The setting of Necromunda is absolutely gorgeous in the industrial hellscape design and it has some of the most fun scenarios in an FPS with amazing set pieces like massive trains, Psyker arenas causing Warp anomalies and chase sequences into high action escapes.The game has a grindable side mission table where some of them are really bad, some really quick and some accidental endurance arenas, amazing variety if you want to tinker with the weapon mods and find loadout combos.It's like trying to blend the best parts of DOOM 2016 and Eternal, with the combo gameplay of Eternal while still having the freedom of a factory load of ammunition on your hands if you just want to go balls to the walls with one weapon of your choice.Overall it's not objectively the "best game", but does it have to be? It got me hooked in all it's unfinished and borked glory, just like many cult classics of today.
