_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game so, so bad because it feels like it should be fantastic, but then there's the... everything else. Side missions are one of your primary sources of income but are so poorly designed that it feels like a joke. Enemies endlessly respawn behind you, to your side, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in front of you. Most enemies are squishy as hell and die in a few shots and some have insane health bars, (yellow shield enemies) but also do some of the most insane hit scan damage of any game ever made. You get absolutely turned inside out in this so fast that it makes Blood look like Knack. What it really wants to be is DOOM Eternal meets EYE Divine Cybermancy (cuz these devs made that game) but instead it's like the Mars level from EYE meets DOOM via Roblox total conversion mod.The shooting is fun and the environments are beautiful. Runs really well and is great conceptually. But it often feels like it was made poorly on purpose, as a joke, and because of that I really struggle to recommend it. I may play more and change my review but the frankly OMEGA ♥♥♥♥ balancing has put me off.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: An incomprehensible mess of a casual-tailored looty-shooty from the same people who made the infamous E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy.Pros:+ Sick soundtrack+ Good voice acting+ Very stylish from start to end+ First few missions are actually funCons:- The game falls apart shortly after- Lootboxes suck (strictly only in-game currency but they still suck)- Story is completely incomprehensible- Only full-auto weapons work (forget shotguns/sniper rifles etc)- Weapon customization is basically useless- Bosses are  bullet-spongy- Short campaign (~5 hours maybe?), side missions only to farm money- Weirdest health system to date?- Takedown animations are super slow and berserk mode sucks- Depth of field cannot be disabled (not even via configs)- Just all-around a confusing mess of a game that gets worse and worse- And you get to mutilate your own dog Sadly I am a stranger to the W40k universe. I don't know if it's the lack of background knowledge, poor writing, or both, but this was probably the densest story I have ever played through. Everyone keeps mentioning character names, factions, locations that I have no clue about. Every single mission I was completely lost as to what is happening or why or where I am even going. I played through the full game twice and I retained nothing. I couldn't even remotely recap the story if I tried. I've completed 100%, played all missions twice, maxed out all upgrades long ago, levelled up my character high enough, and have had a solely loot-focused build for ages now. In all that time I had  +3 (max quality) weapon drop. A shotgun. Which I later sold off because it sucked so much it . I'm not even kidding. I did get like six +3 armors though, but of course you can only equip one at a time. So... Yeah. Thankfully no microtransactions in sight but it still sucks so much. First of all, from my experience the only gun that works past the first few missions is whatever has the highest rate of fire with decent damage. The game is very,  fast-paced. Enemies jump, leap, dash, teleport, and unburrow all around you constantly. You absolutely have no time to aim down the sights, ever - let alone go for headshots (let me reiterate, first few missions are way better and this all does work but it falls apart later on). You cannot afford to miss an important shot either. So forget sniper rifles, shotguns, pistols, and any semi-auto rifles. It's all about full-auto rifles and hipfire. Customization is very poor, vast majority of upgrades are basically "better accuracy, worse handling", which means higher accuracy to already accurate weapons at the cost of time to aim down the sights which you never do anyway. It's useless. The default barrel is always the one that has +damage to it so upgrading it for "less damage, more accuracy" is stupid. I want the opposite! Because... The game eventually gives you numerous options to deal with low-tier enemies with ease. Unfortunately a lot of enemies (especially later on) are bullet sponges and despite all the abilities and customization the only method of dealing with them seems to be "just keep shooting lmao". Bosses are so much worse, though. I take my best-upgraded +2 rifles and I swear I sink at least 500+ bullets into each boss, . It's beyond ridiculous. If there is some strategy to defeating them faster well then I 100%'ed the game and I have not figured it out. I started the game on Old School difficulty but the further I went the more broken everything was. Before you say "git gud lmao" it's not a skill issue really, I simply do not understand how the game wants to be played. So you have two ways of regaining health, using medkits (3 per level, no more, cannot be found on maps) and hurting enemies. The rule is: shortly after taking damage, dealing damage back to enemies restores health; the faster you do it and the closer you are to enemies, the more health you get back. It's all very... Finicky and inconsistent to say the least. The issue with higher difficulties is that you take damage way faster than you dish it out. The game encourages you to like jump on a wall and make multiple kills while wallrunning for style points and apparently extra health back? Except wallrun-kills are the last thing you want to attempt to do (you'll probably die before you connect to the wall). For the reference, both wallrun-related achievements have the lowest completion rate on steam. You get 13 story missions that you can get through in maybe 5 hours or so. You also get side missions but those are like mini-arena mode made of pieces of the same campaign levels. They aren't like secondary quests or anything, they're just generated randomly and there is a tiny (often useless) reward for beating a large number of them. They're there to farm money to beat the campaign easier. Anyway from there on all the content you have left is achievement hunting, if you don't care about steam achievements then you have nothing to do. I do care and I've finished everything in 16 hours total. I did not enjoy most of it to be honest. I did it so that you don't have to :p You start with a perfectly normal mastiff, purely of flesh. And then you rip its jaw off to replace it with cybernetics, saw off every limb to replace them with metal rods, and tear out the spinal cord for "upgrading" it as well. All while the game awards you achievements for "improving" your dog. I mean the process itself isn't graphic, you only get a before/after but sheesh it's just disturbing. Couldn't we have an already augmented dog that I would strengthen and improve over time by just replacing the augs? Not tear most of its flesh away piece by piece, ? One weapon upgrade says it "increases armor penetration". By how much? What is "armor" even? Are all enemies considered armored or just some? Is their full body armored or only some hitboxes? The game never tells you. How is "kill style" calculated exactly? I read all of the tests and speculations I could find but rank A is the best I could ever do no matter how hard I've tried, never S even once. What is the magic instakill blade you pull out during berserk mode? Why cannot it be equipped otherwise if you have it on you? Why don't you get a damage reduction or auto-leaps towards enemies during it like every other game has it? Why do you still use your weak knife by triggering a takedown while in berserk? Why do most weapon upgrades focus on accuracy/stability/handling when none of that matters? Why does my fully-upgraded dog kill humans easily but if it engages an enemy dog they both glitch out and do nothing? Why can motion blur be disabled but depth of field cannot? So many questions, so few answers.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: A Doom style game in the Warhammer 40k universe should be a match made in heaven but for Necromunda it just wasn't very enjoyable.The setting of the seedier areas of a hive world is pretty cool and I thought the graphics and visuals look alright but the gameplay itself just wasn't very good.Doom 2016 and Eternal are great because the movement, gunplay, level designs and enemies are all highly polished and complement each other really well. In Necromunda all those elements lack that necessary polish and are less satisfying. The movement I thought was probably the best of these aspects but even then feels a bit too quick and messy and doesnt sync up well with the gunplay. The guns are also more like peashooters which is a let down given the 40k setting. A bolter should just not feel like that.  The whole looter mechanics around weapons and items just feels overly complex and unsatisfying. I would have preferred picking from a smaller pool of weapons that could be levelled and upgraded through the game like in Doom.The enemies AI is pretty braindead but also paired with amazing aim so they just try and crowd you out and then accurately gun you down. That with the subpar shooting just sort of makes combat feel subpar.So given all that I personally wouldn't recommend it. It has the bare bones of a good game somewhere in there but fails to pull it off.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Launched in a rough state, and there's no reason to play it after you're finished. That said, I don't regret seeing it through to the end. Rarely the game froze for a second when I wasn't in danger, but ultimately performance was fine on my PC, and I had all settings max on 4k with motion blur off. Necromunda: Hired Gun is riddled with jank and bugs, though not unplayable for it, and the way you have to fight can start off pretty limiting. The story turns out to be extremely uninteresting by the end, but combat gets decent by the time you don't have to keep abusing executes. The dog is mostly just a cooldown to let you see enemies, he's a bit frail and buggy, and steals kills that you wanted to survive off of. This thing still needs a lot of polish, there is usually always something annoying you or breaking your immersion. Executes making you fly around the room, audio mixing making story characters inaudible, and such. Not deal-breakers if they amuse you, but it's genuinely quite regular.Once I adjusted to all of its issues, I liked the game overall. I was delighted to explore a whole game where every conceivable object is plastered with the Adeptus Mechanicus insignia. Just as with their last 40k game, all of the gameplay issues getting in the way of your enjoyment are still set against the backdrop of an utterly GORGEOUSLY detailed 40k setting.I recommend giving this one a few weeks before buying, because they might patch some of the more glaring problems out. If it gets attention like that? Hell yeah! Pick this up!

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, especially for those who are fans of the Warhammer 40K property and are looking for a FPS. It might have a touch of jank (grappling hook I'm looking at you!) but its more than worth being able to see the vast amazing setting of the Underhive of Necromunda's Hive Cities in first person rather than in miniature, with its massive machines and constantly grinding industry. If I had to compare it to a game I'd say its mostly similar to DOOM (2016) or DOOM Eternal with a kill and stay mobile or risk being pinned down and swiftly killed. I'd say its weak points are its story (which I found a bit nebulous and disconnected) and a lack of variety and visceral feel of the Doom style executions. Augmetic powers and weapons are both pretty good if a bit lacking compared to the massive amount of weapons just used by the Imperium in WH40K Lore. However for the price and on the whole I certainly and whole-heartedly recommend this game to fans of Warhammer and fans of FPSs like DOOM.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game knowing full well that it'd be a mixed bag and it never stopped being one throughout my initial playthrough. I don't want to write a full dissertion about the issues this game faces but I think the most important one is at the core of its upgrade system.What is the point of having a semi-randomized loot system with tiered rarity to items when, ultimately, the biggest different between rarities is a slight damage boost and little else. Yes, you can add charms and trinkets to make your weapon more powerful. Give additional crit chance, chance for an elemental effect, but ultimately none of it FEELS like it matters when those additions barely move the needle. There's little need for nuance or strategy in loadout.They put an emphasis on balancing your stats with the attachments you can choose but there's truthfully only about 3 attachments for each attachment slot with everything else being a cosmetic reskin. Functionally the same.Armors and abilities have even less customization.Outside of weapons, progression is entirely linear and they're all upgraded from the same currency, your money.If you're willing to grind a few hours of the procedurally generated side missions, you'll easily get enough money to max out your character and companion abilities. Then you're just spending money to customize your guns.Very little would be lost if this loot system was replaced with a traditional weapon wheel.All of this is without me diving into the story which is as ignorable as it is forgettable.The inconsistent and nonsensical melee takedown system.The incoherent rating system, specifically in regards to "Kill Style."The controls being extremely busy.Enemies feeling miserable to takedown once you progress past the halfway point in the campaign (trivial once you max out your character and gain the ability to instantly kill enemies en masse).Uninspired boss fights with poorly explained/telegraphed attacks.A generally flat skill curve.The difficulty scale being extremely out of pocket (just play Normal).Armor feeling lackluster and unimpactful.The wallrun and grapple mechanic being often times broken and irregular.Instantly dying if you fell off the map, consuming your limited self-revives for missing a jump.The long, obnoxious animation to summon your assist.Had this game simply been a Doom 2016 style shooter set in the Warhammer universe, that would've been fine. Perfectly acceptable. Instead it tries to play as if its a looter shooter, a boomer shooter with a stylish system a la Devil May Cry, it wants to be so much more but it is woefully underdeveloped.It does some things right like sound, gunplay, and environmental design (aesthetically) but it falls to make a positive or lasting impression.

_childDocuments_.review: There's good things about the game, but there's a lot of bad things as well. For starters: you can just see enemies spawn in front of you and pop into existence before your eyes, and if not, they're popping in super close to you, which can make certain sections pretty bullsiht. Luckily you have some bullsthi of your own, since takedowns are super busted and give you full invincibility and restore some health when completed and you can pretty much spam them on these enemies that spawn around you, with the exception of enemies that have shields, but break those and they can then be instant killed. Unfortunately this is kinda boring, at one point in either mission 3 or 4 I literally spammed it like 30 times in a row and they kept putting enemies there.Also enemies are just kinda running at you, never take cover, and will just hit you instantly as soon as they see you, which at 1st isnt a huge problem because you can use your limited health kits and revives, but at mission 4 at the part where you have to break some robots, there are enemies that 2-3 shot you and have shields, and more of them will spawn very close to you in a very tight area (a literal mine), so dodge spamming without running into more of them at close range and dying is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and takedown spamming for your life is impossible. Long range attacking the robot and disregarding these enemies is also out, stuff is in the way and enemies are spawning and hurting you, plus that aggros them and then you have the same problem because the robots you need to destroy are beefy and you can just kill them and head out because it takes like 4 mags of ammo. When you finish that, a new enemy variant spawns with more enemies and if you die, there's no checkpoint so it's back to doing the robot part you died a ton on already.The player does get a bunch of cool things they can use, but they aren't really explained, I found out later they had individual buttons for them in the options, on bad default keys and had to remap (it was like 9 on the keyboard to the equals sign?). Gigantic cooldowns though, so bionics couldn't be relied upon.The dog is also a dumbass and is mostly useful for giving you maphacks to see where enemies are. You send him out to attack, he insta kills an enemy after grappling it for a second, but then he just runs right back to you and stands near you? Like no, keep attacking what the hell I'm busy shooting. He will just sit there and die while getting beat up by a big guy if you dont tell him to kill things for you constantly, which a lot of the time the game will go nope sorry, can't reach and he just sits there.There's also just like too much weapon customization and a lot of it is rng gated from loot pickups and it's a bit overwhelming so you just go eh screw it most of the time.I didn't play any B missions or A missions or whatever because I just wanted to do the campaign 1st and come back to those, but I hit a wall on mission 4 like I mentioned up there, so I think I have to to grind my gear up, so this game seems to also have grinding.I'm reminded why I don't buy double A or triple A games too much these days after getting this. They're all obsessed with wallrunning too like it's fun, cause it's not, you get magneted to walls all the time on accident in this game. I did enjoy it a bit, but the negatives just outweigh the fun and it made me regret buying it. There's too much to fix with patches, it's not worth it for them to rework, just go play ULTRAKILL or something unless you're a huge 40k nerd.That being said, I'll probably put some more hours into it to see the side missions, but I already bought it and wont/cant refund it, I dont recommend the same.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that needs tempered expectations. You won't find dozens of hours of playtime here. The story isn't good. A lot of the animations are janky. But the shooting is awesome. Your enemies straight up explode. Constantly. It's weird though, because you don't even have to shoot them. You can just use janky takedowns once you're in melee range. There's loot involved, but you can play through the whole game with whatever you want equipped. Guns can be customized and, most importantly, shooting them is a blast. You heal by doing damage, so I just ran around never using cover, all while shooting everything in the face until said face became hamburger. There are only 13 story missions, but side missions pop up infinitely. Those are set in the story mission levels. They mostly involve killing more things. If the idea of wall running, air-dashing above people, all the while riddling them with bullets 'til they pop doesn't sound like fun to you, you won't like this game. It's short, it's not difficult, and it's quite stupid. But I enjoyed the carnage. A dozen hours is more than enough to see everything the game has to offer, but upgrading bionics is solid. As is upgrading your cyborg dog. You can have it kill people. And really, that's what Necromunda: Hired Gun is about. Vicious slaughter. Nothing more, nothing less. No WH40K knowledge is required. Even if you have it, you might not care about the plot or setting. The levels look awesome, though, with detailed, high-res textures and an excellent use of color. It definitely doesn't look like a smaller game on that front. Unless you're looking at the character models. Jank that way lies. Still, I recommend the game. Maybe not for $40, but I had fun. I also like mindless action, though, which is really all it has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Wait for it to go on sale, play it, then move on after you're boredCustomization: The game offers limited customization options with shallow loot variety. Weapon skins lack an editor, which could have enhanced personalization.Combat: Combat is satisfactory and on par with most FPS games. However, the limited ability menu feels clunky and difficult to use effectively.Levels: The levels visually align with the 40K aesthetic, but the platforming can be confusing, and environmental interactions are sparse. More interactive elements and diverse details could enhance immersion.Stability: Performance issues are minimal, but load times can be excessively long.Content: The game provides a short main story of 15 to 20 hours, with repetitive endgame content. After 21 hours of play, side missions felt monotonous, diminishing replay value.Summary: The game is worth playing if it goes on sale, but it’s likely to be a one-time experience unless you have a strong nostalgic attachment.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I am a huge Doom fan - I've played Doom since I was a kid and I played the two recent iterations. I love them and played the crap out of them, even had Doom for switch. So, I'm going to say it now: this is not a Doom clone at all. It does, however, have that zippy boomer shooter feel you get playing games like Quake, Unreal, and (obviously) Doom. It has finishers, but so did Aliens Vs. Predator on Xbox 360 and that predates a lot of comparisons so go figure.What Necromunda: Hired Gun actually is, is a game that builds off the mistakes of games like Space Hulk: Deathwing. Where there were barely any rewards, or only those given via co-op and surviving relentless hordes of Genestealers, Hired Gun is full of worthwhile upgrades and rewards that make things worth grinding for. The light RPG elements are never pointless, the secrets are worthwhile, and like a lot of games of old - changing the difficulty actually nets you additional rewards to match the additional challenge. You can easily get caught up sinking hours into the semi-random side missions and building up faction rep. You are never not rewarded, and its interesting to see how deep the game gets through repeated playthroughs of levels (you can also get rankings that net you even more stuff).Where things felt off in Deathwing when it came to combat, this game is frantic and brimming with player choice. You got a plethora of abilities at your disposal, which all feel very useful, and have their own twists. The gameplay is fast and fun, but difficult to master. You can go in guns blazing or even semi-stealth if you are really that good (and have the appropriate weapon customization). Every gun feels like it should, something I've never got in any W40K game. Finally, every weapon feels like it has weight and packs the appropriate punch. Atop that, you can add anything from Fire, to Static, to Toxic and Nuclear status effects to every shot (cool).Only problem is its a new game and a few issues appear here and there. I've clipped through a wall and the game crashed once. Not a big deal considering even the mighty Doom Eternal gave me even more trouble when I played through it.Check it out, its a worthwhile game for more then just Warhammer 40k fans. And its better then just about any other shooter released in the last few years (aside from the obvious).

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so the first thing you need to know: this game is janky. That's the first impression it gives and something that remains true, though the game fills out and stabilizes after the first mission. And it's textbook Eastern European jank: the writing is terrible, some of the animations are shockingly out of place, the level design is iffy, the controls deviate from what everyone expects. the checkpoint system is punishing, and everything (from the exposition to the time spent in the hub to the missions to the boss fights) takes three times as long as it should. And it's a DOOM. It's not the first thing that comes to mind when I think of the small-unit tactics of Necromunda, but there you have it. It's an old-school run and gun shooter with a few extras tacked on, and "tacked on" is the exact phrase I mean. Some bits, like the grappling hook, are neat, but none of it adds substantively to the core gameplay, instead existing as new varieties of hammers for new kinds of nails. This part is quite good; the fundamental kinetic shooting play is solid, and if you like this sort of game, it's a good one.I don't care for that sort of game. But I DO like Necromunda. And where this game shines is in evoking the atmosphere of Necromunda. This game offers an unflinching tour of a terrible place that feels just right, with all the weirdness, enormity, and casual disregard for human life you'd expect. The environs are frequently legitimately disturbing. The game makes me uncomfortable in a way that I would honestly not expect from a 40K budget title. But there it is. This is a hive world walking simulator that happens to feature a prodigious amount of gunplay. That's the draw. This game evokes the universe spectacularly well in the form of a perfectly serviceable shooter. If you love Necromunda and you care more about atmosphere than actual writing (and this is 40K so I have to assume that's like 95% of us), this game rules. For anyone else, this game is fine, and you should consider picking it up if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the style of the old classic E.Y.E you will absolutely love this. It doesn't have anywhere near the depth and customization but for a quick action shooter-sorta looter this ain't a bad title. Needs polish, for SURE but in its state it is easily playable but don't expect it to be perfect. There are only a few outstanding issues I would say about this, might as well get them out of the way sooner than later!They can use a bit of work. Especially with the pathing. They will get stuck a lot, and the game will hard stutter whenever a new round of enemies comes within play. I also had multiple instances where doing the side missions ended up needing to be re-done/given up due to AI either not spawning, or on one occurrence was just a model that floated around on the last defense wave. I feel like the game knows this though, as it gives you a dog that will give you wallhack (? I know, little weird. Speaking of the dog ♥♥♥♥ was he pretty much useless, besides using the walls when activating it to find the last straggler I never used him. Constantly pressing C on enemies and bringing out the toy to signal him to attack takes a whopping 3+ seconds in all and it just doesn't fit with the pace of the game. Why they made it like that instead of just having the character voiceline it IDK)While searching through chests and killing enemies you will constantly be showered in these "Trinkets" or "Charms" that you can attach to your weapon or onto your character for a little extra boost. When I say little I mean it. At first I thought the game wanted me to hang onto them in my inventory like Diablo 2 did with Charms but instead you have to add them to your gun through the smith. Then once I actually got a screen that allowed me to see what they did I ended up just not giving a ♥♥♥♥ about them half way through the game. If I got a rare one, cool, but I wasn't rushing to get it put on. There are also damage modifier things but I honestly have forgotten what their called and I just finished this game in less than a day after purchase. Thats how little impact they had, atleast I felt. Once you get to actually customizing the guns and adding more and different attachments you kinda learn what you want. I ended up just maxing damage on a majority of the guns, seemed to work! ( Pro tip - Max damage and then just max the Aimbot skill and its pretty much over. The aimbot skill can DESTROY rooms of enemies and using a sub machine gun with super high recoil, suddenly go to 0 recoil and every shot hitting will make the room much easier )What in the world is up with like 80% of the enemies being female? Don't get me wrong that's completely fine and I am sure it opened the door for more female voice actors and talent alike but I felt like I was just slaughtering women over and over every mission. What's up with that?*Spoiler* Also as a jest little bug report, one of the skills is a strength enhancer which gives you a big sword that basically one shots/Close to one shots. *BUT* with the electric wizard ladies that teleport around they seem to need like, 5 or 6+ hits to kill them, while everyone around them was down in 1 hit. Even with all my skills maxed I never did a one shot to them. Always had to keep going. No biggie :)Forewarning, once you beat the game you are done. Like, nothing else left in the game to do besides dumb repeatable side missions. If I didn't do a bunch of side missions I probably would have finished in -2 hours times, but the fact that it did impact gameplay and time played makes it worth it, but only during the story. Story is done, game is done. Unless you just want to start again with an already pretty shortish game be my guest but I believe this will stay uninstalled for the time being simply because I have nothing to do in the game anymore.There is a wide variety of enemy types, all with different weapons and abilities. Was nice. That's basically all the outstanding issues I had with the game, but I think I am due to give this game the credit it deserves.If you are looking for a good action reaction shooter with a little bit of loot elements and are feelin down for a bit of grinding between missions, I highly suggest this game. The atmosphere, characters and story in general were a solid 9/10 for me. I noticed myself not skipping through dialogue (Except with the bar lady, I get it, rats are drunk and you are for some reason tied to the story because you a bartender. She hears things, and tells you them. Basically it. I would have loved to be able to spend credits and just get my character drunk. Would've been a great chance to introduce random events/Mega Bosses) and actually listening/paying attention to the small details they would say. Which DOES get you some better loot in some cases if you just look around/Go a different route then whats in front of you. The game is linear, but still allows for full exploration. Now you might fall out of the map/insta die due to a invis barrier but if you play games you should know when where you're going is just a pit of death. Speaking of the maps, the design is AWESOME. The whole steampunk/Mechanical vibe the game holds stands out everywhere you look. You are all in caves underground with who knows what and the game shows it. So bravo on that part.Skills are pretty standard but useful. I wish I had used the blast or field skills more, learn the muscle memory of using the wheel and quickly going to the skill and it will make the game so much more fun. I mainly used the aimbot, walls and slow down but I slowly started using the other ones on the bigger enemies. You upgrade yourself as the story goes on, but I went full steam ahead and as soon as I could do the side repeatable bounties on the S tier I knocked them out pretty quickly. If you go full steam ahead you can easily clear a S tier bounty in less than 2 minutes. Maybe 1 depending on the mission itself.The "Takedown" skill/Spam E while shooting the big guys seems to be the way to go for the big guys. I soon realized that the takedown skill is very useful and honestly needed in some spots. Thank goodness they make you invuln while the animation is going because I know for sure I wouldn't survive all the shots from the 5 giant robots surrounding me. Can also acrue for some cheeky fast kills/S bounties for taking down hacked robots.No need to go into it. Its a grapple hook that makes the movement fluid.The gun mechanics and shooting in general feels very solid, not too god like but not too garbo either.

_childDocuments_.review: Get it while on sale.Average shooter, set in a 40k universe. I didn't encounter any major bugs and after using GeForce Experience to optimize the game, I stopped encountering lag/jank.Game has quite a few cons, but, unfortunately, it's one of the best 40k shooters. I'd say this is one of those situations where a "Meh" would work better than a Yes/No.I'm going with Yes because the positives are a bit "heavier" than the negatives.Positive:+ Upgrades drastically change your gameplay;+ You have a doggo THAT YOU CAN PET (I used it as a radar, so, no idea if it's bugged or not. I've seen people complain);+ A large variety of weapons;+ Weapon customization similar to Fallout (worse, but similar);+ Weapons feel ok;+ Voice acting is alright;+ Move or die.Negative:- Main mission is average at best;- Final boss battle feels forced;- Some levels are boring (I've surprised myself on several occasions just rushing the objectives to finish the mission);- Secondary missions seem slapped on;- Reputation system is close to useless (once you max your rep with a faction, you get a random item and that's it);- Your appearance doesn't change when applying upgrades;- The world around you seems dead.

_childDocuments_.review: To all those reviews saying "maybe check it out if you’re a warhammer enthusiast", as an enthusiast I made a list that might be helpful for those who already know all of the gameplay related problems.There are no special skins that look like the classic weapons from the tabletop, like the godwyn bolter or armageddon pattern autogun. The skins are very basic recolors with not even an ultra bump mapped mastercrafted relic. Everything has picatinny rail and the basic level 1 gun looks the same as the higher rarities.Boltguns are just slightly slower machineguns with zero special ammo choices that would explode like a grenade, exactly how you don’t want to see them in a game. Seriously, they are just slightly higher damage generic full auto guns with very manageable recoil. Nothing special and completely forgettable.There is no regular lasgun in the game, but an entire faction has plasmaguns and they aren’t THAT rare in necromunda.  We get 7 different auto/stubber/boltguns in the same sort of “aim,shoot” weapon role, so… why not? They should at least play differently with higher capacity ammo and a different sort of accuracy and recoil.They do have a gravgun, a plasmagun, a grenade launcher, a heavy bolter, 2 heavy stubbers and a hotshot long las, but they don’t feel that special or particularly more deadly because they compete with the same 2 weapon slots as your basic autoguns and ammo is ultra-plentiful and generically fills all weapons.There is no melee weapon component. No chainswords, power swords or even a regular non take down melee button. Just a special berserker “smack then die” speed mode special ability.  So, there is no pistol sword combo, even though that’s what Kal Jerico carries in the cutscenes. 90% of the propaganda posters in this game are directly from the games workshop website, so I’ve seen them all already. The rest of the senary is nice though, and it borrows just enough from the plastic kits to look right without seeming copy/pasted.The great big surprise of Genestealers existing is subverted by you being able to take side missions from the cult already. It consists of one mission with only one special new unit. and it isn’t fun or revisited again.There is a giant faction list who give outside missions, including the Inquisition and enforcers, but you never see any of them in the game, and I’m not even sure what the increases exactly do besides maybe give slightly more money? The 3 gangs fight basically exactly the same. I would have liked to see Cawdor with waves of rabble with scrap shotguns or a more technologically advanced Van Saar with a long range focus or something more dynamic. Esher, Golath, and Orlock will mostly just stand around shooting you regardless of their few unique units. Oh and apparently everyone has Refractor Fields so that’s couldn’t have been a Van Saar gimmick.Story is blah and basically just serves the plot to move to new locations and is extreme loaded to be pretty much have all the important bits in the final cutscene with a mild sequel/dlc open ending.I beat the campaign in 7 hours, then spent another 3 hours messing around cheesing the very easy side missions to max out the dog upgrades that I never used to see if it gave me an achievement or different head pat animation. No achievement, no new head pat. I’m done with the game and looking forward to Darktide.7/10 if on sale for 25 bucks. Nah, no thank you/10 at full price.

The character design is not falling behind either, though the game is somewhat lacking in the animation department- but considering the gameplay speed, you will barely even notice it. _childDocuments_.review: I think this is a game that you're only really going to enjoy if you love the Necromunda/40k setting. I was constantly captivated by the world. Any time you pause you could be a wallpaper or art in a book. The setting is so *chefs kiss*. It's a shame though that you barely get time to look at it. The fast Doom/NecroVision style gunplay is great, but doesn't fit the mood for a multi-millennia old factory world with heavy guns. I really wanted this to play like Bioshock or Metro, where ammo is rare and enemies are tough. Mowing down thousands of people because their lives have no worth is very 40k, but it also means there is little thought to how you kill the about 3 different types of enemies or even bosses. I can't help but feel the grapple hook and double jumping actually hurt the game. I really wanted to take my time in each level because they're so carefully crafted and full of love. I wanted each gun's use to be special and for me to think about which enemy needed what ammo type to kill but there wasn't any point. There is also no point to the story. There is a cutscene at the beginning and at the end and if you can remember what happened then good for you, but I don't think it matters. Even if you try to play this game in one sitting, good luck because it is buggy and the fast movement will get you stuck in some parts where you have to reload levels. Random crashes are also no uncommon. It might sound like this is coming off more as a negative review, but  I know Streum On Studio is full of talented people and I hope they get all even more funding for the next game. I'd like to see what they can do with an even bigger budget.

_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: True to its name, Hired Gun lacks a certain.. support structure. Leaving the player high and dry when things get messy. It sure looks appealing though.As other people have explained, the developers of Hired Gun portray the environmental atmosphere of 40k especially well. An unfortunate side-effect though is that for gameplay purposes everything is a visual mess - navigation, target identification, treasure - all of this would be near impossible to see without the giant outlines placed on them. Which certainly helps, and you do have cybernetics as an excuse; along with the option to turn them off if you're feeling brave.Combat. Combat is of course the main feature. You run around, quite fast, and shoot things. Arguably too fast. It is clear the game wants the experience to be speedy and hectic, akin to the Doom reboot, and to facilitate this you have the power to regain life - with the specific caveat of this being only for a few seconds after you are injured. So yes, get in the fray, take damage, deal damage; but if there is a pause and you are on low health, death is likely your only option. Doom however, provides clear options of what will give you health: execute an enemy, burn an enemy, etc. To be fair, the game does have medkits that you will run out of and revive items, the latter you can buy at any of the many checkpoint servitors around the maps. So you are not stopped from playing or continuing, but it's more the inherent nature of the system that you are nearly expected to take damage - regardless of your attempts - especially if you're playing on hard, and have limited ways to fix it. On hard you can just explode because someone had a moment to look at you funny.Overall Hired Gun is okay. It's not strictly bad, there can be some fun, some nice weapons; but it's not really adequate either. Unfulfilling.On the plus side however, you do get a dog, and you do get to do the petting. Even after you mutilat- er... replace their weak fle- ... upgrade. Even after you upgrade them.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this review by saying I am a huge 40k fan, and this game definitely captures the heart of what I love about Warhammer.  The art direction is absolutely fantastic, and I found myself distracted by set pieces thinking, "Oh hey!  Look at that shrine in the wall!  Such 40k!  So wow!"  It really is good.I'm on an i7-9700 and using a RTX 2070 with everything on ultra with no hitches.  I played with the DLSS settings but the game runs comfortably at 100+ fps.  I see a lot of people having framerate issues, the devs have noted these issues in the forums and are working on an optimization patch.  Personally I have had no crashes, and only stutters on the first mission for 15 seconds.On to the actual review: Is the story going to sweep you away, carried aloft by the Emperor's Angels?  No.  The story poses as a pseudo-detective "find the bad guy by tracking his ganger connections" but we all really know why we play this game.  WE ARE BOUNTY HUNTERS, AND WE HUNT BOUNTIES.  Each mission is really just a framing for some fantastic experiences in a violence soaked 40k theme park.  The gunplay and  game is very Doom Eternal-esque, so if you enjoy that and 40k, give this a try.My favorite things so far:The scale - levels are huge, grand, and packed with verticality.Guns are ridiculously fun to use.Installing augmentations into yourself and your cybermastiff is neat and grant cool abilities.There is a ton of detail relevant to 40k hidden throughout the levels and hub if you feel like appreciating it.What I dislike:The "jank" people refer to I think stems from the over-bobbing of the camera during executions and some animations.  While in real life your head would indeed bob and thrash around like that, it is very visually confusing.The cybermastiff is underutilized, and has pathing issues because of the insane verticality previously mentioned.The story is a bit weak, but I forgive it.Do you like 40k?  Then you will like this game.  It isn't a AAA title by a huge studio, but I am having an absolutely fantastic time playing it.  There are glitches, there are janky animations, and there is an entire level devoted to fighting on a moving train the size of a city block that just screams THIS IS THE IMPERIUM OF MAN.  Absolutely fantastic time so far!  Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I need to preface this like by saying I came into this knowing what I was in for. I've lovingly referred to E.Y.E.: Divine Cybermancy as my favorite worst game ever and was hoping this would be more along that vein. That being an game with a unique spin on things. So, if you're expecting another looter shooter you'll probably be turned off by this game. Necromunda has things we've gotten pretty familiar with at this point: Wall running, double jumping, sliding, directional dashing, health/shield but puts its own spin on it. Your shield refills through pickups, like traditional armor shards, but you're health is recovered by either using 1 of 3 medkits you can carry for each mission, or by damaging enemies after they damage you. The closer you are, the more damage you do and how many enemies you kill recovers more health. This is needed because your health drains like someone forgot to put the plug in during combat. You can also mitigate damage by using any of your movement options. Instead of wall running, double jumping etc. being a means to access other areas it actually gives you a % chance to avoid damage while you are doing it. You also aren't limited in how you can use these tools because of that. Yes, you can wall run off of any surface in this game and I have yet to find an invisible wall. As you can imagine with that, combat can be a bit chaotic. You're moving as much as possible while trying to close the distance to enemies to maximize your health regen in combat. This leads to a con in my opinion: that it limits what weapons are useful. The strategy is fire rate and magazine capacity, always be shooting since it's part of your defense. You also get a boost to auto aim (once upgraded) while wall running. So slower weapons; revolver, precision rifles, explosives are less useful because it slows down your health recovery to be hitting less often and, from what I've experience, the extra damage doesn't offset the health recovery. That's the main meat of things, the movement and unique gameplay style are definitely the star of the show, and the gruesome Warhammer setting is the icing on the cake. While the animations in cutscenes are stiff, the setting is awesome to look at. The game is a little light on dialogue that explains things, so if you're interested Warhammer has plenty you can read up on to bring you up to speed. tl;dr This game is bananas. If you're not prepared for that maybe wait for a sale. The closest game I can compare it to would be Ultra Kill, but that's just because they share some mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game at a 25% discount, figured itd just be a fun DOOM shooter. Instead I was met with laughable ultra quality graphics, a buggy experience (I can't count on my fingers how many times using the grapple followed by an execute has pushed me into the floor which you cant jump out of), poor pacing (the game has these amazing sections where the soundtrack ramps up and you feel like youre living the WH40K life, but those are few and far between and its mostly just fighting 3 or 4 weak enemies mixed in with 1 or 2 "threats") and the worst optimized experience since the ARK: Survival Evolved alpha.All of these things aren't as disappointing though as the failure to incorporate the grittier elements of life in the Human Imperium. You hear about this Silver Talon the whole time and there's the Shadow who is your competitor. But neither of these really incorporate the grittyness of Warhammer 40k. It just feels like another cookie cutter story that fails to utilize the strengths of the setting and falls flat. Where are the enforcers that we always hear about? Why are the Tyranids so boring? This game merely uses WH40K as a background aesthetic and then proceeds to provide a bland experience.If you want to pay 30-40 euros to play a beta build of what could have been an amazing game, but amounts to a mediocre at best experience then buy this game. Otherwise buy DOOM 2016 or DOOM Eternal, your money will be better spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Hired Gun is worthy, as it *is* the game you had hoped the developers would make after their Space Hulk effort, though you may not initially think so. The key to enjoying the game is to acquire weapons with good penetration values in conjunction with the adrenal move/time slow ability. Do that, and you'll be having fun.Initial impressions can lead one to believe a number of things. That shotgun weaponry sucks, which actually only applies to the pistol-class sawed off weapon, by virtue of its lack of the aforementioned penetration. That the game is too lightning-movement oriented, which can be offset by plundering the more reasonable 'slide' maneuver in order to bring about movement dodge benefits. That exploration has too much of an emphasis, until you discover how friendly and forgiving double-jump and grapple mechanics are.Some criticisms bear out, such as being unable to swap out the default pistol since it is utilized in executions. Or map variety in side missions (expanded by completing main missions)... we should have custom environments exclusive to those. Or its peculiar inventory management system. Hired Gun succeeds however once you come to grips with such things. And - to provide necessary emphasis - once you equip a weapon with good penetration. This cannot be over-emphasized. Equipping a bolter rifle or a modified automatic shotgun (rifle) was an eye-opening, game enabling experience. And eminently satisfying. Hopefully the devs expand this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd give this a recommend. I was worried after Deathwing and canceled my preorder originally once I realized this was the same studio, but they've done a pretty good job with this game. The combat system is fun, it kind of reminds me of Outriders (heal off damage/kill, active abilities, mild looter) or DOOM/Rage 2. World design and music is very good. Enemy variety is pretty good as well. Really I think it's just a game that gets more fun as you play. You learn what weapons/mods you like, skills/stats increase making combat faster paced and more satisfying. Right off the bat it was still good, but could have been better. I think the main downsides I see with this game is lacking content a touch for what seems like more of a looter shooter. The location and contract variety especially stand out (since more locations are added as you progress through the story, early game can you see you playing the same side mission three times in a row). Also it seems like there is a problem with occasional CTDs when reloading after a death when out of stims. Finally, like 90% of dialogue is spoken away from the camera or by characters that are masked - not a big deal but a minor annoyance.Again, it's not the most polished game, but I am having fun with it and enjoying what is on offer. It's about a 15-20 hour game depending on how much story vs side missions you do. At 17 hours I have all my upgrades, mission 9 (?) next on story, and a good set of gear (no +3 weapons yet though).

_childDocuments_.review: Streum On Studio once again kicks it out of the park, all three of their retail games show their passion for the Warhammer 40K IP/warhammer as a whole, and this game absolutely nails the look of a grimy, 'wartorn' under-city filled with rival gangs vying for control over scraps and locations.The gameplay is absolutely fantastic, even if unpolished here and there, mostly animations and enemy AI being a bit *broken.* Being able to wallrun, double jump and dash like it's Doom Eternal mixed with Titanfall leads to an incredibly addictive gameplay loop of just darting in and out of cover with the dozen or so weapon types, which was handled in a unique way for looter-shooters, and one that doesn't make the game feel bloated, there's 4 tiers of rarity, the highest one (In comparison being a direct upgrade as you can mod every weapon, tuning it into a slaying machine to benefit your playstyle.Only gripes I can give the game is sound mixing being all over the place, dialogue is pretty unaudible for the most part, soundtrack is perfect though and some guns sound a wee-bit weak, other than that planning on buying the listed soundtrack on steam at some point in the future,

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of being it's own game it tries too hard to be Doom (even down to the music style)  but it fails miserably.    Though the levels can look good and the setting is great the level design is terrible, this seems to be a recurring theme with 40K games unfortunately (great setting and IP but some poor games just cashing in). Breakdown of the issues :-The same maps are used over and over for side missions.Janky movement controls and wall running that other games do expertly this game can't seem to manage. This often sees you vault forward and over objects you're trying to climb.You can get stuck against invisible objects which happened several times within the first handful of levels and you will get stuck in walls/terrain when using the grapple.  Buggy missions objectives that forced a restart over a year after launch (another problem that plagues Warhammer games, get them out quick and abandon them).  Overuse of weapon effects means in the heat of action you often can't see where the enemies are due to plasma blasts and smoke.Voice acting is pathetic, characters models and animations are poor.Instead of trying to do a few things and do them well this title tries to cram in too much and executes it poorly.I wasn't expecting much after seeing the reviews and scores but it was worse than I expected.  Coincidentally this is the second Warhammer game from this studio, the first being Deathwing, which was also poor and terrible for bugs when it launched.  I should have looked at this before buying the game, suffice to say I won't be buying a third game if they do one, utter waste of the license.

The side quests are resued parts of the story levels.What they nailed are the stunning visuals of the 41. Millenium, but overall i'd say the game lacks depths as well as palyer agency. There are no choices presented other than which weapons to use or which upgrades to get and they mean little to no difference. The guns do not really have that warhammer feel but if you get it for half the price its a nice little shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: + This starts as a fairly mundane shooter but turns into a fantastic and frenetic FPS once your arsenal grows and you invest into your characters abilities & kit.  Slowing down time, zipping around on a grappling hook, wall running, launching energy blasts from your arm...you've got a lot of tools at your disposal and by the time you master all of them, you really do feel like a living weapon.  This reminds me a lot of RAGE 2 or Shadow Warrior 2 wherein the tedium can feel "frontloaded" but the game gets better and better as it progresses.+ The environments can be gorgeous; the surreal, gonzo spaces of Strom On Studio's EYE Divine Cybermancy seamlessly translate to the absurd scale and strangeness of WH40K's universe. + Great variety of weapons with thorough customization options:  Boltguns, Plasma Guns, Stubguns, Shotguns, etc.  Almost every single one looks great, is well-animated, and fun to use.- The story is underwhelming; most of the sedated exposition comes from running compulsory triangles between three NPCs in the primary hub (go talk to this guy; okay go talk to the bartender; okay now go talk to the Dome Runner; okay now you can go select your mission).- Despite being set in the WH40K universe, the variety of enemies is fairly limited.  Quick readability on enemies can be difficult as well--you'll mostly be fighting ordinary humans armed with various weapons, but at the speed of Hired Gun's combat, the only real way to distinguish between a thug with a simple autogun vs a heavier machinegun or grenade launcher is when they're actually shooting at you. - General glitchiness and jankiness: Animations bugging out, weird physics bugs, falling through solid objects, side missions sometimes being generated in ways that make them impossible to complete, etc.  MOST of the time the bugs are innocuous, but occasionally they can cause legitimate issues.- There's a half-baked elemental damage/resistance system that struck me as pointless; armors can provide resistances to certain types of damages, but it rarely feels like missions consistently throw specific types of damage at you, so it's hopeless to "gear up in advance" to protect against particular damage types.  Similarly, it seems like there's no real strategy beyond throwing whatever on your weapons for the damage buffs.- Since most weapons can take most of the same modifications, many of them end up feeling  distinct rather than  distinct.  I never thought I'd be saying this, but it might have been better for different weapons to have fewer but more unique assortments of modifications than what we get here.- Stealth could be implemented better.  It  works, but with the way the levels are usually laid out, the occasional hyperawareness of the AI, and the way enemies can often respawn wherever in areas--it all discourages any sort of legitimate stealth approach, for better or worse.  At least "going loud" is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It was not even a year ago that we go the abomination that was Necromunda: Underhive Wars. Hired Gun is in the same setting, but offers up a complete genre shift, so I went into it hoping it could redeem the franchise for me.I think the best way to describe the gameplay here would be as basically a clunkier DOOM, but with an increased emphasis on movement. This game has you double-jumping, sliding into tubes, scaling buildings, wall running, and even grappling – all while shooting. It is a very fast-paced game that goes for that same kind of classic FPS gameplay, one where you’re blasting enemies left and right, swapping weapons in-between, and dashing all over the place.This aspect of the game is solid. It is an absolute rush once it gets going and I never found myself feeling bored with it. Part of this was due to the level design. It’s somehow both very open, yet feels like its packed full of stuff. Pipes going everywhere, machine parts hanging from the ceiling, enemy hiding spots all over – it really nails that underground, industrial Necrumunda look while at the same time providing for some solid movement options. That’s not to say that the movement is perfect though. Wall running is a bit too sticky, you’ll sometimes not grab ledges you mean to grab, and momentum while airborne can get a bit weird too.The gunplay, on the other hand, is pretty good all around. The actual act of shooting feels great and being able to rapidly swap between your arsenal in less than second definitely helps give the game that fast-paced feel to it. There’s also a good amount of guns to choose from and even more so when you consider the fact that each of your weapons can be upgraded individually.Guns, charms, armor, and upgrades all have different rarity levels and can be bought and sold at the hub world. This is also where you can upgrade your own body and that of your dog companion. I have mixed feelings on this part of the game. I liked that the option was there to upgrade and swap around my stuff – but a good chunk of it just felt unnecessary.It was kinda tedious having to cycle through all the stuff I picked up during a mission to determine what I would keep and what I would sell, only to repeat that same process thirty minutes later after the next mission. Something like “discard all but a certain rarity level” would have been very helpful, but even then, I feel like the game went a bit too hard on the looter stuff for how short of an experience it is.The main campaign took me just over six hours to clear. Some are immediately going to be put off by this, but the game was paced well enough that it wasn’t really an issue for me. I did not do any of the side missions until afterwards and you can easily spend double that time doing all of those. Granted, these just earn you credits and affect reputation with different factions – so if you are not really into the whole “looter” element of the game like I was, then they’re pretty much just filler.I mean, this is Warhammer, so I wasn’t really expecting much in the way of story anyways, but there is a decent-sized one here and I was not a fan. The lore is good, but the writing is anything but, jumping all over the place and not really fleshing out any of the characters beyond the surface level. It was more so there as a means to connect the levels in a somewhat coherent manner – so don’t go in expecting much from it.As for the graphics… well, I can’t deny that they’re not the best. It looks like an FPS that came out maybe five years ago and it’s obvious that this is coming from a mid-tier studio trying to make a AAA-looking game. Muddled textures, stiff animations, lifeless faces – graphics are definitely not the strong suit.The music was fine and went for that same style metal soundtrack that DOOM did, but the rest of the sound is subpar at best. For being in this big, underground space with machines and stuff everywhere, there isn’t much in the way of industrial ambience. That and the sound mixing is downright awful at times. Voices are fine during some scenes, but really quiet during others.I had to turn down to medium settings to run the game at 1440p and above 60 fps with my GTX 1070 Ti, which is fine, but there were micro-stutters on top of that. They happened during when I assume the game was loading in new areas in the background, sometimes while I was in combat. This was with the game installed on an NVMe SSD, so it’s not like speed was an issue either.And while I didn’t run into any crashes, I did run into a few bugs. For example, there was a boss fight where I was stuck unable to shoot until I used an ability – lowering and raising my weapons again. Otherwise, the game plays fine. The FPS is mostly stable, the keyboard and mouse controls are fitting, and the variety of settings are nice to have too. The only thing missing there is horizontal FOV. The game has vertical FOV, but not horizontal for some reason.Necromunda: Hired Gun may have some issues, but ultimately, it is still a fun game and worth a look if you’re a Warhammer or FPS fan. The shooting feels great, there’s a ton of movement options, and the level variety has you going all over the place – sampling just about everything that the Underhive has to offer. Still, the gameplay is a bit rough around the edges and there are some technical issues, but hopefully some patches can clean it up a bit. It is far better than the last Necrumunda game we got if anything.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted this game as I love everything warhammer, saw it pop up in a Humble Choice and resubbed. Not disappointed I did. Its a good little game that reminds me a lot of Firewarrior from back in the day. It does a great job of interpreting the source material, provides an interesting perspective on that material (Necromunda rather than 40K: Spacemaries/Fantasy battle) and good gameplay, but dont expect AAA polish:The Good- Atmosphere: I really thought the gritty, harsh reality of the Hive world was done well. The way the characters spoke picked up on nice lore pieces from the source material. - Gun play: felt good, if a little bullet spongy on higher levels. The modification system felt largely irrelevant which was a shame.- Replayability: Even though its limited (so few maps etc) the bounty system is a nice addition to buff out gameplay and let you test out new weapons while earning new equipment. - Length: I found a fair few gold weapons, played on the second highest difficulty and amassed a fortune with the bounty system. 34 hours seems like a nice stay for this one. The Bad- Story: It's pretty disjointed to the point of not really understanding why you are doing things, who people are and their relationship to you, or, why certain things are made a point of (house politics for instance). This could be due to my lack of familiarity with the setting. - Key mapping: I didnt try playing on my controller, but the mapping is hot garbage. There are clearly too many abilities you can unlock with cybernetics and they are mapped from 7-9+...right in the middle of both my hands. Not a problem if you want to remap or program them to your gaming mouse, but I couldn't be bothered and just forgot about them to spray more bullets. Maps: Too few and some are just too hard to navigate (also why the atmosphere is excellent and well done). I wandered around aimlessly trying to find the path forward a few times. Got it in the end but I needed it to be clearer for some levels. The Ugly- Glitches: You will often grapple through walls and get stuck. When this happens you can either try and grapple out, or start again. High 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR: Genuinely brilliant atmosphere, environmental detail, service to the 40K universe and fan service fail to save what is otherwise an utter shambolic disaster of a game. The Emperor is not pleased.Longer review:You are a nameless mercenary employed by a man named Kal Jerico to do combat missions for him in the underhive of the Imperium's largest hive city. The underhive is a grim, filthy, brutal world where life is short, violent and cheap. Gang warfare is constant. Your mission is to help Kal Jerico find answers after a previous employer was assassinated by persons unknown. To help you in your mission you get access to biomechanical modifications that can be upgraded, various weapons that can be customised to suit your play style, and a faithful dog who can also be augmented with various abilities and upgrades. There are 13 main story missions and endless numbers of what appear to be procedurally generated side mission that are generated from small portions of the main campaign missions. Both the main and side missions earn you credits to buy upgrades, better weapons, weapon attachments etc.I should note, and I cannot emphasize this strongly enough, that the level of detail and fan service exhibited by the maps is genuinely amazing. Little details that probably nobody except the most die-hard 40K fanatics will ever even notice, is everywhere. Map design, the texture work and details are all 100% exactly as I would imagine a hive city underhive to be. Genuinely outstanding work by whoever did the art. Weapon models are also familiar from the 40K setting, look suitable and sound great. Even the most hard-core member of the Holy Inquisition would be happy with the way the maps look and feel.So why then the not recommended tag? Well, where do I even start?The core problem with the game is a combination of the enemy spawn mechanic and the core gameplay loop. Your character has a pathetically low amount of health. You have a shield but it's also weak even when fully upgraded. You take mountains of damage from enemies, some of which can nearly 1-shot you on higher difficulties. You can carry health kits, though only 3, and can pick up shield rechargers. It's also possible to get health back via one of your abilities: operated automatically, you can recover health by doing damage to enemies. Sounds reasonable? If only. Many enemies have shields that have to be breached before you can activate a melee kill animation that 1-shots most of them. The problem is this: while the animation is playing out, literally another 5 enemies have spawned in and are actively shooting you from all sides. A grenade has landed at your feet. So, by the time you've actually recovered health it's already been effectively lost due to the amount of damage you're now taking.You might summon your dog who, when fully upgraded, is great at taking out trash-mob enemies. Again though this often doesn't work because about 50% of the time the damned dog won't actively attack and just stands there, also taking damage, until you actively order it to attack something. While you're doing this another 4 enemies have spawned and are yet again all shooting you.This combat system forces you in to an ultra-aggressive balls-to-the-wall gameplay style. Fine, but it's frequently ineffective due to the fundamentally broken spawn mechanic. The game loves to overwhelm the player with enemy numbers. Most are hitscanners and their weapons are accurate at ranges far beyond what your weapons are capable of. Hordes of enemies spawn in areas that you the player cleared literally seconds ago so ducking in to cover to reload often simply results in you taking more damage from a freshly spawned enemy, a grenade or both.The difficulty curve is also very uneven, both for the campaign and side missions. Early campaign missions are OK as are the later ones because by the end you're probably fully upgraded. Mid-campaign missions can however be incredibly unforgiving. Several campaign missions also involve boss fights, two of which also involved never-ending spawns of trash mobs which also simply serve to overwhelm the player. It's simply badly designed. Difficulty also varies widely between side missions that are supposed to have equivalent difficulty, again largely due to the failed and wildly inconsistent enemy spawn mechanic.Story? If you're deeply, and I do mean DEEPLY versed in the Necromunda 40K setting then the story might make sense, though like everything else in the game it's incoherent, poorly told and comes with literally zero exposition or explanation. If you don't have a deep understanding of the Necromunda setting within 40K then the story will be meaningless from start to finish. The end of the story is also fundamentally pointless from the player's perspective and just comes to an abrupt end.After completing the campaign you're left with doing side missions for loot and cash. There are a couple of different types e.g. defend an area, capture an area, eliminate enemy bosses, rescue hostages or take out malfunctioning combat robots. These can be fun within the confines of the failed enemy spawn system but all take place within small areas of the campaign maps so they very quickly become boringly repetative.Other points? Sound design & music is also genuinely excellent. Full marks there as well. Weapons sound meaty to use as do other sound effects. Voice acting is a very mixed bag. Everyone has a thick British accent of varying types. Kal Jerico and the protagonist are well voice acted (mixing is terrible though) but some of the voice acting for human enemies is absolutely abysmal. One faction in particular all have thick cockney accents for some reason that just feel totally out of place. Anyone reading this who's played the game will probably agree that hearing constant shouts of "Aww, I'm not done" sounds frankly asinine.It appears that at some point during development the dev team were ordered to stop and publish. The later campaign maps suffer from some serious performance problems and also appear to not have had a smoothing pass so getting stuck on small terrain objects is a semi-frequent problem.Though the game has been patched several times problems remain. To be fair it's never crashed on me which is good for a game these days but all in all unless you the reader are a serious 40K fanatic I can only recommend staying far away from this game. With the exception of the superb art, map design and fan service literally everything else about this game is a shambles of poor design and poorly thought out game mechanics. For 95% of players I cannot recommend this in any way. If you are a 40K fanatic then wait for this to be on deep, deep sale. It's not even close to being worth the normal asking price. Even as a 40K fan myself, frankly I would refund this if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a longtime fan of Streumon and have preordered every game they have made at full price. EYE is an absolute masterpiece and honestly this gets 40k gunplay right on a lot of levels. I desperately want to like this game. The main problems is that this game is not a first person shooter. The melee takedown bound to the E button is so insanely game breakingly powerful that there is no reason to ever shoot in combat outside of boss battles where the melee takedown doesn't work. The grappling hook and the melee takedown on shielded enemy bionic are by far the most powerful weapons in the game and nothing else comes close. Why should I engage with the combat system and play for score when it's exponentially easier to melee takedown everything and not care about money at all? Why should I care about searching the level for chests in order to get better guns when ultimately all I care about is more money to upgrade my melee takedown to maximum level?There's a lot of good weapons in this game, and no reason to ever engage with any of them because the melee takedown is so insanely overpowered that guns quickly become a vestigial accessory to it, and it ruins the game. Also, the cutscenes being deliberately framed so that the developers would never have to animate the mouth of any character other than Kal Jerico is blatantly obvious, and the entire plot of this game amounts to being a brain dead third stringer in a Kal Jerico plot that you aren't privy to because the writer does not respect you enough to explain the plot to you.There is no reason to pay full price for this game when EYE already exists and doesn't link your end of mission payouts to a horrible system that requires you to play the game suboptimally to get a maximum score. This isn't Devil May Cry and it isn't deep or technical. It's an insanely broken game on a fundamental level. I hate to say it, but this is for the 40k hardcore only, because I would not have paid full price for this game if I wasn't one. I want Streumon to make the brilliant game their stuff shows hints of, but EYE was the closest they came and this honestly feels like a step back from Deathwing. At least the systems in Deathwing had a purpose. This just seems arbitrarily crammed with features with no regard for balance or overall gameplay experience, and much like Diablo 3, 99% of what drops once you start seriously playing the game is unusable vendor trash. This is just not well designed, and it does me no pleasure to say this, because I want Streumon to keep making games and I think they get 40k in a way most developers don't.Really, I blame everything wrong with this game on the hideous post-Carmack Doom revival in 2016 destroying the doom franchise and FPS genre forever over some dumbass meme comic, but that's a much longer story for a separate post. If you love 40k, you'll buy this game and tolerate it because it does the franchise better than anyone else does regardless of how broken it is. If you don't love 40k, don't play this.

_childDocuments_.review: The game wants to be Doom in a 40k skin but sadly struggles. But that doesn't ruin it, the atmosphere of a Hive world is brilliant, the maps while repetitive - if you do any of the side missions - look great. The guns you use feel great and the whole upgrade mechanics are quite in depth. The secondary missions add a bit of repeatability if you are wanting to fully upgrade yourself but......it is let down by difficulty settings that seem to do nothing and an AI that seems to spawn everything behind you. Now that would be fine until you have multiple bullet-sponge enemies in multiple waves. Yes you are given the tools to deal with these but not until you earn money.Basically if you are a 40k fan and want a semi decent Doom skin then you'll enjoy it. Admittedly the few boss fight were pretty intense. But if I wasn't a 40k fan to begin with I don't think I would have stuck it out...

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it for what it is, which is not my favorite style of shooter.  You've got a re-playable mission thing, but there are very few enemy types (factions).  They push for a 'rush through at high speeds gunning' playstyle, while also rewarding scouring the map for hidden items.  :/  Felt a lot like Warframe at times.  Enemies respawn, that is a big push for the rush part - you can get ground down if you aren't moving and gunning.   You literally heal by killing up close.  So if you are willing to play the game the way they intended, it works.  If you can have fun doing that, you'll enjoy this game as a whole.   The art and graphics are great, I enjoyed the story for the type of game it is.  If you've played E.Y.E. you'll recognize the mission vs side mission style (side missions are using the story maps you've unlocked so far, with semi random assigned tasks).  Half way through the story I maxed out everything I could buy doing side missions to boost rep with diff factions thinking that would do something, but the rep doesn't do much...  If you like the 40k setting this has some extra coolness in seeing a great representation of the setting.  The weapons are...  well game balance is what it is.  You won't bother with what are supposed to be the some of the most common weapons in the game world (las anything), and the fancy, powerful, and supposedly super rare stuff...   isn't.   Still fun blasting my way through.  Note that if a main story mission gets hard, do a few side missions to boost your cybernetics to bring down the difficulty of the missions.  With all of it maxed out, all the missions are much, much easier.   I see people saying they are dying but only have a few hours in the game...  Well yeah, you need to get that gear and cybers up - you don't start as a space marine in this one...  You also have a variety of killing methods, try different ones for diff types of enemies.  When in doubt, shoot em in the head.  GL
