_childDocuments_.review: Where to start with this game.... At the surface level Necromunda is an extremely beautiful Warhammer 40k game. It all however starts to go downhill as the game progresses however. I played on the hardest difficulty which wasn't too bad at all if you are experienced with fps shooters. Now lets talk about the bad.-There are A LOT of bugs in this game. The issue with the bugs in this game are the fact that the majority of them force you to reboot the game in order to progress. I've had enemies that spawn in walls and guess what you can't keep going past the enemy you must clear them all out. I've had a dog jump on me and for the remainder of a level my screen was tilted as if playing at a 45 degree angle. It's really, really, buggy.-The cutscenes. These are beyond laughable. The majority of the cutscenes your character's back is to the camera. You can't see anyone talk during the dialog. If your dog jumps at someone in a cutscene its OFF SCREEN. For a 40 dollar game its pretty embarrassing. How can you make such a gorgeous game and simply ignore the cutscenes.-The story. It's bad. The ending is worse. You fight mounds and mounds of people but for what a bounty and no questions asked? Theres no real antagonist here. More over after you beat this game there is zero actual dialogue in the bar that discusses ANYTHING post game. If you talk to the bartender she just says whats up? Again, for a game that is half this price that would be acceptable. For a 40 dollar game however no.-The Grappling Hook- Doesn't always work. It seems like there are fixed locations at which you can grapple and you can go through objects as well when you do so.-The Weapons. They all feel a bit similar the stand out weapons I've noticed were the plasma rifle and bolt. Both awesome feeling guns but the progression system of upgrading the gun never evolves. You get the gun and immediately upgrade attachments and you can ride that weapon until the end. You would think with all the loot you pick up there would be stronger and stronger gun variants you can pick up but nope. It's pretty much fixed to rarity. You get a purple gun and put attachments you have that gun until the last level if you like it.-Health design. This is minor but having no ways to buy more medpacks during a mission but able to buy stims is VERY, VERY, stupid. The only way to regen is shooting when shot at. Yup.-The Loot System. Why... It serves no purpose. As mentioned once you get a gun and put attachments there is no reason to get more loot. Sure you can get a rarity upgrade and occasionally get more damage on a tech but thats it. You pick up loads of garbage thats all. Even on the max difficulty theres no real amazing loot.  The Good:-Beautiful game. Surprisingly ran pretty well on my computer 150+ fps for all levels no bad zones with low frames.-The music is great. Definitely feels like they tried to pull off a doom soundtrack and feel and it works for the most part it was good.-You can pet the dog.-Outlines on enemies and dog gives aoe vision. This is SUCH a nice QoL thing. Actually very happy about this feature.  All in all the game does not feel polished at all has decent shooting. A horrible inventory, story, and is EXTREMELY buggy. I would say steer clear of this and maybe give it a chance if things get updated to the point that there is little to no bugs. If you are a story driven gamer skip this all together. There is no story here besides I want a bounty. You choices that you make in the game don't matter.

_childDocuments_.review: Ive only played a little bit, but I see tons of people comparing this game to DOOM Eternal, if you are here for an experience like what DOOM: Eternal offered, look elsewhere, this game is not at all on par with DOOM at ALL, its not very polished at all, a lot of stiff animations and general 40KFPS jankI am in no way saying this is a bad game though, in fact it's pretty fun, player movement feels great even in the early game, weapons are punchy and sound decent enough, (The heavy bolter sounds like ♥♥♥♥, that gun is supposed to fire what is akin to a 50.cal Barret round, and it sounds like its MAYBE spitting out normal 50.cal like what youd see in a real life machine gun emplacement or the gun on top of a tank)  |But this game IS full of a bunch of stupid mistakes or oversights that should be very obvious from the very start, first and foremost this game is attempting to be a sort of Looter Shooter, and you cant see ANY GUN STATS while in a level. Cmon Streum On Studio what were you thinking with this? Theres not even any menus to check the guns you get from chests and stuff, yet you CAN equip them when they drop. So lets say you equip a gun thats worse off than the one you currently have in your hands, congrats you just gimped yourself for the rest of the level YOU CANNOT go back in a menu to reequip what you started with, in a looter shooter, or see what stats the guns have, IN A LOOTER SHOOTER.The gameplay itself is great, combat feels good, fast, fun i reccomend playing it just for the combat alone, oh and the music and setting? top notch ♥♥♥♥, you guys did amazing with this games atmospherethe stuff I complained about could be fixed with patches so lets hope they doThats all for now, ill update this more probally when I beat itOh and for the 2 people wondering heres the song used in the Cybermastif/best friends trailer

_childDocuments_.review: No.  Not this year at least.These developers have a knack for creating incredibly attentive and perfectly detailed visual representations of the Warhammer 40K universe.  What they lack in specialized skill-sets in creating an objectionably functional product, they make up for in the art department in spades.  However, that's where the quality of the product ends.Literally nothing in this game is responsive. - It suffers from terrible jitter forming from a lack of properly optimized shaders.   - The menu UI is never sure whether you're clicking on objects within a said frame or clicking something else over  China.   - The combat is meant to be fluid with a constant range of motion and animation so that the player seemlessly slides across the landscape and catapults into individual gunplay and melee but...the whole thing is so disjointed that each action is a disconnected container.   - Performing melee action is jarring because it forces the player's camera to reset into some predisposed position after it's completed. - Sometimes weapons shoot.  Sometimes they don't.  Because reasons.  At first I thought it was my mouse input but then I tried a handful of other games in the days and hours that followed and was met with no issues.  In short, inputs lag to a point that they don't function half of the time.The scariest part?  This game had the opportunity to be one of the most potentially awesome flagship titles Focus Home could ever offer.  But, they squandered it by releasing it potentially months or years before it should be considered a complete product.The SAME EXACT thing happened with their previous game:   Space Hulk Deathwing (Enhanced Edition).It took the developers a whopping two whole years to fix and patch the game to a point of a playability.  Again, another title that had ridiculous amounts of potential and they also abandoned it.  Leaving it to rot without fixing any of it's long standing bugs from it's original release or bothering to optimize the game.I don't see this game turning out any differently and, it's tragic.  It could be so, so much more.  These developers are held back by an inept publisher that cares for nothing other than milking a core IP.  If they took their passion elsewhere and got better QA support they would be behemoths for the Games Workshop franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, fast paced shooter based in the 40k universe, specifically Necromunda. If you are a fan a shooters, you will enjoy this game. Each weapon feels different, powerful, and excellent. If your into 40k, you will like this game. The atmosphere, the architecture, and the aura are more than enough, then you get bolters...If you like any of the DOOM games, or even Quake, you will like this game. Same fast paced motion and movement, plus a bit more. The ability to customize your weapons too, is a big bonus. Theres nothing massive you can do, but each item definitely has its own feel. Plus there are different variations on your standard weapons. Again, they all feel different, and each has its own qualities and drawbacks. Having only played 11 hours as of this review, I can wholeheartedly recommend it. Fun missions, excellent level design, very nice gun play, and a bit of customization. so far I'm going to give it a 9/10!

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but it's just an ok game. The design and aesthetic is awesome. The game looks nice, the movement is nice. that's about it. The customising is surface level stat boosts (aside from ammo types). I would have preferred a variety of guns that weren't customisable but played uniquely than many guns that are pretty similar and can be customised to be essentially the same (namely the autoguns and the bolters, they feel the exact same in terms of gameplay and I can customise them to have next to the same stats as the other). The dog that was hyped up in the trailers is literally just an ability that lasts up to, what, 15 seconds? The dog is a short term summon that takes aggro, does damage and give wallhacks. The gunplay is underwhelming, guns don't sound great, and to pretend there's a feeling of impact there's just lots of camera shake and blurring. Sound design in general with Hired gun leaves lots to be desired, the only time I've heard ambient sounds is on a giant moving train, I thought this was a loud industrial hive world? The game is shockingly quiet most of the time, with the occasional "ambient music sound 1.mp3". the music is also ok. The animations are also ok. This game just feels like an indie attempt at DOOM in a 40k setting. The environments of the game are what carries it, personally. And even then, these big open environments don't work well in this kind of game. You can't really take advantage of the movement mechanics in a big arena with no walls other than the perimeter, you just spam dash and slides.In terms of music, I was hoping for more of what was in the trailers, but it's a cheap take on the DOOM tracks.I'm not going to score it out of 10, I either recommend it or I don't. For Hired Gun, I just can't recommend it, even for other 40k fans.I may be wrong in some of my experiences, but I'm not going to force myself to play in the hopes it may get more fun. I feel no emotion out of this game. I'm not even a cool bounty hunter, I'm cheap doomguy, wading through hordes of 40k themed goons, some of which are just bullet sponges.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Hired Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Wallrunning, grappling hooks and glory kills. Got your attention yet? Good!Streum On Studio doesn't make the most polished games ever, but their stuff always oozes heart and soul, and Necromunda: Hired Gun is no exception. This is a movement shooter that's mostly concerned with delivering a fun campaign set in the Warhammer 40k universe, and so far, I haven't been disappointed.Guns feel powerful (they tear off people's limbs willy-nilly) and the movement system is great, especially once you do the second mission where you get a grappling hook and have a double jump ability in addition to being able to wallrun from the get go.Graphically it doesn't look super hot, but the art department did an amazing job conveying the crazy scale of 40k. The soundtrack is nice and the voices can be a mixed bag but I'm kinda used to that in this sort of title.Performance varies between amazing and not so great at times (FPS drops aren't super frequent but they happen from time to time). If you have an RTX card you can use DLSS for some extra oomph.Overall, a really fun experience so far, hopefully it'll stay that way for the duration of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cautious thumbs up and the first game I've truly had a hard time deciding which thumb to choose.It's a very fun old-school shooter like Quake 4 or the Doom reboot, but it has a LOT of issues and ZERO replay value.Pros-> Doggo.> Fun powers.> Hilarious whenever the main character talks. My favorite line is, "YEAH."> Pretty graphics.> Shooting feels tight with most guns.> Traversing the world feels fluid in most areas.Cons-> I felt REALLY bad forcing surgical implants on my doggo and killing enemy puppers.> No alpacas.> In 8 hours, I had 3 game crashes.> (optional) side missions are as boring and basic as they get.> Can only access your equipment when going into a mission. (No inventory menus in the game hub.)> Voice acting is weirdly quiet.> Story is complete trash.> After the latest update, the game has crashed the last four times I tried to use the bionic upgrade menu, so I uninstalled.Shameless Plug:Watch me play the first mission and tell me I'm not pretty?

_childDocuments_.review: Don't bother.I bought it on sale expecting a rough but enjoyable 6/10 game. It's total garbage. The setting is incredible and the level design is wonderful, but it's laid on top of a game I wouldn't recommend if it was free. Animations are janky, combat is weightless, it's filled with systems that take an hour to fiddle with but have no appreciable impact. Worst of all is the health system. It tries to be DOOM Eternal, with you having to be aggressive to stay alive...but the enemies use hitscan so your health can disappear in seconds. So many missions can see 20 minutes flushed down the toilet by an instant loss of all health.Avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that when i DID manage to get this game to run it was a straight up blast, it was like DOOM but with customization to your load outs and you could choose your path to upgrading your merc. Very fast play style and very punishing when it was meant to be, a few times it told me to run i stuck around to see if i could out kill the NPC's but they infinitely kept spawning until i moved on to prove a point that i needed to go.The story writing itself i will say does need some work in the since that it did not explain very well the sheer scale of diversity between alot of the other group, what they represented, or the sheer scale of what kind of world Necromunda actually is. Though i imagine it is rather difficult to do so when it involves the Warhammer universe, as most folks only really keep up with the Space marines part of it. I can say however that how everything goes down in it is pretty accurate to how chaotic and backstabby it is supposed to be in this Hive city.HOWEVER I cannot recommend this game in its current state right at this moment due to the technical issues that i had to nitpick just to get the game to launch. First and formost was the crashing upon launch, the UE4 would actually Hitch and sometimes fail to execute unless you did BOTH of these things. -Disable Fullscreen Optimization- and -Running DX11-, until i did both of these changes i could not even get to the start menu. In fact, the first time it happened i thought it bricked my rig until i realized it caused my whole PC to restart. Even then after i made these changes the game would crash after about 1-2 full missions of like 2 hours playtime, my guess is that it is somehow causing a memory leak of some sort.Over all i can actually say that i enjoyed this game and its pacing of combat, the story doesnt truly have a narrator which is sometimes needed with Warhammer games as those whom have prior knowledge of Necromunda might be able to keep up with what is happening. But definitely someone who has no idea whats going on would be very, VERY confused or not hooked on what kind of universe they just got themselves into. Until these software glitches are fixed however, this review will remain so as a no go for me. Risking my hardware, and getting a headache for one game just not worth it for me. Which is very unfortunate.

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is why I like these devs. They have had a few goes at making 40K games now, and pretty much every time they are able to get the world around the player right. Not all were good, most mediocre of course.  I would dare say this is a solid FPS though, in sound design and the feel of how the guns shoot lining up with how I would expect them to. Enemies are also decently challenging, with a variety of tactics they will use against you, from simply throwing grenades to burrowing under your feet to reposition. Combat is satisfying given said guns also have a distinctly destructive impact on the enemy's bodies, alongside customisation.However. There are issues, no doubt about that. Glory kills, cause that's what they are, sometimes do not quite have the animations line up for where you are supposed to be vs where the enemy NPC is. Switching from a bolter to anything else is highly not recomended, unless you are out of the scarce ammo the game gives you for it... The enemies seem to have an awful lot of bolters and plasma weapons, come to think of it. Standard issue imperial lasguns would be way easier to come by.As for customization, pretty much all guns get all customization options. As in, all guns get the same muzzle types, or no option to customize it, like the heavy stubber not being able to get sights, and cosmetic gun skins are absurdely expensive. 80 000? for no gameplay purpose besides having a shiny gun rather than a black one? Let alone not being able to switch your default revolver to the +1,+2, or +3 revolver which all share the same model and animations Good and bad, moving on.I have noticed enemy Ai can be a bit brain dead at times, seemingly not noticing you are shooting them at extended ranges. On the flipside, being a sneaky git and stabbing most of a group of spread appart enemies from the back does work likely because of this. This game is... a bit above average, in terms of what you should expect. Game is solid, with some polishing up to do at the time of this review. Certainly one of the better 40K games to have come out recently, but that does not mean it is unworthy of criticisim. On the contrary. It should be judged far more harshly as a result, being one of very few in this setting that are actually good,... and that the devs appear to be listening to some of the complaints the comunity has made, such as fixing wonky sights on most guns. Again, trust in the bolter, she will see you straight.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR  Took me a while to decide which direction the thumb goes, but the game as it stands doesn't deserve the $40 price tag. The Good:  The environments are absolutely gorgeous. There is an insane amount of detail in the world. Whoever designed (most of) these levels deserve recognition. The gunplay in the game is very enjoyable. It steals liberally from the DOOM franchise with HP mechanics, rewarding extreme aggression.  So great environments and fun gunplay, why the thumbs down? Well, this is why:THE BAD: The enemy re-spawn rate is both insane, and silly. Insane in quantity, silly in execution. Enemies will absolutely spawn all over the place, starting from inches behind you to being hidden in far away closets. There is no rhyme or reason to this.  It is absolutely immersion breaking. The game play devolves into an "Arena shooter" style experience, which absolutely wastes any potential the setting may provide.THE BADDER: The not enough quotation marks in the world "Plot".  The plot is relayed to you in two different ways: in person and radio dialogue, which is just... just god awful, and in-engine cut scenes, which are less awful, but still bad. Allow me to elaborate:  <pause> HELLO ANTAGONIST, I AM PROTAGONIST..... <long pause><pause> (GRAVEL NOISES) I AM GRUFF BOI WHAT DO YOU WANT.... <long pause>the delivery is on the level of a 5th grade school play, with a LONG pause between lines. Whoever did the conversation mixing for the game should NEVER feel good about this project. This is an absolute failure of the craft. It is absolutely clear that the actors recorded their lines separately, and their conversations were spliced together. Now I realize that this is fairly standard in the industry, but that  just makes this execution even more unacceptable.   The cut scene exposition dumps are just... like... wow. So bad. Literally nothing more than an exposition dump, from characters that I do NOT care about at all. The plot itself is... there? I guess? Some people you don't care about are having a minor disagreement that you don't find out about until the final level, at which point the game stops, and talks to itself for a while about things that I just do NOT care about. The God-awful: The lore. This game bent the lore over a pinball machine. If you want to explore and immerse yourself in a hive world, this is not for you.  Generic fallout 4 enemies.  Guns that are "Generic gun # 344". The bolter is not a bolter. SPOILERS: The largest issue I have with this game is the lore. If this game was NOT called 40K, it would be a better game. Here are some things that stand out:  Genestealers that can't kill a human. Really. The game has a level where you get rushed by DOZENS of genestealers, and you just mow them down without the slightest concern.Psychers. There are SO MANY damned psychers in this game. Near the second half, I killed more psychers than would fill a black ship. The people who wrote the actual "game" part of this game had NO IDEA what the hell they were doing.  They made a generic shooter (A pretty good one too) and then reskinned some stuff with a coat of warhammer paint. This is such a shame, because if they would just use different entities, all of the game could have been lore appropriate. Do I recommend the game? Depends. If you can get it for 20 bucks, and just want a fun shooter, in the vein of DOOM, then yes. If you like the whole "Cyberpunk in a cathedral" aesthetic, go for it. If you want a "40K" experience, then I wouldn't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: So played the game for a couple of hours now and here are my thoughts:Pros:- Graphics look good, though not top notch- i really cant think of moreCons:- The UI is a mess. I just now managed to find out how to equip items from the inventory, since it is not drag and drop (a foolprove system used by games since 20+ years) and also just found out, that only because you have items or charms on your character screen, dosent mean that they are equipped. Usually in onther games, items that are on the character count es equipped and the rest is in a seperate inventory. Not in this game. Also you cant (as far as i know) browse and change your inventory as you please, but only at the start of a mission. Its basically the least intuitive UI i have seen in quite a while and the game dosent do a good job in explaining it.- Movement and combat feels a bit wierd, like as if the character has no weight at all. Comparing it to doom eternal, when i jump from a great height, in doom, the landing will shake a bit the screen and you will get an impact sound. In this game you get neither, which is bad for the immersion. - Abilities: They seem nice, but you need a lot of buttons to make use of them all, which is annoying to learn at the start. I use voice attack now to make it easier. - Dog: I dont really use it much, most of the time i forget about it, since its not constantly around. And the times i do use it, it just seems to get gunned down in a second. So as a verdict, id say, if you are a Warhammer 40k fan (as i am) then the game is a nice addition to the gaming collection, but dont buy it at full prize. For anyone else, there are better titles around in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Gunplay and movement are pretty fun. Lots of abilities means tons of ways to play, whether you want to be a Gun nut, a swift melee killer or a power slinging caster.. or everything at once. The world is exceptional. From the level design to the enemies to the posters on the wall this game screams not only 40k in ways that not many other games have, but it is straight Necromunda. The vertical expanse and space to explore is second to none.Neutral: The story is a little bland. But I mean, its an Action FPS. Its not any worse than say Quake or DoomCons:  You HAVE to know a lot about the world to really enjoy it. While the game does an amazing job dropping you right into the hell of Necromunda, it does a very poor job explaining anything about the world, the players in it, the weapons etc. While its amazing fan service to existing 40k universe fans, its not going to do a lot to bring someone new into the fold. Better environmental story telling or at least discoverable journal entries, data slates etc would be a great way to really build the worldSome of the story telling and level flow is a little quirky. On several occasions I found myself running around a large room for 20 minutes looking for a random crank, button, or lever thats only listed as "Release the Holy Oil" with no indication as to how that is accomplished. There are also some set scenes where your attention isn't encouraged for forced in a direction, leaving you a little confused as to what is happeningOverall, I highly enjoyed Hired gun and hope to see some DLC expanding on the Lore and story of the game, as well as making the side game (the contracts and faction gains) more worth while
